# FERDINANDI KOPF <note>Ferdinand Kopf was likely the editor or a contributor to this specific edition of the Bible.</note>

<image-desc>An ornamental horizontal header band consisting of a repeating decorative pattern of stylized foliage and fleur-de-lis motifs.</image-desc>

**To** conclude, I believe it will be neither unpleasant nor entirely useless if I discuss very briefly the Apocryphal Books, some of which are found in Bibles placed outside the order of the Canonical books. They are as follows: the one hundred and fifty-first Psalm, the Prayer of Manasseh King of Judah, the third and fourth books of Maccabees, and the third and fourth books of Esdras <note>The naming and numbering of these books can vary; for instance, 3 and 4 Esdras are often called 1 and 2 Esdras in modern collections of the Apocrypha.</note>.

Psalm 151 is omitted in the Hebrew, Chaldean <note>A term often used historically for Aramaic translations known as Targums.</note>, and the Vulgate <note>The standard Latin version of the Bible.</note>, and thus it does not appear in most Bibles. For this reason, because it is very short, it is helpful to present it here for the sake of scholarly curiosity.

> 1. *I was small among my brothers, and the youngest in my father’s house; I tended my father’s sheep.*
> 2. *My hands made an instrument, and my fingers fashioned a harp.*
> 3. *And who announced it to my Lord? The Lord himself, he is the hearer of all.*
> 4. *He sent his Angel, and took me from my father’s sheep, and anointed me with his oil of anointing.*
> 5. *My brothers were handsome and tall, but the Lord was not well-pleased with them.*
> 6. *I went out to meet the foreigner <note>Referring to the giant Goliath.</note>, and he cursed me by his idols.*
> 7. *But I, drawing his own sword from him, cut off his head, and took away the reproach from the children of Israel.*

It is clear, therefore, that this is a song of thanksgiving for the victory over Goliath.

**THE PRAYER OF MANASSEH**, which he is said to have dictated in prison in Babylon while weighed down by chains and repenting for his crimes, appears in many places in Bibles and can be read there.

<margin>3 Maccabees has 7 Chapters.</margin>
**THE THIRD BOOK OF MACCABEES**, if it were Canonical, would occupy the place of the first in chronological order; for it contains the history of the persecution stirred up by King Philopator <note>Ptolemy IV Philopator, a King of Egypt (221–204 BC).</note> 

<column-break/>

of Egypt against the Jews in his domain, who were exposed to elephants but were miraculously saved by God. Therefore, although this book deals with events that happened before the age of the Maccabees, it obtained the same name because of a certain similarity in theme.

<margin>Fourth has 15 Chapters.</margin>
**THE FOURTH BOOK OF MACCABEES**, or Josephus’s <note>Attributed traditionally, though likely incorrectly, to the Jewish historian Flavius Josephus.</note> Book on the Rule of Reason, describes the glorious struggles of Eleazar and the seven Maccabean brothers for their faith. Its purpose is to show, by their example, that reason is the mistress over emotions and suffering. However, in the preface of the work, the power of reason is so highly extolled that even those things which we know should be credited to divine grace seem to be attributed to its command.

<margin>The third book of Esdras has 9 Chapters.</margin>
**THE THIRD BOOK OF ESDRAS**, which fell out of the Canon by the authority of the Latin Church, relates almost the same history as the first <note>The canonical Book of Ezra.</note>, but it is interpolated with various additions. Among these, the primary place is held by the story of the Three Bodyguards of King Darius, one of whom is said to have been Zerubbabel. These men challenged each other with a proposed problem: *what is the strongest thing?* Each placed his written opinion under the pillow of the King while he was asleep. The first argued that wine was the strongest; the second, the King; but Zerubbabel defended the idea that although women surpassed these two, Truth surpasses all. The King and all the nobles of the court, in addition to giving great rewards, judged the victory of the cause to the one who defended Truth.

<margin>Fourth has 16 Chapters. Letter to Domnion.</margin>
**THE FOURTH BOOK**, which is likewise circulated under the name of Esdras, contains some good things, but it teems with strange visions about the end of the world and the judgment, etc. For this reason, it was dismissed by St. Jerome as "Apocryphal dreams" and was rejected by the unanimous consensus of both the Latin and Greek Churches.

# THE BOOK OF GENESIS
## IN HEBREW — BERESHIT <note>original: "BERESITH". This is the Hebrew name for the book, meaning "In the beginning."</note>

### CHAPTER ONE.
-> *Concerning the creation of the world, the distinction and ordering of created things, and the formation of man, to whom God subjected all that He had created.* <-

<margin>
Ps. 37:6 and 135:5.
Ecclus. 18:1.
Acts 14:15 and 17:24.
Heb. 11:3.
</margin>
1 <image-desc>Large decorative woodcut initial box containing the letter 'I', featuring elaborate floral and foliate motifs.</image-desc>In the beginning God created heaven and earth.
2 And the earth was empty and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep: and the Spirit of God moved over the waters.
3 <margin>† Hebrew: light <note>original: "lux"</note></margin> And God said: † Let there be light. And light was made.
4 And God saw the light, that it was good: and he divided the light from the darkness.
5 And he called the light Day, and the darkness Night. And there was evening and morning, one day.
6 And God said: Let there be a firmament <term>firmament: from the Latin 'firmamentum', meaning a solid support; ancient peoples envisioned the sky as a solid dome separating the waters of the heavens from the waters of the earth</term> in the midst of the waters: and let it divide the waters from the waters.
7 And God made the firmament, and divided the waters that were under the firmament, from those † that were above the firmament. And it was so.
8 <margin>† Ps. 135:6 and 148:4. Jer. 10:12 and 51:15.</margin> And God called the firmament, Heaven: and there was evening and morning, the second day.
9 And God said: Let the waters that are under the heaven, be gathered together into one place: and let the dry land appear. And it was so.
10 <margin>† Job 38:4. Ps. 32:7 and 88:12 and 135:6.</margin> And God called the dry land † Earth, and the gathering together of the waters he called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
11 And he said: Let the earth bring forth green herbs and such as may seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after its kind, which has its seed in itself upon the earth. And it was so.
12 And the earth brought forth green herbs, and such as yield seed according to their kind, and the tree yielding fruit, each having seed according to its species. And God saw that it was good.
13 And there was evening and morning, the third day.
14 <margin>† Ps. 135:7.</margin> And God said: † Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven, to divide the day and the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years:
15 That they may shine in the firmament of heaven, and give light upon the earth. And it was so.
16 And God made two great lights: a greater light to rule the day, and a lesser light to rule the night: and the stars.
17 And he set them in the firmament of heaven to shine upon the earth.
18 And to rule the day and the night, and to divide the light and the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
19 And there was evening and morning, the fourth day.
20 And God said: Let the waters bring forth the creeping creature having a living soul, and the fowl that may fly over the earth under the firmament of heaven.
21 And God created the great whales, and every

<column-break/>

living and moving soul which the waters brought forth according to their kinds, and every winged fowl according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
22 And he blessed them, saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the waters of the sea: and let the birds be multiplied upon the earth.
23 And there was evening and morning, the fifth day.
24 And God said: Let the earth bring forth the living creature in its kind, cattle and creeping things, and beasts of the earth, according to their species. And it was so.
25 And God made the beasts of the earth according to their species, and cattle, and every thing that creeps on the earth after its kind. And God saw that it was good.
26 <margin>† Below 5:1 and 9:6. 1 Cor. 11:7. † Col. 3:10. † Wisd. 2:23. Ecclus. 17:1. † Matt. 19:4. † Below 8:17 and 9:1. † Below 9:3.</margin> And he said: Let us make man to our † image and likeness: and let him have dominion over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and the beasts, and the whole earth, and every creeping creature that moves upon the earth.
27 And God created man to his own image: † to the image of God he created him: male and female he created them.
28 And God blessed them, saying: † Increase and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it, and rule over the fishes of the sea, and the fowls of the air, and all living creatures that move upon the earth.
29 And God said: Behold I have given you every herb bearing seed upon the earth, and all trees that have in themselves seed of their own kind, † to be your meat <note>original: "escam". In older English, "meat" refers to food in general, not just animal flesh.</note>.
30 And to all beasts of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to all that move upon the earth, and wherein there is life, that they may have to feed upon. And it was so.
31 <margin>† Ecclus. 39:21. Mark 7:37.</margin> † And God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good. And there was evening and morning, the sixth day.

### CHAPTER TWO.
-> *God, having completed the work of six days, rested on the seventh, which he also blessed: he placed man in a paradise distinguished by various fruit-bearing trees and rivers: for whom he formed Eve from his rib as a helper and instituted marriage.* <-

<margin>
† Exod. 20:21 and 31:17.
Deut. 5:14.
Heb. 4:4.
</margin>
1 <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial box containing the letter 'I', featuring floral patterns.</image-desc>So the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture <note>original: "ornatus". Refers to the "host" or the complete array of things filling the heavens and earth.</note> of them.
2 And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made: and † he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had done.
3 And he blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because in it he had ceased from all his work which God created and made.
4 These are the generations <note>original: "generationes". Refers to the origins or history.</note> of the heaven and the earth, when they were created, in the day that the Lord God made the heaven and the earth:
5 And every plant of the field before it sprung up in the earth, and every herb of the ground before it grew: for the Lord God had not rained upon the earth, and there was not a man to till the earth.

6 But a spring rose from the earth, watering the entire surface of the ground.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 15:45.</margin>
7 The Lord God therefore formed man from the dust <note>original: "limo", literally mud or clay</note> of the earth, and breathed into his face the breath of life, and † man became a living soul.
8 Now the Lord God had planted a paradise of pleasure <note>original: "paradisum voluptatis"; often referred to as the Garden of Eden</note> from the beginning: in which he placed the man whom he had formed.
9 And the Lord God brought forth from the ground every tree fair to the sight, and pleasant to eat: the tree of life also in the midst of paradise, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

13 And the name of the second river is Gihon: that is it which encompasses all the land of Ethiopia.
14 And the name of the third river is the Tigris: it flows toward the Assyrians. And the fourth river, that is the Euphrates.
15 The Lord God therefore took the man, and placed him in the paradise of pleasure, to work it and to keep it.
16 And he commanded him, saying: Of every tree of paradise you may eat:
17 But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, you shall not eat; for in whatever day you eat of it, you shall die the death.
18 The Lord God also said: It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a helper like unto himself.
19 Therefore, the Lord God, having formed out of the ground all the animals of the earth, and all the birds of the air, brought them to Adam to see what he would call them: for whatsoever Adam called any living creature, that is its name.
20 And Adam called all the animals by their names, and all the birds of the air, and all the beasts of the earth: but for Adam there was not found a helper like himself.
21 Then the Lord God cast a deep sleep upon Adam: and when he was asleep, he took one of his ribs, and filled up flesh for it.
22 And the Lord God built the rib, which he had taken from Adam, into a woman: and brought her to Adam.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 11:9.</margin>
23 And Adam said: † This now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman <note>original: "Virago". In Latin, this word highlights the derivation from man ("vir"), mirroring how "Woman" is derived from "Man" in English.</note>, because she was taken from man.
<margin>† Matthew 19:5; Mark 10:7; Ephesians 5:31. † 1 Corinthians 6:16.</margin>
24 † Wherefore a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: † and they shall be two in one flesh.
25 And they were both naked, namely Adam and his wife; and they were not ashamed.

### CHAPTER III.

*By the cunning of the serpent, the first parents transgress the commandment of God; the Messiah is promised to the world; and having been punished, they are driven out of paradise.*

1 Now the serpent was more subtle than all the animals of the earth which the Lord God had made. And he said to the woman: Why has God commanded you that you should not eat of every tree of paradise?

<column-break/>

2 To whom the woman answered: Of the fruit of the trees that are in paradise we do eat:
3 But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of paradise, God has commanded us that we should not eat, and that we should not touch it, lest perhaps we die.
<margin>† 2 Corinthians 11:3.</margin>
4 And the serpent said to the woman: † No, you shall not die the death.
5 For God knows that in whatever day you eat thereof, your eyes shall be opened: and you shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.
6 The woman therefore saw that the tree was good to eat, and fair to the eyes, and delightful to behold: and she took of the fruit thereof, and ate: and she gave to her husband, who ate.
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 25:33; 1 Timothy 2:14.</margin>
7 And the eyes of them both were opened: and when they perceived themselves to be naked, they sewed together fig leaves, and made themselves aprons <note>original: "perizomata", referring to loincloths or waist-coverings</note>.
8 And when they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in paradise in the afternoon air, Adam and his wife hid themselves from the face of the Lord God amidst the trees of paradise.
9 And the Lord God called Adam, and said to him: Where are you?
10 Who said: I heard your voice in paradise, and I was afraid, because I was naked, and I hid myself.
11 To whom he said: And who told you that you were naked, unless it be that you have eaten of the tree whereof I commanded you that you should not eat?
12 And Adam said: The woman, whom you gave me as a companion, gave me of the tree, and I ate.
13 And the Lord God said to the woman: Why have you done this? And she answered: The serpent deceived me, and I ate.
14 And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because you have done this, you are cursed among all animals, and beasts of the earth: upon your breast shall you go, and earth shall you eat all the days of your life.
15 I will put enmities between you and the woman, and your seed and her seed: she shall crush your head, and you shall lie in wait for her heel.
16 To the woman also he said: I will multiply your labors and your conceptions: in sorrow shall you bring forth children, and you shall be under the power of your husband: † and he shall have dominion over you.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 14:34.</margin>
17 And to Adam he said: Because you have listened to the voice of your wife, and have eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded you that you should not eat, cursed is the earth in your work: with labor shall you eat thereof all the days of your life.
18 Thorns and thistles shall it bring forth to you, and you shall eat the herbs of the earth.
19 In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread, until you return to the earth out of which you were taken: for dust you are, and into dust you shall return.
20 And Adam called the name of his wife, Eve <note>original: "Heva"</note>: because she was the mother of all the living.
21 The Lord God also made for Adam and his wife garments of skins, and clothed them.
22 And he said: Behold, Adam is become as one of us, knowing good and evil: now, therefore, lest perhaps he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever.
23 And the Lord God sent him out of the paradise of pleasure, to till the earth from which he was taken.
24 And he cast out Adam: and placed before the paradise of pleasure Cherubim, and a flaming sword, turning every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

## CHAPTER IV.

->*Adam begets Cain and Abel from Eve: the wicked Cain kills his brother, the pious Abel; punished by God and living as a fugitive, he fathered Enoch: but Adam also fathered Seth, to whom Enos was born.*<-

1 Now Adam knew <note>original: "cognovit"; a common biblical idiom for sexual intimacy</note> his wife Eve: who conceived and gave birth to Cain, saying: I have possessed a man through God.
2 And again she gave birth to his brother Abel. Now Abel was a shepherd of sheep, and Cain was a tiller of the soil.
3 And it happened after many days that Cain offered gifts to the Lord from the fruits of the earth.
<margin>Hebrews 11:4</margin>
4 Abel also offered from the firstborn of his flock, and from their fat: and the Lord looked with favor upon Abel and his gifts.
5 But to Cain and his gifts, he did not look with favor: and Cain was exceedingly angry, and his countenance fell.
6 And the Lord said to him: Why are you angry? And why has your face fallen?
7 If you do well, will you not receive? But if you do ill, will not sin be present immediately at the door? But its desire shall be under you, and you shall have dominion over it.
8 And Cain said to his brother Abel: Let us go outside. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel, and † killed him.
<margin>† Wisdom 10:3; Matthew 23:35; 1 John 3:12; Jude verse 11.</margin>
9 And the Lord said to Cain: Where is your brother Abel? Who answered: I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?
10 And he said to him: What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to me from the earth.
11 Now therefore, you shall be cursed upon the earth, which has opened its mouth and received your brother’s blood from your hand.
12 When you work the soil, it shall not give you its fruit: you shall be a wanderer and a fugitive upon the earth.
13 And Cain said to the Lord: My iniquity is greater than I may deserve pardon <note>original: "veniam merear"; some translations interpret this as "my punishment is greater than I can bear"</note>.
14 Behold, you cast me out today from the face of the earth; and I shall be hidden from your face, and I shall be a wanderer and a fugitive on the earth: therefore, everyone who finds me will kill me.
15 And the Lord said to him: It shall not be so; but whoever kills Cain shall be punished sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, so that whoever found him would not kill him.
16 And Cain, departing from the face of the Lord, lived as a fugitive in the land to the east of Eden.
17 Moreover, Cain knew his wife; she conceived and gave birth to Enoch: and he built a city, and called its name Enoch, after the name of his son.
18 Furthermore, Enoch fathered Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
19 Who took two wives, the name of one was Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
20 And Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the father of those living in tents and of shepherds.
21 And his brother's name was Jubal: he was the father of those playing the harp and the organ <note>original: "organo"; likely referring to a pipe or wind instrument rather than a modern church organ</note>.
22 Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-cain, who was a hammerer and a smith in all works of brass and iron. And the sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.

<column-break/>

23 And Lamech said to his wives Adah and Zillah: Hear my voice, wives of Lamech, listen to my speech: for I have killed a man to my wounding, and a youth to my bruising.
24 Sevenfold vengeance shall be given for Cain: but for Lamech, seventy times seven.
25 Adam also knew his wife again: and she gave birth to a son, and called his name Seth, saying: God has given me another seed in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.
26 But to Seth also a son was born, whom he called Enos: this man began to call upon the name of the Lord.

## CHAPTER V.

->*The genealogy of Adam and his descendants through Seth is recorded: and the years of their lives even until Noah.*<-

<margin>† Wisdom 1:27; Genesis 9:23; Wisdom 2:17; Ecclesiasticus 1:1; 1 Chronicles</margin>
1 This is the book of the generation of Adam: In the day that God created man, † he made him in the likeness of God.
2 Male and female he created them, and blessed them: and he called their name Adam, in the day they were created.
3 Now Adam lived one hundred and thirty years: and he fathered a son in his own image and likeness, and called his name Seth.
4 And the days of † Adam, after he fathered Seth, were eight hundred years: and he fathered sons and daughters.
5 And all the time that Adam lived was nine hundred and thirty years, and he died.
6 Seth also lived one hundred and five years, and fathered Enos.
7 And Seth lived after he fathered Enos eight hundred and seven years, and fathered sons and daughters.
8 And all the days of Seth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
9 Now Enos lived ninety years, and fathered Cainan.
10 After whose birth he lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and fathered sons and daughters.
11 And all the days of Enos were nine hundred and five years, and he died.
12 Cainan also lived seventy years, and fathered Mahalaleel.
13 And Cainan lived after he fathered Mahalaleel eight hundred and forty years, and fathered sons and daughters.
14 And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.
15 Now Mahalaleel lived sixty-five years, and fathered Jared.
16 And Mahalaleel lived after he fathered Jared eight hundred and thirty years: and he fathered sons and daughters.
17 And all the days of Mahalaleel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.
18 And Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years, and fathered Enoch.
19 And Jared lived after he fathered Enoch eight hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
20 And all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.
21 Furthermore, Enoch lived sixty-five years, and fathered Methuselah.
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 44:16; Hebrews 11:5.</margin>
22 And Enoch walked with God: and he lived, after he fathered Methuselah, three hundred years, and fathered sons and daughters.
23 And all the days of Enoch were three hundred and sixty-five years.

# CHAPTER VI.

*Man's sins were the cause of the flood. Yet Noah was found just, and he is commanded to build an ark in which he and every kind of living creature may be preserved.*

1 And when men began to be multiplied upon the earth, and had fathered daughters,
2 The sons of God, seeing that the daughters of men were beautiful, took for themselves wives from all whom they had chosen. <note>The "sons of God" is a phrase that has sparked much debate, often interpreted as either the descendants of the righteous Seth or as angelic beings.</note>
3 And God said: My spirit shall not remain in man forever, because he is flesh: and his days shall be one hundred and twenty years.
4 Now there were giants <note>original: "Gigantes"; often associated with the Nephilim</note> upon the earth in those days: for after the sons of God went in to the daughters of men, and they gave birth, these are the mighty men of old, famous men.
<margin>† Below 8:21; Matthew 15:19.</margin>
5 And God, seeing that the wickedness of men was great on the earth, and † every thought of their heart was intent on evil at all times,
6 He regretted that he had made man on the earth. And touched with an inward grief of heart,
7 He said: I will erase man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth, from man even to the animals, from the creeping things even to the birds of the air: for it repents me that I have made them.
8 But Noah found grace before the Lord.
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 44:17.</margin>
9 These are the generations of Noah: † Noah was a just and perfect man in his generations, he walked with God.
10 And he fathered three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
11 Now the earth was corrupted before God, and was filled with iniquity.
12 And when God saw that the earth was corrupted (for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth),
13 He said to Noah: The end of all flesh has come before me: the earth is filled with iniquity by their presence, and I will destroy them with the earth.
14 Make for yourself an ark of planed wood: <note>original: "lignis laevigatis"; often referred to in other translations as "gopher wood."</note> you shall make little rooms in the ark, and smear it with bitumen inside and out.
15 And thus shall you make it: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits. <note>A cubit was an ancient unit of measure based on the length of the forearm, roughly 18 inches or 45 centimeters.</note>

<column-break/>

16 You shall make a window in the ark, and finish its top at one cubit: but place the door of the ark on its side: you shall make lower, middle, and third stories in it.
17 Behold, I will bring the waters of a flood upon the earth, to kill all flesh in which is the breath of life under heaven: everything that is on the earth shall be consumed.
18 And I will establish my covenant with you: and you shall enter the ark, you and your sons, your wife, and the wives of your sons with you.
19 And from every living creature of all flesh, you shall bring two of each into the ark, that they may live with you: of the male sex and the female.
20 From the birds according to their kind, and from the cattle in their kind, and from every creeping thing of the earth according to its kind: two of every sort shall enter with you, so that they may live.
21 Therefore, you shall take with you of all foods that can be eaten, and you shall gather them with you: and they shall be for food both for you and for them.
22 Noah therefore did all things which God had commanded him.

<margin>† Hebrews 11:7; 2 Peter 2:5.</margin>

4 For yet a while, and after seven days, I will rain upon the earth for forty days and forty nights: and I will erase every substance that I have made from the surface of the earth.
5 Noah therefore did all things which the Lord had commanded him.

9 Two and two entered to Noah into the ark, male and female, just as the Lord had commanded Noah.

12 And rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
13 On that very day, Noah entered, along with Shem, Ham, and Japheth, his sons; his wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark;
14 They and every animal according to its kind, and all the cattle in their kind, and everything that moves upon the earth in its kind,

### CHAPTER VIII.

> *As the waters of the flood gradually decreased, after the sending out of the raven and the dove, Noah goes out with all who were contained in the ark; and having built an altar, he offers burnt offerings to God in thanksgiving, by which God, being appeased, promises that there shall never again be a flood.*

And God remembered Noah, and all the living creatures, and all the cattle that were with him in the ark, and brought a wind over the earth, and the waters were diminished.
2 The fountains of the deep and the floodgates of heaven were closed: and the rain from heaven was restrained.
3 And the waters returned from off the earth, going and coming: and they began to decrease after one hundred and fifty days.
4 And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, upon the mountains of Armenia. <note>The Latin "montes Armeniae" refers to the region traditionally associated with Mount Ararat.</note>
5 And the waters continued to go and decrease until the tenth month: for in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.
6 And when forty days had passed, Noah, opening the window of the ark which he had made, sent forth a raven:
7 Which went forth and did not return, until the waters were dried up upon the earth.
8 He also sent forth a dove after him, to see if the waters had now ceased upon the face of the earth.
9 But when she found no place for her foot to rest, she returned to him into the ark: for the waters were upon the whole earth: and he stretched forth his hand, and having caught her, brought her into the ark.
10 And having waited yet seven other days, he again sent forth the dove out of the ark.

<column-break/>

11 And she came to him in the evening, carrying a branch of an olive tree with green leaves in her mouth: Noah therefore understood that the waters had ceased upon the earth.
12 And he stayed yet another seven days: and he sent forth the dove, which did not return to him anymore.
13 Therefore, in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the waters were diminished upon the earth: and Noah, opening the roof of the ark, looked, and saw that the surface of the earth was dried.
14 In the second month, the seven and twentieth day of the month, the earth was dried.
15 And God spoke to Noah, saying:
16 Go out of the ark, you and your wife, your sons and the wives of your sons with you.
<margin>† Above 1:22.</margin>
17 All the living creatures that are with you, of all flesh, as well in birds as in beasts and all creeping things that creep upon the earth, bring out with you, and go upon the earth: † increase and multiply upon it.
<margin>28. Below 9:1, 7.</margin>
18 So Noah went out, and his sons, his wife, and the wives of his sons with him.
19 And all the living creatures, cattle, and creeping things that creep upon the earth, according to their kind, went out of the ark.
20 And Noah built an altar to the Lord: and taking of all clean cattle and birds, he offered burnt offerings upon the altar.
<margin>† Above 6:5. Matthew 15:19.</margin>

This indicates God's favorable acceptance of the sacrifice.</note> and said: I will no more curse the earth because of men: † for the sense and thought of the human heart are prone to evil from its youth: therefore I will no more strike every living soul as I have done.
22 All the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, night and day, shall not cease.

24 If there should be fifty righteous men in the city, will they perish together? And will you not spare that place for the sake of the fifty righteous, if they are in it?
25 Far be it from you to do such a thing, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous becomes like the wicked; this is not your way: you who judge all the earth, you will by no means carry out such a judgment."
26 And the Lord said to him: "If I find in Sodom fifty righteous in the middle of the city, I will forgive the whole place for their sake."
27 And Abraham answering, said: "Since I have once begun, I will speak to my Lord, though I am dust and ashes." <note>original: "pulvis & cinis" - a classic expression of human humility and mortality before the Divine.</note>
28 "What if there should be five fewer than fifty righteous? Will you destroy the entire city for the sake of forty-five?" And He said: "I will not destroy it, if I find forty-five there."
29 And again he spoke to Him: "But if forty are found there, what will you do?" He said: "I will not strike it for the sake of the forty."
30 "I pray," he said, "Lord, do not be indignant if I speak: What if thirty should be found there?" He answered: "I will not do it, if I find thirty there."
31 "Since I have once begun," he said, "I will speak to my Lord: What if twenty should be found there?" He said: "I will not kill them for the sake of the twenty."
32 "I beseech you," he said, "Lord, do not be angry if I speak once more: What if ten should be found there?" And He said: "I will not destroy it for the sake of the ten."
33 And the Lord went away, after He ceased speaking to Abraham: and Abraham returned to his place.

### C H A P T E R XX.

->*While Abraham travels as a pilgrim in Gerar, his wife is taken by the king; she is returned untouched at the Lord’s command with great gifts, and after Abraham prays, health is restored to the king’s house.*<-

1 Abraham set out from there into the southern land, and lived between Kadesh and Shur: and he traveled as a stranger in Gerar.
2 And he said of Sarah his wife: "She is my sister." Therefore Abimelech, the king of Gerar, sent and took her.
3 But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said: "Behold, you shall die because of the woman you have taken: for she has a husband."

<column-break/>

4 But Abimelech had not touched her, and he said: "Lord, will you kill a nation that is ignorant and righteous?
5 Did he not say to me: 'She is my sister,' and did she not say: 'He is my brother'? In the simplicity of my heart, and the purity of my hands, I have done this."
6 And God said to him: "I also know that you did this with a simple heart: and therefore I kept you from sinning against me, and I did not allow you to touch her.
7 Now therefore, restore the wife to her husband, for he is a prophet: and he will pray for you, and you shall live. But if you will not restore her, know that you shall die the death, you and all that are yours."
8 And immediately, rising in the night, Abimelech called all his servants: and he spoke all these words in their ears, and all the men were very much afraid.
9 Then Abimelech also called Abraham, and said to him: "What have you done to us? How have we sinned against you, that you have brought a great sin upon me and upon my kingdom? You have done things to us that you ought not to have done."
10 And questioning him again, he said: "What did you see, that you should do this?"
11 Abraham answered: "I thought to myself, saying: 'Perhaps the fear of God is not in this place: and they will kill me because of my wife.'
12 <margin>† Above 12:13</margin> Moreover, she is † truly my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother, and I took her as my wife.
13 But after God led me out from my father's house, I said to her: 'This mercy you shall do for me: in every place where we enter, you shall say that I am your brother.'"
14 <margin>† Below 21:23</margin> † Therefore Abimelech took sheep and oxen, and servants and handmaids, and gave them to Abraham: and he restored Sarah his wife to him,
15 And he said: "The land is before you; live wherever it pleases you."
16 And to Sarah he said: "Behold, I have given a thousand pieces of silver to your brother; this shall be to you a covering of the eyes <note>A figurative expression suggesting a gift to restore her honor or to signify she is a married woman.</note> before all who are with you, and wherever you go: remember that you were taken."
17 And as Abraham prayed, God healed Abimelech and his wife, and his handmaids, and they bore children:
18 For the Lord had closed every womb of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.

17 But God heard the voice of the boy, and the Angel of God called to Hagar from heaven, saying: "What is the matter, Hagar? Do not fear; for God has heard the voice of the boy from the place where he is."
18 "Arise, lift up the boy, and hold him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation."
19 And God opened her eyes; and seeing a well of water, she went and filled the skin, and gave the boy a drink.
20 And God was with him; he grew and lived in the wilderness, and he became a young archer.
21 He lived in the desert of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
22 At that same time, Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham: "God is with you in everything you do."
23 "Therefore, swear to me by God that you will not harm me, nor my descendants, nor my lineage; but according to the kindness <margin>† Above 21:14</margin> that I have shown to you, you shall do to me and to the land in which you have lived as a stranger."
24 And Abraham said: "I will swear."
25 And Abraham complained to Abimelech regarding a well of water which his servants had seized by force.
26 Abimelech replied: "I did not know who did this thing; neither did you tell me, nor did I hear of it until today."
27 So Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them struck a covenant.
28 And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock apart by themselves.
29 Abimelech said to him: "What do these seven ewe lambs mean, which you have set apart?"
30 But he said: "You shall receive the seven lambs from my hand, so that they may be a witness for me that I dug this well."
31 Therefore that place was called Beersheba, because there they both swore an oath.
32 And they entered into a covenant for the well of the oath.

<column-break/>

33 Then Abimelech rose, along with Phicol the commander of his army, and they returned to the land of the Palestinians <note>Original: "Palæstinorum." In this historical context, it refers to the Philistines.</note>. But Abraham planted a grove in Beersheba and there called upon the name of the Lord, the eternal God.
34 And he was a dweller in the land of the Palestinians for many days.

### CHAPTER XXIII.

->*Sarah’s death is mourned, and she is buried in the double cave, which Abraham bought from Ephron with the surrounding field for a sum of money.*<-

1 Sarah lived one hundred and twenty-seven years,
2 and she died in the city of Arba <note>Original: "Arbee," also known as Kiriath-arba.</note>, which is Hebron, in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn and weep for her.
3 And when he had risen up from the funeral rites, he spoke to the sons of Heth <note>Commonly identified as the Hittites.</note>, saying:
4 "I am a newcomer and a stranger among you: give me the right of a burial place with you, so that I may bury my dead."
5 The sons of Heth answered, saying:
6 "Hear us, my lord; you are a prince of God among us: bury your dead in our choice sepulchers: and no one shall be able to prevent you from burying your dead in his monument."
7 Abraham rose and bowed down to the people of the land, namely the sons of Heth:
8 and he said to them: "If it pleases your soul that I should bury my dead, hear me, and intercede for me with Ephron the son of Zohar <note>Original: "Seor."</note>:
9 so that he may give me the double cave <note>Original: "speluncam duplicem," often referred to as the Cave of Machpelah.</note> which he has at the edge of his field: for a fair price let him hand it over to me in your presence as a possession for a burial place."
10 Now Ephron lived in the midst of the sons of Heth. And Ephron answered Abraham in the hearing of all who entered the gate of that city, saying:
11 "Let it not be so, my lord, but rather listen to what I say: I give the field to you, and the cave that is in it, in the presence of the sons of my people; bury your dead."
12 Abraham bowed down before the people of the land.
13 And he spoke to Ephron while the people stood around: "I pray you, please hear me: I will give money for the field: receive it, and so I will bury my dead in it."
14 And Ephron answered:
15 "My lord, hear me: The land you ask for is worth four hundred shekels <note>Original: "siclis."</note> of silver: that is the price between me and you: but what is that? Bury your dead."
16 When Abraham had heard this, he weighed out the money that Ephron had asked for, in the hearing of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver of approved public currency.

<column-break/>

17 And the field that once belonged to Ephron, in which was the double cave, facing Mamre—both the field itself and the cave, and all the trees in all its borders round about—was confirmed
18 to Abraham as a possession, in the sight of the sons of Heth and all who entered the gate of that city.
<margin>† below 35:27.</margin>
19 And so Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the double cave of the field, which faced Mamre; † this is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
20 And the field and the cavern that was in it were confirmed to Abraham as a possession for a monument by the sons of Heth.

### C H A P T E R XXIX.

*Jacob is received by Laban; he served him for seven years under an agreement for his daughter Rachel: when Leah was substituted for her, he was forced to complete seven other years for the same woman: while Rachel remained barren, Leah gave birth to four sons.*

1 Jacob, having set out, came to the land of the East.
2 And he saw a well in a field, and three flocks of sheep lying near it: for from that well the animals were watered, and its mouth was closed by a large stone.
3 And it was the custom that when all the sheep were gathered, they would roll away the stone, and after the flocks were refreshed, they would put it back over the mouth of the well.
4 And he said to the shepherds: Brothers, where are you from? They answered: From Haran.
5 Questioning them, he said: Do you know Laban the son of Nahor? They said: We know him.
6 Is he well? he asked. He is well, they said: and behold, Rachel his daughter comes with her flock.
7 And Jacob said: There is still much daylight remaining: nor is it time for the flocks to be led back to the folds: give the sheep water first, and so lead them back to pasture.
8 They answered: We cannot, until all the cattle are gathered, and we move the stone from the mouth of the well, so that we may water the flocks.
9 While they were still speaking, behold Rachel came with her father’s sheep: for she herself tended the flock.

<column-break/>

10 When Jacob saw her, and knew her to be his cousin, and the sheep of Laban his uncle: he moved the stone with which the well was closed.
11 And after the flock was watered, he kissed her: and lifting up his voice, he wept,
12 And he told her that he was her father’s kinsman <note>original: "frater"; literally "brother," but often used for close male relatives like nephews or cousins.</note>, and the son of Rebecca: but she, hurrying, told her father.
13 Who, when he heard that Jacob his sister's son had come, ran to meet him: and embracing him and kissing him, he led him into his house. Having heard the reasons for his journey,
14 He answered: You are my bone and my flesh. And after the days of one month were completed,
15 He said to him: Because you are my kinsman, shall you serve me for nothing? Tell me what reward you should receive.
16 Now he had two daughters, the name of the elder was Leah: but the younger was called Rachel.
17 But Leah had weak eyes: Rachel was of beautiful form and lovely appearance.
18 Jacob, loving her, said: I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.
19 Laban answered: It is better that I give her to you than to another man; stay with me.
20 So Jacob served seven years for Rachel: and they seemed to him but a few days because of the greatness of his love.
21 And he said to Laban: Give me my wife: because the time is now fulfilled, that I may go in to her.
22 He, having called a great crowd of friends to a feast, held the wedding.
23 And in the evening, he brought Leah his daughter to him,
24 Giving a handmaid to his daughter, named Zilpah. When Jacob had gone in to her according to custom, when morning came, he saw it was Leah:
25 And he said to his father-in-law: What is this you intended to do? Did I not serve you for Rachel? Why have you deceived me?
26 Laban answered: It is not the custom in our place to give the younger in marriage before the elder.
27 Complete the week of days for this union: and I will give you this one also for the work by which you shall serve me another seven years.
28 He agreed to the arrangement: and the week having passed, he took Rachel as his wife:
29 To whom her father had given Bilhah as a servant.
30 And finally having obtained the desired marriage, he preferred his love for the second over the first, serving with him another seven years.
31 But the Lord, seeing that he despised Leah, opened her womb, while her sister remained barren.
32 She conceived and bore a son, and called his name Reuben, saying: The Lord has seen my humiliation; now my husband will love me.
33 And again she conceived and bore a son, and said: Because the Lord heard that I was held in contempt, he has given this one also to me: and she called his name Simeon.
34 And she conceived a third time, and bore another son: and she said: Now also my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons: and for that reason she called his name Levi.

35 She conceived a fourth time, and bore a son and said: Now I will praise the Lord: † and for this reason she called him Judah; and she ceased bearing.

Rachel is barren: she and Leah, who has ceased bearing children, give their handmaids to their husband, from whom each receives two sons: besides these, Leah bears two more sons and a daughter: then Rachel bears Joseph: after their birth, Laban strikes a bargain with Jacob regarding his wages, through which Jacob becomes exceedingly wealthy.

5 After the man went in to her, she conceived and bore a son.

And Rachel said: Give me a portion of your son’s mandrakes.
15 She replied: Does it seem like a small thing to you that you have stolen my husband, unless you also take my son’s mandrakes? Rachel said: Let him sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.
16 And when Jacob returned from the field in the evening, Leah went out to meet him and said: You shall come in to me: because I have hired you as a reward for my son’s mandrakes. And he slept with her that night.

19 Leah, conceiving again, bore a sixth son,

Dismiss me so that I may return to my homeland and to my own country.

28 Decide what wages I should give to you.
29 But he replied: You know how I have served you, and how great your possession has been in my hands.
30 You had little before I came to you, and now you have become rich: and the Lord has blessed you at my coming. It is only just, therefore, that I should at some point provide for my own house as well.

32 Go around all your flocks, and separate all the speckled sheep and those with spotted fleeces: and whatever is dark <note>original: "furvum"</note>, and spotted, and speckled, both among the sheep and among the goats, shall be my wages.
33 and my justice shall answer for me tomorrow, when the time of the agreement comes before you: and all that are not speckled, and spotted, and dark, whether among the sheep or the goats, shall prove me guilty of theft.
34 And Laban said: I am pleased with what you ask.
35 And on that day he separated the goats, and the sheep, and the he-goats, and the rams, that were speckled and spotted: but the entire flock of a single color, that is, of white and black fleece, he handed over to the care of his own sons.
36 And he put a distance of a three days' journey between himself and his son-in-law, who was pasturing the rest of his flocks.
37 Then Jacob, taking green rods of poplar, and almond, and plane trees, peeled them in part: and when the bark was pulled off, whiteness appeared in the parts that had been stripped: but those parts that remained whole stayed green: and in this way a variegated color was produced.
38 And he placed them in the channels where the water was poured out: so that when the flocks came to drink, they would have the rods before their eyes, and would conceive while looking at them <note>This reflects an ancient folk belief that the visual environment of a mother at the time of conception could influence the physical appearance of the offspring.</note>.
39 And it happened that in the heat of breeding, the sheep looked upon the rods and brought forth spotted, and speckled, and those marked with diverse colors.
40 And Jacob divided the flock, and put the rods in the channels before the eyes of the rams: now all the white and black ones belonged to Laban: but the rest to Jacob, the flocks being separated from each other.
41 Therefore, when the sheep were first breeding, Jacob placed the rods in the water channels before the eyes of the rams and the sheep, so that they might conceive while looking at them:
42 But when it was the later breeding and the final conception, he did not place them. And so those that were of the later time became Laban’s: and those of the first time, Jacob’s.
43 And the man was enriched beyond measure, and he had many flocks, handmaids and servants, camels and donkeys.

### CHAPTER XXXI.

*Jacob, at the Lord's command, returns silently to his father with all his belongings, followed by Laban: Rachel, having taken her father's idols, deceives him with a trick when he searches for them: finally, after various complaints and quarrels, Jacob and Laban enter into a covenant, and each departs to his own place.*

1 But after he heard the words of Laban's sons saying: Jacob has taken everything that belonged to our father, and enriched by his wealth, he has become famous:
2 He also noticed Laban’s face, that it was not toward him as it was yesterday and the day before <note>original: "heri & nudius-tertius" — a Latin idiom meaning "recently" or "in times past."</note>,

8 If ever he said: The speckled ones shall be your wages: then all the sheep bore speckled young: but when on the contrary he said: The white ones you shall receive for your reward: then all the flocks bore white ones.

30 Granted, you desired to go to your own people and longed for your father’s house: why have you stolen my gods?
31 Jacob answered: Because I departed without your knowledge, I was afraid that you might take your daughters from me by force.
32 But as for the theft you accuse me of: with whomever you find your gods, let him be put to death before our kinsmen: search, whatever of yours you find with me, and take it. In saying this, he did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.
33 So Laban, entering the tent of Jacob and of Leah, and of both handmaids, found nothing. And when he entered Rachel’s tent,
34 She quickly hid the idols under the camel’s saddle-bags and sat upon them: and as he searched the whole tent and found nothing,
35 She said: Let my lord not be angry that I cannot rise before you: for the way of women <note>A common ancient euphemism for menstruation.</note> is now upon me. Thus the seeker’s diligence was mocked.
36 And Jacob, swelling with anger, said with a quarrel: What is my fault, and what is my sin, that you have burned so fiercely after me,
37 And have searched all my furniture? What have you found of all the goods of your house? Put it here before my kinsmen and your kinsmen, and let them judge between me and you.
38 For twenty years I have been with you: your sheep and goats have not been barren, I have not eaten the rams of your flock:
39 Nor did I show you what was taken by a beast, I made good every loss: whatever was lost by theft, you required of me:
40 By day I was scorched by heat, and by night by frost, and sleep fled from my eyes,
41 And thus for twenty years in your house I served you: fourteen for your daughters, and six for your flocks: you also changed my wages ten times.
42 Unless the God of my father Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac <note>original: "timor Isaac" — a title for God emphasizing the deep reverence Isaac held for the Divine.</note>, had been with me, perhaps you would have sent me away empty-handed: God has looked upon my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you yesterday.
43 Laban answered him: The daughters are mine and the children, and the flocks are mine, and all that you see is mine: what can I do to my children and my grandchildren?
44 Come then, and let us enter into a covenant: that it may be for a testimony between me and you.
45 So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a monument:
46 And he said to his kinsmen: Bring stones.

They gathered stones and made a heap, and they ate there upon it.
47 Laban called it the Heap of Witness <note>original: "Tumulum testis"</note>, and Jacob called it the Mound of Testimony <note>original: "Acervum testimonii"</note>, each according to the custom of his own language.
48 And Laban said: This heap shall be a witness between me and you today; and therefore its name was called Galeed <note>original: "Galaad"</note>, that is, the Heap of Witness.

50 If you afflict my daughters, or if you bring in other wives over them: no witness of our speech is with us except God, who is present and watches.
51 And he said again to Jacob: Behold this heap, and the stone which I have set up between me and you,
52 It shall be a witness: this heap, I say, and the stone shall be for a testimony, if either I cross over it going toward you, or you pass beyond it, thinking to do me harm.
53 May the God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us. Jacob then swore by the Fear <note>This "fear" refers to the deep, holy reverence Jacob held for the God of his father Isaac.</note> of his father Isaac.
54 And having offered sacrifices on the mountain, he called his kinsmen to eat bread. When they had eaten, they remained there.
55 But Laban, rising in the night, kissed his sons and daughters, and blessed them: and he returned to his own place.

### CHAPTER XXXII.

*Jacob, having seen angels, is terrified and sends messengers and gifts to his brother Esau; meanwhile, he wrestles with an angel and receives a blessing and a change of name, after the sinew of his thigh was touched.*

<margin>refer to Genesis 31:15</margin>
1 Jacob also went on the journey he had begun: and the angels of God met him.
2 When he saw them, he said: These are the camps of God: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim <note>The name means "Two Camps" or "Two Hosts."</note>, that is, Camps.
3 Then he sent messengers before him to Esau his brother in the land of Seir, in the region of Edom:
4 And he commanded them, saying: Thus shall you speak to my lord Esau: "This says your brother Jacob: I have lived as a stranger with Laban, and have been there until this present day.
5 I have oxen, and donkeys, and sheep, and menservants, and maidservants: and I send now an embassy to my lord, that I may find favor in your sight."
6 And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying: We came to Esau your brother: and behold, he is hastening to meet you with four hundred men.
7 Jacob was greatly afraid: and in his terror he divided the people who were with him, as well as the flocks, the sheep, the oxen, and the camels, into two companies <note>original: "turmas" — groups or troops.</note>,
8 Saying: If Esau comes to one company and strikes it, the other company which remains will be saved.
9 And Jacob said: O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac: O Lord, who said to me: "Return to your land, and to the place of your birth, and I will do good to you":
10 I am less than all your mercies, and all the truth which you have fulfilled for your servant. With only my staff I crossed this Jordan: and now I return with two companies.
11 Deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, for I fear him greatly: lest perhaps he come and strike the mother with the children.
12 You spoke saying that you would do good to me, and multiply my offspring like the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered because of its multitude.

<column-break/>

13 And when he had slept there that night, he set apart from the things he had, gifts for Esau his brother:
14 Two hundred she-goats, twenty he-goats, two hundred ewes, and twenty rams,
15 Thirty milch camels with their colts, forty cows, and twenty bulls, twenty she-donkeys, and ten of their colts.
16 And he sent them by the hands of his servants, each flock by itself, and said to his servants: Go before me: and let there be a space between flock and flock.
17 And he commanded the first, saying: If you meet my brother Esau, and he asks you, "Whose are you?" or "Where are you going?" or "Whose are these things you are following?"
18 You shall answer: "They belong to your servant Jacob; he has sent these as a gift to my lord Esau: and he himself is coming behind us."
19 In the same way, he gave orders to the second, and the third, and to all who followed the flocks, saying: Speak to Esau with these same words when you find him.
20 And you shall add: "Your servant Jacob himself also follows our path." For he said: I will appease him with the gifts that go before me, and afterward I will see him; perhaps he will be gracious to me.
21 So the gifts went before him, but he himself remained that night in the camp.
22 And when he had risen early, he took his two wives, and as many handmaids, with his eleven sons, and crossed the ford of Jabbok <note>original: "Jaboc" — a tributary of the Jordan River.</note>.
23 And having brought over all things that belonged to him,
24 He remained alone: and behold, a man wrestled with him until morning.
25 When the man saw that he could not overcome him, he touched the sinew of his thigh, and immediately it withered.
26 And he said to him: Let me go, for the dawn is rising. He answered: I will not let you go, unless you bless me.
27 He asked then: What is your name? He answered: Jacob.
28 But the man said: Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel: for if you have been strong against God, how much more shall you prevail against men?
29 Jacob asked him: Tell me, by what name are you called? He answered: Why do you ask my name? And he blessed him in that same place.
30 Jacob called the name of that place Penuel <note>original: "Phanuel" — meaning "The Face of God."</note>, saying: I have seen God face to face, and my soul has been saved.
31 And immediately the sun rose upon him after he passed Penuel: but he limped upon his foot.
32 For this reason the children of Israel, even to this present day, do not eat the sinew <note>term: sciatic nerve <note>The Latin "nervum" refers here to the tendon or nerve in the hip socket. Jewish dietary law (Kosher) still observes this restriction.</note></note> that withered in Jacob’s thigh: because he touched the sinew of his thigh and it became numb.

*Jacob is kindly received by Esau who comes to meet him, and with difficulty he compels Esau to accept the gifts and return home; and so, after Esau had departed, Jacob traveled first to Succoth, then to Salem, where he bought a piece of land, pitched his tents, and built an altar.*

1 Jacob, lifting up his eyes, saw Esau coming, and with him four hundred men: and he divided the children of Leah and Rachel, and of both handmaids:

**14** Let my lord go on before his servant, and I will follow slowly in the footsteps of my children, as I see they are able, until I come to my lord in Seir. <note>Seir was the mountainous region where Esau had settled.</note>

**16** So Esau returned that day by the way he had come into Seir.

### CHAPTER XXXIV.

*Because of the abduction and rape of Dinah by Shechem, son of the prince of the Shechemites, the Shechemites—having first been circumcised—are slain by Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, and their city is plundered by the rest of Jacob's sons; for which reason Simeon and Levi are rebuked by their father.*

**1** Now Dinah, the daughter of Leah, went out to see the women of that region.

<column-break/>

**2** When Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of that land, saw her, he fell in love with her; and he took her by force and slept with her, violating the virgin.
**3** And his soul was knit to her, and he comforted her in her sadness with soft words.
**4** And going to Hamor his father, he said: Get me this girl as my wife.
**5** When Jacob heard this, his sons being absent and occupied with the feeding of the cattle, he remained silent until they returned.
**6** But when Hamor, the father of Shechem, went out to speak to Jacob,
**7** Behold, his sons were coming from the field; and hearing what had happened, they were very angry, because he had committed a foul deed in Israel by violating Jacob's daughter, a thing that is forbidden.
**8** Therefore Hamor spoke to them: The soul of my son Shechem is attached to your daughter; give her to him as a wife.
**9** And let us join in marriages with one another: give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
**10** And dwell with us: the land is in your power; farm it, trade in it, and possess it.
**11** Moreover, Shechem said to her father and her brothers: Let me find favor in your sight; and whatever you decide, I will give.
**12** Increase the dowry and demand gifts, and I will gladly give whatever you ask; only give me this girl as a wife.
**13** The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and his father deceitfully, being enraged by the violation of their sister:
**14** We cannot do what you ask, nor give our sister to an uncircumcised man; for that is forbidden and wicked among us.
**15** But on this condition we may be allied: if you will be like us, and every male among you is circumcised.
**16** Then we will give and receive our daughters and yours mutually; and we will dwell with you and be one people.
**17** But if you will not be circumcised, we will take our daughter and depart.
**18** Their offer pleased Hamor and Shechem his son.
**19** Nor did the young man delay in fulfilling what was asked; for he loved the girl greatly, and he was the most noble in all his father's house.
**20** And entering the gate of the city, they spoke to the people:
**21** These men are peaceful and want to live with us; let them trade in the land and farm it, for it is spacious and wide and needs cultivators. We shall take their daughters as wives and give ours to them.
**22** There is only one thing by which so great a good is delayed: if we circumcise our males, following the custom of their nation.
**23** And their substance, and cattle, and all that they possess will be ours; only let us agree to this, and dwelling together, we shall become one people.
**24** Everyone agreed, and all the males were circumcised.

### CHAPTER XXXV.

*After Jacob had buried the idols of his people near Shechem, at the Lord’s command he went up to Bethel, where, having built an altar, he offered sacrifice to God, and was strengthened by a new appearance of God. Deborah dies: Benjamin is born at the death of his mother Rachel: Reuben commits incest with Bilhah: the sons of Jacob are numbered, and his father Isaac dies.*

<margin>† Above 28:13.</margin> 1 Meanwhile, God spoke to Jacob: Arise, and go up to Bethel, and dwell there, and make an altar to God, who † appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau.
2 Then Jacob, having called together all his household, said: Cast away the foreign gods that are in your midst, and be purified, and change your garments. <note>Changing clothes was a symbolic act of ritual purification before approaching a holy site.</note>
3 Arise, and let us go up to Bethel, so that we may make an altar there to God: who heard me in the day of my trouble, and was the companion of my journey.
4 Therefore, they gave him all the foreign gods they had, and the earrings which were in their ears: and he buried them under the terebinth tree, which is behind the city of Shechem.

### C H A P T E R XXXVII.

*Joseph, accusing his brothers of a crime before his father and telling of the dreams he had seen, stirs up the hatred of his brothers against himself: for which reason, they first wish to kill him, but by the advice of Reuben he is first cast into a cistern, and then sold to the Ishmaelites without Reuben’s knowledge: he is mourned by his father, who believes him to have been killed by a wild beast; meanwhile, Joseph is sold in Egypt to Potiphar.*

And Jacob dwelt in the land of Canaan, in which his father had lived as a stranger.
2 And these are his generations: Joseph, when he was sixteen years old, <note>Modern translations usually state Joseph was seventeen; the Vulgate here records "sedecim" (sixteen).</note> was pasturing the flock with his brothers, while still a boy: and he was with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives: and he accused his brothers before his father of a most wicked crime.
3 Now Israel <note>Jacob was given the name "Israel" in Chapter 32.</note> loved Joseph above all his sons, because he had fathered him in his old age: and he made him a coat of many colors. <note>original: "tunicam polymitam" — This refers to a garment of diverse colors or elaborate embroidery, famously known as the "coat of many colors."</note>
4 And his brothers, seeing that he was loved by their father more than all his sons, hated him: nor could they speak anything peaceably to him.
5 It happened also that he reported a dream he had seen to his brothers: which cause was the seed of even greater hatred.
6 And he said to them: Hear my dream which I have seen:
7 I thought we were binding sheaves in the field: and as if my sheaf arose and stood, and your sheaves, standing around, bowed down to my sheaf.
8 His brothers answered: Shall you be our king? Or shall we be subject to your dominion? This cause of dreams and words, therefore, provided the fuel for envy and hatred.
9 He also saw another dream, which, telling to his brothers, he said: I saw in a dream, as it were the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars, bowing down to me.
10 And when he had related this to his father and his brothers, his father rebuked him, and said: What does this dream mean that you have seen? Shall I and your mother and your brothers bow down to you upon the earth?
11 His brothers therefore envied him: but his father considered the matter in silence.
12 And when his brothers stayed in Shechem to pasture their father’s flocks,
13 Israel said to him: Your brothers are pasturing the sheep in Shechem: come, I will send you to them. When he replied,
14 I am ready, he said to him: Go, and see if all is well with your brothers and the cattle: and report to me what is happening. Being sent from the valley of Hebron, he came to Shechem:
15 And a man found him wandering in the field: and asked him what he was seeking.
16 But he answered: I am seeking my brothers: tell me where they are pasturing the flocks.

### CHAPTER XXXVIII.

*Judah, having had three sons by a Canaanite wife, joined Tamar first to the first and then to the second; after they died, he unknowingly knew her as a prostitute, from which union Perez and Zerah were born.*

1 At that same time, Judah, going down from his brothers, turned aside to a certain Adullamite, named Hirah.

<column-break/>

<margin>† 1 Chronicles 2:3</margin>
2 † And he saw there the daughter of a Canaanite man, named Shua: and taking her to wife, he went in unto her.
3 And she conceived, and bore a son, and called his name Er.
<margin>† Numbers 26:19</margin>
4 † And conceiving again, she bore a son, and called his name Onan.
5 She bore also a third: whom she called Shelah: after whose birth, she ceased to bear children.
6 And Judah gave a wife to his firstborn Er, named Tamar.
<margin>† Numbers 26:19</margin>
7 † And Er, the firstborn of Judah, was wicked in the sight of the Lord: and was slain by him.
8 Judah therefore said to Onan his son: Go in to your brother's wife, and join with her, that you may raise up seed for your brother. <note>This refers to the "Levirate marriage" custom, where a brother was expected to provide an heir for a deceased brother.</note>
9 He, knowing that the children would not be born for himself, when he went in to his brother's wife, spilled his seed upon the ground, lest children should be born in his brother's name.
10 And therefore the Lord struck him, because he did a detestable thing.
11 Wherefore Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law: Remain a widow in your father's house, until my son Shelah grows up: for he feared lest he also might die, as his brothers did. She went her way, and dwelt in her father's house.
12 And after many days had passed, the daughter of Shua, the wife of Judah, died: who, after receiving consolation for his mourning, went up to his sheep-shearers, he and Hirah the Adullamite, the shepherd of his flock, in Timnah.
13 And it was told Tamar, that her father-in-law was going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.
14 And she, putting off the garments of her widowhood, took a veil: and having changed her dress, sat at the crossroads on the way that leads to Timnah: because Shelah had grown up, and she had not received him as a husband.
15 When Judah saw her, he suspected she was a harlot: for she had covered her face, lest she should be known.
16 And going in to her, he said: Allow me to lie with you: for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. She answered: What will you give me to enjoy my company?
17 He said: I will send you a young goat from the flocks. And she said again: I will suffer what you wish, if you will give me a pledge, until you send what you promise.
18 Judah said: What do you wish to be given to you for a pledge? She answered: Your ring, and your bracelet, and the staff which you hold in your hand. Therefore, by a single union the woman conceived,
19 And rising up she went away, and having put off the dress which she had taken, she put on the garments of her widowhood.
20 And Judah sent a young goat by his shepherd, the Adullamite, that he might receive the pledge which he had given to the woman: but when he did not find her,
21 He asked the men of that place: Where is the woman who sat at the crossroads? They all answered: There was no harlot in this place.
22 He returned to Judah, and said to him: I have not found her: moreover, the men of that place told me, that a prostitute never sat there.
23 Judah said: Let her keep them for herself, surely she cannot accuse us of a lie: I sent the goat which I promised, and you did not find her.
24 And behold, after three months they told Judah, saying: Tamar your daughter-in-law has committed fornication, and her womb appears to be swelling. And Judah said: Bring her out that she may be burned.

## C H A P T E R XXXIX.

*While Joseph prospers in the house of his master Potiphar, and as a favorite manages the entire household, he is accused by his mistress after repeatedly rejecting her advances for sex; he is cast into prison, where he earns the favor of the keeper and receives charge of all the prisoners.*

1 Therefore Joseph was brought down into Egypt, and Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh and captain of the army, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hands of the Ishmaelites who had brought him there. <note>original: "eunuchus Pharaonis," though in this context it refers to a high-ranking court official or chamberlain rather than a castrated man.</note>
2 And the Lord was with him, and he was a man who prospered in all things. He lived in the house of his master,
3 Who knew very well that the Lord was with him, and that everything he did was directed by the Lord in his hand.
4 And Joseph found favor in the sight of his master and served him; having been placed in charge of everything, he governed the house entrusted to him and all that had been delivered to him.
5 And the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian because of Joseph, and multiplied all his substance, both in the buildings and in the fields.
6 Nor did the master know anything else [of his own affairs], except for the bread which he ate. Now Joseph was of a beautiful face and handsome in appearance.
7 And so, after many days, his mistress cast her eyes upon Joseph and said: "Sleep with me."
8 But he, by no means consenting to the wicked deed, said to her: "Behold, my master, having entrusted everything to me, does not even know what he has in his own house.
9 Nor is there anything that is not in my power, or that he has not delivered to me, except for you, who are his wife. How then can I do this evil thing and sin against my God?"
10 With words of this kind, day after day, the woman was troublesome to the young man, but he refused the immorality.
11 It happened one day that Joseph entered the house to do some work without any witnesses present.
12 And she, catching the hem of his garment, said: "Sleep with me." But he, leaving his cloak in her hand, fled and went outside.
13 When the woman saw the garment in her hands and that she had been rejected,
14 She called the men of her house and said to them: "Look, he has brought in a Hebrew man to mock us! He came in to me to lie with me, and when I cried out,
15 And he heard my voice, he left the cloak I was holding and fled outside."

<column-break/>

16 Therefore, as proof of her claim, she kept the cloak and showed it to her husband when he returned home,
17 And said: "The Hebrew servant whom you brought to us came in to me to mock me.
18 And when he heard me cry out, he left the cloak I was holding and fled outside."
19 When his master heard these things, being too ready to believe his wife's words, he became very angry.
<margin>† Psalm 104:18.</margin> 20 † And he delivered Joseph into the prison where the king's prisoners were kept, and he was shut up there.
21 But the Lord was with Joseph, and having mercy on him, gave him favor in the sight of the chief of the prison.
22 Who delivered into his hand all the prisoners who were held in custody; and whatever was done, was done under him.
23 Nor did the keeper know anything of the matters entrusted to him, for the Lord was with Joseph and directed all his works.

## C H A P T E R XL.

*Joseph, having interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh's officials in prison, predicted that one would be restored to his former office and the other would be ended by hanging; all of which occurred on Pharaoh's birthday.*

1 After these things had happened, it occurred that two officials, the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker, offended their lord. <note>original: "pincerna" (cupbearer) and "pistor" (baker).</note>
2 And Pharaoh, being angry with them (for one was over the cupbearers and the other over the bakers),
3 He sent them into the prison of the captain of the soldiers, in which Joseph was also bound.
4 But the keeper of the prison delivered them to Joseph, who also served them. Some time passed while they were held in custody.
5 And they both saw a dream on the same night, each according to an interpretation suitable to himself.
6 When Joseph had entered to them in the morning and saw them sad,
7 He questioned them, saying: "Why is your face sadder today than usual?"
8 They answered: "We have seen a dream, and there is no one to interpret it for us." And Joseph said to them: "Does not interpretation belong to God? Tell me what you have seen."
9 The first, the chief of the cupbearers, told his dream: "I saw before me a vine,
10 In which were three branches, growing little by little into buds, and after the flowers, the grapes ripened.
11 And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; so I took the grapes and squeezed them into the cup I was holding, and I gave the drink to Pharaoh."
12 Joseph answered: "This is the interpretation of the dream: The three branches are yet three days,
13 After which Pharaoh will remember your service and restore you to your former rank. You shall give him the cup according to your office, as you were accustomed to do before.
14 Only remember me when it shall be well with you, and show me mercy: that you may suggest to Pharaoh to lead me out of this prison.
15 For I was taken away by stealth from the land of the Hebrews, and here, being innocent, I was cast into the pit." <note>original: "lacum," literally a lake or pit, used here for a dungeon.</note>
16 The chief of the bakers, seeing that he had wisely resolved the dream, said: "I also saw a dream, that I had three baskets of flour upon my head;
17 And in the one basket which was higher than the others, I carried all the foods made by the baker's art, and the birds were eating from it."
