### C H A P T E R XLI.

*Pharaoh dreams of cows and ears of grain. When no one else is able to interpret them, Joseph alone provides the meaning and is therefore placed in charge of all Egypt. He receives Aseneth as his wife from Pharaoh and has two sons before the seven years of famine. Sterility finally follows fertility.*

1 After two years, Pharaoh had a dream. He thought he was standing by the river <note>The Nile, the lifeblood of Egyptian agriculture.</note>.
2 From the river rose seven cows, beautiful and very fat; and they grazed in marshy places.
3 Seven other cows also emerged from the river, foul and wasted with thinness, and they grazed on the very bank of the stream in the green places.
4 And these devoured those whose appearance and physical condition were so wonderful. Pharaoh then woke up.
5 He slept again and saw a second dream: Seven ears of grain were sprouting on a single stalk, full and beautiful.
6 Another seven ears, thin and blasted by the parching heat, grew up.
7 These devoured all the beauty of the former ones. Pharaoh, waking from his rest,
8 and when morning came, being terrified with fear, sent for all the interpreters of Egypt and all the wise men. Having called them, he told them the dream, but there was no one who could interpret it.
9 Then at last the chief cupbearer, remembering, said: "I confess my sin.
10 The king, being angry with his servants, ordered me and the chief baker to be thrust into the prison of the captain of the soldiers.
11 There, in one night, we both saw a dream that foretold the future.
12 There was a Hebrew youth there, a servant of that same captain of the soldiers, to whom we told our dreams.
13 We heard from him whatever the outcome of the event later proved: for I was restored to my office, and the other was hung on a gallows."
14 Immediately, by the king's command, they brought Joseph out of prison and shaved him; and with his clothes changed, they presented him to the king.
15 Pharaoh said to him: "I have seen dreams, and there is no one who can explain them; I have heard that you interpret them most wisely."
16 Joseph answered: "Without me, God will give a favorable answer to Pharaoh."
17 So Pharaoh told what he had seen: "I thought I stood on the bank of the river.
18 And seven cows came up from the stream, very beautiful and fat-fleshed, which grazed on the greenery of the marsh.
19 And behold, seven other cows followed these, so deformed and thin that I have never seen the like in the land of Egypt.
20 These, having devoured and consumed the former ones,

<column-break/>

21 gave no sign of being full; but they remained just as thin and foully wasted as before. Waking up, I fell back into a deep sleep,
22 and saw a dream: Seven ears of grain were sprouting on a single stalk, full and very beautiful.
23 Seven others also, thin and blasted by the parching heat, grew from the stalk.
24 These devoured the beauty of the former ones. I told the dream to the interpreters, and there is no one who can explain it."
25 Joseph answered: "The king's dream is one and the same: God has shown to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
26 The seven beautiful cows and the seven full ears are seven years of plenty; they contain the same meaning for the dream.
27 Also the seven thin and lean cows that came up after them, and the seven thin ears blasted by the burning wind, are seven years of coming famine.
28 Which shall be fulfilled in this order:
29 Behold, seven years of great fertility will come to the entire land of Egypt.
30 These will be followed by seven other years of such sterility that all the previous abundance will be forgotten; for the famine will consume the entire land.
31 And the greatness of the plenty will be lost to the greatness of the scarcity.
32 Now, as for the fact that you saw the dream a second time pertaining to the same thing, it is a sign of certainty: because the word of God is established and will be fulfilled quite soon.
33 Now, therefore, let the king provide a wise and industrious man and place him over the land of Egypt.
34 Let him appoint overseers throughout all the regions and collect a fifth part of the fruits through the seven years of fertility.
35 Let them now gather into storehouses all the grain of the coming years, and let it be stored under Pharaoh's authority and kept in the cities.
36 Thus let it be prepared for the future seven years of famine which will oppress Egypt, so the land may not be consumed by want."
37 The counsel pleased Pharaoh and all his ministers.
38 And he spoke to them: "Could we ever find such a man who is so full of the spirit of God?"
39 He said therefore to Joseph: "Because God has shown you all that you have spoken, could I find anyone wiser or more like you?
<margin>† Psalm 105:21; 1 Maccabees 2:53; Acts 7:10.</margin>
40 † You shall be over my house, and all the people shall obey the command of your mouth; only by the throne of the kingdom will I precede you."
41 Pharaoh said again to Joseph: "Behold, I have appointed you over the entire land of Egypt."
42 And he took the ring from his hand and gave it into Joseph's hand; he dressed him in a robe of fine linen and placed a golden chain around his neck.
43 He made him ride in his second chariot, with a herald crying out that everyone should bow their knee before him, and that they should know he was the ruler over the entire land of Egypt.
44 The king also said to Joseph: "I am Pharaoh; without your command, no one shall move hand or foot in all the land of Egypt."
45 And he changed Joseph's name and called him in the Egyptian tongue, 'Savior of the World' <note>original: "Salvatorem mundi," a Latin translation of the name Zaphenath-paneah</note>. He gave him Aseneth, the daughter of Potipherah, the priest of Heliopolis <note>A major religious center in ancient Egypt, also known as 'On.'</note>, as his wife. And so Joseph went out into the land of Egypt.
46 (He was thirty years old when he stood in the presence of King Pharaoh) and he traveled through all the regions of Egypt.

### CHAPTER XLII.

->*Joseph’s brothers, driven by famine, are sent by their father to Egypt to buy grain; they are recognized by Joseph, but he treats them harshly and casts them into prison. Finally, leaving Simeon in chains, they return home, unknowingly carrying back the money placed in each of their sacks along with the grain.*<-

When Jacob heard that food was being sold in Egypt, he said to his sons: "Why are you negligent?"
2 "I have heard that wheat is being sold in Egypt; go down and buy what is necessary for us, so that we may live and not be consumed by want."
3 So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain in Egypt,
4 while Benjamin was kept at home by Jacob, who had said to his brothers: "Lest perhaps he suffer any evil on the journey."
5 They entered the land of Egypt with others who were traveling to buy, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
6 And Joseph was the governor in the land of Egypt, and at his command, grain was sold to the people. When his brothers had bowed down before him,
7 and he had recognized them, he spoke to them harshly as if to strangers, asking them: "Where have you come from?" They answered: "From the land of Canaan, to buy the necessities of life."
8 And though he recognized his brothers, he was not recognized by them.
9 Remembering the dreams he had once seen, he said to them: "You are spies! You have come to see the weaker parts <note>original: "infirmiora," referring to undefended borders or strategic vulnerabilities</note> of the land."
10 They said: "It is not so, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food."

<column-break/>

11 "We are all the sons of one man; we come in peace, and your servants plot no evil."
12 To whom he replied: "It is otherwise; you have come to consider the unfortified parts of this land."
13 But they said: "We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; the youngest is with our father, and another is no longer alive."
14 "This is what I said," he replied, "you are spies."
15 "By this I shall now put you to the test: by the health of Pharaoh <note>A common Egyptian court oath, swearing by the king's life</note>, you shall not leave here until your youngest brother comes."
16 "Send one of you to bring him; the rest of you shall be in chains until what you have said is proven, whether it be true or false. Otherwise, by the health of Pharaoh, you are spies."
17 So he handed them over to custody for three days.
18 On the third day, having brought them out of prison, he said: "Do what I have said, and you shall live, for I fear God."
19 "If you are men of peace, let one of your brothers be bound in prison; the rest of you go and carry the grain you have bought to your homes."
<margin>† below, 45:5.</margin>
20 † "And bring your youngest brother to me, so that I may prove your words and you may not die." They did as he had said.
21 And they spoke to one another: "We deserve to suffer these things, because we sinned against our brother, seeing the anguish of his soul while he pleaded with us and we did not listen; therefore this tribulation has come upon us."
<margin>† above, 37:21.</margin>
22 † One of them, Reuben, said: "Did I not say to you: † 'Do not sin against the boy,' and you would not listen to me? Behold, his blood is now being required."
23 They did not know that Joseph understood them, because he spoke to them through an interpreter.
24 And he turned away from them for a little while and wept; then he returned and spoke to them.
25 Taking Simeon and binding him in their presence, he commanded his ministers to fill their sacks with wheat and to replace each man's money in their bags, giving them also provisions for the journey; and they did so.
26 But they, carrying the grain on their donkeys, set out.
27 When one of them opened his sack to give his beast fodder at the inn, he noticed the money in the mouth of the sack,
28 and said to his brothers: "My money has been returned; look, it is here in my sack." And being struck with amazement and troubled, they said to one another: "What is this that God has done to us?"
29 And they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan and told him all that had happened to them, saying:
30 "The lord of the land spoke harshly to us and thought we were spies of the province."
31 To whom we answered: "We are men of peace, nor do we devise any snares."

### C H A P T E R  XLIII.

*With great difficulty, Joseph’s brothers persuade their father that they should take Benjamin with them as they return to Egypt, bringing additional gifts and double the money. Once there, they are invited to a banquet, Simeon is released from prison, and they all feast together with Joseph.*

1 Meanwhile, the famine weighed heavily upon all the land.
2 When the food they had brought from Egypt was consumed, Jacob said to his sons: "Return, and buy us a little more food."
3 Judah responded: "That man warned us under a sworn oath, saying: 'You shall not see my face unless you bring your youngest brother with you.'
4 If, therefore, you are willing to send him with us, we will go together and buy the necessities for you.

7 But they answered: "The man questioned us in order about our family: if our father lived, if we had a brother. And we answered him accordingly, following what he asked. Could we have known that he would say, 'Bring your brother with you'?"

### CHAPTER XLVII.

*Joseph, having announced the arrival of his father and brothers to Pharaoh, introduces Jacob with his sons to Pharaoh: the land of Goshen is granted to them to dwell in, and he feeds them during the time of famine. Furthermore, the famine so oppresses Egypt that, having sold their cattle, they were also forced to sell their land: as a result, a fifth part of the crops goes to the kings of Egypt forever, except for the possessions of the priests. After seventeen years, Jacob, having become very wealthy and being now about to die, makes Joseph swear regarding his burial in Canaan.*

1 Joseph therefore entered and announced it to Pharaoh, saying: "My father and brothers, their sheep and herds, and everything they possess, have come from the land of Canaan: and behold, they are staying in the land of Goshen."
2 He also presented five of the most humble <note>The Latin "extremos" can mean "last" or "end," but here it likely refers to five representative brothers chosen for the audience</note> of his brothers before the king.
3 And he asked them: "What is your work?" They answered: "Your servants are shepherds of sheep, both we and our fathers.
4 We have come to live as strangers in your land: because there is no grass for the flocks of your servants, as the famine is growing heavy in the land of Canaan: and we ask that you command us, your servants, to be in the land of Goshen."
5 The king then said to Joseph: "Your father and your brothers have come to you.
6 The land of Egypt is before you: settle them in the best place, and give them the land of Goshen. And if you know there are industrious men among them, appoint them as masters over my own livestock."
7 After this, Joseph introduced his father to the King and stood him before him; and [Jacob], blessing him,
8 was asked by him: "How many are the days of the years of your life?"
9 He replied: "The days of my pilgrimage are one hundred and thirty years; they are few and difficult, and they have not reached the days of my fathers during which they traveled as pilgrims."
10 And having blessed the king, he went out.
11 But Joseph gave a possession to his father and his brothers in Egypt in the best place of the land, Rameses <note>original: "Ramesses," a city or region in the Nile Delta</note>, as Pharaoh had commanded.
12 And he nourished them, and all his father’s house, providing food for each one.
13 For in the whole world bread was lacking, and famine had oppressed the land, especially of Egypt and Canaan.
14 From which he gathered all the money for the sale of grain and brought it into the king's treasury.
15 And when money failed the buyers,

<column-break/>

all of Egypt came to Joseph, saying: "Give us bread: why should we die before you, since our money is failing?"
16 To whom he replied: "Bring your livestock, and I will give you food for them, if you have no money."
17 When they had brought them, he gave them food in exchange for horses, and sheep, and oxen, and donkeys: and he sustained them that year in exchange for their livestock.
18 They also came in the second year and said to him: "We will not hide from our lord that since our money is failing, our livestock have also failed; nor is it hidden from you that we have nothing left besides our bodies and our land.
19 Why then shall we die while you watch? Both we and our land shall be yours: buy us into the king’s service, and provide seed, lest the farmer perish and the land be reduced to a wilderness."
20 Therefore Joseph bought all the land of Egypt, as everyone sold their possessions because of the magnitude of the famine. And he made it subject to Pharaoh,
21 and all its people, from the furthest borders of Egypt to its very ends,
22 Except for the land of the priests, which had been granted to them by the king: to whom also fixed rations from the public granaries were provided, and therefore they were not compelled to sell their possessions.
23 Then Joseph said to the people: "Behold, as you see, Pharaoh possesses both you and your land: take seed and sow the fields,
24 So that you may have crops. You shall give the fifth part to the king: the remaining four parts I allow to you for seed, and for food for your families and children."
25 They replied: "Our salvation is in your hand: only let our lord look upon us with favor, and we will joyfully serve the king."
26 From that time until the present day, in the whole land of Egypt, the fifth part is paid to the kings, and it became like a law, except for the priestly land, which was free from this condition.
27 So Israel dwelt in Egypt, that is, in the land of Goshen, and possessed it: and they were increased and multiplied exceedingly.
28 And he lived in it seventeen years: and all the days of his life became one hundred and forty-seven years.
29 And when he saw the day of his death approaching, he called his son Joseph and said to him: "If I have found favor in your sight, <margin>† Above, chapter 24 verse 2.</margin> † place your hand under my thigh and show me mercy and truth, so that you do not bury me in Egypt:
30 But I will sleep with my fathers, and you shall carry me out of this land and bury me in the tomb of my ancestors." Joseph replied to him: "I will do what you have commanded."
31 And he said: "Swear then to me." As he was swearing, Israel worshipped God, turning toward the head of the bed.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*The names of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt; the new Pharaoh tries in vain to stop their multiplication by imposing heavy burdens, and by the killing and drowning of the male children: concerning the mercy of the midwives, and their reward from God.*

<margin>Genesis 46:8</margin>
1 <image-desc>Decorative initial H containing a landscape with a building</image-desc> These are the names of the sons of Israel who entered into Egypt with Jacob: they entered, each one with his own household:

3 Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,
4 Dan, and Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
5 All the souls of those who came from the loins of Jacob <note>Latin: "femore Jacob", literally "from the thigh," a biblical idiom for biological descendants.</note> were seventy: but Joseph was already in Egypt.
6 When he died, along with all his brothers and that entire generation,

7 The children of Israel grew, and like budding plants they were multiplied: and becoming exceedingly strong, they filled the land.

9 And he said to his people: "Behold, the people of the children of Israel are many, and stronger than we are.
10 Come, let us wisely oppress them, lest they multiply: and if war should break out against us, they might join our enemies, and having defeated us, depart from the land."
11 Therefore he set masters of the works over them to afflict them with burdens: and they built for Pharaoh the store-cities <note>Latin: "urbes tabernaculorum", literally "cities of tents" or "booths," usually translated as "store cities" or "supply centers."</note> of Pithom and Raamses.

15 Then the King of Egypt spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews: one of whom was named Shiphrah <note>Latin: "Sephora".</note>, and the other Puah <note>Latin: "Phua".</note>,
16 Commanding them: "When you act as midwives for the Hebrew women, and the time of delivery arrives: if it is a male, kill him: if it is a female, keep her alive."
17 But the midwives feared God, and did not do according to the command of the king of Egypt, but they saved the males.
18 When they were summoned to him, the king said: "What is this thing you wanted to do, that you would save the boys?"
19 They answered: "The Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women: for they themselves have the skill of midwifery <note>The Latin implies they are vigorous or have the knowledge to deliver themselves.</note>, and they give birth before we can reach them."

### CHAPTER V.

->*Moses and Aaron report God's commands to Pharaoh: he, despising them, oppresses the Israelites more heavily by denying them straw; hearing this, Moses prays to the Lord for them.*<-

1 After these things, Moses and Aaron went in and said to Pharaoh: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Let my people go, that they may sacrifice to me in the desert.
2 But he answered: Who is the Lord, that I should hear His voice and let Israel go? I know not the Lord, and I will not let Israel go.
3 And they said: The God of the Hebrews has called us, that we may go a three days' journey into the wilderness, and sacrifice to the Lord our God: lest perhaps pestilence or the sword fall upon us.
4 The king of Egypt said to them: Why do you, Moses and Aaron, distract the people from their works? Go to your burdens.
5 And Pharaoh said: The people of the land are many: you see that the multitude has increased: how much more if you give them rest from their labors?
6 Therefore he commanded on that day the overseers of the works and the taskmasters <note>original: "exactoribus"</note> of the people, saying:
7 You shall no longer give straw <term>paleas</term> to the people to make bricks, as before: but let them go and gather stubble for themselves.
8 And the measure of bricks, which they made before, you shall impose upon them, neither shall you diminish anything: for they are idle, and therefore they cry out, saying: Let us go and sacrifice to our God.
9 Let them be oppressed with works, and let them fulfill them: so that they may not listen to lying words.
10 Therefore the overseers of the works and the taskmasters went out and said to the people: Thus says Pharaoh: I do not give you straw:
11 Go, and gather it where you can find it, yet nothing of your work shall be diminished.
12 And the people were scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather straw.
13 The overseers of the works also pressed them, saying: Complete your work every day, as you were accustomed to do before when straw was given to you.
14 And they who were over the works of the children of Israel were scourged by Pharaoh's taskmasters, saying: Why have you not filled the measure of bricks as before, neither yesterday nor today?
15 And the officers of the children of Israel came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying: Why do you act so against your servants?
16 Straw is not given to us, and yet bricks are commanded in like manner: behold, we your servants are beaten with whips, and injustice is done against your people.

### C H A P T E R VI.

->*God encourages Moses, revealing His name Jehovah to him; He comforts the Israelites through Moses with the promise of the land of Canaan; the genealogy of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi is recounted, leading down to Moses and Aaron.*<-

1 And the Lord said to Moses: Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh: for by a mighty hand he will let them go, and with a strong hand he will drive them out of his land.
2 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: I am the Lord.
3 I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty; but my name ADONAI <note>The Hebrew name for the Lord, often substituted for the sacred Tetragrammaton. The summary above uses "Jehovah" as was common in later translations.</note> I did not make known to them.
4 And I established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their pilgrimage, in which they were strangers.
5 I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians have oppressed, and I have remembered my covenant.
6 Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord, who will bring you out from the workhouse <note>original: "ergastulo" — a Roman term for a private prison or workshop where slaves were kept in chains</note> of the Egyptians, and will deliver you from slavery, and will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great judgments.
7 And I will take you to myself for a people, and I will be your God; and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the workhouse of the Egyptians.
8 And I will bring you into the land over which I lifted up my hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and I will give it to you to possess: I am the Lord.
9 Moses therefore told all these things to the children of Israel; but they did not listen to him because of their anguish of spirit and their most cruel labor.
10 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
11 Go in, and speak to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
12 Moses answered before the Lord: Behold, the children of Israel do not listen to me; how then will Pharaoh hear me, especially since I am of uncircumcised lips? <note>A metaphor for a speech impediment or lack of eloquence.</note>
13 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and gave them a command for the children of Israel and for Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, that they should lead the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

### CHAPTER VIII.

->The second plague of Egypt is of frogs; for the removal of which Pharaoh promises to let the people go, but does not: therefore the third plague of stinging gnats is added, and the fourth of flies; because of which Pharaoh again promises that he will let the children of Israel go, which he does not do.<-

### CHAPTER IX.

*The fifth plague is the pestilence upon the livestock, the sixth of boils, the seventh of hail, thunder, and lightning: because of which Pharaoh promises he will let the people go if it ceases, but he does not fulfill it, and hardens himself again: however, none of the children of Israel suffer any harm in these evils.*

And the Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharaoh, and speak to him: Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.
2 For if you still refuse, and withhold them:
3 Behold, my hand shall be upon your fields: and upon the horses, and the donkeys, and the camels, and the oxen, and the sheep, a very grievous pestilence.
4 And the Lord will do a marvelous thing between the possessions of Israel and the possessions of the Egyptians, so that nothing at all shall perish of those things that belong to the children of Israel.
5 And the Lord appointed a time, saying: Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing in the land.
6 The Lord therefore did this thing the next day: and all the animals of the Egyptians died: but of the animals of the children of Israel, nothing at all perished.
7 And Pharaoh sent to see: and there was not anything dead of that which Israel possessed. And Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not let the people go.

10 And they took ashes from the kiln, and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses sprinkled it into the air: and there came boils with swelling blisters upon men and beasts.
11 Neither could the magicians <note>original: "malefici" — sorcerers or practitioners of magic.</note> stand before Moses because of the boils that were upon them, and in all the land of Egypt.
12 And the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not hear them, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses.
13 And the Lord said to Moses: Arise early in the morning, and stand before Pharaoh, and you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.
14 For this time I will send all my plagues upon your heart, and upon your servants, and upon your people: that you may know there is none like me in all the earth.
15 For now, stretching out my hand, I will strike you and your people with pestilence, and you shall perish from the earth.
16 <margin>† Romans 9:17</margin> † And for this cause have I set you up, that I may show my power in you, and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.
17 Do you still retain my people, and will you not let them go?
18 Behold, tomorrow at this same hour I will rain down exceeding much hail, such as has not been in Egypt from the day it was founded until this present time.

20 He that feared the word of the Lord among Pharaoh’s servants made his servants and livestock flee into the houses:
21 But he that neglected the word of the Lord left his servants and his livestock in the fields.
22 And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch forth your hand toward heaven, that there may be hail in the whole land of Egypt, upon men, and upon beasts, and upon every herb of the field in the land of Egypt.
23 <margin>† Wisdom 16:16 & 19</margin> † And Moses stretched forth his rod toward heaven, and the Lord gave thunder and hail, and lightning running along the ground <note>original: "discurrentia fulgura" — describes the visual effect of lightning striking and moving across the earth.</note>: and the Lord rained hail upon the land of Egypt.
24 And the hail and fire mixed together were driven along: and it was of such great size as never before appeared in the whole land of Egypt since that nation was founded.
25 And the hail struck in all the land of Egypt all things that were in the fields, from man even to beast: and the hail struck every herb of the field, and it broke every tree of the country.
26 Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, the hail did not fall.
27 And Pharaoh sent and called Moses and Aaron, saying to them: I have sinned even now: the Lord is just: I and my people are wicked.
28 Pray to the Lord that the thunder of God and the hail may cease: that I may let you go, and that you stay here no longer.

## CHAPTER X.

*The eighth sign or plague is of locusts: when these are taken away, Pharaoh is hardened and does not let the people go even as agreed: therefore the ninth is added, namely of thickest darkness: because of this, Pharaoh permits them to leave: but when Moses insists on the release of all, even the livestock, Pharaoh refuses and threatens Moses with death.*

And the Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharaoh: for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants: that I may perform these signs of mine upon him.
2 And that you may tell in the hearing of your son, and of your grandsons, how often I have crushed the Egyptians, and performed my signs among them: and that you may know that I am the Lord.
3 So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and said to him: Thus says the Lord God of the Hebrews: How long will you refuse to submit to me? Let my people go, that they may sacrifice to me.
<margin>† Wisdom 16:9</margin>
4 † But if you resist, and will not let them go: behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your borders:
5 To cover the surface of the earth, so that nothing of it may appear, but let that which was left by the hail be eaten: for they shall gnaw away all the trees that bud in the fields.
6 And they shall fill your houses, and those of your servants, and of all the Egyptians: such as your fathers and grandfathers have not seen, from the day they were born upon the earth, until this present day. And he turned himself away, and went out from Pharaoh.
7 Then Pharaoh’s servants said to him: How long shall we suffer this stumbling block? Let the men go, that they may sacrifice to the Lord their God: do you not see that Egypt is ruined?
8 And they brought Moses and Aaron back to Pharaoh: and he said to them: Go, sacrifice to the Lord your God: but who are they that are to go?
9 Moses said: We will go with our little ones and our elders, with our sons and daughters, with our sheep and herds: for it is the festival of the Lord our God.
10 And Pharaoh answered: May the Lord be with you in the same way that I let you and your little ones go! <note>original: "Sic Dominus fit vobiscum, quo modo ego dimittam vos" — Pharaoh is speaking sarcastically here, essentially saying "the Lord help you if I ever let you go."</note> Who can doubt that you have evil intentions?
11 It shall not be so; but go only you men, and sacri-

<column-break/>

fice to the Lord: for this is what you yourselves requested. And immediately they were cast out from Pharaoh’s presence.
12 Then the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up upon it, and devour every plant that was left by the hail.
13 And Moses stretched out his rod over the land of Egypt: and the Lord brought a burning wind <note>Usually interpreted as a parching east wind from the desert.</note> all that day and night: and when it was morning, the burning wind raised the locusts.
14 And they came up over the whole land of Egypt: and they settled in all the borders of the Egyptians in countless numbers, such as had not been before that time, nor shall be hereafter.
15 And they covered the whole surface of the earth, wasting everything. Therefore the grass of the land was devoured, and whatever fruit was on the trees, which the hail had left: and nothing green at all remained on the trees or the plants of the earth throughout all Egypt.
16 Therefore Pharaoh in haste called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: I have sinned against the Lord your God, and against you.
17 But now forgive my sin even this once, and pray to the Lord your God, that he may take away this death from me.
18 And Moses, going out from the presence of Pharaoh, prayed to the Lord.
19 Who caused a very strong wind to blow from the west, and it seized the locusts and threw them into the Red Sea: not so much as one remained in all the borders of Egypt.
20 And the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
21 Then the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward heaven: and let there be darkness upon the land of Egypt, so thick that it may be felt.
22 And Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven: and there was a horrible darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.
<margin>† Wisdom 17:2. † Wisdom 18:1.</margin>
23 † No one saw his brother, nor moved himself from the place where he was: † but wherever the children of Israel dwelt, there was light.
24 And Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: Go, sacrifice to the Lord: only let your sheep and herds remain, let your little ones go with you.
25 Moses said: You shall also give us victims and burnt offerings, which we may offer to the Lord our God.
26 All our flocks shall go with us: not a hoof shall remain: for they are necessary for the worship of the Lord our God: especially since we do not know what ought to be sacrificed, until we come to the place itself.
27 But the Lord hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let them go.
28 And Pharaoh said to Moses: Get away from me, and take care that you see my face no more: on whatever day you appear before me, you shall die.
29 Moses answered: It shall be done as you have spoken; I will not see your face again.

## CHAPTER XI.

*Before the tenth sign (the slaughter of the firstborn) which the Lord predicts, he encourages the spoiling of Egypt, which was completed after the slaughter.*

And the Lord said to Moses: I will touch Pharaoh and Egypt with one more plague, and after this he shall let you go, and compel you to leave.

## CHAPTER XII.

*The ritual of sacrificing and eating the Paschal lamb is declared and celebrated; its blood is smeared upon the lintels of the houses, and the angel, having slain all the firstborn of Egypt, leaves the Israelites untouched, who then depart with the spoils and riches of Egypt: concerning the rite of the Passover and the eating of unleavened bread, and the time of Israel's dwelling in Egypt.*

1 The Lord also said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt:
2 "This month shall be to you the beginning of months: it shall be the first in the months of the year.
3 Speak to the whole assembly of the children of Israel, and say to them: On the tenth day of this month, let every man take a lamb for his family and his house.
4 But if the number be too small that it cannot suffice for the eating of the lamb, he shall take his neighbor who is joined to his house, according to the number of souls which may be enough to eat the lamb.
5 And the lamb shall be without blemish, a male, one year old; according to which rite you shall also take a kid.
6 And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month: and the whole multitude of the children of Israel shall sacrifice it at evening.
7 And they shall take of its blood, and put it upon both side-posts, and on the upper door-posts of the houses in which they shall eat it.
8 And they shall eat the flesh that night roasted with fire, and unleavened bread with wild lettuces.
9 You shall not eat anything of it raw, nor boiled in water, but only roasted with fire: you shall devour the head with the feet and the entrails.
10 Neither shall anything of it remain until the morning: if anything be left, you shall burn it with fire.
11 And thus you shall eat it: You shall gird your loins,

<column-break/>

and you shall have shoes on your feet, holding staves in your hands, and you shall eat in haste: for it is the Passover <note>original: "Phase", from the Hebrew "Pesach"</note> (that is, the passing over) of the Lord.
12 And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man even to beast: and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments, I the Lord.
13 And the blood shall be unto you for a sign in the houses where you shall be: and I shall see the blood, and shall pass over you: and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy when I shall strike the land of Egypt.
14 And you shall have this day for a memorial; and you shall celebrate it as a solemnity to the Lord in your generations with an everlasting worship.
15 Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread <note>original: "azyma"</note>: on the first day there shall be no leaven in your houses: whosoever shall eat anything leavened, that soul shall perish from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
16 The first day shall be holy and solemn, and the seventh day shall be venerable with the same festivity: you shall do no work in them, except those things which belong to eating.
17 And you shall observe the feast of unleavened bread: for on this very same day I will bring your army out of the land of Egypt, and you shall keep this day in your generations by a perpetual rite.
<margin>Leviticus 23:5. Numbers 28:16.</margin>
18 In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the same month at evening.
19 For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses: he who eats anything leavened, his soul shall perish from the assembly of Israel, as well among strangers as among the natives of the land.
20 You shall eat nothing leavened: in all your habitations you shall eat unleavened bread."
21 And Moses called all the elders of the children of Israel, and said to them: "Go, take an animal for your families, and sacrifice the Passover.
<margin>Hebrews 11:28.</margin>
22 And dip a bunch of hyssop <note>A bushy plant often used in ancient ritual cleansing.</note> in the blood which is at the threshold, and sprinkle the lintel and both side-posts with it: let none of you go out of the door of his house until morning.
23 For the Lord will pass through striking the Egyptians: and when He sees the blood on the lintel and on both side-posts, He will pass over the door of the house, and will not suffer the striker <note>Often interpreted as the "destroying angel".</note> to enter your houses and hurt you.
24 Keep this word as a law for you and your children forever.
25 And when you have entered the land which the Lord will give you as He promised, you shall observe these ceremonies.
26 And when your children shall say to you: 'What is this religious rite?'
27 You shall say to them: 'It is the victim of the Lord's passing over, when He passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, striking the Egyptians, and delivering our houses.' And the people, bowing down, adored.
28 And the children of Israel went out and did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.
<margin>Above 11:5. Wisdom 18:5.</margin>
29 And it came to pass at midnight, the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne, even to the firstborn of the captive woman who was in prison, and all the firstborn of the cattle.

### CHAPTER XIV.

*Pharaoh with his followers pursues Israel; the angel in the pillar of cloud places himself between the two groups; Moses divides the Red Sea, which the Hebrews cross on dry foot; the Egyptians are drowned first by the angel and then by the returning waters, along with all their cavalry and chariots.*

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 "Speak to the children of Israel: Let them turn back and camp over against Pi-hahiroth <note>original: "Phihahiroth"</note>, which is between Migdol <note>original: "Magdalum"</note> and the sea, opposite Baal-zephon <note>original: "Beelsephon"</note>: you shall place your camp before it, by the sea."
3 "And Pharaoh will say regarding the children of Israel: 'They are hemmed in by the land; the desert has shut them in.'"
4 "And I will harden his heart, and he will pursue you: and I will be glorified in Pharaoh, and in all his army: and the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord." And they did so.
5 And it was reported to the king of the Egyptians that the people had fled: and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed toward the people, and they said: "What did we mean to do, to let Israel go from serving us?"
6 Therefore he readied his chariot, and took all his people with him.
7 And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and whatever chariots there were in Egypt: and the captains of the entire army.
8 And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and he pursued the children of Israel: but they had gone out with a high hand <note>original: "manu excelsa" — meaning with boldness or under divine protection</note>.
<margin>† Joshua 24:6. 1 Maccabees 4:7.</margin>
9 † And when the Egyptians pursued the tracks of those going before, they found them in the camp by the sea: all the cavalry and chariots of Pharaoh, and the entire army, were at Pi-hahiroth against Baal-zephon.
10 And when Pharaoh drew near, the children of Israel, lifting up their eyes, saw the Egyptians behind them: and they feared greatly: and they cried out to the Lord,
11 And they said to Moses: "Perhaps there were no graves in Egypt, therefore you have brought us to die in the wilderness: why did you want to do this, to lead us out of Egypt?"
12 "Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying: 'Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians'? For it was much better to serve them than to die in the wilderness."
13 And Moses said to the people: "Do not fear: stand still, and see the great works of the Lord which he will do today: for the Egyptians, whom you see now, you shall never see again forever."
14 "The Lord will fight for you, and you shall keep silence."
15 And the Lord said to Moses: "Why do you cry out to me? Speak to the children of Israel that they may move forward."
16 "But you, lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it: so that the children of Israel may walk through the middle of the sea on dry ground."
17 "And I will harden the heart of the Egyptians so that they pursue you: and I will be glorified in Pharaoh, and in all his army, and in his chariots and in his horsemen."
18 "And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I shall be glorified in Pharaoh, and in his chariots and in his horsemen."

### CHAPTER XVI.

*While the Israelites murmur in the desert of Sin regarding the lack of food, the Lord sends quails and rains down Manna to satisfy them: by the Lord's command, they are to observe the Sabbath, gather the manna, and store it as a memorial; with this, he feeds them daily for forty years.*

<margin>Wisdom 11:2.</margin>
1 And they set out from Elim, and the whole multitude of the children of Israel came into the desert of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai: on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had departed from the land of Egypt.

2 And the entire congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.

3 And the children of Israel said to them: "Would that we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat over the fleshpots and ate bread to the full: why have you brought us into this desert, to kill this whole multitude with hunger?"

4 Then the Lord said to Moses: "Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you: let the people go out and gather what is sufficient for each day: that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not."

5 "But on the sixth day, let them prepare what they bring in: and let it be double what they were accustomed to gather every other day."

6 And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel: "In the evening, you shall know that the Lord has brought you out of the land of Egypt."

7 "And in the morning, you shall see the glory of the Lord: for he has heard your murmuring against the Lord: but as for us, what are we, that you mutter against us?"

8 And Moses said: "The Lord will give you meat to eat in the evening, and bread to the full in the morning: because he has heard your murmurings with which you have murmured against him. For what are we? Your murmuring is not against us, but against the Lord."

9 Moses also said to Aaron: "Say to the whole congregation of the children of Israel: 'Come before the Lord: for he has heard your murmuring.'"

10 And as Aaron spoke to the entire assembly of the children of Israel, they looked toward the wilderness: and behold, the glory † of the Lord appeared in a cloud.

<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 45:3.</margin>
11 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

12 "I have heard the murmuring of the children of Israel. Speak to them: 'In the evening you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread: and you shall know that I am the Lord your God.'"

13 So it came to pass in the evening that quails <note>original: "coturnix"</note> came up and covered the camp: and in the morning, a dew lay all around the camp.

<margin>† Numbers 11:7. Psalm 77:24.</margin>
14 And when it had covered the surface of the earth, there appeared in the wilderness something small and as if pounded by a pestle, like hoarfrost upon the ground.

<margin>Wisdom 16:20. John 6:31.</margin>
15 When the children of Israel saw this, they said to one another: "Manhu?" which means: "What is this?" <note>The Hebrew phrase 'Man hu' is the origin of the word Manna</note> for they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them: † "This is the bread which the Lord has given you to eat."

24 † Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

25 Burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise. <note>This principle is known as the *lex talionis*, or the law of retaliation, intended to limit vengeance to an equivalent of the injury.</note>

26 If anyone strikes the eye of his male or female servant and makes them one-eyed, he shall let them go free for the eye he plucked out.

27 If he also knocks out the tooth of his male or female servant, he shall likewise let them go free.

28 If an ox strikes a man or woman with its horn and they die, it shall be overwhelmed with stones: and its flesh shall not be eaten; the owner of the ox shall also be innocent.

29 But if the ox was a gorer from yesterday and the day before <note>original: "nudiustertius"; a Latin idiom meaning "recently" or "in the past few days"</note>, and they warned its owner, and he did not shut it in, and it kills a man or woman: the ox shall be overwhelmed with stones, and they shall kill its owner.

30 But if a price is imposed on him, he shall give for his life whatever is asked.

31 If it strikes a son or daughter with its horn, it shall be subject to a similar sentence.

32 If it attacks a male or female servant, he shall give thirty shekels <note>original: "siclos"; a standard unit of weight for silver</note> of silver to the master, but the ox shall be crushed with stones.

33 If anyone opens a cistern, or digs one and does not cover it, and an ox or donkey falls into it,

34 The owner of the cistern shall restore the price of the beasts: but that which is dead shall be his own.

<column-break/>

35 If one man's ox wounds the ox of another, and it dies: they shall sell the living ox and divide the price, and they shall divide the carcass of the dead one between them.

36 But if he knew that the ox was a gorer from yesterday and the day before, and its owner did not guard it: he shall restore ox for ox, and shall receive the carcass whole.

### CHAPTER XXII.

->*The punishment for theft and damage caused; the law of deposits, loans, hires, and seduction; the punishment for sorcery, bestiality, and idolatrous sacrifice; the punishment for those harming the stranger, the widow, and the orphan; the law of lending, usury, and pledges, and the obedience regarding tithes, first-fruits, and the firstborn: concerning meat tasted by beasts.*<-

1 **I**f anyone steals an ox or a sheep, and kills or sells it: he shall restore five oxen for one ox, <margin>† 2 Sam. 12:6</margin> † and four sheep for one sheep.

2 If a thief is found breaking in or digging under a house, and dies from a received wound: the striker shall not be guilty of blood.

3 But if he does this after the sun has risen, he has committed homicide, and he himself shall die. If he does not have anything to return for the theft, he himself shall be sold.

4 If that which was stolen is found with him alive, whether ox, donkey, or sheep: he shall restore double.

5 If anyone damages a field or vineyard, and lets his beast loose to graze on another's property: whatever best he has in his own field or vineyard, he shall restore according to the estimation of the damage.

6 If a fire breaks out and finds thorns, and catches heaps of grain, or standing crops in the fields, he who started the fire shall restore the damage.

7 If anyone entrusts money or a vessel to a friend for safekeeping, and it is stolen from him who received it: if the thief is found, he shall restore double.

8 If the thief is hidden, the master of the house shall be brought to the judges <note>original: "deos"; literally "gods," but used here to denote the magistrates acting with divine authority</note>, and shall swear that he did not stretch out his hand against his neighbor's property,

9 To commit fraud, as much in an ox as in a donkey, a sheep, clothing, or whatever can cause damage: the cause of both shall come before the judges: and if they judge against him, he shall restore double to his neighbor.

10 If anyone entrusts a donkey, ox, sheep, or any beast to his neighbor for safekeeping, and it dies, or is weakened, or taken by enemies, and no one saw it:

11 An oath shall be between them, that he did not stretch out his hand to his neighbor's property: and the owner shall accept the oath, and the other shall not be compelled to restore it.

12 † But if it was taken away by theft, he shall restore the damage to the owner. <margin>† Gen. 31:39</margin>

13 If it was eaten by a beast, let him bring that which was killed as evidence, and he shall not restore it.

14 He who asks for any of these things as a loan from his neighbor, and it is weakened or dies while the owner is not present, shall be compelled to restore it.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

*Moses reports the laws brought by God to the people, and the people accept them: he sanctions a covenant between God and the people by offering sacrifices to the Lord and sprinkling the blood of the covenant upon the people. While the others remain at the foot of the mountain, Moses alone ascends the mountain to receive the stone tablets of the law, where he remained with the Lord for forty days and forty nights.*

1 And He said to Moses: Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and you shall worship from afar.

2 Moses alone shall come near to the Lord, but they shall not come close: nor shall the people ascend with him.

3 So Moses came and told the people all the words of the Lord and the judgments: and all the people answered with one voice: We will do all the words of the Lord which He has spoken.

4 Then Moses wrote down all the words of the Lord: and rising early in the morning, he built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars <note>original: "titulos"; standing stones representing the presence of the tribes</note> for the twelve tribes of Israel.

5 And he sent young men from the sons of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings, and they sacrificed peace offerings <note>original: "victimas pacificas"; offerings intended to express gratitude and fellowship</note> of calves to the Lord.

6 Moses took half of the blood and put it into bowls: and the remaining part he poured upon the altar.

7 And taking the Book of the Covenant, he read it in the hearing of the people: who said: All that the Lord has spoken, we will do, and we will be obedient.

<margin>† Heb. 9:20</margin>
8 He then took the blood and sprinkled it upon the people, and said: This is † the blood of the covenant which the Lord has made with you concerning all these words.

9 Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up.

10 And they saw the God of Israel: and under His feet was something like a work of sapphire stone, and like the sky when it is clear.

11 And He did not lay His hand <note>That is, He did not strike or harm them for seeing Him</note> upon those of the sons of Israel who had withdrawn far off; and they saw God, and they ate and drank.

12 And the Lord said to Moses: Come up to me on the mountain, and be there: and I will give you the stone tablets, and the law and the commandments which I have written: that you may teach them.

13 Moses and Joshua his servant rose up, and as Moses was ascending into the mountain of God,

14 He said to the elders: Wait here until we return to you. You have Aaron and Hur with you: if any dispute should arise, you shall refer it to them.

15 And when Moses had gone up, a cloud covered the mountain,

16 And the glory of the Lord dwelt upon Sinai, covering it with a cloud for six days: and on the seventh day He called him from the midst of the darkness.

17 And the appearance of the glory of the Lord was like a burning fire upon the top of the mountain, in the sight of the sons of Israel.

<column-break/>

18 And Moses, entering into the midst of the cloud, went up into the mountain: and he was there forty days and forty nights.

### CHAPTER XXV.

*An offering of firstfruits and gifts is commanded to form God's tabernacle, the Ark of the Covenant, the table for the bread of the presence, and the seven-branched candlestick, and all things pertaining to them: a pattern of all these things is shown.*

### CHAPTER XXVI.

->*The form and construction of the Mosaic tabernacle, the*<-
->*veil, the ark, the mercy seat, the table, the lampstand,*<-
->*and the tent, according to their respective measurements.*<-

1 Moreover, you shall make the tabernacle in this way: You shall make ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and blue <note>original: "hyacintho"</note>, and purple, and scarlet twice-dyed, varied with embroidered work <note>original: "opere plumario"; literally "feather-work," referring to intricate needlework</note>.
2 The length of one curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits: the width shall be four cubits. All the curtains shall be of one measure.
3 Five curtains shall be joined to one another, and the other five shall be coupled together in a similar connection.
4 You shall make loops of blue on the sides and edges of the curtains, so they may be joined together.
5 The curtain shall have fifty loops on each side, so inserted that loop meets loop, and one may be fitted to the other.
6 You shall also make fifty golden rings by which the veils of the curtains are to be joined, so that it becomes one tabernacle.
7 You shall also make eleven curtains of goats' hair <note>original: "saga cilicina"; cloth made of goat hair, often used for tents</note>, to cover the roof of the tabernacle.

<column-break/>

8 The length of one goat-hair curtain shall be thirty cubits: and the width, four: the measure of all the curtains shall be equal.
9 Of these, you shall join five separately, and six you shall couple together, so that you double the sixth curtain at the front of the roof.
10 You shall also make fifty loops on the edge of one curtain, so it can be joined with the other: and fifty loops on the edge of the other curtain, so it may be coupled with the next.
11 You shall also make fifty bronze clasps <note>original: "fibulas æneas"</note>, by which the loops may be joined, so that one single covering is made from all of them.
12 As for the part that remains over in the curtains prepared for the roof—that is, the one curtain that is extra—you shall cover the back of the tabernacle with the half of it.
13 And a cubit shall hang down on one side, and another on the other side, from that which is extra in the length of the curtains, protecting both sides of the tabernacle.
14 You shall also make another covering for the roof of rams' skins dyed red: and over this again, another covering of violet-colored skins <note>original: "ianthinis pellibus"; often translated as badger or porpoise skins</note>.
15 You shall also make the upright boards of the tabernacle of shittim wood,
16 Each of which shall be ten cubits in length, and one and a half cubits in width.
17 In the sides of the board, two mortises <note>original: "incastraturae"; joints or tenons</note> shall be made, by which one board is connected to another board: and in this manner all the boards shall be prepared.
18 Twenty of these shall be on the south side which faces the meridian.
19 For these, you shall cast forty silver bases <note>original: "bases argenteas"; sockets or foundations</note>, so that two bases are placed under each board at the two corners.
20 Likewise on the second side of the tabernacle, which faces the north, there shall be twenty boards,
21 Having forty silver bases: two bases shall be placed under each board.
22 But for the western side of the tabernacle, you shall make six boards,
23 And again another two which are to be set up in the corners at the back of the tabernacle.
24 And they shall be joined from the bottom to the top, and one single joint shall hold them all together. A similar joining shall be maintained for the two boards that are to be placed in the corners.
25 And there shall be eight boards in total, their silver bases numbering sixteen, counting two bases for each board.
26 You shall also make five bars <note>original: "vectes"</note> of shittim wood to hold together the boards on one side of the tabernacle,
27 And five on the other side, and the same number for the western side:
28 These shall be passed through the middle of the boards from one end to the other.
29 You shall also overlay the boards themselves with gold, and cast golden rings in them, through which the bars may hold the boarding together: these bars you shall cover with plates of gold.

32 Which you shall hang before four columns of shittim wood, which themselves shall be overlaid with gold and shall have golden capitals, but silver bases.

->*The altar of burnt offerings and the court of the tabernacle, the screen, the columns, and the oil for the lamps are ordered to be prepared, and the lighting of them.*<-

<margin>Below 38:6</margin>
1 You shall also make an altar of shittim wood, which shall have five <term>cubits <note>an ancient measurement of about 18 inches, the length of a forearm</note></term> in length, and as many in breadth, that is, it shall be square, and three cubits in height.
2 And there shall be horns at the four corners of it: and you shall overlay it with bronze.
3 And you shall make for its use pots to receive the ashes, and shovels and basins, and flesh-hooks, and firepans: all its vessels you shall fashion out of bronze.
4 And a grate in the manner of a bronze net: at the four corners of which there shall be four bronze rings,
5 Which you shall place under the hearth <note>original: "arulam"; a small altar or hearth-top</note> of the altar: and the grate shall reach even to the middle of the altar.
6 You shall also make two poles for the altar of shittim wood, which you shall overlay with plates of bronze:
7 And you shall draw them through the rings, and they shall be on both sides of the altar for carrying it.
<margin>Above 20:24</margin>
8 You shall not make it solid, but empty and hollow on the inside, as it was shown to you on the mountain.
9 You shall also make the court of the tabernacle, on the south side of which, facing the midday sun, there shall be hangings of fine twisted linen: one side shall hold a hundred cubits in length.
10 And twenty columns with as many bronze bases, which shall have their capitals with their engravings of silver.
11 Likewise on the north side along the length there shall be hangings of a hundred cubits, twenty columns, and bronze bases of the same number, and their capitals with their engravings of silver.
12 But in the breadth of the court, which looks toward the west, there shall be hangings of fifty cubits, and ten columns, and as many bases.
13 In that breadth of the court also, which looks toward the east, there shall be fifty cubits.
14 In which hangings of fifteen cubits shall be assigned to one side, and three columns and as many bases:
15 And on the other side there shall be hangings containing fifteen cubits, three columns, and as many bases.
16 But at the entrance of the court there shall be a screen of twenty cubits of blue and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer: it shall have four columns, with as many bases.
17 All the columns of the court round about shall be draped with silver plates, with silver capitals, and bronze bases.

<column-break/>

18 In length the court shall occupy a hundred cubits, in breadth fifty, the height shall be five cubits: and it shall be made of fine twisted linen, and shall have bronze bases.
19 All the vessels of the tabernacle for all uses and ceremonies, as well as its pegs and those of the court, you shall make of bronze.
20 Command the children of Israel that they bring to you the purest oil from olive trees, beaten with a pestle: so that the lamp may burn always
21 In the tabernacle of the testimony, outside the veil which is hung before the testimony. And Aaron and his sons shall arrange it, so that it may give light before the Lord until the morning. It shall be a perpetual service throughout their successions from the children of Israel.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

->*The pontifical vestments of Aaron and his sons are described.*<-

1 Also bring near to yourself Aaron your brother with his sons from among the children of Israel, that they may minister to me in the priesthood: Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
2 And you shall make a holy garment for Aaron your brother, for glory and for beauty.
3 And you shall speak to all the wise of heart, whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they may make Aaron’s garments, in which he being sanctified may minister to me.
4 Now these shall be the garments which they shall make: A <term>breastplate <note>original: "Rationale"; the "breastplate of judgment"</note></term>, and an <term>ephod <note>original: "superhumerale"; a garment worn over the shoulders</note></term>, a robe and a close-fitting linen tunic, a miter <note>original: "cidarim"; a priestly turban</note> and a sash. They shall make holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that they may minister to me in the priesthood.
5 And they shall take gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine linen.
6 And they shall make the ephod of gold and blue and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen, with multi-colored work <note>original: "opere polymito"; diverse or embroidered weaving</note>.
7 It shall have two edges joined at the top on both sides, so that they may come together as one.
8 The very weaving and all the variety of the work shall be of gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen.
9 And you shall take two onyx stones, and engrave on them the names of the children of Israel:
10 Six names on one stone, and the remaining six on the other, according to the order of their birth.
11 With the work of a sculptor and the engraving of a jeweler you shall engrave them with the names of the children of Israel, set in gold and enclosed:
12 And you shall place them on both sides of the ephod, a memorial for the children of Israel. And Aaron shall bear their names before the Lord upon both shoulders, for a remembrance.
13 You shall also make hooks of gold,
14 And two small chains of the purest gold linked to one another, which you shall insert into the hooks.
15 You shall also make the breastplate of judgment with multi-colored work according to the weaving of the ephod, of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen.
16 It shall be square and doubled: it shall have the measure of a span <note>original: "palmi"; the width of a hand or about 9 inches</note> both in length and in breadth.
17 And you shall place in it four rows of stones: in the first row shall be a sardius stone, and a topaz, and an emerald:
18 In the second a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a jasper:

19 In the third row, a jacinth <note>original: "ligurius"; a gemstone likely representing the tribe of Gad or Dan</note>, an agate, and an amethyst:
20 In the fourth row, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a beryl: they shall be set in gold in their rows.
21 And they shall have the names of the children of Israel: they shall be engraved with twelve names, each stone with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
22 You shall make for the breastplate <note>original: "rationali"; often called the Breastplate of Judgment</note> chains linked to one another of the purest gold:
23 And two golden rings, which you shall place at both ends of the breastplate:
24 And you shall join the golden chains to the rings that are at its edges:
25 And the ends of the chains themselves you shall join to two hooks on both sides of the ephod <note>original: "superhumeralis"; a garment worn over the shoulders</note> which faces the breastplate.
26 You shall also make two golden rings, which you shall place at the ends of the breastplate, on the edges that are opposite the ephod and look toward its back.
27 And also two other golden rings, which are to be placed on both sides of the ephod below, which faces toward the front of the lower joining, so that it may be fitted with the ephod,
28 And the breastplate shall be fastened by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue <note>original: "hyacinthina"; a deep blue or violet-colored</note> ribbon, so that the skillfully made joining remains, and the breastplate and the ephod cannot be separated from each other.
29 And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his breast when he enters the Sanctuary, as a memorial before the Lord forever.
30 Moreover, you shall put in the breastplate of judgment the **Urim and Thummim** <note>original: "Doctrinam & Veritatem"; literally "Doctrine and Truth," the Vulgate’s translation for the sacred lots or objects used for divination</note>, which shall be on Aaron's breast when he goes in before the Lord: and he shall always carry the judgment of the children of Israel on his breast in the sight of the Lord.
31 You shall also make the robe of the ephod all of blue,
32 In the middle of which, at the top, shall be an opening for the head, and a woven border around it, as is usually made on the edges of garments, so that it may not easily be torn.
33 And beneath, at the feet of the same robe, all around, you shall make as it were pomegranates <note>original: "mala punica"</note> of blue, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, with bells mixed in the middle,
34 So that there is a golden bell and a pomegranate, and again another golden bell and a pomegranate.
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 45:11</margin>
35 And Aaron shall be clothed with it in the office of his ministry, so that the sound may be heard when he enters and exits the Sanctuary in the sight of the Lord, and he may not die.
36 You shall also make a plate of the purest gold: in which you shall engrave, with the work of an engraver, **Holy to the Lord** <note>original: "Sanctum Domino"</note>.
37 And you shall tie it with a blue ribbon, and it shall be upon the turban <note>original: "tiaram"</note>,
38 Hanging over the forehead of the high priest. And Aaron shall bear the iniquities of those things which the children of Israel have offered and sanctified in all their gifts and donations. And the plate shall always be on his forehead, so that the Lord may be appeased toward them.
39 And you shall weave the tunic of fine linen, and you shall make a turban of fine linen, and a sash <note>original: "balteum"</note> of embroidery work.
40 Furthermore, for the sons of Aaron you shall prepare linen tunics, and sashes and turbans, for glory and beauty:
41 And with all these you shall clothe Aaron your brother and his sons with him. And you shall ordain <note>original: "consecrabis manus"; literally "consecrate their hands," a Hebrew idiom for ordination to the priesthood</note> them all, and sanctify them, so that they may perform the office of priesthood for me.

<column-break/>

42 You shall also make linen undergarments <note>original: "feminalia"; breeches</note> to cover the flesh of their nakedness, from the loins even to the thighs.
43 And Aaron and his sons shall use them when they enter the tabernacle of the testimony, or when they approach the altar to minister in the sanctuary, lest being guilty of iniquity they die. It shall be a law forever to Aaron, and to his seed after him.

### CHAPTER XXIX.

->*What the consecration of the priests should be, and the rite of offering for them, and who may eat these offerings: and concerning the two yearling lambs to be offered daily.*<-

<margin>† Leviticus 9:2</margin>
1 And this also you shall do, so that they may be consecrated to me in the priesthood. Take a calf from the herd, and two rams without blemish,
2 And unleavened bread, and a crust without leaven, which is sprinkled with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil: you shall make them all of fine wheat flour.
3 And having placed them in a basket, you shall offer them: and the calf and the two rams.
4 And you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony. And when you have washed the father with his sons in water,
5 You shall clothe Aaron with his vestments, that is, with the linen garment and the tunic, and the ephod, and the breastplate, which you shall fasten with the sash.
6 And you shall place the turban on his head, and the holy plate upon the turban,
7 And you shall pour the oil of unction upon his head: and by this rite he shall be consecrated.
8 You shall also bring his sons, and clothe them with linen tunics, and gird them with a sash,
9 Namely Aaron and his children, and you shall put miters <note>head coverings</note> on them: and they shall be priests to me by a perpetual religion. After you have initiated <note>literally "filled"</note> their hands,
<margin>† Leviticus 1:3</margin>
10 You shall also bring the calf before the tabernacle of the testimony. And Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon its head,
11 And you shall kill it in the sight of the Lord, near the door of the tabernacle of the testimony.
12 And taking some of the blood of the calf, you shall put it upon the horns of the altar with your finger, and the rest of the blood you shall pour at its base.
<margin>† Leviticus 3:3</margin>
13 You shall also take all the fat that covers the entrails, and the caul of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and offer them as incense <note>as a burnt offering</note> upon the altar:
14 But the flesh of the calf and the hide and the dung you shall burn outside the camp, because it is for sin.
15 You shall also take one ram, upon whose head Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands.
16 And when you have killed it, you shall take of its blood, and pour it around the altar.
17 And the ram itself you shall cut into pieces, and having washed its entrails and feet, you shall place them upon the cut flesh and upon its head.
18 And you shall offer the whole ram as incense upon the altar: it is an oblation to the Lord, a most sweet odor of the victim of the Lord.
19 You shall also take the other ram, upon whose head Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands.
20 And when you have sacrificed it, you shall take of its blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron and of his sons, and upon the thumbs of their right hand and the great toes of their right foot, and you shall pour the blood upon the altar round about.
