21 And when you have taken from the blood that is upon the altar, and from the oil of unction, you shall sprinkle Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their vestments; and they and their garments shall be consecrated.
22 You shall take the fat of the ram, and the tail, and the fat that covers the inner organs, and the mesh of the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right shoulder, because it is the ram of consecration:
23 And a single loaf of bread, a crusty cake sprinkled with oil, and a wafer from the basket of unleavened bread, which is placed in the sight of the Lord:
24 And you shall place all these upon the hands of Aaron and his sons, and you shall sanctify them, elevating them before the Lord.
25 And you shall receive all things from their hands: and you shall burn them upon the altar for a burnt offering <term>holocaustum; a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire as a gift to God</term>, a most sweet odor in the sight of the Lord, because it is His offering.
26 You shall also take the breast from the ram by which Aaron was initiated, and you shall sanctify it, elevated before the Lord, and it shall fall to your portion.
27 And you shall sanctify both the consecrated breast and the shoulder that you separated from the ram,
28 By which Aaron and his sons were initiated, and they shall fall to the portion of Aaron and his sons by a perpetual right from the children of Israel: because they are the first-fruits and the beginnings from their peace offerings <note>original: "victimis eorum pacificis"; offerings intended to express gratitude or fellowship with God</note> which they offer to the Lord.
29 But the holy garment, which Aaron shall use, his sons shall have after him, that they may be anointed in it, and their hands may be consecrated.
30 For seven days, he from among his sons who is appointed high priest <note>original: "pontifex"; literally "bridge-builder," used here for the High Priest</note> in his place shall use it, and who shall enter the tabernacle of testimony to minister in the Sanctuary.
31 And you shall take the ram of consecration and boil its flesh in a holy place:
<margin>† Leviticus 8:31, 24:9. Matthew 12:4.</margin>
32 Which Aaron and his sons shall eat. † Also the loaves, which are in the basket, they shall eat in the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony,
33 So that it may be an appeasing sacrifice, and the hands of those offering may be sanctified. A stranger <note>original: "Alienigena"; referring here to anyone not belonging to the family of the priests</note> shall not eat of them, because they are holy.
34 But if any of the consecrated flesh or the bread remains until morning, you shall burn the remnants with fire: they shall not be eaten, because they are sanctified.
35 All things that I have commanded you, you shall do for Aaron and his sons. For seven days you shall consecrate their hands:
36 And you shall offer a calf for sin every day for atonement. And you shall cleanse the altar when you have offered the victim of expiation, and you shall anoint it for sanctification.
37 For seven days you shall atone for the altar and sanctify it, and it shall be the Holy of Holies; everyone who touches it shall be sanctified.
<margin>† Numbers 28:3.</margin>
38 This is what you shall do on the altar: † Two lambs of a year old every day continually,
39 One lamb in the morning, and the other in the evening,
40 A tenth part of fine flour mixed with beaten oil <note>original: "oleo tufo"; likely referring to the purest oil obtained by pounding olives</note>, which has the measure of a fourth part of a hin <term>hin; an ancient liquid measure, approximately 5 liters</term>, and wine for a libation of the same measure for one lamb.
41 But the other lamb you shall offer in the evening according to the rite of the morning offering, and according to what we have said, for an odor of sweetness:
42 It is a sacrifice to the Lord. A perpetual offering throughout your generations, at the door of the tabernacle of testimony before the Lord, where I will appoint to speak to you.

<column-break/>

43 And there I will command the children of Israel, and the altar shall be sanctified in my glory.
44 I will also sanctify the tabernacle of testimony with the altar, and Aaron with his sons, that they may perform the office of priesthood for me.
45 And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel, and I will be their God,
46 And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, who led them out of the land of Egypt, that I might remain among them, I the Lord their God.

### CHAPTER XXX.

*The institution of the altar of incense, and the money to be collected for the uses of the tabernacle, the making of the bronze basin for the washing of the priests, the holy oil for anointing the priests and the vessels of the temple, the anointing of the incense, and the remaining things which pertain to the tabernacle.*

1 You shall also make an altar for the burning of incense of shittim wood <note>original: "lignis setim"; acacia wood, known for its durability</note>,
2 Having a cubit <term>cubit; an ancient unit of length, roughly 18 inches or 45 centimeters</term> in length, and another in width, that is, four-square, and two cubits in height. Horns shall proceed from it.
3 And you shall overlay it with the purest gold, as well as its grate, and the walls round about, and the horns. And you shall make for it a small crown of gold round about,
4 And two golden rings under the crown on each side, that poles may be put in them, and the altar may be carried.
5 You shall also make the poles themselves of shittim wood, and you shall overlay them with gold.
6 And you shall place the altar opposite the veil that hangs before the ark of the testimony, before the propitiatory <note>original: "propitiatorio"; the "Mercy Seat" or golden cover of the Ark</note> by which the testimony is covered, where I will speak to you.
7 And Aaron shall burn sweet-smelling incense upon it, fragrant in the morning. When he prepares the lamps, he shall burn it:
8 And when he places them in the evening, he shall burn a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout your generations.
9 You shall not offer upon it incense of any other composition, nor an offering, nor a victim, nor shall you pour libations.
10 And Aaron shall pray <note>original: "deprecabitur"; in this context, making atonement or intercession</note> over its horns once a year, with the blood that was offered for sin, and he shall make atonement upon it throughout your generations. It shall be the Holy of Holies to the Lord.
11 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
<margin>† Numbers 1:2.</margin>
12 † When you take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number, each one shall give a price for their souls to the Lord, and there shall be no plague among them when they are counted.
13 And this every one shall give who passes to the name <note>original: "transit ad nomen"; referring to being enrolled in the census</note>, half a shekel <note>original: "sicli"</note> according to the measure of the temple.
<margin>† Leviticus 27:25. Numbers 3:47. Ezekiel 45:12.</margin>
† A shekel has twenty obols <note>original: "obolos"; elsewhere translated as 'gerahs'</note>. The half-part of a shekel shall be offered to the Lord.
14 He who is included in the number, from twenty years and upwards, shall give the price.
15 The rich shall not add to the half-shekel, and the poor shall diminish nothing.
16 And having received the money, which was collected from the children of Israel, you shall deliver it for the uses of the tabernacle of testimony, so that it may be a memorial of them before the Lord, and he may be merciful to their souls.
17 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
18 You shall also make a bronze basin with its base for washing—

### C H A P T E R XXXI.

*Bezalel and Oholiab are appointed by the Lord for the building of the tabernacle and the other things which have been mentioned: concerning the observation of the sabbath, and concerning the two stone tablets of the law given by the Lord to Moses.*

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
3 And I have filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom, and understanding, and knowledge in every work.
4 To devise whatever can be artificially made of gold, and silver, and brass,
5 Of marble, and gems, and variety of wood.
6 And I have given him as a companion Oholiab the son of Ahisa-

<column-break/>

mach of the tribe of Dan. And in the heart of every skillful man I have placed wisdom: that they may make all the things that I have commanded you,
7 The tabernacle of the covenant, and the ark of the testimony, and the propitiatory <term>propitiatorium; the 'mercy seat' or golden cover of the Ark</term> which is over it, and all the vessels of the tabernacle,
8 And the table and its vessels, the most pure lampstand with its vessels, and the altars of incense,
9 And of burnt offerings, and all their vessels, the basin with its base,
10 The holy vestments for the ministry of Aaron the priest, and for his sons, that they may execute their office in sacred things.
11 The oil of unction, and the incense of spices in the Sanctuary; all things that I have commanded you, they shall make.
12 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
13 <margin>† Wisdom 20:8. Ezekiel 20:12.</margin> Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: † See that you keep my sabbath: because it is a sign between me and you in your generations: that you may know that I am the Lord, who sanctifies you.
14 Keep my sabbath: for it is holy to you: he that shall pollute it, shall die the death: he that shall do any work in it, his soul shall perish from the midst of his people.
15 Six days you shall do work: on the seventh day is the sabbath, the holy rest to the Lord: everyone that shall do work on this day, shall die.
16 Let the children of Israel keep the sabbath, and celebrate it in their generations. It is a perpetual covenant
17 <margin>† Genesis 2:2.</margin> Between me and the children of Israel, and a perpetual sign, † for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and in the seventh he ceased from work.
18 <margin>† Deuteronomy 9:10.</margin> And the Lord, when he had ended such words on mount Sinai, gave to Moses † two stone tablets of testimony, written with the finger of God.

*While Moses is absent, the people cast and worship a golden calf; because the calf was worshipped, Moses prays to God; descending from the mountain, he breaks the tablets, burns the calf, and having rebuked Aaron, commands the idolaters to be killed, and obtains pardon for the rest having ascended the mountain again.*

3 And the people did what he had commanded, bringing the earrings to Aaron.
4 <margin>† Psalm 105:19.</margin> † And when he had received them, he formed them by founders' work, and made of them a molten calf, and they said: These are your gods, O Israel, that have brought you out of the land of Egypt.

6 <margin>† 1 Corinthians 10:7.</margin> And rising in the morning, they offered holocausts, and peace offerings, and † the people sat down to eat, and drink, and they rose up to play.

20 And laying hold of the calf which they had made, he burnt it, and ground it even to powder, which he scattered into the water, and gave it to the children of Israel to drink.
21 And he said to Aaron: What has this people done to you, that you should bring upon them a most great sin?

24 And I said to them: Which of you has gold? They took it and gave it to me: and I cast it into the fire, and this calf came forth.
25 Moses therefore seeing that the people were naked <note>the text suggests they were stripped of their spiritual protection and dignity, or perhaps literally stripped of the ornaments used to make the idol</note>, (for Aaron had stripped them because of the shame of their filth, and had set them naked among their enemies)

31 And returning to the Lord, he said: I beseech you, this people has sinned a most great sin, and they have made for themselves gods of gold: either forgive them this trespass,

34 But go, and lead this people where I have spoken to you: my angel shall go before you. And I, in the day of revenge, will visit this sin of theirs also.
35 The Lord therefore struck the people for the guilt of the calf, which Aaron had made.

### CHAPTER XXXVII.

*The ark is formed, the mercy seat, the Cherubim, the table, the lampstand, the lamp, and the altar of incense, for which the incense is composed.*

1 And <term>Bezalel<note>original: "Beseleel"; the chief artisan of the Tabernacle, filled with the Spirit of God for craftsmanship.</note></term> also made the ark of acacia wood, having two and a half cubits in length, and a cubit and a half in width; the height was also one cubit and a half: and he clothed it with the purest gold inside and out.
2 And he made for it a gold crown around it,
3 Casting four gold rings for its four corners: two rings on one side, and two on the other.
4 He also made poles of acacia wood, which he clothed with gold,
5 And which he put into the rings that were on the sides of the ark to carry it.
6 He also made the <term>Mercy Seat<note>original: "propitiatorium"; also called the "oracle," this was the golden lid of the Ark where God's presence was said to dwell.</note></term>, of the purest gold, two cubits and a half in length, and a cubit and a half in width.
7 Also two Cherubim of beaten gold, which he placed on both sides of the Mercy Seat:
8 One Cherub on the top of one side, and the other Cherub on the top of the other side: two Cherubim on each of the tops of the Mercy Seat,
9 Spreading their wings, and covering the Mercy Seat, and looking toward each other and toward it.
10 He also made the table of acacia wood in length two cubits, and in width one cubit, which had in height a cubit and a half.
11 And he surrounded it with the purest gold, and he made for it a golden lip around it,
12 And for the lip itself a polished gold crown of four fingers, and above that, another gold crown.
13 He also cast four gold circles, which he placed in the four corners at each foot of the table
14 Against the crown: and he put the poles into them, so that the table could be carried.
15 These poles he also made of acacia wood, and he surrounded them with gold.

# THE BOOK OF LEVITICUS,
## IN HEBREW: *VAYIKRA*. <note>original: "Vaicra"; meaning "And He called," the opening word of the book in Hebrew.</note>
### CHAPTER I.

-> *The various rites and methods of offering herds, flocks, and birds as burnt offerings.* <-

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'V' containing a scene of sacrifice with figures around a flaming altar.</image-desc>
1 And the Lord called Moses, and spoke to him from the tabernacle of the testimony, saying:
2 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: The man among you who offers a sacrifice to the Lord from the livestock—that is, offering victims from the cattle and the sheep—
<margin>† Exodus 29:10.</margin>
3 † If his offering be a burnt offering from the herd, he shall offer a male without blemish at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, to make himself acceptable to the Lord.
4 And he shall put his hand upon the head of the victim, and it shall be acceptable, and shall serve for his atonement.
5 And he shall immolate the calf before the Lord, and the priests, the sons of Aaron, shall offer its blood, pouring it around the altar which is before the door of the tabernacle.
6 And having flayed the skin of the victim, they shall cut the limbs into pieces.
7 And they shall put fire upon the altar, having first piled the wood:
8 And they shall arrange the limbs that are cut off above, namely the head, and all things that adhere to the liver.

<column-break/>

9 Having washed the intestines and the feet with water, the priest shall burn them upon the altar as a burnt offering and a sweet odor to the Lord.
10 But if the offering is from the flocks, a burnt offering of sheep or goats, he shall offer a male without blemish.
11 And he shall immolate it at the side of the altar that faces the north, before the Lord; and the sons of Aaron shall pour its blood around the altar.
12 And they shall divide the limbs, the head, and all that adhere to the liver, and shall place them upon the wood, under which the fire is to be put.
13 But the intestines and the feet they shall wash with water. And the priest shall burn all the offered parts upon the altar, as a burnt offering and a most sweet odor to the Lord.
14 But if the offering to the Lord be a burnt offering of birds, of turtledoves or young pigeons,
15 The priest shall offer it at the altar: and having twisted the head back to the neck, and having broken the place of the wound, he shall make the blood run down upon the edge of the altar.
16 But the crop of the throat and the feathers he shall cast near the altar toward the east, in the place where the ashes are usually poured out.
17 And he shall break its wings, and shall not cut it, nor divide it with a blade, and he shall burn it upon the altar, with fire placed under the wood. It is a burnt offering and an oblation of a most sweet odor to the Lord.

# THE BOOK OF LEVITICUS.

## CHAPTER II.

*The ritual for the offering of sacrifices: fine flour sprinkled with oil, frankincense, loaves, wafers, and firstfruits; with salt added to all, but never leaven or honey.*

1 When a person <note>original: "anima", literally "soul"; used here to mean any individual.</note> offers a sacrifice of an offering to the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour: and he shall pour oil upon it, and add frankincense,
2 And he shall bring it to the sons of Aaron the priests: one of whom shall take a handful of the fine flour and oil, with all the frankincense, and shall place this <term>memorial portion<note>original: "memoriale"; the part of the offering burned on the altar to represent the whole gift.</note></term> upon the altar as a most sweet aroma to the Lord.
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 7:34.</margin>
3 † What remains of the sacrifice shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is the <term>Most Holy<note>original: "Sanctum sanctorum"; referring here to the portion of the offering that is especially sacred and must be eaten only by priests.</note></term> among the offerings of the Lord.
4 But when you offer a sacrifice baked in an oven: it shall be of fine flour, specifically loaves without leaven, kneaded with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil.
5 If your offering is from a frying pan, made of fine flour sprinkled with oil and without leaven,
6 You shall break it into small pieces, and pour oil over it.
7 But if the sacrifice is from a griddle, the fine flour shall likewise be sprinkled with oil:
8 When you offer this to the Lord, you shall deliver it into the hands of the priest.
9 When he has offered it, he shall take the memorial portion from the sacrifice, and burn it upon the altar as a sweet aroma to the Lord;
10 Whatever is left over shall be for Aaron and his sons, the Most Holy among the offerings of the Lord.
11 Every offering that is offered to the Lord shall be made without leaven, nor shall any leaven or honey be burned in the sacrifice to the Lord.
12 You shall offer only the firstfruits of such things as gifts: but they shall not be placed upon the altar for a sweet aroma.
<margin>† Mark 9:48.</margin>
13 Whatever sacrifice you offer, you shall season with † salt, nor shall you take away the salt of the covenant of your God from your sacrifice. In every offering of yours, you shall offer salt.
14 But if you offer a gift of your firstfruits to the Lord from ears of grain still green, you shall toast them by fire, and crush them in the manner of <term>groats<note>original: "farris"; husked and crushed grain.</note></term>, and thus you shall offer your firstfruits to the Lord,
15 Pouring oil upon it, and adding frankincense, because it is an offering of the Lord.
16 From which the priest shall burn, as a memorial of the gift, a part of the crushed grain and the oil, and all the frankincense.

## CHAPTER III.

*In what manner peace offerings are to be made, namely of oxen, sheep, lambs, and goats; God claims all the fat and blood for Himself, and the eating of them is forbidden.*

1 But if his offering is a <term>peace offering<note>original: "hostia pacificorum"; a sacrifice intended to express or establish a right relationship with God.</note></term>, and he chooses to offer from the oxen, whether male or female, he shall offer them spotless before the Lord.
2 And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his victim, which shall be immolated at the entrance of the tabernacle of the testimony, and the sons of Aaron the priests shall pour the blood around the altar,

<column-break/>

<margin>† Exodus 29:13.</margin>
3 And they shall offer from the peace offering as an offering to the Lord, † the fat that covers the internal organs, and all the fat that is inside:
4 The two kidneys with the fat that covers the flanks, and the <term>caul<note>original: "reticulum"; the fatty membrane or lobe covering the liver.</note></term> of the liver with the little kidneys.
5 And they shall burn them upon the altar as a burnt offering, with wood placed under the fire: as an offering of a most sweet aroma to the Lord.
6 But if his offering for a peace sacrifice is from the sheep, whether he offers a male or a female, they shall be spotless.
7 If he offers a lamb before the Lord,
8 He shall lay his hand upon the head of his victim: which shall be immolated in the vestibule of the tabernacle of the testimony: and the sons of Aaron shall pour its blood around the altar.
9 And they shall offer from the peace sacrifice as a sacrifice to the Lord: the fat and the whole tail
10 With the kidneys, and the fat that covers the belly and all the internal organs, and both little kidneys with the fat that is near the flanks, and the caul of the liver with the little kidneys.
11 And the priest shall burn them upon the altar, as food for the fire and the offering of the Lord.
12 If a goat is his offering, and he offers it to the Lord,
13 He shall lay his hand upon its head: and shall immolate it at the entrance of the tabernacle of the testimony. And the sons of Aaron shall pour its blood around the altar.
14 And they shall take from it, as food for the fire of the Lord, the fat that covers the belly, and that which covers all the internal organs:
15 The two little kidneys with the caul that is over them near the flanks, and the fat of the liver with the little kidneys:
16 And the priest shall burn them upon the altar, as nourishment for the fire and of a most sweet aroma. All the fat shall belong to the Lord
17 By a perpetual law throughout your generations, and in all your dwellings: you shall eat neither blood nor fat at all.

## CHAPTER IV.

*The manner of offering sacrifices for the sins of the priest, the ruler, and the multitude committed through ignorance.*

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Speak to the children of Israel: The soul that sins through ignorance, and does anything against any of the commandments of the Lord which He commanded should not be done:
3 If the priest who is anointed sins, causing the people to transgress, he shall offer for his sin a spotless calf to the Lord:
4 And he shall lead it to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony before the Lord, and shall lay his hand upon its head, and immolate it to the Lord.
5 He shall also take some of the blood of the calf, carrying it into the tabernacle of the testimony.
6 And when he has dipped his finger in the blood, he shall sprinkle it seven times before the Lord toward the veil of the Sanctuary.
7 And he shall put some of the same blood upon the horns of the altar of most grateful incense to the Lord, which is in the tabernacle of the testimony: but all the remaining blood he shall pour at the base of the altar of burnt offerings at the entrance of the tabernacle.

10 Just as it is taken from the calf of the sacrifice of peace offerings: and he shall burn them upon the altar of burnt offerings.
11 But the hide and all the meat, with the head and the feet and the intestines and the dung,
12 And the rest of the body, he shall carry outside the camp to a clean place where the ashes are usually poured out: and he shall burn them upon a pile of wood, which shall be consumed in the place where the ashes are poured.
13 But if the whole multitude of Israel is ignorant, and through lack of knowledge does what is against the commandment of the Lord,
14 And afterward understands its sin, it shall offer a calf for its sin, and shall bring it to the door of the tabernacle.
15 And the elders of the people shall lay their hands upon its head before the Lord. And when the calf is sacrificed in the sight of the Lord,
16 The priest who is anointed shall carry some of its blood into the tabernacle of the testimony <note>Often called the "Tent of Meeting."</note>,
17 Dipping his finger and sprinkling it seven times against the veil.
18 And he shall put some of the same blood on the horns of the altar that is before the Lord in the tabernacle of the testimony: but the rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offerings, which is at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony.
19 And he shall take all its fat and burn it upon the altar:
20 Doing also with this calf as he did before: and the priest praying for them, the Lord will be merciful to them.
21 But the calf itself he shall carry outside the camp, and shall burn it just as the previous calf: because it is for the sin of the multitude.
22 If a prince <note>original: "princeps"; referring to a tribal leader or magistrate.</note> shall sin, and through ignorance do one of many things which is forbidden by the law of the Lord,
23 And afterward understands his sin, he shall offer a sacrifice to the Lord, a male goat from the flock without blemish.
24 And he shall lay his hand upon its head: and when he has sacrificed it in the place where the burnt offering is usually slaughtered before the Lord, because it is for sin,
25 The priest shall dip his finger in the blood of the sacrifice for sin, touching the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pouring the rest at its base.
26 But the fat he shall burn above, just as is usually done in the victims of the peace offerings: and the priest shall pray for him and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
27 But if a person <note>original: "anima", literally "soul."</note> of the people of the land shall sin through ignorance, doing any of those things which are forbidden by the law of the Lord, and commits a fault,
28 And recognizes his sin, he shall offer a female goat without blemish.
29 And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the sacrifice which is for sin, and shall sacrifice it in the place of the burnt offering.
30 And the priest shall take some of the blood with his finger: and touching the horns of the altar of burnt offering, he shall pour the rest at its base.
31 But taking away all the fat, as it is usually taken away from the victims of the peace offerings, he shall burn it upon the altar for a sweet aroma to the Lord: and he shall pray for him, and it shall be forgiven him.

<column-break/>

32 But if he offers a victim for sin from the flocks, namely a sheep without blemish:
33 He shall lay his hand upon its head, and shall sacrifice it in the place where the victims of the burnt offerings are usually slaughtered.
34 And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger; and touching the horns of the altar of burnt offering, he shall pour the rest at its base.
35 Taking away all the fat also, as the fat of the ram which is sacrificed for peace offerings is usually taken: he shall burn it upon the altar as an incense to the Lord: and he shall pray for him and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.

### CHAPTER V.

->*Concerning sacrifices for sins arising from the silence of truth, uncleanness, error, oaths, the abuse of sacred things, and ignorance.*<-

1 If a person <note>original: "anima"</note> sins, and hears the voice of one taking an oath, and is a witness because he either saw it himself or is aware of it: unless he makes it known, he shall bear his iniquity.
2 A person who touches anything unclean, whether it was killed by a beast, or died of itself, or any other creeping thing: and has forgotten his uncleanness, he is guilty and has committed a fault:
3 And if he touches anything of the uncleanness of man, according to all the impurity by which one is usually defiled, and having forgotten it, realizes it afterward, he shall be subject to the fault.
4 A person who swears, and utters with his lips that he would do something either evil or good, and confirms that same thing with an oath and a word, and having forgotten it, afterward understands his fault,
5 Let him perform penance for the sin,
6 And offer from the flocks a lamb or a goat, and the priest shall pray for him and for his sin:
<margin>† Below 12:8; Luke 2:24.</margin>
7 But if he is not able to offer a beast, let him offer two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to the Lord, one for sin, and the other for a burnt offering,
8 And he shall give them to the priest: who, offering the first for sin, shall wring its head back to the feathers <note>original: "pennulas"; referring to the neck area where the wings begin.</note>, so that it stays attached to the neck and is not entirely broken off.
9 And he shall sprinkle some of its blood upon the wall of the altar: but whatever remains, he shall make to drip at its foundation, because it is for sin.
10 But the other he shall burn for a burnt offering, as is usually done: and the priest shall pray for him and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
11 But if his hand is not able to offer two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall offer for his sin the tenth part of an <term>ephah<note>An ancient Hebrew unit of dry volume, roughly equivalent to 22 liters or 3/5 of a bushel.</note></term> of fine flour: he shall not put oil into it, nor place any frankincense upon it, because it is for sin.
12 And he shall deliver it to the priest: who, taking a full handful of it, shall burn it upon the altar as a memorial for him who offered it,
13 Praying for him and making atonement, but the remaining part he himself shall have as a gift.
14 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
15 If a person, transgressing the ceremonies by error, sins in those things which are sanctified to the Lord, he shall offer for his fault a ram without blemish from the flocks, which can be bought for two shekels, according to the weight of the Sanctuary:
16 And he shall restore the loss itself which he caused,

### CHAPTER VI.

*Offering for sin committed with certain knowledge: laws of the burnt offering, the perpetual fire, individual sacrifices and offerings of the priest on the day of his anointing: and generally concerning the victim for sin: and who and when they may eat of these.*

The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 The soul that shall sin, and, despising the Lord, shall deny to his neighbor a deposit which had been committed to his trust, or shall take anything by force, or commit a calumny <note>A false or malicious accusation intended to harm someone's reputation or property.</note>,
3 Or shall find a lost thing, and denying it, shall also forswear himself <note>Commit perjury or swear a false oath.</note>, and do any other of the many things in which men are accustomed to sin,
4 Being convicted of the offense, he shall restore
<margin>Numbers 5:7</margin>
5 All things which he wished to obtain through fraud, in full: and he shall add a fifth part moreover to the owner to whom he had caused the loss.
6 But for his sin he shall offer an unblemished ram from the flock, and shall give it to the priest, according to the estimation and measure of the offense:
7 Who shall pray for him before the Lord, and it shall be forgiven him for every single thing he did in sinning.
8 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
9 Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the burnt offering <note>original: "holocausti"; a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire on the altar.</note>: It shall be burned upon the altar all night until morning: the fire shall be from the same altar.
10 The priest shall be clothed with a tunic and linen breeches: and he shall take the ashes which the devouring fire consumed, and putting them beside the altar,
11 He shall be stripped of his former garments, and being clothed with others, he shall carry them outside the camp, and in a very clean place shall cause them to be consumed even to the embers.
12 And the fire on the altar shall always burn, which the priest shall nourish, putting wood under it every morning, and having laid on the burnt offering, he shall burn the fat of the peace offerings upon it.
13 This is the perpetual fire, which shall never fail on the altar.
14 This is the law of the sacrifice and of the libations <note>Liquid offerings, usually wine or oil.</note>, which the sons of Aaron shall offer before the Lord, and before the altar.
15 The priest shall take a handful of the fine flour, which is sprinkled with oil, and all the frankincense, which is put upon the flour: and he shall burn it on the altar, as a memorial of a most sweet odor to the Lord:
16 But the remaining part of the flour Aaron shall eat with his sons, without leaven: and he shall eat it in the holy place of the court of the tabernacle.
17 But it shall not be leavened for this reason, because part of it is offered for the incense of the Lord. It shall be the Ho-

<column-break/>

-ly of holies <note>original: "Sanctum sanctorum"; designating the highest degree of ritual purity and sacredness.</note>, just as for sin and for trespass.
18 Only the males of the lineage of Aaron shall eat it. It shall be a lawful and everlasting ordinance in your generations concerning the sacrifices of the Lord: everyone who touches them shall be sanctified.
19 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
20 This is the offering of Aaron, and of his sons, which they ought to offer to the Lord on the day of their anointing. They shall offer the tenth part of an ephah <note>A dry measure roughly equivalent to 22 liters.</note> of fine flour in an everlasting sacrifice: half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening:
21 Which shall be fried in a pan sprinkled with oil. But the priest who succeeds his father by right shall offer it warm for a most sweet odor to the Lord,
22 And it shall be wholly burned on the altar.
23 For every sacrifice of the priests shall be consumed with fire, nor shall anyone eat of it.
24 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
25 Speak to Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the victim <note>original: "hostiæ"; the sacrificial animal.</note> for sin: In the place where the burnt offering is offered, it shall be sacrificed before the Lord. It is the Holy of holies.
26 The priest who offers it shall eat it in a holy place, in the court of the tabernacle.
27 Whatever touches its flesh shall be sanctified. If a garment is sprinkled with its blood, it shall be washed in a holy place.
28 But the earthen vessel in which it was cooked shall be broken: but if the vessel is of bronze, it shall be scoured and washed with water.
29 Every male of the priestly race shall eat of its flesh, because it is the Holy of holies.
<margin>† Above 4:5. Hebrews 13:11.</margin>
30 For the victim which is slain for sin, whose blood is carried into the tabernacle of the testimony for atonement in the Sanctuary, shall not be eaten, but shall be burned with fire.

### CHAPTER VII.

*The rite of offering the victim for trespass, and the victim and sacrifices of peace offerings: fat and blood are forbidden to be eaten altogether.*

This also is the law of the victim for trespass <note>Also known as the guilt offering.</note>: it is the Holy of holies:
2 Therefore where the burnt offering is sacrificed, the victim for trespass shall also be slain: its blood shall be poured around the altar.
3 They shall offer from it the tail and the fat that covers the vital organs:
4 The two kidneys, and the fat that is near the flanks, and the membrane of the liver with the kidneys,
5 And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the incense of the Lord for trespass.
6 Every male of the priestly race shall eat these meats in a holy place, because it is the Holy of holies.
7 As the victim is offered for sin, so also for trespass: there shall be one law for both victims: it shall belong to the priest who offered it.
8 The priest who offers the victim of the burnt offering shall have its skin.
9 And every sacrifice of flour that is baked in the oven, and whatever is prepared on the gridiron or in the pan, shall belong to that priest by whom it is offered:
10 Whether they be sprinkled with oil or dry,

**11** This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings <note>original: "hostiæ pacificorum"; these were offerings intended to express or establish a peaceful relationship between the worshiper and God.</note> which is offered to the Lord.
**12** If the offering is for thanksgiving, they shall offer unleavened loaves mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers smeared with oil, and fine flour cooked and mixed with oil:
**13** Also leavened bread, with the sacrifice of thanks which is offered for peace:

**20** The soul that is polluted and eats of the meat of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which has been offered to the Lord, shall perish from his people.

**26** You shall also not take the blood of any animal for food, whether of birds or of cattle.

**31** Who shall burn the fat upon the altar, but the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
**32** The right shoulder also of the peace offerings shall fall to the priest as firstfruits.
**33** He among the sons of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat shall have the right shoulder for his portion.
**34** For I have taken the breast of elevation <note>original: "pectusculum elevationis"; traditionally called the "wave breast."</note> and the shoulder of separation <note>original: "armum separationis"; traditionally called the "heave shoulder."</note> from the children of Israel from their peace offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest, and to his sons, by a perpetual law, from all the people of Israel.
**35** This is the anointing of Aaron and his sons in the ceremonies of the Lord, on the day when Moses offered them to perform the office of the priesthood,

**36** And which the Lord commanded to be given to them by the children of Israel by a perpetual religious observance throughout their generations.
**37** This is the law of the burnt offering, and of the sacrifice for sin and for guilt, and for the consecration and the victims of peace offerings:
**38** Which the Lord established for Moses on Mount Sinai, when he commanded the children of Israel to offer their oblations to the Lord in the desert of Sinai.

### C H A P T E R VIII.

->The consecration of Aaron as High Priest, and his sons as Priests: and the anointing of the tabernacle and its furniture by Moses.<-

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

**5** He said: This is the word which the Lord commanded to be done.

**7** He clothed the High Priest with the linen undergarment, girding him with a belt, and dressing him in a blue tunic, and over it he placed the ephod <note>original: "humerale"; a decorative shoulder-vestment worn by the High Priest.</note>,
**8** Which he bound with a girdle and fitted to the breastplate <note>original: "rationali"; a square piece of fabric worn on the chest.</note>, in which were "Doctrine and Truth" <note>original: "Doctrina & Veritas"; referring to the Urim and Thummim, tools for seeking divine guidance.</note>.
**9** He also covered his head with a turban <note>original: "cidari".</note>, and upon it, against the forehead, he placed the golden plate consecrated in holiness, as the Lord had commanded him.
**10** He also took the anointing oil, with which he smeared the tabernacle with all its furniture.
**11** And when he had sprinkled the altar seven times to sanctify it, he anointed it and all its vessels, and he sanctified the basin with its base with oil.

**14** He also offered a calf for sin: and when Aaron and his sons had placed their hands upon its head,
**15** He sacrificed it: taking up the blood and dipping his finger, he touched the horns of the altar all around: after it was purified and sanctified, he poured the rest of the blood at its base.
**16** But the fat that was over the vitals, and the membrane of the liver, and the two little kidneys with their fat, he burned upon the altar:
**17** The calf with its skin, meat, and dung, he burned outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded.
**18** He also offered a ram as a burnt offering: upon the head of which Aaron and his sons had placed their hands;
**19** He sacrificed it, and poured its blood around the altar.
**20** And cutting the ram itself into pieces, he burned its head, and limbs, and fat with fire,
**21** Having first washed the intestines and the feet: and he burned the whole ram together upon the altar, because it was a burnt offering of most sweet odor to the Lord, as he had commanded him.

**6** And Moses said to Aaron, and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar: "Do not uncover your heads, and do not tear your garments, lest you perhaps die, and indignation <note>divine wrath</note> rise up against the whole community. Let your brothers, and the entire house of Israel, bewail the fire which the Lord has kindled:
**7** But you shall not go out from the doors of the tabernacle, otherwise you shall perish: for the oil of holy unction <note>the sacred anointing oil</note> is upon you." And they did all things according to the precept of Moses.
**8** The Lord also spoke to Aaron:
**9** "Wine, and anything that can intoxicate, you and your sons shall not drink when you enter into the tabernacle of the testimony, lest you die: because it is an eternal precept throughout your generations.
**10** This is so that you may have the knowledge to discern between the holy and the profane, between the polluted and the clean:
**11** And that you may teach the children of Israel all my laws which the Lord has spoken to them by the hand of Moses."
**12** And Moses spoke to Aaron, and to his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: "Take the sacrifice <note>original: "sacrificium"; specifically the grain offering</note> that remains from the offering of the Lord, and eat it without leaven beside the altar, because it is the Holy of Holies.
**13** You shall eat it in a holy place: that which is given to you and your sons from the offerings of the Lord, just as it was commanded me.
**14** Also the breast which was offered, and the shoulder which was set apart, you and your sons and your daughters with you shall eat in a most clean place: for these parts are reserved for you and your children from the peace offerings <note>original: "hostiis salutaribus"; sacrifices intended to express gratitude or fellowship</note> of the children of Israel:
**15** Because they have elevated the shoulder and the breast, and the fat which is burned on the altar, before the Lord; and they belong to you and your sons by a perpetual law, as the Lord has commanded."
<margin>† 2 Maccabees 2:11</margin> **16** † Meanwhile, when Moses looked for the goat which had been offered for sin, he found it had been burned: and being angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the surviving sons of Aaron, he said:
**17** "Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place, which is the Holy of Holies, and was given to you so that you might bear the iniquity of the multitude, and pray for them in the sight of the Lord,
**18** Especially since its blood was not carried into the inner sanctuary? You ought to have eaten it in the Sanctuary, as was commanded me."
**19** Aaron responded: "Behold, today the victim for sin and the burnt offering were offered before the Lord: but this thing has happened to me as you see. How could I eat it, or please the Lord in these ceremonies, with a mourning mind?"
**20** When Moses had heard this, he was satisfied with the explanation.

# CHAPTER XI

->The separation of clean animals from the unclean, and their use, so that the children of Israel may be holy, even as the Lord is.<-

**1** And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
<margin>† Deuteronomy 14:4</margin> **2** "Say to the children of Israel: † These are the animals which you ought to eat among all the living creatures of the earth:
**3** Every animal that has a divided hoof and chews the cud <note>original: "ruminat"; the process of re-chewing partially digested food</note> among the cattle, you shall eat.
**4** But whatever chews the cud, and has a hoof but does not divide it, such as the camel and others, you shall not eat, but shall count it among the unclean.
**5** The rock badger <note>original: "choerogryllus"; likely referring to the hyrax</note>, which chews the cud but does not divide the hoof, is unclean.
**6** Also the hare: for it also chews the cud, but does not divide the hoof.
<margin>† 2 Maccabees 6:18</margin> **7** † And the pig: which, although it divides the hoof, does not chew the cud;
**8** You shall not eat the flesh of these, nor touch their carcasses, because they are unclean to you.
**9** These are the things that are produced in the waters, and which it is lawful to eat. All that has fins and scales, whether in the sea or in the rivers and ponds, you shall eat.
**10** But whatever has not fins and scales, among those things that move and live in the waters, shall be an abomination to you
**11** And shall be held in execration: you shall not eat their flesh, and you shall avoid their carcasses.
**12** All things in the waters that do not have fins and scales shall be polluted.
**13** These are the birds you shall not eat, and which are to be avoided by you: the eagle, and the griffin vulture <note>original: "gryphem"</note>, and the osprey,
**14** And the kite, and the vulture according to its kind,
**15** And every kind of raven in its likeness,
**16** The ostrich, and the night-owl, and the gull, and the hawk according to its kind:
**17** The screech-owl, and the cormorant, and the ibis,
**18** And the swan, and the pelican, and the purple gallinule <note>original: "porphyrionem"; a type of water bird</note>,
**19** The heron, and the plover <note>original: "charadrion"</note> according to its kind, the hoopoe also, and the bat.
**20** Every winged creature that walks upon four feet shall be an abomination to you.
**21** But whatever walks upon four feet, yet has longer hind legs by which it leaps upon the earth,
**22** You ought to eat: such as the migratory locust <note>original: "bruchus"</note> in its kind, and the bald locust, and the beetle <note>original: "ophiomachus"; likely another type of leaping insect</note>, and the grasshopper, each according to its kind.
**23** But whatever other winged creature has only four feet shall be detestable to you:
**24** And whoever touches their carcasses shall be polluted, and shall be unclean until evening:
**25** And if it be necessary for a man to carry any of these dead things, he shall wash his clothes, and shall be unclean until the sun sets.
**26** Every animal which has a hoof but does not divide it, nor chews the cud, shall be unclean: and whoever touches it shall be contaminated.
**27** That which walks upon paws <note>original: "manus"; literally "hands," referring to animals with pads/paws</note>, among all ani-

**28** And he who carries such carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening: because all these things are unclean to you.
**29** These also shall be counted among the polluted of those things that move upon the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the crocodile, each according to its kind,
**30** The shrew-mouse <note>original: "Mygale"</note>, the chameleon, the spotted lizard, the lizard, and the mole:
**31** All these are unclean. Whoever touches their carcasses shall be unclean until the evening:
**32** And anything upon which any of their carcasses falls shall be polluted, whether it be a wooden vessel or a garment, or skins or hair-cloth; and whatever work is done with them, they shall be dipped in water and shall be polluted until the evening, and so afterwards they shall be cleansed.
**33** But a clay vessel into which any of these falls shall be polluted, and therefore must be broken.
**34** All food which you eat, if water has been poured upon it, shall be unclean; and every liquid that is drunk from any vessel shall be unclean.
**35** And whatever of such carcasses falls upon it shall be unclean: whether it be ovens or <term>cooking pots</term> <note>original: "chytropedes"; likely a three-legged cooking stand</note>, they shall be destroyed and shall be unclean.
**36** But fountains and cisterns, and every collection of waters, shall be clean. He who touches their carcass shall be polluted.
**37** If it falls upon seed, it shall not pollute it.
**38** But if anyone pours water upon the seed, and it is afterwards touched by the carcasses, it shall be immediately polluted.
**39** If an animal dies which it is lawful for you to eat, he who touches its carcass shall be unclean until the evening:
**40** And he who eats anything from it, or carries it, shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening.
**41** Everything that crawls upon the earth shall be abominable, nor shall it be taken for food.
**42** Whatever goes upon its breast on four feet, and has many feet, or is drawn along the ground, you shall not eat, because it is abominable.
**43** Do not contaminate your souls, nor touch any of these things, lest you be unclean.
<margin>† 1 Peter 1:16</margin>
**44** For I am the Lord your God: be holy, because I am holy. Do not pollute your souls with any creeping thing that moves upon the earth.
**45** For I am the Lord, who led you out of the land of Egypt, that I might be your God. You shall be holy, because I am holy.
**46** This is the law of the animals and the birds, and of every living soul that moves in the water and crawls on the earth,
**47** That you may know the differences between the clean and the unclean, and know what you ought to eat and what you ought to reject.

### CHAPTER XII.

-> The uncleanness of a woman in childbirth, and her cleansing with an offering. <-

And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

<column-break/>

**2** Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them:
<margin>† Luke 2:22</margin>
If a woman, having received seed, gives birth to a male, she shall be unclean for seven days, according to the days of her menstrual separation.
<margin>† Luke 2:21, John 7:22</margin>
**3** And on the eighth day the infant shall be circumcised:
**4** But she shall remain for thirty-three days in the blood of her purification. She shall not touch anything holy, nor enter into the Sanctuary, until the days of her purification are fulfilled.
**5** But if she gives birth to a female, she shall be unclean for two weeks, according to the custom of her menstrual flow, and she shall remain for sixty-six days in the blood of her purification.
**6** And when the days of her purification are fulfilled, for a son or for a daughter, she shall bring a lamb of one year for a <term>holocaust</term> <note>original: "holocaustum"; a burnt offering completely consumed by fire</note>, and a young pigeon or a turtle-dove for sin, to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and shall deliver them to the priest,
**7** Who shall offer them before the Lord, and shall pray for her, and so she shall be cleansed from the flow of her blood: this is the law for her who gives birth to a male or a female.
<margin>† Above 5:7, 11; Luke 2:24</margin>
**8** But if her hand cannot find <note>meaning: if she cannot afford</note> or she is not able to offer a lamb, she shall take two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, one for a holocaust and the other for sin: and the priest shall pray for her, and so she shall be cleansed.

### CHAPTER XIII.

-> The law and the diagnosis of leprosy entrusted to the Priests, in man and in garment, and what is commanded for the leper. <-

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
**2** A man in whose skin and flesh there arises a different color or a pustule, or something as it were shining—that is, a <term>plague of leprosy</term> <note>original: "plaga leprae"; in the Bible, this term covers various skin conditions, not just modern leprosy</note>—shall be brought to Aaron the priest, or to any one of his sons.
**3** And when he sees the leprosy in the skin, and the hair turned to a white color, and the appearance of the leprosy itself lower than the rest of the skin and flesh; it is a plague of leprosy, and at his judgment he shall be separated.
**4** But if there is a shining whiteness in the skin, and not lower than the rest of the flesh, and the hair is of its former color, the priest shall shut him up for seven days.
**5** And he shall consider him on the seventh day: and if indeed the leprosy has not grown further, nor passed into its former boundaries, he shall shut him up again for another seven days.
**6** And on the seventh day he shall look again: if the leprosy is darker and has not grown in the skin, he shall cleanse him, because it is a scab: and the man shall wash his clothes and be clean.
**7** But if, after he has been seen by the priest and restored to cleanliness, the leprosy grows again, he shall be brought back to him,
**8** And he shall be condemned of uncleanness.
**9** If there is a plague of leprosy in a man, he shall be brought to the priest,
**10** And he shall see him. And when there is a white color in the skin, and it has changed the appearance of the hair, and the living flesh itself appears:
**11** It shall be judged a very old leprosy, and one grown into the skin. Therefore the priest shall declare him contaminated, and shall not shut him up, because it is an evident uncleanness.
**12** But if the leprosy breaks out flourishing and running about in the skin, and covers all the skin from the head to the feet, whatever falls under the sight of the eyes,

**13** The priest shall consider him and judge that the leprosy is most clean: because it has all turned into whiteness, and therefore the man shall be clean.

**15** Then by the judgment of the priest he shall be polluted and shall be counted among the unclean: for if raw flesh is sprinkled with leprosy, it is unclean.
**16** But if it shall be turned again into whiteness and cover the whole man,
**17** The priest shall consider him and decree that he is clean.
**18** Moreover, the flesh and skin in which an ulcer was born and healed,
**19** And in the place of the ulcer a white scar appears, or a reddish one, the man shall be brought to the priest:
**20** Who, when he sees the place of the leprosy lower than the rest of the flesh, and the hair turned into whiteness, shall contaminate him: for the plague of leprosy has arisen in the ulcer.
**21** But if the hair is of its former color, and the scar is somewhat obscure, and is not lower than the neighboring flesh, he shall shut him up for seven days.
**22** And if indeed it grows, he shall adjudge him to have leprosy.
**23** But if it stays in its place, it is the scar of an ulcer, and the man shall be clean.
**24** Moreover, the flesh and skin which fire has burned, and being healed has a white or red scar,
**25** The priest shall consider it, and behold, it is turned into whiteness, and its place is lower than the rest of the skin: he shall contaminate him, because the plague of leprosy has arisen in the scar.
**26** But if the color of the hair has not been changed, nor the plague lower than the rest of the flesh, and the appearance of the leprosy itself is somewhat obscure, he shall shut him up for seven days,
**27** And on the seventh day he shall contemplate it: if the leprosy has grown in the skin, he shall contaminate him.
**28** But if the whiteness stays in its place, not being bright enough, it is the plague of a burn, and therefore he shall be cleansed, because it is the scar of a burning.
**29** A man, or woman, in whose head or beard leprosy has germinated, the priest shall see them.
**30** And if indeed the place is lower than the rest of the flesh, and the hair is yellow and thinner than usual; he shall contaminate them, because it is the leprosy of the head and beard.
**31** But if he sees the place of the spot equal to the neighboring flesh, and the hair black: he shall shut him up for seven days,
**32** And on the seventh day he shall look at it. If the spot has not grown, and the hair is of its own color, and the place of the plague is equal to the rest of the flesh:
**33** The man shall be shaved, except for the place of the spot, and shall be shut up for another seven days.
**34** If on the seventh day the plague is seen to have stayed in its place, and not lower than the rest of the flesh, he shall cleanse him, and his clothes being washed, he shall be clean.
**35** But if after the cleansing the spot grows again in the skin,
**36** He shall no longer seek whether the hair is changed into a yellow color, because he is openly unclean.
**37** Furthermore, if the spot stays, and the hairs are black, let him know that the man is healed, and let him confidently pronounce him clean.
**38** A man, or woman, in whose skin whiteness appears,
**39** The priest shall look at them; if he catches

<column-break/>

a somewhat obscure whiteness shining in the skin, let him know that it is not leprosy, but a spot of white color, and the man is clean.
**40** The man from whose head the hairs fall, is bald and clean:
**41** And if the hairs fall from his forehead, he is forehead-bald <note>original: "recalvaster"; a specific term for receding hair at the front</note> and clean.
**42** But if in the baldness or in the forehead-baldness a white or reddish color arises,
**43** And the priest sees this, he shall condemn him without doubt of the leprosy which has arisen in the baldness.
**44** Whoever therefore is spotted with leprosy, and is separated at the judgment of the priest,
**45** Shall have his clothes unstitched, his head bare, his mouth covered with a cloth, and he shall cry out that he is contaminated and filthy.
**46** All the time that he is a leper and unclean, he shall dwell alone outside the camp.
**47** A woolen or linen garment that has leprosy in it,
**48** In the <term>warp or the woof</term> <note>original: "stamine atque subtegmine"; the vertical and horizontal threads of a fabric</note>, or certainly a skin, or whatever is made of skin,
**49** If it is infected with a white or reddish spot, it shall be accounted leprosy and shall be shown to the priest.
**50** Who, having considered it, shall shut it up for seven days:
**51** And looking at it again on the seventh day, if he finds it has grown, it is a persistent leprosy: he shall judge the garment polluted, and everything in which it is found.
**52** And therefore it shall be burned with flames.
**53** But if he sees it has not grown,
**54** He shall command, and they shall wash that in which the leprosy is, and he shall shut it up for another seven days.
**55** And when he sees that the former appearance has not returned, nor yet that the leprosy has grown, he shall judge it unclean and burn it with fire, because the leprosy is spread in the surface of the garment or throughout the whole.
**56** But if the place of the leprosy is darker after the garment is washed, he shall tear it off and divide it from the solid part.
**57** But if it appears further in those places which before were unspotted, it is a flying and wandering leprosy: it must be burned with fire.
**58** If it ceases, he shall wash with water those things which are pure a second time, and they shall be clean.
**59** This is the law of the leprosy of a woolen and linen garment, of the warp and the woof, and of all leather furniture, how it ought to be cleansed or contaminated.

### C H A P T E R XIV.

->*Sacrifices to be offered for the expiation of a man, a house, and a garment, the leprosy now being cured: the method of investigating, curing, and purifying the leprosy of houses.*<-

<margin>† Matthew 8:4</margin>
**2** This is the rite of a leper, when he is to be cleansed: † He shall be brought to the priest:
**3** Who, going out of the camp, when he finds that the leprosy is cleansed,
<margin>† Mark 1:44; Luke 5:14</margin>
**4** † Shall command him who is purified to offer for himself two live sparrows <note>original: "passeres"; can refer generally to small birds</note> which it is lawful to eat, and cedar wood, and <term>scarlet</term> <note>original: "vermiculum"; literally "little worm," referring to the kermes insect used to make red dye</note>, and hyssop.
**5** And he shall command one of the sparrows to be immolated in an earthen vessel over living waters:
**6** But the other being alive, with the cedar wood and the scarlet and the hyssop, he shall dip in the blood of the immolated sparrow.

**7** With this, he shall sprinkle the person who is to be cleansed seven times, so that he may be rightly purified; then he shall let the living bird <note>original: "passerem"; while often translated as "sparrow," it refers generally to any small bird used in the ritual</note> fly free into the field.

**13** He shall sacrifice the lamb in the place where the sin offering and the burnt offering <note>original: "holocaustum"; a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire</note> are usually sacrificed, that is, in the holy place. For just as the sin offering belongs to the priest, so also does the guilt offering: it is the Holy of Holies <note>original: "Sancta sanctorum"; meaning most holy or set apart</note>.

**30** And he shall offer a turtledove or a young pigeon,

**33** And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
**34** When you have entered the land of Canaan, which I will give to you as a possession, if there is a plague of leprosy in a house,
**35** The owner of the house shall go and tell the priest, saying: "It seems to me there is something like a plague of leprosy in my house."
**36** And the priest shall command that they carry everything out of the house before he enters it to see if it is leprous, so that everything in the house does not become unclean. Afterward, he shall enter to inspect the leprosy of the house.
**37** And when he sees in its walls something like small pits, deformed with paleness or redness, and lower than the rest of the surface,
**38** He shall go out the door of the house and immediately shut it for seven days.
**39** Returning on the seventh day, he shall inspect it; if he finds that the leprosy has grown,
**40** He shall command the stones in which the leprosy is to be pulled out and thrown outside the city into an unclean place.
**41** The house itself shall be scraped on the inside all around, and the dust of the scrapings shall be scattered outside the city in an unclean place.
**42** Other stones shall be put back in place of those that were removed, and the house shall be plastered with other mortar.
**43** But if, after the stones were pulled out and the dust scraped away and other earth smeared on,
**44** The priest enters and sees that the leprosy has returned and the walls are covered with spots, it is a persistent leprosy, and the house is unclean.
**45** They shall immediately destroy it, and throw its stones and wood and all the dust outside the town into an unclean place.
**46** Whoever enters the house while it is closed shall be unclean until evening.
**47** And he who sleeps in it or eats anything there shall wash his clothes.
**48** But if the priest, entering, sees that the leprosy has not grown in the house after it was plastered again, he shall purify it, as health has been restored.
**49** And for its purification, he shall take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet thread <note>original: "vermiculum"; literally 'little worm,' referring to the kermes insect used to make deep red or scarlet dye</note>, and hyssop.
**50** And having sacrificed one bird in an earthen vessel over living waters <term>living waters: naturally flowing water, such as from a spring or stream, as opposed to stagnant water</term>,
**51** He shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet, and the living bird, and dip them all in the blood of the sacrificed bird and in the living waters, and sprinkle the house seven times.
**52** And he shall purify it with the blood of the bird, the living waters, the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet.
**53** When he has let the bird fly away freely into the field, he shall pray for the house, and it shall be rightly cleansed.
**54** This is the law for every kind of leprosy and stroke,
**55** For leprosy of clothes and houses,
**56** For a scar and for erupting pimples, for a shining spot, and for various forms where colors change,
**57** So that it may be known at what time a thing is clean or unclean.

Chapter 16 begins the instructions for the Day of Atonement, the most solemn day in the Hebrew calendar.</meta>

### THE BOOK OF LEVITICUS

### C H A P T E R XV.

->*The atonement and purification for men with discharges, those who have slept together, menstruating women, and those with hemorrhages.*<-

And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
2 Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: Any man who suffers from a discharge from his flesh <note>original: "fluxum feminis"; referring here to a genital discharge, often associated with illness</note> shall be unclean.
3 and he shall be judged to be subject to this vice when a foul humor clings to his flesh and thickens at every moment.
4 Every bed on which he sleeps shall be unclean, and wherever he sits.
5 If any man touches his bed, he shall wash his clothes; and being washed himself with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
6 If he sits where that man had sat, he also shall wash his clothes; and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
7 He who touches his flesh shall wash his clothes; and being washed himself with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
8 If such a man spits upon one who is clean, that person shall wash his clothes; and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
9 The saddle <note>original: "Sagma"; the pack-saddle or seat used for riding</note> upon which he sits shall be unclean.
10 And whatever has been under him who suffers from the discharge shall be polluted until the evening. He who carries any of these things shall wash his clothes; and being washed himself with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
11 Everyone whom such a man touches without having washed his hands first shall wash his clothes; and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
12 An earthen vessel that he touches shall be broken; but a wooden vessel shall be washed with water.
13 If he who suffers this condition is healed, he shall count seven days for his purification; and having washed his clothes and his entire body in living waters <term>living waters: fresh, running water from a spring or stream, rather than stagnant water from a cistern</term>, he shall be clean.
14 And on the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and he shall come before the Lord to the door of the tabernacle of testimony, and shall give them to the priest.
15 The priest shall offer one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering; and he shall pray for him before the Lord, so that he may be cleansed of his discharge.
16 A man from whom the seed of intercourse goes out <note>original: "semen coitus"</note> shall wash his entire body with water; and he shall be unclean until the evening.
17 The garment and the skin he wears he shall wash with water, and it shall be unclean until the evening.
18 The woman with whom he has slept shall be washed with water, and shall be unclean until the evening.
19 A woman who, at the return of the month, suffers a flow of blood, shall be set apart for seven days.
20 Everyone who touches her shall be unclean until the evening.
21 And everything upon which she sleeps or sits during the days of her separation shall be polluted.
22 He who touches her bed shall wash his clothes; and being washed himself with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
23 Whoever touches any vessel upon which she sits shall wash his clothes; and being washed himself with water, he shall be polluted until the evening.
24 If a man sleeps with her during the time of her menstrual blood, he shall be unclean for seven days; and every bed on which he sleeps shall be polluted.

<column-break/>

25 A woman who suffers for many days from a flow of blood not at the time of her menstruation, or who does not cease to bleed after her menstruation, as long as she is subject to this condition, she shall be unclean just as if she were in her menstrual time.
26 Every bed on which she sleeps and every vessel on which she sits shall be polluted.
27 Whoever touches them shall wash his clothes; and being washed himself with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.
28 If the blood stops and ceases to flow, she shall count seven days for her purification.
29 And on the eighth day she shall offer for herself to the priest two turtledoves or two young pigeons at the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
30 The priest shall offer one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering, and he shall pray for her before the Lord and for the flow of her uncleanness.
31 Thus you shall teach the children of Israel to beware of uncleanness, so that they do not die in their filth when they have polluted my tabernacle <note>original: "tabernaculum"; the portable dwelling place of God’s presence</note> which is among them.
32 This is the law of him who suffers a discharge and is polluted by intercourse,
33 and of her who is set apart at the times of her menstruation, or who flows with blood continually, and of the man who sleeps with her.

### C H A P T E R XVI.

->*When and how the priest should enter the Sanctuary, and how he must purify it together with the tabernacle and the altar, drive away the scapegoat, and celebrate the feast of atonements.*<-

And the Lord spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they were killed while offering strange fire <note>original: "ignem alienum"; unauthorized or profane fire offered against God's command</note>:
<margin>
† Above 10:1-2.
† Exodus 30:10. Hebrews 9:7.
</margin>
2 And he commanded him, saying: Speak to Aaron your brother, † that he should not enter at all times into the Sanctuary which is within the veil before the mercy seat <term>mercy seat: the golden cover of the Ark of the Covenant, where God’s presence was said to dwell</term> with which the ark is covered, so that he may not die (for I will appear in a cloud over the oracle)
3 Unless he has first done these things: He shall offer a calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
4 He shall be clothed in a linen tunic; he shall hide his private parts with linen undergarments; he shall be girded with a linen sash, and he shall place a linen turban upon his head. For these are the holy garments, all of which he shall put on after he has been washed.
5 And he shall receive from the entire multitude of the children of Israel two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
6 And when he has offered the calf and prayed for himself and for his house,
7 He shall make the two goats stand before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
8 And casting lots upon both, one for the Lord and the other for the scapegoat <note>original: "capro emissario"; literally the "emissary goat" or "goat that is sent away"</note>:
9 The one whose lot falls to the Lord, he shall offer for a sin offering.
10 But the one whose lot is for the scapegoat, he shall present alive before the Lord, that he may pour out prayers over it and send it out into the wilderness.
11 After these things are duly celebrated, he shall offer the calf, and praying for himself and for his house, he shall sacrifice it.
12 And taking the censer, which he has filled from the coals of the altar, and taking in his hand the finely ground incense, he shall enter within the veil into the holy place.

### CHAPTER XVII.

-> *The Hebrews are commanded to sacrifice to God alone, not to demons, and nowhere except at the door of the tabernacle; and to abstain from eating blood and animals found dead.* <-

1 AND the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Speak to Aaron and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, saying to them: This is the word which the Lord has commanded, saying:
3 Any man of the house of Israel, if he kills an ox or a sheep or a goat, inside the camp or outside the camp,
4 and does not offer it to the Lord at the door of the tabernacle, he shall be guilty of blood: as if he had shed blood, so shall he perish from the midst of his people.
5 Therefore the children of Israel ought to bring to the priest their sacrifices, which they kill in the field, so that they may be sanctified to the Lord before the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and they shall sacrifice them as peace offerings to the Lord.
6 And the priest shall pour the blood upon the altar of the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and shall burn the fat as a sweet odor to the Lord.
7 And they shall no longer sacrifice their victims to demons <note>original: "daemonibus"; likely referring to desert spirits or goat-idols</note>, with whom they have committed fornication. This shall be a perpetual statute for them and their descendants.
8 And you shall say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who travel among you, who offers a burnt offering or a victim,
9 and does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony to be offered to the Lord, shall perish from his people.
10 Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who travel among them, if he eats blood, I will set my face against that soul, and I will destroy him from his people,
11 because the life <note>original: "anima"; literally 'soul' or 'breath of life'</note> of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you, so that upon the altar you may make atonement for your souls with it, and the blood may be for the expiation of the soul.
12 Therefore I said to the children of Israel: No soul among you shall eat blood, nor shall any of the strangers who travel among you.
13 Any man of the children of Israel, or of the strangers who travel among you, if by hunting or fowling he takes a wild beast or a bird which it is lawful to eat, let him pour out its blood and cover it with earth.
<margin>
† Genesis 9:4
Above 7:26
</margin>
14 For the life of all flesh is in the blood: wherefore I said to the children of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, because the life of the flesh is in the blood: and whoever eats it shall perish.
15 The soul that eats an animal that died of itself <note>original: "morticinum"; an animal that died naturally or from disease</note>, or was caught by a beast, whether native or stranger, shall wash his clothes and himself with water, and shall be unclean until evening: and in this way he shall become clean.
16 But if he does not wash his clothes and his body, he shall bear his iniquity.
