## CHAPTER XVIII.

->*The degrees of unlawful marriage, and the avoidance of the practices of the Gentiles and Canaanites regarding various carnal impurities.*<-

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: I am the Lord your God.
3 You shall not act according to the custom of the land of Egypt, in which you lived; and you shall not act according to the manner of the region of Canaan, into which I am about to lead you, nor shall you walk in their ordinances.
4 You shall carry out my judgments, and you shall keep my precepts, and you shall walk in them: I am the Lord your God.
<margin>† Ezekiel 20:11; Romans 10:5; Galatians 3:12.</margin>
5 † Keep my laws and judgments; for if a man does them, he shall live by them. I am the Lord.
6 No man shall approach anyone who is near of his own blood, to reveal her nakedness. <note>original: "revelet turpitudinem"; a biblical idiom for sexual intercourse</note> I am the Lord.
7 You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, nor the nakedness of your mother: she is your mother; you shall not reveal her nakedness.
8 You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife: for it is the nakedness of your father.
9 You shall not reveal the nakedness of your sister, whether she is the daughter of your father or of your mother, whether she was born at home or abroad.
10 You shall not reveal the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter: because it is your own nakedness.
11 You shall not reveal the nakedness of the daughter of your father’s wife, whom she bore to your father, for she is your sister.
12 You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister: because she is the flesh of your father.
13 You shall not reveal the nakedness of your mother’s sister, because she is the flesh of your mother.
14 You shall not reveal the nakedness of your father’s brother, nor shall you approach his wife, who is joined to you by affinity.
15 You shall not reveal the nakedness of your daughter-in-law, because she is your son's wife; you shall not uncover her shame.
16 You shall not reveal the nakedness of your brother’s wife: because it is the nakedness of your brother.
17 You shall not reveal the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son’s daughter, or her daughter’s daughter, to reveal her shame: because they are her flesh, and such a union is incest.
18 You shall not take your wife’s sister as a rival <note>original: "in pellicatum"; referring to taking a second wife who is the sister of the first</note>, nor shall you reveal her nakedness while the first is still living.
19 You shall not approach a woman who is suffering her menstruation, nor shall you reveal her uncleanness.
20 You shall not lie with your neighbor’s wife, nor shall you be defiled by mixing with such a woman.
<margin>† Below 20:2.</margin>
21 † You shall not give any of your seed <note>referring to offspring or children</note> to be consecrated to the idol Moloch <note>a Canaanite god often associated with child sacrifice</note>, nor shall you pollute the name of your God. I am the Lord.
22 You shall not lie with a male as with a female, for it is an abomination.
<margin>† Below 20:16.</margin>
23 † You shall not lie with any beast, nor shall you be defiled with it. † A woman shall not lie down before an animal, nor be joined with it: because it is a heinous crime.
24 Do not be defiled by any of these things, by which all the nations have been contaminated, which I will cast out before your sight,

<column-break/>

25 And with which the land is defiled: whose crimes I will visit, so that it may vomit out its inhabitants.
26 Keep my ordinances and judgments, and do not perform any of these abominations, neither the native-born nor the stranger who sojourns among you.
27 For the inhabitants of the land who were before you did all these execrable things, and defiled it.
28 Beware, therefore, lest it vomit you out in like manner if you do similar things, just as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
29 Every soul that does any of these abominations shall perish from the midst of his people.
30 Keep my commandments. Do not do what those did who were before you, and do not be defiled by them: I am the Lord your God.

## CHAPTER XX.

*Those who offer their offspring to Moloch, who consult magicians or soothsayers, who curse their parents, or who practice various illicit sexual acts are to be punished by death.*

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 You shall say these things to the children of Israel: Any man of the children of Israel, or of the strangers who dwell in Israel, <margin>† Above 18:21.</margin>† if he gives any of his offspring to the idol Moloch, let him die the death: the people of the land shall stone him.
3 And I will set my face against that man: and I will cut him off from the midst of his people, because he has given his offspring to Moloch, and has contaminated my Sanctuary, and polluted my holy name.

<column-break/>

4 But if the people of the land are negligent, and as if valuing my command little, they disregard the man who gave his offspring to Moloch, and refuse to kill him:
5 I will set my face upon that man and upon his kindred, and I will cut him off, and all those who consented with him to commit fornication with Moloch, from the midst of his people.
6 As for the soul that turns aside to magicians and soothsayers, and commits fornication with them, I will set my face against that soul, and I will kill it from the midst of its people.

12 If any man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, let both die, because they have committed a crime: let their blood be upon them.

18 He who copulates with a woman during her menstrual flow and reveals her nakedness, and she herself opens the fountain of her blood, they shall both be killed from the midst of their people.
19 You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister or your father’s sister: he who does this has stripped the shame of his own flesh, they shall both bear their iniquity.
20 He who copulates with the wife of his father's brother or his mother's brother, and reveals the shame of his kin, they shall both bear their sin: they shall die without children.
21 He who takes his brother’s wife does an unlawful thing, he has revealed his brother's nakedness: they shall be without children.
22 Keep my laws and judgments, and do them: lest the land into which you are to enter and dwell vomit you out also.
23 Do not walk in the ordinances of the nations which I am about to expel before you. For they have done all these things, and I have detested them.
24 But I say to you: Possess their land, which I will give to you as an inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey: I am the Lord your God, who has separated you from other peoples.

27 † A man or a woman, in whom there is a pythian <note>original: 'pythonicus', referring to a spirit of divination or a "familiar spirit" often associated with the Oracle of Delphi in later classical contexts</note> or a spirit of divination, shall surely be put to death: they shall overwhelm them with stones: their blood shall be upon them.

### CHAPTER XXI.

->*Concerning which funerals priests may attend, and what kind of wives they may take; those who are unfit for the priesthood: and concerning the daughter of a priest who commits fornication.*<-

1 The Lord also said to Moses: Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them; Let not a priest be defiled by the deaths of his fellow citizens;
2 Except only for his near kinsmen and relatives, that is, for father, and mother, and son, and daughter, and also for a brother,
3 And for a virgin sister who is not married to a husband:
4 But he shall not be defiled even for a leader <note>original: 'principe', meaning a chief or prince</note> of his people.

<margin>† Above 19:27; Ezekiel 44:20.</margin>
5 † They shall not shave their head, nor their beard, nor make incisions in their flesh.
6 They shall be holy to their God, and shall not profane his name: for they offer the incense of the Lord and the bread of their God, and therefore they shall be holy.

<margin>† Above 19:29.</margin>
7 † They shall not take a harlot or a common prostitute as a wife, nor her who has been divorced by her husband: because they are consecrated to their God,
8 And they offer the loaves of proposition <note>original: 'panes propositionis', commonly known as the showbread or bread of the presence</note>. Therefore let them be holy, because I also am holy: the Lord, who sanctifies them.
9 If a priest’s daughter is caught in debauchery and has shamed the name of her father, she shall be burned with flames.
10 The High Priest <note>original: 'Pontifex, id est, sacerdos maximus'</note>, who is the greatest among his brothers, upon whose head the oil of unction has been poured, and whose hands have been consecrated for the priesthood, and who has been clothed in the holy vestments, shall not uncover his head, nor tear his garments:
11 And he shall not go in at all to any dead person: he shall not be defiled even for his father and mother.
12 Nor shall he go out of the holy places, lest he pollute the Sanctuary of the Lord, because the oil of the holy unction of God is upon him: I am the Lord.

<margin>† Ezekiel 44:22.</margin>
13 † He shall take a virgin as his wife:
14 But a widow and a divorced woman, or one who is defiled or a harlot, he shall not take, but a young girl of his own people:
15 Lest he mingle the stock of his lineage with the common people of his nation: because I am the Lord who sanctifies him.
16 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
17 Speak to Aaron: Any man of your seed throughout their families who has a blemish shall not offer bread to his God,
18 Nor shall he approach his ministry: if he be blind, if he be lame, if he has a small, or large, or crooked nose,
19 If he has a broken foot or hand,
20 If he is a hunchback, if he is bleary-eyed <note>original: 'lippus'</note>, if he has a white spot in his eye, if he has a chronic scab, or a dry itch <note>original: 'impetiginem', a skin disease like ringworm</note> on his body, or a hernia.

<column-break/>

21 Anyone of the seed of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall not approach to offer sacrifices to the Lord, nor bread to his God:
22 Yet he shall eat of the bread which is offered in the Sanctuary;
23 Provided only that he does not enter within the veil, nor approach the altar, because he has a blemish, and he must not pollute my Sanctuary. I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
24 Moses therefore spoke to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all Israel, all things that had been commanded to him.

### CHAPTER XXII.

->*Foreigners and the unclean must abstain from eating sanctified things or sacrifices; the blemishes or defects are described which a victim must lack, and what things should be offered.*<-

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they take care regarding those things which are consecrated by the children of Israel, and that they do not pollute the name of the things sanctified to me, which they themselves offer: I am the Lord.
3 Say to them and to their descendants: Every man of your stock who approaches the things that are consecrated, and which the children of Israel have offered to the Lord, while he is in a state of uncleanness, shall perish before the Lord: I am the Lord.
4 A man of the seed of Aaron who is a leper, or suffering a flow of semen, shall not eat of those things which are sanctified to me until he is healed. He who touches anything unclean by reason of a dead body, or from whom semen goes out as in coitus,
5 And he who touches a creeping thing, or anything unclean, the touch of which is filthy,
6 Shall be unclean until evening, and shall not eat of those things which are sanctified: but when he has washed his flesh with water,
7 And the sun has set, then being cleansed he shall eat of the sanctified things, because it is his food.

<margin>† Exodus 22:31; Above 17:15; Deuteronomy 14:21; Ezekiel 44:31.</margin>
8 † That which dies of itself <note>original: 'morticinum', carrion</note> and that which is caught by a beast they shall not eat, nor be polluted by them: I am the Lord.
9 Let them keep my precepts, so that they do not fall into sin and die in the Sanctuary, when they have polluted it: I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
10 No foreigner <note>original: 'alienigena'</note> shall eat of the sanctified things; a guest of the priest or a hired servant shall not eat of them.
11 But whom the priest has bought, and he who is a servant born in his house <note>original: 'vernaculus'</note>, these shall eat of them.
12 If the daughter of a priest is married to anyone of the people, she shall not eat of those things which are sanctified nor of the firstfruits.
13 But if she becomes a widow, or is divorced, and having no children returns to her father's house, she shall be nourished by her father's food as she was accustomed to when a young girl. No foreigner has the power of eating of them.
14 He who eats of the sanctified things through ignorance shall add a fifth part to that which he ate, and shall give it to the priest in the Sanctuary.
15 And they shall not pollute the sanctified things of the children of Israel, which they offer to the Lord:
16 Lest perhaps they bear the iniquity of their crime when they eat the sanctified things: I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
17 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

18 Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or of the strangers who dwell among you, who offers his oblation, whether paying his vows or offering spontaneously, whatever he offers as a burnt sacrifice <note>original: 'holocaustum', a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire</note> to the Lord,
19 To be accepted for you, it shall be an unblemished male from the oxen, the sheep, or the goats.
20 If it has a blemish, you shall not offer it, nor will it be acceptable.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 15:21; Ecclesiasticus 35:14.</margin>
21 † The man who offers a peace offering <note>original: 'victimam pacificorum'</note> to the Lord, either paying his vows or offering spontaneously, whether of oxen or of sheep, shall offer it unblemished so that it may be acceptable: there shall be no defect in it.
22 If it is blind, or broken, or has a scar, or sores, or scurvy, or mange: you shall not offer these to the Lord, nor shall you burn any of them upon the altar of the Lord.
23 An ox or a sheep with a limb too long or too short <note>original: 'aure & cauda amputatis', literally 'with ear or tail cut off' or deformed</note> you may offer as a voluntary gift, but a vow cannot be paid with them.
24 Any animal that has its testicles bruised, or crushed, or cut and removed, you shall not offer to the Lord; and in your land, you shall not do this at all.
25 You shall not offer the bread of your God from the hand of a foreigner, nor anything else he wishes to give: because they are all corrupted and blemished; you shall not receive them.
26 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
27 When an ox, a sheep, or a goat is born, it shall be under its mother’s udder for seven days; but from the eighth day onward, they may be offered to the Lord.
28 Whether it be a cow or a ewe, they shall not be sacrificed on the same day as their young.
29 If you sacrifice a victim for thanksgiving to the Lord, so that it may be pleasing,
30 You shall eat it on the same day; nothing shall remain until the morning of the next day: I am the Lord.
31 Keep my commandments and do them: I am the Lord.
32 Do not profane my holy name, so that I may be sanctified in the midst of the children of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
33 And who led you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the Lord.

### CHAPTER XXIII.

*The solemnities of the Sabbath, Passover, Firstfruits, Weeks, Harvest, Trumpets, Atonement, and Tabernacles, and by what rites they should be performed.*

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall call holy.
3 Six days you shall work: the seventh day, because it is the rest of the Sabbath, shall be called holy: you shall do no work on it: it is the Sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.
4 These, therefore, are the holy feasts of the Lord, which you ought to celebrate in their seasons.
<margin>Exodus 12:2, 18; Numbers 28:16.</margin>
5 † In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, is the Passover <note>original: 'Phase'</note> of the Lord:
6 And on the fifteenth day of this month is the solemnity of the unleavened bread <note>original: 'azymorum'</note> of the Lord. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
7 The first day shall be most celebrated and holy for you: you shall do no servile work on it:

<column-break/>

8 But you shall offer a sacrifice in fire to the Lord for seven days: the seventh day shall be more celebrated and holier: and you shall do no servile work on it.
9 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
10 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: When you have entered the land which I will give you, and have reaped the harvest, you shall carry sheaves of ears, the firstfruits of your harvest, to the priest.
11 He shall lift up the bundle before the Lord, that it may be acceptable for you, on the day after the Sabbath, and he shall sanctify it.
12 And on the same day that the sheaf is consecrated, an unblemished lamb of one year shall be slaughtered as a burnt offering to the Lord.
13 And the drink offerings shall be offered with it: two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for an incense of the Lord and a most sweet odor: also libations of wine, the fourth part of a hin <note>a Hebrew liquid measure, roughly 1.5 liters</note>.
14 You shall not eat bread, or parched grain, or pulse <note>original: 'pultes', a thick pottage or mash made from grain</note> from the harvest, until the day that you offer of it to your God. It is an everlasting precept throughout your generations and in all your dwellings.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 16:9.</margin>
15 † You shall count, therefore, from the day after the Sabbath on which you offered the sheaf of firstfruits, seven full weeks,
16 Until the day after the completion of the seventh week, that is, fifty days: and so you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord
17 From all your dwellings: two loaves of firstfruits made of two tenths of leavened fine flour, which you shall bake as firstfruits for the Lord.
18 And you shall offer with the loaves seven unblemished lambs of one year, and one calf from the herd, and two rams; and they shall be for a burnt offering with their drink offerings, for a most sweet odor to the Lord.
19 You shall also make a male goat for sin, and two lambs of one year for peace offerings.
20 And when the priest has lifted them up with the loaves of firstfruits before the Lord, they shall fall to his use.
21 And you shall call this day most celebrated and most holy: you shall do no servile work on it. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in all your dwellings and generations.
<margin>† Above 19:9.</margin>
22 † After you have reaped the harvest of your land, you shall not cut it to the very ground: nor shall you gather the remaining ears, but you shall leave them for the poor and for strangers. I am the Lord your God.
23 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
<margin>† Numbers 29:1.</margin>
24 † Speak to the children of Israel: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, there shall be a Sabbath for you, a memorial with the sounding of trumpets, and it shall be called holy:
25 You shall do no servile work on it, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord.
26 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
<margin>† Above 16:29; Numbers 29:7; John 7:37.</margin>
27 † On the tenth day of this seventh month, the Day of Atonement <note>original: 'dies expiationum'</note> shall be most celebrated and called holy: and you shall afflict your souls on it, and offer a burnt offering to the Lord.
28 You shall do no servile work during the time of this day: because it is a day of propitiation, so that the Lord your God may be propitious to you.
29 Every soul that is not afflicted on this day shall perish from among its people:
30 And whoever does any work, I will destroy that person from among their people.

31 Therefore, you shall do no work in it: it shall be a perpetual statute for you throughout all your generations and in all your dwellings.

<margin>John 7:37.</margin>
36 And for seven days you shall offer burnt offerings <note>original: "holocausta," sacrifices entirely consumed by fire</note> to the Lord: the eighth day also shall be most famous and most holy, and you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord: for it is an assembly and a gathering; you shall do no servile work in it.

40 And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruits of the fairest tree, and branches of palm trees, and boughs of thick-leaved trees, and willows from the brook, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God.

42 And you shall dwell in booths <note>original: "umbraculis," temporary shelters or tabernacles</note> for seven days: every one who is of the race of Israel shall stay in tabernacles:
43 So that your descendants may learn that I made the children of Israel dwell in tabernacles when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

->*The ritual and time for preparing the lamps and the showbread: the punishment of blasphemers and the law of retaliation.*<-

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Command the children of Israel that they bring to you the purest and clearest olive oil to prepare the lamps continually,
3 Outside the veil of the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. And Aaron shall set them from evening until morning before the Lord, by a perpetual service and rite throughout your generations.
4 They shall be placed upon the purest lampstand <note>the Menorah</note> always in the sight of the Lord.
5 You shall also take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it, each of which shall have two tenths <note>of an ephah, a dry measure</note>:
6 You shall set them six by six, one against another, upon the purest table before the Lord:
7 And you shall put the clearest frankincense upon them, that the bread may be a memorial of the oblation of the Lord.

<column-break/>

8 Every Sabbath they shall be changed before the Lord, being received from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant:
9 And they shall be for Aaron and his sons, that they may eat them in the holy place: because it is the Holy of Holies of the sacrifices of the Lord by a perpetual right.
10 And behold, the son of an Israelite woman, whom she had borne to an Egyptian man among the children of Israel, went out and quarreled in the camp with an Israelite man.
11 And when he had blasphemed the name of the Lord and had cursed Him, he was brought to Moses. (Now his mother’s name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
12 And they put him in prison, until they might know what the Lord would command.
13 And the Lord spoke to Moses,
14 Saying: Bring the blasphemer outside the camp, and let all who heard him lay their hands upon his head, and let the entire people stone him.
15 And you shall speak to the children of Israel: The man who curses his God shall bear his sin:
16 And he who blasphemes the name of the Lord, let him die the death: the whole multitude shall overwhelm him with stones, whether he be a citizen or a stranger. He who blasphemes the name of the Lord, let him die the death.
<margin>† Exodus 21:12.</margin>
17 † He who strikes and kills a man, let him die the death.
18 He who strikes an animal shall render a substitute, that is, life for life.
19 He who causes a blemish in any of his citizens: as he has done, so shall it be done to him:
<margin>† Exodus 21:24. Deuteronomy 19:21. Matthew 5:38.</margin>
20 † Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth shall he restore: what kind of blemish he has caused, such shall he be compelled to suffer.
21 He who strikes a beast of burden shall render another. He who strikes a man shall be punished.
22 Let there be equal judgment among you, whether a stranger or a citizen has sinned: because I am the Lord your God.
23 And Moses spoke to the children of Israel: and they brought him who had blasphemed outside the camp and overwhelmed him with stones. And the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses.

### CHAPTER XXV.

->*The law of the seventh, that is, the Sabbatical year, and the fiftieth year, that is, the Jubilee: interest is not to be taken from brothers, nor are they to be oppressed by perpetual slavery, but rather redeemed by powerful newcomers.*<-

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:
2 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: When you have entered the land which I will give to you, † observe a Sabbath to the Lord.
<margin>† Exodus 23:10.</margin>
3 For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard, and you shall gather its fruits:
4 But in the seventh year, there shall be a Sabbath of the land, of the resting of the Lord: you shall not sow your field, and you shall not prune your vineyard.
5 That which the ground produces of its own accord, you shall not reap: and the grapes of your first-fruits you shall not gather as a vintage: for it is a year of rest for the land:
6 But they shall be for food for you, for you and your servant, for your handmaid and your hired hand, and for the stranger who sojourns with you:
7 For your beasts of burden and your cattle, all things that grow shall provide food.

8 You shall also count for yourself seven weeks of years, that is, seven times seven, which together make forty-nine years:
9 And you shall sound the trumpet in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, at the time of atonement <note>original: "propitiationis," referring to the Day of Atonement or Yom Kippur</note> throughout all your land.
10 And you shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim a release <note>original: "remissionem," a discharge from debt or servitude</note> to all the inhabitants of your land: for it is the Jubilee <note>original: "jubilaeus," from the Hebrew word for a ram's horn used to announce the year</note>. Every man shall return to his possession, and everyone shall return to his former family:
11 Because it is the Jubilee and the fiftieth year. You shall not sow, nor shall you reap what grows of its own accord in the field, and you shall not gather the firstfruits of the vintage,
12 On account of the holiness of the Jubilee, but you shall eat the things offered at once,
13 In the year of the Jubilee, all shall return to their possessions.
14 When you sell anything to your neighbor, or buy from him, do not grieve your brother, but you shall buy from him according to the number of years of the Jubilee.
15 And he shall sell to you according to the calculation of the harvests.
16 The more years that remain after the Jubilee, the more the price shall increase: and the less time you count, the less the purchase shall cost: for he sells to you the time of the harvests.
17 Do not afflict your fellow tribesmen, but let everyone fear his God, because I am the Lord your God.
18 Do my precepts, and keep my judgments, and fulfill them, so that you may dwell in the land without any fear,
19 And the ground may yield its fruits for you, which you may eat until you are satisfied, fearing the attack of no one.
20 But if you should say: What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we have not sown, nor gathered our fruits?
21 I will give my blessing to you in the sixth year, and it shall yield the fruits of three years:
22 And you shall sow in the eighth year, and you shall eat the old fruits until the ninth year: until the new ones grow, you shall eat the old.
23 The land also shall not be sold forever: because it is mine, and you are strangers <note>original: "advenae," those living in a land not their own</note> and my tenants <note>original: "coloni," farmers who work land belonging to another</note>.
24 Therefore all the region of your possession shall be sold under the condition of redemption.
25 If your brother, having been impoverished, sells his little possession, and his close relative wishes to, he can redeem what the other had sold.
26 But if he has no near kinsman, and he himself is able to find the price for redeeming it:
27 The fruits shall be counted from the time he sold it: and what remains, he shall restore to the buyer, and so he shall receive his possession back.
28 But if his hand does not find a way to restore the price, the buyer shall have what he bought until the year of the Jubilee. For in that year every sale shall return to the owner, and to the former possessor.
29 He who sells a house within the walls of a city shall have the liberty of redeeming it until one full year is completed.
30 If he does not redeem it, and the circle of the year has passed, the buyer shall possess it, and his descendants forever, and it cannot be redeemed, even in the Jubilee.
31 But if the house is in a village which

<column-break/>

has no walls, it shall be sold by the law of the fields; if it has not been redeemed before, in the Jubilee it shall return to the owner.
32 The houses of the Levites, which are in cities, can always be redeemed:
33 If they have not been redeemed, they shall return to the owners in the Jubilee, because the houses of the cities of the Levites are for possessions among the children of Israel.
34 But their suburbs <note>original: "suburbana," the pasture lands surrounding the Levite cities</note> shall not be sold, because it is an everlasting possession.
35 If your brother is impoverished, and weak of hand, and you receive him as a stranger and a pilgrim, and he lives with you,
36 Do not take usury <note>original: "usuras," interest on a loan</note> from him, nor more than you gave. Fear your God, so that your brother may be able to live with you.
37 You shall not give him your money for interest, and you shall not exact an overabundance of fruits.
38 I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.
39 If your brother, compelled by poverty, sells himself to you, you shall not oppress him with the service of slaves <note>original: "famulorum," household slaves or bondsmen</note>,
40 But he shall be as a hired servant <note>original: "mercenarius"</note> and a tenant: he shall work with you until the year of the Jubilee,
41 And afterward he shall go out with his children, and shall return to his kindred and to the possession of his fathers.
42 For they are my servants, and I brought them out of the land of Egypt: let them not be sold under the condition of slaves:
43 Do not afflict him by power, but fear your God.
44 Let your bondmen and bondwomen be from the nations that are round about you.
45 And from the strangers who sojourn among you, or who are born of them in your land, these you shall have as servants:
46 And you shall pass them on by hereditary right to your descendants, and you shall possess them forever: but your brothers the children of Israel, do not oppress them by power.
47 If the hand of a stranger or pilgrim becomes strong among you, and your brother, being impoverished, sells himself to him, or to anyone of his lineage:
48 After the sale he can be redeemed. Whoever of his brothers wishes, shall redeem him,
49 Both uncle, and uncle's son, and kinsman, and relative. But if he himself is able, he shall redeem himself.
50 Counting only the years from the time of his sale until the year of the Jubilee: and the money for which he was sold, according to the number of years and the reckoning of a hired servant.
51 If there are more years remaining until the Jubilee, according to these he shall also restore the price.
52 If few, he shall settle the account with him according to the number of years, and shall restore to the buyer what remains of the years,
53 For which he served before, the wages being imputed: he shall not afflict him violently in your sight.
54 But if he cannot be redeemed through these means, in the year of the Jubilee he shall go out with his children.
55 For the children of Israel are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

->*Good things are promised to those who keep God's commands, but many evils to those who do not.*<-

<margin>†Exodus 20:4, Deuteronomy 5:8, Psalm 96:7</margin>
**I** am the Lord your God: You shall not make for yourselves an idol or a carved image, nor shall you set up memorial pillars <note>original: "titulos," referring to standing stones or monuments used in pagan worship</note>, nor shall you place a carved stone in your land to worship it: for I am the Lord your God.

2 Keep my sabbaths, and stand in awe of my Sanctuary: I am the Lord.

<margin>†Deuteronomy 28:1</margin>
3 If you walk in my precepts, and keep my commandments, and do them, I will give you rains in their seasons,

4 And the earth shall bring forth its growth, and the trees shall be filled with fruit.

6 I will give peace in your borders: you shall sleep, and there shall be no one to make you afraid. I will take away evil beasts: and the sword shall not pass through your limits.

7 You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you.

8 Five of yours shall pursue a hundred strangers, and a hundred of you shall pursue ten thousand: your enemies shall fall by the sword in your sight.

9 I will look upon you, and make you grow: you shall be multiplied, and I will establish my covenant with you.

10 You shall eat the oldest of the old store, and when the new comes, you shall cast away the old.

11 I will set my tabernacle in the midst of you, and my soul shall not cast you off.

### CHAPTER XXVII.

->*Various laws are established regarding vows or things offered to God by a vow; and regarding the payment of those and of tithes.*<-

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: The man who makes a vow, and promises his soul to God, shall give the price according to the valuation:

3 If it be a male from the twentieth year until the sixtieth year, he shall give fifty shekels <term>shekel: a "siclus" was a standard unit of weight for silver used in the Sanctuary</term> of silver according to the measure of the Sanctuary:

4 If it be a woman, thirty:

5 But from the fifth year until the twentieth, a male shall give twenty shekels: a female ten:

6 From one month until the fifth year, for a male there shall be given five shekels: for a female, three:

7 A male of sixty years and upwards shall give fifteen shekels: a female ten:

8 If he be poor, and unable to pay the valuation, he shall stand before the priest: and as much as the priest shall value him at, and see that he is able to pay, so much shall he give.

9 But an animal that can be sacrificed to the Lord, if anyone vows it, shall be holy,

10 And it cannot be changed—that is, neither a better for a worse, nor a worse for a better. But if he does change it: both the animal that was changed, and that for which it was changed, shall be consecrated to the Lord.

11 If anyone vows an unclean animal, which cannot be sacrificed to the Lord, it shall be brought before the priest:

12 Who, judging whether it be good or bad, shall set the price.

13 But if he who offers it wishes to give the price, he shall add a fifth part above the valuation.

14 If a man vows his house, and sanctifies it to the Lord, the priest shall consider whether it be good or bad, and according to the price which shall be determined by him, it shall be sold:

15 But if he who had vowed it wishes to redeem it, he shall give the fifth part of the valuation over and above, and he shall have the house.

16 But if he vows a field of his possession,

<column-break/>

And consecrates it to the Lord: the price shall be valued according to the measure of the seed; if the land is sown with thirty measures <note>original: "modiis," a Roman unit of dry volume used here to translate the Hebrew "homer"</note> of barley, let it be sold for fifty shekels of silver.

17 If he vows the field immediately from the year of the beginning of the Jubilee, it shall be valued at as much as it is worth.

18 But if it be some time after: the priest shall calculate the money according to the number of years that remain until the Jubilee, and it shall be deducted from the price.

19 But if he who vowed it wishes to redeem the field, he shall add the fifth part of the estimated money, and he shall possess it.

20 But if he does not wish to redeem it, but it has been sold to any other man, he who vowed it shall not be able to redeem it anymore:

21 Because when the day of the Jubilee comes, it shall be sanctified to the Lord; and the consecrated possession belongs to the right of the priests.

22 If a field is bought, and not sanctified to the Lord from the possession of one’s ancestors,

23 The priest shall calculate the price according to the number of years until the Jubilee: and he who vowed it shall give that amount to the Lord.

24 But in the Jubilee, it shall return to the former owner, who had sold it, and had it in the lot of his possession.

<margin>
† Exodus 30:13.
Numbers 3:47.
Ezekiel 45:12.
</margin>

25 Every valuation shall be weighed by the shekel of the sanctuary. † A shekel has twenty obols <note>original: "obolos," often translated as "gerahs" in English Bibles, the smallest unit of Hebrew currency</note>.

26 The firstborn, which belong to the Lord, no one may sanctify or vow: whether it be an ox or a sheep: they are the Lord's.

27 But if it be an unclean animal, he who offered it shall redeem it according to your valuation, and shall add a fifth part of the price: if he does not wish to redeem it, it shall be sold to another for however much it was valued by you.

28 Everything that is devoted to the Lord—whether it be a man, an animal, or a field—shall not be sold, nor can it be redeemed. Whatever has once been consecrated shall be the most holy <note>original: "sanctum sanctorum"</note> to the Lord.

29 And every devotion <note>original: "consecratio," here referring to "cherem" or things irrevocably devoted to destruction</note> which is offered by a man, shall not be redeemed, but shall surely die.

30 All tithes of the land, whether of the grain or of the fruits of the trees, are the Lord's, and are sanctified to him.

31 But if anyone wishes to redeem his tithes, he shall add a fifth part of them.

32 Of all the tithes of the ox, and the sheep, and the goat that pass under the shepherd's rod, whatever tenth comes shall be sanctified to the Lord.

33 It shall not be chosen whether it be good or bad, nor shall it be exchanged for another: if anyone changes it, both that which was changed and that for which it was changed shall be sanctified to the Lord, and shall not be redeemed.

34 These are the precepts which the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel on mount Sinai.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*The rites and duties of the Levites are distributed according to each family.*<-

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
2 Take the sum of the sons of Kohath <note>original: "Caath"</note> from the midst of the Levites, by their houses and families,
3 from the thirtieth year and upward, even to the fiftieth year, of all who enter to stand and minister in the tabernacle of the covenant.
4 This is the service of the sons of Kohath: the tabernacle of the covenant, and the Holy of Holies.
5 Aaron and his sons shall enter when the camp is to be moved, and they shall take down the veil that hangs before the doors, and wrap the ark of the testimony in it,
6 and they shall cover it again with a covering of violet-colored skins <note>original: "janthinarum pellium", likely referring to a durable, dyed leather</note>, and shall spread over it a cloth entirely of hyacinth-blue, and shall put in the carrying bars.
7 They shall also wrap the table of proposition <note>term: Table of Proposition: The table holding the "Showbread"</note> in a hyacinth-blue cloth, and place with it the censers and little mortars, the cups and bowls for pouring libations: the bread shall always be upon it.
8 And they shall spread over it a scarlet cloth, which they shall cover again with a covering of violet skins, and shall put in the carrying bars.

### CHAPTER V.

->*Concerning those who are unclean and must be removed from the camp: restitution for sins of negligence: concerning firstfruits and offerings: and the law of jealousy.*<-

1 **A**nd the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Command the children of Israel to cast out of the camp every leper <note>original: "leprosum," referring to various infectious skin diseases</note>, and anyone who has a discharge, or who is defiled by contact with the dead.
3 Cast out both male and female from the camp, so they do not contaminate the place where I dwell with you.
4 And the children of Israel did so, and they cast them outside the camp, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses.
5 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
6 Say to the children of Israel: When a man or woman commits any of the sins that commonly happen to people, and through negli-

7 They shall confess their sin and return the principal <note>original: "caput," meaning the main amount or "head" of the debt</note> itself, plus a fifth part added to it, to the person against whom they sinned.
8 But if there is no kinsman to receive it, they shall give it to the Lord, and it shall belong to the priest, except for the ram which is offered for atonement, that it may be a placating sacrifice.

11 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
12 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: If a man’s wife goes astray, and, treating her husband with contempt,
13 Has slept with another man, and her husband could not discover it, but the adultery is hidden and cannot be proven by witnesses because she was not caught in the act;
14 If the spirit of jealousy <note>original: "spiritus zelotypiae," a state of intense suspicion or zeal for marital exclusivity</note> stirs up the man against his wife, who is either defiled or is attacked by a false suspicion,
15 He shall bring her to the priest and shall offer an oblation for her, the tenth part of a measure of barley flour. He shall not pour oil upon it, nor put frankincense on it, because it is a sacrifice of jealousy and an offering for investigating adultery.
16 Therefore, the priest shall offer her and set her before the Lord.
17 And he shall take holy water in an earthen vessel, and he shall cast a little dust from the floor of the Tabernacle into it.
18 When the woman stands in the sight of the Lord, he shall uncover her head <note>The uncovering of the head was a sign of public exposure or shame</note> and place upon her hands the sacrifice of remembrance and the oblation of jealousy. He himself shall hold the most bitter waters, in which he has gathered the curses with an oath.
19 And he shall adjure her, and say: If no other man has slept with you, and if you have not been defiled by deserting your husband’s bed, these most bitter waters, into which I have gathered the curses, shall not harm you.
20 But if you have turned away from your husband and are defiled, and have lain with another man:
21 You shall be subject to these curses: May the Lord make you a curse and an example for all among His people; may He cause your thigh to rot and your womb to swell and burst.
22 May these cursed waters enter into your belly, and as your womb swells, may your thigh rot. And the woman shall answer: Amen, amen <note>original: "Amen, amen," a Hebrew affirmation meaning "So be it, truly"</note>.
23 And the priest shall write these curses in a book and shall wash them out with the most bitter waters into which he gathered the curses,
24 And he shall give them to her to drink. When she has drained them,
25 The priest shall take from her hand the sacrifice of jealousy and shall lift it up before the Lord and place it upon the altar; however, first,
26 He shall take a handful of the sacrifice from that which is offered and burn it upon the altar, and so give the woman the most bitter waters to drink.
27 When she has drunk them, if she is defiled and, having held her husband in contempt, is guilty of adultery, the waters of the curse shall pass through her, and as her belly swells, her thigh shall rot; and the woman shall be a curse and an example to all the people.

<column-break/>

28 But if she has not been defiled, she shall be unharmed and shall bear children.
29 This is the law of jealousy. If a woman turns away from her husband and is defiled,
30 And the husband, stirred by the spirit of jealousy, brings her before the Lord, and the priest does to her according to all that is written:
31 The husband shall be without fault, and she shall bear her own iniquity.

### C H A P T E R VI.

->*The consecration and offering of the Nazirites: and the words with which the priests shall bless the people are prescribed.*<-

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: When a man or a woman makes a vow to be sanctified, and wishes to consecrate themselves to the Lord:
3 They shall abstain from wine and everything that can make one drunk. They shall not drink vinegar made from wine or from any other drink, nor anything squeezed from the grape; they shall not eat fresh or dried grapes
4 All the days in which they are consecrated to the Lord by vow: they shall eat nothing that comes from the vineyard, from the raisin even to the grape-stone.
<margin>Judges 13:5</margin> 5 During the entire time of their separation, no † razor <note>original: "novacula"</note> shall pass over their head until the day is completed for which they are consecrated to the Lord. They shall be holy, letting the hair of their head grow long.
6 During the entire time of their consecration, they shall not go near a dead body,
7 Nor shall they be defiled even at the funeral of their father, mother, brother, or sister, because the consecration of their God is upon their head.
8 All the days of their separation, they shall be holy to the Lord.
9 But if someone dies suddenly in their presence, the head of their consecration shall be polluted: they shall shave it immediately on that same day of their purgation, and again on the seventh day.
10 On the eighth day, however, they shall offer two turtles <note>Turtledoves</note> or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the covenant of testimony.
11 And the priest shall offer one for sin and the other as a burnt offering <note>original: "holocaustum," a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire</note>, and shall pray for them, because they sinned by reason of the dead; and he shall sanctify their head on that day.
12 And they shall consecrate to the Lord the days of their separation, offering a yearling lamb for sin: provided, however, that the previous days are rendered void, because their sanctification was polluted.
13 This is the law of consecration. When the days which they decreed by vow are fulfilled: he shall bring them to the door of the tabernacle of the covenant,
14 And he shall offer his oblation to the Lord: a yearling lamb without blemish for a burnt offering, a yearling ewe without blemish for sin, and a ram without blemish as a peace offering <note>original: "hostiam pacificam," a sacrifice signifying communion between God and the offerer</note>,
15 Also a basket of unleavened bread <note>original: "azymorum"</note> kneaded with oil, and wafers without leaven anointed with oil, along with the drink offerings for each.
16 These the priest shall offer before the Lord, and he shall perform the rites both for sin and for the burnt offering.
17 But the ram he shall immolate as a peace offering to the Lord, offering at the same time the basket of unleavened bread and the drink offerings that are due by custom.

85 So that each silver charger had one hundred and thirty shekels of silver, and each bowl had seventy shekels; that is, the total of all the silver vessels was two thousand four hundred shekels, by the weight of the Sanctuary:
86 Twelve golden mortars full of incense, weighing ten shekels each by the weight of the Sanctuary: that is, one hundred and twenty shekels of gold in total:
87 Twelve oxen from the herd for a burnt offering, twelve rams, twelve year-old lambs, and their libations <note>original: "libamenta," drink offerings typically of wine</note>: twelve male goats for a sin offering.
88 For the sacrifice of peace offerings: twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty male goats, sixty year-old lambs. These things were offered at the dedication of the altar, when it was anointed.
89 And when Moses entered the Tabernacle of the Covenant to consult the oracle, he heard the voice of one speaking to him from the mercy seat <note>original: "propitiatorio," the golden lid of the Ark where atonement was made</note> which was over the Ark of the Testimony between the two Cherubim <note>Angelic figures whose wings overshadowed the Ark</note>, from which also He spoke to him.

### C H A P T E R X.

*God commands two silver trumpets to be made and teaches their use; the order in which the camp moved from the desert of Sinai; Moses prays his kinsman Hobab to set out with them; and the words which Moses spoke when the Ark was lifted up or set down.*

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Make for yourself two silver trumpets of hammered work <note>original: "ductiles," referring to metal beaten into shape with a hammer rather than cast in a mold</note>, which you may use to call together the multitude when the camp must be moved.
3 And when you blow the trumpets, the whole crowd shall gather to you at the door of the Tabernacle of the Covenant.
4 If you sound it once, the princes and the heads of the multitude of Israel shall come to you.
5 But if a longer and more broken blast <note>original: "concisus clangor," likely a series of short, staccato notes used as an alarm</note> sounds, those who are on the eastern side shall move camp first.
6 At the second sound and similar blaring of the trumpet, those who live toward the south shall lift their tents; and in this manner the rest shall do, with the trumpets blaring for the departure.
7 But when the people are to be gathered, the sound of the trumpets shall be simple, and they shall not blare in short bursts.
8 The sons of Aaron the priest shall blow the trumpets: and this shall be a perpetual law throughout your generations.
9 If you go out to war from your land against enemies who fight against you, you shall sound the blaring trumpets, and there shall be a remembrance of you before the Lord your God, so that you may be rescued from the hands of your enemies.
10 If at any time you have a feast, and festival days, and the new moons <note>original: "calendas," the first day of the month in the lunar calendar</note>, you shall sound the trumpets over the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, that they may be a reminder of your God to you: I am the Lord your God.
11 In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was lifted up from the Tabernacle of the Covenant:
12 And the children of Israel set out by their ranks from the desert of Sinai, and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran.
13 And the first ones moved camp according to the command of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
<margin>+ Above, 1:7</margin>

<column-break/>

20 Furthermore, in the tribe of Gad, the prince was Eliasaph the son of Deuel.

23 And in the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, the prince was Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.

26 In the tribe of the sons of Asher, the prince was Pagiel the son of Ocran.

30 To whom he replied: I will not go with you, but I will return to my own land, in which I was born.
31 And Moses said: Do not, I pray, leave us; for you know in which places we ought to pitch camp through the desert, and you shall be our guide.
32 And when you come with us, whatever is best of the riches which the Lord is going to deliver to us, we will give to you.
33 They set out therefore from the mountain of the Lord a journey of three days, and the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord went before them for three days, providing a place for the camp.

## CHAPTER XIV

->*The murmur of the people, having heard the scouts, which Joshua and Caleb try in vain to calm: Moses appeases the angry Lord: all are condemned to die in the wilderness except Caleb and Joshua; and the Israelites fighting against the Lord's will fall to their enemies.*<-

### CHAPTER XVI.

*Korah, Dathan, and Abiram stir up a rebellion against Moses and Aaron, and they strive for the leadership and the priesthood; wherefore the earth swallows them alive: and fire kills the 250 men offering incense: and a fire consumed another 14,700 who were murmuring, which Aaron checked by his prayer.*

1 Now behold Korah the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram the sons of Eliab, and On the son of Peleth of the sons of Reuben,
2 Rose up against Moses, and with them two hundred and fifty other men of the children of Israel, leaders of the assembly, who were called by name at the time of the council.

5 And speaking to Korah and to the whole multitude, he said: In the morning, the Lord will make known who belongs to him, and he will bring the holy ones near to himself: and those whom he chooses shall approach him.
6 Do this therefore: Let each one take his censer <note>A vessel for burning incense.</note>, you, Korah, and all your assembly:

8 And he said again to Korah: Hear, sons of Levi:

11 And your whole group stands against the Lord? For what is Aaron that you should murmur against him?

13 Is it a small thing to you that you have led us out of a land that flowed with milk and honey <note>The rebels sarcastically use the description of the Promised Land to refer to Egypt.</note>, to kill us in the desert, unless you also rule over us?

### CHAPTER XVII.

*Twelve rods having been taken from the leaders of the twelve tribes, only the rod of Aaron blossomed and produced fruit; by this miracle and sign the Priesthood is confirmed to him by God; and the rod was kept in the tabernacle of the testimony.*

7 When Moses had placed them before the Lord in the tabernacle of the testimony:

### CHAPTER XVII.

*Concerning the burdens of the priests and the watches of the Levites: in place of a hereditary portion, firstfruits and offerings and sacrifices are assigned to the priests, while tithes are given to the Levites, who in turn gave a tenth of them to Aaron.*

1 And the Lord said to Aaron: "You, and your sons, and your father's house with you, shall bear the iniquity of the Sanctuary: and you and your sons together shall bear the sins of your priesthood.
2 But also take with you your brothers from the tribe of Levi, and the scepter <note>original: "sceptrum," referring here to the tribe or ancestral branch</note> of your father, and let them be ready and minister to you: but you and your sons shall minister in the tabernacle of the testimony.
3 And the Levites shall keep watch according to your commands, and for all the works of the tabernacle: provided only that they do not approach the vessels of the Sanctuary or the altar, lest both they die and you perish together.
4 Let them be with you, and keep watch in the guards of the tabernacle, and in all its ceremonies. A stranger <note>original: "Alienigena," here meaning anyone who is not a Levite</note> shall not be joined with you.
5 Keep watch in the guard of the Sanctuary, and in the ministry of the altar: lest indignation rise up over the children of Israel.
6 I have given you your brothers the Levites from the midst of the children of Israel: and I have delivered them as a gift to the Lord, to serve in the ministries of his tabernacle.
7 But you and your sons, guard your priesthood: and all things that pertain to the worship of the altar, and are within the veil, shall be administered by the priests: if any outsider approaches, he shall be put to death."
8 And the Lord spoke to Aaron: "Behold, I have given you the charge of my firstfruits. All things that are sanctified by the children of Israel, I have delivered to you and your sons for the priestly office as an everlasting law.
9 These things therefore you shall receive from those which are sanctified and offered to the Lord. Every offering, and sacrifice, and whatever is rendered to me for sin and offense, and goes into the Holy of Holies, shall be yours and your sons'.
10 You shall eat it in the Sanctuary: only males shall eat of it, because it is consecrated to you.
11 But the firstfruits, which the children of Israel shall vow and offer, I have given to you, and to your sons, and your daughters, by a perpetual right: whoever is clean in your house shall eat them.

<column-break/>

12 All the best <note>original: "medullam," literally "marrow" or "pith," referring to the finest quality</note> of the oil, and of the wine, and of the grain, whatever firstfruits they offer to the Lord, I have given to you.
13 All the first beginnings of the fruits, which the soil produces and are brought to the Lord, shall fall to your use: whoever is clean in your house shall eat them.
14 Everything that the children of Israel shall render by vow shall be yours.
15 Whatever first breaks from the womb of all flesh, which they offer to the Lord, whether it be of men or of beasts, shall be yours by right: provided that for the firstborn of a man you receive a price, and every animal that is unclean, you shall cause to be redeemed,
16 Whose redemption shall be after one month, for five shekels of silver, by the weight of the Sanctuary. <margin>† Exod. 30:13. Lev. 27:25. Above 3:47. Ezek. 45:12.</margin> A shekel has twenty obols <note>original: "obolos," a small unit of currency, equivalent to the Hebrew gerah</note>.
17 But the firstborn of an ox and of a sheep and of a goat you shall not cause to be redeemed, because they are sanctified to the Lord: only their blood shall you pour upon the altar, and the fat you shall burn as a most sweet odor to the Lord.
18 But the meats shall fall to your use, just as the consecrated breast and the right shoulder shall be yours.
19 All the firstfruits of the Sanctuary, which the children of Israel offer to the Lord, I have given to you, and to your sons and daughters, by a perpetual right. It is a covenant of salt <note>A "covenant of salt" refers to an unbreakable, permanent agreement, as salt was a preservative</note> forever before the Lord, for you and your sons.
20 And the Lord said to Aaron: "In their land you shall possess nothing, nor shall you have a portion among them: I am your portion and inheritance in the midst of the children of Israel.
21 But to the sons of Levi I have given all the tithes of Israel in possession, for the ministry by which they serve me in the tabernacle of the covenant:
22 So that the children of Israel may no longer approach the tabernacle, nor commit a deadly sin,
23 With only the sons of Levi serving me in the tabernacle, and bearing the sins of the people: it shall be an everlasting law in your generations. <margin>† Deut. 18:1.</margin> They shall possess nothing else,
24 Content with the offering of tithes, which I have set apart for their uses and necessities."
25 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
26 "Command the Levites, and announce: When you have received from the children of Israel the tithes, which I have given to you, offer the firstfruits of them to the Lord, that is, a tenth part of the tithe,
27 That it may be reckoned to you as an offering of the firstfruits, as much from the threshing floors as from the winepresses:
28 And from all things of which you receive firstfruits, offer them to the Lord, and give them to Aaron the priest.
29 All things which you shall offer from the tithes, and shall set apart for the gifts of the Lord, shall be the best and chosen things.
30 And you shall say to them: If you offer all the excellent and better things from the tithes, it shall be reckoned to you as if you had given firstfruits from the threshing floor and the winepress:
31 And you shall eat them in all your places, both you and your families: because it is the reward for the ministry by which you serve in the tabernacle of the testimony.
32 And you shall not sin concerning this, by reserving the choice and fat things for yourselves, lest you pollute the offerings of the children of Israel, and die."

# CHAPTER XIX.

*The rite for preparing the water of cleansing is delivered: the water of expiation was made from the ashes of a red heifer, by which various impurities are washed away; concerning one dying in a tent, and a vessel not having a lid, and touching a human corpse.*

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
2 This is the ritual of the sacrifice which the Lord has ordained: Command the children of Israel that they bring to you a red heifer <note>In Hebrew tradition, a 'parah adumah' or red heifer is a rare animal used for a specific purification ritual.</note> of full age, in which there is no blemish, and which has never carried a yoke.
<margin>Hebrews 13:11</margin>
3 And you shall deliver her to Eleazar the priest, who shall lead her out outside the camp and † sacrifice her in the sight of all.
4 And dipping his finger in her blood, he shall sprinkle it over against the doors of the tabernacle seven times.
5 And he shall burn her while all are watching, delivering her skin and flesh, as well as her blood and dung, to the flames.
6 The priest shall also cast cedar wood, and hyssop, and twice-dyed scarlet <note>original: "coccumque bis tinctum," a crimson thread used in many purification rites</note> into the flame that consumes the heifer.
7 And then finally, having washed his garments and his body, he shall enter into the camp, and he shall be contaminated until the evening.
8 But he also who burned her shall wash his garments and his body, and shall be unclean until the evening.
9 Moreover, a man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and pour them out outside the camp in a very clean place, so that they may be kept for the multitude of the children of Israel, and for the water of sprinkling: because the heifer was burned for sin.
10 And when he who carried the ashes of the heifer has washed his garments, he shall be unclean until the evening. The children of Israel, and the strangers who dwell among them, shall have this as a holy rite by a perpetual law.
11 He who touches the corpse of a human being, and for this reason remains unclean for seven days,
12 Shall be sprinkled with this water on the third and seventh day, and so he shall be cleansed. If he is not sprinkled on the third day, he cannot be cleansed on the seventh.
13 Everyone who touches the corpse of a human soul <note>original: "humanæ animæ morticinum," referring to a dead body</note> and is not sprinkled with this mixture, pollutes the tabernacle of the Lord and shall perish from Israel: because he was not sprinkled with the water of expiation, he shall be unclean, and his filthiness shall remain upon him.
14 This is the law for a man who dies in a tent: All who enter his tent, and all the vessels that are there, shall be polluted for seven days.
15 A vessel that has no lid, nor a covering tied over it, shall be unclean.
16 If anyone in the field touches the corpse of a man who was killed, or one who died on his own, or even a bone of him, or a grave, he shall be unclean for seven days.
17 And they shall take some of the ashes of the burning and of the sin offering, and they shall pour living waters <note>original: "aquas vivas," meaning fresh, running water from a spring rather than stagnant water</note> upon them into a vessel.
18 In which, when a clean man has dipped hyssop, he shall sprinkle with it the whole tent, and all the furniture, and the men polluted by such contagion:

<column-break/>

and all the furniture, and the men polluted by such contagion:
19 And in this manner, the clean man shall purify the unclean on the third and seventh day: and being expiated on the seventh day, he shall wash both himself and his garments, and he shall be unclean until the evening.
20 If anyone is not expiated by this rite, his soul shall perish from the midst of the church <note>original: "ecclesiæ," here referring to the assembly or congregation of Israel</note>: because he has polluted the sanctuary of the Lord and was not sprinkled with the water of cleansing.
21 This shall be a lawful and everlasting precept. He also who sprinkles the water shall wash his garments: Everyone who touches the waters of expiation shall be unclean until the evening.
22 Whatever an unclean person touches, he shall make unclean: and the soul that touches any of these things † shall be unclean until the evening.

# CHAPTER XXIII.

*Balaam, having built altars, prepares himself to curse the Hebrews, but instead of a curse, he blesses the people of Israel once and again; he prophesies many things concerning them.*

4 When he had gone away quickly, God met him. And Balaam spoke to Him: "I have erected seven altars," he said, "and I have placed a calf and a ram upon them."
5 The Lord then put a word into his mouth, and said: "Return to Balak, and this is what you shall speak."

7 And taking up his oracle <note>original: 'parabola', often used in the Vulgate to denote a prophetic song or formal declaration</note>, he said: "From Aram has Balak, the king of the Moabites, brought me, from the mountains of the East: 'Come,' he said, 'and curse Jacob; hurry, and denounce Israel.'
8 How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? By what reason shall I denounce whom the Lord does not denounce?
9 From the highest rocks I shall see him, and from the hills I shall behold him. The people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.

8 God brought him out of Egypt, whose strength is like that of the rhinoceros <note>The Latin 'rhinocerotis' refers to a powerful, horned wild beast, often identified in modern translations as a wild ox or aurochs.</note>. They shall devour the nations that are his enemies, and shall break their bones, and pierce them with arrows.
9 Couching, he slept like a lion, and like a lioness, whom no one shall dare to rouse. He who blesses you shall himself be blessed; he who curses you shall be considered cursed.
10 And Balak, being angry with Balaam, clapped his hands and said: "I called you to curse my enemies, whom, on the contrary, you have blessed three times:
11 Return to your place. I had indeed intended to honor you magnificently, but the Lord has deprived you of the honor intended for you."
12 Balaam answered Balak: "Did I not say to your messengers, whom you sent to me:
<margin>† Above 22:18.</margin>
13 'If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the Lord my God, to speak anything either good or evil from my own heart; but whatever the Lord says, that I will speak'?
14 Nevertheless, as I go to my own people, I will give counsel as to what your people shall do to this people in the latter days."
15 Therefore, taking up his parable, he said again: "Balaam the son of Beor has spoken: the man whose eye has been shut has spoken:
16 The hearer of the words of God has spoken, who knows the doctrine of the Most High, and sees the visions of the Almighty, who falling has his eyes opened.
<margin>† Matthew 2:2.</margin>
17 I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not near. **A STAR SHALL RISE** out of Jacob, and a rod <note>original: 'virga', meaning a staff or scepter representing royal authority</note> shall rise from Israel: and he shall strike the leaders of Moab, and shall lay waste all the children of Seth.
18 And Edom shall be his possession: the inheritance of Seir shall yield to his enemies: but Israel shall act valiantly.
19 Out of Jacob shall come he who shall rule, and shall destroy the remnants of the city."
20 And when he saw Amalek, taking up his parable, he said: "Amalek is the beginning of nations, whose end shall be destruction."
21 He saw also the Kenite: and taking up his parable, he said: "Your dwelling is indeed strong: but if you set your nest in a rock,
22 And you are chosen from the stock of Cain <note>The Latin 'Cin' refers to the Kenites.</note>, how long shall you be able to remain? For Assyria shall capture you."
23 And taking up his parable, he spoke again: "Alas, who shall live when God does these things?
<margin>† Daniel 11:30.</margin>
24 They shall come in galleys from Italy <note>original: 'trieribus de Italia'. The Vulgate identifies 'Chittim' with Italy or Rome.</note>, they shall overcome the Assyrians, and shall lay waste the Hebrews, and at the last they themselves also shall perish."
25 And Balaam rose, and returned to his place: Balak also went the way by which he had come.

# CHAPTER XXV.

->Because of the fornication of Israel with the Moabites and Midianites, God commands the leaders to be hanged, and twenty-four thousand of the people perish: and to Phinehas himself he gives an everlasting priesthood as a reward, because in his divine zeal he had pierced Zimri and Cozbi with a dagger.<-

1 Now Israel stayed at that time in Shittim, and the people committed fornication with the daughters of Moab,
2 Who called them to their sacrifices. And they ate and adored their gods.
<margin>† Joshua 22:17.</margin>
3 And Israel was initiated to Baal-peor <note>original: 'Beelphegor'. This refers to the Israelites joining in the worship of a local pagan deity.</note>: and the Lord being angry,
<margin>† Deuteronomy 4:3.</margin>
4 Said to Moses: "Take all the leaders of the people, and hang them up on gallows against the sun: that my fury may be turned away from Israel."
<margin>† Exodus 32:27.</margin>
5 And Moses said to the judges of Israel: "Let every man kill his neighbors, who have been initiated to Baal-peor."
6 And behold, one of the children of Israel entered in the sight of his brothers to a Midianite harlot, while Moses looked on, and all the multitude of the children of Israel, who were weeping before the doors of the tabernacle.
<margin>† Psalm 105:30. 1 Maccabees 2:26. 1 Corinthians 10:8.</margin>
7 Which when Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, had seen, he rose out of the midst of the multitude, and taking a dagger,
8 Followed the Israelite man into the brothel <note>original: 'lupanar', referring here to the tent where the act was occurring</note>, and pierced them both through together, that is, the man and the woman, through their private parts. And the plague ceased from the children of Israel:
9 And twenty-four thousand men were killed.
10 And the Lord spoke to Moses:
11 "Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned away my wrath from the children of Israel: because he was moved with my zeal against them, so that I myself might not destroy the children of Israel in my zeal.
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 45:30. 1 Maccabees 2:54.</margin>
12 Therefore speak to him: Behold, I give him the peace of my covenant,
13 And it shall be both to him and to his seed a covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he has been zealous for his God, and has atoned for the wickedness of the children of Israel."
14 Now the name of the Israelite man who was killed with the Midianite woman was Zimri <note>original: 'Zambri'</note> the son of Salu, a leader of the kindred and tribe of Simeon.
15 Furthermore, the Midianite woman who was likewise slain was called Cozbi, the daughter of Zur, a most noble prince of the Midianites.
16 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
<margin>† Below 31:2.</margin>
17 "Let the Midianites find you their enemies, and strike them:
18 Because they also have acted as enemies against you, and deceived you with snares through the idol Peor, and Cozbi the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, who was struck in the day of the plague because of the sacrilege of Peor."

### CHAPTER XXVII.

->*The daughters of Zelophehad, in the absence of male offspring, succeed their father in inheritance: the Lord tells Moses he will die when he has viewed the promised land from Mount Abarim, and he appoints Joshua as the leader of the people in his place.*<-

<margin>† Above 26:32, 33. Below 36:1. Joshua 17:3.</margin>
Then the daughters of Zelophehad <note>original: "Salphaad"</note>, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, who was the son of Joseph, came forward: their names are Mahlah, and Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
2 And they stood before Moses and Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the people, at the door of the Tabernacle of the Covenant, and said:
<margin>† Above 16:1.</margin>
3 "Our father died in the desert, and he was not in the sedition which was stirred up against the Lord under Korah, but he died in his own sin: he had no male sons. Why should the name of his family be taken away because he had no son? Give us a possession among the kinsmen of our father."
4 And Moses brought their cause before the judgment of the Lord.
5 Who said to him:
6 "The daughters of Zelophehad demand a just thing: give them a possession among the kinsmen of their father, and let them succeed him in the inheritance.
7 Furthermore, you shall speak these things to the children of Israel:
8 When a man dies without a son, the inheritance shall pass to his daughter.
9 If he has no daughter, he shall have his brothers as successors.

<column-break/>

10 But if he has no brothers, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brothers.
11 And if he has no paternal uncles, the inheritance shall be given to those who are closest to him: and this shall be a holy and perpetual law for the children of Israel, just as the Lord commanded Moses."
<margin>† Deuteronomy 32:49.</margin>
12 The Lord also said to Moses: "Go up into this mountain of Abarim, and behold from there the land which I will give to the children of Israel.
13 And when you have seen it, you also shall go to join your people, just as your brother Aaron went:
<margin>† Above 20:12. Deuteronomy 32:51.</margin>
14 Because you offended me in the desert of Zin <note>original: "Sin"</note> during the strife of the multitude, and you would not sanctify me before them at the waters." These are the waters of contradiction <note>original: "aquæ contradictionis," often called Meribah</note> in Kadesh of the desert of Zin.
15 To which Moses answered:
16 "May the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, provide a man who may be over this multitude:
17 And who can go out and come in before them, and lead them out or bring them in: so that the people of the Lord may not be like sheep without a shepherd."
<margin>† Deuteronomy 3:21.</margin>
18 And the Lord said to him: "Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand upon him.
19 He shall stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole multitude:
20 And you shall give him instructions in the sight of all, and a portion of your glory, so that the entire congregation of the children of Israel may obey him.
21 For him, if anything needs to be done, Eleazar the priest shall consult the Lord. At his word he shall go out and he shall come in, he and all the children of Israel with him, and the rest of the multitude."
22 Moses did as the Lord had commanded. And when he had taken Joshua, he set him before Eleazar the priest and the whole gathering of the people.
23 And having laid his hands upon his head, he repeated all that the Lord had commanded.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

->*Concerning the daily sacrifices, and those of the seventh day, and of the New Moons, and concerning the two solemnities of the Unleavened Bread and the Weeks.*<-

The Lord also spoke to Moses:
2 "Command the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: Offer my oblation and bread, and incense of a most sweet odor, in their due seasons."
<margin>† Exodus 29:38.</margin>
3 These are the sacrifices which you ought to offer: Two yearling lambs without blemish daily for a perpetual burnt offering <note>original: "holocaustum sempiternum"</note>:
4 One you shall offer in the morning, and the other in the evening:
5 A tenth part of an ephah <term>ephah: a dry measure, roughly 22 liters</term> of fine flour, which shall be mixed with the purest oil, and shall have a fourth part of a hin <term>hin: a liquid measure, roughly 4 liters</term>.
6 It is the continual burnt offering which you offered at Mount Sinai for a most sweet odor of the incense of the Lord.
7 And you shall pour a drink offering of a fourth part of a hin of wine for each lamb in the Sanctuary of the Lord.
8 And the other lamb you shall likewise offer in the evening, according to the whole rite of the morning sacrifice and its drink offerings, an offering of most sweet odor to the Lord.
<margin>† Matthew 12:5.</margin>
9 And on the Sabbath day you shall offer two yearling lambs without blemish, and two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil in sacrifice, and the drink offerings,
10 Which are duly poured out every Sabbath for a perpetual burnt offering.
