11 On the new moons <note>original: "calendis," the first day of each month</note>, moreover, you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without blemish,
12 And three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each bull; and two-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each ram;
13 And one-tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each lamb. This is a burnt offering of a most sweet fragrance and an incense-offering to the Lord.
14 The drink offerings of wine to be poured out for each victim shall be these: half a hin <note>a Hebrew unit of liquid measure, roughly 1.5 gallons</note> for each bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a fourth for a lamb. This shall be the burnt offering for every month as they succeed one another throughout the passing year.
15 One male goat shall also be offered to the Lord for sins, as a perpetual burnt offering with its drink offerings.
<margin>Exodus 12:18; Leviticus 23:5.</margin>
16 In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, shall be the Passover <note>original: "Phase," from the Hebrew 'Pesach'</note> of the Lord,
17 And on the fifteenth day is the festival. For seven days they shall eat unleavened bread.
18 The first of these days shall be venerable and holy; you shall do no servile work <note>manual labor or business transactions forbidden on holy days</note> on it.
19 And you shall offer an incense-offering as a burnt offering to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without blemish.
20 And the grain offerings for each, made of fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths for each bull, and two-tenths for the ram,
21 And one-tenth for each of the lambs—that is, for the seven lambs.
22 And one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you,
23 In addition to the morning burnt offering which you shall always offer.
24 Thus you shall do for each of the seven days, providing fuel for the fire <note>original: "fomitem ignis"</note> and a most sweet fragrance to the Lord, which shall rise from the burnt offering and from the drink offerings of each.
25 The seventh day also shall be most celebrated and holy to you; you shall do no servile work on it.
26 The day of the firstfruits also, when you offer new crops to the Lord after the weeks are completed <note>referring to the Feast of Weeks or Pentecost</note>, shall be venerable and holy; you shall do no servile work on it.
27 And you shall offer a burnt offering for a most sweet fragrance to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without blemish;
28 And in their grain offerings, three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, two-tenths for the rams,
29 And one-tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs together; also a male goat
30 Which is sacrificed for atonement; besides the perpetual burnt offering and its grain offerings.
31 You shall offer all these things without blemish, along with their drink offerings.

### CHAPTER XXIX.

->The festivals of the seventh month, and what is to be offered in them: namely, the festival of trumpets, of atonement, and of tabernacles, which have various offerings over eight days.<-

The first day of the seventh month shall also be venerable and holy to you; you shall do no servile work on it, because it is the day of the sounding of trumpets,

2 And you shall offer a burnt offering for a most sweet fragrance to the Lord: one young bull from the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without blemish;
3 And in their grain offerings, three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, two-tenths for the ram,
4 One-tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs together;
5 And one male goat for sin, which is offered for the atonement of the people,
6 Besides the burnt offering of the new moon with its grain offerings, and the perpetual burnt offering with its usual drink offerings. With these same ceremonies you shall offer an incense-offering for a most sweet fragrance to the Lord.
<margin>Leviticus 16:29 and 23:24.</margin>
7 The tenth day of this seventh month shall also be holy and venerable to you, and you shall afflict your souls <note>a traditional reference to fasting and self-denial</note>; you shall do no servile work on it.
8 And you shall offer a burnt offering to the Lord for a most sweet fragrance: one young bull from the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without blemish;
9 And in their grain offerings, three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, two-tenths for the ram,
10 One-tenth for each of the lambs, which are seven lambs in total;
11 And one male goat for sin, besides those things which are usually offered for transgression in atonement, and the perpetual burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
12 And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, which shall be holy and venerable to you, you shall do no servile work, but you shall celebrate a festival to the Lord for seven days.
13 And you shall offer a burnt offering for a most sweet fragrance to the Lord: thirteen young bulls from the herd, two rams, and fourteen yearling lambs without blemish;
14 And for their drink offerings, three-tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, for the thirteen bulls total; and two-tenths for each ram, that is, for the two rams together,
15 And one-tenth for each lamb, for the fourteen lambs total;
16 And one male goat for sin, besides the perpetual burnt offering, and its grain offering and drink offering.

18 And you shall rightly celebrate the grain offerings and drink offerings for each—for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs;

### CHAPTER XXX.

*Concerning the vow and oath of men, and when the vows or oaths of girls and wives are valid or void.*

1 **A**nd Moses told the children of Israel all the things that the Lord had commanded him:
2 And he spoke to the princes of the tribes of the children of Israel: This is the word which the Lord has commanded:
3 If any man makes a vow to the Lord, or binds himself by an oath: he shall not make his word void, but shall fulfill everything that he promised.
4 If a woman makes a vow and binds herself by an oath, being in her father’s house and still in the age of a girl: if her father knows of the vow she promised and the oath by which she bound her soul, and remains silent, she shall be liable for the vow:
5 Whatever she promised and swore, she shall fulfill in deed.
6 But if, immediately as he hears it, her father objects: both her vows and her oaths shall be void, nor shall she be held liable to her promise, because her father objected.
7 If she has a husband and makes a vow, and a word once departing from her mouth has bound her soul by an oath:
8 On the day the husband hears of it, if he does not object, she shall be liable for the vow and shall render whatever she had promised.
9 But if, upon hearing it, he immediately objects and makes her promises void, and the words by which she had bound her soul: the Lord will be merciful to her.
10 A widow and a divorced woman shall render whatever they have vowed.

<column-break/>

11 A wife in the house of her husband, when she has bound herself by a vow and an oath,
12 If the husband hears it and remains silent, and does not object to the promise, she shall render whatever she had promised.
13 But if he immediately objects, she shall not be held liable for the promise: because the husband objected, and the Lord will be merciful to her.
14 If she makes a vow and binds herself by an oath, such as through fasting or abstinence from other things, to humble <note>original: "affligat"; literally to afflict or humble the soul through discipline</note> her soul, it shall be in the husband's discretion whether she shall do it or not do it.
15 But if the husband, hearing it, remains silent and puts off his decision until the next day: whatever she had vowed and promised, she shall render: because as soon as he heard it, he remained silent.
16 But if he objects after he has known of it, he himself shall bear her iniquity <note>original: "iniquitatem"; meaning the husband takes legal responsibility for the broken vow</note>.
17 These are the laws which the Lord established for Moses between a husband and a wife, and between a father and a daughter who is still in the age of a girl, or who remains in her parent's house.

### CHAPTER XXXI.

*After the Midianites were slain by God's command, only the virgins are spared; the substance is divided equally between the combatants and the people, the firstfruits are handed to the Priest and Levites, and thanks are offered to God with gifts because none of the Hebrews died.*

1 **A**nd the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Take vengeance first for the children of Israel upon the Midianites, and so you shall be gathered to your people.
<margin>† Above 25:17.</margin>
3 And immediately Moses said: Arm men from among you for battle, who can seek the vengeance of the Lord upon the Midianites.
4 Let a thousand men be chosen from each of the tribes of Israel to be sent to the war.
5 And they gave a thousand from each tribe, that is, twelve thousand men equipped for battle:
6 Whom Moses sent with Phinehas, the son of Eleazar the priest; he also delivered to him the holy vessels and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
7 And when they had fought against the Midianites and had conquered, they slew all the males,
<margin>† Joshua 13:21.</margin>
8 And their kings: Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, five princes of the nation: they also killed Balaam, the son of Beor, with the sword.
9 And they took their women and little ones, and all their cattle, and all their household goods: whatever they were able to have, they plundered:
10 Both the cities and the villages and the forts did the flame consume.
11 And they took the prey, and everything they had captured, both of men and of beasts,
12 And they brought them to Moses, and Eleazar the priest, and to all the multitude of the children of Israel: but the rest of the equipment they carried to the camp in the plains of Moab near the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
13 And Moses and Eleazar the priest, and all the princes of the assembly, went out to meet them outside the camp.
14 And Moses was angry with the leaders of the army, the tribunes, and the centurions who had come from the war,
15 And he said: Why have you saved the women?

## CHAPTER XXXIII.

### CHAPTER XXXIV.

*The location and limits of the Promised Land according to the four quarters of the world; and it is commanded to be divided by lot, with the names of those who are to divide it being added.*

1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
2 Command the children of Israel, and you shall say to them: When you have entered the land of Canaan, and it has fallen to you by lot as a possession, it shall be terminated by these borders.
<margin>† Joshua 15:1</margin>
3 The southern part shall begin from the wilderness of Zin, which is next to Edom: and its boundaries shall be to the east against the Salt Sea. <note>original: "mare falsissimum" — literally the "most salty sea," referring to the Dead Sea.</note>
4 These shall circle the southern side by the Ascent of the Scorpion, <note>original: "ascensum Scorpionis" — known in Hebrew as Maaleh-akrabbim.</note> so that they pass into Zin, and reach from the south as far as Kadesh-barnea, from where the borders shall go out to the village named Hazar-addar, and extend as far as Azmon.
5 And from Azmon the boundary shall go around to the Torrent of Egypt, <note>Wadi el-Arish</note> and shall end at the shore of the Great Sea. <note>The Mediterranean Sea.</note>
6 Moreover, the western side shall begin from the Great Sea, and shall be closed by that same limit.
7 Furthermore, toward the northern side, the boundaries shall begin from the Great Sea, reaching as far as the highest mountain, <note>Likely Mount Hor in the north, distinct from the mountain where Aaron died.</note>
8 From which they shall come to Hamath, as far as the borders of Zedad:
9 And the boundaries shall go as far as Ziphron, and the village of Enan: these shall be the borders on the North side.
10 From there you shall mark out the boundaries toward the eastern side from the village of Enan as far as Shepham,
11 And from Shepham the borders shall descend to Riblah, facing the fountain of Daphnis: from there they shall reach eastward to the Sea of Chinnereth, <note>The Sea of Galilee.</note>
12 And shall extend as far as the Jordan: and at the last shall be closed by the Salt Sea. You shall have this land according to its borders all around.
13 And Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying: This shall be the land which you shall possess by lot, and which the Lord has commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
14 For the tribe of the children of Reuben by their families, and the tribe of the children of Gad according to the number of their kindreds, and also the half-tribe of Manasseh,
15 That is, two and a half tribes, have received their portion across the Jordan opposite Jericho, on the eastern side.
16 And the Lord said to Moses:

17 These are the names of the men who shall divide the land for you: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun,
18 And one prince from every tribe:
19 Whose names are these: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.

### CHAPTER XXXV.

*Forty-eight cities and their pasture lands are ordered to be assigned to the Levites, and from these, six cities of refuge for unintentional homicide; the law of intentional and unintentional homicide; no one is to be punished on the testimony of only one witness.*

1 The Lord also spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho:
<margin>† Joshua 21:2</margin>
2 Command the children of Israel that they give to the Levites, out of their possessions,
3 Cities to dwell in, and their pasture lands <note>The Latin 'suburbana' refers to the open grazing land surrounding the city walls.</note> round about: so that they may stay in the towns, and the pasture lands shall be for their cattle and beasts:
4 Which shall extend from the walls of the cities outward, round about, for a space of one thousand paces.
5 Toward the east there shall be two thousand cubits, and toward the south likewise there shall be two thousand; toward the sea also, which looks to the west, shall be the same measure, and the northern side shall end with an equal limit; and the cities shall be in the middle, and the pasture lands outside.
6 Moreover, of those towns which you shall give to the Levites, six shall be set apart for the aid of fugitives, so that he who has shed blood may flee to them: and besides these, forty-two other towns,
7 that is, forty-eight in all with their pasture lands.
8 And these cities, which shall be given from the possessions of the children of Israel, more shall be taken from those who have more, and fewer from those who have less: each shall give towns to the Levites according to the measure of their inheritance.
9 The Lord said to Moses:
10 Speak to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them:
<margin>† Deuteronomy 19:2; Joshua 20:2</margin>
11 When you have crossed the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
11 Decide which cities ought to be for the protection of fugitives who have shed blood unintentionally.
12 When the fugitive is in them, the relative of the slain <note>original: "cognatus occisi," often translated as the 'Avenger of Blood'.</note> shall not be able to kill him, until he stands before the multitude, and his case is judged.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 4:41; Joshua 20:7-8</margin>
13 † Moreover, of those cities which are set apart for the assistance of fugitives,
14 Three shall be across the Jordan, and three in the land of Canaan,
15 Both for the children of Israel and for the strangers and pilgrims, so that he who has shed blood unintentionally may flee to them.
16 If anyone strikes with iron, and he who was struck dies: he shall be guilty of murder, and he himself shall die.

<column-break/>

17 If he throws a stone, and the one struck dies: he shall be punished likewise.
18 If he dies having been struck with wood: he shall be avenged by the blood of the striker.
19 The kinsman of the slain shall kill the murderer: as soon as he apprehends him, he shall kill him.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 19:11</margin>
20 † If someone pushes a person out of hatred, or throws something at him by ambush:
21 Or, being an enemy, strikes him with his hand, and he dies: the striker shall be guilty of murder: the relative of the slain shall slay him as soon as he finds him.
22 But if by chance, and without hatred or enmity, he does any of these things,
24 And this is proven in the hearing of the people, and the question of blood is debated between the striker and the next of kin:
25 The innocent man shall be delivered from the hand of the avenger, and shall be returned by sentence to the city to which he had fled, and he shall remain there until the High Priest, who was anointed with the holy oil, dies.
26 If the slayer is found outside the borders of the cities which are assigned to exiles,
27 And is struck down by the one who is the avenger of blood: he who killed him shall be without guilt.
28 For the fugitive ought to have resided in the city until the death of the High Priest; but after he has died, the murderer shall return to his own land.
29 These things shall be everlasting and statutory in all your dwellings.
30 A murderer shall be punished based on witnesses: no one shall be condemned on the testimony of only one.
31 You shall not accept a price <note>original: "pretium," meaning a ransom or 'blood money' to avoid the death penalty.</note> from him who is guilty of blood; he himself shall die immediately.
32 Exiles and fugitives shall in no way be able to return to their own cities before the death of the High Priest.
33 Do not defile the land of your dwelling, which is stained with the blood of the innocent: nor can it otherwise be expiated, except by the blood of him who shed the blood of another.
34 And thus your possession shall be cleansed, while I dwell with you: for I am the Lord who dwells among the children of Israel.

### CHAPTER XXXVI.

*A law is brought forth that daughters who enter into a paternal inheritance should marry within their own tribe, so that tribes are not mixed through marriage and possessions are not confused.*

<margin>† Above 27:1</margin>

3 If men of another tribe take them as wives, their possession will follow them, and being transferred to another tribe, it will be diminished from our inheritance.
4 And so it will happen that when the Jubilee <note>The fiftieth year of remission, a year of celebration where debts were cancelled and land returned to original tribal owners.</note> comes, the distribution of lots will be confused, and the possession of some will pass to others.
5 Moses answered the children of Israel, and at the Lord's command, said: The tribe of the sons of Joseph has spoken rightly.

### CHAPTER IV.

*Moses exhorts the people to keep God’s commandments, using both the blessings of God and the praise they bring; by threatening those who transgress, he forbids every kind of image that might lead to idolatry, foretells his own death, and sets apart three cities of refuge across the Jordan for unintentional and accidental homicides.*

1 **AND** now, Israel, hear the laws and judgments which I teach you: so that by doing them, you may live, and entering in, you may possess the land which the Lord God of your fathers is about to give you.
2 You shall not add to the word that I speak to you, nor shall you take away from it: keep the commands of the Lord your God which I command you.
<margin>Numbers 25:4</margin>
3 Your eyes have seen all that the Lord did against Baal-peor, <note>original: "Beelphegor," a local deity of the Moabites whose worship led the Israelites into sin.</note> how he destroyed all those who followed him from your midst.
4 But you who hold fast to the Lord your God are all alive to this present day.
5 You know that I have taught you the laws and justices, just as the Lord my God commanded me: so shall you do them in the land which you are about to possess:
6 And you shall observe and fulfill them in your work: for this is your wisdom and understanding before the nations, so that when they hear all these laws, they may say: "Behold, a wise and understanding people, a great nation."
7 For there is no other nation so great that has gods drawing near to them, as our God is present to all our prayers.
8 For what other nation is so renowned as to have ceremonies, and just judgments, and a whole law such as I set before your eyes today?
9 Therefore, guard yourself and your soul carefully. Do not forget the words that your eyes have seen, and let them not slip from your heart all the days of your life. You shall teach them to your children and your grandsons,
10 From the day in which you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb, <note>Another name for Mount Sinai.</note> when the Lord spoke to me, saying: "Assemble the people to me, that they may hear my words, and learn to fear me all the time they live on the earth, and may teach their children."

11 And you came to the foot of the mountain, which burned even up to heaven: and there was darkness, and clouds, and gloom upon it.
12 And the Lord spoke to you from the midst of the fire. You heard the sound of his words, but you saw no form at all.
13 And he showed you his covenant, which he commanded you to do, and the ten words, <note>original: "decem verba," referring to what are commonly known as the Ten Commandments.</note> which he wrote on two stone tablets.

17 The likeness of any cattle that are upon the earth, or of birds flying under heaven;
18 Or of reptiles that move on the earth, or of fish that remain in the waters under the earth:

<margin>Hebrews 12:29</margin>

27 And scatter you among all the nations, and you shall remain few in number among the nations to which the Lord will lead you.
28 and there you shall serve gods which were made by the hand of men, of wood and stone, which do not see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.

30 After all the things that were foretold have found you, in the latter time you shall return to the Lord your God, and shall hear his voice.
31 Because the Lord your God is a merciful God: he will not leave you, nor utterly destroy you, nor forget the covenant in which he swore to your fathers.
32 Ask concerning the ancient days, which were before you from the day God created man upon the earth, from one end of heaven to the other, if such a thing has ever happened, or has ever been known,
33 That a people should hear the voice of God speaking from the midst of fire, as you have heard, and lived:
34 Or if God ever acted to enter and take for himself a nation from the midst of other nations, through trials, signs, and wonders, through battle and a strong hand, and an outstretched arm, and horrible visions, according to all the things the Lord your God did for you in Egypt, before your very eyes:
35 So that you might know that the Lord himself is God, and there is no other besides him.

38 To destroy nations greater and stronger than you at your coming: and to bring you in, and give you their land as a possession, as you see on this present day.

### CHAPTER V.

->*A repetition and explanation of the commandments of the Decalogue: and concerning the fear of the children of Israel when they heard the voice of God and saw the mountain burning at the proclamation of the law.*<-

1 And Moses called all Israel and said to them: Hear, Israel, the ceremonies and judgments which I speak in your ears today: learn them, and fulfill them in your work.
2 The Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb. <note>original: "in Horeb"; another name for Mount Sinai.</note>
3 He did not enter into this pact with our fathers, but with us who are present and living today.
4 Face to face he spoke to us on the mountain from the midst of the fire.
<margin>Exodus 20:2, Leviticus 26:1, Psalms 80:11</margin> 5 I was the mediator and go-between <note>original: "sequester & medius"; emphasizing Moses' role as a legal intermediary.</note> for the Lord and you at 그 time, to announce his words to you: for you feared the fire and did not go up the mountain. And he said:
6 **I am** the Lord your God, who led you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
<margin>Exodus 20:3, Psalms 80:10</margin> 7 You shall not have foreign gods in my sight.
<margin>Exodus 20:4, Leviticus 26:1, Psalms 96:7, Exodus 34:14</margin> 8 You shall not make for yourself a carved image, nor the likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is on the earth below, or that dwells in the waters under the earth.
9 You shall not adore them, and you shall not worship them. For I am the Lord your God: a jealous God, <note>original: "Deus æmulator"; a God who demands exclusive devotion.</note> visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,

<column-break/>

10 and showing mercy to many thousands of those who love me and keep my precepts.
<margin>Exodus 20:7, Leviticus 19:22, Matthew 5:33</margin> 11 You shall not use the name of the Lord your God in vain: for he who takes up his name for a trivial thing shall not go unpunished.
12 Observe the Sabbath day, to sanctify it just as the Lord your God commanded you.
13 Six days you shall labor and do all your work.
<margin>Genesis 2.2, Exodus 20:10, Hebrews 4:4</margin> 14 The seventh day is the Sabbath—that is, the rest of the Lord your God. You shall not do any work on it: neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your male or female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your beasts, nor the stranger who is within your gates: so that your male and female servant may rest, just as you do.
15 Remember that you yourself served in Egypt, and the Lord your God led you out from there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. Therefore he commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.
<margin>Exodus 20:12, Ecclesiasticus 3:9, Matthew 15:4, Mark 7:10, Ephesians 6:2</margin> 16 Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, so that you may live a long time and it may be well with you in the land which the Lord your God is about to give you.
17 You shall not kill.
18 Neither shall you commit adultery.
19 And you shall not steal.
20 You shall not speak false testimony against your neighbor.
<margin>Matthew 5:28, Romans 7:7</margin> 21 You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife: nor his house, nor his field, nor his male or female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is his.
22 The Lord spoke these words to your whole multitude on the mountain, from the midst of the fire and the cloud and the darkness, with a great voice, adding nothing more; and he wrote them on two stone tablets, which he delivered to me.
23 But after you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness and saw the mountain burning, you all approached me—the leaders of the tribes and the elders—and you said:
24 "Behold, the Lord our God has shown us his majesty and his greatness: we have heard his voice from the midst of the fire, and we have proven today that though God speaks with man, man may yet live.
25 Why then should we die, and why should this great fire devour us? For if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any longer, we shall die.
26 What is all flesh, that it should hear the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire as we have heard, and be able to live?
27 You go nearer instead: and hear all the things the Lord our God shall say to you: and you shall speak to us, and we, hearing them, will do them."
28 When the Lord had heard this, he said to me: "I have heard the voice of the words of this people which they have spoken to you: they have spoken all things well.
29 Who will grant that they might have such a mind as to fear me and keep all my mandates at all times, so that it might be well with them and their children forever?
30 Go and tell them: Return to your tents.
31 But you, stay here with me: and I will speak to you all my mandates, ceremonies, and judgments: which you shall teach them, so that they may do them in the land which I will give them for a possession."
32 Observe, therefore, and do the things which the Lord God has commanded you: you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left:
33 but walk in the way the Lord commanded.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*The Lord is to be loved with all one's heart, and His commandments are to be carefully observed and impressed upon descendants.*<-

These are the commandments, ceremonies, and judgments which the Lord your God commanded that I should teach you, and that you should do them in the land into which you are crossing to possess:
2 So that you may fear the Lord your God, and keep all His mandates and precepts which I command you, and your children, and your grandchildren, all the days of your life, so that your days may be prolonged.
3 Hear, O Israel, and observe to do what the Lord has commanded you, so that it may be well with you, and you may be multiplied further, just as the Lord the God of your fathers promised you a land flowing with milk and honey.
4 Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one.
<margin>† Below 11:13; Matthew 22:37; Mark 12:30; Luke 10:27.</margin>

7 And you shall tell them to your children, and you shall meditate upon them sitting in your house, and walking on a journey, sleeping and rising up.
8 And you shall bind them like a sign upon your hand, and they shall be moved between your eyes <note>This refers to the practice of wearing phylacteries or tefillin, small leather boxes containing scripture.</note>,
9 And you shall write them upon the threshold and the doors of your house.
10 And when the Lord your God has brought you into the land for which He swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: and has given you great and excellent cities which you did not build,
11 Houses full of all riches which you did not furnish, cisterns which you did not dig, vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant,
12 And you have eaten and been satisfied:
<margin>† Below 10:20; Matthew 4:10; Luke 4:8.</margin>
13 Beware diligently, lest you forget the Lord, who led you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. † You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve Him alone, and you shall swear by His name.
14 You shall not go after the foreign gods of all the nations that are round about you:
15 Because the Lord your God in your midst is a jealous God <note>original: "Deus æmulator"; a God who demands exclusive devotion and is zealous for His people's loyalty.</note>: lest at any time the fury of the Lord your God be kindled against you, and He take you away from the face of the earth.
<margin>† Matthew 4:7; Luke 4:11.</margin>
16 † You shall not tempt the Lord your God, as you tempted Him in the place of temptation <note>original: "in loco tentationis"; a reference to Massah, where the Israelites complained about the lack of water.</note>.

18 And do what is pleasing and good in the sight of the Lord, so that it may be well with you: and that entering in, you may possess the excellent land about which the Lord swore to your fathers,
19 That He would destroy all your enemies before you, as He has spoken.

25 And He will be merciful to us, if we keep and do all His precepts before the Lord our God, as He has commanded us."

### CHAPTER VII.

->*No alliance is to be made with the nations, but their altars, groves, and idols must be destroyed: having recalled God's benefits, He promises help and abundance in all things, provided they observe His commandments.*<-

<margin>† Exodus 23:23 and 33:2.</margin>
When the Lord your God has brought you into the land which you are entering to possess, and has destroyed many nations before you—the Hittite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, the Canaanite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite—seven nations of much greater number than you are, and stronger than you.
<margin>† Exodus 23:32 and 34:15-16.</margin>
2 And the Lord your God has delivered them to you, striking them down even to utter destruction. † You shall not enter into a treaty with them; nor shall you have mercy on them,
<margin>† Exodus 34:16.</margin>
3 Nor shall you join in marriage with them. You shall not give your daughter to his son, nor shall you take his daughter for your son:
4 Because she will seduce your son, lest he follow me, and so that he may rather serve foreign gods: and the fury of the Lord will be kindled, and He will destroy you quickly.
<margin>† Exodus 23:24; Below 12:3 and 16:21.</margin>
5 But rather you shall do these things to them: † Overturn their altars, and break their statues, and cut down their groves <note>original: "lucos"; these were sacred trees or poles used in the worship of the fertility goddess Asherah.</note>, and burn their carvings.
<margin>† Below 14:2 and 26:18.</margin>
6 † Because you are a holy people to the Lord your God. † The Lord your God has chosen you, so that you might be His special people <note>original: "populus peculiaris"; a treasured and distinct possession.</note> out of all the peoples who are upon the earth.
7 Not because you surpassed all nations in number was the Lord joined to you and chose you, since you are fewer than all other peoples:
8 But because the Lord loved you, and kept the oath which He swore to your fathers: and He led you out with a strong hand, and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh the king of Egypt.
9 And you shall know that the Lord your God, He is the strong and faithful God, keeping His covenant and mercy for those who love Him and for those who keep His commandments, unto a thousand generations:
10 And repaying those who hate Him immediately, so that He destroys them and delays no further, instantly restoring to them what they deserve.
11 Keep therefore the precepts and ceremonies and judgments which I command you today to do.
12 If after you have heard these judgments, you keep them and do them, the Lord your God will also keep the covenant for you, and the mercy which He swore to your fathers:
13 And He will love you and multiply you, and will bless the fruit of your womb, and the fruit of your land, your grain, and your vintage and oil, and your herds, the flocks of your sheep upon the land for which He swore to your fathers that He would give it to you.

### CHAPTER VIII.

->The benefits and afflictions which the Lord had sent upon them in the desert are recalled, lest they become forgetful of them and of their God.<-

1 Every commandment which I command you today, take care diligently to do: so that you may live, and be multiplied, and entering in, you may possess the land for which the Lord swore to your fathers.

2 And you shall remember the whole journey by which the Lord your God led you for forty years through the desert, that He might afflict you and test you, and that the things turning in your mind might be made known, whether you would keep His commandments or not.

<margin>† Matthew 4:4; Luke 4:4.</margin>
3 He afflicted you with want, and gave you Manna as food, which you and your fathers did not know: to show you that † man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.

4 Your garment, with which you were covered, did not fail because of age, and your foot was not worn down, though it is now the fortieth year.

<column-break/>

5 So that you may reflect in your heart, that just as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God has disciplined you,

6 That you may keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and walk in His ways, and fear Him.

7 For the Lord your God will bring you into a good land, a land of rivers and waters and springs: in whose plains and mountains the depths of rivers break forth:

8 A land of wheat, barley, and vineyards, in which figs, pomegranates, and olive groves grow: a land of oil and honey.

9 Where without any scarcity you shall eat your bread, and you shall enjoy an abundance of all things: whose stones are iron, and from whose mountains ores of copper are mined:

10 So that when you have eaten and are satisfied, you may bless the Lord your God for the excellent land which He has given to you.

11 Observe and beware that you never forget the Lord your God, and neglect His commandments and judgments and ceremonies, which I command you today:

12 Lest after you have eaten and are satisfied, and have built beautiful houses and lived in them,

13 And have had herds of oxen and flocks of sheep, and plenty of silver and gold and all things,

14 Your heart be lifted up, and you do not remember the Lord your God, who led you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery:

<margin>† Numbers 20:9, 21.</margin>
15 And was your leader in the great and terrible wilderness, † in which there was the serpent with the burning breath, and the scorpion and the <term>dipsas</term> <note>original: "dipsas"; a type of serpent whose bite was said to cause unquenchable thirst, or a reference to a parched region</note>, and no water at all; † who brought out streams from the hardest rock,

<margin>† Exodus 17:6.</margin>
16 And † fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know. And after He afflicted and tested you, at the last He had mercy on you,

<margin>† Exodus 16:14.</margin>
17 Lest you should say in your heart: "My own strength and the power of my hand have provided all these things for me."

18 But remember the Lord your God, that He Himself provided strength for you, so that He might fulfill His covenant, about which He swore to your fathers, as the present day indicates.

19 But if, having forgotten the Lord your God, you follow foreign gods, and serve and adore them: behold, I now predict to you that you shall utterly perish.

20 Just as the nations which the Lord destroyed at your entry, so also you shall perish, if you are disobedient to the voice of the Lord your God.

### CHAPTER IX.

->Pride is restrained, lest future victories be attributed to themselves but only to the Lord; Moses reminds the people of their murmurings and sins in the desert, and his own intercession for the people.<-

1 Hear, O Israel: Today you shall cross the Jordan, to possess nations very great and stronger than you, cities huge and walled up to the sky,

2 A people great and tall, the sons of the <term>Enacim</term> <note>original: "Enacim"; the Anakim, a race of giants mentioned in the Bible</note>, whom you yourself saw and heard of, against whom no one can stand in opposition.

3 You shall know therefore today that the Lord your God Himself will pass before you as a consuming and devouring fire, who shall crush them and destroy and scatter them quickly before your face, just as He spoke to you.

### CHAPTER X.

*The restoration of the second tablets, the duties of the Levites: fear and love of God should move us to keep the commandments; the foreskin of the heart is to be circumcised, strangers are to be loved, and oaths are to be sworn by the name of God.*

<margin>† Exodus 34:1.</margin>
1 AT † that time the Lord said to me: "Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain; and you shall make a wooden ark,
2 And I will write on the tablets the words that were on the ones you broke before, and you shall place them in the ark."
3 Therefore I made an ark of <term>shittim wood<note>Acacia wood, known for its durability.</note></term>. And when I had carved two stone tablets like the first ones, I went up the mountain, holding them in my hands.
4 And He wrote on the tablets, according to what He had written before, the Ten Words <note>The Ten Commandments.</note> which the Lord spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire when the people were gathered; and He gave them to me.
5 Returning from the mountain, I came down and placed the tablets in the ark I had made, where they remain to this day, just as the Lord commanded me.
<margin>† Numbers 33:31; 20:28-29.</margin>

8 At that time He set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord, to stand before Him in ministry, and to give blessings in His name even to the present day.
9 For this reason, Levi has no portion or possession among his brothers, because the Lord Himself is his inheritance, as the Lord your God promised him.
10 And I stayed on the mountain, as before, for forty days and nights; and the Lord heard me even this time, and He was unwilling to destroy you.
11 And He said to me: "Go, and lead the people, so that they may enter and possess the land which I swore to their fathers I would give them."

### CHAPTER XII.

*He commands that idolatry be destroyed; that tithes and first-fruits be rendered; that sacrifices be performed and eaten in a specific place; and that blood and all unclean food be avoided.*

These are the precepts and judgments which you must perform in the land that the Lord God of your fathers is about to give to you, so that you may possess it all the days that you shall walk upon the soil.
2 Utterly destroy all the places where the nations you are to possess worshiped their gods, upon the high mountains, and the hills, and under every leafy tree.
<margin>† Above 7:25; 2 Maccabees 12:40.</margin>
3 † Tear down their altars and break their statues; burn their <term>sacred groves<note>original: "lucos". These were ritual forests or wooden poles dedicated to Canaanite deities like Asherah.</note></term> with fire, and crush their idols into pieces: destroy their names from those places.
4 You shall not do so to the Lord your God.
5 Instead, you shall come to the place which the Lord your God shall choose out of all your tribes, to set His name there and to dwell in it.
6 And there you shall offer your <term>burnt offerings<note>original: "holocausta". Offerings entirely consumed by fire as a sign of total devotion.</note></term> and your victims, your tithes and the first-fruits of your hands, your vows and gifts, and the firstborn of your herds and sheep.
7 And there you shall eat in the sight of the Lord your God; and you and your households shall rejoice in all the things to which you have set your hand, in which the Lord your God has blessed you.
8 You shall not do there the things that we do here today, where every man does what seems right to himself.
9 For until the present time, you have not come to the rest and the possession which the Lord your God is about to give you.
10 You shall cross the Jordan and dwell in the land which the Lord your God will give to you, so that you may rest from all your enemies round about, and live without any fear
11 In the place which the Lord your God shall choose, so that His name may be in it. There you shall bring all that I command: burnt offerings, and victims, and tithes, and the first-fruits of your hands, and whatever is excellent among the gifts that you shall vow to the Lord.
12 There you shall feast before the Lord your God—you, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite who dwells in your cities (for he has no other portion or possession among you).
13 Be careful that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see;
14 But in that place which the Lord shall choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer victims, and you shall do whatever I command you.
15 But if you wish to eat, and the eating of meat delights you, kill and eat according to the blessing of the Lord your God, which He has given you in your cities. Whether it be <term>unclean<note>Referring to ritual impurity or physical blemish.</note></term>—that is, spotted or weak—or <term>clean<note>Ritually pure and without blemish.</note></term>—that is, whole and without spot, such as may be offered—you may eat it as you would the gazelle or the deer.
16 Only without the eating of blood, which you shall pour out upon the earth like water.
17 You may not eat in your towns the tithe of your grain, wine, and oil, nor the first-

<column-break/>

born of your herds and flocks, nor anything you have vowed, nor what you wish to offer spontaneously, nor the first-fruits of your hands.
18 But you shall eat them before the Lord your God in the place which the Lord your God shall choose—you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male and female servant, and the Levite who stays in your cities. And you shall rejoice and be refreshed before the Lord your God in all things to which you extend your hand.
19 Take care that you do not abandon the Levite during all the time you live in the land.
<margin>† Genesis 28:14; Exodus 34:24; Below 29:8.</margin>
20 † When the Lord your God has enlarged your borders, as He spoke to you, and you wish to eat the meat that your soul desires:
21 If the place which the Lord your God has chosen to set His name there is far away, you shall kill from the herds and flocks which you have, just as I have commanded you, and you shall eat in your towns as it pleases you.
22 Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so shall you eat them: both the clean and the unclean shall eat of them together.
23 Only take care of this: that you do not eat the blood. For their blood is the <term>soul<note>original: "anima". In biblical thought, the "life" or "breath" of a creature was believed to reside in its blood.</note></term>, and therefore you must not eat the soul with the meat.
24 Instead, you shall pour it upon the earth like water,
25 So that it may be well with you and your children after you, when you have done what is pleasing in the sight of the Lord.
26 But the things you have sanctified and vowed to the Lord, you shall take up and come to the place which the Lord shall choose.
27 And you shall offer your oblations—the meat and the blood—upon the altar of the Lord your God. You shall pour the blood of the victims on the altar, but the meat you yourself shall eat.
28 Observe and hear all these things that I command you, so that it may be well with you and your children after you forever, when you have done what is good and pleasing in the sight of the Lord your God.
<margin>† Below 19:1.</margin>
29 † When the Lord your God has destroyed before your face the nations which you shall enter to possess, and you have possessed them and dwelt in their land:
30 Beware that you do not imitate them after they have been overthrown at your entry, and that you do not seek out their ceremonies, saying: "Just as these nations worshiped their gods, so I also will worship."
31 You shall not do likewise to the Lord your God. For they have done for their gods all the abominations which the Lord detests, even offering their sons and daughters and burning them with fire.
32 What I command you, that only shall you do for the Lord: neither add anything, nor take anything away.

4 Follow the Lord your God, and

### CHAPTER XV.

->*The law of remission in the seventh year and for whom it is performed: concerning the Hebrew servant who does not wish to be set free: concerning the firstborn to be sanctified to the Lord and eaten.*<-

1 In the seventh year you shall grant a remission, <note>original: "remissionem". This refers to the Sabbatical year (Shmita), where debts were canceled and the land rested.</note>
2 Which shall be celebrated in this order. He to whom anything is owed by a friend or neighbor and brother, will not be able to demand it back, because it is the year of the Lord’s remission.
3 You shall demand it from the foreigner and the stranger; but you shall not have the power to demand it from a citizen and neighbor.
4 And there shall be no one altogether needy or a beggar among you: so that the Lord your God may bless you in the land which He is about to deliver to you as a possession.
5 If, however, you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and keep all the things which He has commanded, and which I command you today, He will bless you, as He promised.
6 You shall lend to many nations, and you yourself shall receive a loan from no one. You shall rule over many nations, and no one shall rule over you.
7 If one of your brothers, who dwell within the gates of your city in the land which the Lord your God is about to give you, falls into poverty: you shall not harden your heart, nor close your hand,
<margin>Matthew 5:42. Luke 6:34.</margin>
8 But you shall open it to the poor man, and you shall lend him what you perceive he needs.
9 Beware lest perhaps an impious thought should steal upon you, and you say in your heart: The seventh year of remission is approaching; and you turn your eyes away from your poor brother, refusing to lend him what he asks: lest he cry against you to the Lord, and it become a sin for you.
10 But you shall give to him: nor shall you act with any craftiness in relieving his necessities: so that the Lord your God may bless you at all times, and in all things to which you set your hand.
<margin>Matthew 26:11.</margin>
11 The poor will not be lacking in the land of your dwelling: <note>This verse is famously cited by Jesus in the Gospels to acknowledge the persistent reality of poverty despite the ideal of verse 4.</note> therefore I command you to open your hand to your needy and poor brother who lives with you in the land.
<margin>Exodus 21:2. Jeremiah 34:14.</margin>
12 When your Hebrew brother or a Hebrew woman is sold to you, and has served you for six years, in the seventh year you shall let them go free:
13 And when you grant them freedom, you shall by no means let them go away empty-handed:
14 But you shall provide a traveling-allowance from your flocks, and from your threshing floor, and your winepress, with which the Lord your God has blessed you.
15 Remember that you yourself served in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God liberated you, and therefore I now command this of you.
16 But if he should say: I do not wish to leave: because he loves you and your house, and feels that it is well with him in your service:
17 You shall take an awl, and pierce his ear in the door of your house, and he shall serve you forever; you shall do likewise to your female servant.
18 Do not turn your eyes away from them when you release them as free people: since they have served you for six years according to the wages of a hired hand: so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works that you do.

<column-break/>

19 Of the firstborn that are born in your herds and in your sheep, whatever is of the male sex, you shall sanctify to the Lord your God. You shall not work with the firstborn of an ox, and you shall not shear the firstborn of the sheep.
20 In the sight of the Lord your God you shall eat them every year, in the place which the Lord shall choose, you and your household.
<margin>Leviticus 22:20-21. Ecclesiasticus 35:14.</margin>
21 But if it has a blemish, or is lame, or blind, or in any part deformed or weak, it shall not be sacrificed to the Lord your God.
22 But you shall eat it within the gates of your city: the clean and the unclean alike shall feed on them, as if it were a roe or a deer. <note>In this context, "clean and unclean" refers to the ritual state of the people eating, not the animal itself.</note>
23 This alone you shall observe: that you do not eat their blood, but pour it out upon the earth like water.

### CHAPTER XVI.

->*The three principal solemnities of the year: Unleavened Bread, Weeks, and Tabernacles: concerning the appointment of just judges, and avoiding occasions of idolatry.*<-

1 Observe the month of new grain, and of the first time of spring, so that you may perform the <term>Passover<note>original: "Phase". Derived from the Hebrew 'Pesach', referring to the passing over of the angel of death in Egypt.</note></term> to the Lord your God: because in that month the Lord your God led you out of Egypt by night.
2 And you shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God from the sheep and from the oxen, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, so that His name may dwell there.
3 You shall not eat leavened bread with it: for seven days you shall eat it without leaven, the bread of affliction, because you departed from Egypt in fear: so that you may remember the day of your departure from Egypt all the days of your life.
4 No leaven shall appear in all your borders for seven days, and none of the meat that was sacrificed in the evening on the first day shall remain until the morning.
5 You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of your cities which the Lord your God is about to give you,
6 But in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, so that His name may dwell there: you shall sacrifice the Passover in the evening at the setting of the sun, at the time when you departed from Egypt.
7 And you shall cook and eat in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, and rising in the morning you shall go to your dwellings.
8 For six days you shall eat unleavened bread: and on the seventh day, because it is the assembly of the Lord your God, you shall do no work.
9 You shall count seven weeks for yourself from that day on which you first put the sickle to the corn.
10 And you shall celebrate the festival day of Weeks to the Lord your God, a voluntary offering of your hand, which you shall offer according to the blessing of the Lord your God:
11 And you shall feast before the Lord your God—you, your son, and your daughter, your male servant, and your female servant, and the Levite who is within your gates, the stranger and the orphan and the widow who dwell with you: in the place which the Lord your God shall choose, so that His name may dwell there:
12 And you shall remember that you were a servant in Egypt: and you shall keep and do the things that are commanded.
13 You shall also celebrate the solemnity of Tabernacles for seven days, when you have gathered your grain from the threshing floor and your wine from the press:

<meta>catchword: 14 And</meta>

14 And you shall feast in your festival, you, your son & daughter, your male servant & female servant, the Levite also & the stranger, the orphan and the widow who are within your gates.
15 For seven days you shall celebrate the feast to the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose: and the Lord your God will bless you in all your crops, & in every work of your hands, and you shall be in joy.
<margin>† Exodus 23:15 & 34:10. Sirach 35:6.</margin>
16 Three times a year all your males shall appear in the sight of the Lord your God, in the place which he shall choose: in the solemnity of unleavened bread, in the solemnity of weeks, & in the solemnity of tabernacles. † They shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed.

<margin>† Exodus 23:8. Leviticus 19:15. Above 1:17. Sirach 20:31.</margin>
19 Nor shall they lean to one side. † You shall not show favoritism, <note>original: "accipies personam", literally "accept a person." It refers to partiality in judgment.</note> nor take gifts: because gifts blind the eyes of the wise, & change the words of the just.
20 Justly you shall pursue what is just: so that you may live & possess the land, which the Lord your God shall give you.
21 You shall not plant a grove, <note>original: "lucum". These were sacred trees or poles associated with the goddess Asherah, common in pagan worship.</note> nor any tree near the altar of the Lord your God.
22 Nor shall you make for yourself, nor set up a statue: <note>original: "statuam". This refers to a cultic pillar or monument used for idolatry.</note> which things the Lord your God hates.

->### CHAPTER XVII.<-

->*Sacrifices to be chosen with care; idolatry to be punished; in grave difficulty one must recur to the high priest and his council; and what must be observed in choosing a king.*<-

1 You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God a sheep or an ox in which there is a blemish, or any defect: because it is an abomination to the Lord your God.
2 When there shall be found among you, within one of your gates which the Lord your God shall give you, a man or woman who does evil in the sight of the Lord your God, & transgresses his covenant,
3 So that they go & serve foreign gods, & adore them, the sun & the moon, & all the host of heaven, which I have not commanded:
4 And this is reported to you, and hearing it you have inquired diligently, & found it to be true, and that an abomination has been committed in Israel:
5 You shall lead the man and woman, who have committed this most wicked thing, to the gates of your city, and they shall be overwhelmed with stones.
<margin>† Below 19:15. Matthew 18:16. 2 Corinthians 13:1.</margin>
6 † By the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he perish who is to be put to death. Let no one be killed on the testimony of only one person against him.
<margin>† Above 13:9.</margin>
7 The hand of the witnesses shall be the first to kill him, † & the hand of the rest of the people shall be sent last: so that you may take away the evil from among you.
<margin>† Above 13:9.</margin>
8 If you perceive a judgment to be difficult & ambiguous among you between blood & blood, cause & cause, leprosy & leprosy: <note>This refers to cases involving homicide, civil disputes, or ritual impurity.</note> and you see that within your gates the words of judgment vary: rise, and go up to the place which the Lord your God shall choose.
<margin>† 2 Chronicles 19:8.</margin>
9 † And you shall come to the priests of the Levite lineage, & to the judge who shall be at that time: and you shall ask of them, and they will show you the truth of the judgment.

<column-break/>

10 And you shall do whatever they say who oversee the place which the Lord has chosen, and whatever they teach you
11 According to his law: and you shall follow their sentence, nor shall you turn to the right nor to the left.
12 But he who acts proudly, refusing to obey the command of the priest, who at that time ministers to the Lord your God, and the decree of the judge, that man shall die, and you shall take away the evil from Israel:
13 And all the people hearing it shall fear, so that no one from then on may swell with pride.
14 When you have entered the land which the Lord your God will give you and possess it, and have lived in it, and you say: I will set a king over me, just as all the nations around me have:
15 You shall appoint him whom the Lord your God shall choose from the number of your brothers. You cannot make a man of another nation king, who is not your brother.
16 And when he is appointed, he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor lead the people back into Egypt, bolstered by the number of cavalry, especially since the Lord has commanded you that you should by no means return any longer by that same way.
17 He shall not have many wives, who might entice his soul, nor immense weights of silver and gold.
18 After he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he shall copy <note>original: "describet", meaning to transcribe or write out.</note> for himself this Deuteronomy <note>original: "Deuteronomium". Literally "the second law," referring here to a copy of the legal code.</note> of the law in a volume, receiving a copy from the priests of the Levite tribe,
19 And he shall have it with him, and read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, & to keep his words & ceremonies, which are commanded in the law.
20 Nor let his heart be lifted up in pride over his brothers, nor turn to the right side or the left, so that he and his sons may reign for a long time over Israel.

->### CHAPTER XVIII.<-

->*Let the offerings and sacrifices fall to the priests and Levites as their possession: all superstition is to be avoided: concerning the true prophet to be raised up, and the false prophet to be killed: how the true is to be discerned from the false.*<-

<margin>† Numbers 18:20. Above 10:9. 1 Corinthians 9:13.</margin>
1 The † priests and Levites, and all who are of the same tribe, shall not have a part and inheritance with the rest of Israel, because they shall eat the sacrifices of the Lord, and his offerings,
2 And they shall receive nothing else from the possession of their brothers: for the Lord himself is their inheritance, just as he spoke to them.
3 This shall be the right <note>original: "judicium", here meaning the legal due or share.</note> of the priests from the people, & from those who offer victims: whether they sacrifice an ox or a sheep, they shall give the priest the shoulder and the stomach:
<margin>† Numbers 18:11.</margin>
4 † The firstfruits of grain, wine, & oil, & a part of the wool from the shearing of the sheep.
5 For the Lord your God chose him from all your tribes, so that he might stand & minister to the name of the Lord, he and his sons forever.
6 If a Levite departs from one of your cities from all Israel in which he dwells, and wishes to come, desiring the place which the Lord shall choose,
7 He shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, just as all his brothers the Levites, who stand at that time before the Lord.

17 And the Lord said to me: They have spoken all things well.

19 But whoever will not hear his words, which he shall speak in my name, I will be the avenger.
20 But the prophet who, corrupted by arrogance, chooses to speak in my name the things I did not command him to say, or speaks in the name of foreign gods, shall be put to death.
21 And if you respond in silent thought: How can I understand the word which the Lord has not spoken?
22 You shall have this sign: If that prophet has predicted something in the name of the Lord, and it does not happen: the Lord has not spoken this, but the prophet has devised it through the swelling of his own mind <note>original: "tumorem animi sui", meaning through his own pride or presumption.</note>: and therefore you shall not fear him.

# C H A P T E R  X I X.

->Six cities of refuge are to be set apart, and who may safely flee to them, and who may not: concerning true and false witnesses, and not moving boundaries.<-

<margin>† Numbers 35:11. Joshua 20:2.</margin>
1 When the Lord your God has destroyed the nations whose land he is about to deliver to you, and you possess it, and dwell in its cities and in its houses:
2 † You shall set apart for yourself three cities in the midst of the land which the Lord your God will give you to possess.
3 Preparing the way diligently: and you shall divide the entire province of your land into three equal parts: so that he who is a fugitive on account of homicide may have a place nearby where he can escape.
4 This shall be the law of the fugitive manslayer whose life is to be preserved: He who has struck his neighbor unknowingly, and who is proved to have had no hatred against him yesterday or the day before <note>A Hebrew idiom meaning "previously" or "in times past."</note>:
5 But went with him simply into the forest to

<column-break/>

cut wood, and in the cutting of the wood the axe flew from his hand, and the iron slipping from the handle struck and killed his friend: he shall flee to one of the aforementioned cities and live:
6 Lest perhaps his neighbor, whose blood was shed, spurred by grief, should pursue and seize him if the way was too long, and strike the soul of him who is not guilty of death: because it is shown that he had no previous hatred against the one who was killed.
7 Therefore I command you that you divide three cities of equal distance between one another.
<margin>† Genesis 28:14. Exodus 34:24. Above 12:20.</margin>
8 † But when the Lord your God has enlarged your borders, as he swore to your fathers, and has given you all the land which he promised to them,
9 (If however you keep his commandments, and do what I command you today, that you love the Lord your God, and walk in his ways at all times) you shall add to yourself three other cities, and you shall double the number of the three cities mentioned above:
10 So that innocent blood is not shed in the midst of the land which the Lord your God will give you to possess, lest you be guilty of blood.
<margin>† Numbers 35:20.</margin>
11 † But if anyone, hating his neighbor, lies in wait for his life, and rising up strikes him, and he dies, and he flees to one of the aforementioned cities,
12 The elders of that city shall send and take him from the place of refuge, and shall deliver him into the hand of the next of kin <note>The "avenger of blood," usually the victim's closest relative responsible for justice.</note> whose blood was shed, and he shall die.
13 You shall not pity him, and you shall take away innocent blood from Israel, so that it may be well with you.
14 You shall not take and move the boundaries of your neighbor, which the predecessors fixed in your possession, which the Lord your God will give you in the land you receive to possess.
<margin>† Above 17:6. Matthew 18:16. 2 Corinthians 13:1.</margin>
15 † A single witness shall not stand against anyone, whatever the sin or crime may be; but by the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall stand.
16 If a lying witness stands against a man, accusing him of transgression,
17 Both of them, whose cause it is, shall stand before the Lord in the sight of the priests and the judges who are in those days.
<margin>† Daniel 13:62.</margin>
18 † And when, searching most diligently, they find that the false witness has spoken a lie against his brother:
19 They shall do to him just as he thought to do to his brother, and you shall take away the evil from your midst:
20 So that others, hearing it, may have fear, and by no means dare to do such things.
<margin>† Exodus 21:23, 24. Leviticus 24:20. Matthew 5:38.</margin>
21 You shall not pity him, † but you shall require life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

# C H A P T E R  X X.

->Who at the time of battle are to be sent home: how the laws of war are to be kept; which trees are to be cut down to build engines, and which are to be left.<-

1 If you go out to war against your enemies, and see cavalry and chariots, and a multitude of the adversary's army greater than you have, you shall not fear them: because the Lord your God is with you, who led you out of the land of Egypt.

2 And when the battle is now approaching, the priest shall stand before the line of battle, and he shall speak thus to the people:
3 Hear, O Israel, today you are joining battle against your enemies; let not your heart be afraid, do not fear, do not give way, nor should you be in dread of them:
4 Because the Lord your God is in your midst, and he will fight for you against your adversaries, to rescue you from danger.
<margin>† 1 Maccabees 3:56.</margin>
5 The commanders also, through each company, shall proclaim in the hearing of the army: † Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he should perhaps die in the war, and another man dedicate it.
6 Who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not yet made it common <note>original: "communem". This refers to the Jewish law where the fruit of a new vineyard was not eaten for the first three years, and was consecrated in the fourth; only in the fifth year did it become "common" for general use.</note> so that everyone may eat of it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he should perhaps die in the war, and another man perform his duty there.
7 Who is the man who has betrothed a wife and has not yet taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he should perhaps die in the war, and another man take her.
<margin>† Judges 7:3.</margin>
8 When these things have been said, they shall add the rest and speak to the people: † Who is the man who is fearful and faint-hearted? Let him go and return to his house, lest he make the hearts of his brothers fear, just as he himself is terrified by fear.
9 And when the commanders of the army have finished speaking and are silent, each one shall prepare his own ranks for fighting.
10 Whenever you approach a city to attack it, you shall first offer it peace.
11 If it receives the offer and opens its gates to you, all the people who are in it shall be saved, and shall serve you under tribute.
12 But if it refuses to enter into a treaty and begins war against you, you shall besiege it.
13 And when the Lord your God has delivered it into your hand, you shall strike down everything in it of the male sex with the edge of the sword,
14 Except for the women and children, the cattle, and the other things that are in the city. You shall divide all the plunder for the army, and you shall eat from the spoils of your enemies, which the Lord your God has given to you.
15 Thus you shall do to all the cities which are very far off from you, and are not among these cities which you are to receive as a possession.
16 But of these cities which shall be given to you, you shall permit nothing at all to live:
17 Instead, you shall kill them with the edge of the sword—namely, the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Canaanite, the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite—just as the Lord your God has commanded you:
18 Lest they perhaps teach you to do all the abominations which they themselves have worked for their own gods, and you sin against the Lord your God.
19 When you have besieged a city for a long time and have surrounded it with fortifications to capture it, you shall not cut down the trees from which food can be eaten, nor should you devastate the surrounding region with axes: since it is a tree and not a man, it cannot increase the number of those fighting against you.
20 But if there are any trees that are not fruit-bearing, but are wild and suitable for other uses, cut them down and build siege engines until you capture the city that fights against you.

### C A P T E R XXI.

->*Caution regarding a hidden murder; a woman captured in war; the firstborn son of an unloved wife; a rebellious son; and him who is hanged on a tree.*<-

When a corpse of a murdered man is found in the land which the Lord your God is about to give to you, and the person guilty of the slaughter is unknown,
2 Your elders and judges shall go out and measure the distances from the location of the corpse to each of the surrounding cities:
3 And whichever city they see to be nearer than the others, the elders of that city shall take a heifer from the herd that has not pulled a yoke nor broken the earth with a plow:
4 And they shall lead her to a rough and rocky valley that has never been plowed or received seed: and there they shall break the neck of the heifer.
5 And the priests, the sons of Levi, shall approach—whom the Lord your God has chosen to minister to him and to bless in his name, and by whose word every matter, and whatever is clean or unclean, shall be judged.
6 And the elders of that city shall come to the slain man and wash their hands over the heifer that was struck down in the valley,
7 And they shall say: Our hands did not shed this blood, nor did our eyes see it.
8 Be merciful, O Lord, to your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, and do not lay innocent blood to the charge of your people Israel. And the guilt of blood shall be taken away from them:
9 But you shall be free from the blood of the innocent which was shed, when you have done what the Lord commanded.
10 If you go out to battle against your enemies, and the Lord your God delivers them into your hand, and you lead them away captive,
11 And you see among the number of the captives a beautiful woman, and fall in love with her and wish to have her as a wife,
12 You shall bring her into your house: she shall shave her hair and trim her nails,
13 And she shall put off the garment in which she was captured: and sitting in your house, she shall mourn for her father and mother for one month: and afterward you shall go in to her, and sleep with her, and she shall be your wife.
14 But if afterward she does not please your mind, you shall let her go free; you cannot sell her for money, nor oppress her by your power: because you have humbled her.
15 If a man has two wives, one beloved and the other unloved <note>original: "odiosam", literally "hateful" or "hated," but in this legal context, it refers to the less-preferred wife in a polygamous marriage.</note>, and they have borne children to him, and the son of the unloved wife is the firstborn,
16 And he wishes to divide his property among his sons: he cannot make the son of the beloved wife the firstborn, or prefer him over the son of the unloved wife,
17 † But he shall acknowledge the son of the unloved wife as the firstborn, and shall give him a double portion of all that he has: for this son is the beginning of his children, and to him the rights of the firstborn are due.
18 If a man has a stubborn and defiant son, who will not hear the command of his father or mother, and being corrected, refuses to obey:
19 They shall take hold of him and lead him to the elders of that city, and to the gate of judgment,
20 And they shall say to them: This son of ours is defiant and stubborn, he refuses to listen to our warnings, he gives himself to revelry, and to luxury, and to banquets:
