## CHAPTER XXII.

*Piety to be exercised toward the property of a neighbor: concerning the clothing of the opposite sex, concerning a bird’s nest found, concerning building a wall around the roof of a house, concerning not mixing things of different kinds, concerning fringes, concerning the signs of virginity, concerning adultery, concerning a woman violated in the city or in the field, and concerning not marrying a father's wife.*

1 <margin>† Exod. 23:4.</margin> You shall not see your brother's ox, or his sheep wandering, and pass by them: but you shall lead them back to your brother,
2 Even if your brother is not nearby, or you do not know him: you shall lead them into your house, and they shall be with you as long as your brother seeks them, until he receives them back.
3 You shall do the same with his donkey, and with his clothing, and with every thing of your brother’s that is lost: if you find it, do not neglect it as if it belonged to another.
4 If you see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen in the way, you shall not disregard it, but you shall help him lift it up.
5 A woman shall not be clothed in a man’s garment, nor shall a man use a woman’s garment: for he who does these things is abominable before God.
6 If, while walking along the way, you find a bird's nest in a tree or on the ground, and the mother sitting upon the young or the eggs: you shall not take her with her young:
7 But you shall let her go, keeping the young you have taken: so that it may be well with you, and you may live for a long time.
8 When you build a new house, you shall make a wall <note>A low wall or parapet for safety on the flat roofs typical of the region.</note> around the roof: lest blood be shed in your house, and you be guilty if someone should slip and fall headlong.
9 You shall not sow your vineyard with a second kind of seed: lest both the seed which you have sown, and the things that grow from the vineyard, be forfeited together <note>original: "sanctificentur", literally 'be sanctified' or 'set apart,' meaning the crop could not be used by the owner because it violated the law against mixing.</note>.
10 You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
11 You shall not wear a garment that is woven of wool and linen together.
12 <margin>† Num. 15:38.</margin> You shall make tassels on the fringes at the four corners of your cloak, with which you cover yourself.
13 If a man takes a wife, and afterward hates her,
14 And seeks occasions to dismiss her, casting a very foul name upon her, and says: "I took this woman as my wife, and when I went in to her, I did not find her to be a virgin":
15 Her father and mother shall take her, and bring the signs of her virginity with them to the elders of the city who are at the gate:
16 And the father shall say: "I gave my daughter as a wife to this man: and because he hates her,
17 He has cast a very foul name upon her, saying: 'I did not find your daughter to be a virgin': and behold, these are the signs of my daughter’s virginity." And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city:
18 And the elders of that city shall take the man, and they shall beat him,
19 Condemning him moreover to pay one hundred shekels of sil-

<column-break/>

-ver, which he shall give to the father of the girl: because he has defamed the reputation of a virgin of Israel with a very foul name: and he shall have her as his wife, and he shall not be able to dismiss her for all the days of his life.
20 But if what he charges is true, and virginity is not found in the girl:
21 They shall cast her out before the doors of her father's house, and the men of that city shall overwhelm her with stones, and she shall die: because she has committed a wicked deed in Israel, by playing the harlot in her father's house: and you shall take away the evil from your midst.
22 <margin>† Lev. 20:10.</margin> If a man sleeps with the wife of another, both shall die, that is, the adulterer and the adulteress: and you shall take away the evil from Israel.
23 If a man has betrothed a young girl who is a virgin, and someone finds her in the city and lies with her,
24 You shall lead them both out to the gate of that city, and they shall be overwhelmed with stones: the girl, because she did not cry out, though she was in the city: the man, because he humbled his neighbor's wife: and you shall take away the evil from your midst.
25 But if the man finds the girl who is betrothed in the field, and laying hold of her, lies with her, he alone shall die:
26 The girl shall suffer nothing, nor is she guilty of death: for just as a robber rises up against his brother and kills him, so also has the girl suffered.
27 She was alone in the field: she cried out, and there was no one there to rescue her.
28 If a man finds a young girl who is a virgin, who does not have a fiancé, and laying hold of her, lies with her, and the matter comes to judgment:
29 <margin>† Exod. 22:16.</margin> He who slept with her shall give to the girl's father fifty shekels of silver, and he shall have her as his wife, because he has humbled her: he shall not be able to dismiss her for all the days of his life.
30 A man shall not take his father's wife, nor reveal his covering <note>A Hebrew idiom for sexual relations, referring here to the father's bed or his right over his wife.</note>.

## CHAPTER XXIII.

*Concerning those who are to be barred from the assembly of God or admitted: the Edomite and the Egyptian are not to be cast out: concerning nocturnal pollution, and the place to be designated for the necessities of nature: concerning the fugitive slave, the wages of a prostitute, the avoiding of usury toward brothers, concerning vows, and the vineyard and standing corn of a neighbor.*

1 A eunuch, whose testicles have been crushed or cut off, or whose member has been severed, shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
2 A <term>mamzer</term> <note>original: "mamzer", meaning one born of an unauthorized or prohibited union, such as incest or certain types of illegitimacy.</note>, that is, one born of a prostitute, shall not enter the assembly of the Lord, even until the tenth generation.
3 <margin>† Neh. 13:1.</margin> The Ammonites and Moabites, even after the tenth generation, shall not enter the assembly of the Lord forever:
4 Because they did not want to meet you with bread and water on the way when you came out of Egypt: and <margin>† Num. 22:5.</margin> because they hired against you Balaam the son of Beor from Mesopotamia of Syria, to curse you:
5 And the Lord your God would not listen to Balaam, and he turned his curse into your blessing, because he loved you.
6 You shall not make peace with them, nor seek their good all the days of your life forever.
7 You shall not abhor the Edomite, because he is your brother: nor the Egyptian, because you were a stranger in his land.

8 Those who are born to them <note>Referring to the Edomites and Egyptians mentioned in the preceding verses, who were allowed entry after several generations.</note> in the third generation may enter into the assembly of the Lord.

11 And he shall not return until he is washed with water toward evening: and after the sun has set, he shall return to the camp.
12 You shall have a place outside the camp to which you may go for the requirements of nature,
13 Carrying a small stake on your belt: and when you sit down, you shall dig a hole around you, and cover the waste that comes from you with the earth you dug up.
14 (For the Lord your God walks in the midst of your camp to rescue you and to deliver your enemies to you); therefore, let your camp be holy, and let no filthiness appear in it, lest He abandon you.
15 You shall not hand over a slave to his master if he has fled to you for refuge.
16 He shall live with you in the place that pleases him, and he shall rest in one of your cities: do not trouble him.
17 There shall be no harlot among the daughters of Israel, nor a male prostitute among the sons of Israel.
18 You shall not offer the hire of a prostitute, nor the price of a dog <note>original: "pretium canis", a derogatory term often understood as the earnings of a male cult prostitute</note>, in the house of the Lord your God, whatever it is that you have vowed: because both are an abomination before the Lord your God.
19 You shall not lend money, or grain, or any other thing to your brother for interest:
20 But only to a foreigner. To your brother, however, you shall lend what he needs without interest: so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your work in the land which you are entering to possess.
21 When you make a vow to the Lord your God, do not delay in fulfilling it: because the Lord your God will surely require it of you; and if you delay, it shall be counted as a sin against you.
22 If you choose not to make a promise, you shall be without sin.
23 But that which has once proceeded from your lips, you shall observe and do as you promised to the Lord your God, spoken by your own will and your own mouth.
24 When you enter your neighbor's vineyard, eat as many grapes as you like: but do not carry any away with you.
25 If you enter into the standing grain of your friend, you may break the ears and rub them in your hand: but you shall not cut them with a sickle.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

-> *A bill of divorce is permitted: mercy toward poor debtors: wages are not to be denied: concerning the judgment of the stranger and the orphan: the remains of the harvest and vintage are to be left for the poor.* <-

<margin>† Matthew 5:31 & 19:7. Mark 10:4.</margin>
1 **S**hould a man take a wife and have her, and she find no favor in his eyes because of some indecency: he shall write a bill of divorce, and give it into her hand, and send her away from his house.

3 And he also hates her, and gives her a bill of divorce, and sends her out of his house, or indeed if he should die:

8 Observe diligently that you do not incur the plague of leprosy, but you shall do whatever the priests of the Levite lineage shall teach you, according to what I have commanded them, and fulfill it carefully.

<margin>† 2 Kings 14:6. 2 Chronicles 25:4. Ezekiel 18:20.</margin>
16 Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers, but each one shall die for his own sin.

19 When you reap the harvest in your field, and having forgotten a sheaf, you leave it behind, you shall not return to take it: but you shall allow the stranger, the orphan, and the widow to take it, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
20 If you gather the fruit of your olive trees, whatever remains on the trees, you shall not return to gather: but you shall leave it for the stranger, the orphan, and the widow.
21 If you gather the vintage of your vineyard, you shall not gather the remaining clusters, but they shall serve the needs of the stranger, the orphan, and the widow.
22 Remember that you also were a slave in Egypt, and therefore I command you to do this thing.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

*Concerning where and to whom the firstfruits and tithes are to be paid, and under what form of words.*

1 And when you have entered the land which the Lord your God is to give you to possess, and have obtained it, and dwell in it:

2 You shall take the firstfruits of all your crops, and put them in a basket, and go to the place which the Lord your God shall choose, so that His name may be invoked there:

3 And you shall go to the priest who shall be in those days, and say to him: I profess this day before the Lord your God, that I have entered into the land for which He swore to our fathers, that He would give it to us.

<column-break/>

4 And the priest, receiving the basket from your hand, shall set it before the altar of the Lord your God:

5 And you shall speak in the sight of the Lord your God: A Syrian <note>original: "Syrus"; most modern translations identify this as "a wandering Aramean," referring to Jacob.</note> pursued my father, who went down into Egypt, and dwelled there as a stranger in very small number: and he grew into a great and strong nation of infinite multitude.

6 And the Egyptians afflicted us, and persecuted us, laying upon us most heavy burdens:

7 And we cried out to the Lord, the God of our fathers: who heard us, and looked upon our humiliation, and our labor, and our distress:

8 And He brought us out of Egypt with a strong hand, and an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs and wonders:

9 And He brought us to this place, and gave us a land flowing with milk and honey.

10 And therefore now I offer the firstfruits of the crops of the land which the Lord has given me. And you shall leave them in the sight of the Lord your God, and adore the Lord your God.

11 And you shall feast on all the good things which the Lord your God has given to you and to your house, you and the Levite, and the stranger who is with you.

12 When you have completed the tithing of all your crops, in the third year of tithes, you shall give it to the Levite, and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, so that they may eat within your gates and be filled.

<margin>† Above 14:29</margin>
13 And you shall speak in the sight of the Lord your God: I have taken that which was sanctified out of my house, and I have given it to the Levite and the stranger, and the fatherless and the widow, as You have commanded me: I have not transgressed Your commandments, nor have I forgotten Your bidding.

14 I have not eaten of them in my mourning, nor have I set them apart in any uncleanness, nor have I spent any of these things in funeral matters. <note>original: "in re funebri"; this refers to avoiding pagan rituals for the dead or ritual impurity during the offering.</note> I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God, and have done all things as You have commanded me.

<margin>† Isaiah 63:15; Bar. 2:16.</margin>
15 Look down from Your sanctuary, and from Your high dwelling place in heaven, and bless Your people Israel, and the land which You have given us, as You swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.

16 This day the Lord your God has commanded you to perform these commandments and judgments: and to keep and fulfill them with all your heart, and with all your soul.

17 You have chosen the Lord today to be your God, and to walk in His ways, and keep His ceremonies, and commandments, and judgments, and to obey His command.

<margin>† Above 7:6.</margin>
18 And the Lord has chosen you today to be a peculiar people to Him, <note>A "peculiar people" here means a "treasured possession" or a people set apart specifically for God's use.</note> as He has spoken to you, and that you should keep all His precepts:

19 And that He may make you higher than all the nations which He has created, for His praise, and name, and glory: that you may be a holy people of the Lord your God, as He has spoken.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

->A manifold blessing is promised to those observing the law, and a curse to those transgressing it.<-

If then you will hear the voice of the Lord your God, to do and to keep all his commandments, which I command you today, the Lord your God will make you more exalted than all the nations that dwell on the earth.

9 The Lord shall raise you up for himself as a holy people, just as he swore to you: if you will keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and walk in his ways.

13 The Lord shall make you the head, and not the tail, and you shall always be above, and not beneath: if only you will hear the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you today, and keep and do them,

14 And do not turn aside from them, neither to the right nor to the left, nor follow strange gods, nor worship them.

21 The Lord shall make the pestilence cling to you, until he consumes you from the land which you are entering to possess.

22 The Lord shall strike you with poverty, fever, and cold, with burning heat and drought, and with corrupted air and <term>rust</term> <note>original: *rubigine*; in an agricultural context, this refers to crop blight or mildew which destroys harvests.</note>, and he shall pursue you until you perish.

23 Let the sky that is above you be brass, and the earth which you tread upon be iron. <note>This imagery describes a total environmental collapse where the sky yields no rain and the ground is too hard to plow.</note>

24 The Lord shall give the rain of your land as dust, and from heaven shall ashes descend upon you, until you are destroyed.

25 The Lord shall deliver you falling before your enemies; by one way you shall go out against them, and by seven ways you shall flee, and you shall be scattered through all the kingdoms of the earth.

26 And let your carcass be food for all the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth, and let there be no one to drive them away.

27 The Lord shall strike you with the boils of Egypt, and the part of the body through which dung is cast out <note>original: *partem corporis, per quam stercora egeruntur*; a traditional reference to hemorrhoids or "emrods."</note>, with scabies also and the itch, so that you cannot be healed.

28 The Lord shall strike you with madness and blindness and fury of mind;

29 And you shall grope at midday as a blind man is accustomed to grope in the dark, and you shall not direct your ways. And at all times you shall suffer slander and be oppressed with violence, nor shall you have anyone to deliver you.

30 You shall take a wife, and another shall sleep with her. You shall build a house, and not dwell in it. You shall plant a vineyard, and not gather the vintage from it.

31 Your ox shall be slaughtered before you, and you shall not eat of it. Your donkey shall be seized in your sight and not restored to you. Your sheep shall be given to your enemies, and there shall be no one to help you.

32 Your sons and your daughters shall be delivered to another people, while your eyes look on and fail at the sight of them all day long, and there shall be no strength in your hand.

33 A people whom you do not know shall eat the fruits of your land and all your labors; and you shall always suffer slander and be oppressed every day,

34 And be astonished at the terror of those things which your eyes shall see.

35 The Lord shall strike you with a most wicked boil on the knees and on the shins; and you cannot be healed from the sole of your foot to the top of your head.

36 The Lord shall lead you, and your king whom you shall appoint over you, into a nation which you and your fathers do not know: and there you shall serve foreign gods of wood and stone.

37 And you shall be lost as a proverb and a story <note>meaning a "byword" or an object of mockery</note> to all the peoples to whom the Lord shall bring you.

->*The covenant and oath of the Israelites with the Lord based on God's benefits, and a threat against those who break the covenant.*<-

1 These are the words of the covenant, which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab: in addition to that covenant which he made with them in Horeb <note>Horeb is another name for Mount Sinai, where the first covenant was established.</note>.

# CHAPTER 30.

->*Moses exhorts those who have fallen to repentance: for true repentance pleases God: the commandment given to us is not set far from us: in its fulfillment or neglect, good and evil are set before us: so that choosing good of our own accord, we may live, and not perish by clinging to evil.*<-

1 Therefore, when all these words have come upon you, the blessing or the curse, which I have set forth in your sight: and you are moved by the repentance of your heart among all the nations into which the Lord your God has dispersed you,

3 The Lord your God will bring back your captivity, and have mercy on you, and will again gather you from all the peoples among whom he previously dispersed you.

### CHAPTER XXXII.

->*The Song of Moses, in which he recounts God’s benefits and the people’s ingratitude often punished by the Lord: Moses is commanded to ascend Mount Abarim <note>Mount Abarim is the mountain range across from Jericho, which includes Mount Nebo.</note> to view the promised land.*<-

1 **H**ear, O heavens, the things I speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
2 May my teaching grow like rain, may my speech flow like dew, like a shower upon the grass, and like droplets upon the herb.
3 For I will call upon the name of the Lord: give magnificence to our God.
4 The works of God are perfect, and all his ways are just: God is faithful and without any iniquity, he is just and upright.

5 They have sinned against him, and they are not his children in their filthiness: a crooked and perverse generation.

9 But the Lord’s portion is his people: Jacob is the cord of his inheritance <note>This "cord" refers to a measuring line used to mark out an allotted piece of land.</note>.
10 He found him in a desert land, in a place of horror and of vast solitude: he led him about and taught him, and he guarded him as the apple of his eye.
11 As an eagle enticing its young to fly, and hovering over them, he spread his wings and took him up, and carried him on his shoulders.
12 The Lord alone was his leader: and there was no foreign god with him.
13 He set him over the high land: so that he might eat the fruits of the fields, that he might suck honey from the rock, and oil from the hardest stone.
14 Butter from the herd, and milk from the sheep with the fat of lambs, and rams of the breed of Bashan <note>Bashan was a region famous for its rich pastures and strong livestock.</note>: and goats with the marrow of wheat, and that he might drink the purest blood of the grape <note>A poetic term for red wine.</note>.
15 The beloved <note>In the original Hebrew, the word is "Jeshurun," a title of endearment for Israel, though the Latin translates it as "dilectus" (beloved).</note> grew fat and kicked: grown thick, fat, and bloated, he forsook God his maker, and departed from God his savior.
16 They provoked him with foreign gods, and stirred him to anger with abominations.
17 They sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods they did not know: new and recent ones arrived, whom their fathers did not worship.
18 You have forsaken the God who begot you, and you have forgotten the Lord your creator.
19 The Lord saw, and he was moved to anger: because his own sons and daughters provoked him.
20 And he said: "I will hide my face from them, and I will consider their final end: for it is a perverse generation, and unfaithful children.
<margin>† Jeremiah 15:14. Romans 10:19.</margin>
21 They have provoked me with that which was not God, and irritated me with their vanities: and † I will provoke them with those who are not a people, and I will irritate them with a foolish nation.
22 A fire is kindled in my fury, and it shall burn even to the lowest depths of hell: it shall devour the earth with its growth, and burn the foundations of the mountains.
23 I will heap evils upon them, and I will spend my arrows among them.
24 They shall be consumed by hunger, and birds shall devour them with a most bitter bite: I will send the teeth of beasts upon them, along with the fury of those that crawl upon the earth, and of serpents.
25 Outside, the sword shall lay them waste, and inside, there shall be dread; the young man and the virgin alike, the suckling with the old man.
26 I said: Where are they? I will make the memory of them cease from among men.
27 But I delayed because of the wrath of the enemies, lest their foes should perhaps grow proud and say: 'Our high hand, and not the Lord, has done all these things.'
28 They are a nation without counsel, and without prudence."

### CHAPTER II.

->*Spies sent into the city of Jericho are hidden by Rahab the harlot; with mercy promised to her and her whole family, they return safely to the camp.*<-

<margin>† Hebrews 11:31. James 2:25.</margin>
1 Therefore Joshua the son of Nun sent from Shittim <note>original: "Setim", a place known for its acacia trees</note> two men as spies in secret, and said to them: Go, and consider the land, and the city of Jericho. And they went and entered the house of a woman who was a harlot, named Rahab, and rested with her.

2 And it was told to the king of Jericho, and said: Behold, men have entered here by night from the children of Israel, to spy out the land.

3 And the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying: Bring out the men who came to you, and entered your house: for they are spies, and have come to consider all the land.

<margin>† Below 6:17.</margin>
4 And the woman, taking the men, hid them, and said: I confess, they came to me, but I did not know where they were from:

5 And when the gate was being closed in the darkness, they also went out together, I do not know where they went: pursue them quickly, and you will overtake them.

6 But she had made the men go up to the roof <note>original: "solarium", the flat rooftop used for drying goods</note> of her house, and covered them with stalks of flax <note>original: "stipula lini"</note>, which were there.

7 Now those who had been sent followed them by the way that leads to the ford of the Jordan: and as soon as they had gone out, the gate was closed.

8 The men who were hiding had not yet fallen asleep, and behold, the woman went up to them, and said:

9 I know that the Lord has delivered the land to you: for the terror of you has fallen upon us, and all the inhabitants of the land have grown faint.

<margin>† Exodus 14:21. † Numbers 21:24.</margin>
10 We have heard that the Lord dried up the waters of the Red Sea at your entry, when you came out of Egypt: and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites <note>original: "Amorrhæorum"</note>, who were beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you killed.

11 And hearing these things, we were very afraid, and our heart grew faint, nor did any spirit remain in us at your entry: for the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in the earth below.

14 They answered her: May our lives be for yours unto death, if only you do not betray us: and when the Lord has delivered the land to us, we will show mercy and truth toward you.

15 She let them down then by a rope from the window: for her house joined the wall.

16 And she said to them: Climb up to the mountains, lest those returning should perhaps meet you: and hide there for three days, until they return, and so you shall go on your way.

17 And they said to her: We shall be innocent of this oath, by which you have bound us:

18 If, when we enter the land, this scarlet cord <note>original: "funiculus coccineus"</note> is the sign, and you tie it in the window through which you let us down: and gather your father and your mother, and your brothers, and all your kindred into your house.

19 He who goes out the door of your house, his blood shall be upon his own head, and we shall be blameless. But the blood of all who are with you in the house shall rebound upon our heads, if anyone touches them.

20 But if you wish to betray us, and bring this matter into the open, we shall be free from this oath, by which you have bound us.

21 And she answered: As you have spoken, so let it be: and sending them away to go, she hung the scarlet cord in the window.

22 But they, walking, came to the mountains, and stayed there three days, until those who had pursued them returned: for having searched all along the way, they did not find them.

24 And they said: The Lord has delivered all this land into our hands, and all the inhabitants thereof are struck down with fear.

### C H A P T E R IV.

->*Twelve stones are gathered from the dried Jordan as a memorial for posterity, and another twelve are set up in the bed of the Jordan itself.*<-

1 When they had crossed over, the Lord said to Joshua:
2 Choose twelve men, one from each tribe:
3 And command them to take from the middle of the Jordan’s channel, where the feet of the priests stood, twelve very hard stones, which you shall place in the location of the camp where you pitch your tents this night.
4 And Joshua called the twelve men whom he had chosen from the children of Israel, one from each tribe,
5 And he said to them: Go before the ark of the Lord your God to the middle of the Jordan, and carry from there each of you a stone on your shoulders, according to the number of the children of Israel,
6 So that it may be a sign among you; and when your children ask you tomorrow, saying: "What do these stones mean to you?"
7 You shall answer them: The waters of the Jordan failed before the ark of the covenant of the Lord when it crossed over it; therefore these stones were placed

<column-break/>

as a monument for the children of Israel forever.
8 The children of Israel did, therefore, as Joshua commanded them, carrying twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan’s channel, as the Lord had ordered him, according to the number of the children of Israel, to the place where they camped, and there they placed them.
9 Joshua also placed another twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan’s channel, where the priests stood who carried the ark of the covenant; and they are there to this present day.
10 But the priests who carried the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until all things were finished which the Lord had commanded Joshua to speak to the people, and which Moses had told him. And the people hurried and crossed over.
11 And when they had all crossed, the ark of the Lord also crossed, and the priests went before the people.

13 And forty thousand fighting men in troops and divisions marched through the plains and fields of the city of Jericho.

15 And he said to him:
16 Command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant to come up out of the Jordan.
17 And he commanded them, saying: Come up out of the Jordan.
18 And when they had come up carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord and began to tread on dry ground, the waters returned to their channel and flowed just as they were accustomed to do before.
19 Now the people came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and they camped in Gilgal <note>original: "Galgalis"</note> against the eastern side of the city of Jericho.
20 And the twelve stones which they had taken from the channel of the Jordan, Joshua placed in Gilgal,
21 And he said to the children of Israel: When your children ask their fathers tomorrow, and say to them: "What do these stones mean?"
22 You shall teach them and say: Israel passed through this Jordan on a dry riverbed,
23 For the Lord your God dried up its waters in your sight until you passed over,
24 <margin>† Exodus 14:21.</margin> Just as he had done before in the Red Sea, which he dried up until we passed through,
25 So that all the peoples of the earth may learn the most powerful hand of the Lord, and so that you also may fear the Lord your God at all times.

## CHAPTER VI.

*After various circuits of seven days with the ark, Jericho is captured and utterly destroyed; only Rahab is saved with her kin; a curse is laid upon the rebuilder of the city.*

1 Now Jericho was shut up and fortified for fear of the children of Israel, and no one dared to go out or come in.

2 And the Lord said to Joshua: Behold, I have given into your hand Jericho, and its king, and all its valiant men.

3 You shall circle the city, all you men of war, once a day: so shall you do for six days.

12 Therefore Joshua rising in the night, the priests took up the ark of the Lord,

13 And seven of them took the seven trumpets used in the jubilee: and they went before the ark of the Lord walking and sounding the trumpets: and the armed people went before them, while the rest of the common people followed the ark, sounding the trumpets.

14 And they circled the city on the second day once, and returned to the camp. Thus they did for six days.

15 But on the seventh day, rising at dawn, they circled the city seven times, as it had been arranged.

21 And they killed all that were in it, from man to woman, from infant to the old. They also struck down the oxen and sheep and donkeys with the edge of the sword.

### CHAPTER VII

->*After the city of Ai is scouted, the people of Israel retreat before their enemies because of a theft from the devoted things of Jericho; therefore, after Joshua’s lamentation, Achan is chosen by lot and stoned by the command of the Lord.*<-

<margin>† See below 22:20; 1 Chronicles 2:7</margin>
But the children of Israel violated the commandment and took for themselves from the <term>anathema</term> <note>original: "de anathemate"; this refers to the "ban" or things "devoted to destruction" which were strictly forbidden for personal use.</note>. For Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took something from the devoted things: and the Lord became angry against the children of Israel.
2 And when Joshua sent men from Jericho against Ai, which is near Bethaven, on the eastern side of the town of Bethel, he said to them: Go up, and scout the land. Following his commands, they scouted Ai.
3 And returning, they said to him: Let not all the people go up, but let two or three thousand men go and destroy the city. Why should all the people be troubled in vain against such a very few enemies?
4 Therefore, three thousand fighting men went up: who immediately turned their backs and fled,
5 Being struck down by the men of the city of Ai. And thirty-six men from among them fell; and the adversaries pursued them from the gate as far as Shebarim, and they fell as they fled headlong. And the heart of the people was struck with fear, and it melted like water.
6 But Joshua tore his clothes, and fell face down on the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, both he and all the elders of Israel: and they cast dust upon their heads.
7 And Joshua said: Alas, Lord God, why did You wish to lead this people across the Jordan River, to deliver us into the hands of the Amorite and destroy us? I wish that, as we had begun, we had remained across the Jordan.
8 My Lord God, what shall I say, seeing Israel turning their backs to their enemies?
9 The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it, and gathering together, they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. And what will You do for Your great name?

<column-break/>

10 And the Lord said to Joshua: Arise, why do you lie face down on the ground?
11 Israel has sinned and transgressed my covenant. They have taken from the devoted things, and have stolen and lied, and hidden it among their own goods.
12 Nor will Israel be able to stand before their enemies, and they shall flee from them: because they are polluted by the <term>anathema</term> <note>the forbidden loot</note>. I will be with you no longer, until you crush the one who is guilty of this crime.
13 Arise, sanctify the people, and say to them:
<margin>† Leviticus 20:7; Numbers 11:18; Above 3:5; 1 Samuel 16:5</margin>
Be sanctified for tomorrow: for thus says the Lord God of Israel: There is a devoted thing in your midst, O Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until the one who is contaminated by this crime is removed from among you.
14 And you shall come forward in the morning, each by your tribes: and whichever tribe the lot finds, it shall come forward by its families, and the family by its houses, and the house man by man.
15 And whoever is caught in this crime shall be burned with fire along with all his substance: because he has transgressed the covenant of the Lord and has committed a foul deed in Israel.
16 Joshua, therefore, rising in the morning, brought Israel forward by their tribes, and the tribe of Judah was found.
17 When that tribe was presented according to its families, the family of Zerah was found. Presenting that family by its houses, he found Zabdi.
18 Dividing his house into individual men, he found Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah.
19 And Joshua said to Achan: My son, give glory to the Lord God of Israel, and confess, and tell me what you have done; do not hide it.
20 And Achan answered Joshua, and said to him: In truth I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and I have done thus and so.
21 For I saw among the spoils a very good scarlet cloak, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a gold bar of fifty shekels: and being filled with greed, I took them and hid them in the ground in the middle of my tent, and I covered the silver in a dug hole.
22 Joshua therefore sent messengers, who, running to his tent, found everything hidden in that same place, along with the silver.
23 And taking them from the tent, they brought them to Joshua and to all the children of Israel, and they threw them down before the Lord.
24 Then Joshua, taking Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the cloak, and the gold bar, and his sons and daughters, his oxen and donkeys and sheep, and the tent itself, and all his furniture (and all Israel with him), led them to the Valley of Achor.
25 Where Joshua said: Because you have troubled us, may the Lord trouble you on this day. And all Israel stoned him: and all that was his was consumed by fire.
<margin>† 2 Samuel 18:17</margin>
26 And they gathered over him a great heap of stones, which remains even to this present day. And the fury of the Lord was turned away from them. And the name of that place was called the Valley of Achor <note>Achor means "trouble" in Hebrew, creating a wordplay with Joshua’s statement</note> even until today.

## CHAPTER VIII.

*Ai having been conquered, its king is hanged, and a stone altar is erected: Deuteronomy is written upon the stones, and the people are blessed.*

1 Then the Lord said to Joshua: Do not fear, nor be dismayed: take with you all the multitude of fighting men, and rising up, go up to the town of Ai: behold, I have delivered into your hand its king, and people, and city, and land.
2 <margin>Above 6:24</margin> And you shall do to the city of Ai and its king † just as you did to Jericho and its king: but the booty and all the livestock you shall take as plunder for yourselves; place an ambush for the city behind it.
3 So Joshua and all the army of fighting men rose up to go up to Ai: and choosing thirty thousand strong men, he sent them out at night,
4 And he commanded them, saying: Place an ambush behind the city: do not go too far away, and all of you be ready.
5 <margin>Above 4</margin> But I and the rest of the multitude who are with me will approach from the front against the city. And when they come out against us, † just as we did before, we will flee and turn our backs:
6 Until those pursuing are drawn further away from the city: for they will think we are fleeing just as before.
7 While we are fleeing and they are pursuing, you shall rise up from the ambush and lay waste to the city: and the Lord your God will deliver it into your hands.
8 And when you have taken it, set it on fire, and you shall do all things as I have commanded.
9 And he sent them away, and they proceeded to the place of ambush, and they sat between Bethel and Ai, on the western side of the city of Ai: but Joshua remained that night in the midst of the people.
10 Rising at dawn, he reviewed his companions and went up with the elders at the head of the army, fortified by the help of the fighters.
11 And when they had come and gone up opposite the city, they stood on the northern side of the city, between which and them was a valley in the middle.
12 Now he had chosen five thousand men and placed them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the western part of that same city:
13 But all the rest of the army directed their line to the north, so that the rear of that multitude reached the western side of the city. Joshua went that night and stood in the middle of the valley.
14 When the king of Ai saw this, he hurried in the morning and went out with all the army of the city, and directed his line toward the desert, not knowing that an ambush lay hidden behind his back.
15 But Joshua and all Israel gave way, feigning fear and fleeing by the way of the wilderness.
16 And they, shouting together and encouraging one another, pursued them. And when they had withdrawn from the city,
17 And not even one man remained in the city of Ai or Bethel who did not pursue Israel (just as they had broken out, leaving the towns open,)
18 The Lord said to Joshua: Lift up the shield <note>original: "clypeum" — while the Latin says "shield," some biblical scholars interpret this as a spear or javelin used as a signal.</note> that is in your hand against the city of Ai, for I will deliver it to you.
19 And when he had raised the shield opposite the ci-

<column-break/>

ty, the ambush, which was hidden, rose up immediately: and proceeding to the city, they took it and set it on fire.
20 But the men of the city who were pursuing Joshua, looking back and seeing the smoke of the city rising up to heaven, could no longer flee here or there: especially since those who had feigned flight and were heading toward the wilderness turned back most bravely against their pursuers.
21 And Joshua and all Israel, seeing that the city was taken and the smoke of the city was rising, turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
22 Indeed, those also who had taken and set fire to the city came out from the city against their own <note>meaning the enemy's men who were now trapped</note>, and began to strike the enemies in the middle. Since the adversaries were being slaughtered from both sides, so that no one from such a great multitude was saved,
23 They also captured the king of the city of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
24 Therefore, when all were slain who had pursued Israel as they headed toward the deserts, and they had fallen by the sword in that same place, the children of Israel returned and struck the city.
25 Now those who fell on that same day, from man to woman, were twelve thousand people, all of the city of Ai.
26 But Joshua did not draw back his hand, which he had stretched out on high holding the shield, until all the inhabitants of Ai were slain.
27 However, the children of Israel divided the cattle and the booty of the city among themselves, just as the Lord had commanded Joshua.
28 Who burned the city and made it an everlasting mound:
29 Its king he also hanged on a gallows <note>original: "patibulo" — a wooden frame or tree used for public execution</note> until evening and the setting of the sun. And Joshua commanded, and they took down his corpse from the cross: and they cast it at the very entrance of the city, piling over him a great heap of stones, which remains until this present day.
30 Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord God of Israel on Mount Ebal:
31 <margin>† Exodus 20:25, Deuteronomy 27:5</margin> † Just as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded the children of Israel, and as it is written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of unhewn stones which iron had not touched: and he offered upon it burnt offerings <note>original: "holocausta"</note> to the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings.
32 And he wrote upon the stones the Deuteronomy <note>The "Second Law" or a copy of the law</note> of the law of Moses, which he had set forth before the children of Israel.
33 Then all the people, and the elders, and the leaders and judges stood on both sides of the ark, in the sight of the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger as the native. Half of them were near Mount Gerizim, and half near Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded. And first he blessed the people of Israel.
34 After these things, he read all the words of the blessing and the curse, and all things that were written in the book of the law.
35 Nothing from those things which Moses had commanded did he leave untouched, but he repeated everything before all the multitude of Israel, with the women and children and the strangers who dwelt among them.

### CHAPTER IX.

*The Gibeonites, through the pretense of a long journey, deceive Joshua and the leaders of the Israelites; they are spared because of an oath, but after a murmur follows, they are bound to perpetual servitude.*

1 Having heard these things, all the kings across the Jordan, who lived in the mountains and the plains, in the coastal regions and the shores of the great sea, <note>The "great sea" refers to the Mediterranean.</note> those also who lived near Lebanon—the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—
2 Gathered together as one to fight against Joshua and Israel with a single mind and the same intent.
3 But those who lived in Gibeon, <note>Gibeon was a major city of the Hivites, located just north of Jerusalem.</note> hearing all that Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai:
4 Craftily planning, they took provisions for themselves, putting old sacks on their donkeys, and wine-skins that were torn and sewn back together,
5 And very old sandals which, as a sign of their age, were sewn with patches, and they dressed in old clothes. The bread also, which they carried for the journey, was hard and broken into pieces.
6 They went to Joshua, who then stayed in the camp at Gilgal, and said to him, and at the same time to all of Israel: We have come from a far-off land, desiring to make peace with you. And the men of Israel responded to them, and said:
7 Perhaps you live in the land which is owed to us, and we cannot enter into a treaty with you.
8 But they said to Joshua: We are your servants. To whom Joshua said: Who are you? And where did you come from?
9 They answered: From a very distant land your servants have come in the name of the Lord your God. For we have heard the fame of His power, and all that He did in Egypt,
<margin>† Numbers 21:24.</margin>
10 And to the two kings of the Amorites who were across the Jordan, Sihon the king of Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan who was in Ashtaroth:
11 And our elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us: Take provisions in your hands for a very long journey, and meet them, and say: We are your servants, enter into a treaty with us.
12 Look, these loaves of bread: when we left our homes to come to you, we took them hot; now they have become dry and broken by too much age.
13 These wine-skins we filled when new; now they are burst and undone. The clothes and sandals we wear, and which we have on our feet, are worn out and almost consumed because of the length of the long journey.
14 They <note>The leaders of Israel.</note> therefore accepted some of their provisions, but they did not ask the mouth of the Lord. <note>original: "os Domini" — This indicates they failed to consult the divine oracle or the high priest before making a decision.</note>
<margin>† 2 Samuel 21:2.</margin>
15 And Joshua made peace with them, and having entered into a treaty, he promised that they would not be killed; the leaders of the assembly also swore an oath to them.
16 But three days after the treaty was made, they heard that they lived nearby and would be in their midst.
17 And the children of Israel moved their camp and came to their cities on the third day, the names of which are: Gibeon, and Chephirah, and Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.

<column-break/>

18 And they did not strike them down, because the leaders of the assembly had sworn to them in the name of the Lord God of Israel. Therefore all the common people <note>original: "vulgus" - referring to the general population of the Israelite camp.</note> murmured against the leaders.
19 Who answered them: We have sworn to them in the name of the Lord God of Israel, and therefore we cannot touch them.
20 But this we will do to them: Let them be reserved to live, lest the wrath of the Lord be stirred against us if we commit perjury:
21 But let them live in such a way that they may cut wood and carry water for the use of the whole multitude. While they were saying these things:
22 Joshua called the Gibeonites and said to them: Why did you wish to deceive us with fraud, saying: "We live very far from you," when you are in our very midst?
23 Therefore, you shall be under a curse, and there shall not fail from your lineage those who cut wood and carry water for the house of my God.
24 They answered: It was told to us, your servants, that the Lord your God had promised His servant Moses to deliver the whole land to you, and to destroy all its inhabitants. Therefore we feared greatly for our lives, compelled by the terror of you, and we undertook this plan.
25 But now we are in your hand: do to us what seems good and right to you.
26 Joshua therefore did as he had said, and delivered them from the hands of the children of Israel, so that they were not killed.
27 And on that day he decreed that they should be in the service of the whole people and of the altar of the Lord, cutting wood and carrying water, even unto this present time, in the place which the Lord should choose.

### CHAPTER X.

*Five kings attacking the city of Gibeon are defeated while the sun remains unmoved for the space of one day; and being dragged from a cave, they are hanged, and several other kings and cities are destroyed.*

1 When Adoni-zedek, the king of Jerusalem, had heard these things—namely, that Joshua had captured Ai and had overthrown it (for just as he had done to Jericho and its king, so he did to Ai and its king) and that the Gibeonites had defected to Israel and were their allies—
2 He feared greatly. For Gibeon was a large city, one of the royal cities, and greater than the town of Ai, and all its warriors were very brave.
3 Adoni-zedek the king of Jerusalem sent, therefore, to Hoham the king of Hebron, and to Piram the king of Jarmuth, to Japhia the king of Lachish, and to Debir the king of Eglon, saying:
4 Come up to me and bring aid, so that we may conquer Gibeon, because it has defected to Joshua and to the children of Israel.
5 Therefore the five kings of the Amorites gathered and went up—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—together with their armies, and they set up camp around Gibeon, attacking it.
6 But the inhabitants of the besieged city of Gibeon sent to Joshua, who then stayed in the camp at Gilgal, and said to him: Do not withdraw your hands from helping your servants; come up quickly and deliver us, and bring aid: for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the mountains have gathered against us.

7 So Joshua went up from Gilgal, and all the army of fighting men with him, the most valiant of men.

8 And the Lord said to Joshua: Do not fear them: for I have delivered them into your hands: none of them shall be able to resist you.

9 Joshua therefore fell upon them suddenly, having marched up from Gilgal all through the night:

10 And the Lord threw them into a panic before Israel: and he crushed them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and pursued them along the way that goes up to Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

11 And as they fled from the children of Israel, and were on the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord cast down great stones <note>These are understood to be large, miraculous hailstones.</note> from heaven upon them as far as Azekah: and many more died from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel had struck with the sword.

12 Then Joshua spoke to the Lord, on the day when He delivered the Amorite into the sight of the children of Israel, and he said in their presence: Sun, do not move over Gibeon, and Moon, over the valley of Ajalon.

<margin>Sirach 46:5, 28</margin>
13 And the Sun and Moon stood still, until the people had taken vengeance upon their enemies. Is this not written in the Book of the Upright? <note>original: "libro justorum," often referred to as the Book of Jasher, a lost collection of ancient Hebrew heroic songs and poetry.</note> So the Sun stood still in the middle of the sky, and did not hasten to set for the space of a whole day.

14 There was never before nor after so long a day, while the Lord obeyed the voice of a man, and fought for Israel.

15 And Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.

16 For the five kings had fled, and hidden themselves in a cave of the city of Makkedah.

17 And it was reported to Joshua that the five kings had been found hiding in the cave of the city of Makkedah.

18 He commanded his companions, saying: Roll great stones to the mouth of the cave, and station industrious men to guard those who are shut inside:

19 But you, do not stay there; pursue the enemies, and cut down the hindmost of those who flee: do not allow them to enter the defenses of their cities, whom the Lord your God has delivered into your hands.

20 Therefore, when the adversaries had been struck with a great slaughter, and were almost consumed to the point of utter destruction, those who were able to escape from Israel entered into the fortified cities.

21 And the whole army returned to Joshua at Makkedah, where the camp was then located, safe and in full number: and no one dared to mutter even a word <note>original: "mutire," literally to mutter or make a sound like a 'mu'; it signifies that the opposition was completely silenced.</note> against the children of Israel.

22 And Joshua commanded, saying: Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out to me the five kings who are hiding in it.

23 And the attendants did as they had been commanded: and they led out to him the five kings from the cave: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

24 And when they had been led out to him, he called all the men of Israel, and said to the leaders of the army who were with him: Go, and place your feet upon the necks of these kings. And when they had gone forward and stepped upon the necks of those subjected to them,

25 He said to them again: Do not fear, nor be dismayed; be comforted and be strong: for so shall the Lord do to all your enemies, against whom you fight.

26 And Joshua struck and killed them, and hanged them upon five poles: and they remained hanging until evening.

<column-break/>

<margin>Deuteronomy 21:23</margin>
27 And when the sun was setting, he commanded his companions to take them down from the gallows. Once taken down, they threw them into the cave in which they had hidden, and placed great stones over its mouth, which remain to this day.

28 On that same day, Joshua also took Makkedah, and struck it with the edge of the sword, <note>original: "in ore gladii," a common idiom for total military destruction.</note> and killed its king and all its inhabitants: he did not leave even small remnants within it. And he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.

29 Then he passed with all Israel from Makkedah to Libnah, and fought against it:

30 Which the Lord delivered, with its king, into the hands of Israel: and they struck the city with the edge of the sword, and all its inhabitants: they did not leave any remnants in it. And they did to the king of Libnah, <margin>Above 6:2</margin> as he had done to the king of Jericho.

31 From Libnah he passed to Lachish with all Israel: and having arranged the army in a circle, he attacked it.

32 And the Lord delivered Lachish into the hands of Israel, and he took it on the second day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every soul that was in it, just as he had done to Libnah.

33 At that time, Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish: and Joshua struck him with all his people until they were utterly destroyed.

34 And he passed from Lachish to Eglon, and surrounded it.

35 And he took it on the same day: and struck with the edge of the sword all the souls that were in it, according to all that he had done to Lachish.

36 He also went up with all Israel from Eglon to Hebron, and fought against it:

37 He took it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, along with its king, and all the towns of that region, and all the souls that had stayed in it: he did not leave any remnants in it: as he had done to Eglon, so he did also to Hebron, consuming with the sword everything he found in it.

38 From there he returned to Debir,

39 And he took it and laid it waste: he struck its king and all the surrounding towns with the edge of the sword: he did not leave any remnants in it: as he had done to Hebron and Libnah and to their kings, so he did to Debir and its king.

40 So Joshua struck all the hill country, the south, the lowlands, and the slopes, <note>original: "Asedoth," which refers to the mountain slopes or the springs of Pisgah.</note> with their kings: he did not leave any remnants in it, but killed everything that could breathe, as the Lord the God of Israel had commanded him,

41 From Kadesh-barnea even unto Gaza. All the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon,

42 And all the kings and their regions he took and devastated in one single campaign: for the Lord the God of Israel fought for him.

43 And he returned with all Israel to the place of the camp in Gilgal.

->*Lots are assigned to the half-tribe of Manasseh and the daughters of Zelophehad, and the lot of the sons of Joseph is increased.*<-

<margin>Numbers 26:30.</margin>
2 And to the rest of the children of Manasseh according to their families: to the children of Abiezer, and the children of Helek, and the children of Asriel, and the children of Shechem, and the children of Hepher, and the children of Shemida: these are the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph, by their clans.

3 But Zelophehad <note>original: "Salphaad"</note>, the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, but only daughters: whose names are these, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
4 And they came before Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the princes, saying: The Lord commanded by the hand of Moses that a possession be given to us in the midst of our brothers. And he gave them a possession in the midst of their father’s brothers according to the command of the Lord.
5 And there fell ten portions <note>original: "funiculi," literally "measuring lines"</note> to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan across the Jordan.
6 For the daughters of Manasseh possessed an inheritance in the midst of his sons: and the land of Gilead fell to the lot of the sons of Manasseh who remained.
7 And the border of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethath, which looks toward Shechem: and it goes out to the right near the inhabitants of the fountain of Tappuah.
8 For the land of Tappuah had fallen to the lot of Manasseh, which is near the borders of Manasseh but belongs to the children of Ephraim.
9 And the border of the Valley of Reeds goes down to the south of the torrent of the cities of Ephraim, which are in the midst of the cities of Manasseh: the border of Manasseh is from the north of the torrent, and its exit goes to the sea:
10 So that the possession of Ephraim is to the south, and Manasseh to the north, and the sea closes both, and they are joined together in the tribe of Asher to the north, and in the tribe of Issachar to the east.
11 And the inheritance of Manasseh in Issachar and in Asher was Beth-shean and its hamlets, and Ibleam with its villages, and the inhabitants of Dor with its towns, also the inhabitants of Endor with its hamlets: and likewise the inhabitants of Taanach with its hamlets, and the inhabitants of Megiddo with its hamlets, and the third part of the city of Nopheth.
12 Nor could the children of Manasseh overthrow these cities, but the Canaanite began to dwell in his land.
13 But after the children of Israel grew strong, they subdued the Canaanites and made them tributaries, but did not kill them.
14 And the sons of Joseph spoke to Joshua, and said: Why have you given me a possession of only one lot and one portion, since I am of such a great multitude, and the Lord has blessed me?

### CHAPTER XVIII

->*Men are sent to survey the land for the remaining seven tribes, and the lot is assigned to Benjamin.*<-

1 All the children of Israel gathered together at Shiloh, and there they set up the Tabernacle of the Testimony, and the land was subdued before them.
2 But there remained seven tribes of the children of Israel who had not yet received their possessions.
3 Joshua said to them: "How long will you remain idle and neglect to enter and possess the land which the Lord God of your fathers has given you?
4 Choose three men from each tribe, so that I may send them; let them go and travel through the whole land and map it <note>Original: "describant," meaning to map or write a description</note> according to the number of each multitude, and bring the description to me.
5 Divide the land into seven parts: let Judah remain in his territory in the south, and the house of Joseph in the north.
6 Map the land between them into seven parts, and bring it here to me, so that I may cast lots for you here before the Lord your God.
7 For the Levites have no portion among you; rather, the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. And Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their possessions across the Jordan to the east, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave to them."
8 When the men rose to go and survey the land, Joshua commanded them, saying: "Go around the land and describe it, and return to me; so that here in Shiloh, before the Lord, I may cast lots for you."
9 So they went and traveled through it, and divided it into seven parts, writing them in a book <note>Original: "volumine," referring to a scroll or volume</note>. They returned to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
10 He then cast lots before the Lord in Shiloh, and divided the land for the children of Israel into seven parts.
11 And the first lot came up for the children of Benjamin, according to their families, to possess the land between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.
12 Their northern border started from the Jordan, passing by the side of Jericho on the north, and from there climbing westward to the mountains, reaching the wilderness of Beth-aven,

### CHAPTER XX.

->Six cities of refuge on this side and across the Jordan, and those who may flee to them: and how long they ought to remain there.<-

1 **A**nd the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them:
<margin>Numbers 35:11.</margin>
2 Set aside the cities of the fugitives, † of which I spoke to you by the hand of Moses;
<margin>Deuteronomy 19:2.</margin>
3 That whoever has struck down a person unknowingly may flee to them: and may be able to escape the wrath of the neighbor, who is the avenger of blood <note>The "avenger of blood" was usually the nearest relative of a deceased person, culturally authorized to seek retribution</note>:
4 When he has fled to one of these cities, he shall stand before the gate of the city, and shall speak to the elders of that city those things which prove him innocent: and so they shall receive him, and give him a place to dwell.
5 And when the avenger of blood has pursued him, they shall not deliver him into his hands: because he struck his neighbor in ignorance, and he is not proven to be his enemy from two or three days before.
6 And he shall dwell in that city, until he stands before judgment to give an account of his deed, and until the high priest dies, who shall be in that time: then the manslayer shall return, and enter into his city and his own house from which he had fled.
7 And they appointed Kedesh in Galilee on the mountain of Naphtali, and Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.
<margin>Deuteronomy 4:43.</margin>
8 And across the Jordan toward the eastern side of Jericho, † they established Bezer, which is situated in the plain of the wilderness, from the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.
9 These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel, and for the strangers who dwelt among them, so that whoever had struck a person unknowingly might flee to them, and not die by the hand of the neighbor.

30 Having heard these things, Phinehas the priest, and the princes of the embassy of Israel who were with him, were appeased: and they most willingly accepted the words of the children of Reuben, and Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

32 And he returned with the princes from the children of Reuben and Gad, from the land of Gilead, in the borders of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and reported to them.

33 And the report pleased all who heard it. And the children of Israel praised God, and spoke no more of going up against them to fight and destroy the land of their possession.

34 And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar which they had built, "Our Witness," for the Lord himself is God.

*Under the leadership of Judah, along with his brother Simeon, many cities of the nations are conquered: Othniel, having captured Kiriath-sepher, marries Achsah the daughter of Caleb, with the addition of irrigated land: the Canaanites are kept as tributaries.*

1 After the death of Joshua, the children of Israel consulted the Lord, saying: "Who shall go up before us against the Canaanite, and be the leader of the war?"

3 And Judah said to Simeon his brother: "Come up with me into my allotted lot, and fight against the Canaanite, so that I may also go with you into your lot." And Simeon went with him.
4 And Judah went up, and the Lord delivered the Canaanite and the Perizzite into their hands: and they struck down ten thousand men in Bezek.
5 And they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek, and they fought against him, and they struck the Canaanite and the Perizzite.
6 But Adoni-bezek fled: whom they pursued and captured, cutting off the tips of his hands and feet.
7 And Adoni-bezek said: "Seventy kings, with the tips of their hands and feet cut off, used to gather the remains of food under my table: as I have done, so God has repaid me." And they brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.
8 Then the children of Judah, attacking Jerusalem, took it, and struck it with the edge of the sword, delivering the entire city to be burned.

### CHAPTER II.

> *The Angel of God recounts his favors; hearing this, the people weep: yet after the death of Joshua and his contemporaries, Israel—though frequently delivered—always falls back into worse ways.*

1 And an angel of the Lord went up from Gilgal <note>original: "Galgalis"</note> to the place of the weepers, and said: "I led you out of Egypt, and brought you into the land for which I swore to your fathers: and I promised that I would never make void my covenant with you:
2 On the condition that you should not make a league with the inhabitants of this land, but should overthrow their altars: and you would not hear my voice: why have you done this?
3 Therefore I would not destroy them from before your face: so that you may have enemies, and their gods may be a ruin to you."

18 And when the Lord raised up judges, in their days he was moved by mercy, and heard the groaning of the afflicted, and delivered them from the slaughter of the oppressors.

22 That through them I may test Israel, whether they will keep the way of the Lord, and walk in it, as their fathers kept it, or not."
23 The Lord therefore left all these nations, and would not quickly overthrow them, nor did he deliver them into the hands of Joshua.

### CHAPTER III.

1 These are the nations which the Lord left behind, that by them he might instruct Israel, and all those who did not know the wars of the Canaanites:
2 So that afterwards their children might learn to fight with enemies, and have a custom of warring:
3 Five lords <note>original: "satrapas" - referring to the five city-state rulers of the Philistine pentapolis</note> of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and Sidonians, and also the Hivites <note>original: "Hevæum"</note>, who dwelt in mount Lebanon, from mount Baal Hermon even to the entrance of Hamath <note>original: "Emath"</note>.
4 And he left them, that in them he might try Israel, whether they would hear the commandments of the Lord, which he had commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses, or not.
5 So the children of Israel dwelt in the midst of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
6 And they took their daughters as wives, and they gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.
7 And they did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgot their God, serving the Baals <note>original: "Baalim"</note> and the Asherahs <note>original: "Astaroth"</note>.
8 And the Lord, being angry against Israel, delivered them into the hands of Cushan-rishathaim <note>original: "Chusan Rasathaim"</note> king of Mesopotamia, and they served him eight years.
9 And they cried out to the Lord: who raised up for them a savior, and delivered them, namely Othniel <note>original: "Othoniel"</note> the son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb:
10 And the Spirit of the Lord was in him, and he judged Israel. And he went out to battle, and the Lord delivered into his hands Cushan-rishathaim king of Syria <note>The Latin text here uses "Syria" interchangeably with "Mesopotamia" to refer to the region of Aram</note>, and he overwhelmed him.
11 And the land rested for forty years, and Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
12 But the children of Israel added to do evil in the sight of the Lord: who strengthened against them Eglon king of Moab: because they did evil in his sight.
13 And he joined to him the children of Ammon, and Amalek, and he went and struck Israel, and possessed the city of palms <note>Jericho</note>.
14 And the children of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years:
15 And afterwards they cried out to the Lord: who raised up for them a savior called Ehud <note>original: "Aod"</note>, the son of Gera, the son of Jemini, who used both hands as the right <note>A Latin idiom for being left-handed</note>. And the children of Israel sent gifts by him to Eglon king of Moab.
16 And he made himself a two-edged sword, having a handle in the middle of the length of a palm of the hand, and he girded it under his cloak <note>original: "sagum"</note> on his right thigh.
17 And he offered the gifts to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was very fat.
18 And when he had offered the gifts to him, he followed his companions who had come with him.
19 And returning from Gilgal <note>original: "Galgalis"</note>, where the idols were, he said to the king: "I have a secret word for you, O king." And he commanded silence: and all who were around him went out.
20 Ehud went in to him: but he was sitting 

<column-break/>

alone in a summer upper room <note>original: "æstivo cœnaculo"</note>: and he said: "I have a word from God for you." He immediately rose from his throne.
21 And Ehud reached out his left hand, and took the dagger <note>original: "sicam"</note> from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly
22 So strongly, that the handle followed the iron into the wound, and was enclosed by the very thick fat. Nor did he draw out the sword, but as he had struck, he left it in the body: and immediately, by the secret parts of nature, the dung of the bowels burst forth.
23 But Ehud, having very carefully closed the doors of the upper room and fastened them with a bolt,
24 Escaped through a back door. And the king's servants entering, saw the doors of the upper room closed, and they said: "Perhaps he is purging his bowels in the summer chamber."
25 And waiting a long time until they were ashamed, and seeing that no one opened, they took a key: and opening they found their lord lying dead on the ground.
26 But Ehud, while they were troubled, escaped, and passed by the place of the idols, from where he had returned. And he came to Seirah:
27 And immediately the trumpet sounded in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel went down with him, he himself walking at the head.
28 Who said to them: "Follow me: for the Lord has delivered our enemies the Moabites into our hands." And they went down after him, and occupied the fords of the Jordan that cross into Moab: and they did not allow anyone to pass:
29 But they struck the Moabites at that time, about ten thousand, all robust and strong men: none of them could escape.
30 And Moab was humbled on that day under the hand of Israel: and the land rested for eighty years.
31 After him was Shamgar <note>original: "Samgar"</note> the son of Anath, who struck six hundred men of the Philistines with a plowshare <note>original: "vomere"</note>: and he also defended Israel.

### CHAPTER IV.

> *Deborah the prophetess and Barak fight successfully against Sisera the commander of king Jabin’s army, whom Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite <note>original: "Cinæi"</note> kills as a fugitive.*

1 And the children of Israel added to do evil in the sight of the Lord after the death of Ehud,
<margin>† 1 Samuel <note>original: "1. Reg." - in the Vulgate, the books of Samuel are titled 1 and 2 Kings</note> 12:9.</margin>

### CHAPTER V.

->*The triumphal song and thanksgiving of Deborah and Barak after the victory.*<-

1 And Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying:

2 You of Israel who willingly offered your lives to danger, bless the Lord.

3 Hear, O kings; give ear, O princes: It is I, it is I who shall sing to the Lord, I will sing psalms to the Lord the God of Israel.

4 Lord, when you went out of Seir, and passed through the regions of Edom, the earth trembled, and the heavens and clouds poured down water.

5 The mountains melted before the face of the Lord, even Sinai before the face of the Lord God of Israel.

6 In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the paths were quiet: and those who traveled through them walked by crooked bypasses.

7 The brave men in Israel ceased and were quiet: until Deborah arose, a <term>mother in Israel</term><note>A title of honor signifying Deborah's role as a protector, counselor, and source of life for the nation.</note> arose.

8 The Lord chose new wars, and he himself overthrew the gates of the enemies: a shield or spear was hardly seen among forty thousand of Israel.

9 My heart loves the princes of Israel: you who of your own will offered yourselves to danger, bless the Lord.

10 You who ride upon <term>shining donkeys</term><note>original: "nitentes asinos" — likely white donkeys, which were expensive and used by nobility or judges.</note>, and sit in judgment, and walk on the way, speak.

11 Where the chariots were crushed, and the army of the enemy was stifled, there let the justice of the Lord be told, and his mercy toward the brave of Israel: then the people of the Lord went down to the gates, and obtained the sovereignty.

12 Arise, arise, Deborah, arise, arise, and speak a song: arise, Barak, and take your captives, O son of Abinoam.

13 The remnant of the people are saved, the Lord has fought among the brave.

14 From Ephraim he destroyed them in Amalek, and after him from Benjamin among your people, O Amalek: from Machir the princes came down, and from Zebulun those who led the army to war.

15 The leaders of Issachar were with Deborah, and followed the steps of Barak, who gave himself to danger as if headlong into a pit: Ruben being divided against himself, a contention of great-hearted men was found.

16 Why do you dwell between two borders, that you may hear the whistling of the flocks? Ruben being divided against himself, a contention of great-hearted men was found. <note>This refers to the tribe of Reuben failing to join the battle, preferring to stay with their sheep.</note>

17 Gilead rested beyond the Jordan, and Dan was busy with ships: Asher dwelt on the seashore, and stayed in the harbors.

18 But Zebulun and Naphtali offered their lives to death in the region of Merom.

19 The kings came and fought, the kings of Canaan fought in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, and yet they took no spoil.

20 From heaven it was fought against them: the stars remaining in their order and course, fought against Sisera.

21 The brook Kishon dragged away their carcasses, the brook Cadumim, the brook Kishon: trample, my soul, upon the strong ones.

22 The horse hooves fell off as the strongest of the enemies fled in headlong haste.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*With the Israelites oppressed by Midian, Gideon is chosen as an aid through many signs; after a sacrifice and an altar were erected to God, he destroyed the altar of Baal, and again a sign is given to him in a fleece.*<-

But the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord: who delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years,
2 And they were greatly oppressed by them. And they made for themselves dens and caves in the mountains, and very strong places for resistance.

### CHAPTER VIII.

->*The tribe of Ephraim rises up against Gideon, thinking itself despised; he calms them with gentle words, and having conquered Zebah and Zalmunna, he destroyed the men of Succoth and Penuel. From the earrings and other gifts of the people, he made an Ephod, which brought ruin to his house and to Israel. After he had ruled for forty years, having fathered seventy sons by his wives and one, Abimelech, by a concubine, he died, and Israel returned to idolatry.*<-

1 And the men of Ephraim said to him: What is this thing you intended to do, that you did not call us when you went to fight against Midian? And they rebuked him strongly, nearly using force. 
2 To whom he replied: What have I been able to do that compares to what you have done? Is not the gleaning <note>original: "racemus"</note> of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer? <note>Gideon uses a humble metaphor: even the small part Ephraim played at the end was more significant than his own family's entire effort.</note>
3 Into your hands the Lord delivered the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; what could I do that compares to what you have done? When he had said this, their spirit, which was swelling against him, grew calm.
4 And when Gideon came to the Jordan, he crossed it with the three hundred men who were with him; and because of their weariness, they were unable to pursue those who fled.
5 And he said to the men of Succoth: Give, I pray you, bread to the people who are with me, because they are failing; so that we may be able to pursue Zebah <note>original: "Zebee"</note> and Zalmunna <note>original: "Salmana"</note>, the kings of Midian.
6 The princes of Succoth responded: Perhaps the palms of the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna are already in your hand, and therefore you demand that we give bread to your army. <note>Succoth refused to help because they feared the Midianite kings would return and punish them if Gideon failed.</note>
7 To whom he said: Therefore, when the Lord has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hands, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns and briers of the desert.
8 And going up from there, he came to Penuel <note>original: "Phanuel"</note>; and he spoke similar things to the men of that place. And they answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered.
9 He said therefore to them: When I return as a victor in peace, I will destroy this tower.
10 Now Zebah and Zalmunna were resting with all their army. For fifteen thousand men remained from all the troops of the eastern peoples, a hundred and twenty thousand warriors who drew the sword having been slain.
<margin>† Hosea 10:14</margin>

17 He also overthrew the tower of Penuel, having killed the inhabitants of the city.
