19 To whom he replied: They were my brothers, the sons of my mother; as the Lord lives, if you had saved them, I would not kill you.
20 And he said to Jether, his firstborn: Rise and kill them. But he did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a boy.

21 And Zebah and Zalmunna said: You rise and fall upon us: because according to his age, so is a man's strength. Gideon rose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna; and he took the ornaments and crescents <note>original: "bullas"</note> with which the necks of royal camels are usually decorated.
22 And all the men of Israel said to Gideon: Rule over us, both you and your son, and your son's son: because you have delivered us from the hand of Midian.
23 To whom he said: I will not rule over you, nor shall my son rule over you, but the Lord shall rule over you.

25 They answered: We will give them most gladly. And spreading a cloak upon the ground, they threw the earrings from the prey into it.
26 And the weight of the requested earrings was one thousand seven hundred gold shekels <note>original: "sicli"</note>, besides the ornaments and necklaces and purple clothing which the kings of Midian were accustomed to use, and besides the golden chains of the camels.
27 And Gideon made an Ephod <note>A ceremonial priestly vestment, but here it became an object of worship or a localized shrine.</note> from it, and placed it in his city, Ophrah <note>original: "Ephra"</note>. And all Israel committed spiritual harlotry <note>original: "fornicatus est"</note> with it, and it became a ruin to Gideon and all his house.
28 Thus was Midian humbled before the children of Israel, nor could they lift their necks any further; and the land was at rest for forty years, during which Gideon presided.
29 And so Jerubbaal <note>original: "Jerobaal"</note> the son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house.
30 And he had seventy sons, who issued from his thigh, because he had many wives.
31 Moreover, his concubine whom he had in Shechem bore him a son named Abimelech.
32 And Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father in Ophrah, of the family of Ezri.

<summary>Gideon completes the defeat of Midian by capturing and executing kings Zebah and Zalmunna, punishes the uncooperative Israelites of Succoth and Penuel, and creates a golden Ephod that leads the nation back into idolatry before his death.</summary>

### CHAPTER IX.

->*Abimelech, having slain his seventy brothers, tyrannically usurps the command; who, after the parable of Jotham his brother who had been saved, defeated the army of Gaal and burned the tower of Shechem, and was finally crushed by a woman with a fragment of a millstone.*<-

1 Now Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem to his mother’s brothers, and spoke to them and to all the kindred of his mother’s father’s house, saying:
2 Speak to all the men of Shechem: Which is better for you, that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, should rule over you, or that one man should rule? And consider that I am your own bone and your own flesh.
3 And his mother’s brothers spoke all these words concerning him to all the men of Shechem; and their hearts inclined after Abimelech, for they said: "He is our brother."
4 And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of Baal-berith. With this, Abimelech hired worthless and wandering men <note>original: "viros inopes & vagos," implying social outcasts or mercenaries</note> for himself, and they followed him.
5 And he came to his father’s house in Ophrah and killed his brothers, the seventy sons of Jerubbaal, upon a single stone. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, remained, for he was hidden.
6 Then all the men of Shechem gathered together, and all the families of the city of Millo <note>likely referring to a fortification or "the fill" of the city</note>; and they went and made Abimelech king, by the oak that stood in Shechem.
7 When this was told to Jotham, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim; and lifting up his voice, he cried out and said: Listen to me, men of Shechem, so that God may listen to you.
8 The trees went forth to anoint a king over themselves; and they said to the olive tree: "Rule over us."
9 But it answered: "Can I leave my fatness <note>original: "pinguedinem," referring to the oil</note>, which both gods and men use, and come to be promoted among the trees?"
10 And the trees said to the fig tree: "Come, and take the kingdom over us."
11 But it answered them: "Can I leave my sweetness and my most delicious fruits, and go to be promoted among the other trees?"
12 And the trees said to the vine: "Come, and rule over us."
13 But it answered them: "Can I leave my wine, which cheers God and men, and be promoted among the other trees?"
14 Then all the trees said to the bramble <note>original: "rhamnum," a thorny bush of little value</note>: "Come, and rule over us."
15 And it answered them: "If you truly constitute me king over you, come and rest under my shadow; but if you will not, let fire come out of the bramble and devour the cedars of Lebanon."
16 Now therefore, if you have acted rightly and without sin in making Abimelech king over you, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and with his house,

<column-break/>

and have repaid him for his benefits, who fought for you,
17 and gave his life to dangers to rescue you from the hand of Midian,
18 you who have now risen up against my father’s house and have killed his sons, seventy men, upon a single stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the inhabitants of Shechem because he is your brother:
19 If, therefore, you have acted rightly and without fault toward Jerubbaal and his house, rejoice today in Abimelech, and let him rejoice in you.
20 But if perversely: let fire come out from him and consume the inhabitants of Shechem and the town of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem and from the town of Millo, and devour Abimelech.
21 When he had said these things, he fled and went to Beer; and he lived there for fear of his brother Abimelech.
22 So Abimelech reigned over Israel for three years.
23 And the Lord sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the inhabitants of Shechem; and they began to detest him,
24 and to cast the crime of the murder of the seventy sons of Jerubbaal and the shedding of their blood upon Abimelech their brother, and upon the rest of the princes of the Shechemites who had helped him.
25 And they set ambushes against him on the tops of the mountains; and while they waited for his arrival, they committed robberies, taking spoils from those passing by; and it was told to Abimelech.
26 Then Gaal the son of Ebed came with his brothers and passed into Shechem. At his arrival, the inhabitants of Shechem were encouraged,
27 and they went out into the fields, wasting the vineyards and treading the grapes. And having formed choirs of singers, they entered the temple of their god, and amid feasting and drinking, they cursed Abimelech,
28 while Gaal the son of Ebed cried out: "Who is Abimelech, and what is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and has he not appointed his servant Zebul as governor over the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem? Why then should we serve him?
29 Would that someone would put this people under my hand, so that I might remove Abimelech from the midst." And it was said to Abimelech: "Gather a multitude of the army, and come."
30 For Zebul, the ruler of the city, hearing the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, was very angry.
31 And he secretly sent messengers to Abimelech, saying: "Behold, Gaal the son of Ebed has come into Shechem with his brothers, and he is inciting the city against you.
32 Therefore, rise by night with the people who are with you and lie hidden in the field.
33 and early in the morning at sunrise, rush upon the city. And when he comes out against you with his people, do to him what you are able."
34 So Abimelech rose by night with all his army and set ambushes near Shechem in four places.
35 And Gaal the son of Ebed went out and stood in the entrance of the city gate. Then Abimelech and all the army with him rose from the place of the ambush.
36 And when Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul: "Behold, a multitude is descending from the mountains." To which he replied: "You see the shadows of the mountains as if they were the heads of men, and you are deceived by this error."

## CHAPTER X.

*Tola is made leader; after his life ends, Jair succeeds him. The Israelites, however, falling into idolatry, are handed over to the Philistines and Ammonites. When they repent, the Lord reproaches their ingratitude, but finally takes pity on them.*

1 After Abimelech, there arose a leader in Israel, Tola the son of Puah, the uncle of Abimelech <note>original: "patrui Abimelech," though genealogically Tola is usually identified as the son of Puah, son of Dodo</note>, a man of Issachar, who lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
2 And he judged Israel for twenty-three years, and he died and was buried in Shamir.
3 He was succeeded by Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel for twenty-two years.
4 He had thirty sons, riding on thirty donkey colts <note>original: "pullos asinarum," a sign of wealth and high social status in the ancient Near East</note>, and they were leaders of thirty cities; which from his name are called Havoth-jair (that is, the Villages of Jair) even to this day, in the land of Gilead.
5 And Jair died, and was buried in the place called Kamon.
6 But the children of Israel, adding new sins to their old ones, did evil in the sight of the Lord and served idols: the Baals and Ashtoreths, and the gods of Syria, Sidon, Moab, the children of Ammon, and the Philistines. They abandoned the Lord and did not worship Him.
7 Against them the Lord was angry and delivered them into the hands of the Philistines and the children of Ammon.
8 And they were afflicted and vehemently oppressed for eighteen years—all those who lived across the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
9 To such an extent that the children of Ammon, having crossed the Jordan, devastated Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim; and Israel was greatly distressed.
10 And crying out to the Lord, they said: "We have sinned against You, because we have forsaken the Lord our God and have served the Baals."
11 The Lord spoke to them: "Did not the Egyptians and the Amorites, the children of Ammon and the Philistines,
12 The Sidonians also, and Amalek, and Canaan, oppress you? And you cried to Me, and I rescued you from their hands.
13 And yet you have left Me and worshipped foreign gods; therefore, I will no longer deliver you.
14 Go and call upon the gods you have chosen; let them deliver you in the time of your distress."
15 And the children of Israel said to the Lord: "We have sinned; do to us whatever pleases You; only deliver us now."
16 Saying these things, they cast out all the idols of foreign gods from their borders and served the Lord God; and He grieved over their miseries.
17 Thus the children of Ammon, calling one another together in Gilead, pitched their tents; against them the children of Israel gathered and camped in Mizpah.
18 And the leaders of Gilead said to one another: "Whoever is the first among us to begin to fight against the children of Ammon shall be the leader of the people of Gilead."

## CHAPTER XI.

Jephthah is made judge, and being set on fire by the Spirit of God, he first deals with the king of the Ammonites through reason; later, when he had defeated them, he sacrifices his only daughter to God because of a rash vow he had made.
</insert>

1 Now Jephthah the Gileadite was at that time a very valiant man and a warrior, the son of a harlot, born to Gilead.
2 But Gilead also had a wife, from whom he fathered sons; and when they grew up, they drove Jephthah out, saying: "You shall not be an heir in our father's house, because you were born of another mother."
3 Fleeing and avoiding them, he lived in the land of Tob; and there gathered to him needy men and bandits <note>original: "latrocinantes," referring to men living outside the law, often as mercenary soldiers or raiders</note>, and they followed him as their leader.
4 In those days, the children of Ammon were making war against Israel.
5 And as they pressed hard against them, the elders of Gilead went to take Jephthah from the land of Tob to help them.
6 And they said to him: "Come and be our leader, and fight against the children of Ammon."

7 He answered them: "Are you not the ones who hated me, and drove me out of my father's house? And now you come to me, compelled by necessity?"
8 And the princes of Gilead said to Jephthah: "It is for this very reason that we have now come to you—that you may go with us, and fight against the children of Ammon, and be the leader of all who dwell in Gilead."
9 Jephthah said to them: "If you truly come to me so that I may fight for you against the children of Ammon, and the Lord delivers them into my hands, shall I be your prince?"
10 They answered him: "The Lord, who hears these things, is himself the mediator and witness that we will perform our promises."
11 So Jephthah went with the princes of Gilead, and all the people made him their leader. And Jephthah spoke all his words before the Lord in Mizpah.
12 Then he sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, who were to say on his behalf: "What is there between me and you, that you have come against me to lay waste to my land?"

# CHAPTER XII.

->*The Ephraimites, unjustly rising up against Jephthah,*<-
->*are slain at the fords of the Jordan to the number of 42,000,*<-
->*because they could not pronounce the word Shibboleth;*<-
->*when he passed away, he was succeeded by the leaders Ibzan,*<-
->*Elon, and Abdon.*<-

But behold, a rebellion arose in Ephraim: for crossing over toward the north, they said to Jephthah: "Why did you go to fight against the children of Ammon and refuse to call us, so that we might go with you? Therefore, we will burn down your house."
2 To whom he replied: "I and my people had a fierce dispute with the children of Ammon: and I called you to provide me help, but you refused to do it.
3 Seeing this, I put my life in my hands <note>original: "posui animam meam in manibus meis," a Hebrew idiom meaning to risk one's life or take a great personal danger</note>, and I crossed over to the children of Ammon, and the Lord delivered them into my hands. What have I done to deserve that you should rise up against me in battle?"
4 Therefore, having called all the men of Gilead to him, he fought against Ephraim: and the men of Gilead struck down Ephraim, because he had said: "Gilead is a fugitive from Ephraim, and dwells in the midst of Ephraim and Manasseh."
5 And the Gileadites seized the fords of the Jordan, through which Ephraim was to return. And when anyone from the number of Ephraim who was fleeing came to them and said: "I pray you, let me cross over," the Gileadites said to him: "Are you an Ephraimite?" and when he said: "I am not,"
6 They questioned him: "Say then, *Shibboleth*," which is interpreted as an "ear of grain" <note>original: "Scibboleth, quod interpretatur Spica." This was a linguistic test; the Ephraimites lacked the "sh" sound in their dialect</note>. He would answer, "Sibboleth," being unable to express the "ear of grain" with that same letter. And immediately they would seize him and slit his throat at the very passage of the Jordan. And there fell at that time forty-two thousand from Ephraim.
7 Thus Jephthah the Gileadite judged Israel for six years: and he died, and was buried in his city, Gilead.
8 After him, Ibzan <note>original: "Abesan"</note> of Bethlehem judged Israel:
9 He had thirty sons and as many daughters, whom he sent abroad to be given to husbands, and he took wives for his sons of the same number, bringing them into his house. He judged Israel for seven years.
10 And he died, and was buried in Bethlehem.
11 He was succeeded by Elon <note>original: "Ahialon"</note> the Zebulunite: and he judged Israel for ten years:
12 And he died, and was buried in Zebulun.
13 After him, Abdon, the son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, judged Israel:
14 He had forty sons, and thirty grandsons from them, who rode upon seventy donkey colts <note>a sign of wealth and status in the ancient world</note>, and he judged Israel for eight years:
15 And he died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, on the mountain of Amalek.

# CHAPTER XIII.

->*The Israelites, having fallen again into idolatry, are*<-
->*delivered to the Philistines: Samson’s birth is*<-
->*foretold by an angel to his mother, and then to his father,*<-
->*and having been born, he is blessed by the Lord.*<-

And again the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord: who delivered them into the hands of the Philistines for forty years.
2 Now there was a certain man of Zorah <note>original: "Saraa"</note>, and of the stock of Dan, named Manoah <note>original: "Manue"</note>, who had a sterile wife.
<margin>† but Genesis 16:11; 1 Samuel 1:20.</margin>
3 To her the angel of the Lord appeared, and said to her: "You are sterile and without children: but you shall conceive and bear a son: † take care therefore that you do not drink wine or strong drink <note>original: "siceram," referring to any fermented intoxicating liquor other than wine</note>, nor eat anything unclean:
<margin>Luke 1:31; Numbers 6:3-4.</margin>
5 Because you shall conceive and bear a son, whose head no razor shall touch: for he shall be a Nazirite <note>term: Nazirite. From the Hebrew 'nazir' (consecrated/separated). A person who took a vow to abstain from alcohol, cutting hair, and contact with the dead</note> of God from his infancy, and from his mother’s womb, and he himself shall begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
6 When she had come to her husband, she said to him: "A man of God came to me, having an angelic countenance, exceeding terrible. When I asked him who he was, and where he came from, and by what name he was called, he would not tell me:
7 But he answered this: 'Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son: take care that you drink no wine, nor strong drink, and that you eat nothing unclean: for the boy shall be a Nazirite of God from his infancy, from the womb of his mother even until the day of his death.'"
8 Therefore Manoah prayed to the Lord, and said: "I beseech you, Lord, that the man of God, whom you sent, may come again, and teach us what we ought to do for the boy who is to be born."
9 And the Lord heard Manoah as he prayed, and the angel of God appeared again to his wife as she sat in the field. But Manoah her husband was not with her. When she had seen the angel,
10 She made haste, and ran to her husband: and she told him, saying: "Behold, the man has appeared to me, whom I had seen before."
11 He arose and followed his wife: and coming to the man, he said to him: "Are you the one who spoke to the woman?" and he replied: "I am."
12 To whom Manoah said: "When your word shall be fulfilled, what do you wish the boy to do? Or from what must he keep himself?"
13 And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah: "From all the things that I spoke to your wife, let him abstain:
14 And whatever comes from the vine, let him not eat: wine and strong drink let him not drink, let him eat no unclean thing: and what I have commanded her, let him fulfill and keep."
15 And Manoah said to the angel of the Lord: "I pray you to yield to my requests, and let us prepare for you a kid from the goats."
16 To whom the angel replied: "If you compel me, I will not eat your bread: but if you wish to make a burnt offering, offer it to the Lord." And Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the Lord.
17 And he said to him: "What is your name, so that, if your word is fulfilled, we may honor you?"

### CHAPTER XIV.

*Samson takes a Philistine wife; while visiting her, he tore a lion apart, in whose mouth honey was later found, from which he took a riddle: when it was proposed to his companions, they learned the interpretation through Samson’s wife.*

1 Samson then went down to Timnah, and seeing there a woman from the daughters of the Philistines,
2 he went up and told his father and mother, saying: "I have seen a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines: I ask that you take her as a wife for me."
3 His father and mother said to him: "Is there no woman among the daughters of your brothers, or among all my people, that you wish to take a wife from the Philistines, who are uncircumcised?" And Samson said to his father: "Take this one for me, for she has pleased my eyes."
4 Now his parents did not know that this matter was from the Lord, and that he was seeking an occasion against the Philistines; for at that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.
5 So Samson went down with his father and mother to Timnah. And when they had come to the vineyards of the town, a fierce young lion appeared, roaring, and it rushed at him.
6 But the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon Samson, and he tore the lion to pieces, as if he were tearing a young goat into bits, though he had nothing at all in his hand: and he did not want to tell this to his father or mother.
7 And he went down and spoke to the woman who had pleased his eyes.
8 And after some days, returning to take her, he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and behold, there was a swarm of bees in the mouth of the lion, and a honeycomb.
9 When he had taken it in his hands, he ate it on the way; and coming to his father and mother, he gave them a portion, and they also ate; yet he did not want to tell them that he had taken the honey from the body of the lion.
10 So his father went down to the woman and prepared a feast for his son Samson; for this was what young men were accustomed to do.
11 Therefore, when the citizens of that place saw him, they gave him thirty companions to be with him.
12 Samson said to them: "I will propose a riddle to you; if you solve it for me within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and as many tunics.

<column-break/>

13 But if you cannot solve it, you shall give me thirty linen garments and the same number of tunics." They replied to him: "Propose the riddle, so that we may hear it."
14 And he said to them: "Out of the eater came food, and out of the strong came sweetness" <note>The "eater" and "strong" refer to the lion, while the "food" and "sweetness" refer to the honey Samson found inside it.</note>: nor could they solve the proposition for three days.
15 And when the seventh day arrived, they said to Samson’s wife: "Coax your husband, and persuade him to reveal to you what the riddle means; for if you will not do it, we will burn you and your father’s house. Did you call us to the wedding just to strip us bare?"
16 She shed tears before Samson and complained, saying: "You hate me and do not love me; therefore, you do not want to explain the riddle you proposed to the children of my people." But he answered: "I would not even tell my father and mother; and should I tell you?"
17 So she wept before him for the seven days of the feast; and finally on the seventh day, as she was troublesome to him, he explained it. She immediately revealed it to her fellow citizens.
18 And they said to him on the seventh day before the setting of the sun: "What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion?" He said to them: "If you had not plowed with my heifer <note>original: "Si non arassetis in vitula mea," a proverbial expression meaning they used his wife to extract the answer from him</note>, you would not have found out my riddle."
19 And so the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men there, whose garments he took and gave to those who had solved the riddle. And being very angry, he went up to his father’s house.
20 But his wife took one of his friends and groomsmen as a husband.

### CHAPTER XV.

*With three hundred foxes and torches, Samson burns the Philistines' crops, and having broken the ropes with which he was bound, he struck down a thousand Philistines with the jawbone of a donkey, from whose molar tooth water flowed for him when he was thirsty.*

1 But after a little while, when the days of the wheat harvest were near, Samson came, wishing to visit his wife, and brought her a young goat. And when he wanted to enter her chamber as usual, her father forbade him, saying:
2 "I thought you hated her, and therefore I gave her to your friend; but she has a sister who is younger and more beautiful than she; let her be your wife instead."
3 Samson answered him: "From this day on, there shall be no blame on me against the Philistines; for I will do you harm."
4 And he went and caught three hundred foxes, and joined their tails together, and tied torches in the middle.
5 Setting these on fire, he let them loose so they would run here and there. They immediately went into the grain fields of the Philistines. When these were set on fire, both the crops already gathered and those still standing in the stalk were burned, so much so that the flame even consumed the vineyards and olive groves.
6 And the Philistines said: "Who has done this thing?" They were told: "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite; because he took his wife and gave her to another, Samson did this." And the Philistines went up and burned both the woman and her father.
7 Samson said to them: "Though you have done this, I will still seek revenge upon you, and then I will rest."

12 They said, "We have come to bind you and deliver you into the hands of the Philistines." Samson said to them: "Swear and promise me that you will not kill me yourselves."

14 When he had come to the place of the Jawbone, and the Philistines met him with shouting, the Spirit of the Lord rushed upon him; and just as flax is consumed at the scent of fire, so the bonds with which he was tied were scattered and loosened.
15 And finding a jawbone—that is, the jawbone of a donkey—that was lying there, he snatched it up and killed a thousand men with it.
16 And he said: "With the jawbone of a donkey, with the jaw of a young donkey, I have destroyed them and struck down a thousand men."
17 When he had finished singing these words, he threw the jawbone from his hand and called the name of that place Ramath-lechi, which is translated as "the Height of the Jawbone."
18 Being very thirsty, he cried out to the Lord and said: "You have given this greatest salvation and victory into the hand of your servant; behold, I am dying of thirst and falling into the hands of the uncircumcised."
19 So the Lord opened a molar tooth in the jawbone <note>While the text says God opened a tooth in the donkey's jawbone, many interpreters suggest this refers to a hollow place in the ground at the location called Lechi (the Jawbone)</note>, and water came out of it. When he had drunk, his spirit was revived and his strength returned. Therefore the name of that place was called "The Spring of the One Crying Out from the Jawbone" even to this day.
20 And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines for twenty years.

### CHAPTER XVI.

*Samson, with guards watching him, carried the gates of the city of Gaza to a mountain; later, having been deceived by Delilah—to whom he had often lied—the cause of his strength was known. He is captured, mocked, and blinded by his enemies, whom he eventually killed along with himself, specifically 3,000 Philistines.*

1 He also went to Gaza and saw there a harlot and went in to her.
2 When the Philistines heard this, and the rumor spread among them that Samson had entered the city, they surrounded him, placing guards at the gate of the city. They waited there in silence all night so that they might kill him as he left in the morning.

the doors of the gate with their posts and the bar, and placing them on his shoulders, he carried them to the top of the mountain that faces Hebron.

6 So Delilah spoke to Samson: "Tell me, I pray you, wherein your greatest strength lies, and what it is that, if you were bound with it, you could not break free?"
7 Samson answered her: "If I am bound with seven gut strings <note>original: "nerviceis funibus"; cords made of animal sinew or bowstrings</note> that are not yet dry but still moist, I shall be weak like other men."

9 With an ambush hidden with her in the bedroom waiting for the outcome, she cried out to him: "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" But he snapped the bonds just as a thread of hemp is snapped when it feels the scent of fire; and the secret of his strength was not known.
10 And Delilah said to him: "Behold, you have mocked me and spoken falsely. At least now tell me what you should be bound with."
11 He answered her: "If I am bound with new ropes that have never been used for work, I shall be weak and like other men."
12 Delilah bound him with these again and cried: "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" while the ambush was prepared in the bedroom. He snapped them like weaver's threads.
13 Delilah said to him again: "How long will you deceive me and tell me lies? Show me what you should be bound with." Samson answered her: "If you weave the seven locks of my head with a web and fasten them into the ground with a pin, I shall be weak."
14 When Delilah had done this, she said to him: "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" Rising from sleep, he pulled out the pin with the hair and the web.
15 And Delilah said to him: "How can you say you love me, when your heart is not with me? Three times you have lied to me and would not tell me wherein your greatest strength lies."
16 And when she was bothersome to him and pressed him continually for many days, giving him no space for rest, his soul fainted and was weary even unto death.

If my head were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I would grow weak and be like all other men."
18 Seeing that he had confessed his whole heart to her, she sent to the princes of the Philistines and commanded: "Come up once more, for now he has opened his heart to me." They came up, bringing the money they had promised.

### C H A P T E R XVII.

> *Micah’s mother casts an idol for him from saved silver, over which he first appoints his own son as priest, and later a Levite from Bethlehem.*

At that time there was a certain man from the hill country of Ephraim named Micah,

2 Who said to his mother: "The eleven hundred silver pieces which you had set aside for yourself, and concerning which I heard you swear an oath—behold, I have them, they are with me." She replied to him: "Blessed be my son by the Lord."

3 So he returned them to his mother, who had said to him: "I have consecrated and vowed this silver to the Lord, so that my son may receive it from my hand and make a carved and a cast image <note>original: "sculptile atque conflatile"</note>; and now I deliver it to you."

4 He therefore returned them to his mother; and she took two hundred silver pieces and gave them to a silversmith, that he might make from them a carved and a cast image, which remained in Micah's house.

<column-break/>

5 He also set apart a small shrine in his house for God, and made an ephod and teraphim <note>original: "ephod, & theraphim"; the text explains these as a "priestly garment and idols"</note>, and he consecrated one of his sons, who became his priest.

6 In those days there was no king in Israel, but everyone did what seemed right to himself.

7 There was also another young man from Bethlehem in Judah, from that kindred; he was a Levite, and he lived there.

8 Leaving the city of Bethlehem, he wished to travel as a pilgrim to wherever he might find a suitable place. When he had come into the hill country of Ephraim while traveling, and had turned aside for a while into the house of Micah,

9 He was asked by Micah where he had come from. He answered: "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to live wherever I am able and where I see it will be useful for me."

10 And Micah said: "Stay with me, and be a father and a priest to me; and I will give you ten silver pieces every year, and a double set of clothing, and the things necessary for your food."

11 He agreed and stayed with the man, and he was to him as one of his sons.

12 And Micah consecrated him <note>original: "implevitque Michas manus ejus" - literally "filled his hands," a Hebrew idiom for ordination</note>, and had the young man as a priest in his house.

13 "Now I know," he said, "that God will do good to me, since I have a priest of the Levite race."

### C H A P T E R XVIII.

> *After first sending spies, six hundred men from the tribe of Dan followed, seeking a possession for themselves; and having taken Micah’s idol and priest, they took the city of Laish by force and inhabited it.*

In those days there was no king in Israel, and the tribe of Dan was seeking a possession for itself to dwell in; for until that day they had not received a strong portion among the other tribes.

2 Therefore the sons of Dan sent five very brave men of their lineage and family from Zorah and Eshtaol to explore the land and inspect it diligently; and they said to them: "Go, and survey the land." When they had gone and come into the hill country of Ephraim, and had entered the house of Micah, they rested there;

3 And recognizing the voice of the young Levite, and making use of his lodging, they said to him: "Who brought you here? What are you doing here? For what reason did you want to come here?"

4 He answered them: "Micah has provided this and that for me, and hired me for a wage to be his priest."

5 Then they asked him to consult the Lord, so that they might know whether they would proceed on a prosperous journey and if the matter would have a successful outcome.

6 He answered them: "Go in peace; the Lord looks upon your way and the journey you are taking."

7 So the five men departed and came to Laish <note>original: "Lais"</note>; and they saw the people living there without any fear, according to the custom of the Sidonians, secure and quiet, with no one at all resisting them, and of great wealth, separated far from Sidon and from all other men.

8 And returning to their brothers in Zorah and Eshtaol, they answered those who asked what they had done:

9 "Arise, let us go up against them; for we have seen a land that is very rich and fertile. Do not be negligent, do not delay; let us go and possess it, there will be no labor."

### CHAPTER XIX.

->*When a Levite was bringing his wife back from her parents' house, she was killed with monstrous lust by the inhabitants of Gibeah who were of the tribe of Benjamin. The husband, having cut the body into twelve parts, sent a portion to each tribe, calling upon the remaining tribes to avenge this unspeakable crime.*<-

1 There was a certain man, a Levite, living on the side of Mount Ephraim, who took a wife from Bethlehem in Judah.
2 She left him and returned to her father's house in Bethlehem, and remained with him for four months.
3 Her husband followed her, wishing to be reconciled to her and to speak kindly to her, to bring her back with him, having with him a servant and two donkeys. She received him and brought him into her father's house. When his father-in-law heard this and saw him, he met him joyfully,
4 and embraced the man. The son-in-law stayed in his father-in-law's house for three days, eating and drinking with him as a friend.
5 On the fourth day, rising up in the night, he wished to set out; but his father-in-law held him back and said to him: "Taste a little bread first and strengthen your stomach, and so you shall depart."
6 They sat down together, and ate and drank. And the father of the girl said to his son-in-law: "I pray you to stay here today, and let us be merry together."
7 But he, rising up, began to want to depart. Nevertheless, his father-in-law held him fast and made him stay with him.
8 When morning came, the Levite prepared for his journey. To whom his father-in-law said again: "I beg you to take a little food, and having regained your strength until the day grows late, depart afterward." So they ate together.
9 And the young man rose up to go with his wife and servant. His father-in-law spoke to him again: "Consider that the day is declining toward sunset and approaches evening; stay with me today also, and spend a joyful day, and tomorrow you shall set out to go to your house."
10 The son-in-law would not agree to his words, but immediately set out and came opposite Jebus, which is called by another name, Jerusalem, leading with him two loaded donkeys and his concubine.
11 And they were now near Jebus, and the day was turning into night. The servant said to his master: "Come, I beseech you, let us turn aside to the city of the Jebusites and stay in it."

14 They passed by Jebus, therefore, and continued the journey they had begun; and the sun set on them near Gibeah, which is in the tribe of Benjamin.
15 And they turned aside to it, to stay there.

18 He replied to him: "We set out from **Bethlehem in Judah**, and we are traveling to our home on the side of Mount Ephraim, from where we journeyed to Bethlehem; and now we are going to the **house of God** <note>Likely referring to the Tabernacle at Shiloh or the city of Bethel</note>, and no one is willing to receive us under their roof.
19 We have straw and hay for the donkeys' fodder, and bread and wine for the use of myself and your handmaid, and for the servant who is with me; we lack nothing except a place to stay."
20 The old man answered him: "Peace be with you; I will provide all things that are necessary; only, I pray, do not remain in the square."
21 And he led him into his house and gave fodder to the donkeys; and after they had washed their feet, he received them into a feast.
<margin>† Genesis 19:5</margin>
22 While they were feasting and refreshing their bodies with food and drink after the labor of the journey, the men of that city, **sons of Belial** <note>A Hebrew idiom meaning "worthless" or "lawless" men</note> (that is, without a yoke), came and, surrounding the old man’s house, began to beat on the doors, crying out to the master of the house and saying: † "Bring out the man who entered your house, so that we may abuse him."
23 The old man went out to them and said: "Do not, brothers, do not do this evil, for this man has entered my home as a guest; cease from this folly.
24 I have a virgin daughter, and this man has a concubine; I will bring them out to you so that you may humble them and satisfy your lust; only, I beseech you, do not commit this crime against nature against this man."
25 They were unwilling to listen to his words; seeing this, the man led out his concubine to them and handed her over to be mocked. When they had abused her all night, they let her go in the morning.
26 But the woman, as the darkness receded, came to the door of the house where her master was staying, and there she collapsed.
27 When morning came, the man rose and opened the door to continue the journey he had begun; and behold, his concubine lay before the door with her hands spread upon the threshold.
28 Thinking she was resting, he spoke to her: "Rise, and let us walk." When she made no answer, realizing she was dead, he took her up and placed her on the donkey, and returned to his own home.
29 When he had entered, he took a sword and, cutting the corpse of his wife—bones and all—into twelve pieces and parts, he sent them into all the borders of Israel.
30 When everyone saw this, they cried out: "Never has such a thing been done in Israel from the day our fathers came up out of Egypt until the present time; give your judgment, and decide in common what needs to be done."

### CHAPTER XX.

*Because of this crime, the remaining tribes fought against Benjamin; being twice inferior in the war, and committing to battle a third time by the Lord's command, they utterly destroyed that tribe, except for six hundred men who had fled into the wilderness.*

<margin>† Hosea 9:9</margin>
1 Therefore, all the children of Israel went out and gathered together as one man, † from **Dan to Beersheba** <note>A common biblical phrase indicating the entire extent of the land from north to south</note>, along with the land of Gilead, unto the Lord in **Mizpah** <note>original: "Maspha"</note>.
2 And all the leaders of the people and all the tribes of Israel met in the assembly of the people of God: four hundred thousand foot soldiers.
3 (Nor did it escape the children of Benjamin that the children of Israel had gone up to Mizpah.) And the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, was asked how such a great crime had been committed.
4 He answered: "I came into Gibeah of Benjamin with my wife, and I turned aside there;
5 and behold, the men of that city surrounded the house where I was staying at night, wishing to kill me, and they harassed my wife with an incredible fury of lust; finally, she died.
6 I took her and cut her into pieces, and sent the parts into all the borders of your possession, because never has such a great wickedness and such a grand outrage been done in Israel.
7 All you children of Israel are present; decide what you ought to do."
8 And all the people standing, as if by the speech of one man, answered: "We will not return to our tents, nor shall anyone enter his own house;
9 but let us do this in common against Gibeah.
10 Let ten men be chosen out of a hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to carry food for the army, so that we may fight against Gibeah of Benjamin and repay it for the crime it deserves."
11 And all Israel gathered at the city as if one man, with the same mind and one counsel.
12 And they sent messengers to the whole tribe of Benjamin, saying: "Why has such a great wickedness been found among you?
13 Hand over the men of Gibeah who committed this outrage, so that they may die, and the evil may be taken away from Israel." But they would not listen to the command of their brothers, the children of Israel.
14 Instead, from all the cities that were of their lot, they gathered in Gibeah to bring them help and to fight against the whole people of Israel.
15 And twenty-five thousand men of Benjamin who draw the sword were found, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah,
16 who were seven hundred very brave men, fighting with the left hand as well as the right; and so skilled at throwing stones with slings at a fixed target that they could even hit a hair, and the strike of the stone would by no means be carried to either side.
17 Of the men of Israel, besides the children of Benjamin, four hundred thousand were found who draw the sword and were prepared for battle.
18 These, rising up, came to the house of God, that is, in **Shiloh** <note>original: "Silo"</note>; and they consulted God, saying: "Who shall be the leader in our army?"

44 Moreover, those who were killed in that same place were eighteen thousand men, all most robust fighters.

In that flight also, as they wandered and moved in different directions, the Israelites killed five thousand men. And as they moved further, they pursued them and killed another two thousand.
46 And so it happened that all who fell of Benjamin in various places were twenty-five thousand men, warriors most ready for battle.
47 Thus, out of the whole number of Benjamin, six hundred men were able to escape and flee into the wilderness: and they stayed at the rock of Rimmon for four months.
48 But the sons of Israel, returning, struck all the remains of the city with the sword, from men even to cattle; and the devouring flame consumed all the cities and villages of Benjamin.

## CHAPTER ONE

*Elimelech of Bethlehem, on account of a great famine, departs into the land of Moab with his wife Naomi and two sons; when he and his sons die there, Naomi returns to Bethlehem with her daughter-in-law Ruth, and wishes no longer to be called Naomi, but Mara.*

1 <image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'I' inside a square frame depicting a figure in a landscape with a building in the background.</image-desc> IN the days of one of the **judges** <note>original: "unius judicis," referring to the tribal leaders before the era of kings</note>, when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. And a man of Bethlehem-Judah went to travel in the region of **Moab** <note>original: "Moabitide," a kingdom east of the Dead Sea</note> with his wife and two children.

2 He was called **Elimelech**, and his wife **Naomi**; and his two sons, one **Mahlon** <note>original: "Mahalon"</note> and the other **Chilion** <note>original: "Chelion"</note>, Ephrathites from Bethlehem-Judah. And entering the region of Moab, they stayed there.

3 And Elimelech, the husband of Naomi, died; and she remained with her sons.

4 They took wives of the Moabites, one of whom was called **Orpah** and the other **Ruth**. And they lived there ten years.

5 And both Mahlon and Chilion died; and the woman was left alone, deprived of her two children and her husband.

<column-break/>

6 And she arose to go to her homeland with both her daughters-in-law from the region of Moab; for she had heard that the Lord had looked upon his people and had given them food.

7 She departed therefore from the place of her pilgrimage with both her daughters-in-law; and being now on the way to return to the land of Judah,

8 She said to them: "Go to your mother’s house; may the Lord deal mercifully with you, as you have dealt with the dead and with me.

9 May he grant you to find rest in the houses of the husbands whom you shall marry." And she kissed them. And they began to weep with a loud voice,

10 and to say: "We will go with you to your people."

11 To whom she replied: "Return, my daughters; why do you come with me? Do I have any more sons in my womb, that you might hope for husbands from me?

12 Return, my daughters, and go your way; for I am now worn out with old age, and not fit for the **marriage bond** <note>original: "vinculo conjugali"</note>. Even if I could conceive this night and bear sons,

13 if you chose to wait until they grew up and reached the years of puberty, you would be old women before you married. Do not do so, I pray you, my daughters; for your distress weighs more heavily upon me, and the hand of the Lord has gone out against me."

## CHAPTER II.

*Ruth, pressed by hunger, finds favor with Boaz, her kinsman, while gathering ears of grain in his field; returning to her mother-in-law in the evening, she brings her much grain and the remains of her food.*

1 Now Elimelech had a kinsman, a powerful man of great wealth named Boaz.
2 And Ruth the Moabite said to her mother-in-law: "If you command it, I will go into the field and gather the ears of grain that escape the hands of the reapers, wherever I may find favor with a kind master of the house." She answered her: "Go, my daughter."
3 She went, therefore, and gathered the ears of grain behind the backs of the reapers. And it happened that the owner of that field was named Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.
4 And behold, he himself was coming from Bethlehem, and he said to the reapers: "The Lord be with you." They answered him: "May the Lord bless you."
5 And Boaz said to the young man who was in charge of the reapers: "Whose girl is this?"
6 He answered him: "This is the Moabite woman who came with Naomi from the region of Moab.
7 She asked to gather the remaining ears of grain, following the footsteps of the reapers; and she has stood in the field from morning until now, and has not returned home even for a moment."
8 And Boaz said to Ruth: "Listen, daughter, do not go into another field to gather, nor depart from this place, but stay close to my young women,
9 and where they reap, follow them. For I have commanded my servants that no one should be troublesome to you; but 

<column-break/>

even if you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink the waters of which the young men also drink."
10 She, falling on her face and bowing to the ground, said to him: "How is this for me, that I should find favor in your eyes, and that you would deign to notice me, a foreign woman?"
11 He answered her: "All things have been reported to me which you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband: and how you left your parents, and the land in which you were born, and came to a people whom you did not know before.
12 May the Lord reward you for your work, and may you receive a full reward from the Lord God of Israel, to whom you have come, and under whose wings you have fled for refuge."
13 She said: "I have found favor in your eyes, my lord, who has comforted me and spoken to the heart of your handmaid, though I am not like one of your young women."
14 And Boaz said to her: "When the hour for eating comes, come here and eat bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar." So she sat at the side of the reapers, and he heaped up <term>parched grain<note>original: "polentam," referring here to toasted or roasted kernels of grain</note></term> for her; she ate and was satisfied, and took away the leftovers.
15 And she rose from there to gather the ears of grain as was the custom. But Boaz commanded his servants, saying: "Even if she wishes to reap with you, do not forbid her.
16 And also, throw down some of your bundles on purpose and allow them to remain, so that she may gather them without shame, and let no one rebuke her as she gathers."
17 So she gathered in the field until evening; and when she had beaten out and shaken what she had gathered with a rod, she found a measure of barley of about an <term>ephah<note>An ancient Hebrew dry measure roughly equal to 22 liters or three Roman modii</note></term>, that is, three <term>measures<note>original: "modios"</note></term>.
18 Carrying these, she returned to the city and showed them to her mother-in-law; moreover, she brought forth and gave to her the remains of her food, with which she had been satisfied.
19 And her mother-in-law said to her: "Where did you gather today, and where did you do your work? Blessed be he who had mercy on you." And she told her with whom she had worked, and gave the name of the man, saying he was called Boaz.
20 Naomi answered her: "May he be blessed by the Lord: for the same kindness which he showed to the living, he has preserved also for the dead." And again she said: "The man is our close relative."
21 And Ruth said, "He also commanded me this, that I should stay close to his reapers until all the crops were harvested."
22 Her mother-in-law said to her: "It is better, my daughter, that you go out with his young women to reap, lest in another field someone might resist you."
23 So she stayed joined to the young women of Boaz; and she reaped with them until the barley and the wheat were stored in the barns.

16 And came to her mother-in-law. Who said to her: "What have you done, daughter?" And she told her all that the man had done for her.
17 And she said: "Behold, he gave me six measures of barley, and said: I do not want you to return empty-handed to your mother-in-law."
18 And Naomi said: "Wait, daughter, until we see what end the matter will have: for the man will not rest unless he has fulfilled what he spoke."

## CHAPTER IV.

->*Boaz, before the elders of the city, takes possession of Elimelech's estate, and takes Ruth, the daughter-in-law of the deceased, as his wife (another closer kinsman yielding his right of kinship), from whom he fathered Obed, the grandfather of King David.*<-

**B**oaz therefore went up to the gate, and sat there. And when he had seen the kinsman

<column-break/>

passing by, of whom mention was made before, he said to him: "Turn aside for a moment, and sit here," calling him by his name. He turned aside and sat down.
2 Then Boaz, taking ten men from the elders of the city, said to them: "Sit here."
3 When they were seated, he spoke to the kinsman: "Naomi, who has returned from the region of Moab, is selling a portion of the field of our brother Elimelech;
4 I wanted you to hear this, and to tell you before all those sitting here, and before the elders of my people. If you wish to possess it by right of kinship: buy it and possess it: but if it displeases you, tell me this same thing, so that I may know what I ought to do: for there is no kinsman except you, who are first, and I, who am second." And he answered: "I will buy the field."
5 To whom Boaz said: "When you buy the field from the hand of the woman, you must also take Ruth the Moabite, who was the wife of the deceased: so that you may raise up the name of your kinsman in his inheritance."
6 He answered: "I yield my right of kinship: for I ought not to destroy the posterity of my own family: use my privilege, which I profess I willingly forfeit."
<margin>† Deuteronomy 25:7.</margin>
7 † Now this was the custom in ancient times in Israel among kinsmen: whenever one yielded his right to another, so that the grant would be firm, the man would take off his shoe and give it to his neighbor: this was the testimony of yielding in Israel. <note>This "shoe ceremony" symbolized the transfer of the right to walk upon and possess the land.</note>
8 Therefore Boaz said to his kinsman: "Take off your shoe." Which he immediately loosed from his foot.
9 Then he said to the elders and to all the people: "You are witnesses today that I have purchased all that belonged to Elimelech, and Chilion, and Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi;
10 And that I have taken Ruth the Moabite, the wife of Mahlon, in marriage, to raise up the name of the deceased in his inheritance, lest his name be blotted out from his family and his brothers and his people. You, I say, are witnesses of this matter."
11 All the people who were at the gate and the elders answered: "We are witnesses: may the Lord make this woman, who enters your house, like Rachel and Leah, who built up the house of Israel: that she may be an example of virtue in Ephrata, and have a famous name in Bethlehem;
<margin>† Genesis 38:29.</margin>
12 And may your house be like the house of Perez, † whom Tamar bore to Judah, from the seed which the Lord shall give you from this young woman."
13 So Boaz took Ruth and received her as his wife: and he went in to her, and the Lord granted her to conceive, and she bore a son.
14 And the women said to Naomi: "Blessed be the Lord, who has not allowed a successor to your family to fail, and may his name be called in Israel.
15 And may you have someone to comfort your soul and nourish your old age: for he is born of your daughter-in-law, who loves you, and who is much better to you than if you had seven sons."
16 And Naomi, taking the child, placed him in her bosom, and performed the office of a nurse.
17 And the neighboring women, congratulating her and saying: "A son is born to Naomi," called his name Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

# THE FIRST BOOK 
# OF SAMUEL,
### WHICH WE CALL THE
# FIRST BOOK OF KINGS
<note>original: "Primum Regum" — In the Latin Vulgate tradition, the books of 1 & 2 Samuel and 1 & 2 Kings were often grouped together as the four Books of Kings.</note>

### CHAPTER ONE.

<margin>I</margin>
*Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah; Hannah was barren for a long time and, saddened by the taunts of her rival, poured out a prayer to the Lord in Shiloh before Eli. She gave birth to Samuel, and once he was weaned, she offered him to the Lord as she had vowed.*

<margin>1</margin> THERE was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

<margin>2</margin> And he had two wives: the name of the first was Hannah, and the name of the second was Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

<margin>3</margin> This man went up from his city on the appointed days to worship and sacrifice to the Lord of hosts in Shiloh. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there serving as priests of the Lord.

<margin>4</margin> The day came, and Elkanah offered a sacrifice; he gave portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.

<margin>5</margin> But to Hannah he gave one portion with sadness, for he loved Hannah, though the Lord had closed her womb.

<margin>6</margin> Her rival also afflicted her and troubled her greatly, to the point of reproaching her because the Lord had closed her womb.

<margin>7</margin> And so it happened every year, when the time returned for them to go up to the temple of the Lord, that she would provoke her; and so Hannah wept and would not take any food.

<margin>8</margin> Then Elkanah her husband said to her: "Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? Why is your heart so troubled? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"

<margin>9</margin> So Hannah rose after she had eaten and drunk in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair before the doorposts of the temple of the Lord.

<margin>10</margin> Since Hannah was embittered in soul, she prayed to the Lord, weeping abundantly,

<margin>11</margin> And she made a vow, saying: "Lord of hosts, if you will look down and see the affliction of your servant, and be mindful of me, and not forget your handmaid, and give your servant a male child: I will give him to the Lord all the days of his life, and no razor shall touch his head." <note>This refers to the Nazarite vow, a person set apart for God's service who abstained from cutting their hair and drinking wine.</note>

<margin>12</margin> And it happened, as she multiplied her prayers before the Lord, that Eli observed her mouth.

<column-break/>

<margin>13</margin> Now Hannah was speaking in her heart, and only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard at all. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk,

<margin>14</margin> And he said to her: "How long will you be drunk? Digest a little of the wine with which you are soaked."

<margin>15</margin> Hannah answered and said: "Not so, my lord; for I am an exceedingly unhappy woman. I have drunk neither wine nor anything that can intoxicate, but I have poured out my soul in the sight of the Lord.

<margin>16</margin> Do not count your handmaid as one of the daughters of Belial <note>original: "filia Belial" — A term meaning "daughter of worthlessness" or a wicked woman.</note>, for out of the abundance of my grief and sorrow I have spoken until now."

<margin>17</margin> Then Eli said to her: "Go in peace: and may the God of Israel grant you the petition you have asked of Him."

<margin>18</margin> And she said: "May your handmaid find grace in your eyes." And the woman went her way and ate, and her countenance was no longer changed with sadness.

<margin>19</margin> And they rose early in the morning and worshipped before the Lord; then they returned and came to their house in Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the Lord remembered her.

<margin>20</margin> And it came to pass after the passage of days that Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she called his name Samuel <note>A Hebrew name meaning "God has heard" or "Asked of God."</note>: because she had asked for him from the Lord.

<margin>21</margin> Then her husband Elkanah went up with all his household to offer the Lord the solemn sacrifice and his vow.

<margin>22</margin> But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband: "I will not go until the infant is weaned, then I will bring him so that he may appear before the sight of the Lord and remain there forever."

<margin>23</margin> Elkanah her husband said to her: "Do what seems good to you, and stay until you have weaned him; I pray that the Lord may fulfill His word." So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him.

<margin>24</margin> And after she had weaned him, she took him with her, along with three calves, three measures of flour, and a jar of wine, and she brought him to the house of the Lord in Shiloh. But the child was still very young.

<margin>25</margin> And they sacrificed a calf and presented the boy to Eli.

<margin>26</margin> And Hannah said: "I beseech you, my lord, as your soul lives, my lord: I am the woman who stood here before you, praying to the Lord."

### CHAPTER II.

->*Hannah’s song in thanksgiving; she later gives birth to three sons and two daughters; because of the sins of Eli’s sons and their father’s excessive indulgence, a threat and the death of his sons are predicted for him and his house.*<-

1 “My heart exults in the Lord, and my horn <note>A biblical symbol for strength or dignity.</note> is exalted in my God: my mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I have rejoiced in your salvation.

### CHAPTER III.

->*Samuel is called four times by the Lord and reports the revelation made to him against Eli; he gradually becomes known to all Israel for his prophecies.*<-

1 Now the boy Samuel ministered to the Lord before Eli, and the word of the Lord was precious <note>original: "pretiosus" — in this context meaning rare or highly valued because it was so infrequent</note> in those days; there was no manifest vision.
2 And it happened one day, while Eli was lying in his place—and his eyes had grown dim so that he could not see—
3 Before the lamp of God went out, Samuel was sleeping in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was.
4 And the Lord called Samuel. And he answering, said: "Here I am."
5 And he ran to Eli, and said: "Here I am, for you called me." And he said: "I did not call; go back and sleep." And he went and slept.
6 And the Lord called Samuel again. And Samuel, rising up, went to Eli and said: "Here I am, because you called me." And he answered: "I did not call you, my son; go back and sleep."
7 Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, nor had the word of the Lord yet been revealed to him.
8 And the Lord called Samuel again a third time. And rising up, he went to Eli,
9 And said: "Here I am, because you called me." Then Eli understood that the Lord was calling the boy, and he said to Samuel: "Go and sleep; and if he calls you hereafter, you shall say: 'Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and slept in his place.
10 And the Lord came and stood; and he called as he had called the second time: "Samuel, Samuel." And Samuel said: "Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening."
11 And the Lord said to Samuel: "Behold, I am doing a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of everyone who hears it shall tingle."
12 "In that day I will raise up against Eli all the things I have spoken concerning his house; I will begin, and I will finish."
13 "For I foretold to him that I would judge his house forever because of iniquity, because he knew his sons were acting unworthily and he did not correct them."
14 "Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of his house shall not be expiated with victims and offerings forever."
15 And Samuel slept until morning, and he opened the doors of the house of the Lord. And Samuel feared to tell the vision to Eli.
16 Then Eli called Samuel, and said: "Samuel, my son?" And he answering, said: "I am here."
17 And he asked him: "What is the word that the Lord has spoken to you? I pray you, do not hide it from me; may God do these things to you, and add more, if you hide a word from me of all the things that were said to you."
18 So Samuel told him all the words, and hid nothing from him. And he answered: "It is the Lord; let him do what is good in his eyes."

<column-break/>

19 And Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and not one of his words fell to the ground <note>An idiom meaning that none of his prophecies failed to come true.</note>.
20 And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was a faithful prophet of the Lord.
21 And the Lord appeared again in Shiloh, for the Lord had revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh according to the word of the Lord. And the word of Samuel came to all Israel.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*The Israelites are struck down by the Philistines, and again after bringing the Ark into the camp; the Ark is captured and the two sons of Eli are killed; hearing this, Eli falls and dies, and his daughter-in-law dies in childbirth.*<-

1 And it happened in those days that the Philistines gathered for battle: and Israel went out to meet the Philistines in war, and camped near the Stone of Help <note>original: "lapidem adjutorii" — later known as Ebenezer</note>. Now the Philistines came to Aphek,
2 And they drew up their lines against Israel. When the battle was joined, Israel turned their backs to the Philistines, and there were slain in that battle, scattered through the fields, about four thousand men.
3 And the people returned to the camp, and the elders of Israel said: "Why has the Lord struck us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord to us from Shiloh, and let it come into our midst, so that it may save us from the hand of our enemies."
4 So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant of the Lord of hosts sitting upon the Cherubim: and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were with the ark of the covenant of God.
5 And when the ark of the covenant of the Lord came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great cry, and the earth resounded.
6 And the Philistines heard the sound of the shouting, and they said: "What is this sound of great shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they realized that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp.
7 And the Philistines were afraid, saying: "God has come into the camp." And they groaned, saying:
8 "Woe to us! For there was no such great joy yesterday or the day before; woe to us! Who shall save us from the hand of these sublime Gods? These are the Gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the desert."
9 "Be strengthened, and be men, O Philistines: lest you serve the Hebrews as they have served you: be strengthened and fight."
10 So the Philistines fought, and Israel was struck down, and every man fled to his tent: and there was a very great slaughter: and thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell.
11 And the ark of God was captured: and the two sons of Eli died, Hophni and Phinehas.
12 And a man of Benjamin, running from the battle line, came to Shiloh that day with his clothes torn and dust sprinkled on his head.
13 When he arrived, Eli was sitting upon a chair facing the road, watching. For his heart was trembling for the ark of God. And after that man entered, he reported it to the city: and the whole city wailed.
14 And Eli heard the sound of the outcry, and said: "What is this sound of this tumult?"

### C H A P T E R V.

->*Dagon falls prostrate once and again before the ark, with his head and hands cut off at the threshold. The Philistines are also struck with tumors and mice, and they drive the ark away from themselves.*<-

The Philistines, however, took the ark of God and carried it from the Stone of Help <note>original: "a lapide adjutorii" — known as Ebenezer</note> into Ashdod.
2 And the Philistines took the ark of God, and brought it into the temple of Dagon, and set it next to Dagon.
3 And when the people of Ashdod rose early the next day, behold, Dagon lay face down on the ground before the ark of the Lord; and they took Dagon and restored him to his place.
4 And rising again early the next morning, they found Dagon lying on his face on the ground before the ark of the Lord; but the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold.
5 Furthermore, only the trunk of Dagon remained in its place. For this reason, the priests of Dagon and all who enter his temple do not step upon the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod, even to this day.
<margin>† Psalm 77:66</margin>
6 But the hand of the Lord was heavy upon the people of Ashdod, and he destroyed them; † and he struck Ashdod and its borders in the more secret parts of the buttocks <note>original: "in secretiori parte natium" — referring to hemorrhoids or painful tumors</note>. And the villages and fields in the midst of that region bubbled up, and mice were born, and there was a confusion of great death in the city.
7 And when the men of Ashdod saw this kind of plague, they said: "The ark of the God of Israel must not stay with us, for his hand is hard upon us and upon Dagon our god."
8 And sending messengers, they gathered all the lords of the Philistines to them and said: "What

<column-break/>

shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" And the people of Gath answered: "Let the ark of the God of Israel be carried around." And they carried the ark of the God of Israel around.
9 But while they were carrying it around, the hand of the Lord came upon every city with a very great slaughter; and he struck the men of every city, from the small to the great, and their bowels came out and rotted <note>The Latin "computrescebant promentes extales eorum" describes a gruesome physical affliction of the intestines.</note>. And the people of Gath took counsel and made for themselves seats of skins.
10 Therefore they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And when the ark of God came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying: "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel to us, to kill us and our people."
11 So they sent and gathered all the lords of the Philistines, who said: "Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its own place, so that it does not kill us and our people."
12 For there was the fear of death in every city, and the hand of God was very heavy; and the men who had not died were struck in the secret part of their buttocks, and the wailing of every city rose up to heaven.

### C H A P T E R VI.

### CHAPTER XIII.

->*The Philistines are seen by Saul to be armed with a great apparatus against Israel; the terrified Hebrews hide in caves. Because Saul offered a burnt offering without waiting for Samuel's arrival, he is told he is rejected by the Lord. Concerning the precaution of the Philistines so that the Israelites would be deprived of weapons.*<-

1 Saul was a son of one year <note>This is a literal translation of the Latin "Filius unius anni," a difficult verse that likely refers to the first year of his reign or his age when anointed, though the numbers in the source manuscripts are often considered incomplete by scholars.</note> when he began to reign, and he reigned over Israel for two years.
2 And Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel: two thousand were with Saul in Michmash <note>original: "Machmas"</note> and on Mount Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah <note>original: "Gabaa"</note> of Benjamin; the rest of the people he sent back, each to his own tent.
3 And Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Gibeah. When the Philistines heard of it, Saul sounded the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!"
4 And all Israel heard the news: "Saul has struck the garrison of the Philistines." And Israel raised itself up against the Philistines. The people were then called out after Saul to Gilgal <note>original: "Galgala"</note>.
5 And the Philistines gathered to fight against Israel: thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and the rest of the troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They went up and encamped in Michmash, to the east of Beth-aven.
6 When the men of Israel saw that they were in a tight spot (for the people were distressed), they hid themselves in caves, in thickets, in rocks, in holes, and in cisterns.
7 And some Hebrews crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. And while Saul was still

<column-break/>

in Gilgal, all the people who followed him were trembling with fear.
8 And he waited seven days, according to the appointment set by Samuel, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people began to slip away from him.
9 Saul therefore said, "Bring me the burnt offering <note>original: "holocaustum"</note> and the peace offerings." And he offered the burnt offering.
10 And it happened that as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel arrived; and Saul went out to meet him and greet him.
11 And Samuel said to him, "What have you done?" Saul answered, "Because I saw that the people were slipping away from me, and you had not come within the appointed days, and the Philistines were gathered at Michmash,
12 I said: 'Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not appeased the face of the Lord.' Compelled by necessity, I offered the burnt offering."
13 And Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly, and you have not kept the commandments of the Lord your God, which he commanded you. If you had not done this, the Lord would have prepared your kingdom over Israel forever.
<margin>$\dagger$ Acts 13:22</margin>
14 But now your kingdom shall rise no further. $\dagger$ The Lord has sought for himself a man after his own heart, and the Lord has commanded him to be the leader over his people, because you have not observed what the Lord commanded."
15 Then Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the people who were attacking them, coming from Gilgal to Gibeah on the hill of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.
16 And Saul and Jonathan his son, and the people found with them, were in Gibeah of Benjamin; but the Philistines were encamped in Michmash.
17 And three companies of raiders came out from the camp of the Philistines to plunder. One company turned toward the way of Ophrah <note>original: "Ephra"</note> to the land of Shual <note>original: "Sual"</note>.
18 Another entered by the way of Beth-horon, and the third turned toward the border overlooking the valley of Zeboim <note>original: "Seboim"</note> toward the desert.
19 Now, no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel; for the Philistines had taken care lest the Hebrews should make swords or spears.
20 Therefore all Israel went down to the Philistines so that each man could sharpen his plowshare, his hoe, his axe, and his mattock.
21 Thus the edges of the plowshares, hoes, pitchforks, and axes were blunt, even down to the repair of the goads.
22 And so it came to pass on the day of battle that neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan, except for Saul and Jonathan his son.
23 And a garrison of the Philistines went out to cross over to Michmash.

### CHAPTER XV.

*Saul is sent by the Lord to utterly destroy the Amalekites. By sparing Agag their king and keeping much of the plunder, he is accused of disobedience. Despite his claims of obedience, he is rejected from the kingship. After Agag is killed, Samuel mourns for the rejected Saul.*

### CHAPTER XVII.

*With the Philistines gathered against Israel for battle, David killed the giant Goliath—who trusted in his armor and strength—with a single sling, and brought the champion’s head to Saul after the Philistines were scattered.*

1 Now the Philistines, gathering their troops for battle, assembled at Socoh in Judah: and they pitched camp between Socoh and Azekah, in the borders of Domnus <note>original: "Domnus," likely a variant of Ephes-dammim, meaning "boundary of blood."</note>.
2 Furthermore, Saul and the men of Israel gathered and came into the Valley of the Terebinth <note>original: "Vallem terebinthi," known as the Valley of Elah, named for its large terebinth trees.</note>, and they drew up their battle line to fight against the Philistines.
3 And the Philistines stood on a mountain on one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side: and there was a valley between them.
4 And there went out from the camp of the Philistines a champion <note>original: "vir spurius," literally "a man of the space between," referring to a warrior who fights in single combat on behalf of an army.</note> named Goliath, of Gath, whose height was six cubits and a span <note>This would make him approximately nine feet, nine inches tall.</note>.
5 And he had a bronze helmet upon his head, and he was clothed with a coat of scale armor: and the weight of his armor was five thousand shekels of bronze.
6 And he had bronze greaves <note>term: "greaves" are armor pieces used to protect the shins.</note> on his legs, and a bronze shield covered his shoulders.
7 And the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam <note>A heavy wooden roller used in a loom, indicating the spear's massive size.</note>: and the iron head of his spear weighed six hundred shekels: and his armor-bearer walked before him.
8 And standing there, he cried out against the ranks of Israel, and said to them: "Why have you come out prepared for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and you the servants of Saul? Choose a man from among you, and let him come down for single combat.
9 If he is able to fight with me and kills me, we will be your servants: but if I prevail and kill him, you shall be our servants, and serve us."
10 And the Philistine said: "I have defied the ranks of Israel this day: Give me a man, and let him enter into single combat with me."
11 And Saul and all the Israelites, hearing such words from the Philistine, were dismayed and greatly afraid.
<margin>† See above 16:1.</margin>
12 Now David was the son of an Ephrathite man from Bethlehem in Judah, whose name was Jesse, who had eight sons; and in the days of Saul, he was an old man, well advanced in years among men.
13 And his three eldest sons followed Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons who went to the war were Eliab the firstborn, the second Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
14 But David was the youngest. While the three eldest followed Saul,
15 David went and returned from Saul to feed his father’s flock in Bethlehem.
16 And the Philistine came forward morning and evening, and stood there for forty days.
17 And Jesse said to David his son: "Take for your brothers an ephah <note>A dry measure roughly equal to 20 quarts.</note> of parched grain, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to your brothers,
18 And carry these ten small cheeses to the captain <note>original: "tribunum," a military commander of a thousand men.</note>: and see how your brothers are doing, and learn with whom they are stationed."
19 Now Saul, and they, and all the sons of Israel were in the Valley of the Terebinth fighting against the Philistines.
