20 And so David rose early in the morning and left the flock with a keeper: and being loaded, he went as Jesse had commanded him: and he came to the place of the barrier <note>original: "Magala," referring to the circular barricade of carts and baggage around the camp.</note>, and to the army, which was going out to the fight shouting for the battle.
21 For Israel had drawn up their line, and the Philistines were prepared on the opposite side.
22 David, therefore, leaving the things he had brought under the hand of the keeper of the baggage, ran to the place of the battle and asked if all was well with his brothers.
23 And while he was still speaking with them, that champion appeared coming up, Goliath by name, the Philistine of Gath, from the camp of the Philistines: and David heard him speaking these same words.
24 And all the Israelites, when they saw the man, fled from his face, fearing him greatly.
25 And someone of Israel said: "Have you seen this man who has come up? For he has come up to defy Israel. The man, therefore, who shall kill him, the king will enrich with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and will make his father’s house free from tribute <note>Meaning the family would be exempt from taxes or forced labor.</note> in Israel."
26 And David spoke to the men who stood with him, saying: "What shall be given to the man who kills this Philistine and takes away the reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, who has defied the armies of the living God?"
27 And the people repeated the same words to him, saying: "These things shall be given to the man who kills him."
28 When Eliab, his eldest brother, heard him speaking with the others, he was angry with David, and said: "Why did you come, and why did you leave those few sheep in the desert? I know your pride and the wickedness of your heart: because you have come down to see the battle."
29 And David said: "What have I done? Is it not just a word?"

32 And when he was brought before him, David said: "Let no man’s heart fail because of him: I, your servant, will go and fight against the Philistine."
33 And Saul said to David: "You are not able to resist this Philistine, nor to fight against him: for you are but a boy, but he is a man of war from his youth."

36 For I, your servant, killed both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be like one of them. Now I will go and take away the reproach of the people: for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, who has dared to curse the army of the living God?"
37 And David said: "The Lord who delivered me from the paw of the lion, and from the paw of the bear, he will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." And Saul said to David: "Go, and the Lord be with you."

### C H A P T E R XVIII.

->*Jonathan is joined to David in a most close bond: Saul, hearing David and himself compared, hates him bitterly, wherefore being driven by an evil spirit he tries to pin David down with a spear: and Merab his daughter, whom he had promised to David, he gives to another: but Michal the younger daughter he craftily betrothes to David as a wife in exchange for a hundred Philistine foreskins.*<-

1 AND it came to pass when he had finished speaking to Saul: the soul of Jonathan was knit to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. 
2 And Saul took him that day, and did not allow him to return to his father's house. 
3 Then David and Jonathan made a covenant: for he loved him as his own soul. 
4 For Jonathan stripped himself of the robe with which he was clothed, and gave it to David, and the rest of his garments, even to his sword and his bow, and even to his belt. 
5 And David went out to all things wherever Saul sent him, and he acted prudently: and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the eyes of all the people, and especially in the sight of Saul's servants. 
6 Moreover, when David returned after slaying the Philistine, the women came out of all the cities of Israel, singing and leading dances to meet king Saul, with timbrels of joy, and with sistrums <note>A sistrum is an ancient percussion instrument, often made of metal, that makes a rattling sound when shaken.</note>.

9 Therefore Saul did not look upon David with a right eye from that day and forward. 
10 And after another day, the evil spirit of God came upon Saul, and he prophesied <note>In this context, "prophesied" suggests a state of ecstatic or frantic raving, rather than predicting the future.</note> in the midst of his house: but David played the harp with his hand, as he did every day: and Saul held a spear,

### C H A P T E R XIX.

*Saul, wishing to kill David, is appeased by the voice of Jonathan; he attempts again to strike him through while he plays the harp before him; David flees and is protected by the ingenuity of Michal; Saul pursues him to Naioth to see Samuel, and after sending three groups of messengers who all prophesy, he himself begins to prophesy.*

And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David. But Jonathan, the son of Saul, loved David greatly.

# CHAPTER XX.

->*Jonathan, after renewing his covenant with David, tries in vain to reconcile him with his father; he nonetheless delivers him from Saul's hands by the signal of three arrows.*<-

1 David fled from Naioth in Ramah and came to speak with Jonathan: "What have I done? What is my guilt, and what is my sin against your father, that he seeks my life?" 
2 Jonathan said to him, "Far be it! You shall not die. For my father will do nothing, great or small, without first revealing it to me. Why would my father hide this one thing from me? It cannot be so." 
3 But David swore an oath again, saying, "Your father certainly knows that I have found favor in your eyes, and he says to himself, 'Let Jonathan not know this, lest he be grieved.' But truly, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, there is only (so to speak) a single step between me and death." 
4 Then Jonathan said to David, "Whatever your soul desires, I will do for you." 
5 David said to Jonathan, "Behold, tomorrow is the New Moon <term>New Moon (calendæ): A monthly religious festival in Israel marked by sacrifices and a royal banquet.</term>, and I am expected to sit with the king at the feast. Let me go, so that I may hide in the field until the evening of the third day. 
6 If your father looks for me and asks where I am, answer him: 'David earnestly asked me for leave to hurry to Bethlehem, his own city, because there is a yearly sacrifice there for his whole clan.' 
7 If he says, 'Good,' then your servant is safe. But if he becomes angry, know that his evil intent is determined. 
8 Therefore, show kindness to your servant, for you have brought me into a covenant of the Lord with you. But if there is any guilt in me, kill me yourself; why should you bring me to your father?" 
9 And Jonathan said, "Far be it from you! If I knew for certain that my father’s evil intent was determined against you, would I not tell you?" 
10 David then asked Jonathan, "Who will tell me if your father answers you harshly?" 
11 Jonathan said to David, "Come, let us go out into the field." And when they had both gone out into the field,

But if my father’s malice persists against you, I will reveal it to you <note>original: "revelabo aurem tuam," literally "I will reveal it to your ear."</note> and send you away, that you may go in peace. And may the Lord be with you, as He has been with my father. 
14 And if I am still alive, show me the kindness of the Lord; but if I should die,

24 So David hid in the field. When the New Moon came, the king sat down to eat.

37 So when the lad came to the place of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan cried out after the lad, saying: “Behold, the arrow is further on, beyond you.”
38 And Jonathan cried out again after the lad, saying: “Make haste quickly, do not stand still.” So Jonathan's lad gathered up the arrows and brought them to his master.
39 But he knew nothing of what was being done; for only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
40 Jonathan then gave his weapons to the lad and said to him: “Go, carry them into the city.”
41 And when the lad had gone, David rose from the place, which faced toward the south, and falling prostrate on the ground, he bowed three times; and kissing one another, they wept together, but David wept more.
42 Then Jonathan said to David: “Go in peace; as we have both sworn in the name of the Lord, saying: May the Lord be between me and you, and between my seed and your seed forever.”
43 And David arose and departed; and Jonathan went into the city.

### CHAPTER XXI.

->*David, a fugitive, comes to the priestly city of Nob. Driven by hunger, he eats the consecrated bread given by Ahimelech in the presence of Doeg the Edomite. After taking Goliath's sword, he feigns madness out of fear before King Achish of Gath.*<-

1 David then came to Nob to Ahimelech the priest; and Ahimelech was astonished that David had come. And he said to him: “Why are you alone, and no one is with you?”
2 And David said to Ahimelech the priest: “The king has commanded me a certain matter, and said: ‘Let no man know the thing for which you are sent by me, nor what kind of commands I have given you.’ For I have also appointed my servants to such and such a place.
3 Now, therefore, if you have anything at hand, even five loaves of bread, give them to me, or whatever you can find.”
4 And the priest, answering David, said to him: “I have no common bread at hand, but only holy bread; <note>original: "panem sanctum". This refers to the Showbread, twelve loaves set out before the Lord in the Tabernacle every Sabbath, which were legally reserved for the priests alone.</note> are the young men clean, especially from women?”
5 And David answered the priest and said to him: “Truly, if it concerns women, we have kept ourselves from them since yesterday and the day before, when we set out, and the vessels <note>In this context, "vessels" likely refers to the men's bodies or their travel gear, implying they were ritually pure.</note> of the young men were holy. Moreover, this journey is profane <note>original: "polluta". David argues that even if the journey itself is a secular mission, they are personally sanctified.</note>, but it too shall be sanctified today in the vessels.”
<margin>† Matthew 12:3, 4.</margin>
6 † So the priest gave him the sanctified

<column-break/>

bread; for there was no bread there but only the bread of Presence, which had been taken away from before the Lord, that hot bread might be set there.
7 Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, inside the Tabernacle of the Lord; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the most powerful of Saul's herdsmen.
8 And David said to Ahimelech: “Do you have a spear or a sword at hand? For I did not bring my sword or my weapons with me, because the king's business was urgent.”
9 And the priest said: “Behold, here is the sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you slew in the Valley of the Terebinth; <note>This refers to the Valley of Elah, where David's famous duel with the giant took place.</note> it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. <note>The ephod was a ceremonial garment worn by the High Priest, often associated with seeking divine oracles.</note> If you wish to take it, take it; for there is no other here besides it.” And David said: “There is none other like it, give it to me.”
10 So David arose and fled that day from the face of Saul; and he came to Achish, the king of Gath.
11 And the servants of Achish said to him when they saw David: “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing of him in dances, saying: <margin>† Above 18:7; Sirach 47:7.</margin> † Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?”
12 David took these words to heart and was very much afraid of Achish, the king of Gath.
13 And he changed his appearance before them, and slipped down between their hands, and stumbled against the doors of the gate, and his spittle ran down upon his beard.
14 And Achish said to his servants: “You see the man is mad; why have you brought him to me?
15 Do we lack madmen, that you have brought this one in to act mad in my presence? Shall this fellow enter my house?”

### CHAPTER XXII.

->*David receives many followers at the cave of Adullam; from there he goes to the king of Moab; then, by the counsel of the prophet Gad, he returns to the land of Judah. Saul, however, ordered all the priests of Nob to be killed by Doeg the Edomite, except for Abiathar, who fled to David.*<-

1 David therefore departed from there and fled to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and all his father's house heard of it, they went down to him there.
2 And all those who were in distress, and oppressed by debt, and embittered in soul, gathered to him; and he became their prince, and there were with him about four hundred men.
3 And David went from there to Mizpah of Moab and said to the king of Moab: “Let my father and my mother stay with you, I pray you, until I know what God will do for me.”
4 And he left them before the face of the king of Moab; and they stayed with him all the days that David was in the stronghold.
5 And Gad the prophet said to David: “Do not stay in the stronghold; depart and go into the land of Judah.” And David departed and came into the forest of Hereth.
6 And Saul heard that David had appeared, along with the men who were with him. Now Saul was staying in Gibeah, and was in the grove which is in Ramah, holding a spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.

### CHAPTER XXIII.

1 And they told David, saying: "Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and they are plundering the threshing floors."
2 Therefore David consulted the Lord, saying: "Shall I go and strike these Philistines?" And the Lord said to David: "Go, and you shall strike the Philistines, and save Keilah."
3 But the men who were with David said to him: "Behold, we are afraid even here in Judea; how much more if we go to Keilah against the ranks of the Philistines?"
4 So David consulted the Lord again. And He answering, said to him: "Arise, and go to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand."
5 David and his men went to Keilah and fought against the Philistines; he drove away their livestock and struck them with a great slaughter; and David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
6 Now it happened that when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he had come down with an ephod in his hand.
7 It was reported to Saul that David had come to Keilah, and Saul said: "God has delivered him into my hands, for he is shut in by entering a city that has gates and bars."
8 And Saul commanded all the people to go down to Keilah for battle, to besiege David and his men.
9 When David learned that Saul was secretly preparing evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest: "Bring the ephod here."
10 And David said:
> "O Lord God of Israel, your servant has heard a report that Saul intends to come to Keilah to destroy the city because of me.
11 > Will the men of Keilah deliver me into his hands? And will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? O Lord God of Israel, tell your servant."
And the Lord said: "He will come down."
12 Then David said:
> "Will the men of Keilah deliver me and the men who are with me into the hands of Saul?"
And the Lord said: "They will deliver you."
13 So David and his men, about six hundred, arose and departed from Keilah; they wandered here and there, uncertain of their way. And it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah and was saved, so he called off the expedition.
14 David stayed in the wilderness in very strong places, and he remained on a mountain in the desert of Ziph, a shaded mountain. Saul sought him every day, but God did not deliver him into his hand.
15 And David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life. Now David was in the desert of Ziph, in the forest.
16 And Jonathan, the son of Saul, arose and went to David in the forest, and strengthened his hand in God; and he said to him:
17 "Do not fear, for the hand of my father Saul shall not find you; and you shall reign over Israel."

### CHAPTER XXIV.

*David, hiding in the cave of Engedi, cuts off the edge of the cloak of the pursuing Saul, and so that he would not be killed, he set him free; because of this, Saul acknowledges his guilt, and knowing David is to be king, after taking an oath from him not to wipe out Saul’s family, he is reconciled to him.*

David then went up from there and lived in the safest parts of Engedi.
2 And when Saul had returned, after he had pursued the Philistines, they told him, saying: "Behold, David is in the desert of Engedi."

4 And he came to the sheepfolds, which offered themselves to the traveler; and there was a cave there, which Saul entered in order to relieve himself <note>original: *purgaret ventrem*, literally "to purge his belly."</note>; meanwhile, David and his men were hiding in the inner part of the cave.
5 And the servants of David said to him: "Behold the day of which the Lord spoke to you: 'I

will deliver your enemy to you, so that you may do to him as it pleases in your eyes.'" Then David arose, and silently cut off the edge of Saul's cloak.

7 And he said to his men: "May the Lord be merciful to me, that I should not do this thing to my master, the <term>Anointed of the Lord</term> <note>original: *christo Domini*. The term refers to a king consecrated by holy oil.</note>, as to stretch forth my hand against him, because he is the Lord’s anointed."
8 And David restrained his men with his words, and did not permit them to rise up against Saul; meanwhile, Saul, rising from the cave, went on the journey he had begun.
9 Then David also arose after him; and leaving the cave, he cried out after Saul’s back, saying: "My lord king!" And Saul looked behind him; and David, bowing himself face-down to the earth, did obeisance.
10 And he said to Saul: "Why do you listen to the words of men who say, 'David seeks evil against you'?
11 Behold, today your eyes have seen that the Lord delivered you into my hand in the cave; and I thought to kill you, but my eye spared you; for I said: I will not stretch forth my hand against my lord, because he is the Lord’s anointed.
12 Rather, my father, see and recognize the edge of your cloak in my hand; since when I cut off the top of your cloak, I would not stretch forth my hand against you. Take notice and see that there is no evil in my hand, nor iniquity, nor have I sinned against you; yet you lie in wait for my life to take it away.
13 May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me upon you; but let my hand not be upon you.
14 As it is said in the ancient proverb: 'From the wicked shall wickedness come forth' <note>original: *AB IMPIIS egredietur impietas*</note>; therefore let my hand not be upon you.
15 Whom do you pursue, O king of Israel? Whom do you pursue? You pursue a dead dog, and a single flea.
16 May the Lord be judge, and judge between me and you: and may He see, and judge my cause, and rescue me from your hand."
17 And when David had finished speaking words of this kind to Saul, Saul said: "Is this your voice, my son David?" And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
18 And he said to David: "You are more righteous than I; for you have repaid me with good, while I have returned evil to you.
19 And you have shown today what good things you have done for me: how the Lord delivered me into your hand, and you did not kill me.
20 For who, when he has found his enemy, will let him go on a good path? But may the Lord return this reward to you, for what you have worked upon me today.
21 And now, because I know that you shall most certainly reign, and shall hold the kingdom of Israel in your hand:
22 Swear to me in the Lord, that you will not destroy my seed after me, nor take away my name from the house of my father."

### CHAPTER XXV.

->Samuel dies and is mourned; David, after being denied food by the churlish Nabal, threatens him with death; David is appeased by the excellent speech of Abigail, whom he later marries after Nabal's death, along with Ahinoam; meanwhile, Saul gives his daughter Michal to Phalti.<-

1 And Samuel died, and all Israel gathered together and mourned for him, and they buried him at his home in Ramah. And David, rising up, went down into the desert of Paran.

3 The name of the man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigail. She was a most prudent and beautiful woman, but her husband was harsh, ill-mannered, and malicious; he was of the family of Caleb.

5 He sent ten young men and said to them: "Go up to Carmel, and when you come to Nabal, greet him peacefully in my name.
6 And you shall say: 'Peace be to my brothers and to you, and peace to your house, and peace to all that you possess.
7 I have heard that your shepherds, who were with us in the desert, were shearing; we never troubled them, nor was anything ever missing from their flock during all the time they were with us in Carmel.
8 Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Now, therefore, let my young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a good day <note>A day of feasting and celebration during the sheep-shearing season.</note>. Whatever your hand finds, give it to your servants and to your son David.'"
9 And when David’s young men arrived, they spoke all these words to Nabal in David's name, and then they waited in silence.
10 But Nabal, answering David's servants, said: "Who is David? And who is the son of Jesse? Today, servants who flee from their masters have increased.

12 So David’s young men turned back on their way and returned to tell him all the words he had spoken.
13 Then David said to his men: "Let every man gird on his sword." And every man girded on his sword, and David also girded on his own sword. About four hundred men followed David, while two hundred stayed behind with the baggage.
14 But one of the servants told Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying: "Behold, David sent messengers from the desert to bless our master, and he turned them away.
15 These men were very good to us and did not trouble us; nor did we ever lose anything all the time we were with them in the desert.
16 They were like a wall to us both by night and by day, all the days we were with them pasturing the flocks.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

1 And the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying: "Behold, David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah, which faces the wilderness."
2 And Saul arose and went down to the desert of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to seek David in the desert of Ziph.

### C H A P T E R XXVII.

*David, not daring to trust the inconstancy of Saul, becomes a fugitive among Achish, from whom he obtained the city of Ziklag; for this reason it became the inheritance of the kings of Judah, from where he carried out many raids against the Amalekites and neighboring places, deceiving King Achish.*

1 And David said in his heart: "I shall one day fall into the hands of Saul; is it not better that I flee and be saved in the land of the Philistines, so that Saul may despair and cease to seek me in all the borders of Israel? I will therefore flee from his hands."
2 And David arose, and he and the six hundred men with him went to Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
3 And David lived with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each man with his household; David and his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite, and Abigail the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
4 And it was reported to Saul that David had fled to Gath, and he no longer sought him.
5 David then said to Achish: "If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be given to me in one of the cities of this region, that I may live there; for why should your servant stay in the royal city with you?"
6 Therefore Achish gave him Ziklag <note>original: "Siceleg."</note> on that day; for which reason Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah even to this day.
7 And the number of days that David lived in the region of the Philistines was four months. <note>The Latin Vulgate says "four months," though some Hebrew manuscripts suggest "a year and four months."</note>
8 And David and his men went up and carried out raids against the Geshurites, and the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for these villages were inhabited in the land from ancient times, as one goes toward Shur even to the land of Egypt.
9 And David struck the whole land, leaving neither man nor woman alive; and taking the sheep, and oxen, and donkeys, and camels, and clothing, he returned and came to Achish.
10 And Achish would say to him: "Whom have you attacked today?" David would answer: "Against the south of Judah, and against the south of Jerahmeel, and against the south of the Kenites."
11 David saved neither man nor woman alive, nor did he bring them to Gath, saying: "Lest perhaps they should speak against us, saying: 'This David did.'" And this was his practice all the days he lived in the region of the Philistines.
12 So Achish believed David, saying: "He has worked much evil against his people Israel; therefore he shall be my servant forever."

### CHAPTER XXIX.

*David, setting out with the Philistines against Israel, is sent back, because the princes feared that in battle he might become an adversary to them; he is ordered to return to Ziklag.*

1 **T**hen all the troops of the Philistines were gathered together at Aphek: and Israel also encamped by the fountain which was in Jezreel.
2 And the lords <note>original: "satrapae." The commanders of the five Philistine city-states.</note> of the Philistines marched in hundreds and thousands: but David and his men were in the rear guard with Achish.
3 And the princes of the Philistines said to Achish: "What do these Hebrews want?" And Achish said to the princes of the Philistines: "Do you not know David, who was the servant of Saul the king of Israel, and has been with me for many days, or rather years, and I have found nothing in him from the day he fled to me until this day?"
<margin>1 Chronicles 12:19</margin>
4 But the princes of the Philistines were angry with him, and they said to him: "Let this man return, and let him stay in his place where you have appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest he become an adversary to us when we begin to fight: for how else can he appease his master, except with our heads?"
5 "Is this not David, to whom they sang in dances, saying: 'Saul struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
6 Therefore Achish called David, and said to him: "As the Lord lives, you are upright and good in my sight: and your going out and your coming in with me in the camp is pleasing: and I have not found any evil in you from the day you came to me until this day: but you do not please the lords.

<column-break/>

7 Return therefore, and go in peace, and do not offend the eyes of the lords of the Philistines."
8 And David said to Achish: "But what have I done, and what have you found in me your servant, from the day I was in your presence until this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"
9 And Achish answering, spoke to David: "I know that you are good in my eyes, even as an angel of God: but the princes of the Philistines have said: 'He shall not go up with us to the battle.'
10 Therefore arise early in the morning, you and the servants of your lord who came with you: and when you have risen in the night, and it begins to grow light, go."
11 So David and his men rose in the night to depart in the morning, and to return to the land of the Philistines: but the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

### CHAPTER XXX.

*While David was absent with his men, the Amalekites burned Ziklag and carried off the spoil; David pursues and kills them, recovering the spoil, which he divided equally among all his companions, even those who, being weary, had stayed behind with the baggage.*

<margin>1 Chronicles 12:20</margin>
1 **W**hen David and his men had come to Ziklag <note>original: "Siceleg."</note> on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid from the south into Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
2 And they had taken the women captive from there, from the least to the greatest: and they had not killed anyone, but had carried them off and went on their way.
3 So when David and his men came to the city, and found it burned with fire, and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters taken captive,
4 David and the people who were with him lifted up their voices and wept until they had no more tears left in them.
5 For David's two wives had also been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelite, and Abigail the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
6 And David was greatly distressed: for the people wanted to stone him, because the soul of every man was bitter for his sons and his daughters: but David was strengthened in the Lord his God.
7 And he said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech: "Bring the ephod <note>A ceremonial vestment used by the high priest to discern the will of God.</note> to me." And Abiathar brought the ephod to David,
8 And David consulted the Lord, saying: "Shall I pursue these thieves, and shall I overtake them, or not?" And the Lord said to him: "Pursue: for without doubt you shall overtake them and recover the spoil."
9 So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came as far as the brook Besor: and some, being weary, stayed behind.
10 But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred stayed behind, who were too weary to cross the brook Besor.
11 And they found an Egyptian man in the field, and brought him to David: and they gave him bread to eat, and water to drink,
12 Also a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins. And when he had eaten, his spirit returned, and he was refreshed.

# THE SECOND BOOK
## OF SAMUEL,

->WHICH WE CALL THE SECOND BOOK OF KINGS.<-

### CHAPTER ONE.

<margin>David, having killed the messenger who claimed to have killed Saul, mourns him with the others who were slain, tearing his garments, fasting, and commanding that the sons of Judah be taught the use of the bow.</margin>

1 Now it happened, after Saul was dead, that David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites <note>The Amalekites were long-standing enemies of the Israelites; David had just recovered his people and property from them.</note> and remained in Ziklag for two days.
2 On the third day, a man appeared coming from Saul's camp with his clothes torn and dust scattered on his head. When he came to David, he fell upon his face and bowed in reverence.
3 David said to him: "Where do you come from?" And he said to him: "I have escaped from the camp of Israel."
4 David said to him: "What is the word of what has happened? Tell me." He said: "The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people have fallen and are dead; even Saul and his son Jonathan have perished."
5 And David said to the young man who was reporting to him: "How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?"
6 The young man who told him said: "By chance I came upon Mount Gilboa, and Saul was leaning upon his spear; meanwhile, the chariots and horsemen were closing in on him.
7 And looking behind him and seeing me, he called out. When I answered, 'I am here,'
8 He said to me: 'Who are you?' And I said to him: 'I am an Amalekite.'
9 And he spoke to me: 'Stand over me and kill me, for anguish has seized me, and yet my whole life is still within me.'
10 So standing over him, I killed him; for I knew that he could not live after his fall. And I took the crown that was on his head and the armchair-band <note>original: "armillam," an armlet or bracelet often worn as a symbol of royalty.</note> from his arm, and I have brought them here to you, my lord."
11 Then David, taking hold of his clothes, tore them, as did all the men who were with him.
12 And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until evening for Saul, and for his son Jonathan, and for the people of the Lord, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
13 And David said to the young man who had told him: "Where are you from?" He answered: "I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite."
<margin>† Psalm 104:15.</margin>
14 And David said to him: "Why were you not afraid to put forth your hand to kill the Lord’s anointed?" <note>original: "christum Domini." This term literally means "the Christ of the Lord," referring to the sacred status of a king consecrated with holy oil.</note>
15 And David, calling one of his young men, said: "Go, fall upon him." And he struck him, and he died.

<column-break/>

16 And David said to him: "Your blood be upon your own head; for your own mouth has spoken against you, saying: 'I have killed the Lord’s anointed.'" <note>original: "christum Domini"</note>
17 Then David lamented with this kind of lamentation over Saul and over his son Jonathan,
(18 And he commanded that they should teach the sons of Judah the use of the bow, as it is written in the Book of the Upright.) <note>original: "libro justorum," often referred to as the Book of Jasher, a lost collection of Hebrew poetry.</note> And he said: "Consider, O Israel, those who are dead, wounded upon your high places.
19 The illustrious of Israel are slain upon your mountains; how have the mighty fallen?
20 Do not announce it in Gath, nor proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon <note>Gath and Ashkelon were major cities of the Philistines, the enemies of Israel.</note>, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
21 You mountains of Gilboa, let neither dew nor rain come upon you, nor let there be fields of firstfruits; for there the shield of the heroes was cast away, the shield of Saul, as if he had not been anointed with oil.
22 From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the heroes, the arrow of Jonathan never turned back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
23 Saul and Jonathan, lovable and beautiful in their life, in death also they were not divided; swifter than eagles, stronger than lions.
24 Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet in your delights, who provided golden ornaments for your attire.
25 How have the mighty fallen in battle? Jonathan, slain on your high places?
26 I grieve for you, my brother Jonathan, exceedingly beautiful and lovable beyond the love of women. As a mother loves her only son, so did I love you.
27 How have the robust fallen, and the weapons of war perished?"

### CHAPTER TWO.

<margin>David, commanded by the oracle of God to go up to Hebron, is there anointed as king over Judah; he commends the men of Jabesh-Gilead for the burial of Saul; however, the anointing of Ishbosheth as king over Israel brought about grave rebellion and battle between the two houses.</margin>

1 Therefore after these things, David consulted the Lord, saying: "Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah?" And the Lord said to him: "Go up." And David said: "Where shall I go up?" And He answered him: "Into Hebron."
2 So David went up, and his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
3 Moreover, David led up the men who were with him, each with his household; and they dwelt in the towns of Hebron.

5 So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-Gilead, and said to them: "May you be blessed by the Lord, you who have shown this mercy to your lord Saul and have buried him. <note>The people of Jabesh-Gilead had a long-standing loyalty to Saul because he had rescued them from the Ammonites at the start of his reign.</note>
6 And now may the Lord indeed repay you with mercy and truth; and I also will show you favor because you have done this thing.
7 Let your hands be strengthened, and be valiant men; for although your lord Saul is dead, the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."
8 But Abner the son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul and led him through the camps,
9 And he made him king over Gilead, and over Gessuri <note>original: "Gessuri"; likely referring to the Geshurites</note>, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
10 Ishbosheth, the son of Saul, was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for two years; only the house of Judah followed David.
11 And the number of days that David remained as ruler in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
12 And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from the camps to Gibeon.
13 Then Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out and met them by the pool of Gibeon. And when they had met together, they sat down opposite each other: these on one side of the pool, and those on the other.
14 And Abner said to Joab: "Let the young men arise and compete <note>original: "ludant"; literally 'play,' but here referring to a ritualized and lethal combat between champions</note> before us." And Joab answered: "Let them arise."
15 So they arose and went over, twelve in number from Benjamin on the side of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and twelve from the servants of David.
16 And each one, having grabbed his opponent by the head, thrust his sword into his side, and they fell down together; and the name of that place was called: The Field of the Strong, in Gibeon.
17 And a very fierce battle broke out on that day: and Abner and the men of Israel were put to flight by the servants of David.
18 Now the three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. <note>Zeruiah was David's sister, making these three men David's nephews and most trusted military leaders.</note> Moreover, Asahel was a very swift runner, like one of the gazelles that dwell in the woods.
19 And Asahel pursued Abner, and did not turn to the right or to the left, never ceasing to chase Abner.
20 Then Abner looked behind him and said: "Is that you, Asahel?" And he answered: "It is I."
21 And Abner said to him: "Turn aside to the right or to the left, and catch one of the young men and take his spoils for yourself." But Asahel would not stop pressing him.
22 And Abner spoke again to Asahel: "Withdraw, do not follow me, lest I be compelled to strike you down to the ground, and then I will not be able to lift my face to your brother Joab."
23 But he refused to listen and would not turn aside; therefore Abner struck him with the back of his spear in the groin and pierced him through, and he died in that same place. And all who passed by the place where Asahel had fallen and died stood still.
24 While Joab and Abishai pursued the fleeing Abner, the sun set; and they came as far as the hill of the aqueduct, which is opposite the valley of the desert road in Gibeon.
25 And the sons of Benjamin gathered together to Abner: and forming a single wedge, they stood on the top of a hill.
26 And Abner cried out to Joab and said:

<column-break/>

"Must your sword rage until total slaughter? Do you not know that desperation is dangerous? <note>original: "periculosa sit desperatio"; Abner warns that cornered men fight more bitterly.</note> How long will it be until you tell the people to cease pursuing their brothers?"
27 And Joab said: "As the Lord lives, if you had spoken sooner, the people would have withdrawn from pursuing their brothers even in the morning."
28 So Joab sounded the trumpet, and the whole army stopped; they pursued Israel no further, nor did they continue the battle.
29 Then Abner and his men went through the plains all that night; and they crossed the Jordan, and having passed through all of Beth-horon, they came to the camp.
30 Moreover, Joab returned, having left Abner, and gathered all the people; and nineteen men were missing from David's servants, besides Asahel.
31 But David's servants had struck down three hundred and sixty men of Benjamin and the men who were with Abner, and they died.
32 And they took up Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb in Bethlehem; and Joab and the men who were with him marched all night, and they reached Hebron at the very break of dawn.

### C H A P T E R VII.

*David proposing to build a house for the Lord is first praised by Nathan the prophet, but afterwards, by the command of the Lord, he is forbidden; however, a son is promised to him who shall build it, for which he gives thanks to the Lord.*

**I**t came to pass, when the king sat in his house and the Lord had given him rest on every side from all his enemies,
<margin>
† 1 Chronicles 17:1
</margin>
2 He said to Nathan the prophet: "Do you see that I dwell in a house of cedar, while the ark of God is placed in the midst of skins <note>Referring to the tent curtains of the tabernacle.</note>?"
3 And Nathan said to the king: "Go, do all that is in your heart, for the Lord is with you."
4 But it happened that night that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying:
5 "Go and speak to my servant David: Thus says the Lord: Would you build me a house to dwell in?

### CHAPTER VIII.

->*The various victories of David, who made many peoples tributary to whom the Israelites used to pay tribute: the congratulations of Toi <note>Latin: *Thou*</note>, king of Hamath, concerning the defeat of King Hadadezer <note>Latin: *Adarezer*</note>, from whom David took much spoil: the officials whom David kept are enumerated.*<-

<margin>† 1 Chronicles 18:1</margin>
1 And it came to pass after this, that David struck the Philistines and humbled them, and David took the bridle of tribute <note>Latin: *frenum tributi*. In the Hebrew text, this is 'Metheg-ammah,' likely a place name or a metaphor for David taking control over the Philistine capital.</note> out of the hand of the Philistines. 
2 And he struck Moab, and measured them with a cord, leveling them to the ground: he measured out two cords, one for killing, and one for keeping alive: and Moab became servants to David, under tribute. 
3 David also struck Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when he went to extend his dominion over the river Euphrates. 
4 And after David captured from his side one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand footmen, he hamstrung <note>Latin: *ibnervavit*, a variant of *unnervavit*. This was a common practice in ancient warfare to disable enemy chariot horses.</note> all the chariot horses; but he left enough for a hundred chariots.

6 And David placed a garrison in Syria of Damascus: and Syria became servant to David under tribute: and the Lord preserved David in everything to which he set out. 
7 And David took the golden shields which the servants of Hadadezer had, and brought them to Jerusalem. 
8 And from Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a very great amount of bronze. 
9 And Toi, the king of Hamath, heard that David had struck down all the strength of Hadadezer, 
10 And Toi sent Joram his son to King David, to greet him and congratulate him, and to give thanks because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him down. For Toi was an enemy of Hadadezer, and in his hand were vessels of gold, and vessels of silver, and vessels of bronze: 
11 These also King David sanctified to the Lord, along with the silver and gold which he had sanctified from all the nations he had subdued: 
12 From Syria, and Moab, and the children of Ammon, and the Philistines, and Amalek, and from the spoils of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah. 
13 David also made a name for himself when he returned after capturing Syria in the Valley of Salt, having slain eighteen thousand: 
14 And he placed guards in Edom <note>Latin: *Idumæa*</note>, and established a garrison: and all of Edom became servant to David, and the Lord preserved David in everything to which he set out. 
15 And David reigned over all Israel: David also performed judgment and justice for all his people. 
16 And Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the army; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was the recorder <note>Latin: *a commentariis*, meaning the official in charge of the royal records or annals.</note>; 
17 And Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, were priests; and Seraiah was the scribe. 
18 And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and Pelethites <note>The Cherethites and Pelethites were likely David's royal bodyguard, possibly of foreign (Cretan and Philistine) origin.</note>; and the sons of David were priests <note>Latin: *sacerdotes*. In modern scholarship, this is often interpreted as "chief officials," as the priesthood was technically reserved for Levites.</note>.

### CHAPTER X.

*Hanon, king of the Ammonites, after inflicting an insult upon the envoys of David whom he had sent to comfort him over the death of his father, gathers the forces of five kings of Syria against David, but is defeated by him twice.*

1 It happened after this that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanon his son reigned in his place.
<margin>1 Chronicles 19</margin>
2 David said: "I will show kindness to Hanon, the son of Naas <note>Nahash</note>, just as his father showed kindness to me." David therefore sent his servants to comfort him over the death of his father. But when David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon,
3 The princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanon their lord: "Do you think that David has sent comforters to you out of respect for your father? Has David not rather sent his servants to you to investigate and spy out the city, so that he might overthrow it?"
4 Therefore, Hanon took David’s servants and shaved off half of their beards, and cut off half of their garments even to the buttocks, and sent them away.
5 When this was reported to David, he sent messengers to meet them—for the men were very deeply humiliated—and David commanded them: "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, and then return."
6 When the children of Ammon saw that they had done an injury to David, they sent and hired for wages the Syrians of Rohob and the Syrians of Soba, twenty thousand foot soldiers; and from the king of Maacha a thousand men; and from Istob twelve thousand men.
7 When David heard this, he sent Joab and the entire army of warriors.
8 The children of Ammon came out and drew up their battle line at the very entrance of the gate; but the Syrians of Soba and Rohob, and the men of Istob and Maacha, were by themselves in the field.
9 Joab, seeing that the battle was prepared against him both in front and from behind, chose the best from all the elite of Israel and drew up a line against the Syrians.

<column-break/>

10 The rest of the people he handed over to his brother Abisai, who drew up the line against the children of Ammon.
11 Joab said: "If the Syrians prevail against me, you shall help me; but if the children of Ammon prevail against you, I will come to your aid.
12 Be a man of courage, and let us fight for our people and for the city of our God; and the Lord will do what is good in His sight."
13 So Joab and the people who were with him entered the battle against the Syrians, who immediately fled from before him.
14 And the children of Ammon, seeing that the Syrians had fled, also fled from before Abisai and entered the city. Then Joab returned from the children of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.
15 The Syrians, seeing that they had fallen before Israel, gathered themselves together.
16 Adarezer <note>Hadadezer</note> sent and brought out the Syrians who were across the river, and led their army; Sobach, the captain of Adarezer’s host, was their leader.
17 When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Syrians drew up their line against David and fought against him.
18 The Syrians fled before Israel, and David destroyed seven hundred chariots of the Syrians and forty thousand horsemen; he also struck down Sobach, the captain of the host, who died there.
19 All the kings who were under the protection of Adarezer, seeing themselves defeated by Israel, were terrified and fled—fifty-eight thousand before Israel. They made peace with Israel and served them; and the Syrians were afraid to provide any further help to the children of Ammon.

### CHAPTER XI.

*While Joab besieges Rabba, a city of the Ammonites, David, staying at home, committed adultery with Bathsheba, and to hide it, added the murder of her husband, Uriah; and having taken her as his wife, and a son being born to her, he provoked the Lord to anger.*

6 Then David sent to Joab, saying: "Send Uriah the Hittite to me." And Joab sent Uriah to David.

### CHAPTER XII.

*David, rebuked by Nathan through a parable, brings judgment upon himself; whereupon Nathan threatens him with many troubles. When David is moved to repentance, his guilt is forgiven, though the punishment remains. After the child dies, Solomon is born; and the city of Rabbah is destroyed with great vengeance, and the most precious crown of its king is taken, as David deals severely with the Ammonites.*

The Lord therefore sent Nathan to David; and when he had come to him, he said to him: “There were two men in one city, one rich and the other poor.
2 The rich man had very many sheep and oxen.
3 But the poor man had nothing at all except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished, and which had grown up with him and his children together, eating of his bread, and drinking from his cup, and sleeping in his bosom; and she was like a daughter to him.
4 But when a certain traveler came to the rich man, he was unwilling to take from his own sheep and oxen to provide a feast for the traveler who had come to him; he took the poor man’s sheep and prepared a meal for the man who had come to him.”
5 Then David’s anger was greatly kindled against that man, and he said to Nathan: “As the Lord lives, the man who has done this is a son of death <term>son of death: a Hebrew idiom meaning "one who deserves to die"</term>.
<margin>† Exodus 22:1</margin>
6 He shall restore the sheep fourfold, because he did this thing and did not spare him.”
7 Then Nathan said to David: “You are that man. Thus says the Lord God of Israel: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I rescued you from the hand of Saul,
8 and I gave you the house of your lord and the wives of your lord into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah; and if these things are small, I would have added much greater things for you.
9 Why then have you despised the word of the Lord, to do evil in my sight? You have struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and you have taken his wife to be your wife, and you have killed him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
10 For which reason, the sword shall not depart from your house forever, because you have despised me and taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.’
11 Therefore thus says the Lord: ‘Behold, I will raise up evil against you from your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he shall sleep with your wives in the sight of this sun.
<margin>† Below 16:22</margin>
12 For you acted secretly; but I will do this thing in the sight of all Israel, and in the sight of the sun.’”
13 And David said to Nathan: “I have sinned against the Lord.” And Nathan said to David: “The Lord also has taken away your sin; you shall not die.
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 47:13</margin>
14 Nevertheless, because by this deed you have given the enemies of the Lord occasion to blaspheme, the son who is born to you shall die the death.”
15 And Nathan returned to his house. And the Lord struck the little child whom the wife of Uriah had borne to David, and his condition was desperate.

### CHAPTER XIII.

->Absalom, on account of the incest with his sister Tamar, kills his brother Amnon during a banquet: and his father being angry, he fled to the king of Gessur, and remained there for three years.<-

1 And it happened after this, that Amnon the son of David loved the most beautiful sister of Absalom the son of David, named Tamar,
2 And he pined for her exceedingly, so that he fell sick for love of her: because she was a virgin, and it seemed difficult to him to do anything dishonorable with her.
3 Now Amnon had a friend, named Jonadab, the son of Shimeah <note>original: 'Semmaa'</note> the brother of David, a very clever man.
4 Who said to him: "Why do you grow so thin from day to day, O son of the king? Why do you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him: "I love Tamar the sister of my brother Absalom."
5 To whom Jonadab replied: "Lie down upon your bed, and pretend to be ill: and when your father comes to visit you, say to him: 'I pray you, let my sister Tamar come, that she may give me food, and make a broth <note>original: 'pulmentum'</note>, that I may eat from her hand.'"
6 So Amnon lay down, and began to pretend he was sick: and when the king had come to visit him, Amnon said to the king: "I beseech you, let my sister Tamar come, that she may make two little cakes <note>original: 'sorbitiunculas'</note> in my sight, and I may take food from her hand."
7 David therefore sent to Tamar's house, saying: "Come to the house of your brother Amnon, and make him a broth."
8 And Tamar came to the house of her brother Amnon: but he was lying down: and she took flour and mixed it: and melting it, she cooked the cakes in his sight.
9 And taking what she had cooked, she poured it out, and set it before him, but he would not eat: and Amnon said: "Drive everyone out from me." And when they had driven everyone out,
10 Amnon said to Tamar: "Bring the food into the chamber, that I may eat from your hand." Tamar therefore took the cakes she had made, and brought them to her brother Amnon in the chamber.
11 And when she had offered him the food, he caught hold of her, and said: "Come, lie with me, my sister."
12 She answered him: "Do not, my brother, do not oppress me, for this is not lawful in Israel: do not do this folly.
13 For I shall not be able to bear my shame, and you will be as one of the fools in Israel: but rather speak to the king, and he will not deny me to you."
14 But he would not yield to her prayers, but prevailing by strength, he oppressed her, and lay with her.
15 Then Amnon hated her with an exceeding great hatred: so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her before. And Amnon said to her: "Arise, and go."
16 She answered him: "This evil, which you now do against me, in driving me out, is greater than that which you did before." And he would not listen to her:
17 But calling the servant who ministered to him, he said: "Drive this woman out from me, and shut the door after her."
18 And she was clothed in a robe reaching to the ankles <note>original: 'talari tunica'</note>: for the virgin daughters of the king used such garments. His servant therefore drove her out: and shut the doors after her.

19 And she, sprinkling ashes on her head, and having torn her long robe <note>original: "talari tunica" refers to a garment reaching the ankles, often a sign of status or virginity among royalty</note>, and having placed her hands upon her head, went on her way entering and crying out.

21 When King David heard these words, he was greatly saddened, yet he would not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, for he loved him, because he was his firstborn.
22 Furthermore, Absalom did not speak to Amnon, neither evil nor good: for Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated his sister Tamar.
23 And it happened after two full years that Absalom had sheep-shearers in Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king's sons.
24 And he came to the king, and said to him: "Behold, your servant’s sheep are being shorn: let the king, I pray, come with his servants to his servant."
25 And the king said to Absalom: "No, my son, do not ask that we all come, lest we be a burden to you." And when he pressed him, and he would not go, he blessed him.
26 And Absalom said: "If you will not come, let at least my brother Amnon come with us, I beseech you." And the king said to him: "It is not necessary for him to go with you."
27 Absalom therefore compelled him, and he sent Amnon and all the king's sons with him. And Absalom had prepared a feast like the feast of a king.
28 Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying: "Watch when Amnon is drunk with wine, and when I say to you: 'Strike him,' then kill him: do not fear: for it is I who command you: take courage, and be strong men."
29 So the servants of Absalom did against Amnon as Absalom had commanded them. And all the king's sons rose up and each mounted his mule and fled.
30 And while they were still on their way, the rumor reached David, saying: "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons, and not even one of them remains."
31 The king therefore rose up and tore his garments: and he fell upon the ground, and all his servants who stood by him tore their garments.
32 But Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, answering, said: "Let not my lord the king think that all the young men, the king's sons, are slain: Amnon alone is dead, for by the mouth of Absalom this has been determined from the day that he oppressed his sister Tamar.
33 Now therefore, let not my lord the king take this thing to heart, saying: 'All the king's sons are slain': because Amnon alone is dead."
34 But Absalom fled: and the young man who was a watchman lifted up his eyes and looked: and behold, many people were coming by a roundabout way from the side of the mountain.
35 And Jonadab said to the king: "Behold, the king's sons are here: according to the word of your servant, so it has happened."
36 And when he had finished speaking, the king's sons appeared: and entering they lifted up their voices and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept with an exceedingly great weeping.

<column-break/>

37 But Absalom, fleeing, went to Talmai the son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur <note>Geshur was a small kingdom to the north; Talmai was Absalom's maternal grandfather</note>. And David mourned for his son every day.
38 And when Absalom had fled and come into Geshur, he was there for three years.
39 And King David ceased to pursue Absalom, because he was comforted over the death of Amnon.

### C H A P T E R XIV.

*By the cleverness of a woman of Tekoa, Joab arranges for Absalom to be called back from Geshur to Jerusalem; regarding the beauty and children of Absalom, who for two years after his return did not see his father's face, until he ordered Joab’s harvest to be set on fire.*

1 Now Joab the son of Zeruiah, understanding that the king’s heart was turned toward Absalom,
2 Sent to Tekoa, and brought from there a wise woman: and said to her: "Feign that you are mourning, and put on a mourning garment, and do not anoint yourself with oil, that you may be like a woman who has now for a long time been mourning for the dead:
3 And you shall go in to the king, and speak to him words of this kind." And Joab put the words in her mouth.
4 And so when the woman of Tekoa had entered to the king, she fell before him upon the ground, and worshipped, and said: "Save me, O king."
5 And the king said to her: "What cause have you?" And she answered: "Alas, I am a widow woman: for my husband is dead.
6 And your handmaid had two sons: who quarreled against each other in the field, and there was no one who could stop them: and the one struck the other and killed him.
7 And behold, the whole kindred rising against your handmaid, says: 'Deliver him who struck his brother, that we may kill him for the life of his brother whom he slew, and that we may destroy the heir': and they seek to quench my spark which is left, so that no name or remnant of my husband shall remain upon the earth."
8 And the king said to the woman: "Go to your house, and I will give orders concerning you."
9 And the woman of Tekoa said to the king: "Upon me, my lord the king, let the iniquity be, and upon my father's house: but let the king and his throne be innocent."
10 And the king said: "He who contradicts you, bring him to me, and he shall not touch you anymore."
11 She said: "Let the king remember the Lord his God, that the next of kin <note>original: "proximi sanguinis" refers to the 'avenger of blood' in ancient law</note> may not be multiplied to take revenge, and that they may by no means kill my son." And he said: "As the Lord lives, not a hair of your son shall fall to the ground."
12 Then the woman said: "Let your handmaid speak a word to my lord the king." And he said: "Speak."
13 And the woman said: "Why have you thought such a thing against the people of God, and why has the king spoken this word, so as to sin, and not bring back his own banished one?
<margin>† Ezekiel 18:32 and 33:11</margin> 14 We all die, and like water we slip away into the earth, which does not return: nor does God desire a soul to perish, but he recalls his thoughts lest he who is cast off should perish utterly.
15 Now therefore, I have come to speak to—

### C H A P T E R XV.

> *Absalom, having won the favor of the people for himself, conspires against his father in Hebron, whom his father flees, having sent back a few with the Ark; and among others Hushai is sent back, to frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel.*

1 Therefore after these things, Absalom made for himself chariots, and horsemen, and fifty men who should run before him.
2 And rising early in the morning, Absalom stood near the entrance of the gate, and every man who had business to come to the king's judgment, Absalom called to him, and said: From what city are you? Who answering said: Your servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
3 And Absalom answered him: Your words seem to me good and just. But there is no one appointed by the king to hear you: and Absalom said:
4 Who would appoint me judge over the land, that all who have business might come to me, and I might judge justly?
5 Moreover, when a man came near to him to greet him, he put out his hand, and taking hold of him, he kissed him.
6 And he did this to all Israel who came to judgment, to be heard by the king, and he enticed the hearts of the men of Israel.
7 But after forty years <note>Many biblical scholars suggest this should be 'four years', as forty years exceeds David's total reign; it is widely considered a scribal error in the manuscript tradition</note>, Absalom said to King David: I will go, and pay my vows which I vowed to the Lord in Hebron:
8 For your servant made a vow, while he was in Geshur of Syria, saying: If the Lord brings me back to Jerusalem, I will sacrifice to the Lord.
9 And King David said to him: Go in peace. And he arose, and went to Hebron.
10 But Absalom sent scouts into all the tribes of Israel, saying: As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, say: Absalom has reigned in Hebron.
11 Furthermore, two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom, having been invited, going with a simple heart, and knowing nothing of the cause.
12 Absalom also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city Gilo. And while he was offering sacrifices, a strong conspiracy was formed, and the people running together increased with Absalom.
13 A messenger therefore came to David, saying: With all their heart, all Israel follows Absalom.
14 And David said to his servants who were with him in Jerusalem: Arise, let us flee: for there shall be no escape for us from the face of Absalom: hasten to go out, lest perhaps he coming should overtake us, and bring ruin upon us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword.
15 And the king's servants said to him: All things whatsoever our lord the king shall command, we your servants will gladly perform.
16 The king therefore went out, and all his house, on their feet: and the king left ten women as concubines <note>term: "concubines" refers here to secondary wives who held legal status but lower social standing than primary wives</note> to keep the house.

### CHAPTER XVI.

->*Ziba brings provisions and, being a slanderer, is granted the goods of Mephibosheth. David forbids the killing of the cursing Shimei. Absalom, having entered Jerusalem, follows the advice of Ahithophel and publicly goes in to his father’s concubines.*<-

**A**nd when David had passed a little beyond the top of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with two donkeys laden with two hundred loaves of bread, and a hundred bunches of raisins, and a hundred cakes of dried figs, and a skin of wine.
2 And the king said to Ziba: What do these things mean? And Ziba answered: The donkeys are for the king's household to sit on: the bread and figs are for your servants to eat: and the wine is for anyone to drink who faints in the desert.
<margin>† Below 19:27.</margin>
3 And the king said: Where is your master's son? † And Ziba answered the king: He remains in Jerusalem, saying: Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.
4 And the king said to Ziba: All that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours. And Ziba said: I pray that I may find grace before you, my lord king.
5 Then King David came as far as Bahurim: and behold, a man of the family of the house of Saul came out from there, named Shimei, the son of Gera; he came out † cursing as he went,
<margin>† 1 Kings 2:8.</margin>
6 And he threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David: and all the people and all the warriors walked on his right and on his left.
7 And thus Shimei spoke when he cursed the king: Come out, come out, you man of blood, and you man of Belial <note>original: "vir Belial"; a term meaning a wicked, worthless, or lawless person</note>.
8 The Lord has repaid you for all the blood of the house of Saul: because you have usurped the kingdom in his place, and the Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son: and behold, your evils press upon you, because you are a man of blood.
9 Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah <note>original: "Sarviæ"</note> said to the king: Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go and cut off his head.
10 And the king said: What is it to me and to you, you sons of Zeruiah? Let him be, that he may curse: for the Lord has commanded him to curse David: and who is he that dares say, why has he done so?
11 And the king said to Abishai and to all his servants: Behold, my own son, who came out of my own body, seeks my life: how much more now this son of Benjamin <note>original: "filius Jemini"</note>? Let him be, that he may curse according to the command of the Lord:
12 Perhaps the Lord may look upon my affliction, and the Lord may render me good for this cursing today.
13 And so David and his companions went along the way with him. But Shimei walked along the ridge of the mountain opposite him, cursing, and throwing stones at him, and scattering earth.
14 And the king and all the people with him arrived weary, and they refreshed themselves there.
15 Meanwhile, Absalom and all his people entered Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

### C H A P T E R XVII.

->*Hushai thwarts the counsel of Ahithophel regarding the immediate pursuit of David, and makes this known to David through messengers. Following Hushai's advice, David crosses the Jordan, which leads Ahithophel to hang himself. Three of David's friends bring gifts so that his people, lacking necessities, would not fail.*<-

Ahithophel then said to Absalom: "I will choose for myself twelve thousand men, and rising up I will pursue David this night.
2 And falling upon him (for he is weary and weak-handed) I will strike him with terror; and when all the people who are with him have fled, I will strike down the king while he is alone.
3 And I will bring back all the people, as one man is won over; for you seek only the life of one man, and all the people shall be at peace."
4 And his words pleased Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
5 But Absalom said: "Call Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear what he too has to say."
6 And when Hushai had come to Absalom, Absalom said to him: "Ahithophel has spoken in this manner; should we do it or not? What counsel do you give?"
7 And Hushai said to Absalom: "The counsel that Ahithophel has given this time is not good."
8 And Hushai added: "You know your father and the men who are with him are very brave and bitter in spirit, like a bear in the wild when her cubs have been taken; moreover, your father is a man of war, and he will not stay with the common people.
9 Perhaps even now he is hiding in some pit or in some other place he chooses; and when anyone falls at the start, whoever hears of it will say, 'A slaughter has occurred among the people following Absalom.'
10 Then even the bravest, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will melt with fear; for all the people of Israel know that your father is a hero and that those who are with him are strong."

<column-break/>

11 "But this seems to me to be the right counsel: Let all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, as numerous as the sand of the sea; and you shall be in their midst.
12 And we will fall upon him in whatever place he may be found; and we will cover him as the dew falls upon the earth; and we will not leave of the men who are with him even one.
13 And if he should enter into any city, all Israel shall bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it into the torrent, until not even a pebble of it is found."
14 And Absalom and all the men of Israel said: "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For by the Lord's will, the profitable counsel of Ahithophel was defeated, so that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom.
15 Then Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests: "In such and such a way did Ahithophel give counsel to Absalom and the elders of Israel; and in such and such a way did I give counsel.
16 Now therefore send quickly and tell David, saying: 'Do not stay this night in the plains of the wilderness, but without delay cross over, lest the king and all the people with him be swallowed up.'"
17 But Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by the fountain of Rogel; a maidservant went and told them, and they went on to carry the message to King David, for they could not be seen or enter the city.
18 However, a certain boy saw them and told Absalom; but they quickly entered the house of a certain man in Bahurim who had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
19 Then a woman took a cloth and spread it over the mouth of the well, as if spreading out dried grains <note>original: "ptisanas," hulled barley or groats</note>; and so the matter was hidden.
20 When Absalom’s servants came to the house and asked the woman, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" she replied: "They passed by in haste, after tasting a little water." But when those who sought them did not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

22 David therefore arose, and all the people who were with him, and they crossed the Jordan until daybreak; and not even one was left who had not crossed the river.
23 Furthermore, when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey, rose up, and went to his house in his own city; and having set his house in order, he died by hanging, and was buried in the tomb of his father.

## CHAPTER XVIII.

*Absalom is defeated in battle, and while hanging from an oak tree is pierced by Joab; hearing this, David wept bitterly for him.*

1 So David reviewed his people and appointed over them commanders of thousands and hundreds.
2 He placed a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, a third under Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under Ittai of Geth. The king said to the people: "I will surely go out with you myself."
3 But the people answered: "You shall not go out; for if we flee, they will not care much about us; or if half of us fall, they will not care; for you alone are accounted as ten thousand. It is better, therefore, that you remain in the city as a reserve for us."
4 The king said to them: "Whatever seems right to you, I will do." So the king stood by the gate, and the people went out by their companies, by hundreds and by thousands.
5 And the king commanded Joab, and Abishai, and Ittai, saying: "Spare for my sake the young man Absalom." And all the people heard the king giving this command to all the leaders concerning Absalom.
6 So the people went out into the field against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
7 And the people of Israel were defeated there by David’s army, and a great slaughter took place that day, of twenty thousand men.
8 The battle was scattered over the face of the whole land, and the forest consumed many more of the people than the sword devoured that day.
9 It happened that Absalom met the servants of David while riding on a mule; and when the mule went under the thick branches of a great oak, his head got caught in the oak. He was suspended between heaven and earth, while the mule he was riding on kept going.
10 Someone saw this and told Joab, saying: "I saw Absalom hanging from an oak."
11 Joab said to the man who told him: "If you saw him, why did you not strike him to the ground? I would have given you ten silver shekels and a belt."
12 He said to Joab: "Even if you weighed out a thousand pieces of silver into my hands, I would never lay a hand on the king's son. For in our hearing the king commanded you, and Abishai, and Ittai, saying: 'Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.'
13 Moreover, if I had acted boldly against my own life, nothing can be hidden from the king; would you have stood by me?"
14 Joab said: "I will not waste time with you as you wish, but I will strike him before you." So he took three spears in his hand and thrust them into Absalom's heart; and while he was still gasping, clinging to the oak,

<column-break/>

15 Ten young men who were Joab's armor-bearers ran and struck him, killing him.
16 Then Joab sounded the trumpet and held back the people from pursuing the fleeing Israelites, wishing to spare the multitude.
17 They took Absalom and threw him into a great pit in the forest, and piled a very large heap of stones over him. All Israel then fled to their own tents.
18 Now Absalom, while he was still alive, had set up a monument for himself in the King’s Valley; for he said: "I have no son, and this shall be a memorial to my name." He called the monument by his own name, and it is called "Absalom’s Hand" <note>original: "Manus Absalom"; a Hebrew idiom used for a monument or memorial pillar</note> to this day.
19 Then Ahimaaz son of Zadok said: "I will run and tell the king that the Lord has delivered judgment for him from the hand of his enemies."
20 Joab said to him: "You shall not be a messenger today, but you shall bring news another day. Today I do not want you to carry news, for the king’s son is dead."
21 Then Joab said to the Cushite: "Go and tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed to Joab and ran.
22 Ahimaaz son of Zadok said again to Joab: "What is the harm if I also run after the Cushite?" Joab said to him: "Why do you want to run, my son? You will not receive a reward for this news."
23 He replied: "What if I run anyway?" Joab said: "Run." So Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain <note>original: "viam compendii," implying a shortcut or more direct route</note> and outran the Cushite.
24 David was sitting between the two gates. The lookout, who was on the roof of the gate by the wall, lifted his eyes and saw a man running alone.
25 He called out and told the king. The king said: "If he is alone, there is good news in his mouth." As he hurried and came closer,
26 The lookout saw another man running, and shouting from the roof, he said: "I see another man running alone." The king said: "This one also brings good news."
27 The lookout said: "I observe the running of the first one; it is like the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok." The king said: "He is a good man and comes with good news."
28 Ahimaaz cried out and said to the king: "Peace be to you, O king." And bowing before the king with his face to the ground, he said: "Blessed be the Lord your God, who has delivered up the men who lifted their hands against my lord the king."
29 The king said: "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" Ahimaaz said: "I saw a great commotion when your servant Joab sent me, your servant, O king, but I do not know anything else."
30 The king said: "Step aside and stand here." So he stepped aside and stood there.
31 Then the Cushite appeared and said: "I bring good news, my lord king; for the Lord has judged for you today against the hand of all who rose up against you."
32 The king said to the Cushite: "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" The Cushite answered: "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up against him for evil, become like that young man."

33 The king was deeply moved and went up to the room over the gate and wept. As he went, he said: "O my son Absalom, Absalom my son! Would that I had died for you, O Absalom my son, my son Absalom!"
