### CHAPTER XIX.

David, moved by the words of Joab, ceases to mourn for Absalom and reconciles with those who conspired against him. He is led back to Jerusalem by the men of Judah; he grants pardon to Shimei <note>original: "Semei"</note> as he begs for mercy; and he receives Mephibosheth <note>original: "Miphiboseth"</note>, ordering him to divide his lands with Ziba <note>original: "Siba"</note>. Barzillai takes his leave of the king, leaving Chimham <note>original: "Chamaam"</note> in his place, while the men of Israel and Judah argue sharply over their loyalty to David.

---

1 It was reported to Joab that the king was weeping and mourning for his son.
2 And so the victory of that day was turned into mourning for all the people, for the people heard it said that day: "The king is grieving for his son."
3 The people stole into the city that day like people who are ashamed and flee from a battle.
4 Furthermore, the king covered his head and cried out with a loud voice: "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"
5 Then Joab went into the house to the king and said: "Today you have shamed the faces of all your servants who saved your life, and the lives of your sons and daughters, and the lives of your wives and concubines.
6 You love those who hate you, and you hate those who love you. You have shown today that you do not care for your commanders or your servants; for I truly see now that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, then you would be pleased.
7 Now therefore, get up, go out, and speak to the satisfaction of your servants. For I swear to you by the Lord, that if you do not go out, not even one man will stay with you tonight. And this will be worse for you than all the evils that have come upon you from your youth until now."
8 So the king got up and sat in the gate. And it was announced to all the people that the king was sitting in the gate, and the whole multitude came before the king. Meanwhile, the men of Israel had fled to their own tents.
9 And all the people throughout all the tribes of Israel were at odds, saying: "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies and saved us from the hand of the Philistines, yet now he has fled the land because of Absalom.
10 But Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. How long will you remain silent about bringing the king back?"
11 King David then sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, saying: "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying: 'Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house?' (For the talk of all Israel had reached the king in his house.)
12 'You are my brothers, my own bone and my own flesh; why then are you the last to bring back the king?'
13 And say to Amasa: 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? May God do such things to me, and more also, if you do not become the commander of the army before me forever in place of Joab.'"
14 And he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as if they were one man; and they sent word to the king, saying: "Return, you and all your servants."
15 So the king returned and came as far as the Jordan, and all of Judah came to Gilgal <note>original: "Galgalam"</note> to meet the king and to escort him across the Jordan.

23 And the king said to Shimei: "You shall not die." And the king swore an oath to him.
24 Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came down to meet the king. He had not washed his feet or trimmed his beard, nor had he washed his clothes from the day the king departed until the day he returned in peace.

### CHAPTER XX.

> *Joab, along with his brother Abishai, pursues Sheba <note>original: "Seba"</note>, the son of Bichri, who is stirring up a rebellion against David in Israel. He kills Amasa on the way, and finally departs from the siege of Abel-beth-maachah <note>original: "Abelæ"</note> after Sheba’s head is thrown over the wall.*

1 **I**t also happened that there was a man of Belial <note>a term used to describe a wicked or worthless person; original: "vir Belial"</note> there named Sheba, the son of Bichri, a man of the tribe of Benjamin. He blew the trumpet and said: "We have no part in David, nor any inheritance in the son of Jesse! Return to your tents, O Israel!" 
2 And so all Israel separated from David and followed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah stayed close to their king, from the Jordan all the way to Jerusalem. 
3 When the king came to his house in Jerusalem, he took the ten women, the concubines whom he had left to guard the house, and put them under guard. He provided them with food, but he did not go in to them; they were shut away until the day of their death, living as if in widowhood. 
4 Then the king said to Amasa: "Call all the men of Judah to me within three days, and you be present here yourself." 
5 So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he stayed longer than the time the king had appointed for him. 
6 And David said to Abishai: "Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Therefore, take your lord’s servants and pursue him, lest he find fortified cities and escape us." 
7 So Joab's men went out with him, as well as the Cherethites and the Pelethites <note>The king’s elite bodyguard; original: "Cerethi quoque & Phelethi"</note>, and all the mighty men. They went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

<column-break/>

8 When they were near the great stone in Gibeon <note>original: "Gabaon"</note>, Amasa came to meet them. Now Joab was wearing a tight-fitting tunic suited to his stature, and over it he was girded with a sword hanging down to his loins in a sheath; it was made so that with a slight movement it could come out and strike. 
<margin>† 1 Kings 2:5</margin> 
9 Joab said to Amasa: "Is it well with you, my brother?" And with his right hand Joab took Amasa by the chin, as if to kiss him. 
10 But Amasa did not notice the sword which Joab had, and Joab struck him in the side, spilling his intestines onto the ground; he did not need to strike a second time, and Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba the son of Bichri. 
11 Meanwhile, one of Joab's young men stood by the body and said: "Whoever wants to be for Joab, let him follow David." 
12 Now Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. When the man saw that all the people stopped to look at him, he moved Amasa from the road into a field and covered him with a garment, so that those passing by would not stop because of him. 
13 Once he was moved from the road, every man went on, following Joab to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri. 
14 Now Sheba had passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maachah <note>original: "Abelam, & Bethmaacha"</note>, and all the chosen men had gathered to him. 
15 So they came and besieged him in Abel-beth-maachah; they cast up a siege mound against the city, and the city was besieged. All the crowd that was with Joab labored to throw down the walls. 
16 Then a wise woman cried out from the city: "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab: Come here, that I may speak with you." 
17 When he had come near her, she said: "Are you Joab?" And he answered: "I am." She spoke to him thus: "Hear the words of your handmaid." He answered: "I am listening." 
18 And she spoke again, saying: "A saying was used in the old proverb: 'Those who ask, let them ask in Abel,' and so they settled matters. 
19 Am I not one of those who speak the truth in Israel? And yet you seek to destroy a city and to overturn a mother-city in Israel. Why would you ruin the inheritance of the Lord?" 
20 Joab answered and said: "Far be it, far be it from me! I do not wish to ruin or destroy. 
21 The matter is not so. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against King David. Deliver him alone, and we will depart from the city." And the woman said to Joab: "Behold, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall." 
22 Then she went to all the people and spoke to them with wisdom; and they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri and threw it to Joab. He blew the trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his own tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.

### CHAPTER XXI.

*A three-year famine is sent because of Saul's unjust cruelty toward the Gibeonites; to turn it away, at their request, David hands over the remaining descendants of Saul (except Mephibosheth) to be executed. He then orders their bones, along with those of Saul and Jonathan, to be given proper burial. Four wars of David against the Philistines are also recounted.*

1 Now there was a famine in the days of David for three years continually; and David consulted the oracle of the Lord. And the Lord said: "It is because of Saul and his blood-guilty house, because he put the Gibeonites to death."
<margin>† Below 9:25</margin>
2 Therefore, having called the Gibeonites, the king spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but were the remnant of the Amorites; for the children of Israel had sworn an oath to them, but Saul sought to strike them down in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah.)
3 David said to the Gibeonites: "What shall I do for you? And what shall be your atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the Lord?"
4 And the Gibeonites said to him: "It is not a matter of silver or gold for us against Saul or against his house; nor do we wish that any man of Israel be put to death." The king said to them: "What then do you wish me to do for you?"
5 They said to the king: "The man who crushed us and oppressed us unjustly—we ought to destroy him so utterly that not one of his race remains within all the borders of Israel.
6 Let seven men of his sons be delivered to us, so that we may crucify <note>In this context, the Latin *crucifigamus* refers to a public execution where the bodies were hung or displayed as a sign of judgment.</note> them before the Lord in Gibeah of Saul, who was once the chosen of the Lord." And the king said: "I will give them."
<margin>† 1 Samuel 18:3</margin>
7 But the king spared Mephibosheth <note>original: "Miphiboseth"</note>, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, because of the oath of the Lord that had been made between David and Jonathan, the son of Saul.
8 So the king took the two sons of Rizpah <note>original: "Respha"</note>, the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul: Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal <note>Most ancient manuscripts and scholars suggest this was actually Merab, Saul's other daughter, as Michal had no children.</note>, the daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel, the son of Barzillai, who was from Meholath.
9 And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, who crucified them on the mountain before the Lord; and these seven fell together, put to death in the first days of the harvest, when the barley harvest was beginning.
10 Then Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, took sackcloth and spread it out for herself upon the rock, from the beginning of the harvest until water dropped upon them from heaven; and she did not allow the birds to tear them by day, nor the beasts by night.
11 And it was told to David what Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.
<margin>† 1 Samuel 31:12</margin>
12 And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-Gilead, who had stolen them from the street of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them when they killed Saul in Gilboa.

14 And they buried them with the bones of Saul and Jona-

## CHAPTER XXIII.

->The last words of David, and a catalog of his illustrious men.<-

1 Now these are the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said: The man said, who was appointed concerning the anointed of the God of Jacob, the excellent singer of Israel:
2 The Spirit of the Lord has spoken through me, and his word through my tongue.
3 The God of Israel said to me, the Strong One of Israel spoke, the Ruler of men, the just ruler in the fear of God.
4 Like the light of the morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds that glistens, and like the grass that sprouts from the earth after the rains.
5 Nor is my house so great before God, that he should enter into an eternal covenant with me, firm in all things and secured. For all my salvation, and all my will: nor is there anything from it that does not sprout.
6 But transgressors shall all be plucked out like thorns: which are not taken up with hands.
7 And if anyone wishes to touch them, he must be armed with iron and the wood of a spear, and they shall be burned with fire even unto nothing.
<margin>† 1 Chronicles 11:10.</margin>
8 † These are the names of David's strong men. Sitting in the chair, the most wise prince among the three, he is like a very tender little worm of the wood <note>This odd phrase in the Latin Vulgate, "vermiculus," is likely a translation error or a corrupted reading of the Hebrew name "Adino the Eznite."</note>, who killed eight hundred in one onset.
9 After him was Eleazar the son of his uncle, an Ahohite, among the three strong men who were with David when they defied the Philistines, and they were gathered there for battle.
10 And when the men of Israel had gone up, he stood and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and became stiff with the sword: and the Lord wrought a great salvation on that day: and the people who had fled returned to take the spoils of the slain.
11 And after him was Shammah the son of Agee of Arari: and the Philistines were gathered at a station: for there was a field full of lentils. And when the people had fled from the face of the Philistines,
12 He stood in the middle of the field, and defended it, and struck the Philistines: and the Lord wrought a great salvation.
13 Also before this, three who were leaders among the thirty descended and came to David at harvest time into the cave of Adullam: and the camps of the Philistines were placed in the Valley of the Giants.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

->David, rebuked by the prophet Gad for having numbered the people, chooses a three-day plague from among three offered scourges. As the plague rages through the people and 70,000 are killed, David prays to the Lord; being advised by the prophet Gad, he purchases the threshing floor of Araunah and builds an altar, and the plague ceases.<-

<margin>1 Chronicles 21:1</margin>
1 And again the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he incited David among them, saying: "Go, number Israel and Judah." 
2 And the king said to Joab, the commander of his army: "Travel through all the tribes of Israel from Dan to Beersheba, and number the people, so that I may know their total." 
3 And Joab said to the king: "May the Lord your God increase your people a hundredfold more than they are now, in the sight of my lord the king; but why does my lord the king desire such a thing?" 
4 However, the king's word prevailed over the words of Joab and the commanders of the army. So Joab and the leaders of the soldiers went out from the presence of the king to number the people of Israel. 
5 When they had crossed the Jordan, they came to Aroer, to the right of the city which is in the valley of Gad. 
6 And through Jazer they passed into Gilead, and into the lower land of Hodsi, and they came to the woodlands of Dan. And circling near Sidon, 
7 They passed near the walls of Tyre, and through all the land of the Hivite and the Canaanite, and they came to the south of Judah in Beersheba. 
8 And having surveyed the entire land, they arrived in Jerusalem after nine months and twenty days. 
9 Joab then gave the number of the census of the people to the king; and there were found in Israel eight hundred thousand strong men who could draw the sword, and in Judah five hundred thousand fighting men. 
10 But David's heart struck him <note>Meaning he felt a deep pang of conscience or guilt.</note> after the people were numbered. And David said to the Lord: "I have sinned greatly in what I have done; but I pray you, Lord, take away the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly." 
11 So David rose in the morning, and the word of the Lord came to the prophet Gad, David’s <term>Seer</term> <note>original: "Videntem," a title for a prophet who receives divine visions.</note>, saying: 
12 "Go and speak to David: Thus says the Lord: I give you a choice of three things; choose one of them that you wish for me to do to you." 
13 And when Gad had come to David, he told him, saying: "Either seven years of famine shall come upon you in your land; or for three months you shall flee from your adversaries and they shall pursue you; or certainly there shall be three days of pestilence in your land. Now, therefore, deliberate, and see what word I shall return to Him who sent me." 
<margin>1 Chronicles 21:13</margin>

<margin>a</margin> David, worn out by old age, is kept warm by the girl Abishag while remaining chaste; but while Adonijah <note>original: "Adonia"</note> seizes the kingdom, Bathsheba <note>original: "Bethsabee"</note>, directed by the counsel of Nathan, obtains from David that Solomon be anointed king; hearing this, Adonijah flees!

### CHAPTER XII.

*David, rebuked under a parable proposed by Nathan, pronounces judgment upon himself; whereupon Nathan threatens him with many troubles. When David is moved to repentance, his guilt is forgiven, though the punishment remains. After the child dies, Solomon is born. The city of Rabbah is destroyed with great vengeance, and the most precious crown of its king is taken; the Ammonites are severely punished.*

The Lord therefore sent Nathan to David. And when he had come to him, he said to him: "There were two men in one city, one rich and the other poor.
2 The rich man had very many sheep and oxen.
3 But the poor man had nothing at all except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished, and which had grown up with him and his children together, eating of his bread, drinking from his cup, and sleeping in his bosom; and she was like a daughter to him.
4 But when a certain traveler had come to the rich man, he was unwilling to take from his own sheep or oxen to provide a feast for that traveler who had come to him; instead, he took the poor man’s sheep and prepared a meal for the man who had come to him."
5 And David’s anger was greatly kindled against that man, and he said to Nathan: "As the Lord lives, the man who has done this is a son of death!" <note>The phrase "son of death" (filius mortis) is a Hebrew idiom meaning the person deserves to die.</note>
<margin>† Exodus 22:1</margin> 6 "† He shall restore the sheep fourfold, because he did this thing and had no pity."
7 Then Nathan said to David: "You are that man. Thus says the Lord God of Israel: 'I anointed you king over Israel, and I rescued you from the hand of Saul,
8 And I gave you your master’s house and your master’s wives into your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah; and if these things are small, I would have added much greater things for you.
9 Why then have you despised the word of the Lord, to do evil in my sight? You have struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and have taken his wife to be your wife, and have killed him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
10 Therefore, the sword shall never depart from your house, because you have despised me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.'
11 Thus therefore says the Lord: 'Behold, I will raise up evil against you from your own house, and <margin>† Below 16:22</margin> I will take your wives before your eyes and † give them to your neighbor, and he shall sleep with your wives in the sight of this sun.
12 For you did it secretly, but I will do this thing in the sight of all Israel, and in the sight of the sun.'"
13 And David said to Nathan: "I have sinned against the Lord." And Nathan said to David: "† The <margin>† Ecclesiasticus 47:13</margin> Lord also has taken away your sin; you shall not die.
14 Nevertheless, because by this deed you have given the enemies of the Lord occasion to blaspheme, the son who is born to you shall surely die."
15 And Nathan returned to his house. And the Lord struck the child that the wife of Uriah had borne to David, and his life was despaired of.

### CHAPTER XIII.

*Absalom, on account of the incest committed with his sister Tamar, kills his brother Amnon during a feast: and his father being angry, he flees to the king of Geshur, where he remains for three years.*

And it came to pass after this, that Amnon the son of David fell in love with the very beautiful sister of Absalom the son of David, whose name was Tamar.
2 And he pined for her so greatly that he fell sick for love of her: because she was a virgin, it seemed difficult to him to do anything dishonestly with her.
3 But Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother, a very shrewd man.
4 And he said to him: "Why do you waste away so with leanness from day to day, O son of the king? Why do you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him: "I love Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom."
5 To whom Jonadab replied: "Lie down upon your bed and pretend to be sick: and when your father comes to visit you, say to him: 'I pray you, let my sister Tamar come to give me food, and let her make a broth, that I may eat from her hand.'"
6 So Amnon lay down and began to pretend he was sick: and when the king came to visit him, Amnon said to the king: "I pray you, let my sister Tamar come and make two small cakes <note>original: *sorbitiunculas*</note> in my sight, that I may take food from her hand."
7 Then David sent to Tamar at the house, saying: "Go to the house of your brother Amnon, and make him a broth."

14 But he would not listen to her prayers, but prevailing by his strength, he forced her and lay with her.

### C H A P T E R XV.

->*Absalom, having won the favor of the people for himself, conspires against his father in Hebron; his father flees, having sent back a few men with the Ark; and among others, Hushai is sent back to thwart the counsel of Ahithophel.*<-

Therefore after these things, Absalom provided for himself chariots, and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
2 And rising early in the morning, Absalom would stand by the entrance of the gate; and every man who had a dispute to bring to the king's judgment, Absalom would call to himself and say: From what city are you? And the man would answer: I, your servant, am from such-and-such a tribe of Israel.

8 For your servant made a vow when he was in Geshur of Syria, saying: "If the Lord brings me back to Jerusalem, I will offer a sacrifice to the Lord."
9 And King David said to him: Go in peace. And he arose and went to Hebron.
10 But Absalom sent spies into all the tribes of Israel, saying: As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, say: "Absalom has become king in Hebron."
11 Moreover, two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom, having been invited; they went with simple hearts, being entirely ignorant of the plan.
12 Absalom also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city Gilo. And while he was offering sacrifices, a powerful conspiracy was formed, and the people flocking together increased around Absalom.
13 Then a messenger came to David, saying: With all their heart, all Israel follows Absalom.
14 And David said to his servants who were with him in Jerusalem: Arise, let us flee; for there will be no escape for us from the face of Absalom. Hurry to leave, lest he come and overtake us, and bring ruin upon us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword.
15 And the king's servants said to him: We, your servants, will gladly perform all things whatever our lord the king shall command.
16 The king therefore went out, and all his household followed on foot; and the king left ten women, his concubines, to keep the house.

### CHAPTER XVI.

->*Ziba brings food to David and slanders Mephibosheth. David forbids Shimei, who was cursing him, to be killed. Absalom enters Jerusalem and, on Ahithophel's advice, goes in publicly to his father's concubines.*<-

1 And when David had passed a little beyond the top of the mountain, **Ziba**, the servant of **Mephibosheth**, appeared to meet him with two donkeys laden with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred bunches of raisins, a hundred cakes of figs, and a skin of wine.
2 And the king said to Ziba: "What do these things mean?" And Ziba answered: "The donkeys are for the king's household to sit on; the bread and figs for your servants to eat; and the wine for any who may faint in the desert to drink."
<margin>† Below, 19:27.</margin>
3 And the king said: "Where is your master’s son?" † And Ziba answered the king: "He remained in Jerusalem, saying: 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.'"
<note>Ziba is accusing Mephibosheth—the son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul—of treason. Later chapters suggest this was a lie to steal Mephibosheth's lands.</note>
4 And the king said to Ziba: "Let all that belonged to Mephibosheth be yours." And Ziba said: "I pray that I may find grace before you, my lord king."
5 Then King David came as far as **Bahurim**: and behold, there came out a man of the family of the house of Saul named **Shimei**, the son of Gera, and as he came out, he † cursed,

6 And he threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David: and all the people and all the warriors walked on the right and on the left side of the king.
7 And Shimei spoke thus when he cursed the king: "Come out, come out, you man of blood, and you man of **Belial**."
<note>Belial is a term for a wicked, worthless, or lawless person.</note>
8 "The Lord has repaid you for all the blood of the house of Saul, because you have usurped the kingdom in his place, and the Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son: and behold, your evils press upon you, because you are a man of blood."
9 Then **Abishai** the son of Zeruiah said to the king: "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? I will go and cut off his head."
10 And the king said: "What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Let him be, that he may curse: for the Lord has commanded him to curse David: and who is he that dares to say, why has he done so?"
11 And the king said to Abishai and to all his servants: "Behold, my son, who came out of my own body, seeks my life: how much more now this son of **Jemini**? Let him alone that he may curse according to the commandment of the Lord:
<note>A 'son of Jemini' refers to a Benjamite, the tribe of the former King Saul.</note>
12 Perhaps the Lord may look upon my affliction, and the Lord may render me good for this day's cursing."
13 So David and his companions walked by the way with him. And Shimei walked along the side of the mountain over against him, cursing and throwing stones at him, and scattering earth.
14 And the king and all the people with him arrived weary, and they were refreshed there.
15 But Absalom and all his people entered Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

### CHAPTER XVII.

*Hushai thwarts the plan of Ahithophel to overwhelm David immediately, and informs David of this through messengers; following Hushai's advice, David crosses the Jordan, because of which Ahithophel hangs himself: three of David's friends bring gifts so that his people would not perish for lack of necessities.*

1 Then Ahithophel said to Absalom: "I will choose for myself twelve thousand men, and rising up I will pursue David this night.
2 And coming upon him (for he is weary and weak-handed), I will strike him: and when all the people who are with him have fled, I will strike the king while he is alone.
3 And I will bring back all the people, as one man is wont to return: for you seek only one man: and all the people shall be at peace."
4 And his saying pleased Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
5 But Absalom said: "Call **Hushai the Archite** also, and let us hear what he too has to say."
6 And when Hushai had come to Absalom, Absalom said to him: "Ahithophel has spoken a word of this sort: should we do it or not? What counsel do you give?"
7 And Hushai said to Absalom: "The counsel that Ahithophel has given is not good this time."
8 And Hushai added further: "You know your father and the men who are with him are very brave and bitter in spirit, just like a bear in the woods when her cubs are taken away: moreover, your father is a man of war, and he will not stay with the people.
9 Perhaps even now he is hiding in pits, or in some place he has chosen: and when anyone falls at the start, whoever hears of it will say: 'A slaughter has happened among the people who followed Absalom.'
10 And even the bravest, whose heart is like a lion's, will melt with fear: for all the people of Israel know that your father is a hero, and all who are with him are strong."

<column-break/>

11 "But this seems to me to be the right counsel: Let all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as numerous as the sand of the sea: and you shall be in the midst of them.

13 And if he has entered into any city, all Israel shall bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it into the torrent, until not even a pebble is found of it."
14 And Absalom and all the men of Israel said: "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For by the Lord's will, the profitable counsel of Ahithophel was defeated, so that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom.
15 Then Hushai said to **Zadok** and **Abiathar** the priests: "In such and such a way did Ahithophel give counsel to Absalom and the elders of Israel: and I gave such and such counsel.
16 Now therefore, send quickly and tell David, saying: 'Do not stay tonight in the plains of the desert, but without delay cross over: lest perhaps the king be swallowed up, and all the people who are with him.'"
17 Now **Jonathan** and **Ahimaaz** were staying by the fountain of **Rogel**: a maidservant went and told them: and they went on to bring the message to King David, for they could not be seen or enter the city.

19 And the woman took and spread a covering over the mouth of the well, as if drying **peeled barley**: and so the matter was hidden.

### CHAPTER XVIII.

1 David then mustered his people and appointed captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
2 And he put a third of the people under the hand of Joab, a third under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third under the hand of Ittai, who was from Gath <note>Ittai was a Philistine loyalist from Gath who refused to leave David's side during the rebellion.</note>; and the king said to the people: "I will surely go out with you myself."
3 But the people answered: "You shall not go out: for if we flee, they will not care much about us; or if half of us fall, they will not care enough; because you alone are counted as ten thousand: it is better therefore that you stay in the city to provide us with help."
4 The king said to them: "Whatever seems right to you, I will do." So the king stood by the gate, and the people went out by their companies, by hundreds and by thousands.
5 And the king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying: "Keep the young man Absalom safe for my sake." And all the people heard the king commanding all the captains regarding Absalom.
6 So the people went out into the field against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
7 And the people of Israel were defeated there by David’s army, and a great slaughter occurred that day, of twenty thousand men.
8 The battle there was scattered over the face of the whole land, and the forest consumed many more of the people than the sword had devoured that day.
9 Now it happened that Absalom met the servants of David while riding on a mule: and as the mule went under the thick branches of a great oak, his head caught fast in the oak; and as he hung between heaven and earth, the mule he was riding on passed on.
10 Someone saw this and reported it to Joab, saying: "I saw Absalom hanging from an oak."
11 Joab said to the man who told him: "If you saw him, why did you not strike him to the ground? I would have given you ten silver shekels and a belt."
12 He said to Joab: "Even if you weighed out a thousand pieces of silver into my hands, I would never stretch out my hand against the king's son: for in our hearing the king commanded you, Abishai, and Ittai, saying: 'Guard the young man Absalom for my sake.'
13 Moreover, if I had acted boldly against my own life, nothing could have been hidden from the king, and would you have stood by me?"
14 Joab said: "I will not waste time as you wish, but I will attack him before you." He then took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom; and while he was still gasping, hanging in the oak,

<column-break/>

15 Ten young men who were Joab's armor-bearers ran and struck him, and killed him.
16 Then Joab blew the trumpet and held back the people, so they would not pursue the retreating Israelites, wishing to spare the multitude.
17 And they took Absalom and threw him into a great pit in the forest, and piled a very great heap of stones over him; and all Israel fled to their tents.
18 Now Absalom, while he was still alive, had set up a monument for himself in the King’s Valley; for he said: "I have no son, and this shall be a memorial to my name." And he called the monument by his own name, and it is called **Absalom’s Hand** to this day.
<note>original: "Manus Absalom." In Hebrew, the word for "hand" (Yad) is also used to mean a monument or memorial.</note>
19 Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said: "Let me run and bring news to the king, that the Lord has delivered judgment for him from the hand of his enemies."
20 But Joab said to him: "You shall not be a messenger this day, but you shall bring news on another day: today I do not want you to bring news, for the king's son is dead."
21 And Joab said to the Cushite: "Go and tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed to Joab and ran.
22 But Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said again to Joab: "What prevents me from also running after the Cushite?" Joab said to him: "Why do you want to run, my son? You will not be a bearer of good news."
23 He answered: "But what if I run anyway?" And he said to him: "Run." So Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain and passed the Cushite.
24 Now David was sitting between the two gates; and the watchman, who was on the roof of the gate upon the wall, lifted up his eyes and saw a man running alone.
25 He cried out and told the king; and the king said: "If he is alone, there is good news in his mouth." As he hurried and came closer,
26 The watchman saw another man running, and shouting from the roof, he said: "I see another man running alone." And the king said: "He also is a bearer of good news."
27 Then the watchman said: "I perceive the running of the first one is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok." And the king said: "He is a good man and comes with good news."
28 Ahimaaz cried out and said to the king: "Greetings, O King." And bowing before the king with his face to the ground, he said: "Blessed be the Lord your God, who has shut up the men who lifted their hands against my lord the king."
29 The king said: "Is the young man Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz said: "I saw a great tumult when your servant Joab sent me, your servant, O king; I know nothing else."
30 The king said to him: "Step aside and stand here." And when he had stepped aside and stood there,
31 The Cushite appeared, and coming, he said: "I bring good news, my lord king; for the Lord has judged for you today from the hand of all those who rose up against you."
32 The king said to the Cushite: "Is the young man Absalom safe?" To which the Cushite replied: "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up against him for evil, become like that young man."
33 The king was deeply moved, and he went up to the room over the gate and wept. And as he went, he spoke thus: "My son Absalom, Absalom my son! <margin>† Below 19:4.</margin> Who would grant that I might die for you, Absalom my son, my son Absalom?"

# CHAPTER XIX.

*David, moved by the words of Joab, ceases to mourn for Absalom and reconciles his conspirators to himself; he is led back to Jerusalem by the men of Judah and grants pardon to Shimei as he begs for mercy; he receives Mephibosheth, ordering him to divide the fields with Ziba; bidding farewell to Barzillai, he retains Chimham with him, while Israel and Judah contend sharply for David.*

---

1 It was reported to Joab that the king was weeping and mourning for his son.
2 And the victory that day was turned into mourning for all the people, for the people heard it said that day: "The king is grieving for his son."
3 And the people stole into the city that day, just as people who are shamed and fleeing from battle are accustomed to steal away.
4 Furthermore, the king covered his head and cried out with a loud voice: "My son Absalom, Absalom my son, my son!"
5 Then Joab entered the house to the king and said: "Today you have shamed the faces of all your servants who saved your life, and the lives of your sons and daughters, and the lives of your wives and concubines.
6 You love those who hate you, and you hate those who love you; and you have shown today that you do not care for your commanders or your servants. Truly I realize now that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, then you would be pleased.
7 Now therefore, rise up and go out, and speak to satisfy your servants; for I swear to you by the Lord that if you do not go out, not even one man will remain with you tonight. And this will be worse for you than all the evils that have come upon you from your youth until the present."
8 So the king rose and sat in the gate; and it was announced to all the people that the king was sitting in the gate. And the entire multitude came before the king, but Israel <note>Here, "Israel" refers to the tribes that had supported Absalom's rebellion.</note> fled to their own tents.
9 All the people throughout all the tribes of Israel were at odds, saying: "The king delivered us from the hand of our enemies; he saved us from the hand of the Philistines; and now he has fled the land because of Absalom.
10 But Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Why do you remain silent now about bringing the king back?"
11 Then King David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, saying: "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying: 'Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house?' (For the talk of all Israel had reached the king in his house.)
12 'You are my brothers, my own bone and my own flesh; why are you the last to bring back the king?'
13 And say to Amasa <note>Amasa was the commander of Absalom's rebel army; David offers him Joab's position as a political move to unify the kingdom.</note>: 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? May God do this to me, and more also, if you are not the commander of the army before me always in place of Joab.'"
14 And he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as if they were one man; and they sent word to the king, saying: "Return, you and all your servants."
15 So the king returned and came as far as the Jordan; and all Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and to escort him across the Jordan.

<column-break/>

<margin>† 1 Kings 1:8</margin> 16 Then Shimei the son of Gera, the son of Jemini from Bahurim, hurried and descended with the men of Judah to meet King David,
17 with a thousand men from Benjamin. Ziba, the servant of the house of Saul, was also there with his fifteen sons and twenty servants; and they rushed into the Jordan before the king.
18 They crossed the fords to escort the king's household and to do according to his command. But Shimei the son of Gera fell prostrate before the king as he was crossing the Jordan,
19 and said to him: "Do not hold me guilty, my lord, nor remember the wrongs of your servant on the day you, my lord king, went out from Jerusalem; do not take it to heart, O king.
20 For I, your servant, acknowledge my sin; and therefore, I have come today as the first of all the house of Joseph to descend and meet my lord the king."
21 But Abishai the son of Zeruiah <note>Abishai was Joab's brother and a fierce, often violent, supporter of David.</note> answered and said: "Should Shimei not be put to death for these words, because he cursed the Lord’s anointed?"
22 David said: "What is there between me and you, sons of Zeruiah? Why do you act as an adversary <note>original: "satan." In this context, it refers to a legal adversary or accuser rather than the spiritual entity.</note> to me today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Do I not know that today I have been made king over Israel?"
23 And the king said to Shimei: "You shall not die." And he swore an oath to him.
24 Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came down to meet the king; his feet were unwashed and his beard untrimmed, and he had not washed his clothes from the day the king departed until the day he returned in peace.
25 When he met the king at Jerusalem, the king said to him: "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"

### CHAPTER XX.

*Joab, along with his brother Abishai, pursues Sheba the son of Bichri, who stirred up a rebellion against David in Israel; he kills Amasa on the road, and finally departs from the siege of Abel once Sheba's head is thrown over the wall.*

Accidentally, there happened to be a man of Belial <note>A Hebrew idiom meaning a wicked or lawless person</note> there named Sheba <note>original: "Seba"</note>, the son of Bichri <note>original: "Bochri"</note>, a man of Benjamin. He blew the trumpet and said: "We have no part in David, nor any inheritance in the son of Jesse. Return to your tents, O Israel!"
2 And all Israel separated from David and followed Sheba, the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah stayed close to their king, from the Jordan all the way to Jerusalem.
3 When the king came to his house in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines whom he had left to guard the house and put them in confinement, providing them with food. But he did not go in to them; they were shut away until the day of their death, living as widows.
4 Then the king said to Amasa: "Call together all the men of Judah for me within three days, and be present here yourself."
5 So Amasa went to call Judah together, but he delayed beyond the time the king had appointed for him.
6 And David said to Abishai <note>original: "Abisai"</note>: "Now Sheba, the son of Bichri, will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your lord’s servants and pursue him, lest he find fortified cities and escape us."
7 So Joab's men went out with him, along with the

Cherethites <note>original: "Cerethi"</note> and the Pelethites <note>original: "Phelethi"</note>. All the mighty men went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba, the son of Bichri.
8 And when they were at the great stone in Gibeon <note>original: "Gabaan"</note>, Amasa came to meet them. Now Joab was wearing a tight tunic fitted to his stature, and over it he was girded with a sword in a scabbard hanging at his thigh; the sword was fashioned so that with a slight movement it could drop out and strike.

11 Meanwhile, one of Joab’s young men stood by Amasa’s body and said: "Whoever wishes to be for Joab and for David, let him follow Joab!"
12 But Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. When the man saw that all the people stopped to look at him, he moved Amasa from the road into a field and covered him with a garment, so that those passing by would not stop because of him.
13 Once he was moved from the road, every man went on, following Joab to pursue Sheba, the son of Bichri.

18 She spoke again: "In the old days, a proverb used to be said: 'Let those who have questions ask them in Abel,' and so matters were settled.

21 That is not the case. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, has lifted up his hand against King David. Hand him over alone, and we will depart from the city." And the woman said to Joab: "Behold, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall."
22 She then went to all the people and spoke to them with wisdom. They cut off the head of Sheba, the son of Bichri, and threw it to Joab. He blew the trumpet, and they withdrew from the city, every man to his tent. Joab then returned to Jerusalem to the king.

### CHAPTER XXI.

->*A three-year famine is sent because of Saul's injury to the Gibeonites. To stop it, at their request, David hands over the remaining family of Saul—except for Mephibosheth—to be executed. He then orders their bones, along with those of Saul and Jonathan, to be buried. Four wars of David against the Philistines are also recounted.*<-

1 A famine occurred in the days of David for three consecutive years, and David consulted the oracle of the Lord. And the Lord said: "It is because of Saul and his bloody house, because he killed the Gibeonites."

2 The king called the Gibeonites and spoke to them. (Now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but the remnants of the Amorites; the children of Israel had sworn an oath to them, but Saul sought to strike them down in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah.)
3 David said to the Gibeonites: "What shall I do for you? And what will be your atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of the Lord?"

And the king said: "I will give them."

### CHAPTER XXIII.

->The last words of David, and a catalog of his illustrious men.<-

1 Now these are the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said: The man said, who was appointed concerning the <term>christ</term> <note>anointed one</note> of the God of Jacob, the excellent psalmist of Israel:
2 The Spirit of the Lord has spoken through me, and his word through my tongue.
3 The God of Israel said to me, the Strong One of Israel spoke, the Ruler of men, the just ruler in the fear of God.
4 Like the light of the morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds that glitters, and like the grass that sprouts from the earth through rain.
5 Nor is my house so great before God, that he should enter into an eternal covenant with me, firm in all things and fortified. For all my salvation, and all my will: nor is there anything from it that does not sprout.
6 But transgressors shall all be plucked out like thorns: which are not taken up by hands.
7 And if anyone wishes to touch them, he shall be armed with iron and the wood of a spear, and they shall be burned with fire even unto nothing.
<margin>† 1 Chronicles 11:10.</margin>

13 Also, three who were leaders among the thirty had gone down before, and had come at the time of harvest to David in the cave of Adullam <note>original: "Odollam"</note>: and the camps of the Philistines were placed in the Valley of the Giants.

### C H A P T E R XXIV.

->*David, rebuked by the prophet Gad for numbering the people, chooses the three-day plague out of three offered punishments. While the plague rages among the people and 70,000 are slain, David prays to the Lord; and being advised by the prophet Gad, he builds an altar at the threshing floor of Areuna for a price, and the plague ceases.*<-

<margin>1 Chronicles 21:1</margin>
1 AND the anger of the Lord was again kindled against Israel, and he stirred up David among them, saying: "Go, number Israel and Judah."
2 And the king said to Joab, the general of his army: "Travel through all the tribes of Israel from Dan even to Beersheba, and number the people, so that I may know their number."
3 And Joab said to the king: "May the Lord your God add to your people, however many they are now, and increase them an hundredfold in the sight of my lord the king; but why does my lord the king want such a thing?"

7 They passed near the walls of Tyre, and all the land of the Hivites and Canaanites, and they came to the south of Judah in Beersheba.
8 And having surveyed the whole land, they returned to Jerusalem after nine months and twenty days.
9 So Joab gave the number of the census of the people to the king, and there were found in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men who could draw the sword; and in Judah five hundred thousand fighting men.
10 But David’s heart struck him after the people were numbered; and David said to the Lord: "I have sinned greatly in what I have done; but I pray you, O Lord, take away the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
11 Therefore David arose in the morning, and the word of the Lord came to the prophet Gad, David’s Seer, saying:
12 "Go, and say to David: Thus says the Lord: I give you the choice of three things; choose one of them which you will, that I may do it to you."
13 And when Gad had come to David, he told him, saying: "Either seven years of famine shall come to you in your land; or for three months you shall flee from your adversaries, and they shall pursue you; or surely for three days there shall be a pestilence in your land. Now therefore deliberate, and see what word I shall respond to him who sent me."
14 And David said to Gad: "I am in great distress; <margin>1 Chronicles 21:13</margin> but it is better that I fall into the hands of the Lord (for his mercies are many) than into the hands of men."

41 Now Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it just as their feast was ending. And Joab, hearing the sound of the trumpet, said: "What does the noise of the city in such an uproar mean?"

50 But Adonijah, fearing Solomon, rose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar. <note>The "horns" were the corners of the sacrificial altar. Taking hold of them was a traditional plea for sanctuary or divine protection.</note>

53 So King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and did reverence to King Solomon; and Solomon said to him: "Go to your house."

### CHAPTER V.

->Hiram grants woodcutters to Solomon for the building of the temple, to whom Solomon grants food: the number of woodcutters, those carrying burdens, stone-cutters, and their overseers.<-

Hiram the king of Tyre also sent his servants to Solomon: for he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father: because Hiram had been a friend of David at all times.
2 And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying:
3 You know the will of David my father, and that he could not build a house to the name of the Lord his God because of the wars pressing in on every side, until the Lord put them under the soles of his feet.
4 But now the Lord my God has given me rest on every side: and there is no adversary <note>original: "satan" — here meaning a political opponent or accuser</note>, nor evil occurrence.
5 Therefore I intend to build a temple to the name of the Lord my God, just as the Lord spoke to my father David, saying: † Your son, whom I will give in your place upon your throne, he shall build a house to my name.
<margin>† 2 Samuel 7:13; 1 Chronicles 22:10 <note>original: "2. Reg. 7. 13. 1. Par. 22. 10."</note></margin>
6 Command therefore that your servants cut for me cedars of Lebanon, and let my servants be with your servants: and I will give you the wages of your servants whatever you shall ask: for you know how there is not in my people a man who knows how to cut wood like the Sidonians.
7 So when Hiram had heard the words of Solomon, he rejoiced greatly and said: Blessed be the Lord God today, who has given David a most wise son over this very great people.
8 And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying: I have heard whatever you commanded me: I will do all your will regarding the cedar and fir wood.
9 My servants shall bring them down from Lebanon to the sea: and I will arrange them in rafts on the sea, as far as the place you indicate to me: and I will land them there, and you shall take them: and you shall provide my necessities, that food may be given to my house.

13 And King Solomon chose workmen out of all Israel, and the draft was thirty thousand men.
14 And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand every month by turns, so that for two months they were in their own houses: and Adoniram was in charge of this draft.
15 And Solomon had seventy thousand who carried burdens, and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains;
16 Besides the overseers who were over every work, numbering three thousand three hundred, who gave orders to the people and to those who did the work.

18 Which the masons of Solomon and the masons of Hiram did hew: and the <term>Gebalites<note>original: "Giblii"; these were inhabitants of the city of Gebal, also known as Byblos, famous for their skill in stonework and shipbuilding.</note></term> prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

## CHAPTER VI.

->The form and construction of the temple regarding its principal<-
->interior and exterior parts.<-

1 <margin>2 Chronicles 3:1.</margin> And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year, in the month of <term>Ziv<note>The second month of the Hebrew ecclesiastical calendar, occurring around April/May.</note></term> (which is the second month) of Solomon’s reign over Israel, that the house began to be built for the Lord.
2 Now the house which King Solomon built for the Lord had sixty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and thirty cubits in height.
3 And the portico was before the temple, twenty cubits in length, according to the measure of the breadth of the temple: and it had ten cubits of breadth before the face of the temple.
4 And he made slanted windows in the temple.
5 And upon the wall of the temple he built a structure of stories round about, in the walls of the house round about the temple and the <term>oracle<note>The inner sanctuary or "Holy of Holies," the most sacred part of the Temple.</note></term>, and he made side-chambers round about.
6 The story that was below was five cubits in breadth, and the middle story was six cubits in breadth, and the third story was seven cubits in breadth. And he placed beams in the house round about on the outside, so that they should not be fastened into the walls of the temple.
7 And when the house was being built, it was built of stones hewn and finished: so that hammer, and axe, and every iron tool were not heard in the house while it was being built.
8 The door for the middle side-chamber was in the right side of the house: and by winding stairs they went up into the middle chamber, and from the middle into the third.
9 And he built the house, and finished it: he also covered the house with ceilings of cedar.

<column-break/>

10 And he built a structure of stories over all the house, five cubits in height, and he covered the house with cedar wood.
11 And the word of the Lord came to Solomon, saying:
12 This house, which you are building—if you will walk in my precepts, and execute my judgments, and keep all my commandments, walking in them: I will fulfill my word to you, <margin>† 2 Samuel 7:16.</margin> which I spoke to David your father.
13 <margin>17.</margin> And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel, <margin>† 1 Chronicles 22:9.</margin> and I will not forsake my people Israel.
14 So Solomon built the house, and finished it.
15 And he built the walls of the house on the inside with cedar boards, from the floor of the house to the top of the walls, and even to the ceilings, he covered it with cedar wood on the inside: and he covered the floor of the house with planks of fir.
16 And he built a space of twenty cubits at the rear part of the temple with cedar boards, from the floor to the upper parts: and he made the inner house of the oracle into the Holy of Holies.
17 Now the temple itself, before the doors of the oracle, was forty cubits long.
18 And all the house was covered within with cedar, having its carvings and its joints skillfully made, and prominent engravings: all were covered with cedar boards; nor could any stone be seen at all in the wall.
19 And he prepared the oracle in the middle of the house, in the inner part, to set there the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
20 Now the oracle had twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits in height, and he covered it and overlaid it with the purest gold: and he also overlaid the altar with cedar.
21 He also covered the house before the oracle with the purest gold, and fastened the plates with golden nails.
22 And there was nothing in the temple that was not covered with gold: moreover, the whole altar of the oracle he covered with gold.
23 And he made in the oracle two <term>cherubim<note>Celestial winged beings that symbolized the presence of God; here, they serve as massive guardians over the Ark.</note></term> of olive wood, ten cubits high.
24 One wing of a cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub was five cubits: that is, they had ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other wing.
25 The second cherub was also ten cubits: in the same measure, and the work was the same in the two cherubim,
26 That is, one cherub had a height of ten cubits, and likewise the second cherub.
27 And he placed the cherubim in the midst of the inner temple: and the cherubim stretched forth their wings, and one wing touched the wall, and the wing of the second cherub touched the other wall: and the other wings in the middle part of the temple touched each other.
28 He also overlaid the cherubim with gold.
29 And all the walls of the temple round about he carved with various engravings and carvings: and he made in them cherubim, and palms, and various pictures, as if standing out and emerging from the wall.
30 Moreover, the floor of the house he overlaid with gold, both inside and out.
31 And at the entrance of the oracle he made little doors of olive wood, and doorposts of five angles.

### C H A P T E R VII.

->*The Palace of Solomon, the House of the Forest of Lebanon, and the house of his wife; the various and most sumptuous furnishings of the temple.*<-

<margin>† Below, 9:10.</margin>
1 And Solomon built his own house in thirteen years, and brought it to full perfection.
2 He built also the House of the Forest of Lebanon, being a hundred cubits long, and fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high: with four galleries between columns of cedar: for he had cut down cedar trees to make the columns.
3 And he covered the whole ceiling with cedar planks, which was supported by forty-five columns. One row had fifteen columns
4 Placed opposite one another,
5 And facing each other, with equal space between the columns, and above the columns were square beams, equal in every part.
6 And he made a porch of columns fifty cubits long, and thirty cubits wide: and another porch in front of the greater porch: and columns, and <term>epistyles<note>original: "epiphylia"; these are the horizontal beams or lintels that rest upon the tops of columns.</note></term> above the columns.
7 He also made the porch of the throne, where the judgment seat is, and covered it with cedar wood from the floor even to the top.
8 And the small house, in which he sat to judge, was in the middle of the porch, of similar workmanship.
<margin>† Above, 3:1.</margin>
He also made a house for the daughter of Pharaoh († whom Solomon had taken to wife) of such workmanship as this porch.
9 All these were made of costly stones, which were sawed to a certain rule and measure, both within and without: from the foundation even to the top of the walls, and on the outside even to the great court.
10 And the foundations were of costly stones, great stones of ten or eight cubits.
11 And above there were costly stones of equal measure, cut in the same way, and likewise of cedar.
12 And the great court was round, with three rows of cut stones, and one row of hewn cedar: just as in the inner court of the house of the Lord, and in the porch of the house.

15 And he cast two columns of brass, each column being eighteen cubits high:

and a line of twelve cubits went around both columns.

17 And there was a kind of network, and chains intertwined with one another with wonderful workmanship. Both capitals of the columns were cast: there were seven rows of lattices on one capital, and seven lattices on the other capital.
18 And he finished the columns, and two rows of lattices around each, to cover the capitals that were on the top of the pomegranates: and in the same way he made the second capital.
19 And the capitals that were upon the tops of the columns were worked like lilies in the porch, of four cubits.
20 And again, there were other capitals on the top of the columns above, according to the measure of the column, near the network: and there were two hundred rows of pomegranates around the second capital.
21 And he set up the two columns in the porch of the temple: and when he had set up the right column, he called its name <term>Jachin<note>The name means "He shall establish."</note></term>: likewise he set up the second column, and called its name <term>Boaz<note>The name means "In Him is strength."</note></term>.
22 And upon the tops of the columns he placed work in the form of lilies: and the work of the columns was finished.

### C H A P T E R VIII.

->*The Temple, with the Ark brought into it, is dedicated, while a cloud fills it. Solomon, after a long prayer, blesses the people: the number of oxen and sheep sacrificed at this celebrated festival.*<-

<margin>† 2 Chronicles 5:1.</margin>
Then all the elders of Israel were gathered together with the chiefs of the tribes, and the leaders of the families of the children of Israel, to King Solomon in Jerusalem: that they might bring the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord from the City of David, which is Zion.
2 And all Israel assembled before King Solomon in the month of <term>Ethanim<note>original: "Ethanim"; the seventh month of the Hebrew calendar (Sept/Oct), during which the Harvest Festival occurred.</note></term>, on the solemn feast day, which is the seventh month.
3 And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the Ark,

5 And King Solomon, and all the multitude of Israel that had assembled to him, walked with him before the Ark, and they sacrificed sheep and oxen without estimate or number.
6 And the priests brought the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord into its place, in the <term>oracle<note>original: "oraculum"; the inner sanctuary or Holy of Holies where God's presence was said to dwell.</note></term> of the temple, into the Holy of Holies, under the wings of the cherubim.
7 For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the Ark, and protected the Ark and its carrying-poles from above.

### C H A P T E R X.

*The Queen of Sheba comes to King Solomon: marveling at his wisdom, magnificence, and governance, she departs after giving and receiving grand gifts. Solomon receives much tribute and gold from elsewhere; he constructs magnificent vessels, shields, and a throne, and possesses much precious furniture in vessels, chariots, and horses, in an abundance of silver and cedars.*

<margin>† 2 Chronicles 9:1; Matthew 12:42; Luke 11:31</margin>
But when the Queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame in the name of the Lord, she came to test him with riddles.
2 And entering Jerusalem with a great train and riches, with camels carrying spices and exceedingly much gold and precious gems, she came to King Solomon and spoke to him of all that she had in her heart.
3 And Solomon answered all the questions she proposed: there was no word that could be hidden from the king, which he did not explain to her.
4 When the Queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house which he had built,
5 And the food of his table, and the dwellings of his servants, and the order of his ministers and their clothing, and the cupbearers, and the burnt offerings which he offered in the house of the Lord: she was breathless with wonder.
6 And she said to the king: "The report is true which I heard in my own land,
7 Concerning your words and your wisdom: and I did not believe those who told me until I came myself and saw with my own eyes. I have found that the half had not been told to me: your wisdom and your works are greater than the rumor I heard.
8 Blessed are your men, and blessed are your servants, who stand before you always and hear your wisdom.
9 Blessed be the Lord your God, who was pleased with you and placed you upon the throne of Israel, because the Lord has loved Israel 

<column-break/>

forever, and appointed you king to perform judgment and justice."

22 Because the king's fleet went by sea with the fleet of Hiram once every three years to Tarshish, bringing from there gold, and silver, and ivory <note>original: "dentes elephantorum" — literally 'elephant teeth'.</note>, and apes, and peacocks.
23 So King Solomon was magnified above all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

28 And horses were brought to Solomon out of Egypt and from Kue <note>original: "Coa" — a region in Cilicia (modern Turkey) known for horse breeding.</note>. For the king's merchants bought them from Kue and brought them at a fixed price.

## CHAPTER XI.

*Solomon is joined to many foreign women, and being infatuated by them, he turns to their idols: at which the Lord was angry and raised up adversaries against him, Hadad, Rezon, and Jeroboam; to whom, through the prophet Ahijah, he promises the kingdom of Israel, while one tribe is preserved for Solomon's son: Solomon dies after forty years of reign, and his son Rehoboam succeeds him.*

### CHAPTER XII.

The Lord also disperses Rehoboam's army against Jeroboam through the prophet Shemaiah. ### CHAPTER XIII.

->*A prophet sent from Judah to Jeroboam prophesies concerning the destruction of the altar and the birth of King Josiah; the hand of Jeroboam, which had withered, is restored to health; the returning prophet is killed by a lion because he was disobedient to the word of God; and Jeroboam increases his impiety.*<-

And behold, a man of God came from Judah 
by the word of the Lord to Bethel, while

### CHAPTER XIV.

*Ahijah the prophet, questioned by the wife of Jeroboam regarding their sick son Abijah, predicts that the son will die and that the house of Jeroboam will be utterly overthrown. When Jeroboam dies, his son Nadab succeeds him. Meanwhile, the King of Egypt plunders the house of the Lord in Jerusalem; upon the death of Rehoboam, his son Abijah succeeds him.*

AT that time, Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

2 And Jeroboam said to his wife: "Arise, and change your clothing so that you are not recognized as the wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh, where the prophet Ahijah <margin>† Above, 11:31.</margin> is, who told me that I would reign over this people.

3 Take also in your hand ten loaves of bread, and a cake, and a jar of honey, and go to him; for he will show you what will happen to this boy."

4 Jeroboam's wife did as he had said. She arose and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah; but he could not see, because his eyes had grown dim due to his old age.

5 And the Lord said to Ahijah: "Behold, the wife of Jeroboam enters to consult you regarding her son who is sick. You shall say such and such to her." Therefore, when she entered, she pretended to be someone else.

6 When Ahijah heard the sound of her feet coming through the door, he said: "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why do you pretend to be another? For I have been sent to you as a messenger of harsh news.

7 Go and tell Jeroboam: 'Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Because I exalted you from the midst of the people and made you a leader over my people Israel,

8 And I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you—yet you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, doing what was pleasing in my sight.

9 But you have done more evil than all who were before you, and you have made for yourself foreign and cast gods to provoke me to anger, and you have cast me behind your back.

10 Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon <margin>† Below, 15:29.</margin> the house of Jeroboam, and I will cut off from Jeroboam every male <note>original: "mingentem ad parietem," literally "one who urinates against a wall," a common biblical idiom for males.</note>, whether bond or free, in Israel. And I will sweep away the remnants of the house of Jeroboam, as dung is swept away until it is clean.

11 Those of Jeroboam’s house who die in the city, the dogs shall eat; and those who die in the field, the birds of the air shall devour; for the Lord has spoken.'

12 Therefore, arise and go to your house. And as your feet enter the city, the boy shall die.

13 And all Israel shall mourn for him and bury him;

<column-break/>

for he alone of Jeroboam's family shall be brought to a grave, because in him alone has some good thing been found by the Lord God of Israel in the house of Jeroboam.

14 Moreover, the Lord has appointed for himself a king over Israel who will strike down the house of Jeroboam in this day and in this time.

15 And the Lord God of Israel will strike Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water; and he will uproot Israel from this good land which he gave to their fathers, and he will scatter them beyond the river, because they have made for themselves groves <note>original: "lucos," referring to Asherah poles, cultic objects dedicated to a Canaanite goddess.</note> to provoke the Lord.

16 And the Lord will give up Israel because of the sins of Jeroboam, who sinned and made Israel to sin."

17 And so Jeroboam's wife arose and departed, and she came to Tirzah. And as she crossed the threshold of the house, the boy died.

18 And they buried him. And all Israel mourned for him according to the word of the Lord, which he spoke through the hand of his servant Ahijah the prophet.

19 But the rest of the acts of Jeroboam—how he fought and how he reigned—behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

20 And the days in which Jeroboam reigned were twenty-two years. And he slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.

21 Now <margin>† 2 Chronicles 12:13.</margin> Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in the city of Jerusalem, which the Lord chose from all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonitess.

22 And Judah did evil before the Lord, and they provoked him more than all their fathers had done with the sins they committed.

23 For they also built for themselves altars, and statues, and groves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

24 There were even effeminate <note>referring to male cult prostitutes who were part of the pagan religious practices.</note> people in the land, and they committed all the abominations of the nations which the Lord had destroyed before the face of the children of Israel.

25 And in the fifth year of King Rehoboam's reign, Shishak, the king of Egypt, came up against Jerusalem.

26 And he took away the treasures of the house of the Lord and the royal treasures; he plundered everything. He also took the golden shields which Solomon had made.

27 In their place, King Rehoboam made bronze shields <margin>† Above, 10:16.</margin> and committed them to the hands of the captains of the shield-bearers and those who kept watch before the door of the king's house.

28 And whenever the king entered the house of the Lord, those who had the duty of going before him would carry them, and later they would bring them back to the armory of the shield-bearers.

29 But the rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.

30 And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.

31 And Rehoboam slept with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonitess. And Abijah his son reigned in his place.

# CHAPTER XV.

*The pious son Asa succeeds the wicked King Abijam of Judah; he fights against Baasha, the king of Israel, having obtained help from Ben-hadad, the king of Syria. Upon his death, Asa is succeeded by his son Jehoshaphat. Meanwhile, Baasha kills Nadab, the son of Jeroboam, along with his entire family, and reigns over Israel for twenty-four years—one wicked ruler following another.*

1 Therefore, in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, Abijam began his reign over Judah.

4 Nevertheless, for David's sake, the Lord his God gave him a lamp <note>In this context, a "lamp" refers to a successor or an enduring dynasty to keep the light of David’s line burning.</note> in Jerusalem, that He might raise up his son after him and establish Jerusalem.

In the Latin Vulgate, this refers to the worship of a fertility idol, usually identified with the goddess Asherah in the Hebrew text.</note> and in her grove which she had consecrated; he overturned her grotto, broke the most shameful idol into pieces, and burned it at the brook Kidron.

### CHAPTER XVIII.

*As the famine increases, Elijah meets Obadiah, who is seeking grass for the cattle; he with difficulty persuades Obadiah to announce his presence to Ahab. Elijah is then confronted by Ahab: out of zeal for God, Elijah orders the 850 false prophets to be slain, after fire is given from heaven to consume the burnt offering, and he obtains rain from God.*

1 After many days, the word of the Lord came to Elijah, in the third year, saying:

<column-break/>

Go, and show yourself to Ahab, that I may give rain upon the face of the earth.
2 Elijah went therefore to show himself to Ahab: and there was a grievous famine in Samaria.
3 And Ahab called Obadiah <note>original: "Abdiam"</note>, the steward of his house: now Obadiah feared the Lord greatly.
4 For when Jezebel killed the prophets of the Lord, he took a hundred prophets, and hid them by fifties in caves, and fed them with bread and water.
5 Ahab said then to Obadiah: Go into the land, to all the fountains of waters, and into all the valleys, if perhaps we may find grass to save the horses and mules, that the beasts may not utterly perish.
6 And they divided the countries between them, that they might go round about them: Ahab went one way, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
7 And as Obadiah was on the way, Elijah met him: and when he knew him, he fell on his face, and said: Are you my lord Elijah?
8 He answered: I am. Go, and tell your lord: Elijah is here.
9 And he said: What have I sinned, that you would deliver me your servant into the hand of Ahab, to kill me?
10 As the Lord your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you: and when they all answered: He is not here; he took an oath of every kingdom and nation, because you were not found.
11 And now you say to me: Go, and tell your lord: Elijah is here.
12 And when I am gone from you, the Spirit of the Lord will carry you into a place that I know not: and I shall go in and tell Ahab, and he, not finding you, will kill me: but your servant has feared the Lord from his infancy.
13 Has it not been told to you, my lord, what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of the Lord, how I hid a hundred men of the prophets of the Lord, by fifties in caves, and fed them with bread and water?
14 And now you say: Go, and tell your lord: Elijah is here: that he may kill me?
15 Elijah said: As the Lord of hosts lives, before whose face I stand, this day I will show myself to him.
16 Obadiah therefore went to meet Ahab, and told him: and Ahab came to meet Elijah.
17 And when he had seen him, he said: Are you he that troubles Israel?
18 And he said: I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father’s house, you who have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and have followed the Baals <note>original: "Baalim," the plural form of the pagan god Baal</note>.
19 Nevertheless, send now, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal, and the four hundred prophets of the groves <note>original: "prophetas lucorum," likely referring to the prophets of Asherah</note>, who eat at Jezebel's table.
20 Ahab sent to all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together unto mount Carmel.
21 And Elijah coming to all the people, said: How long do you halt between two sides? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people did not answer him a word.
22 And Elijah said again to the people: I only remain a prophet of the Lord: but the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men.

### CHAPTER XXI.

*Naboth, having denied his vineyard to King Ahab, is accused by false witnesses at Jezebel’s command and is stoned; this being done, Elijah threatens Ahab with many evils as he hastens to occupy the vineyard, though Ahab avoids these by humbling himself.*

After these words, at that time, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, next to the palace of Ahab, king of Samaria.

2 Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying: "Give me your vineyard, so that I may make a vegetable garden of it, because it is nearby and close to my house; and I will give you a better vineyard for it. Or, if it seems more convenient to you, I will give you the price in silver for what it is worth."

3 Naboth answered him: "The Lord be merciful to me, that I should not give the inheritance of my fathers to you." <note>Under Mosaic law, ancestral land was considered a sacred trust that was not to be sold permanently.</note>

4 Ahab came into his house indignant and gnashing his teeth at the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, saying: "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." And casting himself upon his bed, he turned his face to the wall and would eat no bread.

5 But Jezebel his wife came in to him and said: "What is this, that your soul is so grieved, and why do you eat no bread?"

6 He answered her: "I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him: 'Give me your vineyard for money, or if it pleases you, I will give you a better vineyard for it.' And he said: 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"

7 Then Jezebel his wife said to him: "You are of great authority, and you govern the kingdom of Israel well. Arise and eat bread, and be of good cheer; I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."

8 So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name and sealed them with his ring, and sent them to the elders and the leading men who were in his city and dwelt with Naboth.

9 And this was the substance of the letters: "Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth among the chief of the people,

10 And bring in two men, sons of Belial <note>original: "filios Belial" — a Hebrew idiom for wicked, lawless, or worthless men.</note> against him, and let them bear false witness, saying: 'He has cursed God and the king.' Then lead him out and stone him, and so let him die."

11 The citizens, the elders, and the leading men who dwelt with him in the city did as Jezebel had commanded them, and as it was written in the letters she had sent to them.

12 They proclaimed a fast and set Naboth among the chief of the people.
