5 And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: "As I am, so are you; my people and your people are one, and my horsemen are your horsemen." And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: "Inquire, I pray you, for the word of the Lord today."
6 Therefore, the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said to them: "Should I go to Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or should I remain still?" And they replied: "Go up, and the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king."
7 But Jehoshaphat said: "Is there not here some other prophet of the Lord, so that we might inquire through him?"
8 And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat: "There remains one man through whom we can inquire of the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good for me, but evil: Micaiah the son of Imlah." To which Jehoshaphat said: "Let not the king say such things."
9 The king of Israel therefore called a certain eunuch and said to him: "Hurry and bring Micaiah the son of Imlah."
10 Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah each sat on his throne, dressed in royal robes, in a courtyard near the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying in their presence.
11 Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah also made for himself horns of iron and said: "Thus says the Lord: With these you shall gore Syria until you have destroyed it."
12 And all the prophets prophesied similarly, saying: "Go up to Ramoth-Gilead and go prosperously, and the Lord will deliver it into the king's hands."
13 But the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying: "Behold, the words of the prophets with one voice predict good things for the king; let your word, therefore, be like theirs, and speak good things."
14 Micaiah said to him: "As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, that I will speak."
15 So he came to the king, and the king said to him: "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-Gilead to battle, or should we stop?" And he answered him: "Go up and go prosperously, and the Lord will deliver it into the king's hands." <note>Micaiah likely spoke this with a sarcastic tone, mimicking the false prophets before giving his true vision.</note>

17 And he said: "I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And the Lord said: 'These have no master; let each one return to his house in peace.'"

# THE BOOK OF KINGS

### ACCORDING TO THE HEBREWS
# THE SECOND BOOK OF KINGS. <note>original: "Malachim Secundus." *Malachim* is the Hebrew word for "Kings." In the tradition of the Latin Vulgate used here, the books of Samuel and Kings were numbered together as 1, 2, 3, and 4 Kings.</note>

### CHAPTER ONE.

<margin>
Ahaziah, king of Israel, wishing to consult Beelzebub about his illness, is rebuked by Elijah and prophesied to die: two captains of fifty sent to Elijah are devoured by heavenly fire along with their soldiers; the third captain is saved by his own humility, and Elijah descends with him to Ahaziah: who, upon dying, is succeeded by his brother Joram.
</margin>

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'P' containing a figure of a man.</image-desc>
1 Now Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.
2 And Ahaziah <note>Latin: "Ochozias"</note> fell through the lattice of his upper chamber which he had in Samaria, and was injured. He sent messengers, saying to them: "Go, consult Beelzebub, the god of Ekron <note>Latin: "Accaron"</note>, to see whether I might recover from this illness of mine."
3 But the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, saying: "Arise, and go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and you shall say to them: Is there no God in Israel, that you go to consult Beelzebub, the god of Ekron?
4 Therefore, thus says the Lord: From the bed onto which you have climbed, you shall not come down, but you shall surely die." And Elijah went his way.
5 And the messengers returned to Ahaziah. He said to them: "Why have you returned?"
6 But they answered him: "A man met us and said to us: 'Go, and return to the king who sent you, and you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord: Is it because there was no God in Israel that you send to consult Beelzebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore, from the bed onto which you have climbed, you shall not come down, but you shall surely die.'"
7 And he said to them: "What was the appearance and dress of that man who met you and spoke these words?"
8 And they said: "A hairy man, and girt with a leather belt <note>original: "zona pellicea"</note> around his waist." And he said: "It is Elijah the Tishbite."
9 And he sent to him a captain of fifty, and the fifty men who were under him. He went up to him, and as he was sitting on the top of a hill, he said: "Man of God, the king has commanded that you come down."
10 And Elijah, answering, said to the captain of fifty: "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty." Therefore, fire came down from heaven and devoured him and the fifty who were with him.
11 And again he sent to him another captain of fifty, and fifty with him. He spoke to him: "Man of God, thus says the king: Hurry, come down."

<column-break/>

12 Answering, Elijah said: "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty." Therefore, fire came down from heaven and devoured him and his fifty.
13 Again he sent a third captain of fifty, and the fifty who were with him. When he had come, he fell on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him, saying: "Man of God, do not despise my life, nor the lives of your servants who are with me.
14 Behold, fire came down from heaven and devoured the first two captains of fifty and the fifties who were with them; but now I beseech you to have mercy on my life."
15 And the angel of the Lord spoke to Elijah, saying: "Go down with him, do not be afraid." Therefore he arose and went down with him to the king,
16 and spoke to him: "Thus says the Lord: Because you sent messengers to consult Beelzebub, the god of Ekron, as if there were no God in Israel from whom you could ask for a word, therefore from the bed onto which you have climbed, you shall not come down, but you shall surely die."
17 So he died according to the word of the Lord which Elijah had spoken, and Joram his brother reigned in his place, in the second year of Jehoram <note>Latin: "Joram"</note> the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah; for he had no son.
18 Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?

### CHAPTER TWO.

<margin>
Elisha, the inseparable companion of Elijah, crosses the Jordan with him after the water is divided by Elijah’s cloak: Elijah having been taken up into heaven in a chariot of fire, Elisha receives his double spirit, and again divides the waters of the Jordan with Elijah’s cloak and crosses on dry land. Elijah is sought but not found: the water of Jericho and the barrenness of the land are healed by salt cast by Elisha; forty-two boys mocking Elisha are torn apart by bears.
</margin>

2 And Elijah said to Elisha: "Stay here, for the Lord has sent me as far as Bethel." But Elisha said to him: "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." And when they had gone down to Bethel,
3 the sons of the prophets who were in Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him: "Do you know that today the Lord will take your master away from you?" And he answered: "I also know it; be silent."

4 And Elijah <note>Latin: *Elias*</note> said to Elisha <note>Latin: *Eliseus*</note>: "Stay here, for the Lord has sent me to Jericho." And he replied: "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." And when they had come to Jericho,
5 The sons of the prophets <note>A term for a community or school of prophets who studied under a master like Elijah.</note> who were in Jericho approached Elisha and said to him: "Do you know that today the Lord will take your master away from you?" And he said: "I also know it; be silent."
6 And Elijah said to him: "Stay here, for the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan." And he said: "As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they both went on together.
7 And fifty men of the sons of the prophets followed them and stood at a distance, facing them; but the two of them stood by the Jordan.
8 And Elijah took his mantle, and rolled it up, and struck the waters, which were divided to each side; and they both crossed over on dry ground.
9 And when they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha: "Ask what you wish me to do for you, before I am taken from you." And Elisha said: "I beseech you, let a double portion of your spirit <note>This refers to the legal right of a firstborn son to inherit a double share of his father's estate, marking Elisha as Elijah's primary successor.</note> be upon me."
10 He answered: "You have asked a difficult thing; nevertheless, if you see me when I am taken from you, you shall have what you asked; but if you do not see me, it shall not be."
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 48:13; 1 Maccabees 2:58.</margin>
11 And as they went on, walking and talking together, behold, a fiery chariot and fiery horses separated the two of them: and Elijah ascended by a whirlwind into heaven.
12 And Elisha saw it, and cried out: "My father, my father! The chariot of Israel and its driver!" And he saw him no more: and he took hold of his own clothes and tore them into two pieces.
13 And he took up the mantle of Elijah, which had fallen from him; and returning, he stood upon the bank of the Jordan,
14 And with the mantle of Elijah, which had fallen from him, he struck the waters, and they were not divided; and he said: "Where is the God of Elijah even now?" And he struck the waters again, and they were divided here and there, and Elisha crossed over.
15 And the sons of the prophets, who were at Jericho opposite him, seeing this, said: "The spirit of Elijah has rested upon Elisha." And coming to meet him, they bowed down to the ground before him,
16 And they said to him: "Behold, there are fifty strong men with your servants who can go and search for your master, lest perhaps the spirit of the Lord has taken him and cast him upon one of the mountains, or into one of the valleys." And he said: "Do not send them."
17 But they urged him until he yielded and said: "Send them." And they sent fifty men; who, when they had searched for three days, did not find him.
18 And they returned to him while he stayed in Jericho; and he said to them: "Did I not say to you: Do not send?"
19 And the men of the city said to Elisha: "Behold, the situation of this city is very good, as you yourself, lord, can see; but the waters are very bad, and the land is barren."
20 And he said: "Bring me a new vessel, and put salt in it." And when they had brought it,
21 He went out to the spring of the waters and cast the salt into it, and said: "Thus says the Lord: I have healed

<column-break/>

these waters, and there shall no longer be death or barrenness in them."
22 And the waters were healed even to this day, according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.
23 And he went up from there to Bethel; and as he was going up by the way, little boys <note>The Latin *pueri parvi* can mean children, but in this context, it often refers to young men or youths from the city mocking the prophet's authority.</note> came out of the city and mocked him, saying: "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"
24 And when he looked back, he saw them and cursed them in the name of the Lord: and two bears came out of the forest and mauled forty-two of the boys.
25 And from there he went to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

### CHAPTER III.

->*On account of the king of Moab breaking the treaty he had with the king of Israel, the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom march against him; when they were nearly killed by thirst, the Lord, through Elisha, promises water without rain, and victory over the king of Moab, who, by sacrificing his firstborn, prevents the destruction of the city.*<-

1 Now Joram the son of Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat <note>Latin: *Josaphat*</note> king of Judah. And he reigned twelve years.
2 And he did evil before the Lord, but not like his father and mother: for he removed the statues of Baal which his father had made.
3 Nevertheless, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat <note>Latin: *Nabat*</note>, who made Israel to sin, and he did not depart from them.
4 Now Mesha <note>Latin: *Mesa*</note> king of Moab raised many sheep, and he paid to the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and one hundred thousand rams, with their wool.
5 But when Ahab was dead, he broke the treaty which he had with the king of Israel.
6 Therefore King Joram went out on that day from Samaria and mustered all Israel.
7 And he sent to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying: "The king of Moab has revolted from me; come with me against him to battle." He answered: "I will go up: he who is mine is yours: my people are your people, and my horses are your horses."
8 And he said: "By which way shall we go up?" And he answered: "Through the desert of Edom <note>Latin: *Idumææ*</note>."
9 So the king of Israel, and the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out, and they marched for seven days, and there was no water for the army or for the pack animals that followed them.
10 And the king of Israel said: "Alas, alas, alas! The Lord has gathered us three kings together to deliver us into the hands of Moab."
11 But Jehoshaphat said: "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, so that we may pray to the Lord through him?" And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered: "Elisha the son of Shaphat <note>Latin: *Saphat*</note> is here, who used to pour water on the hands of Elijah." <note>An idiom meaning he was Elijah’s personal attendant or disciple.</note>
12 And Jehoshaphat said: "The word of the Lord is with him." And the king of Israel, and Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and the king of Edom went down to him.
13 And Elisha said to the king of Israel: "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and your mother." And the king of Israel said to him: "Why has the Lord gathered these three kings together to deliver them into the hands of Moab?"

### C H A P T E R IV.

*Elisha obtains oil for a widow oppressed by debts, with which she may pay her creditors; for the Shunammite woman, his hostess, he obtains a son, whom he later raises after death; also, by casting flour into a pot, he removes its bitterness, and with a few loaves he satisfies many.*

1 Now a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying: "Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant was one who feared the Lord; and behold, the creditor has come to take my two sons to serve him as slaves."
2 And Elisha said to her: "What do you wish for me to do for you? Tell me, what do you have in your house?"

<column-break/>

But she answered: "I, your handmaid, have nothing in my house except a little oil, with which I may be anointed."
3 And he said to her: "Go, borrow empty vessels from all your neighbors, and not a few."
4 "And go in, and shut your door, when you and your sons are inside; and pour from it into all these vessels; and when they are full, set them aside."
5 So the woman went and shut the door upon herself and upon her sons; they brought the vessels to her, and she poured.
6 And when the vessels were full, she said to her son: "Bring me another vessel." And he answered: "I have no more." Then the oil stopped flowing.
7 And she came and told the man of God. And he said: "Go, sell the oil, and pay your creditor; and you and your sons live on the rest."
8 And it happened on a certain day that Elisha passed through Shunem; and there was a great woman there <note>A "great woman" usually indicates one of high social status or wealth.</note>, who persuaded him to eat bread; and as he frequently passed that way, he would turn aside to her house to eat bread.
9 And she said to her husband: "I perceive that this is a holy man of God, who passes by us frequently."
10 "Let us therefore make for him a small upper room, and let us put in it for him a bed, and a table, and a chair, and a candlestick, so that when he comes to us, he may stay there."
11 And so it happened one day that he came and turned into the upper room, and rested there.
12 And he said to Gehazi his servant: "Call this Shunammite." And when he had called her, and she stood before him,
13 He said to his servant: "Say to her: Behold, you have been diligent in serving us in all things; what do you wish for me to do for you? Do you have any business, and do you wish me to speak to the king, or to the commander of the army?" And she answered: "I dwell in the midst of my own people."
14 And he said: "What then does she want me to do for her?" And Gehazi said: "Do not ask; for she has no son, and her husband is old."
15 So he commanded him to call her; and when she had been called and stood before the door,
16 He said to her: "At this time, and in this same hour, if life be a companion <note>A Hebrew idiom meaning "at this time next year."</note>, you shall have a son in your womb." But she answered: "Do not, I beseech you, my lord, man of God, do not lie to your handmaid."
17 And the woman conceived, and bore a son, at the time and in the same hour that Elisha had said.
18 And the boy grew. And on a certain day, when he had gone out to his father, to the reapers,
19 He said to his father: "My head hurts, my head hurts!" But he said to a servant: "Take him and lead him to his mother."
20 And when he had taken him and led him to his mother, she set him upon her knees until noon, and he died.
21 And she went up and laid him upon the bed of the man of God, and shut the door; and going out,
22 She called her husband, and said: "Send with me, I pray you, one of the servants and a donkey, that I may run to the man of God and return."
23 And he said to her: "Why are you going to him? Today is neither the New Moon <note>original: "Calendæ."</note> nor the Sabbath." And she answered: "I will go."

28 Then she said to him: "Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say to you: Do not deceive me?"

31 Now Gehazi had gone on before them and had laid the staff upon the face of the boy, but there was neither voice nor sense. He went back to meet Elisha and told him, saying: "The boy has not awakened."

32 So Elisha entered the house, and behold, the boy lay dead upon his bed.

33 He went in and shut the door upon himself and the boy, and prayed to the Lord.

34 And he went up and lay upon the boy; he put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands. He stretched himself over him, and the flesh of the child grew warm.

35 Then he returned and walked once to and fro in the house; then he went up and stretched himself over him again. And the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

36 Then Elisha called Gehazi and said to him: "Call this Shunammite woman." And she was called and came in to him. He said: "Take up your son."

37 She came and fell at his feet, bowing to the ground; then she took up her son and went out.

38 And Elisha returned to Gilgal. Now there was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets <note>term: "sons of the prophets" refers to a community or school of prophets living and studying together under a master like Elisha.</note> were sitting before him. He said to one of his servants: "Set on the large pot and cook pottage for the sons of the prophets."

39 And one went out into the field to gather wild herbs, and he found a sort of wild vine and gathered from it wild gourds <note>original: "colocynthidas." These are bitter, vine-growing fruits, often toxic if not prepared correctly.</note>, filling his cloak. He returned and sliced them into the pot of pottage, for he did not know what they were.

40 Then they poured it out for the men to eat. But as they were eating the pottage, they cried out, saying: "There is death in the pot, O man of God!" And they could not eat it.

41 But he said: "Bring some flour." And when they had brought it, he cast it into the pot and said: "Pour it out for the people, that they may eat." And there was no longer any bitterness in the pot.

42 A certain man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing the man of God bread of the firstfruits: twenty

barley loaves and fresh grain in his sack. And Elisha said: "Give it to the people, that they may eat."

43 And his servant answered him: "How much is this, that I should set it before a hundred men?" He said again: "Give it to the people, that they may eat; for thus says the Lord: They shall eat, and there shall be some left over."

44 So he set it before them; and they ate, and there was some left over, according to the word of the Lord.

### CHAPTER V.

*The king of Israel tore his clothes because the king of Syria had commanded that he cure Naaman the leper; Elisha cleanses Naaman of his leprosy by a sevenfold washing in the Jordan; meanwhile, Gehazi is afflicted with the leprosy because he deceitfully extorted gifts that Elisha had refused.*

Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master and highly respected, because by him the Lord had given victory to Syria. He was a valiant man and wealthy, but he was a leper.

2 Now raiding parties had gone out from Syria and had led away captive from the land of Israel a little girl, who waited upon Naaman's wife.

3 And she said to her mistress: "I wish my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria; he would surely cure him of the leprosy which he has."

4 So Naaman went in to his lord and told him, saying: "Thus and so spoke the girl from the land of Israel."

5 And the king of Syria said to him: "Go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." And when he had set out, he took with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of clothing.

6 And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, which said: "When you receive this letter, know that I have sent Naaman my servant to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy."

7 And when the king of Israel had read the letter, he tore his clothes and said: "Am I God, that I can kill and give life, that this man sends to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Take note and see how he seeks an excuse against me."

8 But when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to him, saying: "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel."

9 So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha’s house.

10 And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying: "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh shall be restored to health, and you shall be clean."

11 But Naaman was angry and went away, saying: "I thought that he would surely come out to me, and stand and call upon the name of the Lord his God, and touch the place of the leprosy with his hand, and heal me."

12 "Are not the Abana and Pharphar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and went away in a rage.

13 But his servants came near and spoke to him: "Father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, surely you would have done it. How much more, then, when he says to you: Wash, and you shall be clean?"

### CHAPTER VI.

->Elisha makes the iron of the axe swim; the soldiers of the king of Syria are led as if blinded into Samaria by Elisha, whom they were trying to capture because he revealed the secrets of their king to the king of Israel; and afterward, while the Syrians are besieging Samaria, mothers eat their own sons because of the famine, for which Elisha is ordered by the king to be killed.<-

1 Now the sons of the prophets <note>A community of disciples or students following Elisha's leadership.</note> said to Elisha: "Behold, the place where we live before you is too cramped for us."
2 "Let us go as far as the Jordan, and let each of us take a single beam from the woods, so that we may build ourselves a place to live there." And he said: "Go."
3 And one of them said: "Come then, and you also go with your servants." He answered: "I will come."
4 And he went with them. And when they had come to the Jordan, they began to cut wood.
5 But it happened that as one was cutting down a beam, the iron of the axe fell into the water; and he cried out and said: "Alas, alas, alas, my lord! and this very thing I had borrowed!"
6 But the man of God said: "Where did it fall?" And he showed him the place. Then he cut a piece of wood and threw it there; and the iron floated.
7 And he said: "Pick it up." And he stretched out his hand and took it.
8 Now the king of Syria was at war against Israel, and he took counsel with his servants, saying: "In such and such a place let us lay an ambush."
9 Therefore the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying: "Beware that you do not pass by that place, for the Syrians are there in ambush."
10 The king of Israel then sent to the place which the man of God had told him, and occupied it beforehand, and protected himself there not once or twice.
11 And the heart of the king of Syria was troubled because of this thing; and having called his servants, he said: "Why do you not show me who among you is the traitor to the king of Israel?"
12 And one of his servants said: "By no means, my lord king; but Elisha the prophet, who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel all the words that you speak in your private chamber."
13 And he said to them: "Go and see where he is, so that I may send and capture him." And they reported to him, saying: "Behold, he is in Dothan."
14 Therefore he sent horses and chariots there, and the strength of an army; and when they had come by night, they surrounded the city.
15 And the servant of the man of God, rising early, went out and saw the army surrounding the city, with horses and chariots; and he told him, saying: "Alas, alas, alas, my lord! what shall we do?"
16 But he answered: "Do not fear; for there are more with us than there are with them."
17 And when Elisha had prayed, he said: "Lord, open the eyes of this man, that he may see." And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw: and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
18 Indeed, the enemies came down to him; but Elisha prayed to the Lord, saying: "Strike, I beseech you, this people with blindness." And the Lord struck them so they could not see, according to the word of Elisha.

2 Then one of the captains, on whose hand the king leaned, answering the man of God, said: "Even if the Lord should make floodgates in heaven, could that which you speak possibly happen?" Elisha said: "You shall see it with your eyes, but you shall not eat of it."
3 Now there were four leprous men at the entering in of the gate: and they said to one another: "Why are we sitting here until we die?
4 If we choose to enter the city, we shall die of famine; if we stay here, we must also die. Come, therefore, and let us desert to the camp of Syria. If they spare us, we shall live; but if they choose to kill us, we shall die regardless."
5 So they arose in the evening to go to the Syrian camp. And when they had come to the edge of the Syrian camp, they found no one there.
6 For the Lord had caused a sound to be heard in the camp of Syria, of chariots, and horses, and a very great army: and they said to one another: "Behold, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and of the Egyptians, and they are coming upon us."
7 Therefore they arose and fled in the dark, and left behind their tents, and their horses and donkeys in the camp, and fled, seeking only to save their own lives.
8 So when those lepers came to the edge of the camp, they entered one tent, and ate and drank; and they took from there silver and gold and clothing, and went and hid it. And they returned again to another tent, and taking things from there in the same way, they hid them.
9 Then they said to one another: "We are not doing right: for this is a day of good news. If we keep silent and will not tell it until morning, we shall be charged with a crime: come, let us go and report it in the king's court."
10 And when they had come to the gate of the city, they told them, saying: "We went to the camp of Syria, and we found no man there, but only horses and donkeys tied, and the tents standing."
11 Then the gatekeepers went and reported it inside the king's palace.
12 And the king arose in the night and said to his servants: "I will tell you what the Syrians have done to us. 16 And the people went out and plundered the camp of Syria: and a measure of fine flour was sold for a stater, and two measures of barley for a stater, according to the word of the Lord.

# CHAPTER VIII.

*After the seven-year famine predicted by Elisha, the Shunammite woman, who had traveled abroad on his advice, returns and recovers her fields and their produce; Elisha predicts that the sick Ben-hadad will die and that the wicked Hazael will reign; Joram, king of Judah, struck the Edomites because they had revolted from him; he is succeeded by his wicked son Ahaziah.*

<margin>See chapter 4, verse 35.</margin>
1 Now Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying: "Arise, go, you and your household, and travel wherever you can find a place to stay; for the Lord has called for a famine, and it shall come upon the land for seven years."
2 She arose and did according to the word of the man of God; and going with her household, she lived in the land of the Philistines for many days.
3 And when the seven years were finished, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines; and she went forth to petition the king for her house and for her fields.
4 Now the king was speaking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying: "Tell me all the great things that Elisha has done."
5 And while he was telling the king how Elisha had raised the dead to life, the woman whose son he had restored to life appeared, crying out to the king for her house and for her fields. And Gehazi said: "My lord king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life."
6 And the king questioned the woman, and she told him the story. Then the king assigned her an official, saying: "Restore to her everything that was hers, and all the produce of the fields from the day she left the land until the present."
7 Elisha also came to Damascus while Ben-hadad, the king of Syria, was sick; and they told the king, saying: "The man of God has come here."
8 And the king said to Hazael: "Take gifts with you and go to meet the man of God, and consult the Lord through him, saying: 'Shall I be able to recover from this illness?'"
9 So Hazael went to meet him, taking with him gifts and all the good things of Damascus—forty camels' worth of burdens. And when he stood before him, he said: "Your son Ben-hadad, king of Syria, has sent me to you, saying: 'Shall I be able to be healed from this illness?'"
10 And Elisha said to him: "Go, tell him: 'You shall be healed'; however, the Lord has shown me that he shall surely die."
11 And Elisha stood with him and was troubled, even to the point of blushing <note>original: "suffusionem vultus"; a reddening or embarrassment of the face</note>; and the man of God wept.
12 And Hazael said: "Why does my lord weep?" And he said: "Because I know the evils you will do

<column-break/>

to the children of Israel. Their fortified cities you will set on fire, and their young men you will kill with the sword, and their little ones you will dash to pieces, and their pregnant women you will rip open."
13 And Hazael said: "But what am I, your servant—a dog—that I should do such a great thing?" And Elisha said: "The Lord has shown me that you shall be king over Syria."
14 And when he had departed from Elisha, he came to his master, who said to him: "What did Elisha say to you?" And he answered: "He told me: 'You shall receive your health.'"
15 But when the next day came, he took a thick cloth, soaked it in water, and spread it over the king's face; and when he was dead, Hazael reigned in his place.
16 In the fifth year of Joram, son of Ahab, king of Israel, and of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, Joram the son of Jehoshaphat began to reign as king of Judah.

22 So Edom revolted from being under Judah to this day. Then Libnah also revolted at that time.

### CHAPTER X.

-> Jehu orders the seventy sons of Ahab and the forty-two brothers of Ahaziah to be killed; he wipes out the entire lineage of Ahab and craftily assembles and slaughters all the priests of Baal, burning his statue and turning his temple into a latrine; nevertheless, Jehu continues in the worship of the golden calves, and for this reason, Israel is violently struck by Hazael; Jehu dies and is succeeded by his son Jehoahaz. <-

1 Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of the city, to the elders, and to those who raised Ahab's children, saying:
2 "As soon as you receive this letter—since you have your master’s sons with you, and you have chariots, horses, fortified cities, and weapons—
3 choose the best and most fit of your master’s sons, place him on his father’s throne, and fight for your master’s house."
4 But they were terrified beyond measure and said: "Look, two kings could not stand before him; how then shall we be able to resist?"
5 Therefore, the supervisors of the palace, the governors of the city, the elders, and the guardians sent word to Jehu, saying: "We are your servants; we will do whatever you command us. We will not appoint a king; do whatever pleases you."
6 He wrote them a second letter, saying: "If you are on my side and will obey me, take the heads of your master’s sons and come to me at Jezreel by this same hour tomorrow." Now the king's sons, seventy men, were being raised by the leading men of the city.
7 When the letter reached them, they took the king's sons and slaughtered the seventy men; they put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
8 A messenger came and told him: "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." He replied: "Pile them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
9 When morning came, he went out, stood there, and said to all the people: "You are innocent. If I conspired against my master and killed him, who then struck down all of these?
<margin>1 Kings 21:29 <note>original: "3 Reg. 21. 29."</note></margin>
10 See then that none of the Lord's words, which the Lord spoke against the house of Ahab, have fallen to the ground; the Lord has done what he spoke by the hand of his servant Elijah."
11 So Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, along with all his great men, his acquaintances, and his priests, until no survivor was left.
12 Then he set out and went toward Samaria. When he reached the Shepherds' Meeting-house <note>original: "Cameram pastorum." This refers to Beth-Eked, a place where shepherds gathered to shear sheep.</note> on the way,
13 he met the brothers of Ahaziah, king of Judah, and

asked them: "Who are you?" They answered: "We are the brothers of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen."

And Jehonadab answered: "It is." Jehu said: "If it is, give me your hand." He gave him his hand, and Jehu lifted him up into the chariot.

19 "Now therefore, summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I have a great sacrifice for Baal. Whoever is missing shall not live." But Jehu was acting with trickery, so that he might destroy the worshippers of Baal.
20 He said: "Sanctify a solemn assembly for Baal." And he issued the call.

24 So they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and told them: "If any of the men I bring into your hands escapes, your life shall be for his life."
25 As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu commanded the soldiers and captains: "Go in and strike them down; let no one escape." ## C H A P T E R XI.

*Athaliah, having heard of her son's death, extinguishes all the royal seed by the sword, except for Joash, and usurps the kingdom; but by the command of Jehoiada the priest she is slain, and Joash is established as king of Judah, after the altars and images of Baal are destroyed.*

<margin>2 Chronicles 22:10 <note>original: "2 Par. 22. 10." Paralipomenon is the Greek/Latin name for Chronicles.</note></margin>
1 Now Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah, seeing that her son was dead, arose and slew all the royal seed.
2 But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being slain, along with his nurse, from the bedchamber: and she hid him from the face of Athaliah, so that he was not killed.
3 And he was with her for six years secretly in the house of the Lord: while Athaliah reigned over the land.
<margin>2 Chronicles 23:1 <note>original: "2 Par. 23. 1."</note></margin>
4 But in the seventh year, Jehoiada sent and took the centurions and the soldiers, and brought them to himself into the temple of the Lord, and made a covenant with them: and taking an oath from them in the house of the Lord, he showed them the king's son.
5 And he commanded them, saying: "This is the thing that you must do:
6 Let a third part of you enter in on the Sabbath, and keep the watch of the king's house. And let a third part be at the gate of Sur: and a third part at the gate behind the dwelling of the shield-bearers: and you shall keep the watch of the house of Messah.
7 But let two parts of you, all who go out on the Sabbath, keep the watch of the house of the Lord about the king.
8 And you shall surround him, having your weapons in your hands: and if anyone enters the precinct of the temple, let him be slain: and you shall be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."
9 And the centurions did according to all that Jehoiada the priest had commanded them: and each taking his men who entered on the Sabbath, with those who went out on the Sabbath, they came to Jehoiada the priest.
10 And he gave them the spears and the armor of King David, which were in the house of the Lord.
11 And they stood, each having his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the temple even to the left side of the altar and of the sanctuary, around the king.
12 And he brought forth the king's son, and placed up-

<column-break/>

on him the crown and the testimony: and they made him king, and anointed him: and clapping their hands, they said: "Long live the king."
13 And Athaliah heard the noise of the people running: and she went in to the crowds in the temple of the Lord,
14 and she saw the king standing upon the dais according to the custom, and the singers and the trumpets near him, and all the people of the land rejoicing and sounding the trumpets: and she tore her garments, and cried out: "Treason! Treason!"
15 But Jehoiada commanded the centurions who were over the army, and said to them: "Lead her out beyond the precincts of the temple, and whoever follows her, let him be struck with the sword." For the priest had said: "Let her not be slain in the temple of the Lord."
16 And they laid hands on her, and pushed her through the way by which the horses enter near the palace, and she was slain there.
17 Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord, and the king, and the people, that they should be the people of the Lord; and also between the king and the people.
18 And all the people of the land went into the temple of Baal, and destroyed his altars, and broke his images in pieces thoroughly: they also slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altar. And the priest appointed guards in the house of the Lord.
19 And he took the centurions, and the legions of the <term>Cherethites and Pelethites</term><note>The Cherethites and Pelethites were the king's elite royal bodyguards.</note>, and all the people of the land, and they brought down the king from the house of the Lord: and they came by the way of the gate of the shield-bearers into the palace, and he sat upon the throne of the kings.
20 And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet: but Athaliah was slain with the sword in the king's house.
21 And Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.

## C H A P T E R XII.

*Joash arranges the money of the treasury for the restoration of the temple repairs; but he sends all the treasures of the temple and the palace to Hazael king of Syria, who was preparing war against Jerusalem; at last he is slain by his servants, and his son Amaziah succeeds him.*

In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash began to reign: and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Zibiah of Beersheba.
2 And Joash did what was right before the Lord all the days that Jehoiada the priest taught him.
3 Nevertheless, he did not take away the high places: for the people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.
4 And Joash said to the priests: "All the money for the holy things that is brought into the temple of the Lord by those who pass by, which is offered for the price of a soul <note>This refers to the half-shekel tax or census ransom paid by individuals.</note>, and all that they bring into the temple of the Lord voluntarily and by the choice of their own heart:
5 let the priests take it according to their order, and let them restore the <term>sartatecta</term><note>sartatecta: a Latin architectural term meaning the "roofs and walls," referring to the general maintenance and structural repair of a building.</note> of the house, wherever they see any repair is needed."
6 Therefore, even until the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not restored the repairs of the temple.
7 And King Joash called Jehoiada the high priest, and the priests, saying to them: "Why do you not restore the repairs of the temple? Therefore, do not receive any more money according to your order, but give it up for the restoration of the temple."

### CHAPTER XIII.

*Jehoahaz, king of Israel, is most severely afflicted by the king of Syria because of his sins, but is delivered after turning to the Lord: upon his death, his son Joash succeeds him, who defeated the Syrians according to the prophecy of the dying Elisha; a certain dead man is brought back to life when thrown into the tomb of the deceased Elisha.*

In the twenty-third year of Joash, the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for seventeen years.

<column-break/>

2 And he did evil before the Lord, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, and he did not depart from them.
3 And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hand of Hazael, king of Syria, and into the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael, all their days.
4 But Jehoahaz entreated the face of the Lord, and the Lord heard him: for he saw the distress of Israel, because the king of Syria had oppressed them.
5 And the Lord gave Israel a savior, and they were delivered from the hand of the king of Syria: and the children of Israel dwelt in their tents as in times past.
6 Nevertheless, they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who made Israel to sin, but walked in them: and even the <term>sacred grove<note>original: "lucus," likely referring to an Asherah pole or a cultic site for a Canaanite goddess</note></term> remained in Samaria.
7 And there was left to Jehoahaz of the people only fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen: for the king of Syria had destroyed them and reduced them to be like the dust of the threshing floor.
8 Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
9 And Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria: and Joash his son reigned in his place.
10 In the thirty-seventh year of Joash, king of Judah, Joash the son of Jehoahaz began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for sixteen years.
11 And he did what is evil in the sight of the Lord: he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, but he walked in them.
12 Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might, and how he fought against Amaziah, king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
13 And Joash slept with his fathers: and Jeroboam sat upon his throne. Furthermore, Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
14 Now Elisha was sick with the illness of which he was to die: and Joash, king of Israel, went down to him and wept before him, saying: "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its driver!"
15 And Elisha said to him: "Bring a bow and arrows." And when he had brought him a bow and arrows,
16 He said to the king of Israel: "Put your hand upon the bow." And when he had put his hand upon it, Elisha put his hands upon the king's hands,
17 And said: "Open the window toward the east." And when he had opened it, Elisha said: "Shoot an arrow." And he shot it. And Elisha said: "The arrow of the Lord's salvation, and the arrow of salvation against Syria: and you shall strike Syria in Aphek until you have consumed it."
18 And he said: "Take the arrows." And when he had taken them, he said to him again: "Strike the ground with an arrow." And when he had struck three times and then stopped,
19 The man of God was angry with him and said: "If you had struck five or six or seven times, you would have struck Syria even to destruction: but now you shall strike Syria only three times."
20 So Elisha died, and they buried him.

## C A P T E R XIV.

*Amaziah puts to death the killers of his father Jehoash and defeats Edom; but having become arrogant by this victory, he provokes Jehoash, king of Israel, to war, is captured by him, and Jerusalem is plundered. Meanwhile, Jeroboam succeeds his father Jehoash as king of Israel and delivers Israel from distress; he is succeeded by his son Zechariah. Furthermore, a conspiracy is formed against Amaziah, king of Judah, and he is killed by his own people; he is succeeded by his son Azariah, who was ungodly.*

1 In the second year of Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah, the son of Jehoash, king of Judah, began to reign.

2 † He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Joadan of Jerusalem.

4 Except for this one thing: he did not remove the <term>high places<note>original: "excelsa," referring to local shrines or altars on hills where the people offered sacrifices outside of the central Temple in Jerusalem</note></term>; for the people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places.

## CHAPTER XV.

->*Azariah the leper is succeeded by his son Jotham in Judah. Meanwhile, in Israel, Zechariah is succeeded by Shallum, then Menahem, who becomes a tributary to the King of the Assyrians. He is followed by Pekahiah, and then Pekah; during Pekah's time, Tiglath-Pileser conquers a large part of the Israelites and carries them off to Assyria. He is succeeded by Hoshea. In Judah, upon the death of Jotham, his son Ahaz succeeds him.*<-

1 In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam, the king of Israel, Azariah <note>Also known as Uzziah.</note>, son of Amaziah, king of Judah, began his reign.
2 He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem; his mother’s name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
3 And he did what was pleasing before the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
4 Nevertheless, he did not demolish the high places <note>Local shrines where the people offered sacrifices outside of the central Temple in Jerusalem.</note>; the people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places.
<margin>† 2 Chronicles 26:21</margin>
5 † But the Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death, and he lived in a <term>separate house<note>Latin: "domo libera." This refers to a house of quarantine or isolation required for those with leprosy.</note></term> apart; while Jotham, the king’s son, governed the palace and judged the people of the land.
6 Now the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Words of the Days <note>The Chronicles.</note> of the Kings of Judah?
7 And Azariah slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his ancestors in the City of David; and Jotham his son reigned in his place.
8 In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria for six months.
9 And he did what was evil before the Lord, just as his fathers had done; he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
10 Then Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him and struck him openly and killed him, and reigned in his place.
11 Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, are they not written in the Book of the Words of the Days of the Kings of Israel?
<margin>† See above, 10:30</margin>
12 † This was the word of the Lord which he spoke to Jehu, saying: "Your sons shall sit upon the throne of Israel even to the fourth generation." And so it came to pass.
13 Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah, king of Judah; and he reigned for one month in Samaria.
14 And Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and he struck Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him, and reigned in his place.
15 Now the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy by which he laid his traps, are they not written in the Book of the Words of the Days of the Kings of Israel?
16 Then Menahem struck Tiphsah, and everyone who was in it, and its borders starting from Tirzah—for they had refused to open the gates to him—and he killed all the pregnant women and ripped them open.
17 In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah, king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi reigned over Israel for ten years in Samaria.

<column-break/>

18 And he did what was evil before the Lord; he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, all his days.
19 Pul, the king of the Assyrians, came into the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand <term>talents<note>A talent was a massive unit of weight; 1,000 talents of silver would have been a staggering sum, approximately 34 metric tons.</note></term> of silver, so that he might help him and strengthen his kingdom.
20 And Menahem exacted the silver from Israel—from all the powerful and wealthy men—to give to the king of the Assyrians: fifty <term>shekels<note>A shekel was a smaller unit of silver weight.</note></term> of silver for each man. So the king of the Assyrians turned back and did not stay in the land.
21 Now the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Words of the Days of the Kings of Israel?
22 And Menahem slept with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.

26 Now the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Words of the Days of the Kings of Israel?
27 In the fifty-second year of Azariah, king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for twenty years.
28 And he did what was evil before the Lord; he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
29 In the days of Pekah, king of Israel, Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, came and took Ijon, and Abel-beth-maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali; and he carried them away into Assyria.

### CHAPTER XVI.

->*Ahaz consecrates his son to idols by fire; while the kings of Israel and Syria besiege Jerusalem, he obtains help from the king of the Assyrians by sending gifts; for whose sake he removes the worship of God to sacrifice to the gods of the Assyrians; he is succeeded by his pious son Hezekiah.*<-

1 In the seventeenth year of Pekah <note>original: "Phacee"</note>, son of Remaliah, Ahaz, son of Jotham, king of Judah, began to reign.
<margin>† 2 Chronicles 28:1</margin>
2 Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: he did not do what was pleasing in the sight of the Lord his God, as David his father had done.
3 But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel: moreover, he even <term>consecrated his son<note>Refers to the practice of passing a child through fire, a ritual associated with the god Molech.</note></term>, passing him through fire according to the idols of the nations which the Lord destroyed before the children of Israel.
4 He also offered victims, and burned incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
<margin>† Isaiah 7:1</margin>
5 Then Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to Jerusalem to fight: and when they besieged Ahaz, they were not able to overcome him.
6 At that time Rezin, king of Syria, restored <term>Elath<note>Latin: "Ailam." An important port city on the Red Sea.</note></term> to Syria, and drove the Jews out of Elath: and the Edomites came into Elath, and have lived there even to this day.
7 But Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser <note>original: "Theglathphalasar"</note>, king of the Assyrians, saying: I am your servant, and your son: come up, and save me from the hand of the king of Syria, and from the hand of the king of Israel, who have risen up against me.
8 And when he had gathered the silver and gold that could be found in the house of the Lord, and in the king's treasures, he sent gifts to the king of the Assyrians.
9 And he agreed to his will: for the king of the Assyrians went up against Damascus, and laid it waste: and he transported its inhabitants to <term>Kir<note>Latin: "Cyrenem." Identifying this as the biblical Kir, the place of Syrian origin and exile.</note></term>, and he killed Rezin.
10 And king Ahaz went to meet Tiglath-Pileser, king of the Assyrians, in Damascus: and when he had seen the altar of Damascus, king Ahaz sent to Urijah <note>original: "Uriam"</note> the priest a model of it, and a likeness according to all its workmanship.
11 And Urijah the priest built an altar: according to all that king Ahaz had commanded from Damascus, so did Urijah the priest, until king Ahaz returned from Damascus.
12 And when the king had come from Damascus, he saw the altar, and venerated it: and he went up and offered burnt offerings, and his sacrifice,
13 And he poured drink offerings, and shed the blood of the peace offerings, which he had offered upon the altar.
14 Furthermore, the bronze altar, which was before the Lord, he moved from the front of the temple, and from the place of the altar, and from the place of the temple of the Lord: and he placed it by the side of the altar toward the north.
15 King Ahaz also commanded Urijah the priest, saying: Upon the greater altar offer the morning burnt offering, and the evening sacri-

<column-break/>

fice, and the king's burnt offering, and his sacrifice, and the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their sacrifices, and their drink offerings: and all the blood of the burnt offering, and all the blood of the victim you shall pour upon it: but the bronze altar shall be <term>prepared for my will<note>original: "paratum ad voluntatem meam." This implies Ahaz intended to use the original holy altar for private divination or personal inquiry rather than public worship.</note></term>.
16 Urijah the priest therefore did according to all that king Ahaz had commanded.
17 And king Ahaz took away the carved bases, and the laver that was above them: and he took down <term>the Sea<note>A massive bronze basin used for ritual washing in Solomon's Temple.</note></term> from the bronze oxen that supported it, and set it upon a pavement laid with stone.
18 The <term>Sabbath canopy<note>Latin: "Musach." Likely a covered walkway or royal pavilion used on the Sabbath.</note></term> also, which he had built in the temple, and the king's outer entrance, he turned toward the temple of the Lord, because of the king of the Assyrians.
19 Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz, which he did, are they not written in the Book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
20 And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with them in the city of David, and Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

### CHAPTER XVII.

->*After many crimes of the children of Israel are recounted, Shalmaneser, finding that Hoshea has ceased to pay the ancient tribute to the Assyrians, transports Israel into Assyria: and because the Assyrians sent into Samaria were being devoured by lions for not knowing the worship of God, an Israelite priest is sent to them to instruct them: and so it happened that they served both God and idols.*<-

# CHAPTER XXI.

-> Because of the abominable impiety of Manasseh, the Lord foretells that he will destroy Judah and Jerusalem; when he dies, his impious son Amon succeeds him; and when he is killed by his servants, his pious son Josiah reigns over Judah. <-

1 <margin>2 Chronicles 33:1</margin> Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem; his mother's name was Hephzibah.
2 And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, according to the idols of the nations which the Lord destroyed before the face of the children of Israel.
3 <margin>† 2 Chronicles 33:3</margin> And he turned and rebuilt the high places <note>Local shrines for unauthorized worship</note> which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he set up altars to Baal, and made sacred groves as Ahab king of Israel had done, and adored all the host of heaven, and served them.
4 <margin>† 2 Samuel 7:10</margin> And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord said: "In Jerusalem I will put my name."
5 And he built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the temple of the Lord.
6 And he made his son pass through fire; and he practiced soothsaying, and observed omens, and instituted spirit-mediums <note>original: pythones; refers to those claiming to consult the spirits of the dead</note>, and multiplied diviners, to do evil before the Lord and to provoke him.
7 <margin>† 2 Samuel 7:26; 1 Kings 8:16 & 9:5</margin> He also set the idol of the grove, which he had made, in the temple of the Lord; concerning which the Lord spoke to David and to Solomon his son: "In this temple, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.
8 And I will no longer make the foot of Israel wander from the land which I gave to their fathers; if only they will observe to do all that I have commanded them, and all the law that my servant Moses commanded them."
9 But they did not listen; instead, they were seduced by Manasseh to do evil worse than the nations which the Lord destroyed before the face of the children of Israel.
10 And the Lord spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying:
11 <margin>† Jeremiah 15:4</margin> "Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these most wicked abominations, beyond all that the Amorites did before him, and has made Judah also to sin with his uncleanness;
12 Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I will bring evils upon Jerusalem and Judah, so that whoever hears of it, both his ears shall tingle.
13 And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria, and the plummet <note>original: pondus; a weight used to check if a wall is straight</note> of the house of Ahab; and I will wipe out Jerusalem as writing-tablets are usually wiped; and in wiping it, I will turn it over and draw the stylus frequently over its face. <note>An image of total erasure and destruction, like smoothing wax on a tablet to delete the message.</note>
14 And I will forsake the remnants of my inheritance, and deliver them into the hands of their enemies; and they shall be for a desolation and a prey to all their adversaries;
15 Because they have done evil before me, and have continued to provoke me, from the day their fathers came out of Egypt, even to this day."
16 Moreover, Manasseh shed very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem even to the brim; besides his sins with which he made Judah to sin, to do evil before the Lord.

<summary>King Hezekiah is miraculously healed and granted fifteen more years of life, but his pride in showing his wealth to Babylonian envoys leads to a prophecy of future exile. His son Manasseh succeeds him, reversing Hezekiah's reforms with extreme idolatry and violence, leading God to decree the destruction of Jerusalem.</summary>

### CHAPTER XXII.

> *Josiah restores the temple and the worship of God. They consult the Lord concerning the discovered book of Deuteronomy. Josiah, terrified by the threats and punishments recorded therein, receives an answer from the prophetess: though the evils written in the book will be brought upon Judah because their fathers neglected the worship of God, he himself shall first die in peace.*

<margin>2 Chronicles 34:1</margin>
1 **J**osiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
2 And he did what was pleasing before the Lord, and walked in all the ways of David his father; he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
3 Now in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam, the scribe of the temple of the Lord, saying to him:
4 "Go to Hilkiah the high priest, so that the money may be melted down <note>original: "confletur," meaning to gather or smelt the collected coins into a sum</note> which has been brought into the temple of the Lord, which the doorkeepers of the temple have collected from the people.
5 And let it be given to the craftsmen by the overseers of the house of the Lord; and let them distribute it to those who work in the temple of the Lord, to repair the structural damage <term>sarta tecta|literally "repaired roofs," a legal and architectural term for general building maintenance</term> of the temple.
6 That is, to the carpenters and masons, and to those who repair broken sections, and so that timber and quarried stones may be bought to restore the temple of the Lord.
7 However, let no accounting be made with them for the silver they receive, but let them hold it in their power and in good faith."
8 Then Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe: "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan, who also read it.

11 And the king had heard the words of the book of the Law of the Lord, he tore his garments.
12 And he commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Achbor the son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying:
13 "Go and consult the Lord for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this scroll which has been found. For the great wrath of the Lord is kindled against us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of this book, to do everything that is written for us."
14 So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum, the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe, who lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter <note>original: "in Secunda," referring to the Mishneh, a newer district of the city</note>; and they spoke to her.
15 And she answered them: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to me:
16 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring evils upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the words of the Law which the king of Judah has read.
17 Because they have forsaken me and have sacrificed to foreign gods, provoking me in all the works of their hands; and my indignation shall be kindled against this place, and it shall not be extinguished.'
18 But to the king of Judah, who sent you to consult the Lord, thus you shall say: 'Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Because you have heard the words of the scroll,
19 And your heart was terrified, and you humbled yourself before the Lord after hearing the words against this place and its inhabitants—namely, that they should become a desolation and a curse—and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, says the Lord.
20 Therefore, I will gather you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your tomb in peace, so that your eyes shall not see all the evils which I am about to bring upon this place.'"

### CHAPTER XXIV.

*Jehoiakim serves the king of Babylon for three years, then suffers various raids. 27 Now it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, released Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
28 And he spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
29 So he changed his prison garments, and he ate bread continually before the king all the days of his life.
30 And his allowance was a regular allowance given to him by the king, a portion for every day, all the days of his life.

18 The sons of Reuben, and Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, were fighting men, carrying shields and swords, and drawing the bow, and trained for battle: forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty, going forth to war.
19 They fought against the Hagrites; and the Jeturites, and Naphish, and Nodab,
20 Provided help against them. And the Hagrites were delivered into their hands, and all who were with them, because they called upon God while they were fighting: and He heard them, because they had put their trust in Him.
21 And they took all that they possessed: fifty thousand camels, and two hundred and fifty thousand sheep, and two thousand donkeys, and a hundred thousand human lives.
22 For many were wounded and fell, because the war was of the Lord. And they dwelt in their place until the exile <note>original: "transmigrationem," referring to the Babylonian or Assyrian captivity</note>.
23 The sons of the half-tribe of Manasseh also possessed the land from the borders of Bashan as far as Baal-hermon, and Senir, and mount Hermon; for they were a great number.
24 And these were the heads of the houses of their kindred: Epher, and Ishi, and Eliel, and Azriel, and Jeremiah, and Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, very strong and powerful men, and famous leaders in their families.

<column-break/>

25 But they abandoned the God of their fathers, and committed fornication after the gods of the people of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.
26 And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of the Assyrians, and the spirit of Tiglath-Pileser <note>original: "Thelgathphalnasar"</note> king of Assyria: and he carried away Reuben, and Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them into Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and the river Gozan, even to this day.

11 When the men of Jabesh Gilead had heard this—all that the Philistines had done to Saul—
12 every one of the valiant men rose up and took the bodies of Saul and his sons; they brought them to Jabesh and buried their bones under the oak that was in Jabesh, and they fasted for seven days.

### CHAPTER XIX.

*Hanun, the king of Ammon, insults David’s servants who had come to offer comfort for his father's death; he is subsequently attacked by David and defeated along with his Syrian allies.*

<margin>† 2 Samuel 10:1</margin>
1 Now it happened that Nahash the king of the sons of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his place.
2 And David said: "I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, for his father showed grace to me." So David sent messengers to comfort him over the death of his father. But when they had come into the land of the sons of Ammon to comfort Hanun,
3 The princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun: "Do you perhaps think that out of honor for your father David has sent men to comfort you? Do you not realize that his servants have come to you to explore, investigate, and spy out your land?"
4 Therefore, Hanun seized David's servants and shaved them; he cut off their tunics from the buttocks down to the feet and sent them away.
5 When they had departed and reported this to David, he sent men to meet them (for they had suffered a great insult) and commanded that they should stay in Jericho until their beards grew back, and then they should return.
6 Now when the sons of Ammon saw that they had done an injury to David, both Hanun and the rest of the people sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen for themselves from Mesopotamia, Syrian Maakah, and Zobah.
7 And they hired thirty-two thousand chariots and the king of Maakah with his people. When they arrived, they camped opposite Medeba. The sons of Ammon also gathered from their cities and came to the battle.
8 When David heard of this, he sent Joab and the entire army of valiant men.

<column-break/>

9 Then the sons of Ammon went out and drew up their battle line near the gate of the city; but the kings who had come to help stood separately in the field.
10 Joab, realizing that the battle was being waged against him both from the front and from the rear, chose the strongest men of all Israel and marched against the Syrians.
11 The rest of the people he put under the command of his brother Abishai, and they marched against the sons of Ammon.
12 And he said: "If the Syrians prevail against me, you shall help me; but if the sons of Ammon prevail against you, I will be your defense."
13 "Be of good courage, and let us act manfully for our people and for the cities of our God; and may the Lord do what is good in His sight."
14 So Joab and the people who were with him advanced against the Syrians for battle, and he put them to flight.
15 Moreover, when the sons of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they also fled from his brother Abishai and entered the city; then Joab also returned to Jerusalem.
16 But the Syrians, seeing that they had fallen before Israel, sent messengers and brought out the Syrians who were across the river; and Shophach, the captain of Hadadezer’s army, was their leader.
17 When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and fell upon them; he drew up his line opposite them as they fought against him.
18 But the Syrians fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand chariot-drivers and forty thousand footmen of the Syrians, as well as Shophach, the captain of the army.
19 And when the servants of Hadadezer saw that they were overcome by Israel, they went over to David and served him; and Syria would no longer provide help to the sons of Ammon.

<margin>9</margin> The son who shall be born to you shall be a most quiet man: for I will make him rest from all his enemies round about: and for this reason he shall be called Peaceable <note>original: "Pacificus," a translation of the name Solomon, derived from the Hebrew word for peace, "Shalom"</note>: and I will give peace and quietness in Israel all his days.
<margin>10</margin> <margin>† 2 Samuel 7:13; 1 Kings 5:5; † 2 Samuel 7:14; Hebrews 1:5 <note>The margin refers to 2 and 3 Regum; in older Latin Bibles, the books of Samuel and Kings were often numbered together as 1, 2, 3, and 4 Kings</note></margin> 10 † He shall build a house to my name, and he shall be a son to me, and I will be a father to him: and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'
<margin>11</margin> Now therefore, my son, may the Lord be with you, and prosper, and build the house for the Lord your God, just as he has spoken concerning you.
<margin>12</margin> May the Lord also give you wisdom and understanding, so that you may rule Israel, and keep the law of the Lord your God.
<margin>13</margin> For then you shall be able to prosper, if you keep the commandments and judgments which the Lord commanded Moses to teach Israel: be strong and act manfully, do not fear, nor be dismayed.
<margin>14</margin> Behold, in my poverty <note>original: "paupertate mea," likely referring to his labors or the hardships of his reign rather than a lack of wealth</note> I have prepared the expenses for the house of the Lord: a hundred thousand talents of gold, and a thousand thousand talents of silver; but of the brass and iron there is no weight, for the number is overcome by the magnitude: I have prepared wood and stones for all the costs.
<margin>15</margin> You have also many craftsmen: stonecutters, and masons, and woodworkers, and those most skilled in every art for doing the work,
<margin>16</margin> In gold and silver and brass and iron, of which there is no number. Arise therefore, and act, and the Lord will be with you."
<margin>17</margin> David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son.
<margin>18</margin> Saying: "You see that the Lord your God is with you, and has given you rest on every side, and has delivered all your enemies into your hands, and the land is subdued before the Lord, and before his people.
<margin>19</margin> Give your hearts therefore and your souls to seek the Lord your God: and arise, and build a sanctuary for the Lord God, so that the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the vessels consecrated to the Lord, may be brought into the house which is being built to the name of the Lord."

### C H A P T E R XXIII.

->*David, being old, having designated Solomon as king, assigns the duties of the numbered Levites; and the sons of Moses are numbered among the Levites.*<-

Therefore David, old and full of days, made Solomon his son king over Israel.
2 And he gathered all the princes of Israel, and the priests and Levites.

5 Furthermore, four thousand were gatekeepers: and as many singers singing to the Lord on the instruments which he had made for singing.
<margin>† Above 6:1</margin> 6 † And David distributed them by the divisions of the sons of Levi, namely, Gershon <note>original: "Gerson"</note>, Kohath <note>original: "Caath"</note>, and Merari.

### CHAPTER XXV.

->*From the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, the singers, players of the psaltery and the harp, twenty-four families and turns are distributed by lot.*<-

1 Therefore David and the commanders of the army set apart for the ministry the sons of Asaph, and Heman, and Jeduthun <note>original: "Idithun"</note>: who should prophesy with harps, and psalteries <note>A stringed instrument like a zither or lyre.</note>, and cymbals, serving in their dedicated office according to their number.

3 Furthermore, of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, and Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hand of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with a harp to give thanks and praise to the Lord.
4 Concerning Heman also: the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamti-ezer, and Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth.

6 All these were distributed under the hand of their father to sing in the temple of the Lord, with cymbals, and psalteries, and harps, for the ministries of the house of the Lord near the king: namely, Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.
7 And their number with their brothers, who were instructed in the song of the Lord—all of them teachers—was two hundred and eighty-eight.

### C H A P T E R XXVII.

*The twelve princes are recounted, each of whom was in charge of twenty-four thousand during his month; additionally, the princes or prefects of the tribes, the treasurers, and the rest of the king’s property are listed.*

1 Now the children of Israel according to their number, the heads of families, the tribunes <note>original: "tribuni," commanders of a thousand</note>, the centurions <note>original: "centuriones," commanders of a hundred</note>, and the officers who served the king in their divisions, coming in and going out month by month throughout the year; twenty-four thousand were in each division.
2 Over the first division in the first month was Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel, and under him were twenty-four thousand.
3 He was of the sons of Perez, the chief of all the captains of the army in the first month.
4 Over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and after him was another named Mikloth, who governed a part of the army of twenty-four thousand.
5 The captain of the third division in the third month was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada the priest: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
6 This is that Benaiah, the most valiant among the thirty, and above the thirty: and over his division was Amizabad his son.
7 The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
8 The fifth, for the fifth month, was the prince Shamhuth the Izrahite: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
9 The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
10 The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite of the sons of Ephraim: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
11 The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbekai the Hushathite of the lineage of Zerah: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
12 The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite of the sons of Benjamin <note>original: "Jemini"</note>: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
13 The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai, and he was a Netophathite of the lineage of Zerah: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
14 The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite of the sons of Ephraim: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
15 The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of the lineage of Othniel: and in his division were twenty-four thousand.
16 Furthermore, over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, the leader was Eliezer the son of Zichri; of the Simeonites, the leader was Shephatiah the son of Maachah;
