### CHAPTER XXIX.

*The expenses prepared by David for the building of the temple are recounted, to which the princes and the people add many gifts: David, blessing the Lord, prays for Solomon and the people; and after sacrifices are offered with great joy, Solomon is anointed king a second time in place of his father David, who rested in peace in the fortieth year of his reign.*

1 And King David said to all the assembly: God has chosen Solomon my son alone, who is still a boy and tender: for the work is great, nor is a dwelling being prepared for man, but for God.

2 And I with all my strength have prepared the expenses for the house of my God. Gold for the vessels of gold, and silver for those of silver, brass for the brass ones, iron for the iron ones, wood for the wooden ones: and onyx stones, and stones like antimony <note>original: "stibinos," likely referring to dark, glistening stones</note>, and of various colors; and every kind of precious stone, and Parian marble in great abundance:

3 And beyond these things, which I have offered into the house of my God from my own stores, I give gold and silver to the temple of my God, besides those things which I have prepared for the holy house:

4 Three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir <note>original: "Ophir," a region famous in antiquity for the highest quality gold</note>: and seven thousand talents of the most refined silver, for overlaying the walls of the temple.

5 And wherever gold is needed for gold work, and wherever silver is needed for silver work, let the works be done by the hands of the craftsmen: and if anyone offers willingly, let him fill his hand today and offer what he wishes to the Lord.

6 Then the princes of the families, and the leaders of the tribes of Israel, and the tribunes, and the centurions, and the overseers of the king's possessions, made their promises.

7 And they gave for the works of the house of God five thousand talents of gold, and ten thousand solidi <note>original: "solidos," a gold coin</note>: ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of brass: and also one hundred thousand talents of iron.

8 And with whomever stones were found, they gave them into the treasures of the house of the Lord, by the hand of Jahiel the Gershonite.

9 And the people rejoiced when they promised their vows willingly: for they offered them to the Lord with their whole heart: and King David also rejoiced with great joy.

10 And he blessed the Lord before the whole multitude, and said: Blessed are you, O Lord God of Israel our father, from eternity to eternity.

11 Yours, O Lord, is the magnificence, and the power, and the glory, and the victory: and to you be praise: for all things that are in heaven and on earth are yours: yours, O Lord, is the kingdom, and you are above all princes.

12 Yours are riches, and yours is glory; you rule over all, in your hand is strength and power: in your hand is greatness, and the empire of all things.

13 Now therefore, our God, we confess to you, and we praise your glorious name.

14 Who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to promise all these things to you? All things are yours: and we have given to you what we received from your hand.

### C H A P T E R  II.

*Architects and workmen are appointed for the building of the temple; Solomon agrees with King Hiram to send a skilled craftsman and to provide timber for the temple structure.*

**S**olomon decided to build a house for the name of the Lord, and a palace for himself.

2 And he counted out seventy thousand men to carry burdens on their shoulders, eighty thousand to quarry stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.

<margin>† 1 Kings 5:2</margin>
3 He also sent word to Hiram, the king of Tyre, saying: "As you dealt with my father David, and sent him cedar logs to build himself a house to live in,

4 so deal with me, that I may build a house to the name of the Lord my God, to consecrate it for burning incense before Him, and for fragrant spices, and for the continual setting out of the showbread, and for the burnt offerings in the morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the festivals of the Lord our God forever, as has been commanded to Israel.

5 For the house I wish to build is great; for our God is greater than all gods.

6 Who then can prevail to build Him a worthy house? If the heavens and the heavens of heavens cannot contain Him, who am I that I should build Him a house? It is for this purpose only: that incense may be burned before Him.

7 Therefore, send me a man of skill, who knows how to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, purple, scarlet, and blue cloth, and who knows how to engrave, to work with the craftsmen I have with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.

8 Send me also cedar, juniper, and pine logs from Lebanon; for I know that your servants are skilled at cutting the timber of Lebanon. My servants will work with your servants,

9 so that a great deal of timber may be prepared for me. For the house I desire to build is exceedingly great and wonderful.

10 Furthermore, for the workmen who will cut the timber, I will give as food for your servants twenty thousand <term>cors<gloss>A "corus" was a large dry measure, roughly equal to 10 or 12 bushels.</gloss></term> of wheat, and as many cors of barley, and

<column-break/>

twenty thousand <term>baths<gloss>original: "metretas." A liquid measure of about 8 or 9 gallons.</gloss></term> of wine, and twenty thousand baths <note>original: "fata." Another term for the bath measure.</note> of oil."

11 Then Hiram, the king of Tyre, replied in a letter he sent to Solomon: "Because the Lord loved His people, He has made you king over them."

12 And he added, saying: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who gave King David a wise son, learned, sensible, and prudent, to build a house for the Lord and a palace for himself.

13 I have therefore sent you a prudent and most skillful man, Hiram-Abi <note>original: "Hiram, patrem meum." Literally "Hiram, my father," but in this context, it is often understood as a title or a proper name, Hiram-Abi, meaning "Master Hiram" or "Hiram the counselor."</note>,

14 the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, whose father was a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, marble, and wood, as well as in purple, blue, fine linen, and scarlet. He can perform any kind of engraving and devise any design required for the work, alongside your craftsmen and the craftsmen of my lord David, your father.

15 Therefore, my lord, send to your servants the wheat, barley, oil, and wine which you have promised.

16 We will cut logs from Lebanon, as many as you need, and will bring them to you in rafts by sea to Joppa; it will then be your task to transport them to Jerusalem."

17 Solomon then took a census of all the foreign men <note>original: "proselytos." Meaning "sojourners" or non-Israelite residents.</note> who were in the land of Israel, following the census his father David had taken, and they were found to be one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.

18 He assigned seventy thousand of them to carry burdens, eighty thousand to quarry stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred as overseers to keep the people working.

*The Temple is built, including the porch, the veil, and two bronze columns before the doors of the temple.*

**A**nd Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, which had been shown to his father David, in the place David had prepared on the † threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

2 He began to build in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.

3 These are the foundations which Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length, by the older measure, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.

4 The porch in front, which spanned the full width of the house, was twenty cubits long; and the height was one hundred and twenty cubits <note>At roughly 180 feet, this is exceptionally tall; some scholars believe this might be a scribal variation from 20 cubits, but the text records 120.</note>; and he overlaid it on the inside with the purest gold.

5 The main hall he paneled with fir wood and overlaid it with plates of the finest gold <note>original: "obrizi." Refers to gold that has been refined or tested for purity.</note> throughout; and he carved palm trees and chain-like patterns entwined with one another upon it.

6 He also paved the floor of the temple with most precious marble of great beauty.

7 The gold was of the highest quality; with its plates he overlaid the house, its beams, its posts, its walls, and its doors; and he carved cherubim upon the walls.

### C H A P T E R IV.

->*The construction of the bronze altar, the molten sea, the ten basins, the golden lampstands, the tables, the bowls, and the other things that belonged to the temple and its decoration.*<-

He also made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
<margin>† 1 Kings 7:23</margin>
2 He also made a molten sea <note>original: "Mare fusile." This was a massive bronze basin used by the priests for ritual washing.</note> of ten cubits from brim to brim, perfectly round; it was five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.
3 There were also figures of oxen under it, and for ten cubits they encircled the sea on the outside. There were two rows of oxen, cast in one piece with the sea.
4 And the sea itself sat upon twelve oxen, of which three looked toward the north, three toward the west, three toward the south, and the remaining three toward the east, having the sea set upon them; the hindquarters of the oxen were all turned inward under the sea.
5 Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was like the brim of a cup, or like a blossoming lily; it held three thousand measures <note>original: "metretas." A unit of liquid volume, often translated as "baths."</note>.
6 He also made ten basins: and he put five on the right and five on the left, to wash in them all the things that they were to offer as burnt offerings; but the priests washed themselves in the sea.

<column-break/>

7 He also made ten golden lampstands, according to the pattern they were commanded to be made: and he placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
8 He also made ten tables: and he placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left; and a hundred golden bowls.
9 He also made the court of the priests, and a great hall: and doors in the hall, which he overlaid with bronze.
10 And he placed the sea on the right side, toward the southeast.
11 Furthermore, Hiram made the pots, the flesh-hooks, and the bowls; and he finished all the king’s work in the house of God:
12 That is, the two columns, and the architraves, and the capitals, and the two networks to cover the capitals above the architraves.
13 Also four hundred pomegranates, and two networks, so that two rows of pomegranates were joined to each network, which covered the architraves and the capitals of the columns.
14 He also made bases, and the basins which he set upon the bases;
15 One sea, and the twelve oxen under the sea.
16 And the pots, and the flesh-hooks, and the bowls. All the vessels did Hiram, his master craftsman <note>original: "Hiram pater ejus." The word 'pater' (father) is often used as a title of respect for a master or advisor.</note>, make for Solomon in the house of the Lord out of the purest bronze.
17 The king cast them in the region of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
18 Now the multitude of vessels was so great that the weight of the bronze was beyond reckoning.
19 And Solomon made all the vessels for the house of God: the golden altar, and the tables, and the Bread of Presence <note>original: "panes propositionis." Also known as Showbread.</note> upon them;
20 Also the lampstands with their lamps, to burn before the sanctuary according to the ritual, of the purest gold;
21 And the floral ornaments, and the lamps, and the golden tongs; all were made of the finest gold.
22 The censers also, and the incense burners, and the bowls, and the mortars, were of the purest gold. And he carved the doors of the inner temple—that is, the Holy of Holies—and the outer doors of the temple were of gold. And so all the work that Solomon made in the house of the Lord was completed.

6 Moreover, King Solomon and the entire assembly of Israel, and all who had gathered before the ark, were sacrificing rams and oxen without number; for the multitude of victims was so great.

8 For the cherubim spread their wings over the place where the ark was set, covering the ark itself and its poles <note>original: "vectibus." These were the long staves used to carry the ark.</note>.

12 Both the Levites and the singers—namely, those under Asaph, those under Heman, and those under Jeduthun, with their sons and brothers—clothed in fine linen, were sounding cymbals, harps, and lyres, standing at the eastern side of the altar; and with them were one hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets.
13 Therefore, while the trumpets, the voices, the cymbals, the organs, and the various types of musical instruments sounded together and raised their voices on high, the sound was heard far away. When they began to praise the Lord and say: "Give thanks to the Lord because He is good, because His mercy endures forever," the house of God was filled with a cloud,
14 So that the priests could not stand and minister because of the darkness. For the glory of the Lord had filled the house of God.

### CHAPTER VI.

*Solomon blesses the people of Israel and gives thanks to God for the fulfillment of the promise made to David; he stood as a suppliant before the multitude, praying that God might hear the vows of those who pray in this temple.*

<margin>3 Kings 8:12</margin>
**T**hen Solomon said: The Lord promised that He would dwell in a thick cloud:
2 But I have built a house to His name, that He might dwell there forever.
3 And the king turned his face and blessed the entire assembly of Israel (for the whole crowd stood attentive) and said:
4 Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has fulfilled by His work what He spoke to my father David, saying:
5 From the day that I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel for a house to be built to my name; nor did I choose any other man to be a leader over my people Israel,

7 And since it had been the will of my father David to build a house to the name of the Lord God of Israel,

11 And I have placed in it the ark, in which is the covenant of the Lord, which He made with the children of Israel.
12 Then he stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of the entire assembly of Israel and stretched out his hands.
13 For Solomon had made a bronze platform <note>original: "basim." A raised scaffold or dais.</note> and had placed it in the middle of the court <note>original: "basilicæ." In this context, it refers to the temple courtyard or royal hall.</note>, being five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high; and he stood upon it. Then, kneeling on his knees before the whole assembly of Israel and raising his palms toward heaven,
<margin>† 2 Maccabees 2:8</margin>
14 He said, † O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven or on earth: You who keep covenant and mercy with Your servants who walk before You with all their heart:
15 You who have granted to Your servant David my father whatever You spoke to him: and what You promised with Your mouth, You have fulfilled with Your work, as the present time proves.
16 Now therefore, O Lord God of Israel, fulfill for Your servant David my father whatever You spoke, saying: "There shall not fail you a man in my sight to sit upon the throne of Israel, provided that your children guard their ways and walk in my law, just as you have walked before me."

19 But it was made only for this: that You might look upon the prayer of Your servant and his supplication, O Lord my God: and that You might hear the prayers which Your servant pours out before You:
20 That You may open Your eyes upon this house day and night, upon the place in which You promised that Your name would be invoked,
21 And that You might hear the prayer which Your servant prays in it: hear the prayers of Your servant and of Your people Israel. Whoever shall pray in this place, hear from Your dwelling place, that is, from the heavens, and be merciful.
22 If anyone sins against his neighbor and comes ready to swear an oath against him, binding himself with a curse before the altar in this house:
23 You will hear from heaven and perform the judgment of Your servants, so that You repay the wicked man's way upon his own head, and vindicate the just man, rewarding him according to his justice.
24 If Your people Israel are defeated by enemies (for they will sin against You) and they turn and perform penance, and entreat Your name, and pray in this place,
25 You will hear from heaven and be merciful to the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back into the land which You gave to them and to their fathers.

### C H A P T E R VIII.

*After various cities are built by Solomon, he makes the remnants of the foreign nations his subjects; he offers burnt offerings, and establishes the ministries of the priests and Levites according to the arrangement of David. A fleet is sent out, and a great amount of gold is brought back from Ophir to Solomon.*

<margin>3 Kings 9, 10.</margin>1 And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, after Solomon had built the house of the Lord and his own house:

2 He rebuilt the cities which Hiram had given to Solomon, and caused the children of Israel to dwell there.

3 He also went to Hamath-zobah <note>original: "Emath Suba." A kingdom in central Syria.</note> and conquered it.

4 And he built Palmyra <note>original: "Palmiram," also known as Tadmor.</note> in the desert, and he built other very strong cities in Hamath.

5 And he constructed Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities having walls, gates, bars, and bolts;

6 Baalath also, and all the strongest cities that belonged to Solomon, and all the chariot cities, and the cities for the horsemen. Everything that Solomon desired and planned to build, he built in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.

7 As for all the people who were left of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not of the stock of Israel:

8 Solomon subjected their children and descendants, whom the Israelites had not destroyed, to forced labor, as it remains to this day.

9 But of the children of Israel, he did not appoint any to serve the king's works; for they were men of war, chief captains, and princes of his chariots and horsemen.

10 Now all the chief officers of King Solomon's army were two hundred and fifty, who instructed the people.

11 And he moved the daughter of Pharaoh from the City of David into the house he had built for her. For the king said: My wife shall not dwell in the

<column-break/>

house of David, king of Israel, because it is sanctified, for the Ark of the Lord has entered into it.

12 Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the Lord upon the altar of the Lord, which he had built before the porch.

13 So that on each day an offering might be made according to the commandment of Moses, on the Sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the festival days three times a year—that is, on the Feast of Unleavened Bread, on the Feast of Weeks, and on the Feast of Tabernacles.

14 And he appointed, according to the arrangement of his father David, the offices of the priests in their ministries, and the Levites in their order to give praise and to minister before the priests according to the daily ritual, and the gatekeepers in their divisions for every gate; for so David, the man of God, had commanded.

15 And they did not deviate from the king's commands, neither the priests nor the Levites, regarding anything he had commanded, or concerning the oversight of the treasuries.

16 Solomon had all his expenses prepared from the day he founded the house of the Lord until the day he finished it.

17 Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber <note>original: "Asiongaber."</note> and to Eloth <note>original: "Ailath."</note> on the shore of the Red Sea, which is in the land of Edom.

18 And Hiram sent him ships by the hands of his servants, and sailors who were experienced with the sea; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir <note>A region of uncertain location, famous in antiquity for its high-quality gold.</note>, and they took from there four hundred and fifty talents <note>A "talent" was a massive unit of weight, roughly 75 pounds or 34 kilograms.</note> of gold, and brought it to King Solomon.

### C H A P T E R IX.

*The Queen of Sheba, admiring the wisdom of Solomon, departs after giving and receiving gifts. The weight of gold brought annually to Solomon is recorded; he constructs spears, shields, and all golden feast vessels, and an ivory throne overlaid with gold. The greatness of Solomon's wealth, wisdom, and power is described; he dies in the fortieth year of his reign and is succeeded by his son Rehoboam.*

<margin>3 Kings 10:1; Matthew 12:42; Luke 11:31.</margin>1 And when the Queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to Jerusalem to test him with riddles, with great wealth and camels carrying spices, and plenty of gold, and precious gems. And when she came to Solomon, she spoke to him of everything that was in her heart.

2 And Solomon explained to her all that she proposed; there was nothing that he did not make clear to her.

3 And after she saw the wisdom of Solomon, and the house he had built,

4 As well as the food of his table, the dwellings of his servants, the attendance of his ministers and their clothing, the cupbearers and their garments, and the burnt offerings which he sacrificed in the House of the Lord, there was no longer any spirit left in her for wonder.

5 And she said to the king: The report was true which I heard in my own land regarding your virtues and your wisdom.

6 I did not believe those who told me until I came myself, and my own eyes saw it, and I proved that barely half of your wisdom had been told to me; you have surpassed your fame with your virtues.

7 Blessed are your men, and blessed are your servants who stand before you at all times and hear your wisdom.

# C A P U T XI.
<note>Chapter 11</note>

*Rehoboam, while wishing to recover his father's entire kingdom by arms, is commanded by God through Shemaiah not to fight against Israel. After Rehoboam built many cities, the Levites and priests who had been rejected by Jeroboam, as well as other worshippers of God, flocked to him. Rehoboam, however, took many wives and concubines.*

<margin>3 Kings 12:21</margin>
1 When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he gathered the entire house of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand chosen fighting men, to battle against Israel and to return his kingdom to himself.
2 But the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, a man of God, saying:
3 "Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel who are in Judah and Benjamin:
4 > 'Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up, nor shall you fight against your brothers; let every man return to his house, for this thing has been done by my will.'"
When they heard the word of the Lord, they returned and did not go against Jeroboam.
5 Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built walled cities in Judah.
6 He built up Bethlehem, Etam, and Tekoa,
7 Beth-zur, Soko, and Adullam,
8 as well as Gath, Mareshah, and Ziph,

10 Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which were in Judah and Benjamin, most strongly fortified cities.

13 Moreover, the priests and Levites who were in all Israel came to him from all their territories,
14 leaving their suburbs and their possessions and crossing over to Judah and Jerusalem; this was because Jeroboam and his successors had cast them out so they could not perform the priesthood of the Lord.
15 Jeroboam had appointed for himself priests for the high places, and for the demons, and for the calves which he had made. <note>original: "dæmoniorum." This likely refers to the "goat-idols" or satyrs associated with the paganized worship established in the northern kingdom.</note>
16 But also from all the tribes of Israel, whoever had set their heart to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem

<column-break/>

to sacrifice their victims before the Lord, the God of their fathers.
17 And they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and confirmed Rehoboam the son of Solomon for three years; for they walked in the ways of David and Solomon for only those three years.
18 Rehoboam took as a wife Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth, the son of David; and also Abihail, the daughter of Eliab, the son of Jesse,
19 who bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
20 After her, he also took Maacah the daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
21 Now Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and concubines; for he had taken eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
22 He appointed Abijah, the son of Maacah, as the head—the leader over all his brothers—for he intended to make him king,
23 because he was wiser and more powerful than all his other sons; and he placed him in all the regions of Judah and Benjamin, and in all the walled cities; and he provided them with plenty of food, and he sought many wives for them.

# C A P U T XII.
<note>Chapter 12</note>

*On account of the sins of Rehoboam and the people of Judah, in the fifth year of his reign, God delivers them to Shishak, the king of Egypt. Having captured the most fortified cities of Judah, he plunders Jerusalem, taking away the treasures of the king and the temple, as well as the gold and silver shields, in place of which Rehoboam made bronze ones. When he died, his son Abijah succeeded him.*

1 When the kingdom of Rehoboam had been strengthened and made firm, he abandoned the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
2 In the fifth year of the reign of Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem (because they had sinned against the Lord)
3 with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen; nor was there any counting the common people who came with him from Egypt—namely, Libyans, Troglodytes, and Ethiopians. <note>original: "Troglodytæ." Traditionally understood as "cave-dwellers," referring to tribes from the Red Sea coast or Ethiopia.</note>
4 And he took the most fortified cities in Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.
5 Then Shemaiah the prophet went to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah, who had gathered in Jerusalem fleeing from Shishak, and he said to them:
> "Thus says the Lord: You have abandoned me, and so I have abandoned you into the hand of Shishak."
6 Then the leaders of Israel and the king were dismayed and said: "The Lord is just."
7 When the Lord saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying:
> "Because they have humbled themselves, I will not destroy them; I will give them a little help, and my fury shall not pour out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
8 > Nevertheless, they shall serve him, so that they may know the difference between my service and the service of a kingdom of the lands."
9 So Shishak king of Egypt departed from Jerusalem, having taken away the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king's house; he took everything with him, including the golden shields which Solomon had made.
10 In their place, the king made bronze ones and delivered them to the commanders of the shield-bearers, who guarded the entrance of the palace.

### CHAPTER XIII.

*Abijah, going to war against Jeroboam, discourages Jeroboam’s army from fighting against him, since they had God as their leader whom the others had cast away; trusting in the Lord, he emerges victorious, captures various cities, and from fourteen wives fathers thirty-eight children.*

<margin>1 Kings 15:2</margin>
1 In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah.
2 He reigned for three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Micaiah, the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

<margin>1 Kings 15:7</margin>
3 When Abijah entered into battle, he had an army of most valiant men, and four hundred thousand chosen men. Jeroboam, on the other hand, drew up his battle line with eight hundred thousand men, who were also chosen and most courageous for war.
4 Then Abijah stood upon Mount Zemaraim, which is in Ephraim, and said: "Listen to me, Jeroboam, and all Israel!
5 Do you not know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons by a <term>covenant of salt</term>? <note>original: "pactum salis." A covenant of salt refers to an unbreakable, perpetual agreement, as salt was a symbol of preservation and permanence.</note>
6 Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord.
7 And there were gathered to him worthless men, and sons of Belial <note>original: "filii Belial." This Hebrew term refers to wicked, lawless, or good-for-nothing people.</note>; and they prevailed against Rehoboam the son of Solomon. For Rehoboam was young <note>original: "rudis," meaning inexperienced or unrefined.</note> and faint-hearted, and could not resist them.
8 And now you say that you can resist the kingdom of the Lord, which they possess through the sons of David, because you have a great multitude of people and the golden calves which Jeroboam made for you as gods.

<margin>1 Kings 12:31</margin>
9 Have you not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites? And have you not made priests for yourselves, just like all the peoples of other lands? Whoever comes and consecrates his hand with a young bull from the herd and seven rams, becomes a priest for those who are not gods.
10 But as for us, the Lord is our God, and we have not forsaken Him; the priests who minister to the Lord are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites are in their proper order.

<column-break/>

11 They also offer burnt offerings to the Lord every single day, morning and evening, and incense prepared according to the precepts of the law; and the bread is set forth upon a most pure table; and we have the golden lampstand and its lamps, to be lit always in the evening. For we keep the commandments of the Lord our God, whom you have forsaken.
12 Therefore, in our army, God is the leader, along with His priests, who sound the trumpets and cry out against you. O children of Israel, do not fight against the Lord God of your fathers, for it will not profit you."
13 While he was saying these things, Jeroboam was setting an ambush from behind. And while he stood facing the enemy, he surrounded the unsuspecting men of Judah with his army.
14 And when Judah looked back, they saw the battle pressing upon them both from the front and from behind; and they cried out to the Lord, and the priests began to blow the trumpets.
15 And all the men of Judah raised a shout. And behold, as they shouted, God terrified Jeroboam and all Israel who stood against Abijah and Judah.
16 And the children of Israel fled before Judah, and God delivered them into their hands.
17 So Abijah and his people defeated them with a great slaughter; and five hundred thousand valiant men of Israel fell wounded.
18 Thus the children of Israel were humbled at that time, and the children of Judah were greatly strengthened, because they had trusted in the Lord, the God of their fathers.
19 And Abijah pursued Jeroboam as he fled, and he took his cities: Bethel and its villages, and Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephron also and its villages.
20 Nor was Jeroboam able to resist any longer in the days of Abijah; and the Lord struck him, and he died.
21 Therefore Abijah, having strengthened his empire, took fourteen wives, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
22 The rest of the acts of Abijah, and of his ways and works, are written most diligently in the Book of Iddo the Prophet.

### CHAPTER XIV.

<margin>1 Kings 15:8</margin>

3 And he broke the statues and cut down the sacred groves.
4 And he commanded Judah to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, and to follow the law and all the commandments.
5 And he removed the altars and shrines from all the cities of Judah, and he reigned in peace.
6 He also built fortified cities in Judah, because he was at rest, and no wars arose in his time, for the Lord granted him peace.
7 He said to Judah: "Let us build these cities..."

### CHAPTER XV.

*Azariah prophesies that Israel would be for a long time without the true worship of God, the priesthood, and the law; comforted by this prophet’s exhortation, Asa removes the filth of the idols and strips his own idolatrous mother of her authority; the people, meanwhile, swear an oath to serve God.*

1 Now Azariah the son of Obed, when the spirit of God came upon him,

2 Went out to meet Asa, and said to him: Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: The Lord is with you, because you have been with him. If you seek him, you will find him; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.

3 For many days shall pass in Israel without the true God, and without a teaching priest, and without the law.

4 And when they shall return in their distress to the Lord the God of Israel, and seek him, they shall find him.

5 In 그 time there shall be no peace for him that goes out or him that comes in, but terrors on every side among all the inhabitants of the lands.

6 For nation shall fight against nation, and city against city, because the Lord will trouble them with every distress.

7 You, therefore, be strengthened, and let not your hands be weakened; for there shall be a reward for your work.

8 When Asa had heard these words, namely the 

<column-break/>

prophecy of Azariah the son of Obed the prophet, he was encouraged, and he took away the idols from all the land of Judah, and from Benjamin, and from the cities of mount Ephraim which he had captured; and he dedicated the altar of the Lord which was before the porch of the Lord.

9 And he gathered together all Judah and Benjamin, and the strangers with them from Ephraim, from Manasseh, and from Simeon; for many had fled to him from Israel, seeing that the Lord his God was with him.

10 And when they had come to Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa,

11 They sacrificed to the Lord on that day, from the spoils and the prey which they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand rams.

12 And he entered according to custom to strengthen the covenant, that they should seek the Lord the God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul.

13 And if anyone, he said, does not seek the Lord the God of Israel, let him die, from the least to the greatest, from man even to woman.

14 And they swore an oath to the Lord with a loud voice, with shouting, and with the sound of trumpets, and with the blast of horns,

15 All those who were in Judah with rejoicing; for with all their heart they swore, and with their whole will they sought him, and they found him; and the Lord gave them rest on every side.

16 Moreover, he deposed Maachah, the mother of King Asa, from her royal authority, because she had made an idol of Priapus <note>original: "simulacrum Priapi." In the Latin Vulgate, "Priapus" is used to describe a shameful or fertility-related idol, likely an Asherah pole or similar pagan image.</note> in a grove; all of which he crushed, and breaking it into pieces, he burned it at the brook Kidron.

17 But the high places were left in Israel; yet the heart of Asa was perfect all his days.

18 And those things which his father had vowed, and he himself, he brought into the house of the Lord: silver, and gold, and various vessels of furniture.

19 And there was no war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.

### CHAPTER XVI.

*While Baasha, king of Israel, fights against Asa, Asa calls upon Ben-hadad, king of Syria, for help; he casts Hanani the prophet into stocks for rebuking him for this; and being tormented by a pain in his feet, putting his hope in the skill of physicians, he dies in the forty-first year of his reign.*

1 In the thirty-sixth year of his reign, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built a wall around Ramah, so that no one could safely go out or come in from the kingdom of Asa.

2 Then Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasures of the house of the Lord, and from the king’s treasures, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Syria, who dwelt in Damascus, saying:

3 There is a league between me and you, as my father and your father had an agreement; for which reason I have sent you silver and gold, that you may break the league which you have with Baasha king of Israel, and make him withdraw from me.

4 When this was known, Ben-hadad sent the captains of his armies to the cities of Israel; and they struck Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-maim, and all the walled cities of Naphtali.

5 When Baasha heard this, he ceased building Ramah, and interrupted his work.

### CHAPTER XVII.

*Pious Jehoshaphat succeeds his father Asa, becoming powerful in wealth and arms; he sends teachers of the law of God throughout all Judah; his commanders are listed along with the number of soldiers under them.*

1 And Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place, and he grew strong against Israel.
2 He stationed companies of soldiers in all the walled cities of Judah. He also placed garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim which his father Asa had captured.
3 And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of David his father. He did not put his hope in the Baals <note>original: "Baalim" - the plural form of Baal, referring to the various local pagan deities of the region.</note>,
4 But in the God of his father; and he walked according to His commandments, and not according to the sins of Israel.
5 Therefore the Lord established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat; and he attained infinite riches and great glory.
6 And when his heart had taken courage in the ways of the Lord, he also took away the high places and the sacred groves from Judah.
7 In the third year of his reign, he sent some of his princes—Benhail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah—to teach in the cities of Judah.
8 And with them he sent the Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah; and with them the priests Elishama and Jehoram.

<column-break/>

9 And they taught the people in Judah, having the book of the Law of the Lord with them; they went about through all the cities of Judah and instructed the people.
10 Thus the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Judah, so that they did not dare to make war against Jehoshaphat.
11 Moreover, the Philistines brought gifts and silver as tribute to Jehoshaphat, and the Arabs brought cattle: seven thousand seven hundred rams, and as many he-goats.
12 So Jehoshaphat grew and was magnified to a great height, and he built houses like towers and walled cities in Judah.
13 He prepared many works in the cities of Judah. There were also fighting men and robust soldiers in Jerusalem,
14 Whose number, according to their houses and families, was this: In Judah, the commanders of the army were Adnah the leader, and with him three hundred thousand most valiant men.
15 After him was Jehohanan the prince, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand.
16 After him also was Amasias the son of Zichri, consecrated to the Lord, and with him two hundred thousand brave men.
17 Following him was Eliada, robust in battle, and with him two hundred thousand men who held the bow and shield.
18 After him also was Jozabad, and with him one hundred and eighty thousand ready soldiers.
19 All these were at the hand of the king, besides those whom he had placed in the walled cities throughout all Judah.

### CHAPTER XVIII.

*Jehoshaphat, joined in alliance with the impious Ahab by the marriage of his son Jehoram to Ahab’s daughter, goes up with him against Ramoth-Gilead. Four hundred and fifty <note>Though the header says 450, verse 5 mentions 400.</note> false prophets promise victory, but Micaiah, prophesying the opposite, is imprisoned; however, Ahab is killed in battle according to Micaiah’s prophecy.*

3 And Ahab, the king of Israel, said to Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah: Will you come with me to Ramoth-Gilead? He replied: As I am, so are you; as your people are, so are my people; we will be with you in the war.
4 And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: I pray you, consult the word of the Lord for the present.
5 Therefore, the king of Israel gathered together four hundred prophets and said to them: Should we go to Ramoth-Gilead to fight, or should we remain quiet? They said: Go up, and God will deliver it into the hand of the king.
6 But Jehoshaphat said: Is there not also a prophet of the Lord here, so that we may inquire of Him as well?

34 And the battle ended on that day; however, the king of Israel stood in his chariot against the Syrians until evening, and he died as the sun was setting.

## CHAPTER XX.

*While the Ammonites, Moabites, and Syrians rise up against Jehoshaphat, he, having proclaimed a fast, flees as a suppliant to God together with his people; and thus, being delivered from them as they slaughter one another, he collects the spoils: but for entering into a treaty with the wicked Ahaziah, he is corrected by the prophet and punished by God.*

1 After these things, the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and with them some of the Ammonites, gathered against Jehoshaphat to fight against him.
2 And messengers came and told Jehoshaphat, saying: A great multitude has come against you from those places which are across the sea, and from Syria, and behold, they stand in Hazazon-tamar, which is En-Gedi.
3 Then Jehoshaphat, struck with fear, devoted himself entirely to entreating the Lord, and he proclaimed a fast for all of Judah.
4 And Judah was gathered together to pray to the Lord; moreover, everyone came from their cities to beseech him.
5 And when Jehoshaphat stood in the midst of the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord before the new court,
6 He said: O Lord God of our fathers, you are God in heaven, and you rule over all the kingdoms of the nations; in your hand is strength and power, nor can anyone resist you.
7 Did you not, our God, kill all the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the seed of Abraham your friend forever?
8 And they dwelt in it, and built a sanctuary there for your name, saying:
9 If evils fall upon us—the sword of judgment, pestilence, or famine—we will stand before this house in your presence, in which your name is invoked; and we will cry out to you in our tribulations, and you will hear us and save us.

12 O our God, will you not then judge them? In us, indeed, there is not enough strength to resist this multitude that rushes upon us. But since we do not know what we ought to do, this alone remains for us: to turn our eyes toward you.
13 And all of Judah stood before the Lord with their little ones, and their wives, and their children.

24 Moreover, when Judah came to the watchtower that looks out over the wilderness, they saw from afar the whole region for miles around full of corpses, and not a single person remained who had been able to escape death.
25 Jehoshaphat then came, and all the people with him, to carry away the spoils of the dead; and they found among the bodies various furnishings, as well as clothes and most precious vessels, and they plundered them, so that they could not carry everything, nor could they take away the spoils for three days because of the greatness of the prey.
26 On the fourth day, however, they gathered in the Valley of Blessing; <note>original: "valle Benedictionis," often referred to as the Valley of Berachah.</note> for because they blessed the Lord there, they called that place the Valley of Blessing even to this present day.

28 And they entered Jerusalem with harps, and lyres, and trumpets, into the house of the Lord.
29 And the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the Lord had fought against the enemies of Israel.

18 And after all these things, the Lord struck him with an incurable disease of the bowels.
19 And as day followed day, and the spans of time rolled on, the circle of two years was completed; and thus, consumed by a long wasting away so that he even voided his own intestines, he lost his life along with his health. He died of a most terrible infirmity, and the people did not perform a funeral fire for him <note>A traditional honor involving the burning of spices and incense for a deceased king.</note> according to the custom of burning, as they had done for his ancestors.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

*Joash, during the life of Jehoiada, was good and pious, and ordered money to be gathered for the repairs <note>Latin: *sartatecta*, a legal term referring to keeping a building "covered and tight," or in good repair.</note> of the temple. Then, after Jehoiada's death, he became impious and ordered the killing of Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada. In the following year, Judah and Jerusalem were plundered by the Syrians, and Joash was killed by his own servants.*

1 Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.

26 Those who conspired against him were Zabad, the son of Shimeath an Ammonitess, and Jozabad, the son of Shimrith a Moabitess.
27 Now his sons, and the great sum of money that had been gathered under him, and the restoration of the house of God, are written more diligently in the Book of Kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

**35** There were many burnt offerings, with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings for the burnt offerings; and the service of the house of the Lord was completed.
**36** And Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced because the ministry of the Lord had been fulfilled; for it had been decided that this should be done suddenly.

->**C H A P T E R XXX.**<-
---

**H**ezekiah also sent to all Israel and Judah, and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh <note>Northern tribes that were part of the separate Kingdom of Israel</note>, that they should come to the House of the Lord in Jerusalem and keep the Passover <note>original: "Phase," the Latinized form of the Hebrew "Pesach"</note> for the Lord God of Israel.
**2** For the king, the leaders, and the whole assembly of Jerusalem had taken counsel and decreed to keep the Passover in the second month.
**3** For they could not keep it at the proper time <note>The first month, Nisan</note> because enough priests had not been sanctified and the people had not yet gathered in Jerusalem.
**4** And the proposal pleased the king and the whole multitude.
**5** They decreed to send messengers throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that they should come and keep the Passover to the Lord God of Israel in Jerusalem; for many had not done so as prescribed in the law.
**6** And the runners went out with the letters by command of the king and his leaders throughout all Israel and Judah, according to what the king had ordered, proclaiming: "Children of Israel, return to the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and He will return to the remnant that escaped the hand of the king of the Assyrians.
**7** Do not be like your fathers and brothers who withdrew from the Lord God of their fathers, who gave them up to destruction, as you yourselves see.
**8** Do not stiffen your necks as your fathers did; yield yourselves to the Lord and come to His sanctuary, which He has sanctified forever. Serve the Lord the God of your fathers, and the wrath of His fury will be turned away from you.
**9** For if you return to the Lord, your brothers and children will find mercy before the masters who led them away captive, and they will return to this land; for the Lord your God is pious and clement, and He will not turn His face from you if you return to Him."
**10** So the runners went swiftly from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh as far as Zebulun, but they mocked and sneered at them.
**11** Nevertheless, some men from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun, following the counsel, came to Jerusalem.

### C H A P T E R XXXI.

*The people demolish idols and sacred groves in Judah and Ephraim; Hezekiah organizes the priests and Levites into their orders of ministry; the people offer most abundantly, and storehouses are established to preserve and distribute the offerings to the Levite lineage.*

**1** When these things had been duly celebrated, all Israel who were found in the cities of Judah went out and broke the idols, cut down the sacred groves, demolished the high places, and destroyed the altars, not only throughout all Judah and Benjamin, but also in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they were utterly overturned; then all the children of Israel returned to their own possessions and cities.
**2** And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites by their groups, each man in his own office—both the priests and the Levites—for burnt offerings and peace offerings, to minister, to give thanks, and to sing praise within the gates of the camp of the Lord.
**3** The king’s portion was also set, that from his own substance burnt offerings should be offered every morning

<column-break/>

and evening. Also on the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the other solemnities, just as it is written in the law of Moses.
**4** He also commanded the people dwelling in Jerusalem to give portions to the priests and the Levites, so that they might devote themselves to the law of the Lord.
**5** When this command reached the ears of the multitude, the children of Israel offered the firstfruits of grain, wine, oil, and honey; and they offered tithes <note>A tenth part of one's produce given as a tax for religious purposes</note> of everything that the ground brings forth.
**6** Moreover, the children of Israel and Judah who dwelt in the cities of Judah offered tithes of oxen and sheep, and the tithes of holy things which they had vowed to the Lord their God; and carrying everything, they made many heaps.
**7** In the third month they began to lay the foundations of the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished them.
**8** And when Hezekiah and his princes came in and saw the heaps, they blessed the Lord and the people of Israel.
**9** And Hezekiah questioned the priests and Levites as to why the heaps lay there in such a way.
**10** Azariah, the chief priest from the line of Zadok, answered him, saying: "Since the firstfruits began to be offered in the house of the Lord, we have eaten and been satisfied, and many things remain, because the Lord has blessed his people; this great abundance which you see is what is left over."
**11** Therefore Hezekiah commanded that they prepare storehouses <note>original: "horrea"; granaries or treasuries</note> in the house of the Lord. And when they had done so,
**12** They brought in the firstfruits, the tithes, and whatever they had vowed, faithfully. Their overseer was Cononiah the Levite, and Shimei his brother was second,
**13** And after him Jahiel, Azariah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were overseers under the hands of Cononiah and Shimei his brother, by the command of King Hezekiah and Azariah, the high priest of the house of God, to whom all things pertained.
**14** But Kore, the son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper of the east gate, was in charge of the things that were voluntarily offered to the Lord, and the firstfruits and the things consecrated for the Holy of Holies.
**15** And under his care were Eden, Benjamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, to faithfully distribute portions to their brothers, both small and great:
**16** Excepting the males from three years old and upward, to all who entered the temple of the Lord, and whatever was required for each day’s ministry and observances according to their divisions,
**17** To the priests by their families, and to the Levites from the twentieth year and upward, by their orders and groups,
**18** And to the whole multitude, including their wives and their children of both sexes, food was faithfully provided from those things which had been sanctified.
**19** Also for the sons of Aaron in the fields and the suburbs of every city, men were appointed to distribute portions to every male among the priests and the Levites.
**20** Thus Hezekiah did all that we have said throughout all Judah; and he worked what was good, right, and true before the Lord his God.

### CHAPTER XXXII.

*While Sennacherib invades Judah and blasphemes the God of heaven, Hezekiah encourages the people to trust in the Lord, from whom the enemy tries to turn him away with threats and blasphemies; however, while Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, an angel destroys the army of Sennacherib, who, fleeing, is killed by his sons; then Hezekiah, lifted up by too much success, offends God, and is succeeded by his wicked son Manasseh.*

<margin>2 Kings 18:13; 2 Chronicles 32; Isaiah Chapter 36.</margin>
**1** After these things and this kind of truth <note>original: "veritatem"; referring to Hezekiah's faithful and sincere reforms</note>, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians came and, entering Judah, besieged the fortified cities, wishing to take them for himself.
**2** When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come, and that the whole force of the war was turned against Jerusalem,
**3** He took counsel with the princes and the strongest men to stop up the heads of the springs that were outside the city; and when everyone's opinion agreed with this,
**4** He gathered a great multitude, and they stopped up all the springs and the brook that flowed through the middle of the land, saying: "Lest the kings of the Assyrians come and find an abundance of water."
**5** He also acted industriously and built up the entire wall that had been broken down, and raised towers upon it, and another wall outside; and he restored Millo <note term="Millo">A term for a specific rampart or fortification within the City of David, likely a terrace or filled-in earthwork</note> in the city of David, and prepared weapons of every kind and shields.
**6** And he appointed captains of the warriors in the army, and called them all together in the street of the gate of the city, and spoke to their hearts, saying:
**7** "Act manfully and be strengthened; do not fear, nor be terrified of the king of the Assyrians and the whole multitude that is with him: for there are many more with us than with him.
**8** For with him is an arm of flesh; with us is the Lord our God, who is our helper and fights for us." And the people were encouraged by these words of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
**9** After these things were done, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians sent his servants to Jerusalem (for he himself with his whole army was besieging Lachis) to Hezekiah king of Judah, and to all the people who were in the city, saying:
**10** "Thus says Sennacherib king of the Assyrians: In whom do you have confidence, that you sit besieged in Jerusalem?
**11** Does Hezekiah deceive you, to deliver you to death by famine and thirst, asserting that the Lord your God will deliver you from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
**12** Is this not the same Hezekiah who destroyed his high places and altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying: 'You shall adore before one altar, and upon it you shall burn incense'?
**13** Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Have the gods of the nations and of all the lands been able to deliver their region from my hand?
**14** Who is there among all the gods of the nations which

my fathers destroyed, who was able to rescue his people from my hand, that your God should also be able to rescue you from this hand?

**16** And his servants spoke many other things against the Lord God, and against Hezekiah his servant.
**17** He also wrote letters full of blasphemy against the Lord God of Israel, and spoke against him: "Just as the gods of the other nations could not deliver their people from my hand, so also the God of Hezekiah will not be able to rescue his people from this hand."
**18** Furthermore, they shouted with a great cry in the Jewish language <note>Referring to Hebrew, the local language of Judah, intended to incite fear in the common people listening on the walls</note> against the people sitting on the walls of Jerusalem, to terrify them and take the city.
**19** And they spoke against the God of Jerusalem, as they did against the gods of the peoples of the earth, the works of the hands of men.
**20** Therefore Hezekiah the king, and Isaiah the son of Amoz the prophet, prayed against this blasphemy, and cried out even to heaven.

**26** And he was humbled afterwards, because his heart had been exalted, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and therefore the wrath of the Lord did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
**27** Now Hezekiah was rich and very famous, and gathered for himself many treasures of silver and gold and precious stones, spices, and arms of every kind, and vessels of great price.

**6** and, having been sanctified, slaughter the <term>Passover lamb</term> <note>original: "Phase"; the Latin Vulgate term for the Hebrew "Pesach" or Passover</note>. Prepare your brothers as well, so that they may act according to the words which the Lord spoke through the hand of Moses."
**7** Furthermore, Josiah gave to all the people who were found there for the Passover solemnity lambs and kids from the flocks, and thirty thousand other cattle, as well as three thousand oxen—all these from the king’s own substance.
**8** His leaders also offered what they had vowed of their own free will, both to the people and to the priests and Levites. Moreover, Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the princes of the house of the Lord, gave to the priests for the Passover two thousand six hundred mixed cattle and three hundred oxen.
**9** Then Konaniah, and Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, as well as Hashabiah, Jehiel, and Jozabad, the princes of the Levites, gave to the other Levites five thousand cattle and five hundred oxen for the celebration of the Passover.
**10** The service was prepared, and the priests stood in their offices, with the Levites in their divisions, according to the king’s command.
**11** And the Passover lamb was sacrificed; the priests sprinkled the blood with their hands, and the Levites flayed the skins of the burnt offerings.
**12** They set these aside to give to the various houses and families to be offered to the Lord, as it is written in the Book of Moses; they did the same with the oxen.
**13** And they roasted the Passover lamb over the fire, according to what is written in the law; but the peace offerings they boiled in cauldrons, kettles, and pots, and distributed them quickly to all the people.
**14** Afterward, they prepared for themselves and for the priests, for the priests were occupied in offering burnt sacrifices and fat until nightfall; therefore the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron, last of all.
**15** Moreover, the singers, the sons of Asaph, stood in their order according to the command of David, and Asaph, and Heman, and Jeduthun, the king’s prophets. The gatekeepers also watched at each gate, so that they did not depart from their service for even a moment; for this reason, their brothers the Levites prepared food for them.
**16** Thus all the service of the Lord was duly completed on that day, to keep the Passover and to offer burnt sacrifices upon the altar of the Lord, according to the command of King Josiah.
**17** And the children of Israel who were present kept the Passover at that time, and the feast of unleavened bread for seven days.
**18** There was no Passover like this in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; nor did any of all the kings of Israel keep such a Passover as Josiah did, with the priests, the Levites, all Judah,

<column-break/>

and Israel that was present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
**19** This Passover was celebrated in the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign.
<margin>4 Kings 23:29 <note>In modern Bibles, this is 2 Kings 23:29</note></margin>
**20** After Josiah had restored the temple, Necho, King of Egypt, came up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.
**21** But Necho sent messengers to him, saying: "What is there between me and you, O King of Judah? I do not come against you today, but I fight against another house, to which God has commanded me to go in haste. Cease acting against God, who is with me, lest He destroy you."
**22** Josiah would not turn back, but prepared for war against him, and did not listen to the words of Necho which came from the mouth of God; instead, he went to fight in the plain of Megiddo.
<margin>† Zechariah 12:11</margin>
**23** And there he was wounded by archers, and he said to his servants: "Carry me out of the battle, for I am severely wounded."
**24** They transferred him from that chariot into another chariot that followed him in the royal fashion, and they carried him to Jerusalem. There he died and was buried in the mausoleum of his fathers, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned him.
**25** Jeremiah especially lamented him; and all the male and female singers, to this very day, repeat their lamentations over Josiah; it has become like a law in Israel. Behold, it is said to be written in the Book of Lamentations.
**26** Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and his deeds of mercy, which were commanded by the law of the Lord,
**27** and his works, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

->CHAPTER ONE.<-

->*Cyrus, after the seventy years of Babylonian captivity were completed, being divinely inspired, releases the Israelites from captivity and restores 5,400 vessels of Solomon’s temple, granting permission for the temple’s reconstruction.*<-

<margin>2 Chronicles 36:22; Jeremiah 25:12 & 29:10</margin>
In the first year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, so that the word of the Lord from the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of the Persians: and he sent a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, even in writing, saying:
**2** "Thus says Cyrus, king of the Persians: The Lord God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has commanded me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judea.
**3** Who is there among you of all His people? May his God be with him. Let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judea, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel; He is the God who is in Jerusalem.
**4** And let all the rest, in all places wherever they live, be helped by the men of their place with silver and gold, and with goods and cattle,

<column-break/>

besides that which they offer voluntarily for the temple of God, which is in Jerusalem."
**5** Then the chiefs of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin arose, along with the priests and the Levites, and everyone whose spirit God had stirred up, to go up to build the temple of the Lord, which was in Jerusalem.
**6** And all those who were around them helped their hands with vessels of silver and gold, with goods and livestock, and with furnishings, besides those things which they had offered freely.
**7** King Cyrus also brought out the vessels of the temple of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and had placed in the temple of his god.
**8** Cyrus, king of the Persians, brought them out by the hand of Mithridates the son of Gazabar, and numbered them out to Sheshbazzar <note>original: "Sassabasar"</note>, the prince of Judah.
**9** And this is their number: thirty golden basins, a thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives, thirty golden cups,
**10** four hundred and ten silver cups of a second sort, and a thousand other vessels.
**11** All the vessels of gold and silver were five thousand four hundred: Sheshbazzar took them all, with those who returned from the <term>transmigration</term> <note>original: "transmigratione"; the movement or exile of the people from Babylon back to Jerusalem.</note> from Babylon to Jerusalem.

### CHAPTER IV.

*The Samaritan enemies of Israel, who had been sent from Assyria to inhabit the cities of Samaria, hinder the restoration of the temple and the city because they were not admitted to build with them, and they manage to halt the work until the second year of Darius.*

1 Now the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple to the Lord God of Israel;
2 And approaching Zerubbabel and the

<column-break/>

heads of the families, they said to them: "Let us build with you, for like you, we seek your God; behold, we have sacrificed victims to him since the days of Esarhaddon <note>original: "Asor Haddan"</note> king of Assyria, who brought us here."
3 But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of the families of Israel, said to them: "It is not for you and us together to build a house to our God, but we ourselves alone will build to the Lord our God, as Cyrus the king of the Persians has commanded us."
4 It happened then, that the people of the land discouraged the people of Judah, and troubled them in their building.
5 And they hired counselors against them to frustrate their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
6 And in the reign of Ahasuerus <note>original: "Assueri," likely referring to Xerxes I</note>, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
7 And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam <note>original: "Beselam"</note>, Mithredath, and Tabeel, and the rest who were in their council, wrote to Artaxerxes king of the Persians; and the letter of accusation was written in Aramaic <note>original: "Syriace"</note>, and was read in the Aramaic language.
8 Rehum the chancellor <note>original: "Beelteem," a title transliterated from Aramaic</note> and Shimshai <note>original: "Samsai"</note> the scribe wrote a letter from Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes in this manner:
9 Rehum the chancellor, and Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their counselors, the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Dehavites, and the Elamites,
10 And the rest of the nations whom the great and glorious Asenaphar <note>Commonly identified as Ashurbanipal.</note> brought over and settled in the cities of Samaria, and in the rest of the regions across the river in peace.
11 (This is the copy of the letter which they sent to him): To King Artaxerxes, your servants, the men who are across the river, send greetings.
12 Be it known to the king, that the Jews who came up from you to us have come to Jerusalem, that rebellious and wicked city, which they are rebuilding, setting up its walls and repairing the foundations.
13 Now therefore be it known to the king, that if this city is rebuilt and its walls restored, they will not pay tribute, nor taxes, nor annual revenues, and this loss will fall upon the kings.
14 Now because we eat the salt of the palace <note>A common idiom meaning they were in the king's service or supported by him.</note>, and because we think it unlawful to see the king’s harm, we have therefore sent and informed the king,
15 So that you may search in the books of the histories of your fathers, and you shall find it written in the records; and you shall know that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that seditions have been stirred up in it from olden times; for which cause the city itself was destroyed.
16 We inform the king that if that city is rebuilt and its walls restored, you will have no possession across the river.
17 The king sent word to Rehum the chancellor, and Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest who were in their council, the inhabitants of Samaria and the others across the river, saying: Greetings and peace.
18 The accusation which you sent to us has been clearly read before me,
19 And I have given the command, and they have searched, and they have found that this city from olden times has rebelled against kings, and seditions and battles are stirred up in it;

20 For there were very powerful kings in Jerusalem, who also ruled over all the region across the river: they also received tribute, taxes, and revenue.
21 Now therefore, hear the decree: Prohibit those men, so that the city is not rebuilt, until perhaps a command is issued by me.
22 Take care that you do not fulfill this negligently, lest the evil gradually grow against the kings.
23 Therefore, a copy of King Artaxerxes' edict was read before Rehum, Beeltetham, and Shimshai <note>original: "Samsai"</note> the scribe, and their counselors: and they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and prohibited them by force and strength.
24 Then the work on the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was interrupted, and it was not done until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of the Persians.

### CHAPTER V.

*By the exhortation of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, the building of the temple is resumed, despite the futile efforts of the officials across the river in Samaria—appointed by the king of the Assyrians—to stop it.*

1 Now the prophet Haggai <note>original: "Aggæus"</note> and Zechariah <note>original: "Zacharias"</note> the son of Iddo <note>original: "Addo"</note> prophesied to the Jews who were in Judea and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel.
2 Then Zerubbabel <note>original: "Zorobabel"</note> son of Shealtiel <note>original: "Salathiel"</note>, and Jeshua <note>original: "Josue"</note> son of Jozadak <note>original: "Josedec"</note>, rose up and began to build the temple of God in Jerusalem, and with them were the prophets of God helping them.
3 At that same time, Tattenai <note>original: "Thathanai"</note>, who was the governor <note>original: "dux"</note> across the river, came to them, with Shethar-Bozenai <note>original: "Stharbuzanai"</note> and their counselors; and they spoke to them thus: "Who gave you counsel to build this house and to restore its walls?"
4 To which we answered them, [telling them] what the names of the men were who were the authors of that building.
5 But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, and they could not stop them. And it pleased them that the matter be referred to Darius, and then they would satisfy the king against that accusation.
6 A copy of the letter which Tattenai, the governor of the region across the river, and Shethar-Bozenai, and his advisors the Apharsachites <note>original: "Arphasachæi"</note> who were across the river, sent to King Darius.
7 The message which they had sent to him was written thus: "To King Darius, all peace."
8 "Be it known to the king that we went to the province of Judea, to the house of the great God, which is being built with unpolished stone, and timber is being placed in the walls; and that work is being diligently constructed, and it grows in their hands."
9 "Therefore we questioned those elders, and spoke to them thus: 'Who gave you the power to build this house and to restore these walls?'"
10 "We also asked them for their names, so that we might report them to you; and we wrote down the names of those men who are the leaders among them."
11 "And they answered us with this kind of speech, saying: 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the temple that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel had built and constructed.'"
12 "But after our fathers provoked the God of heaven to anger, he delivered <column-break/> them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar <note>original: "Nabuchodonosor"</note>, the Chaldean king of Babylon; he also destroyed this house, and carried its people away to Babylon."
13 "But in the first year of Cyrus, king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree that this house of God should be built."
14 "For King Cyrus also brought out from the temple of Babylon the gold and silver vessels of the temple of God—which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple that was in Jerusalem and carried into the temple of Babylon—and they were given to one named Sheshbazzar <note>original: "Sassabafar"</note>, whom he also appointed as governor."
15 "And he said to him: 'Take these vessels, and go, and place them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be built in its place.'"
16 "Then that Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the temple of God in Jerusalem; and from that time until now it is being built, and it is not yet completed."
17 "Now therefore, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king's library, which is in Babylon, whether it was indeed commanded by King Cyrus that the house of God in Jerusalem should be built; and let the king's will concerning this matter be sent to us."

### CHAPTER VI.

*King Darius orders the decree of Cyrus regarding the construction of the temple—found in his library—to be carried out with the expenses provided; the temple is completed in the sixth year of Darius and dedicated with great joy and many victims, and the Passover is celebrated for seven days.*

1 Then King Darius gave a command; and they searched in the library of books which were stored in Babylon.
2 And in Ecbatana <note>original: "Ecbatanis"</note>, which is a fortress in the province of Media, a scroll was found, and in it such a record was written:
3 "In the first year of King Cyrus: King Cyrus decreed that the house of God which is in Jerusalem should be built, in the place where they offer sacrifices, and that they should lay foundations supporting a height of sixty cubits, and a width of sixty cubits,"
4 "Three rows of unpolished stones, and then rows of new timber; the expenses shall be given from the king's house."
5 "Also let the gold and silver vessels of the temple of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple of Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, be returned and brought back to the temple in Jerusalem to their place, which were also placed in the temple of God."
6 "Now therefore, Tattenai, governor of the region across the river, Shethar-Bozenai, and your counselors the Apharsachites <note>original: "Apharsachæi"</note>, who are across the river, withdraw far from them,"
7 "And let that temple of God be built by the governor of the Jews and by their elders, so that they may build that house of God in its place."
8 "Moreover, a command has been issued by me as to what must be done by those elders of the Jews, so that the house of God may be built: namely, that from the king’s treasury—that is, from the taxes collected from the region across the river—the expenses be diligently given to those men, lest the work be hindered."
9 "And if it should be necessary, let young bulls, lambs, and kids for a burnt offering to the God of heaven, [as well as] wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the rite of the priests who are in Jerusalem, be given to them day by day, so that there may be no complaint in anything."

### CHAPTER VII.

*Ezra the scribe, having gathered companions, goes up to Jerusalem with the king's edict and great gifts, to teach the law of God and to govern the people; the king's edict is recorded.*

1 Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, Ezra <note>original: "Esdras"</note> the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,

4 Son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
5 Son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest from the beginning.
6 This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a skilled scribe <note>original: "scriba velox," literally a swift or quick scribe</note> in the law of Moses, which the Lord God had given to Israel: and the king granted him

19 The vessels also, which are given to you for the ministry of the house of your God, deliver in the sight of God in Jerusalem.

21 And by me. I, Artaxerxes the king, have established and decreed to all the keepers of the public chest who are across the river, that whatever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, shall ask of you, you shall give it without delay,
22 Even to a hundred talents of silver, and to a hundred cores <note>term: "coros," a large dry measure</note> of wheat, and to a hundred baths <note>term: "batos," a liquid measure</note> of wine, and to a hundred baths of oil, and salt without measure.
