## CHAPTER VIII.

->*An account of those who went up from Babylon with Ezra: who, having declared a fast to pray to God for guidance on their journey, arrived safely in Jerusalem, and brought the vessels they carried with them into the temple along with sacrifices.*<-

**1 These** then are the leaders of the families, and the genealogy of those who went up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
**2** Of the sons of Phinehas <note>original: "Phinees"</note>, Gershom. Of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel. Of the sons of David, Hattush <note>original: "Hattus"</note>.
**3** Of the sons of Shecaniah <note>original: "Secheniæ"</note>, and the sons of Parosh <note>original: "Pharos"</note>, Zechariah <note>original: "Zacharias"</note>: and with him were counted one hundred and fifty men.
**4** Of the sons of Pahath-Moab <note>original: "Phahath Moab"</note>, Eliehoenai <note>original: "Elioenai"</note> son of Zerahiah <note>original: "Zarehe"</note>, and with him two hundred men.
**5** Of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel <note>original: "Ezechiel"</note>, and with him three hundred men.
**6** Of the sons of Adin <note>original: "Adan"</note>, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men.
**7** Of the sons of Elam <note>original: "Alam"</note>, Jeshaiah <note>original: "Isaias"</note> son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men.
**8** Of the sons of Shephatiah <note>original: "Saphariæ"</note>, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men.
**9** Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah <note>original: "Obedia"</note> son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen men.
**10** Of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah <note>original: "Josphiæ"</note>, and with him one hundred and sixty men.
**11** Of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men.
**12** Of the sons of Azgad <note>original: "Azgae"</note>, Johanan son of Hakkatan <note>original: "Eccetan"</note>, and with him one hundred and ten men.
**13** Of the sons of Adonikam, who were the last: and these are their names: Eliphelet, and Jeiel <note>original: "Jehiel"</note>, and Shemaiah <note>original: "Samaias"</note>, and with them sixty men.
**14** Of the sons of Bigvai <note>original: "Begui"</note>, Uthai and Zaccur <note>original: "Zachur"</note>, and with them seventy men.
**15** And I gathered them at the river that runs toward Ahava, and we stayed there three days: and I searched among the people and the priests for the sons of Levi, and found none there.
**16** Therefore I sent Eliezer, and Ariel, and Shemaiah, and Elnathan, and Jarib, and another Elnathan, and Nathan, and Zechariah, and Meshullam <note>original: "Mosollam"</note>, who were leaders: and Joiarib, and Elnathan, who were wise men.
**17** And I sent them to Iddo <note>original: "Eddo"</note>, who is the chief at the place of Casiphia <note>original: "Chasphiæ"</note>, and I put words in their mouths to speak to Iddo and his brothers, the Nethinim <note>original: "Nathinæos," meaning temple servants</note>, at the place of Casiphia, so they would bring us ministers for the house of our God.
**18** And by the good hand of our God upon us, they brought us a very learned man from the

<column-break/>

sons of Mahli <note>original: "Moholi"</note> son of Levi son of Israel, and Sherebiah <note>original: "Sarabiam"</note> with his sons and his brothers, eighteen in all,
**19** And Hashabiah <note>original: "Hasabiam"</note>, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, and his brothers and his sons, twenty in all:
**20** And of the Nethinim, whom David and the princes had appointed for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty Nethinim: all of these were called by their names.
**21** And I proclaimed a fast there by the river Ahava, that we might afflict ourselves before the Lord our God, and seek from him a straight path for us, and for our children, and for all our substance.
**22** For I was ashamed to ask the king for an escort and horsemen to defend us from the enemy on the way: because we had told the king: "The hand of our God is upon all who seek him in goodness: but his power, and his strength, and his wrath are against all who forsake him."
**23** So we fasted, and petitioned our God for this: and it happened prosperously for us.
**24** And I set apart twelve of the leaders of the priests, Sherebiah, and Hashabiah, and with them ten of their brothers.
**25** And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold, and the consecrated vessels of the house of our God, which the king and his counselors, and his princes, and all the Israelites who were found there had offered:
**26** And I weighed into their hands six hundred and fifty talents <term>talent: a large unit of weight, roughly 75 pounds</term> of silver, and one hundred silver vessels, and one hundred talents of gold:
**27** And twenty golden bowls, weighing a thousand darics <note>original: "solidos," likely referring to the Persian gold coin</note>, and two vessels of the finest polished bronze, as beautiful as gold.
**28** And I said to them: "You are the holy ones of the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and gold are a voluntary offering to the Lord the God of our fathers:
**29** Watch and guard them until you weigh them before the leaders of the priests, and the Levites, and the heads of the families of Israel in Jerusalem, into the treasury of the house of the Lord."
**30** So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold, and the vessels, to carry them to Jerusalem into the house of our God.
**31** Then we set out from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to proceed to Jerusalem: and the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of the enemy and from those lying in wait along the way.
**32** And we came to Jerusalem, and stayed there for three days.
**33** On the fourth day, the silver, and the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the house of our God by the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, and with him Eleazar the son of Phinehas, and with them Jozabad the son of Jeshua <note>original: "Josue"</note>, and Noadiah the son of Binnui <note>original: "Bennoi"</note>, the Levites,
**34** According to the number and weight of everything: and all the weight was recorded at that time.
**35** Moreover, the children of the exile who had come out of captivity offered burnt offerings <note>original: "holocautomata"</note> to the God of Israel: twelve calves for all the people of Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve he-goats for sin: all as a burnt offering to the Lord.
**36** And they delivered the king's edicts to the satraps <note>original: "satrapis," provincial governors</note> who were in the king's presence, and to the governors across the river, and they supported the people and the house of God.

### CHAPTER IX.

->*Upon hearing that the Jews have contracted marriages with the Gentiles, Ezra rends his garments, confesses the people's sins, and mourns before the Lord.*<-

**1** Now after these things were completed, the leaders came to me, saying: The people of Israel and the Levites have not separated themselves from the people of the lands and their abominations—namely, the Canaanites <note>original: "Chananæi"</note>, the Hittites <note>original: "Hethæi"</note>, the Perizzites <note>original: "Pherezæi"</note>, the Jebusites <note>original: "Jebusæi"</note>, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites <note>original: "Amorrhæorum"</note>.
**2** For they have taken of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and they have mixed the holy offspring <note>original: "semen sanctum"; literally "holy seed"</note> with the peoples of the lands. Even the hand of the leaders and magistrates was foremost in this transgression.
**3** And when I heard this report, I rent my cloak and my tunic, and I pulled out the hair of my head and my beard, and I sat down mourning.
**4** Then all those who feared the word of the God of Israel gathered to me because of the transgression of those who had come from the captivity; and I sat sorrowful until the evening sacrifice.
**5** And at the evening sacrifice, I rose up from my affliction, and with my cloak and tunic rent, I bowed my knees and spread out my hands to the Lord my God.
**6** And I said:
> My God, I am confounded and ashamed to lift up my face to you, for our iniquities are multiplied over our heads, and our sins have grown up even to heaven,
**7** From the days of our fathers; indeed, we ourselves have sinned greatly even to this day. Because of our iniquities, we ourselves, and our kings, and our priests, have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to confusion of face, as it is this day.
**8** And now, as if for a small moment, our prayer has been made before the Lord our God, that a remnant might be left to us, and that a peg <note>original: "paxillus"; a metaphor for a secure foothold or a small stake in a tent, representing security</note> might be given to us in His holy place, and that our God might enlighten our eyes and give us a little life in our bondage.
**9** For we are bondmen, yet in our bondage our God has not forsaken us, but has extended mercy to us before the king of the Persians, to give us life, and to set up the house of our God, and to rebuild its ruins, and to give us a wall <note>original: "sepem"; literally a hedge or fence</note> in Judah and Jerusalem.
**10** And now, O our God, what shall we say after this? For we have forsaken your commandments,
**11** Which you commanded by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying: The land into which you go to possess it is an unclean land, according to the uncleanness of the peoples and of the other lands, by the abominations of those who have filled it from one end to the other <note>original: "ab ore usque ad os"; literally "from mouth to mouth"</note> with their filthiness.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 7:3</margin>
**12** Now therefore, do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or their prosperity, so that you may be strengthened, and eat the good things of the land, and have your children as heirs forever.
**13** And after all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and for our great sin,

<column-break/>

because you, our God, have delivered us from our iniquity and have given us salvation as it is today;
**14** Should we turn back and make your commandments void, and join in marriage with the peoples of these abominations? Would you not be angry with us even to total destruction, until no remnant or salvation was left?
**15** O Lord God of Israel, you are just, for we are left as a remnant that should be saved, as it is this day. Behold, we are before you in our sin, for no one can stand before you because of this.

### CHAPTER X.

->*Ezra, having called together all the children of the captivity, commands the foreign wives to be put away; after they promised to do so, those in charge of the task and those who had contracted such marriages are listed.*<-

**1** Now while Ezra was thus praying and making supplication, weeping and lying prostrate before the temple of God, a very great assembly of men, women, and children out of Israel gathered to him; and the people wept with much lamentation.
**2** And Shecaniah <note>original: "Sechenias"</note> the son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra:
> We have trespassed against our God, and have taken foreign wives from the people of the land. Yet now, if there is repentance in Israel concerning this,
**3** Let us make a covenant with the Lord our God, to put away all the wives and those who are born of them, according to the will of the Lord and of those who fear the commandment of the Lord our God; let it be done according to the law.
**4** Arise, it is your duty to decide, and we will be with you; take courage and do it.
**5** Then Ezra arose and made the leaders of the priests and the Levites, and all Israel, swear that they would do according to this word; and they swore.
**6** And Ezra rose up from before the house of God and went to the chamber of Jehohanan <note>original: "Johanan"</note> the son of Eliashib; and when he entered there, he ate no bread and drank no water, for he mourned for the transgression of those who had come out of the captivity.
**7** And a proclamation was sent throughout Judah and Jerusalem to all the children of the captivity, that they should gather at Jerusalem.
**8** And whoever did not come within three days, according to the counsel of the princes and the elders, all his substance should be forfeited, and he himself should be cast out from the assembly of the captivity.
**9** Then all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered at Jerusalem within three days; it was the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month. And all the people sat in the street of the house of God, trembling because of the sin and because of the rain.
**10** And Ezra the priest stood up and said to them:
> You have transgressed and have taken foreign wives, to increase the guilt of Israel.
**11** And now, make confession to the Lord, the God of your fathers, and do His pleasure; separate yourselves from the people of the land and from the foreign wives.
**12** And the whole multitude answered and said with a loud voice:
> As you have said to us, so let it be done.
**13** But because the people are many, and it is a time of rain, and we are not able to stand outside, and the work is not for one day or two—

*Nehemiah, the cupbearer of Artaxerxes, having heard of the affliction of the Jews who remained from the captivity, weeps and fasts for many days, confessing the sins of the people and seeking mercy from God.*

**1** The words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah. And it came to pass in the month of Chislev <note>roughly November/December</note>, in the twentieth year, as I was in the citadel of Susa.

### C H A P T E R  II.

*Nehemiah, having obtained letters from the king, comes to Jerusalem; he encourages and applies himself to the restoration of the walls, while his enemies rage in vain.*

Now it happened in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes: and wine was before him, and I lifted the wine, and gave it to the king: and I was as one languishing <note>original: "languidus," meaning appearing sickly or sorrowful</note> before his face.
**2** And the king said to me: Why is your face sad, since I do not see that you are sick? This is not without cause, but some evil I know not of is in your heart. And I was struck with a great and exceeding fear:
**3** And I said to the king: O King, live forever: why should my face not mourn, since the city of the house of my father's sepulchers <note>tombs or burial places</note> lies deserted, and its gates are consumed by fire?
**4** And the king said to me: For what thing do you make a request? And I prayed to the God of heaven,
**5** And I said to the king: If it seems good to the king, and if your servant finds favor before your face, that you would send me into Judea, to the city of my father's sepulcher, and I will build it.
**6** And the king said to me, and the queen who was sitting beside him: How long will your journey be, and when will you return? And it pleased the king's face, and he sent me: and I set a time for him.
**7** And I said to the king: If it seems good to the king, let letters be given to me for the governors of the region across the river <note>The Euphrates, referring to the province of Trans-Euphrates</note>, that they may allow me passage until I come into Judea:
**8** And a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king's forest, that he may give me timber, that I may be able to cover the gates of the tower of the house, and the walls of the city, and the house that I shall enter. And the king granted this to me according to the good hand of my God upon me.
**9** And I came to the governors of the region across the river, and gave them the king's letters. Now the king had sent with me captains of the soldiers and horsemen.
**10** And Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, an Ammonite, heard of it: and they were saddened with great affliction, that a man had come who sought the prosperity of the children of Israel.
**11** And I came to Jerusalem, and was there for three days,
**12** And I rose in the night, I and a few men with me, and I did not tell anyone what God had put in my heart to do in Jerusalem, and there was no beast with me, except the animal on which I sat.
**13** And I went out through the valley gate by night, and before the dragon's fountain, and to the dung gate, and I considered the wall of Jerusalem which was broken down, and its gates consumed by fire.
**14** And I passed on to the fountain gate, and to the king's aqueduct, and there was no place for the beast on which I sat to pass.
**15** And I went up by the torrent in the night, and con-

**16** But the magistrates did not know where I had gone, or what I was doing: but neither to the Jews, nor to the priests, nor to the nobles, nor to the magistrates, nor to the rest who were doing the work, had I told anything up to that point.
**17** And I said to them: You know the affliction in which we are: because Jerusalem is deserted, and its gates are consumed by fire: come, and let us build the walls of Jerusalem, and let us no longer be a reproach.
**18** And I showed them the hand of my God, that it was good upon me, and the king's words, which he had spoken to me, and I said: Let us rise up and build. And their hands were strengthened for the good work.

**20** And I returned a word to them, and said to them: The God of heaven himself helps us, and we are his servants: let us rise up and build: but you have no part, nor right, nor memory in Jerusalem.

### ->C H A P T E R IV.<-

> *While Sanballat and Tobiah, with other nations, oppose them, the Jews build with one hand and hold a sword in the other: and through Nehemiah praying to God against their mocking and traps, the work is completed.*

**1** Now it happened that when Sanballat heard that we were building the wall, he was very angry: and moved with great rage, he mocked the Jews.
**2** And he spoke before his brothers and the multitude of the Samaritans: "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will the nations let them be? Will they sacrifice, and finish in a single day? Will they be able to build stones out of the heaps of dust that have been burned?"
**3** But Tobiah the Ammonite, standing near him, said: "Let them build: if a fox climbs up, he will leap over their stone wall."
**4** "Hear, O our God, for we have become a thing of contempt: turn back their reproach upon their own heads, and give them up to be despised in a land of captivity.
**5** Do not cover their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out before your face, for they have mocked the builders."
**6** And so we built the wall, and joined the whole together as far as the half-way point: and the heart of the people was encouraged to work.
**7** Now it happened that when Sanballat, and Tobiah, and the Arabs, and the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the scar <note>original: "cicatrix," referring to the gaps in the wall being closed or "healed"</note> of the wall of Jerusalem was being closed up, and that the breaches had begun to be stopped, they were exceedingly angry.
**8** And they all gathered together to come and fight against Jerusalem, and to prepare ambushes.
**9** But we prayed to our God, and set guards upon the wall day and night against them.
**10** And Judah said: "The strength of the laborer is weakened, and there is too much rubble, and we shall not be able to build the wall."
**11** And our enemies said: "Let them not know, and let them be unaware, until we come into their midst and kill them, and cause the work to cease."
**12** It happened, however, that when the Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times, from all the places from which they came to us,
**13** I stationed the people in order in the place behind the wall round about, with their swords, and spears, and bows.
**14** And I looked around and arose: and I said to the nobles and the officials, and to the rest of the common people: "Do not be afraid of them; remember the Lord, great and terrible, and fight for your brothers, and your sons, and your daughters, and your wives, and your houses."
**15** And it happened that when our enemies heard that it had been told to us, God brought their counsel to nothing. And we all returned to the walls, each one to his own work.

### CHAPTER V.

*In the midst of great poverty, Nehemiah rebukes the greedy rich and forbids usury <term>usury: the practice of lending money at unreasonably high interest rates</term>, freely giving of his own to those in need: thus he removes this obstacle to the work.*

**1** **And** there arose a great cry of the people and of their wives against their Jewish brothers.
**2** And there were those who said: "Our sons and our daughters are very many: let us receive grain for their price, so that we may eat and live."
**3** And there were those who said: "Let us mortgage our fields, and vineyards, and our houses, and let us receive grain during the famine."
**4** And others said: "Let us borrow money for the king's tribute, and let us give up our fields and vineyards.
**5** And now, our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, and our children are like their children: behold, we are bringing our sons and our daughters into subjection as slaves, and some of our daughters are already bondwomen, nor do we have the means to redeem them, while others possess our fields and our vineyards."
**6** And I was very angry when I heard their cry according to these words.
**7** And my heart considered it within me: and I rebuked the nobles and officials, and said to them: "Do you each exact usury <note>original: "usuras."</note> from your brothers?" And I gathered a great assembly against them,
**8** And I said to them: "We, as you know, have redeemed our Jewish brothers who were sold to the Gentiles, according to our ability: and will you then sell your brothers, so that we must buy them back?" And they were silent, nor could they find anything to answer.
**9** And I said to them: "The thing that you are doing is not good: why do you not walk in the fear of our God, so that we may not be a reproach to the nations that are our enemies?
**10** Both I, and my brothers, and my servants, have lent money and grain to many: let us not demand this back in common, let us forgive the debt that is owed to us.
**11** Restore to them this very day their fields, and their vineyards, and their olive groves, and their houses: and even more, the hundredth part <note>The "hundredth part" likely refers to a monthly interest rate of 1%, totaling 12% annually.</note> of the money, the grain, the wine, and the oil, which you are accustomed to exact from them, give back for them."

<column-break/>

**12** And they said, "We will restore them, and we will require nothing from them: and we will do just as you say." And I called the priests and made them swear an oath to act according to what I had said.
**13** Furthermore, I shook out my lap <note>original: "excussi sinum meum." This was a symbolic gesture: as the dust is shaken from a garment, so would a person be "shaken out" of God's blessing if they broke the promise.</note>, and said: "So may God shake out every man from his house and from his labors who does not fulfill this word: let him be so shaken out and become empty." And the whole multitude said: "Amen." And they praised God. Therefore the people did according to what was said.
**14** Moreover, from that day when the king commanded me to be the governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year even to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, for twelve years, I and my brothers did not eat the provisions that were due to the governors.
**15** But the former governors who were before me burdened the people, and took from them bread, and wine, and money, forty shekels <note>original: "siclos."</note> every day: even their servants oppressed the people. But I did not do so because of the fear of God.
**16** On the contrary, I built in the work of the wall, and I bought no land, and all my servants were gathered together for the work.
**17** Also there were at my table one hundred and fifty men, both Jews and officials, besides those who came to us from the nations that are around us.
**18** And there was prepared for me every day one ox, six chosen rams, besides poultry, and every ten days various wines, and many other things I provided: furthermore, I did not demand the provisions of my governorship: for the people were greatly impoverished.
**19** Remember me, my God, for good, according to all that I have done for this people.

### CHAPTER VI.

*Sanballat with his associates, inviting Nehemiah to a treaty with treacherous letters, threatens an accusation of seeking the kingdom; he tries to hinder the building, but does not terrify Nehemiah or change his purpose: and when the wall was completed, all the neighboring nations were afraid.*

**1** **Now it happened**, when Sanballat, and Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had built the wall, and that there was no breach left in it (though up to that time I had not set up the leaves in the gates),
**2** Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying: "Come, and let us strike a treaty together in the villages in the plain of Ono." But they were thinking to do me harm.
**3** Therefore I sent messengers to them, saying: "I am doing a great work, and I cannot come down: lest perhaps it be neglected while I come and go down to you."
**4** And they sent to me according to this word four times: and I answered them according to the previous word.
**5** Then Sanballat sent his servant to me a fifth time with a similar message, and he had a letter in his hand written in this manner:
**6** "IT IS REPORTED AMONG THE NATIONS, and Geshem has said it, that you and the Jews intend to rebel, and for that reason you are building the wall, and you wish to raise yourself up as king over them; for which cause
**7** You have also appointed prophets, who should preach concerning...

**8** And I sent to them, saying: "It has not been done according to these words which you speak: for you are making these things up out of your own heart."
**9** For all these people were trying to frighten us, thinking that our hands would cease from the work, and we would rest. For which cause I strengthened my hands even more:
**10** And I entered the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah the son of Mehetabel in secret. He said: "Let us consult together in the house of God in the middle of the temple, and let us shut the doors of the building: because they are coming to kill you, and they are coming by night to slay you."
**11** And I said: "Should a man like me flee? And who like me would enter the temple to save his life? I will not enter."
**12** And I understood that God had not sent him, but that he had spoken to me as if prophesying, because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
**13** For he had taken a bribe, so that being terrified I might do it, and sin, and they might have an evil report with which to reproach me.
**14** Remember me, O Lord, regarding Tobiah and Sanballat, according to these works of theirs: and also Noadiah the prophetess, and the rest of the prophets, who were trying to frighten me.
**15** And the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul <note>Elul: the sixth month of the Hebrew calendar, roughly August–September.</note>, in fifty-two days:
**16** It happened therefore when all our enemies heard of it, that all the nations who were around us were afraid, and they were cast down within themselves, and knew that this work had been done by God.
**17** But also in those days, many letters of the nobles of the Jews were sent to Tobiah, and from Tobiah they came to them.
**18** For there were many in Judea bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah:
**19** They also praised him in my presence, and reported my words to him: and Tobiah sent letters to terrify me.

### CHAPTER VIII.

> *Ezra recites and explains the words of the Law clearly to the people, after silence is made by the Levites; Nehemiah consoles the grieving people, and they celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days with leafy branches, while Ezra reads every day from the book of the Law.*

1 And the seventh month had come, and the children of Israel were in their cities. And all the people gathered as one man at the open square that is before the Water Gate; and they told Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the Law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded for Israel.
2 So Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly of men and women, and all who could understand, on the first day of the seventh month.
3 And he read from it openly in the square that was before the Water Gate, from morning until midday, in the presence of the men and the women and those who could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive to the book.
4 And Ezra the scribe stood upon a wooden platform which he had made for speaking; and beside him stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right hand; and on his left, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
5 And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people—for he stood above all the people—and when he opened it, all the people stood up.
6 And Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God; and all the people answered, "<note>original: "Amen, Amen"</note> Truly, truly," lifting up their hands; and they bowed their heads and worshipped God with their faces to the ground.
7 Furthermore, Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, kept the people silent to hear the Law; and the people stood in their place.
8 And they read in the book of the Law of God distinctly and clearly so as to be understood; and they understood when it was read.
9 And Nehemiah (he is the Atherfatha) and Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who interpreted for all the people, said: "This day is holy to the Lord our God; do not mourn, and do not weep." For all the people wept when they heard the words of the Law.
10 And he said to them: "Go, eat the fat, and drink the sweet wine <note>original: "mulsum" - a traditional drink made of wine and honey.</note>, and send portions to those who have nothing prepared for themselves; for this is the holy day of the Lord, and do not be sad, for the joy of the Lord is our strength."
11 And the Levites quieted all the people, saying: "Be still, for the day is holy, and do not grieve."
12 So all the people went their way to eat, and to drink, and to send portions, and to make great joy, because they had understood the words that had been taught to them.
13 And on the second day, the heads of the families of all the people, the priests, and the Levites, were gathered to Ezra the scribe, so that he might interpret for them the words of the Law.

### C H A P T E R IX.

->*The people in fasting and sackcloth, repentant, separate themselves from foreigners; the Levites confess the benefits of God and the sins of the Israelites, and pray for the people, thus striking a covenant with the Lord.*<-

1 Now on the twenty-fourth day of this month, the children of Israel gathered together in fasting and in sackcloth, and with dust upon them.
2 And the offspring of the children of Israel were separated from every foreign child; and they stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.
3 And they rose up to stand: and they read from the volume of the law of the Lord their God four times in the day, and four times they confessed and adored the Lord their God.
4 Then there stood up upon the step of the Levites: Joshua, and Bani, and Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani; and they cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God.
5 And the Levites—Joshua, and Kadmiel, Bunni, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said: “Arise, bless the Lord your God from eternity unto eternity; and let them bless your high and glorious name with every blessing and praise.”
6 You yourself, Lord, you alone have made heaven, and the heaven of heavens, and all their host; the earth and everything that is in it; the seas and everything that is in them; and you give life to all these things, and the host of heaven adores you.
<margin>† Genesis 11:31.</margin>
7 You yourself, O Lord God, who chose Abram and led him out from the fire of the Chaldeans <note>original: "igne Chaldæorum." This refers to the city of Ur. In Hebrew, "Ur" can also mean "fire" or "light," leading to a tradition that Abraham was miraculously saved from a literal fire.</note>, and gave him the name Abraham.
8 And you found his heart faithful before you; and you struck a covenant with him to give him the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Perizzite, and the Jebusite, and the Girgashite, to give it to his offspring; and you have fulfilled your words, because you are just.
9 And you saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and you heard their cry at the Red Sea.
10 And you gave signs and wonders against Pharaoh, and against all his servants, and against all the

<column-break/>

people of that land; for you knew that they acted proudly against them; and you made a name for yourself, as it is to this day.
11 And you divided the sea before them, and they passed through the midst of the sea on dry land; but their pursuers you threw into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.
12 And in a column of cloud you were their leader by day, and in a column of fire by night, so that the way by which they went might appear to them.
13 You also descended upon Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven, and you gave them right judgments, and the law of truth, ceremonies, and good precepts.
14 And you showed them your sanctified Sabbath, and you commanded them mandates, and ceremonies, and the law, by the hand of Moses your servant.
15 You also gave them bread from heaven in their hunger, and you brought water out of the rock for them in their thirst, and you told them to enter and possess the land over which you lifted your hand to deliver it to them.
16 But they and our fathers acted proudly, and hardened their necks, and did not hear your commandments.
17 And they refused to hear, and they did not remember your wonders which you had done for them. And they hardened their necks, and set their heads to return to their bondage, as if in defiance. But you, O God, are forgiving, gracious and merciful, long-suffering and of much compassion, and you did not abandon them,
18 And even when they had made for themselves a molten calf and said, “This is your God who led you out of Egypt,” and committed great blasphemies,
19 Yet you, in your many mercies, did not leave them in the desert. The column of cloud did not depart from them by day to lead them on the way, nor the column of fire by night to show them the journey by which they were to go.
20 And you gave your good spirit to teach them, and you did not withhold your manna from their mouths, and you gave them water in their thirst.
21 For forty years you fed them in the desert, and nothing was lacking to them; their garments did not grow old, and their feet were not worn down.
22 And you gave them kingdoms and peoples, and distributed portions to them; and they possessed the land of Sihon, and the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, the king of Bashan.
23 And you multiplied their children like the stars of heaven, and brought them to the land of which you had told their fathers that they should enter and possess it.
24 And the children came and possessed the land, and you humbled before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hands—both their kings and the peoples of the land—to do with them as they pleased.
25 And so they took fortified cities and a fat soil, and possessed houses full of all goods, cisterns built by others, vineyards, and olive groves, and many fruit-bearing trees; and they ate, and were filled, and grew fat, and abounded in delights in your great goodness.
26 But they provoked you to wrath, and withdrew from you, and cast your law behind their backs; and they killed your prophets who testified against them that they might return to you; and they committed great blasphemies.

These same Levites shall receive tithes from all the cities where we labor.

39 For the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall carry the firstfruits of the grain, the wine, and the oil to the treasury; and the holy vessels shall be there, along with the priests, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the ministers; and we will not neglect the house of our God.

->*An account is given of the inhabitants of Jerusalem and of the cities of Judah after the restoration.*<-

1 Now the leaders of the people dwelt in Jerusalem: but the rest of the people cast lots to bring one part out of ten to dwell in Jerusalem, the holy city, while nine parts remained in the other cities.

9 But in all these things I was not in Jerusalem, because in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, the king of Babylon, I went to the king, and at the end of some days I asked leave of the king. <note>original: "anno trigesimo secundo Artaxerxis." <meta>This page transitions from the historical administration of Nehemiah in Jerusalem to the Book of Tobit (labeled Tobias in the Latin Vulgate). While Nehemiah dealt with the restoration of the Jewish community after the Babylonian exile, the story of Tobit takes place earlier, during the Assyrian captivity of the northern tribes.</meta>

# THE BOOK OF TOBIT <note>In the Latin tradition, both the father and the son are named Tobias. In most modern English Bibles, the father is called Tobit and the son is called Tobias to avoid confusion.</note>

## CHAPTER ONE

> Tobias, having been established in captivity, does not depart from the law of God; he teaches his son Tobias, born of his wife Anna, to fear God. Having found favor with King Shalmaneser, he goes wherever he wishes; he consoles his fellow captives and helps them with alms; he lends ten talents of silver to Gabael; Sennacherib persecutes him for burying those who were slain.

1 <margin>† 2 Kings 17:3 and 18:2</margin> Tobias, from the tribe and city of Naphtali (which is in the upper parts of Galilee above Naasson, beyond the road which leads to the west, having the city of Safed to its left),
2 † When he had been taken captive in the days of Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, though placed in captivity, he did not desert the way of truth,
3 So that everything he was able to have, he shared daily with his fellow-captive brothers who were of his own kindred.
4 And though he was the youngest of all in the tribe of Naphtali, yet he did nothing in a childish manner in his conduct.
5 <margin>† 1 Kings 12:28</margin> Finally, when all went to the golden calves which Jeroboam the king of Israel had made, he alone fled the company of all,
6 But he proceeded to Jerusalem to the temple of the Lord, and there he adored the Lord God of Israel, faithfully offering all his first-fruits and his tithes,
7 So that in the third year he administered the entire tithe to the proselytes and strangers.
8 These and similar things the little boy observed according to the law of God.
9 But when he had become a man, he took a wife named Anna from his own tribe, and fathered a son by her, giving him his own name.
10 From infancy, he taught him to fear God and to abstain from all sin.
11 Therefore, when he had come into captivity with his wife and son to the city of Nineveh with all his tribe,
12 (Even though everyone else ate from the foods of the Gentiles) he guarded his soul, and was never contaminated by their food.
13 And because he was mindful of the Lord with all his heart, God gave him favor in the sight of Shalmaneser the king,
14 And he gave him the power to go wherever he wished, having the freedom to do whatever he wanted.
15 He went, therefore, to all who were in captivity, and gave them advice for their salvation.
16 But when he had come to Rages, a city of the Medes, and had ten talents of silver from the wealth with which he had been honored by the king:
17 <margin>b l m f b</margin> And when among the great multitude of his kindred he saw Gabael in need, who was of his own tribe, he gave him the aforementioned weight of silver under a written bond. <note>original: "sub chirographo." This refers to a signed legal document or promissory note.</note>
18 But after much time, King Shalmaneser being dead, when his son Sennacherib reigned in his place, and held the children of Israel in hatred in his sight:
19 Tobias went daily through all his kindred, and consoled them, and distributed to each one, as much as he could, from his own resources:

<column-break/>

20 He fed the hungry, provided clothing for the naked, and carefully provided burial for those who were dead or had been slain.
21 <margin>† 2 Kings 19:35; Ecclesiasticus 48:24; 2 Maccabees 8:19</margin> † Finally, when King Sennacherib had returned, fleeing from Judea from the plague which God had brought upon him because of his blasphemy, and being angry he killed many of the children of Israel, Tobias buried their bodies.
22 But when this was reported to the king, he ordered him to be killed, and took away all his substance.
23 But Tobias, fleeing with his son and his wife, lay hidden and destitute, because many people loved him.
24 <margin>† 2 Kings 19:37; 2 Chronicles 32:21; Isaiah 37:38</margin> † But after forty-five days, the king's own sons killed him.
25 And Tobias returned to his house, and all his property was restored to him.

## CHAPTER TWO

> Tobias, exhausted by the burial of the dead, is blinded by the droppings of a swallow as a test of patience; and having suffered reproach from his wife and friends who mocked him, he endures it most patiently like Job.

1 After these things, when it was a feast day of the Lord, and a good dinner was prepared in the house of Tobias,
2 He said to his son: Go, and bring some of our tribe who fear God, so that they may feast with us.
3 And when he had gone, he returned and told him that one of the children of Israel lay strangled in the street. And immediately leaping up from his place at the table, leaving his dinner, he came to the body fasting:
4 And taking it up, he carried it to his house secretly, so that, when the sun had set, he might cautiously bury him.
5 And when he had hidden the body, he ate his bread with mourning and trembling,
6 <margin>† Amos 8:10; 1 Maccabees 1:41</margin> Remembering that word which the Lord spoke through Amos the prophet: Your feast days shall be turned into lamentation and mourning.
7 But when the sun had set, he went and buried him.
8 Now all his neighbors rebuked him, saying: Already for this reason you were ordered to be killed, and you narrowly escaped the sentence of death, and do you bury the dead again?
9 <margin>† Above 1:13</margin> † But Tobias, fearing God more than the king, took the bodies of the slain, and hid them in his house, and buried them in the middle of the night.
10 Now it happened that one day, exhausted from burying, he came to his house and threw himself down next to a wall and fell asleep,
11 And while he was sleeping, hot droppings from a swallows' nest fell upon his eyes, and he became blind.
12 Now the Lord permitted this temptation to happen to him, so that an example of his patience might be given to posterity, just as with holy Job.
13 For since he had always feared God from his infancy and kept his commandments, he did not grumble against God because the affliction of blindness had come upon him:

<meta>catchword: 14 But</meta>

<summary>This page introduces Tobias (Tobit), a devout Israelite captive in Nineveh who risks his life to perform acts of charity and bury the dead. Despite his faithfulness, he is struck with blindness, a trial the text compares to the suffering of Job.</summary>

14 But he remained unmoved in the fear of God, giving thanks to God all the days of his life.
15 For just as kings insulted blessed Job, so did his parents and kinsmen mock his life, saying:
16 "Where is your hope, for which you performed alms and burials?" <note>Tobias’s relatives are comparing his situation to that of Job, whose friends also questioned his righteousness in the face of suffering.</note>

18 For we are the children of the holy ones, and we look for that life which God will give to those who never change their faith from Him."
19 Now Anna his wife went to weaving work every day, and she brought home the food she could get from the labor of her hands.
20 And it happened that she received a young goat and brought it home.
21 When her husband heard the sound of it bleating, he said: "See that it is not perhaps stolen; return it to its owners, for it is not lawful for us either to eat anything stolen or to touch it."
<margin>† Job 2:9</margin>

23 And with these and other such words, she upbraided him.

### CHAPTER III.

> On account of his wife's insults, Tobias prays to God desiring to die; similarly, Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, prays with a three-day fast because of a maidservant's reproach concerning her seven husbands who were killed by a demon. The prayers of both are heard, and the angel Raphael is sent to heal them.

1 **T**hen Tobias groaned, and began to pray with tears,
2 Saying: "You are righteous, O Lord, and all your judgments are just, and all your ways are mercy, and truth, and judgment.
3 And now, O Lord, be mindful of me, and do not take vengeance for my sins, nor remember my offenses, or those of my parents.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 28:15</margin>
4 † Because we have not obeyed your commandments, we have been delivered into plunder, and captivity, and death, and into a proverb, and a reproach to all the nations among whom you have dispersed us.
5 And now, O Lord, your judgments are great, because we have not acted according to your commandments, and have not walked sincerely before you.
6 And now, O Lord, do with me according to your will, and command my spirit to be received in peace: for it is better for me to die than to live."
7 It happened on the same day that Sarah, the daughter of Raguel in Rages, a city of the Medes, also heard a reproach from one of her father's maidservants,
8 Because she had been given to seven husbands, and a demon named Asmodeus had killed them as soon as they had gone in to her.
9 Therefore, when she rebuked the girl for her fault, she answered her, saying: "May we never see a son or daughter from you on the earth, you murderer of your husbands!
10 Do you also want to kill me, as you have already killed seven men?" At this voice, she went into an upper chamber of her house, and for

<column-break/>

three days and three nights she did not eat or drink.
11 But persisting in prayer, she entreated God with tears that He would deliver her from this reproach.
12 And it happened on the third day, as she completed her prayer, blessing the Lord,
13 She said: "Blessed is your name, O God of our fathers, who, though you are angry, will show mercy, and in the time of tribulation you forgive the sins of those who call upon you.
14 To you, O Lord, I turn my face; to you I direct my eyes.
15 I beg, O Lord, that you release me from the bond of this reproach, or surely take me away from the earth.
16 You know, O Lord, that I have never desired a man, and have kept my soul clean from all lust.
17 I never joined myself with those who play; nor have I made myself a partner with those who walk in lightheadedness. <note>original: "levitate" — meaning frivolity or lack of moral seriousness.</note>
18 But I consented to take a husband with your fear, not with my own lust.
19 And either I was unworthy of them, or they perhaps were not worthy of me; because perhaps you have kept me for another man.
20 For your counsel is not within the power of man.
21 But this everyone who worships you holds for certain: that his life, if it has been tested, will be crowned; if it has been in tribulation, it will be delivered; and if it has been under correction, it will be allowed to come to your mercy.
22 For you do not delight in our destruction; because after a storm, you make it calm; and after weeping and mourning, you pour in joy.
23 Let your name, O God of Israel, be blessed forever."
24 At that time, the prayers of both were heard in the sight of the glory of the Most High God.
25 And the holy angel of the Lord, Raphael, was sent to heal them both, whose prayers were recited at one time in the sight of the Lord.

### CHAPTER IV.

> Tobias, thinking that he would soon die, impresses most pious counsels for salvation upon his son; he declares the virtue of almsgiving and informs him of the ten talents of silver lent to Gabael.

1 **T**herefore, when Tobias thought that his prayer was heard so that he might die, he called to himself Tobias his son.
2 And he said to him: "Hear, my son, the words of my mouth, and lay them in your heart as a foundation.
<margin>† Exodus 20:12</margin>
3 When God has received my soul, bury my body; and you shall honor your mother all the days of her life.
<margin>Sirach 7:29</margin>
4 † For you ought to remember what and how great dangers she suffered for you in her womb.
5 And when she also has completed the time of her life, bury her near me.
6 But all the days of your life, have God in your mind; and beware that you never consent to sin, and disregard the commandments of the Lord our God.
<margin>† Proverbs 3:9; Sirach 4:1, 14:3; Luke 14:13</margin>
7 † Give alms from your substance, and do not turn your face away from any poor person; for so it will happen that the face of the Lord will not be turned away from you."

### CHAPTER V.

*While young Tobias seeks a companion and guide for the journey to Rages of the Medes, the Angel Raphael meets him in disguise. The father entrusts his son to him, and after they depart, the mother weeps over her son's absence.*

Then Tobias answered his father and said: "I will do everything you have commanded me, father.
2 But how I am to claim this money, I do not know. He does not know me, and I do not know him. What sign shall I give him? Moreover, I have never known the road that leads there."
3 Then his father answered him and said: "I have his written bond here with me; when you show it to him, he will pay it back immediately.
4 But go now and look for some faithful man who might go with you for a guaranteed wage, so that you may receive the money while I am still alive."

<column-break/>

7 But he <note>the stranger</note> answered: "I am of the children of Israel." And Tobias said to him: "Do you know the way that leads into the region of the Medes?"
8 He answered: "I know it; and I have traveled all its paths frequently. I have stayed with our brother Gabelus, who lives in Rages, a city of the Medes, which is situated on the mountain of Ecbatana."
9 Tobias said to him: "Wait for me, I pray, until I tell these things to my father."
10 Then Tobias went in and told all these things to his father. His father, being amazed at this, asked that the man might come in to him.
11 And so he entered and greeted him, saying: "May joy be with you always."
12 And the elder Tobias said: "What kind of joy shall I have, I who sit in darkness and do not see the light of heaven?"
13 The young man <note>the Angel Raphael in disguise</note> said to him: "Be of good courage; it is near at hand that you shall be healed by God."
14 Therefore Tobias said to him: "Can you lead my son to Gabelus in Rages, the city of the Medes? And when you return, I will pay you your wage."
15 And the Angel said to him: "I will lead him there, and I will bring him back to you."
16 Tobias answered him: "I pray you, tell me, from what house or what tribe are you?"
17 The Angel Raphael said to him: "Do you seek the lineage of a hireling, or the hireling himself to go with your son?
18 But so that I do not make you anxious: I am Azarias, the son of the great Ananias." <note>Azarias means "The Lord has helped." The angel uses a human name as a disguise.</note>
19 And Tobias answered: "You are of a great lineage. But I ask that you not be angry that I wished to know your family."
20 The Angel said to him: "I will lead your son there healthy, and I will bring him back to you healthy."
21 Tobias responded, saying: "May you travel well; may God be on your journey, and may His angel accompany you."
22 Then, after everything was prepared that they were to carry on the road, Tobias said farewell to his father and his mother, and they both walked out together.

<margin>† Below 10:4</margin>
23 † And when they had set out, his mother began to weep and say: "You have taken the staff of our old age <note>original: "baculum senectutis nostrae" - a metaphor for a child who supports their elderly parents</note> and sent him away from us.
24 Would that the money for which you sent him had never existed!
25 For our poverty was enough for us, so that we could count it as riches that we saw our son."
26 And the elder Tobias said to her: "Do not weep; our son will arrive safe, and he will return safe to us, and your eyes shall see him.
27 For I believe that a good Angel of God accompanies him and disposes all things well that concern him, so that he shall return to us with joy."
28 At these words, his mother ceased her weeping and was silent.

### CHAPTER VI

*At the Angel's urging, Tobias captures a lunging fish and guts it, reserving its heart, gall, and liver for medicines. They visit Raguel so that, by the Angel's command, Tobias may ask for his daughter Sarah in marriage—whose seven previous husbands a demon had killed—learning from the Angel the proper purpose for entering into and maintaining a marriage.*

1 And Tobias went forward, and the dog followed him, and he stayed the first night by the river Tigris.
2 And he went out to wash his feet, and behold, a massive fish lunged out to devour him.
3 Being terrified of it, Tobias cried out with a loud voice, saying: Lord, it is attacking me!
4 And the Angel said to him: Grab it by the gill, and pull it toward you. When he had done this, he drew it onto dry land, and it began to pant at his feet.
5 Then the Angel said to him: Gut this fish, and keep its heart, gall, and liver for yourself; for these are useful and necessary as medicines.
6 When he had done this, he roasted its flesh, and they took it with them on the way; the rest they salted, enough to last them until they reached Rages, a city of the Medes.
7 Then Tobias questioned the Angel, and said to him: I beseech you, brother Azarias, to tell me what remedy these parts possess, which you ordered me to keep from the fish?
8 And the Angel, answering, said to him: If you place a small piece of its heart upon coals, its smoke drives out every kind of demon, whether from a man or from a woman, so that it may no longer come near them.
9 And the gall is effective for anointing eyes in which there is a white film <note>original: "albugo" - a white spot or cataract on the eye</note>, and they shall be healed.
10 And Tobias said to him: Where do you wish for us to stay?
11 And the Angel, answering, said: There is a man here named Raguel, a kinsman of your tribe, and he has a daughter named Sarah; he has no other male or female child but her.
<margin>† Numbers 27:8 and 36:8</margin>
12 All his substance is due to you, and it is right for you to take her as your wife.
13 Therefore, ask for her from her father, and he will give her to you as a wife.
14 Then Tobias answered and said: I hear that she has been given to seven husbands, and they have died; but I have also heard that a demon killed them.
15 Therefore I fear lest perhaps these things happen to me also; and since I am the only child of my parents, I would bring down their old age with sorrow to the underworld <note>original: "ad inferos" - referring to the grave or the place of the dead</note>.
16 Then the Angel Raphael said to him: Listen to me, and I will show you who they are over whom the demon can prevail.
17 For those who enter into marriage in such a way as to exclude God from themselves and from their minds, and give themselves to their lust like a horse or a mule, which have no understanding—the demon has power over them.
18 But you, when you have taken her, enter the chamber, and for three days remain continent from her, and give yourself to nothing else but to join her in prayer.

<column-break/>

19 On that very night, when the liver of the fish is burned, the demon shall be driven away.
20 But on the second night, you shall be admitted into the society of the holy patriarchs.
21 And on the third night, you shall obtain a blessing, so that children may be born of you in safety.
22 When the third night is passed, you shall take the virgin in the fear of the Lord, moved more by the love of children than by lust, so that you may obtain a blessing in your children through the seed of Abraham.

### CHAPTER VII

*Sarah, having been requested by Tobias, is given to him as a wife by Raguel on the advice of Raphael, and the marriage documents are signed; the wedding is celebrated.*

1 And they entered into Raguel's house, and Raguel received them with joy.
2 And Raguel, looking at Tobias, said to his wife Anna: How much this young man resembles my cousin!
3 And when he had said this, he asked: Where are you from, young men, our brothers? And they said: We are from the tribe of Naphtali, from the captivity of Nineveh.
4 And Raguel said to them: Do you know my brother Tobias? They said: We know him.
5 And while he was saying many good things about him, the Angel said to Raguel: Tobias, about whom you ask, is this man's father.
6 And Raguel threw himself forward and kissed him with tears, and weeping upon his neck,
7 He said: A blessing be upon you, my son, for you are the son of a good and most excellent man.
8 And Anna his wife, and Sarah their daughter, also wept.
9 After they had spoken, Raguel ordered a ram to be killed and a feast to be prepared. And when he urged them to sit down for a meal,
10 Tobias said: I will not eat or drink here today unless you first confirm my petition, and promise to give me your daughter Sarah.
11 Hearing this word, Raguel was terrified, knowing what had happened to those seven men who had gone in to her; and he began to fear lest perhaps it might happen to this man in the same way. While he hesitated and gave the petitioner no answer,
12 The Angel said to him: Do not fear to give her to him, for your daughter is owed as a wife to this man who fears God; for this reason, no one else could have her.
13 Then Raguel said: I do not doubt that God has admitted my prayers and tears into His sight.
<margin>† Numbers 36:4</margin>
14 And I believe that He has made you come to me for this reason: so that she might be joined to her own kindred according to the law of Moses; and now, do not doubt that I will deliver her to you.
15 And taking his daughter's right hand, he placed it in the right hand of Tobias, saying: May the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob be with you, and may He join you together, and fulfill His blessing in you.
16 And they took paper and made a written contract of the marriage.

### CHAPTER VIII.

*Tobias enters the bridal chamber and places a piece of the roasted fish liver [on coals]; the demon is bound by Raphael. Tobias and Sarah spend the night unharmed in prayer together; meanwhile, a grave that had been prepared is filled back in, and as the parents give thanks to God, a great feast is prepared. Half of the family's goods are assigned as a dowry, with the remaining half to follow after the parents' passing.*

1 But after they had finished dining, they brought the young man in to her.
2 Tobias, remembering the Angel's instructions, took a piece of the liver from his pouch and placed it upon live coals.
3 Then the Angel Raphael seized the demon and bound him in the desert of Upper Egypt.
4 Then Tobias exhorted the virgin and said to her: Sarah, arise, and let us pray to God today, and tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow: for during these three nights we are joined to God; and when the third night has passed, we shall be in our own marriage.
5 For we are the children of saints, and we cannot be joined together in the same manner as the gentiles <note>The Latin "gentes" refers to people who do not know the God of Israel.</note> who do not know God.
6 So they both arose together and prayed earnestly that health might be granted to them.
7 And Tobias said: Lord God of our fathers, may the heavens and the earth bless you, and the sea, and the fountains, and the rivers, and all your creatures that are in them.
<margin>
Genesis 2:7
</margin>
8 † You made Adam from the dust of the earth, and you gave him Eve as a helper.
9 And now, Lord, you know that I do not take my sister <note>A term of endearment for a wife among the ancient Israelites.</note> as a wife for the sake of lust, but only out of a love for posterity, in which your name may be blessed forever and ever.
10 Sarah also said: Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, and let us grow old together in good health.
11 And it happened around cock-crow <note>Very early morning, before dawn.</note> that Raguel ordered his servants to be called, and they went with him to dig a grave.
12 For he said: Lest perhaps the same thing should happen to him as happened to those other seven men who went in to her.
13 And when they had prepared the pit, Raguel returned to his wife and said to her:
14 Send one of your maidservants to see if he is dead, so that I may bury him before it becomes light.
15 So she sent one of her maidservants. When she entered the chamber, she found them safe and sound, sleeping together.
16 And returning, she brought the good news: and they blessed the Lord, namely Raguel and his wife Anna,
17 And they said: We bless you, Lord God of Israel, because it did not happen as we expected.

<column-break/>

18 For you have shown us your mercy, and you have shut out from us the enemy who persecuted us.
19 You have had pity on two only-children. Grant them, Lord, to bless you more fully, and to offer a sacrifice of praise to you for their health, so that all nations may know that you alone are God in all the earth.
20 And immediately Raguel commanded his servants to fill in the pit they had made before it grew light.
21 Moreover, he told his wife to prepare a feast and get ready everything necessary for food for those on a journey.
22 He also had two fat cows and four rams killed, and a feast prepared for all his neighbors and all his friends.
23 And Raguel urged Tobias to stay with him for two weeks.
24 And of all that Raguel possessed, he gave half to Tobias, and he made a legal document <note>original: "scripturam"</note> so that the half which remained should come under the ownership of Tobias after their death.

### CHAPTER IX.

*At the request of Tobias, Raphael travels to Gabelus: having received the money, he brings him to Tobias’s wedding: Gabelus then blesses Tobias and Sarah.*

1 Then Tobias called the Angel to him, whom he still thought to be a man, and said to him: Brother Azarias, I ask that you listen to my words.
2 If I were to give myself to be your slave, I would not be worthy of your care.
3 Nevertheless, I beseech you to take with you animals and servants and go to Gabelus in Rages, the city of the Medes: return his bond <term>bond: "chirographum," a handwritten acknowledgment of debt</term> to him, receive the money from him, and ask him to come to my wedding.
4 For you yourself know that my father is counting the days: and if I delay even one day more, his soul will be saddened.
5 And surely you see how Raguel has bound me by an oath, an oath which I cannot ignore.
6 Then Raphael, taking four of Raguel's servants and two camels, went to Rages, the city of the Medes: and finding Gabelus, he returned his bond to him and received all the money from him.
7 And he told him everything that had happened concerning Tobias, the son of Tobias: and he made him come with him to the wedding.
8 And when he had entered Raguel’s house, he found Tobias reclining at the table: and jumping up, they kissed each other; and Gabelus wept and blessed God,
9 And said: May the God of Israel bless you, because you are the son of a most excellent and just man, one who fears God and performs acts of charity.
10 And may a blessing be spoken over your wife and over your parents:
11 And may you see your children and your children's children, even to the third and fourth generation: and may your seed be blessed by the God of Israel, who reigns forever and ever.
12 And when they had all said "Amen," they approached the feast: but they celebrated the marriage feast with the fear of the Lord.

### CHAPTER X.

1 **B**ut while Tobias made delays because of the wedding, his father Tobias was anxious, saying: "Why do you think my son delays, or why is he detained there?"
2 "Do you think Gabelus is dead, and no one will return the money to him?"
3 And he began to be exceedingly sorrowful, and Anna his wife with him; and they both began to weep together, because their son did not return to them on the appointed day.
<margin>† Smp. 5. 23. <note>original: "Smp." This likely refers to a cross-reference in a variant manuscript or a liturgical citation.</note></margin>
4 † His mother therefore wept with inconsolable tears and said: "Woe, woe is me, my son! Why did we send you to travel, you who are the light of our eyes, the staff of our old age, the comfort of our life, and the hope of our future?"
5 "Having everything at once in you alone, we ought not to have let you go from us."
6 Tobias said to her: "Be silent and do not be troubled; our son is safe. That man with whom we sent him is faithful enough."
7 But she could in no way be comforted; instead, she would rush out every day and look around, circling all the roads by which there seemed a hope of his return, so that she might see him coming from afar, if it were possible.
8 But indeed, Raguel said to his son-in-law: "Stay here, and I will send a messenger of your well-being to Tobias your father."
9 To whom Tobias said: "I know that my father and my mother are now counting the days, and their spirit is tormented within them."
10 And when Raguel pleaded with Tobias with many words, and he would by no means listen to him, he delivered Sarah to him, and half of all his substance in male and female servants, in cattle, in camels, and in cows, and in much money; and he dismissed him from him, safe and rejoicing,
11 Saying: "May the holy Angel of the Lord be in your journey, and bring you through unharmed, and may you find everything right concerning your parents, and may my eyes see your children before I die."
12 And the parents, taking hold of their daughter, kissed her and let her go,
13 Admonishing her to honor her parents-in-law <note>original: "foceros," a typo for "soceros."</note>, to love her husband, to rule the family, to govern the house, and to show herself irreproachable.

->*Leaving Sarah and the rest of the family behind on the journey, Tobias and Raphael go on ahead and are joyfully received by Tobias's parents. ### CHAPTER XI.

1 **A**nd as they were returning, they came to Charan <note>Haran</note>, which is midway on the journey toward Nineveh, on the eleventh day.
2 And the Angel said: "Brother Tobias, you know in what state you left your father."

<column-break/>

3 "If it pleases you, therefore, let us go on ahead, and let the household follow our journey at a slow pace, together with your wife and with the animals."
4 And when it had pleased him that they should go, Raphael said to Tobias: "Take some of the fish gall with you, for it will be necessary." So Tobias took some of that gall, and they departed.
5 But Anna sat by the way every day, on the brow of a hill, from where she could look out from a distance.
6 And while she was watching for his arrival from that same spot, she saw him from afar and immediately recognized her son coming; and running, she told her husband, saying: "Behold, your son comes."
7 And Raphael said to Tobias: "As soon as you enter your house, immediately adore the Lord your God; and giving thanks to Him, go to your father and kiss him."
8 "And immediately smear upon his eyes some of this fish gall that you carry with you. For you should know that his eyes will soon be opened, and your father shall see the light of heaven and shall rejoice at the sight of you."
9 Then the dog <note>The inclusion of the dog is a famous detail in the Book of Tobit, often depicted in art as a symbol of fidelity.</note> that had been with them on the road ran ahead, and arriving like a messenger, rejoiced with the wagging of its tail.
10 And his blind father, rising up, began to run, stumbling with his feet; and giving his hand to a servant boy, he went out to meet his son.
11 And receiving him, he kissed him, as did his wife, and they both began to weep for joy.
12 And when they had adored God and given thanks, they sat down.
13 Then Tobias, taking the fish gall, anointed his father’s eyes.
14 And he waited for about half an hour; and a white film <term>albugo</term> <note>A term for a white opacity of the cornea, similar to a cataract.</note> began to come out of his eyes, like the membrane of an egg.
15 Which Tobias took hold of and drew away from his eyes, and immediately he regained his sight.
16 And they glorified God—namely he, and his wife, and all who knew him.
17 And Tobias said: "I bless You, Lord God of Israel, because You have chastised me, and You have saved me; and behold, I see my son Tobias."
18 After seven days, Sarah his son’s wife also entered, along with the whole household in good health, and the cattle, and the camels, and much money of his wife's, and also that money which he had received from Gabelus.
19 And he told his parents all the benefits of God, which He had done for him through the man who had led him.
20 And Achior and Nabath <note>Relatives of Tobias, sometimes identified in other traditions as Ahikar.</note>, cousins of Tobias, came, rejoicing for Tobias and congratulating him on all the good things that God had shown toward him.
21 And feasting for seven days, they all rejoiced with great joy.

2 Tobias, answering, said to his father: "Father, what reward shall we give him? Or what could be worthy of his benefits?"
3 "He led me and brought me back healthy; he himself received the money from Gabelus; he caused me to have a wife and himself restrained the demon from her; he brought joy to her parents; he rescued me from being devoured by the fish; he also made you see the light of heaven, and through him, we have been filled with all good things. What worthy thing can we give him for all these?"
4 "But I ask you, my father, to request of him if perhaps he would deign to take for himself half of all the things that have been brought."
5 And calling him—the father and the son—they took him aside and began to ask that he would deign to accept half of all things they had brought.
6 Then he said to them secretly: "Bless the God of heaven, and confess to him before all the living, because he has shown his mercy to you."
7 "For it is good to hide the secret of a king <note>original: "sacramentum regis." This phrase implies that while earthly political secrets should be kept, divine works must be proclaimed.</note>, but to reveal and confess the works of God is honorable."
8 "Prayer with fasting is good, and almsgiving <note>original: "eleemosyna." The practice of giving to the poor as a religious duty.</note> is better than hiding away treasures of gold."
9 "Because almsgiving delivers from death, and it is that which purges sins, and makes one find mercy and eternal life."
10 "But those who commit sin and iniquity are enemies of their own soul."
11 "I reveal the truth to you then, and I will not hide the secret word from you."
12 "When you prayed with tears, and buried the dead, and left your dinner, and hid the dead in your house by day and buried them by night, I offered your prayer to the Lord."
13 "And because you were acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove you."
14 "And now the Lord has sent me to heal you, and to deliver Sarah, your son’s wife, from a demon."
15 "For I am the Angel Raphael <term>Angel: a messenger from God. Raphael is traditionally one of the archangels</term>, one of the seven who stand before the Lord."
16 And when they had heard these things, they were troubled, and trembling they fell upon their face on the earth.
17 And the Angel said to them: "Peace be to you, do not fear."
18 "For when I was with you, I was there by the will of God; bless him and sing to him."
19 "I seemed indeed to eat and drink with you; but I use an invisible food and a drink that cannot be seen by men."
20 "It is time, therefore, that I return to him who sent me; but you, bless God and tell of all his wonderful works."
21 And when he had said these things, he was taken from their sight, and they could see him no more.
22 Then, prostrate for three hours on their faces, they blessed God; and rising up, they told of all his wonderful works.

### CHAPTER XIV

*The elder Tobias, being about to die at the age of 102, exhorts his son and grandsons to piety; he urges them to move from Nineveh once his parents are buried, for he says it is to be overthrown, and Jerusalem is to be restored. The son, observing this, eventually returns to his parents-in-law, and there, having completed 99 years, he dies.*

1 And the words of Tobias were finished. And after Tobias was restored to sight, he lived forty-two years, and saw the sons of his grandsons.
2 And so, having completed one hundred and two years, he was buried honorably in Nineveh.
3 For he lost the light of his eyes at fifty-six years of age, but received it back when he was sixty.
4 The rest of his life was spent in joy, and he proceeded in peace with good progress in the fear of God.
5 But at the hour of his death, he called to him his son Tobias, and the seven young men who were his grandsons, and said to them:
6 "The destruction of Nineveh is near; for the word of the Lord does not <margin>† Isaiah (?) 13:8</margin> fail; and our brothers, who have been scattered from the land of Israel, shall return to it.
7 "All its deserted land shall be filled, and the house of God, which was burned within it,

<column-break/>

shall be rebuilt again: and all those who fear God shall return there,
8 "And the nations shall leave their idols, and shall come to Jerusalem, and shall dwell in it,
9 "And all the kings of the earth shall rejoice in it, worshipping the King of Israel.
10 "Therefore, my sons, hear your father: serve the Lord in truth, and seek to do the things that please him.
11 "And command your children to do justice and almsgiving, so that they may be mindful of God, and bless him at all times in truth, and with all their strength.
12 "Now therefore, sons, hear me, and do not remain here: but on whatever day you shall bury your mother with me in one grave, from that moment direct your steps to leave this place:
13 "For I see that its iniquity <note>original: "iniquitas ejus." Referring to the wickedness of the city of Nineveh.</note> will bring an end to it."
14 And it happened after the death of his mother, that Tobias departed from Nineveh with his wife, and his sons, and his sons’ sons, and returned to his parents-in-law.
15 And he found them healthy in a good old age: and he took care of them, and he himself closed their eyes: and he inherited the entire estate of the house of Raguel: and he saw the fifth generation, the children of his grandchildren.
16 And having completed ninety-nine years in the fear of the Lord, they buried him with joy.
17 And all his kindred, and all his generation, continued in a good life, and in holy conduct, so that they were accepted both by God and by men, and by all the inhabitants of the land.
