7. He scorns the crowd of the city, he does not hear the shout of the driver.
8. He looks around the mountains for his pasture, and seeks out every green thing.
9. Will the rhinoceros <note>original: "rhinoceros"; in the Latin Vulgate, this refers to the *re'em*, a powerful, untamable wild ox</note> be willing to serve you, or will he stay at your manger?
10. Will you bind the rhinoceros with your strap to plow? Or will he break the clods of the valleys after you?
11. Will you have confidence in his great strength, and leave your labors to him?
12. Will you trust him to return your seed to you, and gather your threshing floor?
13. The wing of the ostrich is like the wings of the heron and the hawk.
14. When she leaves her eggs on the earth, perhaps you will warm them in the dust?
15. She forgets that a foot may trample them, or a beast of the field crush them.
16. She is hardened against her young as if they were not hers; she has labored in vain with no fear compelling her.
17. For God has deprived her of wisdom, nor has He given her understanding.
18. When the time comes, she lifts her wings on high: she laughs at the horse and his rider.
19. Will you give strength to the horse, or will you surround his neck with neighing?
20. Will you startle him like locusts? The glory of his nostrils is terror.
21. He digs the earth with his hoof, he exults boldly: he goes forward to meet armed men.
22. He scorns fear, nor does he yield to the sword.
23. Over him the quiver shall rattle, the spear and shield shall vibrate.
24. Fervent and snorting, he swallows the ground, nor does he notice the sounding of the trumpet blast.
25. When he hears the trumpet, he says: "Aha!" He smells the battle from afar, the encouragement of the leaders, and the shouting of the army.
26. Does the hawk grow feathers by your wisdom, spreading its wings toward the south?
27. Will the eagle be lifted up at your command, and place its nest in high places?
28. It stays in the rocks, and dwells in the craggy flints and inaccessible cliffs.
29. From there it looks for food, and its eyes behold from afar.
30. Its young lick up blood: and wherever the carcass is, it is there immediately.
31. And the Lord added, and spoke to Job:
32. Will he who contends with God rest so easily? Surely he who rebukes God ought to answer Him.
33. Then Job, answering the Lord, said:
34. I who have spoken lightly, what can I answer? I will put my hand over my mouth.
35. I have spoken one thing, which I wish I had not said, and another, to which I will add no more.

### CHAPTER XLI.

*The might of Leviathan <note>The Latin text here uses "Behemoth," but the chapter describes Leviathan.</note> is explained more fully according to his members, his hardness, and his pride.*

1 I will not rouse him as if I were cruel: for who can resist my countenance?
2 Who has given to me first, that I should repay him? All things that are under heaven are mine.
3 I will not spare him, nor his mighty words, nor those composed for entreaty.
4 Who shall reveal the face of his garment? And who shall enter into the midst of his mouth?
5 Who shall open the doors of his face? Terror is round about his teeth.
6 His body is like molten shields, shut close with scales pressing upon each other.

<column-break/>

7 One is joined to another, and not even a breathing hole <note>original: "spiraculum"; refers to an air passage or vent.</note> gets between them.
8 One shall stick to another, and holding each other they shall by no means be separated.
9 His sneezing is a splendor of fire, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.
10 Out of his mouth proceed lamps, like torches of lighted fire.
11 Out of his nostrils proceeds smoke, like a pot heated and boiling.
12 His breath makes coals burn, and a flame goes out of his mouth.
13 In his neck strength shall dwell, and want <note>original: "egestas"; sometimes interpreted as "terror" or "destruction" in this context.</note> goes before his face.
14 The members of his flesh cling together: he shall send lightning against him, and they shall not be carried to another place.
15 His heart shall be hardened like a stone, and shall be as tight as a smith's anvil.
16 When he is raised up, the angels <note>original: "angeli"; in the context of the Vulgate, this can refer to mighty beings or "the gods."</note> shall fear, and being terrified they shall be purified.
17 When the sword reaches him, it shall not be able to hold, nor the spear, nor the breastplate.
18 For he shall esteem iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
19 The archer shall not put him to flight, the stones of the sling are turned into stubble for him.
20 He shall esteem the hammer as stubble, and he shall deride the shaking of the spear.
21 Under him shall be the rays of the sun, and he shall spread gold under him like mud.
22 He shall make the deep sea boil like a pot, and shall set it as when ointments boil.
23 A path shall shine after him, he shall esteem the abyss as growing old.
24 There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him, who was made to fear no one.
25 He beholds every high thing, he is king over all the children of pride.

### CHAPTER XLII.

*Job acknowledges that he has spoken foolishly, and he is preferred by the Lord over his friends, and he prays for them: receiving double what he had lost, and finally full of days he rested in peace.*

1 Then Job answering the Lord, said:

5 With the hearing of the ear I have heard you, but now my eye sees you.
6 Therefore I reprehend myself, and do penance in embers and ashes.

1 *Unto the end, a Psalm of David.*
### XVIII.
<note>Modern Bibles number this as Psalm 19. It is a famous hymn praising God’s revelation through nature and the Law.</note>

2 The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament <note>original: "firmamentum" — the "expanse" of the sky, thought of as a solid dome in ancient cosmology.</note> announces the works of his hands.
3 Day unto day utters speech, and night unto night shows knowledge.
4 There are no languages nor speeches where their voices are not heard.
<margin>Romans 10:18</margin>
5 † Their sound has gone forth into all the earth: and their words unto the ends of the world.
<margin>Luke 24:46</margin>
6 He has set his tabernacle in the sun: † and he, as a bridegroom coming out of his bridal chamber,
Has rejoiced as a giant <note>original: "gigas" — referring to a champion or strong man ready for a race.</note> to run the way.
7 His going out is from the highest heaven:
And his circuit even to the summit thereof: and there is no one that can hide himself from his heat.
8 The law of the Lord is spotless, converting souls: the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones.
9 The justices of the Lord are right, rejoicing hearts: the commandment of the Lord is light, enlightening the eyes.
10 The fear of the Lord is holy, enduring for ever and ever: the judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves.
11 More to be desired than gold and many precious stones: and sweeter than honey and the honeycomb.
12 For your servant keeps them, and in keeping them there is a great reward.
13 Who can understand sins? From my secret ones cleanse me:
14 And from those of others spare your servant.
If they shall have no dominion over me, then shall I be spotless: and I shall be cleansed from the greatest sin.
15 And the words of my mouth shall be such as may please: and the meditation of my heart shall be always in your sight.
O Lord, my helper, and my redeemer.

7 You have hated those who observe vanities <note>meaning false idols or useless superstitions</note> to no purpose.
But I have hoped in the Lord:
8 I will exult, and rejoice in your mercy.
For you have regarded my humility, you have saved my soul from necessities <note>original: "necessitatibus" — distresses or inescapable troubles</note>.
9 Nor have you shut me up in the hands of the enemy: you have set my feet in a spacious place.
10 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: my eye is troubled with wrath, as are my soul and my belly <note>the "belly" or "venter" was seen as the seat of deep emotion</note>:
11 For my life has failed in sorrow: and my years in groanings.
My strength is weakened in poverty: and my bones are troubled.
12 I am become a reproach among all my enemies, and very much to my neighbors, and a fear to my acquaintances.
Those who saw me fled away from me:
13 I am forgotten, like one dead from the heart.
I am become like a broken vessel:
14 For I have heard the blame of many living round about:
While they assembled together against me, they consulted to take away my life.
15 But I have hoped in you, O Lord, I said: You are my God:
16 My lots <note>original: "sortes" — one's destiny or portion of life</note> are in your hands.
Deliver me from the hand of my enemies, and from those who persecute me.
17 Make your face shine upon your servant, save me in your mercy:
18 O Lord, let me not be confounded, for I have called upon you.
Let the impious be ashamed, and be brought down into hell:
19 Let deceitful lips be made mute.
Which speak iniquity against the just, in pride and in abuse.
20 How great is the multitude of your sweetness, O Lord, which you have hidden for those who fear you.

<column-break/>

Which you have perfected for those who hope in you, in the sight of the sons of men.
21 You shall hide them in the secret of your face from the disturbance of men.
You shall protect them in your tabernacle from the contradiction of tongues.
22 Blessed be the Lord: for he has shown his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.
23 But I said in the excess of my mind <note>original: "in excessu mentis meae" — in a moment of panic or distraction</note>: I am cast away from before your eyes.
Therefore you heard the voice of my prayer, when I cried to you.
24 Love the Lord, all you his saints: for the Lord will require truth, and will repay abundantly those who act with pride.
25 Act manfully <note>original: "Viriliter agite" — a call to courage and strength</note>, and let your heart be strengthened, all you who hope in the Lord.

-> *To David himself, a meditation.* <note>original: "intellectus" — a poem of instruction or insight</note> *XXXI.* <-

<margin>Romans 4:7.</margin>
Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven: and whose sins are covered.
2 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not imputed sin, and in whose spirit there is no guile.
3 Because I was silent, my bones grew old, while I cried out all the day long.
4 For day and night your hand was heavy upon me: I am turned in my anguish, while the thorn is fastened <note>original: "configitur spina" — a metaphor for the piercing pain of a guilty conscience</note>.
5 I have made my sin known to you: and my injustice I have not hidden.
<margin>† Isaiah 65:24.</margin>
† I said: I will confess my injustice against myself to the Lord: and you have forgiven the impiety of my sin.
6 For this shall every saint pray to you, in a seasonable time.
Yet in a flood of many waters, they shall not come near him.
7 You are my refuge from the tribulation which has surrounded me: my joy, deliver me from those who encompass me.
8 I will give you understanding, and I will instruct you in this way in which you shall go: I will fix my eyes upon you.
9 Do not become like the horse and the mule, which have no understanding.
With bit and bridle bind their jaws, those who do not come near to you.
10 Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy shall encompass him who hopes in the Lord.
11 Be glad in the Lord and exult, you just, and glory, all you who are right of heart.

### For David himself. XXXIV. <note>In modern Bibles, this is Psalm 35. It is a plea for God to act as a legal advocate and a warrior against enemies.</note>

**J**udge, O Lord, those who harm me; fight against those who fight against me.
2 Take up arms and shield: and rise up to help me.
3 Draw out the spear <note>original: "frameam" — a word for a spear or a sword</note>, and block the way against those who persecute me: say to my soul: I am your salvation.
<margin>† Below 39:15.</margin>
4 † Let them be confounded and put to shame, who seek after my soul.
Let them be turned back and confounded, who devise evil against me.
5 Let them become like dust before the face of the wind: and let the Angel of the Lord drive them away.

7 For without cause they have hidden their snare for my destruction: without cause they have reproached my soul.
8 Let a trap come upon him which he does not know: and let the snare which he has hidden catch him: and let him fall into that very trap.
9 But my soul shall exult in the Lord: and shall rejoice in his salvation.
10 All my bones shall say: Lord, who is like you?
Delivering the needy from the hand of those stronger than him: the needy and the poor from those who rob him.
11 Unjust witnesses rising up, questioned me about things I did not know.
12 They repaid me evil for good: to the barrenness of my soul.
13 But as for me, when they were troublesome to me, I was clothed in sackcloth.
I humbled my soul with fasting: and my prayer shall be turned back into my own bosom.
14 As if for a neighbor or our own brother, so did I act to please: as one mourning and sorrowful, so was I humbled.
15 But they rejoiced against me and gathered together: scourges were gathered over me, and I did not know why.
16 They were scattered, yet felt no remorse; they tempted me, they mocked me with mockery: they gnashed their teeth at me.
17 Lord, when will you look upon me? Restore my soul from their malice, my only one <note>original: "unicam meam" — referring to his life or soul as his most precious, solitary possession</note> from the lions.

22 You have seen, O Lord, do not be silent: O Lord, do not depart from me.

### 1 A Psalm of David, for a remembrance of the Sabbath. XXXVII. <note>In modern Bibles, this is Psalm 38. The "remembrance of the Sabbath" likely refers to the "memorial offering" or the "shewbread" presented on the Sabbath.</note>

### To the end, a Psalm of David himself. XL. <note>Psalm 41 in modern Bibles. This psalm focuses on the treatment of the poor and the treachery of friends.</note>

2 Blessed is he who understands the needy and the poor: the Lord will deliver him in the evil day.
3 May the Lord preserve him, and give him life, and make him blessed upon the earth: and not deliver him up to the will of his enemies.
4 The Lord bring him help upon his bed of sorrow: you have turned all his bedding <note>original: "stratum" — implying a complete refreshing or changing of the sickbed.</note> in his sickness.
5 I said: O Lord, have mercy on me: heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.
6 My enemies have spoken evil against me: "When will he die, and his name perish?"
7 And if he came in to see me, he spoke vain things: his heart gathered iniquity to itself.
He went out, and spoke to the same purpose.
8 All my enemies whispered against me: they thought evil against me.
9 They determined an unjust word against me: "Will he that sleeps rise no more?"
<margin>† Acts 1:16. <note>In the New Testament, Peter applies this verse to the betrayal by Judas Iscariot.</note></margin>
10 † For even the man of my peace, in whom I trusted: who ate my bread, has greatly increased his treachery <note>original: "supplantationem" — literally a tripping up or an overthrowing.</note> against me.
11 But you, O Lord, have mercy on me, and raise me up: and I will repay them.
12 By this I knew that you have preferred me: because my enemy shall not rejoice over me.
13 But you have upheld me because of my innocence: and you have established me in your sight forever.

### To the end, Understanding for the sons of Korah. XLI. <note>Psalm 42 in modern Bibles. The "sons of Korah" were a family of Levites who served as temple singers and gatekeepers.</note>

2 As the deer longs for the springs of water: so my soul longs for you, O God.
3 My soul has thirsted after the strong living God: when shall I come and appear before the face of God?
4 My tears have been my bread day and night: while it is said to me daily: "Where is your God?"
5 These things I remembered, and I poured out my soul within me: for I shall go over into the place of the wonderful tabernacle, even to the house of God:
With the voice of joy and praise: the sound of one feasting.
6 Why are you sad, my soul? and why do you disquiet me?
Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: the salvation of my countenance,
7 And my God.
My soul is troubled within myself: therefore I will remember you from the land of Jordan and Hermon, <note>original: "Hermoniim" — the mountain range in the north of Israel.</note> from the little mountain.

<column-break/>

8 Deep calls unto deep, at the voice of your flood-gates. <note>original: "cataractarum" — can refer to waterfalls or the windows of heaven.</note>
All your heights and your waves have passed over me.

With me is a prayer to the God of my life,
10 I will say to God: You are my sustainer,
Why have you forgotten me? and why do I go mourning, while the enemy afflicts me?
11 While my bones are broken, my enemies who trouble me have reproached me.
While they say to me day by day: "Where is your God?"
12 Why are you sad, my soul? and why do you disquiet me?
Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

### A Psalm of Asaph. XLIX. <note>Psalm 50 in modern Bibles. Asaph was a contemporary of David and a leader of the temple choir.</note>

1 **T**he God of gods, the Lord, has spoken: and he has called the earth,
From the rising of the sun to its setting:
2 Out of Zion is the perfection of his beauty.
3 God shall come manifestly: our God shall come and shall not keep silence.
A fire shall burn before him: and a mighty tempest shall be round about him.
4 He shall call the heavens from above: and the earth, to judge his people.
5 Gather to him his saints: who set his covenant before sacrifices.
6 And the heavens shall declare his justice: for God is the judge.
7 Hear, O my people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to you: I am God, your God.
8 I will not reprove you for your sacrifices: and your burnt offerings are always in my sight.
9 I will not accept calves from your house: nor he-goats from your flocks.
10 For all the beasts of the woods are mine: the cattle on the mountains, and the oxen.
11 I know all the fowls of the air: and the beauty of the field is with me.
12 If I should be hungry, I would not tell you: for the world is mine, and the fullness thereof.
13 Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? Or shall I drink the blood of goats?
14 Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: and pay your vows to the Most High.
15 And call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me.
16 But to the sinner God has said: Why do you declare my justices, and take my covenant in your mouth?
17 For you have hated discipline: and have cast my words behind you.
18 If you saw a thief, you ran with him: and you have been a partaker with adulterers.
19 Your mouth has abounded with evil: and your tongue framed deceits.
20 Sitting, you spoke against your brother, and laid a scandal against your mother's son:
21 These things you have done, and I was silent.
You thought unjustly that I should be like you: I will reprove you, and set them before your face.
22 Understand these things, you who forget God: lest he snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.
23 The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: and there is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God.

2 Deliver me from my enemies, O my God: and defend me from those who rise up against me.

### A Psalm of David; when he was in the desert of Idumea. LXII. <note>Modern Psalm 63. Idumea is the biblical name for Edom, a harsh desert region.</note>

O God, my God, for you I watch from the break of dawn.
2 My soul has thirsted for you; in how many ways my flesh has longed for you.
3 In a desert land, pathless and waterless: so in the sanctuary I have appeared before you, that I might see your power and your glory.
4 Because your mercy is better than lives: my lips shall praise you.
5 Thus will I bless you in my life, and in your name I will lift up my hands.
6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: and my mouth shall praise you with lips of joy.
7 If I have remembered you upon my bed, in the morning I will meditate on you.
8 Because you have been my helper.
And in the shadow of your wings I will rejoice.
9 My soul has stuck close behind you: your right hand has received me.
10 But they have sought my soul in vain; they shall go into the lower parts of the earth:
11 They shall be delivered into the hands of the sword; they shall be the portions of foxes.
12 But the king shall rejoice in God; all they who swear by him shall be praised: because the mouth of those speaking wicked things is stopped.

### Unto the end, a Psalm of David. LXIII. <note>Modern Psalm 64. The phrase "Unto the end" is a common heading in the Psalms, often interpreted as a dedication to the choirmaster or a reference to the Messiah.</note>

2 Hear, O God, my prayer when I make supplication: deliver my soul from the fear of the enemy.
3 You have protected me from the assembly of the wicked: from the multitude of those working iniquity.
4 For they have sharpened their tongues like a sword: they have bent their bow, a bitter thing,
5 That they may shoot in secret at the innocent.
6 Suddenly they will shoot at him, and will not fear: they have grown firm in their wicked speech.
They have talked of hiding snares: they said: Who shall see them?
7 They have searched out iniquities: they have failed in their search.
A man shall approach to a deep heart:
8 And God shall be exalted.
The arrows of children are become their wounds.
9 And their tongues are made weak against them.
All who saw them were troubled:
10 And every man was afraid.
And they declared the works of God: and understood his deeds.
11 The just shall rejoice in the Lord, and shall hope in him, and all the upright in heart shall be praised.

### Unto the end, a Psalm of David, a Song of Jeremiah and Ezekiel for the people of the exile, when they began to go out. LXIV. <note>Modern Psalm 65. This subtitle suggests the psalm was used by the Jewish people as they prepared to return from the Babylonian Captivity.</note>

2 A hymn is due to you, O God, in Sion: and a vow shall be paid to you in Jerusalem.
3 Hear my prayer: all flesh shall come to you.

<column-break/>

4 The words of the wicked have prevailed over us: and you will be merciful to our impieties.
5 Blessed is he whom you have chosen and taken up: he shall dwell in your courts.
We shall be filled with the good things of your house: holy is your temple,
6 Wonderful in equity.
Hear us, O God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth, and in the sea afar off.
7 You who prepare the mountains by your strength, being girded with power:
8 Who trouble the depth of the sea, the noise of its waves.
The nations shall be troubled,
9 And those who dwell at the borders shall be afraid at your signs: you shall make the outgoings of the morning and the evening joyful.
10 You have visited the earth and watered it: you have enriched it in many ways.
The river of God is filled with water; you have prepared their food: for so is its preparation.
11 Fill its furrows with water, multiply its fruits: the springing plant shall rejoice in its droplets.
12 You will bless the crown of the year of your goodness: and your fields shall be filled with plenty.
13 The beautiful places of the wilderness shall grow fat, and the hills shall be girded with joy.
14 The rams of the flock are clothed, and the valleys shall abound with corn: they shall shout, yea, they shall sing a hymn.

### Unto the end, a Song of a Psalm of the resurrection. LXV. <note>Modern Psalm 66.</note>

Shout with joy to God, all the earth.
2 Sing a psalm to his name: give glory to his praise.

6 Who turned the sea into dry land, in the river they shall pass through on foot: there we shall rejoice in him.
7 Who rules by his power forever; his eyes behold the nations: let not those who provoke him be exalted in themselves.
8 O nations, bless our God: and make the voice of his praise to be heard.
9 Who has set my soul unto life: and has not suffered my feet to be moved.
10 For you, O God, have proved us: you have tried us by fire, as silver is tried.
11 You have brought us into a snare, you have laid afflictions on our back:
12 You have set men over our heads.
We have passed through fire and water: and you have brought us out into a place of refreshment.
13 I will go into your house with <term>burnt offerings</term> <note>original: "holocaustis." A sacrifice entirely consumed by fire.</note>: I will pay you my vows,
14 Which my lips have uttered.
And my mouth has spoken, in my affliction.
15 I will offer to you fat burnt offerings with the incense of rams: I will offer to you bullocks with goats.
16 Come, hear, and I will tell you, all you who fear God, what great things he has done for my soul.

->Unto the end, a Psalm of David, in remembrance, that the Lord saved him. LXIX.<- <note>Modern Psalm 70. This short psalm is almost identical to the end of Psalm 40 and is used as a standard opening prayer in the Western liturgy.</note>

1 O God, come to my assistance: O Lord, make haste to help me.
3 Let them be confounded and ashamed who seek my soul:
4 Let them be turned backward and blush for shame who wish me evil:
Let them be turned back at once and blush for shame, who say to me: "Aha, aha!"
5 Let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you, and let those who love your salvation say always: "The Lord be magnified."
6 But I am needy and poor: O God, help me.
You are my helper and my deliverer: O Lord, do not delay.

# Psalm.
->For Solomon. 71. <note>Psalm 72 in modern numbering. This is a royal psalm, often read as a prophecy of the coming Messiah.</note><-

O God, give your judgment to the king: and your justice to the son of the king:
2 To judge your people in justice, and your poor in judgment.
3 Let the mountains receive peace for the people, and the hills justice.
4 He shall judge the poor of the people, and save the children of the poor: and he shall humble the oppressor.
5 And he shall continue with the sun, and before the moon, throughout all generations.
6 He shall come down like rain upon the fleece: <note>Original: "vellus." A reference to Gideon's fleece, often interpreted as a gentle, miraculous arrival.</note> and like drops falling upon the earth.
7 In his days justice shall arise, and abundance of peace: until the moon be taken away.
8 And he shall rule from sea to sea: and from the river unto the ends of the earth.
9 Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down: and his enemies shall lick the ground.
10 The kings of Tarshish <note>A distant, wealthy port, likely in Spain.</note> and the islands shall offer presents: the kings of the Arabs and of Sheba shall bring gifts:
11 And all the kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him:
12 For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty: and the poor man who had no helper.
13 He shall spare the poor and the needy: and he shall save the souls of the poor.
14 He shall redeem their souls from usury and iniquity: and their name shall be honorable in his sight.
15 And he shall live, and to him shall be given the gold of Arabia, and they shall adore him always: they shall bless him all the day.
16 And there shall be a firm support <note>Original: "firmamentum." Often interpreted as an abundance of grain.</note> in the earth on the tops of the mountains; its fruit shall be exalted above Lebanon: and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth.
17 May his name be blessed for ever: his name continues before the sun.
18 And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: all nations shall magnify him.
19 Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who alone does wonderful things:
20 And blessed be the name of his majesty for ever: and the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty: so be it, so be it.
The praises of David, the son of Jesse, are ended. <note>This marks the traditional end of the second collection of Psalms.</note>

# A Psalm of Asaph. 72. <note>Psalm 73 in modern numbering. Asaph was a temple musician.</note>

How good is God to Israel, to those who are of a right heart!
2 But my feet were almost moved: my steps had well-nigh slipped.
3 For I was envious of the wicked, seeing the peace of sinners.
4 For there is no regard for their death: and there is strength in their wounds.
5 They are not in the labor of men, and they shall not be scourged with other men:
6 Therefore pride has held them fast; they are covered with their iniquity and impiety.
7 Their iniquity has come forth as it were from fatness: <note>A metaphor for excess and luxury.</note> they have passed into the desire of the heart.
8 They have thought and spoken wickedness: they have spoken iniquity on high.
9 They have set their mouth against heaven: and their tongue has passed through the earth.
10 Therefore my people will turn here: and full days shall be found in them.
11 And they said: How does God know, and is there knowledge in the Most High?
12 Behold, these are sinners, and abounding in the world, they have obtained riches.
13 And I said: Then have I justified my heart in vain, and washed my hands among the innocent in vain:
14 And I have been scourged all the day long, and my chastisement has been in the mornings.
15 If I said: I will speak thus: behold, I should condemn the generation of your children.
16 I studied that I might know this, but it was a labor before me:
17 Until I go into the sanctuary of God: and understand their final end.
18 But indeed, because of their deceits you have set it for them: you have cast them down while they were being lifted up.
19 How they are brought to desolation! They have suddenly failed: they have perished because of their iniquity.
20 Like the dream of those who awaken, O Lord, in your city you shall reduce their image to nothing.
21 For my heart was inflamed, and my reins <note>The "reins" or kidneys were considered the seat of deep emotion.</note> were changed:
22 And I was reduced to nothing, and I knew it not.
23 I became like a beast of burden before you: and I am always with you.
24 You have held my right hand: and by your will you have conducted me, and with glory you have received me.
25 For what have I in heaven? And besides you, what do I desire upon earth?
26 My flesh and my heart have failed: God is the God of my heart, and God is my portion for ever.
27 For behold, they who go far from you shall perish: you have destroyed all those who are unfaithful to you.
28 But for me, it is good to adhere to God: to put my hope in the Lord God:
That I may announce all your praises, in the gates of the daughter of Zion.

### Unto the end, for Jeduthun, A Psalm of Asaph. 76. <note>Psalm 77 in modern numbering. Jeduthun was one of the three directors of music in the Temple.</note>

2 With my voice I cried to the Lord: with my voice to God, and he gave ear to me.
3 In the day of my trouble I sought God, with my hands lifted up to him in the night: and I was not deceived.
My soul refused to be comforted,
4 I was mindful of God, and was delighted, and was exercised: and my spirit fainted.
5 My eyes anticipated the night watches: I was troubled, and I spoke not.
6 I thought upon the days of old: and I had in my mind the eternal years.
7 And I meditated in the night with my own heart, and I was exercised, and I swept my spirit.
8 Will God then cast off forever? Or will he never be more favorable again?
9 Or will he cut off his mercy until the end, from generation to generation?
10 Or will God forget to show mercy? Or will he shut up his mercies in his anger?
11 And I said: "Now I have begun: this is the change of the right hand of the Most High." <note>Meaning the speaker begins to find hope by remembering how God's power has changed situations in the past.</note>
12 I was mindful of the works of the Lord: for I will remember your wonders from the beginning,
13 And I will meditate on all your works: and I will be exercised in your inventions. <note>Original: "adinventionibus." Referring to God's designs or marvelous deeds.</note>
14 Your way, O God, is in the holy place: who is the great God like our God?
15 You are the God who does wonders.
You have made your power known among the nations:
16 You have redeemed your people with your arm, the sons of Jacob and Joseph.

### A Psalm of Asaph. LXXVIII. <note>Psalm 79 in modern Bibles. This is a communal lament, likely written after the Babylonian destruction of Jerusalem.</note>

O God, the nations have come into your inheritance, they have defiled your holy temple: they have made Jerusalem like a hut for orchard-keepers. <note>Original: "pomorum custodiam." This suggests a flimsy, temporary shelter, emphasizing how ruined and desolate the city has become.</note>
2 They have given the dead bodies of your servants as meat for the birds of the air: the flesh of your saints to the beasts of the earth.
3 They have poured out their blood like water round about Jerusalem: and there was no one to bury them.
4 We have become a reproach to our neighbors: a scorn and derision to those who are around us.
5 How long, Lord, will you be angry forever: will your jealousy be kindled like fire?
<margin>† Jeremiah 10:25.</margin>
6 † Pour out your wrath upon the nations that have not known you: and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon your name.
7 For they have devoured Jacob: and have made his place desolate.
<margin>† Isaiah 64:9.</margin>
8 † Remember not our old iniquities, let your mercies quickly prevent us: for we have become exceeding poor.
9 Help us, O God our Savior: and for the glory of your name, Lord, deliver us: and be merciful to our sins, for your name's sake:
10 Lest they should say among the nations: Where is their God? And let the vengeance for the blood of your servants, which has been shed, be known among the nations before our eyes.

<column-break/>

11 Let the groaning of the prisoners come before you.
According to the greatness of your arm, take possession of the children of those who have been put to death.
12 And render to our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom: the reproach with which they have reproached you, O Lord.
13 But we, your people, and the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever:
From generation to generation we will announce your praise.

### To the end, For those who shall be changed, a testimony of Asaph, Psalm LXXIX. <note>Psalm 80 in modern Bibles. The phrase "For those who shall be changed" (Pro iis qui commutabuntur) is a translation of the Hebrew musical direction "Shoshannim," meaning "Lilies."</note>

Give ear, O you who rule Israel: you who lead Joseph like a sheep.
You who sit upon the cherubim, shine forth
2 Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh.
3 Stir up your power, and come, to save us.
4 O God, convert us: and show us your face, and we shall be saved. <note>The word "convert" (converte) here carries the sense of "restore" or "bring us back."</note>
5 O Lord God of hosts, how long will you be angry against the prayer of your servant?
6 Will you feed us with the bread of tears: and give us tears to drink in measure?
7 You have made us a source of contention to our neighbors: and our enemies have scoffed at us.
8 O God of hosts, convert us: and show us your face, and we shall be saved.
9 You brought a vine out of Egypt: you cast out the nations, and planted it.
10 You were the guide of its journey in its sight: you planted its roots, and it filled the land.
11 Its shadow covered the mountains: and its branches the cedars of God.
12 It stretched out its boughs even to the sea: and its shoots even to the river.

14 The boar from the wood has laid it waste: and a singular wild beast has devoured it.
15 O God of hosts, return: look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vine.
16 And perfect that which your right hand has planted: and look upon the son of man <note>In this context, "son of man" refers to the king or the people of Israel whom God has strengthened.</note> whom you have confirmed for yourself.
17 Things set on fire and dug up will perish at the rebuke of your face.
18 Let your hand be upon the man of your right hand: and upon the son of man whom you have confirmed for yourself.
19 And we do not depart from you, you will quicken us: and we will call upon your name.
20 O Lord God of hosts, convert us: and show us your face, and we shall be saved.

I was delivered up, and I did not come forth:

17 Your wrath has come upon me: and your terrors have troubled me.
18 They have surrounded me like water all the day: they have surrounded me all at once.
19 You have put far from me friend and neighbor: and my acquaintances because of misery.

### A Song of Praise by David. XC.
<note>Psalm 91 in modern Bibles. This is a famous psalm of protection, often used in the liturgy of Compline (night prayer).</note>

He who dwells in the aid of the Most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of heaven.
2 He shall say to the Lord: You are my sustainer and my refuge: my God, in him will I hope.
3 For he has delivered me from the snare of the hunters: and from the harsh word.
4 He will overshadow you with his shoulders: and under his wings you shall hope.
5 His truth shall compass you with a shield: you shall not be afraid of the terror of the night,
6 Of the arrow that flies in the day, of the business that walks about in the dark: of invasion, or of the noonday devil <note>original: "dæmonio meridiano" — historically interpreted by monks as 'acedia' or spiritual sloth that strikes in the middle of the day</note>.
7 A thousand shall fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand: but it shall not come near you.
8 But you shall consider with your eyes: and shall see the reward of the wicked.
9 Because you, O Lord, are my hope: you have made the Most High your refuge.
10 No evil shall come to you: and the scourge shall not come near your dwelling.
<margin>Matthew 4:6.</margin>
11 For he has given his angels charge over you: to keep you in all your ways.
<margin>chapter 4</margin>
12 In their hands they shall bear you up: lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.
13 You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk <note>original: "basiliscium" — a mythical serpent king; here representing deadly spiritual enemies</note>: and you shall trample underfoot the lion and the dragon.
14 Because he hoped in me, I will deliver him: I will protect him, because he has known my name.
15 He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: I am with him in tribulation: I will deliver him, and I will glorify him.
16 I will fill him with length of days: and I will show him my salvation.

### A Psalm of a Song, on the Sabbath Day. XCI.

It is good to give praise to the Lord, and to sing to your name, O Most High:
2 To show forth your mercy in the morning, and your truth throughout the night;
3 Upon an instrument of ten strings, upon the psaltery: with a song, upon the harp.
4 For you have delighted me, O Lord, in your workmanship: and I shall rejoice in the works of your hands.
5 How great are your works, O Lord! 

<column-break/>

Your thoughts are made exceeding deep.
7 The senseless man shall not know: and the fool shall not understand these things.
8 When sinners shall spring up like grass: and all who work iniquity shall appear:
That they may perish for ever and ever:
9 But you, O Lord, are the Most High for evermore.
10 For behold, your enemies, O Lord, for behold, your enemies shall perish: and all the workers of iniquity shall be scattered.
11 And my horn shall be exalted like that of the unicorn <note>original: "unicornis" — often a translation for a wild ox or a creature of great strength</note>: and my old age shall be anointed with plentiful mercy.
12 And my eye has looked down upon my enemies: and my ear shall hear of the downfall of the malignant who rise up against me.
13 The just shall flourish like the palm tree: he shall grow up like the cedar of Libanus <note>Lebanon</note>.
14 They that are planted in the house of the Lord shall flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
15 They shall still increase in a fruitful old age: and shall be well-treated,
16 That they may announce:
That the Lord our God is righteous: and there is no iniquity in him.

### A Song of Praise for David himself, on the day before the Sabbath, when the earth was founded. XCII.

The Lord has reigned, he is clothed with beauty: the Lord is clothed with strength, and has girded himself.
For he has established the world, which shall not be moved.
2 Your throne is prepared from of old: you are from everlasting.
3 The floods have lifted up, O Lord: the floods have lifted up their voice.
The floods have lifted up their waves,
4 With the noise of many waters.
Wonderful are the surges of the sea: wonderful is the Lord on high.
5 Your testimonies are made exceedingly credible: holiness becomes your house, O Lord, unto length of days.

### A Psalm for David himself. On the fourth day of the week. XCIII.

The Lord is the God of vengeance: the God of vengeance has acted freely.
2 Lift yourself up, you who judge the earth: render a reward to the proud.
3 How long shall sinners, O Lord: how long shall sinners glory?
4 Shall they utter, and speak iniquity: shall all speak who work injustice?
5 They have humbled your people, O Lord: and have vexed your inheritance.
6 They have slain the widow and the stranger: and have murdered the fatherless.
7 And they have said: The Lord shall not see, nor shall the God of Jacob understand.
8 Understand, you senseless among the people: and you fools, be wise at last.
9 He who planted the ear, shall he not hear? Or he who formed the eye, does he not consider?
10 He who chastises nations, shall he not rebuke: he who teaches man knowledge?
11 The Lord knows the thoughts of men, that they are vain.

The numbering and titles reflect the liturgical and historical tradition of the Latin Church.</meta>

12 Blessed is the man whom you shall instruct, O Lord, and shall teach him out of your law:
13 That you may give him rest from the evil days, until a pit be dug for the sinner.
14 For the Lord will not cast off his people, and he will not forsake his inheritance.
15 Until justice be turned into judgment: and all they that are upright in heart follow after it.
16 Who shall rise up for me against the evildoers? or who shall stand with me against the workers of iniquity?
17 Unless the Lord had helped me, my soul had almost dwelt in hell <note>original: "inferno" — referring to Sheol or the place of the dead.</note>.
18 If I said: My foot is moved: your mercy, O Lord, assisted me.
19 According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, your comforts have given joy to my soul.
20 Does the throne of iniquity cling to you, you who frame labor in a commandment? <note>This verse suggests that corrupt rulers try to give their injustice the appearance of law.</note>
21 They will hunt after the soul of the just, and will condemn innocent blood.
22 But the Lord is become my refuge; and my God is the help of my hope.
23 And he will render them their iniquity: and in their malice he will destroy them: the Lord our God will destroy them.

### A Song of Praise for David himself. XCIV.
<note>Psalm 95 in modern Bibles. This is the "Venite," the traditional opening psalm for the Liturgy of the Hours.</note>

1 Come, let us exult in the Lord: let us rejoice in God our Savior.
2 Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
3 For the Lord is a great God: and a great king above all gods.
4 For in his hand are all the ends of the earth: and the heights of the mountains are his.
5 For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land.
6 Come, let us adore, and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us.
7 For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand.
<margin>† Hebrews 3:7, 8 & 4:7.</margin>
8 † Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
9 As in the provocation according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<margin>† Numbers 14:24.</margin>
10 † Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart.
<margin>† Hebrews 4:3.</margin>
11 † And these have not known my ways: † as I swore in my wrath: They shall not enter <note>original: "Si introibunt" — literally "If they shall enter," a Hebrew idiom for a strong negative oath: "They shall never enter."</note> into my rest.

### A Song for David himself. When the house was built after the captivity. (1 Chronicles 15.) XCV.
<note>Psalm 96 in modern Bibles. This psalm celebrates the restoration of the Temple and God’s kingship over all nations.</note>

1 Sing to the Lord a new song: sing to the Lord, all the earth.
2 Sing to the Lord, and bless his name: show forth his salvation from day to day.
3 Declare his glory among the Gentiles, his wonders among all people.
4 For the Lord is great, and exceedingly to be praised: he is terrible above all gods.
5 For all the gods of the Gentiles are demons <note>original: "dæmonia" — in early Christian thought, the pagan gods were often interpreted as fallen angels or demons.</note>: but the Lord made the heavens.
6 Thanksgiving and beauty are in his sight,

<column-break/>

holiness and magnificence in his sanctuary.
7 Bring to the Lord, O you kindreds of the Gentiles, bring to the Lord glory and honor:
8 Bring to the Lord glory to his name.
Bring sacrifices, and come into his courts:
9 Adore the Lord in his holy court.
Let all the earth be moved at his presence:
10 Say among the Gentiles that the Lord has reigned.
For he has corrected the world, which shall not be moved: he will judge the people with equity.
11 Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad, let the sea be moved, and the fullness thereof.
12 The fields shall be joyful, and all things that are in them.
Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice
13 Before the face of the Lord, because he comes: because he comes to judge the earth.
He shall judge the world with equity, and the people with his truth.

### For David himself, when his land was restored. XCVI.
<note>Psalm 97 in modern Bibles. A celebration of God’s sovereignty over the elements and his victory over idols.</note>

1 The Lord has reigned, let the earth rejoice: let many islands be glad.
2 Clouds and darkness are round about him: justice and judgment are the correction of his throne.
3 Fire shall go before him, and shall burn his enemies round about.
4 His lightnings have shone forth to the world: the earth saw and trembled.
5 The mountains melted like wax at the presence of the Lord: at the presence of the Lord, all the earth.
6 The heavens declared his justice: and all people saw his glory.
<margin>† Exodus 20:4, Leviticus 6:1, Deuteronomy 5:8.</margin>
7 † Let them all be confounded that adore graven things <note>original: "sculptilia" — idols or carved images.</note>: and that glory in their idols.
† Adore him, all you his angels:
8 Zion heard, and was glad.
And the daughters of Judah rejoiced, because of your judgments, O Lord:
<margin>† Hebrews 1:6.</margin>
9 For you are the Lord most high over all the earth: you are exalted exceedingly above all gods.
<margin>† Amos 5:15, Romans 12:9.</margin>
10 † You that love the Lord, hate evil: the Lord preserves the souls of his saints, he will deliver them out of the hand of the sinner.
11 Light is risen to the just, and joy to the right of heart.
12 Rejoice, you just, in the Lord: and give praise to the remembrance of his holiness.

### A Psalm for David himself. XCVII.
<note>Psalm 98 in modern Bibles. A joyful hymn of victory and salvation.</note>

1 Sing to the Lord a new song: because he has done wonderful things.
His right hand has wrought salvation for him: and his holy arm.
2 The Lord has made known his salvation: he has revealed his justice in the sight of the Gentiles.
3 He has remembered his mercy and his truth toward the house of Israel.
<margin>† Isaiah 52:10 & Luke 3:6.</margin>
† All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
4 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: make a joyful noise, and rejoice, and sing psalms.
5 Sing to the Lord upon the harp <note>original: "cithara"</note>, upon the harp and with the voice of a psalm:
6 With ductile trumpets <note>original: "tubis ductilibus" — trumpets made of hammered or drawn metal.</note>, and the sound of a horn trumpet. Make a joyful noise before the Lord our King.

### 1 A Psalm for David himself. XCVIII.
<note>This corresponds to Psalm 99 in modern Bibles. It focuses on the holiness of God's reign.</note>

1 The Lord has reigned, let the people be angry <note>original: "irascantur" — while modern versions often say "tremble," the Latin suggests a stir of emotion or anger against his rule</note>: he who sits upon the cherubim, let the earth be moved.
2 The Lord is great in Zion: and high above all peoples.
3 Let them give praise to your great name: for it is terrible and holy:
4 And the king's honor loves judgment.
You have prepared directions: judgment and justice in Jacob you have performed.
5 Exalt the Lord our God, and adore his footstool: for it is holy.
6 Moses and Aaron are among his priests: and Samuel among those who call upon his name:
They called upon the Lord, and he heard them:
7 He spoke to them in the pillar of a cloud.
They kept his testimonies, and the commandment which he gave them.
8 O Lord our God, you heard them: O God, you were merciful to them, and took vengeance on all their inventions <note>original: "adinventiones" — referring to the people's sinful schemes or idols</note>.
9 Exalt the Lord our God, and adore upon his holy mountain: for the Lord our God is holy.

### 1 A Psalm in confession. XCIX.
<note>Psalm 100 in modern Bibles. Traditionally known as the "Jubilate Deo," a song of joyful praise.</note>

2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: serve the Lord with gladness.
Come in before his presence with exceeding joy.
3 Know that the Lord himself is God: he made us, and not we ourselves:
We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture:
4 Go into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: give thanks to him.
Praise his name:
5 For the Lord is sweet, his mercy is forever, and his truth reaches from generation to generation.

### 1 A Psalm for David himself. C.
<note>Psalm 101 in modern Bibles. A vow of personal integrity for a ruler.</note>

1 Mercy and judgment I will sing to you, O Lord:
I will sing,
2 And I will understand in the innocent way, when you shall come to me.
I walked in the innocence of my heart, in the midst of my house.
3 I did not set before my eyes any unjust thing: I hated those who work transgressions.
4 A perverse heart did not cleave to me: I did not know the malignant one who turned away from me:
5 The one who secretly slandered his neighbor, him did I pursue.
With a proud eye and an insatiable heart, with such a one I did not eat.
6 My eyes are upon the faithful of the land, that they may sit with me: he who walks in the innocent way, he served me.

<column-break/>

7 He who works pride shall not dwell in the midst of my house: he who speaks iniquitous things did not prosper in the sight of my eyes.
8 In the morning I put to death all the sinners of the land: that I might destroy out of the city of the Lord all those who work iniquity.

### 1 The prayer of the poor man,
### When he was anxious, and poured out his prayer in the sight of the Lord. CI.
<note>Psalm 102 in modern Bibles. This is one of the seven "Penitential Psalms," expressing deep distress and hope for Zion’s restoration.</note>

2 O Lord, hear my prayer: and let my cry come to you.
3 Turn not away your face from me: in what day soever I am in trouble, incline your ear to me.
In what day soever I shall call upon you, hear me speedily:
4 For my days have vanished like smoke: and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire <note>original: "cremium" — dry brushwood or sticks for burning</note>.
5 I am smitten like grass, and my heart is withered: because I forgot to eat my bread.
6 From the voice of my groaning, my bone has cleaved to my flesh.
7 I am become like a pelican of the wilderness: I am become like a night-raven <note>original: "nycticorax" — likely an owl or another nocturnal bird of prey</note> in the house.
8 I have watched, and am become like a solitary sparrow upon the housetop.
9 All the day long my enemies reproached me: and they who praised me swore against me.
10 For I did eat ashes like bread, and mingled my drink with weeping.
11 Because of the face of your wrath and indignation: for having lifted me up, you have cast me down.
12 My days have declined like a shadow: and I am withered like grass.
13 But you, O Lord, endure forever: and your memorial to generation and generation.
14 You shall arise and have mercy on Zion: for the time to have mercy on it is come, for the time is here.
15 For its stones have pleased your servants: and they shall have pity on its earth.
16 And the nations shall fear your name, O Lord: and all the kings of the earth your glory.
17 For the Lord has built up Zion: and he shall be seen in his glory.
18 He has had regard to the prayer of the humble: and he has not despised their petition.
19 Let these things be written for another generation: and the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord:
20 Because he has looked forth from his high sanctuary: from heaven the Lord has looked upon the earth:
21 That he might hear the groans of those in fetters: that he might release the children of the slain:
22 That they may declare the name of the Lord in Zion: and his praise in Jerusalem.
23 When the people assemble together, and kings, to serve the Lord.
24 He answered him in the way of his strength: Declare to me the fewness of my days.
25 Call me not away in the midst of my days: your years are unto generation and generation.
26 In the beginning, O Lord, you founded the earth: and the heavens are the works of your hands.
27 They shall perish, but you remain: and all of them shall grow old like a garment.
And as a covering you shall change them, and they shall be changed:
28 But you are the selfsame, and your years shall not fail.
29 The children of your servants shall continue: and their seed shall be directed forever.

It concludes with an affirmation of God's eternal nature in contrast to the passing world.</summary>

### For David himself. CII.
<note>This corresponds to Psalm 103 in modern Bibles. It is a hymn of praise for God's mercy and compassion.</note>

1 **B**less the Lord, O my soul: and let all that is within me bless his holy name.
2 Bless the Lord, O my soul: and do not forget all his benefits.
3 Who is favorable to all your iniquities: who heals all your infirmities.
4 Who redeems your life from destruction: who crowns you with mercy and compassion.
5 Who satisfies your desire with good things: your youth shall be renewed like the eagle’s. <note>The "renewal of the eagle" refers to an ancient belief that eagles regained their youth after molting their feathers.</note>
6 The Lord performs mercies, and justice for all who suffer wrong.
7 He made his ways known to Moses, and his will to the children of Israel.
<margin>Exodus 34:6; Numbers 14:18.</margin>
8 The Lord is compassionate and merciful: long-suffering, and plenteous in mercy.
9 He will not be angry forever: nor will he threaten for eternity.
10 He has not dealt with us according to our sins: nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.
11 For according to the height of the heaven above the earth, he has strengthened his mercy toward those who fear him.
12 As far as the east is from the west: so far has he removed our iniquities from us.
13 As a father has compassion on his children, so has the Lord had compassion on those who fear him:
14 For he himself knows our frame <note>original: "figmentum" — the way we are formed or fashioned</note>.
He remembers that we are dust:
15 As for man, his days are like grass; like a flower of the field, so shall he flourish.
16 For the spirit <note>or breath/wind</note> shall pass through him, and he shall not remain: and he shall know his place no more.
17 But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity, and unto eternity, upon those who fear him.
And his justice is unto children’s children,
18 To those who keep his covenant <note>original: "testamentum"</note>:
And are mindful of his commandments, to perform them.
19 The Lord has prepared his throne in heaven: and his kingdom shall rule over all.
20 Bless the Lord, all you his Angels: mighty in power, performing his word, to hear the voice of his commands.
21 Bless the Lord, all you his hosts: his ministers, who do his will.
22 Bless the Lord, all his works: in every place of his dominion, bless the Lord, O my soul.

### For David himself. CIII.
<note>This corresponds to Psalm 104 in modern Bibles. It is a poetic celebration of the creation of the world.</note>

1 **B**less the Lord, O my soul: O Lord my God, you are exceedingly magnified.
You have put on praise and beauty:
2 Clothed with light as with a garment:
Stretching out the heaven like a skin <note>referring to the fabric of a tent</note>:
3 Who covers its higher parts with waters.
Who makes the clouds your ascent: who walks upon the wings of the winds.
<margin>Hebrews 1:7.</margin>
4 Who makes your angels spirits; and your ministers a burning fire.
5 Who founded the earth upon its own stability: it shall not be moved forever and ever.
6 The deep, like a garment, is its clothing: the waters shall stand above the mountains.
7 At your rebuke they shall flee: at the voice of your thunder they shall be afraid.

<column-break/>

8 The mountains ascend: and the plains descend into the place which you have founded for them.
9 You have set a bound which they shall not pass over: neither shall they return to cover the earth.
10 You send forth springs in the valleys: between the midst of the mountains the waters shall pass through.
11 All the beasts of the field shall drink: the wild asses shall wait in their thirst.
12 Above them the birds of the air shall dwell: from the midst of the rocks they shall give forth their voices.
13 Watering the mountains from the heights above: the earth shall be filled with the fruit of your works:
14 Bringing forth grass for the cattle, and herbs for the service of men:
That you may bring bread out of the earth:
15 And that wine may cheer the heart of man:
That he may make the face cheerful with oil: and that bread may strengthen man’s heart.
16 The trees of the field shall be saturated, and the cedars of Lebanon, which he has planted:
17 There the sparrows shall make their nests.
The house of the heron <note>original: "herodii"</note> is their leader:
18 The high mountains are for the stags, the rock is a refuge for the hedgehogs <note>original: "herinaciis" — often interpreted as rock hyraxes in modern scholarship, but "hedgehogs" in the Vulgate tradition</note>.
19 He made the moon for seasons: the sun knows its setting.
20 You appointed darkness, and it was made night: in it all the beasts of the woods shall wander.
21 The young lions roaring after their prey, and seeking their meat from God.
22 The sun has risen, and they are gathered together: and they shall lie down in their dens.
23 Man shall go forth to his work: and to his labor until the evening.
24 How magnified are your works, O Lord! you have made all things in wisdom: the earth is filled with your possession.
25 This great sea, stretching out its arms: there are creeping things without number.
Small animals with the great:
26 There the ships shall pass.
That dragon <note>original: "draco" — referring to the Leviathan</note>, whom you have formed to play therein:
27 All expect of you that you give them food in season.
28 What you give to them, they shall gather: when you open your hand, all shall be filled with goodness.
29 But if you turn away your face, they shall be troubled: you shall take away their breath, and they shall fail, and shall return to their dust.
30 You shall send forth your spirit, and they shall be created: and you shall renew the face of the earth.
31 May the glory of the Lord endure forever: the Lord shall rejoice in his works:
32 He looks upon the earth, and makes it tremble: he touches the mountains, and they smoke.
<margin>Below 145:2.</margin>
33 † I will sing to the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.
34 May my speech be pleasing to him: but I will take delight in the Lord.
35 Let sinners fail from the earth, and the unjust, so that they be no more: bless the Lord, O my soul.

### Alleluia. (1 Chronicles 16:8.) CIV.
<note>This corresponds to Psalm 105 in modern Bibles. It is a historical psalm calling Israel to remember God's wonders.</note>

<margin>1 Chronicles 16:8; Isaiah 12:4.</margin>
1 **G**ive glory to the Lord, and call upon his name: declare his deeds among the Gentiles.
2 Sing to him, and chant to him: relate all his wondrous works.
3 Glory in his holy name: let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
4 Seek the Lord, and be strengthened: seek his face evermore.

1 Unto the end, a Psalm of David.

### CVIII. <note>Modern Psalm 109. This is known as an imprecatory psalm, where the speaker calls for divine justice against a treacherous enemy. In Christian tradition, it is often viewed as a prophecy of the fate of Judas Iscariot.</note>

2 O God, be not silent to my praise: for the mouth of the sinner, and the mouth of the deceitful man is opened against me.
3 They have spoken against me with a deceitful tongue, and they have surrounded me with words of hatred: and they have fought against me without cause.
4 In return for my love, they spoke against me: but I gave myself to prayer.
5 And they repaid me evil for good: and hatred for my love.
6 Set a sinner over him: and let the devil <note>original: "diabolus" — also translated as 'an accuser' or 'the adversary'</note> stand at his right hand.
7 When he is judged, let him go out condemned: and let his prayer become sin.
8 Let his days be few: and let another take his office <note>original: "episcopatum" — literally his 'overseership' or bishopric. Cited in Acts 1:20 regarding the replacement of Judas</note>.
9 Let his children be orphans: and his wife a widow.
10 Let his children be carried about as wanderers, and let them beg: and let them be cast out of their dwellings.
11 Let the moneylender search through all his substance: and let strangers plunder his labors.
12 Let there be none to help him: nor let there be any to have pity on his fatherless children.
13 Let his posterity be cut off: in one generation let his name be blotted out.
14 Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered in the sight of the Lord: and let not the sin of his mother be blotted out.
15 Let them be before the Lord always, and let the memory of them perish from the earth:
16 Because he remembered not to show mercy.

17 But persecuted the poor and needy man, and the broken in heart, to put him to death.

20 This is the work of those who speak against me before the Lord: and who speak evil things against my soul.

Deliver me,
22 For I am needy and poor: and my heart is troubled within me.

30 I will give great thanks to the Lord with my mouth: and in the midst of many I will praise him.
31 Because he has stood at the right hand of the poor, to save my soul from persecutors.

### Praise the Lord <note>original: "Alleluja"</note>. 118 <note>Modern Bibles: Psalm 119</note>.

### ALEPH <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet. This psalm is an acrostic, where each section begins with a different letter.</note>.

1 Blessed are the undefiled in the way: who walk in the law of the Lord.
2 Blessed are they who search his testimonies: that seek him with their whole heart.
3 For they who work iniquity have not walked in his ways.
4 You have commanded your commandments to be kept most diligently.
5 O! that my ways may be directed to keep your justifications.
6 Then I shall not be confounded, when I shall look into all your commandments.
7 I will praise you with uprightness of heart, because I have learned the judgments of your justice.
8 I will keep your justifications: do not utterly forsake me.

### BETH <note>The second letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>.

9 By what does a young man correct his way? By observing your words.
10 With my whole heart have I sought after you: let me not stray from your commandments.
11 Your words have I hidden in my heart: that I may not sin against you.
12 Blessed are you, O Lord: teach me your justifications.
13 With my lips I have pronounced all the judgments of your mouth.
14 I have been delighted in the way of your testimonies, as much as in all riches.
15 I will be exercised in your commandments: and I will consider your ways.
16 I will meditate on your justifications: I will not forget your words.

### GIMEL <note>The third letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>.

17 Give bountifully to your servant, enliven me: and I shall keep your words.
18 Open my eyes: and I will consider the wondrous things of your law.
19 I am a sojourner on the earth: hide not your commandments from me.
20 My soul has coveted to long for your justifications at all times.
21 You have rebuked the proud: cursed are they who decline from your commandments.
22 Remove from me reproach and contempt: because I have sought after your testimonies.
23 For princes sat and spoke against me: but your servant was exercised in your justifications.
24 For your testimonies are my meditation: and your justifications are my counsel.

### DALETH <note>The fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>.

<meta>This page continues Psalm 118 (Psalm 119 in modern Bibles), the longest psalm in the collection. It is an alphabetic acrostic, where each section begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet. This page covers the sections for the letters Daleth (concluding), He, Vau, Zain, Heth, Teth, Jod, Caph, and the beginning of Lamed.</meta>

# THE BOOK OF PSALMS.

26 I have declared my ways, and you heard me: teach me your justifications <note>original: "justificationes," referring to God's statutes or divine decrees</note>.
27 Instruct me in the way of your justifications: and I shall be occupied with your wondrous works.
28 My soul has grown heavy with weariness: strengthen me in your words.
29 Remove from me the way of iniquity: and have mercy on me through your law.
30 I have chosen the way of truth: I have not forgotten your judgments.
31 I have clung to your testimonies, O Lord: do not let me be put to shame.
32 I have run the way of your commandments, since you have enlarged my heart <note>meaning to be given a sense of freedom or understanding</note>.

->HE <note>The fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note><-

33 Set before me, O Lord, the way of your justifications as a law: and I will always seek after it.
34 Give me understanding, and I will search your law: and I will keep it with my whole heart.
35 Lead me into the path of your commandments: for this is what I have desired.
36 Incline my heart toward your testimonies: and not toward greed.
37 Turn away my eyes, lest they see vanities: give me life in your way.
38 Establish your word <note>original: "eloquium," meaning speech or promised word</note> for your servant, in your fear.
39 Take away the reproach that I have feared: for your judgments are delightful.
40 Behold, I have longed for your commandments: give me life in your justice.

->VAU <note>The sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note><-

41 And let your mercy come upon me, O Lord: your salvation, according to your word.
42 And I will answer a word to those who reproach me: for I have hoped in your words.
43 And do not take the word of truth utterly out of my mouth: for I have hoped exceedingly in your judgments.
44 And I will keep your law always, forever and ever.
45 And I walked in a wide place <note>original: "in latitudine," a metaphor for freedom and lack of distress</note>: because I have sought out your commandments.
46 And I spoke of your testimonies in the presence of kings: and I was not ashamed.
47 And I meditated on your commandments, which I loved.
48 And I lifted up my hands to your commandments, which I loved: and I was occupied with your justifications.

->ZAIN <note>The seventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note><-

49 Be mindful of your word to your servant, in which you have given me hope.
50 This has comforted me in my humiliation: for your word has given me life.
51 The proud acted iniquitously in every way: but I did not turn away from your law.
52 I remembered your judgments from of old, O Lord: and I was comforted.
53 Faintness has taken hold of me, because of the sinners who forsake your law.
54 Your justifications were like songs to me, in the place of my pilgrimage.
55 In the night I remembered your name, O Lord: and I kept your law.
56 This happened to me because I sought after your justifications.

->HETH <note>The eighth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note><-

57 O Lord, my portion, I have said: I will keep your law.
58 I entreated your face with my whole heart: have mercy on me according to your word.

<column-break/>

59 I thought on my ways: and turned my feet toward your testimonies.
60 I am ready, and I am not troubled: that I may keep your commandments.
61 The cords of sinners have wrapped around me: and I have not forgotten your law.
62 At midnight I rose to give praise to you, for the judgments of your justification.
63 I am a companion to all who fear you and keep your commandments.
64 The earth, O Lord, is full of your mercy: teach me your justifications.

->TETH <note>The ninth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note><-

65 You have dealt kindly with your servant, O Lord, according to your word.
66 Teach me goodness, and discipline, and knowledge: for I have believed your commandments.
67 Before I was humbled, I committed offenses: therefore I have kept your word.
68 You are good: and in your goodness teach me your justifications.
69 The iniquity of the proud has been multiplied against me: but I will search your commandments with my whole heart.
70 Their heart is curdled like milk <note>metaphor for being insensitive or stubborn</note>: but I have meditated on your law.
71 It is good for me that you have humbled me: that I may learn your justifications.
72 The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver.

->JOD <note>The tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note><-

73 Your hands have made me and fashioned me: give me understanding, and I will learn your commandments.
74 Those who fear you will see me and be glad: because I have hoped exceedingly in your words.
75 I know, O Lord, that your judgments are equitable: and in your truth you have humbled me.
76 Let your mercy be ready to comfort me, according to your word to your servant.
77 Let your tender mercies come to me, and I shall live: for your law is my meditation.
78 Let the proud be ashamed, because they have acted unjustly and iniquitously against me: but I will be occupied with your commandments.
79 Let those who fear you turn to me: and those who know your testimonies.
80 Let my heart be undefiled in your justifications, so that I am not put to shame.

->CAPH <note>The eleventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note><-

81 My soul has fainted for your salvation: and in your word I have hoped exceedingly.
82 My eyes have failed looking for your word, saying: When will you comfort me?
83 For I have become like a wineskin in the frost <note>shriveled or weathered by trial</note>: but I have not forgotten your justifications.
84 How many are the days of your servant? When will you execute judgment on those who persecute me?
85 The wicked have told me fables: but they are not like your law.
86 All your commandments are truth: they have persecuted me unjustly, help me.
87 They had almost finished me off on the earth: but I did not forsake your commandments.
88 Give me life according to your mercy: and I shall keep the testimonies of your mouth.

->LAMED <note>The twelfth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note><-

89 Forever, O Lord, your word remains in heaven.
90 Your truth is from generation to generation: you have founded the earth, and it remains.
91 By your ordinance the day continues: for all things serve you.

2 Then our mouth was filled with joy: and our tongue with exultation.
Then they shall say among the nations: The Lord has done great things for them.
3 The Lord has done great things for us: we have become joyful.
4 Turn back our captivity, O Lord, like a torrent in the south <note>original: "austro," referring to the Negev desert, where dry riverbeds flash with water after rain</note>.

### 1 A Song of Ascents of David. CXXXII.
<note>Psalm 133 in modern numbering. This brief poem celebrates the unity of the community gathered at the Temple.</note>

Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity:
2 Like the ointment upon the head, which runs down upon the beard, the beard of Aaron <note>Aaron was the first High Priest; the oil signifies a sacred setting apart or consecration.</note>:
Which runs down to the hem of his garment:
3 Like the dew of Hermon <note>Mount Hermon is a high peak known for its heavy dew, used here as a symbol of refreshment.</note>, which descends upon the mountain of Zion.

### 1 A Song of Ascents. CXXXIII.
<note>Psalm 134 in modern numbering. This is the final "Song of Ascents," traditionally associated with the night watchmen in the Temple.</note>

Behold now, bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord.
Who stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God,
2 In the nights lift up your hands toward the holy places, and bless the Lord.
3 May the Lord bless you out of Zion, he who made heaven and earth.
