# THE BOOK OF PSALMS.

### 1 A Psalm of David, for Jeremiah. CXXXVI.
<note>While attributed to David in the title, this psalm clearly dates to the Babylonian Exile (c. 586–538 BC). Jeremiah is mentioned in some ancient titles as the prophet who foretold this captivity.</note>

By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: when we remembered Zion.
2 On the willows in her midst, we hung up our instruments <note>original: "organa nostra." Likely referring to lyres or harps used for temple music.</note>.
3 For there they who led us away captive asked us for the words of songs.
And they who carried us away said: Sing us a hymn from the songs of Zion.
4 How shall we sing the song of the Lord in a foreign land?
5 If I forget you, O Jerusalem, let my right hand be forgotten <note>Some traditions translate this as "let my right hand wither" or "lose its skill."</note>.
6 Let my tongue cleave to my jaws if I do not remember you:
If I do not set Jerusalem at the beginning of my joy.
7 Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom, in the day of Jerusalem:
Who say: Raze it, raze it, even to its very foundation.
8 O miserable daughter of Babylon: blessed is he who shall repay you with the same payment you have paid to us.
9 Blessed is he who shall take and dash your little ones against the rock <note>A stark expression of the "lex talionis" (law of retaliation) and the raw grief of a displaced people seeking divine justice against their oppressors.</note>.

### 1 For David himself. CXXXVII.

I will praise you, O Lord, with my whole heart: for you have heard the words of my mouth.
In the sight of the angels I will sing praise to you:
2 I will worship toward your holy temple, and give praise to your name,
For your mercy and your truth: for you have magnified your holy name above all things.
3 In whatever day I call upon you, hear me: you shall multiply strength in my soul.
4 Let all the kings of the earth praise you, O Lord: for they have heard all the words of your mouth:
5 And let them sing in the ways of the Lord: for great is the glory of the Lord.
6 For the Lord is high, and looks upon the lowly: and the lofty he knows from afar.
7 If I walk in the midst of tribulation, you will revive me: and you have stretched forth your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and your right hand has saved me.
8 The Lord will repay for me: O Lord, your mercy endures forever: do not despise the works of your hands.

### 1 To the end, a Psalm of David. CXXXVIII.
<note>This psalm is a famous meditation on God's "omniscience" (all-knowing) and "omnipresence" (being everywhere).</note>

Lord, you have proved me and known me:
2 You have known my sitting down and my rising up.
3 You have understood my thoughts from afar: you have searched out my path and my boundaries <note>original: "funiculum meum," literally a measuring cord.</note>.
4 And you have foreseen all my ways: for there is no word on my tongue.
5 Behold, O Lord, you have known all things, the newest and the ancient: you have formed me, and laid your hand upon me.
6 Your knowledge has become wonderful to me: it is high, and I cannot attain to it.
7 Where shall I go from your spirit? and where shall I flee from your face?

<column-break/>

<margin>Amos 9:2.</margin>
8 † If I ascend into heaven, you are there: if I descend into hell <note>original: "infernum," referring here to the realm of the dead, Sheol.</note>, you are present.
9 If I take my wings early in the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea:
10 Even there your hand shall lead me: and your right hand shall hold me.
11 And I said: Perhaps darkness shall cover me: and night shall be my light in my pleasures.
12 For darkness shall not be dark to you, and night shall be as light as the day: its darkness and its light are alike to you.
13 For you have possessed my reins <note>original: "renes," literally kidneys, considered by the ancients to be the seat of emotions and the inner self.</note>: you have protected me from my mother’s womb.
14 I will praise you, for you are fearfully magnified: wonderful are your works, and my soul knows them right well.
15 My bone was not hidden from you, which you made in secret: nor my substance in the lower parts of the earth.
16 Your eyes saw my unformed substance <note>original: "imperfectum meum," often interpreted as the embryo or fetus.</note>, and in your book all shall be written: days shall be formed, and no one was yet in them.
17 But to me, your friends, O God, are made exceedingly honorable: their principality is exceedingly strengthened.
18 I will number them, and they shall be multiplied above the sand: I rose up, and I am still with you.
19 If you, O God, will kill the wicked: you men of blood, depart from me:
20 Because you say in your thoughts: They shall receive your cities in vanity.
21 Have I not hated them, O Lord, who hated you: and pined away because of your enemies?
22 I have hated them with a perfect hatred: and they are become enemies to me.
23 Prove me, O God, and know my heart: examine me, and know my paths.
24 And see if there be in me a way of iniquity: and lead me in the eternal way.

### 1 To the end, a Psalm of David. CXXXIX.

2 Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: rescue me from the unjust man.
3 Who have devised iniquities in their hearts: all the day long they designed battles.
<margin>See Psalm 5:11; Romans 3:13.</margin>
4 † They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent: the venom of asps is under their lips.
5 Keep me, O Lord, from the hand of the sinner: and rescue me from unjust men.
Who have devised to trip up my steps:
6 The proud have hidden a snare for me:
And they have stretched out cords for a trap: they have set a stumbling block for me by the wayside.
7 I said to the Lord: You are my God: hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication.
8 O Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation: you have overshadowed my head in the day of battle.
9 Do not give me up, O Lord, from my desire to the sinner: they have plotted against me, do not abandon me, lest they should triumph.
10 The head of those surrounding me: the labor of their own lips shall cover them.
11 Burning coals shall fall upon them, you shall cast them into the fire: in miseries they shall not stand.
12 A man of many words shall not be prospered upon the earth: evils shall catch the unjust man unto destruction.
13 I know that the Lord will do justice for the needy: and revenge for the poor.
14 But the righteous shall give praise to your name: and the upright shall dwell with your countenance.

### A Psalm of David. CXL.
<note>In modern Bibles following the Hebrew numbering, this is Psalm 141. It is a prayer for protection against both external enemies and the internal temptation to sin.</note>

Lord, I have cried to you, hear me: attend to my voice, when I cry to you.
2 Let my prayer be directed as incense in your sight: the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
3 Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth: and a door of enclosure around my lips.
4 Incline not my heart to words of malice, to make excuses for sins. <note>original: "ad excusandas excusationes in peccatis." This refers to the human tendency to justify one's own wrongdoings.</note>
With men who work iniquity, I will not communicate with the best of them.
5 The just man shall correct me in mercy, and shall reprove me: but let not the oil of the sinner fatten my head.
For yet my prayer shall be in their good pleasure:
6 Their judges, joined to the rock, have been swallowed up.
They shall hear my words because they were powerful:
7 As when the thickness of the earth is broken up upon the ground.
Our bones are scattered near hell:
8 But to you, O Lord, Lord, are my eyes: in you have I hoped, do not take away my soul.
9 Keep me from the snare which they have set for me: and from the stumbling blocks of those who work iniquity.
10 The wicked shall fall into his net: I am alone until I pass by.

Lord, hear my prayer: give ear to my petition in your truth: hear me in your justice.

## A Praise of David himself. CXLIV.
<note>In modern Bibles following the Hebrew numbering, this is Psalm 145. It is the last psalm explicitly attributed to David and is an alphabetical acrostic in the original Hebrew, though the Latin translation here follows the flow of the prose.</note>

I will extol you, my God the king: and I will bless your name forever, and forever and ever.
2 Every day I will bless you: and I will praise your name forever, and forever and ever.
3 Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised: and of his greatness there is no end.
4 Generation and generation shall praise your works: and they shall declare your power.
5 They shall speak of the magnificence of the glory of your holiness: and shall tell of your wondrous works.
6 And they shall speak of the might of your terrible acts: and shall declare your greatness.
7 They shall publish the memory of the abundance of your sweetness: and shall rejoice in your justice.
8 The Lord is gracious and merciful: patient, and plenteous in mercy.
9 The Lord is sweet to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.
10 Let all your works, O Lord, confess to you: and let your saints bless you.
11 They shall speak of the glory of your kingdom: and shall tell of your power:
12 To make your power known to the sons of men: and the glory of the magnificence of your kingdom.
13 Your kingdom is a kingdom of all ages: and your dominion is in every generation and generation.
The Lord is faithful in all his words: and holy in all his works.
14 The Lord lifts up all who fall: and sets up all who are cast down.
15 The eyes of all hope in you, O Lord: and you give them meat in due season.
16 You open your hand: and fill every living creature with blessing.
17 The Lord is just in all his ways: and holy in all his works.
18 The Lord is near to all who call upon him: to all who call upon him in truth.
19 He will do the will of those who fear him, and he will hear their prayer: and will save them.
20 The Lord keeps all those who love him: and all sinners he will destroy.
21 My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord: and let all flesh bless his holy name forever, and forever and ever.

19 Who declares his word to Jacob: his justices and his judgments to Israel.

# THE BOOK OF PROVERBS,
### WHICH THE HEBREWS

->CHAPTER ONE.<-

*The utility of parables: hearing and the study of wisdom are commended; the son is admonished not to follow the flatteries of sinners: wisdom invites one to embrace her, and threatens destruction to those who despise her.*

1 The parables of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel.
2 To know wisdom and instruction:
3 To understand words of prudence: and to receive the training of doctrine, justice, and judgment, and equity;
4 That craftiness <note>In this context, "astutia" (craftiness) refers to practical shrewdness or cleverness in navigating life, rather than deceit.</note> may be given to the little ones, knowledge and understanding to the youth.
5 A wise man shall hear and become wiser: and he that is intelligent shall possess the rudders of guidance.
6 He shall understand a parable, and the interpretation, the words of the wise, and their riddles.
<margin>† Psalm 110:10. Eccl. 1:16.</margin>
7 † The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Fools despise wisdom and instruction.
8 Hear, my son, the instruction of your father, and forsake not the law of your mother:
9 That grace may be added to your head, and a collar to your neck.
10 My son, if sinners should entice you, do not consent to them.
11 If they should say: "Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us hide snares against the innocent without cause:
12 Let us swallow him alive like hell <note>Original: *infernus*, referring here to the grave or the underworld (Sheol).</note>,

<column-break/>

and whole, like one descending into the pit.
13 We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoils.
14 Cast your lot with us, let there be one purse for us all."
15 My son, do not walk with them, restrain your foot from their paths.
<margin>† Isaiah 59:7.</margin>
16 † For their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed blood.
17 But in vain is the net thrown before the eyes of those that have wings.
18 They themselves also lie in wait against their own blood, and plot deceits against their own souls.
19 Such are the paths of every covetous man: they take away the lives of the possessors.
20 Wisdom preaches abroad, she utters her voice in the streets:
21 At the head of the crowds she cries out, at the gates of the city she brings forth her words, saying:
22 "How long, little ones, will you love childhood, and fools desire those things which are harmful to them, and the imprudent hate knowledge?
23 Turn at my correction: behold I will bring forth my spirit for you, and I will show you my words.
<margin>† Isaiah 65:12. & 66:4. Jeremiah 7:13.</margin>
24 † Because I called, and you refused: I stretched out my hand, and there was no one who would look.
25 You have despised all my counsel, and neglected my rebukes.
26 I also will laugh at your destruction, and I will mock when that which you feared comes upon you."

<summary>This page concludes the Book of Psalms with a universal call to praise and introduces the Book of Proverbs, establishing the fear of the Lord as the foundation of wisdom and warning against the violent enticements of the wicked.</summary>

27 When sudden calamity rushes in, and destruction falls upon you like a storm: when tribulation and distress come upon you:
28 Then they shall call upon me, and I will not hear: they shall rise in the morning, and they shall not find me:
29 Because they have hated discipline, and have not chosen the fear of the Lord,
30 Nor consented to my counsel, and detracted from all my correction.
31 Therefore they shall eat the fruits of their own way, and shall be filled with their own devices.
32 The turning away of the simple <note>Latin: "parvulorum"—literally "little ones," referring to the naive or spiritually immature.</note> shall kill them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.
33 But he that shall hear me, shall rest without terror, and shall enjoy abundance, without fear of evils.

### CHAPTER II.

*How many goods the acquisition of wisdom confers, and how many evils it turns away; with which the gifts of God come, and without which one wanders everywhere.*

My son, if thou wilt receive my words, and wilt hide my commandments with thee,
2 That thy ear may hear wisdom: incline thy heart to know prudence.
3 For if thou shalt call for wisdom, and incline thy heart to prudence:
4 If thou shalt seek her as money, and shalt dig her up as treasures:
5 Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and shalt find the knowledge of God:
6 Because the Lord giveth wisdom: and out of his mouth cometh prudence and knowledge.
7 He will keep the salvation of the righteous, and protect them that walk in simplicity,
8 Keeping the paths of justice, and guarding the ways of saints.
9 Then shalt thou understand justice, and judgment, and equity, and every good path.
10 If wisdom shall enter into thy heart, and knowledge shall please thy soul:
11 Counsel shall guard thee, and prudence shall keep thee,
12 That thou mayst be delivered from the evil way, and from the man that speaketh perverse things:
13 Who leave the right way, and walk by dark ways:
14 Who are glad when they have done evil, and rejoice in most wicked things:
15 Whose ways are perverse, and their steps infamous.
16 That thou mayst be delivered from the strange woman <note>A common biblical metaphor for temptation or foreign idolatry.</note>, and from the stranger, who softeneth her words,
17 And forsaketh the guide of her youth,
18 And hath forgotten the covenant of her God: for her house is inclined unto death, and her paths to hell.
19 All that go in unto her, shall not return, neither shall they take hold of the paths of life.
20 That thou mayst walk in a good way: and keep the paths of the just.
21 For they that are upright shall dwell in the earth, and the simple shall continue in it.
<margin>† Job 18:17</margin>
22 † But the wicked shall be destroyed from the earth: and they that do unjustly shall be taken away from it.

<column-break/>

### CHAPTER III.

*Wisdom prolongs life: mercy and truth are not to be forsaken: trust in God: the fear of God: God is to be honored: the correction of God is to be borne with joy: the praise of wisdom: all things are prosperous for those following wisdom: one must give to a friend immediately, and do him no harm: one must not contend: the wicked are not to be imitated: the destruction of the impious, and the blessing of the pious.*

My son, forget not my law, and let thy heart keep my precepts.
2 For they shall add to thee length of days, and years of life, and peace.
3 Let not mercy and truth leave thee, put them about thy neck, and write them in the tablets of thy heart:
4 And thou shalt find grace, and good discipline, before God and men.
5 Have confidence in the Lord with all thy heart, and lean not upon thy own prudence.
6 In all thy ways think on him, and he will direct thy steps.
<margin>† Romans 12:16</margin>
7 † Be not wise in thy own conceit: fear God, and depart from evil:
8 For it shall be health to thy navel, and moisture to thy bones.
<margin>† Tobit 4:7; Luke 14:13</margin>
9 † Honor the Lord with thy substance, and give him of the first of all thy fruits:
10 And thy barns shall be filled with abundance, and thy presses shall run over with wine.
<margin>† Hebrews 12:5; Revelation 3:19</margin>
11 † My son, reject not the discipline of the Lord: and do not faint when thou art corrected by him.
12 For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth: and as a father in the son he pleaseth himself.
13 Blessed is the man that findeth wisdom, and is rich in prudence:
14 The purchasing thereof is better than the merchandise of silver, and her fruit than the chiefest and purest gold:
15 She is more precious than all riches: and all the things that are desired, are not to be compared with her.
16 Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and glory.
17 Her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are peaceable.
18 She is a tree of life <note>original: "Lignum vitae"—a reference back to the garden of Eden, suggesting wisdom restores what was lost.</note> to them that shall lay hold on her: and he that shall retain her is blessed.
19 The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth, hath established the heavens by prudence.
20 By his wisdom the depths have broken out, and the clouds grow thick with dew.
21 My son, let not these things depart from thy eyes: Keep the law and counsel:
22 And there shall be life to thy soul, and grace to thy throat.
23 Then shalt thou walk confidently in thy way, and thy foot shall not stumble:
24 If thou sleep, thou shalt not fear: thou shalt rest, and thy sleep shall be sweet.
25 Be not afraid of sudden fear, nor of the power of the wicked falling upon thee.
26 For the Lord will be at thy side, and will keep thy foot that thou be not taken.
27 Do not withhold him from doing good, who is able: if thou art able, do good thyself also.
28 Say not to thy friend: Go, and come again: tomorrow I will give to thee: when thou canst give at present.
29 Do not devise evil against thy friend, when he hath confidence in thee.

30 Do not contend against a man without cause, when he himself has done you no harm.
<margin>† Psalm 36:1.</margin>
31 † Do not envy the unjust man, nor imitate his ways:
32 Because every deceiver is an abomination to the Lord, and his communication is with the simple <note>Latin: "simplicibus"—those who are sincere, innocent, or without guile.</note>.
33 Poverty from the Lord is in the house of the wicked: but the dwellings of the just shall be blessed.
34 He himself shall mock the mockers, and to the mild he will give grace.
35 The wise shall possess glory: the exaltation of fools is disgrace.

# CHAPTER IV.

*A wise man, by his own example, exhorts others to seek wisdom, the benefits of which he explains; the way of the wicked is to be avoided, and that of the just embraced: concerning the guarding of the heart, the mouth, and one's steps.*

1 Hear, O children, the discipline of a father, and attend that you may know prudence.
2 I will give you a good gift; do not forsake my law.
3 For I also was the son of my father, tender and an only child in the sight of my mother:
4 And he taught me, and said: Let your heart receive my words, keep my precepts, and you shall live.
5 Possess wisdom, possess prudence: do not forget, nor turn away from the words of my mouth.
6 Do not forsake her, and she shall guard you: love her, and she shall preserve you.
7 The beginning of wisdom: possess wisdom, and in all your possessions, acquire prudence:
8 Seize her, and she shall exalt you: you shall be glorified by her, when you have embraced her.
9 She shall give to your head an increase of graces, and a noble crown shall protect you.
10 Hear, O my son, and receive my words, that the years of your life may be multiplied.
11 I will show you the way of wisdom, I will lead you through the paths of equity:
12 Which, when you have entered, your steps shall not be narrowed, and when running you shall not have a stumbling block.
13 Hold fast to discipline, do not let her go: guard her, for she is your life.
14 Do not delight in the paths of the wicked, nor let the way of evil men please you.
15 Flee from it, do not pass through it: turn away, and leave it.
16 For they do not sleep unless they have done evil: and sleep is snatched from them unless they have caused someone to fall.
17 They eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of iniquity.
18 But the path of the just, like a shining light, goes forward and increases even unto the perfect day.
19 The way of the wicked is dark: they know not where they may fall.
20 My son, listen to my words, and incline your ear to my sayings.
21 Let them not depart from your eyes, keep them in the middle of your heart:
22 For they are life to those who find them, and health to all flesh.
23 With all watchfulness guard your heart, because life proceeds from it.
24 Remove from you a crooked mouth, and let detracting lips be far from you.

<column-break/>

25 Let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids precede your steps.
26 Direct the path for your feet, and all your ways shall be established.
27 Do not turn to the right, nor to the left: turn your foot away from evil: for the Lord knows the ways which are on the right: but those are perverse which are on the left. But he himself shall make your courses straight, and will lead your journeys in peace.

# CHAPTER V.

*He commands to avoid the harlot: so that labors and years are not lost: let one's own wife be loved, and the stranger shunned.*

1 My son, attend to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my prudence.
2 That you may guard your thoughts, and your lips may preserve discipline. Do not attend to the deceit of a woman.
3 For the lips of a harlot are a dripping honeycomb, and her throat is smoother than oil:
4 But her end is as bitter as wormwood <note>Latin: "absynthium"—a plant known for its extreme bitterness, often used as a metaphor for sorrow or calamity.</note>, and sharp as a two-edged sword.
5 Her feet go down into death, and her steps penetrate into hell <note>Latin: "inferos"—the underworld or the place of the dead.</note>.
6 They do not walk through the path of life, her steps are wandering and untraceable.
7 Now therefore, my son, hear me, and do not depart from the words of my mouth.
8 Make your way far from her, and do not approach the doors of her house.
9 Give not your honor to strangers, and your years to the cruel.
10 Lest strangers perhaps be filled with your strength, and your labors be in another's house,
11 And you groan in the end, when you have consumed your flesh and your body, and say:
12 Why have I detested discipline, and my heart did not consent to rebukes,
13 Nor did I hear the voice of those teaching me, and I did not incline my ear to my masters?
14 I was almost in all evil, in the midst of the church and the synagogue <note>Latin: "ecclesiæ & synagogæ"—referring generally to the public assembly or religious congregation.</note>.
15 Drink water from your own cistern, and the streams of your own well:
16 Let your fountains be diverted abroad, and divide your waters in the streets.
17 Keep them for yourself alone, nor let strangers be partakers with you.
18 Let your source <note>Latin: "vena"—literally a vein or a stream, here referring to a source of life or offspring.</note> be blessed, and rejoice with the woman of your youth:
19 A most dear hind, and a most grateful fawn: let her breasts intoxicate you at all times, in her love be delighted continually.
20 Why are you seduced, my son, by a strange woman, and why are you cherished in the bosom of another?
<margin>† Job 14:16 & 31:4 & 34:21.</margin>
21 † The Lord beholds the ways of man, and considers all his steps.
22 His own iniquities catch the wicked man, and he is bound by the ropes of his sins.
23 He himself shall die, because he had no discipline, and in the multitude of his folly he shall be deceived.

### C H A P T E R VI.

> *The one who acts as a guarantor must labor to free himself from the pledge given; the ant is held up as an example to rouse the lazy to work; the Apostate is described; six things which the Lord hates are listed; he exhorts the keeping of the law, and that you should not lust after a woman's beauty, but rather avoid the company of an adultress.*

1 My son, if you have stood surety <term>surety: a formal promise to take responsibility for another person’s debt</term> for your friend, you have struck your hand in agreement with a stranger.
2 You are ensnared by the words of your own mouth, and caught by your own speech.
3 Do therefore what I say, my son, and deliver yourself: for you have fallen into the hand of your neighbor. Run about, make haste, and stir up your friend.
4 Give no sleep to your eyes, nor let your eyelids slumber.
5 Deliver yourself like a doe from the hand, and like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
6 Go to the ant, O sluggard, and consider her ways, and learn wisdom:
7 Who, having no leader, nor teacher, nor prince,
8 Provides her food in the summer, and gathers what she may eat during the harvest.
9 How long will you sleep, O sluggard? When will you rise out of your sleep?
<margin>† Below 24:33.</margin>
10 † You will sleep a little, you will slumber a little, you will fold your hands a little to sleep:
11 And want shall come upon you like a traveler, and poverty like an armed man. But if you are diligent, your harvest shall come like a fountain, and poverty shall flee far from you.
12 An apostate man <note>original: *Homo apostata*—here meaning a person who has abandoned moral integrity or is "worthless."</note>, a useless man, walks with a perverse mouth,
13 He winks with his eyes, stamps with his foot, and speaks with his finger,
14 With a depraved heart he devises evil, and at all times he sows quarrels.
15 To such a one his destruction shall come instantly, and he shall suddenly be crushed, and shall no longer have a remedy.
16 There are six things which the Lord hates, and the seventh his soul detests:
17 Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,
18 A heart devising wicked thoughts, feet swift to run into evil,
19 A deceitful witness uttering lies, and him who sows discord among brothers.
20 My son, keep the precepts of your father, and do not forsake the law of your mother.
21 Bind them in your heart continually, and wrap them around your throat.
22 When you walk, let them go with you; when you sleep, let them guard you, and when you wake, speak with them.
23 Because the commandment is a lamp, and the law is a light, and the way of life is the rebuke of discipline:
24 That they may guard you from the evil woman, and from the flattering tongue of the stranger <note>original: *extraneæ*—referring to a woman outside the covenant or an adulteress.</note>.
25 Let not your heart lust after her beauty, nor be captured by her glances:
26 For the price of a harlot is barely the cost of one loaf of bread: but the woman catches the precious soul of a man.
27 Can a man hide fire in his bosom, so that his garments do not burn?

<column-break/>

28 Or walk upon hot coals, so that the soles of his feet are not scorched?
29 So it is with him who goes in to his neighbor's wife; he shall not be clean when he has touched her.
30 The fault is not great when someone has stolen: for he steals to fill his hungry soul:
31 Yet if caught, he shall restore sevenfold, and shall give up all the substance of his house:
32 But he who is an adulterer, on account of the poverty of his heart, shall lose his own soul:
33 He gathers shame and dishonor upon himself, and his reproach shall not be blotted out:
34 Because the jealousy and fury of the husband will not spare him on the day of vengeance,
35 Nor will he yield to any man's prayers, nor will he accept many gifts for redemption.

### C H A P T E R VII.

> *He exhorts the youth to embrace wisdom and keep the commandments: and to avoid the flatteries of harlots, which he describes at length.*

1 My son, keep my words, and lay up my precepts within you.
2 Son, keep my commandments, and you shall live: and keep my law as the apple of your eye:
3 Bind it upon your fingers, write it upon the tablets of your heart.
4 Say to wisdom: You are my sister: and call prudence your friend,
5 That she may guard you from the strange woman, and from the outsider who makes her words sweet.
6 For from the window of my house I looked out through the lattice,
7 And I see the little ones, I observe a foolish youth,
8 Who passes through the street near the corner, and walks near the way of her house,
9 In the dark, as the day grows late, in the darkness and gloom of the night.
10 And behold, a woman meets him in the attire of a harlot, prepared to capture souls: talkative and wandering,
11 Impatient of quiet, not able to keep her feet within her own house,
12 Now outside, now in the streets, now lying in wait near the corners.
13 And taking hold of the youth, she kisses him, and with a bold face she flatters him, saying:
14 I vowed victims for salvation <note>original: *Victimas pro salute*—peace offerings or thank-offerings.</note>, today I have paid my vows.
15 Therefore I came out to meet you, desiring to see you, and I have found you.
16 I have woven my bed with cords, I have spread it with embroidered carpets from Egypt.
17 I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh, and aloes, and cinnamon.
18 Come, let us be intoxicated with breasts <note>In this context, meaning "with delights" or "pleasures."</note>, and let us enjoy the embraces we desire, until the day dawns.
19 For my husband is not in his house, he has gone a very long way.
20 He took a bag of money with him: he will return to his house on the day of the full moon.
21 She ensnared him with many words, and drew him in with the flattery of her lips.
22 Immediately he follows her like an ox led to the slaughter, and like a frisking lamb, the fool not knowing that he is being dragged to bonds,
23 Until an arrow pierces his liver: just as if a bird hastens to the snare, and knows not that the danger is to his soul.

23 Now therefore, my son, hear me, and attend to the words of my mouth.
25 Let not your mind be drawn away into her ways: nor be deceived by her paths.
26 For she has cast down many wounded, and even the strongest have been killed by her.
27 Her house is the way to the underworld <note>original: *inferi*—referring to the grave or the realm of the dead</note>, reaching into the inner chambers of death.

### CHAPTER VIII.

*Wisdom invites all to embrace her, commending herself in many ways; she is co-eternal with God, ordering all things alongside Him. Those who seek her are blessed, while those who despise her will ultimately meet a miserable end.*

1 Does not wisdom cry out, and prudence lift up her voice?
2 Standing upon the highest and loftiest peaks above the way, in the middle of the paths,
3 Beside the gates of the city, at the very doors, she speaks, saying:
4 To you, O men, I call, and my voice is to the sons of men.
5 O little ones <note>original: *parvuli*—meaning the simple, young, or inexperienced</note>, understand shrewdness, and you fools, take notice.
6 Hear, for I am about to speak of great things: and my lips shall be opened to preach what is right.
7 My throat shall meditate on the truth, and my lips shall detest the wicked man.
8 All my words are just; there is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
9 They are right to those who understand, and just to those who find knowledge.
10 Receive my instruction rather than money: choose learning more than gold.
11 For wisdom is better than all the most precious things: and nothing that is desired can be compared to her.
12 I, wisdom, dwell in counsel, and I am present among learned thoughts.
13 The fear of the Lord hates evil: I detest arrogance, pride, the wicked way, and the double-tongued mouth.
14 Counsel is mine, and equity; prudence is mine, and strength is mine.
15 By me kings reign, and the makers of laws decree just things.
16 By me princes rule, and the powerful decree justice.
17 I love those who love me: and those who watch for me in the morning shall find me.
18 With me are riches and glory, proud wealth and justice.
19 For my fruit is better than gold and precious stones, and my offspring <note>original: *genimina*—literally "buds" or "products"</note> better than choice silver.
20 I walk in the ways of justice, in the midst of the paths of judgment,
21 That I may enrich those who love me, and fill their treasuries.
22 The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made anything from the start.
23 I was ordained from eternity, and from of old, before the earth was made.
24 The depths did not yet exist, and I was already conceived: the fountains of water had not yet burst forth.
25 The mountains had not yet been established with their heavy mass: I was brought forth <note>original: *parturiebar*—literally "born" or "delivered," signifying Wisdom’s existence before the physical world</note> before the hills.

<column-break/>

26 As yet he had not made the earth, nor the rivers, nor the poles <note>original: *cardines*—literally "hinges" or "pivots," referring to the structural foundations of the world</note> of the globe.
27 When he prepared the heavens, I was there: when he fenced in the depths with a fixed law and a circle.
28 When he established the sky above, and balanced the fountains of waters.
29 When he set a limit for the sea, and laid down a law for the waters that they should not pass their bounds: when he weighed the foundations of the earth.
30 I was with him, composing all things: and I was delighted every day, playing before him at all times;
31 Playing in the world: and my delights were to be with the children of men.
32 Now therefore, children, hear me: Blessed are they who keep my ways.
33 Hear instruction, and be wise, and do not cast it away.
34 Blessed is the man who hears me, and who watches at my gates daily, and waits at the posts of my doors.
35 He who finds me, shall find life, and shall draw salvation from the Lord.
36 But he who sins against me, shall hurt his own soul. All they who hate me, love death.

### CHAPTER IX.

*Wisdom, having built her house, attracts all to herself, prolongs life, and delivers from the foolish and wandering woman; furthermore, the wicked and the scoffer will not accept instruction, but the just and the wise will.*

1 Wisdom has built herself a house; she has hewn out seven pillars.
2 She has sacrificed her victims, mixed her wine, and set her table.
3 She has sent her maids to call to the citadel, and to the walls of the city:
4 If anyone is a little one, let him come to me. And to the foolish she said:
5 Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine which I have mixed for you.
6 Forsake your childhood <note>original: *infantiam*—here used to mean spiritual immaturity or ignorance</note>, and live, and walk by the ways of prudence.
7 He who instructs a scoffer does himself an injury: and he who rebukes a wicked man brings a stain upon himself.
8 Do not rebuke a scoffer, lest he hate you: Rebuke a wise man, and he will love you.
9 Give an opportunity to a wise man, and wisdom shall be added to him. Teach a just man, and he will hasten to receive it.
<margin>† Psalm 111:10; Above 1:7; Ecclesiasticus 1:16.</margin>
10 † The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy ones is prudence.
11 For through me your days shall be multiplied, and years of life shall be added to you.
12 If you are wise, you shall be so for yourself: but if you are a mocker, you alone shall bear the evil.
13 A foolish and clamorous woman, full of allurements and knowing nothing at all,
14 Sat at the door of her house upon a seat in a high place of the city,
15 To call those who pass by the way, and those going on their journey:
16 Whoever is a little one, let him turn aside to me. And to the senseless she said:
17 Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread is more pleasant.
18 And he did not know that giants <note>original: *gigantes*—referring to the shades or spirits of the dead</note> are there, and her guests are in the depths of hell.

## THE PARABLES OF SOLOMON.

### CHAPTER X.

*He alternates his discourse between the wise son and the foolish; the just and the wicked; the diligent and the idle; the simple and the crooked: concerning charity and hatred: concerning the good of the tongue, and its evil.*

1 A wise son makes a father glad: but a foolish son is a sorrow to his mother.
2 <margin>Below 11:4</margin> Treasures of wickedness shall profit nothing: but justice shall deliver from death.
3 The Lord will not afflict the soul of the just with famine, and he will subvert the deceits of the wicked.
4 The slack hand has wrought poverty: but the hand of the strong prepares riches.
He who leans on lies, this man feeds the winds: and he follows flying birds. <note>This second half of verse 4 is an ancient Latin addition; it suggests that the dishonest person pursues things that are fleeting and impossible to catch.</note>
5 He who gathers in the harvest is a wise son: but he who snores in the summer is a son of confusion.
6 The blessing of the Lord is upon the head of the just: but iniquity covers the mouth of the wicked.
7 The memory of the just is with praises: and the name of the wicked shall rot.
8 The wise of heart receives precepts: the foolish is beaten by his lips.
9 He who walks simply <note>original: *simpliciter*—meaning with integrity or without hidden motives</note> walks confidently: but he who perverts his ways shall be made manifest.
10 <margin>Sirach 27:25</margin> He who winks with the eye shall cause sorrow: and the foolish in lips shall be beaten.
11 The mouth of the just is a vein of life: and the mouth of the wicked covers iniquity.
12 <margin>1 Cor. 13:4; 1 Pet. 4:8</margin> Hatred stirs up strifes: and charity covers all sins.
13 Wisdom is found on the lips of the wise: and a rod for the back of him who lacks heart <note>original: *indiget corde*—a common Hebrew idiom for someone lacking in sense or moral understanding</note>.
14 The wise hide knowledge: but the mouth of the fool is close to confusion.
15 The substance of a rich man is his city of strength: the dread of the poor is their poverty.
16 The work of the just is unto life: but the fruit of the wicked is unto sin.
17 The way of life is for him who keeps discipline: but he who leaves behind rebukes, wanders.
18 Lying lips hide hatred: he who brings forth insult is unwise.
19 In much speaking, sin shall not be lacking: but he who moderates his lips is most prudent.
20 The tongue of the just is choice silver: but the heart of the wicked is for nothing.
21 The lips of the just instruct many: but those who are untaught shall die in the poverty of their heart.
22 The blessing of the Lord makes men rich, nor shall affliction be joined to them.
23 A fool commits a crime as if in jest: but wisdom is prudence to a man.
24 That which the wicked man fears shall come upon him: to the just, their desire shall be given.
25 Like a passing storm, the wicked shall be no more: but the just is like an everlasting foundation.
26 Like vinegar to the teeth, and smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who sent him.
27 The fear of the Lord shall add days: and the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
28 The expectation of the just is joy: but the hope of the wicked shall perish.
29 The way of the Lord is the strength of the simple: and dread to those who work evil.

<column-break/>

30 The just shall never be moved: but the wicked shall not dwell upon the earth.
31 The mouth of the just shall bring forth wisdom: the tongue of the perverse shall perish.
32 The lips of the just consider what is pleasing: and the mouth of the wicked, perverse things.

### CHAPTER XI.

*The benefits of equity, justice, and the other virtues; and the disadvantages of vices and vain riches.*

1 A deceitful scale is an abomination before the Lord: and a just weight is his will.
2 Where pride is, there shall be insult: but where humility is, there also is wisdom.
3 The simplicity of the just shall direct them: and the deceit of the perverse shall lay them waste.
4 <margin>Above 10:2</margin> Riches shall not profit in the day of vengeance: but justice shall deliver from death.
5 The justice of the simple shall direct his way: and the wicked shall fall in his own wickedness.
6 The justice of the upright shall deliver them: and the unjust shall be caught in their own snares.
7 When the wicked man is dead, there shall be no more hope: and the expectation of the anxious shall perish.
8 The just is delivered from distress: and the wicked shall be given up in his place.
9 The pretender <note>original: *simulator*—one who feigns virtue or hides their true intentions</note> deceives his friend with his mouth: but the just shall be delivered by knowledge.
10 The city shall exult in the good of the just: and in the destruction of the wicked there shall be praise.
11 By the blessing of the just the city shall be exalted: and by the mouth of the wicked it shall be subverted.
12 He who despises his friend is lacking in heart: but a prudent man will keep silence.
13 He who walks deceitfully reveals secrets: but he who is faithful of spirit conceals what is entrusted by a friend.
14 Where there is no governor, the people shall fall: but there is safety where there is much counsel.
15 He who gives a guarantee for a stranger shall be afflicted with evil: but he who avoids snares shall be secure.
16 A gracious woman shall find glory: and the robust shall have riches.
17 A merciful man does good to his own soul: but he who is cruel casts away even his kinsmen.
18 The wicked performs an unstable work: but to him who sows justice, there is a faithful reward.
19 Mildness prepares life: and the pursuit of evils, death.
20 A crooked heart is abominable to the Lord: and his will is in those who walk simply.
21 Hand in hand, the evil man shall not be innocent: but the seed of the just shall be saved.
22 Like a golden ring in the snout of a pig, so is a beautiful and foolish woman.
23 All the desire of the just is good: the expectation of the wicked is fury.
24 Some distribute their own goods and become richer: others seize what is not theirs and are always in poverty.
25 The soul that blesses shall be made fat: and he who satisfies others shall himself also be satisfied. <note>The Latin *inebriat* literally means to make drunk or drench, here used metaphorically for one who generously pours out bounty onto others.</note>
26 He who hides grain shall be cursed among the people: but a blessing is upon the head of those who sell it.
27 He rises well at dawn who seeks good things: but he who is an investigator of evils shall be oppressed by them.

<summary>This page contains Chapters 10 and 11 of Proverbs, marking the beginning of the specific "Parables of Solomon." These verses use short, contrasting couplets to illustrate the difference between a life of virtue and a life of vice, focusing on themes of honesty, diligence, and the power of speech.</summary>
<keywords>Solomon, Proverbs, wisdom, justice, wickedness, diligence, integrity, wealth, humility, charity, tongue, equity</keywords>

28 He who trusts in his riches shall fall: but the just shall spring up like a green leaf.
29 He who troubles his own house shall possess the winds: and the fool shall serve the wise.
30 The fruit of the just man is the tree of life: and he who wins souls is wise.
31 <margin>1 Peter 4:18</margin> If the just man is recompensed upon the earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner? <note>original: *Si iustus in terra recipit*—This implies that if even the righteous are disciplined or rewarded here, the wicked certainly cannot escape their fate.</note>

### CHAPTER XII.

->He speaks alternately of diligent discipline and the hatred of it; of the wicked and the just, the worker and the idle, the fool and the wise, and of the good and evil uses of the tongue.<-

1 He who loves discipline, loves knowledge: but he who hates reproof is foolish.
2 He who is good shall draw grace from the Lord: but he who trusts in his own thoughts acts wickedly.
3 A man shall not be strengthened by wickedness: and the root of the just shall not be moved.
4 A diligent woman is a crown to her husband: but she who does things worthy of confusion is as rottenness in his bones.
5 The thoughts of the just are judgments: and the counsels of the wicked are fraudulent.
6 The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood: the mouth of the just shall deliver them.
7 Overturn the wicked, and they shall be no more: but the house of the just shall stand forever.
8 A man shall be known by his learning: but he who is vain and heartless shall be exposed to contempt.
9 <margin>† Sirach 10:30</margin> Better is the poor man who provides for himself, than he who is boastful but lacks bread.
10 The just man knows the lives of his beasts: but the bowels <note>original: *viscera*—metaphorically meaning the innermost feelings or "mercies"</note> of the wicked are cruel.
11 <margin>† Sirach 20:30</margin> He who works his land shall be filled with bread: but he who pursues idleness is most foolish.
He who is sweet in his wine-gathering, leaves behind reproach in his own strongholds. <note>This second half of verse 11 is an addition found in the Latin tradition, warning that one who focuses only on pleasure (the vintage) neglects his security.</note>
12 The desire of the wicked is the fortification of the worst men: but the root of the just shall prosper.
13 For the sins of the lips, ruin draws near to the evil man: but the just man shall escape from distress.
14 By the fruit of his own mouth shall every man be filled with good things, and according to the works of his hands shall it be repaid to him.
15 The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he who is wise listens to counsels.
16 A fool immediately shows his anger: but he who dissembles an injury is shrewd.
17 He who speaks what he knows is a pointer of justice: but he who lies is a fraudulent witness.
18 There is one who promises, and is pierced in conscience as if by a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.
19 The lip of truth shall be steadfast forever: but he who is a hasty witness fashions a tongue of lies.
20 Deceit is in the heart of those who think evil thoughts: but joy follows those who take counsels of peace.
21 Whatever happens to the just man, it shall not make him sad: but the wicked shall be filled with evil.
22 Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord: but they who deal faithfully please him.
23 A shrewd man conceals his knowledge: and the heart of fools provokes folly.

<column-break/>

24 The hand of the strong shall bear rule: but the hand that is slack shall serve under tribute.
25 Grief in the heart of a man shall humble him, and he shall be made glad by a good word.
26 He who overlooks a loss for the sake of a friend is just: but the way of the wicked shall deceive them.
27 The fraudulent man shall not find gain: and the substance of a man shall be the price of gold. <note>This suggests that a man's true worth or character is more valuable than physical wealth.</note>
28 In the path of justice is life: but the devious way leads to death.

### CHAPTER XIII.

->Concerning the wise son: of the guarding of the mouth and being thoughtless in speaking: of the rich poor man and the poor rich man; the lamp of the wicked; substance gained in haste and the delaying of hope: all things are to be done with counsel, and one must walk with the wise: of sparing the rod, and the insatiable belly of the wicked.<-

1 A wise son is the doctrine of his father: but he who is a mocker does not listen when he is rebuked.
2 By the fruit of his own mouth shall a man be filled with good things: but the soul of transgressors is iniquitous.
3 He who guards his mouth guards his soul: but he who is thoughtless in speech shall feel evils.
4 The sluggard wills and wills not: but the soul of those who work shall be made fat.
5 The just man shall detest a lying word: but the wicked man confounds others, and shall himself be confounded.
6 Justice guards the way of the innocent: but wickedness supplants the sinner.
7 There is one who is as if he were rich, when he has nothing: and there is one who is as if he were poor, when he is in great riches.
8 The redemption of a man's soul is his riches: but he who is poor does not endure rebuke.
9 The law of the just brings joy: but the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
10 Among the proud there are always brawls: but they who do all things with counsel are governed by wisdom.
11 Substance gathered in haste shall be diminished: but that which is collected little by little by the hand shall be multiplied.
12 Hope which is deferred afflicts the soul; a desire that comes is a tree of life.
13 He who detracts from anything binds himself for the future: but he who fears the commandment shall dwell in peace.
Deceitful souls wander in sins: but the just are merciful and show pity. <note>This second part of verse 13 is unique to the Latin and certain Greek versions, emphasizing the connection between righteousness and mercy.</note>
14 The law of the wise is a fountain of life, so that he may decline from the ruin of death.
15 Good doctrine shall give grace: in the way of scorners is a whirlpool. <note>original: *vorago*—an abyss or pit; implying that those who despise wisdom fall into a trap of their own making.</note>
16 The shrewd man does all things with counsel: but he who is a fool opens up his own folly.
17 The messenger of the wicked shall fall into evil: but a faithful envoy is health.
18 Poverty and ignominy to him who deserts discipline: but he who yields to the one rebuking him shall be glorified.
19 A desire, if it be accomplished, delights the soul: fools detest those who flee from evils.
20 He who walks with the wise shall be wise: a friend of fools shall be made like them.
21 Evil pursues sinners: and good things shall be repaid to the just.
22 A good man leaves his children and grandchildren as heirs: and the substance of the sinner is kept for the just.

It emphasizes the power of the tongue, the value of hard work, and the importance of accepting discipline.</summary>

23 Much food is found in the fallow lands of the fathers: but for others it is gathered without judgment. <note>original: *novalibus*—This refers to land that has been plowed but left unseeded to regain fertility, suggesting that even untilled land can be productive through ancestral wisdom.</note>
24 He who spares the rod hates his son: but he who loves him instructs him diligently.
25 The just man eats and fills his soul: but the belly of the wicked is never satisfied.

### CHAPTER XIV.

*Wisdom and folly are of various conditions: by prudence, any state is properly regulated, through which one is moved to mercy and moderates their affections: but vices destroy men.*

1 A wise woman builds her house: but the foolish one will pull down with her hands even that which is built.
<margin>† Job 12:4</margin> 2 He who walks in the right path and fears God is despised by him who walks in a path of ill repute.
3 In the mouth of a fool is the rod of pride: but the lips of the wise preserve them.
4 Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty: but where there is much harvest, there the strength of the ox is manifest.
5 A faithful witness does not lie: but a deceitful witness utters falsehoods.
6 A scorner seeks wisdom and finds it not: the teaching of the prudent is easy.
7 Go against a foolish man, and he knows nothing of the lips of prudence.
8 The wisdom of a clever man is to understand his way: and the imprudence of fools is wandering.
9 A fool will mock at sin, but grace shall dwell among the just.
10 The heart that knows the bitterness of its own soul, a stranger shall not mingle in its joy.
11 The house of the wicked shall be destroyed: but the tabernacles of the just shall flourish.
12 There is a way which seems right to a man: but its latter ends lead to death.
13 Laughter shall be mixed with sorrow, and mourning takes hold of the end of joy.
14 A fool shall be filled with his own ways, and a good man shall be above him.
15 The innocent man believes every word: the cunning man considers his steps.
To a deceitful son there shall be nothing good: but for a wise servant his actions shall be prosperous, and his way shall be directed. <note>This second half of verse 15 is a specific addition found in the Latin Vulgate tradition.</note>
16 A wise man fears and turns away from evil: the fool leaps over and is confident.
17 An impatient man will act foolishly: and a crafty man is hateful.
18 The little ones shall possess folly, and the cunning shall wait for knowledge.
19 The evil shall lie down before the good: and the wicked before the gates of the just.
20 The poor man shall be hateful even to his own neighbor: but the friends of the rich are many.
21 He who despises his neighbor sins: but he who has mercy on the poor shall be blessed.
He who trusts in the Lord loves mercy.
22 They err who work evil: mercy and truth prepare good things.
23 In every work there shall be abundance: but where there are many words, there is often poverty.
24 The crown of the wise is their riches: the madness of fools is imprudence.
25 A faithful witness delivers souls: and the double-dealer utters lies.

<column-break/>

26 In the fear of the Lord is the confidence of strength, and there shall be hope for his children.
27 The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life, so that they may turn away from the ruin of death.
28 In the multitude of people is the dignity of the king: and in the small number of commoners is the shame of the prince.
29 He who is patient is governed by great prudence: but he who is impatient exalts his own folly.
30 Soundness of heart is the life of the flesh; envy is the rottenness of the bones.
<margin>† Below 17:5</margin> 31 He who slanders the needy reproaches his Maker: but he honors Him who has mercy on the poor.
32 The wicked man shall be driven out in his malice: but the just man has hope in his death.
33 In the heart of the prudent man wisdom rests, and it shall also instruct the unlearned.
34 Justice exalts a nation: but sin makes peoples miserable.
35 An intelligent minister is acceptable to the king: the useless one shall suffer his wrath.

### CHAPTER XV.

*A soft answer: the tongue of the wise and the immoderate: the strength of the just man's house: the victims of the wicked are unpleasing: all things are known to God: a joyful heart: the days of the poor are evil: a secure mind: to be invited to herbs: a wrathful and quarrelsome man: praise for the patient: the path of the pious: the house of the proud: sins are purged by faith and mercy: concerning one who rejects discipline: praise of the fear of the Lord and humility.*

<margin>† Below 25:15</margin> 1 A soft answer breaks wrath: a harsh word stirs up fury.
2 The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge: the mouth of fools bubbles over with folly.
3 In every place the eyes of the Lord behold the good and the evil.
4 A peaceful tongue is a tree of life: but that which is immoderate shall crush the spirit.
5 A fool mocks the discipline of his father: but he who heeds rebukes shall become more cunning.
In the abundance of justice there is the greatest strength: but the thoughts of the wicked shall be rooted out.
6 The house of the just is very strong: and in the fruits of the wicked is great trouble.
7 The lips of the wise shall scatter knowledge: the heart of fools shall be unlike them.
<margin>† Below 21:27. Sirach 34:21.</margin> 8 The victims of the wicked are abominable to the Lord: the vows of the just are pleasing.
9 The way of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord: he who follows justice is loved by Him.
10 Evil doctrine is for him who deserts the way of life: he who hates rebukes shall die.
11 Hell and destruction are before the Lord: how much more the hearts of the children of men? <note>original: *Infernus*—This refers to the underworld or the state of the dead (Sheol), emphasizing that nothing is hidden from God.</note>
12 A pestilent man does not love him who corrects him: nor does he go to the wise.
<margin>† Below 17:22</margin> 13 A joyful heart cheers the face: in the sadness of the soul the spirit is cast down.
14 The heart of the wise seeks teaching: and the mouth of fools feeds on lack of skill.
15 All the days of the poor are evil: a secure mind is like a continual feast.
16 Better is a little with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures that cannot satisfy.
17 It is better to be invited to a meal of herbs with charity, than to a fatted calf with hatred.
18 A wrathful man provokes quarrels: he who is patient calms those that have been stirred up.

19 The way of the slothful is like a hedge of thorns: the path of the just is without stumbling.
20 A wise son makes a father joyful: but a foolish man despises his mother.
21 Folly is joy to a fool: but a prudent man directs his steps.
22 Designs are brought to nothing where there is no counsel: but where there are many counselors, they are established.
23 A man rejoices in the utterance of his own mouth: and a word spoken in due time is best.
24 The path of life is above for the learned, so that he may turn away from the deepest hell. <note>original: *inferno novissimo*—referring to the lowest parts of the underworld or the state of the dead.</note>
25 The Lord will demolish the house of the proud: and he will make firm the boundaries of the widow.
26 Evil thoughts are an abomination to the Lord: and pure speech, most beautiful, shall be established by him.
27 He who follows greed troubles his own house: but he who hates bribes shall live.
<margin>† See below 16:6.</margin>
† By mercy and faith sins are purged: and by the fear of the Lord everyone turns away from evil.
28 The mind of the just meditates on obedience: the mouth of the impious overflows with evils.
29 The Lord is far from the impious: and he will hear the prayers of the just.
30 The light of the eyes rejoices the soul: a good reputation nourishes the bones.
31 The ear that listens to the reproofs of life shall dwell in the midst of the wise.
32 He who rejects discipline despises his own soul: but he who yields to reproof is a possessor of the heart. <note>original: *possessor est cordis*—a Latin idiom meaning one who gains understanding or wisdom.</note>
33 The fear of the Lord is the discipline of wisdom: and humility precedes glory.

### CHAPTER XVI.

> *Man prepares the soul, but God is the weigher of spirits; he directs the tongue and the ways of men, working all things for his own sake; to him, every arrogant person is an abomination. By mercy sins are redeemed. Weights and scales are the judgments of God. The indignation and clemency of the king. The praise of wisdom, prudence, the learned, the sweet in word, and the patient. The foolish and perverse are blamed. Lots are tempered by the Lord.*

1 It belongs to **m**an to prepare the soul: and to the Lord to govern the tongue.
<margin>† See below 21:2.</margin>
2 † All the ways of a man are open to his eyes: the Lord is the weigher of spirits.
3 Reveal your works to the Lord, and your thoughts shall be directed.
4 The Lord has worked all things for his own sake: even the impious man for the evil day.
5 Every arrogant man is an abomination to the Lord: even if hand be joined to hand, he is not innocent.
The beginning of a good way is to do justice: and it is more acceptable to God than to immolate sacrifices.
<margin>† Above 15:27.</margin>
6 † By mercy and truth iniquity is redeemed: and by the fear of the Lord one turns away from evil.
7 When the ways of a man please the Lord, he will convert even his enemies to peace.
8 Better is a little with justice, than many fruits with iniquity.
9 The heart of man disposes his way: but it is for the Lord to direct his steps.

<column-break/>

10 Divination is in the lips of the king: his mouth shall not err in judgment. <note>original: *divinatio*—implies a prophetic or divinely inspired decision.</note>
11 Weight and scales are the judgments of the Lord: and all the stones of the bag are his work. <note>original: *lapides sæculi*—referring to the stone weights kept in a merchant's bag.</note>
12 They who act impiously are abominable to the king: because the throne is established by justice.
13 Just lips are the will of kings: he who speaks right things shall be loved.
14 The indignation of the king is as messengers of death: and a wise man will appease it.
15 In the cheerfulness of the king’s countenance is life: and his clemency is like the late rain. <note>original: *imber serotinus*—the crucial rain before harvest time.</note>
16 Possess wisdom, for it is better than gold: and acquire prudence, for it is more precious than silver.
17 The path of the just avoids evils: the guardian of his own soul keeps his way.
18 Pride precedes destruction: and the spirit is exalted before a fall.
19 It is better to be humbled with the meek than to divide spoils with the proud.
20 The learned in word shall find good things: and he who hopes in the Lord is blessed.
21 He who is wise in heart shall be called prudent: and he who is sweet in speech shall attain greater things.
22 Learning is a fountain of life to its possessor: the doctrine of fools is fatuity.
23 The heart of the wise shall instruct his mouth: and shall add grace to his lips.
24 Well-ordered words are as a honeycomb: sweetness to the soul, and health to the bones.
25 There is a way that seems right to a man: and the ends thereof lead to death.
26 The soul of him who labors, labors for himself, because his mouth has compelled him.
27 An impious man digs up evil, and in his lips a fire burns.
28 A perverse man stirs up strife: and one full of words separates leaders.
29 An unjust man entices his friend: and leads him by a way that is not good.
30 He who with staring eyes thinks of wicked things, biting his lips, brings evil to pass.
31 Old age is a crown of dignity, which shall be found in the ways of justice.
32 A patient man is better than a strong man: and he who masters his mind is better than a conqueror of cities.
33 Lots are cast into the lap, but they are tempered by the Lord.

### CHAPTER XVII.

> *A dry morsel with joy. A wise servant. The Lord proves hearts. Despising the poor. Rejoicing at another’s ruin. The crown of old age. Concealing a fault. A fool trusting in his folly. Riches are useless to a fool. Making one’s house high. A friend loves at all times. A joyful mind and a sad spirit. The silent fool.*

1 Better is a **m**orsel of dry bread with joy, than a house full of victims with strife. <note>original: *victimis*—referring to the meat of sacrificed animals which provided a feast.</note>
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 10:28.</margin>
2 † A wise servant shall rule over foolish sons, and shall divide the inheritance among brothers.
3 As silver is tried by fire, and gold in the furnace: so the Lord proves hearts.
4 The evil man obeys an unjust tongue, and the deceitful man yields to lying lips.
<margin>† Above 14:31.</margin>
5 † He who despises the poor upbraids his Maker: and he who rejoices at the ruin of another shall not go unpunished.

6 The crown of the elderly is their children’s children: and the glory of children is their fathers.
7 Well-composed words do not suit a fool: nor do lying lips suit a prince.
8 A most welcome gemstone is the expectation of one who waits; <note>original: *expectatio præstolantis*—this suggests a precious gift or bribe that opens doors for the giver.</note> wherever he turns himself, he understands prudently.
9 He who conceals a fault seeks friendships: he who repeats it in another’s hearing separates allies.
10 A correction benefits a prudent man more than a hundred lashes benefit a fool.
11 An evil man always seeks quarrels: but a cruel angel shall be sent against him.
12 It is better to meet a bear whose cubs have been snatched away than a fool trusting in his own folly.
<margin>Romans 12:17, 1 Thessalonians 5:15, 1 Peter 2:9.</margin>
13 † He who returns evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
14 He who lets out water is the beginning of quarrels: and before he suffers insult, he abandons judgment.
<margin>† Isaiah 5:23.</margin>

16 What does it profit a fool to have riches, when he cannot buy wisdom?
He who builds his house high seeks ruin: and he who avoids learning will fall into evils.
17 He who is a friend loves at all times: and a brother is proven in times of distress.
18 A foolish man will clap his hands <note>A gesture of making a pledge or strike a bargain.</note> when he stands surety for his friend.
19 He who meditates on discords loves brawls, and he who exalts his doorway seeks ruin.
20 He who is of a perverse heart shall not find good: and he who shifts his tongue shall fall into evil.
21 A fool is born to his own disgrace: nor shall a father rejoice in a foolish son.
<margin>† Above 15:13.</margin>
22 † A joyful mind makes for a flourishing life: a sad spirit dries up the bones.
23 The impious man receives gifts from the bosom <note>original: *de sinu*—referring to a secret bribe hidden in one's robes.</note> so that he may pervert the paths of judgment.
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 2:14 & 8:1.</margin>
24 † Wisdom shines in the face of the prudent: the eyes of fools are on the ends of the earth.
25 A foolish son is the anger of the father: and the grief of the mother who bore him.
26 It is not good to inflict loss upon the just: nor to strike a prince who judges rightly.
<margin>† James 1:19.</margin>
27 † He who moderates his words is learned and prudent: and the man of understanding is of a precious spirit.
28 Even a fool, if he remains silent, shall be reckoned as wise: and if he closes his lips, as a man of intelligence.

### C H A P T E R XVIII.

->*Concerning withdrawing from a friend: concerning the incorrigible: one must not deviate from the truth: the mouth of the fool: the just man accusing himself: a brother helping a brother: the fruit of the mouth: the good and bad woman: the speech of the rich and the poor: the friendly man.*<-

1 He who wishes to withdraw from a friend seeks excuses: at all times he shall be subject to reproach.
2 A fool does not receive words of prudence: unless you say those things which are already in his heart.
3 The impious man, when he has come into the depths of sins, feels contempt: but disgrace and reproach follow him.
4 The words from a man's mouth are deep water: and the fountain of wisdom is an overflowing torrent.

<column-break/>

5 To show partiality to the person of the impious is not good, that you might turn away from the truth of judgment.
6 The lips of a fool mingle in brawls: and his mouth provokes quarrels.
7 The mouth of a fool is his destruction: and his own lips are the ruin of his soul.
8 The words of the double-tongued <note>original: *bilinguis*—referring to a gossiper or deceitful speaker.</note> are as if simple: and they reach even to the inner parts of the belly.
Fear casts down the lazy: but the souls of the effeminate shall go hungry.
9 He who is soft and lax in his work is the brother of him who wastes his own labors.
10 The name of the Lord is a most strong tower: the just man runs to it and shall be exalted.
11 The substance of the rich man is his city of strength, and like a mighty wall surrounding him.
12 Before it is crushed, the heart of a man is exalted: and before he is glorified, he is humbled.
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 11:8.</margin>
13 † He who answers before he hears shows himself to be a fool and worthy of confusion.
14 The spirit of a man sustains his weakness: but who can sustain a spirit that is easily provoked to anger?
15 A prudent heart shall possess knowledge: and the ear of the wise seeks doctrine.
16 A man’s gift enlarges his way, and makes room for him before princes.
17 The just man is the first to accuse himself: then his friend comes and will search him out.
18 The lot <note>The casting of lots to determine a divine or random outcome.</note> suppresses contradictions, and it decides even between the powerful.
19 A brother who is helped by a brother is like a strong city: and judgments are like the bars of cities.
20 From the fruit of a man's mouth shall his belly be filled: and the harvest of his lips shall satisfy him.
21 Death and life are in the power of the tongue: those who love it shall eat its fruits.
22 He who finds a good wife finds a good thing: and he shall draw delight from the Lord.
He who expels a good wife expels a good thing: but he who keeps an adulteress is a fool and impious.
23 The poor man speaks with entreaties: and the rich man will speak harshly.
24 A man amiable in society shall be more of a friend than a brother.

### C H A P T E R XIX.

->*A poor man walking in simplicity: riches add friends: one who falsifies words: a false witness: luxury does not suit a fool: doctrine is proven through patience: the anger and cheerfulness of a king: a quarrelsome woman: a prudent wife is given by God: laziness: keeping the commandment: mercy toward the poor: the instruction of a son: accepting counsel: a lying man: the fear of the Lord: laziness: the pestilent: the disobedient to parents: an iniquitous witness: mockers.*<-

1 Better is the poor man who walks in his simplicity than a rich man twisting his lips, and a fool.
2 Where there is no knowledge of the soul, it is not good: and he who is hasty with his feet shall stumble.
3 The folly of a man trips up his steps: and he frets in his mind against God.
4 Riches add many friends: but from the poor man, even those whom he had are separated.
<margin>† Daniel 13:61.</margin>
5 † A false witness shall not go unpunished: and he who speaks lies shall not escape.
6 Many worship the person of the powerful, and are friends of him who bestows gifts.

### CHAPTER XX.

*Wine is a thing of luxury: on sinning against the king, and abandoning contentions: the sluggard who will not work because of the cold: the king upon his throne: no one can say he has a clean heart: divers weights: sleep is not to be loved: "It is bad," says the buyer: the bread of lying: revealing mysteries: evil is not to be returned for evil: devouring holy things: a hasty inheritance: mercy, truth, and clemency strengthen the king's throne.*

1 Wine is a thing of luxury, and drunkenness is tumultuous: whoever is delighted by these shall not be wise.
2 As the roaring of a lion, so is the terror of the king: he who provokes him sins against his own soul.
3 It is an honor for a man who separates himself from contentions: but all fools are mixed up in insults.

6 Many men are called merciful: but who shall find a faithful man?
7 The just man, who walks in his simplicity, shall leave behind blessed children.
8 A king, who sits upon the throne of judgment, scatters all evil with his gaze.

### CHAPTER XXI.

*The heart of the king is in the hand of the Lord, to whom mercy and judgment are more pleasing than a sacrifice: he who gathers treasures iniquitously: it is better to sit in a corner of the housetop than, etc. he who stops his ear to the poor, etc. he who loves feasts: the impious shall be given for the just: he who guards his mouth: desires kill the sluggard: there is no wisdom against the Lord: the horse is prepared for battle, etc.*

1 As the divisions of waters, so is the heart of the king in the hand of the Lord: whithersoever He wills, He shall turn it.

### CHAPTER XXII.

-> Praise of a good name: the shrewd man seeing evil: a youth in his way: sowing iniquity: cast out the mocker: loving purity of heart: the lazy man says "A Lion!", etc.: the mouth of a stranger: folly in the heart of a boy: slandering the poor: wisdom must be heard: avoid being a surety for debts: old landmarks to be kept: swift in his work, etc. <-

4 The end of modesty is the fear of the Lord, riches and glory and life.

5 Weapons and swords are in the way of the perverse: but the guardian of his own soul stays far from them.

# CHAPTER XXIII.

*How one should eat with a prince: that riches are not to be sought, nor the food of the envious: that orphans are not to be oppressed: the child is to be corrected: wisdom is to be sought: sinners and gluttons are to be avoided: parents are to be honored: the harlot and drunkenness are to be avoided.*

1 When you sit to eat with a prince, consider diligently what is set before your face:
2 And put a knife to your throat, if you have control over your soul <note>original: *animam tuam*—here meaning one's appetite or desires</note>.
3 Do not desire his meats, in which is the bread of deceit.
4 Do not labor to be rich: but set a limit to your own prudence.
5 Do not lift up your eyes to riches which you cannot have: because they shall make themselves wings like those of an eagle, and shall fly towards heaven.
6 Do not eat with an envious man, and do not desire his meats:
7 Because, like a fortune-teller and a diviner, he thinks of what he does not know <note>original: *arioli & conjectoris*—referring to one who guesses or looks for hidden meanings</note>.
"Eat and drink," he will say to you: but his mind is not with you.
8 The meats which you had eaten, you shall vomit up: and you shall lose your beautiful words.
9 Do not speak in the ears of the foolish: because they will despise the instruction of your speech.
10 Do not touch the boundaries of little ones: and do not enter into the field of orphans:
11 For their near kinsman is strong: and he himself will judge their cause against you.
12 Let your heart enter into instruction, and your ears to the words of knowledge.
<margin>Above 13:24; 22:15.</margin>
13 Do not withhold discipline from a child: for if you strike him with the rod, he shall not die.
14 You shall strike him with the rod, and deliver his soul from hell <note>original: *inferno*—referring here to the grave or destruction</note>.
15 My son, if your mind be wise, my heart shall rejoice with you:
16 And my inward parts shall exult, when your lips shall speak what is right.
<margin>Below 24:1.</margin>
17 † Let not your heart envy sinners: but be in the fear of the Lord all day long:
18 Because you shall have hope in the end, and your expectation shall not be taken away.
19 Hear, my son, and be wise: and guide your mind in the way.
20 Do not be in the feasts of great drinkers, nor in the revelries of those who contribute meat to eat:
21 Because those who spend their time in drinking and giving pledges <note>original: *symbola*—contributions for a shared feast or drinking party</note> shall be consumed, and drowsiness shall be clothed with rags.
22 Hearken to your father, who begot you: and do not despise your mother when she is old.
23 Buy truth, and do not sell wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
24 The father of the just rejoices with joy: he who has begotten a wise son shall rejoice in him.
25 Let your father and your mother be joyful, and let her who bore you exult.
26 My son, give me your heart: and let your eyes keep my ways.
27 For a harlot is a deep ditch: and a foreign woman is a narrow well.

<column-break/>

28 She lies in wait in the way like a robber, and those whom she sees off their guard, she will kill.
29 Who has woe? Whose father has woe? Who has brawls? Who has pits? Who has wounds without cause? Who has redness of eyes?
30 Is it not those who linger over wine, and study the draining of cups?
31 Do not look upon the wine when it grows yellow, when its color shines in the glass: it goes in pleasantly,
32 But in the end it will bite like a snake, and spread its poison like a basilisk <note>original: *regulus*—a "little king" or mythical serpent whose breath or look was fatal</note>.
33 Your eyes shall behold strange women, and your heart shall speak perverse things.
34 And you shall be as one sleeping in the midst of the sea, and as a pilot fast asleep, having lost the tiller.
35 And you shall say: "They beat me, but I was not grieved: they dragged me, and I did not feel it: when shall I awake, and find wine again?"

# CHAPTER XXIV.

*Envy of the wicked: wisdom and learning: the thought of a fool: the oppressed are to be rescued: teaching is to be used like honey: one must not lie in wait for the just: the fall of an enemy: detractors: judging justly: no one should be boasted of, nor evil returned for evil: the field of the sluggard: poverty comes to the sleepy sluggard.*

<margin>Above 23:17.</margin>
1 Do not envy evil men, nor desire to be with them:
2 Because their mind meditates robberies, and their lips speak deceits.
3 By wisdom a house shall be built, and by prudence it shall be strengthened.
4 By instruction the storerooms shall be filled with all precious and most beautiful substance.
5 A wise man is strong: and a learned man is robust and powerful.
6 Because war is managed by disposition: and there shall be safety where there are many counsels.
7 Wisdom is too high for a fool; in the gate he shall not open his mouth.
8 He who thinks to do evil shall be called a fool.
9 The thought of a fool is sin: and the detractor is the abomination of men.
10 If you lose hope, being weary in the day of distress, your strength shall be diminished.
<margin>† Psalm 81:4.</margin>
11 † Rescue those who are being led to death: and do not cease to deliver those who are being dragged to destruction.
12 If you say: "Strength is not sufficient": he who is the inspector of the heart, he understands, and nothing escapes the savior of your soul, and he shall render to a man according to his works.
13 Eat honey, my son, because it is good, and the honeycomb which is most sweet to your throat.
14 So also is the doctrine of wisdom to your soul: which when you have found, you shall have hope in the end, and your hope shall not perish.
15 Do not lie in wait, nor seek wickedness in the house of the just, nor spoil his rest.
16 For a just man shall fall seven times, and shall rise again: but the wicked shall fall into evil.
17 When your enemy falls, do not rejoice, and let not your heart exult in his ruin:
18 Lest perhaps the Lord see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
19 Do not contend with the most wicked, nor envy the ungodly:
20 Because evil men have no hope of things to come: and the lamp of the wicked shall be put out.
