### CHAPTER VII.

*Since there is one entrance into life for all, and a similar exit; wisdom is to be chosen above all things, bringing with her every good, and possessing within herself a manifold spirit of understanding; which the author here extols in a wondrous way, having been abundantly moved by her.*

1 I myself am also a mortal man, like everyone else, and a descendant of that earthly one who was first made <note>A reference to Adam, the first human formed from the earth.</note>, and in my mother's womb I was shaped into flesh,
<margin>† Job 10:10.</margin>
2 In the space of ten months † I was curdled in blood, from the seed of man and the pleasure that accompanies sleep <note>An ancient biological view of conception and gestation.</note>.
3 And when I was born, I drew in the common air and fell upon the earth, which is made alike for all, and my first voice was a cry, just like everyone else.
4 I was nursed in swaddling clothes and with great cares.
5 For no king had any other beginning of birth.
<margin>† Job 1:21; 1 Timothy 6:7.</margin>
6 † For there is but one entrance into life for all, and a similar departure.
7 Because of this, I prayed, and understanding was given to me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came into me.
8 And I preferred her before kingdoms and thrones, and I accounted riches as nothing in comparison to her.
<margin>† Job 28:15; Proverbs 8:11.</margin>
9 † Neither did I compare any precious stone to her: for all gold, in comparison to her, is but a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay in her sight.
10 I loved her more than health and beauty, and I chose to have her instead of light: for her light never goes out.
<margin>† 1 Kings 3:13; Matthew 6:33.</margin>
11 † Now all good things came to me together with her, and innumerable riches through her hands,
12 And I rejoiced in all these things, because this wisdom went before me, and I did not know that she is the mother of all these things.
13 Which I learned without deception and share without envy, and I do not hide her riches.
14 For she is an infinite treasure to men: those who use it become partakers of the friendship of God, being commended for the gifts of instruction.
15 But God has granted me to speak according to my mind, and to conceive thoughts worthy of the things given to me: because He is the leader of wisdom and the director of the wise.

<column-break/>

16 For in His hand are both we and our words, as well as all wisdom, and the knowledge and skill of our works.
17 For He has given me true knowledge of the things that are: to know the structure of the world, and the powers of the elements,
18 The beginning, the end, and the middle of times, the changes of the solstices, and the transformations of the seasons,
19 The cycles of the years, and the positions of the stars,
20 The natures of animals, and the tempers of wild beasts, the force of winds, and the reasonings of men, the diversities of plants, and the medicinal virtues of roots,
21 And all such things as are hidden and unforeseen, I have learned: for wisdom, the <term>artificer</term> <note>original: "artifex" — a master craftsman or creator.</note> of all things, taught me.
22 For in her is a spirit of understanding: holy, unique, manifold, subtle, eloquent, mobile, undefiled, certain, sweet, loving that which is good, sharp, which nothing can hinder, doing good,
23 Kind to man, steadfast, assured, secure, having all power, overseeing all things, and containing all spirits: intelligible, pure, and subtle.
24 For wisdom is more mobile than all motions: she reaches everywhere because of her purity.
25 For she is a breath <note>original: "vapor" — often used in a philosophical sense to mean an emanation or aura.</note> of the power of God, and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty God: and therefore no defiled thing can enter into her.
<margin>† Hebrews 1:3.</margin>
26 † For she is the brightness of eternal light, and the unspotted mirror of God’s majesty, and the image of His goodness.
27 And being but one, she can do all things: and remaining in herself, she makes all things new, and through nations she conveys herself into holy souls, making them friends of God and prophets.
28 For God loves no one except him who dwells with wisdom.
29 For she is more beautiful than the sun, and above every arrangement of the stars; compared with the light, she is found to be prior.
30 For night follows the light, but malice does not overcome wisdom.

### CHAPTER VIII.

*Since all desirable things accompany wisdom: she is to be sought above all else, and asked of God, from whom alone self-control is given.*

1 She reaches, therefore, from end to end mightily, and orders all things sweetly.
2 I have loved her, and sought her out from my youth, and I desired to take her as my spouse, and I became a lover of her beauty.
3 She glorifies her noble birth by having companionship with God: and the Lord of all things has loved her.
4 For she is the teacher of the knowledge of God, and the chooser of His works.
5 And if riches are desired in life, what is richer than wisdom, which works all things?
6 But if understanding works: who of all the things that are is a greater <term>artificer</term> than she?
7 And if a man loves justice: her labors have great virtues: for she teaches temperance, and prudence, and justice, and fortitude, than which nothing is more useful in life for men.
8 And if a man desires a multitude of knowledge: she knows things past, and judges of things to come: she knows the subtleties of...

### CHAPTER IX.

### CHAPTER X.

->*Wisdom led the children of Israel through the desert, having conquered their enemies and given them water from the rock. 26 And how could anything endure unless You willed it? Or how could that which was not called by You be preserved?
27 But You spare all things, because they are Yours, O Lord, You who love souls.

### CHAPTER XIII.

*Those who do not recognize God through His creatures, but instead worship the creatures themselves as gods, are vain: but those are much more foolish who call the work of a craftsman a god, asking for future things from a senseless idol.*

<margin>Romans 1:18.</margin>
1 All men are vain in whom there is no knowledge of God: and from those things which are seen to be good, they could not understand "He who is" <note>original: "eum qui est"; a reference to the divine name revealed to Moses</note>, nor by attending to the works did they acknowledge who the craftsman was;
<margin>Deuteronomy 4:19 and 17:3.</margin>
2 But they thought either fire, or wind <note>original: "spiritum"</note>, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the great water, or the sun and moon, to be the gods that rule the world.
3 If they were delighted by the beauty of these things and took them to be gods: let them know how much more beautiful the Lord of them is: for the author of beauty made all these things.
4 Or if they admired their power and works, let them understand by them, that he who made them is stronger than they:
5 For by the greatness of the beauty and of the creature, the creator of them may be seen in a knowable way.
6 But yet in these the complaint is less. For they perhaps err while seeking God and wishing to find him.
<margin>Romans 1:21.</margin>
7 † For while they are occupied with his works, they search: and they are persuaded that the things are good which are seen.
8 But again, even these are not to be excused.
9 For if they could know so much as to be able to judge the world: how did they not more easily find the Lord thereof?
10 But they are unhappy, and their hope is among the dead, who have called "gods" the works of the hands of men: gold and silver, the invention of art, and the likenesses of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
<margin>† Isaiah 44:12; Jeremiah 10:3.</margin>
11 † Or if a skillful carpenter has cut down a straight tree from the woods, and skillfully scrapes off all the bark, and using his art, diligently fashions a vessel useful for the business of life,
12 And uses the leftover scraps of his work to prepare his food:
13 And the rest of these, which he makes for no use—being a crooked piece of wood and full of knots—he carves diligently in his leisure, and by the knowledge of his art fashions it, and makes it like the image of a man,
14 Or compares it to some animal, painting it with red chalk, and making its color red with paint, and covering every spot that is in it:
15 And makes for it a worthy dwelling, and placing it in a wall, and fastening it with iron,
16 Lest it should fall, providing for it, knowing that it cannot help itself: for it is an image, and it needs help.
17 And making a vow for his possessions, and for his children, and for his marriage, he inquires of it. He is not ashamed to speak to that which has no soul:

### CHAPTER XIV.

->*The useful invention of the ship, by which even in the time of the flood the human race was preserved; however, the idol is cursed along with its maker; the origin and progress of idols and idolatry, and the many evils that proceed from idolatry.*<-

Again, another person intending to sail, and beginning to make a journey through the fierce waves, invokes a piece of wood more fragile than the ship that carries him. 
2 For the desire for gain devised the ship, and the craftsman’s wisdom built it. 
3 But your providence, O Father, governs it: <margin>† Exodus 14:22.</margin> for you have given a way even in the sea, and a most certain path among the waves, 
4 Showing that you are powerful to save from all things, even if someone should go to sea without skill. 
5 But so that the works of your wisdom should not be in vain, for this reason men also trust their lives to a small piece of wood, and crossing the sea in a boat, they are saved. 
6 <margin>† Genesis 6:4 and 7:7.</margin> For even from the beginning, when the proud giants perished, the hope of the world <note>Noah and his family</note> fled to a boat, and transmitted to the world the seed of birth, which was governed by your hand. 
7 For blessed is the wood through which righteousness is brought about. <note>original: "lignum per quod fit justitia"; traditionally interpreted by Christian scholars as a reference to both Noah's Ark and the Cross of Christ.</note> 
8 <margin>† Psalm 113; Baruch 6:3.</margin> But the idol that is made by hands is cursed, both it and he who made it: because he indeed worked on it, but the thing itself, though it was fragile, was called a god. 
9 For the ungodly and his ungodliness are equally hateful to God. 
10 For that which is made shall suffer torment together with him who made it. 
11 Therefore, there shall be no regard for the idols of the nations: since the creatures of God are turned into an object of hatred, and a temptation for the souls of men, and a snare for the feet of the foolish. 
12 For the beginning of spiritual fornication <note>The biblical term for turning away from God to worship idols</note> is the seeking out of idols; and the invention of them is the corruption of life. 
13 For they were not from the beginning, nor shall they be forever. 
14 For the vanity of men brought them into the world, and therefore a brief end has been found for them. 
15 For a father, grieving with bitter sorrow, made an image of his son who was quickly taken from him; and him who was then but a dead man, he now began to worship as a god, and established sacred rites and sacrifices among his servants. 
16 Then, as time passed, the wicked custom became strong and this error was kept as a law, and by the command of tyrants, statues were worshipped. 
17 And since men could not honor those in person because they lived far away, they brought their likeness from afar and made an evident image of the king whom they wished to honor, so that by their diligence they might worship him as if he were present. 
18 Moreover, the extraordinary diligence of the craftsman pushed even those who did not know the king to worship him.

<column-break/>

19 For he, wishing to please the one who employed him, labored with his art to make the likeness even more beautiful. 
20 And the multitude of men, led away by the beauty of the work, now esteemed as a god him who a little while before had been honored only as a man. 
21 And this became the deception of human life: for men, serving either their own affection or kings, gave the incommunicable name <note>original: "incommunicabile nomen"; the unique name of the one true God</note> to stones and wood. 
22 And it was not enough for them to have erred concerning the knowledge of God; but while living in a great war of ignorance, they call so many and such great evils "peace." 
23 <margin>† Deuteronomy 18:10; Jeremiah 7:6.</margin> For while they sacrifice their own children, or perform dark sacrifices, or hold vigils full of madness, 
24 They no longer keep either life or marriage pure; but one kills another through envy, or grieves him by adultery. 
25 And all things are mixed together: blood, murder, theft and fraud, corruption and unfaithfulness, turmoil and perjury, the harassment of good men, 
26 Forgetfulness of God, the defiling of souls, the changing of nature in birth, the instability of marriage, and the disorder of adultery and shamelessness. 
27 For the worship of unspeakable idols is the cause, the beginning, and the end of all evil. 
28 For either they are mad when they are happy, or they prophesy lies, or they live unjustly, or they quickly commit perjury. 
29 For while they trust in idols that have no soul, they swear falsely and do not expect to be harmed. 
30 Therefore, for both reasons, justice shall come upon them worthily: because they thought ill of God by attending to idols, and they swore unjustly, in deceit despising justice. 
31 For it is not the power of those by whom they swear, but the punishment of sinners that always follows the transgression of the unjust.

### CHAPTER XV.

->*The voice of the faithful commending the sweetness and mercy of God, by whose grace they were saved from idolatry; it also wonderfully mocks the makers and worshippers of idols.*<-

BUT you, our God, are sweet and true, patient, and ordering all things in mercy. 
2 For even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your greatness; and if we do not sin, we know that we are counted as yours.

4 For the invention of man's wicked art has not led us into error, nor has the fruitless labor of a shaded painting—a statue carved and covered in various colors, 
5 The sight of which gives desire to the foolish, so that he loves the lifeless form of a dead image. 
6 Lovers of evil are worthy to have their hope in such things: both those who make them, and those who love them, and those who worship them.

### CHAPTER XVI.

->*While the Egyptians suffered worthy punishments for their idolatry, the Hebrews received food from God; though they were punished for a time by the bite of serpents, they were healed by God through the raised bronze serpent. The wicked, however, were consumed by death through locusts and flies and fire mixed with hail, while the Hebrews, having received manna, were satisfied and strengthened.*<-

1 **F**or these reasons, and through similar things, they worthily suffered torments, and were destroyed by a multitude of beasts.

<margin>$\dagger$ Numbers 11:31.</margin>
2 In place of these torments, you dealt well with your people, $\dagger$ for whom you provided the desire of their own delight, a new flavor, preparing quails <note>original: "ortygometram"; the Greek term for quails, referring to the miraculous food in the desert.</note> as their food.

3 So that those others, though they desired food, might be turned away even from necessary appetite because of the things shown and sent to them <note>The plagues of frogs, flies, and locusts made the Egyptians loathe food.</note>. But these people, after being in want for a short time, tasted a new food.

4 For it was necessary that ruin should come without excuse upon those who practiced tyranny; but to these others, it was only to be shown how their enemies were being destroyed.

<column-break/>

5 $\dagger$ <margin>$\dagger$ Numbers 21:6.</margin> For even when the savage rage of beasts came upon them, they were being destroyed by the bites of twisting serpents.

6 But your anger did not remain forever; they were troubled for a short time for the sake of correction, having a sign of salvation <note>The bronze serpent raised by Moses.</note> to remind them of the commandment of your law.

7 For he who turned toward it was healed, not by what he saw, but by you, the Savior of all.

8 And in this you showed our enemies that you are the one who delivers from every evil.

9 $\dagger$ <margin>$\dagger$ Exodus 10:4, 8, 24.</margin> For the bites of locusts and flies killed those others, and no healing for their lives was found, because they were worthy to be destroyed by such things.

10 <margin>Revelation 9:7.</margin> But not even the teeth of venomous dragons overcame your children; for your mercy came and healed them.

11 For they were bitten to keep your words in memory, and were quickly saved, lest falling into deep forgetfulness, they might not be able to use your help.

12 For neither herb nor ointment <note>original: "malagma"; a medicinal plaster or emollient.</note> healed them, but your word, O Lord, which heals all things.

13 $\dagger$ <margin>$\dagger$ Deuteronomy 32:39; 1 Samuel 2:6; Tobit 13:2.</margin> For it is you, O Lord, who have power over life and death, and you lead down to the gates of death and bring back again.

14 A man indeed kills through malice, but when the spirit has gone forth, it shall not return, nor shall he call back the soul that has been received.

15 But it is impossible to escape your hand.

16 $\dagger$ <margin>$\dagger$ Exodus 9:23.</margin> For the wicked, denying they knew you, were scourged by the strength of your arm; they suffered persecution through strange waters, and hails, and rains, and were consumed by fire.

17 For what was most wonderful: in the water, which extinguishes all things, the fire had more power; for the world is the defender of the righteous.

18 For at one time the fire was tamed, so that the animals sent against the wicked might not be burned, but that they, seeing this, might know they were suffering persecution by the judgment of God.

19 And at another time, even in the water, the fire burned beyond its natural power on every side, to destroy the crops of a wicked land.

20 $\dagger$ <margin>$\dagger$ Exodus 16:14; Numbers 11:7; Psalm 78:25; John 6:31.</margin> In contrast to these things, you nourished your people with the food of angels, and provided them bread from heaven prepared without labor, having in itself every delight and the sweetness of every taste.

21 For your sustenance showed your sweetness, which you have toward your children; and serving the will of each one, it was turned to what every person wanted.

22 $\dagger$ <margin>$\dagger$ Exodus 9:24.</margin> But snow and ice withstood the force of fire and did not melt, so that they might know that fire, burning in the hail and flashing in the rain, destroyed the fruits of the enemies.

23 But this fire, again, so that the righteous might be nourished, even forgot its own power.

24 For creation, serving you the Creator, exerts its strength for torment against the unjust, and becomes gentle for the benefit of those who trust in you.

15 Then, if any of them had fallen down, he was kept shut up in a prison without iron bars.

17 For with one chain of darkness they all

<column-break/>

were bound together. Whether it was a whistling wind, or the sweet sound of birds among the thick branches of trees, or the force of water running violently,
18 Or the heavy crash of rocks falling down, or the unseen running of playing animals, or the powerful voice of bellowing beasts, or an echo resounding from the highest mountains; these things made them faint for fear.
19 For the whole world was illuminated with clear light, and was occupied with unhindered works.
20 But over them alone was spread a heavy night, an image of the darkness that was to come upon them. They were therefore heavier to themselves than the darkness.

### ON
# ECCLESIASTICUS
## OF JESUS, SON OF SIRACH.

<image-desc>A decorative fleuron ornament consisting of a central circle flanked by symmetrical leafy scrollwork.</image-desc>

### PROLOGUE.

Many and great things have been shown to us through the Law, the Prophets, and others who followed them, regarding wisdom. In these matters, Israel ought to be praised for the sake of its teaching and wisdom, because it is necessary not only for the speakers themselves to be skilled, but even for outsiders to be able to become most learned, both by speaking and by writing. 

My grandfather Jesus, after he had devoted himself more fully to the diligent reading of the Law, the Prophets, and the other books which were handed down to us by our fathers, wished also to write something himself regarding those things which pertain to teaching and wisdom. He did this so that those desiring to learn, having become skilled in these matters, might apply themselves more and more in mind and be strengthened for a life lived according to the Law. 

I exhort you, therefore, to come with goodwill and to read with more attentive study, and to be indulgent in those places where we seem—while following the patterns of wisdom—to fall short in the composition of words. For Hebrew words lack <note>That is, they lose some of their original force or nuance</note> when they have been translated into another language. Not only these, but even the Law itself, the Prophets, and the rest of the books have no small difference when they are compared to their original forms. 

For in the thirty-eighth year, in the time of King Ptolemy Euergetes <note>This likely refers to Ptolemy VII Physcon, who reigned in the 2nd century BCE; his 38th year would be roughly 132 BCE</note>, after I arrived in Egypt and had been there for a long time, I found books left there <note>original: "libros relictos," often understood as instructional records or a specific type of school work</note> of no small or contemptible teaching. Therefore, I thought it good and necessary to add some diligence and labor of my own to translate this book. With much wakefulness and learning over a span of time, I brought this book to completion to give it to those who wish to set their minds to it and learn how they ought to form their character—those who have proposed to live their lives according to the Law of the Lord.

<summary>This page contains the translator's prologue to the Book of Ecclesiasticus, where the author's grandson explains his motivations for translating the work from Hebrew into Greek for the Jewish community in Egypt.</summary>
<keywords>Ecclesiasticus, Sirach, Prologue, translation, Hebrew, Egypt, Ptolemy Euergetes, Wisdom, Law of the Lord</keywords>

## CHAPTER ONE.

*Incomprehensible wisdom, which shines through all created things, flows from an eternal origin from God Almighty alone; He gives it to those who love and revere Him. For the fear of the Lord, which is praised here in many ways, brings not only wisdom but all other virtues; one must approach God with a simple heart.*

<margin>1 Kings 3:9 and 4:9 <note>Original: "3. Reg." (3rd Book of Kings), which in modern Bibles is 1 Kings.</note></margin>
1 All wisdom is from the Lord God, and has always been with Him, and exists before all ages.
2 Who has numbered the sand of the sea, the drops of rain, and the days of time? Who has measured the height of heaven, the breadth of the earth, and the depth of the abyss?
3 Who has searched out the wisdom of God, which precedes all things?
4 Wisdom was created before all things, and the understanding of prudence is from eternity.
5 The source of wisdom is the word of God on high, and its entrance is the eternal commandments.
6 To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed, and who has known its subtle ways?
7 To whom has the discipline of wisdom been revealed and made manifest? And who has understood the many ways of its entrance?
8 There is one most high Creator, the Almighty, a powerful King and one to be greatly feared, sitting upon His throne, the God who rules.
9 He created her <note>In Latin and Greek, "Wisdom" (Sapientia/Sophia) is a feminine noun.</note> in the Holy Spirit; He saw her, numbered her, and measured her.
10 And He poured her out upon all His works, and upon all flesh according to His gift, and has offered her to those who love Him.
11 The fear of the Lord <term>Fear of the Lord: A biblical term for deep, loving reverence and awe toward God, rather than terror.</term> is honor, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of exultation.
12 The fear of the Lord shall delight the heart, and shall give gladness, and joy, and length of days.
13 It shall go well at the last for him who fears the Lord, and he shall be blessed on the day of his death.
14 The love of God is honorable wisdom.
15 To those whom she appears in a vision, they love her by seeing her and by acknowledging her great wonders.
<margin>† Psalm 111:10; Proverbs 1:7 and 9:10 <note>Original: "Psal. 110. 10," following the Vulgate numbering.</note></margin>
16 † The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; it was created with the faithful in the womb, it walks with chosen women, and is recognized among the just and faithful.
17 The fear of the Lord is the religious devotion of knowledge.
18 Religious devotion shall guard and justify the heart; it shall give pleasantness and joy.
19 It shall go well for him who fears the Lord, and he shall be blessed in the days of his fulfillment.
20 To fear God is the fullness of wisdom, and there is fullness from her fruits.
21 She shall fill his whole house with her generations, and the storehouses with her treasures.
22 The fear of the Lord is a crown of wisdom, filling one with peace and the fruit of salvation:
23 He saw her and numbered her; both, however, are gifts of God.

<column-break/>

24 Wisdom will bestow knowledge and the understanding of prudence; she exalts the glory of those who hold onto her.
25 The root of wisdom is to fear the Lord, and her branches are long-lived.
26 In the treasures of wisdom is understanding and the religious devotion of knowledge; but wisdom is an abomination to sinners.
27 The fear of the Lord drives out sin:
28 For he who is without fear cannot be justified, for the anger of his pride is his own downfall.
29 A patient man shall endure until the right time, and afterward joy shall be restored to him.
30 Good sense will hide his words until the right time, and the lips of many shall declare his understanding.
31 In the treasures of wisdom is the significance of discipline:
32 But the worship of God is an abomination to a sinner.
33 My son, if you desire wisdom, maintain justice, and God will provide it to you.
34 For the fear of the Lord is wisdom and discipline; and what is well-pleasing to Him is
35 Faith and gentleness; and He will fill his treasures.
36 Do not be distrustful of the fear of the Lord, and do not approach Him with a double heart.
37 Do not be a hypocrite in the sight of men, and do not let your own lips be a cause of stumbling.
38 Pay attention to these things, lest perhaps you fall and bring dishonor upon your soul,
39 And God reveal your secrets and cast you down in the midst of the assembly <note>Latin: "synagogae," referring to the gathering of the community.</note>,
40 Because you approached the Lord wickedly, and your heart is full of deceit and guile.

## CHAPTER II.

*He who is about to serve God should stand in justice, in the fear of God and in patience; let those who fear God believe and trust in Him, and they will receive the greatest fruits from this. Woe to the unfaithful and the impatient; the effects of divine fear are also explained.*

<margin>Matthew 4:1; 2 Timothy 3:12.</margin>
1 My son, coming to the service of God, stand in justice and fear, and prepare your soul for temptation.
2 Humbly steady your heart and endure; incline your ear and receive words of understanding, and do not be hasty in the time of darkness.
3 Sustain the supports of God; join yourself to God and endure, so that your life may increase in your final days.
4 Accept everything that is applied to you; endure in sorrow, and have patience in your humiliation:
<margin>† Wisdom 3:6.</margin>
5 † For gold and silver are tested in fire, but acceptable men are tested in the furnace of humiliation.
6 Believe in God, and He will recover you; direct your way and hope in Him. Keep His fear, and grow old in it.
7 You who fear the Lord, wait for His mercy; and do not turn away from Him, lest you fall.

*The honor of parents earns a manifold blessing from God, while dishonor brings a curse; modesty of spirit is praised over curiosity, and the hard, wicked, and proud heart is condemned, while the wise man and the one who gives alms are praised.*

### CHAPTER IV.

->*He encourages works of mercy and wisdom in many ways, showing its benefits: the difference between good and bad shame: wisdom must not be hidden, nor the truth contradicted: one must strive for justice: let your actions match your words: be kind toward those under your authority and not greedy.*<-

<margin>Tobit 4:7</margin>
1 My son, do not defraud the poor of their alms, and do not turn your eyes away from the poor.
2 Do not despise a hungry soul, and do not provoke a poor man in his need.
3 Do not afflict the heart of the needy, and do not defer the gift to one who is in distress.
4 Do not reject the petition of the afflicted, and do not turn your face away from the destitute.
5 Do not turn your eyes away from the needy out of anger, and do not give those who seek you a reason to curse you behind your back.
6 For if one curses you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard; for He who made him will hear him.
7 Make yourself affable to the congregation of the poor, humble your soul before an elder, and bow your head to a great man.
8 Bow your ear to the poor without sadness, pay your debt, and answer him with peace and mildness.
9 Deliver him who suffers injury from the hand of the proud, and do not be faint-hearted in your soul when judging.
10 In judging, be merciful to orphans as a father, and as a husband to their mother.
11 And you shall be as an obedient son of the Most High, and He will have mercy on you more than a mother.
12 Wisdom inspires life in her children; she takes up those who seek her and goes before them in the way of justice.
13 And he who loves her, loves life; and those who watch for her shall embrace her delight.
14 Those who hold her fast shall inherit life; and wherever she enters, God will bless.
15 Those who serve her shall be obedient to the Holy One; and those who love her, God loves.
16 He who hears her shall judge the nations; and he who gazes upon her shall remain confident.
17 If he trusts her, he shall inherit her, and his offspring shall be established <note>Original: "in confirmatione creaturae illius." This implies that the benefits of wisdom are passed down through generations.</note>.
18 For she walks with him in temptation, and at first she chooses him.
19 She will bring fear and dread and trial upon him; and she will torment him with the tribulation of her teaching, until she tests him in his thoughts and can trust his soul.
20 Then she will strengthen him, and lead him on a straight path, and make him glad.
21 She will reveal her secrets to him, and heap upon him knowledge and the understanding of justice.
22 But if he goes astray, she will forsake him and deliver him into the hands of his enemy.
23 Son, observe the time and avoid evil.
24 For the sake of your soul, do not be ashamed to speak the truth.
25 For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that brings glory and grace.
26 Do not accept a person's favor against your own soul <note>Meaning: do not show partiality or yield to peer pressure if it harms your integrity.</note>, nor tell a lie against your soul.
27 Do not show undue respect to your neighbor in his fall,

<column-break/>

28 Nor withhold a word in a time of salvation. Do not hide your wisdom in its beauty.
29 For wisdom is discerned by the tongue; and sense, and knowledge, and teaching by the word of the wise, and steadfastness in the works of justice.
30 In no way contradict the word of truth, and be ashamed of the lie of your ignorance.
31 Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not subject yourself to every man for the sake of sin.
32 Do not resist the face of the powerful, nor strive against the current of a river.
33 For the sake of justice, struggle for your soul; and even unto death, fight for justice, and God will defeat your enemies for you.
34 Do not be hasty with your tongue, nor useless and slack in your works.
35 Do not be like a lion in your own house, terrifying those of your household and oppressing those subject to you.
36 Let not your hand be stretched out to receive, but closed when it comes to giving.

---

### CHAPTER V.

->*One must not persist in sin because of confidence in riches, youth, strength, or the mercy of the Lord: do not be wavering, but firm and gentle in the way of the Lord, and sensible in words: do not be a gossip or double-tongued.*<-

1 Do not rely on unjust possessions, and do not say: "I have enough for my life"; for it shall be of no use in the time of vengeance and darkness.
2 Do not follow the desires of your heart in your strength.
3 And do not say: "How was I able?" or "Who will subject me because of my deeds?" For God will surely take vengeance.
4 Do not say: "I have sinned, and what grief has befallen me?" For the Most High is a patient rewarder.
5 Concerning a sin that has been forgiven, do not be without fear, nor add sin upon sin.
6 And do not say: "The mercy of the Lord is great; He will have mercy on the multitude of my sins."
<margin>† Proverbs 10:6</margin>
7 For mercy and wrath come quickly from Him, and His wrath looks upon sinners.
8 Do not delay to be converted to the Lord, and do not put it off from day to day.
9 For His wrath shall come suddenly, and in the time of vengeance He will destroy you.
<margin>† Proverbs 11:4, 28</margin>
10 Do not be anxious for unjust riches; for they shall not profit you in the day of darkness and vengeance.
11 Do not winnow in every wind <note>A metaphor for being inconsistent or following every popular opinion.</note>, and do not go into every way; for so is every sinner proven by a double tongue.
12 Be steadfast in the way of the Lord, and in the truth of your understanding and knowledge, and let the word of peace and justice follow you.
13 Be mild in hearing the word, so that you may understand; and with wisdom offer a true answer.
14 If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, let your hand be over your mouth, lest you be caught in an undisciplined word and be put to shame.
15 Honor and glory are in the speech of the sensible man, but the tongue of the imprudent is his own ruin.
16 Do not be called a whisperer <note>A gossip or slanderer.</note>, and do not be caught by your own tongue and put to shame.
17 For shame and repentance are upon the thief,

### CHAPTER VI.

*Reproach, envy, and ferocity push away the love of one's neighbor; sweetness in words and peaceful conduct help it. Friends are many, but a true friend cannot be valued enough. How wisdom is to be loved and kept; the company of the prudent must be sought, and God’s commands observed.*

Do not become an enemy to your neighbor instead of a friend; for the wicked man shall inherit reproach and contumely, as will every sinner who is envious and double-tongued.
<margin>† Romans 12:16; Philippians 2:3.</margin>
2 † Do not extol yourself in the thoughts of your soul like a bull, lest perhaps your strength be shattered through folly,
3 and it eat up your leaves, and destroy your fruit, and you be left like a dry tree in the wilderness.
4 For a wicked soul shall destroy the one who possesses it, makes him a joy to his enemies, and shall lead him into the lot of the impious.
5 A sweet word multiplies friends and appeases enemies, and an agreeable tongue <note>original: "lingua eucharis" — a gracious or pleasant way of speaking</note> abounds in a good man.
6 Let many be at peace with you, but let your counselor be one among a thousand.
7 If you would gain a friend, test him before you take him, and do not be quick to trust him.
8 For there is a friend according to his own occasion, and he will not stay in the day of your trouble.
9 And there is a friend who turns to enmity, and there is a friend who will disclose hatred, strife, and insults.
10 There is also a friend who is a companion at the table, but he will not remain in the day of necessity.
11 If a friend remains steadfast, he will be as your equal and will act with confidence among your household.
12 If he humbles himself before you and hides himself from your face, you will have a good and harmonious friendship.
13 Separate yourself from your enemies, and take heed of your friends.
14 A faithful friend is a strong protection, and he who has found one has found a treasure.
15 Nothing can be compared to a faithful friend, and no weight of gold or silver is worth more than the goodness of his fidelity.
16 A faithful friend is the medicine of life and immortality; and those who fear the Lord shall find him.
17 He who fears God shall have a good friendship likewise, because his friend shall be like him.
18 My son, receive instruction from your youth, and you shall find wisdom even until your grey hairs.
19 Come to her like one who plows and sows, and wait for her good fruits.
20 For in working for her, you shall labor but a little, and shall soon eat of her produce.
21 How very harsh wisdom is to unlearned men! The senseless man will not remain with her.
22 She will be like a heavy stone of trial upon them, and they will not delay to cast her away.
23 For the wisdom of doctrine is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many; but to those by whom she is known, she remains even until they see God. <note>original: "Sapientia enim doctrinæ secundum nomen est ejus" — This refers to a linguistic play on the word Wisdom (Sophia) appearing similar to "hidden" or "disciplined" in the original languages.</note>

<column-break/>

24 Listen, my son, and receive the counsel of understanding, and do not reject my advice.
25 Put your feet into her fetters, and your neck into her chains.
26 Bow your shoulder and carry her, and do not be grieved by her bonds.
27 Come to her with all your mind, and keep her ways with all your strength.
28 Search for her, and she shall be made known to you; and when you have attained her, do not let her go.
29 For in the end, you shall find rest in her, and she shall turn into your delight.
30 Then her fetters shall be a strong protection for you, and her chains a robe of glory.
31 For the beauty of life is in her, and her bonds are a saving bandage.
32 You shall put her on as a robe of glory, and set her upon you as a crown of joy.
33 My son, if you pay attention to me, you shall learn; and if you apply your mind, you shall be wise.
34 If you incline your ear, you shall receive instruction; and if you love to listen, you shall be wise.
<margin>† Below, 8:9.</margin>
35 † Stand in the company of prudent elders, and join yourself to their wisdom from your heart, so that you may hear every discourse about God, and that the proverbs of praise do not escape you.
36 And if you see a man of understanding, go to him early, and let your foot wear out the steps of his doors.
<margin>† Psalm 1:2.</margin>
37 † Keep your thoughts on the precepts of God, and be most constant in His commandments; and He will give you a heart, and the desire for wisdom shall be given to you.

### CHAPTER VII.

*Abstaining from evil: ambition, presumption, faint-heartedness, lying, wordiness before elders, and presumption in offerings are forbidden. Praise for agriculture, a good wife, and a useful servant. Parents should educate sons and marry off daughters; children should honor parents. God and His priests are to be honored; an exhortation to works of mercy and remembering the end.*

Do no evil, and no evil shall take hold of you.
2 Depart from the wicked, and evils shall depart from you.
3 My son, do not sow evils in the furrows of injustice, and you shall not reap them sevenfold.
4 Do not seek leadership from the Lord, nor the seat of honor from the king.
<margin>† Job 9:2, 20; Psalm 142:2; Ecclesiastes 7:17; Luke 18:11.</margin>
5 † Do not justify yourself before God, for He is the knower of the heart; and do not seek to appear wise before the king.
6 Do not seek to be made a judge unless you have the strength to break through iniquities; lest perhaps you fear the face of the powerful, and create a scandal against your own integrity.
7 Do not sin against the city's populace, nor cast yourself among the people.
<margin>† Below, 12:7.</margin>
8 † Do not bind sins together twofold; for even in one, you shall not go unpunished.
9 Do not be faint-hearted in your soul;
10 Do not neglect to pray and to give alms.
11 Do not say: "God will look upon the multitude of my gifts, and when I offer them to the Most High God, He will accept them."

12 Do not mock a man in the bitterness of his soul: † for there is one who humbles and exalts, God the overseer.

14 Do not desire to tell any lie; for the habit of lying is not good.

24 Do you have livestock? Look after them; and if they are useful, let them remain with you.

30 Remember that you would not have been born but for them; and repay them as they have done for you.

32 With all your strength love Him who made you, and do not abandon His ministers.

35 You shall offer the gift of the arms and the sacrifice of sanctification to the Lord, and the first fruits of the holy things:

36 And stretch out your hand to the poor, so that your atonement and blessing may be perfected.

37 Let the grace of a gift be in the sight of all the living, and do not withhold grace from the dead <note>Likely referring to the duty of providing proper burials and remembering the deceased.</note>.

### CHAPTER VIII.

->*One must not contend with the powerful, the wealthy, the talkative, or the unlearned; the repentant and the old should not be despised: do not rejoice over a dead enemy: elders must be heard, and sinners and the insolent rebuked: lending: standing surety: against a judge: with the bold: with the angry: with fools: with a stranger.*<-

Do not argue with a powerful man, lest you fall into his hands.

<margin>† Matthew 25:25.</margin>
2 † Do not contend with a wealthy man, lest he bring a lawsuit against you.

<margin>† Below 31:6.</margin>
3 † For gold and silver have destroyed many, and have reached even to the hearts of kings and turned them.

4 Do not argue with a talkative man, and do not heap wood upon his fire.

5 Do not associate with an unlearned man, lest he speak ill of your lineage.

<margin>† 2 Corinthians 2:6.</margin>
6 Do not despise a man turning himself away from sin, † nor reproach him: remember that we are all under correction.

<margin>† Galatians 6:1; Leviticus 19:32.</margin>
7 † Do not despise a man in his old age: for some of us are growing old.

8 Do not rejoice over your dead enemy: knowing that we all die, and we do not wish others to rejoice <note>The Latin implies we would not want others to take pleasure in our own deaths.</note>.

<margin>† Above 6:35.</margin>
9 † Do not despise the discourse of wise elders, and occupy yourself with their proverbs.

10 For from them you shall learn wisdom and the doctrine of understanding, and how to serve great men without complaint.

11 Do not let the discourse of the elders pass you by; for they themselves learned from their fathers:

12 Because from them you will learn understanding, and how to give an answer in the time of necessity.

13 Do not kindle the coals of sinners by rebuking them, lest you be burned by the flame of the fire of their sins.

14 Do not stand before the face of an insolent man, lest he sit like an ambush for your mouth <note>Meaning he may twist your words to trap you.</note>.

<margin>† Below 29:4.</margin>
15 † Do not lend money to a man more powerful than you; and if you do lend, consider it as lost.

16 Do not stand surety <note>To "stand surety" means to guarantee someone else's debt or legal obligation.</note> beyond your means; and if you do, think of it as if you must pay.

17 Do not judge against a judge; for he judges according to what is just.

<margin>† Genesis 4:8.</margin>
18 † Do not travel on the road with a bold man, lest he burden you with his evils; for he goes according to his own will, and you will perish along with his folly.

<margin>† Proverbs 22:24.</margin>
19 † Do not start a quarrel with an angry man, and do not go into the desert with a bold man: for blood is as nothing before him, and where there is no help, he will strike you down.

20 Do not take counsel with fools; for they cannot love anything except what pleases them.

21 Do not take counsel before a stranger; for you do not know what he will bring forth.

22 Do not reveal your heart to every man, lest he offer you false favor and then insult you.

### C H A P T E R IX.

*How one must act prudently with women, and how their company and affection is dangerous for men: an old friend must be kept: the glory of a sinner is not to be envied: one should keep away from a man who has the power to kill: one should deal with the wise, and keep God before one's eyes.*

1 **Do not** be jealous of the wife of your bosom <note>original: "sinus tui" — literally "of your fold" or "of your breast," a poetic term for a spouse</note>, lest she show against you the malice of a wicked lesson.
2 Do not give a woman power over your soul, lest she enter into your strength and you be put to shame.
3 Do not look upon a woman of many desires <note>original: "multivolam" — referring to a woman who is promiscuous or fickle</note>, lest perhaps you fall into her snares.
4 Do not be constant with a female dancer, nor listen to her, lest perhaps you perish in her influence.
<margin>† Genesis 34:2.</margin>
5 Do not gaze at a young girl, lest perhaps you be tripped up by her beauty.
<margin>† Proverbs 5:3.</margin>
6 Do not give your soul to harlots in any matter, lest you destroy yourself and your inheritance.
7 Do not look around in the streets of the city, nor wander about in its squares.
<margin>† Genesis 34:2 & 13:1.</margin>
8 Turn away your face from an adorned woman, and do not gaze at the beauty of another.
<margin>† 2 Samuel 11:4.</margin>
9 Because of the beauty of a woman many have perished: and from this, desire is kindled like a fire.
<margin>† Matthew 5:28.</margin>
10 Every woman who is a harlot shall be trodden underfoot like dung in the way.
11 Many, having admired the beauty of another man's wife, have become outcasts; for her conversation burns like fire.
12 Do not sit at all with another man’s wife, nor lie down with her upon the elbow <note>This refers to the ancient custom of reclining at tables during meals.</note>:
13 And do not argue with her over wine, lest perhaps your heart turn toward her, and by your blood you slip into destruction.
14 Do not forsake an old friend: for a new one will not be like him.
15 A new friend is like new wine: it will grow old, and then you shall drink it with sweetness.
<margin>† Judges 9:4. 2 Samuel 15:10.</margin>
16 Do not envy the glory and riches of a sinner: for you do not know what his ruin shall be.
17 Let the injury of the unjust not please you, knowing that the impious man shall not please even down to the depths of hell.
18 Keep far from a man who has the power to kill, and you will not suspect the fear of death.
19 And if you approach him, do not commit any fault, lest perhaps he take away your life.
20 Know that it is a sharing in death: for you will walk in the midst of snares, and walk upon the weapons of those who grieve.
21 According to your ability, guard yourself from your neighbor, and treat with the wise and the prudent.
22 Let just men be your guests, and let your glory be in the fear of God.
23 And let the thought of God be in your mind, and let all your discourse be on the precepts of the Most High.
24 The work of craftsmen shall be praised for their hand, and the prince of the people for the wisdom of his speech, but the word of the elders for their sense.
25 A talkative man is a terror in his city: and he who is reckless in his speech shall be hated.

<column-break/>

### C H A P T E R X.

*A wise judge is useful: a foolish one is ruinous: subjects imitate their ruler: everything is in the hand of God: injuries are to be forgotten: the detestation of pride, injustice, insult, and greed: man's life is short and after death he is a worm: departure from God is the cause of pride: nations destroyed by God because of pride: praise of the fear of God: a just poor man is not to be despised, nor a sinful rich man honored: the soul is to be kept in meekness.*

1 **A wise** judge shall judge his people, and the government of a sensible man shall be stable.
<margin>† Proverbs 29:12.</margin>
2 As the judge of the people is, so are his ministers: and what kind of man the ruler of the city is, such also are those who dwell in it.
<margin>† 1 Kings 12:13.</margin>
3 A foolish king shall destroy his people: and cities shall be inhabited through the sense of the powerful.
4 The power of the earth is in the hand of God: and in due time he will raise up a useful ruler over it.
5 The prosperity of man is in the hand of God, and he will place his honor upon the face of the scribe.
6 Do not remember every injury of your neighbor, and do nothing through injurious deeds.
<margin>† Leviticus 19:13.</margin>
7 Pride is hateful before God and men: and all iniquity of the nations is execrable.
<margin>† Daniel 4:14.</margin>
8 Sovereignty is transferred from nation to nation because of injustices, and injuries, and insults, and various deceits.
9 But nothing is more wicked than a greedy man. Why are earth and ashes proud? <note>original: "terra & cinis" — a humble reminder of human mortality and origins.</note>
10 Nothing is more iniquitous than to love money: for such a one even has his own soul for sale: because in his life he has cast away his inner parts.
11 All power is a short life. A long illness burdens the doctor.
12 The doctor cuts short a brief illness: so also a king is here today, and tomorrow he shall die.
13 For when a man dies, he shall inherit serpents, and beasts, and worms.
14 The beginning of human pride is to fall away from God:
15 Because his heart has departed from him who made him: for pride is the beginning of all sin; he who holds to it shall be filled with maledictions, and it shall ruin him in the end.
16 Therefore the Lord has disgraced the assemblies of the wicked, and has destroyed them even to the end.
17 God has destroyed the seats of proud leaders, and has made the mild sit in their place.
18 God has dried up the roots of proud nations, and planted the humble from among those very nations.
19 The Lord has overturned the lands of the nations, and destroyed them down to the foundation.
20 He has withered them, and dispersed them, and made the memory of them to cease from the earth.
21 God has destroyed the memory of the proud, and left the memory of those humble in mind.
22 Pride was not created for men; nor was wrathful anger for the race of women.
23 This seed of men shall be honored, which fears God: but that seed shall be dishonored, which passes over the commandments of the Lord.
24 In the midst of brothers, their ruler is in honor: and those who fear the Lord shall be in his eyes.
25 The glory of the rich, of the honored, and of the poor, is the fear of God:

27 The great man, the judge, and the powerful are in honor: yet none is greater than he who fears God.
<margin>† Proverbs 17:2</margin> 28 Free men shall serve a sensible servant: and a wise and disciplined man will not murmur when corrected, and the ignorant man will not be honored.

## CHAPTER XI.

->*The wisdom of the humble; no one should be judged by appearance; one should not boast of clothing and honor; one should not question a matter before judgment; temporal things should not be accumulated, nor should one trust or boast in them; good and evil come from God; be mindful of good and evil; not everyone should be invited into the house, and one must beware of the snares of the deceitful.*<-

<margin>Genesis 41:40; Daniel 6:3; John 7:18</margin> 1 The wisdom of the humble man shall lift up his head, and shall make him sit in the midst of great men.
2 Do not praise a man for his beauty, nor despise a man for his appearance.
3 The bee is small among flying things, yet its fruit holds the beginning of sweetness.
<margin>† Matthew 12:21, 12</margin> 4 † Never boast in your clothing, nor be extolled in the day of your honor: for the works of the Most High alone are wonderful—His works are glorious, hidden, and unseen.
5 Many tyrants have sat upon a throne, and the one never suspected has worn the crown.
<margin>† 1 Samuel 15:28; Esther 6:7</margin> 6 † Many powerful men have been greatly oppressed, and the glorious have been delivered into the hands of others.
7 Before you inquire, do not blame anyone; and when you have inquired, rebuke justly.
<margin>† Proverbs 18:13</margin> 8 † Before you hear, do not answer a word: and in the midst of speeches, do not interrupt.
9 Do not strive in a matter that does not trouble you: and do not sit in judgment with sinners.
<margin>1 Timothy 6:9</margin> 10 My son, let your actions not be concerned with too many things: for if you are rich, you will not be free from fault. If you pursue them, you will not overtake them; and you will not escape if you run ahead.
<margin>† Ecclesiastes 4:8</margin> 11 † There is a man who labors, hastens, and grieves as an impious man, and all the more he shall not abound.
12 There is a man who is withered and needs recovery, lacking in strength and abounding in poverty:
<margin>† Job 2:10</margin> 13 And † the eye of God looked upon him for good, and raised him up from his lowliness, and lifted up his head: and many wondered at him, and honored God.
<margin>† Job 1:10</margin> 14 † Good and evil, life and death, poverty and wealth <note>original: "honestas" — in this context, it refers to social standing or respectability derived from prosperity</note> are from God.
15 Wisdom, discipline, and the knowledge of the law are with God. Love and the ways of the good are with Him.

<column-break/>

16 Error and darkness were created together with sinners: but those who exult in evils grow old in evil.
17 God’s gift remains for the just, and his progress shall have success forever.
18 There is one who grows rich by acting sparingly, and this is the portion of his reward.
<margin>† Luke 12:19</margin> 19 In that he says: † I have found rest for myself, and now I will eat of my goods alone:
20 Yet he does not know that time will pass and death approaches, and he will leave all things to others and die.
21 Stand firm in your covenant <note>original: "testamento" — referring to the religious agreement or the Law of God</note>, and speak of it, and grow old in the work of your commandments.
22 Do not dwell on the works of sinners. But trust in God and stay in your place.
23 For it is easy in the eyes of God to suddenly make the poor man rich.
24 The blessing of God hastens toward the reward of the just, and in a swift hour his progress bears fruit.
25 Do not say: "What do I need, and what good things will I have from this?"
26 Do not say: "I am sufficient for myself; what harm will I suffer after this?"
<margin>† Below 18:25</margin> 27 † In the day of good things, do not be unmindful of evils: and in the day of evils, do not be unmindful of good things:
28 Since it is easy before God on the day of death to repay each one according to his ways.
29 The malice of an hour makes one forget great luxury, and at the end of a man is the uncovering of his works.
30 Praise no man before his death, for a man is known through his children.
31 Do not bring every man into your house: for many are the snares of the deceitful man.
32 For as the hearts of those who stink belch out, and as a partridge is led into a cage, and as a deer into a snare: so also is the heart of the proud, and like a scout watching for the fall of his neighbor.
33 For turning good into evil, he lies in wait, and he will place a stain upon the chosen.
34 From a single spark a fire is increased, and from one deceitful man blood is increased: for the sinful man lies in wait for blood.
35 Watch yourself against a pestilent man <note>original: "pestifero" — a man who is morally corrupting or destructive like a plague</note>, for he crafts evils: lest perhaps he bring upon you eternal mockery.
36 Admit a stranger into your house, and he will subvert you in a whirlwind, and estrange you from your own people.

## CHAPTER XII.

->*Good must be done to the just: but the impious and sinners are not to be received: it is difficult to distinguish friends from enemies, nor should enemies ever be trusted, no matter how much they pretend friendship.*<-

1 If you do good, know to whom you do it, and there will be much gratitude for your good deeds.
2 Do good to the just man, and you will find a great reward: and if not from him, certainly from the Lord.
3 For it is not well for him who is constant in evils, nor for him who gives no alms: for the Most High also hates sinners, and has shown mercy to those who repent.
<margin>† Galatians 6:10</margin> 4 † Give to the merciful, and do not receive the sinner: and He will return vengeance to the impious and sinners, keeping them for the day of vengeance.
5 Give to the good, and do not receive the sinner.
6 Do good to the humble, and do not give to the impious: forbid that bread be given to him, lest in those things he become more powerful than you:

7 For you will find double the evil in all the good you do for him: because the Most High also hates sinners and will take vengeance on the ungodly.
8 A friend is not recognized in good times, and an enemy is not hidden in bad times.
9 When a man is in good circumstances, his enemies are in sorrow; but in his misfortune, even a friend is recognized <note>Meaning a "fair-weather" friend reveals their true nature by leaving during hard times.</note>.
10 Do not trust your enemy forever; for just as copper rusts, so does his wickedness.
11 And even if he goes about bowed down and humbled, apply your mind and guard yourself against him.
12 Do not place him near you, nor let him sit at your right hand, lest perhaps he turn into your place and seek your chair <note>original: "cathedram" — referring to a seat of authority or honor</note>; and at the end you will recognize my words, and be pricked by my sayings.
13 Who will have pity on a snake charmer bitten by a serpent, or on any who approach wild beasts? So it is with one who associates with a wicked man and is entangled in his sins.
14 He will stay with you for one hour; but if you turn aside, he will not endure it.
15 <margin>† Jeremiah 41:6</margin> † The enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he plots to subvert you into a pit.
16 The enemy cries with his eyes, but if he finds an opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.
17 And if evils befall you, you will find him there before you.
18 The enemy cries with his eyes, and pretending to help, he will undermine your heels.
19 He will shake his head and clap his hands, and whispering many things, he will change his expression.

### CHAPTER XIII.

->*It is dangerous to associate with the proud, the rich, and the powerful: love God and your neighbor: the rich man does not fit with the poor man, and while the latter is despised, the former is honored.*<-

1 <margin>† Above 7:2</margin> Whoever touches pitch <note>original: "picem" — a sticky, black resin; the proverb means that associating with bad influences inevitably stains one's character.</note> shall be defiled by it: † and he who communicates with the proud shall put on pride.
2 He who communicates with one more honorable than himself takes a weight upon himself. Do not become a partner to one richer than yourself.
3 What does a kettle have in common with an earthenware pot? For when they collide, the pot will be broken.
4 The rich man has done wrong and rages; but the poor man, though harmed, remains silent.
5 If you give generously, he will accept you; but if you have nothing, he will abandon you.
6 If you have property, he will live with you and empty you out, and he himself will not grieve for you.
7 If you are necessary to him, he will trick you; smiling, he will give you hope, telling you good things and saying, "What do you need?"
8 And he will shame you with his feasts until he drains you twice or thrice; and at the last, he will mock you. Later, seeing you, he will abandon you and shake his head at you.
9 Humble yourself before God, and wait for His hands.
10 Take care that you are not seduced into folly and humbled.
11 Do not be humble in your wisdom, lest being humbled, you be seduced into folly.
12 When invited by a more powerful man, withdraw; for by this, he will invite you all the more.
13 Do not be pushy, lest you be pushed back; and do not be too far from him, lest you be forgotten.

<column-break/>

14 Do not pretend to speak with him as an equal, nor believe his many words: for with much talk he will test you, and smiling, he will question you about your secrets.
15 His cruel mind will store up your words; and he will not spare you from malice or chains.
16 Beware for yourself, and attend diligently to what you hear: for you walk with your own ruin.
17 Hearing these things, look at them as if in a dream, and you will stay awake.
18 Love God throughout all your life, and call upon Him for your salvation.
19 Every animal loves its own kind; so also every man loves his neighbor.
20 All flesh shall be joined to its own kind, and every man shall associate with his peer.
21 As a wolf will never associate with a lamb, so a sinner will not with the just.
22 <margin>† 2 Corinthians 6:14</margin> † What fellowship has a holy man with a dog? Or what part has a rich man with the poor?
23 The wild donkey <note>original: "onager" — a wild ass of central Asia, used here as a symbol of prey</note> in the desert is the lion's prey; so also the poor are the pastures of the rich.
24 And just as humility is an abomination to the proud, so is the poor man an object of loathing to the rich.
25 When a rich man is shaken, he is supported by his friends; but when the humble man falls, he is driven away even by those he knows.
26 When a rich man is deceived, many come to his rescue; he has spoken proudly, and they justified him.
27 The humble man is deceived, and moreover, he is rebuked; he spoke sensibly, and no place was given to him.
28 The rich man spoke, and everyone was silent, and they carry his word up to the clouds.
29 The poor man spoke, and they say: "Who is this?" and if he stumbles, they will overthrow him.
30 Wealth is good if there is no sin in the conscience: and poverty is most wicked in the mouth of the ungodly.
31 The heart of a man changes his face, whether for good or for evil.
32 The sign of a good heart and a happy face is found only with difficulty and with labor.

### CHAPTER XIV.

->*Blessed is he who has not slipped in word: riches are destructive to the greedy and the envious, and both suffer misery: one must do good with wealth before death, which does not tarry: on the frailty of man: blessed is he who studies wisdom and justice.*<-

1 <margin>Below 19:17</margin> Blessed is the man who has not slipped by a word from his mouth, and is not stung with the sorrow of sin.
2 Happy is he who has not had sadness of mind, and has not fallen from his hope.
3 For a greedy and stingy man, wealth is without reason, and for an envious man, what use is gold?
4 He who gathers unjustly from his own soul gathers for others, and another will live luxuriously upon his goods.
5 He who is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? And he shall not take joy in his own goods.
6 There is nothing more wicked than one who envies himself, and this is the reward of his malice.
7 And if he does good, he does it ignorantly and unwillingly; and in the end, he reveals his malice.
8 The eye of the envious man is wicked; turning away his face, and despising his own soul.
9 The eye of the greedy man is insatiable in his portion of iniquity; he will not be satisfied until he consumes his own soul, drying it up.

### CHAPTER XVI.

->One should not rejoice in wicked children: concerning the wrath of God against the evil and His mercy toward the good: great are the merits of works of mercy: no one can hide himself from the knowledge and judgment of God, whose works are unsearchable by man.<-

**D**o not rejoice in wicked children, if they be multiplied: nor take delight in them, if the fear of God is not in them.

3 For one who fears God is better than a thousand wicked children.
4 And it is better to die without children than to leave behind wicked children.
5 By one sensible man a country shall be inhabited, but by three wicked men it shall be made a wilderness.
6 My eye has seen many such things, and my ear has heard even stronger things than these.

12 For mercy and wrath are with Him. He is powerful in forgiveness, and in pouring out wrath.
13 As His mercy is, so is His correction: He judges a man according to his works.

*The creation of our first parents, the gifts bestowed upon them and the commands proposed to them: the distinction of the human race into various nations, over which he placed rulers, and how he perpetually watches them and all their works: the virtue of almsgiving: he exhorts sinners to repentance while they are healthy, setting forth the mercy of God.*

### CHAPTER XVIII.

->*The great works of God are inscrutable to man: the misery of man, and God’s mercy toward him: one must have mercy on one’s neighbor: how the weak should behave: how one ought to pray: God’s judgment must be considered, and one must turn away from one’s own lusts:*<-

<margin>Genesis 1:1.</margin>
1 He who lives forever created all things at once <note>The Latin "simul" suggests God created the universe as a whole, rather than in disjointed parts.</note>. God alone shall be justified, and he remains an invincible king forever.
2 Who is capable of recounting his works?
3 For who shall search out his <term>magnalia</term> <note>original: "magnalia"—meaning great or mighty works that display divine power.</note>?
4 Who shall declare the power of his greatness? Or who shall set out to recount his mercy?
5 It is not possible to diminish or to add, nor is it possible to find the great works of God.
6 When a man has finished, then he shall begin; and when he rests, he shall be at a loss.
7 What is man, and what is his grace? And what is his good, or what is his evil?
<margin>† Psalm 89:10.</margin>
8 † The number of the days of men is at most a hundred years; they are accounted as a drop of water from the sea, and as a pebble of sand, so are these few years in the day of eternity.
9 Because of this, God is patient with them, and pours out his mercy upon them.
10 He saw the presumption of their heart, that it is evil, and he knew their ruin, that it is wicked.
11 Therefore he fulfilled his atonement in them, and showed them the way of equity.
12 The compassion of a man is toward his neighbor, but the mercy of God is upon all flesh.
13 He who has mercy teaches and instructs, like a shepherd with his flock.
14 He has mercy on the one who receives the doctrine of compassion, and on the one who hastens in his judgments.
15 My son, in your good deeds give no complaint, and in every gift do not give the sadness of an evil word.
16 Shall not the dew cool the heat? So also a good word is better than a gift.
17 Behold, is not a word better than a good gift? But both are found with a justified man.
18 A fool will reproach bitterly; and a gift from the undisciplined makes the eyes waste away.
19 Before judgment, prepare justice for yourself; and before you speak, learn.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 11:28.</margin>
20 Before sickness, apply medicine; and † before judgment, examine yourself, and in the sight of God you shall find atonement.
21 Before sickness, humble yourself; and in the time of infirmity, show your way of life.
<margin>† Luke 18:1; 1 Thessalonians 5:17.</margin>
22 † Do not be hindered from praying always, and do not fear to be justified even until death; for the reward of God remains forever.

<margin>† Above, 11:27.</margin>

26 From morning until evening the time shall be changed, and all these things are swift in the eyes of God.
27 A wise man will fear in all things, and in the days of sin he will guard against sluggishness.
28 Every shrewd person recognizes wisdom, and will give praise to the one who finds her.
29 Those who are sensible in their words have also acted

32 Do not take pleasure in crowds, not even in small ones; for their gathering is constant.
33 Do not be reduced to nothing by struggling to pay interest when you have nothing in your purse; for you will be a hater of your own life.

### CHAPTER XIX.

->*Concerning wine, luxury, talkativeness, one who believes too quickly, one who rejoices over iniquity, one who hates correction, one who exults in malice, the discretion to be kept in words, correction, feigned humility, and the praise of the one who remains silent.*<-

1 A drunken worker will not grow rich; and he who neglects small things will fall little by little.
<margin>† Genesis 19:33; 3 Kings 11:1.</margin>
2 † Wine and women make wise men fall away, and they shall rebuke the sensible.
3 And he who joins himself to harlots will be wicked; rottenness and worms shall inherit him, and he shall be held up as a greater example, and his soul shall be taken out of the number.
<margin>† Joshua 9:15 and 22:11.</margin>
4 † He who believes quickly is light of heart and shall be diminished; and he who sins against his own soul shall be held as nothing.
5 He who rejoices in iniquity shall be branded; and he who hates correction, his life shall be shortened; and he who hates talkativeness extinguishes malice.
6 He who sins against his own soul shall repent; and he who delights in malice shall be branded.
7 Do not repeat a wicked and harsh word, and you shall not be diminished.
8 Do not tell your mind to friend or enemy; and if you have a fault, do not reveal it.
9 For he will hear you and watch you, and as if defending your sin, he will hate you, and thus he will always be against you.
10 Have you heard a word against your neighbor? Let it die within you, trusting that it will not burst you <note>This is a vivid metaphor for keeping a secret; the word will not cause you to explode if you keep it inside.</note>.
11 At the presence of a word, a fool is in labor, like the groaning of a woman giving birth to a child.
12 As an arrow fixed in the flesh of a thigh, so is a word in the heart of a fool.
<margin>† Leviticus 19:17; Matthew 18:15; Luke 17:3.</margin>
13 † Rebuke a friend, lest perhaps he did not understand, and may say: "I did not do it"; or if he did it, that he may not do it again.
14 Rebuke a neighbor, lest perhaps he did not say it; and if he did say it, lest perhaps he repeat it.
15 Rebuke a friend; for often a fault is committed.
16 And do not believe every word; there is one who slips with the tongue, but not from the heart.
<margin>† James 3:8.</margin>
17 † For who is there that has not offended with his tongue? Rebuke your neighbor before you threaten him.
18 And give place to the fear of the Most High: because all wisdom is the fear of God, and in it is the fear of God, and in all wisdom is the fulfillment of the law.
19 But the instruction of wickedness is not wisdom; and the thinking of sinners is not prudence.
20 There is a wickedness, and in it is an abomination; and there is a fool who is lacking in wisdom.
21 Better is a man who is lacking in wisdom and failing in sense but in fear, than one who abounds in sense and transgresses the law of the Most High.
22 There is a certain cleverness, and it is itself unjust.
23 There is one who utters a sure word... <note>original catchword: "rans"—likely continuing "enarrans" (explaining/narrating) on the next page.</note>

### CHAPTER XX.

*Concerning correction and the repentance of the one corrected; concerning the silent and the talkative; concerning the gifts of the wise and the fool; concerning false promises and lies; concerning the wise man who pleases great men; concerning not accepting gifts, and hidden wisdom.*

1 How much better it is to rebuke than to be angry, and not to prevent him who confesses in prayer!
2 The lust of a eunuch will deflower a young girl— <note>This is a proverbial way of saying that some actions are fundamentally unnatural or impossible, or that a person is attempting something for which they lack the proper capacity.</note>
3 So is he who performs an unjust judgment by force.
4 How good it is for the one corrected to show repentance! For in this way you shall escape voluntary sin.
5 There is one who is silent and is found to be wise; and there is one who is hateful, who is bold in his speaking.
6 There is one who is silent because he has no sense of speech; and there is one who is silent because he knows the proper time.
7 A wise man will hold his peace until the right time, but the wanton and the imprudent will not observe the time.
8 He who uses many words shall hurt his own soul; and he who takes authority to himself unjustly shall be hated.
9 There is success in evil things for an undisciplined man, and there is a discovery that leads to loss.
10 There is a gift that is not profitable, and there is a gift whose reward is double.
11 There is a reduction because of glory, and there is one who shall lift up his head from humility.
12 There is one who buys many things for a small price, yet pays for them sevenfold.
13 A man wise in words makes himself lovable, but the charms of fools shall be wasted.
14 The gift of the foolish will not be profitable to you, for his eyes are sevenfold <note>Meaning he looks for a sevenfold return on his "generosity."</note>.
15 He will give little and upbraid much, and the opening of his mouth is like a fire.
16 A man lends today and asks for it back tomorrow; such a man is hateful.
17 The fool shall have no friend, and there shall be no thanks for his good deeds.
18 For those who eat his bread have false tongues. How often, and how many, shall laugh him to scorn?
19 For he has not distributed what was meant to be held with a right sense, and likewise what was not meant to be held.
20 A slip of a false tongue is like one falling on a pavement; so the fall of the wicked shall come quickly.
21 An ungracious man is like a vain fable; it will be constantly in the mouth of the undisciplined.
22 A proverb shall be rejected from the mouth of a fool, for he does not speak it in its proper time.

<column-break/>

23 There is one who is hindered from sinning because of poverty, and in his rest he shall still be pricked by desire.
24 There is one who will lose his soul through shame, and because of an imprudent person he will lose it; by showing favoritism to persons, he will destroy himself.
25 There is one who, out of shame, makes a promise to a friend, and has gained him as an enemy for no reason.
26 A lie is a wicked reproach in a man, and it will be continually in the mouth of the undisciplined.
27 A thief is better than the persistence of a lying man; yet both shall inherit destruction.
28 The manners of lying men are without honor, and their shame is with them without ceasing.
29 A man wise in words shall advance himself, and a prudent man shall please great men.
30 He who tills his land shall raise a high heap of crops, and he who works justice shall himself be exalted; but he who pleases great men shall escape iniquity.
<margin>† Exodus 23:8. Deuteronomy 16:19.</margin>
31 † Presents and gifts blind the eyes of judges, and like a muzzle on the mouth, they turn away their rebukes.
<margin>† Below 41:17.</margin>
32 † Wisdom that is hidden, and a treasure that is not seen: what profit is there in either of them?
33 Better is he who hides his folly than the man who hides his wisdom.

### CHAPTER XXI.

*Teaches that sin must be fled: first in general, then specifically by listing various sins.*

1 My son, have you sinned? Do so no more; but ask forgiveness for your former sins, that they may be forgiven you.
2 Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent; for if you go near them, they will take hold of you.
3 Its teeth are the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
4 All iniquity is like a two-edged <term>rhomphaia</term> <note>original: "rhomphæa"—a large, heavy sword. This image emphasizes that sin inflicts a deep, wide, and potentially fatal wound.</note>; there is no healing for its wound.
5 Verbal abuse and injuries shall bring wealth to nothing, and the house that is very rich shall be brought to nothing by pride; so the substance of the proud shall be rooted out.
6 The prayer of the poor man goes from his mouth to His ears <note>Meaning God's ears.</note>, and judgment shall come to him speedily.
7 He who hates correction is on the track of the sinner; but he who fears God will turn to his own heart.
8 A man mighty with a bold tongue is known from afar, but a man of sense knows when he himself might slip.
9 He who builds his house with other men’s money is like one who gathers his stones in winter <note>Building stones gathered in winter were often damaged by frost and were prone to cracking, making them a poor foundation.</note>.
<margin>† Above 16:7.</margin>
10 † The assembly of sinners is like tow <note>Tow is the coarse, flammable part of flax.</note> heaped together, and their end is a flame of fire.
11 The way of sinners is paved with stones, but at the end of them are hell, and darkness, and punishments.
12 He who keeps justice shall master his own thoughts.
13 The perfection of the fear of God is wisdom and understanding.
14 He who is not wise in what is good will not be taught.
15 But there is a wisdom which abounds in evil; and there is no true sense where there is bitterness.
