# CHAPTER XXII.

*Concerning the stoning of the lazy, the undisciplined son, and the foolish daughter; music during mourning; teaching a fool; weeping for the dead; not speaking with a fool; concerning the heart of the foolish and the fearful; concerning keeping faith with a friend, and the guarding of the mouth.*

**1** The lazy man <note>original: "piger"</note> is stoned with a dirty stone, and everyone will speak of his disgrace.
**2** The lazy man is stoned with the dung of oxen; and everyone who touches him will shake his hands.
**3** The shame of a father comes from an undisciplined son; and a daughter shall result in loss.
**4** A prudent daughter is an inheritance to her husband; but she who brings shame becomes a disgrace to her parent.
**5** A bold woman shames both father and husband, and she will not be valued less than the impious; she will be dishonored by both.
**6** A story told at the wrong time is like music during mourning; but whips and instruction are wisdom at all times.
**7** He who teaches a fool is like one who glues together a broken pot.
**8** He who tells a story to someone not listening is like one who wakes a sleeper from a deep sleep.
**9** He who speaks wisdom to a fool speaks to one who is asleep; and at the end of the story the fool says: "Who is this?"
<margin>Below 38. 16.</margin>
**10** Weep over the dead, for his light has failed; and weep over the fool, for his sense has failed.

<column-break/>

**11** Weep only a little over the dead, because he has found rest.
**12** For the wicked life of the most wicked is worse than the death of a fool.
<margin>Genesis 50:10.</margin>
**13** Mourning for the dead lasts seven days; but for a fool and the impious, it lasts all the days of their lives.
**14** Do not talk much with a fool, and do not go with the senseless.
**15** Keep yourself from him, so that you do not have trouble, and you will not be defiled by his sin.
**16** Turn away from him, and you will find rest, and you will not be worn out by his folly.
**17** What is heavier than lead? And what is its name other than "fool"?
<margin>Proverbs 27:3.</margin>
**18** It is easier to carry sand, and salt, and a mass of iron than an imprudent man, and a fool, and the impious.
**19** A wooden binding tied into the foundation of a building will not be loosened; so also is a heart established in the thought of counsel.
**20** The thought of the sensible person, at all times, will not be corrupted by fear.
**21** Just as stakes in high places and walls built without mortar set against the wind will not remain;
**22** So also a fearful heart in the thought of a fool will not resist against the force of fear.
**23** Just as a trembling heart in the thought of a fool is always afraid, so is he who remains in the commandments of God always.
**24** Pricking the eye brings out tears; and he who pricks the heart brings forth feeling.
**25** Throwing a stone at birds drives them away; so also he who insults a friend dissolves the friendship.
**26** Even if you have drawn a sword against a friend, do not despair; for there is a way back.
**27** If you have opened a sad mouth <note>Meaning to speak harsh or hurtful words.</note> against a friend, do not fear; for there is reconciliation: except for insults, and reproach, and pride, and revealing a secret, and a treacherous wound; in all these things a friend will flee.
**28** Keep faith with a friend in his poverty, so that you may also rejoice in his prosperity.
**29** In the time of his trouble remain faithful to him, so that you may also be a co-heir in his inheritance.
**30** Before the fire of a furnace there is vapor, and the smoke of the fire rises; so also before blood there are curses, and insults, and threats.
**31** I will not be ashamed to greet a friend, nor will I hide myself from his face: and if evils happen to me through him, I will endure it.
**32** Everyone who hears will beware of him.
<margin>Psalm 140:3.</margin>
**33** Who will set a guard over my mouth, and a sure seal upon my lips, so that I do not fall by them, and my tongue does not destroy me?

### ->CHAPTER XXIV.<-

->*Wisdom describes her manifold praises and origin, and wonderfully invites all to embrace her, illuminating everything with the splendor of her doctrine.*<-

1 Wisdom shall praise her own soul, and shall be honored in God, and shall glory in the midst of her people.
2 And in the assembly of the Most High she shall open her mouth, and shall glory in the sight of His power,
3 And in the midst of her people she shall be exalted, and in the holy fullness she shall be admired,
4 And in the multitude of the elect she shall have praise, and among the blessed she shall be blessed, saying:
5 I came out of the mouth of the Most High, the firstborn before every creature:
6 I made it so that an unfailing light should arise in the heavens, and like a mist I covered all the earth:
7 I dwelt in the highest places, and my throne is in a pillar of cloud.
8 I alone circled the vault of heaven, and penetrated the depth of the abyss; I walked on the waves of the sea,
9 And I stood in every land: and in every people,
10 And in every nation I held the primacy.
11 And by my power I have trodden under foot the hearts of all—the excellent and the humble: and in all these things I sought rest, and I shall dwell in the inheritance of the Lord.
11 <note>The numbering repeats in the original text.</note> Then the Creator of all things commanded and spoke to me: and He who created me rested in my tabernacle,
14 <note>The numbering skips from 11 to 14 in the source.</note> And He said to me: Dwell in Jacob, and let your inheritance be in Israel, and strike roots in my chosen ones <note>original: "delictis meis" — this is likely a printer's error for "electis meis" (my chosen ones).</note>.
<margin>† Proverbs 8:22.</margin>
14 † From the beginning, and before the ages, I was created, and even unto the world to come I shall not cease, and in the holy dwelling I have ministered before Him.
15 And so in Sion I was established, and in the sanctified city I likewise rested, and in Jerusalem is my power.

41 I am like a brook of immense water from a river; I am like the channel of a canal <note>original: "fluvii Diorix"</note>, and like an aqueduct I came out of paradise.
42 I said: I will water my garden of plants, and I will water abundantly the fruits of my meadow.
43 And behold, my brook became abundant, and my river drew near to the sea.
44 For I make doctrine shine like the morning light to all, and I will declare it even to those far off.
45 I will penetrate all the lower parts of the earth, and I will behold all those who sleep, and I will enlighten all who hope in the Lord.
46 I will yet pour out doctrine like prophecy, and leave it to those who seek sa-

<column-break/>

pience, and I shall not cease for their descendants even unto the holy age.
<margin>† Below 33:18.</margin>
47 † See that I have not labored for myself alone, but for all those who seek the truth.

## CHAPTER XXV.

->*Three things that please God, and three that he hates: nine wonderful things: the praise of the fear of God: a striking detestation of a wicked woman: from woman came the beginning of sin and death: the dominion of a woman is not to be endured.*<-

IN three things my spirit is pleased, which are approved before God and men:
2 The concord of brothers, and the love of neighbors, and a man and wife who agree well together.
3 Three sorts of people my soul hates, and I am greatly burdened by their souls:
4 A poor man who is proud: a rich man who is a liar: an old man who is a fool and senseless.
5 If you have not gathered in your youth, how shall you find anything in your old age?
6 How beautiful is judgment in white hair, and for the elderly to know counsel!
7 How beautiful is wisdom for the aged, and understanding and counsel for the honored!
8 The crown of old men is great experience, and their glory is the fear of God.
9 There are nine wonderful things <note>original: "insuspicabilia" — things unexpected or marvelous to the heart</note> of the heart which I have magnified, and a tenth I will tell with my tongue to men:
10 A man who has joy in his children, and who lives to see the downfall of his enemies.
<margin>† Below 26:1.</margin>
11 † Blessed is he who dwells with a sensible woman, † and he who has not slipped with his tongue, and he who has not served those unworthy of himself.
<margin>† Above 14:1 and 19:16. James 3:1.</margin>
12 Blessed is he who finds a true friend, and he who declares justice to an ear that hears.
13 How great is he who finds wisdom and knowledge! But there is none above him who fears the Lord.
14 The fear of God has set itself above all things:
15 Blessed is the man to whom it is given to have the fear of God: he who holds it, to whom shall he be likened?
16 The fear of God is the beginning of his love: and the beginning of faith must be joined to it.
17 All wounds are the sadness of the heart: and all malice is the wickedness of a woman.
18 And one may see every wound, but not a wound of the heart:
19 And every wickedness, but not the wickedness of a woman:
20 And every covering <note>original: "obductum" — likely referring to a veiled threat or a hidden trap</note>, but not the covering of those who hate:
21 And every vengeance, but not the vengeance of enemies.
22 There is no head more wicked than the head of a serpent:
23 And there is no anger above the anger of a woman.
<margin>† Proverbs 21:19.</margin>
† It will be more pleasing to dwell with a lion and a dragon, than to live with a wicked woman.
24 The wickedness of a woman changes her face: and she darkens her countenance like a bear, and shows herself like sackcloth <note>A symbol of mourning or bitterness.</note> in the midst of her neighbors.
25 Her husband groaned, and hearing it, he sighed a little.
26 All malice is short compared to the malice of a woman; let the lot of sinners fall upon her.
27 As the climbing of a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a talkative woman to a quiet man.

### C H A P T E R XXVI.

*In turn, he sets forth the praises of a good woman, and the reproaches of an evil and jealous one; daughters to be guarded; three things to be feared; two things causing grief, and two dangerous things.*

1 **B**lessed is the husband of a good wife: for the number of his years is doubled.
2 A brave woman delights her husband, and he shall fulfill the years of his life in peace.
3 A good wife is a good portion; she shall be given to a man among those who fear God, as a reward for his good deeds.
4 Whether a man be rich or poor, he has a good heart, and at all times his face is cheerful.
5 My heart has been afraid of three things, and at the fourth my face was fearful:
6 The slander of a city, the gathering of a mob,
7 And a lying accusation; all these are more grievous than death.
8 A jealous woman is a sorrow of the heart and a mourning.
9 In a jealous woman is a lash of the tongue, shared with everyone.
10 A wicked woman is like a yoke of oxen that is shaken; he that has hold of her is like one who catches a scorpion.
11 A drunken woman is a cause of great anger; and her disgrace and filthiness shall not be hidden.
12 The fornication of a woman shall be known by the haughtiness of her eyes and by her eyelids.
<margin>† Below, 42:11</margin>
13 Over a daughter who will not turn away from trouble, keep a firm watch; lest, finding an opportunity, she take advantage of herself.
14 Beware of all the irreverence of her eyes, and do not wonder if she neglects you.
15 Like a thirsty traveler, she will open her mouth to the spring and drink of every water near her; she will sit down near every post, and open her quiver to every arrow until she fails.
16 The grace of a diligent woman shall delight her husband, and shall fatten his bones.
17 Her discipline is a gift from God.
18 A sensible and silent woman is a soul beyond price; there is no exchange for a well-instructed soul.
19 Grace upon grace is a holy and modest woman.
20 No weight of gold is worth a soul that practices self-control.
21 Like the sun rising in the world in the highest places of God, so is the beauty of a good woman an ornament to her house.
22 Like a lamp shining upon the holy lampstand, so is the beauty of a face upon a steady age.

<column-break/>

23 Like golden pillars upon silver bases, so are firm feet upon the soles of a stable woman.
24 Eternal foundations upon a solid rock, so are the commandments of God in the heart of a holy woman.
25 My heart is grieved over two things, and at the third, anger comes upon me:
26 A warrior failing because of poverty; a sensible man who is despised;
27 And one who crosses over from righteousness to sin: God has prepared him for the sword <note>original: "rhomphæa" — a large, double-edged sword or divine judgment</note>.
28 Two types of life have appeared difficult and dangerous to me: a merchant is hardly freed from negligence; and a tavern-keeper shall not be justified from the sins of his lips.

### C H A P T E R XXVII.

*Many sin because of poverty and the love of riches: the fear of the Lord is to be kept constantly: temptation tests the one who is tried: justice should be followed: the inconsistency of a fool: modesty should be kept in words: a friend's secrets should not be revealed: concerning the winking eye and the deceitful man.*

1 **B**ecause of poverty many have sinned; and he who seeks to be enriched turns away his eye.
2 As a stake is fixed in the middle of a joint of stones, so also sin shall be narrowed between buying and selling.
3 Guilt shall be crushed together with the sinner.
4 Unless you hold yourself instantly in the fear of the Lord, your house shall quickly be overthrown.
5 As the dust remains when a sieve is shaken, so the deficiency <note>original: "aporia" — a state of difficulty or being at a loss</note> of a man remains in his thought.
6 The furnace tests the potter's vessels, and the trial of tribulation tests just men.
7 As the cultivation of a tree shows its fruit, so the word shows the thought of a man's heart.
8 Do not praise a man before he speaks; for this is the test of men.
9 If you follow justice, you shall grasp it; and you shall put it on like a robe of honor, and you shall dwell with it, and it shall protect you forever; and on the day of recognition, you shall find a firm support.
10 Birds flock to their own kind; and truth shall return to those who practice it.
11 The lion always lies in wait for the hunt; so do sins for those who work iniquity.
12 A holy man remains in wisdom like the sun; but a fool changes like the moon.
13 In the midst of the senseless, keep your word for the right time; but in the midst of the thoughtful, be constant.
14 The storytelling of sinners is hateful, and their laughter is in the pleasures of sin.
15 Speech that swears much makes the hair of the head stand on end, and its irreverence makes one plug their ears.
16 The shedding of blood occurs in the strife of the proud; and their cursing is grievous to hear.
17 He who reveals the secrets of a friend loses his trust, and will not find a friend for his own soul.
18 Love your neighbor, and be joined with him in faith.
19 But if you reveal his secrets, do not follow after him.
20 For as a man who loses his friend, so is he who loses the friendship of his neighbor.

### C H A P T E R XXVIII.

->*Vengeance is not to be sought, but offenses are to be forgiven: one must cease from anger and strife: the evil tongue and its dangers, and concerning the "third tongue": ears should be hedged against a wicked tongue, and a muzzle placed on the mouth.*<-

<margin>Deuteronomy 32:35</margin>
<margin>Matthew 6:14</margin>
<margin>Mark 11:25</margin>
<margin>Romans 12:19</margin>
1 He who wishes to be avenged shall find vengeance from the Lord, and He will surely keep his sins in mind.
2 Forgive your neighbor who harms you: and then when you pray, your sins shall be forgiven.
3 Does a man reserve anger for another man, and yet seek a remedy from God?
4 He has no mercy on a man like himself, and does he entreat for his own sins?
5 Though he is but flesh, he reserves anger, and yet asks for propitiation from God; who will plead for his offenses?
6 Remember your end, and cease from enmity.
7 For decay and death loom over His commandments.
8 Remember the fear of God, and do not be angry with your neighbor.
9 Remember the covenant of the Most High, and overlook the ignorance of your neighbor.
10 Abstain from strife, and you will diminish sins:
11 For a hot-tempered man kindles strife; and a sinful man will trouble his friends, and sow enmity in the midst of those who are at peace.
12 For as the wood of the forest is, so the fire burns; and according to a man's strength, so will his anger be; and according to his wealth, he will lift up his anger.
13 A hasty quarrel kindles a fire; and a hasty strife sheds blood; and a testifying tongue brings death.

<column-break/>

14 If you blow upon a spark, it shall burn like fire; and if you spit upon it, it shall be extinguished: both come out of the mouth.
15 The whisperer and the double-tongued are accursed: for they have troubled many who were at peace.
16 A "third tongue" <note>original: "lingua tertia"; a Hebrew idiom referring to slander or gossip that affects three parties: the speaker, the listener, and the victim</note> has moved many, and dispersed them from nation to nation.
17 It has destroyed the walled cities of the rich, and dug out the houses of great men.
18 It has cut down the strength of peoples, and dissolved strong nations.
19 A third tongue has cast out valiant women, and deprived them of their labors.
20 He who pays attention to it shall have no rest, nor shall he have a friend in whom he may find repose.
21 The blow of a whip creates a bruise; but the blow of the tongue will break bones.
22 Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, but not so many as those who have perished by their own tongue.
23 Blessed is he who is protected from a wicked tongue, who has not passed into its anger, and who has not drawn its yoke, and is not bound in its chains:
24 For its yoke is an iron yoke, and its chain is a chain of bronze.
25 Its death is a most wicked death, and even hell is more useful than it.
26 Its persistence shall not remain, but it shall hold the ways of the unjust: and in its flame it shall not burn the just.
27 Those who abandon God shall fall into it, and it shall burn in them and not be extinguished, and it shall be sent upon them like a lion, and shall wound them like a leopard.
28 Hedge your ears with thorns, do not listen to a wicked tongue, and make doors and bars for your mouth.
29 Melt down your gold and your silver, and make a scale for your words, and a right muzzle for your mouth:
30 And take heed lest you slip with your tongue, and fall in the sight of your enemies who lie in wait for you, and your fall be incurable unto death.

### C H A P T E R XXIX

->*Help should be given to a neighbor through a loan, and faith must be kept with the lender: and although many may break faith, one must not for that reason cease from almsgiving, the praises of which are described: thanks should be given to a guarantor, and faith kept: he discusses in what the beginning of a man's life consists, and concerning wandering and ungrateful guests.*<-

1 He who shows mercy lends to his neighbor: and he who is strong of hand keeps the commandments.
2 Lend to your neighbor in the time of his necessity, and again, repay your neighbor in his time.
3 Confirm your word, and act faithfully with him: and at all times you will find what is necessary for you.
4 Many have looked upon a loan as if it were a windfall <note>original: "inventionem"; literally a 'finding' or 'discovery,' implying they treat the borrowed money as something they found for free rather than a debt to be repaid</note>, and have brought trouble to those who helped them.
5 Until they receive it, they kiss the hands of the giver, and in their promises they humble their voice:
6 But in the time of repayment, he will ask for more time, and will speak words of weariness and murmuring, and will make excuses about the timing:
7 If he is able to repay, he will resist; he will hardly return half a coin, and will count that as a windfall.

### CHAPTER XXX.

*Children are to be educated with discipline, and how ruinous it is to indulge them: health of the body is better than riches: and how harmful and to be avoided is sadness for a man, while joy of the heart is most useful.*

<margin>Proverbs 13:24 and 23:13.</margin>
1 He who loves his son frequently applies the whip to him, so that he may rejoice in his later years, and not have to knock at his neighbors' doors.
2 He who teaches his son will be praised in

him, and among his household, he will boast of him.

6 For he left behind a defender of the house against enemies, and one who returns kindness to friends.

14 Better is a poor man who is healthy and strong in his might, than a rich man who is weak and afflicted with illness.

### CHAPTER XXXI.

*The watchfulness of honesty: foresight in thought: the labor of the rich and the poor: one who loves gold: the many falls caused by gold: praise of the rich man without stain: modesty to be kept at the table: praise of sobriety, and the condemnation of gluttony: praise for the moderate use of wine, and the condemnation of its excessive use.*

1 The watchfulness of honesty will wear away the flesh, and the thought of it takes away sleep.

2 Anxiety for the future diverts the mind, and a heavy infirmity makes the soul sober.
3 The rich man has labored in gathering wealth, and in his rest he will be filled with his riches.
4 The poor man has labored in his meager living, and at the end he remains in want.
5 He who loves gold will not be justified: and he who pursues corruption will be filled by it.

17 Do not be crowded in a feast.
18 Understand the needs of your neighbor by your own.

21 And if you sit in the midst of many, do not reach out your hand before them, nor be the first to ask for a drink.
22 How sufficient is a little wine for a well-taught man! In sleeping you will not be troubled by it, and you will feel no pain.
23 Watching, and bitterness <note>original: "cholera," referring here to bile or digestive distress caused by excess</note>, and pangs of the bowels are for an intemperate man:
24 The sleep of health is for a temperate man: he will sleep until morning, and his soul will be delighted within him.
25 And if you have been forced to eat too much, rise from the midst, vomit <note>In the ancient world, this was sometimes advised as a medical remedy to relieve the stomach after accidental overindulgence</note>: and it will refresh you, and you will not bring infirmity upon your body.
26 Hear me, my son, and do not despise me: and in the end you will find my words to be true.
27 In all your works be quick, and no infirmity shall meet you.
28 Many lips will bless the one who is generous with bread, and the testimony of his truth is faithful.
29 The city will grumble against the one who is stingy with bread, and the testimony of his wickedness is true.

31 Fire tests hard iron: so wine will test the hearts of the proud when drunk in excess.
32 Wine is like life to men if drunk soberly: if you drink it moderately, you will be sober.
33 What is life to him who is diminished by wine?
34 What defrauds life? Death.

39 Wine drunk in excess is bitterness of the soul.
40 The heat of drunkenness is the stumbling block of the fool, lessening strength and causing wounds.
41 At a banquet of wine, do not rebuke your neighbor: and do not despise him in his joy.
42 Do not speak words of reproach to him: and do not press him by demanding repayment.

### CHAPTER XXXII.

*The duty of a good leader: the elder should speak: one should be silent where there is no listener: the joy of music at a feast: the young should remain silent: the praise of silence: one's own house must be examined: the praise of the fear of the Lord: the sinner avoids correction: nothing should be done without counsel.*

1 Have they made you a leader? Do not be puffed up: be among them as one of themselves.
2 Take care of them, and then sit down; and when you have fulfilled all your duties, take your place:
3 So that you may rejoice because of them, and receive a crown as an ornament of grace, and gain the honor of the invitation.
4 Speak, you who are older: for it becomes you
5 To speak the first word with careful knowledge, and do not hinder the music.
6 Where there is no one to hear, do not pour out words, and do not be puffed up with your wisdom at an unsuitable time.
7 A gem of carbuncle in an ornament of gold, so is a concert of music at a banquet of wine.
8 Like a signet of emerald in a setting of gold, so is the melody of music with pleasant and moderate wine.
9 Listen in silence, and for your reverence, good grace shall come to you.
10 Young man, speak scarcely in your own cause.
11 If you are asked twice, let your answer be brief.
12 In many things be as if you do not know, and listen in silence while also seeking knowledge.
13 In the midst of great men, do not be forward: and where old men are present, do not speak much.
14 Before the hail comes lightning: and before a bashful man goes grace, and for your reverence, good grace shall come to you.
15 And at the hour of rising, do not linger: but run home before others, and there find your rest, and there take your pastime,
16 And follow your own thoughts, but not in sin or proud speech.
17 And above all these things, bless the Lord who made you, and who satisfies you with all his good things.
18 He who fears the Lord will receive his doctrine: and those who watch for him shall find a blessing.
19 He who seeks the law shall be filled with it: and he who acts deceitfully shall find a stumbling block in it.
20 Those who fear the Lord shall find righteous judgment, and shall kindle justice like a light.

21 A sinful man will avoid correction, and according to his own will he will find an excuse <note>original: "comparationem," literally a comparison or a way to justify his actions</note>.
22 A man of counsel will not lose understanding; a stranger and a proud man will not be struck with fear.

### CHAPTER XXXIII.

*The one who fears the Lord and the wise man are praised: the inconsistency of the fool's heart: the mocking friend: days and times are from God, who created and arranged all other things, in whose hand man is like clay in the hand of the potter: evil against good: possessions should be distributed to others not during life, but at death: and how servants are to be treated.*

1 No evils shall happen to him who fears the Lord, but in temptation God will preserve him, and deliver him from evils.
2 A wise man does not hate the commandments and justices, and he will not be shattered like a ship in a storm.
3 A man of understanding believes the law of God, and the law is faithful to him.
4 He who clarifies an inquiry will prepare his word, and having prayed in such a way, he will be heard; he will preserve discipline, and then he will answer.
<margin>† See above, 21:17.</margin>
5 † The heart of a fool is like a cartwheel: and his thoughts are like a turning axle.
6 A mocking friend is like a stallion, which neighs under everyone who sits upon it.
7 Why does one day excel another, and again one light exceed another, and one year another, all coming from the sun?
8 They were separated by the knowledge of the Lord, when the sun was made, and when it kept the commandment.
9 And he changed the seasons and their feast days, and at those times they celebrated the feast days at their appointed hour.
<margin>† Genesis 2:7.</margin>
10 Some of them God exalted and magnified, and some of them he placed in the number of ordinary days. And all men are from the ground, † and from the earth, from where Adam was created.
11 In the fullness of his discipline, the Lord separated them, and changed their ways.
12 Some of them he blessed and exalted: and some of them he sanctified and drew to himself: and some of them he cursed and brought low, and turned them away from their station.
<margin>† Romans 9:21.</margin>
13 † Like the clay of the potter in his hand, to mold it and arrange it.
14 All his ways are according to his arrangement: so is man in the hand of him who made him, and he will render to him according to his judgment.
15 Good is set against evil, and life against death: so also is the sinner set against the just man. And so look upon all the works of the Most High. Two and two, and one against another.
16 And I, the last to wake, have kept watch as one who gathers grapes after the vintage-gatherers.

<column-break/>

17 In the blessing of God, I also have hoped: and like one who gathers grapes, I have filled the winepress.
<margin>† See above, 24:47.</margin>
18 † Behold, for I have not labored for myself alone, but for all who seek discipline.
19 Hear me, you great men, and all the people, and you rulers of the Church, perceive with your ears.
20 To son and wife, to brother and friend, do not give power over yourself during your life: and do not give your possession to others, lest it repent you, and you have to entreat them for it.
21 While you yet live and draw breath, let no man <note>original: "omnis caro," literally "all flesh," meaning any mortal person</note> change you.
22 For it is better that your children should ask of you, than that you should look toward the hands of your children.
23 In all your works be excellent.
24 Do not bring a stain upon your glory. In the day of the completion of the days of your life, and at the time of your death, distribute your inheritance.
25 Fodder, and a rod, and a burden for the donkey: bread, and discipline, and work for a servant.
26 He works under discipline, and seeks to rest: slacken your hands upon him, and he seeks liberty.
27 The yoke and the strap bow down a hard neck, and constant labors bend a servant.
28 For a malevolent servant there is torture and fetters: put him to work, so that he is not idle:
29 For idleness has taught much wickedness.
30 Set him to work: for so it befits him. But if he is not obedient, bow him down with fetters, and do not be excessive toward any person: but without judgment do nothing grave.
<margin>† See above, 7:23.</margin>
31 † If you have a faithful servant, let him be to you as your own soul: treat him as a brother, because you have acquired him with the blood of your soul <note>This implies the servant was purchased at a great personal cost or effort</note>.
32 If you injure him unjustly, he will take to flight:
33 And if he departs in pride, you will not know whom to ask, nor in what way to look for him.

### CHAPTER XXXIV.

*The vanity of dreams, divinations, omens, and lies: praise for those who are experienced: the happiness of those who fear God: the offerings of the wicked: defrauding the poor: one building and another destroying: doing penance and not abstaining from sins.*

1 Vain hope and a lie belong to a foolish man: and dreams lift up the imprudent.
2 Like one who catches at a shadow and pursues the wind, so is he who pays attention to lying visions.
3 The vision of dreams is this according to that: a likeness of a man before the face of a man.
4 What can be made clean by the unclean? And what truth can be told by a liar?
5 Divination of error, and lying omens, and the dreams of evildoers are vanity.
6 And like a woman in labor, your heart suffers fantasies: unless a visitation has been sent out by the Most High, do not set your heart upon them:
7 For dreams have made many to err, and those who hoped in them have fallen away.
8 The word of the law shall be fulfilled without a lie, and wisdom shall be made plain in the mouth of the faithful.
9 He who has not been tested, what does he know? A man experienced in many things will think upon many things: and he who has learned much will relate understanding.
10 He who is not experienced knows little: but he who has been involved in many things multiplies cunning.

### C H A P T E R XXXVII.

*The detestation of a false friend: do not forget a true friend: discernment in seeking advice, and with whom you should consult, and from whom you should hide yourself and your counsel: praise for the judgment of a holy man: the wicked word: four things arise from the heart: praise of the skillful and wise man: he who speaks <term>sophistically</term> <note>using clever but deceptive or fallacious reasoning</note> is hateful: test your own soul: and if it be wicked, do not give it power: the ruin caused by gluttony.*

Every friend will say: "I too have joined in friendship": but there is a friend who is a friend in name only.

<column-break/>

Does this not cause a sadness even unto death?
2 But a companion and a friend shall be turned into an enemy.
3 O most wicked presumption, from where were you created to cover the dry land with malice, and with your deceitfulness?
4 A companion rejoices with a friend in delights, but in the time of tribulation he will be an adversary.
5 A companion sympathizes with a friend for the sake of his belly <note>meaning out of a desire for food or self-interest</note>, and he will take up a shield against the enemy.
6 Forget not your friend in your mind, and be not unmindful of him in your wealth.
7 Do not take counsel with one who lays a trap for you, and hide your counsel from those who are jealous of you.
8 Every counselor offers advice, but there is a counselor who is for himself.
9 Guard your soul from a counselor: first know what his own need is: for he will think within his own mind:
10 Lest perhaps he drive a stake into the ground, and say to you:
11 "Your way is good"; and then stand on the opposite side to see what happens to you.
12 Treat with an irreligious man about holiness, and with the unjust about justice, and with a woman about her rival: with a coward about war, with a merchant about transport, with a buyer about selling, with an envious man about giving thanks,
13 With the ungodly about piety, with the dishonest about honesty, with the field laborer about any work,
14 With the yearly laborer about the completion of the year, with a lazy servant about much work: do not look to these for any counsel.
15 But be constant with a holy man, whomever you know to be observant of the fear of God,
16 Whose soul is according to your own soul: and who, when you stumble in the darkness, will grieve with you.
17 Establish within yourself a heart of good counsel: for there is nothing of more value to you than it.
18 The soul of a holy man sometimes tells the truth more than seven watchmen sitting on high to look out.
19 And in all these things pray to the Most High, that he may direct your way in truth.
20 Before all works let a true word go before you, and before every act, stable counsel.
21 A wicked word will change the heart: from which four parts arise: good and evil, life and death: and the tongue is the constant ruler of them. There is a man who is clever and a teacher of many, yet he is useless to his own soul.
22 A skillful man has taught many, and is sweet to his own soul.
23 He who speaks <term>sophistically</term> is hateful: in everything he shall be found wanting.
24 Grace has not been given to him by the Lord: for he is deprived of all wisdom.
25 There is a wise man who is wise for his own soul: and the fruit of his understanding is laudable.
26 A wise man instructs his people, and the fruits of his understanding are faithful.
27 A wise man shall be filled with blessings, and those who see him shall praise him.
28 The life of a man is in the number of days: but the days of Israel are innumerable.
29 A wise man shall inherit honor among the people, and his name shall live forever.

# CHAPTER XXXVIII.

*Honor the physician: medicine is given to man by God: how the sick person should behave toward God and the physician: the dead must be wept for, but one must restrain oneself from sorrow which does not profit the dead and harms you: but remember that you also shall die: every craftsman considers the things in which he works: and these are indeed necessary in the community, but they do not excel in dignity or wisdom.*

1 **H**onor the physician because of necessity: for the Most High created him.
2 For all healing is from God, and he shall receive a gift from the king.
3 The skill of the physician shall exalt his head, and in the sight of great men he shall be praised.
4 The Most High created medicines out of the earth, and a wise man will not abhor them.
<margin>Exodus 15:25.</margin>
5 † Was not the bitter water made sweet by wood? <note>A reference to Moses sweetening the waters of Marah</note>
6 Their virtue was made known to men, and the Most High gave knowledge to men, so that he might be honored in his wonders.
7 By these he shall heal and mitigate pain, and the apothecary <note>original: "unguentarius," a maker of ointments and perfumes</note> shall make sweet pigments, and shall prepare ointments for health, and his works shall not be consumed.
8 For the peace of God is upon the face of the earth.
<margin>Isaiah 38:3.</margin>
9 † My son, in your sickness do not neglect yourself, but pray to the Lord, and he shall heal you.
10 Turn away from sin, and direct your hands, and cleanse your heart from every offense.
11 Give a sweet savor and a memorial of fine flour, and make a fat offering, and then give place to the physician:
12 For the Lord created him: and let him not depart from you, because his works are necessary.
13 For there is a time when you may fall into their hands:
14 And they shall pray to the Lord, that he may direct their rest and their healing, according to their way of life.
15 He who sins in the sight of him who made him, shall fall into the hands of the physician.
16 My son, shed tears over the dead, and begin to weep as if you had suffered dreadfully, and according to custom cover his body, and do not neglect his burial.
17 But because of talk <note>original: "delaturam," referring to public expectation or gossip</note>, bear his mourning bitterly for one day, and be comforted for your sadness,
18 And observe the mourning according to his merit for one day, or two, to avoid detraction <note>To avoid the criticism of others who might think you did not care for the deceased</note>.
<margin>Proverbs 15:13, 17:22.</margin>
19 † For sorrow hastens death, and it crushes one's strength, and the sorrow of the heart bows the neck.
20 In being led away, sorrow remains: and the substance of the poor man is according to his heart.
21 Do not give your heart over to sorrow, but drive it from you: and remember your own end,
22 Do not forget: for there is no returning, and you shall do him no good, and you shall hurt yourself.

<column-break/>

23 Remember my judgment: for yours also shall be such: mine yesterday, and yours today. <note>A common epitaph sentiment: the dead person speaks to the living</note>
<margin>2 Samuel 12:21.</margin>
24 † When the dead is at rest, let his memory rest also, and comfort him at the departing of his spirit.
25 The wisdom of a scribe comes in the time of leisure, and he who has little business shall acquire wisdom: with what wisdom shall he be filled?
26 He who holds the plow, and he who glories in the goad, who drives the oxen with a sting, and is occupied in their labors, and whose talk is about the offspring of bulls.
27 He shall give his heart to turning furrows, and his wakefulness is for the foddering of heifers.
28 So also the smith and the architect, who passes the night as the day, who carves engraved signets, and his diligence varies the pattern: he shall give his heart to the likeness of the picture, and his wakefulness shall perfect the work.
29 So the blacksmith sitting by the anvil, and considering the iron work: the vapor of the fire scorches his flesh, and he struggles in the heat of the furnace:
30 The noise of the hammer is ever in his ears, and his eye is upon the pattern of the vessel:
31 He shall give his heart to the finishing of his works, and his wakefulness shall adorn them to perfection.
32 So the potter sitting at his work, turning the wheel with his feet, who is always placed in anxiety for his work, and all his operation is by number.
33 With his arm he shall fashion the clay, and before his feet he shall bend his strength.
34 He shall give his heart to complete the glazing, and his wakefulness shall clean the furnace.
35 All these have trusted in their hands, and every one is wise in his own art.
36 Without all these a city is not built.
37 And they shall not inhabit, nor walk about, and they shall not leap into the assembly <note>original: "ecclesiam," referring to the public or religious gathering</note>.
38 They shall not sit upon the judge’s seat, and they shall not understand the covenant of judgment, nor shall they make discipline and judgment plain, and they shall not be found in parables:
39 But they shall strengthen the state of the world, and their prayer is in the exercise of their craft, applying their soul, and searching in the law of the Most High.

# CHAPTER XXXIX.

4 He shall serve among great men, and shall appear before the governor.
5 He shall pass into the land of foreign nations: for he shall try good and evil among men.

### C H A P T E R XL.

->*Man is subject to great labor, a heavy yoke, and various miseries: all things are fleeting: the wicked with their riches are soon to be destroyed: praise of a self-sufficient life: he commends various pairs, though he prefers other things to them: praise for the fear of the Lord: act so that you do not lack, nor look toward another's table, from which a disciplined and learned man keeps himself.*<-

3 From him who sits upon a glorious throne, even to him who is humbled in earth and ashes:

5 And in the time of rest upon his bed, the sleep of the night changes his knowledge.
6 Little or nothing is his rest, and his sleep is like a watchman's day.
7 He is troubled in the vision of his heart, as one who has escaped in the day of battle. In the time of his safety he rose up, and wondered that there was no fear:

### C H A P T E R X L I.

*To whom the memory of death is bitter, and to whom it is not: do not fear death, but remember those who came before and those who will follow, being content with the divine arrangement concerning you: the curse remaining upon the ungodly: care for a good name: hidden wisdom and hidden treasure are useless: how one should be ashamed of sins: do not turn your face from a neighbor, nor look upon another's wife, nor reproach someone after giving a gift.*

1 O death, how bitter is the memory of you to a man who has peace in his possessions;
2 To a man who is at rest, whose ways are directed in all things, and who is still strong enough to take food!
3 O death, your judgment is good to a man in need, whose strength fails,
4 Who is failing in age, who is anxious about all things, and to the untrusting man who loses patience!
5 Do not fear the judgment of death. Remember the things that were before you, and the things that are to come upon you: this is the judgment from the Lord upon all flesh.
6 And what will come upon you in the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether it be ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years.
7 For in the grave <note>original: "inferno," referring here to the realm of the dead or Sheol rather than a place of punishment</note> there is no complaining about life.
8 The children of abominations become the children of sinners, and those who frequent the houses of the ungodly.
9 The inheritance of the children of sinners shall perish, and with their seed shall be a constant reproach.
10 Children complain of an ungodly father, because they are in reproach on his account.
11 Woe to you, ungodly men, who have forsaken the law of the Lord Most High.
12 And if you are born, you shall be born in a curse; and if you die, your portion shall be in a curse.

### C H A P T E R X L I I.

*Secrets not to be revealed: one must abstain from partiality toward persons and many other vices listed here: what is given and received should be written down: concerning the anxious guarding of a daughter, and that the guard should be strengthened over a lustful woman: it is dangerous to dwell with a woman: but better is the iniquity of a man than a woman doing well <note>This verse reflects the ancient patriarchal context of the author, Ben Sira, who often expressed severe warnings regarding women and social reputation</note>: the works of the Lord, who sees all things even the secrets of the heart, are perfect and desirable.*

1 Do not repeat a thing you have heard from the revelation of a secret word, and you will truly be without shame, and will find grace in the sight of all men: do not be ashamed because of all these things, † and do not accept a person's status so as to sin.

### CHAPTER XLIII.

*The greatness of the Creator shines forth in the ornament and beauty of the heavens, namely in the sky, the moon, the stars, the rainbow, snow, hail, clouds, thunder, the frost from the North, the hoarfrost, and the sea, in which there are many kinds of beasts: finally, no one is sufficient to praise God.*

1 The firmament of the height is its beauty, the appearance of the sky in a vision of glory.
2 The sun, when it appears, announcing at its rising, a wonderful vessel, the work of the Most High.
3 At noon it burns the earth, and who can endure in the presence of its heat? guarding a furnace in the works of heat:
4 Threefold the sun burns the mountains, breathing out

<column-break/>

fiery rays, and shining with its rays it blinds the eyes.
5 Great is the Lord who made it, and at his words it has hastened its course.
6 And the moon in all things in its season, a showing of the time, and a sign of the ages.
7 From the moon is the sign of a feast day, a light that decreases in its perfection.
8 The month is named according to its name, increasing wonderfully in its perfection.
9 A vessel of the camps on high, shining gloriously in the firmament of heaven.
10 The beauty of the sky is the glory of the stars, the Lord illuminating the world on high.
11 At the words of the Holy One they will stand for judgment, and they shall not fail in their watches.
<margin>† Genesis 9:13.</margin>
12 See the rainbow, and bless him † who made it: it is very beautiful in its brightness.
13 It has encompassed the sky in the circle of its glory, the hands of the Most High have opened it.
14 By his command he has hastened the snow, and he hastens to send out the lightnings of his judgment.
15 Therefore the treasures are opened, and the clouds fly out like birds.
16 In his greatness he has positioned the clouds, and the hailstones are broken.
17 In his sight the mountains shall be moved, and by his will the South wind <note>original: "Notus," the personification of the South wind.</note> shall blow.
18 The voice of his thunder shall strike the earth, the storm of the north wind, and the gathering of the whirlwind:
19 And as a bird lighting to sit, he scatters the snow, and its descent is like a locust landing.
20 The eye shall admire the beauty of its whiteness, and the heart shall be astonished at its rain.
21 He shall pour out the frost like salt upon the earth: and when it freezes, it shall become like the tops of a thistle.
22 The cold north wind blows, and the ice congeals from the water; it shall rest upon every gathering of waters, and shall clothe the waters like a breastplate.
23 And it shall devour the mountains: and burn the desert, and extinguish the green, as if by fire.
24 The medicine for all is in the speed of a cloud: and the dew meeting the heat that comes shall make it humble.
25 By his word the wind is stilled, and by his thought he has calmed the deep, and the Lord has planted islands in it.
26 Let those who sail the sea tell of its dangers: and hearing with our ears, we shall wonder.
27 There are extraordinary works, and wonders; various kinds of beasts, and all cattle, and the creation of sea-monsters.
28 Because of him the end of the journey is established, and by his word all things are composed.
29 We shall say much, and yet fail in words: but the sum of our words is, He is in all.
30 When we glory, what shall we be able to do? for he is the Almighty above all his works.
31 The Lord is terrible and exceedingly great, and his power is wonderful.
32 Glorify the Lord as much as you can, for he will yet exceed it, and his magnificence is wonderful.
33 Blessing the Lord, exalt him as much as you can: for he is greater than all praise.
34 Exalting him, be filled with strength; do not labor: for you shall never comprehend him.

# THE PROPHECY OF ISAIAH.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*The time in which Isaiah prophesied over Judah and Jerusalem, which, because of its ingratitude and other crimes, was struck by God with every kind of punishment, yet did not return to him: wherefore he says that a most wretched desolation looms over them: their sacrifices and festivals are rejected: and what they ought to do to be received back into God's grace: again, because of the falling away from former virtue into various sins, a heavy vengeance: and finally their future liberation and restoration to a happier state is prophesied.*

1 The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
2 Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken. I have nourished and brought up children, but they have rebelled against me.
3 The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s crib: but Israel has not known me, and my people have not understood.
4 Woe to the sinful nation, a people weighed down with ini-

quity, a wicked seed, unprincipled children: they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, they have gone backward and become estranged.

6 From the sole of the foot even to the top of the head, there is no health in it; wounds, and bruises, and swelling sores, they are not bound up, nor treated with medicine, nor soothed with oil.

31 And your strength shall be like the glowing spark of tow <note>coarse flax or hemp fiber</note>, and your work like a spark: and both shall be set on fire together, and there shall be no one to extinguish it.

### CHAPTER III.

*The future grave affliction and desertion of the Jews because of their sins, and the dominion of boys and the effeminate: he reproves the sins of the leaders: likewise he foretells that the pride and curious luxury of the daughters of Zion shall be turned into shame.*

For behold, the Sovereign Lord of hosts shall take away from Jerusalem, and from Judah, the valiant and the strong, every strength of bread, and every strength of water;
2 The strong man, and the man of war, the judge, and the prophet, and the soothsayer, and the elder;
3 The captain over fifty, and the honorable in countenance, and the counselor, and the wise among the master-builders, and the skillful in mystical speech.
4 And I will give children to be their princes, and the effeminate <note>The Latin 'effeminati' here suggests weak-willed or unstable rulers who lack moral fortitude</note> shall rule over them.
5 And the people shall rush, man against man, and every one against his neighbor: the child shall make a tumult against the elder, and the base man against the noble.
5 For a man shall take hold of his brother, one of the household of his father, saying: You have a garment, be our prince, and let this ruin be under your hand.
7 In that day he shall answer, saying: I am no healer, and in my house there is no bread, nor clothing: do not appoint me a prince of the people.
8 For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their inventions are against the Lord, to provoke the eyes of his majesty.
9 The look of their countenance answers them: and they have proclaimed their sin like Sodom, and have not hidden it: woe to their souls, for evils are rendered to them.
10 Say to the just man that it is well, for he shall eat the fruit of his inventions.
11 Woe to the wicked man unto evil: for the reward of his hands shall be made unto him.
12 As for my people, their oppressors have stripped them, and women have ruled over them. O my people, they that call you blessed, the same deceive you, and destroy the way of your steps.
13 The Lord stands up to judge, and he stands to judge the people.
14 The Lord will come into judgment with the elders of his people, and its princes: for you have devoured the vineyard, and the spoil of the poor is in your house.
15 Why do you crush my people, and grind the faces of the poor, says the Lord God of hosts?
16 And the Lord said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and have walked with necks stretched out, and went with beckoning eyes, and clapped their hands, walking with their feet, and moving with a measured pace:
17 The Lord will make bald the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion, and the Lord will strip their hair.
18 In that day the Lord will take away the ornaments of their shoes, and little moons <note>original: "lunulas," crescent-shaped ornaments or necklaces</note>,
19 And chains, and necklaces, and bracelets, and headbands,
20 And hair-pins, and leg-bands, and little chains <note>original: "murenulas," likely referring to necklaces shaped like lampreys or small chains</note>, and perfume-bottles, and earrings,
21 And rings, and jewels hanging on the forehead,

<column-break/>

22 And changes of apparel, and short cloaks, and fine linen, and needles,
23 And mirrors, and fine muslins, and ribbons, and summer-veils.
24 And instead of a sweet smell there shall be a stench, and instead of a girdle, a rope; and instead of curled hair, baldness; and instead of a breastplate, sackcloth.
25 Your most beautiful men also shall fall by the sword, and your strong ones in battle.
26 And her gates shall lament and mourn, and she shall sit desolate on the ground.

### CHAPTER IV.

*Seven women shall desire one husband: the branch of the Lord shall be exalted: and the remnants of Israel, their filth being washed away, shall be safe, and shall be endowed with great security and happiness.*

And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying: We will eat our own bread, and be covered with our own garments: only let your name be called upon us, take away our reproach.
2 In that day, the branch of the Lord shall be in magnificence and glory, and the fruit of the earth shall be high, and a joy to those who have been saved out of Israel.
3 And it shall come to pass: everyone that shall be left in Zion, and shall remain in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, everyone that is written in life in Jerusalem.
4 If the Lord shall wash away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall wash the blood of Jerusalem out of the midst thereof, by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning.
5 And the Lord will create upon every place of Mount Zion, and where he is invoked, a cloud by day, and smoke and the brightness of a flaming fire by night: for over all the glory shall be a protection.
6 And there shall be a tabernacle for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for security, and a covert from the whirlwind, and from rain.

### CHAPTER V.

*Under the figure of a sterile vineyard delivered to plundering, he prophesies the judgment and desertion of the Jews, and their sins are described: avarice in joining together possessions: drunkenness and contempt for the knowledge of God: the enlargement of hell: the humiliation of the proud, and the exaltation of God: also the happiness of the righteous, and woe denounced against various kinds of sinners: and a sign to be raised among the nations against the Jews.*

### C H A P T E R VI.

*Isaiah, having seen the majesty of the Lord, condemns himself for having been silent, but his lips being cleansed, he offers himself for preaching: the people are foretold to be blinded until the desolation of the cities of Judah, and a future consolation for that which was left behind.*

1 **IN** the year in which king Uzziah <note>original: "Ozias," the king of Judah who reigned for 52 years and died circa 740 BCE</note> died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high and elevated: and those things that were under him filled the temple.
2 The Seraphim <note>Celestial beings whose name implies "burning ones."</note> stood upon it: one had six wings, and the other had six wings: with two they covered his face, and with two they covered his feet, and with two they did fly.
<margin>† Revelation 4:8.</margin>
3 And they cried one to another, and said: † Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of hosts, all the earth is full of his glory.
4 And the lintels of the doors were moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.
5 And I said: Woe is me, because I have held my peace; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people that has unclean lips, and I have seen with my eyes the King the Lord of hosts.
6 And one of the Seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a live coal, which he had taken with the tongs off the altar.
7 And he touched my mouth, and said: Behold this has touched your lips, and your iniquities shall be taken away, and your sin shall be cleansed.
8 And I heard the voice of the Lord saying: Whom shall I send? and who shall go for us? And I said: Lo, here am I, send me.
9 And he said: Go, and you shall say to this people:
<margin>† Matthew 13:14; Mark 4:12; Luke 8:10; John 12:40; Acts 28:26; Romans 11:8.</margin>
† Hear, you that hear, and do not understand: and see the vision, and do not know it.
10 Blind the heart of this people, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes: lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I heal them.
11 And I said: How long, O Lord? And he said: Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without a man, and the land shall be left desolate.
12 And the Lord shall remove men far away, and she that was left in the midst of the earth shall be multiplied.
13 And there shall be still a tithing therein, and she shall return, and shall be for a show as a terebinth tree, and as an oak that spreads its branches: that which shall stand therein shall be a holy seed.

### CHAPTER VII.

*While Jerusalem is besieged by the Syrians and by Israel, Isaiah prophesies that they shall not prevail, and gives the wicked King Ahaz a sign of liberation: a virgin who shall bear a son whose name is Emmanuel. He also predicts the desertion of Israel, and the most heavy affliction and solitude of Judah.*

<margin>2 Kings 16:5</margin>
1 And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz, the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to fight against it; and they could not prevail against it.
2 And they told the house of David, saying: "Syria has rested upon Ephraim" <note>This means Syria has allied itself with the northern kingdom of Israel, often called Ephraim.</note>, and his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the woods are moved by the face of the wind.
3 And the Lord said to Isaiah: "Go out now to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub <note>original: "derelictus est Jasub," a name meaning 'a remnant shall return'</note>, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, in the way of the fuller’s field.
4 And you shall say to him: See that you be quiet; do not fear, and let your heart not be afraid of these two tails of smoking firebrands, in the wrath of the fury of Rezin, king of Syria, and of the son of Remaliah.
5 Because Syria has taken counsel against you, unto the evil of Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying:
6 'Let us go up to Judah, and rouse it, and tear it away to us, and let us place a king in the midst of it, the son of Tabeel.'
7 Thus says the Lord God: It shall not stand, and this shall not be.
8 But the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within sixty-five years, Ephraim shall cease to be a people.
9 And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you will not believe, you shall not continue."
10 And the Lord spoke again to Ahaz, saying:
11 "Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God, either in the depth of hell, or in the heights above."
12 And Ahaz said: "I will not ask, and I will not tempt the Lord." <note>Ahaz feigns piety here to avoid following God's direction, as he had already sought an alliance with Assyria.</note>
13 And he said: "Hear then, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to be troublesome to men, that you are troublesome also to my God?
<margin>Matthew 1:23; Luke 1:31</margin>
14 Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign. **Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel.** <note>original: "Emmanuel," meaning 'God with us'</note>
15 He shall eat butter and honey, that he may know how to refuse the evil, and to choose the good.
16 For before the child knows how to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land which you abhor shall be forsaken by the face of her two kings.
17 The Lord shall bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon your father’s house, days that have not come since the days of the separation of Ephraim from Judah with the king of the Assyrians."
18 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost parts of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
19 And they shall come, and shall all of them rest in the torrents of the valleys, and in the holes of the rocks, and in all the thickets, and in all the crevices.
20 In that day the Lord shall shave with a hired razor—by those who are beyond the river, by the king of the Assyrians—the head, and the hairs of the feet, and the whole beard. <note>Shaving the beard and body was a sign of extreme humiliation and mourning in the ancient Near East.</note>

<column-break/>

21 And it shall come to pass in that day, that a man shall nourish a young cow and two sheep,
22 And for the abundance of milk he shall eat butter; for everyone who is left in the midst of the land shall eat butter and honey.
23 And it shall come to pass in that day, that every place where there were a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, shall be turned into thorns and briers.
24 They shall go in there with arrows and bows, because briers and thorns shall be in all the land.
25 And as for all the mountains that shall be raked with a hoe, the fear of thorns and briers shall not come there; and they shall be for the ox to feed in, and for the cattle to tread upon.

### CHAPTER VIII.

*Isaiah is commanded to write the name of the child about to be born in a book; he predicts that the kingdoms of Israel and Syria are to be destroyed, and the affliction of Judah, though followed by a future liberation from God, even though many in Judah shall fall. He commands the testimony to be bound and the law to be sealed, adding the evils that threaten those who withdraw from the law.*

1 And the Lord said to me: "Take a great book, and write in it with a man’s pen: 'Take the spoils quickly, plunder speedily.'" <note>This refers to the name of Isaiah's second son, Maher-shalal-hash-baz.</note>
2 And I took to myself faithful witnesses, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah.
3 And I went to the prophetess <note>This refers to Isaiah's wife.</note>; and she conceived, and bore a son. And the Lord said to me: "Call his name: 'Hasten to take the spoils; make haste to plunder.'
4 For before the child knows how to call his father and his mother, the strength of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of the Assyrians."
5 And the Lord spoke to me again, saying:
6 "Because this people has rejected the waters of Shiloah <note>original: "Siloe," a pool in Jerusalem representing God's quiet protection</note> that go with silence, and has instead taken up Rezin and the son of Remaliah:
7 Therefore, behold, the Lord will bring upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of the Assyrians and all his glory; and he shall come up over all his channels, and shall overflow all his banks.
8 And he shall pass through Judah, overflowing and going over; he shall reach even to the neck. And the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of your land, O Emmanuel."
9 Gather yourselves together, O you people, and be overcome; and give ear, all you distant lands: strengthen yourselves and be overcome; gird yourselves and be overcome.
10 Take counsel together, and it shall be brought to nothing; speak a word, and it shall not be done: because God is with us.
11 For thus says the Lord to me: As he taught me with a strong hand, that I should not walk in the way of this people, saying:
12 "Do not say: 'A conspiracy'; for all that this people speaks is a conspiracy. Neither fear their fear, nor be afraid.
13 Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.
<margin>Luke 2:34; Romans 9:33; 1 Peter 2:7</margin>
14 And he shall be a sanctuary to you. But he shall be **for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of offense** to the two houses of Israel; for a snare and for a ruin to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
15 And very many of them shall stumble and fall, and shall be broken in pieces, and shall be snared and taken."

**22** And he shall look toward the earth, and behold tribulation and darkness, faintness and anguish, and a gloom following him, and he cannot fly away from his distress.

### CHAPTER XIII.

*The vast and cruel devastation of the Babylonians by the Medes.*

1 **The burden** <note>original: "ONus," a term used in prophecy to signify a heavy message of judgment or an oracle</note> of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.

3 I have commanded my sanctified ones, and I have called my strong ones in my wrath, those who exult in my glory.

5 To those coming from a far country, from the end of heaven: the Lord and the vessels of his fury, to destroy the whole land.
6 Howl, for the day of the Lord is near: it shall come as a devastation from the Lord.
7 Because of this, all hands shall be weakened, and every heart of man shall waste away,
8 And shall be crushed. Torsions and pains shall take hold; they shall be in pain as a woman in labor: everyone shall be amazed at his neighbor: their faces shall be as burnt countenances.
9 Behold, the day of the Lord shall come, cruel, and full of indignation, and of wrath and fury, to place the land in solitude, and to crush its sinners out of it.
<margin>† Ezekiel 32:7. Joel 2:10 & 3:15. Matthew 24:29. Mark 13:24. Luke 21:25.</margin>
10 † For the stars of heaven and their brightness shall not expand their light: the sun is darkened at its rising, and the moon shall not shine in her light.

12 A man shall be more precious than gold, and a person more than pure gold from Ophir <note>original: "mundo obrizo," referring to highly refined or pure gold</note>.
13 For this I will trouble the heaven: and the earth shall be moved from its place, because of the indignation of the Lord of hosts, and because of the day of the wrath of his fury.
14 And it shall be like a fleeing doe, and like a sheep: and there shall be no one to gather them: everyone shall turn to his own people, and each shall flee to his own land.

### CHAPTER XIV.

*A prophecy concerning the consolation of the Jews and their deliverance from Babylonian captivity, and the crushing of the Babylonians: whose vast pride, breadth of dominion, and cruelty are explained, together with the punishment of the Philistines and others who rejoiced over the calamity of the Jews.*

1 **The time** is near for its coming, and its days shall not be prolonged. For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose out of Israel, and will make them rest upon their own ground; the stranger shall be joined to them, and shall adhere to the house of Jacob.
2 And the people shall take them and bring them into their place: and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord as male and female servants: and they shall be taking those who had taken them, and they shall subject their oppressors.
3 And it shall come to pass in that day: when God shall have given you rest from your labor, and from your shaking, and from the hard servitude in which you served before:
4 You shall take up this parable <note>original: "parabolam," here meaning a taunt or a proverb</note> against the king of Babylon, and you shall say: How has the oppressor ceased, how has the tribute rested?
5 The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked, the rod of the rulers,
6 Striking the people in indignation with an incurable plague, subjecting nations in fury, persecuting cruelly.
7 All the earth is quiet and still, it has rejoiced and exulted:
8 Even the fir trees have rejoiced over you, and the cedars of Lebanon, saying: since you have slept, no one comes up to cut us down.
9 Hell <note>original: "Infernus," the realm of the dead or Sheol</note> below is troubled to meet your coming; it has stirred up the giants for you. All the princes of the earth have risen from their thrones, all the leaders of nations.
10 All shall answer and say to you: You also are wounded just as we were, you have become like us.
11 Your pride is drawn down to the depths, your carcass has fallen: the moth shall be strewn under you, and worms shall be your covering.
12 How you have fallen from heaven, O Lucifer <note>original: "lucifer," literally "light-bringer" or the "morning star"</note>, who rose in the morning? You have fallen to the earth, you who wounded the nations?

## CHAPTER XV.

*The ruin of the Moabites is predicted, and the compassion of the prophet toward Moab.*

1 The burden of Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste, it is silent: because in the night the wall of Moab is laid waste, it is silent.

<column-break/>

<margin>† Jeremiah 48:37. Ezekiel 7:18.</margin>
2 The house has gone up, and Dibon to the high places to wail over Nebo and over Medeba; Moab has howled: † on every head there is baldness, and every beard is shaved. <note>Shaving the head and beard were traditional signs of extreme mourning and humiliation.</note>
3 In its streets they are girded with sackcloth: upon its roofs, and in its squares, every howl descends into weeping.
4 Heshbon has cried out, and Elealeh, their voice is heard as far as Jahaz; over this the ready men of Moab shall howl, his soul shall howl to you.
5 My heart shall cry to Moab, its bars even to Zoar, like a three-year-old heifer: for by the ascent of Luhith he shall go up weeping, and in the way of Horonaim they shall raise a cry of destruction.
6 For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate, for the grass has withered, the sprout has failed, all greenness has perished.
7 According to the greatness of their work and their visitation, they shall lead them to the torrent of the willows.
8 For the cry has gone around the border of Moab: its howling even to Gallim, and its cry even to the Well of Elim.
9 For the waters of Dibon are filled with blood: for I will place additions upon Dibon: a lion for those who have fled from Moab, and for the remnants of the land.

Moab shall appear upon his high places; he shall enter into his sanctuaries to pray, and he shall not prevail.
13 This is the word that the Lord spoke against Moab from that time:
14 And now the Lord has spoken, saying: Within three years, like the years of a hired hand <note>A "hired hand" or laborer's years refers to a strictly counted period of time, with no extensions.</note>, the glory of Moab shall be taken away from all the great multitude of people, and what is left shall be small and few, by no means many.

## CHAPTER XVII.

->*The Syrian allies of the people of Israel having been laid waste,*<-
->*Israel likewise shall be devastated, because it has forgotten*<-
->*God its Savior, to whom it shall return when pressed by calamity:*<-
->*and a "woe" is denounced against the persecutors of the Lord’s people.*<-

1 The burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus shall cease to be a city, and shall be like a heap of stones in ruin.
2 The abandoned cities of Aroer <note>Aroer was a region in the territory of Moab/Ammon, often changing hands.</note> shall be for flocks; they shall rest there, and there shall be no one to terrify them.
3 And the help of Ephraim <note>Ephraim represents the northern kingdom of Israel.</note> shall cease, and the kingdom from Damascus: and the remnants of Syria shall be like the glory of the children of Israel: says the Lord of hosts.
4 And it shall come to pass in that day: the glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall waste away.
5 And it shall be as when one gathers the standing corn in the harvest, and his arm shall glean the ears; and it shall be as one seeking ears of grain in the valley of Rephaim <note>The Valley of Rephaim was a fertile plain near Jerusalem.</note>.
6 And there shall be left in it as a cluster of grapes, and as the shaking of an olive tree: two or three olives on the top of a branch, or four or five on the top of its fruit-bearing boughs: says the Lord God of Israel.
7 In that day a man shall bow down to his Maker, and his eyes shall look to the Holy One of Israel:
8 And he shall not bow down to the altars which his hands made: and he shall not look to the things that his fingers have wrought, the sacred groves and the shrines.
9 In that day his strong cities shall be abandoned like the plows and the crops which were left before the face of the children of Israel, and the land shall be a desert.
10 Because you have forgotten God your Savior, and have not remembered your strong helper: therefore you shall plant a faithful plantation, but you shall sow a foreign seed.
11 In the day of your planting it shall be a wild grape, and in the morning your seed shall flourish: the harvest is taken away in the day of inheritance; and there shall be heavy sorrow.
12 Woe to the multitude of many peoples, like the multitude of the roaring sea: and the noise of the crowds, like the sound of many waters.
13 The peoples shall roar like the sound of flooding waters, but He shall rebuke him, and he shall flee far away: and he shall be carried off like the dust of the mountains before the face of the wind, and like a whirlwind before a tempest.
14 In the time of evening, behold, there is trouble: in the morning, and he shall not remain: this is the portion of those who have laid us waste, and the lot of those who plunder us.

## CHAPTER XVIII.

->*Against the Egyptians who had enticed the Jews to*<-
->*trust in them: a consolation of the Jewish people*<-
->*regarding their return to Jerusalem is added.*<-

1 Woe to the land of the whirring of wings <note>original: "cymbalo alarum." This likely refers to the swarms of insects or the sails of ships in the Upper Nile region.</note>, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,

<column-break/>

2 Who sends ambassadors by sea, even in vessels of papyrus upon the waters. Go, you swift messengers, to a nation mangled and torn, to a people more terrible than any other; to a nation expecting and trodden down, whose land the rivers have spoiled.
3 All you inhabitants of the world, who dwell upon the earth, when the signal is lifted up on the mountains, you shall see it; and when the trumpet sounds, you shall hear it:
4 For thus says the Lord to me: I will take my rest, and I will consider in my dwelling place, like the clear light of midday, and like a cloud of dew in the day of harvest.
5 For before the harvest it was all in flower, and the unripened fruit shall bud forth, and its small branches shall be cut off with pruning hooks: and the things that were left shall be cut away and shaken out.
6 And they shall be left together for the birds of the mountains, and the beasts of the earth: and the birds shall be upon them all summer, and all the beasts of the earth shall winter upon them.
7 In that time a gift shall be brought to the Lord of hosts from a people torn and mangled, from a people more terrible than any other, from a nation expecting, expecting and trodden down, whose land the rivers have spoiled: to the place of the name of the Lord of hosts, Mount Sion.

## CHAPTER XIX.

->*He describes more fully the punishment of the Egyptians: and*<-
->*that they, having turned to God and being sent a Savior,*<-
->*shall be comforted.*<-

1 The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord will ascend upon a swift cloud, and will enter into Egypt, and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in its midst.
2 And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and a man shall fight against his brother, and a man against his friend, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
3 And the spirit of Egypt shall be broken within its bowels, and I will cast down its counsel: and they shall consult their idols, and their diviners, and their mediums <note>original: "pythones," referring to those possessed by a spirit of divination.</note>, and their soothsayers.
4 And I will deliver Egypt into the hand of cruel masters, and a strong king shall rule over them, says the Lord God of hosts.
5 And the water of the sea shall fail, and the river shall be wasted and dried up.
6 And the rivers shall fail: the streams of the embankments shall be thinned and dried up. The reed and the bulrush shall wither:
7 The channel of the river shall be laid bare from its source, and every seeded field by the water shall be dried up; it shall wither, and shall be no more.
8 And the fishermen shall mourn, and all who cast a hook into the river shall lament, and those who spread a net upon the face of the waters shall languish.
9 Those who work in flax shall be confounded, both those who comb and those who weave fine linen.
10 And its watered places shall be failing: all those who made ponds to catch fish.
11 The princes of Tanis <note>original: "Taneos." Tanis (Zoan) was a major city and royal residence in the Nile Delta.</note> are fools, the wise counselors of Pharaoh have given foolish counsel. How do you say to Pharaoh: I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?
12 Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you, and let them show what the Lord of hosts has purposed concerning Egypt.
