13 The princes of Tanis <note>original: "Taneos." Tanis was a major city in the Nile Delta, often a royal residence.</note> have become fools; the princes of Memphis <note>original: "Mempheos." Memphis was the ancient capital of Lower Egypt.</note> have withered away; they have deceived Egypt, the cornerstone of its people.
14 The Lord has mingled a spirit of confusion in her midst; and they have caused Egypt to stray in all her works, as a drunken man staggers and vomits.
15 And there shall be no work for Egypt that the head or the tail, the palm branch or the reed, might perform <note>This idiom refers to all levels of society, from the highest leaders to the lowest workers.</note>.
16 In that day, Egypt shall be like women; they shall be stunned and afraid because of the waving of the hand of the Lord of hosts, which he shall shake over it.
17 And the land of Judah shall be a terror to Egypt; everyone who remembers it shall tremble because of the counsel of the Lord of hosts, which he has determined against it.
18 In that day, there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan <note>That is, Hebrew, indicating the spread of Jewish influence or worship.</note> and swearing by the Lord of hosts; one shall be called the City of the Sun.
19 In that day, there shall be an altar of the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the Lord near its border.
20 It shall be for a sign and for a witness to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt. For they shall cry to the Lord because of the oppressor, and he shall send them a savior and a defender to deliver them.
21 And the Lord shall be known by Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know the Lord in that day; they shall worship him with sacrifices and offerings; they shall make vows to the Lord and perform them.
22 And the Lord shall strike Egypt with a plague and shall heal her; they shall return to the Lord, and he shall be appeased toward them and shall heal them.
23 In that day, there shall be a highway from Egypt to the Assyrians; the Assyrian shall enter Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria, and the Egyptians shall serve with the Assyrians.
24 In that day, Israel shall be the third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the land,
25 Which the Lord of hosts has blessed, saying: Blessed be my people of Egypt, and the work of my hands the Assyrian: but Israel is my inheritance.

### CHAPTER XX.

*Because Isaiah is commanded to walk naked and barefoot, the captivity of the Egyptians and Ethiopians by the Assyrians is predicted, while the Jews are stunned by their affliction.*

1 In the year that Tartan <note>Tartan was a title for the Assyrian commander-in-chief.</note> entered Ashdod <note>original: "Azotum."</note>, when Sargon the king of the Assyrians had sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it:
2 At that time, the Lord spoke by the hand of Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying: Go, and loose the sackcloth from your loins, and take off your shoes from your feet. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot <note>In the biblical context, "naked" often means wearing only an undergarment, stripped of the outer prophetic robe.</note>.
3 And the Lord said: As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and a wonder over Egypt and over Ethiopia <note>original: "Aethiopiam," referring to the Kingdom of Kush.</note>,
4 So shall the king of the Assyrians lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, with their buttocks uncovered to the shame of Egypt.
5 And they shall be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia their hope, and of Egypt their glory.
6 And the inhabitant of this isle <note>Referring to the coastland of Philistia or Judah.</note> shall say in that day: Behold, this was our hope, to whom we

<column-break/>

fled for help, that they might deliver us from the face of the king of the Assyrians: and how shall we be able to escape?

### CHAPTER XXI.

*The ruin of Babylon by the Medes and Persians: the burden of Edom and Arabia.*

1 The burden of the desert of the sea. As whirlwinds come from the South, so it comes from the desert, from a terrible land.
2 A harsh vision is announced to me: he who is unfaithful acts unfaithfully, and he who is a spoiler wastes. Go up, O Elam; besiege, O Mede; I have made all her groaning to cease.
3 Therefore my loins are filled with pain; anguish has seized me like the pangs of a woman in labor; I fell down when I heard it, I was troubled when I saw it.
4 My heart withered, darkness stunned me; Babylon, my beloved, is made a wonder to me.
5 Prepare the table, behold from the watchtower those eating and drinking; arise, O princes, take up the shield.
6 For thus the Lord has said to me: Go and set a watchman; and whatever he sees, let him announce it.
7 And he saw a chariot with two horsemen, a rider on a donkey, and a rider on a camel; and he looked diligently with great heed.
<margin>$\dagger$ Habakkuk 2:1</margin>
8 And a lion cried: I am upon the watchtower of the Lord, standing continually by day; and $\dagger$ I am at my guard post, standing all night.
<margin>$\dagger$ Jeremiah 51:8; Revelation 14:8</margin>
9 Behold, here comes a man in a chariot with two horsemen, and he answered and said: $\dagger$ Fallen, fallen is Babylon, and all the graven images of her gods are broken to the ground.
10 O my threshing, and the children of my floor! That which I have heard from the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, I have announced to you.
11 The burden of Dumah <note>Dumah is often associated with Edom or the region of Seir.</note> calls to me out of Seir: Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?
12 The watchman said: The morning comes, and also the night; if you will inquire, inquire; return, come.
13 The burden in Arabia. In the forest at evening you shall sleep, in the paths of Dedanim <note>The Dedanites were a North Arabian tribe of merchants.</note>.
14 Meet the thirsty and bring them water, you who inhabit the land of the south; meet the fugitive with bread.
15 For they have fled from the face of the swords, from the face of the drawn sword, from the face of the bent bow, and from the face of a heavy battle.
16 For thus the Lord says to me: Within one year, as the year of a hired hand, and all the glory of Kedar <note>Kedar was a powerful nomadic tribe in the Arabian desert.</note> shall be taken away.
17 And the remainder of the number of the mighty archers of the children of Kedar shall be diminished; for the Lord God of Israel has spoken it.

## CHAPTER XXII.

*The word of the Lord against Jerusalem, whose devastation the prophet laments: and that having neglected God, she fortifies herself in vain to resist the Assyrians: they are rebuked because when they ought to mourn, they indulge their gluttony; and after the rejection of Shebna, the overseer of the temple, Eliakim is substituted, to whom great power is given.*

1 **The** burden <note>original: "Onus." In prophetic literature, a "burden" refers to a heavy or solemn message of judgment.</note> of the valley of vision <note>This is a symbolic name for Jerusalem, perhaps referring to the valleys surrounding the city where prophets received visions.</note>. What is the matter with you now, that you have all gone up to the housetops?
2 Full of shouting, a populous city, an exultant city: your slain are not slain by the sword, nor dead in battle.
3 All your princes have fled together, and are bound hard: all who were found are bound together; they have fled far away.
4 Therefore I said: Turn away from me, I will weep bitterly; do not labor to comfort me over the devastation of the daughter of my people.
5 For it is a day of slaughter, and of trampling, and of weeping, to the Lord God of hosts in the valley of vision, searching the wall, and magnificent upon the mountain.
6 And Elam <note>A region in what is now southwest Iran; its soldiers served in the Assyrian army.</note> took the quiver, with the chariot of the horseman, and the shield uncovered the wall.
7 And your chosen valleys shall be full of chariots, and horsemen shall set their seats at the gate.
8 And the covering of Judah shall be revealed, and you shall see in that day the armory of the house of the forest <note>original: "domus saltus." This refers to the "House of the Forest of Lebanon," a building in Jerusalem used as an armory.</note>.
9 And you shall see the breaches of the city of David, for they are multiplied: and you have gathered together the waters of the lower pool,
10 And you have numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and destroyed houses to fortify the wall.
11 And you made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool: and you have not looked up to him who made it, nor seen its maker from afar.
12 And the Lord God of hosts shall call in that day to weeping, and to mourning, to baldness, and to girding with sackcloth:
<margin>† Wisdom 2:6.</margin>
13 And behold joy and gladness, killing calves and slaughtering rams, eating meat and drinking wine: † Let us eat and drink; for tomorrow we shall die.
<margin>Below 56:12. 1 Cor. 15:32.</margin>
14 And the voice of the Lord of hosts was revealed in my ears: If this iniquity shall be forgiven you until you die, says the Lord God of hosts.
15 Thus says the Lord God of hosts: Go, enter in to him who dwells in the tabernacle, to Shebna <note>original: "Sobnam." Shebna was a high-ranking official, often identified as the royal steward or treasurer.</note> the overseer of the temple, and say to him:
16 What are you doing here, or who are you here? Because you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here, you have diligently hewn a memorial on high, a dwelling for yourself in the rock.
17 Behold, the Lord will cause you to be carried away, as a rooster <note>original: "gallus gallinaceus." The Vulgate uses this specific image to describe the forceful tossing away of the official.</note> is carried away, and he will lift you up like a garment.
18 Crowning, he will crown you with tribulation, he will toss you like a ball into a wide and spacious land: there you shall die, and there shall be the chariot of your glory, the shame of the house of your Lord.
19 And I will drive you out from your station, and depose you from your ministry.
20 And it shall come to pass in that day: I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah.
21 And I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt,

<column-break/>

and I will give your power into his hand: and he shall be like a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
<margin>† Revelation 3:7. Job 12:14.</margin>
22 † And I will lay the key of the house of David upon his shoulder: and † he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.
23 And I will fix him as a peg in a faithful place, and he shall be for a throne of glory to his father's house.
24 And they shall hang upon him all the glory of his father's house, different kinds of vessels, every small vessel, from the cups to every musical instrument.
25 In that day, says the Lord of hosts: The peg that was fixed in the faithful place shall be taken away, and it shall be broken, and shall fall, and that which hung upon it shall perish, because the Lord has spoken.

## CHAPTER XXIII.

*The devastation of Tyre for seventy years is foretold because of her pride, and afterwards she shall be restored.*

1 **The** burden of Tyre. Howl, you ships of the sea, for the house is laid waste, from where they were accustomed to come: it is revealed to them from the land of Cyprus <note>original: "Cethim." Kittim or Chittim, usually referring to Cyprus or the Western Mediterranean islands.</note>.
2 Be silent, you who inhabit the island: the merchants of Sidon, crossing over the sea, have filled you.
3 On great waters was the seed of the Nile, the harvest of the river was her revenue: and she became the marketplace of nations.
4 Be ashamed, O Sidon: for the sea says, the strength of the sea: saying: I have not been in labor, nor have I given birth, nor have I nourished young men, nor brought up virgins.
5 When it shall be heard in Egypt, they will be in pain when they hear of Tyre:
6 Cross over the seas, howl, you who inhabit the island:
7 Is not this your city, which boasted from early days in her antiquity? Her own feet shall lead her far away to wander.
8 Who has planned this against Tyre, once crowned, whose merchants were princes, whose traders were the renowned of the earth?
9 The Lord of hosts has planned this, to bring down the pride of all glory, and to lead into disgrace all the renowned of the earth.
10 Pass through your land like a river, O daughter of the sea, there is no girdle <note>Likely referring to a harbor wall or a physical constraint on her movements.</note> for you anymore.
11 He has stretched out his hand over the sea, he has troubled kingdoms: the Lord has given a command against Canaan, to destroy its strongholds.
12 And he said: You shall no longer boast, while suffering oppression, O virgin daughter of Sidon: rise up and cross over to Cyprus <note>original: "Cethim."</note>, even there you shall have no rest.
13 Behold the land of the Chaldeans, such a people was not, Assyria founded it: they have led its strong ones into captivity, they have undermined its houses, they have brought it to ruin.
14 Howl, you ships of the sea, for your strength is laid waste.
15 And it shall come to pass in that day: You shall be forgotten, O Tyre, for seventy years, like the days of one king; but after seventy years, it shall be for Tyre like the song of a harlot.
16 Take a harp, go about the city, O harlot forgotten; play well, sing many songs, that you may be remembered.
17 And it shall be after seventy years: The Lord will visit Tyre, and restore her to her wages, and she shall commit fornication <note>Used here metaphorically for commercial trade with foreign nations.</note> again with all the kingdoms of the world upon the face of the earth.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

*The evils which the Lord will bring upon the whole world because of sins, with the consolation of a remnant added in the meantime: and how terrible the day of divine judgment will be.*

1 **Behold**, the Lord shall lay waste the earth, and strip it, and afflict its face, and scatter its inhabitants.
<margin>† Hosea 4:9</margin>
2 † And it shall be: as with the people, so with the priest; and as with the servant, so with his master; as with the handmaid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the moneylender, so with the borrower; as with the creditor, so with the debtor.
3 With desolation shall the earth be laid waste, and it shall be spoiled with pillage; for the Lord has spoken this word.
4 The earth mourned and faded away, and grew weak; the world faded away, the pride of the people of the earth grew weak.
5 And the earth is infected by its inhabitants; because they have transgressed the laws, they have changed the ordinance, they have broken the everlasting covenant.
6 Therefore a curse shall devour the earth, and its inhabitants shall sin; and therefore its cultivators shall go mad <note>original: "insanient." While some translations use "burned," the Latin implies a state of being driven to madness or ruin.</note>, and few men shall be left.
7 The vintage has mourned, the vine has grown weak, all who were joyful in heart have sighed.
8 The mirth of timbrels has ceased, the noise of the joyful is silent, the sweetness of the harp is still.
9 They shall not drink wine with a song; the drink shall be bitter to those who drink it.
10 The city of vanity <note>original: "civitas vanitatis." This likely refers to a generic city representing worldly chaos or pride.</note> is broken down; every house is shut up, with no one entering.
11 There shall be a crying for wine in the streets; all joy is abandoned; the mirth of the earth is carried away.
12 Desolation is left in the city, and calamity shall oppress the gates.
13 For these things shall be in the midst of the earth, in the midst of the people, as if a few olives that remain should be shaken off the olive tree, or as grapes when the vintage is ended.
14 These shall lift up their voice and give praise; when the Lord shall be glorified, they shall make a joyful noise from the sea.
15 Therefore, in your teachings <note>original: "in doctrinis." Some versions interpret this as "in the fires" or "in the east."</note> glorify the Lord; in the islands of the sea, the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
16 From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the Just One. And I said: My secret is mine, my secret is mine <note>original: "Secretum meum mihi." A difficult Hebrew idiom often translated as "I pine away" or "Woe is me," expressing the prophet's personal distress at the vision.</note>, woe to me! The prevaricators have dealt treacherously, and with the treachery of transgressors they have prevaricated.
17 Fear, and the pit, and the snare are upon you, O inhabitant of the earth.
<margin>† Jeremiah 48:44</margin>
18 And it shall be: † he who flees from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he who rids himself of the pit shall be taken by the snare; for the floodgates from on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth shall be shaken.
19 With breaking shall the earth be broken, with crushing shall the earth be crushed, with commotion shall the earth be moved.

<column-break/>

20 With agitation shall the earth be shaken like a drunkard, and shall be removed like the tent of a single night; and its iniquity shall be heavy upon it, and it shall fall, and shall not rise again.
21 And it shall be: in that day the Lord shall visit <note>In a biblical context, for God to "visit" often means to come in judgment.</note> upon the host of heaven on high, and upon the kings of the earth who are upon the earth.
22 And they shall be gathered together as in the gathering of one bundle into the pit, and they shall be shut up there in prison; and after many days they shall be visited.
23 And the moon shall blush, and the sun shall be confounded, when the Lord of hosts shall reign on Mount Sion and in Jerusalem, and shall be glorified in the sight of his elders.

### CHAPTER XXV.

*The prophet gives thanks to God for His wonderful works, and for the benefits to be bestowed on His people on Mount Sion.*

1 **O Lord**, You are my God; I will exalt You, and I will confess to Your name; for You have done wonderful things, Your ancient designs are faithful, amen.
2 For You have turned the city into a heap, the strong city into a ruin, the house of strangers; so that it is no longer a city, and shall never be built again.
3 Therefore shall the strong people praise You, the city of mighty nations shall fear You.
4 For You have been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress; a hope from the whirlwind, a shadow from the heat; for the blast of the mighty is like a whirlwind beating against a wall.
5 As heat in a thirsty land, You shall bring down the noise of strangers; and as with heat under a burning cloud, You shall make the branch of the mighty to wither.
6 And the Lord of hosts shall make for all peoples on this mountain a feast of fat things, a feast of wine, of fat things full of marrow, of wine purified from the lees.
7 And He shall destroy on this mountain the face of the bond <note>original: "faciem vinculi," referring to the veil or covering of mourning and death that hangs over all people.</note> tied over all peoples, and the web that He has woven over all nations.
8 He shall cast down death forever;
<margin>† Revelation 7:17 and 21:4</margin>
† and the Lord God shall wipe away tears from every face, and the reproach of His people He shall take away from all the earth; for the Lord has spoken it.
9 And it shall be said in that day: Behold, this is our God, we have waited for Him, and He will save us; this is the Lord, we have endured for Him, we shall exult and be joyful in His salvation.
10 For the hand of the Lord shall rest upon this mountain; and Moab shall be threshed under Him, as straw is threshed by a wagon.
11 And He shall stretch forth His hands under him, as a swimmer stretches out to swim; and He shall bring down his glory with the dashing of His hands.
12 And the bulwarks of your high walls shall fall, and be brought low, and shall be pulled down to the ground, even to the dust.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

*A song of thanksgiving for the exaltation of the just and the humiliation of the wicked, and concerning the resurrection of the dead.*

1 **In** that day this song shall be sung in the land of Judah:
Zion, the city of our strength, the Savior; a wall and a bulwark shall be set therein.

2 Open the gates, and the righteous nation that keeps the truth shall enter.
3 The old error has passed away: you will preserve peace; peace, because we have hoped in you.
4 You have hoped in the Lord for eternal ages, in the Lord God, the strong one forever.
5 For he shall bring down those dwelling on high; he shall humble the exalted city: he shall humble it even to the ground, he shall pull it down even to the dust.
6 The foot shall trample it, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy.
7 The path of the just is straight, the track of the just is straight for walking.
8 And in the path of your judgments, O Lord, we have waited for you; your name and your memorial are the desire of the soul.
9 My soul has desired you in the night: but also with my spirit in my innermost heart <note>original: "praecordiis," literally the area around the heart; it implies the seat of deep emotion and thought.</note> I will watch for you in the morning. When you perform your judgments on earth, the inhabitants of the world shall learn justice.
10 Let us have mercy on the wicked, yet he will not learn justice: in the land of the holy ones he has done wicked things, and he shall not see the glory of the Lord.
11 Lord, let your hand be exalted, and let them not see: let the jealous people see and be confounded: and let fire devour your enemies.
12 Lord, you will give us peace: for you have worked all our works for us.
13 O Lord our God, other masters besides you have possessed us; only in you let us remember your name.
14 Let the dying not live, let the giants <note>original: "gigantes," referring to the Rephaim, often understood in this context as the "shades" or the spirits of the dead who cannot rise to trouble the earth again.</note> not rise again: therefore you have visited and crushed them, and destroyed all memory of them.
15 You have been indulgent to the nation, Lord, you have been indulgent to the nation: have you been glorified? You have extended all the borders of the earth.
16 Lord, in distress they sought you; in the tribulation of a murmur <note>original: "murmuris," suggesting a whispered prayer or a low groaning of the spirit.</note> your teaching was with them.
17 Like a woman who conceives, when she approaches childbirth, crying out in her pains, so we have become before your face, Lord.
18 We have conceived, and as it were labored, and brought forth wind <note>original: "spiritum," which can mean spirit or wind; here it signifies a hollow, fruitless labor.</note>: we have not worked salvation on the earth, therefore the inhabitants of the earth have not fallen.
19 Your dead shall live, my slain shall rise again: awake, and give praise, you who dwell in the dust: because your dew is the dew of light, and you shall pull down the land of the giants into ruin.
20 Go, my people, enter into your chambers, shut your doors over you, hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation passes by.

21 † For behold, the Lord will come out of his place to visit the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth against him; and the earth shall reveal her blood, and shall no longer cover her slain.

### CHAPTER XXVII.

*The punishment of Leviathan: the Lord’s fatherly correction of the children of Israel: The fortified city shall be desolated: the children of Israel, having returned from the Assyrians and Egypt, shall worship the Lord in Jerusalem.*

1 **I**n that day the Lord with his hard, and great, and strong sword shall visit Leviathan the bar-serpent <note>original: "serpentem vectem," likely referring to a straight or fleeing serpent.</note>, and upon Leviathan the crooked serpent, and he shall kill the whale <note>original: "cetum," a term for a massive sea creature or monster.</note> that is in the sea.
2 In that day a vineyard of pure wine shall sing to him.

<column-break/>

3 I am the Lord, who keeps it; I will give it to drink suddenly: lest perhaps it be visited against it, I keep it night and day.
4 Indignation is not <note>The word "est" (is) appears to have a strike-through or ink blot over it</note> in me; who will give me thorn and brier in battle: shall I march over it, shall I set it on fire together?
5 Or rather shall he take hold of my strength? He shall make peace with me, peace he shall make with me.
6 Those who enter with violence against Jacob, Israel shall blossom and bud, and they shall fill the face of the world with seed.
7 Has he struck him according to the wound of the one who struck him? Or as he killed those slain by him, so is he slain?
8 In measure against measure, when it is cast away, you shall judge it: he has meditated in his hard spirit through the day of heat.
9 Therefore upon this the iniquity of the house of Jacob shall be forgiven: and this is all the fruit—that his sin should be taken away—when you shall have set all the stones of the altar like crushed stones of ashes; the sacred groves and shrines shall not stand.
10 For the fortified city shall be desolate, the beautiful city shall be left, and shall be abandoned like a wilderness: there the calf shall feed, and there he shall lie down, and consume its treetops.
11 In the drought its harvests shall be crushed, women coming and teaching it: for it is not a wise people, therefore he who made them will not have mercy on them; and he who formed them will not spare them.
12 And it shall be: In that day the Lord shall strike from the channel of the river even to the torrent of Egypt, and you shall be gathered one by one, children of Israel.
13 And it shall be: In that day a great trumpet shall be blown, and those who were lost shall come from the land of the Assyrians, and those who were cast out in the land of Egypt, and they shall worship the Lord in the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

*The Lord threatens the proud and drunken Israelites, because the priests give themselves to drunkenness, and the princes mock the words and threats of the prophets, placing their hope in a lie: concerning the cornerstone to be placed in the foundations of Zion, concerning their punishment, and the consolation of a few good people.*

1 **W**oe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, and to the falling flower, the glory of his exultation, who were on the peak of the richest valley, wandering because of wine.
2 Behold the Lord is powerful and strong, like a rush of hail; a breaking whirlwind, like the rush of many waters overflowing, and sent out over a spacious land.
3 The crown of the pride of the drunkards of Ephraim shall be trampled under feet.
4 And the falling flower of the glory of his exultation, which is upon the peak of the valley of the fat ones, shall be as a first-ripe fruit before the ripeness of autumn, which when he who sees it looks at it, as soon as he has it in his hand, he shall devour it.
5 In that day the Lord of hosts shall be a crown of glory, and a garland of exultation to the remnant of his people:
6 And a spirit of judgment to him who sits in judgment, and strength to those returning from war to the gate.
7 But these also have been ignorant because of wine, and have wandered because of drunkenness: the priest and the prophet

### C A P T E R XXIX.

->*The siege and affliction of Jerusalem, the crushing of the nations besieging it: concerning the sealed book, and the blindness of the Jews: woe is denounced against those deep of heart: he predicts that the remnant of Jacob shall be enlightened and converted to God.*<-

WOE to Ariel, Ariel the city which David took: year is added to year: the solemnities have finished their cycle. <note>Ariel is a symbolic name for Jerusalem, often interpreted as "Lion of God" or "Altar-hearth."</note>
2 And I will trench Ariel around, and it shall be sad and mourning, and it shall be to me as Ariel.
3 And I will surround you like a sphere on every side, and I will cast up a mound against you, and I will place fortifications for your siege.
4 You shall be brought low, you shall speak from the earth, and your speech shall be heard from the ground: and your voice shall be like that of a spirit <note>original: "pythonis," referring to a ventriloquist or a familiar spirit from the underworld</note> from the earth, and your speech shall mutter from the ground.
5 And the multitude of those who winnow you shall be like fine dust: and the multitude of those who have prevailed against you shall be like passing chaff.
6 And it shall happen suddenly, in an instant. From the Lord of hosts it shall be visited with thunder, and shaking of the earth, and a great voice of whirlwind and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire.
7 And the multitude of all the nations that have fought against Ariel shall be like the dream of a vision by night, and all who have campaigned, and besieged, and prevailed against it.
8 And as a hungry man dreams and eats, but when he has awakened, his soul is empty; and as a thirsty man dreams and drinks, and after he has awakened, he is still weary and thirsty, and his soul is empty: so shall be the multitude of all the nations that have fought against Mount Zion.
9 Be astonished, and wonder; waver, and stagger: be drunk, but not with wine; be moved, but not with intoxication.
10 For the Lord has mixed for you a spirit of deep sleep; he will close your eyes; he will cover your prophets and your princes who see visions.
11 And the vision of all things shall be to you like the words of a sealed book; when they give it to a man who knows letters, they shall say: Read this: and he shall answer: I cannot, for it is sealed.
12 And the book shall be given to one who does not know letters, and it shall be said to him: Read: and he shall answer: I do not know letters.
<margin>† Matthew 15:8. Mark 7:6.</margin>

14 Therefore, behold, I will proceed to cause admiration in this people by a great and stupendous miracle: † for wisdom shall perish from its wise men, and the understanding of its prudent men shall be hidden.

### C H A P T E R XXX.

->*A threat against the Jews who, without consulting the Lord while the Assyrians were pressing them, fled to the Egyptians: he denounces a heavy affliction upon them because they were unwilling to hear the warnings of the prophets, but instead sought vain protections: how kind God will be to those who return to him: and concerning the great happiness of those who revere him, and the judgment of the ungodly.*<-

Woe to the rebellious children, says the Lord, that you would carry out a plan, but not from me; and begin a web <note>often interpreted as a woven alliance or treaty</note>, but not by my spirit, that you might add sin upon sin:
2 You who walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth, hoping for help in the strength of Pharaoh, and having confidence in the shadow of Egypt.
3 And the strength of Pharaoh shall be to your confusion, and confidence in the shadow of Egypt to your shame.
4 For your princes were in Tanis, and your messengers reached as far as Hanes.
5 They were all confounded because of a people that could not profit them: they were not for help or for any utility, but for confusion and reproach.
6 The burden of the beasts of the south. In a land of tribulation and distress, from which come the lioness and the lion, the viper and the flying serpent <note>original: "regulus volans," likely referring to a venomous desert snake</note>, they carry their riches upon the shoulders of young asses, and their treasures upon the humps of camels, to a people that shall not be able to profit them.
7 For Egypt shall help in vain and to no purpose; therefore I have cried out concerning this: It is only pride, be still.

11 Take away from me the way, turn aside from me the path, let the Holy One of Israel cease from before our face.

15 For thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel: If you return and rest, you shall be saved: in silence and in hope shall be your strength. And you would not:

23 And rain shall be given to your seed, wherever you shall sow in the land: and the bread of the corn of the earth shall be most plentiful and fat; in that day the lamb shall feed at large in your possession:

### CHAPTER XXXI.

->*He predicts that the Jews, who have abandoned trust in God and flee to the Egyptians and human defenses, shall be consumed along with their helpers; but those returning to the Lord shall be liberated by divine power.*<-

1 Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, trusting in horses, and placing their confidence in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong: and they have not looked to the Holy One of Israel, nor have they sought the Lord.
2 But He, being wise, has brought evil, and has not taken back His words: and He will rise up against the house of the wicked, and against the help of those who work iniquity.
3 Egypt is man, and not God: and their horses are flesh, and not spirit: and the Lord shall stretch out His hand, and the helper shall fall, and he who is helped shall fall, and they shall all be consumed together.
4 For thus says the Lord to me: Just as a lion or a lion's cub roars over its prey, and when a multitude of shepherds comes against him, he will not fear their voice nor be terrified by their numbers: so shall the Lord of hosts descend to fight upon Mount Zion, and upon its hill.
5 Like birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts protect Jerusalem; protecting and delivering, passing over and saving.
6 Return, O children of Israel, just as you had deeply revolted.
7 For in that day every man shall cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made for you as a sin.
8 And the Assyrian shall fall by a sword not of man, and a sword not of a mortal shall devour him, and he shall flee not from the face of the sword: and his young men shall be made to pay tribute.
9 And his strength shall pass away because of terror, and his princes shall flee in fear: says the Lord, whose fire is in Zion, and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

### CHAPTER XXXII.

->*Regarding the king and princes who will reign in justice and the happiness of the subject people; however, future calamity is predicted for the foolish prince and the wealthy women; also, the beauty of peace and wealthy rest is promised to the people of God.*<-

1 Behold, a king shall reign in justice, and princes shall rule in judgment.
2 And a man shall be as a hiding place from the wind, and as one who conceals himself from a storm; like rivers of water in thirst, and the shadow of a projecting rock in a desert land.
3 The eyes of those who see shall not be dim, and the ears of those who hear shall listen diligently.
4 And the heart of fools shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers shall speak quickly and plainly.
5 He who is foolish shall no longer be called a prince, nor shall the deceitful be called great.
6 For the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will work iniquity, to practice hypocrisy and speak deceitfully to the Lord, to leave the soul of the hungry empty and take away drink from the thirsty.
7 The instruments of the deceitful are very evil: for he has devised schemes to destroy the meek with lying words, even when the poor man speaks what is right.
8 But the prince shall devise things worthy of a prince, and he shall stand above the leaders.
9 Rise up, you wealthy women, and hear my voice: you confident daughters, give ear to my speech.
10 For after a year and some days, you who are confident shall be troubled: for the vintage is finished, the gathering shall come no more.
11 Be astonished, you wealthy women; be troubled, you confident ones: strip yourselves and be ashamed, gird your loins <note>A reference to putting on sackcloth as a sign of mourning</note>.
12 Mourn upon your breasts, for the delightful countryside, for the fertile vineyard.
13 Upon the ground of my people shall thorns and briars come up: how much more upon all the houses of joy in the exulting city?
14 For the house is abandoned, the multitude of the city is left behind; darkness and groping have come upon the caves forever. The joy of wild asses, the pastures of flocks,
15 Until the spirit is poured upon us from on high: and the desert shall become a fruitful field <note>original: "charmel," a term for fertile garden land or an orchard</note>, and the fruitful field shall be regarded as a forest.
16 And judgment shall dwell in the wilderness, and justice shall sit in the fruitful field.
17 And the work of justice shall be peace, and the service of justice shall be silence and security forever.
18 And my people shall sit in the beauty of peace, and in the tabernacles of confidence, and in wealthy rest.
19 But there shall be hail when the forest falls, and the city shall be deeply humbled.
20 Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, sending out the feet of the ox and the ass.

# CHAPTER XXXIII.

->*He speaks collectively of the downfall of Sennacherib, and the liberation of the Jews, and the exaltation of divine power: he inveighs against hypocrites: [describing] what kind of people they must be who are to dwell with the Lord in the high places. Jerusalem truly shall be a wealthy dwelling, in which the Lord, our king and lawgiver, shall be magnified.*<-

1 Woe to you who plunder, shall you not also be plundered? And you who despise, shall you not also be despised? When you have finished plundering, you shall be plundered: when, weary, you cease to despise, you shall be despised.
2 O Lord, have mercy on us: for we have waited for you: be our arm in the morning, and our salvation in the time of trouble.
3 At the voice of the angel the people fled, and at your exaltation the nations were scattered.
4 And your spoils shall be gathered together as the locust <note>original: "bruchus," referring to a wingless locust or its larva</note> is gathered, as when the trenches have been filled with it.
5 The Lord is magnified, for He has dwelt on high: He has filled Zion with judgment and justice.
6 And there shall be faith in your times: the riches of salvation are wisdom and knowledge: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.
7 Behold, those who see shall cry out without, the angels of peace <note>likely referring to ambassadors or messengers seeking peace</note> shall weep bitterly.
8 The ways are made desolate, the traveler has ceased on the path, the covenant is made void, he has rejected the cities, he has no regard for men.
9 The earth has mourned and languished: Lebanon is confounded and has grown foul, and Sharon is become like a desert: and Bashan and Carmel are shaken.
10 Now will I arise, says the Lord: now will I be exalted, now will I be lifted up.
11 You shall conceive heat, you shall bring forth stubble: your breath like fire shall devour you.
12 And the people shall be as the ashes of a fire, thorns gathered together shall be burnt with fire.
13 Hear, you who are far off, what I have done, and you who are near, acknowledge my strength.
14 The sinners in Zion are terrified, trembling has seized the hypocrites. Which of you can dwell with devouring fire? Which of you shall dwell with everlasting burnings?
<margin>† Psalm 14:2</margin>
15 He who walks in justices, and speaks the truth, who rejects greed from oppression, and shakes his hands from every bribe, who stops his ears lest he hear of blood, and closes his eyes lest he see evil.
16 This man shall dwell on high, the fortifications of rocks shall be his height: bread is given to him, his waters are sure.
17 His eyes shall see the King in His beauty, they shall behold the land from afar.
<margin>† 1 Cor. 1:20</margin>
18 Your heart shall meditate on fear: where is the learned man? Where is he who ponders the words of the law? Where is the teacher of little ones?
19 You shall not see the impudent people, a people of deep speech: so that you cannot understand the eloquence of their tongue, in which there is no wisdom.
20 Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnity: your eyes shall see Jerusalem, a wealthy habitation, a tabernacle that can never be moved: neither shall its nails be taken away forever, and none of its cords shall be broken:

<column-break/>

21 Because only there is our Lord magnificent: a place of rivers, very broad and open streams: no ship of rowers shall pass through it, nor shall any great galley <note>original: "trieris," a trireme or large warship</note> cross it.

24 Neither shall the neighbor say: I am weak: the people who dwell therein shall have their iniquity taken away from them.

# CHAPTER XXXIV.

->*The bitter vengeance of God upon all nations: the crushing and perpetual desolation of Edom is also predicted.*<-

1 Draw near, you nations, and hear; and listen, you peoples: let the earth hear, and its fullness, the world, and everything that sprouts from it.
2 Because the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies: He has killed them, and given them over to slaughter.
3 Their slain shall be cast out, and a stench shall rise from their corpses: the mountains shall melt with their blood.
4 And all the host of heaven shall rot, and the heavens shall be rolled up like a book: and all their host shall fall away, as the leaf falls from the vine and from the fig tree.
5 Because my sword is inebriated in heaven: behold, it shall descend upon Edom <note>original: "Idumæam"</note>, and upon the people of my slaughter, for judgment.
6 The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made thick with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the blood of marrow-filled rams: for the sacrifice of the Lord is in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
7 And the unicorns <note>original: "unicornes," usually referring to wild oxen in a biblical context</note> shall descend with them, and the bulls with the mighty: their land shall be soaked with blood, and their ground with the fat of the greasy ones.
8 Because it is the day of the Lord's vengeance, the year of retribution for the judgment of Zion.
9 And its torrents shall be turned into pitch, and its soil into sulfur: and its land shall become burning pitch.
10 It shall not be extinguished night or day, its smoke shall go up forever: from generation to generation it shall be desolate, for ages of ages no one shall pass through it.
11 And the bittern <note>original: "onocrotalus," sometimes translated as pelican</note> and the hedgehog <note>original: "ericius"</note> shall possess it: the ibis and the raven shall dwell in it: and a measuring line shall be stretched over it to reduce it to nothing, and a plumb-line unto desolation.
12 Its nobles shall not be there: they shall rather call upon the king, and all its princes shall be reduced to nothing.
13 And thorns and nettles shall spring up in its houses, and the buckthorn <note>original: "paliurus," a thorny shrub</note> in its fortifications: and it shall be a lair of dragons <note>original: "draconum," likely referring to jackals or serpents</note>, and a pasture for ostriches.
14 And demons shall meet with satyrs <note>original: "onocentauris," literally ass-centaurs</note>, and the hairy one <note>original: "pilosus," often understood as a wild goat or satyr</note> shall cry out to his fellow: there the night-monster <note>original: "lamia," a mythological creature</note> has lain down, and found rest for herself.
15 There the hedgehog had its den, and nourished its young, and dug around, and cherished them in its shadow: there the kites were gathered together, one to another.
16 Seek diligently in the book of the Lord and read: not one of them was missing, one [has not sought] the other...

### CHAPTER XXXV.

->*Concerning the future consolation, joy, security, and perpetual happiness of those who shall believe in Christ.*<-

1 **T**he desert and the pathless land shall be glad, and the wilderness shall rejoice, and shall flourish like the lily.
2 Budding, it shall bud, and shall rejoice with joy and praise: the glory of Lebanon is given to it: the beauty of Carmel and Sharon, they themselves shall see the glory of the Lord, and the beauty of our God.
3 Strengthen the slack hands, and firm up the weak knees.
4 Say to the faint-hearted: Take courage, and do not fear: behold, your God will bring the vengeance of retribution: God himself will come and save you.
5 Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
6 Then shall the lame man leap like a hart <note>a male deer</note>, and the tongue of the mute shall be free: for waters are broken out in the desert, and streams in the wilderness.
7 And that which was dry land shall become a pool, and the thirsty land shall become springs of water. In the dens where dragons <note>original: "dracones," often referring to jackals or serpents in a desolate place</note> used to dwell, there shall rise the greenness of the reed and the bulrush.
8 And a path and a way shall be there, and it shall be called the Holy Way: the defiled shall not pass over it, and this shall be a straight path for you, so that even fools shall not wander astray upon it.
9 No lion shall be there, nor shall any evil beast go up by it, nor be found there; but those who have been delivered shall walk there.
10 And the redeemed by the Lord shall return, and shall come into Zion with praise, and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and mourning shall flee away.

### CHAPTER XXXVI.

->*Sennacherib, having captured the fortified cities of Judah, sends Rabshakeh to take Jerusalem: with various insults hurled at Hezekiah and blasphemies against God, he exhorts the people of Jerusalem to surrender.*<-

<margin>
4 Kings 18:13 <note>Today known as 2 Kings</note>
2 Chronicles 32:1
Sirach 48:20
</margin>
1 **A**nd it came to pass in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, that Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, came up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and took them.
2 And the king of the Assyrians sent Rabshakeh <note>a high-ranking military title, often rendered as "Chief Cup-bearer"</note> from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a great army, and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool on the way to the Fuller’s Field.
3 And there went out to him Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder.
4 And Rabshakeh said to them: Say to Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you trust?
5 Or by what counsel or strength do you intend to rebel? In whom do you have confidence, that you have revolted from me?
6 Behold, you trust in this broken staff of a reed,

<column-break/>

upon Egypt: which if a man leans upon it, it will go into his hand and pierce it: so is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all who trust in him.
7 But if you answer me: We trust in the Lord our God: is it not He whose high places and altars Hezekiah has taken away, and said to Judah and Jerusalem: You shall worship before this altar?
8 And now, deliver yourself up to my lord the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, and you will not be able on your part to provide riders for them.
9 And how will you withstand the face of even one judge of the least of my lord's servants? But if you trust in Egypt, in chariots, and in horsemen:
10 And now, have I come up to this land to destroy it without the Lord's will? The Lord said to me: Go up against this land, and destroy it.
11 Then Eliakim, and Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh: Speak to your servants in the Syrian language <note>Aramaic, the international language of diplomacy at the time</note>: for we understand it: do not speak to us in the Jews' language <note>Hebrew</note> in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.
12 And Rabshakeh said to them: Has my lord sent me to your lord and to you, to speak all these words, and not rather to the men who sit on the wall, that they may eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?
13 Then Rabshakeh stood and cried with a loud voice in the Jews' language, and said: Hear the words of the great king, the king of the Assyrians.
14 Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to deliver you.
15 And do not let Hezekiah give you confidence in the Lord, saying: The Lord will surely deliver us, this city shall not be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.
16 Do not listen to Hezekiah: for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me <note>an idiom for making peace or surrendering</note>, and come out to me, and eat every one of his own vine, and every one of his own fig tree: and drink every one the water of his own cistern,
17 Until I come and take you away to a land that is like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
18 Let not Hezekiah disturb you, saying: The Lord will deliver us. Have any of the gods of the nations delivered their own land from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
19 Where is the god of Hamath and Arpad? Where is the god of Sepharvaim? Have they delivered Samaria from my hand?
20 Who is there among all the gods of these lands that has delivered his country out of my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?
21 But they held their peace, and did not answer him a word. For the king had commanded, saying: You shall not answer him.
22 Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph, the recorder, went in to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and told him the words of Rabshakeh.

# CHAPTER XXXVII.

*Hezekiah is dismayed on account of the blasphemies of both Rabshakeh and Sennacherib; he sends word to Isaiah so that he might entreat the Lord, who, strengthening him, promises divine aid: and after the army of Sennacherib was slain by an angel, he himself is killed by his own sons.*

<margin>4 Kings 19:1 <note>This refers to the parallel account found in the historical book of 2 Kings in modern Bibles.</note></margin>
**1** And it came to pass, when King Hezekiah <note>original: "Ezechias"</note> had heard it, he tore his garments, and clothed himself in sackcloth <note>a coarse fabric worn as a sign of mourning or repentance</note>, and entered into the house of the Lord.
**2** And he sent Eliakim, who was over the household, and Shebna <note>original: "Sobnam"</note> the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
**3** And they said to him: Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of tribulation, and of correction, and of blasphemy: for the children have come to the birth, and there is no strength to bring them forth.
**4** If in any way the Lord your God might hear the words of Rabshakeh <note>original: "Rabsacis," the chief cup-bearer and royal messenger of the Assyrian king</note>, whom the king of the Assyrians his lord has sent to blaspheme the living God, and to reproach with the words which the Lord your God has heard: lift up your prayer therefore for the remnant that are found.
**5** And the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
**6** And Isaiah said to them: Thus shall you say to your lord: Thus says the Lord: Do not fear because of the words which you have heard, with which the servants of the king of the Assyrians have blasphemed me.
**7** Behold, I will send a spirit upon him, and he shall hear a rumor, and shall return to his own land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.
**8** And Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of the Assyrians warring against Libnah <note>original: "Lobnam"</note>. For he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
**9** And he heard concerning Tirhakah <note>original: "Tharaca"</note> king of Ethiopia, people saying: He has come out to fight against you. And when he had heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying:
**10** Thus shall you say to Hezekiah king of Judah, speaking: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you, saying: Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.
**11** Behold, you have heard all that the kings of the Assyrians have done to all the lands which they have subverted, and can you be delivered?
**12** Did the gods of the nations deliver those whom my fathers subverted: Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the children of Eden who were in Telassar?
**13** Where is the king of Hamath <note>original: "Emath"</note>, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena <note>original: "Ana"</note>, and of Ivvah <note>original: "Ava"</note>?
**14** And Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers, and read them, and went up into the house of the Lord, and Hezekiah spread them out before the Lord.
**15** And Hezekiah prayed to the Lord, saying:
**16** Lord of hosts <note>original: "exercituum," literally 'of armies'</note>, God of Israel, who sits upon the cherubim: you alone are the God of all the kingdoms of the earth, you have made heaven and earth.

**18** Truly, O Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have laid waste the lands, and their regions.
**19** And they have cast their gods into the fire: for they were not gods, but the works of the hands of men, wood and stone: and they have broken them to pieces.
**20** And now, O Lord our God, save us from his hand: and let all the kingdoms of the earth know that you alone are the Lord.

**23** Whom have you reproached, and whom have you blasphemed, and against whom have you exalted your voice, and lifted up the height of your eyes? Against the Holy One of Israel.

**25** I have dug, and drunk water, and with the sole of my foot I have dried up all the rivers of the embankments.
**26** Have you not heard what I have done to it from of old? From the days of antiquity I have formed it: and now I have brought it to pass: and it has served for the uprooting of resisting hills, and of fortified cities.
**27** Their inhabitants, with a shortened hand, have trembled and been confounded: they became like the grass of the field, and the green herb of the pasture, and the grass of the rooftops, which withered before it could ripen.
**28** I have known your dwelling, and your going out, and your coming in, and your madness against me.
**29** When you raged against me, your pride ascended into my ears: I will therefore put a ring in your nose, and a bit in your lips, and I will lead you back by the way by which you came.
**30** And this shall be a sign to you: Eat this year what grows of itself, and in the second year eat of the fruits: but in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them.
**31** And that which shall be saved of the house of Judah, and that which remains, shall strike root downward, and bear fruit upward:
**32** For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and salvation from mount Zion: the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.
**33** Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians: He shall not enter into this city, and he shall not shoot an arrow there, and the shield shall not occupy it, and he shall not cast up a rampart around it.

### CHAPTER XXXIX.

*When Hezekiah had shown his treasures to the messengers sent by the king of Babylon, he is forewarned by Isaiah of their future removal to Babylon.*

<margin>† 4 Kings 20:12</margin> 1 At that time Merodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and gifts to Hezekiah: for he had heard that he had been sick and was recovered.
2 And Hezekiah rejoiced over them, and showed them the storehouse of his aromatics, and of silver, and gold, and perfumes, and precious ointment, and all the storehouses of his furniture, and all things that were found in his treasures. 4 And he said: What have they seen in your house? And Hezekiah said: They have seen all things that are in my house: there was nothing in my treasures that I have not shown them.
5 And Isaiah said to Hezekiah: Hear the word of the Lord of hosts.
6 Behold, the days shall come, and all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have laid up in store until this day, shall be carried away to Babylon: nothing shall be left, says the Lord.
7 And of your sons, who shall issue from you, whom you shall beget, they shall take away, and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
8 And Hezekiah said to Isaiah: The word of the Lord, which he has spoken, is good. And he said: Let there only be peace and truth in my days.

### CHAPTER XLI.

->*The Lord contends with idol-worshippers regarding His power and the various magnificent favors shown to the Jewish people: by these He proves His might and His kindness toward humanity, while simultaneously demonstrating the helplessness of idols and the emptiness of those who worship them.*<-

1 Let the islands keep silence before me, and the nations change their strength: let them come near, and then speak, let us come together to judgment.
2 Who has raised up the just man from the east, and called him to follow him? He shall give the nations in his sight, and he shall obtain kings: he shall give them as dust to his sword, as stubble driven by the wind to his bow.
3 He shall pursue them, he shall pass in peace, the path shall not appear at his feet.

† Below 41:6 & 48:12 & Revelation 1:8, 17 & 22:13.
</margin>
4 Who has wrought these things, and done them, calling the generations from the beginning? I the Lord, † I am the first and the last.
5 The islands saw, and feared, the ends of the earth were astonished, they drew near, and came.
6 Every one shall help his neighbor, and say to his brother: Be of good courage.
7 The coppersmith striking with the hammer encouraged him that forged at that time, saying: It is good for soldering: and he strengthened it with nails, that it should not be moved.
8 And you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend:
9 In whom I have taken you from the ends of the earth, and from its remote parts have called you, and said to you: You are my servant, I have chosen you, and have not cast you away.
10 Fear not, for I am with you: turn not aside, for I am your God: I have strengthened you, and have helped you, and the right hand of my just one has upheld you.
11 Behold all who fight against you shall be confounded and ashamed: they shall be as if they were not, and the men shall perish who contradict you.
12 You shall seek them, and shall not find them, your rebellious men: they shall be as if they were not: and as a consumption <note>original: "consumptio"; a wasting away or total destruction</note>, the men that war against you.
13 For I am the Lord your God, taking you by the hand, and saying to you: Fear not, I have helped you.

### CHAPTER XLII.

> *The Father is well pleased in his son Christ, whose virtues and the works he is to perform the prophet explains, exhorting all nations to praise and thanksgiving: he adds also that the wicked, idolaters, and the ungrateful shall be severely punished by the Lord, complaining greatly of the ingratitude of the servants of God.*

<margin>Matthew 12:18.</margin>
1 Behold my servant, I will receive him: my chosen one, my soul is well pleased in him: I have sent my spirit upon him, he shall bring forth judgment to the nations.
2 He shall not cry out, nor show favoritism to any person, nor shall his voice be heard abroad.
3 A bruised reed he shall not break, and a smoking wick <note>original: "linum fumigans"</note> he shall not quench: he shall bring forth judgment in truth.

### C H A P T E R  XLIII.

*He makes the believing people secure, promising that their future multiplication will come from the whole world, with a narration of God's past and future benefits toward his people, by which he proves himself to be the only true God: adding a grave expostulation against the ingratitude of the Jews.*

1 **A**ND now thus says the Lord who created you, Jacob, and formed you, Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you, and I have called you by your name: you are mine.
2 When you pass through the waters, I will be with you, and the rivers shall not cover you: when you walk in the fire, you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not burn in you.
3 Because I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your savior; I have given Egypt as your ransom <note>original: "propitiationem"; here meaning a price paid to deliver someone</note>, Ethiopia and Seba for you.

5 Do not fear, for I am with you: I will lead your offspring from the east, and gather you from the west.
6 I will say to the north: Give up: and to the south: Do not hold back: bring my sons from afar, and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
7 And everyone who calls upon my name, I have created him for my glory, I have formed him, and I have made him.
8 Bring out the blind people, even those who have eyes; and the deaf, even those who have ears.
9 All the nations are gathered together, and the tribes are collected: who among you shall announce this, and make us hear the first things? Let them bring their witnesses, let them be justified, and let them hear, and say: It is the truth.
10 You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen: so that you may know, and believe me, and understand that I myself am he. Before me no God was formed, and after me there shall be none.

*God comforts his people, being about to pour out his spirit upon them, and waters upon the thirsty: he is the first and the last and the only God, the creator and moderator of all things: the great vanity, even the stupidity, of idols, their craftsmen, and idolaters is clearly exposed: accordingly, the people are called back from idols to God, in whose hand are all things.*

3 For I will pour out waters upon the thirsty, and streams upon the dry ground: I will pour out my spirit upon your seed, and my blessing upon your offspring.
4 And they shall spring up among the grass, like willows by the flowing waters.
5 This one shall say: I am the Lord’s: and another shall call on the name of Jacob: and this one shall write with his hand: To the Lord: and shall be likened to the name of Israel.

*A prophecy concerning Cyrus and the victories to be granted to him by God, including a rebuke because he does not acknowledge God in these matters, though He alone is God, the Lord of all, whom no one can contradict. ### C H A P T E R XLVI.

*The vanity of idols is shown, and their destruction is foretold; the Jews with the remnant of Israel are called back to God, showing God’s great kindness toward them: a heavy rebuke is added for their ingratitude and idolatry: and they are urged to return to him, who alone knows and can do all things, promising them salvation through his son.*

1 Bel is broken, Nebo <note>Bel and Nebo were two of the primary deities of the Babylonian pantheon.</note> is crushed: their idols are placed upon beasts and cattle, your heavy burdens even unto weariness.

2 They have decayed and are crushed together: they could not save the one who carried them, and their soul <note>original: "anima"; here it refers to the very essence or "life" of the idols being taken away</note> shall go into captivity.

3 Listen to me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, you who are carried from my womb, who are borne from my belly.

5 To whom have you likened me, and made me equal, and compared me, and made me similar?

6 You who take gold from the bag, and weigh out silver with a scale: hiring a goldsmith to make a god: and they fall down and worship.

### C H A P T E R XLVII.

*The humiliation and crushing of Babylon is foretold because of her pride, arrogance, and cruelty toward her Jewish captives: and because she placed her hope in sorceries, astrologers, and enchanters.*

1 Come down, sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon; sit on the ground: there is no throne for the daughter of the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans were the ethnic group that formed the ruling class of the Neo-Babylonian Empire.</note>, for you shall no longer be called soft and tender.

2 Take the millstone and grind flour: uncover your shame, lay bare your shoulder, reveal your legs, cross the rivers.

<margin>
† Nahum 3:5.
</margin>
3 † Your nakedness shall be revealed, and your disgrace shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and no man shall resist me.

4 Our Redeemer, the Lord of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.

5 Sit in silence, and enter into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for you shall no longer be called the mistress of kingdoms.

6 I was angry with my people, I have profaned my inheritance, and given them into your hand: you showed them no mercy: you have laid your yoke very heavily upon the aged.

7 And you said: "I shall be a mistress forever." You did not take these things to heart, nor did you remember your end.

<margin>
† Revelation 18:7.
</margin>
8 And now hear these things, you who are delicate and dwell confidently, who say in your heart: † "I am, and there is no one else besides me; I shall not sit as a widow, nor shall I know the loss of children."

<margin>
† Below 51:19.
</margin>
9 † These two things shall come upon you suddenly in one day, the loss of children and widowhood: they have all come upon you because of the multitude of your sorceries, and because of the great hardness of your enchanters.

10 And you had confidence in your wickedness, and said: "There is no one who sees me." Your wisdom and your knowledge, this has deceived you. And you said in your heart: "I am, and there is no other besides me."

11 Evil shall come upon you, and you will not know its origin: and calamity shall fall upon you, which you will not be able to atone for: misery shall come upon you suddenly, which you will not know.

12 Stand now with your enchanters, and with the multitude of your sorceries, in which you have labored from your youth, if perhaps it may profit you, or if you can become stronger.

13 You have failed in the multitude of your counsels: let the astrologers <term>augures: those who predict the future by observing signs in the sky</term> of the heavens stand and save you, they who gazed at the stars and counted the months, that they might announce the things to come to you.

14 Behold, they have become like stubble, the fire has burned them: they shall not deliver their soul from the power of the flame: there are no coals to warm them, nor a hearth to sit by.

15 Thus have the things become to you in which you have labored: your merchants from your youth, each one has wandered in his own way; there is no one to save you.

### CHAPTER XLVIII.

->*The Lord rebukes the hypocrisy, ingratitude, and stubbornness of the Jews; showing that He, and not idols, had announced future events and fulfilled them: nevertheless, for the sake of His own name, He will spare them: and thus He kindly calls them back to Himself, proving that He alone is the true God, aware of all things, and the redeemer and governor of His people: also lamenting their transgression of His commandments, by the observance of which they would have been happy.*<-

1 Hear these things, O house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, and have come forth from the waters of Judah, who swear by the name of the Lord, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in justice.
2 For they are named after the holy city, and are stayed upon the God of Israel: the Lord of hosts is his name.
3 The former things I declared of old, and they went forth from my mouth, and I made them heard: suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
4 For I knew that you are stubborn, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead is bronze.
5 I foretold it to you from of old: before they came to pass I showed them to you, lest perhaps you should say: "My idols have done these things, and my carved images and my molten images have commanded them."
6 You have heard, see it all: but have you announced even one? I have shown you new things from this time, even hidden things that you do not know:
7 They are created now, and not from of old: even before this day, you did not hear them, lest perhaps you should say: "Behold, I knew them."
8 You have neither heard, nor known, nor was your ear opened of old: for I know that you will surely deal treacherously, and I called you a transgressor from the womb.
9 For my name’s sake I will put my wrath far off: and for my praise I will curb you, lest you perish.
10 Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of poverty <note>original: "camino paupertatis" — elsewhere translated as the furnace of affliction or trial</note>.

13 My hand also founded the earth, and my right hand measured the heavens: I will call them, and they shall stand together.
14 Assemble yourselves, all of you, and hear: who among them has announced these things? The Lord has loved him, he will perform his will in Babylon, and his arm shall be on the Chaldeans.
15 I, even I, have spoken, and I have called him: I have brought him, and his way is made prosperous.
16 Come near to me, and hear this: I have not spoken in secret from the beginning: from the time before it was done, I was there: and now the Lord God has sent me, and his spirit.
17 Thus says the Lord your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the Lord your God who teaches you profitable things, governing you in the way in which you walk.
18 O that you had attended to my commandments: your peace would have been like a river, and your justice like the waves of the sea.
19 And your seed would have been as the sand, and the offspring of your womb like the pebbles thereof: his name would not have perished, nor would it have been worn away from before my face.

### CHAPTER XLIX.

->*Christ is appointed as the leader of the nations and of the Jews who are to be saved, and he is given as a covenant for the people to be called from every part of the world: and having shown the great happiness of those who believe in Christ, he exhorts them to give thanks: he also kindly consoles Zion, which complained that she was forsaken by God: promising that she would be glorious throughout the whole world, with all people flocking to her, and her enemies being crushed.*<-

### CHAPTER L.

->*It is not through God's lack of power, but because of their own iniquities, that the synagogue <note>Refers here to the Jewish community that rejected Christ, as interpreted by the period's theologians</note> remains rejected, refusing to receive Christ, who omitted nothing that ought to have been done to be received by her: indeed, out of love for her, he gave himself up to shameful afflictions: and therefore he announces that the synagogue shall perish in sorrows.*<-

1 Thus says the Lord: What is this bill of your mother's divorce, by which I have put her away? Or who is my creditor, to whom I sold you? Behold, you are sold for your iniquities, and for your wicked deeds I have put your mother away.
<margin>† Below 59:1.</margin> 
2 Because I came, and there was no man: I called, and there was none that would hear. † Has my hand been shortened and made little, that I cannot redeem? Or is there no strength in me to deliver? Behold, at my rebuke I will make the sea a desert, I will turn the rivers into dry land: the fish shall rot for want of water, and shall die for thirst.
3 I will clothe the heavens with darkness, and will make sackcloth their covering.
4 The Lord has given me a learned tongue, that I should know how to sustain him that is weary with a word: he awakens me in the morning, in the morning he awakens my ear, that I may hear him as a teacher.

<column-break/>

5 The Lord God has opened my ear, and I do not resist: I have not gone backward.
<margin>† Matthew 26:67.</margin> 
6 † I have given my body to the strikers, and my cheeks to those who plucked them: I have not turned away my face from those who rebuked me and spit upon me.

<margin>† Romans 8:33.</margin>

11 Behold, all you that kindle a fire, encompassed with flames, walk in the light of your fire, and in the flames which you have kindled: this is done to you by my hand, you shall sleep in sorrows.

### CHAPTER LI.

->*He exhorts Zion by the example of Abraham, to whom God fulfilled his promises, so that she herself may surely trust that she will receive the promised consolation from God: he discusses at length the consolation, salvation, and great happiness of Zion (that is, the Church) to come through Christ, and the Evangelical law, and the humiliation of the enemies of the Church.*<-

1 Hear me, you that follow what is just, and seek the Lord: look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the hole of the pit from which you were dug out.
2 Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you: for I called him when he was but one, and blessed him, and multiplied him.
3 Therefore the Lord will comfort Zion, and will comfort all her ruins: and he will make her desert like a place of delights, and her wilderness like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness shall be found in her, thanksgiving and the voice of praise.
4 Attend to me, my people, and listen to me, my tribe: for a law shall go forth from me, and my judgment shall rest as a light to the nations.
5 My Just One is near at hand, my Savior has gone forth, and my arms shall judge the people: the islands shall look for me, and shall wait for my arm.
<margin>† Psalm 36:3</margin>

<margin>† Psalm 36:3</margin> 
7 Hear me, you that know what is just, my people † in whose heart is my law: fear not the reproach of men, and be not afraid of their blasphemies.
8 For the worm shall eat them up like a garment, and the moth shall consume them like wool: but my salvation shall be forever, and my justice from generation to generation.
9 Arise, arise, put on strength, O arm of the Lord: arise as in the days of old, in the generations of ages. Have you not struck the proud one <note>original: "superbum," often interpreted as Rahab or Egypt</note>, and wounded the dragon?

12 Therefore I will distribute to him very many, and he shall divide the spoils of the strong, because he delivered his soul unto death, and was counted among the wicked; and he himself bore the sins of many, † and prayed for the transgressors.

# C H A P T E R LIV.

*He invites the Church to rejoice, because she shall be more numerous from among the Gentiles than the Synagogue once was; and being spread throughout the world, she shall live in security under the perpetual protection of God, having forgotten her old calamity. He also describes how she shall be built of precious stones, founded in justice; and all within her shall be taught by God, enjoying a multitude of peace.*

<margin>Luke 23:29; Galatians 4:27.</margin>
1 Praise, O barren woman who does not bear; sing praise, and shout for joy, you who did not give birth, for many are the children of the deserted woman, more than of her who has a husband, says the Lord.
2 Enlarge the place of your tent, and stretch out the skins of your tabernacles; do not spare them. Make your cords long, and strengthen your stakes.
3 For you shall penetrate to the right and to the left; and your offspring shall inherit the nations, and shall inhabit the deserted cities.
4 Do not fear, for you shall not be confounded, nor shall you blush; for you shall not be ashamed, because you shall forget the confusion of your youth, and you shall no longer remember the reproach of your widowhood.
<margin>† Luke 1:32.</margin>
5 For he who made you shall rule over you, † the Lord of Hosts is his name; and your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, shall be called the God of all the earth.
6 For the Lord has called you like a woman forsaken and grieving in spirit, and like a wife cast off from her youth, says your God.
7 For a small moment I have forsaken you, but with great mercies I will gather you.
8 In a moment of indignation I hid my face a little while from you, but with everlasting mercy I have had pity on you, says the Lord your Redeemer.
<margin>† Genesis 9:11.</margin>
9 † This is to me as in the days of Noah, to whom I swore that I would no longer bring the waters of Noah over the earth; so I have sworn not to be angry with you, nor to rebuke you.
10 For the mountains shall be moved, and the hills shall tremble; but my mercy shall not depart from you, and the covenant of my peace shall not be moved, says the Lord who has mercy on you.
11 Poor little one, tossed by the storm, with-

<column-break/>

out any consolation. Behold, I will lay your stones in order, and I will found you upon sapphires,
12 And I will make your bulwarks of jasper, and your gates of carved stones, and all your borders of desirable stones.
<margin>† John 6:45.</margin>
13 † All your children shall be taught by the Lord; and great shall be the peace of your children.
14 And you shall be founded in justice; stay far from oppression, for you shall not fear; and from terror, for it shall not come near you.
15 Behold, a neighbor shall come, who was not with me; the stranger who was once yours shall be joined to you. <note>original: "accola... advena" — The Latin text here implies the gathering of outsiders and foreigners into the community.</note>

17 Every instrument that is formed against you shall not prosper; and every tongue that resists you in judgment, you shall judge. This is the inheritance of the servants of the Lord, and their justice is with me, says the Lord.

*Calling all to the faith, he promises an abundance of spiritual gifts: the wicked are recalled from their sins, as the Lord is merciful and true in his promises. Concerning the progress of the preaching of the Gospel, and the happiness of the believers.*

1 All you who thirst, come to the waters; and you who have no money, hurry, buy, and eat. Come, buy wine and milk without money and without any exchange.

8 For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, says the Lord.
9 For as the heavens are exalted above the earth, so are my ways exalted above your ways, and my thoughts above your thoughts.
10 And as the rain and the snow descend from heaven and do not return there, but soak the earth and water it, making it to spring forth and giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater;
11 So shall my word be, which goes forth from my mouth: it shall not return to me empty, but it shall do whatever I willed, and it shall prosper in the things for which I sent it.
12 For you shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace; the mountains and the hills shall sing praise before you, and all the trees of the country shall clap their hands.
