## CHAPTER LVI.

*The Lord encourages everyone of every nation or condition to keep His commandments; comfort for righteous eunuchs: the house of God is a house of prayer; a grave rebuke and threat against the shepherds of Jerusalem, whom He calls blind and mute, shameless dogs.*

<margin>Wisdom 1</margin> Thus says the Lord: Keep judgment, and do justice: because my salvation is near to come, and my justice to be revealed.

2 Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who shall take hold of it: keeping the Sabbath so as not to profane it, keeping his hands from doing any evil.

3 And let not the son of the stranger, who adheres to the Lord, speak, saying: "The Lord will divide and separate me from His people." And let not the eunuch <note>In ancient society, eunuchs were often excluded from religious assemblies; here, Isaiah prophesies their full inclusion.</note> say: "Behold, I am a dry tree."

4 For thus says the Lord to the eunuchs: They who shall keep my Sabbaths, and shall choose the things that I have willed, and shall hold fast to my covenant:

5 I will give to them in my house, and within my walls, a place and a name better than sons and daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, which shall not perish.

6 And the children of the stranger, who adhere to the Lord, to worship Him, and to love His name, to be His servants: everyone who keeps the Sabbath so as not to profane it, and who holds fast to my covenant:

<margin>Jeremiah 7:11; Matthew 21:13; Mark 11:17; Luke 19:46.</margin> 7 I will bring them into my holy mountain, and I will make them joyful in my house of prayer: their holocausts and their victims shall please me upon my altar: † for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.

8 Says the Lord God, who gathers the dispersed of Israel: I will still gather others to him, besides those who are gathered.

9 All you beasts of the field, come to devour, all you beasts of the forest.

10 His watchmen are all blind, they are all ignorant: mute dogs, not able to bark, seeing vain things, sleeping, and loving dreams.

11 And most shameless dogs, they have never known satisfaction: the shepherds themselves knew no understanding: all have turned aside into their own way, <margin>† Jeremiah 6:23 and 8:19.</margin> everyone to his own avarice, from the highest even to the least.

12 "Come," they say, "let us take wine, and be filled with drunkenness: and it shall be as it is today, so also tomorrow, and much more abundantly."

## CHAPTER LVII.

*The death of the righteous, and their future rest, is not understood by the wicked, with whom God here disputes over idolatry and their other crimes, announcing they will be humbled: but to the converted, peace and comfort are promised, while the heart of the wicked is like a boiling sea, which has no peace.*

The just man perishes, and there is no one who considers it in his heart: and men of mercy are gathered away <note>original: "colliguntur" — taken away or gathered by death.</note>, because there is no one who understands: for the just man is gathered away from the face of malice.

2 Let peace come, let him rest in his bed who has walked in his uprightness.

<column-break/>

3 But you, come near here, you sons of the sorceress, the seed of the adulterer and the harlot.

4 Upon whom have you made sport? Upon whom have you opened your mouth wide, and put out your tongue? Are you not wicked children, a lying seed?

5 You who comfort yourselves with gods <note>Referring to idols.</note> under every leafy tree, sacrificing little children in the torrents, under the high rocks!

6 In the parts of the torrent is your portion, this is your lot: and to them you have poured out a drink offering, you have offered a sacrifice; shall I not be indignant over these things?

7 Upon a high and lofty mountain you have set your bed, and you went up there to offer victims.

8 And behind the door, and behind the post, you have set up your memorial <note>Private household idols or tokens of pagan worship.</note>: for near me you have uncovered yourself, and have received an adulterer: you have enlarged your bed, and made a covenant with them: you have loved their bed with an open hand.

9 And you have adorned yourself for the king with ointment, and multiplied your perfumes. You sent your legates far off, and you were humbled even to hell.

10 You have labored in the multitude of your ways: you did not say: "I will rest": you have found life for your hand, therefore you did not ask.

11 For whom have you been so anxious and afraid, that you have lied, and have not remembered me, nor thought of me in your heart? For I have been silent, and as one not seeing, and you have forgotten me.

12 I will declare your justice, and your works shall not profit you.

13 When you cry out, let your gathered followers deliver you, but the wind shall carry them all off, a breeze shall take them: but he who has confidence in me shall inherit the land, and shall possess my holy mountain.

<margin>† Below 61:10.</margin> 14 And I will say: † Make a way, provide a path, turn aside from the track, take away the stumbling blocks from the path of my people.

15 For thus says the High and Lofty One, who inhabits eternity: and His name is Holy, dwelling in the high and in the holy place, and with a contrite and humble spirit: to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.

16 For I will not contend forever, nor will I be angry unto the end: because a spirit shall go forth from my face, and I will make the breath of life.

17 Because of the iniquity of his avarice, I was angry, and I struck him: I hid my face from you, and was indignant: and he went wandering in the way of his own heart.

18 I saw his ways, and I healed him, and brought him back, and restored comforts to him, and to those who mourn for him.

19 I created the fruit of the lips, peace, peace to him who is far off, and to him who is near, says the Lord, and I healed him.

20 But the wicked are like a boiling sea, which cannot rest, and its waves overflow into trampling and mud.

<margin>† Above 48:22.</margin> 21 † There is no peace for the wicked, says the Lord God.

### CHAPTER LVIII.

> *He rebukes the hypocrisy of the Jews, showing that their fasting is not acceptable to God: and what things ought to accompany it, which, when applied, bring many benefits to men: how the Sabbath should be celebrated, by setting aside one's own will, and what the reward is for those who celebrate it so.*

Cry out, do not cease, lift up your voice like a trumpet, and announce to my people their wicked deeds, and to the house of Jacob their sins.
2 For they seek me from day to day, and desire to know my ways: like a nation that has done justice, and has not forsaken the judgment of its God: they ask me for the judgments of justice: they desire to draw near to God.
3 "Why have we fasted, and you did not see? Why have we humbled our souls, and you did not notice?" Behold, on the day of your fast your own will is found, and you demand payment from all your debtors.
4 Behold, you fast for quarrels and strife, and you strike with a wicked fist. Do not fast as you have done until this day, so that your cry may be heard on high.
<margin>† Zechariah 7:5.</margin>
5 Is this the kind of fast that I have chosen, for a man to afflict his soul for a day? Is it to bow his head like a hook <note>original: "circulum"; refers to the bending of the head in a circular or hooked fashion to perform a show of humility</note>, and to spread out sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast, and a day acceptable to the Lord?
6 Is not this rather the fast that I have chosen? Loose the bands of wickedness, undo the heavy burdens, let those who are broken go free, and break every yoke.
<margin>† Ezekiel 18:7. Matthew 25:35.</margin>
7 Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the needy and the wanderers into your house: when you see the naked, cover him, and do not despise your own flesh.
8 Then shall your light break forth like the morning, and your health shall rise up quickly, and your justice shall go before your face, and the glory of the Lord shall gather you up.
9 Then you shall call, and the Lord shall hear: you shall cry, and He shall say: "Behold, I am here," if you take away the chain from your midst, and stop pointing the finger, and speaking that which is not profitable.
10 When you pour out your soul for the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light shall rise in the darkness, and your darkness shall be like the noonday.
11 And the Lord will give you rest always, and will fill your soul with brightness, and will deliver your bones, and you shall be like a watered garden, and like a fountain of water whose waters do not fail.
<margin>† Below 61:4.</margin>
12 And the deserts of old shall be built up in you: you shall raise up the foundations of generation after generation: and you shall be called the builder of hedges, turning the paths into rest.
13 If you turn away your foot from the Sabbath, from doing your own will on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight, and the holy of the Lord glorious, and glorify Him while you do not follow your own ways, and your own will is not found, so that you speak your own word:
14 Then you shall delight in the Lord, and I will lift you up above the high places of the earth, and I will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

### CHAPTER LIX.

> *God is powerful and kind to save the Jews, but their iniquities, which the Prophet pursues, prevent them from being heard and saved: because of which they themselves confess they are justly deserted and blinded by God, and afflicted by various evils: concerning the fury of the Lord against evil, and His kindness toward the repentant.*

<margin>Numbers 11:23. Above 50:2.</margin>
Behold, the hand of the Lord is not shortened that it cannot save, nor is His ear heavy that it cannot hear:
2 But your iniquities have divided you from your God, and your sins have hidden His face from you so that He would not hear.
<margin>† Above 1:15.</margin>
3 For your hands are polluted with blood, and your fingers with iniquity: your lips have spoken lies, and your tongue speaks wickedness.
4 There is no one who calls upon justice, nor is there anyone who judges truly: but they trust in nothing, and speak vanities: <margin>† Job 15:35.</margin> they have conceived labor, and brought forth iniquity.
5 They have broken the eggs of asps <note>The "asp" or "viper" here symbolizes the poisonous nature of their deeds</note>, and have woven the webs of spiders: he who eats of their eggs shall die: and that which is warmed shall break forth into a basilisk <note>original: "regulum"; a legendary serpent king whose gaze or breath was lethal</note>.
6 Their webs shall not be for clothing, nor shall they be covered with their works: their works are useless works, and the work of iniquity is in their hands.
<margin>† Proverbs 1:16. Romans 3:15.</margin>
7 Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are useless thoughts: wasting and destruction are in their ways.
8 They have not known the way of peace, and there is no judgment in their steps: their paths are made crooked for them: everyone who treads in them is ignorant of peace.
9 Therefore judgment is far from us, and justice shall not overtake us: we looked for light, and behold darkness, for brightness, and we walked in the dark.
10 We have groped for the wall like the blind, and we have felt our way as if we had no eyes: we have stumbled at noonday as if in the dark, in misty places like the dead.
11 We shall all roar like bears, and moan like mourning doves: we looked for judgment, and it is not; for salvation, and it is far from us.
12 For our iniquities are multiplied before you, and our sins have answered us: because our wicked deeds are with us, and we have known our iniquities.
13 To sin and to lie against the Lord: and we have turned away so that we would not go after the back of our God, that we might speak slander and transgression: we have conceived and spoken from the heart words of falsehood.
14 And judgment is turned backward, and justice has stood far off: because truth has fallen in the street, and equity could not enter.
15 And truth has been forgotten: and he who departed from evil lay open to be a prey: and the Lord saw it, and it appeared evil in His eyes, because there is no judgment.
16 And He saw that there is no man: and He was distressed because there is no one to intervene: and His own arm brought salvation to Him, and His own justice confirmed Him.

### CHAPTER LX.

*The Church is stirred to rejoicing because the glory of the Lord shines forth in her, to which many nations shall draw near; those who do not come to her shall perish. In her shall be found peace, justice, and the praise of God; iniquity shall be taken away, and the Lord shall be to her an everlasting light and glory.*

Arise, shine, O Jerusalem: for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
2 For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and a thick cloud the peoples: but the Lord shall rise upon you, and his glory shall be seen upon you.

6 A flood of camels shall cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah: <note>Midian and Ephah were Arabian peoples associated with the desert caravan trade, here symbolizing the wealth of distant nations flowing toward Jerusalem.</note> all those from Sheba shall come, bringing gold and frankincense, and proclaiming praise to the Lord.
7 All the flocks of Kedar shall be gathered to you, the rams of Nebaioth shall serve you: <note>Kedar and Nebaioth were sons of Ishmael, representing the Arab peoples of the desert; their flocks coming to the Temple signifies universal worship.</note> they shall be offered upon my welcoming altar, and I will glorify the house of my majesty.
8 Who are these, that fly like clouds, and like doves to their windows?
9 For the coastlands wait for me, and the ships of the sea in the first place, to bring your sons from afar; their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the Lord your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
10 And the children of foreigners shall build up your walls, and their kings shall serve you: for in my wrath I struck you, but in my favour I have had mercy on you.

13 The glory of Lebanon shall come to you, the fir tree, the box tree, and the pine together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary: and I will glorify the place of my feet. <note>"The place of my feet" is a reverential expression for the Temple, understood as the footstool of God's throne.</note>

16 You shall suck the milk of the nations, and you shall be nursed at the breast of kings: and you shall know that I am the Lord your Saviour, and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
17 For bronze I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver; and for wood, bronze, and for stones, iron: and I will make your overseers peace, and your rulers justice.

21 And your people shall all be righteous; they shall possess the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, to glorify me.
22 The least shall become a thousand, and the smallest a very strong nation: I am the Lord; in its time I will bring this to pass suddenly.

### CHAPTER LXI.

*He beautifully sets forth the office of Christ the Saviour and the restoration of the human race: also that the nations are to be converted to the faith by the preaching of Christ's ministers: to which is added the consolation of believers and the glory of those ministers. The rejoicing Church wonderfully congratulates herself on her own happiness.*

<margin>Luke 4:18.</margin>
The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me: he has sent me to bring good news to the meek, to heal the broken-hearted, and to proclaim freedom to captives, and release to those who are imprisoned: <note>Jesus quotes this very verse in the synagogue at Nazareth (Luke 4:18), declaring it fulfilled in himself — a passage foundational to the Christian understanding of the Messiah's mission.</note>
<margin>† Matthew 5:5.</margin>

3 To give to the mourners of Zion: to give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning, a garment of praise instead of a spirit of heaviness: and they shall be called in her the strong ones of justice, the planting of the Lord, to glorify him.
<margin>† Above, Chapter 58:12.</margin>

6 But you shall be called priests of the Lord: men shall speak of you as ministers of our God: you shall eat the wealth of the nations, and in their glory you shall pride yourselves.
7 For your double shame and dishonour, they shall praise their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess double; everlasting joy shall be theirs.

### CHAPTER LXII.

*The Prophet does not cease to announce Christ on account of the impious, prophesying of Christ's coming and the conversion of the nations: concerning the happiness, glory, and exaltation of the Church out of God’s gracious good pleasure toward her: concerning the preachers of the Church, and the Gospel to be spread throughout the world.*

For Zion’s sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not rest, until her Just One goes forth as brightness, and her Savior be lighted as a lamp.
2 And the nations shall see your Just One, and all kings your Renowned One, and you shall be called by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord shall name.
3 And you shall be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God.
4 You shall no longer be called Forsaken <note>original Latin: "Derelicta"</note>: and your land shall no longer be called Desolate, but you shall be called "My Will is in Her" <note>original Latin: "voluntas mea in ea," often rendered as Hephzibah</note>, and your land "Inhabited" <note>original Latin: "Inhabitata," often rendered as Beulah</note>, because the Lord has been well pleased with you: and your land shall be inhabited.
5 For a young man shall dwell with a virgin, and your sons shall dwell in you. And the bridegroom shall rejoice over the bride, and your God shall rejoice over you.
6 Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen; all day and all night forever they shall not be silent. You who remember the Lord, do not keep silent,
7 And give him no silence, until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth.
<margin>† Above 57:14.</margin>
8 The Lord has sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength: Surely I will no longer give your grain to be food for your enemies: and the sons of foreigners shall not drink your wine, in which you have labored.
9 For those who gather it shall eat it, and shall praise the Lord: and those who bring it together shall drink it in my holy courts.
<margin>† Above 57:14.</margin>

<margin>† Zechariah 9:9. Matthew 21:5.</margin>

12 And they shall call them: The holy people, the redeemed of the Lord. And you shall be called: A sought-after city, and not Forsaken.

### CHAPTER LXIII.

*The Lord says that He is sprinkled with blood while He alone conquered the enemies: God bestowed many benefits upon Israel, but because of their iniquities they were forsaken by Him: the prophet, however, mindful of the mercies of the Lord, invokes His mercy upon His people, whom he laments as being deserted by God.*

<margin>† Revelation 19.</margin>
Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? <note>Bozrah was a principal city of Edom, a nation often portrayed as an enemy of Israel.</note> This one beautiful in his robe, walking in the greatness of his strength. "It is I, who speak justice, and am a defender to save."
2 Why then is your clothing red, and your garments like those of people treading in a winepress? <note>The treading of grapes was a common image for divine judgment and the shedding of blood.</note>
3 I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there is no man with me: I have trodden them in my fury, and have trampled them in my wrath, and their blood is sprinkled upon my garments, and I have stained all my clothing.
<margin>† Above 34:8.</margin>
4 For the day of vengeance is in my heart, the year of my redemption has come.
5 I looked around, and there was no helper; I sought, and there was no one to assist: and my own arm saved me, and my indignation itself assisted me.
6 And I have trampled the peoples in my fury, and made them drunk in my indignation, and I have brought down their strength to the earth.
7 I will remember the mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all the things the Lord has rendered to us, and for the multitude of good things to the house of Israel, which he has bestowed on them according to his indulgence, and according to the multitude of his mercies.
8 And he said: Nevertheless, they are my people, children who do not deny: and he became a savior to them.
9 In all their tribulation he was not troubled, and the angel of his presence <note>original Latin: "faciei ejus," literally "of his face"</note> saved them: in his love, and in his indulgence he himself redeemed them, and he carried them, and lifted them up all the days of old.
10 But they provoked him to wrath, and afflicted his holy spirit: and he was turned into an enemy to them, and he himself fought against them.
<margin>† Exodus 14:25.</margin>
11 And he remembered the days of old, of Moses, and of his people: Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who put his holy spirit in the midst of him?
12 Who led Moses by the right hand with the arm of his majesty, who divided the waters before them, to make for himself an everlasting name?
13 Who led them through the depths, like a horse in the desert that does not stumble.
14 Like an animal descending into the field, the Spirit of the Lord was its leader: so did you lead your people, to make for yourself a glorious name.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 26:15. Baruch 2:16.</margin>
15 Look down from heaven, and behold from your holy habitation, and from the habitation of your glory: where is your zeal, and your strength? The multitude of your bowels <note>A Hebrew idiom for deep compassion or pity.</note>, and of your mercies? They have restrained themselves toward me.
16 For you are our father, and Abraham did not know us, and Israel was ignorant of us: you, O Lord, are our father, our redeemer, your name is from eternity.
17 Why have you made us err, O Lord, from your ways: have you hardened our heart so that we would not fear you?

# CHAPTER LXIV.

*The Prophet prays that God might make His name and power known to His enemies; having also mentioned the happiness prepared for those who wait for God, he confesses and mourns the iniquities, uncleanness, and exile of his people, praying for liberation.*

1 O that you would rend the heavens and come down: the mountains would melt away at your presence.
2 They would waste away as if consumed by fire, the waters would boil with fire, so that your name might be made known to your enemies: the nations would be troubled at your presence.
3 When you perform wonders, we shall not be able to bear them: you descended, and the mountains flowed away at your presence.
<margin>1 Corinthians 2:9.</margin>
4 From of old they have not heard, nor perceived with their ears: † the eye has not seen, O God, besides you, what you have prepared for those who wait for you. <note>This famous verse is quoted by St. Paul to describe the hidden wisdom and rewards of God.</note>
5 You have met him who rejoices and does justice: they shall remember you in your ways: behold, you are angry, for we have sinned: in them <note>In our sins or in your ways</note> we have been always, and we shall be saved.
6 And we have all become like the unclean, and all our justices <note>original: "justitiæ nostræ"—our righteous deeds</note> are like a menstrual rag: <note>Often translated as "filthy rags," this refers to a cloth used during menstruation, symbolizing deep ritual and moral impurity.</note> and we have all fallen like a leaf, and our iniquities like the wind have carried us away.
7 There is no one who calls upon your name: who rises up and takes hold of you: you have hidden your face from us, and you have crushed us by the hand of our own iniquity.
8 And now, O Lord, you are our father, and we are the clay: and you are our potter, and we are all the work of your hands.
<margin>Psalm 78:8.</margin>

*The conversion of the nations, and the rejection of the Jews on account of their iniquities and idolatry, though a small remnant of them is preserved; warnings are given to those who rejected God’s law, and all prosperous and new things are announced to the servants of God: the prophet deals at length with their happiness and God’s kindness toward them.*

### CHAPTER LXVI.

*The Lord of heaven and earth does not look toward a temple, which the Jews wished to build for him as a place of rest, but toward a humbled spirit: the sacrifices of the old law are rejected: the stubbornness of the Jews against Christ and his disciples is shown to be punished: concerning the birth of Christ and the fruitfulness of the Church, in which all are exhorted to rejoice together, showing the benefits they will receive from the Lord, and what the judgment of the wicked will be, and how the nations will be converted through the preaching of Christ’s disciples: also concerning the final retribution of the wicked and the good.*

<margin>
† Acts 7:49 & 17:24.
</margin>
Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: what is this house that you will build for me? and what is this place of my rest?
2 My hand has made all these things, and all these things were made, says the Lord: but to whom shall I look, except to the poor man, and him who is contrite in spirit, and trembles at my words?
3 He who sacrifices an ox is as if he killed a man; he who slaughters a sheep is as if he clubbed a dog to death; he who offers an oblation is as if he offered swine’s blood; he who burns incense is as if he blessed an idol: <note>God rejects outward religious rituals when the heart is wicked, comparing them to murder or unclean acts.</note> all these things they have chosen in their own ways, and their soul has delighted in their abominations.
4 Therefore I also will choose their delusions, and I will bring upon them the things they feared: because I called, and there was no one who answered; I spoke, and they did not hear; and they did evil in my eyes, and chose the things I did not want.
<margin>
† Proverbs 1:24.
Isaiah 65:12.
Jeremiah 7:13.
</margin>

6 A voice of the people from the city, a voice from the temple, the voice of the Lord rendering retribution to his enemies.
7 Before she was in labor, she gave birth: before her pain came, she brought forth a male child. <note>This is traditionally interpreted as the sudden and miraculous birth of the Church or the arrival of Christ.</note>

9 Shall I, who make others give birth, not give birth myself, says the Lord? If I, who

<column-break/>

grant generation to others, shall I be sterile, says the Lord your God?
10 Rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad with her, all you who love her: rejoice for joy with her, all you who mourn over her,
11 That you may suck and be filled from the breast of her consolations: that you may milk out and flow with delights from the abundance of her glory.
12 For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like a flooding torrent, which you shall suck: you shall be carried at the breasts, and be dandled upon the knees.

18 But I know their works and their thoughts: I come that I may gather all nations and tongues: and they shall come and shall see my glory.

# THE PROPHECY OF JEREMIAH.

-> CHAPTER ONE. <-

*Jeremiah is set apart in his mother's womb and sent by the Lord during the time of Josiah, King of Judah, to prophesy. He pleads his youth as an excuse, but being instructed by God, he receives invincible strength and is commanded to prophesy the destruction of Jerusalem under the symbols of a branch and a boiling pot.*

<image-desc>Decorative initial letter V with a woodcut scene showing a landscape with a river and a person kneeling or a similar small architectural/nature detail.</image-desc>
The words of Jeremiah, the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin.
2 To whom the word of the Lord came in the days of Josiah, the son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
3 It came also in the days of Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the exile of Jerusalem, in the fifth month.
4 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
5 Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you; and before you came forth from the belly, I set you apart, and I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
6 And I said: "Ah, ah, ah, Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am a child." <note>Jeremiah expresses his inadequacy, using a Hebrew expression of alarm or grief represented here by "A, a, a."</note>
7 And the Lord said to me: "Do not say, 'I am a child'; for you shall go to all to whom I shall send you, and you shall speak whatever I command you.
8 Do not be afraid of their faces, for I am with you to deliver you," says the Lord.
9 And the Lord put forth his hand and touched my mouth; and the Lord said to me: "Behold, I have put my words in your mouth.
<margin>Below, 8:7.</margin>
10 See, I have set you this day over nations and over kingdoms, † to root up, and to pull down, and to waste, and to destroy, and to build, and to plant."
11 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" And I said: "I see a watching branch." <note>original: "virgam vigilantem." This is a wordplay; in Hebrew, the word for almond tree sounds like the word for "watching" or "hastening," signifying that God is watching over his word to perform it quickly.</note>
12 And the Lord said to me: "You have seen well; for I will watch over my word to perform it."
13 And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying: "What do you see?" And I said: "I see a boiling pot, and its face is from the face of the north."
<margin>Below, 6.</margin>
14 And the Lord said to me: "† From the north shall an evil break forth upon all the inhabitants of the land.
15 For behold, I will call together all the families of the kingdoms of the north," says the Lord; "and they shall come, and every one shall set his throne in the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, and upon all its walls round about, and upon all the cities of Judah.
16 And I will speak my judgments with them, concerning all the wickedness of those who have forsaken me, and have offered libations to strange gods, and have adored the work of their own hands.
17 You, therefore, gird up your loins, and arise, and speak to them all that I command you. Do not be afraid of their faces; for I will not make you fear their countenance.
<margin>Below, 27.</margin>
18 † For behold, I have made you this day a fortified city,

<column-break/>

and an iron pillar, and a wall of brass, over all the land, to the kings of Judah, to its princes, and to its priests, and to the people of the land.
19 And they shall fight against you, but they shall not prevail; for I am with you," says the Lord, "to deliver you."

-> CHAPTER II. <-

*The Lord sternly expostulates with the children of Israel and Judah, especially with the shepherds and prophets, because, disregarding the various benefits received from God, and having left him who is the fountain of living water, they worshipped idols from which they could expect nothing good; indeed, while they were entirely given over to idolatry, robbery, and cruelty, they sought to justify themselves, and therefore he predicts they are to be devastated.*

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 "Go, and cry in the ears of Jerusalem, saying: Thus says the Lord: I have remembered you, pitying your youth, and the love of your espousals, when you followed me in the desert, in a land that is not sown.
3 Israel was holy to the Lord, the firstfruits of his increase; all who devour him offend; evils shall come upon them," says the Lord.
4 Hear the word of the Lord, O house of Jacob, and all the families of the house of Israel.
<margin>† Micah 6:3.</margin>
5 Thus says the Lord: "† What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they have gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and have become vain?
6 And they have not said: 'Where is the Lord, who made us come up out of the land of Egypt; who led us through the desert, through a land uninhabited and impassable, through a land of drought, and the image of death, through a land in which no man walked, nor did any man dwell?'
7 And I brought you into the land of Carmel, that you might eat its fruit and its best things; and when you entered, you defiled my land, and made my inheritance an abomination.
8 The priests did not say: 'Where is the Lord?' and those who held the law did not know me, and the shepherds transgressed against me; and the prophets prophesied in Baal, and followed idols.
9 Therefore I will yet contend in judgment with you," says the Lord, "and I will plead with your children.
10 Pass over to the islands of Kittim, and see; and send into Kedar, and consider diligently; and see if such a thing has been done. <note>Kittim refers to the west (Cyprus/Greece) and Kedar to the east (Arabia), representing the entire known world.</note>
11 If a nation has changed its gods, and certainly they are no gods; but my people have changed their glory for an idol.
12 Be astonished, O heavens, at this, and O gates thereof, be very desolate," says the Lord.
13 "For my people have done two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and have dug for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
14 Is Israel a slave, or a home-born servant? Why then is he become a prey?
15 The lions have roared upon him, and have given..."

32 Can a virgin forget her ornament, or a bride her breast-band? <note>original: "fasciae pectoralis" — a decorative sash or girdle</note> Yet my people have forgotten me for days without number.
33 Why do you strive to show that your way is good to seek love, you who have even taught your wicked ways to be your own?
34 Also on your wings is found the blood of the souls of the poor and innocent; I did not find them in pits, but in all the things I mentioned above.
35 And you said: "I am without sin and innocent: and therefore let your wrath be turned away from me." Behold, I will contend with you in judgment, because you said: "I have not sinned."

<column-break/>

36 How exceedingly cheap you have become, repeating your ways! You shall be confounded by Egypt just as you were confounded by Assyria.
37 For from there also you shall go forth with your hands upon your head: because the Lord has crushed your confidence, and you shall have no prosperity in it.

### CHAPTER III.

*God, with incomparable mercy, calls His people back to Himself from the idolatry in which Judah even surpassed Israel: promising that He will take them as children and give them true shepherds, so that they may worship the Lord in peace in Jerusalem; concerning the future glory and exaltation of Jerusalem, the gathering of the nations to her, and the repentance of the people.*

It is commonly said: If a man puts away his wife, and she leaves him and marries another man, will he return to her again? Shall that woman not be polluted and defiled? Yet you have committed fornication with many lovers: nevertheless, return to me, says the Lord, and I will receive you.
2 Lift up your eyes to the high places, and see where you have not prostituted yourself: you sat in the ways, waiting for them like a robber in the wilderness: and you have polluted the land with your fornications and your wicked deeds.
3 Therefore the showers of rain have been withheld, and there has been no late rain: you have the forehead of a harlot, you refused to blush.
4 Therefore, at least from this time, call me: "My father, you are the guide of my youth."
5 Will you be angry forever, or will you persist until the end? Behold, you have spoken and done evil things, as much as you were able.
<margin>Above 2:20.</margin>
6 And the Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah: Have you seen what rebellious Israel has done? She went away by herself upon every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and played the harlot there.
7 And I said, when she had done all these things: "Return to me"; and she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
8 And I saw that for the very reason that rebellious Israel had committed adultery, I had put her away and given her a <term>bill of divorce<gloss>original: "libellum repudii" — a formal document ending a marriage</gloss></term>: yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear, but went and played the harlot herself also.
9 And by the ease of her fornication she defiled the land, and committed adultery with stone and wood.
10 And in all this, her treacherous sister Judah has not returned to me with her whole heart, but in falsehood, says the Lord.
11 And the Lord said to me: Rebellious Israel has justified her soul in comparison to treacherous Judah.
12 Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say: Return, rebellious Israel, says the Lord, and I will not turn my face away from you: for I am holy, says the Lord, and I will not be angry forever.
13 Only acknowledge your iniquity, that you have transgressed against the Lord your God: and you have scattered your ways to strangers under every leafy tree, and you have not heard my voice, says the Lord.
14 Return, O children who have turned away, says the Lord: for I am your husband: and I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you into Zion.

*The Lord promises pardon if they truly turn back and circumcise their hearts, threatening heavy evils if they persist in their malice: wherefore the prophet mourns, seeing the land about to be devastated and reduced to a wilderness, yet in such a way that there shall not be a total destruction.*

## CHAPTER IV.

1 If you will return, O Israel, says the Lord, return to me: if you will take away your stumbling blocks from my sight, you shall not be moved.
2 And you shall swear: "As the Lord lives," in truth, and in judgment, and in justice: and the nations shall bless him, and shall praise him.
<margin>† Hosea 10:12.</margin>
3 For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and Jerusalem: † Break up your fallow ground <note>original: "novale" — land left unplowed; a metaphor for preparing a hardened heart for spiritual seeds</note>, and sow not among thorns:
4 Be circumcised to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your hearts, you men of Judah, and inhabitants of Jerusalem: lest my indignation come forth like fire, and be kindled, and there be none to quench it, because of the malice of your thoughts.
5 Announce in Judah, and make it heard in Jerusalem: speak, and sound the trumpet in the land: cry out aloud, and say: "Gather together, and let us enter into the fortified cities."
<margin>† Above 1:14.</margin>

8 For this, gird yourselves with haircloth, lament and howl: because the fierce anger of the Lord is not turned away from us.
9 And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord: The heart of the king shall perish, and the heart of the princes: and the priests shall be astonished, and the prophets shall be dismayed.
10 And I said: Alas, alas, alas, Lord God, have you then deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying: "You shall have peace": and behold the sword reaches even to the soul?
11 At that time it shall be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A scorching wind in the ways that are in the desert—the ways of the daughter of my people—not to fan, nor to cleanse.
12 A spirit full of these things shall come to me: and now I will speak my judgments with them.
13 Behold, he shall come up like a cloud, and his chariots like a tempest: his horses are swifter than eagles: woe to us, for we are laid waste.
14 Wash your heart from malice, O Jerusalem, that you may be saved: how long shall hurtful thoughts remain in you?
15 For a voice of one declaring from Dan, and making known the idol from Mount Ephraim.
16 Tell the nations: Behold, it is heard in Jerusalem that guardians are coming from a far country, and giving out their voice against the cities of Judah.
17 They are set against her round about like keepers of fields: because she has provoked me to wrath, says the Lord.

19 My bowels, my bowels! I am in pain; the senses of my heart are troubled within me: I will not hold my peace, for my soul has heard the sound of the trumpet, the cry of battle.
20 Destruction upon destruction is called for, and the whole land is laid waste: suddenly my tents are destroyed, my curtains in a moment.
21 How long shall I see the one fleeing, and hear the sound of the trumpet?
22 For my foolish people have not known me: they are senseless and mad children: they are wise to do evils, but to do good they have no knowledge.
23 I beheld the earth, and behold, it was empty and nothing <note>The Latin "vacua... et nihili" mirrors the "tohu wa-bohu" of Genesis 1, suggesting a reversal of creation</note>: and the heavens, and there was no light in them.
24 I saw the mountains, and behold, they trembled: and all the hills were troubled.
25 I looked, and there was no man: and every bird of the air was gone.
26 I looked, and behold, Carmel was a wilderness: and all its cities were destroyed before the face of the Lord, and before the face of his fierce anger.
27 For thus says the Lord: All the land shall be desolate, yet I will not make a final end.
28 The earth shall mourn, and the heavens above shall grieve: because I have spoken, I have purposed, and I have not repented, nor have I turned away from it.
29 At the noise of the horseman and the archer, the whole city has fled: they have entered into thickets, and climbed up the rocks: all the cities are forsaken, and not a man dwells in them.

### CHAPTER V.

*The Lord seeks a just man in Jerusalem, that he might show her mercy: but both the common people and the nobles are hardened and poured out in their wickedness and idolatry; therefore he threatens them with devastation from a foreign people, because they have become blind and deaf, yet not unto a total destruction.*

1 **R**un through the streets of Jerusalem, and see, and consider, and seek in her broad places, if you can find a man doing judgment and seeking faith: and I will be merciful to her.

2 And if they say, "As the Lord lives," even this they will swear falsely.

3 O Lord, your eyes look upon faith: you have struck them, and they did not grieve: you have bruised them, and they refused to receive discipline: they have made their faces harder than a rock, and they refused to return.

4 But I said: Perhaps they are poor and foolish, ignorant of the way of the Lord and the judgment of their God.

5 I will go therefore to the nobles, and will speak to them: for they have known the way of the Lord and the judgment of their God: but behold, these also have altogether broken the yoke and burst the bonds.

6 Therefore a lion from the forest has struck them, a wolf of the evening has devastated them, a leopard watches over their cities: everyone who goes out from them shall be taken: because their transgressions are multiplied, and their rebellions are strengthened.

7 How can I be merciful to you? Your children have forsaken me, and swear by those who are not gods: I fed them to the full, and they committed adultery, and they flocked to the harlot's house.

<margin>† Ezekiel 23:11.</margin>
8 They are become like amorous horses and stallions: everyone neighed after his neighbor's wife.

9 Shall I not visit for these things, says the Lord? And shall my soul not be avenged on such a nation?

10 Go up upon her walls, and destroy them, but do not make a total destruction: take away her branches, for they are not the Lord's.

11 For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously with me, says the Lord.

12 They have denied the Lord, and said: "It is not he: neither shall evil come upon us: we shall not see the sword or famine."

13 The prophets have spoken into the wind, and there was no divine answer in them: therefore these things shall happen to them.

14 Thus says the Lord God of hosts: Because you have spoken this word: behold, I will make my words in your mouth as fire, and this people as wood, and it shall devour them.

15 Behold, I will bring upon you a nation from afar, O house of Israel, says the Lord; a robust nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you will not know, nor will you understand what they say.

16 Their quiver is like an open tomb, they are all valiant men.

17 And they shall eat up your harvest and your bread: they shall devour your sons and your daughters: they shall eat up your flocks and your herds: they shall eat your vine

and your fig tree: and they shall destroy your fortified cities, in which you trust, with the sword.

23 But this people has an incredulous and provoking heart, they have revolted and gone away.

24 And they have not said in their heart: "Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us the early and the late rain in its season: who preserves for us the fullness of the yearly harvest."

25 Your iniquities have turned these things away: and your sins have withheld good things from you.

26 For among my people are found wicked men who lie in wait like fowlers <note>Hunters who trap birds</note>, setting snares and traps to catch men.

27 As a trap is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit: therefore they have become great and rich.

29 Shall I not visit for these things, says the Lord? Or shall my soul not be avenged on such a nation?

30 Astonishing and wonderful things are done in the land:

31 The prophets prophesied lies, and the priests applauded with their hands: and my people loved such things: what then shall be done in the end thereof?

### CHAPTER VI.

*The calamity and devastation of Jerusalem by the Assyrians <note>While the text mentions the North, historically this refers to the impending Babylonian invasion, often associated with the northern route</note> is foretold, because they despised the law of the Lord and would not hear rebukes: but all, and especially the leaders, prophets, and priests, were devoted to greed and deceit; and therefore God rejects both them and their sacrifices: he therefore commands the prophets to mourn for them, since they could not be purified by the furnace.*

1 **S**trengthen yourselves, you children of Benjamin, in the midst of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a standard over Beth-Haccerem <note>Tekoa and Beth-Haccerem were strategic high points used for signal fires and warnings</note>: for evil is seen from the north, and great destruction.

2 I have compared the daughter of Sion to a beautiful and delicate woman.

3 The shepherds with their flocks shall come to her: they have pitched their tents around her: everyone shall feed those who are under his hand.

4 Prepare war against her: arise, and let us go up at midday: woe to us, for the day has declined, for the shadows of the evening are grown longer.

5 Arise <note>The Latin text ends on a partial word 'Sur-', which likely continues as 'Surgite' meaning 'Arise' on the following page</note>

<summary>Jeremiah 5 and 6 describe the total moral collapse of Jerusalem, where neither the poor nor the rich follow God's law. Consequently, the Lord warns of an inevitable invasion from a foreign nation as punishment for their deceit and idolatry.</summary>

### CHAPTER VIII.

*Because the kings, nobles, priests, and prophets, as well as the rest of the people, have turned to idolatry; and having not considered the judgment of the Lord, all have left the truth and devoted themselves to greed and idolatry, and provoking the Lord, they refused to repent: therefore they shall be most cruelly afflicted by their enemies.*

AT that time, says the Lord: They shall cast out the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of its princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of those who inhabited Jerusalem, out of their graves:

2 And they shall spread them out to the sun, and the moon, and all the host of heaven <note>The 'host of heaven' refers to the stars and celestial bodies which the Israelites had begun to worship.</note>, which they loved, and which they served, and after which they walked, and which they sought, and adored: they shall not be gathered, and they shall not be buried: they shall be as dung upon the face of the earth.

3 And death shall be chosen rather than life by all who remain of this wicked family in all the places that are left, to which I have cast them out, says the Lord of hosts.

4 And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: Shall he who falls not rise again? And he who is turned away, shall he not return?

5 Why then has this people in Jerusalem turned away with a contentious turning away? They have gripped onto a lie, and they have refused to return.

6 I attended, and listened: no one speaks what is good, there is no one who does penance for his sin, saying: What have I done? All are turned to their own course, like a horse rushing headlong into battle.

7 The stork in the sky knows her appointed time, the turtle-dove, and the swallow, and the crane, have observed the time of their coming: but my people have not known the judgment of the Lord.

8 How do you say: We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us? Truly the lying pen of the scribes <note>Jeremiah suggests that the religious scholars have distorted the written scriptures to justify their actions.</note> has worked a lie.

9 The wise men are confounded, they are terrified and captured: for they have cast away the word of the Lord, and there is no wisdom in them.

10 Therefore I will give their women to strangers, their fields to heirs: because from the least even to the greatest, all follow greed: from the prophet even to the priest, all act deceitfully. <margin>† Isaiah 56:11. Above 6:13.</margin>

11 † And they healed the wound of the daughter of my people to their shame, saying: Peace, peace: when there was no peace.

12 They are confounded, because they have committed abomination: or rather, they were not confounded by their confusion, and they did not know how to blush: therefore they shall fall among those who fall, in the time of their visitation they shall fall, says the Lord.

13 Gathering, I will gather them, says the Lord; there is no grape on the vines, and there are no figs on the fig tree, the leaf has fallen off: and I have given them things that have passed away.

14 Why do we sit still? ### C H A P T E R XI.

> *Because he is cursed who does not hear nor keep the covenant of the Lord given to the fathers, therefore it is commanded to the prophet that he should preach its observance to the Jews, but in vain, since they rather follow the crimes of their fathers and various idolatries; therefore the Lord will bring inevitable evils upon them, nor will idols, nor the prayer of the righteous, nor the fact that they were previously loved by God, profit them. He reports the wicked designs of the Jews concerning the prophet himself to destroy him from the earth; but those who refuse to hear the prophecy in the name of the Lord shall be destroyed.*

1 The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, saying:
2 Hear the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,

4 Which I commanded your fathers on the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, from the iron furnace, saying: Hear my voice, and do all things that I command you, and you shall be my people, and I will be your God:
5 That I may fulfill the oath which I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day. And I answered and said: Amen, O Lord.
6 And the Lord said to me: Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, saying: Hear the words of this covenant and do them:
7 For I have earnestly protested to your fathers on the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt even to this day; rising early and protesting, I said: Hear my voice:
8 And they did not hear, nor did they incline their ear, but each one walked in the wickedness of his own evil heart; and I brought upon them all the words of this covenant which I commanded them to do, and they did not do them.
9 And the Lord said to me: A conspiracy is found among the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
10 They have returned to the former iniquities of their fathers who refused to hear my words; and these also have gone after foreign gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant which I made with their fathers.
11 Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring evils upon them from which they shall not be able to escape; and they shall cry to me, and I will not hear them.
12 And the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall go and cry to the gods to whom they offer sacrifice, and they shall not save them in the time of their affliction.

### CHAPTER XII.

*The prophet wonders at the prosperity of the wicked, who are nevertheless being prepared for the day of slaughter, and who are the cause of the land's mourning: the inheritance has turned against its Lord; the shepherds have destroyed the Lord’s vineyard, and so it is given over to waste, though the Lord will again have mercy upon it after its enemies have been devastated.*

1 <margin>† Job 1. 7. 10. 1. 3.</margin> You indeed are just, O Lord, if I dispute with you; nevertheless, I will speak just things to you: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why is it well with all those who transgress and act iniquitously?
2 You have planted them, and they have taken root; they thrive and bring forth fruit. You are near to their mouths, but far from their kidneys <note>Meaning they speak of God, but do not feel or honor Him in their innermost being.</note>.
3 But you, O Lord, know me, you have seen me, and you have tested my heart with you. Gather them together like a flock for the slaughter, and set them apart for the day of execution.
4 How long shall the earth mourn, and every herb of the field wither, because of the malice of those who dwell in it? The beasts and the birds are consumed, because they said: "He shall not see our final end."
5 "If you have labored running with footmen, how can you contend with horses? And if you have been secure in a land of peace, what will you do in the pride of the Jordan?" <note>Referring to the thickets and floods along the Jordan river where lions were known to hide.</note>
6 For even your brothers and the house of your father, even they have fought against you, and have cried out after you with a full voice: do not believe them when they speak good things to you.
7 "I have left my house, I have abandoned my inheritance; I have given my beloved soul into the hands of her enemies."
8 "My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; she has raised her voice against me, therefore I have hated her."
9 "Is my inheritance to me like a bird of many colors? <note>original: "avis discolor" — often translated as a 'speckled bird' or a bird of prey that attracts the attack of other birds.</note> Is it

<column-break/>

not a bird dyed all over? Come, gather together all the beasts of the earth, hasten to devour."
10 Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard; they have trampled my portion underfoot. They have turned my desirable portion into a desolate wilderness.
11 They have laid it waste, and it has mourned before me. The whole land is made desolate because there is no one who considers it in his heart.
12 Upon all the paths of the wilderness the spoilers have come, for the sword of the Lord shall devour from one end of the earth to the other; there is no peace for any flesh.
13 They have sown wheat and reaped thorns; they have received an inheritance, and it shall not profit them. You shall be confounded by your fruits because of the wrath of the Lord’s fury.
14 Thus says the Lord against all my wicked neighbors who touch the inheritance that I have distributed to my people Israel: "Behold, I will pluck them out of their land, and I will pluck the house of Judah out from the midst of them."
15 "And when I have plucked them out, I will turn and have mercy on them: and I will lead them back, every man to his inheritance, and every man into his land."
16 "And it shall be: if they will truly learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, 'As the Lord lives,' just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they shall be built up in the midst of my people."
17 "But if they will not hear, I will utterly pluck up that nation with uprooting and destruction," says the Lord.

### CHAPTER XIII.

*Just as Jeremiah's linen loincloth, hidden at the Euphrates, rotted; so Judah, which at first clung to the Lord, is cast off by Him because of pride and idolatry, and all are scattered: they are nevertheless called back by the prophet so that they might avoid evils through their repentance; otherwise, Judah shall be taken away because of its iniquities, which it cannot be led to repent of due to a deep-seated habit in evil: the prophet’s compassion is also interposed.*

1 Thus says the Lord to me: "Go, and get yourself a linen loincloth <note>term: "lumbare" — a waistband or belt worn close to the skin.</note>, and put it upon your loins, and do not put it into water."
2 And I got the loincloth according to the word of the Lord, and I put it around my loins.
3 And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, saying:
4 "Take the loincloth that you have, which is around your loins, and arise, go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in a hole of the rock."
5 So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the Lord had commanded me.
6 And it came to pass after many days, the Lord said to me: "Arise, go to the Euphrates, and take the loincloth from there, which I commanded you to hide there."
7 And I went to the Euphrates, and I dug, and I took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it; and behold, the loincloth was rotted, so that it was fit for no use.
8 Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
9 "Thus says the Lord: In this way I will make the pride of Judah rot, and the great pride of Jerusalem."

16 Give glory to the Lord your God before it grows dark, and before your feet stumble upon the gloomy mountains; you will look for light, and He will turn it into the shadow of death and into thick darkness.
<margin>† Lamentations 1:2.</margin>

19 The cities of the south are shut up, and there is no one to open them; all Judah has been carried away in a total exile.
20 Lift up your eyes and see those who come from the north: where is the flock that was given to you, your noble cattle?

<margin>† Below 30:14.</margin>

### CHAPTER XIV.

*A great drought in the land of Judah because of the people's sins; and as the prophet prays for their liberation and mercy, he is forbidden by the Lord to pray for them. Neither does God accept their fasts and victims. The prophets who promise them security shall perish along with them. Jeremiah mourns the sorrows of sword and famine, and having confessed the people's sins, he prays for mercy.*

1 The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the words of the drought.
2 Judah has mourned, and its gates have fallen into decay; they are blackened upon the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem has gone up.
3 The great men sent their underlings for water: they came to draw it and found no water; they carried back their vessels empty. They were confounded and afflicted, and they covered their heads.
4 Because of the devastation of the earth, for no rain has come upon the land, the farmers were confounded; they covered their heads.
5 For even the doe gave birth in the field and abandoned her young, because there was no grass.
6 And the wild donkeys stood upon the crags; they gasped for air like dragons <note>original: "dracones" — referring to large serpents or monsters panting for breath in the heat.</note>; their eyes failed because there was no herbage.
7 "If our iniquities have answered against us, O Lord, act for the sake of your name; for our rebellions are many; we have sinned against you.
8 O Expectation of Israel, its Savior in time of trouble: why will you be like a stranger in the land, and like a traveler turning aside to stay for a night?
9 Why will you be like a wandering man, like a strong man who cannot save? Yet you are among us, O Lord, and your name is invoked upon us; do not forsake us."
10 Thus says the Lord to this people, who have loved to move their feet and have not rested, and have not pleased the Lord: "Now He will remember their iniquities and visit their sins."
<margin>† Above 7:16 & 11:14.</margin>
11 And the Lord said to me: "Do not pray for this people for their good.
12 When they fast, I will not hear their prayers; and if they offer holocausts and victims, I will not accept them; for I will consume them by the sword, and by famine, and by pestilence."
<margin>† Above 5:12. Below 23:17.</margin>
13 And I said, "Ah, ah, ah <note>original: "A a a" — an onomatopoeic cry of lament or distress.</note>, Lord God! The prophets say to them: 'You shall not see the sword, and there shall be no famine among you, but He will give you true peace in this place.'"
<margin>† Below 29:9.</margin>
14 And the Lord said to me: "The prophets prophesy falsely in my name; I did not send them, and I did not command them, nor have I spoken to them. They prophesy to you a lying vision, and divination, and fraud, and the deceit of their own hearts.
15 Therefore, thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name, whom I did not send, saying: 'Sword and famine shall not be in this land': By sword and famine those prophets shall be consumed.
16 And the people to whom they prophesy shall be cast out in the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and the sword, and there will be no one to bury them—they and their wives, their sons and their daughters; and I will pour out their own evil upon them."

### CHAPTER XV.

*The Lord declares that he will not be moved even by the prayers of Moses or Samuel, but will hand the people of Jerusalem over to pestilence, sword, famine, and captivity, because they have not improved after being punished. The prophet complains that he has become an occasion of discord, and again that in announcing the word of God he has suffered reproach. The Lord promises him help along with the devastation of the Jews; he also promises strength, liberation, and mercy to those who turn back to him.*

1 And the Lord said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my heart would not be toward this people. Cast them out from my sight, and let them go.
<margin>† Zechariah 11:9.</margin>
2 And if they say to you: "Where shall we go?" You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: Those destined for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; and those for captivity, to captivity.
3 And I will appoint over them four kinds of destruction, says the Lord: the sword to slay, dogs to tear, and the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
<margin>† 4 Kings 21:2, 11.</margin>
4 And I will give them over to be a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh <note>Manasseh was a king of Judah notorious for his extreme idolatry; biblical history views his reign as the "point of no return" for Judah's sins.</note> son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for all that he did in Jerusalem.
5 For who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will mourn for you? Or who will go to ask for your peace?
6 You have forsaken me, says the Lord, you have gone backward. Therefore I will stretch out my hand over you and destroy you; I am weary of relenting.
7 And I will scatter them with a winnowing fan at the gates of the land; I have slain and destroyed my people, and yet they have not returned from their ways.
8 Their widows have become more numerous for me than the sand of the sea. I have brought upon them, against the mother of the young man, a destroyer at noon; I have brought terror upon the cities suddenly.
<margin>† 1 Samuel 2:5; Amos 8:9.</margin>
9 She who bore seven has grown weak, her soul has fainted; her sun has gone down while it was still day; she is confounded and ashamed. And the rest of them I will give to the sword in the sight of their enemies, says the Lord.
10 Woe is me, my mother! Why did you bear me, a man of strife, a man of discord to all the

earth? I have not lent on interest, nor has anyone lent to me; yet everyone curses me.
11 The Lord says: Surely your remnant shall be for good; surely I will cause the enemy to treat you well in the time of affliction and in the time of tribulation.
12 Can iron break iron from the north <note>The "iron from the north" refers to the military might of the Babylonians, which was far stronger than the local forces of Judah.</note>, or bronze?

16 Your words were found, and I ate them <note>original: "comedi eos" — This represents the prophet's total internalization and acceptance of God's message.</note>; and your word became to me the joy and gladness of my heart, for your name is called upon me, O Lord God of hosts.

21 And I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked, and I will redeem you from the hand of the strong.

### CHAPTER XVI.

*The Lord forbids the prophet to take a wife, announcing that the Jews will perish by various kinds of death so that the dead will neither be buried nor mourned by the living, because of the idolatry of the fathers and sons and their abandonment of the Law of the Lord. But afterward, through fishermen and hunters, the Lord will lead them back to their land, where they and the nations will confess their sins to the Lord.*

1 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 You shall not take a wife, nor shall you have sons or daughters in this place.
3 For thus says the Lord concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, and concerning their mothers who bore them, and concerning their fathers who begot them in this land:
4 They shall die of deadly diseases; they shall not be mourned or buried; they shall be as dung on the face of the earth. They shall be consumed by the sword and by famine, and their corpses shall be food for the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth.
5 For thus says the Lord: Do not enter the house of feasting, nor go to mourn or console them; for I have taken away my peace from this people, says the Lord, even my lovingkindness and mercies.

# CHAPTER XVIII.

*By the example of the potter, the Lord shows that the house of Israel is in his hand, so that he may do to them according to their merits, even if he had previously said he would do otherwise: because of the obstinate malice of the Jews, destruction is denounced against them: the conspiracy of the Jews against Jeremiah, his own lamentation to God, and the announcement of the punishments that will follow his enemies.*

**1** The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
**2** Arise and go down into the potter's house, and there you shall hear my words.
**3** And I went down into the potter's house, and behold, he was doing work upon the wheel <note>original: "super rotam" — the horizontal wheel used for shaping clay</note>.
**4** And the vessel which he was making from the clay with his hands was spoiled: and turning back, he made it into another vessel, just as it had pleased his eyes to make.
**5** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
<margin>† Isaiah 45:9. Romans 9:20.</margin>
**6** † Can I not do to you as this potter does, house of Israel, says the Lord? Behold, as the clay is in the hand of the potter, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
**7** Suddenly I will speak against a nation and against a kingdom, † to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy it.
<margin>† Above 1:10.</margin>
**8** If that nation repents of its evil, about which I have spoken against it: I also will repent of the evil that I thought to do to it.

<column-break/>

**9** And suddenly I will speak of a nation and of a kingdom, to build it up and to plant it.
**10** If it does evil in my eyes, so as not to hear my voice: I will repent of the good that I spoke to do for it.
**11** Now therefore, say to the man of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am framing evil against you, and I am thinking a thought against you: † let each one return from his evil way, and make your ways and your efforts right.
<margin>† 2 Kings 17:13. Below 25:5 and 35:15. Jonah 3:9.</margin>
**12** But they said: We have lost hope: for we will go after our own thoughts, and each of us will do according to the wickedness of his own evil heart.
**13** Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask the nations: Who has heard such horrible things as the virgin of Israel has done excessively?
**14** Does the snow of Lebanon fail from the rock of the field? Or can the cold flowing waters that burst forth be pulled away?
**15** Because my people have forgotten me, offering sacrifices in vain, and stumbling in their ways, in the ancient paths <note>original: "semitis sæculi" — literally 'paths of the age' or 'eternal paths'</note>, to walk in a path not trodden:
<margin>† Below 19:8 and 49:13 and 50:13.</margin>
**16** † So that their land should become a desolation, and a perpetual whistling: everyone who passes through it shall be astonished, and shall shake his head.
**17** Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before the enemy: I will show them the back, and not the face, in the day of their destruction.
**18** And they said: Come, and let us devise plots against Jeremiah: for the law shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet: come, and let us strike him with the tongue <note>original: "percutiamus eum lingua" — likely meaning to bring false accusations or to silence him through verbal attacks</note>, and let us not pay attention to any of his words.
**19** Give heed to me, O Lord, and hear the voice of my adversaries.
**20** Is evil returned for good, because they have dug a pit for my soul? Remember that I stood in your sight to speak good for them, and to turn away your indignation from them.
**21** Therefore, give their children over to famine, and deliver them into the hands of the sword: let their wives be without children, and become widows: and let their men be killed by death: let their young men be pierced through with the sword in battle.
**22** Let a cry be heard from their houses: for you will bring a robber upon them suddenly: because they have dug a pit to take me, and have hidden snares for my feet.
**23** But you, O Lord, know all their counsel against me for death: do not be appeased by their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out from your face: let them be overthrown in your sight, in the time of your fury deal with them.

<margin>† Above 18:16. Below 49:13 and 50:13.</margin>
8 And I will make this city a source of horror, and a hissing: everyone who passes by it shall be horrified, and shall hiss over all its plagues.

9 And I will feed them with the flesh of their sons, and the flesh of their daughters: and every one shall eat the flesh of his friend in the siege, and in the distress with which their enemies, and those who seek their lives, shall enclose them.

10 And you shall break the flask in the eyes of the men who go with you.

11 And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Even so will I break this people, and this city, as a potter's vessel is broken, which cannot be made whole again: and they shall be buried in Topheth, because there is no other place to bury.

12 Thus will I do to this place, says the Lord, and to its inhabitants: and I will make this city like Topheth.

13 And the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses of the kings of Judah, shall be like the place of Topheth, unclean: all the houses on whose roofs they have sacrificed to all the host of heaven, and have poured out drink offerings to foreign gods.

14 Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, where the Lord had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the house of the Lord, and said to all the people:

15 Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will bring upon this city, and upon all its towns, all the evils that I have spoken against it: because they have hardened their necks, so as not to hear my words.

### CHAPTER XX.

*Jeremiah responds to the messengers of King Zedekiah regarding the siege of King Nebuchadnezzar, that Judah is to be laid waste by pestilence, sword, famine, and captivity, and only those who go over to the Chaldeans shall live: he also exhorts them to execute judgment, lest the indignation of the Lord consume them entirely.*

**T**he word which came to Jeremiah from the Lord, when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur the son of Malchiah, and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, saying:

4 Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war <note>original: "vasa belli" — literally "vessels of war," referring to any military equipment or arms</note> that are in your hands, with which you fight against the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans were the ruling ethnic group of the Babylonian Empire at this time</note> who besiege you outside the walls: and I will gather them into the midst of this city.
5 And I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand, and with a strong arm, and in fury, and in indignation, and in great wrath.

8 And to this people you shall say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death.

# C H A P T E R XXIV.

->*The basket of good figs represents the Jews captured in Babylon, whom the Lord says He will bring back to their land and who will return to Him with all their heart; the basket of bad figs signifies those who remained in Jerusalem and later fled to Egypt, whom He says He will give over to reproach and a curse.*<-

**1** The Lord showed me: and behold, two baskets full of figs were set before the temple of the Lord. This was after Nebuchadnezzar <note>original: "Nabuchodonofor"</note> king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah <note>also known as Jehoiachin</note> son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and the princes, the craftsmen, and the smiths <note>original: "fabrum, & incluforem," meaning the skilled laborers and artisans whose removal weakened the nation's infrastructure.</note> from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
**2** One basket had very good figs, like the figs that ripen first; but the other basket had very bad figs, which could not be eaten because they were so rotten.
**3** And the Lord said to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" And I said: "Figs; the good figs are very good, and the bad figs are very bad, so that they cannot be eaten."
**4** And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
**5** Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so will I acknowledge the exiles of Judah, whom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans <note>The people of Babylon.</note>, for their own good.
**6** And I will set my eyes upon them for their restoration, and I will bring them back to this land; I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
**7** <margin>See above, 7:23; below, 31:33</margin> And I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the Lord; and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, for they shall return to me with their whole heart.
**8** <margin>See below, 29:17</margin> And like the worst figs, which cannot be eaten because they are so bad: thus says the Lord, so will I treat Zedekiah king of Judah, and his princes, and the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this city, and those who dwell in the land of Egypt.
**9** I will deliver them up to be distressed and afflicted by all the kingdoms of the earth: to be a reproach, a proverb, a taunt, and a curse in all the places where I have driven them.
**10** And I will send among them the sword, famine, and pestilence, until they are consumed from the land which I gave to them and to their fathers.

### C H A P T E R XXVII.

> *With bonds sent to various kings, he says that if they are willing to serve the king of Babylon and his descendants, they shall remain in their own land; otherwise they shall perish by the sword, famine, and pestilence; attacking the false prophets who prophesy otherwise, deceiving the people: he also foretells that the sacred vessels which remain are to be carried into Babylon, and finally brought back to Jerusalem.*

**1** IN the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim <note>original: Joakim</note> son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
**2** Thus says the Lord to me: Make for yourself bonds and chains: and you shall put them on your neck.
**3** And you shall send them to the king of Edom, and to the king of Moab, and to the king of the children of Ammon, and to the king of Tyre, and to the king of Sidon; by the hand of the messengers who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
**4** And you shall command them to speak to their masters: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Thus shall you say to your masters.
**5** I have made the earth, and men, and the beasts that are upon the face of the earth, by my great power, and by my outstretched arm: and I have given it to whomsoever it pleased in my eyes.
**6** And now therefore I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar <note>original: Nabuchodonosor</note> the king of Babylon, my servant: moreover I have given him the beasts of the field also to serve him.
**7** And all nations shall serve him: and his son, and his son’s son: until the time of his land and of himself comes: and many nations and great kings shall serve him.
**8** But the nation and kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and whosoever will not bend his neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon: I will visit upon that nation with the sword, and with famine, and with pestilence, says the Lord, until I consume them by his hand.

**9** † Therefore do not listen to your prophets, and diviners, and dreamers, and soothsayers, and sorcerers, who say to you: You shall not serve the king of Babylon.
**10** For they prophesy a lie to you: to remove you far from your land, and to cast you out, and that you should perish.
