## CHAPTER XXVIII

*Hananiah the false prophet, having taken the chains from Jeremiah's neck, prophesies that the sacred vessels along with the king and the captive people will be brought back after two years; but Jeremiah is commanded to prophesy the contrary, and to denounce him with death, which followed in the same year according to Jeremiah's word.*

**1** And it came to pass in that year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fourth month, that Hananiah the son of Azur, a prophet from Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of the Lord, in the presence of the priests and all the people, saying:
**2** Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
**3** Within two full years, I will cause all the vessels of the house of the Lord to be brought back to this place, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away from this place and carried to Babylon.
**4** And I will bring back to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, 

<column-break/>

and all the captives of Judah who went into Babylon, says the Lord; for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
**5** Then the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah in the sight of the priests and in the sight of all the people who stood in the house of the Lord.
**6** And the prophet Jeremiah said: Amen, may the Lord do so; may the Lord fulfill your words which you have prophesied, so that the vessels may be brought back to the house of the Lord, and all the captives from Babylon to this place.
**7** Nevertheless, hear now this word that I speak in your ears and in the ears of all the people:
**8** The prophets who were before me and before you from the beginning prophesied against many lands and against great kingdoms, of war, and of affliction, and of famine.
**9** The prophet who prophesies peace: when his word comes to pass, then it shall be known that the Lord has truly sent that prophet.
**10** Then Hananiah the prophet took the chain <note>Jeremiah was wearing a wooden yoke or chain as a symbolic sign of servitude to Babylon.</note> from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it.
**11** And Hananiah spoke in the sight of all the people, saying: Thus says the Lord: Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all nations within two full years.
**12** And the prophet Jeremiah went his way. And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, after Hananiah the prophet had broken the chain from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, saying:
**13** Go and tell Hananiah: Thus says the Lord: You have broken chains of wood, but you shall make for them chains of iron.
**14** For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I have put a yoke of iron upon the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they shall serve him; moreover, I have given him the beasts of the earth also.
**15** And the prophet Jeremiah said to Hananiah the prophet: Hear now, Hananiah: The Lord has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie.
**16** Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will send you away from the face of the earth; this year you shall die, because you have spoken against the Lord.
**17** And Hananiah the prophet died that year, in the seventh month.

### C H A P T E R XXX.

*He prophesies to the Jews and the children of Israel of their return from the heavy captivity in which they were held because of their sins; that after their return they shall serve the Lord and David their king, whom he shall raise up for them in great prosperity and security, their enemies having been devastated.*

1 This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
2 Thus says the Lord God of Israel, saying: Write for yourself all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.
3 For behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will bring back the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, says the Lord; and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.
4 And these are the words that the Lord spoke to Israel and to Judah:
5 For thus says the Lord: We have heard a voice of terror; there is fear and no peace.
6 Ask and see if a man can give birth? Why then have I seen every man with his hand on his loins, like a woman in labor, and all faces turned to a sickly yellow?
<margin>† Joel 2:2, 11; Amos 5:18; Zephaniah 1:15.</margin>
7 † Alas, for that day is great, and there is none like it; it is the time of tribulation for Jacob, but he shall be saved out of it.
8 And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord of hosts: I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds asunder, and strangers shall no longer rule over him.
9 But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

Having previously addressed the exiles in Babylon regarding their long stay there, the prophet now turns to the future restoration of both Israel (the northern kingdom) and Judah (the southern kingdom), promising a return to their land and a new relationship with God.</meta>

# THE PROPHECY OF JEREMIAH

10 † Therefore, do not fear, my servant Jacob, says the Lord, and do not be dismayed, O Israel: for behold, I will save you from a far-off land, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob shall return and be at rest; he shall overflow with all good things, and there shall be no one to make him afraid.
11 For I am with you, says the Lord, to save you. Though I make a full end of all the nations among whom I have scattered you, I will not make a full end of you; but I will discipline you in judgment <note>In this context, "judgment" refers to a measured, just correction rather than total destruction.</note>, so that you do not think yourself innocent.
12 For thus says the Lord: Your fracture is incurable, your wound is most grievous.
13 There is no one to judge your cause or to bind you up; there is no useful medicine for you.
14 All your lovers <note>The "lovers" refer to the foreign nations and political allies Israel relied on instead of God.</note> have forgotten you; they will not seek you out. † For I have struck you with the blow of an enemy, with a cruel castigation, because of the multitude of your iniquities and because your sins have become hardened.
15 Why do you cry out over your affliction? Your sorrow is incurable. Because of the multitude of your iniquities and your hardened sins, I have done these things to you.
16 Therefore, all who devour you shall be devoured; all your enemies shall be led into captivity; those who waste you shall be wasted, and all who prey upon you I will give for a prey.
17 For I will bring a scar over you <note>original: "obducam cicatricem," an idiom for the skin closing over a wound as it heals.</note> and I will heal you of your wounds, says the Lord. Because they called you an outcast, saying: "This is Zion, who has no one to look after her."
18 Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob, and have mercy on his dwellings; the city shall be rebuilt on its own hilltop, and the temple shall be founded according to its proper order.
19 And out of them shall come praise and the voice of those who make merry. I will multiply them, and they shall not be diminished; I will glorify them, and they shall not be weakened.
20 Their children shall be as they were from the beginning, and their assembly shall remain before me; and I will punish all who afflict them.
21 And their leader shall be one of their own, and their prince shall proceed from their midst. I will bring him near, and he shall approach me; for who is this that would set his heart to draw near to me, says the Lord?
22 And you shall be my people, and I will be your God.
23 Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord, a fury going forth, a rushing storm; it shall rest upon the head of the wicked.
24 The Lord will not turn back the wrath of his indignation until he has executed and performed the thoughts of his heart; in the latter days, you shall understand these things.

### C H A P T E R XXXI.

*The Lord says that he will bring back the people of Israel from captivity so that they may serve the Lord in an abundance of good things. Therefore, Rachel is commanded to weep for her children no longer. Israel acknowledges that he was justly punished and therefore performs penance. Of the new thing, that a woman shall encompass a man. The Lord will watch over the restoration of Israel. Concerning the sour grape. Concerning the new covenant which the Lord will strike with the house of Israel, and that he will never cast away all of its descendants.*

1 At that time, says the Lord, I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.

<column-break/>

2 Thus says the Lord: The people who remained after the sword found grace in the desert; Israel shall go to his rest.
3 The Lord appeared to me from afar. I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore, taking pity, I have drawn you to myself.
4 And I will build you up again, and you shall be built, O virgin of Israel. You shall yet be adorned with your tambourines and go forth in the choir of those who play.
5 You shall yet plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria; the planters shall plant, and they shall not gather the vintage until the proper time comes.
6 <margin>† Isaiah 2:3; Micah 4:2.</margin> For there shall be a day when the watchmen on Mount Ephraim <note>Ephraim was the dominant tribe of the northern kingdom of Israel.</note> shall cry out: † "Arise, and let us go up to Zion to the Lord our God."
7 For thus says the Lord: Rejoice with gladness for Jacob, and neigh <note>original: "hinnite," literally to neigh like a horse, used here to mean a loud cry of triumph.</note> against the head of the Gentiles; shout, sing, and say: "Save your people, O Lord, the remnant of Israel!"
8 Behold, I will bring them from the north country and gather them from the ends of the earth. Among them will be the blind and the lame, the woman with child and she who is in labor together—a great company of those returning here.
9 They shall come with weeping, and I will bring them back with mercy; I will lead them by the rivers of water in a straight path, and they shall not stumble in it. For I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
10 Hear the word of the Lord, O nations, and declare it in the islands that are far off, and say: "He who scattered Israel will gather him, and will keep him as a shepherd keeps his flock."
11 For the Lord has redeemed Jacob and delivered him from the hand of one mightier than he.
12 And they shall come and give praise on the mountain; they shall flow together to the good things of the Lord—to the grain, the wine, the oil, and the young of the cattle and herds. Their soul shall be like a watered garden, and they shall hunger no more.
13 Then the virgin shall rejoice in the dance, the young men and old men together. I will turn their mourning into joy, and I will comfort them and make them glad after their sorrow.
14 I will saturate the soul of the priests with fatness, and my people shall be filled with my good things, says the Lord.
15 <margin>† Matthew 2:18.</margin> Thus says the Lord: † A voice was heard in the high places, of lamentation, of mourning, and of weeping: Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted for them, because they are no more.
16 Thus says the Lord: Let your voice cease from mourning and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work, says the Lord; and they shall return from the land of the enemy.
17 And there is hope for your future, says the Lord; the children shall return to their own borders.
18 I have surely heard Ephraim grieving as he was moved away: "You have chastised me, and I was instructed like an untamed bullock. Convert me, and I shall be converted, for you are the Lord my God."
19 For after you converted me, I did penance; and after you showed me, I struck my thigh <note>Striking the thigh was a traditional gesture of grief, shame, or regret.</note>. I was confounded and ashamed, because I bore the reproach of my youth.
20 Is Ephraim not my honorable son, a darling child? For since I spoke of him, I will surely remember him still. Therefore, my heart is troubled for him; in mercy, I will have mercy on him, says the Lord.
21 Set up a signpost for yourself, place for yourself markers of bitterness <note>original: "amaritudines." While the Latin means "bitternesses," in this context it refers to stone pillars or signposts used to mark a path.</note>; set your heart toward the right way in which you walked. Return, O virgin of Israel, return to these cities of yours.

<summary>This passage records God's promise to restore the exiled people of Israel and Judah, moving from descriptions of their "incurable" wounds to a future of rebuilding, joy, and divine mercy. It famously features Rachel weeping for her children and the eventual repentance of Ephraim.</summary>

# THE PROPHECY OF JEREMIAH

22 How long will you drift away in your comforts, O wandering daughter? For the Lord has created a new thing on the earth: **A WOMAN SHALL ENCOMPASS A MAN.** <note>This enigmatic phrase has been interpreted in many ways: some see it as a reversal of roles where the weak protect the strong, while Christian tradition historically viewed it as a prophecy of the Virgin Birth.</note>
23 Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: They shall yet speak this word in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I turn back their captivity: "May the Lord bless you, O beauty of justice, O holy mountain!"
24 And Judah and all its cities shall dwell in it together, the farmers and those who lead the flocks.
25 For I have saturated the weary soul, and I have filled every hungry soul.
26 Thereupon I was awakened as if from sleep, and I saw, and my sleep was sweet to me.
27 Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of men and the seed of cattle.
28 And just as I have watched over them to pluck up, and to pull down, and to scatter, and to destroy, and to afflict, so will I watch over them to build and to plant, says the Lord.
<margin>† Ezekiel 18:2</margin> 29 In those days they shall say no more: "The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the children's teeth are set on edge." <note>This was a common proverb expressing the idea that children were punished for the sins of their ancestors.</note>
30 But every one shall die for his own iniquity; every man who eats the sour grape, his own teeth shall be set on edge.
<margin>† Hebrews 8:8</margin> 31 Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a **new covenant** with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:
32 Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt—the covenant which they made void, though I was their master, says the Lord.
<margin>† Hebrews 10:16</margin> 33 But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law within them, and I will write it upon their heart; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
<margin>† Acts 10:43</margin> 34 And they shall no longer teach every man his neighbor and every man his brother, saying: "Know the Lord," for all shall know me, from the least of them to the greatest, says the Lord; for I will be merciful to their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.
35 Thus says the Lord, who gives the sun for a light by day, and the order of the moon and the stars for a light by night; who stirs up the sea, and its waves roar—the Lord of hosts is his name:
36 If these laws should fail before me, says the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall fail from being a nation before me forever.
37 Thus says the Lord: If the heavens above can be measured, and the foundations of the earth below can be searched out, then I will also cast away all the seed of Israel for all that they have done, says the Lord.
38 Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when the city shall be rebuilt for the Lord, from the tower of Hananeel to the corner gate.
39 And the measuring line shall go out further over against it upon the hill of Gareb, and it shall encompass Goatha,
40 And the whole valley of dead bodies, and of ashes, and all the region of death even to the brook of Kidron, and to the corner of the horse gate toward the east—it shall be Holy to the Lord. It shall not be plucked up or destroyed any more forever.

### CHAPTER XXXII.

*While Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem, Jeremiah, placed in the court of the prison, buys a field in Anathoth at the command of the Lord from his cousin, and orders the deed of purchase to be preserved. He recounts before the Lord the benefits bestowed upon the Israelites. The Lord says that He will deliver the city and its people into the hands of the king of Babylon because of their idolatry, but afterward He will recall them to Jerusalem and strike a new covenant with them, so that they may serve Him with all their heart.*

1 The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah; this was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
2 At that time, the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the house of the king of Judah.
3 For Zedekiah, king of Judah, had shut him up, saying: "Why do you prophesy, saying: 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will give this city into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it'?
4 And Zedekiah, king of Judah, shall not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon; and his mouth shall speak with his mouth, and his eyes shall see his eyes.
5 And he shall lead Zedekiah into Babylon, and there he shall be until I visit him, says the Lord; but if you fight against the Chaldeans, you shall have no success."
6 And Jeremiah said: "The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
7 'Behold, Hanameel the son of Shallum, your uncle, shall come to you, saying: "Buy my field which is in Anathoth, for the right of kinship is yours to buy it."'
8 And Hanameel, my uncle's son, came to me according to the word of the Lord, to the entry of the prison, and said to me: 'Possess my field which is in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin; for the inheritance belongs to you, and you are the next of kin to possess it.' Then I understood that this was the word of the Lord.
9 And I bought the field from Hanameel, my uncle's son, which is in Anathoth, and I weighed out the money for him: seven staters and ten silver pieces. <note>original: "septem stateres, & decem argenteos." The "stater" was a specific weight or coin; the total reflects seventeen shekels of silver.</note>
10 And I wrote it in a deed, and sealed it, and called witnesses; and I weighed the silver in the scales.
11 And I took the deed of possession, both the one that was sealed with stipulations and terms, and the one that was open on the outside.
12 And I gave the deed of possession to Baruch, the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, in the sight of Hanameel my cousin, and in the sight of the witnesses who were written in the book of purchase, and in the sight of all the Jews who sat in the court of the prison.
13 And I commanded Baruch before them, saying:
14 'Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Take these deeds, this sealed deed of purchase and this open deed, and put them in an earthenware vessel, so that they may last for many days.'
15 For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: 'Houses and fields and vineyards shall yet be possessed in this land.'
16 And I prayed to the Lord after I had delivered the deed of possession to Baruch the son of Neriah, saying:
17 'Alas, alas, alas, O Lord God! Behold, you have made the heaven and the earth by your great power and by your outstretched arm; no word shall be difficult for you.
<margin>† Exodus 34:7</margin> 18 You show mercy to thousands, and you ren—'

<summary>Jeremiah proclaims the New Covenant, where God's law is written on the heart rather than stone. Amidst the siege of Jerusalem, the prophet buys a field in Anathoth as a tangible sign of hope that the people will one day return and possess the land again.</summary>

20 You who have set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt even until this day, and in Israel, and among men, and have made yourself a name, as it is this day.
21 And you brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt, with signs, and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with a stretched-out arm, and with great terror.
22 And you gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
23 And they entered in, and possessed it: and they did not obey your voice, and did not walk in your law: all that you commanded them to do, they did not do: and all these evils have come upon them.
24 Behold, the siege mounds <note>original: "munitiones" - these were ramps of earth built by attackers to reach the top of city walls.</note> are built up against the city to take it: and the city is given into the hands of the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans were the ruling class of the Neo-Babylonian Empire under Nebuchadnezzar II.</note>, who fight against it, by the face of the sword, and of famine, and of pestilence: and whatever you have spoken has happened, as you yourself see.
25 And yet you say to me, Lord God: "Buy a field for silver, and call witnesses"—even though the city is given into the hands of the Chaldeans?
26 And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
27 Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: shall any word be difficult for me?
28 Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will deliver this city into the hands of the Chaldeans, and into the hands of the king of Babylon, and they shall take it.
29 And the Chaldeans that fight against this city shall come and set it on fire, and burn it, with the houses upon whose roofs they offered sacrifice to Baal, and poured out drink offerings to strange gods, to provoke me to wrath.
30 For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have continually done evil in my eyes from their youth: the children of Israel who even until now exasperate me with the work of their hands, says the Lord.
31 For this city has been to me a provocation of my fury and my indignation, from the day that they built it, until this day, in which it shall be taken out of my sight.
32 Because of all the evil of the children of Israel, and of the children of Judah, which they have done, provoking me to anger, they and their kings, their princes, and their priests, and their prophets, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
33 And they have turned their backs to me, and not their faces: though I taught them early in the morning, and instructed them, and they would not listen to receive discipline.
34 † And they set their idols in the house in which my name is called upon, to defile it.
35 And they built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Ennom <note>Also known as Gehenna; it was a site of ritual infanticide and later became a symbol for a place of punishment.</note>, to consecrate their sons and their daughters to Moloch: which I did not command them, nor did it enter into my heart, that they should do this abomination, and cause Judah to sin.
36 And now, because of these things, thus says the Lord the God of Israel to this city, of which you say

<column-break/>

that it shall be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon by the sword, and by famine, and by pestilence:
37 Behold, I will gather them together out of all the lands to which I have cast them out in my fury, and in my wrath, and in great indignation: and I will bring them back to this place, and I will cause them to dwell confidently.
38 And they shall be my people, and I will be their God.
39 And I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me all days: and that it may be well with them, and with their children after them.
40 And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, and will not cease to do them good: and I will put my fear in their heart, that they may not revolt from me.
41 And I will rejoice over them, when I shall do them good: and I will plant them in this land in truth, with my whole heart, and with all my soul.
42 For thus says the Lord: Just as I have brought upon this people all this great evil, so will I bring upon them all the good that I now speak to them.
43 And fields shall be possessed in this land, of which you say that it is desolate, because there remains neither man nor beast, and it is given into the hands of the Chaldeans.
44 Fields shall be bought with money, and deeds shall be written, and sealed, and witnesses shall be taken: in the land of Benjamin, and round about Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, and in the mountain cities, and in the plains, and in the cities that are toward the south: for I will bring back their captivity, says the Lord.

# CHAPTER XXXIII.

> *The Lord promises that he will forgive the sins of his people, and bring them back from captivity, with many blessings following: the branch of justice shall spring forth from David, doing justice and judgment in the land, and the covenant of the Lord with David and the seed of Jacob is most firm, to be greatly multiplied.*

1 † AND the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was yet shut up in the court of the prison, saying:
2 Thus says the Lord, who will do it, and will form it, and prepare it, the Lord is his name.
3 Cry to me, and I will hear you: and I will show you great and mighty things which you know not.
4 For thus says the Lord the God of Israel to the houses of this city, and to the houses of the king of Judah, which are destroyed, and to the siege works, and to the sword
5 Of those who come to fight with the Chaldeans, and to fill them with the dead bodies of the men whom I have struck in my fury and in my indignation, hiding my face from this city because of all their malice.
6 Behold, I will bring them a scar and health <note>The Latin "cicatricem" (scar) here refers to the closing and healing of a wound.</note>, and I will cure them: and I will reveal to them the prayer of peace and truth.
7 And I will bring back the captivity of Judah, and the captivity of Jerusalem: and I will build them as from the beginning.
8 And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity, by which they have sinned against me: and I will be merciful to all their iniquities, by which they have sinned against me, and despised me.
9 And it shall be to me a name, and a joy, and a praise, and an exultation among all the nations...

<summary>Jeremiah questions God about buying land while Jerusalem falls to Babylon, receiving a divine assurance that after the destruction, God will gather the people back, establish an everlasting covenant, and restore the lineage of David. The text emphasizes that the same God who brought judgment is the one who will bring healing and peace.</summary>

22 Just as the stars of heaven cannot be numbered, nor the sand of the sea measured, so will I multiply the offspring of David my servant, and the Levites who minister to me.

23 And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:

24 Have you not seen what this people has spoken, saying: "The two families <note>The kingdoms of Israel and Judah.</note> which the Lord had chosen are cast off"? Thus they have despised my people, as if they were no longer a nation in their sight.

25 Thus says the Lord: If I have not established my covenant between day and night and the laws of heaven and earth,

26 Then I will also cast away the offspring of Jacob and David my servant, so that I do not take from his offspring rulers for the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have mercy on them.

### C H A P T E R XXXIV.

> *The Lord foretells that he will deliver King Zedekiah into the hands of the king of Babylon, along with Jerusalem, which he shall burn with fire, because they did not keep the covenant they had struck before the Lord concerning the freeing of those Hebrew children whom they had subjected to slavery.*

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth that were under the power of his hand, and all the peoples, fought against Jerusalem and against all its cities, saying:

2 Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and say to him: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will deliver this city into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire.

3 And you shall not escape from his hand, but you shall surely be captured and delivered into his hand. Your eyes shall see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and his mouth shall speak with your mouth, and you shall enter Babylon.

4 Yet hear the word of the Lord, O Zedekiah king of Judah: Thus says the Lord to you: You shall not die by the sword,

5 But you shall die in peace. And according to the burnings <note>A reference to the aromatic spices and funeral pyres used in royal burials.</note> of your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so shall they burn for you; and they shall lament for you, saying, "Alas, Lord!" For I have spoken the word, says the Lord.

6 And Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.

7 And the army of the king of Babylon fought against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah that were left: against Lachish and against Azekah; for these fortified cities were all that remained of the cities of Judah.

8 The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem, proclaiming:

9 That every man should let his manservant and every man his maidservant—Hebrew man or Hebrew woman—go free, and that no one should lord it over them, that is, over a Jew and his brother.

10 And all the princes and all the people who had entered into the covenant heard that everyone should let his manservant and everyone his maidservant go free, and no longer lord it over them; they obeyed, therefore, and let them go.

11 But afterward they turned back, and took back the servants and handmaids whom they had set free, and brought them back into subjection as servants and handmaids.

12 And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

13 Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I made a covenant with your fathers in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, saying:

### C H A P T E R XXXV.

*By the example of the obedience of the Rechabites, who kept the difficult commands of their father, the Lord rebukes the stubborn disobedience of the Jews toward His own commands: therefore the Lord foretells evil for the latter, but good for the former.*

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
2 Go to the house of the Rechabites <note>The Rechabites were a nomadic group who followed strict ancestral rules to maintain their distinct identity and devotion.</note>: and speak to them, and bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the side chambers of the treasures, and give them wine to drink.
3 And I took Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, and his brothers, and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites:
4 And I brought them into the house of the Lord, to the treasure room of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, a man of God, which was next to the treasure room of the princes, above the treasure of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, who was the keeper of the threshold.
5 And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine, and cups: and I said to them: Drink wine.
6 And they answered: We will not drink wine: because Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying: You shall drink no wine, neither you, nor your children, forever:
7 Neither shall you build houses, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyards, nor have any: but you shall dwell in tents all your days, that you may live many days upon the face of the earth, in which you are strangers.
8 Therefore we have obeyed the voice of Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father, in all that he commanded us, so as to drink no wine all our days: we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters:

<column-break/>

9 And not to build houses for ourselves to dwell in: and we have had neither vineyard, nor field, nor seed:
10 But we have dwelt in tents, and have been obedient, according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us.
11 But when Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon came up to our land, we said: Come, let us enter into Jerusalem from the face of the army of the Chaldeans, and from the face of the army of Syria: and we have remained in Jerusalem.
12 And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
13 Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Go, and say to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Will you not receive instruction, to obey my words, says the Lord?
14 The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, which he commanded his sons, that they should drink no wine, have prevailed: and they have drunk none to this day, because they have obeyed the command of their father: but I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you have not obeyed me.
15 And I have sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending, and saying: † Return every man from <margin>† Above 18:11 and 25:5</margin> his wicked way, and make your efforts good; and do not follow strange gods; nor worship them: and you shall dwell in the land which I gave to you and to your fathers: and you have not inclined your ear, nor listened to me.
16 For the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have kept the command of their father, which he commanded them: but this people has not obeyed me.
17 Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will bring upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, all the affliction that I have spoken against them: because I have spoken to them, and they have not heard: I have called them, and they have not answered me.
18 And to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have obeyed the command of Jonadab your father, and have kept all his commandments, and have done all that he commanded you:
19 Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: There shall not want a man from the line of Jonadab the son of Rechab, standing in my presence for all days.

### CHAPTER XXXVIII.

> *Jeremiah, delivered to the princes by the king, is cast into a muddy pit, from where he is drawn out by Ebed-Melech by order of the king; staying in the entry of the prison, he persuades the king to go out to the Chaldeans, otherwise he himself shall not escape them, and the city shall be burned by them with fire: the king also commands Jeremiah to keep this conversation secret.*

Now Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur the son of Malchiah, heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people, saying:

2 "Thus says the Lord: † 'Whoever remains in this city shall die by the sword, and by famine, and by pestilence: but he who flees to the Chaldeans shall live, and his soul shall be safe and alive.'
3 Thus says the Lord: 'This city shall surely be delivered into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he shall take it.'"
4 And the princes said to the king: "We pray you that this man may be put to death: for he deliberately weakens the hands of the men of war who remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, speaking to them according to these words: for indeed this man does not seek peace for this people, but evil."
5 And King Zedekiah said: "Behold, he is in your hands: for it is not lawful for the king to deny you anything."
6 They took Jeremiah therefore, and cast him into the pit <note>original: "lacum"</note> of Malchiah the son of Amelech, which was in the entry of the prison: and they let Jeremiah down with ropes into the pit, in which there was no water, but mud: and so Jeremiah sank into the mire.
7 Now Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian, a <term>eunuch</term> <note>A high-ranking court official, often of foreign birth.</note> who was in the king's house, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the pit: moreover, the king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate.
8 And Ebed-Melech went out of the king's house, and spoke to the king, saying:
9 "My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have perpetrated against Jeremiah the prophet, casting him into the pit so that he may die there of hunger, for there is no more bread in the city."
10 The king therefore commanded Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian, saying: "Take thirty men with you from here, and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the pit before he dies."
11 So Ebed-Melech, taking the men with him, entered the king's house, which was under the storehouse: and he took from there old rags, and ancient things that had rotted, and let them down by cords to Jeremiah in the pit.
12 And Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian said to Jeremiah: "Put these old rags, and these torn and rotten things, under the armpits of your hands, and over the ropes": and Jeremiah did so.
13 And they drew up Jeremiah with the ropes, and brought him out of the pit: but Jeremiah remained in the entry of the prison.
14 And King Zedekiah sent, and took Jeremiah the prophet to him at the third door, which was in the house of the Lord: and the king said to Jeremiah: "I am asking you for a word; hide nothing from me."
15 But Jeremiah said to Zedekiah: "If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you counsel, you will not listen to me."

## CHAPTER XXXIX.

*Jerusalem is captured by the king of Babylon; King Zedekiah is caught while fleeing along with his princes; his sons are slaughtered before his eyes along with the nobles; he himself is blinded and led in chains to Babylon; the wall of Jerusalem is torn down and the palace and other houses are burned with fire; part of the common people are transferred to Babylon, and part are left in Jerusalem; meanwhile, Jeremiah is led out free from the court of the guard.*

3 And all the princes of the king of Babylon entered and sat in the middle gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim, Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag, and all the rest of the princes of the king of Babylon.

Having captured him, they brought him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at <term>Riblah</term> <note>An ancient city in the land of Hamath (modern-day Syria) used as a military headquarters.</note>, which is in the land of Hamath, and he passed judgment upon him.

17 But I will deliver you on that day, says the Lord; and you shall not be given into the hand of the men whom you fear.
18 For I will surely deliver you, and you shall not fall by the sword; but your life shall be given to you as a prize of war, because you have put your trust in me, says the Lord."

**5** And if you choose not to come with me, then live with <term>Gedaliah</term> <note>Godolias in the original Latin.</note> son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has placed over the cities of Judah. Live with him in the midst of the people; or go wherever it pleases you to go. The captain of the guard also gave him food and small gifts, and sent him away.
**6** And Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at <term>Mizpah</term> <note>Masphath in the original Latin; an ancient town near Jerusalem used as an administrative center.</note>, and lived with him in the midst of the people who had been left in the land.
**7** When all the captains of the army who were scattered through the regions, they and their companions, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he had committed to him men, women, and children, and the poor of the land who had not been carried away to Babylon:
**8** They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai, who were from Netophah, and Jezaniah son of the Maachathite, they and their men.

### C H A P T E R  X L I .

> *Ishmael by treachery kills Gedaliah the governor, along with the Jews and Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah; and killing eighty others, he spared ten who said they had treasures: and finally, fearing Johanan and the captains of the warriors, he fled with eight men, the people he had taken captive having been liberated: all those who remain, however, decide to flee into Egypt from the face of the Chaldeans.*

**AND** it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal seed, and the nobles of the King and ten men with him, came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah: and they ate bread there together in Mizpah.
**2** And Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him arose and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword, and they killed him, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
**3** All the Jews also who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, and the men of war, Ishmael struck down.
**4** And on the second day after he had killed Gedaliah, while no man yet knew of it,
**5** There came men from Shechem, and from Shiloh, and from Samaria, eighty men, having their beards shaven and their clothes torn, and looking disheveled; and they had offerings and incense in their hands to offer in the house of the Lord.
**6** And Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went: and when he met them, he said to them: "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
**7** And when they had come to the middle of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah killed them near the middle of a pit, he and the men who were with him.
**8** But ten men were found among them who said to Ishmael: "Do not kill us, for we have stores in the field of wheat, and barley, and oil, and honey." And he stopped, and did not kill them with their brothers.
**9** Now the pit into which Ishmael had thrown all the corpses of the men whom he had struck down because of Gedaliah, was the one which King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.
**10** And Ishmael led away captive all the remnant of the people who were in Mizpah: the king’s daughters, and all the people who remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. And Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them and departed to go over to the children of Ammon.
**11** But Johanan son of Kareah, and all the captains of the warriors who were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
**12** And taking all the men, they set out to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him by the great waters which are in <term>Gibeon</term> <note>Gabaon in the original Latin.</note>.
**13** And when all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the captains of the warriors who were with him, they were glad.
**14** And all the people whom Ishmael had taken from Mizpah turned back and went to Johanan son of Kareah.

### CHAPTER XLII.

*Jeremiah is sent to pray and consult the Lord on behalf of the remnant of the Jews; he responds that they will be safe if they remain in Judah. However, if they flee to Egypt, he says they will all die by the sword, famine, and plague.*

**1** And all the captains of the warriors approached, including Johanan son of Kareah, and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and the rest of the common people from the least to the greatest.
**2** And they said to Jeremiah the prophet: "Let our petition fall before you: pray for us to the Lord your God, for all this remnant; for we are left but a few out of many, as your eyes see us.
**3** And let the Lord your God show us the way in which we should walk, and the word that we should do."
**4** Then Jeremiah the prophet said to them: "I have heard you. Behold, I will pray to the Lord your God according to your words; and every word, whatever he answers me, I will indicate to you, and I will hide nothing from you."
**5** And they said to Jeremiah: "May the Lord be a witness of truth and faith between us, if we do not act according to every word for which the Lord your God shall send you to us.
**6** Whether it is good or evil, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we send you, so that it may be well with us when we have heard the voice of the Lord our God."
**7** Now when ten days were completed, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
**8** And he called Johanan son of Kareah, and all the captains of the warriors who were with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest.
**9** And he said to them: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present your prayers in his sight:
**10** If you remain quietly in this land, I will build you up and not destroy you; I will plant you and not pluck you up; for now I am appeased concerning the evil I have done to you.
**11** Do not fear the king of Babylon, whom you dread in your fear; do not fear him, says the Lord, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
**12** And I will show you mercies, and I will have pity on you, and I will make you dwell in your own land.
**13** But if you say: 'We will not dwell in this land,' and do not listen to the voice of the Lord your God,

<column-break/>

**14** saying: 'By no means, but we will go to the land of Egypt, where we shall see no war, nor hear the sound of the trumpet, nor suffer hunger; and there we will dwell.'
**15** Because of this, now hear the word of the Lord, you remnant of Judah: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: If you set your faces to enter Egypt, and go in to dwell there,
**16** the sword which you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt; and the famine for which you are anxious will cling to you in Egypt, and there you shall die.
**17** And all the men who have set their faces to enter Egypt to dwell there shall die by the sword, and by famine, and by plague; none of them shall remain or escape from the face of the evil that I will bring upon them.
**18** For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Just as my fury and my indignation have been poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so shall my indignation be poured out upon you when you enter Egypt; and you shall be an object of swearing, and of horror, and a curse, and a reproach; and you shall never see this place again.
**19** The word of the Lord is upon you, O remnant of Judah: Do not enter Egypt. Knowing this, you shall know that I have protested to you this day,
**20** because you have deceived your own souls. For you sent me to the Lord our God, saying: 'Pray for us to the Lord our God, and according to all that the Lord our God shall say to you, so declare to us, and we will do it.'
**21** And I have declared it to you today, and you have not listened to the voice of the Lord your God concerning all the things for which he has sent me to you.
**22** Now therefore, knowing this you shall know that you shall die by the sword, and by famine, and by plague in the place where you desired to enter to dwell."

### CHAPTER XLIII.

*The remnant of the Jews, not listening to the Lord's command which Jeremiah reported, set out together with Jeremiah and Baruch for Egypt; where Jeremiah, having arrived, prophesies that the king of Babylon will devastate the land of Egypt along with its idols and will rule over it.*

**1** And it came to pass, when Jeremiah had finished speaking to the people all the words of the Lord their God, for which the Lord their God had sent him to them—all these words—
**2** that Azariah son of Hoshaiah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and all the proud men spoke, saying to Jeremiah: "You are speaking a lie; the Lord our God has not sent you, saying: 'Do not enter Egypt to dwell there.'
**3** But <term>Baruch</term> <note>Jeremiah's scribe and close associate.</note> son of Neriah incites you against us, to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, to kill us, and to cause us to be carried away to Babylon."
**4** And so Johanan son of Kareah, and all the captains of the warriors, and all the people, did not listen to the voice of the Lord to remain in the land of Judah.
**5** But Johanan son of Kareah and all the captains of the warriors took all the remnant of Judah, who had returned from all the nations to which they had previously been dispersed, to dwell in the land of Judah;

### CHAPTER XLIV.

*The Jews in Egypt are rebuked by Jeremiah for their idolatry; they obstinately respond, along with a multitude of women, that they will persist in their long-standing idolatry. Jeremiah predicts that they shall all be consumed by the sword and famine, that the king of Egypt will be delivered into the hands of his enemies, and that the land of Egypt will be utterly laid waste.*

**1** **The word** that came to Jeremiah for all the Jews who lived in the land of Egypt—those living in Migdol, in Tahpanhes, in Memphis, and in the land of Pathros <note>original: Phatures; Upper Egypt.</note>—saying:
**2** "Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: You have seen all this evil that I brought upon Jerusalem and upon all the cities of Judah; and behold, they are desolate today, and no one lives in them.
**3** This was because of the wickedness they committed to provoke me to anger, going to offer sacrifice and worship foreign gods whom neither they, nor you, nor your fathers knew.
**4** And I sent to you all my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them <note>A Hebrew idiom meaning "to do something persistently or diligently."</note>, saying: ‘Do not do this abominable thing which I hate.’
**5** But they did not listen, nor did they incline their ear to turn from their evils and stop sacrificing to foreign gods.
**6** Therefore my indignation and my fury were poured out and kindled in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem; and they have been turned into a wasteland and a desolation, as it is this day.
**7** And now, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Why do you commit this great evil against your own souls, to cut off from you man and woman, child and infant from the midst of Judah, leaving yourselves no remnant at all?

<column-break/>

**8** Why do you provoke me with the works of your hands, sacrificing to foreign gods in the land of Egypt where you have come to live? Will you perish and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
**9** Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers, and the evils of the kings of Judah, and the evils of their wives, and your own evils, and the evils of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the regions of Jerusalem?
**10** They have not been cleansed even to this day; they have not feared, nor have they walked in the law of the Lord or in my precepts which I set before you and before your fathers.
**11** Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: <margin>† Amos 9:4</margin> Behold, I will set my face against you for evil, and I will destroy all of Judah.
**12** And I will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces to enter the land of Egypt to live there; and they shall all be consumed in the land of Egypt. They shall fall by the sword and by famine; from the least to the greatest they shall be consumed. By the sword and by famine they shall die; and they shall be an object of an oath, a wonder, a curse, and a reproach.
**13** For I will punish those who live in the land of Egypt, just as I punished Jerusalem, with the sword, famine, and plague.
**14** And there shall be none who escape or remain of the remnant of the Jews who have gone to live as foreigners in the land of Egypt, to return to the land of Judah, to which they lift up their souls to return and live; they shall not return, except for those who flee."
**15** Then all the men who knew that their wives offered sacrifice to foreign gods, and all the women who stood by—a great multitude—and all the people living in Pathros in the land of Egypt, answered Jeremiah, saying:
**16** "As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you.
**17** Instead, we will certainly do every word that goes out of our own mouth: to sacrifice to the queen of heaven <note>Likely referring to Astarte or Ishtar, a Mesopotamian and Canaanite goddess of fertility and war.</note> and to pour out drink offerings to her, just as we and our fathers, our kings and our princes have done in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of bread, and it was well with us, and we saw no evil.
**18** But since the time we stopped sacrificing to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by the sword and famine."
**19** "And if we sacrifice to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, did we make cakes to worship her and pour out drink offerings to her without our husbands' consent?"
**20** Then Jeremiah said to all the people—to the men, to the women, and to all the people who had given him that answer:
**21** "The sacrifice that you offered in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings and your princes, and the people of the land—did not the Lord remember them, and did it not come into His heart?
**22** The Lord could no longer bear it because of the wickedness of your deeds and because of the abominations you committed; therefore your land has become a desolation, an astonishment, and a curse, without an inhabitant, as it is this day."

2 "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, to you, Baruch:

5 And do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says the Lord; but I will give you your life as a prize of war <note>original: animam tuam in salutem; literally "your life for salvation," a Hebrew idiom meaning that while he loses everything else, his life will be spared as if it were a spoil of war.</note> in all places wherever you go.'"

11 Go up to Gilead and take balm <note>original: resinam; the famous "balm of Gilead" was a medicinal resin used for healing wounds.</note>, O virgin daughter of Egypt! In vain do you multiply medicines; there shall be no healing for you.

22 Her voice shall sound like brass <note>original: "vox ejus quasi æris sonabit"; while modern translations often compare Egypt's voice to a hissing serpent, the Latin describes a metallic, ringing sound, perhaps of armor or trumpets.</note>: for they shall hurry with an army, and come against her with axes, like those who cut wood.
23 They have cut down her forest, says the Lord, which cannot be counted; they are multiplied more than locusts, and are without number.
24 The daughter of Egypt is shamed, and delivered into the hand of the people of the north.
25 The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, said: "Behold, I will visit punishment upon the noise of Alexandria <note>original: "Alexandriæ"; in the Latin Vulgate, this refers to the city of No-Amon or Thebes, which was the Egyptian capital; Alexandria as we know it was not yet founded in Jeremiah's time.</note>, and upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt, and upon its gods, and upon its kings, and upon Pharaoh, and upon those who trust in him.
26 And I will give them into the hands of those who seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants; and after this, it shall be inhabited as in the days of old," says the Lord.
<margin>† Isaiah 43:1 & 44:2.</margin>
27 "And you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, and do not be dismayed, Israel: for behold, I will save you from afar, and your offspring from the land of your captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall rest, and shall prosper; and there shall be no one to make him afraid.
28 And you, do not fear, my servant Jacob," says the Lord, "for I am with you; for I will consume all the nations to which I have driven you; but I will not consume you, but will correct you in judgment, nor will I spare you as if you were innocent."

### CHAPTER XLVII.

*The destruction of the Philistines, Tyre, Sidon, Gaza, and Ashkelon is predicted.*

The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza:
2 Thus says the Lord: "Behold, waters rise up from the north, and they shall be like an overflowing torrent, and they shall cover the land and its fullness, the city and its inhabitants. Men shall cry out, and all the inhabitants of the land shall howl,
3 At the noise of the pomp of arms, and of his warriors, at the commotion of his chariots, and the multitude of his wheels. Fathers did not look back to their sons, their hands being feeble <note>original: "manibus dissolutis"; literally "with dissolved hands," a metaphor for being paralyzed by fear.</note>
4 Because of the coming of the day in which all the Philistines shall be laid waste, and Tyre and Sidon shall be destroyed with all their remaining helpers: for the Lord has laid waste the Philistines, the remnant of the island of Cappadocia <note>original: "insulæ Cappadociæ"; typically identified with the island of Crete (Caphtor), the ancestral home of the Philistines.</note>.
5 Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silent, and the remnant of their valley: how long will you cut yourself? <note>Self-cutting and shaving the head were ancient mourning rituals.</note>
6 O sword of the Lord, how long will you not be quiet? Enter into your scabbard, rest, and be still."
7 How can it rest, when the Lord has commanded it against Ashkelon, and against its maritime regions, and has appointed it there?

### CHAPTER XLVIII.

*The Lord predicts the destruction of Moab and all its cities, but in the latter days their captivity is to be released; he who does the work of the Lord deceitfully and keeps his sword from blood is called cursed.*

TO Moab thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: "Woe to Nebo, for it is laid waste and shamed: Kiriathaim is taken: the stronghold is shamed and has trembled.
2 There is no more rejoicing in Moab against Heshbon: they have devised evil. 'Come, and let us cut her off from being a nation': therefore you shall be silent and still, and the sword shall follow you.
3 A voice of crying at Horonaim: great desolation and crushing.
4 Moab is crushed: announce the cry to her little ones.
5 For by the ascent of Luhith, weeping shall go up with tears; for in the descent of Horonaim the enemies have heard the howling of destruction:
6 Flee, save your lives: and you shall be like tamarisk <note>original: "myricæ"; a desert shrub symbolizing desolation and survival in harsh conditions.</note> in the desert.
<margin>† Above 27:6.</margin>
7 For because you had confidence in your fortifications and in your treasures, you also shall be taken: and Chemosh <note>The national god of the Moabites.</note> shall go into captivity, his priests and his princes together.
8 And the spoiler shall come to every city, and no city shall be saved: and the valleys shall perish, and the plains shall be destroyed, because the Lord has spoken.
9 Give a flower <note>original: "florem"; can mean a bloom or salt, but contextually refers to the fleeting glory or the need for wings to flee.</note> to Moab, for she shall go out flowering: and her cities shall be desert and uninhabitable.
10 Cursed is he who does the work of the Lord deceitfully: and cursed is he who keeps back his sword from blood.
11 Moab has been fertile from his youth, and has rested on his dregs <note>original: "fæcibus"; a winemaking metaphor meaning Moab has been undisturbed and unchanged, like wine not poured from one jar to another.</note>: nor has he been poured from vessel to vessel, and has not gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed.
12 Therefore behold, the days come," says the Lord, "and I will send to him those who order and tip over jars, and they shall lay him low, and empty his vessels, and break their jars together.
<margin>† 1 Kings 12:29.</margin>
13 And Moab shall be shamed by Chemosh, as the house of Israel was shamed by Bethel <note>Bethel was the site of the golden calf worship, which failed to save the northern kingdom of Israel.</note>, in which it had confidence.
14 How do you say: 'We are valiant, and robust men for battle'?
15 Moab is laid waste, and her cities are cut down: and her chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter," says the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts.
16 The destruction of Moab is near to come: and his evil shall run very swiftly.
17 Console him, all you who are round about him; and all you who know his name, say: 'How is the strong staff broken, the glorious rod?'
18 Come down from glory, and sit in thirst, O inhabitant of the daughter of Dibon: because the spoiler of Moab has come up to you, he has destroyed your fortifications.
19 Stand by the way, and look out, inhabitant of Aroer: ask him who flees: and say to him who has escaped: 'What has happened?'
20 Moab is shamed, because he is conquered."

### CHAPTER XLIX.

->*The desolation of Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and the kingdoms of Hazor and Elam is foretold; however, the captivity of the children of Ammon and Elam is to be ended.*<-

1 To the children of Ammon. Thus says the Lord: Does Israel have no sons? Or has he no heir? Why then has Milcom <note>original: "Melchom"; the national god of the Ammonites, often associated with human sacrifice.</note> possessed Gad as an inheritance, and his people dwelt in its cities?
2 Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will cause the din of battle to be heard against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and it shall be scattered in turmoil, and her daughter-cities shall be burnt with fire, and Israel shall possess those who possessed him, says the Lord.
3 Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste: cry out, you daughters of Rabbah, gird yourselves with sackcloth; mourn and go about the hedges, for Milcom shall be led into captivity, his priests and his princes together.
4 Why do you glory in the valleys? Your valley has flowed away, O delicate daughter, who trusted in your treasures and said: "Who shall come against me?"
5 Behold, I will bring terror upon you, says the Lord God of hosts, from all those who are around you: and you shall be scattered every man from before his face, and there shall be none to gather the fugitives.
6 And after these things I will bring back the captives of the children of Ammon, says the Lord.
7 To Edom <note>original: "Idumæam"; the land of the descendants of Esau.</note>. Thus says the Lord of hosts: Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the sons? Has their wisdom become useless?
8 Flee and turn your backs; go down into the deep pit, inhabitants of Dedan: for I have brought the destruction of Esau upon him, the time of his visitation.
9 If grape-gatherers had come upon you, would they not have left a cluster? If thieves in the night, they would have taken only what was enough for them.
10 But I have uncovered Esau, I have revealed his hidden places, and he cannot be hidden: his offspring is laid waste, and his brothers, and his neighbors, and he shall not be.
11 Leave your orphans: I will make them live; and your widows shall hope in me.
12 For thus says the Lord: Behold, they whose judgment was not to drink the cup <note>The "cup" is a frequent biblical metaphor for God's wrath or judgment.</note>, shall surely drink; and shall you be left as if innocent? You shall not be innocent, but you shall surely drink.
13 For I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that Bozrah shall be a desolation, and a reproach, and a desert, and a curse: and all its cities shall be everlasting wastes.

### CHAPTER 50.

->*Babylon, which afflicts the children of Israel in captivity, shall be completely devastated by the kings of the North once the people have been successfully led back twice to their own land.*<-

The word that the Lord spoke against Babylon and against the land of the Chaldeans <note>The region surrounding Babylon.</note> by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.
2 Declare among the nations, and make it heard; lift up a standard, preach it, and do not conceal it. Say: Babylon is taken, Bel is confounded, Merodach <note>Bel and Merodach (Marduk) were the primary gods of the Babylonians.</note> is defeated, her sculptures are confounded, their idols are overcome.
3 For a nation has come up against her from the North, which shall make her land a desolation; and there shall be no one to dwell in it, from man to beast; they have moved and gone away.
4 In those days and at that time, says the Lord, the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together; walking and weeping, they shall hurry, and seek the Lord their God.
5 They shall ask the way to Zion, with their faces turned toward it. They shall come and join themselves to the Lord in an everlasting covenant that shall never be forgotten.
6 My people have been a lost flock; their shepherds have deceived them and made them wander on the mountains; they have gone from mountain to hill, they have forgotten their resting place.
7 All who found them have devoured them, and their enemies said: "We have not sinned," because they sinned against the Lord, the beauty of justice, and the hope of their fathers, the Lord.
8 Depart from the midst of Babylon, and go out of the land of the Chaldeans; and be like the rams <note>original: "hœdi"; literally young goats or bucks leading the flock.</note> before the flock.
9 For behold, I am stirring up and will bring against Babylon a great assembly of nations from the north country; and they shall be prepared against her, and from there she shall be taken. Their arrow is like that of a mighty destroyer; it shall not return empty.
10 And Chaldea shall be a prey; all who waste her shall be filled, says the Lord.
11 Because you rejoiced and spoke great things, you who plundered my inheritance; because you are spread out like calves upon the grass and have bellowed like bulls.
12 Your mother is deeply confounded, and she who bore you is leveled with the dust; behold, she shall be the last among the nations, a desert, pathless, and dry.
13 Because of the wrath of the Lord, it shall not be inhabited, but shall be wholly reduced to a desolation; everyone who passes through Babylon shall be appalled and shall hiss at all her wounds.

### CHAPTER LI.

->*The evils threatening Babylon from the kings of the Medes are foretold.*<-

**T**hus says the Lord: Behold, I will raise up against Babylon and against its inhabitants, who have lifted up their heart against me, as it were a pestilential wind.
2 And I will send winnowers to Babylon, and they shall winnow her and shall destroy her land: for they have come against her on every side in the day of her affliction.

64 And you shall say: "Thus shall Babylon be submerged, and she shall not rise from the face of the affliction which I bring upon her, and she shall be dissolved." Thus far are the words of Jeremiah.

### CHAPTER LII.

> *A repetition of what precedes: namely, that Jerusalem, having been besieged by Nebuchadnezzar, is captured after two years; and King Zedekiah of Judah, while fleeing, is brought back; and his sons having been slaughtered before his eyes along with the princes of Judah, he is blinded and led bound into Babylon. And after the temple, the palace, and the other houses are burned, everyone is moved to Babylon except for a few vine-dressers and farmers. Likewise the vessels of the temple, among which are described two bronze columns. Also the number of Jews moved to Babylon at different times, where King Jehoiachin is exalted after being brought out of prison after 37 years.*

<margin>2 Kings 24:18; 2 Chronicles 36:11.</margin>
1 Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign: and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
2 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
3 For the fury of the Lord was against Jerusalem and Judah, until He cast them out from His presence: and Zedekiah revolted from the king of Babylon.
<margin>2 Kings 25:1; Jeremiah 39:1; and above.</margin>
4 And it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month: Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem; and they besieged it and built fortifications against it round about.
5 And the city was besieged until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
6 But in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, famine took hold of the city: and there was no food for the people of the land.
7 And the city was broken into, and all its men of war fled; and they went out of the city by night, by the way of the gate which is between the two walls and leads to the king's garden (while the Chaldeans were surrounding the city), and they went by the way that leads into the desert.
8 But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king: and they overtook Zedekiah in the desert, which is near Jericho: and all his retinue fled from him.
9 And when they had captured the king, they brought him to the king of Babylon in Riblah, which is in the land of Hamath: and he spoke judgments against him.
10 And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes: and he also killed all the princes of Judah in Riblah.
11 And he put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with shackles; and the king of Babylon brought him into Babylon and placed him in the house of the prison until the day of his death.
12 In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month—this is the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard <note>original: "princeps militiæ" — the chief executioner or commander of the bodyguard</note>, who stood before the king of Babylon, came into Jerusalem:
13 And he burned the house of the Lord, and the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great house he consumed with fire.
14 And the whole army of the Chaldeans, who were with the master of the guard, destroyed the entire wall of Jerusalem round about.
15 Then Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carried away some of the poor people, and the rest of the common folk who remained in the city, and the fugitives who had defected to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.

17 The Chaldeans <note>The Babylonians</note> also broke into pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the bronze sea <note>A massive ceremonial basin for washing</note> that was in the house of the Lord, and they carried all their bronze to Babylon.
18 They also took away the pots, the flesh-hooks, the musical instruments <note>original: "psalteria" — though in this liturgical context it likely refers to snuffers or sacrificial bowls</note>, the vials, the small mortars, and all the bronze vessels used in the temple service.
19 The captain of the guard also took the water pots, the censers, the pitchers, the basins, the lampstands, the mortars, and the cups: whatever was of gold, he took as gold, and whatever was of silver, he took as silver.
20 As for the two pillars, the one "sea," and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the bases—which King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord—the weight of the bronze from all these vessels was beyond calculation.
21 Regarding the pillars, the height of each pillar was eighteen cubits <note>About 27 feet or 8 meters</note>, and a line of twelve cubits measured its circumference; its thickness was four fingers, and it was hollow inside.
22 And a bronze capital was on top of each; the height of one capital was five cubits. There was latticework and pomegranates all around the crown, all made of bronze. The second pillar and its pomegranates were similar.
23 There were ninety-six pomegranates hanging down, and the total number of pomegranates surrounding the latticework was one hundred.
24 The captain of the guard also took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.
25 And from the city he took one eunuch who was in charge of the fighting men, and

<column-break/>

seven men from those who "saw the king’s face" <note>Inner-circle advisors</note> who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the young recruits, and sixty men of the common people who were found in the midst of the city.
26 Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
27 And the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah was carried away captive out of its own land.
28 This is the number of people whom Nebuchadnezzar carried away: in the seventh year, three thousand and twenty-three Jews.
29 In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, eight hundred and thirty-two souls from Jerusalem.
30 In the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away seven hundred and forty-five Jewish souls. All the souls together were four thousand six hundred.
31 And it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, showed favor to <note>original: "elevavit... caput" — literally "lifted the head," meaning to pardon or show mercy</note> Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
32 He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
33 He changed Jehoiachin’s prison clothes, and the king ate bread in his presence continually all the days of his life.
34 And for his food, a regular allowance was given to him by the king of Babylon, a portion for each day, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.

### CHAPTER ONE.

#### ALEPH <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet. This poem is an acrostic, with each verse beginning with a successive letter.</note>
1 How solitary sits the city that was full of people! She who was mistress of the nations has become like a widow; the princess of provinces has been made a subject of tribute.

#### BETH <note>The second letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>
<margin>Jeremiah 13:17</margin>
2 Weeping, she has wept in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks. There is no one to comfort her among all her dear ones; all her friends have despised her and have become her enemies.

#### GIMEL <note>The third letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>
3 Judah has migrated because of affliction and the greatness of her slavery; she has dwelt among the nations, yet she has found no rest. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the midst of her distress.

<column-break/>

#### DALETH <note>The fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>
4 The roads to Zion mourn because no one comes to the solemn feast. All her gates are destroyed, her priests groan, her virgins are disheveled, and she herself is overwhelmed with bitterness.

#### HE <note>The fifth letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>
5 Her adversaries have become her masters, and her enemies have been enriched, because the Lord has spoken against her for the multitude of her iniquities. Her little ones have been led into captivity before the face of the oppressor.

#### VAU <note>The sixth letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>
6 All her beauty has departed from the daughter of Zion. Her princes have become like rams that find no pasture, and they have gone away without strength before the face of the pursuer.

#### ZAIN <note>The seventh letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>
7 Jerusalem remembered the days of her affliction and the betrayal of all her precious things which she had from the days of old, when her people fell into the enemy's hand and there was no helper. The enemies saw her and mocked her sabbaths.

<note>The Book of Lamentations consists of five poems mourning the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BCE. In the original Hebrew, these chapters are acrostics, where each verse begins with a successive letter of the alphabet. This Latin version preserves the Hebrew letter names as headings for each stanza.</note>

->N U N.<-

->A I N.<-

->S A D E.<-

->C O P H.<-

->R E S.<-

### C H A P T E R  II.

->A L E P H.<-

1 **H**ow has the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his fury: he has cast down from heaven to earth the glory of Israel, and has not remembered his footstool <note>Often referring to the Ark of the Covenant or the Temple</note> in the day of his anger.

->B E T H.<-

->G H I M E L.<-

3 In the wrath of his fury he has broken every horn <note>A symbol of strength and power</note> of Israel: he has turned back his right hand from the face of the enemy: and he has burned in Jacob like a fire of devouring flame round about.

->D A L E T H.<-

4 He has bent his bow like an enemy, he has strengthened his right hand like an adversary: and he has killed all that was beautiful to the eye in the tabernacle of the daughter of Zion, he has poured out his indignation like fire.

->H E.<-

5 The Lord has become like an enemy: he has cast down Israel, he has cast down all her walls: he has destroyed her strongholds, and has filled the daughter of Judah with mourning and lamentation.

->V A U.<-

6 And he has destroyed his tent like a garden: he has demolished his tabernacle: the Lord has delivered into oblivion in Zion the festivals and the Sabbath; and in the indignation of his fury, he has despised both king and priest.

->Z A I N.<-

7 The Lord has rejected his altar, he has cursed his sanctuary: he has delivered the walls of her towers into the hand of the enemy: they have made a noise in the house of the Lord, as if on a solemn feast day.

->H E T H.<-

8 The Lord purposed to destroy the wall of the daughter of Zion: he stretched out his measuring line, and did not turn back his hand from destruction: the rampart has mourned, and the wall is equally destroyed.

->T H E T H.<-

9 Her gates are sunk into the earth: he has destroyed and broken her bars; her king and her princes are among the Gentiles: the law is no more, and her prophets have found no vision from the Lord.

->J O D.<-

10 The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground and are silent: they have sprinkled dust upon their heads and girt themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem cast their heads down to the ground.

->C A P H.<-

11 My eyes have failed with weeping, my bowels are troubled: my liver <note>In ancient psychology, the liver was considered the seat of deep emotion</note> is poured out upon the earth because of the destruction of the daughter of my people, when the little ones and the infants fainted in the streets of the town.

->L A M E D.<-

12 They said to their mothers: "Where is the grain and wine?" when they fainted like the wounded in the streets of the city: when they breathed out their souls into their mothers' laps.
