### CHAPTER ONE.

*The Jews from Babylon send the book of Baruch to those who were in Jerusalem, together with collected funds, so that with the offering of burnt sacrifices they may pray for them, and for Nebuchadnezzar and his son Belshazzar, and they confess their sins.*

**1** And these are the words of the book which Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, the son of Zedekiah, the son of Hasadiah, the son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylonia,
**2** In the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans <note>The Babylonians, who conquered Jerusalem</note> took Jerusalem and burned it with fire.
**3** And Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who came to hear the book,
**4** And in the hearing of the powerful, the sons of the kings, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of the people, from the least to the greatest of them, even all those living in Babylonia by the river Sud.
**5** And when they heard it, they wept, and fasted, and prayed in the sight of the Lord.
**6** And they collected money according to what each man's hand was able to give,
**7** And they sent it to Jerusalem to Jehoiakim the son of Hilkiah, the son of Shallum, the priest, and to the priests, and to all the people who were found with him in Jerusalem:
**8** At the time when he received the vessels of the temple of the Lord, which had been taken away from the temple, to return them to the land of Judah on the tenth day of the month Sivan—the silver vessels which Zedekiah the son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made,
**9** After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had captured Jeconiah, and the princes, and all the powerful men, and the people of the land, from Jerusalem, and led them bound to Babylon.
**10** And they said: "Behold, we have sent money to you; with this, buy burnt offerings <term>holocautomata: sacrifices entirely consumed by fire</term> and incense, and prepare grain offerings <note>original: "manna"; here referring to the 'mincha' or cereal offering rather than the bread from heaven</note>, and offer for sin at the altar of the Lord our God.
**11** And pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and for the life of Belshazzar his son, that their days may be as the days of heaven upon the earth:
**12** And that the Lord may give us strength, and enlighten our eyes, that we may live under the shadow <note>Under the protection or rule</note> of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Belshazzar his son, and serve them for many days, and find grace in their sight.
**13** And pray for us ourselves to the Lord our God: for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and his fury has not been turned away from us even to this day.
**14** And read this book, which we have sent to you to be recited in the temple of the Lord, on a feast day, and at a convenient time:
<margin>† Isaiah 1:26</margin>
**15** And you shall say: † Justice belongs to the Lord our God, but to us the confusion of our face <note>A biblical expression for public shame or disgrace</note>, as it is this day to all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
**16** To our kings, and to our princes, and to our priests, and to our prophets, and to our fathers.
<margin>† Daniel 9:5</margin>
**17** † We have sinned before the Lord our God, and we did not believe, being distrustful of him:

<column-break/>

**18** And we were not subject to him, and we did not hear the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his commandments which he gave to us.
**19** From the day on which he led our fathers out of the land of Egypt, even to this day, we were unbelieving toward the Lord our God: and we were scattered and fell away, so as not to hear his voice.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 28:15</margin>
**20** † And many evils and curses have clung to us, which the Lord established through Moses his servant: who led our fathers out of the land of Egypt, to give us a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today.
**21** And we did not hear the voice of the Lord our God according to all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us:
**22** And we have gone away, every one into the inclination of our own evil heart, to serve foreign gods, doing evil before the eyes of the Lord our God."

### CHAPTER TWO.

*The Jews in captivity confess that the evils which God had threatened through his prophets have happened to them because of their sins; therefore, pouring out prayers, they seek the mercy which he had promised through Moses that he would give to those who repent.*

**1** Because of this, the Lord our God has confirmed his word, which he spoke to us, and to our judges who judged Israel, and to our kings, and to our princes, and to all Israel and Judah:
<margin>† Deuteronomy 28:53</margin>
**2** That the Lord would bring upon us great evils, such as have not been done under heaven, just as they have been done in Jerusalem, † according to what is written in the law of Moses,
**3** That a man should eat the flesh of his own son, and the flesh of his own daughter <note>Referring to the desperate famine during the siege of Jerusalem</note>.
**4** And he has delivered them into the hand of all the kings who are around us, as a reproach and a desolation among all the peoples where the Lord has scattered us.
**5** And we have been made to be beneath, and not above: because we have sinned against the Lord our God by not obeying his voice.
<margin>† Above 1:15</margin>
**6** † Justice belongs to the Lord our God, but to us and to our fathers the confusion of face, as it is this day.
**7** For the Lord has spoken against us all these evils which have come upon us:
**8** And we have not entreated the face of the Lord our God, that we might return, every one of us, from our very wicked ways.
**9** And the Lord has kept watch over the evils, and has brought them upon us: for the Lord is just in all his works which he has commanded us:
**10** And we have not heard his voice to walk in the precepts of the Lord, which he set before our face.
<margin>† Daniel 9:15</margin>
**11** † And now, O Lord God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand, and with signs, and with wonders, and with your great power, and with a high arm, and have made a name for yourself, as it is this day:
**12** We have sinned, we have acted impiously, we have behaved unjustly, O Lord our God, in all your justifications.
**13** Let your anger be turned away from us: for we are left...

### CHAPTER III.

> They continue to confess their sins and the sins of their fathers, beseeching God for mercy: Israel is said to be in captivity because it has forsaken the way of wisdom, which is not found by the powerful, the wealthy, or the giants, but had been delivered to the people of Israel by God, whom all his creatures obey: and it is added concerning Christ's coming in the flesh.

1 AND now, O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the soul in anguish and the troubled spirit cries out to you:
2 Hear, O Lord, and have mercy, for you are a merciful God, and have mercy on us: for we have sinned before you.
3 For you sit forever, and shall we perish for eternity?
4 O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear now the prayer of the dead of Israel <note>Likely referring to those who are "as dead" in exile or the spirits of the ancestors</note>, and of their children who have sinned before you, and have not heard the voice of the Lord their God, and so these evils have clung to us.
5 Do not remember the iniquities of our fathers, but remember your hand and your name at this time:
6 For you are the Lord our God, and we will praise you, O Lord:
7 Because for this reason you have put your fear in our hearts, that we might call upon your name and praise you in our captivity, because we are converted from the iniquity of our fathers, who sinned before you.
8 And behold, we are in our captivity today, where you have scattered us as a reproach, and as a curse, and for sin, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, who departed from you, O Lord our God.
9 Hear, O Israel, the commandments of life: give ear, that you may know wisdom.
10 How is it, Israel, that you are in the land of your enemies?
11 You have grown old in a foreign land, you are defiled with the dead: you are counted with those who go down into the underworld.
12 You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom.
13 For if you had walked in the way of God, you would surely have dwelt in everlasting peace.
14 Learn where there is wisdom, where there is strength, where there is understanding: so that you may know at the same time where there is length of days and life, where there is the light of the eyes and peace.
15 Who has found its place? And who has entered into its treasures?
16 Where are the princes of the nations, and those who rule over the beasts that are upon the earth?
17 Those who play with the birds of the air,
18 Those who treasure up silver and gold, in which men trust, and there is no end to their acquiring? Those who work in silver and are anxious, and there is no finding of their works?
19 They are exterminated, and have gone down to the underworld, and others have risen up in their place.

### CHAPTER IV.

> Jerusalem mourns her desolation and encourages her children to be of good courage: for just as God delivered them to their adversaries because of their sins, so he will punish their enemies once they are set free.

1 This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that exists forever; all who hold to it shall come to life; but those who have abandoned it, to death.
2 Return, O Jacob, and take hold of it; walk by the way to its splendor, in the presence of its light.
3 Do not give your glory to another, nor your dignity to a foreign nation.
4 We are blessed, O Israel: because the things that please God are made manifest to us.
5 Be of better courage, O people of God, the memorial of Israel:
6 You were sold to the nations, not for your destruction: but because you provoked God to wrath by your anger, you were delivered to your adversaries.

7 For you provoked him who made you, the eternal God, by sacrificing to demons and not to God.
8 For you forgot the God who nourished you, and you grieved your nurse, Jerusalem.
9 For she saw the wrath coming upon you from God, and she said: "Listen, you neighbors of Zion, for God has brought great mourning upon me."
10 For I have seen the captivity of my people, of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal one has brought upon them.
11 For I nourished them with joy, but I sent them away with weeping and mourning.
12 Let no one rejoice over me, a widow and desolate: I am forsaken by many because of the sins of my children, because they turned aside from the law of God.
13 For they did not know his justices, nor did they walk by the ways of God's commandments, nor did they enter the paths of his truth with justice.
14 Let the neighbors of Zion come and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal one has brought upon them.
15 For he has brought upon them a nation from afar, a wicked nation of a strange language.
16 They have not respected the elderly, nor pitied the children; they have led away the widow's beloved ones and left the mother desolate without her children.
17 But as for me, how can I help you?
18 For he who brought these evils upon you will himself snatch you from the hands of your enemies.
19 Walk, my children, walk: for I am left alone.
20 I have put off the robe of peace and put on the sackcloth of my prayer <note>Original: "obsecrationis," meaning earnest entreaty or petitioning.</note>, and I will cry out to the Most High in my days.
21 Be of better courage, my children; cry out to the Lord, and he will deliver you from the hand of the princes of your enemies.
22 For I have hoped for your salvation from the Eternal one: and joy has come to me from the Holy One because of the mercy that shall come to you from our eternal Savior.
23 For I sent you out with mourning and weeping: but the Lord will bring you back to me with joy and gladness forever.
24 For just as the neighbors of Zion have seen your captivity from God, so shall they quickly see your salvation from God, which shall come upon you with great honor and eternal splendor.
25 My children, endure patiently the wrath that has come upon you: for your enemy has persecuted you, but you shall quickly see his destruction, and you shall step upon his neck.
26 My delicate ones have walked rough ways: for they were led away like a flock plundered by enemies.
27 Be of better courage, my children, and cry out to the Lord: for you shall be remembered by him who led you away.
28 For just as it was your mind to wander from God, so shall you seek him ten times more as you return.
29 For he who brought these evils upon you will bring back to you eternal gladness with your salvation.
30 Be of better courage, O Jerusalem, for he who named you encourages you.
31 The wicked who troubled you shall perish, and those who rejoiced at your ruin shall be punished.
32 The cities which your children served shall be punished, even she <note>Likely referring to Babylon.</note> who received your sons.
33 For just as she rejoiced in your ruin and was glad at your fall, so shall she be grieved in her own desolation.

### CHAPTER VI.

*Jeremiah prophesies that the Jews held captive among the Babylonians will be freed after seven generations; he warns them to beware of their idolatry, showing by many examples that idols are weak, entirely lacking in sense, and utterly vain.*

The copy of the letter which Jeremiah sent to those who were to be led away as captives into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to announce to them what had been commanded him by God.

<margin>† Jeremiah 25:9.</margin>
1 † BECAUSE of the sins you have committed before God, you shall be led away as captives into Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians.
2 Having entered into Babylon, you shall be there for many years, and for a long time, even for seven generations <note>While Jeremiah elsewhere specifies 70 years, the term "generations" here may be used loosely to emphasize the long duration of the exile.</note>; but after this, I will lead you out from there in peace.

5 When you see the crowd behind and before them,

6 For my Angel is with you: and I myself will watch over your souls.
7 For their tongue is polished by a craftsman, and even they themselves are gilded and silvered; they are false, and they cannot speak.
8 And as if for a girl who loves ornaments, they take gold and craft it.
9 Their gods certainly have golden crowns upon their heads; from which the priests steal gold and silver, and spend it upon themselves.
10 They even give some of it to prostitutes, and they deck out harlots: and again, when they receive it back from the harlots, they ornament their gods.
11 But these [idols] are not delivered from rust and moths.
12 Though they are covered with purple clothing, they wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, which is very thick among them.
13 One holds a scepter like a man, like a judge of a region, yet he does not kill anyone who sins against him.
14 He also has a sword and an axe in his hand; yet he does not deliver himself from war or from thieves. By this you may know that they are not gods.
15 Therefore, do not fear them. For just as a person's vessel is made useless when it is broken, such are their gods.
16 When they are set up in the temple, their eyes are full of dust from the feet of those who enter.
17 And as the doors are shut fast around someone who has offended the king, or as if one were led to a tomb as a dead man, so the priests secure the doors with bars and locks, lest they be plundered by thieves.
18 They light lamps for them, and indeed many, though the idols can see none of them; they are like the beams in a house.
19 They say that serpents which come out of the earth lick their hearts <note>Meaning the wooden core of the idol.</note> while they are eating them and their garments, yet they do not feel it.
20 Their faces are blackened by the smoke that is made in the temple.
21 Owls and swallows and other birds fly over their bodies and over their heads, and cats do the same.
22 By this you may know that they are not gods. Therefore, do not fear them.
23 Even the gold they have is for appearance. Unless someone wipes away the rust, they will not shine; for even while they were being cast, they felt nothing.
24 They were bought at every price, though there is no breath <note>Original: "spiritus," referring to the life-force or breath of life.</note> in them.

...wearing torn tunics, with their heads and beards shaved, and their heads uncovered.
31 They roar, crying out before their gods, as at a funeral feast <note>original: "coena mortui"; referring to ancient mourning banquets where loud lamentation was customary.</note>.
32 The priests take their garments and dress their own wives and children.
33 Neither if they suffer any evil from anyone, nor if they receive any good, are they able to repay it; they can neither set up a king, nor take one away.
34 Likewise, they can neither give riches nor repay evil. If anyone makes a vow to them and does not fulfill it, they do not even demand it back.
35 They do not rescue a person from death, nor do they snatch the weak from the hand of the powerful.
36 They do not restore sight to a blind man, nor will they deliver a person from their necessity.
37 They will not take pity on the widow, nor do good to the orphans.
38 Their gods are like stones taken from the mountain—wooden, stone, gold, and silver. Those who worship them will be put to shame.
39 How, then, is it to be thought or said that they are gods?
40 For even the Chaldeans <term>Chaldæis: the people of Babylonia, famous for their astronomers and priests</term> themselves do not honor them; when they hear of a mute man who cannot speak, they offer him to Bel <note>Bel (or Marduk) was the patron deity of Babylon.</note>, asking him to make the man speak:
41 As if those who have no movement could feel! And they themselves, when they understand this, will abandon them; for their gods have no sense.
42 The women sit in the streets, wrapped in cords, burning olive stones <note>This refers to a Babylonian ritual described by ancient historians where women sat in the temple precinct until chosen by a stranger.</note>.
43 And when one of them, pulled away by a passerby, has slept with him, she reproaches her neighbor that she was not held worthy like herself, and that her cord was not broken.
44 Everything done for them is a lie. How can it be thought or said that they are gods?
45 They are made by craftsmen and goldsmiths. They will be nothing else but what the priests want them to be.
46 Even the craftsmen who make them do not live for a long time. Can the things they have manufactured be gods?
47 They have left behind only lies and disgrace for those who come after.
48 For when war and evils come upon them, the priests consult among themselves where they might hide with them.
49 How, then, should they be perceived as gods, when they neither deliver themselves from war nor rescue themselves from evils?
50 Since they are made of wood, gilded, and silver-plated, it will be known afterward by all nations and kings that they are false; it is manifest that they are not gods, but the works of human hands, and no work of God is with them.
51 From what, then, is it not known that they are not gods, but the work of human hands, and that no work of God is in them?
52 They do not raise up a king for a region, nor will they give rain to humanity.

<column-break/>

53 They will not decide a judgment, nor will they deliver regions from injury; for they are as powerless as crows <term>corniculæ: small crows or jackdaws, implying they are common and insignificant</term> between heaven and earth.
54 For when fire falls upon the house of gods made of wood, silver, and gold, their priests will flee and be saved; but the gods themselves will be burned in the middle like beams.
55 They will not resist a king or a war. How, then, can it be thought or accepted that they are gods?
56 These gods of wood, stone, gold, and silver will not deliver themselves from thieves or robbers; those who are stronger than them
57 will take away the gold, the silver, and the garment with which they are covered, and they will depart; nor will the gods help themselves.
58 Therefore, it is better to be a king who shows his power, or a useful vessel in a house in which the owner takes pride, or even a door in a house that guards the things within it, than to be these false gods.
59 The sun, the moon, and the stars, since they are bright and sent forth for our benefit, are obedient to God.
60 Likewise, when the lightning appears, it is clearly seen; and the wind blows in every region.
61 And the clouds, when they are commanded by God to travel over the whole world, perform what is commanded of them.
62 The fire, also, sent from above to consume mountains and forests, does what it was told. But these idols are not like any of these things, neither in appearance nor in power.
63 Therefore, it is neither to be thought nor said that they are gods, since they can neither judge a case nor do anything for humanity.
64 Knowing, therefore, that they are not gods, do not fear them.
65 For they will neither curse nor bless kings.
66 They do not show signs in the heavens to the nations, nor will they shine like the sun, nor give light like the moon.
67 The beasts are better than they are, for they can flee under a roof and help themselves.
68 In no way, therefore, is it manifest to us that they are gods; for this reason, do not fear them.
69 For like a scarecrow <note>original: "formido"; a thing of fear meant to scare birds.</note> in a garden of cucumbers that guards nothing, so are their gods of wood, silver, and gold.
70 In the same way, they are like a white thorn bush in a garden, upon which every bird sits. Their gods of wood, gold, and silver are like a dead body cast out into the darkness.
71 From the purple and the fine linen <note>original: "murice"; the murex shell used to make purple dye.</note> that rot upon them, you will know that they are not gods. They themselves are finally eaten away and will be a disgrace in the land.
72 Better, therefore, is the righteous man who has no idols; for he shall be far from disgrace.

# THE PROPHECY OF EZEKIEL.

## CHAPTER ONE.

*The time and place in which the visions of God were shown to Ezekiel: namely, in the midst of fire, the likeness of four living creatures are described, as well as the wheels, the firmament, the throne, and a man sitting upon the throne surrounded by fire.*

<margin>
† See below, 3:23, 10:20, 43:3.
</margin>
And it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, when I was in the midst of the captives by the river Chebar <note>original: "Chobar"; a canal or river in Mesopotamia where Jewish exiles were settled.</note>, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
2 On the fifth day of the month, which was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin,
3 The word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans <term>Chaldæorum: the Babylonians</term>, by the river Chebar; and the hand of the Lord was upon him there.
4 And I looked, and behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, and a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was round about it; and out of the midst of it there was something like the appearance of <term>electrum: a brilliant alloy of gold and silver, or perhaps glowing amber, used here to describe a supernatural radiance</term>, that is, out of the midst of the fire.
5 And in the midst of it was the likeness of four living creatures: and this was their appearance: there was the likeness of a man in them.
6 Every one had four faces, and every one had four wings.
7 Their feet were straight feet, and the sole of their foot was like the sole of a calf's foot, and they sparkled like the appearance of glowing brass.
8 And they had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides; and they had faces and wings on all four sides.
9 And the wings of one were joined to the wings of another; they did not turn when they went, but every one went straight forward.
10 As for the likeness of their faces: there was the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side of all four; and the face of an ox on the left side of all four; and the face of an eagle above all four.
11 Thus were their faces: and their wings were stretched upward; two wings of every one were joined, and two covered their bodies.
12 And every one went straight forward: where the impulse of the spirit was to go, thither they went, and they did not turn back when they walked.
13 And as for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like glowing coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps. This vision moved to and fro in the midst of the living creatures, a brightness of fire, and out of the fire went forth lightning.
14 And the living creatures ran and returned like the appearance of a flash of lightning.
15 Now as I beheld the living creatures, behold, one wheel appeared upon the earth beside the living creatures, having four faces.
16 And the appearance of the wheels and their work was like the sight of the sea <note>original: "maris"; often interpreted as chrysolite or beryl, a sea-green precious stone.</note>: and the four of them had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.
17 When they went, they went upon their four sides, and they did not turn when they walked.
18 The wheels also had a stature, and a height,

<column-break/>

and a dreadful appearance: and the whole body was full of eyes round about all four of them.
<margin>
† See below, 10:12.
</margin>
19 And when the living creatures walked, the wheels also walked together beside them: and when the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels also were lifted up at the same time.
20 Whithersoever the spirit went, thither as the spirit went, the wheels also were lifted up together, following it. For the spirit of life was in the wheels.
21 When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels also were lifted up together, following them: for the spirit of life was in the wheels.
22 And over the heads of the living creatures was the likeness of a firmament <term>firmamenti: the expanse of the sky or a solid dome</term>, like the appearance of terrible crystal, stretched out over their heads above.
23 And under the firmament their wings were straight, one toward another: every one had two wings covering their body, and the other was covered likewise.
24 And I heard the noise of their wings, like the noise of many waters, like the noise of the most high God: when they walked, it was like the noise of a multitude, like the noise of an army: and when they stood, their wings were let down.
25 For when a voice came from above the firmament that was over their heads, they stood, and let down their wings.
26 And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, like the appearance of a sapphire stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it.
27 And I saw as it were the appearance of electrum, like the appearance of fire within it round about: from his loins and upward, and from his loins even downward, I saw as it were the appearance of fire shining round about.
28 As the appearance of the bow that is in a cloud in the day of rain: this was the appearance of the brightness round about.

## CHAPTER II.

*The terrified prophet is strengthened so that he may fearlessly rebuke the rebellious children of Israel, to see if they might finally repent of their long-standing sins; he is commanded to eat a scroll written within and without, in which were lamentations, and a song, and woe.*

THIS was the vision of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard the voice of one speaking. And he said to me: Son of man <note>This title is used throughout Ezekiel to emphasize the prophet's mortality in the presence of the Divine.</note>, stand upon thy feet, and I will speak to thee.
2 And the spirit entered into me after he spoke to me, and he set me upon my feet: and I heard him speaking to me,
3 And saying: Son of man, I send thee to the children of Israel, to apostate nations that have revolted from me: they and their fathers have transgressed my covenant even unto this day.
4 And the children are of a hard face and an indomitable heart, to whom I send thee: and thou shalt say to them: Thus saith the Lord God:
5 If peradventure they will hear, and if peradventure they will cease <note>that is, cease their rebellion or listen to the warning</note>, for they are a provoking house: and they shall know that there hath been a prophet in the midst of them.

Now, the focus shifts to the prophet’s specific instructions: he is to be a messenger to a stubborn and rebellious people, regardless of whether they listen.</meta>

# THE PROPHECY OF EZEKIEL.

6 You therefore, son of man, do not fear them, nor be afraid of their words: though unbelievers and subversives are with you, and you dwell among scorpions: do not fear their words, and do not be dismayed by their looks, for they are a provoking house. <note>original: "domus exasperans"; a recurring phrase describing Israel as a household that constantly irritates or rebels against God.</note>
7 You shall therefore speak my words to them, whether they hear, or whether they cease to listen: for they are provokers.
8 But you, son of man, hear whatever I speak to you, and do not be a provoker, as that house is a provoker: open your mouth and eat whatever I give to you.
<margin>Behold</margin> 9 And I looked, and behold, a hand was sent to me, in which was a rolled-up book: and he spread it before me, which was written within and without: and there were written in it lamentations, and a song, and woe. <note>In antiquity, scrolls were usually written on only one side; a scroll written on both sides indicates an overflow of message, in this case, a surplus of sorrow.</note>

### CHAPTER III.

*Once the book is eaten, the prophet is given a face of adamant so that he may fearlessly rebuke the most hardened children of Israel living in exile: he is appointed as a watchman, who, if he does not announce the looming evil he has seen, is held guilty for the one who perishes; but if he announces it, he delivers his own soul, even if the other perishes: then, entering the plain and seeing the glory of the Lord there, he is ordered to be shut up in his house, as if bound and mute.*

1 And he said to me: Son of man, eat whatever you find: eat this volume, and go and speak to the children of Israel.
2 And I opened my mouth, and he fed me that volume:
<margin>Revelation 9.</margin> 3 And he said to me: Son of man, your belly shall eat, and your bowels shall be filled with this volume, which I give you. And I ate it: and it became in my mouth sweet as honey.
4 And he said to me: Son of man, go to the house of Israel, and you shall speak my words to them.
5 For you are not sent to a people of profound speech and of an unknown tongue, but to the house of Israel:
6 Nor to many peoples of profound speech and of an unknown tongue, whose words you cannot understand: and if you were sent to them, they would listen to you.
7 But the house of Israel will not listen to you: because they will not listen to me: for all the house of Israel is of a brazen forehead and a hard heart.
8 Behold, I have made your face stronger than their faces, and your forehead harder than their foreheads.
9 I have made your face like <term>adamant: a legendary stone of indestructible hardness, often identified with diamond or emery</term>, and like flint: do not fear them, nor be dismayed by their presence: for they are a provoking house.
10 And he said to me: Son of man, all my words, which I speak to you, take into your heart, and hear with your ears:
11 And go, enter into the <term>transmigration: the exile or captivity</term>, to the children of your people, and you shall speak to them, and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: if perhaps they will hear, and if they will cease.
12 And the spirit took me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great commotion, saying: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place;
13 And the sound of the wings of the living creatures striking one against another, and the sound of the wheels following the living creatures, and the sound of a great commotion.

<column-break/>

14 The spirit also lifted me up and took me: and I went away bitter in the indignation of my spirit: for the hand of the Lord was with me, strengthening me.
15 And I came to the exile, to the <term>heap of new fruits: in Latin "acervum novarum frugum," a literal translation of the Hebrew place-name Tel-Abib</term>, to those who dwelt by the river Chebar, and I sat where they sat: and I remained there seven days mourning in the midst of them.
16 And when seven days had passed, the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
<margin>† Below 33:7.</margin> 17 Son of man, I have made you a <term>speculator: a watchman or scout</term> to the house of Israel: and you shall hear the word from my mouth, and shall announce it to them from me.
18 If, when I say to the wicked: You shall surely die: you do not announce it to him, nor speak that he may be turned from his wicked way and live: that same wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood at your hand.
19 But if you announce it to the wicked, and he is not converted from his wickedness, and from his wicked way: he indeed shall die in his iniquity, but you have delivered your soul.
20 Moreover, if the just man turns from his justice, and commits iniquity: I will lay a stumbling-block before him, he shall die, because you did not announce it to him: he shall die in his sin, and his justices which he has done shall not be remembered: but I will require his blood at your hand.
21 But if you announce to the just man that the just should not sin, and he does not sin: he shall surely live, because you announced it to him, and you have delivered your soul.
22 And the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he said to me: Rise and go out into the plain, and there I will speak with you.
<margin>† Above 1:3.</margin> 23 And rising, I went out into the plain: and behold, the glory of the Lord stood there, like the glory which I saw by the river Chebar: and I fell upon my face.
24 And the spirit entered into me, and set me upon my feet: and he spoke to me, and said to me: Go in, and shut yourself up in the midst of your house.
25 And you, son of man, behold, chains are placed upon you, and they shall bind you with them: and you shall not go out from the midst of them.
26 And I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, and you shall be dumb, and not as a man rebuking: for they are a provoking house.
27 But when I have spoken to you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: He that hears, let him hear: and he that ceases, let him cease: for they are a provoking house.

### CHAPTER IV.

*The prophet is commanded to portray the siege of Jerusalem, and to sleep upon his left side for 390 days, and upon his right for 40, and to prepare for himself vile and foully made food, by which he signifies the calamity of the children of Israel, and the siege and affliction of those dwelling in Jerusalem.*

1 And you, son of man, take a brick, and lay it before you: and you shall describe upon it the city of Jerusalem.
2 And you shall ordain a siege against it, and build fortifications, and carry up a mound, and set a camp against it, and place battering rams round about.

4 And you shall sleep on your left side, and lay the iniquities of the house of Israel upon it; for the number of days that you sleep upon that side, you shall bear their iniquity.

<margin>† Numbers 14:34</margin>

7 And you shall turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and your arm shall be bared: and you shall prophesy against it.

9 And take for yourself wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and fitches <note>original: "viciam"; likely referring to spelt or a similar grain used as animal fodder, indicating the desperate measures of a famine.</note>: and put them into one vessel, and make bread for yourself according to the number of days that you shall sleep on your side: for three hundred and ninety days you shall eat it.
10 And your food, which you shall eat, shall be by weight: twenty shekels <note>original: "stateres"; a unit of weight roughly equal to 11 grams. Eating only 8 ounces of bread a day represents extreme rationing.</note> a day: from time to time you shall eat it.
11 And you shall drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin <note>A "hin" was about 6 liters; Ezekiel is allowed only about 1 liter of water per day.</note>: from time to time you shall drink it.
12 And you shall eat it as a barley cake baked under the ashes: and with the dung that comes out of a man, you shall cover it in their sight.

14 And I said: "Alas, alas, alas, Lord God! <note>original: "A a a, Domine Deus"; an exclamation of deep distress.</note> Behold, my soul has never been polluted: and from my infancy until now I have never eaten anything that died of itself, or was torn by beasts, nor has any unclean flesh entered into my mouth."

17 So that, as bread and water fail, each one may fall toward his brother: and they shall waste away in their iniquities."

### C H A P T E R V.

*By the hair of the prophet’s head and beard, shorn by the Lord’s command and destroyed in various ways, the Jews are designated to be consumed by famine and the sword because of their sins: so much so that fathers eat their sons, and sons eat their fathers. The remainder are to be led into captivity, where they shall be a reproach and a wonder to the nations, whose wickedness they had surpassed.*

1 And you, son of man, take a sharp sword that acts as a razor: and take it, and draw it over your head and over your beard; and take for yourself a balance scale, and divide the hair.

<column-break/>

2 A third part you shall burn with fire in the midst of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled: and you shall take a third part and strike it with the sword round about it: and another third part you shall scatter to the wind, and I will unsheathe a sword after them.
3 And you shall take from there a small number: and bind them in the hem of your cloak.
4 And of these you shall take again, and cast them into the midst of the fire, and burn them with fire: and from there a fire shall go out into all the house of Israel.
5 Thus says the Lord God: This is Jerusalem, I have set her in the midst of the nations, and the lands that are round about her.
6 And she has despised my judgments, so as to be more wicked than the nations; and my precepts, more than the lands that are round about her: for they have cast off my judgments, and have not walked in my precepts.
7 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have surpassed the nations that are round about you, and have not walked in my precepts, and have not kept my judgments, and have not acted according to the judgments of the nations that are round about you:
8 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I come against you, and I myself will execute judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations.
9 And I will do in you that which I have not done, and the likes of which I will not do again, because of all your abominations.
10 Therefore fathers shall eat their sons in your midst, and sons shall eat their fathers, and I will execute judgments in you, and I will scatter all your remnants to every wind.
11 Therefore as I live, says the Lord God: because you have violated my sanctuary with all your offenses and with all your abominations: I also will break you, and my eye shall not spare, nor will I have mercy.
12 A third part of you shall die of the plague, and shall be consumed by famine in your midst: and a third part of you shall fall by the sword round about you: and a third part of you I will scatter to every wind, and I will unsheathe a sword after them.
13 And I will fulfill my fury, and cause my indignation to rest upon them, and I will be comforted: and they shall know that I the Lord have spoken in my zeal, when I have fulfilled my indignation upon them.
14 And I will make you a desert and a reproach among the nations that are round about you, in the sight of everyone that passes by.
15 And you shall be a reproach and a taunt, an example and an astonishment among the nations that are round about you, when I shall have executed judgments in you in fury, and in indignation, and in rebukes of wrath.
16 I the Lord have spoken: When I shall send the most grievous arrows of famine upon them, which shall be deadly, and which I will send to destroy you: <margin>† Above 4:16</margin> and † I will break among you the staff of bread.
17 And I will send famine upon you, and evil beasts even to your utter destruction: and pestilence and blood shall pass through you, and I will bring the sword upon you; I the Lord have spoken.

### C H A P T E R VI.

<margin>Because of the manifold idolatry of the children of Israel, the destruction of their cities and high places is foretold; those who escape the plague, the sword, and famine shall be scattered among the nations, where, weighed down by evils, they shall turn back to the Lord.</margin>

1 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy to them,
<margin>† Below 36:1</margin>
3 And say: † Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God: Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and the hills, to the rocks and the valleys: Behold, I will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places, <note>The "high places" (original: *excelsa*) were hilltop shrines where the Israelites often syncretized the worship of God with pagan rituals.</note>
4 And I will demolish your altars, and your images shall be broken: and I will cast down your slain before your idols.
5 And I will lay the carcasses of the children of Israel before the face of your idols: and I will scatter your bones around your altars,
6 In all your dwelling places. The cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be demolished and scattered: and your altars shall perish and be broken: and your idols shall cease and be crushed, and your shrines shall be destroyed, and your works shall be blotted out.
7 And the slain shall fall in your midst: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
8 And I will leave a remnant of you, those who have escaped the sword among the nations, when I have scattered you through the lands.
9 And those of you who are delivered shall remember me among the nations to which they were led captive: because I have crushed their heart which was fornicating and departing from me, and their eyes which went whoring after their idols: and they shall be loathsome to themselves because of the evils they have done in all their abominations.
10 And they shall know that I the Lord have not spoken in vain, that I would do this evil to them.
11 Thus says the Lord God: Strike your hand, and stamp your foot, and say: Alas! for all the abominations of the evils of the house of Israel: for they shall fall by the sword, by famine, and by the plague. <note>These physical gestures—striking the hand and stamping the foot—were outward signs of intense grief and the gravity of the divine warning.</note>
12 He that is far off shall die of the plague: he that is near shall fall by the sword: and he that remains and is besieged shall die of famine: and I will accomplish my indignation upon them.
13 And you shall know that I am the Lord, when your slain shall be in the midst of your idols, round about your altars, on every high hill, and on all the tops of the mountains, and under every leafy tree, and under every thick oak, the places where they burned sweet-smelling incense to all their idols.
14 And I will stretch forth my hand upon them: and I will make the land desolate and abandoned, from the desert of Deblatha, in all their dwelling places: and they shall know that I am the Lord.

### C H A P T E R VII.

<margin>The prophet announces that the final and inevitable devastation of the whole land of Judea is close at hand because of their crimes.</margin>

1 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 And you, son of man, thus says the Lord God to the land of Israel: The end is come, the end is come upon the four quarters of the land.

<column-break/>

3 Now the end is upon you, and I will send my fury upon you: and I will judge you according to your ways: and I will set all your abominations against you.
4 And my eye shall not spare you, and I will have no mercy: but I will lay your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in your midst: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
5 Thus says the Lord God: One affliction, behold, one affliction comes.
6 The end is come, the end is come, it has awoken against you: behold, it comes.
7 Destruction is come upon you, you who dwell in the land: the time is come, the day of slaughter is near, and not of the glory of the mountains.
8 Now very soon I will pour out my wrath upon you, and I will accomplish my fury in you: and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will lay all your crimes upon you.
9 And my eye shall not spare, nor will I have mercy: but I will lay your ways upon you, and your abominations shall be in your midst: and you shall know that I am the Lord who strikes.
10 Behold the day, behold it comes: destruction has gone forth, the rod has blossomed, pride has budded:
11 Iniquity has risen into a rod of impiety: nothing shall remain of them, nor of the people, nor of the noise of them: and there shall be no rest in them.
12 The time is come, the day draws near: let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn: for wrath is upon all the people thereof.
13 For the seller shall not return to that which he has sold, even while they are yet alive: for the vision regarding all the multitude thereof shall not return: and no man shall be strengthened in the iniquity of his life.
14 Blow the trumpet, let all be made ready, yet there is none that goes to battle: for my wrath is upon all the people thereof.
15 The sword is outside; and the plague and famine within: he that is in the field shall die by the sword: and they that are in the city shall be devoured by pestilence and famine.
16 And they that escape from them shall be saved: and they shall be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them trembling, every one for his own iniquity.
17 All hands shall be made feeble, and all knees shall flow with water. <note>original: "fluent aquis"; a biblical idiom describing the loss of all strength and the onset of terror, often compared to melting or becoming liquid like water.</note>
<margin>† Isaiah 15:2; Jeremiah 48:37</margin>
18 † And they shall gird themselves with haircloth, and fear shall cover them, and confusion shall be on every face, and baldness upon all their heads.
<margin>† Proverbs 11:4; Zephaniah 1:18; Ecclesiasticus 5:10</margin>
19 Their silver shall be cast forth, and their gold shall be as a dunghill. † Their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the Lord. They shall not satisfy their soul, and their bellies shall not be filled: because it has become the stumbling-block of their iniquity.
20 And they have turned the ornament of their jewels into pride, and have made of it the images of their abominations and idols: for this reason I have given it to them for uncleanness:
21 And I will give it into the hands of strangers for a spoil, and to the wicked of the earth for a prey, and they shall defile it.
22 And I will turn my face away from them, and they shall violate my secret place: and robbers shall enter into it, and defile it. <note>The "secret place" (original: *arcanum meum*) refers to the Holy of Holies in the Temple, the most sacred space of the sanctuary.</note>
23 Make a conclusion: for the land is full of the judgment of blood, and the city is full of iniquity.

### C H A P T E R VIII.

*Ezekiel, after seeing a likeness of God, is caught up in spirit to Jerusalem and sees the terrible idolatries of the Jews under various figures: for which reason the Lord says He will ✝ not spare them, nor hear their prayers.*

1 And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month: I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, and there the hand of the Lord God fell upon me.
2 And I looked, and behold, a likeness with the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his waist and downward, fire; and from his waist and upward, like the appearance of brightness, as the sight of amber. <note>original: "electri" — a precious, glowing alloy of gold and silver, used here to describe the radiating brilliance of the divine presence.</note>
<margin>† Daniel 14:35.</margin>
3 And the likeness of a hand was put forth and took me by a lock of my head: and the spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven, and brought me in the vision of God into Jerusalem, near the inner gate that looked toward the north, where the idol of jealousy was placed to provoke rivalry.
4 And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the vision I had seen in the plain.
5 And He said to me: Son of man, lift up your eyes toward the way of the north. And I lifted up my eyes toward the way of the north: and behold, to the north of the altar gate, the idol of jealousy was at the very entrance.
6 And He said to me: Son of man, do you see what these are doing, the great abominations that the house of Israel commits here, so that I must go far away from my sanctuary? But turn again and you shall see even greater abominations.
7 And He brought me to the door of the court: and I looked, and behold, there was a single hole in the wall.
8 And He said to me: Son of man, dig through the wall. And when I had dug through the wall, a single door appeared.
9 And He said to me: Go in, and see the wicked abominations that these men are doing here.
10 And I went in and saw, and behold, every likeness of creeping things and animals, an abomination, and all the idols of the house of Israel were painted on the wall all around.
11 And seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan standing in the midst of them, were standing before the paintings: and each man had a censer in his hand: and a cloud of smoke rose up from the incense.
12 And He said to me: Surely you see, son of man, what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, each one in the secret of his chamber: for they say: The Lord does not see us, the Lord has forsaken the land.
13 And He said to me: Turn again and you shall see greater abominations which these men are doing.

<column-break/>

14 And He brought me through the door of the gate of the house of the Lord, which looked toward the north: and behold, women sat there weeping for Adonis. <note>original: "Adonidem" — the Latin refers to the Greek figure Adonis, used here to translate the Hebrew "Tammuz," a Mesopotamian god of vegetation whose seasonal "death" was marked by ritual wailing.</note>
15 And He said to me: Surely you have seen, son of man: turn again and you shall see abominations even greater than these.
16 And He brought me into the inner court of the house of the Lord: and behold, at the door of the temple of the Lord, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men, with their backs toward the temple of the Lord and their faces toward the east: and they were worshipping toward the rising of the sun.
17 And He said to me: Surely you have seen, son of man: is it a light thing for the house of Judah to commit these abominations which they have committed here? For having filled the land with iniquity, they have turned to provoke me: and behold, they put a branch to their nose. <note>A ritual gesture whose exact meaning is debated, though it likely refers to a specific pagan ceremony or a gesture of contempt toward God.</note>
18 Therefore I also will act in fury: my eye shall not spare, nor will I have mercy: and when they cry to my ears with a loud voice, I will not hear them.

### C H A P T E R IX.

*Six men appear and are commanded to slay everyone in Jerusalem ✝ who has not been marked with the sign of the Tau by the man dressed in linen: which being done, the Lord responds to the crying prophet that this shall happen because their crimes demand it.*

1 And He cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying: The visitations of the city have drawn near, and each man has a weapon of destruction in his hand.
2 And behold, six men came from the way of the upper gate, which faces the north: and each man had a weapon of death in his hand: and one man in the midst of them was clothed in linen, with a writer’s ink-horn at his waist: and they entered and stood beside the bronze altar.
3 And the glory of the Lord of Israel was taken up from the cherub, where it had been, to the threshold of the house: and He called the man who was clothed in linen and had the writer’s ink-horn at his waist.

Revelation 7:3.

4 And the Lord said to him: Go through the midst of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem: † and mark the sign of the Tau upon the foreheads of the men who sigh and mourn over all the abominations that are done in its midst. <note>The "Tau" was the last letter of the ancient Hebrew alphabet, shaped like a cross (+ or X). In the Christian tradition, this was often interpreted as a prefiguration of the Cross of Christ.</note>
5 And to the others He said in my hearing: Go through the city following him, and strike: let your eye not spare, nor have any mercy.
6 Kill the old man, the youth, and the virgin, the little child and the women, even to utter destruction: but do not kill anyone upon whom you see the Tau; and begin at my sanctuary. They began, therefore, with the elders who were before the face of the house.
7 And He said to them: Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain: go out. And they went out and struck those who were in the city.
8 And the slaughter being finished, I remained: and I fell upon my face, and crying out, I said: Alas, alas, alas, Lord God: will You then destroy all the remnant of Israel, pouring out Your fury upon Jerusalem?

10 Therefore my eye shall not spare, neither will I have pity: I will return their way upon their own head.
11 And behold, the man who was clothed in linen, who had the inkhorn <note>original: "atramentarium" — a container for ink, usually carried at the waist by scribes.</note> at his side, reported the matter, saying: I have done as you commanded me.

### CHAPTER X.

*The man clothed in linen is commanded to take burning coals of fire from the midst of the wheels, which are under the Cherubim, and to scatter them over the city: a description is given of the vision of God, the cherubim, and the four wheels.*

AND I saw, and behold, in the firmament <note>The "firmament" refers to a vast expanse or canopy above the celestial beings.</note> that was over the head of the cherubim, there appeared over them something like a sapphire stone, with the appearance of the likeness of a throne.
2 And he spoke to the man who was clothed in linen, and said: Go in between the wheels that are under the cherubim, and fill your hand with burning coals of fire that are between the cherubim, and pour them over the city. And he went in before my eyes.
3 Now the cherubim stood on the right side of the house <note>The "house" refers to the Temple in Jerusalem.</note> when the man went in, and a cloud filled the inner court.
4 And the glory of the Lord went up from above the cherub to the threshold of the house: and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the Lord.
5 And the sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard even to the outer court, like the voice of the Almighty God speaking.
6 And when he had commanded the man clothed in linen, saying: Take fire from the midst of the wheels that are between the cherubim: he went in and stood beside a wheel.
7 And a cherub stretched out his hand from the midst of the cherubim to the fire that was between the cherubim, and took some, and put it into the hands of him who was clothed in linen: who took it and went out.
8 And there appeared in the cherubim the likeness of a man’s hand under their wings.
9 And I saw, and behold, four wheels beside the cherubim: one wheel beside one cherub, and another wheel beside another cherub: and the appearance of the wheels was like the sight of a chrysolite stone. <note>original: "lapis chrysolithi" — a yellow or golden-hued gemstone.</note>
10 And as for their appearance, the four had one likeness: as if a wheel were in the midst of a wheel.
11 When they moved, they went toward their four sides: and they did not turn as they went, but to the place where the first one headed, the others followed, and they did not turn.
12 And their whole body, and their necks, and their hands, and their wings, and the circles, were full of eyes, all around the four wheels.
13 And he called these wheels "whirling," <note>original: "volubiles" — indicating a rolling or rapid revolving motion.</note> in my hearing.
14 And every one had four faces: the first face was the face of a cherub: and the second face, the face of a man: and in the third, the face of a lion: and in the fourth, the face of an eagle.
15 And the cherubim were lifted up: this is the living creature that I had seen by the river Chebar. <note>original: "Chobar" — a river or canal in Babylonia where Ezekiel received his first visions.</note>
16 And when the cherubim moved, the wheels also went beside them: and when the cherubim lifted up their wings to mount up from the earth, the wheels did not stay behind, but they also were beside them.

<column-break/>

17 When they stood, these stood: and when they were lifted up, these were lifted up: for the spirit of life was in them.
18 And the glory of the Lord went out from the threshold of the temple: and stood over the cherubim.
19 And the cherubim, lifting up their wings, were raised from the earth before me: and as they went out, the wheels also followed: and it stood at the entrance of the east gate of the Lord's house: and the glory of the God of Israel was over them.
<margin>† See Chapter 1:3.</margin> 20 This is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel by the river Chebar, and I understood that they were cherubim.
21 Every one had four faces, and every one four wings: and the likeness of a man’s hand was under their wings.
22 And as for the likeness of their faces, they were the same faces which I had seen by the river Chebar, and their look, and the impulse of every one to go straight forward.

### CHAPTER XI.

*Against Jaazaniah and Pelatiah who were giving wicked counsel, saying: "Have not houses been built lately? This city is the cauldron, and we are the meat." Ezekiel prophesies that they and all who will not repent shall be punished: and while Ezekiel was prophesying, Pelatiah died: but he says he will bring the remnant of Israel back into their own land, and give them a heart of flesh, so that they may worship and fear the Lord.*

AND the spirit lifted me up, and brought me to the east gate of the house of the Lord, which looks toward the rising sun: and behold, at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men: and I saw in the midst of them Jaazaniah <note>original: "Jezoniam"</note> the son of Azzur, and Pelatiah <note>original: "Pheltiam"</note> the son of Benaiah, princes of the people.
2 And he said to me: Son of man, these are the men who study iniquity, and give very wicked counsel in this city,
3 Saying: Have not houses been built lately? This is the cauldron, <note>original: "lebes" — a large cooking pot or kettle. The leaders used this as a metaphor of safety, suggesting the city walls would protect them like a pot protects meat from fire, but God subverts this image to one of being "cooked" in judgment.</note> and we are the meat.
4 Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, O son of man.
5 And the spirit of the Lord fell upon me, and said to me: Speak: Thus says the Lord: Thus have you spoken, O house of Israel, and I know the thoughts of your heart.
6 You have killed many in this city, and you have filled its streets with the slain.
7 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Your slain, whom you have laid in the midst of it, they are the meat, and this is the cauldron: and I will bring you out of the midst of it.
8 You have feared the sword, and I will bring the sword upon you, says the Lord God.
9 And I will cast you out of the midst of it, and I will deliver you into the hands of enemies, and I will execute judgments upon you.
10 You shall fall by the sword: I will judge you in the borders of Israel, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
11 This shall not be a cauldron to you, and you shall not be as meat in the midst of it: I will judge you in the borders of Israel.
12 And you shall know that I am the Lord: because you have not walked in my commandments, and have not executed my judgments, but you have acted according to the judgments of the nations that are round about you.
13 And it came to pass, when I prophesied, that Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died, and I fell upon my face, crying with a loud voice, and said: Alas, alas, alas, Lord God: will you make an end of the remnant of Israel?

14 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
15 Son of man, your brothers, your brothers, the men of your kinship, and all the house of Israel, all of them, to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said: "Depart far from the Lord; the land is given to us for a possession."
16 Therefore say these things: Thus says the Lord God: Because I have sent them far away among the nations, and because I have scattered them among the lands, I will be to them a modest sanctuary <note>original: "sanctificationem modicam" — literally a "small sanctification," but often understood as a "little sanctuary" or a temporary presence of God while they are away from the Temple.</note> in the lands to which they have come.
17 Therefore speak: Thus says the Lord God: I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you from the lands in which you have been scattered, and I will give you the soil of Israel.
18 And they shall enter there, and they shall take away all its offenses and all its abominations from it.
<margin>Jeremiah 31:33. Below 36:26.</margin>
19 † And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them; and I will take away the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them a heart of flesh:
20 That they may walk in my precepts, and keep my judgments, and do them: and that they may be my people, and I may be their God.
21 But as for those whose heart walks after their offenses and abominations, I will lay their way upon their own head, says the Lord God.
22 Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, and the wheels with them; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them.
23 And the glory of the Lord went up from the midst of the city, and stood upon the mountain that is on the east side of the city <note>This refers to the Mount of Olives.</note>.
24 And the spirit lifted me up, and brought me into Chaldea, to the exile <note>original: "transmigrationem" — the community of those who had been carried away into captivity.</note>, in a vision, by the spirit of God: and the vision which I had seen went up from me.
25 And I spoke to the exile all the words of the Lord, which he had shown me.

### ->CHAPTER XII.<-

*Ezekiel portends by his actions the future captivity of Jerusalem and its king, the rest being consumed by the sword, pestilence, and famine in Jerusalem; he also shows that the vision of the prophets shall not be in vain, nor delayed for a long time.*

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a rebellious house <note>original: "domus exasperantis" — a house that provokes or exasperates.</note>; they have eyes to see, and see not; and ears to hear, and hear not; for they are a rebellious house.
3 Therefore, son of man, prepare for yourself the baggage of an exile <note>original: "vasa transmigrationis" — the essential items one would carry when being forced to move or go into captivity.</note>, and you shall go into exile by day in their sight; and you shall go from your place to another place in their sight, if perhaps they will consider; for they are a rebellious house.
4 And you shall bring out your baggage like the baggage of an exile by day in their sight; and you shall go out in the evening in their sight, as one goes out into exile.
5 Before their eyes, dig through the wall for yourself, and go out through it.
6 In their sight you shall be carried upon shoulders, you shall be carried out in the dark: you shall cover your face, and you shall not see the ground: for I have set you as a sign <note>original: "portentum" — an omen or a symbolic warning.</note> to the house of Israel.
7 I did therefore as the Lord had commanded me: I brought out my baggage like the baggage of an exile by day: and in the evening I dug through the wall for myself with my hand: and I went out in the dark, carried on shoulders in their sight.

<column-break/>

8 And the word of the Lord came to me in the morning, saying:
9 Son of man, has not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said to you: "What are you doing?"
10 Say to them: Thus says the Lord God: This burden <note>A "burden" in prophecy often refers to a heavy message of judgment.</note> concerns the prince who is in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel, who are in the midst of them.
11 Say: I am your sign; as I have done, so shall it be done to them: into exile and into captivity they shall go.
12 And the prince who is in the midst of them shall be carried on shoulders, he shall go out in the dark: they shall dig through the wall to bring him out: his face shall be covered, so that he may not see the ground with his eye.
<margin>† Below 17:20.</margin>
13 † And I will spread my net over him, and he shall be taken in my snare: and I will bring him into Babylon, into the land of the Chaldeans, yet he shall not see it, and there he shall die <note>This is a famous prophecy regarding King Zedekiah, who was blinded by the Babylonians before being taken to Babylon; thus he arrived there but could not "see" the land.</note>.
14 And all that are about him, his guard and his troops, I will scatter into every wind: and I will draw out the sword after them.
15 And they shall know that I am the Lord, when I have dispersed them among the nations, and scattered them in the lands.
16 But I will leave a few men of them from the sword, and from famine, and from pestilence: that they may declare all their wicked deeds among the nations to which they shall go: and they shall know that I am the Lord.
17 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
18 Son of man, eat your bread with quaking: and drink your water with trembling and with sorrow.
19 And say to the people of the land: Thus says the Lord God to those who dwell in Jerusalem, in the land of Israel: They shall eat their bread with care, and drink their water in desolation, that the land may be laid waste of its fullness, because of the iniquity of all who dwell in it.
20 And the cities that are now inhabited shall be laid waste, and the land shall be desolate: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
21 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
22 Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel, saying: "The days shall be prolonged, and every vision shall fail"?
23 Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God: I will make this proverb to cease, neither shall it be commonly used anymore in Israel: but speak to them that the days are at hand, and the fulfillment of every vision.
24 For there shall be no more any vain vision, nor ambiguous divination in the midst of the children of Israel.
25 For I the Lord will speak: and whatever word I shall speak, it shall come to pass, and it shall be prolonged no more: but in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak the word, and will perform it, says the Lord God.
26 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
27 Son of man: behold, the house of Israel says: "The vision that this man sees is for many days to come: and he prophesies of times that are far off."
28 Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Not one of my words shall be prolonged anymore: the word which I have spoken shall be fulfilled, says the Lord.

->THE PROPHECY OF EZEKIEL.<-

*The Lord threatens the false prophets who divine from their own imaginations and lead the people astray by promising a false peace, like smearing a wall with mud lacking straw; likewise, He speaks against the daughters of Israel who prophesy from their own hearts and sew magic cushions for every elbow.*

# CHAPTER XIII.

1 **AND** the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, prophesy to the prophets of Israel who are prophesying: and you shall say to those who prophesy from their own hearts: Hear the word of the Lord:
<margin>Jeremiah 23.</margin>
3 Thus says the Lord God: † Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own spirit and see nothing.
<margin>Below 14:9, 34:2.</margin>
4 Your prophets, O Israel, were like foxes in the deserts.
5 You have not gone up to the breaches, nor built a wall for the house of Israel, that you might stand in battle on the day of the Lord.
6 They see vain things and divine lies, saying: "The Lord says," when the Lord has not sent them: and they have persisted in confirming their word.
7 Have you not seen a vain vision and spoken a lying divination? And you say, "The Lord says," even though I have not spoken.
8 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have spoken vain things and seen lies: therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord God.
9 And my hand shall be upon the prophets who see vain things and divine lies: they shall not be in the council of my people, and they shall not be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor shall they enter into the land of Israel: and you shall know that I am the Lord God.
10 Because they have deceived my people, saying: "Peace," and there is no peace: and one built a wall, but they smeared it with mud without straw. <note>original: "luto absque paleis" — This refers to untempered mortar. Without straw to bind it, the mud or plaster would crack and fail when exposed to the elements.</note>
11 Say to those who smear it without proper tempering, that it shall fall: for there shall be an overwhelming rain, and I will cause great hailstones to rush down from above, and a stormy wind to tear it down.
12 Indeed, behold, when the wall has fallen, will it not be said to you: "Where is the smearing that you smeared upon it?"
13 Therefore thus says the Lord God: I will cause a stormy wind to break out in my indignation, and there shall be an overwhelming rain in my fury: and great stones in my wrath to consume it.
14 And I will destroy the wall that you have smeared without tempering: and I will level it to the ground, and its foundation shall be revealed: and it shall fall, and be consumed in its midst: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
15 And I will fulfill my indignation upon the wall, and upon those who smear it without tempering, and I will say to you: The wall is no more, and those who smeared it are no more.
16 The prophets of Israel, who prophesy to Jerusalem and see a vision of peace for her, when there is no peace, says the Lord God.
17 And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people, who prophesy from their own hearts: and prophesy against them.
18 And say: Thus says the Lord God: Woe to those who sew magic cushions <note>original: "pulvillos" — likely ritual amulets or bands worn on the wrists used in folk magic or divination.</note> for every elbow of the hand: and make veils for the heads of persons of every age to catch souls. And when they caught

<column-break/>

the souls of my people, they promised life to their own souls.
19 And they profaned me among my people for a handful of barley and a piece of bread, to kill souls that should not die, and to keep alive souls that should not live, lying to my people who believe in lies.
20 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against your magic cushions, with which you catch flying souls: and I will tear them from your arms: and I will let go the souls that you catch, souls made to fly away.
21 And I will tear your veils, and deliver my people from your hand, and they shall no longer be in your hands to be preyed upon: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
22 Because with lies you have made the heart of the righteous man mourn, whom I have not saddened: and you have strengthened the hands of the wicked, so that he would not return from his evil way and live.
23 Therefore you shall see vain things no more, nor divine divinations any longer, and I will deliver my people from your hand: and you shall know that I am the Lord.

# CHAPTER XIV.

*The Lord threatens the idolaters who come to the prophets to consult the Lord through them, saying He will destroy them and the deceived prophets, that He may answer them according to their iniquities; however, Noah, Daniel, and Job would deliver only themselves by their own righteousness, and not the wicked, from the famine, evil beasts, sword, and plague which the Lord will send upon a sinful people: a consolation for the remnant of Israel is also added.*

1 **AND** some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.
2 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
3 Son of man, these men have placed their uncleanness <note>original: "immunditias" — often used in the Vulgate to refer to idols or ritual impurities.</note> in their hearts, and have set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face: should I, when asked, answer them?
4 Therefore speak to them, and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Any man of the house of Israel who places his uncleanness in his heart, and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to the prophet asking me through him: I the Lord will answer him according to the multitude of his uncleanness:
5 That the house of Israel may be caught in their own heart, by which they have departed from me through all their idols.
6 Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Be converted, and depart from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your defilements.
7 For any man of the house of Israel, or of the proselytes <note>original: "proselytis" — converts or foreigners living among the Israelites.</note> whoever is a stranger in Israel, if he separates himself from me and places his idols in his heart, and sets the stumbling block of his iniquity before his face, and comes to a prophet to ask me through him: I the Lord will answer him by myself.
8 And I will set my face against that man, and make him an example and a proverb, and I will destroy him from the midst of my people: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
<margin>† Above 3:3.</margin>
9 † And when the prophet has erred and spoken a word: I the Lord have deceived 그 prophet: <note>In this context, it suggests God permits the prophet to be led by his own false desires as a form of judgment on both the prophet and the people who seek him.</note> and I will stretch out my hand upon him and destroy him from the midst of my people Israel.

<summary>Ezekiel condemns false prophets who offer "whitewashed" hope and women who practice ritual magic, while also warning that God will judge idolaters who seek divine guidance without genuine repentance.</summary>
