### CHAPTER XV.

*Just as wood cut from the vine serves only the fire, he predicts that the Jews, on account of their long-standing sins, are to be burned along with Jerusalem.*

1 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, what shall be done with the wood of the vine, above all the trees of the groves that are among the trees of the forests?
3 Shall wood be taken from it to make any work, or shall a peg <note>original: "paxillus", a small wooden pin or stake</note> be fashioned from it to hang any kind of vessel upon?
4 Behold, it is given to the fire for fuel: the fire has consumed both ends of it, and the middle of it is reduced to ash: shall it be useful for any work?
5 Even when it was whole, it was not fit for any work: how much less, when the fire has de-

<column-break/>

voured and burned it, shall any work be made of it?
6 Therefore thus says the Lord God: As the wood of the vine among the trees of the forests, which I have given to the fire to be devoured, so will I deliver up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
7 And I will set my face against them: they shall go out from the fire, yet the fire shall consume them: and you shall know that I am the Lord, when I have set my face against them,
8 And I have made the land impassable and desolate: because they have been transgressors, says the Lord God.

### CHAPTER XVI.

*Jerusalem, at first most cast down, but raised up by God in a wondrous way, shows her ingratitude through various idolatries, in which she surpassed even Samaria and Sodom; therefore the Lord will deliver her to devastation and shame before all nations; yet He will keep His covenant with her remnant.*

1 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations:
3 And you shall say: Thus says the Lord God to Jerusalem: Your root and your generation are from the land of Canaan: your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite <note>original: "Cethæa"</note>.
4 And as for your birth, on the day you were born, your umbilical cord was not cut; and you were not washed in water for your health, nor salted with salt <note>Rubbing a newborn with salt was an ancient practice intended to cleanse and toughen the skin</note>, nor wrapped in swaddling clothes.
5 No eye spared you to do even one of these things for you out of compassion: but you were cast out upon the face of the earth in the worthlessness of your soul, on the day that you were born.
6 But passing by you, I saw you being trampled in your own blood: and I said to you when you were in your blood: Live: I said, I say, to you: In your blood, live.
7 I made you multiply like the bud of the field: and you were increased, and became great, and you entered into and arrived at womanhood <note>original: "mundum muliebrem", referring to reaching the age of maturity and beauty</note>: your breasts grew, and your hair sprouted: and you were naked, and full of confusion.
8 And I passed by you, and saw you: and behold, your time was the time of lovers: and I spread my garment over you, and covered your shame. And I swore to you, and entered into a covenant with you (says the Lord God) and you became mine.
9 And I washed you with water, and cleansed your blood from you: and I anointed you with oil.
10 And I clothed you with multi-colored garments, and shod you with violet-colored leather <note>original: "janthino", likely a precious blue or violet dye</note>: and I girded you with fine linen, and clothed you with subtle fabrics.
11 And I adorned you with ornaments, and put bracelets on your hands, and a chain around your neck.
12 And I put a jewel upon your forehead <note>original: "os", literally "mouth", but often used for the face or forehead in this context</note>, and rings in your ears, and a crown of beauty upon your head.
13 And you were adorned with gold and silver, and were clothed with fine linen, and embroidered silk <note>original: "polymito"</note>, and many colors: you ate fine flour, and honey, and oil, and became exceedingly beautiful: and you advanced even to a kingdom.
14 And your name went out among the nations because of your beauty: for you were perfect in my beauty, which I had put upon you, says the Lord God.
15 But having confidence in your beauty, you committed fornication in your own name: and you offered your fornication to every passer-by, to become his.
16 And taking from your garments, you made for yourself high-

### C H A P T E R XVII.

*By a parable of two eagles, and a planted and growing vine which shall not prosper, it is declared that the king of Babylon, having moved King Jehoiachin to Babylon, shall appoint Zedekiah as king in his place: who, having abandoned the treaty entered into with Nebuchadnezzar, fled to the king of Egypt; for which reason he shall be delivered by the Lord into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, and having been led into Babylon, shall die there: but the Lord shall exalt the humble after the high one has been brought low.*

AND the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, propose a riddle, and tell a parable to the house of Israel,
3 And you shall say: Thus says the Lord God: A great eagle with large wings, with long-reaching limbs, full of feathers and variety <note>original: "varietate," referring to the speckled or multi-colored plumage of the eagle, representing the diverse nations under the Babylonian Empire</note>, came to Lebanon, and took the marrow of the cedar.
4 He plucked off the top of its twigs: and carried it away into the land of Canaan <note>Here, "Canaan" refers to a land of trade or merchants, specifically Babylon</note>, and placed it in a city of merchants.
5 And he took some of the seed of the land, and placed it in the ground for seed, so that it might establish a root over many waters: he placed it on the surface.
6 And when it had sprouted, it grew into a spreading vine of low stature, with its branches turning toward him: and its roots were under him: thus it became a vine, and produced shoots, and sent out branches.
7 And there was another great eagle, with large wings and many feathers: and behold, this vine, as if sending its roots toward him, extended its branches toward him, so that he might water it from the garden-beds of its growth.
8 It was planted in good soil over many waters: that it might produce leaves and bear fruit, so that it might be a great vine.
9 Say: Thus says the Lord God: Shall it then prosper? Shall he not pull up its roots, and strip off its fruit, and dry up all the shoots of its growth, and it shall wither? And this without a great arm or many people to pull it up by the roots.
10 Behold, it is planted: shall it then prosper? Shall it not wither when the burning wind touches it? In the beds where it grew, it shall wither.
11 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
12 Say to the rebellious house: Do you not know

<column-break/>

what these things signify? Say: Behold, the king of Babylon comes to Jerusalem: and he shall take the king and its princes, and lead them to himself in Babylon.
13 And he shall take one of the royal seed, and strike a treaty with him: and receive an oath from him: but he shall also take away the strong men of the land,
14 So that the kingdom might be humble and not be lifted up, but keep his covenant and observe it.
15 But he, departing from him, sent messengers to Egypt, that they might give him horses and many people. Shall he prosper, or obtain salvation <note>original: "salutem," here meaning safety or success in war</note>, who has done these things? And shall he who breaks a treaty escape?
16 As I live, says the Lord God: in the place of the king who appointed him king, whose oath he made void, and whose treaty he broke with him, in the midst of Babylon he shall die.
17 And not with a great army, nor with many people, shall Pharaoh wage war against him: even with the casting up of a siege-mound and the building of ramparts to kill many souls.
18 For he had despised the oath so as to break the treaty, and behold, he had given his hand: and since he has done all these things, he shall not escape.
19 Therefore thus says the Lord God: As I live, the oath which he despised and the treaty which he violated, I will lay upon his own head.
<margin>† Above 12:13. Below 32:3.</margin>
20 And I will spread my net over him, and he shall be caught in my snare: and I will lead him into Babylon, and I will judge him there for the violation by which he despised me.
21 And all his fugitives with his whole troop shall fall by the sword: and the survivors shall be scattered to every wind: and you shall know that I the Lord have spoken.
22 Thus says the Lord God: I myself will take from the marrow of the high cedar, and set it: from the top of its branches I will pluck a tender twig, and I will plant it upon a mountain high and eminent.
23 On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, and it shall break forth into a bud, and bear fruit, and it shall become a great cedar: and all birds shall dwell under it, and every winged creature shall nest under the shadow of its branches.
24 And all the trees of the region shall know that I the Lord have humbled the high tree, and exalted the low tree: and I have dried up the green tree, and made the dry tree to flourish. I the Lord have spoken, and have done it.

### C H A P T E R XVIII.

*The parable of the Jews having been rejected, He says that the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, nor vice versa, but each shall bear his own: but if the wicked man performs penance, he shall be saved: however, if the just man abandons his justice, he shall be damned: therefore the Lord exhorts them to penance and the renewal of the heart.*

AND the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 What is it that you turn into this proverb among you in the land of Israel, saying:
<margin>† Jeremiah 31:29.</margin>
> The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the teeth of the children are set on edge?
3 As I live, says the Lord God, this parable shall no longer be a proverb for you in Israel.

4 Behold, all souls are mine: as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sins, it shall die.
5 And if a man be just, and does judgment and justice,
6 And has not eaten upon the mountains <note>To "eat upon the mountains" refers to participating in pagan sacrificial banquets held at high-altitude shrines, which was a form of idolatry.</note>, and has not lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel: and has not defiled his neighbor's wife, and has not approached a woman in her uncleanness:
<margin>Isaiah 58:7. Matthew 25:35.</margin>
7 And has not saddened any man: but has restored the pledge to the debtor <note>A "pledge" was collateral, such as a cloak, which the law required to be returned before sunset so the poor could sleep.</note>, has taken nothing by force: has given his bread to the hungry, and has covered the naked with a garment:
8 Has not lent upon usury <note>The charging of interest on loans to fellow Israelites, which was forbidden in the Mosaic law.</note>, nor taken any increase: has withdrawn his hand from iniquity, and has executed true judgment between man and man:
9 Has walked in my commandments, and kept my judgments to do the truth: he is just, he shall surely live, says the Lord God.
10 But if he begets a son who is a robber, a shedder of blood, and who does any of these things:
11 And though he does not do all these duties, but even eats upon the mountains, and defiles his neighbor's wife:

13 Who gives upon usury, and takes increase: shall such a one live? He shall not live: since he has done all these detestable things, he shall die the death; his blood shall be upon him.
14 But if he begets a son, who, seeing all his father's sins which he has done, is afraid, and does not do the like to them:
15 Who has not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, and has not defiled his neighbor's wife:
16 And has not saddened any man, nor withheld the pledge, nor taken by violence, but has given his bread to the hungry, and covered the naked with a garment:
17 Who has withdrawn his hand from hurting the poor, has not received usury and increase, has kept my judgments, and walked in my commandments: this man shall not die for the iniquity of his father, but he shall surely live.
18 As for his father, because he oppressed, and offered violence to his brother, and wrought evil in the midst of his people, behold, he is dead in his own iniquity.
19 And you say: Why does the son not bear the iniquity of his father? Verily, because the son has wrought judgment and justice, has kept all my commandments, and done them, he shall surely live.

22 I will not remember all his iniquities that he has wrought: in his justice which he has wrought, he shall live.

All his justices which he has done shall not be remembered: in the prevarication by which he has prevaricated, and in his sin which he has committed, in them he shall die.

## CHAPTER XX.

->The Lord refuses to answer the children of Israel because they transgressed his mandates both in Egypt, in the desert, and in the promised land, and worshipped idols, for which he often threatened them with evils; but he spared them so that his name would not be blasphemed among the nations. Now, after all these things, he says he will call them back to his land, where they may serve him; he also commands to prophesy against the southern forest.<-

1 AND it came to pass in the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month: men of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the Lord, and they sat before me.
2 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
3 Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel, and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, I will not answer you, says the Lord God.
4 If you judge them, if you judge them, son of man, show them the abominations of their fathers.
5 And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: In the day when I chose Israel, and lifted up my hand <note>original: "levavi manum meam" — This gesture signifies a solemn oath or a vow.</note> for the offspring of the house of Jacob, and appeared to them in the land of Egypt, and lifted up my hand for them, saying: I am the Lord your God:
6 In that day I lifted up my hand for them, that I might bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land which I had provided for them, flowing with milk and honey: which is the most excellent among all lands.
7 And I said to them: Let every man cast away the offenses of his eyes, and do not be defiled with the idols of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.
8 But they provoked me, and would not hear me: no one cast away the abominations of his eyes, nor did they leave the idols of Egypt: and I said I would pour out my indignation upon them, and fulfill my wrath in them, in the midst of the land of Egypt.
9 But I acted for my name's sake, that it might not be profaned before the nations in whose midst they were, and among whom I appeared to them to bring them out of the land of Egypt.
10 Therefore I cast them out of the land of Egypt, and brought them into the desert.
<margin>† Leviticus 18:5.</margin>
11 And I gave them my precepts, and I showed them my judgments, which if a man do, he shall live in them.
<margin>† Romans 10:5. † Exodus 20:8 & 31:13. Deuteronomy 5:12.</margin>
12 Moreover, I also gave them my Sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them: and that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
13 And the house of Israel provoked me in the desert; they did not walk in my precepts, and they cast away my judgments, which if a man do, he shall live in them: and they greatly profaned my Sabbaths. Therefore I said I would pour out my fury upon them in the desert, and consume them.

<column-break/>

14 But I acted for my name's sake, that it might not be profaned before the nations, from which I cast them out in their sight.
15 I therefore lifted up my hand against them in the desert, that I would not bring them into the land which I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the chief of all lands:
16 Because they cast away my judgments, and did not walk in my precepts, and profaned my Sabbaths: for their heart went after idols.
17 Yet my eye spared them, so that I did not kill them: nor did I consume them in the desert.
18 But I said to their children in the wilderness: Walk not in the precepts of your fathers, nor keep their judgments, nor be defiled with their idols:
19 I am the Lord your God: walk in my precepts, keep my judgments, and do them:
20 And sanctify my Sabbaths, that they may be a sign between me and you, and that you may know that I am the Lord your God.
21 But the children embittered me: they did not walk in my precepts, nor did they keep my judgments to do them—which if a man do, he shall live in them—and they profaned my Sabbaths: and I threatened to pour out my fury upon them, and fulfill my wrath in them in the desert.
22 But I turned back my hand, and acted for my name's sake, that it might not be profaned before the nations, before whose eyes I had cast them out.
23 Again I lifted up my hand against them in the wilderness, to scatter them among the nations, and disperse them through the lands:
24 Because they had not performed my judgments, and had rejected my precepts, and had profaned my Sabbaths, and their eyes had been after the idols of their fathers.
25 And so I gave them precepts that were not good, and judgments in which they should not live. <note>This verse is often interpreted to mean that God permitted them to be subject to the laws of their enemies or their own corrupt desires as a form of divine abandonment.</note>
26 And I polluted them in their own gifts, when they offered up everything that opens the womb <note>This refers to the "firstborn," often implying the horrific practice of child sacrifice to the god Moloch, which the Israelites had adopted.</note>, on account of their crimes: so that they might know that I am the Lord.
27 Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel: and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God: In this also your fathers blasphemed me, when they despised me with contempt:
28 And when I had brought them into the land over which I lifted up my hand to give it to them: they saw every high hill, and every leafy tree, and they sacrificed their victims there: and they offered there the provocation of their oblation, and they placed there their sweet odors, and poured out their drink offerings.
29 And I said to them: What is the high place <term>Bamah: A hilltop shrine often used for forbidden sacrificial rites.</term> to which you go? And its name is called the High Place even to this day.
30 Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Truly, are you polluted in the way of your fathers, and do you commit fornication after their stumbling blocks?
31 And in the offering of your gifts, when you pass your children through the fire, you are polluted with all your idols even to this day: and shall I answer you, house of Israel? As I live, says the Lord God, I will not answer you.
32 Neither shall the thought of your mind come to pass, when you say: We will be like the nations, and like the families of the earth, to worship wood and stone.

34 And I will bring you out from the peoples, and I will gather you from the lands in which you were scattered; with a mighty hand, and with an outstretched arm, and with fury poured out, I will reign over you.
35 And I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples <note>This refers to the period of exile, comparing the Babylonian captivity to the original wandering in the wilderness after the Exodus from Egypt.</note>, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.
36 Just as I contended in judgment against your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I judge you, says the Lord God.
37 And I will make you pass under my scepter, and I will bring you into the bonds of the covenant.
38 And I will purge from among you the transgressors and the wicked; I will lead them out of the land where they dwell as strangers, but they shall not enter the land of Israel: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
39 And as for you, O house of Israel, thus says the Lord God: Go, serve every one of you your idols. But if even in this you will not listen to me, do not pollute my holy name any longer with your gifts and with your idols.
40 For on my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord God, there the whole house of Israel shall serve me; all of them, I say, in the land. There they shall be pleasing to me, and there I will require your firstfruits and the best of your tithes, in all your sanctified offerings.
41 I will accept you as a sweet fragrance <note>original: "odorem suavitatis"</note> when I lead you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands in which you were scattered; and I will be sanctified in you in the sight of the nations.
42 And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I have brought you into the land of Israel, into the land for which I lifted up my hand <note>A gesture of taking a solemn oath.</note> to give it to your fathers.
43 And there you shall remember your ways and all your crimes by which you were defiled; and you shall be loathsome in your own sight for all your evil deeds which you have committed.
44 And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I have dealt well with you for my name’s sake, and not according to your evil ways, nor according to your wicked crimes, O house of Israel, says the Lord God.
45 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
46 Son of man, set your face against the way of the South <note>original: "Austri"</note>, and drop your word toward the Southwest <note>original: "Africum"</note>, and prophesy against the forest of the southern field.
47 And you shall say to the southern forest: Hear the word of the Lord: thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will kindle a fire in you, and it shall devour every green tree in you, and every dry tree. The flaming fire shall not be quenched, and every face from the South to the North shall be scorched by it.
48 And all flesh shall see that I, the Lord, have kindled it; it shall not be quenched.
49 And I said: Ah, ah, ah, Lord God! They say of me: "Does he not speak in parables?" <note>The people complained that Ezekiel's metaphors—like the burning forest—were too obscure to understand, a common dismissal of his prophetic warnings.</note>

### CHAPTER XXI.

->*He prophesies of a dreadful and manifold sword coming upon Jerusalem, and upon the children of Ammon, from the king of Babylon; who at last must also be judged in his own land, and utterly destroyed.*<-

1 AND the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, and drop your word toward the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the soil of Israel:
3 And say to the land of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, and I will draw my sword from its sheath, and I will cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked.
4 Because I have cut off from you the righteous and the wicked, therefore my sword shall go out from its sheath against all flesh from the South even to the North:
5 That all flesh may know that I, the Lord, have drawn my sword from its sheath, and it shall not be returned.
6 And you, son of man, groan with the breaking of your loins, and groan with bitterness before their eyes.
7 And when they say to you: "Why do you groan?" you shall say: "Because of the news." For it comes, and every heart shall melt, and all hands shall hang limp, and every spirit shall faint, and water shall flow down all knees <note>A vivid physiological description of extreme terror or loss of bladder control.</note>: behold, it comes, and it shall be done, says the Lord God.
8 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
9 Son of man, prophesy, and say: Thus says the Lord God: Speak: A sword, a sword is sharpened and polished.
10 It is sharpened to slaughter victims; it is polished that it may glitter. You who move the scepter of my son, you have cut down every tree. <note>This refers to the Babylonian king's sword destroying the Judean royal line.</note>
11 And I have given it to be polished, so that it may be held in the hand; this sword is sharpened, and it is polished, to be put into the hand of the slayer.
12 Cry out and wail, son of man, for this sword is used against my people, against all the leaders of Israel who had fled; they are delivered to the sword together with my people; therefore strike your thigh <note>A traditional gesture of grief or mourning.</note>.
13 Because it has been tested; and what if it should even subvert the scepter, so that it shall be no more? says the Lord God.
14 You therefore, son of man, prophesy, and strike hand against hand, and let the sword be doubled, and let the sword of the slain be tripled: this is the sword of the great slaughter, which makes them stand amazed,
15 and their hearts to melt, and multiplies their ruins. At all their gates I have set the terror of the sharpened and polished sword, made to flash, and girded for slaughter.
16 Be sharpened, go to the right, or to the left, wherever the desire of your edge is turned.
17 I also will strike my hands together, and I will satisfy my indignation; I, the Lord, have spoken.
18 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
19 And you, son of man, mark out two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come; both shall come from one land. And he shall choose a place with his hand; he shall choose it at the head of the way to the city.
20 You shall mark a way for the sword to come to Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and to Judah, into the well-fortified Jerusalem.

21 For the king of Babylon stood at the crossroads, at the head of two ways, seeking a divination, shuffling arrows: he consulted idols, and examined the liver. <note>original: "exta consuluit." This refers to hepatoscopy, an ancient form of divination where a priest or king would inspect the liver of a sacrificed animal to predict the future.</note>
22 At his right hand the divination pointed toward Jerusalem, that he should set up battering rams, to open the mouth in slaughter, to lift up the voice in shouting, to set up battering rams against the gates, to cast up a mound, and to build siege-works.
23 And it shall be to them like a false oracle in their eyes, imitating the rest of the sabbaths: but he himself will remember their iniquity, so that they may be captured.
24 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have remembered your iniquity, and have uncovered your transgressions, and your sins have appeared in all your thoughts: because, I say, you have remembered them, you shall be captured by the hand.
25 And you, O profane and wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come in the time of preordained iniquity:
26 Thus says the Lord God: Remove the miter, take off the crown: is it not this which has exalted the humble, and brought down the high?
27 Overturned, overturned, overturned will I make it: and this shall not be, until he comes to whom judgment belongs, and I will deliver it to him. <note>This "overturning" refers to the end of the Davidic monarchy in Jerusalem until the arrival of the Messiah.</note>
28 And you, son of man, prophesy, and say: Thus says the Lord God to the children of Ammon, and to their reproach, and you shall say: The sword, the sword, unsheathe yourself to kill, polish yourself to destroy, and to shine,
29 While they see vain things for you, and divine lies: that you might be laid upon the necks of the wicked who are wounded, whose day has come in the time of preordained iniquity.
30 Return to your scabbard, to the place where you were created; in the land of your birth I will judge you,
31 And I will pour out my indignation upon you: in the fire of my fury I will blow upon you, and I will deliver you into the hands of foolish men, who fashion destruction.
32 You shall be fuel for the fire, your blood shall be in the midst of the land, you shall be forgotten: for I, the Lord, have spoken it.

### CHAPTER XXII.

->He recounts various crimes perpetrated in Jerusalem, on account of which he says he will pour out his indignation upon them: and he recounts the crimes of the priests, the princes, the false prophets, and the people of the land, so that no one was found who would stand in the way to turn away the fury of the Lord.<-

1 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 And you, son of man, will you not judge, will you not judge the city of blood?
3 And you shall show her all her abominations, and say: Thus says the Lord God: The city sheds blood in her own midst, that her time may come: and she has made idols against herself, to be defiled.
4 By the blood which you have shed, you have offended; and in your idols which you have made, you are defiled: and you have caused your days to draw near, and have brought on the time of your years: therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations, and a mockery to all lands.
5 Those who are near, and those who are far from you,

<column-break/>

shall triumph over you: you who are filthy, infamous, and great in destruction.
6 Behold, the princes of Israel, every one according to his power, have been in you to shed blood.
7 They have treated father and mother with contempt in you, they have oppressed the stranger in your midst, they have grieved the orphan and the widow among you:
8 You have despised my sanctuaries, and profaned my sabbaths.
9 There have been slanderers in you to shed blood, and they have eaten upon the mountains in you, they have committed wickedness in your midst.
10 They have uncovered the nakedness of the father in you, they have humbled the uncleanness of the menstruating woman in you.
<margin>† Jeremiah 5:7.</margin>
11 And every man has committed abomination with his neighbor's wife, and the father-in-law has wickedly defiled his daughter-in-law, the brother has oppressed his sister, his father's daughter, in you.
12 They have taken bribes in you to shed blood: you have taken usury and increase, and greedily oppressed your neighbors: and you have forgotten me, says the Lord God.
13 Behold, I have struck my hands together at your greed which you have practiced, and at the blood which has been shed in your midst.
14 Will your heart endure, or will your hands be strong, in the days that I shall bring upon you? I the Lord have spoken, and I will do it.
15 And I will scatter you among the nations, and disperse you through the lands, and I will cause your filthiness to be consumed out of you.
16 And I will possess you in the sight of the nations: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
17 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
18 Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross <term>scoria: the waste matter or slag left over after metal has been smelted in a furnace</term> to me: all these are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead in the midst of the furnace: they have become the dross of silver.
19 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have all become dross, therefore behold, I will gather you into the midst of Jerusalem,
20 As silver, and brass, and tin, and iron, and lead are gathered into the midst of the furnace: that I may kindle a fire in it to melt it: so will I gather you in my fury, and in my wrath, and I will rest: and I will melt you down.
21 And I will gather you, and kindle you in the fire of my fury, and you shall be melted in the midst of it.
22 As silver is melted in the midst of a furnace, so shall you be in the midst of it: and you shall know that I am the Lord, when I have poured out my indignation upon you.
23 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
24 Son of man, say to her: You are an unclean land, not rained upon in the day of fury.
25 There is a conspiracy of prophets in her midst, like a roaring lion snatching the prey; they have devoured souls, they have taken riches and precious things, they have multiplied her widows in her midst.
26 Her priests have despised my law, and profaned my sanctuaries: they have made no distinction between the holy and the profane: and they have not understood the difference between the defiled and the clean: and they have turned away their eyes from my sabbaths, and I was profaned in their midst.

### CHAPTER XXIII.

*Under the figure of the many lewd acts of two harlots, Oolla and Ooliba, and their punishment, the Lord shows the various idolatries of Samaria and Jerusalem, for which they are to be delivered into disgrace among the nations whose idolatry they imitated.*

1 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother,
3 And they committed fornications in Egypt; in their youth they committed fornications. There their breasts were pressed, and the paps of their virginity were bruised.
4 Their names were Oolla, the elder, and Ooliba, her younger sister. And they became mine, and they bore sons and daughters. As for their names: Samaria is Oolla, and Jerusalem is Ooliba. <note>original: "Oolla... Ooliba." These names are symbolic: Oolla (Oholah) means "Her own tent," referring to Samaria's self-made shrines; Ooliba (Oholibah) means "My tent is in her," referring to the Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem.</note>
5 And Oolla committed fornication while she was mine, and she lusted after her lovers, after the Assyrians who were near her,
6 Who were clothed in blue, princes and magistrates, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding upon horses.
7 And she committed her fornications with them, with all the chosen sons of the Assyrians; and with all those after whom she lusted, she was defiled with their idols.
8 Moreover, she did not leave her fornications which she had brought from Egypt; for they had lain with her in her youth, and they bruised the breasts of her virginity, and poured out their fornication upon her.
9 Therefore I delivered her into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the sons of Assur, after whose lust she went mad.
<margin>See above, chapter 16:37.</margin> 10 They uncovered her nakedness; they took her sons and her daughters, and slew her with the sword. And they became famous among women, and they executed judgments upon her.
11 And when her sister Ooliba saw this, she was even more mad with lust than she; and her fornication was more than the fornication of her sister.
12 She lusted after the sons of the Assyrians, the governors and magistrates coming to her, clothed in various garments, horsemen riding on horses, and all of them young men of excellent form.
13 And I saw that she was defiled; that they both took the same way.
14 And she increased her fornications; and when she saw men depicted on the wall, images of the Chaldeans portrayed with colors,

<column-break/>

15 Girded with belts around their loins, and dyed turbans upon their heads, having the appearance of all the captains, the likeness of the sons of Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans, in which they were born.
16 She doted upon them with the desire of her eyes, and sent messengers to them into Chaldea.
17 And when the sons of Babylon had come to her, to the bed of her breasts, they defiled her with their lewdness, and she was defiled by them, and her soul was glutted with them.
18 She also laid bare her fornications and uncovered her nakedness; and my soul withdrew from her, just as my soul had withdrawn from her sister.
19 For she multiplied her fornications, remembering the days of her youth, in which she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt.
20 And she went mad with lust for their company, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys, and whose flow is like the flow of horses.
21 And you have revisited the wickedness of your youth, when your breasts were pressed in Egypt, and the paps of your virginity were bruised.
22 Therefore, Ooliba, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will raise up all your lovers against you, with whom your soul has been glutted, and I will gather them against you from every side:
23 The sons of Babylon, and all the Chaldeans, the nobles, and the tyrants, and the princes, all the sons of the Assyrians, young men of excellent form, all of them governors and magistrates, princes of princes, and renowned riders of horses.
24 And they shall come against you equipped with chariots and wheels, a multitude of people; they shall be armed against you on every side with breastplate, and shield, and helmet. And I will set judgment before them, and they shall judge you according to their own judgments.
25 And I will set my jealousy against you, which they shall exercise with you in fury. They shall cut off your nose and your ears, and those who remain shall fall by the sword. They shall take your sons and your daughters, and your remnant shall be devoured by the fire.
26 And they shall strip you of your garments, and take away the vessels of your glory.
27 And I will make your wickedness to cease from you, and your fornication from the land of Egypt; so that you shall not lift up your eyes to them, and shall remember Egypt no more.
28 For thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will deliver you into the hands of those whom you hate, into the hands of those with whom your soul has been glutted.
29 And they shall deal with you in hatred, and shall take away all your labors, and shall leave you naked and full of disgrace; and the nakedness of your fornications shall be revealed, your wickedness and your fornications.
30 They have done these things to you because you have played the harlot after the nations, among whom you were defiled with their idols.
31 You have walked in the way of your sister, and I will give her cup into your hand.
32 Thus says the Lord God: You shall drink your sister’s cup, deep and wide; you shall be laughed to scorn and held in derision, for the cup contains much.
33 You shall be filled with drunkenness and sorrow, with the cup of grief and sadness, the cup of your sister Samaria.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

->Under the figure of a pot filled with the choicest parts of meat and bones, and set upon the fire, and under the figure of the death of Ezekiel's wife, for whom he is commanded to make no mourning, the Lord signifies that the house of Israel is to be delivered to destruction and its children to be slaughtered, with no mourning following because of their numbed spirit.<-

AND the word of the Lord came to me, in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, saying:

2 Son of man, write down the name of this day, on which the king of Babylon has strengthened himself against Jerusalem this very day.

3 And you shall speak a parable to the rebellious <column-break/> house, and say to them: Thus says the Lord God: Set on the pot; set it on, I say, and put water into it.

4 Gather its pieces into it, every good part, the thigh and the shoulder, choice pieces and full of bones.

5 Take the fattest of the flock, and heap up the bones under it; the boiling of it has overflowed, and its bones are boiled in the midst of it.

6 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of blood, to the pot whose rust <term>rust: in this context, the Latin 'rubigo' refers to the scum or corrosion inside the pot, symbolizing the persistent impurity and sin of Jerusalem</term> is in it, and whose rust has not gone out of it; cast it out piece by piece, for no lot has fallen upon it.

7 For her blood is in her midst; she shed it upon the clearest rock; she did not shed it upon the ground, so that it might be covered with dust.

8 To bring up my indignation and to take vengeance, I have placed her blood upon the clearest rock so that it should not be covered.

<margin>† Woe 24 1. Hab.</margin>
9 Therefore thus says the Lord God: † Woe to the city of blood, for which I will make a great pyre.

<margin>12.</margin>
10 Heap up the bones, which I will burn with fire; the flesh shall be consumed, and the whole composition shall be cooked, and the bones shall waste away.

11 Also set it empty upon the coals, so that its brass may grow hot and melt, and its filthiness may be melted in its midst, and its rust may be consumed.

12 It has been sweated with much labor, and its excessive rust has not gone out of it, even by fire.

13 Your filthiness is abominable: because I wanted to cleanse you, and you were not cleansed from your filth; nor shall you be cleansed until I have caused my indignation to rest upon you.

14 I the Lord have spoken: It shall come, and I will do it; I will not pass it by, nor spare, nor be appeased; according to your ways and according to your inventions <note>original: "adinventiones", referring to the sinful deeds or devices they devised</note> I will judge you, says the Lord.

15 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

16 Son of man, behold, I take away from you the desire of your eyes with a stroke; and you shall not lament, nor weep, nor shall your tears run down.

17 Sigh in silence, you shall make no mourning for the dead; let your crown be bound upon you, and your shoes shall be on your feet, nor shall you cover your face with a cloth, nor eat the bread of mourners.

18 So I spoke to the people in the morning, and my wife died in the evening; and I did in the morning as he had commanded me.

19 And the people said to me: Why do you not tell us what these things signify that you are doing?

20 And I said to them: The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

21 Speak to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will profane my sanctuary, the pride of your empire, and the desire of your eyes, and the thing over which your soul trembles; and your sons and your daughters, whom you have left behind, shall fall by the sword.

22 And you shall do as I have done: you shall not cover your faces with a cloth, and you shall not eat the bread of mourners.

23 You shall have crowns on your heads and shoes on your feet; you shall not lament nor weep, but you shall waste away in your iniquities, and each one shall groan to his brother.

### CHAPTER XXV.

*The Lord threatens destruction to the regions of Ammon, Moab, Edom <note>original: "Idumae"</note>, and Philistia <note>original: "Palaestinae"</note>, because they afflicted the children of Israel and rejoiced over their affliction.*

AND the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, set your face against the children of Ammon, and you shall prophesy concerning them.
3 And you shall say to the children of Ammon: Hear the word of the Lord God: Thus says the Lord God: Because you said, "Aha! Aha!" <note>original: "Euge, euge", an exclamation of derision or triumph</note> over my sanctuary, because it was profaned; and over the land of Israel, because it was made desolate; and over the house of Judah, because they were led into captivity:
4 Therefore, behold, I will deliver you to the people of the East for an inheritance, and they shall place their sheepfolds in you, and set up their tents in you; they shall eat your fruits, and they shall drink your milk.
5 And I will make Rabbah <note>The capital city of the Ammonites</note> a stable for camels, and the children of Ammon a resting place for flocks: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
6 For thus says the Lord God: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet, and rejoiced with all your heart over the land of Israel.
7 Therefore, behold, I will stretch out my hand over you, and will deliver you for a spoil to the nations, and I will cut you off from the peoples, and destroy you from the lands, and crush you: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
8 Thus says the Lord God: Because Moab and Seir have said: "Behold, the house of Judah is like all other nations":
9 Therefore, behold, I will lay open the flank of Moab from the cities—from his cities, I say, and from his frontiers, the glory of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, and Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim,
10 To the people of the East together with the children of Ammon, and I will give it for an inheritance: so that the memory of the children of Ammon may be no more among the nations.
11 And I will execute judgments in Moab: and they shall know that I am the Lord.
12 Thus says the Lord God: Because Edom <note>original: "Idumaea"</note> has acted revengefully to spite the children of Judah, and has deeply offended by seeking revenge against them:
13 Therefore thus says the Lord God: I will stretch out my hand over Edom, and will take away from it both man and beast, and will make it desolate from the South <note>original: "Austro"</note>: and those who are in Dedan shall fall by the sword.
14 And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel: and they shall act in Edom according to my anger and my fury: and they shall know my vengeance, says the Lord God.

<column-break/>

15 Thus says the Lord God: Because the Philistines <note>original: "Palaestini"</note> have acted revengefully, and have taken vengeance with all their soul, killing and fulfilling old enmities:
16 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will stretch out my hand over the Philistines, and will kill the killers, and destroy the remnant of the sea coast:
17 And I will execute great acts of vengeance upon them, rebuking them in fury: and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I have laid my vengeance upon them.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

*The Lord predicts the destruction of the famous city of Tyre, because it rejoiced over the devastation of Jerusalem.*

AND it came to pass in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, that the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, because Tyre has said of Jerusalem: "Aha! the gates of the people are broken, she is turned to me: I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste."
3 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, O Tyre, and I will cause many nations to come up against you, as the sea causes its waves to come up.
4 And they shall destroy the walls of Tyre, and break down her towers: and I will scrape her dust from her, and make her like a bare rock.
5 She shall be a place for the drying of nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord God, and she shall be a spoil for the nations.
6 Her daughters also <note>Small towns or villages dependent on the main city</note> who are in the field shall be slain by the sword: and they shall know that I am the Lord.
7 For thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will bring against Tyre Nebuchadnezzar <note>original: "Nabuchodonosor"</note> king of Babylon from the North, the king of kings, with horses, and chariots, and horsemen, and a company, and a great people.
8 He shall slay your daughters in the field with the sword: and he shall surround you with fortifications, and cast up a mound round about: and he shall lift up the shield against you.
9 And he shall set engines of war and battering rams <note>original: "arietes"</note> against your walls, and shall destroy your towers with his armor.
10 By the abundance of his horses their dust shall cover you: at the noise of the horsemen, and of the wheels, and of the chariots, your walls shall shake, when he enters your gates as one enters a city that is broken into.
11 With the hoofs of his horses he shall tread down all your streets: he shall slay your people with the sword, and your noble statues shall fall to the ground.
12 They shall lay waste your riches, they shall make a spoil of your merchandise: and they shall destroy your walls, and pull down your fine houses: and they shall lay your stones, and your timber, and your dust in the midst of the waters.

### CHAPTER XXVII.

*The ruin of the maritime and most wealthy city of Tyre is lamented, with a list of the goods that were usually brought to it from every region.*

1 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 You therefore, son of man, take up a lamentation over Tyre:
3 And you shall say to Tyre, which dwells at the entry of the sea, and is the merchant of the peoples to many islands: Thus says the Lord God: O Tyre, you have said: I am of perfect beauty, <note>original: "Perfecti decoris ego sum"</note>
4 And situated in the heart of the sea. Your neighbors, who built you, have perfected your beauty:
5 They built you with fir-trees from Sanir <note>The Amorite name for Mount Hermon</note> with all the planks of the sea: they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.
6 They carved oars for you from the oaks of Bashan: and they made your benches for you from Indian ivory, and your cabins from the islands of Italy.
7 Fine multi-colored linen <note>original: "Byssus varia"</note> from Egypt was woven for your sail, to be put upon the mast: blue and purple from the islands of Elishah <note>likely referring to the coastal regions of Greece or Cyprus</note> became your covering.
8 The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers: your wise men, O Tyre, became your pilots.
9 The elders of Gebal <note>original: "Giblii"</note> and its prudent men provided sailors for the service of your various merchandise: all the ships of the sea and their mariners were among your trading people.
10 Persians, and Lydians, and Libyans were in your army, your men of war: they hung the shield and the helmet in you for your ornament.
11 The sons of Arvad with your army were upon your walls all around: and the Pygmies <note>The Latin "Pygmaei" translates the Hebrew "Gammadim," referring to watchmen or a specific group of soldiers</note> who were in your towers, hung their quivers on your walls round about: they completed your beauty.
12 The Carthaginians were your merchants, filling your fairs with a multitude of all kinds of riches: with silver, iron, tin, and lead.
13 Greece, Tubal, and Meshech <note>original: "Thubal, & Mosoch"</note> were your traders: they brought slaves <note>original: "mancipia"</note> and vessels of brass to your people.

<column-break/>

14 From the house of Togarmah <note>original: "Thogorma," a region in Armenia</note>, they brought horses, and horsemen, and mules to your marketplace.
15 The sons of Dedan were your merchants; many islands were the trade of your hand: they exchanged ivory tusks and ebony in payment to you.
16 Syria <note>original: "Syrus"</note> was your merchant because of the multitude of your works: they set forth in your market gems, and purple, and embroidered works, and fine linen, and silk, and chodchod <note>likely a precious stone like ruby or agate</note>.
17 Judah and the land of Israel were your traders: they set forth in your fairs the finest wheat, and balsam, and honey, and oil, and resin.
18 Damascus was your merchant in the multitude of your works, in the multitude of diverse riches, in rich wine, and in wool of the best color.
19 Dan, and Greece, and Mosel, set forth in your fairs wrought iron: stacte <note>an oil of myrrh</note> and sweet cane were in your trade.
20 Dedan were your traders in carpets for sitting.
21 Arabia, and all the princes of Kedar, were the merchants of your hand: your merchants came to you with lambs, and rams, and goats.
22 The sellers of Sheba and Raamah <note>original: "Saba, & Reema"</note> were your merchants: with all the finest spices, and precious stones, and gold, which they set forth in your market.
23 Haran, and Canneh, and Eden were your merchants: Sheba, Assur, and Chilmad were your sellers.
24 They were your merchants in many ways, with wrappings of blue cloth, and of embroidery, and of precious treasures, which were wrapped up and bound with cords: they also had cedars in your merchandise.
25 The ships of the sea were your leaders in your trade: and you were filled, and glorified exceedingly in the heart of the sea.
26 Your rowers have brought you into many waters: the south wind <note>original: "ventus auster"</note> has broken you in the heart of the sea.
27 Your riches, and your treasures, and your manifold equipment, your mariners and your pilots, who held your goods and were over your people: also your men of war who were in you, with all your multitude which is in your midst, shall fall into the heart of the sea in the day of your ruin.
28 At the sound of the cry of your pilots, the fleets shall be troubled.
29 And all who held the oar shall come down from their ships: the mariners and all the pilots of the sea shall stand upon the land:
30 And they shall wail over you with a loud voice, and shall cry bitterly: and they shall cast dust upon their heads, and shall be sprinkled with ashes.
31 And they shall shave their heads for you, and be girded with sackcloth <note>original: "ciliciis"</note>: and they shall weep for you in bitterness of soul with most bitter weeping.
32 And they shall take up a mournful song over you, and shall lament you: Who is like Tyre, which has become silent in the midst of the sea?
33 You who, by the exit of your merchandise from the sea, filled many peoples: in the multitude of your riches and your people, you enriched the kings of the earth.
34 Now you are broken by the sea, your riches are in the depths of the waters, and all your multitude that was in your midst has fallen.
35 All the inhabitants of the islands are astonished at you, and all their kings, being struck with the storm, have changed their countenances.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

*The ruin of the king of Tyre, who was previously exalted in the greatest glory, on account of his excessive pride and other iniquities: likewise the devastation of Sidon, and the restoration of the children of Israel to their own land, once their enemies have been laid waste.*

1 AND the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
2 Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre: Thus says the Lord God: Because your heart is lifted up, and you have said: "I am a god, and I sit in the chair of God in the heart of the sea," though you are a man and not a god, and you have set your heart as if it were the heart of a god.
3 Behold, you are wiser than Daniel: <note>Daniel was a contemporary of Ezekiel, renowned for his wisdom and ability to interpret secrets; here, Ezekiel uses the comparison ironically.</note> no secret is hidden from you.
4 In your wisdom and your prudence you have made yourself strong: and you have acquired gold and silver in your treasuries.
5 By the greatness of your wisdom, and by your trading, you have increased your strength: and your heart is lifted up in your power.
6 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because your heart is lifted up as if it were the heart of a god:
7 Therefore, behold, I will bring upon you strangers, the most robust of nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom, and they shall defile your splendor.
8 They shall kill you and pull you down: and you shall die the death of those who are slain in the heart of the sea.
9 Will you still say: "I am a god," in the presence of those who kill you, when you are a man and not a god, in the hand of those who slay you?
10 You shall die the death of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers: for I have spoken, says the Lord God.
11 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre:
12 And you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord God: You were the seal of resemblance, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty,
13 You were in the delights of the paradise of God: every precious stone was your covering: the sardius, the topaz, and the jasper, the chrysolite, and the onyx, and the beryl, the sapphire, and the carbuncle, and the emerald: gold was the work of your beauty: and your ornaments were prepared on the day you were created.
14 You were an outstretched and protecting cherub, <note>A cherub is a high-ranking celestial being; here, the king is compared to a guardian spirit in Eden before his fall.</note> and I set you on the holy mountain of God; you walked in the midst of stones of fire.
15 You were perfect in your ways from the day of your creation, until iniquity was found in you.
16 By the abundance of your trade, your inner parts were filled with iniquity, and you sinned: and I cast you out from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, O protecting cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire.
17 And your heart was lifted up in your beauty: you have lost your wisdom in your splendor, I have cast you to the ground: I have set you before the face of kings, so that they might look upon you.
18 In the multitude of your iniquities, and by the iniquity of your trade, you have defiled your sanctuary: therefore I will bring forth a fire from the middle of you, which shall devour you, and I will reduce you to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all who see you.

<column-break/>

19 All who see you among the nations shall be astonished at you: you are brought to nothing, and you shall not exist forever.
20 And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
21 Son of man, set your face against Sidon: and you shall prophesy concerning it,
22 And you shall say: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in your midst: and they shall know that I am the Lord, when I have executed judgments in her, and shall be sanctified in her.
23 And I will send pestilence upon her, and blood in her streets: and the slain shall fall in her midst by the sword on every side: and they shall know that I am the Lord.
24 And there shall be no more for the house of Israel a stumbling-block of bitterness, nor a thorn bringing pain from every side of those who are against them: and they shall know that I am the Lord God.
25 Thus says the Lord God: When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they are scattered, I shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the nations: and they shall dwell in their own land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.
26 And they shall dwell in it secure: and they shall build houses, and plant vineyards, and shall dwell confidently, when I have executed judgments upon all those who are against them on every side: and they shall know that I am the Lord their God.

and to his people: To whom are you like in your greatness?

**4** The waters nourished him, the deep <note>original: 'abyssus', referring here to the subterranean source of waters</note> exalted him: its rivers ran around his roots, and it sent out its streams to all the trees of the region.

*If the watchman <note>original: 'speculator', a sentry or lookout</note> does not announce the approaching evil he has seen, he shall be guilty of those who perish: but if he announces it, only he who did not take heed for himself shall be guilty. Also, if the just man leaves his justice, he shall be condemned, and if the impious man is converted, he shall be saved. Nor should they trust in the land given to them for a possession, because they shall be destroyed for their iniquities, and the land shall be reduced to a wilderness.*

**6** But if the watchman sees the sword coming, and does not sound the trumpet, and the people do not take heed, and the sword comes and takes a life from among them: he indeed is taken in his iniquity, but I will require his blood at the hand of the watchman.

**9** But if you announce to the wicked man that he should be converted from his ways, and he is not converted from his way: he shall die in his iniquity: but you have delivered your soul.

> *The Lord says that He will deliver His sheep from the hands of the shepherds who, neglecting the flock, seek only what is their own; and that He will feed them in judgment, raising up over them His servant David, under whom they shall feed securely in all the plenty of the earth: and He shows that His flock is the people of Israel, and He is their God.*

**11** For thus says the Lord God: Behold, I myself will seek my sheep, and will visit them.

**13** And I will bring them out from the peoples, and gather them from the lands, and will bring them into their own land: and I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, by the rivers, and in all the inhabited places of the land.
**14** In the most plentiful pastures will I feed them, and on the high mountains of Israel shall be their pastures: there they shall rest on the green grass, and in fat pastures they shall feed upon the mountains of Israel.
**15** I will feed my sheep and I will cause them to lie down, says the Lord God.
**16** That which was lost I will seek, and that which was cast away I will bring back, and that which was broken I will bind up, and that which was weak I will strengthen, and that which was fat and strong I will guard: and I will feed them in judgment.

**1** AND the word of the Lord came to me, saying:

**15** As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was laid waste, so will I do to you: you shall be laid waste, O Mount Seir, and all Edom: and they shall know that I am the Lord.

### CHAPTER 37.

> *Under the figure of dry bones coming back to life, he describes the children of Israel who despair of all prosperity, being led back into their land; and by two joined pieces of wood, he signifies that the kingdoms of Judah and Israel shall be one, who under one king and shepherd, David, shall observe the commandments of the Lord, who will make an everlasting covenant with them.*

The hand of the Lord was upon me, and led me out in the spirit of the Lord; and he set me down in the midst of a plain that was full of bones.
**2** And he led me all around them; there were very many on the surface of the plain, and they were exceedingly dry.
**3** And he said to me: Son of man, do you think these bones shall live? And I said: Lord God, you know.
**4** And he said to me: Prophesy concerning these bones, and say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord.
**5** Thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will send spirit into you, and you shall live.
**6** I will lay sinews upon you, and will cause flesh to grow over you, and will stretch skin over you; and I will give you spirit, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
**7** And I prophesied as he had commanded me; and as I prophesied, there was a sound, and behold, a shaking; and the bones came together, each one to its joint.
**8** And I saw, and behold, sinews and flesh grew upon them, and skin was stretched over them from above; but they had no spirit in them.
**9** And he said to me: Prophesy to the spirit; prophesy, son of man, and say to the spirit: Thus says the Lord God: Come, spirit, from the four winds, and breathe upon these slain, that they may come to life again.

### CHAPTER XXXVIII.

->While the children of Israel live securely in their towns after being brought back from captivity, the Lord will bring Gog against them in the last days with infinite armies: but then He will consume him and his army with many disasters.<-

<margin>† Below 39:1; Apocalypse [Revelation] 20:7</margin>
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
**2** Son of man, set your face against Gog, the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy about him,
**3** And you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal,
**4** And I will turn you about, and I will put a bit in your jaws: and I will lead you out, and all your army, horses and horsemen all clothed with breastplates, a great multitude, seizing spear and shield and sword.
**5** Persians, Ethiopians, and Libyans with them, all with shields and helmets:
**6** Gomer, and all his troops, the house of Togarmah, from the remote parts of the north, and all its strength, and many peoples with you.
**7** Prepare, and equip yourself, and all your multitude that is gathered to you: and be a guard for them.
**8** After many days you shall be visited: in the last of the years you shall come to the land that has returned from the sword, and has been gathered from many peoples to the mountains of Israel, which had been continually deserted: this [land] was led out from the peoples, and they shall all dwell in it confidently.
**9** And you shall go up like a storm, and you shall come like a cloud, to cover the land—you, and all your troops, and many peoples with you.
**10** Thus says the Lord God: In that day, words shall rise up in your heart, and you shall conceive an evil thought:
**11** And you shall say: I will go up to the land without a wall: I will come to those who are at rest and dwelling securely: all these dwell without a wall, they have no bars or gates:
**12** That you may seize spoils, and invade for prey, so that you may lay your hand upon those who had been deserted, and afterwards restored, and upon the people who are gathered from the nations, who have begun to possess and to be inhabitants of the navel of the earth. <note>The "navel of the earth" is a poetic and traditional way of referring to Jerusalem or the Land of Israel as the central point of the world.</note>
**13** Sheba, and Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish, and all its lions shall say to you: Have you come to take spoils? Behold, have you gathered your multitude to seize prey, that you may take away silver and gold, and carry off furniture and substance, and seize infinite plunder?
**14** Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: Thus says the Lord God: Shall you not know in that day, when my people Israel shall dwell confidently?
**15** And you shall come from your place from the remote parts of the North, you and many peoples with you, all of them riders of horses, a great company, and a mighty army.
**16** And you shall go up over my people Israel like a cloud, to cover the earth. In the last days you shall be, and I will bring you upon my land: that the nations may know me, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes, O Gog.

### CHAPTER XXXIX.

> *The Lord will bring Gog against Israel, but will destroy him there with all his army; the people will be occupied for seven months in his burial to cleanse the land. The Lord delivered the children of Israel into captivity because of their sins, but he will lead them back into their own land for the glorification of his name.*

1 **A**nd you, son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, Gog, the chief prince <note>The Latin "principem capitis" translates the Hebrew "Rosh," which can mean either "head/chief" or a specific place name.</note> of Meshech and Tubal:
2 And I will turn you around, and lead you out, and I will make you come up from the farthest sides of the North: and I will bring you upon the mountains of Israel.
3 And I will strike your bow out of your left hand, and I will cause your arrows to fall out of your right hand.
4 You shall fall upon the mountains of Israel, you and all your troops, and the peoples who are with you; I have given you to be devoured by the wild birds and the beasts of the earth.
5 You shall fall upon the open field: for I have spoken, says the Lord God.
6 And I will send fire upon Magog, and upon those who dwell securely in the islands: and they shall know that I am the Lord.
7 And I will make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel, and I will no longer allow my holy name to be profaned: and the nations shall know that I am the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
8 Behold, it is coming, and it is done, says the Lord God: this is the day of which I have spoken.
9 And the inhabitants shall go out from the cities of Israel, and they shall kindle a fire and burn the weapons—the shields and spears, the bows and arrows, the hand-staves and pikes—and they shall burn them with fire for seven years.
10 And they shall not carry wood out of the fields, nor cut it down out of the forests: because they shall burn the weapons with fire, and they shall plunder those to whom they were a prey, and they shall spoil their spoilers, says the Lord God.

<column-break/>

11 And it shall come to pass on that day: I will give Gog a place for a burial in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers <note>A geographical location east of the Dead Sea, reimagined here as a massive graveyard for the invading forces.</note> to the east of the sea, which shall cause those who pass by to stand in awe: and there they shall bury Gog, and all his multitude, and it shall be called the Valley of the Multitude of Gog.
12 And the house of Israel shall bury them, so that they may cleanse the land for seven months.
13 Indeed, all the people of the land shall bury them, and it shall be a renowned day for them, in which I am glorified, says the Lord God.
14 And they shall continually appoint men to survey the land, to bury and to seek out those who remained upon the face of the earth, so that they may cleanse it: and after seven months they shall begin to search.
15 And they shall travel through the land: and when they see a human bone, they shall set up a marker <note>original: "titulum"</note> next to it, until the gatherers of the dead <note>original: "pollinctores," those who prepare bodies for burial.</note> have buried it in the Valley of the Multitude of Gog.
16 And the name of the city shall be Hamonah <note>Hamonah means "Multitude."</note>, and they shall cleanse the land.
17 And you, son of man, thus says the Lord God: Speak to every fowl, and to all the birds, and to all the beasts of the field: Assemble yourselves, make haste, come together from every side to my victim <note>Or "sacrifice." The destruction of the enemy is described as a ritual cleansing or feast for nature.</note>, which I slay for you, a great victim upon the mountains of Israel: that you may eat flesh and drink blood.
18 You shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth: of rams, and of lambs, and of goats, and of bulls, and of fatted animals, and of all fatlings.
19 And you shall eat fat until you are full, and drink blood until you are drunk, of the victim which I shall slay for you.
20 And you shall be filled at my table with the horse and the brave rider, and with all the men of war, says the Lord God.
21 And I will set my glory among the nations: and all the nations shall see my judgment which I have executed, and my hand which I have laid upon them.
22 And the house of Israel shall know that I am the Lord their God, from that day and forward.
23 And the nations shall know that the house of Israel was led away captive for their iniquity, because they forsook me, and I hid my face from them: and I delivered them into the hands of their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
24 According to their uncleanness and their crimes I dealt with them, and I hid my face from them.
25 Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Now I will bring back the captivity of Jacob, and I will have mercy on the whole house of Israel: and I will be jealous for my holy name.
26 And they shall bear their confusion, and all the transgressions by which they transgressed against me, when they shall dwell securely in their land, fearing no one:
27 And when I have brought them back from the peoples, and gathered them from the lands of their enemies, and have been sanctified in them in the eyes of many nations.
<margin>† Above 26. 23.</margin>
28 † And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, because I caused them to be transported among the nations, and have gathered them back to their own land, and have not left any of them there.
29 And I will not hide my face from them any longer, because I have poured out my spirit upon all the house of Israel, says the Lord God.

->### CHAPTER XL.<-

> *The Prophet is shown the future rebuilding of the city, along with the measurements in length, width, and height of the individual gate-houses, chambers, pillars, windows, vestibules, side-rooms, and steps: likewise the measuring of the four tables for the offering of sacrifices: further, the side-chambers for the singers and priests, and the vestibules of the temple.*

1 **IN** the twenty-fifth year of our exile <note>original: "transmigrationis nostrae," referring to the Babylonian Captivity</note>, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down: on this very day the hand of the Lord was upon me, and He led me there.
2 In the visions of God He brought me into the land of Israel, and set me down upon a very high mountain: upon which there was something like a structure of a city facing the South.
3 And He introduced me there: and behold, there was a man whose appearance was like the appearance of bronze, with a linen cord in his hand and a measuring reed <term>calamus</term> <note>calamus: a reed used as a standard measure, approximately 10 to 11 feet long</note> in his hand: and he stood in the gateway.
4 And the same man spoke to me: Son of man, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and set your heart upon all that I shall show you: for you have been brought here so that these things may be shown to you: announce everything that you see to the house of Israel.
5 And behold, there was a wall on the outside, surrounding the house on every side, and in the man's hand was a measuring reed of six cubits and a handbreadth <note>original: "sex cubitorum, & palmo." A cubit was about 18 inches; the "long cubit" used here included an extra palm's width</note>: and he measured the width of the structure as one reed, and the height as one reed.
6 And he came to the gate that looked toward the East, and climbed its steps: and he measured the threshold of the gate as one reed in width—that is, one threshold as one reed in width:
7 And each chamber <term>thalamus</term> <note>thalamus: a small side-room or guard-chamber within the gateway</note> was one reed long and one reed wide: and between the chambers were five cubits:
8 And the threshold of the gate by the vestibule of the gate on the inside was one reed.
9 And he measured the vestibule of the gate as eight cubits, and its pillars <term>frontem</term> <note>frons/frontem: the projecting posts or architectural "fronts" of the gateway</note> as two cubits: and the vestibule of the gate was on the inside.
10 Furthermore, the chambers of the gate facing the East were three on this side and three on that: the three had the same measure, and the pillars on both sides had the same measure.
11 And he measured the width of the threshold of the gate as ten cubits: and the length of the gate as thirteen cubits:
12 And there was a border before the chambers of one cubit: and the border of one cubit ended on both sides: the chambers themselves were six cubits on this side and that.
13 And he measured the gate from the roof of one chamber to the roof of the other, a width of twenty-five cubits: door facing door.
14 And he made the pillars sixty cubits: and the court reached to the pillar of the gate, all around the circuit.
15 And from the face of the entrance gate to the face of the vestibule of the inner gate was fifty cubits.
16 And there were narrow windows <note>original: "fenestras obliquas," splayed windows that are narrow on the outside and wider on the inside</note> in the chambers, and in their pillars within the gate all around: likewise there were windows in the vestibules all around the interior, and upon the pillars was the engraving of palm trees.
17 And he led me out to the outer court, and be-

<column-break/>

hold, there were side-chambers <term>gazophylacia</term> <note>gazophylacia: storerooms or treasuries used for sacred vessels or by the priests</note>, and a stone-paved floor in the court all around: thirty side-chambers surrounding the pavement.
18 And the pavement at the front of the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates, was lower.
19 And he measured the width from the face of the lower gate to the front of the inner court on the outside, one hundred cubits toward the East and toward the North.
20 He also measured the gate that looked toward the North of the outer court, both in its length and in its width.
21 And its chambers, three on this side and three on that: and its pillars and its vestibule were according to the measure of the first gate, its length was fifty cubits and its width was twenty-five cubits.
22 Its windows, and its vestibule, and its engravings were according to the measure of the gate that looked toward the East: and its ascent had seven steps, and there was a vestibule before it.
23 And the gate of the inner court was opposite the northern gate and the eastern gate: and he measured from gate to gate one hundred cubits.
24 And he led me toward the south, and behold, a gate that looked toward the south: and he measured its pillars and its vestibule according to the previous measurements.
25 And its windows and vestibules all around were like the other windows: fifty cubits in length and twenty-five cubits in width.
26 And it was ascended by seven steps: and there was a vestibule before its doors: and there were carved palm trees, one on this side and another on that, upon its pillars.
27 And there was a gate of the inner court on the southern way: and he measured from gate to gate on the southern way, one hundred cubits.
28 And he introduced me into the inner court at the southern gate: and he measured the gate according to the previous measurements:
29 Its chamber, and its pillar, and its vestibule by the same measures: and its windows and its vestibule all around, fifty cubits in length and twenty-five cubits in width.
30 And there was a vestibule all around twenty-five cubits in length and five cubits in width.
31 And its vestibule faced the outer court, and there were palm trees on its pillars: and there were eight steps by which it was ascended.
32 And he introduced me into the inner court by the eastern way: and he measured the gate according to the previous measurements.
33 Its chamber, and its pillar, and its vestibule as before: and its windows and its vestibules all around, fifty cubits in length and twenty-five cubits in width.
34 And its vestibule—that is, of the outer court—had carved palm trees on its pillars on both sides: and its ascent was by eight steps.
35 And he introduced me to the gate that looked toward the north: and he measured it according to the previous measurements.
36 Its chamber, and its pillar, and its vestibule, and its windows all around, fifty cubits in length and twenty-five cubits in width.

**45** And he said to me: This chamber, which faces the south way, shall be for the priests who keep watch over the services of the temple.
**46** Furthermore, the chamber that faces the north way shall be for the priests who keep watch for the ministry of the altar: these are the sons of Zadok <note>The Zadokites were a line of priests descended from Zadok, who remained faithful to King David and Solomon; in Ezekiel's vision, they alone are permitted to approach the altar</note>, who, among the sons of Levi, approach the Lord to minister to Him.
**47** And he measured the court, a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, forming a square: and the altar stood before the front of the temple.
**48** And he led me into the vestibule of the temple: and he measured the vestibule, five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side: and the width of the gate was three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.
**49** The length of the vestibule was twenty cubits, and the width was eleven cubits, and it was reached by eight steps. And there were pillars by the fronts; one on this side, and another on that side.
