# CHAPTER XLI.

->The arrangement for the rebuilding of the temple according to its<-
->individual parts.<-

**1** **AND** he led me into the temple, and he measured the fronts, six cubits of width on this side, and six cubits on that side, which was the width of the tabernacle.
**2** And the width of the gate was ten cubits: and the sides of the gate were five cubits on this side, and five cubits on that side: and he measured its length as forty cubits, and its width as twenty cubits.
**3** Then he went inside and measured the front of the door at two cubits: and the door itself at six cubits: and the width of the door at seven cubits.
**4** And he measured its length as twenty cubits, and its width as twenty cubits before the face of the temple: and he said to me: This is the Holy of Holies <note>original: "sanctum sanctorum," the most sacred inner sanctum of the Temple where the Ark of the Covenant was historically kept</note>.

<column-break/>

**5** And he measured the wall of the house as six cubits: and the width of the side-chamber as four cubits all around the house.
**6** And the side-chambers, side by side, were twice thirty-three: and there were projections which entered through the wall of the house, in the sides all around, to serve as supports, so that they did not touch the wall of the temple itself.
**7** And there was a broad passage that wound upward by a spiral staircase <note>original: "cochleam," literally a snail-shell, describing a winding stair</note>, and it led into the upper room of the temple in a circle: therefore the temple was wider in the upper parts: and so from the lower parts one ascended to the upper parts through the middle.
**8** And I saw in the house a raised height all around, the foundations of the side-chambers to the measure of a reed <term>calamus</term> of six cubits.
**9** And the width of the outer wall of the side-chamber was five cubits: and the inner house was within the side-chambers of the house.
**10** And between the chambers was a width of twenty cubits all around the house on every side.
**11** And there was a door of the side-chamber for prayer: one door toward the north way, and one door toward the south way: and the width of the place for prayer was five cubits all around.
**12** And the building that was separate and turned toward the way facing the sea was seventy cubits wide: and the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around: and its length was ninety cubits.
**13** And he measured the length of the house as a hundred cubits: and the separate building and its walls were a hundred cubits in length.
**14** Also the width before the face of the house, and of that which was separate toward the east, was a hundred cubits.
**15** And he measured the length of the building facing that which was separate at the back: the galleries <note>original: "ethecas," derived from a Greek term for corridors or storage porches</note> on both sides were a hundred cubits: and he measured the inner temple and the vestibules of the court.
**16** The thresholds, and the slanted windows, and the galleries all around in three parts, opposite the threshold of each, were paneled with wood all around: and from the ground up to the windows, and the windows were closed by doors.
**17** And up to the inner house, and outside along every wall all around, inside and out, it was by measure.
**18** And it was crafted with cherubim and palm trees: so that a palm tree was between cherub and cherub, and every cherub had two faces.
**19** The face of a man was toward the palm tree on one side, and the face of a lion was toward the palm tree on the other side, depicted throughout the whole house all around.
**20** From the ground up to the upper parts of the gate, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the temple.
**21** The doorpost was square, and the face of the sanctuary was one appearance against the other.
**22** The height of the wooden altar was three cubits, and its length was two cubits: and its corners, its length, and its walls were of wood. And he spoke to me: This is the table that stands before the Lord.
**23** And there were two doors in the temple and in the sanctuary.
**24** And in the two doors on both sides were two small doors which were folded into each other: for there were two doors on each side of the main doors.

### CHAPTER XLII.

->*Concerning the chambers and other things pertaining to the use of the sacred rites to be rebuilt.*<-

AND he led me out into the outer court by the way leading to the north, and he brought me into the chamber <term>gazophylacium</term> <note>original: "gazophylacium"; a room for storage, treasury, or official use within the temple</note> which was opposite the separate building and opposite the house facing north.
**2** In the face of its length, one hundred cubits <term>cubitus</term> <note>cubit: an ancient measurement based on the length of the forearm, roughly 18 inches</note> from the north door, and the width was fifty cubits.
**3** Opposite the twenty cubits of the inner court, and opposite the stone-paved floor of the outer court, where there was a portico joined to a triple portico.
**4** And before the chambers was a walkway ten cubits wide, looking toward the interior by a path of one cubit. And their doors faced north.
**5** Where the chambers in the upper stories were lower, because they supported the porticoes that projected from them, from the lower and middle parts of the building.
**6** For they were three stories high <note>original: "Tristega"</note> and did not have columns like the columns of the courts; therefore they projected from the lower and middle ones fifty cubits from the ground.
**7** And the outer wall <note>original: "peribolus"</note> followed the chambers that were in the way of the outer court before the chambers; its length was fifty cubits.
**8** Because the length of the chambers of the outer court was fifty cubits, and the length before the face of the temple was one hundred cubits.
**9** And beneath these chambers was the entrance from the east for those entering them from the outer court.
**10** In the width of the court's wall, which was against the eastern way, in the face of the separate building, and there were chambers before the building.
**11** And the path before their face was like the likeness of the chambers that were in the way of the north: according to their length, so also was their width; and all their entrances, and likenesses, and their doors.
**12** According to the doors of the chambers that were in the way looking toward the South: a door at the head of the path, which path was before the separate vestibule for those entering by the eastern way.
**13** And he said to me: The northern chambers and the southern chambers that are before the separate building: these are the holy chambers in which the priests who approach the Lord in the Most Holy Place <note>original: "sancta sanctorum"</note> shall eat; there they shall place the most holy things, and the offering for sin, and for guilt; for the place is holy.
**14** When the priests have entered, they shall not go out from the holy places into the outer court; and there they shall lay aside their garments in which they minister, because they are holy; and they shall be clothed in other garments, and so they shall go forth to the people.

<column-break/>

**15** And when he had finished measuring the inner house, he led me out by the way of the gate that looked toward the eastern way, and he measured it on every side round about.
**16** And he measured toward the east wind with the measuring reed <term>calamus</term> <note>calamus: a reed used as a standard measure, approximately 10 to 11 feet long</note>, five hundred reeds by the measuring reed round about.
**17** And he measured toward the north wind, five hundred reeds by the measuring reed round about.
**18** And to the south wind he measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed round about.
**19** And to the west wind he measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
**20** By the four winds he measured its wall on every side round about, its length being five hundred cubits and its width five hundred cubits, dividing between the sanctuary and the place of the common people.

### CHAPTER XLIII.

->*As the Glory of the Lord appears, the Prophet hears that the children of Israel shall no longer defile the name of the Lord, and what the measurements of the altar shall be, and the sacrifices for its purification for seven days.*<-

AND he led me to the gate that looked toward the eastern way.
**2** And behold, the glory of the God of Israel entered by the eastern way; and his voice was like the voice of many waters, and the earth shone with his majesty.
<margin>† Above 9. 1.</margin>
<margin>‡ Above 1. 1.</margin>
**3** † And I saw a vision according to the appearance that I had seen when he came to destroy the city; and the appearance was according to the sight ‡ I had seen by the river Chebar <note>original: "Chobar"</note>; and I fell upon my face.
**4** And the majesty of the Lord entered the temple by the way of the gate that looked toward the east.
**5** And the spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court; and behold, the house was filled with the glory of the Lord.
**6** And I heard one speaking to me from the house, and a man who stood beside me.
**7** He said to me: Son of man, the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, where I dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever; and the house of Israel shall no longer defile my holy name, they and their kings, by their spiritual infidelities <note>original: "fornicationibus"; in prophetic literature, this often refers to the worship of other gods</note>, and by the ruins of their kings, and in high places.
**8** Who built their threshold next to my threshold, and their doorposts next to my doorposts, and there was a wall between me and them; and they defiled my holy name with the abominations they committed; for which reason I consumed them in my anger.
**9** Now therefore let them put away far their infidelity and the ruins of their kings from me; and I will dwell in the midst of them forever.
**10** But you, son of man, show the temple to the house of Israel, and let them be confounded by their iniquities, and let them measure the structure.
**11** And let them be ashamed of all they have done: the form of the house, and its structure, its exits and its entrances, and all its description, and all its precepts, and all its order and all its laws show to them; and you shall write it in their sight, so that they may keep all its descriptions and its precepts, and do them.

**12** This is the law of the house on the summit of the mountain: Its entire boundary round about is the most holy place; this, therefore, is the law of the house.

**13** And these are the measurements of the altar in the most accurate cubits <note>original: "cubito verissimo"</note>, which consisted of a cubit and a handbreadth: its base was a cubit deep and a cubit wide, and its border at its edge round about was one handbreadth; this also was the trench of the altar.

**14** And from the base on the ground to the lowest ledge were two cubits, and the width was one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge were four cubits, and the width was one cubit.

**15** The <term>Ariel</term> <note>original: "Ariel"; the hearth of the altar where the fire burned</note> itself was four cubits high; and from the Ariel upward, there were four horns.

**16** And the Ariel was twelve cubits in length by twelve cubits in width: a square with equal sides.

**17** And the ledge was fourteen cubits in length by fourteen cubits in width at its four corners; and the rim round about it was half a cubit, and its base was one cubit all around; and its steps faced toward the East.

**18** And he said to me: Son of man, thus says the Lord God: These are the rites of the altar, on whatever day it shall be constructed: so that burnt offerings <term>holocaustum</term> <note>original: "holocaustum"; an offering entirely consumed by fire</note> may be offered upon it, and blood may be poured out.

**19** And you shall give to the Priests and Levites, who are of the seed of <term>Zadok</term> <note>original: "Sadoc"; a high priest during the reigns of David and Solomon whose descendants were granted exclusive priestly rights in Ezekiel’s vision</note>, who approach me, says the Lord God, to offer me a calf from the herd for a sin offering.

**20** And taking some of its blood, you shall put it on its four horns, and upon the four corners of the ledge, and upon the rim round about: and you shall cleanse it and make atonement for it.

**21** And you shall take the calf which was offered for the sin offering: and you shall burn it in a designated place of the house outside the sanctuary.

**22** And on the second day you shall offer an unblemished male goat for a sin offering: and they shall cleanse the altar, just as they cleansed it with the calf.

**23** And when you have finished cleansing it, you shall offer an unblemished calf from the herd, and an unblemished ram from the flock.

**24** And you shall offer them in the sight of the Lord: and the priests shall cast salt upon them, and shall offer them as a burnt offering to the Lord.

**25** For seven days you shall provide a goat for a sin offering daily: and they shall offer an unblemished calf from the herd and a ram from the sheep.

**26** For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar, and shall cleanse it: and they shall <term>consecrate</term> it <note>original: "implebunt manum ejus," literally "fill its hand," a Hebrew idiom for ordination or consecration</note>.

**27** And when these days are completed, on the eighth day and thereafter, the priests shall offer upon the altar your burnt offerings and those which they offer for peace: and I will be appeased toward you, says the Lord God.

### CHAPTER XLIV.

->The gate of the sanctuary is closed, through which only God shall enter: the uncircumcised in flesh and heart shall not enter the sanctuary, nor the Levites who followed idols, but these shall be ministers of the house: however, the sons of Zadok the priests shall enter, and the laws for these are established.<-

AND he turned me back to the way of the gate of the outer sanctuary, which faced toward the East: and it was closed.

**2** And the Lord said to me: This gate shall be closed: it shall not be opened, and no man shall pass

<column-break/>

through it: because the Lord God of Israel has entered through it, and it shall be closed.

**3** For the Prince. The Prince himself shall sit in it, to eat bread before the Lord: he shall enter by way of the porch of the gate, and shall go out by the same way.

**4** And he brought me by way of the North gate in the sight of the house: and I saw, and behold, the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord, and I fell upon my face.

**5** And the Lord said to me: Son of man, set your heart, and see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I speak to you concerning all the ceremonies of the house of the Lord, and concerning all its laws: and set your heart upon the ways of the temple through all the exits of the sanctuary.

**6** And you shall say to the house of Israel that provokes me: Thus says the Lord God: Let all your wicked deeds be enough for you, O house of Israel:

**7** Because you bring in foreign children, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary and defile my house, and you offer my bread, the fat, and the blood: and you break my covenant with all your wicked deeds.

**8** And you have not kept the ordinances of my sanctuary: and you have appointed for yourselves guards of my observations in my sanctuary.

**9** Thus says the Lord God: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter my sanctuary—any foreign son who is in the midst of the children of Israel.

**10** Moreover, the Levites, who departed far from me in the error of the children of Israel, and strayed from me after their idols, and have borne their iniquity:

**11** They shall be overseers <term>æditui</term> <note>temple servants or wardens</note> in my sanctuary, and gatekeepers of the house, and ministers of the house: they themselves shall slaughter the burnt offerings and the victims for the people: and they themselves shall stand in their sight, to minister to them.

**12** Because they ministered to them in the sight of their idols, and became a stumbling block of iniquity to the house of Israel: therefore I have lifted up my hand against them, says the Lord God, and they shall bear their iniquity.

**13** And they shall not approach me to perform the office of priesthood for me, nor shall they come near to any part of my sanctuary by the Holy of Holies: but they shall bear their shame, and the wicked deeds they have committed.

**14** And I will make them gatekeepers of the house in all its ministry, and in everything that shall be done in it.

**15** But the Priests and the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the ceremonies of my sanctuary when the children of Israel strayed from me, they shall approach me to minister to me: and they shall stand in my sight to offer me the fat and the blood, says the Lord God.

**16** They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall approach my table to minister to me, and they shall keep my ceremonies.

**17** And when they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed in linen garments: nor shall anything woolen be upon them when they minister in the gates of the inner court and within.

**18** There shall be linen headbands <term>vittæ</term> upon their heads, and linen breeches <term>feminalia</term> shall be upon their loins, and they shall not be girded in sweat <note>meaning they should not wear materials that cause sweating, which was considered ritual impurity</note>.

### CHAPTER XLV.

*In the division of the land, after the firstfruits are set apart for the Lord, a certain portion is to be assigned to the priests, the Levites, the city, and the prince. Fairness must be maintained in weights, measures, firstfruits, and sacrifices; these sacrifices shall be offered on the first and seventh days of the first month, and during the solemnities of Passover and Tabernacles.*

**1** And when you begin to divide the land by lot, set apart firstfruits for the Lord, a holy portion of the land, twenty-five thousand cubits in length and ten thousand in width; it shall be holy in all its borders round about.
**2** And from this there shall be a square for the sanctuary, five hundred by five hundred cubits on all four sides, with fifty cubits for its open space round about.
**3** And by this measure you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand, and in it shall be the temple, the holy of holies.

<column-break/>

**4** This holy portion of the land shall be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who draw near to the ministry of the Lord; it shall be a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
**5** A length of twenty-five thousand and a width of ten thousand shall also belong to the Levites, who minister to the house; they shall possess twenty chambers.
**6** And you shall assign the possession of the city as five thousand cubits in width and twenty-five thousand in length, adjacent to the holy portion of the sanctuary; it shall belong to the whole house of Israel.
**7** And a portion shall be for the prince on both sides of the holy portion and the city’s possession, facing the holy portion and the city’s possession: from the West side toward the Sea, and from the East side toward the East. Its length shall correspond to one of the tribal portions, from the western border to the eastern border.
**8** This shall be his possession of land in Israel; and my princes shall no longer oppress my people, but they shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
**9** Thus says the Lord God: Let it suffice you, princes of Israel; cease from iniquity and robberies, and execute judgment and justice; separate your boundaries from my people, says the Lord God.
**10** You shall have just scales, a just <term>ephah</term> <note>original: "ephi"; a dry measure of about 22 liters</note>, and a just <term>bath</term> <note>original: "batus"; a liquid measure of about 22 liters</note>.
**11** The ephah and the bath shall be of the same size, so that the bath contains a tenth part of a <term>chorus</term> <note>original: "cori"; a larger unit of measurement, about 220 liters</note>, and the ephah a tenth part of a chorus; their measurement shall be according to the chorus.
<margin>† Exodus 30:13. Leviticus 27:25. Numbers 3:47.</margin> **12** † Now the <term>shekel</term> <note>original: "siclus"</note> has twenty <term>gerahs</term> <note>original: "obolos"</note>. Moreover, twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels shall make one <term>mina</term> <note>original: "mnam"; a unit of weight or currency</note>.
**13** And these are the firstfruits that you shall take: a sixth part of an ephah from a chorus of wheat, and a sixth part of an ephah from a chorus of barley.
**14** The measure of oil likewise: a bath of oil is the tenth part of a chorus; ten baths make a chorus, for ten baths fill a chorus.
**15** And you shall take one ram out of a flock of two hundred from the rich pastures of Israel for a grain offering, for a burnt offering, and for peace offerings, to make atonement for them, says the Lord God.
**16** All the people of the land shall be bound to give these firstfruits to the prince in Israel.
**17** And it shall be the prince's duty to provide burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the solemnities, the New Moons, the Sabbaths, and all the festivals of the house of Israel; he shall provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings to make atonement for the house of Israel.
**18** Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take a young bull without blemish from the herd, and you shall cleanse the sanctuary.
**19** And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the house, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the posts of the gate of the inner court.
**20** And so you shall do on the seventh day of the month for everyone who has sinned through ignorance or error; thus you shall make atonement for the house.
**21** In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, the solemnity of the Passover shall be for you; for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.
**22** And on that day the prince shall provide for himself and for all the people of the land a bull for a sin offering.

## CHAPTER XLVI.

*The gate is to be opened only on Sabbaths and New Moons; the burnt offerings the prince shall offer on these days, and which gate he or the people shall use to enter or exit the temple; concerning the prince’s voluntary and daily burnt offerings; concerning his gifts given to sons or servants; the places where the priests boil the sacrifices and the ministers cook the victims for the people.*

**1** Thus says the Lord GOD: The gate of the inner court that faces toward the east shall be shut during the six working days; but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened.
**2** And the prince shall enter by the way of the porch of the outer gate and shall stand by the post of the gate; then the priests shall offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings. He shall worship at the threshold of the gate and then go out; but the gate shall not be shut until the evening.
**3** Likewise, the people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate before the Lord on the Sabbaths and on the New Moons.
**4** And this is the burnt offering that the prince shall offer to the Lord on the Sabbath day: six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish.
**5** The grain offering shall be an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs, the grain offering shall be whatever his hand is able to give, along with a hin of oil for every ephah.
**6** And on the day of the New Moon, it shall be a young calf from the herd without blemish, and six lambs and a ram, all without blemish.
**7** He shall provide an ephah for the calf and an ephah for the ram as a grain offering, and for the lambs as much as his hand can manage, with a hin of oil for every ephah.
**8** And when the prince enters, he shall go in by the way of the porch of the gate, and he shall go out by the same way.
**9** But when the people of the land come before the Lord during the solemn feasts, he who enters by the way of the north gate to worship shall go out by the way of the south gate; and he who enters by the way of the south gate shall go out by the way of the north gate. He shall not return by the way of the gate through which he entered, but shall go out straight ahead. <note>This movement ensured a continuous flow of people and prevented congestion during the high holy days.</note>
**10** And the prince shall be in the midst of them; when they go in, he shall go in, and when they go out, he shall go out.
**11** And at the fairs and the solemn feasts, the grain offering shall be an ephah for a calf and an ephah for a ram; and for the lambs, the offering shall be as much as his hand is able to give, with a hin of oil for every ephah.
**12** Now when the prince provides a voluntary burnt offering or voluntary peace offerings to the Lord, the gate that faces toward the east shall be opened for him; he shall perform his burnt offering and his peace offerings as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he shall go out, and after he has gone out, the gate shall be shut.

<column-break/>

**13** And you shall provide a lamb of the same year without blemish for a daily burnt offering to the Lord; you shall provide it every morning.
**14** And you shall provide a grain offering with it every single morning: a sixth part of an ephah, and a third part of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour. This is a grain offering to the Lord by a perpetual ordinance, continual and forever.
**15** Thus they shall provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil every single morning for a perpetual burnt offering.
**16** Thus says the Lord GOD: If the prince gives a gift to any of his sons, it is his inheritance and shall belong to his sons; they shall possess it by right of inheritance.
**17** But if he gives a gift of his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of liberty <note>The "year of liberty" refers to the Jubilee year, occurring every 50 years, when debts were forgiven and land returned to its original owners.</note>, and then it shall return to the prince; but his inheritance shall belong to his sons.
**18** Moreover, the prince shall not take from the people’s inheritance by violence, to evict them from their possession; but he shall give an inheritance to his sons out of his own possession, so that my people are not scattered, every man from his own possession.
**19** Then he brought me through the entrance, which was at the side of the gate, into the holy chambers for the priests, which faced toward the north; and behold, there was a place at the extreme western end.
**20** And he said to me: This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering; so that they do not carry them out into the outer court and thereby sanctify the people. <note>Coming into contact with these "most holy" offerings would make the common people ritually "set apart" in a way that interfered with their daily lives.</note>
**21** Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me around to the four corners of the court; and behold, in every corner of the court there was a small courtyard.
**22** In the four corners of the court there were courtyards set apart, forty cubits long and thirty wide; these four in the corners were of one measure.
**23** And there was a wall built around all four courtyards, and kitchens were built under the rows of walls round about.
**24** Then he said to me: This is the house of the kitchens, where the ministers of the house of the Lord shall boil the sacrifices of the people.

The boundaries of the holy land, which is to be divided among the twelve tribes of Israel and the foreigners.*

**2** Then he brought me out by way of the north gate and led me around the outside to the outer gate, by the way that faces toward the east; and behold, there ran out waters from the right side.
**3** And when the man went out toward the east with a measuring line in his hand, he measured a thousand cubits, and he led me through the water; the water was up to my ankles.

## CHAPTER XLVIII.

->*The division of the holy land into the twelve tribes: where the firstfruits and the sanctuary are located; the place of the Priests and Levites; the measurement of the city in a square with its suburbs; the possession of the prince; and the twelve gates of the city according to the twelve tribes.*<-

**1** And these are the names of the tribes from the northern borders along the way of Hethlon, as one goes to Hamath, at Hazar-enan, the border of Damascus to the north along the way of Hamath. From the eastern side to the sea, Dan: one portion.
**2** And alongside the border of Dan, from the eastern side to the side of the sea, Asher: one portion.
**3** And alongside the border of Asher, from the eastern side to the side of the sea, Naphtali: one portion.
**4** And alongside the border of Naphtali, from the eastern side to the side of the sea, Manasseh: one portion.
**5** And alongside the border of Manasseh, from the eastern side to the side of the sea, Ephraim: one portion.
**6** And alongside the border of Ephraim, from the eastern side to the side of the sea, Reuben: one portion.
**7** And alongside the border of Reuben, from the eastern side to the side of the sea, Judah: one portion.
**8** And alongside the border of Judah, from the eastern side to the side of the sea, shall be the firstfruits <note>In this context, the "firstfruits" (original: "primitiæ") refers to the Sacred Contribution—a special portion of land set apart for the Lord, the Priests, and the City.</note> which you shall set apart, twenty-five thousand cubits in width and in length, just like the other tribal portions from the eastern side to the side of the sea; and the sanctuary shall be in the middle of it.

**9** The firstfruits that you shall set apart for the Lord shall be twenty-five thousand cubits in length and ten thousand in width.

**10** And these shall be the holy firstfruits for the priests: toward the north twenty-five thousand in length, and toward the sea ten thousand in width, and toward the east ten thousand in width, and toward the south twenty-five thousand in length; and the sanctuary of the Lord shall be in the middle of it.

**11** The sanctuary shall be for the priests of the sons of Zadok, who kept my ceremonies and did not go astray when the children of Israel went astray, as the Levites also went astray.

**13** And for the Levites likewise, alongside the borders of the priests, there shall be twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in width. The entire length shall be twenty-five thousand, and the width ten thousand.

**14** And they shall not sell any of it, nor exchange it, nor shall the firstfruits of the land be transferred, for they are sanctified to the Lord.

**15** But the five thousand cubits that remain in width, along the twenty-five thousand, shall be common land <note>original: "profana"; land for general use rather than strictly sacred use.</note> for the city, for dwellings, and for suburbs; and the city shall be in the middle of it.

# THE PROPHECY OF DANIEL.

### CHAPTER ONE.

<margin>*Daniel, Ananias, Misael, and Azarias are chosen in captivity so that, having been taught the language of the Chaldeans, they might serve the king. After their names are changed, they obtain permission from the chief of the eunuchs to eat only vegetables and drink water. Having done this, their appearance was healthier than those who ate the royal food. God gave them wisdom, and to Daniel, He also gave the understanding of dreams.*</margin>

In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
**2** And the Lord delivered Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into his hand, along with part of the vessels of the house of God; and he carried them away into the land of Shinar <term>Shinar: An ancient name for the region of Babylonia/Mesopotamia</term> to the house of his god, and he brought the vessels into the treasury of his god.
**3** And the king commanded Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring in some of the children of Israel, of the royal seed and of the nobles,
**4** Youths in whom there was no blemish, handsome in form, and skilled in all wisdom, gifted with knowledge, and taught in discipline, who would be able to stand in the king's palace, so that he might teach them the literature and the language of the Chaldeans.
**5** And the king appointed for them a daily portion of his own food and of the wine which he himself drank, so that after being nourished for three years, they might stand in the presence of the king.

<column-break/>

**6** Now among these from the children of Judah were Daniel, Ananias, Misael, and Azarias.
**7** And the chief of the eunuchs gave them names; to Daniel, Belteshazzar; to Ananias, Shadrach; to Misael, Meshach; and to Azarias, Abednego.
**8** But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not be defiled with the king's table, nor with the wine of his drink; and he requested of the chief of the eunuchs that he might not be contaminated.
**9** And God gave Daniel grace and mercy in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs.
**10** And the prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel: "I fear my lord the king, who has appointed your food and your drink; for if he sees your faces looking thinner than the other youths of your age, you will endanger my head with the king."
**11** Then Daniel said to the steward <note>original: "Malasar," likely a proper name or the Hebrew title 'Melzar' for a guardian or steward</note>, whom the prince of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Ananias, Misael, and Azarias:
**12** "I beseech you, test your servants for ten days, and let us be given vegetables <note>original: "legumina," which includes beans, lentils, and other plant-based foods</note> to eat and water to drink.
**13** Then compare our faces and the faces of the youths who eat of the king's food; and as you see fit, deal with your servants."
**14** Having heard this proposal, he tested them for ten days.
**15** And after ten days, their faces appeared better and more well-nourished than all the youths who ate the royal food.

### CHAPTER II.

*When the wise men of the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans were a social class of priests and astronomers in Babylon famous for their occult knowledge</note> were unable to interpret the dream of Nebuchadnezzar, and all were ordered to be put to death, the mystery was revealed to Daniel as he prayed. He reveals to the king his own dream concerning a certain great statue, and provides the explanation regarding four kingdoms; because of this, Nebuchadnezzar worshipped Daniel and ordered sacrifices and incense to be offered to him, confessing the Lord God and exalting Daniel.*

IN the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar had a dream, and his spirit was terrified, and his dream fled from him.
**2** Then the king commanded that the soothsayers, magicians, sorcerers, and Chaldeans be called together to declare the king's dreams to him; and when they had come, they stood before the king.
**3** And the king said to them: "I have seen a dream; and being confused in mind, I do not know what I saw."
**4** The Chaldeans answered the king in Aramaic <note>original: "Syriace," referring to the Aramaic language, which was the diplomatic language of the era; the biblical text actually switches from Hebrew to Aramaic at this point</note>: "O King, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare its interpretation."
**5** And the king, answering, said to the Chaldeans: "The matter has escaped me. Unless you tell me the dream and its meaning, you shall perish and your houses shall be confiscated."
**6** "But if you tell me the dream and its meaning, you shall receive from me rewards, gifts, and great honor. Therefore, tell me the dream and its interpretation."
**7** They answered a second time, saying: "Let the King tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare its interpretation."
**8** The king answered and said: "I know for certain that you are stalling for time, knowing that the matter has escaped me."
**9** "If, therefore, you do not tell me the dream, there is but one sentence for you: that you have also composed a fallacious interpretation full of deceit to speak to me until the time passes. Therefore, tell me the dream, so that I may know that you are also speaking its true interpretation."
**10** Then the Chaldeans, answering before the king, said: "There is no man on earth, O king, who can fulfill your word; nor has any king, however great and powerful, ever asked such a thing of any soothsayer, magician, or Chaldean."

<column-break/>

**11** "For the matter that you require, O king, is difficult; nor will anyone be found who can declare it in the presence of the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with men."
**12** Upon hearing this, the king, in a great rage and fury, commanded that all the wise men of Babylon should perish.
**13** And the decree having gone forth, the wise men were being put to death; and Daniel and his companions were sought after, that they might perish.
**14** Then Daniel inquired concerning the law and the decree from Arioch, the captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
**15** And he asked him who had received authority from the king, for what reason such a cruel decree had gone forth from the presence of the king. When Arioch had explained the matter to Daniel,
**16** Daniel went in and petitioned the king to give him time to declare the solution to the king.
**17** And he went into his house and explained the business to his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
**18** so that they might seek mercy from the presence of the God of heaven concerning this sacred secret <note>original: "sacramento," here used in the sense of a divine mystery or hidden plan</note>, so that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
**19** Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel through a vision in the night; and Daniel blessed the God of heaven,
**20** and speaking, he said: "Blessed be the name of the Lord from age to age; for wisdom and strength are His."
**21** "And He changes the times and the ages; He transfers kingdoms and establishes them; He gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who understand instruction."
**22** "He reveals deep and hidden things, and knows what is established in the darkness; and the light is with Him."
**23** "To You, O God of our fathers, I give thanks and praise, because You have given me wisdom and strength; and now You have shown me what we asked of You, because You have opened the king’s word to us."
**24** After this, Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and spoke thus to him: "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon; bring me into the king's presence, and I will tell the solution to the king."
**25** Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel to the king and said to him: "I have found a man among the children of the captivity of Judah who can announce the solution to the king."
**26** The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar: "Do you truly think you can declare to me the dream that I saw, and its interpretation?"
**27** And Daniel, answering before the king, said: "The mystery about which the king inquires, the wise men, the magicians, the soothsayers, and the diviners cannot declare to the king."
**28** "But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, who has shown to you, King Nebuchadnezzar, what things are to come in the final times. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed are of this kind:"
**29** "You, O king, began to think upon your bed what would happen hereafter; and He who reveals mysteries showed you what is to come."
**30** "As for me, this secret was revealed to me not because of any wisdom that is in me more than in all the living, but so that the interpre-"

**31** You, O king, were watching, and behold, there was a single great statue: that statue was massive and its height was towering; it stood before you, and its appearance was terrible.
**32** The head of this statue was of the finest gold, but its chest and arms were of silver; then its belly and thighs were of bronze.
**33** Its legs, however, were of iron; part of its feet was iron, and another part was clay. <note>original: "fictilis," referring to molded pottery or fired clay</note>
**34** You watched until a stone was cut from a mountain without hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay, and crushed them.
**35** Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed together and reduced like the chaff <note>original: "favillam," literally the ash or dust from a summer threshing floor</note> of a summer threshing floor, which are carried away by the wind; and no place was found for them. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the entire earth.
**36** This is the dream. We will also tell its interpretation before you, O king.
**37** You are the king of kings; and the God of heaven has given you the kingdom, the strength, the empire, and the glory.
**38** And all the places where the children of men dwell, and the beasts of the field; the birds of the air he has also given into your hand, and he has established all things under your dominion: you, therefore, are the golden head.
**39** And after you shall rise another kingdom, smaller than yours, of silver; and another third kingdom of bronze, which shall rule over the whole earth.
**40** And the fourth kingdom shall be like iron: just as iron crushes and subdues all things, so shall it crush and break all these.
**41** Furthermore, because you saw the feet and the toes to be part potter's clay and part iron, the kingdom shall be divided; yet it shall arise from the root <note>original: "plantario," meaning the planting or source</note> of the iron, according to what you saw of iron mixed with clay from the earth.
**42** And as the toes of the feet were part iron and part clay, the kingdom shall be partly solid and partly broken.
**43** Because you saw the iron mixed with clay from the earth, they shall indeed mingle themselves with the seed of man, but they shall not stick to one another, just as iron cannot be mixed with clay.
**44** But in the days of those kingdoms, the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed, and his kingdom shall not be delivered to another people; it shall crush and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever.
**45** According to what you saw—that the stone was cut from the mountain without hands and crushed the clay, the iron, the bronze, the silver, and the gold—the great God has shown the king what is to come hereafter: and the dream is true, and its interpretation is faithful.
**46** Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and worshipped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer sacrifices and incense to him.
**47** Speaking then, the king said to Daniel: "Truly your God is the God of gods, and the Lord of kings, and a revealer of mysteries, since you were able to open this secret."
**48** Then the king raised Daniel to a high position, and gave him many great gifts; and he appointed him as prince over all the provinces of Babylon, and chief of the magistrates over all the wise men of Babylon.
**49** But Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed over the works of the province of Babylon, Sha-

<column-break/>

drach, Meshach, and Abednego; Daniel himself, however, remained at the king's gates.

### CHAPTER III.

> *Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah <note>These are the Hebrew names for Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego</note>, refusing to worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, are bound and sent into the furnace of burning fire; remaining unharmed within it, they confess to the Lord that they suffer these afflictions because of the sins of their nation; and seeking His mercy, they exhort every creature to bless the Lord. Observing this, Nebuchadnezzar was struck with wonder, and after they emerged from the furnace, he blessed their God, ordering that anyone who blasphemes Him should be killed.*

King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and he set it up in the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
**2** Therefore King Nebuchadnezzar sent to gather the satraps, the magistrates, and the judges, the captains, and the rulers, <note>original: "tyrannos," used here in the ancient sense of absolute lords or governors</note> and the prefects, and all the princes of the regions, so that they might come together for the dedication of the statue which King Nebuchadnezzar had erected.
**3** Then the satraps, magistrates, and judges, the captains, and the rulers, and the nobles who were established in power, and all the princes of the regions were gathered to come to the dedication of the statue which King Nebuchadnezzar had erected; and they stood in the presence of the statue which King Nebuchadnezzar had placed.
**4** And a herald cried out mightily: "To you it is said, O peoples, tribes, and languages:
**5** In the hour that you hear the sound of the trumpet, and the flute, and the harp, the sackbut, and the psaltery, and the symphony <note>A 'symphonia' likely refers to a bagpipe or a specific musical ensemble</note>, and every kind of music, fall down and worship the golden statue which King Nebuchadnezzar has established.
**6** But if anyone does not fall down and worship, he shall be cast into a furnace of burning fire in that same hour."
**7** Therefore, immediately after all the people heard the sound of the trumpet, flute, and harp, the sackbut, and psaltery, and symphony, and every kind of music, all the peoples, tribes, and languages fell down and worshipped the golden statue which King Nebuchadnezzar had established.
**8** And immediately at that time, certain Chaldean men came forward and accused the Jews.
**9** And they said to King Nebuchadnezzar: "O king, live forever!
**10** You, O king, have made a decree that every man who hears the sound of the trumpet, flute, and harp, sackbut, and psaltery, and symphony, and every kind of music, should prostrate himself and worship the golden statue;
**11** And if anyone does not fall down and worship, he should be cast into a furnace of burning fire.
**12** There are certain Jewish men whom you have appointed over the works of the region of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men, O king, have despised your decree; they do not worship your gods, and they do not adore the golden statue which you have erected."
**13** Then Nebuchadnezzar, in fury and in rage, commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought; and they were immediately brought before the king.

### CHAPTER IV.

*The dream of King Nebuchadnezzar concerning a tall tree being cut down is interpreted by Daniel alone, showing that the king himself would be driven from his kingdom for seven years to live with the beasts. He is urged, therefore, to redeem his sins with alms; but the dream is nevertheless fulfilled because of his pride, until he acknowledged the God of heaven, and then he is restored to his kingdom.*

**1** I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at rest in my house, and flourishing in my palace.
**2** I saw a dream that terrified me; and my thoughts upon my bed, and the visions of my head, troubled me.
**3** And a decree was issued by me to bring in before me all the wise men of Babylon, that they might show me the interpretation of the dream.
**4** Then the soothsayers, magicians, Chaldeans <note>original: "Chaldæi," here referring to a class of learned astrologers and diviners</note>, and diviners entered, and I told the dream in

6 Then the king’s face was changed, and his thoughts troubled him: and the joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees struck one against the other.
7 The king therefore cried out loudly to bring in the magicians, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. And speaking out, the king said to the wise men of Babylon: "Whoever shall read this writing, and make its interpretation known to me, shall be clothed in purple, and shall have a golden chain about his neck, and shall be the third in my kingdom."
8 Then all the king’s wise men entered, but they could neither read the writing nor show the interpretation to the king.
9 Because of this, King Belshazzar was greatly troubled, and his countenance was changed: and his nobles also were in turmoil.
10 Now the queen, on account of what had happened to the king and his nobles, entered the banquet hall: and speaking out, she said: "O king, live forever: let not your thoughts trouble you, nor let your face be changed.
11 There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him: and in the days of your father, knowledge and wisdom were found in him: for King Nebuchadnezzar your father appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and soothsayers; your father, I say, O king:
12 Because an extraordinary spirit, and prudence, and understanding, and the interpretation of dreams, and the revealing of secrets, and the solving of difficulties <note>original: "solutio ligatorum," literally the 'untying of knots' or 'loosening of bonds'</note> were found in him, that is, in Daniel: to whom the king gave the name Belteshazzar. Now therefore let Daniel be called, and he will tell the interpretation."
13 Then Daniel was brought in before the king. To whom the king spoke, saying: "Are you that Daniel of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom my father the king brought out of Judea?

<column-break/>

14 I have heard of you, that you have the spirit of the gods: and that more abundant knowledge, understanding, and wisdom are found in you.
15 And now the wise magicians have entered into my sight to read this writing, and to show its interpretation to me: and they were unable to declare the meaning of this word.
16 Furthermore, I have heard of you, that you can interpret obscure things, and resolve what is tied: if therefore you are able to read the writing and show its interpretation to me, you shall be clothed in purple, and shall have a golden chain around your neck, and you shall be the third prince in my kingdom."
17 To which Daniel, answering, said before the king: "Keep your rewards for yourself, and give the gifts of your house to another: but I will read the writing to you, O king, and I will show you its interpretation.
18 O king, the Most High God gave the kingdom and magnificence, glory and honor, to Nebuchadnezzar your father.
19 And because of the magnificence he had given him, all peoples, tribes, and languages trembled and feared him: whom he willed, he killed: and whom he willed, he struck: and whom he willed, he exalted: and whom he willed, he humbled.
20 But when his heart was lifted up, and his spirit hardened in pride, he was deposed from the throne of his kingdom, and his glory was taken away:
21 <margin>† Above in 4:12</margin> And he was cast out from the sons of men, and his heart was placed with the beasts, and his dwelling was with the wild asses: he also ate grass like an ox, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven, until he knew that the Most High has power in the kingdom of men: and He will raise over it whomever He wills.
22 You also, his son, Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all these things:
23 But you have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven: and the vessels of His house have been brought before you: and you, and your nobles, and your wives, and your concubines, have drunk wine from them: you have also praised gods of silver, and gold, and bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor feel: but the God who holds your breath in His hand, and all your ways, you have not glorified.
24 Therefore the knuckles of the hand were sent by Him, which wrote this that is inscribed.
25 And this is the writing that has been set down: MANE, THECEL, PHARES. <note>These are Latin transliterations of the Aramaic: Mene, Tekel, and Peres.</note>
26 And this is the interpretation of the word. MANE <note>Numbered</note>: God has numbered your kingdom, and has finished it.
27 THECEL <note>Weighed</note>: You are weighed in the balance, and are found wanting.
28 PHARES <note>Divided</note>: Your kingdom is divided, and is given to the Medes and Persians."
29 Then, at the king's command, Daniel was clothed in purple, and a golden chain was put around his neck: and it was proclaimed of him that he should have power as the third in his kingdom.
30 That same night, Belshazzar the Chaldean king was slain.
31 And Darius the Mede succeeded to the kingdom, being sixty-two years old.

### C H A P T E R VI.

*Daniel is appointed over the governors of the kingdom, and being accused of not observing the king's edict because he prayed to the God of heaven, he was cast into the lions' den; on the following day he was brought out unharmed, while his accusers were thrown in and suddenly torn to pieces: moved by this event, the king commanded that his God be feared throughout his provinces.*

1 It pleased Darius, and he appointed over the kingdom one hundred and twenty satraps <term>satrap: a provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire</term>, to be throughout his whole kingdom.
2 And over them three princes, of whom Daniel was one: so that the satraps might give an account to them, and the king should suffer no trouble.
3 Therefore Daniel surpassed all the princes and satraps: because the spirit of God was more abundant in him.
4 Furthermore, the king thought to set him over the entire kingdom: whereupon the princes and satraps sought an occasion to find a charge against Daniel concerning the king's business: but they could find no cause or suspicion, because he was faithful, and no fault or suspicion was found in him.
5 Then these men said: We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, unless perhaps in the law of his God.
6 Then the princes and satraps crept in <note>original: "furripuerunt," likely a variant of "surripuerunt," meaning they approached the king together or by stealth</note> to the king, and spoke thus to him: King Darius, live forever:
7 All the princes of your kingdom, the magistrates, and satraps, senators, and judges, have consulted together to issue an imperial decree and an edict: That whoever shall ask any petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of you, O king, shall be cast into the lions' den.
8 Now therefore, O king, confirm the sentence, and write the decree: so that what is established by the Medes and Persians may not be changed, nor may anyone be allowed to violate it.
9 Accordingly, King Darius proposed and established the edict.
10 Now when Daniel had learned of this, that is, that the law was established, he went into his house: and with the windows open in his upper room <term>cænaculo: an upper chamber or dining room, often used for prayer</term> toward Jerusalem, three times a day he knelt down, and adored, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had been accustomed to do before.
11 Then those men, searching diligently, found Daniel praying and making supplication to his God.
12 And approaching, they spoke to the king about the edict: O king, did you not decree that every man who should ask anything of any of the gods or men for thirty days, except yourself, O king, should be cast into the lions' den? To whom the king answered, saying: The word is true, according to the decree of the Medes and Persians, which it is not lawful to violate.
13 Then they answered and said before the king: Daniel, who is of the children of the captivity of Judah, has not regarded your law, nor the edict that you established: but three times a day he prays his prayer.
14 When the king had heard these words, he was greatly grieved: and he set his heart on Daniel to deliver him, and he labored until sunset to rescue him.

<column-break/>

15 But those men, understanding the king's intent, said to him: Know, O king, that it is the law of the Medes and Persians that every decree which the king has established may not be changed.
16 Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the lions' den. And the king said to Daniel: Your God, whom you always worship, he will deliver you.
17 And a stone was brought, and placed over the mouth of the den: which the king sealed with his own ring, and with the ring of his nobles, so that nothing might be done against Daniel.
18 And the king went to his house, and slept without eating, and no food was brought before him; moreover, sleep departed from him.
19 Then the king, rising at the first light of dawn, went in haste to the lions' den:
20 And approaching the den, he cried out to Daniel with a tearful voice, and spoke to him: Daniel, servant of the living God, do you think your God, whom you serve always, was able to deliver you from the lions?
21 And Daniel, answering the king, said: King, live forever:
<margin>† 1 Maccabees 2:60.</margin>
22 † My God sent his Angel, and shut the mouths of the lions, and they have not hurt me: because before him justice was found in me: and also before you, O king, I have done no wrong.
23 Then the king was exceedingly glad for him, and commanded that Daniel be brought up out of the den: and Daniel was brought up out of the den, and no injury was found in him, because he believed in his God.
24 And by the king's command, those men who had accused Daniel were brought: and they were cast into the lions' den, they, and their children, and their wives: and they did not reach the floor of the den before the lions seized them, and crushed all their bones.
25 Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, tribes, and languages dwelling in the whole earth: May PEACE be multiplied to you.
26 A decree has been established by me, that in all my empire and kingdom, men should tremble and fear the God of Daniel. For he is the living God, and eternal forever: and his kingdom shall not be destroyed, and his power shall endure forever.
27 He is the deliverer and the savior, performing signs and wonders in heaven and on earth: who has delivered Daniel from the lions' den.
<margin>† Above 1:21.</margin>
28 † Furthermore, Daniel continued until the reign of Darius, and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

2 I saw in my vision by night, and behold, the four winds of heaven fought upon the great sea.

### C H A P T E R X.

*Where Daniel afflicts himself and sees a man clothed in linen, who is described here; being terrified and trembling, he is comforted once and again. Concerning the resistance of the prince of the kingdom of the Persians, the prince of the Greeks, and Michael the prince of the Jews, who alone brings aid.*

**I**n the third year of Cyrus, king of the Persians, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar; and it was a true word, and great strength. And he understood the word, for understanding is necessary in a vision.

<column-break/>

2 In those days, I, Daniel, mourned for the space of three weeks.
3 I ate no desirable bread, and neither meat nor wine entered my mouth, nor was I anointed with ointment, until the three weeks were fully completed.
4 And on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was by the great river, which is the Tigris.
5 And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, there was a man clothed in linen, and his loins were girded with fine gold <note>original: "auro obrizo," pure or refined gold</note>.
6 And his body was like chrysolite <note>a yellowish-green gemstone</note>, and his face like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like burning lamps; and his arms and the parts downward to the feet were like the appearance of glowing brass; and the voice of his words was like the voice of a multitude.
7 And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision; for the men who were with me did not see it, but a great terror fell upon them, and they fled and hid themselves.
8 And I, being left alone, saw this great vision; and no strength remained in me; moreover, my appearance was changed in me, and I fainted and had no strength at all.
9 And I heard the voice of his words; and as I heard, I lay struck with fear upon my face, and my face pressed against the earth.
10 And behold, a hand touched me and lifted me up upon my knees and the joints of my hands.
11 And he said to me: "Daniel, man of desires, understand the words that I speak to you, and stand upright; for I am now sent to you." And when he had spoken this word to me, I stood up trembling.
12 And he said to me: "Do not fear, Daniel; for from the first day that you set your heart to understand, to afflict yourself in the sight of your God, your words have been heard; and I have come because of your words.
13 But the prince <note>referring to a spiritual or angelic power representing the nation</note> of the kingdom of the Persians resisted me for twenty-one days; and behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I remained there near the king of the Persians.
14 But I have come to teach you what things shall happen to your people in the latter days, because the vision is yet for many days."
15 And when he was speaking to me in such words, I cast my face down to the ground and was silent.
16 And behold, something like the likeness of a son of man touched my lips; and opening my mouth, I spoke and said to him who stood before me: "My lord, at the sight of you, my joints are loosened, and no strength has remained in me.
17 And how can the servant of my lord speak with my lord? For no strength remains in me, and even my breath is stopped."
18 Therefore, he who looked like a man touched me again and strengthened me.
19 And he said: "Fear not, man of desires; peace be to you; be take courage and be strong." And when he spoke to me, I recovered my strength and said: "Speak, my lord, for you have strengthened me."
20 And he said: "Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight against the prince of the Persians. When I was coming forth, the prince of the Greeks appeared, coming.
21 But I will tell you what is set down in the scripture of truth: and there is no one [who helps me in all these things...]

## C H A P T E R XI.

*A prophecy concerning the kings of the Persians and the king of the Greeks: regarding the wars and plots between the kings of the South and the North, and regarding the king who will not respect the God of gods, but will speak many things against Him, and which provinces will escape him, and which he will rule over.*

1 **A**nd I, from the first year of Darius the Mede, stood by him so that he might be strengthened and confirmed.
2 And now I will announce the truth to you: Behold, three more kings shall stand in Persia, and the fourth shall be enriched with exceeding riches above all others: and when he has grown strong through his riches, he shall stir up all against the kingdom of Greece.
3 But a mighty king shall rise, and he shall rule with great power, and shall do whatever he pleases. <note>This "mighty king" is historically identified as Alexander the Great.</note>
4 And when he has stood up, his kingdom shall be broken, and it shall be divided toward the four winds of heaven: but not to his own posterity, nor according to the power with which he ruled: for his kingdom shall be torn to pieces, even for others besides these.
5 And the king of the South <note>Latin: rex Austri; historically the Ptolemaic dynasty in Egypt</note> shall be strengthened: and one of his princes shall prevail over him, and shall rule with authority: for his dominion shall be great.
6 And after the end of years they shall be joined in alliance: and the daughter of the king of the South shall come to the king of the North <note>Latin: rex Aquilonis; historically the Seleucid dynasty in Syria</note> to make friendship, but she shall not obtain the strength of her arm, nor shall her offspring stand: and she herself shall be delivered up, along with those who brought her, her youths, and those who supported her in those times.
7 And a plant from the bud of her roots shall stand up; and he shall come with an army, and shall enter the province of the king of the North: and he shall abuse them, and prevail.
8 Moreover, their gods, and their carvings, and also their precious vessels of silver and gold, he shall carry away as captives into Egypt: he shall prevail against the king of the North.
9 And the king of the South shall enter into the kingdom, and shall return to his own land.
10 But his sons shall be provoked, and they shall gather a multitude of many armies: and he shall come in haste, and like a flood: and he shall return, and be stirred up, and shall join battle with his strength.
11 And the king of the South, being provoked, shall go forth and fight against the king of the North, and shall prepare an exceeding great multitude, and the multitude shall be given into his hand.
12 And he shall take the multitude, and his heart shall be lifted up, and he shall cast down many thousands, but he shall not prevail.
13 For the king of the North shall return, and shall prepare a multitude much greater than before: and at the end of times and years, he shall come in haste with a great army and exceeding riches.

### C H A P T E R XII.

*After a great affliction, the remnant of the Jews shall at last be saved; and some from the dead shall indeed rise to life, and some to reproach; the learned and the teachers shall shine: concerning two standing at the banks of the river, and a man dressed in linen, who reveals the determination of the time; and concerning the completion of this prophecy after the set time.*

1 **I**n that time Michael shall rise, the great prince, who stands for the children of your people: and a time shall come such as has not been from the time that nations began to exist until that time. And in that time your people shall be saved, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
2 <margin>Matthew 46 above 7. <note>Likely a citation to the Gospel of Matthew's discourse on the end times.</note></margin> And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake: † some to eternal life, and others to reproach so that they may see it forever.

6 And I said to the man who was clothed in linen, who stood upon the waters of the river: How long until the end of these wonders?
7 <margin>Revelation 5.</margin> And I heard the man who was clothed in linen, who stood upon the waters of the river, † when he had lifted up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, and had sworn by Him who lives forever, that it shall be for a time, and times, and half a time <note>A symbolic prophetic duration often interpreted as three and a half years.</note>. And when the scattering of the hand of the holy people is finished, all these things shall be completed.

12 Blessed is he who waits, and reaches one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.

### C H A P T E R XIII.

*The most chaste Susanna is falsely accused of adultery by lustful elders when they could not enjoy intimacy with her: but as she was being led to death, God heard her prayer: and through the boy Daniel, the old men were convicted by their own mouths, and the people killed them according to the law of retaliation.*

1 **A**nd there was a man dwelling in Babylon, and his name was Joakim:
2 And he took a wife named Susanna, the daughter of Helcias, exceedingly beautiful, and one who feared God.
3 For her parents, since they were just, had educated their daughter according to the law of Moses.
4 Now Joakim was very rich, and he had an orchard near his house: and the Jews flocked to him, because he was the most honorable of all.
5 And two old men were appointed as judges from among the people in that year: concerning whom the Lord spoke: "Iniquity came out from Babylon from the ancient judges, who seemed to rule the people."
6 These men frequented the house of Joakim, and all who had legal disputes came to them.
7 But when the people had returned at noon, Susanna would enter and walk in her husband's orchard.
8 And the old men saw her entering every day and walking; and they became inflamed with lust for her:
9 And they perverted their own minds, and turned away their eyes so that they would not look toward heaven, nor remember just judgments.
10 They were both, therefore, wounded with love for her, yet they did not show their grief to one another:
11 For they were ashamed to reveal their lust to each other, desiring to lie with her:
12 And they watched every day with greater anxiety to see her. And one said to the other:
13 "Let us go home, for it is the hour for lunch." And having gone out, they departed from each other.
14 And when they had returned, they came together: and questioning each other about the reason, they confessed their lust: and then they jointly set a time when they might be able to find her alone.
15 And it happened, while they were watching for a suitable day, she entered one day just as yesterday and the day before, with only two young girls, and she wished to wash in the orchard: for it was hot:

-># THE PROPHECY OF DANIEL.<-

65 And King Astyages <note>Astyages was the last king of the Median Empire; his death marks the transition of power to the Persians.</note> was laid to rest with his ancestors, and Cyrus the Persian took over his kingdom.

### CHAPTER XIV.

<margin>The deceptions of the priests of the idol Bel, who were secretly taking away the food placed for him, were revealed to the king by Daniel: and after they were put to death, the idol along with its temple was destroyed. Similarly, Daniel killed the dragon <note>original: "draconem"—likely referring to a large serpent or a mythical beast</note> that the Babylonians worshiped by throwing a mass made of pitch, fat, and hair into its mouth. Because of this, at the insistence of the Babylonians, he was cast into the lions' den, but was preserved unharmed; a meal was even brought to him from Judea by the prophet Habakkuk. Seeing this, the king—after his enemies were devoured by the lions in a moment—ordered everyone to fear the God of Daniel.</margin>

1 Now Daniel was a guest of the king, and was honored above all his friends.
2 There was also an idol among the Babylonians named Bel: and every day there were spent on him twelve <term>artabae</term> <note>A Persian unit of dry measure, roughly equivalent to 50 liters.</note> of fine flour, forty sheep, and six <term>amphorae</term> <note>A large ceramic jar used for liquids like wine.</note> of wine.
3 The king also worshiped him, and went every day to adore him; but Daniel worshiped his own God. And the king said to him: "Why do you not adore Bel?"
4 He answered and said to him: "Because I do not worship idols made by hands, but the living God, who created heaven and earth, and has power over all flesh."
5 And the king said to him: "Does it not seem to you that Bel is a living god? Do you not see how much he eats and drinks every day?"
6 And Daniel said, smiling: "Do not be deceived, O king: for this idol is clay within and bronze without, and he has never eaten anything."
7 Then the king was angry and called his priests, and said to them: "Unless you tell me who it is that eats these expenses, you shall die.
8 But if you can show that Bel eats these things, Daniel shall die, because he has blasphemed against Bel." And Daniel said to the king: "Let it be done according to your word."
9 Now the priests of Bel were seventy, besides their wives, and little ones, and children. And the king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel.
10 And the priests of Bel said: "Behold, we go outside; and you, O king, set out the food, and mix the wine, and shut the door, and seal it with your ring.
11 And when you come in the morning, if you do not find everything eaten by Bel, we will suffer death, or else Daniel, who has lied against us."
12 But they were confident, because they had made a hidden entrance under the table, and they always entered through it and devoured those things.
13 So it happened that after they had gone out, the king set the food before Bel: Daniel commanded his servants, and they brought ashes, and he sifted them through the whole temple in the presence of the king. Then they went out, shut the door, and sealed it with the king's ring, and departed.
14 But the priests entered by night according to their custom, along with their wives and their children: and they ate and drank everything.
15 And the king arose at the first light of dawn, and Daniel with him.
16 And the king said: "Are the seals intact, Daniel?" He answered: "They are intact, O king."
17 And as soon as he had opened the door, the king looked at the table and cried out with a loud voice: "Great are you, Bel, and there is no deceit in you!"

<column-break/>

18 And Daniel laughed, and held the king back from entering inside; and he said: "Look at the floor, observe whose footprints these are."
19 And the king said: "I see the footprints of men, and women, and children." And the king was angry.
20 Then he apprehended the priests, and their wives, and their children; and they showed him the hidden little doors through which they used to enter and consume what was on the table.
21 Therefore the king killed them, and delivered Bel into Daniel's power, who overthrew him and his temple.
22 And there was a great dragon in that place, and the Babylonians worshiped it.
23 And the king said to Daniel: "Behold, now you cannot say that this is not a living God; therefore, adore him."
24 And Daniel said: "I adore the Lord my God, for he is the living God; but this one is not a living god.
25 But you, O king, give me permission, and I will kill the dragon without sword or club." And the king said: "I give it to you."
26 Then Daniel took pitch, and fat, and hair, and boiled them together; and he made lumps and put them into the dragon's mouth, and the dragon burst open. And he said: "Behold him whom you worshiped."
27 When the Babylonians heard this, they were greatly indignant; and gathering against the king, they said: "The king has become a Jew; he has destroyed Bel, killed the dragon, and put the priests to death."
28 And when they came to the king, they said: "Deliver Daniel to us, otherwise we will kill you and your house."
29 The king therefore saw that they rushed upon him violently, and being compelled by necessity, he delivered Daniel to them.
30 They cast him into the lions' den, and he was there for six days.
31 Moreover, in the den there were seven lions, and they were given two bodies and two sheep every day; but then they were not given to them, so that they might devour Daniel.
32 Now the prophet Habakkuk was in Judea, and he had cooked a stew and put bread into a bowl, and was going into the field to carry it to the reapers.
33 And the Angel of the Lord said to Habakkuk: "Carry the meal that you have into Babylon to Daniel, who is in the lions' den."
34 And Habakkuk said: "Lord, I have not seen Babylon, and I do not know the den."
<margin>† Ezekiel 8:3 <note>A cross-reference to a similar miraculous transport in the Book of Ezekiel.</note></margin>
35 Then the Angel of the Lord took him by the crown of his head, and carried him by the hair of his head, and set him in Babylon over the den, in the rush of his spirit.
36 And Habakkuk cried out, saying: "Daniel, servant of God, take the meal that God has sent to you."
37 And Daniel said: "You have remembered me, O God, and you have not forsaken those who love you."
38 And Daniel rose and ate. Moreover, the Angel of the Lord immediately restored Habakkuk to his own place.
39 Then the king came on the seventh day to mourn Daniel; and he came to the den and looked in, and behold, Daniel was sitting in the midst of the lions.
40 And the king cried out with a loud voice, saying: "Great are you, O Lord God of Daniel!" And he drew him out of the lions' den.
41 Moreover, those who had been the cause of his destruction, he cast into the den, and they were devoured in a moment before his eyes.
42 Then the king said: "Let all who dwell in the whole earth fear the God of Daniel: for he is the Savior, performing signs and wonders on the earth, who has delivered Daniel from the lions' den."
