# THE PROPHECY OF HOSEA.

## CHAPTER ONE.

<margin>
*At what time Hosea prophesied, who was commanded to take a wife of fornications and fathered two sons and one daughter by her: whom he is commanded to name according to the consequences that the Lord had decreed to bring upon His people: concerning the conversion of the Gentiles, and the future restoration of the children of Judah and Israel in this same chapter.*
</margin>

1 **T**he word of the Lord that came to Hosea <note>original: "Osee"</note> the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.
2 The beginning of the Lord’s speaking to Hosea: and the Lord said to Hosea: "Go, take for yourself a wife of fornications, and have for yourself children of fornications: because the land, by fornicating, shall commit fornication away from the Lord."
3 So he went and took Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim: and she conceived and bore him a son.
4 And the Lord said to him: "Call his name Jezreel <note>original: "Jezrahel"</note>: for in a little while, I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will cause the kingdom of the house of Israel to cease.
5 And on that day, I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel."
6 And she conceived again and bore a daughter. And He said to him: "Call her name **Without Mercy** <note>original: "Absque misericordia," or Lo-Ruhamah in Hebrew</note>: for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, but I will utterly forget them.
7 But I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them by the Lord their God: and I will not save them by bow, or sword, or war, or horses, or horsemen."
8 And she weaned her who was named **Without Mercy**. And she conceived and bore a son.
9 And He said: "Call his name **Not My People** <note>original: "Non populus meus," or Lo-Ammi in Hebrew</note>: for you are not my people, and I will not be yours.
<margin>
† Romans 9:26.
</margin>
10 And the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea, which is without measure and cannot be numbered. † And it shall be in the place where it was said to them: 'You are not my people,' it shall be said to them: 'Sons of the living God.'
11 And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together: and they shall appoint for themselves one head, and shall come up from the land: for great is the day of Jezreel."

---

## CHAPTER II.

<margin>
*The Lord threatens Israel, like an adulterous wife, with divorce, and hedges her ways with thorns so that she may return to her husband: and since she does not recognize from whom she receives her abundance of goods, He says He will take away from her all things in which she delights: and so He would finally lead her back to Himself and gift her with great happiness: and concerning the calling of the Gentiles.*
</margin>

1 **S**ay to your brothers: "My people"; and to your sister: "You have obtained mercy."
2 Judge your mother, judge her: for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband:

<column-break/>

let her take away her fornications from her face, and her adulteries from between her breasts.
3 Lest perhaps I strip her naked, and set her as she was on the day she was born: and I will make her like a wilderness, and set her like an impassable land, and kill her with thirst.
4 And I will not have mercy on her children: for they are the children of fornications.
5 For their mother has played the harlot; she who conceived them has been put to shame: for she said: "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
6 Because of this, behold, I will hedge up your way with thorns, and I will wall it up with a stone wall: and she shall not find her paths.
7 And she shall follow her lovers and shall not overtake them: and she shall seek them and shall not find them, and she shall say: "I will go and return to my first husband: because it was better for me then than it is now."
8 And she did not know that I gave her the corn, and the wine, and the oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they used for Baal <note>original: "Baal," the Canaanite deity</note>.
9 Therefore I will turn back, and I will take my corn in its time, and my wine in its season, and I will take away my wool and my flax, which covered her shame.
10 And now I will reveal her folly in the eyes of her lovers: and no man shall rescue her out of my hand.
11 And I will cause all her joy to cease, her solemnities, her new moons, her sabbaths, and all her festive times.
12 And I will destroy her vines and her fig trees, of which she said: "These are my wages, which my lovers have given me": and I will turn them into a forest, and the beasts of the field shall eat them.
13 And I will visit upon her the days of the Baals <note>original: "Baalim," the plural of Baal</note>, to whom she burned incense, and adorned herself with her earrings and her jewelry, and went after her lovers, and forgot me, says the Lord.
14 Because of this, behold, I will allure <note>original: "lactabo"—literally to entice or draw in</note> her, and lead her into the wilderness: and I will speak to her heart.
15 And I will give her vinedressers from that same place, and the Valley of Achor <note>Achor means "trouble," here transformed into a place of hope.</note> to open up hope: and she shall sing there as in the days of her youth, and as in the days of her coming up from the land of Egypt.
16 And it shall be in that day, says the Lord: she shall call me "My Husband" <note>original: "Vir meus"</note>: and she shall no longer call me "My Master" <note>original: "Baali," a pun on the name of the idol Baal, which also means lord/master.</note>.
17 And I will take away the names of the Baals from her mouth, and she shall no longer remember their names.
18 And I will strike a covenant with them on that day, with the beasts of the field, and with the birds of the sky, and with the creeping things of the earth: and I will break the bow, and the sword, and war from the earth: and I will make them sleep in confidence.
19 And I will betroth you to me forever: and I will betroth you to me in justice, and judgment, and in mercy, and in compassions.
20 And I will betroth you to me in faith: and you shall know that I am the Lord.
21 And it shall be in that day: I will hear, says the Lord, I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth.

<summary>This page contains the opening chapters of the Book of Hosea, where the prophet is commanded to marry an unfaithful woman as a living metaphor for God's relationship with the unfaithful kingdom of Israel. It details the symbolic naming of Hosea's children and God's alternate threats of punishment and promises of future restoration and betrothal.</summary>
<keywords>Hosea, Gomer, Jezreel, adultery, covenant, Baal, restoration, prophecy, Israel, Judah</keywords>

22 And the earth shall hear the grain, and the wine, and the oil: and these shall hear Jezreel <note>original: "Jezrahel," a name meaning "God sows"</note>.
23 And I will sow her for myself in the earth, and I will have mercy on her who was called **Without mercy** <note>original: "Absque misericordia," referring to the prophet's daughter Lo-Ruhamah</note>.
<margin>
Romans 9:25.
1 Peter 2:10.
</margin>
24 † And I will say to "Not my people": "You are my people": and he shall say: "You are my God."

### CHAPTER III.

*The Prophet is commanded again to love an adulteress, who must nevertheless wait for him many days; this signifies that the children of Israel, who sit for many days without a king or sacrifice, will at last return to the Lord.*

AND the Lord said to me: Go again, and love a woman loved by a friend, yet an adulteress: just as the Lord loves the children of Israel, even as they look toward foreign gods and love the dregs of grapes <note>original: "vinacia uvarum," likely referring to raisin cakes used in pagan sacrificial feasts</note>.
2 And I bought <note>original: "fodi," literally "dug" or "acquired"</note> her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, and a homer <note>original: "coro," a large dry measure</note> of barley, and half a homer of barley.
3 And I said to her: You shall wait for me many days: you shall not play the harlot, and you shall not belong to another man, and I also will wait for you.
4 Because for many days the children of Israel shall sit without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an altar, and without an ephod <note>a priestly garment used for seeking oracles</note>, and without teraphim <note>original: "theraphim," small household idols</note>.
<margin>
Ezekiel 34:23.
</margin>
5 † And after this, the children of Israel shall return and seek the Lord their God and David their king: and they shall tremble before the Lord and His goodness in the last days.

### CHAPTER IV.

*The Lord threatens the land of Israel because of the many sins of the people, who have rejected knowledge and are devoted to idolatry; He says He will leave Israel in its sins, desiring that Judah does not imitate them.*

Hear the word of the Lord, children of Israel, for the Lord has a judgment against the inhabitants of the land: for there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God in the land.
2 Cursing, and lying, and murder, and theft, and adultery have overflowed, and blood touches blood.
3 For this reason the land shall mourn, and everyone who dwells in it shall languish, along with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air; and even the fish of the sea shall be gathered up.
4 Nevertheless, let no one judge, and let no man be rebuked: for your people are like those who argue with the priest.
5 And you shall fall this day, and the prophet also shall fall with you; in the night I have made your mother silent.
6 My people have been silenced because they lacked knowledge: because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, so that you shall not serve as a priest to me; and since you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
7 As they increased in number, so they sinned against me: I will change their glory into shame.
8 They eat the sins of my people, and they lift up their souls toward their iniquity.
<margin>
Isaiah 24:2.
</margin>
9 † And it shall be: as the people, so the priest: and I will visit his ways upon him and repay him for his thoughts.
10 And they shall eat and not be satisfied; they have committed fornication and have not ceased: because they have abandoned the Lord to not keep His ways.
11 Fornication, and wine, and drunkenness take away the heart.
12 My people have consulted their wooden idol,

<column-break/>

and their staff has spoken to them: for the spirit of fornications has deceived them, and they have gone whoring away from their God.
13 They sacrificed on the tops of the mountains and burned incense upon the hills: under the oak, the poplar, and the terebinth <note>a large, shade-giving tree</note>, because its shade was good: therefore your daughters shall commit fornication, and your brides shall be adulteresses.
14 I will not punish your daughters when they commit fornication, nor your brides when they commit adultery: since the men themselves consorted with harlots and sacrificed with the effeminate <note>original: "effeminatis," often referring to male cult prostitutes in pagan temples</note>, and the people without understanding shall be beaten.
15 If you, Israel, commit fornication, let not Judah at least offend: and do not enter into Gilgal <note>original: "Galgala"</note>, and do not go up to Beth-aven <note>original: "Bethaven," a mocking name meaning "House of Vanity" or "Idolatry," used for Bethel</note>, nor swear: "As the Lord lives."
16 For Israel has wandered away like a stubborn cow: now the Lord will feed them like a lamb in a wide pasture.
17 Ephraim <note>the largest tribe, often used to represent the whole Northern Kingdom of Israel</note> is a companion of idols; let him alone.
18 Their banquet is separated, they have committed fornication upon fornication: her protectors have loved to bring shame.
19 For the wind <note>original: "spiritus"</note> has bound them in its wings, and they shall be put to shame by their sacrifices.

### CHAPTER V.

*The Lord threatens that He will punish Israel for its sins, and likewise Judah; nor will human help be of use when the Lord is opposed to them.*

Hear this, O priests, and attend, O house of Israel, and listen, O house of the king: for judgment is against you, because you have become a snare at the lookout <note>original: "speculationi," possibly Mizpah</note>, and a net spread over Tabor <note>original: "Thabor," a prominent mountain</note>.
2 And you have turned sacrifices into the depths: and I am the teacher <note>original: "eruditor," also meaning chastiser</note> of them all.
3 I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me: for now Ephraim has committed fornication; Israel is defiled.
4 They will not set their thoughts to return to their God: for the spirit of fornications is in their midst, and they have not known the Lord.
5 And the arrogance of Israel shall answer to his face: and Israel and Ephraim shall fall in their iniquity; Judah also shall fall with them.
6 With their flocks and their herds they shall go to seek the Lord, and they shall not find Him: He has been withdrawn from them.
7 They have dealt treacherously against the Lord, for they have fathered alien children: now the new moon <note>original: "mensis," a month or its festival</note> shall devour them with their portions.
8 Blow the horn in Gibeah <note>original: "Gabaa"</note>, the trumpet in Ramah <note>original: "Rama"</note>: wail in Beth-aven, behind your back, O Benjamin.
9 Ephraim shall be in desolation in the day of correction: among the tribes of Israel I have shown the truth.
10 The princes of Judah have become like those who move the boundary stone: I will pour out my wrath upon them like water.
11 Ephraim suffers oppression, broken by judgment: because he began to follow after filth <note>original: "sordes," referring to idols or worldly commands</note>.
12 And I am like a moth to Ephraim: and like rot to the house of Judah.
13 And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his wound: and Ephraim went to Assyria <note>original: "Assur"</note>, and sent to King Vengeance <note>original: "Ultorem," likely a title for the Assyrian king</note>: but he will not be able to heal you, nor will he be able to release the wound from you.

<summary>This page contains the continuation of Hosea's prophecy, shifting from the personal allegory of his marriage to direct rebukes against Israel (Ephraim) and Judah for their idolatry and lack of spiritual knowledge. It highlights the futility of seeking help from foreign powers like Assyria when the people have abandoned God.</summary>

# THE PROPHECY OF HOSEA.

14 For I am like a lioness to Ephraim, and like a young lion to the house of Judah: I, even I, will seize and go away; I will take them, and there is no one who can rescue them.
15 Going, I will return to my place: until you are exhausted <note>original: "deficiatis," meaning to faint or be spent</note> and seek my face.

### CHAPTER VI.

*Having returned to the Lord in their distress, they promise themselves salvation from Him with great confidence; the Lord's relationship with Israel and Judah is explained, showing that neither benefits nor the warnings of the prophets have called them back from idolatry and other iniquities, since He prefers mercy over sacrifice.*

1 In their distress, they will rise early to seek me: come, and let us return to the Lord:
2 For he has seized us, and he will heal us; he will strike, and he will cure us.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 15:4.</margin>
3 He will bring us back to life after two days: on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight. We shall know, and we shall follow on to know the Lord: his going forth is prepared like the dawn, and he comes to us like the early rain, and the late rain upon the earth.
4 What shall I do for you, Ephraim? What shall I do for you, Judah? Your mercy is like a morning cloud, and like the dew that passes away in the morning.
5 Because of this, I have hewn them <note>original: "dolavi," like carving or dressing stone</note> by the prophets; I have slain them by the words of my mouth: and your judgments shall go forth like the light.
<margin>
† 1 Samuel 15:12.
Ecclesiastes 4:17.
Matthew 9:13 and 12:7.
</margin>
6 For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
7 But they, like Adam, have transgressed the covenant; there they have dealt treacherously against me.
8 Gilead <note>original: "Galaad"</note> is a city of those who work idols, tripped up <note>original: "supplantata," meaning deceitfully undermined</note> by blood.
9 And like the jaws of robbing men, a company of priests, they murder those passing on the way from Shechem <note>original: "Sichem"</note>: for they have committed a crime.
10 In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: there are the fornications of Ephraim; Israel is defiled.
11 But you also, O Judah, set a harvest for yourself, when I shall restore the captivity of my people.

### CHAPTER VII.

*When the Lord was about to heal Israel, their iniquities stood in the way: for consenting to the malice of their kings, they all burned intensely with idolatry. Having abandoned the Lord and turned to Egypt for help, they were carried away to the Assyrians.*

1 When I wished to heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim was revealed, and the malice of Samaria, because they have worked a lie: and the thief has entered to plunder, the little robber is outside.
2 And lest they should say in their hearts that I remember all their malice: now their own inventions have surrounded them, they have been done before my face.
3 In their malice they have made the king glad: and in their lies, the princes.
4 All of them are adulterers, like an oven heated by a baker: the city rested a little while from the mixing of the leaven, until the whole was leavened.
5 On the day of our king: the princes began to rage with wine: he stretched out his hand with mockers.
6 For they have applied their heart like an oven while he laid snares for them: all night he

<column-break/>

who baked them slept, in the morning it was set ablaze like a flaming fire.
7 All are heated like an oven, and have devoured their judges: all their kings have fallen: there is no one among them who cries out to me.
8 Ephraim was mixed among the peoples: Ephraim has become like bread baked under the ashes <note>original: "subcinericius panis," a cake cooked on hot coals that was not flipped over, leaving it half-burnt and half-raw</note>, which is not turned.
9 Strangers have devoured his strength, and he did not know it: even gray hairs are spread upon him, and he was ignorant of it.
10 And the pride of Israel shall be humbled before his face: nor have they returned to the Lord their God, and they have not sought him in all these things.
11 And Ephraim has become like a deceived dove without a heart: they called upon Egypt, they went to the Assyrians.
12 And when they have set out, I will spread my net over them: I will bring them down like a bird of the sky, I will strike them according to the report of their assembly.
13 Woe to them, for they have withdrawn from me: they shall be laid waste, because they have transgressed against me: and I redeemed them: and they themselves have spoken lies against me.
14 And they have not cried out to me in their heart, but they wailed in their beds: they ruminated <note>original: "ruminabant," literally "chewed the cud"</note> over grain and wine, and they withdrew from me.
15 And I trained them, and strengthened their arms: and they have thought of malice against me.
16 They returned so that they might be without a yoke: they have become like a deceitful bow: their princes shall fall by the sword because of the rage of their tongue. This is their derision in the land of Egypt.

### CHAPTER VIII.

*He foretells that Samaria with its calf will be destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar because of idolatry: nor will their sacrifices be accepted: the cities of Judah shall also be burned.*

1 Let the trumpet be in your throat like an eagle over the house of the Lord: because they have transgressed my covenant, and have broken my law.
2 They shall call upon me: "My God, we, Israel, have known you."
3 Israel has cast away what is good, the enemy shall pursue him.
4 They have reigned, but not by me: they have stood as princes, and I did not know it: they have made idols for themselves from their silver and their gold, so that they might perish.
5 Your calf, O Samaria, is cast away; my fury is kindled against them: how long will they be unable to be cleansed?
6 For it is even from Israel: a craftsman made it, and it is not God: for the calf of Samaria shall be like spider webs <note>original: "aranearum telas," signifying something fragile and worthless</note>.
7 For they shall sow the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: there is no standing stalk in it, the bud shall yield no meal: and if it should yield it, strangers shall eat it.
8 Israel is swallowed up: now he has become among the nations like an unclean vessel.
9 For they have gone up to Assyria <note>original: "Assur"</note>, a wild ass solitary for himself: Ephraim has given gifts to lovers.
10 But even though they have hired the nations with a reward, now I will gather them: and they shall rest a little while from the burden of the king and the princes.
11 Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning: altars have been made for him unto crime.
12 I will write for him my manifold laws, which are accounted as something foreign <note>original: "alienæ," as if belonging to a stranger</note>.

<summary>Hosea warns Israel and Judah of divine judgment, comparing God's anger to a lion and the people's fickle devotion to a morning mist. The text highlights the hollowness of their sacrifices and their reliance on foreign powers like Egypt and Assyria instead of God.</summary>

### C H A P T E R IX.

->*The Lord will bring famine and captivity upon the people of Israel because of their sins: nor will their sacrifices be pleasing to him: and because they persist in sins, they shall remain perpetually cast out by the Lord, wanderers among the nations.*<-

1 **D**o not rejoice, O Israel, do not exult like the nations: for you have played the harlot against your God, you have loved a bribe <note>original: "mercedem," referring to the "wages" of a prostitute</note> upon every threshing floor of wheat.
2 The threshing floor and the winepress shall not feed them, and the wine shall fail them.
3 They shall not dwell in the Lord’s land: Ephraim has returned to Egypt, and among the Assyrians he has eaten polluted food.
4 They shall not offer wine-offerings to the Lord, and they shall not please him: their sacrifices are like the bread of mourners: all who eat it shall be contaminated: for their bread is for their own souls, it shall not enter into the house of the Lord.
5 What will you do on the solemn day, on the day of the feast of the Lord?
6 For behold, they are gone away because of destruction: Egypt shall gather them, Memphis shall bury them: the nettle shall inherit their desirable silver, and the burr shall be in their tabernacles.
7 The days of visitation have come, the days of retribution have come: know, O Israel, that the prophet is a fool, the spiritual man is mad, because of the multitude of your iniquity, and the multitude of your madness.
8 The watchman of Ephraim is with my God: the prophet is become a snare of ruin upon all his ways, madness in the house of his God.
<margin>† Judges 19:25.</margin>
9 † They have sinned deeply, as in the days of Gibeah <note>original: "Gabaa," a reference to a notorious crime in the book of Judges</note>: he will remember their iniquity, and he will visit their sins.
10 I found Israel like grapes in the desert, I saw their fathers like the first-fruits of a fig tree at its top: but they went into Baal-peor <note>original: "Beelphegor"</note>, and were alienated in confusion, and became abominable like the things they loved.
11 Ephraim has flown away like a bird, their glory from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.
12 And even if they should bring up their children, I will make them childless among men: but woe also to them when I depart from them.
13 Ephraim, as I saw, was like Tyre, founded in beauty: and Ephraim shall lead out his children to the slayer.
14 Give them, O Lord. What will you give them? Give them a childless womb, and dry breasts.
<margin>† 1 Samuel 8:5.</margin>
15 † All their wickednesses are in Gilgal <note>original: "Galgal"</note>, for there I held them in hatred: because of the malice of their inventions, I will cast them out of my house: I will no longer love them, for all their princes are rebels.
16 Ephraim is struck, their root is dried up: they shall yield no fruit. And even if they should give birth, I will kill the beloved offspring of their womb.
17 My God will cast them away, because they did not hear him: and they shall be wanderers among the nations.

<column-break/>

### C H A P T E R X.

->*On account of idolatry, Israel is handed over to the Assyrians: and when they are called back by the Lord to judgment, they continue to follow their own ways; all their fortifications shall be laid waste.*<-

1 **I**srael is a leafy vine, his fruit is matched to him: according to the multitude of his fruit, he has multiplied altars, according to the abundance of his land, he has overflowed with idols.
2 Their heart is divided, now they shall perish: he himself shall break down their idols, he shall lay waste their altars.
3 For now they shall say: We have no king: for we do not fear the Lord: and what will a king do for us?
4 You speak words of a useless vision, and you make a covenant: and judgment shall spring up like bitterness upon the furrows of the field.
5 The inhabitants of Samaria have worshipped the calves of Beth-aven <note>original: "Bethaven," meaning "House of Iniquity/Vanity," a derogatory name for Bethel</note>: for its people have mourned over it, and its temple-wardens have exulted over it in its glory, which has departed from it.
6 For indeed it was carried into Assyria: a gift for the avenging king: confusion shall seize Ephraim, and Israel shall be confounded in his own will.

*The Lord threatens a great affliction upon the nations, with which they afflicted his people; and that he will judge them all in the valley of Jehoshaphat: a fountain shall come forth from the house of the Lord, and Judah shall be inhabited forever, its blood having been cleansed.*

14 And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah: and it shall devour its palaces with shouting in the day of battle, and with a whirlwind in the day of commotion.
15 And Melchom <note>original: "Melchom," referring to Milcom or Molech, the national god of the Ammonites.</note> shall go into captivity: he himself, and his princes together, says the Lord.

### CHAPTER II.

*The vengeance of the Lord upon Moab, Judah, and Israel; and he threatens them with destruction, which they shall not be able to escape: because, having received benefits, they were always ungrateful, and cast away the law of God.*

1 Thus says the Lord: For three crimes of Moab, and for four, I will not convert him: because he burned the bones of the king of Edom even into ashes.
2 And I will send a fire into Moab, and it shall devour the houses of Kerioth: and Moab shall die with a noise, and with the sound of the trumpet.
3 And I will destroy the judge from the midst thereof, and will slay all his princes with him, says the Lord.
4 Thus says the Lord: For three crimes of Judah, and for four, I will not convert him: because he has cast away the law of the Lord, and has not kept his commandments: for their idols have deceived them, after which their fathers had gone.
5 And I will send a fire into Judah, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem.
6 Thus says the Lord: For three crimes of Israel, and for four, I will not convert him: because he has sold the just man for silver, and the poor man for a pair of shoes.
7 Who trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the earth, and turn aside the way of the humble: and a son and his father have gone to the same girl, to violate my holy name.
8 And they sat down upon pledged garments near every altar: and they drank the wine of the condemned in the house of their God.

Deuteronomy 2:24.

Deuteronomy 8:2.

9 † But I exterminated the Amorite from before them: whose height was like the height of cedars, and he was strong as an oak: and I crushed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.
10 † It is I who made you come up from the land of Egypt, and I led you in the desert forty years, that you might possess the land of the Amorite.

11 And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites <note>Nazarites were individuals consecrated to God by a vow, which included abstaining from wine and leaving their hair uncut.</note>: is it not even so, O children of Israel, says the Lord?
12 And you gave the Nazarites wine to drink: and commanded the prophets, saying: Prophesy not.
13 Behold, I will groan <note>original: "stridebo," referring to the creaking or groaning sound of a heavy load.</note> under you, as a wagon groans that is laden with hay.
14 And flight shall perish from the swift, and the strong shall not keep his strength, and the mighty shall not save his life:
15 And he that holds the bow shall not stand, and the swift of foot shall not be delivered, and the rider of the horse shall not save his life:
16 And the stout-hearted among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day, says the Lord.

## CHAPTER III.

*He reproves the house of Israel, once a uniquely chosen people, for various crimes: of which he says a few shall be saved from the coming affliction with which he threatens them.*

1 Hear this word that the Lord has spoken against you, O children of Israel: against the whole family which I brought up out of the Land of Egypt, saying:
2 You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will visit <note>In this context, "visit" means to inspect and punish for sins.</note> upon you all your iniquities.
3 Can two walk together, except they be agreed?
4 Will a lion roar in the forest, unless he has prey? will a young lion cry out of his den, if he has taken nothing?
5 Can a bird fall into a snare upon the earth where no fowler is? shall a snare be taken up from the earth before it has caught something?
6 Shall a trumpet be blown in a city, and the people not be afraid? shall there be evil <note>Here "evil" refers to calamity or disaster, not moral wickedness.</note> in a city, and the Lord has not done it?
7 For the Lord God does no word <note>original: "verbum," meaning a deed or a decree.</note>, unless he reveals his secret to his servants the prophets.
8 The lion shall roar, who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, who will not prophesy?
9 Publish it in the palaces of Ashdod <note>original: "Azoti," the Latin name for the Philistine city of Ashdod.</note>, and in the palaces of the Land of Egypt: and say: Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the many follies in the midst thereof, and those that suffer oppression in its inner chambers.
10 And they have not known how to do the right thing, says the Lord, laying up iniquity and robberies in their palaces.
11 Therefore thus says the Lord God: The land shall be distressed, and surrounded: and your strength shall be taken away from you, and your palaces shall be plundered.
12 Thus says the Lord: As if a shepherd should rescue out of the mouth of a lion two legs, or the tip of an ear: so shall the children of Israel be rescued, who dwell in Samaria in the corner of a bed, and on a couch in Damascus.
13 Hear, and testify in the house of Jacob, says the Lord God of hosts:
14 That in the day when I shall begin to visit the transgressions of Israel, I will visit upon him, and upon the altars of Bethel: and the horns of the altar <note>The "horns" were the four projections at the corners of the altar, considered the most sacred parts.</note> shall be cut off, and fall to the ground.
15 And I will strike the winter house with the summer house: and the houses of ivory shall perish, and many palaces shall be destroyed, says the Lord.

<column-break/>

## CHAPTER IV.

*He inveighs against the wicked leaders of Samaria under the figure of fat cows, mocking their idolatry: and because the children of Israel could not be called back from their sins by various scourges, the Lord threatens them with things similar to those they had suffered before, exhorting them to turn to the almighty God.*

1 Hear this word, you fat cows <note>A metaphor for the wealthy and self-indulgent elite who lived in luxury at the expense of the poor.</note> that are on the mountain of Samaria: you that oppress the needy, and crush the poor: that say to your masters: Bring, and we will drink.
2 The Lord God has sworn by his holiness: that behold the days shall come upon you, and they shall lift you up on poles, and your remains in boiling pots.
3 And you shall go out through the breaches, one over against another, and you shall be cast out into Armon, says the Lord.
4 Come to Bethel, and act impiously; to Gilgal, and multiply transgressions: and bring your victims in the morning, your tithes in three days.
5 And sacrifice a sacrifice of praise with leaven: and call for voluntary offerings, and announce them: for so you liked to do, O children of Israel, says the Lord God.
6 Wherefore I also have given you cleanness of teeth <note>A biblical idiom for famine or a total lack of food.</note> in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places: and you have not returned to me, says the Lord.
7 I also have withheld the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one part was rained upon, and the part whereupon I rained not, withered.
8 And two and three cities went to one city to drink water, and they were not satisfied: and you did not return to me, says the Lord.
<margin>† Haggai 2:18.</margin>
9 † I struck you with a scorching wind, and with mildew, the multitude of your gardens, and of your vineyards: your oliveyards and your fig-yards the caterpillar has eaten: and you did not return to me, says the Lord.
10 I sent death among you in the way of Egypt, I struck your young men with the sword, even to the captivity of your horses: and I made the stench of your camps to come up into your nostrils: and you did not return to me, says the Lord.
<margin>† Genesis 19:24.</margin>
11 I overthrew you † as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were as a firebrand snatched from the burning: and you did not return to me, says the Lord.
12 Therefore thus will I do to you, O Israel: and after I have done these things to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel.
13 For behold, he that forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares his word to man, who makes the morning mist, and walks upon the high places of the earth: The Lord God of hosts is his name.

### CHAPTER V.

->*The Prophet mourns the fall of Israel, calling them to seek the Lord so that they might escape the punishments due for their sins, for which there will be weeping everywhere: the Lord hates their feasts and sacrifices, and because of their idolatry, he threatens them with captivity.*<-

1 Hear this word which I take up against you as a lamentation: The house of Israel has fallen, and she shall rise no more.
2 The virgin of Israel is cast down upon her land, there is none to raise her up.
3 For thus says the Lord God: The city from which a thousand went out shall have a hundred left in it: and that from which a hundred went out shall have ten left in the house of Israel.
4 For thus says the Lord to the house of Israel: Seek me, and you shall live.
5 And seek not Bethel, and into Gilgal <note>original: "Galgalam"</note> enter not, and to Beersheba <note>original: "Bersabee"</note> you shall not pass: because Gilgal shall be led into captivity: and Bethel shall be useless <note>In Hebrew, this is a pun: Bethel, meaning "House of God," will become Beth-aven, or "House of Vanity/Nothingness."</note>.
6 Seek the Lord, and live: lest perhaps the house of Joseph be burnt with fire, and it shall devour, and there shall be none to quench Bethel.
7 You who turn judgment into wormwood <note>a plant known for its extreme bitterness, here symbolizing the corruption of justice into something poisonous</note>, and leave off justice in the earth.
<margin>† Below 9:6.</margin>
8 He that makes Arcturus and Orion <note>constellations used here to show God's power over creation</note>, and turns darkness into morning, and changes day into night: † who calls the waters of the sea, and pours them out upon the face of the earth: The Lord is his name.
9 Who smiles destruction upon the strong, and brings desolation upon the mighty.
10 They have hated him that rebukes in the gate <note>the city gate was the site of the local court</note>: and they have abhorred him that speaks perfectly.
<margin>† Zephaniah 1:13.</margin>
11 Therefore, because you robbed the poor, and took from him choice spoils: † you shall build houses of squared stone, and shall not dwell in them: you shall plant delightful vineyards, and shall not drink the wine of them.
12 For I know your many crimes, and your heavy sins: enemies of the just, taking bribes, and oppressing the poor in the gate:
13 Therefore the prudent man shall keep silence in that time, for it is an evil time.
14 Seek good, and not evil, that you may live: and the Lord the God of hosts will be with you, as you have said.
<margin>† Psalm 96:10. Romans 12:9.</margin>
15 † Hate evil, and love good, and establish judgment in the gate: if perhaps the Lord God of hosts may have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.
16 Therefore thus says the Lord God of hosts, the ruler: In all the streets there shall be wailing: and in all places that are outside, they shall say, woe, woe: and they shall call the farmer to mourning, and those that are skillful in lamentation to wailing.
17 And in all vineyards there shall be wailing: because I will pass through the midst of you, says the Lord.
<margin>† Jeremiah 30:7. Joel 2:11. Zephaniah 1:15. † Isaiah 1:11. Jeremiah 7:20. Malachi 1:12.</margin>
18 † Woe to them that desire the day of the Lord: to what end is it for you? this day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.
19 As if a man should flee from the face of a lion, and a bear should meet him: or should enter into the house, and lean with his hand upon the wall, and a serpent should bite him.
20 Shall not the day of the Lord be darkness, and not light: and obscurity, and no brightness in it?
21 † I hate, and have rejected your festivities: and I will not receive the odor <note>referring to the scent of burnt offerings</note> of your assemblies.

<column-break/>

22 But if you offer me holocausts <note>burnt offerings entirely consumed by fire</note>, and your gifts, I will not receive them: and I will not look upon the vows of your fat beasts.
23 Take away from me the noise of your songs: and I will not hear the canticles of your lyre.
24 And judgment shall be revealed as water, and justice as a mighty torrent.
<margin>† Acts 7:42.</margin>
25 † Did you offer victims and sacrifice to me in the desert for forty years, O house of Israel?
26 And you carried the tabernacle for your Moloch <note>a pagan deity associated with child sacrifice</note>, and the image of your idols, the star of your god, which you made for yourselves.
27 And I will cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus, says the Lord, the God of hosts is his name.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*The Lord threatens the proud, and those who live in luxury, with destruction and exile, together with the rest of the people of Israel, whose pride he detests.*<-

<margin>Luke 6:24.</margin>
1 Woe to you that are wealthy in Sion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria: the chief men, the heads of the peoples, who enter pompously into the house of Israel.
2 Pass over to Calneh <note>original: "Chalane"</note>, and see, and go from there to Hamath <note>original: "Emath"</note> the great: and go down to Geth of the Philistines, and to all the best kingdoms of these: if their border be larger than your border.
3 You that are separated for the evil day: and approach the throne of iniquity.
4 You that sleep upon beds of ivory, and are wanton on your couches: you that eat the lamb from the flock, and the calves from the midst of the herd.
5 You that sing to the sound of the psaltery <note>a stringed instrument similar to a harp</note>: they thought they had instruments of music like David.
6 Drinking wine in bowls, and anointed with the best ointments: and they felt nothing for the affliction of Joseph.
7 Wherefore now they shall go into captivity at the head of those that go into exile: and the faction of the wanton shall be taken away.
<margin>† Jeremiah 51:14.</margin>
8 † The Lord God has sworn by his own soul, says the Lord God of hosts: I detest the pride of Jacob, and I hate his houses, and I will deliver up the city with its inhabitants.
9 And if there remain ten men in one house, they also shall die.
10 And a man's kinsman shall take him up, and shall burn him, that he may carry the bones out of the house: and he shall say to him that is in the inner rooms of the house: Is there yet any with you?
11 And he shall answer: There is an end. And he shall say to him: Be silent, and remember not the name of the Lord.
12 For behold the Lord shall command, and shall strike the greater house with ruins, and the lesser house with clefts.
13 Can horses run upon rocks, or can it be plowed with wild oxen <note>original: "bubalis"</note>, since you have turned judgment into bitterness, and the fruit of justice into wormwood?
14 You that rejoice in nothing: you that say: Have we not taken horns <note>a common biblical symbol for strength or military power</note> to ourselves by our own strength?
15 For behold, I will raise up against you, O house of Israel, says the Lord God of hosts, a nation: and it shall crush you from the entrance of Hamath, even to the torrent of the desert.

### CHAPTER VII.

*The Prophet prays against the punishments he sees looming, and the Lord threatens captivity, which Amos prophesies under the parable of a mason's trowel <note>original: "trullæ cæmentarii." While many modern Bibles translate this as a "plumb line," the Latin text specifies a trowel used for spreading mortar.</note>, despite the opposition of Amaziah the priest of Bethel: who accuses Amos before the king of Israel, urging Amos to go and prophesy in the land of Judah: but he shows that he was made a prophet by the Lord to prophesy over Israel, and he foretells afflictions for both Amaziah and Israel.*

1 **T**hese things the Lord God showed to me: and behold, a maker of locusts <note>representing a plague of insects</note> appeared at the beginning of the shooting up of the late rain; and behold, the late rain came after the king's mowing.
2 And it came to pass, when they had finished eating the grass of the land, I said: O Lord God, be merciful, I beseech thee: who shall raise up Jacob, for he is small?
3 The Lord had pity regarding this; It shall not be, said the Lord.
4 These things the Lord God showed to me: and behold, the Lord God called for judgment by fire: and it devoured the great abyss, and consumed a portion of the land at the same time.
5 And I said: O Lord God, cease, I beseech thee: who shall raise up Jacob, for he is small?
6 The Lord had pity regarding this: This also shall not be, said the Lord God.
7 These things the Lord showed to me: and behold, the Lord was standing upon a plastered wall, and in his hand was a mason's trowel.
8 And the Lord said to me: What do you see, Amos? And I said: A mason's trowel. And the Lord said: Behold, I will set a trowel in the midst of my people Israel: I will no longer pass them by <note>meaning He will no longer overlook their sins</note>.
9 And the high places of the idol <note>referring to the illegitimate shrines</note> shall be demolished, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste: and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
10 And Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam the king of Israel, saying: Amos has rebelled against you in the midst of the house of Israel: the land is not able to bear all his words.
11 For thus Amos says: Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall be led away captive from their own land.
12 And Amaziah said to Amos: O seer, go, flee into the land of Judah: and eat bread there, and prophesy there.
13 But in Bethel you shall not prophesy anymore: because it is the king's sanctuary, and it is the house of the kingdom.
14 And Amos answered, and said to Amaziah: I am not a prophet, and I am not the son of a prophet: but I am a herdsman plucking sycamore figs <note>original: "vellicans sycomoros." This refers to the practice of piercing the fruit of the sycamore-fig tree to ensure it ripened properly.</note>.
15 And the Lord took me as I followed the flock: and the Lord said to me: Go, prophesy to my people Israel.
16 And now hear the word of the Lord: You say: You shall not prophesy against Israel, and you shall not drop your word against the house of the idol.
17 Therefore thus says the Lord: Your wife shall be a harlot in the city, and your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, and your land shall be measured out with a line: and you shall die in a polluted land, and Israel shall be led away captive out of their own land.

<column-break/>

### CHAPTER VIII.

*Amos, under the parable of a fruit hook <note>original: "uncinus pomorum." Often interpreted as a basket of summer fruit.</note>, prophesies that the end of the kingdom of Israel is near, because of the oppression of the poor: he explains the bitterness of the looming calamity: and says their festivals will be turned into mourning, and denounces a future famine of the word of God.*

1 **T**hese things the Lord God showed to me: and behold, a hook for fruit.
2 And he said: What do you see, Amos? And I said: A hook for fruit. And the Lord said to me: The end has come upon my people Israel: I will no longer pass them by.
3 And the hinges of the temple shall creak in that day, says the Lord God: many shall die: silence shall be cast in every place.
4 Hear this, you that crush the poor, and make the needy of the land to fail,
5 Saying: When will the month <note>referring to the New Moon festival</note> pass, that we may sell our wares; and the sabbath, that we may open the wheat: that we may diminish the measure, and increase the shekel <note>the weight of the silver required</note>, and use deceitful scales,
6 That we may possess the needy for silver and the poor for a pair of shoes, and sell even the refuse of the wheat.
7 The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob: If I ever forget all their works.
8 Shall not the land tremble because of this, and everyone mourn that dwells in it: and it shall rise up like a river, and be cast out, and flow away like the river of Egypt?
9 And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord God: the sun shall go down at midday, and I will make the earth dark in the day of light:
<margin>
† Tobit 2:6.
1 Maccabees 1:41.
</margin>
10 † And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation: and I will bring sackcloth upon every back of yours, and baldness upon every head: and I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and the end thereof like a bitter day.
11 Behold, the days come, says the Lord: and I will send a famine into the land: not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the word of the Lord.
12 And they shall be moved from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east: they shall go about seeking the word of the Lord, and shall not find it.
13 In that day the beautiful virgins and the young men shall faint for thirst:
14 They that swear by the sin of Samaria, and say: Your god lives, O Dan, and the way of Beersheba <note>original: "Bar-sabee"</note> lives: and they shall fall, and shall rise no more.

Referring to the lintel or capital of a column.</note>, and let the doorposts be moved: for greed is in the head of them all, and I will kill the last of them with the sword: there shall be no flight for them: they shall flee, and he that flees shall not be saved.

2 † If they go down even into hell <note>original: "infernum," the grave or the underworld</note>, from there my hand shall bring them out: and if they climb up to heaven, from there I will bring them down.

# THE PROPHECY OF OBADIAH.

### THE ONLY CHAPTER.

->He prophesies destruction against the Edomites, who afflicted and mocked the children of Israel: who, nevertheless, being restored, shall receive dominion over those who afflicted them.<-

<margin>† Jeremiah 49:14.</margin>
<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial V containing a scene of a figure, likely the prophet Obadiah, in a room.</image-desc>
1 **T**he Vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord God to Edom <note>Edom refers to the nation descended from Esau, Jacob's brother</note>: † We have heard a report from the Lord, and he has sent an envoy to the nations: Arise, and let us rise up against him in battle.
2 Behold, I have made you small among the nations: you are greatly despised.
3 The pride of your heart has lifted you up, you who dwell in the clefts of the rocks, setting your throne on high; you who say in your heart: Who shall bring me down to the ground?
4 Though you be exalted as the eagle, and though you set your nest among the stars: from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.
5 If thieves had come into you, if robbers by night, how would you have been silent? Would they not have stolen only what was enough for them? If the grape-gatherers had come into you, would they not at least have left a cluster for you?

# THE PROPHECY OF JONAH.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*Jonah is sent by the Lord to preach in Nineveh, but he flees by ship toward Tarshish away from the face of the Lord. The Lord sends a storm upon the ship, and after lots are cast, Jonah is discovered and thrown into the sea, causing the storm to cease.*

1 And the word of the Lord came to Jonah the son of Amittai <note>original: "Amathi"</note>, saying:
2 Arise, and go to Nineveh, the great city, and preach in it: for its wickedness has ascended before me.
3 And Jonah rose up to flee to Tarshish <note>likely a port in Spain, representing the furthest possible point from where he was sent</note> from the face of the Lord, and he went down to Joppa, and found a ship going to Tarshish: and he paid the fare for it, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish away from the face of the Lord.
4 But the Lord sent a great wind into the sea: and a great tempest was made in the sea, and the ship was in danger of being broken to pieces.
5 And the sailors were afraid, and the men cried out to their god: and they threw the cargo <note>original: "vasa," literally vessels or equipment</note> that was in the ship into the sea to lighten it; but Jonah had gone down into the inner parts of the ship, and was sleeping in a heavy slumber.
6 And the shipmaster came to him, and said to him: Why are you weighed down by sleep? Rise, call upon your God, if perhaps God will think of us, and we may not perish.
7 And each man said to his companion: Come, let us cast lots, so that we may know why this evil is upon us. And they cast lots: and the lot fell upon Jonah.
8 And they said to him: Tell us for whose sake this evil is upon us: what is your work? What is your land, and where are you going? Or from what people are you?
9 And he said to them: I am a Hebrew, and I fear the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.
10 And the men were struck with a great fear, and said to him: Why have you done this? (For the men knew that he was fleeing from the face of the Lord, because he had told them.)
11 And they said to him: What shall we do to you, so that the sea may be calm for us? For the sea was surging and swelling.
12 And he said to them: Take me up, and throw me into the sea, and the sea shall be calm for you: for I know that it is because of me that this great tempest has come upon you.
13 And the men rowed hard to return to the dry land, but they were not able: because the sea surged and swelled against them.
14 And they cried to the Lord, and said: We beseech you, O Lord, let us not perish for the life of this man, and do not lay innocent blood upon us: for you, O Lord, have done as it pleased you.
15 And they took Jonah, and threw him into the sea: and the sea ceased from its raging.
16 And the men feared the Lord with a great fear, and offered sacrifices to the Lord, and made vows.

## CHAPTER II.

*The Prophet, recounting the manifold injustice and other sins of his people, predicts that vengeance and captivity are imminent for them; and mourning because of this, he announces the future gathering of the remnant.*

**1** Woe to you who devise useless things and work evil in your beds: in the morning light they carry it out, because their hand is against God.
**2** And they have coveted fields and taken them by force, and snatched away houses: and they oppressed the man and his house, the man and his inheritance.
**3** Therefore, thus says the Lord: Behold, I am planning an evil against this family: from which you shall not remove your necks, and you shall not walk proudly, because it is a most wicked time.
**4** In that day a parable shall be taken up against you, and a song shall be sung with sweetness, of those saying: We are wasted with devastation: the portion of my people is changed: how shall he depart from me, when he returns, he who would divide our regions?
**5** For this reason, you shall have no one to cast a cord for a lot <note>A "cord for a lot" refers to the ancient practice of measuring out land portions for inheritance.</note> in the assembly of the Lord.
**6** Do not speak, you who speak: It shall not drop <note>original: "stillabit" — a prophetic term for "preaching" or "dropping" divine words like rain</note> upon these, confusion shall not take hold.
**7** The house of Jacob says: Has the spirit of the Lord been shortened, or are such his thoughts? Are not my words good with him who walks uprightly?
**8** And on the contrary, my people have risen up as an adversary: you have taken away the cloak from off the tunic: and those who were passing by in simplicity, you turned into war.
**9** You have cast out the women of my people from the house of their delights: from their little ones you have taken away my praise forever.
**10** Arise and go, you who have no rest here: because of its uncleanness, it shall be corrupted with a most foul rot.
**11** Would that I were not a man having the spirit, and that I would rather speak a lie: I will "drop" to you in wine and in drunkenness: and it shall be this people upon whom it is "dropped." <note>Micah uses "dropping" (preaching) ironically here, suggesting the people only want prophets who "drop" talk of wine and luxury.</note>
**12** In gathering, I will gather all of you, O Jacob: I will bring the remnant of Israel together, I will set them together like a flock in the fold, like cattle in the midst of the pens; they shall make a noise by reason of the multitude of men.
**13** For he who opens the way <note>original: "pandens iter"</note> shall ascend before them: they shall divide and pass through the gate, and enter by it: and their king shall pass before them, and the Lord at their head.

## CHAPTER III.

*On account of the sins of the princes, judges, false prophets, and priests of the people of Israel, the Lord threatens a heavy vengeance and the destruction of Jerusalem.*

**1** And I said: Hear, you princes of Jacob, and you leaders of the house of Israel: Is it not your place to know judgment?
**2** You who hate the good and love the evil: who violently strip their skins from off them, and their flesh from off their bones?

<column-break/>

**3** Who have eaten the flesh of my people, and flayed their skin from off them: and have broken their bones, and chopped them as if for a kettle, and like meat in the middle of a pot.
**4** Then they shall cry to the Lord and he will not hear them: and he will hide his face from them at that time, just as they have acted wickedly in their own inventions.
**5** Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray: who bite with their teeth and preach peace: and if anyone does not give something into their mouths, they declare a holy war against him.
**6** Therefore, night shall be to you instead of a vision, and darkness to you instead of divination: and the sun shall set upon the prophets, and the day shall be darkened over them.
**7** And they who see visions shall be confounded, and the diviners shall be put to shame: and they shall all cover their faces, because there is no answer from God.
**8** But truly, I am filled with the strength of the spirit of the Lord, with judgment, and with power: to announce to Jacob his wickedness, and to Israel his sin.
**9** Hear this, you princes of the house of Jacob, and you judges of the house of Israel: you who abominate judgment, and pervert all straight things.
**10** You who build Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.
<margin>
† Ezekiel 22:27.
Zephaniah 3:3.
</margin>
**11** Its princes judged for bribes, and its priests taught for a price, and its prophets divined for money: and they leaned upon the Lord, saying: Is not the Lord in our midst? No evil shall come upon us.
<margin>
† Jeremiah 26:18.
</margin>
**12** Because of this, on account of you, † Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall be like a heap of stones, and the mountain of the temple like the high places of the forests.

### CHAPTER VI.

->The Lord disputes with the ungrateful, recounting the benefits bestowed upon them, indicating also what is good, and what the Lord requires from his people: but on account of injustice and other crimes of the children of Israel, the Lord threatens them with various afflictions.<-

**1** Hear what the Lord says: Arise, contend in judgment against the mountains: and let the hills hear your voice.

**9** The voice of the Lord cries to the city, and salvation shall be for those fearing your name: Hear, O tribes, and who will approve it?
**10** Is there yet fire in the house of the wicked, treasures of iniquity, and a small measure full of wrath?

### CHAPTER VII.

*The Prophet mourns that so few remain who are not wicked: he shows that trust is to be placed in no man, but in God the Savior alone: who will have mercy on Zion: and having put her enemies to shame, he will lead her back to himself, fulfilling the promises made to the fathers.*

**1** Woe to me, for I have become like one who gathers the grape-clusters of the vintage in autumn: there is no cluster to eat, my soul has desired the early-ripe figs.
**2** The holy man has perished from the earth, and there is none upright among men: they all lie in wait for blood, every man hunts his brother to death.
**3** The evil of their hands they call good: the prince demands, and the judge is for pay: and the great man has spoken the desire of his soul, and they have troubled it.
**4** He who is best among them is like a <term>paliurus</term> <note>original: "paliurus" — a species of prickly shrub or thorn-bush</note>: and he who is upright is like a thorn from a hedge. The day of your watchmen, your visitation comes: now shall be their ruin.
**5** Do not believe a friend: and do not trust in a leader: from her who sleeps in your bosom, keep the doors of your mouth.
<margin>† Matthew 10:35. † Matthew 10:36.</margin>
**6** † For the son dishonors the father, and the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law: † and a man’s enemies are those of his own household.
**7** But I will look to the Lord, I will wait for God my Savior: my God will hear me.
**8** Do not rejoice over me, my enemy, because I have fallen: I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light.
**9** I will bear the anger of the Lord, because I have sinned against him, until he judges my cause, and carries out

my judgment: he will lead me out into the light, I shall see his justice.
**10** And my enemy shall look on, and she who says to me: "Where is the Lord your God?" shall be covered with shame. My eyes shall behold her: now she shall be trodden down like the mud of the streets.
**11** The day comes that your walls may be built: in that day the law shall be far removed.
**12** In that day they shall come even to you from Assyria, and even to the fortified cities: and from the fortified cities even to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
**13** And the land shall be a desolation because of its inhabitants, and because of the fruit of their thoughts.

**16** The nations shall see, and shall be confounded in all their strength: they shall lay their hand upon their mouth, their ears shall be deaf.

<meta>This page continues the prophetic books of the Old Testament. ->THE PROPHECY OF NAHUM.<-

### CHAPTER II.

> *The siege of Nineveh and its plunder by the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans, along with the Medes, were the historical conquerors of the Assyrian capital in 612 BCE.</note>, because she acted proudly against the people of the Lord.*

**1** He who scatters has come up before your face, he who keeps the siege: watch the way, fortify your loins, strengthen your power greatly.
**2** For the Lord has restored the pride of Jacob, like the pride of Israel: because the spoilers have laid them waste, and have ruined their branches.
**3** The shield of his mighty men is fiery, the men of the army are in scarlet: the reins of the chariot are like fire in the day of his preparation, and the drivers are dazed.
**4** They are thrown into confusion in the journeys: the chariots collide in the streets: their appearance is like lamps, like lightning running to and fro.
**5** He will remember his strong men, they shall stumble in their paths: they shall quickly ascend its walls, and a <term>protective covering</term> <note>original: "umbraculum" — a defensive screen or shed used by besiegers to protect themselves from missiles while attacking a wall</note> shall be prepared.
**6** The gates of the rivers are opened, and the temple is razed to the ground.
**7** And the soldier is led away captive: and her handmaids moaned, groaning like doves, murmuring in their hearts.
**8** And Nineveh is like a pool of water; but they have fled: "Stand, stand!" and there is none who returns.
**9** Plunder the silver, plunder the gold: and there is no end to the riches from all the desirable vessels.
**10** She is laid waste, and torn, and mangled: and the heart melts, and the knees tremble, and there is weakness in all the loins: and the faces of them all are like the blackness of a pot.
**11** Where is the dwelling of the lions, and the pastures of the lion cubs, to which the lion went to enter therein, the lion's cub, and there was none to make them afraid?
**12** The lion took enough for his cubs, and killed for his lionesses: and he filled his dens with prey, and his lair with rapine.
**13** Behold, I am against you, says the Lord of hosts, and I will burn your chariots even unto smoke, and the sword shall devour your young lions: and I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers shall no longer be heard.

### CHAPTER III.

> *Nineveh, the city of blood, is predicted to be laid waste under the name of an adulteress: which is confirmed by the example of Alexandria <note>The Latin text uses "Alexandria," though modern scholars identify the city intended as No-Amon (Thebes) in Egypt.</note> devastated by the Babylonians: nor will there be anyone to grieve for Nineveh, or to comfort her over her own destruction.*

<margin>Zechariah 4:9. Habakkuk 2:2.</margin>
**1** Woe to the city of blood, all full of lies and tearing apart: rapine shall not depart from you.

<column-break/>

**2** The sound of the whip, and the sound of the rushing wheel, and of the neighing horse, and of the burning chariot, and of the horseman charging:
**3** And of the flashing sword, and the glittering spear, and of a multitude slain, and of a heavy ruin: neither is there an end of corpses, and they shall fall down upon their bodies.
**4** Because of the multitude of the fornications of the beautiful and graceful harlot, who possesses sorceries, who sold nations in her fornications, and families in her sorceries:
<margin>Isaiah 47:3.</margin>
**5** Behold, I am against you, says the Lord of hosts, and I will reveal your shame in your face, and I will show your nakedness to the nations, and your disgrace to the kingdoms.
**6** And I will cast abominations upon you, and I will treat you with insults, and I will set you as an example.
**7** And it shall be: everyone who sees you will shrink back from you, and shall say: "Nineveh is laid waste: who will shake his head over you? Where shall I seek a comforter for you?"
**8** Are you better than Alexandria <note>original: "Alexandria populorum" — a reference to the Egyptian city of Thebes (No-Amon), which was thought to be as impregnable as Nineveh.</note> of the peoples, that dwells in the rivers? Water is round about it: whose riches is the sea, and the waters are its walls.
**9** Ethiopia was her strength, and Egypt, and there is no end: Africa and the Libyans were your helpers.
**10** But she also was led away into exile into captivity: her little ones were dashed to pieces at the head of every street, and they cast lots for her famous men, and all her nobles were bound in fetters.
**11** And you therefore shall be drunken, and shall be despised: and you shall seek help from the enemy.
**12** All your strongholds are like fig trees with their early figs: if they are shaken, they shall fall into the mouth of the eater.
**13** Behold, your people are women in your midst: the gates of your land shall be opened wide to your enemies, fire shall devour your bars.
**14** Draw water for yourself for the siege, build up your strongholds: go into the mud, and tread it, and hold fast the brick-mold.
**15** There the fire shall devour you: you shall perish by the sword, it shall devour you like the <term>bruchus</term> <note>original: "bruchus" — a species of locust, often referring to the larva or a wingless developmental stage.</note>: gather together like the <term>bruchus</term>, multiply like the locust.
**16** You have made your merchants more numerous than the stars of heaven: the <term>bruchus</term> has spread himself out, and has flown away.
**17** Your guards are like locusts: and your little ones are like the locusts of locusts, which settle in the hedges in the cold day: the sun has risen, and they have flown away, and the place where they were is not known.
**18** Your shepherds have slumbered, O king of Assyria: your princes shall be buried: your people have hidden in the mountains, and there is none to gather them.
**19** Your destruction is not hidden, your wound is most grievous: all who have heard the report of you, have clapped their hands over you: for upon whom has your malice not passed continually?

<meta>This page transitions from the conclusion of the Prophecy of Nahum to the beginning of the Prophecy of Habakkuk. While Nahum celebrated the fall of Nineveh, Habakkuk grapples with the rising power of the Babylonians (Chaldeans) and the problem of why a holy God allows the wicked to oppress the righteous.</meta>

->THE PROPHECY OF HABAKKUK.<-

## CHAPTER ONE.

*The Prophet wonders why the wicked man prospers and prevails against the just; for the Lord raises up the Chaldeans against the Jews, who attribute their victory not to the Lord, but to their own idol.*

1 <image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'O' inside a square frame featuring floral patterns and scrolls.</image-desc> The <term>burden</term> <note>original: "Onus" — in prophetic literature, this refers to a heavy message or a solemn oracle of judgment</note> which Habakkuk the Prophet saw.
2 How long, O Lord, shall I cry out and You will not hear? Shall I cry out to You while suffering violence, and You will not save?
3 Why have You shown me iniquity and labor, to see plunder and injustice against me? Judgment has been made, and contradiction is more powerful.
4 Because of this, the law is torn apart, and judgment does not reach its end: because the wicked prevail against the just, therefore perverted judgment goes forth.
<margin>† Acts 13:41.</margin>
5 † Look among the nations, and see: admire, and be astonished: for a work is done in your days which no one will believe when it is told.

8 Its horses are lighter than leopards and swifter than evening wolves; and its horsemen shall be spread abroad: for its horsemen shall come from afar, they shall fly like an eagle hastening to eat.
9 They shall all come for the prey, their faces are like a burning wind: and they shall gather captives like the sand.
10 And they shall triumph over kings, and tyrants shall be their laughingstock: they shall laugh at every fortress, and shall heap up a mound and take it.
11 Then their spirit shall be changed, and they shall pass over and fall: this is the strength of their god.

13 Your eyes are pure, so that You may not see evil, and You cannot look upon iniquity: why do You look upon those who act iniquitously, and remain silent while the wicked devours one more just than himself?
14 And You will make men like the fish of the sea, and like crawling things that have no ruler:
15 They have lifted up everything with a hook, dragged it in their dragnet, and gathered it into their net. Over this they shall rejoice and exult.
16 Therefore they will offer victims to their dragnet and sacrifice to their net: because through them their portion is made fat, and their food choice.
17 Therefore, then, they spread their dragnet, and will not spare to continually slay the nations.

## CHAPTER II.

*The Prophet exhorts the people to turn back to God before the Lord’s wrath comes upon them, and all the meek of the earth to seek the Lord: announcing that destruction hangs over the Philistines, Moabites, Ammonites, Ethiopians, and Assyrians.*

1 Assemble yourselves, be gathered together, O nation not worthy to be loved:
2 Before the decree brings forth the day that passes like dust, before the fierce anger of the Lord comes upon you, before the day of the Lord’s indignation comes upon you.
3 Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth, who have wrought His judgment: seek the just, seek the meek: if by any means you may be hidden in the day of the Lord’s anger.
4 For Gaza shall be destroyed, and Ashkelon shall be a desert, they shall cast out Ashdod at noon-day, and Ekron shall be rooted up.
5 Woe to you who inhabit the seacoast <note>original: "funiculum maris" — literally "the cord of the sea," referring to the allotted territory or border along the Mediterranean.</note>, a nation of destroyers: the word of the Lord is against you, O Canaan, the land of the Philistines, and I will destroy you, so that there shall be no inhabitant.
6 And the seacoast shall be a resting place for shepherds, and folds for cattle:
7 And it shall be the portion of him that shall remain of the house of Judah: there they shall feed, in the houses of Ashkelon they shall rest in the evening: because the Lord their God will visit them, and will turn away their captivity.
8 I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the blasphemies of the children of Ammon: with which they have reproached my people, and have magnified themselves against their borders.
9 Therefore as I live, says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, the dryness of thorns, and heaps of salt, and a desert even for ever: the residue of my people shall plunder them, and the remnant of my nation shall possess them.
10 This shall befall them for their pride: because they have blasphemed, and have magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts.

<margin>† Isaiah 34:11</margin>

15 This is the glorious city that dwelt in confidence: that said in her heart: I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desert, a place for beasts to lie down in? every one that passes by her shall hiss, and wag his hand.

# THE PROPHECY OF HAGGAI

### CHAPTER ONE

*The time when Haggai prophesied: he rebukes the Jews because, while neglecting the house of God, they cared for their own buildings: for which cause he says a barrenness was sent upon them by God: and at that time the governor Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest, together with the people, being stirred up, begin to build the house of God.*

<margin>Ezra 1:1</margin>

### C A P U T III.

5 And he said: Put a clean turban <note>original: "cidarim"—a ritual head-covering or mitre</note> upon his head. And they put a clean turban upon his head, and clothed him with garments: and the Angel of the Lord stood by.

10 In that day, says the Lord of hosts, every man shall call his friend under the vine, and under the fig tree.

10 For who has despised the days of small things? And they shall rejoice, and shall see the tin stone <note>A plumb line used for measuring during construction</note> in the hand of Zerubbabel. These are the seven eyes of the Lord, which run to and fro through the whole earth.
11 And I answered, and said to him: what are these two olive trees, to the right of the lampstand, and to its left?
12 And I answered a second time, and said to him: What are the two branches of the olive trees, which are next to the two golden pipes, in which are the golden funnels?
13 And he spoke to me, saying: Do you not know what these are? And I said: No, my lord.
14 And he said: These are the two sons of oil <note>original: "filii olei"—the "anointed ones," referring to the royal leader Zerubbabel and the priestly leader Joshua</note>, who stand before the Ruler of the whole earth.

### CHAPTER V.

->*A flying scroll, by which the wicked shall be judged: a woman sitting in an amphora with a mass of lead, and two winged women lifting her into the air.*<-
And I turned, and lifted up my eyes: and I saw, and behold, a flying scroll.
2 And he said to me: What do you see? And I said: I see a flying scroll: its length is twenty cubits, and its width is ten cubits.
3 And he said to me: This is the curse that goes out over the face of the whole earth: for every thief, as it is written there, shall be judged: and every one who swears falsely <note>taking a false oath in God's name</note> shall likewise be judged by it.
4 I will bring it forth, says the Lord of hosts, and it shall come to the house of the thief, and to the house of him who swears falsely by my name: and it shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it, both its timber and its stones.
5 And the Angel who spoke in me went out: and he said to me: Lift up your eyes, and see what this is that goes out.
6 And I said: What is it? And he said: This is an amphora <note>original: "amphora"—the Latin translates the Hebrew "ephah," a large grain-measuring jar</note> going out. And he said: This is their eye <note>Symbolizing their appearance or their iniquity</note> in all the earth.
7 And behold, a lead talent was being carried, and behold, one woman sitting in the middle of the amphora.
8 And he said: This is wickedness. And he threw her into the middle of the amphora, and cast the mass of lead into its mouth.
9 And I lifted up my eyes, and saw: and behold, two women coming out, and the spirit was in their wings, and they had wings like the wings of a kite: and they lifted up the amphora between the earth and the heaven.
10 And I said to the Angel who spoke in me: Where are these carrying the amphora?
11 And he said to me: That a house may be built for it in the land of Shinar <note>The region of Babylon</note>: and it shall be established, and set there upon its own base.

And I turned, and lifted up my eyes, and saw: and behold, four chariots coming out from between two mountains: and the mountains were mountains of bronze.

### C A P U T VIII.

*Just as the Lord afflicted his people because of their sins and made Jerusalem desolate, so now he causes it to be greatly inhabited and will give all prosperity, provided they serve him; to whom other nations shall be joined: concerning the hem of a Jew's garment being grasped by ten men of the Gentiles.*

1 And the word of the Lord of hosts came, saying:
2 Thus says the Lord of hosts: "I have been jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and with great indignation I have been jealous for her."
3 Thus says the Lord of hosts: "I have returned to Zion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem: and Jerusalem shall be called the City of Truth, and the Mountain of the Lord of hosts, the Sanctified Mountain."
4 Thus says the Lord of hosts: "Old men and old women shall yet sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of their great age.
5 And the streets of the city shall be filled with boys and girls, playing in its streets."
6 Thus says the Lord of hosts: "If it seems difficult in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, shall it also be difficult in my eyes? says the Lord of hosts."

### CHAPTER IX.

*He prophesies against the cities of Syria and the proud Philistines: Christ the King will come to Zion sitting upon the foal of a donkey, and having abolished war, He will rule the world in great peace; He also released the captives from the pit by the blood of His covenant: all things are said to be prosperous for the people of God, because He Himself will protect them.*

1 The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach <note>Hadrach was a region in northern Syria, near Damascus</note>, and Damascus shall be its resting place: for the eye of man, and of all the tribes of Israel, is toward the Lord.
2 Hamath also shall be in its borders, and Tyre, and Sidon: for they have taken to themselves great wisdom.
3 And Tyre built her own fortification, and heaped up silver like the dust, and gold like the mud of the streets.
4 Behold, the Lord shall possess her, and shall strike her strength in the sea, and she shall be devoured by fire.
5 Ashkelon shall see it, and shall fear; and Gaza, and shall be very sorrowful; and Ekron, because her hope is put to shame: and the king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall not be inhabited.
6 And a divider shall sit in Ashdod, and I will destroy the pride of the Philistines.
7 And I will take away his blood from his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth, and even he shall be left for our God, and he shall be like a leader in Judah, and Ekron shall be like a Jebusite <note>The Jebusites were the original inhabitants of Jerusalem who were eventually absorbed into Israel</note>.
8 And I will encompass my house with those who serve me in war, going and returning, and the oppressor <note>original: "exactor"—a tax-gatherer or slave-driver</note> shall no longer pass over them: for now I have seen with my own eyes.
