### CHAPTER XI.

*After the death of Alexander and likewise of Ptolemy—who had invaded Alexander's kingdom by deceit, having taken his daughter away from him and given her in marriage to Demetrius—this Demetrius honors Jonathan with letters of immunity and tributes. Jonathan, however, sends him auxiliary soldiers who, having killed a hundred thousand in one day, delivered the king from the citizens of Antioch and set fire to Antioch. But when the king broke the treaty made with Jonathan, Antiochus, the son of Alexander, having defeated Demetrius and reigning, makes a treaty with Jonathan, who with his brother Simon often emerges victorious against the foreigners.*

AND the king of Egypt gathered an army as numerous as the sand which is by the seashore, and many ships: and he sought to obtain Alexander's kingdom by deceit and to add it to his own kingdom.
2 And he went into Syria with peaceful words, and they opened the cities to him and met him: because King Alexander had commanded them to go out to meet him, since he was his father-in-law.
3 But when Ptolemy entered a city, he placed a garrison of soldiers in every city.
4 And as he approached Azotus, they showed him the temple of Dagon burned with fire, and Azotus and its surroundings demolished, and the bodies cast out, and the mounds of those who had been slain in the war, which they had made by the wayside.
5 And they told the king that Jonathan had done these things, in order to make him hated: and the king remained silent.
6 And Jonathan met the king at Joppa with glory, and they greeted one another: and they slept there.
7 And Jonathan went with the king as far as the river called Eleutherus: and he returned to Jerusalem.
8 But King Ptolemy obtained dominion over the cities as far as Seleucia by the sea, and he planned evil designs against Alexander.
9 And he sent messengers to Demetrius, saying: "COME, let us make a treaty between us, and I will give you my daughter, whom Alexander has, and you shall reign in the kingdom of your father."

2 He also sent letters to the Spartans and to other places according to the same form.
3 They went to Rome, entered the senate chamber, and said: "Jonathan the High Priest and the Jewish nation have sent us to renew friendship and alliance as it was before."
4 And the Romans gave them letters to the governors of various places, so that they might lead them back to the land of Judah in peace.

6 "JONATHAN the High Priest, and the elders of the nation, and the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people, to their brothers the Spartans, greetings.
7 Long ago, letters were sent to Onias the High Priest from Arius, who was then reigning among you, stating that you are our brothers, as the copy below contains.
8 Onias received the man who had been sent with honor, and accepted the letters, in which the alliance and friendship were clearly stated.
9 Although we have no need of these things—having for our comfort the Holy Books <note>original: "sanctos libros"; referring to the Hebrew Scriptures</note> which are in our hands—
10 we preferred to send word to you to renew our brotherhood and friendship, lest we should become strangers to you; for much time has passed since you last sent word to us.
11 We, therefore, at all times without ceasing, on our festival days and other appropriate days, remember you in the sacrifices we offer and in our prayers, as it is right and fitting to remember brothers.
12 We rejoice, therefore, in your glory.
13 But as for us, many troubles and many wars have surrounded us, and the kings around us have attacked us.
14 We did not wish to be a burden to you, or to our other allies and friends, during these wars.
15 For we have had help from heaven, and we have been delivered, and our enemies have been brought low.
16 Therefore, we have chosen Numenius the son of Antiochus and Antipater the son of Jason, and have sent them to the Romans to renew our former friendship and alliance.
17 We have also commanded them to come to you and greet you, and to deliver our letters to you concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.
18 And now, you will do well to send us a reply regarding these matters."

20 Arius, king of the Spartans, to Onias the high priest, greetings.

25 And he went out from Jerusalem and met them in the region of Amathis <note>The region of Hamath in Syria</note>; for he did not give them the opportunity to enter his own territory.
26 And he sent scouts into their camp; and they returned and reported that they were planning to come upon them by night.
27 But when the sun had set, Jonathan commanded his men to keep watch and to be ready in arms for battle the whole night, and he placed guards all around the camp.
28 And the adversaries heard that Jonathan and his men were prepared for war; and they were afraid and trembled in their hearts, and they lit fires in their camp <note>To hide their retreat by making it look like the camp was still occupied</note>.
29 Jonathan, however, and those who were with him, did not know this until morning; for they saw the lights burning.
30 And Jonathan pursued them, but did not overtake them; for they had crossed the river Eleutherus.

53 And all the nations that were around them sought to crush them; for they said:
54 "They have no leader or helper; now therefore let us fight against them, and let us blot out the memory of them from among men."

# CHAPTER XIII.

> *After Simon took up the leadership in place of his brother Jonathan, he sent the requested money to Tryphon, along with the sons of Jonathan, for his ransom; Tryphon, however, having received the money, killed the brother along with his sons; after they were buried and mourned, Simon magnificently built a tomb for his parents and brothers in Modein; Tryphon, having killed Antiochus, invaded his kingdom; and Simon, having obtained letters of treaty and immunity from King Demetrius, captured Gezer and gained the citadel of Jerusalem; because of this, they celebrate a joyful feast, which is commanded to be held annually among the Jews.*

54 And Simon saw his son John, that he was a valiant man of war; and he made him commander of all the forces; and he lived in Gazara.

# THE FIRST BOOK OF MACCABEES.

### CHAPTER XIV.

*Demetrius is defeated and captured by the general of Arsaces; Simon and his people enjoy a great peace. Letters are sent to him from the Spartans and Romans renewing their treaty, offering high praise for Simon, who had sent a golden shield of one thousand minas to the Romans.*

**I**n the one hundred and seventy-second year <note>140 BCE</note>, King Demetrius <note>Demetrius II Nicator</note> gathered his army and marched into Media to secure reinforcements for himself so that he might fight against Tryphon.
2 And Arsaces <note>Mithridates I, King of the Parthians and Medes</note>, the king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius had entered his borders, and he sent one of his princes to capture him alive and bring him to him.
3 And he went and struck the camp of Demetrius; he captured him, led him to Arsaces, and placed him in custody.
4 And the whole land of Judah was quiet all the days of Simon, and he sought the good of his nation; and his authority and his glory pleased them all his days.
5 And with all his glory, he took Joppa for a port, and made it an entrance to the islands of the sea.
6 He enlarged the borders of his nation and took possession of the region.
7 He gathered many captives and gained dominion over Gazara, Beth-zur, and the Citadel <note>The Acra, the Greek fortress in Jerusalem</note>; he removed the impurities from it, and there was no one who could resist him.
8 And every man cultivated his own land in peace; and the land of Judah gave its fruits, and the trees of the fields their fruit.
9 The elders all sat in the streets and discussed the good things of the land, and the young men clothed themselves in glory and the robes of war.
10 He distributed provisions to the cities and established them as fortified strongholds, until the fame of his glory was spoken of to the ends of the earth.
11 He made peace upon the land, and Israel rejoiced with great joy.
12 And every man sat under his vine and under his fig tree <note>A biblical expression signifying a time of ultimate safety and prosperity</note>, and there was no one to make them afraid.
13 There was no one left to fight them on the earth; kings were crushed in those days.
14 And he strengthened all the humble of his people; he sought out the Law and removed every wicked and evil person.
15 He glorified the sanctuary and multiplied the vessels of the holy things.
16 And it was heard in Rome that Jonathan was dead, and even as far as the Spartans, and they were very grieved.
17 But when they heard that Simon his brother had been made high priest in his place, and that he held the entire region and the cities within it,
18 They wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew the friendship and alliance they had made with Judas and Jonathan, his brothers.
19 And these were read in the presence of the assembly in Jerusalem. And this is the copy of the letters which the Spartans sent:
20 **T**HE rulers and the cities of the SPARTANS, to Simon the high priest, and the elders, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews, our brothers: greetings.
21 The ambassadors who were sent to our people have reported to us concerning your glory, honor, and joy; and we rejoiced at their arrival.

<column-break/>

23 And it pleased the people to receive the men honorably, and to place a copy of their words in the public records of the people, so that it might be a memorial for the Spartan people. Moreover, we have written a copy of these things to Simon the high priest.
24 After this, Simon sent Numenius to Rome, carrying a large golden shield weighing one thousand minas <note>Approximately 1,250 lbs or 570 kg of gold</note>, to establish an alliance with them. When the Roman people heard
25 These words, they said: "What thanks shall we give to Simon and his sons?
26 For he has restored his brothers, and has driven the enemies of Israel away from them." And they established liberty for him and recorded it on bronze tablets, and placed them on pillars on Mount Zion.
27 And this is a copy of the writing: ON the eighteenth day of the month Elul <note>Late summer, roughly August/September</note>, in the one hundred and seventy-second year, being the third year under Simon the high priest in Asaramel <note>Possibly a title meaning "Prince of the People of God"</note>,
28 In the great assembly of the priests, and the people, and the princes of the nation, and the elders of the region, these things were made known: Since wars have frequently broken out in our region,
29 Simon the son of Mattathias, of the sons of Jarib, and his brothers, put themselves in danger and resisted the adversaries of their nation, so that their sanctuary and the Law might stand; and they glorified their nation with great glory.
30 Jonathan gathered his nation together and became their high priest, and was joined to his people.
31 And their enemies wanted to trample and crush their region, and to stretch out their hands against their sanctuary.
32 Then Simon resisted and fought for his nation; he spent much of his own money, armed the men of valor of his nation, and gave them wages.
33 He fortified the cities of Judea, and Beth-zur, which was on the borders of Judea, where the weapons of the enemies were formerly kept; and he placed a garrison of Jewish men there.
34 And he fortified Joppa, which was by the sea, and Gazara, which is on the borders of Azotus, where the enemies formerly lived; and he settled Jews there, and placed in them everything suitable for their repair.
35 And the people saw the actions of Simon and the glory he intended to bring to his nation, and they appointed him their leader and high priest, because he had done all these things, and because of the justice and faith which he preserved for his nation, and because he sought in every way to exalt his people.
36 And in his days, prosperity was achieved by his hands, so that the Gentiles were removed from their region, including those in the City of David in Jerusalem, in the Citadel, from which they used to go out and contaminate everything around the holy places, dealing a great blow to purity.
37 And he settled Jewish men in it for the protection of the region and the city, and he raised the walls of Jerusalem.

### C H A P T E R XV.

*Antiochus, son of Demetrius, sends letters of friendship to Simon. The Romans recommend the Jews, as their allies, to other nations by letter. While Antiochus pursues Tryphon, he refuses the military aid sent by Simon and sends Athenobius to him, who demands many things as if they were debts. Having received Simon’s response, he appoints Cendebeus as commander of the army against him, while he himself pursues Tryphon.*

1 And King Antiochus <note>Antiochus VII Sidetes</note>, son of Demetrius, sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon the priest and prince of the Jewish nation, and to the whole nation;
2 and they were to this effect: **KING** Antiochus to Simon, the High Priest, and to the Jewish nation, greetings.
3 Since certain troublemakers <note>original: "pestilentes"</note> have seized the kingdom of our fathers, I intend to reclaim the kingdom and restore it as it was before; and I have raised a great multitude of soldiers and prepared ships of war.
4 I intend to march through the country so that I may take revenge on those who have ruined our country and who have laid waste many cities in my kingdom.
5 Now therefore, I confirm to you all the tax exemptions which all the kings before me granted you, and whatever other gifts they remitted to you.
6 I also permit you to strike your own coinage for your country;
7 and let Jerusalem be holy and free. All the weapons you have prepared and the strongholds you have built and which you hold shall remain yours.

<column-break/>

<margin>x</margin> 8 And every debt to the king, and those that shall be due to the king, from this time and for all time, are remitted to you.
9 When we have obtained our kingdom, we will glorify you, and your nation, and the Temple with great glory, so that your fame may be made manifest in all the earth.
10 In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year <note>138 BCE</note>, Antiochus went into the land of his fathers, and all the armies came together to him, so that few were left with Tryphon.
11 And King Antiochus pursued him, and he came to Dor <note>a coastal fortress city south of Mount Carmel</note>, fleeing by the sea-coast.
<margin>x</margin> 12 For he knew that evils were gathering against him, and the army had deserted him.
13 And Antiochus encamped against Dor with one hundred and twenty thousand men of war and eight thousand cavalry.
14 And he surrounded the city, and ships approached from the sea; they harassed the city from land and sea, and permitted no one to enter or leave.
15 Then Numenius and those who were with him arrived from the city of Rome, having letters written to kings and countries, in which these things were contained:
16 **LUCIUS** <note>likely Lucius Caecilius Metellus Calvus</note>, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy <note>Ptolemy VIII Physcon of Egypt</note>, greetings.
17 The ambassadors of the Jews, our friends, have come to us to renew the old friendship and alliance, being sent by Simon the prince of the priests and the Jewish people.
<margin>18</margin> 18 They also brought a golden shield of one thousand minas <note>a "mina" was a unit of weight; this shield was exceptionally heavy and valuable, intended as a diplomatic gift</note>.
19 It has therefore pleased us to write to the kings and countries, that they should not do them any harm, nor fight against them, their cities, or their countries, and that they should not give aid to those who fight against them.
<margin>20</margin> 20 And it seemed good to us to accept the shield from them.
21 If, therefore, any troublemakers have fled from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the High Priest, so that he may punish them according to his law.
22 These same things were written to King Demetrius, to Attalus, to Ariarathes, and to Arsaces,
23 and to all the countries: to Lampsacus, to the Spartans, and to Delos, and to Myndus, and to Sicyon, and to Caria, and to Samos, and to Pamphylia, and to Lycia, and to Halicarnassus, and to Cos, and to Side, and to Aradus, and to Rhodes, and to Phaselis, and to Gortyna, and Cnidus, and Cyprus, and Cyrene.
24 And they wrote a copy of these things to Simon the High Priest and to the Jewish people.
25 But King Antiochus besieged Dor for a second time, constantly bringing up his forces and making siege engines; and he shut Tryphon in so that he could not get out.
26 And Simon sent to him two thousand chosen men as reinforcements, and silver, and gold, and many vessels;
27 but he would not receive them, but broke all the agreements he had made with him before, and distanced himself from him.
28 And he sent to him Athenobius, one of his friends, to negotiate with him, saying: "You hold Joppa and Gazara, and the Citadel that is in Jerusalem—cities of my kingdom.
29 You have laid waste their borders and have caused great havoc in the land, and have seized dominion over many places in my kingdom.
30 Now therefore, give up the cities which you have occupied..."

41 He stationed cavalry and an army there so that they might go out and patrol the roads of Judea, just as the king had commanded him.

### CHAPTER XVI.

> *The aged Simon sends his army with his sons Judas and John against Cendebaeus. After this is settled, Ptolemy, Simon’s son-in-law, inflamed by the ambition to rule, receives his father-in-law and his sons Mattathias and Judas at a banquet and kills them by treachery to seize the provinces of Judea. Furthermore, the messengers he sent to kill John by treachery are themselves killed by him, and John succeeds his father in the high priesthood.*

1 Then John <note>John Hyrcanus I, who would become one of the most powerful Hasmonean rulers.</note> went up from Gazara and told Simon his father what Cendebaeus was doing to their people.
2 Simon called his two eldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them: "I, and my brothers, and my father's house, have fought the enemies of Israel from our youth until this day; and it has prospered in our hands to rescue Israel many times.
3 But now I have grown old; you, however, be in my place and in my brothers' place, and go out and fight for our nation. May help from heaven be with you."
4 So he chose twenty thousand fighting men and cavalry from the region; they marched against Cendebaeus and stayed the night in Modin.

<column-break/>

5 They rose early in the morning and went into the plain; and behold, a massive army of infantry and cavalry was coming to meet them, and there was a rushing stream between them.
6 John and his people moved their camp opposite them. He saw that the people were afraid to cross the stream, so he crossed over first; when the men saw him, they crossed after him.
7 He divided the people, placing the cavalry in the middle of the infantry; for the enemy's cavalry was very numerous.
8 Then they sounded the sacred trumpets, and Cendebaeus and his army were put to flight; many of them fell wounded, and the survivors fled into the stronghold.
9 At that time, Judas, John's brother, was wounded; but John pursued them until he came to Cedron, which Cendebaeus had built.
10 They fled as far as the towers in the fields of Azotus <note>The ancient Philistine city of Ashdod.</note>, and he burned them with fire. Two thousand of their men fell, and John returned to Judea in peace.
11 Now Ptolemy, the son of Abobus, had been appointed commander in the plain of Jericho, and he had much silver and gold.
12 For he was the son-in-law of the High Priest.
13 But his heart was lifted up with pride, and he wanted to take over the region; so he plotted treachery against Simon and his sons to eliminate them.
14 Now Simon was visiting the cities in the region of Judea and taking care of them. He went down to Jericho with his sons Mattathias and Judas in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year <note>134 BCE</note>, in the eleventh month; this is the month of <term>Shebat</term><note>original: "Sabath"; the eleventh month of the Hebrew calendar, occurring around January/February.</note>.
15 The son of Abobus received them deceitfully into a small fortress called Doch, which he had built. He gave them a great banquet but hid men there.
16 When Simon and his sons had drunk freely, Ptolemy and his men rose up, took their weapons, rushed into the banquet hall, and killed him, his two sons, and some of his servants.
17 Thus he committed a great act of treachery in Israel and returned evil for good.
18 Ptolemy wrote these things down and sent them to the king, asking him to send an army to help him and to hand over the region, their cities, and the tributes to him.
19 He sent others to Gazara to kill John; and he sent letters to the military officers, inviting them to come to him so that he might give them silver, gold, and gifts.
20 He sent others to occupy Jerusalem and the temple mount.
21 But someone ran ahead and told John in Gazara that his father and brothers had perished, and said: "He has sent men to kill you too."
22 When he heard this, he was greatly alarmed. He seized the men who had come to destroy him and killed them; for he knew that they were seeking to destroy him.
23 As for the rest of the acts of John, and his wars, and the brave deeds he performed, and the building of the walls he constructed, and his other achievements—
24 behold, these are written in the book of the days of his priesthood, from the time he was made High Priest after his father.

It marks the transition of power to Simon's son, John Hyrcanus I.</summary>

### CHAPTER ONE

*The Jews living in Jerusalem write to the Jews in Egypt, reporting the death of Antiochus and his followers which occurred in Persia; they give thanks to God and urge them to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles and the Day of the Given Fire following the return from captivity. The history of these events and the prayer of Nehemiah are related here.*

1 **T**O THE brothers, the Jews throughout Egypt: the brothers who are in Jerusalem and in the region of Judea send greetings and good peace.
2 May God do good to you and remember His covenant which He spoke to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, His faithful servants.
3 May He give all of you a heart to worship Him and to do His will with a great heart and a willing spirit.
4 May He open your heart to His law and His commandments, and bring peace.
5 May He hear your prayers and be reconciled to you, and not desert you in the time of evil.
6 And now, we are here praying for you.
7 During the reign of Demetrios, in the one hundred and sixty-ninth year, <note>Roughly 143 BCE in the Seleucid calendar.</note> we Jews wrote to you during the tribulation and the violence that came upon us in those years, from the time Jason deserted the holy land and the kingdom.
8 They burned the gate and shed innocent blood; but we prayed to the Lord and were heard. We offered a sacrifice and fine flour, we lit the lamps, and we set out the loaves.
9 And now, observe the days of the Feast of Tabernacles <note>original: *scenopegiæ*, the Jewish festival of Sukkot, often called the Feast of Booths.</note> in the month of Kislev. <note>original: *Casleu*, the ninth month of the Hebrew calendar, falling in November or December.</note>
10 In the one hundred and eighty-eighth year, <note>Roughly 124 BCE.</note> the people who are in Jerusalem and in Judea, and the Senate, and Judas, to Aristobulus—the teacher of King Ptolemy, who is of the lineage of the anointed priests—and to the Jews who are in Egypt: greetings and good health.
11 Having been delivered by God from great dangers, we give Him great thanks, as we have fought against such a king.
12 For He Himself drove out of Persia those who fought against us and the holy city.
13 For when the leader himself was in Persia with a vast army, he fell in the temple of Nanea, <note>A Babylonian and Persian goddess often identified with Artemis or Aphrodite.</note> deceived by the trickery of Nanea’s priests.
14 For Antiochus and his friends came to the place as if to marry her, and to take her great wealth under the name of a dowry.
15 When the priests of Nanea had set the riches out, and he had entered the enclosure of the temple with a few men, they closed the temple
16 once Antiochus had entered. Opening a hidden entrance in the ceiling, they threw stones and struck down the leader and those who were with him. They

<column-break/>

cut them limb from limb, and cutting off their heads, they threw them outside.
17 Blessed be God in all things, who delivered up the impious.
18 Since we are about to celebrate the purification of the temple on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Kislev, we thought it necessary to notify you, so that you also may observe the Feast of Tabernacles and the Day of the Fire, which was given when Nehemiah offered sacrifices after the temple and the altar were rebuilt.
19 For when our fathers were being led away into Persia, the priests who were then worshippers of God took the fire from the altar and hid it secretly in a valley where there was a deep, dry pit; and there they kept it safe, so that the place was unknown to anyone.
20 But when many years had passed, and it pleased God that Nehemiah should be sent by the king of Persia, he sent the grandsons of those priests who had hidden the fire to look for it. As they told us, they did not find fire, but thick water. <note>original: *aquam crassam*. This substance, which ignited miraculously, is often interpreted as naphtha or petroleum.</note>
21 He ordered them to draw it up and bring it to him. Then the priest Nehemiah ordered the sacrifices that had been laid out to be sprinkled with that water—both the wood and the things laid upon it.
22 When this was done and the time came for the sun to shine (which previously had been hidden by clouds), a great fire was kindled, so that everyone wondered.
23 Meanwhile, all the priests made a prayer while the sacrifice was being consumed; Jonathan began it, and the others responded.
24 And the prayer of Nehemiah was in this manner: "O LORD God, Creator of all things, terrible and strong, just and merciful, who alone are the good King,
25 alone gracious, alone just, and almighty, and eternal; who deliver Israel from every evil, who chose the fathers and sanctified them:
26 Accept the sacrifice for all Your people Israel, and guard Your portion, and sanctify it.
27 Gather our dispersed people, deliver those who are enslaved to the Gentiles, and look upon those who are despised and abominable, so that the Gentiles may know that You are our God.
28 Punish those who oppress us and treat us with contempt in their pride.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 30:3, 5. See below, 2:18.</margin>
29 Establish Your people in Your holy place, † as Moses said."
30 Then the priests sang hymns until the sacrifice was consumed.
31 When the sacrifice was finished, Nehemiah ordered the remaining water to be poured over the larger stones.
32 When this was done, a flame was kindled from them, but it was consumed by the light that shone from the altar.
33 When the matter became known, it was reported to the king of the Persians that in the place where the priests who were exiled had hidden the fire, water had appeared, with which Nehemiah and his companions had purified the sacrifices.
34 After considering the matter diligently, the king...

### C H A P T E R II.

*Jeremiah, during the Babylonian captivity, entrusts the sacred fire and the Law of God to those being exiled. On the mountain which Moses climbed to see the promised land, Jeremiah hides the tabernacle, the ark, and the altar of incense, intended to remain there until the people’s return from the Babylonian captivity. Certain deeds of Moses and Solomon are touched upon here; as well as the deeds of Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, which are condensed from five volumes by Jason of Cyrene into this single book.*

1 It is found in the records of the prophet Jeremiah that he commanded those who were being deported to take some of the fire, as has been described and as he commanded those in exile.
2 And he gave them the Law so they would not forget the Lord's precepts, and that they would not stray in their minds when seeing the idols of gold and silver and their ornaments.
3 Saying other things of this kind, he exhorted them not to remove the Law from their hearts.
4 It was also in that same writing how the prophet, by a divine revelation made to him, commanded that the tabernacle and the ark should accompany him until
<margin>† Deuteronomy 34:1.</margin>
he went out to the mountain where Moses had ascended and saw God’s inheritance.
5 And when Jeremiah arrived there, he found a cave-like place; and he brought the tabernacle, the ark, and the altar of incense into it, and blocked the entrance.
6 Some of those who followed him came up to mark the spot for themselves, but they could not find it.
7 When Jeremiah learned of this, he rebuked them, saying: "The place shall remain unknown until God gathers the congregation of the people together and becomes merciful."
8 "Then the Lord will show these things, and the majesty of the Lord shall appear, and there shall be a cloud, just as 
<margin>† 1 Kings 8:11; 2 Chronicles 6:14.</margin>
it was manifested to Moses, and as when Solomon asked that the place be sanctified for the great God, He manifested these things."
9 For he [Solomon] magnificently displayed wisdom; and as one possessing wisdom, he offered the sacrifice of the dedication and the completion of the temple.
<margin>† Leviticus 9:24. † 2 Chronicles 7:1.</margin>
10 Just as Moses prayed to the Lord and fire descended from heaven and consumed the holocaust, so also Solomon prayed, and fire descended from heaven and consumed the holocaust.
<margin>† Leviticus 10:16–17.</margin>
11 And Moses said, "Because the sin offering was not eaten, it was consumed."
12 Similarly, Solomon celebrated the dedication for eight days.
13 These same things were also set down in the records and memoirs of Nehemiah: and how, by constructing a library, he gathered books from various regions—the books of the Prophets, and of David, and the letters of the kings, and concerning votive offerings.
14 In like manner, Judas [Maccabeus] also gathered all those books which had been scattered because of the war that happened to us, and they are now with us.
15 If, therefore, you desire these books, send messengers who may carry them to you.

<column-break/>

16 Since we are about to celebrate the purification <note>referring to the rededication of the Temple, or Hanukkah</note>, we have written to you: you will do well, therefore, if you observe these days.
17 It is God who liberated His people and restored the inheritance to everyone, along with the kingdom, the priesthood, and the sanctuary,
<margin>† Deuteronomy 30:3–5; Above, 1:29.</margin>
18 as He promised in the Law. We hope that He will soon have mercy on us and gather us from under the heavens into the holy place.
19 For He has rescued us from great perils and has cleansed the place.
20 Now, concerning Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, the purification of the great temple, and the dedication of the altar;
21 and also the battles concerning Antiochus the Illustrious <note>Antiochus IV Epiphanes</note> and his son Eupator;
22 and the heavenly apparitions shown to those who acted bravely for the Jews, so that, although they were few, they vindicated the whole region and put the barbarian multitude to flight;
23 and they recovered the temple, famous throughout the whole world, liberated the city, and restored the laws which had been abolished, the Lord being merciful and gracious to them:
24 all these things, which were comprised in five books by Jason of Cyrene, we have attempted to condense into a single volume.
25 For considering the vast number of books and the difficulty for those wishing to engage with historical narratives due to the sheer volume of material,
26 we have taken care to provide pleasure for those who wish to read, and to make it easier for the studious to commit the events to memory, so that all who read might find utility.
27 And for us indeed, who have undertaken this work of condensing for the sake of brevity, it was no easy labor, but rather a task full of sleepless nights and sweat—
28 just as those who prepare a banquet and seek to satisfy the will of others for the sake of many people's gratitude, we willingly undergo this labor.
29 We leave the matter of accuracy regarding every detail to the original authors, while we strive to follow the rules of brevity.
30 For just as the architect of a new house must care for the entire structure, while the one who takes care of the painting must seek out what is fit for decoration, so it must be judged in our case.
31 Indeed, to collect insights, to organize the discourse, and to examine every single part with curiosity is the duty of a history's original author;
32 but to pursue brevity of speech and to avoid long executions of events should be granted to the one who summarizes.
33 From here, then, we shall begin the narrative; let it suffice to have said this much in the preface. For it is foolish to overflow before the history begins, but to be cut short in the history itself.

He is later freed through the sacrifice and prayers of the high priest Onias, and after giving thanks to God and Onias, he tells the king and all others of God's great works.*

### CHAPTER XII.

*He excuses the disciples plucking ears of grain on the Sabbath, and also heals a withered hand on the Sabbath: quietly withdrawing from the plotting of the Pharisees and commanding the various people he healed to remain silent, he fulfills the prophecy of Isaiah; having healed a possessed man who was blind and mute, he proves the Pharisees are speaking falsely when they blasphemously claim he casts out demons by <term>Beelzebub</term>; he speaks of the unpardonable blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, and that an account must be given for every idle word: then to the Scribes and Pharisees seeking a sign, he says the sign of Jonah shall be given: and who are his true mother and brothers.*

<margin>† 1 Samuel 21:4.</margin>

4 How he entered into the house of God and ate the <term>bread of presence</term> <note>original: *panes propositionis*; also known as showbread, these were twelve loaves set out in the Temple as an offering, reserved only for priests.</note>, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, but for the priests alone?
<margin>† Leviticus 24:9. † Numbers 28:9.</margin>
5 Or have you not read in the law, † that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple violate the Sabbath and are without guilt?
6 But I tell you, that something greater than the temple is here.
<margin>† 1 Samuel 15:22. Ecclesiastes 4:17. Hosea 6:6.</margin>
7 But if you knew what this means: † I desire mercy, and not sacrifice: you would never have condemned the innocent.
8 For the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.

### CHAPTER XIII.

*Sitting in a small boat, he presents to the crowds the parables of the sower and of the weeds: which he also interprets for the disciples: likewise the parables concerning the grain of mustard seed, the leaven hidden in the flour, the treasure and the pearl that were found: and the net cast into the sea, which parable he also explains: teaching in his own country, he says that a prophet is not without honor except in his own country.*

1 On that day, Jesus, going out of the house, sat by the sea.

8 But others fell upon good ground, and they yielded fruit: some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold.

### C H A P T E R XV.

*The traditions of the Pharisees concerning the washing of hands and other matters, which they placed before the commandments of God: and what things truly defile a man: the Canaanite woman, through persevering faith and supplication, obtains the healing of her daughter: Jesus, having healed various infirmities near the Sea of Galilee, satisfies four thousand men with seven loaves and a few small fish, with seven baskets of remains being taken up.*

### C H A P T E R  X V I I.

*The transfiguration of Christ on the mountain, which he commands the disciples to keep in silence, until he rises from the dead: he says that Elijah is to come, indeed that he has already come, but was not recognized, namely John the Baptist: he heals the lunatic boy, whom the disciples could not heal because of their little faith: showing how great is the power of faith similar to a grain of mustard seed, fasting, and prayer: he foretells his passion: he also pays the didrachma <note>A silver coin equal to two drachmas, the amount of the annual Temple tax.</note> for himself and Peter, having found a stater <note>A silver coin equal to four drachmas.</note> in the mouth of a fish.*

<margin>Mark 9:1.</margin> <margin>Luke 8:28.</margin>
1 **And** after six days Jesus took Peter, and James, and John his brother, and led them up into a high mountain by themselves:
2 And he was transfigured before them. And his face shone like the sun: and his garments became white as snow.
3 And behold, there appeared to them Moses and Elijah talking with him.
4 Then Peter answering, said to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here: if you will, let us make here three tabernacles <note>Temporary shelters or booths used during the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles.</note>, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
<margin>† Above 3:17.</margin> <margin>2 Peter 1:17.</margin>
5 While he was yet speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them. † And behold, a voice out of the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear him.
6 And the disciples hearing it, fell upon their face, and were very much afraid.
7 And Jesus came and touched them: and said to them: Arise, and do not be afraid.
8 And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one, except Jesus alone.
9 And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying: Tell the vision to no one, until the Son of Man rises from the dead.

### CHAPTER XVIII.

*With a little child set before them, he teaches who is greater in the kingdom of heaven, and how one must beware of causing the little ones to stumble: how a brother sinning against us ought to be corrected, and if he does not listen to the church, he should be treated as a <term>heathen and a tax collector <note>original: "ethnicus & publicanus." ### CHAPTER XX.

*He proposes a parable about the laborers hired into the vineyard, to the last of whom is given the same denarius as to the first: Jesus predicts his passion and resurrection to the disciples; and on the occasion of the ambition of the sons of Zebedee, he teaches the disciples that they ought to be greater not by power and the display of dominion, but by the duty of ministry: and as he departs from Jericho, he gives sight to two blind men.*

## CHAPTER XXV.

->*He proposes parables concerning the ten virgins, and the talents distributed to the servants, whose lord, returning from a journey, rewards or punishes each according to their merits: he sets the final judgment before their eyes, and the reasons for the rewarding of the good and the punishment of the evil.*<-

1 Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins: who, taking their lamps, went out to meet the bridegroom and the bride.
2 Now five of them were foolish, and five were wise:
3 But the five foolish ones, having taken their lamps, did not take oil with them:
4 Whereas the wise ones took oil in their vessels along with the lamps.
5 But as the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and slept.
6 But at midnight a cry was made: "Behold, the bridegroom is coming, go out to meet him."
7 Then all those virgins rose up and trimmed their lamps.
8 And the foolish said to the wise: "Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out."
9 The wise answered, saying: "Lest there perhaps not be enough for us and for you, go instead to those who sell, and buy for yourselves."
10 But while they went to buy, the bridegroom came: and those who were ready entered with him into the wedding, and the door was shut.
11 Finally the remaining virgins also came, saying: "Lord, Lord, open to us."
12 But he answering said: "Truly I say to you, I do not know you."

17 Likewise, he who had received two gained another two.
18 But he who had received one, going away, dug in the earth and hid his lord's money.

20 And he who had received five talents, coming forward, offered another five talents, saying: "Lord, you delivered five talents to me; behold, I have gained another five on top of them."

# C H A P T E R XXVII.

*Judas, having returned the silver pieces, hangs himself by a noose: Jesus, accused before Pilate, does not answer: Pilate's wife calls him a just man: Barabbas, however, is preferred: Pilate, having washed his hands, delivers Jesus to be scourged and crucified: who, having been mocked in many ways by the soldiers, is led to be crucified: and having drunk wine mixed with gall, is crucified between thieves, his garments being divided: blasphemies are cast at him by many different people: darkness arises, and Jesus, crying out "Eli," and having received a drink, expires with a cry, and various signs occur: the body of Jesus, buried by Joseph, is guarded by soldiers.*

Now when morning was come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, that they might put him to death.

<margin>† Acts 1:18.</margin>

### C H A P T E R XXVIII.

> *An earthquake having occurred and the guards having been terrified, an Angel tells the women of the resurrection of Christ; who, appearing to them, commands (as the Angel also had commanded) that they tell the disciples they will see the Lord in Galilee: the soldiers guarding the tomb, corrupted by money, say the body of Christ was taken by theft: the disciples, seeing the Lord in Galilee, are commanded to go and teach and baptize all nations.*

1 <margin>Mark 16:1. John 20:11.</margin> Now late on the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the sepulcher.
2 And behold, there was a great earthquake: for an Angel of the Lord descended from heaven: and drawing near, he rolled back the stone and sat upon it.
3 His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was like snow.
4 And for fear of him, the guards were terrified and became like dead men.
5 But the Angel answered and said to the women: "Do not be afraid; for I know that you seek Jesus, who was crucified.
6 He is not here: for he has risen, as he said. Come and see the place where the Lord was laid.
7 And going quickly, tell his disciples that he has risen: and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him: behold, I have told you."
8 And they went out quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, running to tell his disciples.
9 And behold, Jesus met them, saying: "Greetings." <note>original: "Avete." This was a common Latin greeting, here translating the Greek salutation "Chaire."</note> And they came near and took hold of his feet and adored him.
10 Then Jesus said to them: "Do not be afraid: go, tell my brothers to go into Galilee, and there they shall see me."
11 When they had gone, behold, some of the guards came into the city and reported to the chief priests all the things that had happened.
12 And when they had assembled with the elders and taken counsel, they gave a large sum of money to the soldiers,
13 Saying: "Say that his disciples came by night and stole him away while we were sleeping.
14 And if this is heard by the governor, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble."
15 So they took the money and did as they were instructed. And this story has been spread among the Jews even to this day.
16 But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had directed them.
17 And seeing him, they adored him; but some doubted.
18 And Jesus, drawing near, spoke to them, saying: "All power has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
19 <margin>† Mark 16:15.</margin> † Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit:
20 Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age."

->THE HOLY<-
# GOSPEL OF JESUS CHRIST
->ACCORDING TO MARK.<-

->CHAPTER ONE.<-

John preaches in the austerity of life and baptizes with water; but Christ indeed with the Holy Spirit. Christ, having been baptized by John and dwelling with wild beasts in the desert, is tempted by Satan after a fast of forty days. After John is handed over <note>original: "tradito"; referring to John the Baptist's arrest</note>, Jesus begins to preach in Galilee. Having called Simon and Andrew, and James and John the sons of Zebedee, He enters Capernaum and other places in Galilee; there, while preaching, He heals the mother-in-law of Simon and a leper, whom He sends to the priests, as well as many who were demon-possessed or ill, to the great amazement of all.

### CHAPTER II.

While the Scribes murmur because he forgives the sins of a paralytic, he heals him, bidding him to carry his bed; he calls Levi while dining with many tax collectors; he gives a reason, when the Pharisees murmur, as to why he associates with sinners and why his disciples do not fast, whom he also excuses for plucking ears of grain on the Sabbath.

<margin>Matthew 9:1.</margin>
1. And again he entered Capernaum after some days,
2. And it was heard that he was in the house, and many gathered, so that there was no room even at the door; and he spoke the word to them.
<margin>† Luke 5:18.</margin>
3. And they came to him, bringing a paralytic, who was carried by four men.
4. And when they could not bring him to him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was; and making an opening, they let down the bed <note>original: "grabatum"; a simple pallet or cot</note> in which the paralytic lay.
5. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic: "Son, your sins are forgiven you."
6. But some of the Scribes were sitting there, thinking in their hearts:
7. "Why does this man speak this way? He blasphemes: † Who can forgive sins, but God alone?"
<margin>† Job 14:4. Isaiah 44:25.</margin>
8. Immediately Jesus, knowing in his spirit that they were thinking these things within themselves, said to them: "Why do you think these things in your hearts?
9. Which is easier, to say to the paralytic: 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say: 'Rise, take up your bed, and walk'?
10. But so that you may know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins," (he said to the paralytic)
11. "I say to you: Rise, take up your bed, and go into your house."
12. And immediately he rose; and, having taken up the bed, he went out in the sight of all, so that everyone wondered and honored God, saying: "We have never seen anything like this."
13. And he went out again to the sea; and the whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
<margin>† Matthew 9:9. Luke 5:27.</margin>
14. And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus <note>Traditionally identified as the Apostle Matthew</note> sitting at the tax office <note>original: "telonium"; a place for collecting tolls or taxes</note>, and said to him: "Follow me." And rising up, he followed him.
15. And it happened, as he sat at meat in his house, many tax collectors <note>original: "publicani"; individuals contracted by the Roman state to collect taxes, often loathed by the public</note> and sinners sat down together with Jesus and his disciples; for there were many who followed him.
16. And the Scribes and Pharisees, seeing that he ate with tax collectors and sinners, said to his disciples: "Why does your teacher eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
17. Having heard this, Jesus said to them: "Those who are healthy have no need

of a physician, but those † who are ill: † for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners."

20. † But the days will come when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then they shall fast in those days.
<margin>† Matthew 9:15. Luke 5:35.</margin>
21. No one sews a patch of raw cloth onto an old garment; otherwise, the new patch pulls away from the old, and a greater tear is made.
22. And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise, the wine will burst the skins, and the wine will be spilled, and the skins will be lost; but new wine must be put into new wineskins."
23. † And it happened again, when the Lord was walking through the grainfields on the Sabbath, that his disciples began to go along and pluck ears of grain.

25. And he said to them: † "Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry, he and those who were with him?

27. And he said to them: "The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
28. Therefore the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."

### CHAPTER III.

After he had healed the withered hand, the Pharisees with the Herodians took counsel on what to do against him as people confessed to him, whose infirmities he heals; he sends the twelve chosen by him (who are listed here) to preach, having given them power over infirmities and demons; he convicts the Scribes of falsehood who blasphemously said he casts out demons by Beelzebub, speaking of the unpardonable blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, and who are his mother and brothers.

### CHAPTER VI.

*They marvel at the teaching of Christ in his own country; where, however, because of their unbelief, he performed few miracles: sending the Apostles to preach, he instructs them on what they should observe: Herod, hearing the fame of Christ, says that John the Baptist has risen again; whose head he had delivered to the dancing daughter of Herodias because of an oath: in the desert he satisfies five thousand men with five loaves and two fish: walking upon the sea, he calms the storm: in the land of Gennesaret he heals many by the touch of the hem of his garment.*

### C H A P T E R VII.

->*The Pharisees are rebuked, having accused the disciples of Christ for eating with unwashed hands, while they themselves transgressed the commandments of God for the sake of their own traditions; declaring what things can defile a man, namely those which come out of the heart: he delivers the daughter of the Syrophoenician woman from a demon due to her persistent plea: and he heals a man who was deaf and mute.*<-

<margin>Matt. 15:2</margin>
And the Pharisees and some of the Scribes, coming from Jerusalem, gathered together before him.

2 † And when they had seen some of his disciples eating bread with common hands, that is, unwashed, they found fault.

3 For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, do not eat unless they wash their hands frequently, holding to the tradition of the elders:

4 And coming from the market, unless they wash <note>original: "baptizentur"; literally "baptized" or ritually immersed.</note>, they do not eat: and there are many other things which have been handed down to them to observe, the washings of cups, and of pitchers, and of bronze vessels, and of beds:

<margin>Isaiah 29:13</margin>
6 But answering, he said to them: "Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written: † This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

7 But in vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines and precepts of men.

8 For leaving aside the commandment of God, you hold the tradition of men, the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other things similar to these."

9 And he said to them: "Well do you make void the commandment of God, so that you may keep your own tradition.

<margin>Exod. 20:12 Deut. 5:16 Ephes. 6:2</margin>

<margin>Matt. 15:10</margin>

### CHAPTER VIII.

*With seven loaves and a few small fish, he satisfies four thousand people: he commands the disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees: he heals a blind man gradually: when the Apostles are asked who they say Jesus is, Peter confesses that he is the Christ: and shortly after, Peter is called Satan by him because he rebuked him while he predicted his own passion: regarding taking up the cross, and that nothing should be dearer than the soul.*

<margin>Matth. 15:32</margin>
1 IN those days, when there was again a great multitude and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples together and said to them:
2 "I have compassion on the crowd, because behold, they have now stayed with me for three days and have nothing to eat:
3 And if I send them away fasting to their own home, they will faint on the way: for some of them have come from far away."

### CHAPTER XII.
<-

*He tells a parable about a vineyard leased to farmers, who killed the servants and the son of the master of the house: he is tested by the Pharisees regarding the payment of taxes to Caesar, and by the Sadducees regarding the resurrection: he is questioned by a Scribe about the first commandment: he himself asks how the scribes say that Christ is the son of David, teaching that they should be avoided: he praises a widow for the two mites put into the treasury.*

<margin>
Isaiah 5:1.
Jeremiah 2:21. &
Matthew 21:33.
Luke 20:9.
</margin>
**A**nd he began to speak to them in parables: A man planted a vineyard, and put a hedge around it, and dug a pit for the winepress, and built a tower, and leased it to farmers, and went on a journey into a far country.
2 And at the season he sent a servant to the farmers, so that he might receive from the farmers some of the fruit of the vineyard.
3 Who, having seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
4 And again he sent to them another servant: and him they wounded in the head, and treated shamefully.
5 And again he sent another, and him they killed: and many others: beating some, and killing others.
6 Therefore, having yet one son, most dear to him: he also sent him to them last of all, saying: They will respect my son.
7 But the tenants said to one another: This is the heir: come, let us kill him: and the inheritance shall be ours.
8 And seizing him, they killed him: and cast him out of the vineyard.
9 What therefore will the Lord of the vineyard do? He will come, and destroy the tenants: and will give the vineyard to others.

->CHAPTER XIV.<-

*The chief priests consult about killing Jesus: he is poured over with precious ointment by a woman while the disciples murmur: he is sold by Judas; he speaks to the disciples at the supper about his betrayal, in which he hands over the bread and wine, consecrated as his body and blood, to the disciples: he predicts that all will be scandalized, and Peter's triple denial: and after a triple prayer he is taken by the Jews; from one of whom Peter cuts off an ear: and with the disciples fleeing, he is accused before Caiaphas by false witnesses, judged guilty of death, is spat upon and beaten, and denied three times by Peter.*

### C H A P T E R XV.

->*Jesus, accused before Pilate, answers nothing; Barabbas is chosen, and Jesus is delivered to be crucified. Having been mocked in many ways by the soldiers, he is led away to be crucified. His garments being divided, he is crucified between thieves and hears the blasphemies of various people hurled at him. Darkness falls; and Jesus, crying out "Eli" and being given vinegar to drink, expires with a loud cry. His body is buried by Joseph.*<-

38 And the veil of the temple was torn in two, from the top to the bottom.
39 Now when the Centurion <note>A Roman officer in charge of one hundred men.</note>, who stood facing him, saw that he had died after crying out in this way, he said: "Truly this man was the Son of God."
<margin>† Matthew 27:55</margin>
40 There were also women looking on from a distance; among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joseph, and Salome.
<margin>† Luke 8:2</margin>
41 Even when he was in Galilee, they followed him and ministered to him; and many other women were there who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
<margin>† Matthew 27:57; Luke 23:50; John 19:38</margin>
42 And when evening had already come (because it was the Day of Preparation, which is the day before the Sabbath),
43 Joseph of Arimathea, a noble decurion <note>A high-ranking member of the council or Sanhedrin.</note> who was himself waiting for the kingdom of God, came and went boldly to Pilate to request the body of Jesus.
44 But Pilate wondered if he were already dead. And summoning the centurion, he questioned him as to whether he was already dead.
45 And when he had learned the truth from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
46 Then Joseph, having bought a linen shroud and taking him down, wrapped him in the linen and placed him in a tomb which had been hewn out of rock, and he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
47 And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joseph watched to see where he was laid.

-># C H A P T E R XVI.<-

*While the women are amazed at the tomb of Christ, an Angel announces his resurrection; he first appears to Mary Magdalene, then to two disciples in another form; finally appearing to the eleven as they reclined at table, having rebuked their unbelief, he sends them out to preach and baptize throughout the whole world, with signs to follow those who believe, and so he ascends into heaven.*

<margin>Matthew 28:1</margin>
AND when the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome—

<margin>Luke 24:1; John 20:1</margin>
—bought spices, so that they might come and anoint Jesus.
2 And very early in the morning, on the first day of the week <note>original: "una sabbatorum," literally the first of the Sabbaths/weeks.</note>, they came to the tomb, just as the sun had risen.
3 And they said to one another: "Who will roll away the stone for us from the entrance of the tomb?"
4 But looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away; for it was very large.
<margin>† Matthew 28:5; Luke 24:4; John 20:12</margin>
5 And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a white robe, and they were utterly amazed.
6 But he said to them: "Do not be terrified; you seek Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. See the place where they laid him.
<margin>† Above 14:28</margin>
7 But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he goes before you into Galilee; there you shall see him, just as he told you."
8 But they went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and fear had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
<margin>† John 20:16</margin>
9 Now rising early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
10 She went and told those who had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
11 And they, hearing that he was alive and had been seen by her, did not believe it.
<margin>† Matthew 24:13</margin>
12 After these things, he showed himself in another form to two of them as they were walking, while they were going into the country.
13 And they went and told the others, but they did not believe them either.
14 Lastly, he appeared to the eleven as they reclined at table, and he rebuked their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen that he had risen.
15 And he said to them: "Go into the whole world and preach the Gospel to every creature.
16 He who believes and is baptized shall be saved; but he who does not believe shall be condemned.
<margin>† Acts 16:18; † Acts 2:4 & 10:46; † Acts 28:8; † Luke 24:51</margin>
17 And these signs shall follow those who believe: In my name they shall cast out demons; they shall speak with new tongues;
18 They shall pick up serpents; and if they drink anything deadly, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover."
19 And so the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven, and sits at the right hand of God.
20 But they went forth and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word by the signs that followed.

### CHAPTER ONE

*Gabriel the angel announces to Zechariah the priest the conception of John by Elizabeth, who was barren; because he did not believe the Angel, Zechariah is made mute. The same Gabriel announces to Mary the conception of Jesus, the Son of God, by the Holy Spirit. At Mary’s greeting, John leaps in the womb, and Elizabeth prophesies; Mary herself sings a song of thanksgiving to the Lord. At the circumcision of the newborn John, his father Zechariah, having regained his speech, utters a song of thanksgiving.*

<margin>1</margin> Inasmuch as many have taken it in hand to set in order a narrative of the things that have been accomplished among us:

<margin>2</margin> Just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning saw them themselves and were ministers of the word:

3 It seemed good to me also, having followed all things diligently from the beginning, to write to you in an orderly way, most excellent Theophilus,

4 So that you may know the truth of those words in which you have been instructed.

<margin>1 Chronicles 24:10</margin>
5 There was in the days of Herod, king of Judea, a certain priest named Zechariah <note>original: Zacharias</note>, † of the division of Abijah <note>original: de vice Abia; Abijah was the head of the eighth of the twenty-four priestly divisions established by King David</note>, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.

6 And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord without blame,

7 And they had no son, because Elizabeth was barren, and they both were well advanced in years.

8 And it happened that while he was performing the priest's office in the order of his division before God,

9 According to the custom of the priesthood, it fell to him by lot to enter into the temple of the Lord to burn incense:

11 And an Angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense.

13 But the Angel said to him: "Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard; and your wife Elizabeth shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name John:

14 And you shall have joy and gladness, and many shall rejoice at his birth:

15 For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord; and he shall drink no wine nor strong drink <note>original: siceram; a fermented, intoxicating beverage made from grain or fruit other than grapes</note>, and he shall be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb:

16 And many of the children of Israel shall he turn to the Lord their God:

17 And he shall go before him in the spirit and

power of Elijah: † to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the incredulous to the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a perfect people." <margin>† Malachi 4:6; Matthew 11:14</margin>

27 To a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary.

33 And of his kingdom there shall be no end.

36 And behold, your cousin Elizabeth, she also has conceived a son in her old age; and this is the sixth month with her, who is called barren:

37 Because no word shall be impossible with God."

### C H A P T E R II.

*By the decree of Augustus, Joseph goes up with Mary to Bethlehem, where she gives birth to the Savior; his birth having been heard of from an Angel, the shepherds come in haste to see him: the circumcised child is called Jesus: whom, after the days of purification, being brought to Jerusalem to be presented to the Lord, the old man Simeon blesses, and prophesies concerning the mother's sorrows in the passion; and Anna, the aged prophetess, confesses the Lord: Jesus at twelve years old, full of wisdom and grace, having been lost by his parents, is found in the midst of the doctors; and he goes down to Nazareth, being subject to them.*

*John is sent by the Lord to fulfill the prophecy of Isaiah by his preaching: and he gives counsel to the crowds, the tax collectors, and the soldiers, telling what each ought to do; and he testifies to the excellence of Christ and of his baptism, upon whom, when he was baptized, the dove descends, and the voice of the Father is heard: and his genealogy is woven, ascending from Joseph even to Adam.*

5 Every valley shall be filled: and every mountain and hill shall be brought low: and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways plain:

### CHAPTER IV.

*Jesus, after a fast of forty days and having overcome the temptations of Satan, reads in the synagogue at Nazareth the prophecy of Isaiah written concerning himself; and says that a prophet is not accepted in his own homeland, for which reason they wish to throw him down from the hill: he casts out a demon in Capernaum, heals the mother-in-law of Simon, and many others from various sicknesses, and drives out demons.*

1 <margin>Matthew 4:1, Mark 1:12</margin> And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan; and was led by the Spirit into the desert,

### CHAPTER VII.

> *Having marveled at the faith of the Centurion, he heals his servant while absent: near the gate of the city of Nain, he raises the only son of a widow: in the presence of the disciples of John the Baptist, who asked through them whether he was the one who was to come, he performs many signs: and as they departed, he highly extols John: the life of neither John nor Christ pleased the Jews, whom he compares to children calling out to one another in the marketplace: his feet are anointed by a sinful woman, and he answers Simon who murmured at this by proposing the parable of the two debtors, and the woman's sins are forgiven.*

### C H A P T E R IX.

*Sending the disciples to preach, he delivers to them the precepts to be kept: Herod, having heard the fame of Christ, desires to see him: Jesus satisfies five thousand men from five loaves and two fishes: Peter confesses him as the Christ of God: he foretells his passion, and concerning the taking up of one's own cross: in the Transfiguration Moses and Elijah are joined in majesty: at the prayers of a father he casts out a demon from a son: a contention arises among the Apostles concerning primacy: the sons of Zebedee wish the Samaritans to be consumed by heavenly fire for refusing to receive Jesus: he does not receive one who wishes to follow; but calls another, and does not permit him to first bury his father.*

### C H A P T E R X.

*Sending seventy-two others before him to every city, he delivers the precepts they should observe in preaching; and when they rejoice that demons are subject to them, he says they should not rejoice chiefly for this reason: he threatens the obstinate cities in which many miracles had been performed; and exulting in the spirit, he confesses to the Father: to a lawyer who tests him, after the precept of love for God and neighbor is recited, he shows who is a neighbor through the parable of the man going down from Jerusalem: to Martha who is serving and complaining about her sister Mary, he says that Mary has chosen the best part.*

1 And after these things, the Lord designated seventy-two others: and he sent them two by two before his face into every city and place where he himself was to come.

### CHAPTER XI.

*He teaches the disciples to pray, showing that all things are obtained through persevering prayer; having cast out a mute demon, he refutes those saying he casts out demons by <term>Beelzebub</term> <note>A name derived from a Philistine god, used here as a title for the prince of demons.</note>; a certain woman calls the womb that bore Jesus blessed; concerning the sign of Jonah, the Queen of the South, and the Ninevites, and the simple and evil eye; he rebukes the Pharisee who had invited him and was murmuring because he ate with unwashed hands; he censures the hypocrisy of the Pharisees and Scribes, saying the blood of all the Prophets will be required of this generation.*

1 And it came to pass, as he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said to him: "Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples."
<margin>Matthew 6:9.</margin>
2 And he said to them: "When you pray, say: Father, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come.
3 Give us this day our daily bread.
4 And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone who is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation."
5 And he said to them: "Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go to him at midnight, and say to him: 'Friend, lend me three loaves,
6 Because a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,'
7 And he from within answering should say: 'Do not be troublesome to me, the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed, I cannot rise and give to you.'
8 And if he shall persevere in knocking: I tell you, even if he will not rise and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence he will rise and give him as many as he needs.
<margin>Matthew 7:7, 21:22. Mark 11:24. John 14:13. James 1:5.</margin>
9 And I say to you: Ask, and it shall be given to you: seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you.
10 For everyone who asks, receives: and he who seeks, finds: and to him who knocks, it shall be opened.
<margin>Matthew 7:9.</margin>
11 And which of you, if he asks his father for bread, will he give him a stone? Or a fish, will he give him a serpent instead of a fish?
12 Or if he asks for an egg, will he reach him a scorpion?
13 If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children: how much more will your Father from heaven give the good spirit to those who ask him?"
<margin>Matthew 9:32 & 12:22. Luke 11:22.</margin>
14 And he was casting out a demon, and it was mute. And when he had cast out the demon, the mute man spoke, and the crowds wondered.
<margin>Matthew 9:34. Mark 3:22.</margin>
15 But some of them said: "He casts out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons."
16 And others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
17 But he, seeing their thoughts, said to them: "Every kingdom divided against itself shall be brought to desolation, and house shall fall upon house.
18 And if Satan also is divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? Because you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebub."

19 "And if I cast out demons by Beelzebub <note>original: 'Beelzebub' — a Philistine god, often used in the New Testament as a name for the prince of demons or Satan.</note>, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore, they shall be your judges.

# CHAPTER XII.

> *He teaches that one must beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and that everything hidden will be revealed: also who is to be feared: concerning blasphemy against the Holy Spirit: he strengthens the Apostles against persecutions: he does not wish to involve himself in dividing the inheritance of brothers: through the parable of the rich man he calls them away from greed, forbidding worry about food and clothing; and he encourages them that their loins be girded: and who is a faithful or unfaithful steward: he comes to send fire upon the earth and division: he reproaches them because they do not judge the time of grace: he warns that everyone should strive to free themselves from their adversary.*

<margin>† Matthew 16:6; † Mark 8:15.</margin>
1 Meanwhile, as many thousands of the crowd stood around, so that they trod upon one another, he began to say to his disciples: "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

<margin>† Matthew 10:26; Mark 4:22.</margin>
2 For there is nothing covered that shall not be revealed; nor hidden that shall not be known.

3 For whatever things you have said in the dark shall be told in the light; and what you have spoken in the ear in the inner chambers shall be preached on the housetops.

4 And I say to you, my friends: Do not be terrified of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.

5 But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear him who, after he has killed, has power to cast into Gehenna <note>original: 'gehennam' — a place of punishment; hell.</note>; yes, I say to you, fear him."

### CHAPTER XIII.

*On the occasion of the Galileans murdered during their sacrifices, and those upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, He urges repentance, otherwise they will be destroyed like the unfruitful fig tree: He rebukes the ruler of the synagogue, who was indignant because He had healed a woman with a spirit of infirmity on the Sabbath: He compares the kingdom of heaven to a mustard seed and to leaven: concerning the narrow gate: and that some will knock in vain once the door is closed: He calls Herod a fox, and says Jerusalem is to be abandoned because of its cruelty.*

1 Now there were some present at that very time telling him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
2 And answering, he said to them: "Do you think that these Galileans were greater sinners than all other Galileans because they suffered such things?
3 I tell you, no: but unless you repent, you will all likewise perish.
4 Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you think they were more guilty than all the men living in Jerusalem?
5 I tell you, no: but if you do not repent, you will all likewise perish."
6 He also spoke this parable: "A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it, and found none.
7 And he said to the dresser of the vineyard: 'Behold, for three years now I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and I find none: cut it down, then; why does it even take up the ground?'
8 But he, answering, said to him: 'Lord, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put in dung:
9 And if it bears fruit, well; but if not, you shall cut it down in the future.'"
10 Now he was teaching in their synagogue on the Sabbaths.
11 And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity <note>or a spirit of illness</note> for eighteen years: and she was bent over, and could not look upwards at all.
12 When Jesus saw her, he called her to him and said to her: "Woman, you are delivered from your infirmity."
13 And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she was made straight, and she glorified God.
14 But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, answering, said to the crowd: "There are six days in which one ought to work: come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day."
15 Then the Lord, answering him, said: "Hypocrite, does not each one of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or his donkey from the stall and lead it to water?

<column-break/>

16 And ought not this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound, behold, for eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath day?"
17 And when he said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed: and all the people rejoiced in all the glorious things that were done by him.
18 He said therefore: "What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?
<margin>† Matthew 13:31. Mark 4:31.</margin> 19 † It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and cast into his garden; and it grew, and became a great tree: and the birds of the air rested in its branches."
20 And again he said: "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
<margin>† Matthew 13:33.</margin> 21 † It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures <term>original: 'sata' — a Greek and Hebrew dry measure equal to about a peck and a half</term> of flour, until the whole was leavened."
22 And he went through the cities and villages teaching, and making his way toward Jerusalem.
23 And someone said to him: "Lord, are there few who are saved?" But he said to them:
<margin>† Matthew 7:13.</margin> 24 † "Strive to enter through the narrow gate: for many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.
<margin>† Matthew 25:10.</margin> 25 † But when the master of the house has entered and shut the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying: 'Lord, open to us': and answering, he will say to you: 'I do not know where you are from.'
26 Then you will begin to say: 'We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.'
<margin>† Matthew 7:23. & † Psalm 6:9. Matthew 25:41.</margin> 27 And he will say to you: † 'I do not know where you are from: depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.'
28 There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves cast out.
29 And they will come from the East and the West, and the North and the South, and will sit down in the kingdom of God.
<margin>† Matthew 19:30 and 20:16. Mark 10:31.</margin> 30 † And behold, there are those who are last who will be first, and there are those who are first who will be last."
31 On that same day, some of the Pharisees came, saying to him: "Leave, and go away from here, for Herod wants to kill you."
32 And he said to them: "Go and tell that fox: 'Behold, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I am finished.'
33 Nevertheless, I must walk today and tomorrow and the following day: for it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.
<margin>† Matthew 23:37.</margin> 34 † Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you, how often I wanted to gather your children together, as a bird gathers her nestlings under her wings, and you would not!
35 Behold, your house will be left to you deserted. And I tell you, that you will not see me until the time comes when you say: 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'"
