### C H A P T E R XIV.

*In the house of a leader of the Pharisees, he heals a man with dropsy on the Sabbath, showing the lawyers and Pharisees that this is lawful; and noting their ambition, he teaches the invited guest to sit in the lowest place: a parable about those invited to a dinner who make excuses: whoever follows Christ must renounce all things, taking up his cross, even to the point of hating his own life: one wishing to build a tower first calculates the costs: the commendation of salt.*

1 AND it happened when Jesus entered the house of a certain leader of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.
2 And behold, there was a certain man with dropsy <term>original: 'hydropicus' — a condition involving an accumulation of fluid in the body, which was often used in sermons as a metaphor for greed</term> before him.
3 And responding, Jesus spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying: "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?"
4 But they were silent. But he, taking hold of him, healed him and sent him away.
5 And responding to them, he said: "Which of you, if an ass or an ox falls into a pit, will not immediately pull it out on the Sabbath day?"
6 And they could not answer him regarding these things.
7 And he also told a parable to those invited, noticing how they chose the first places at the table, saying to them:
8 "When you are invited to a wedding, do not sit down in the first place, lest perhaps someone more honorable than you has been invited by him;
9 And he who called you and him comes and says to you: 'Give this man your place': and then you begin with shame to take the lowest place.
10 But when you are called, go, sit in the lowest place: so that when he who invited you comes, he may say to you: 'Friend, move up higher.' Then you will have glory in the presence of those sitting at the table with you:
<margin>† Proverbs 25:7.</margin>
11 † Because everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled: and he who humbles himself shall be exalted.
<margin>† Matthew 23:12. Below 18:14.</margin>
12 And he also said to him who had invited him: † "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor your wealthy neighbors: lest perhaps they also invite you in return, and a repayment be made to you.
<margin>† Tobit 4:7. Proverbs 3:9.</margin>
13 But when you make a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind:
14 And you will be blessed, because they have nothing to repay you with: for it will be repaid to you at the resurrection of the righteous."
15 When one of those sitting at the table with him heard these things, he said to him: "Blessed is he who shall eat bread in the kingdom of God."
<margin>Matthew 22:2. Revelation 19:9.</margin>
16 But he said to him: † "A certain man gave a great dinner, and invited many.
17 And he sent his servant at the hour of the dinner to say to those invited to come, for all things were now ready.
18 And they all began together to make excuses. The first said to him: 'I have bought a farm, and I must go out and see it: I ask you, have me excused.'
19 And another said: 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them: I ask you, have me excused.'
20 And another said: 'I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.'
21 And the servant returned and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant: 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city: and

<column-break/>

bring in here the poor, and the crippled, and the blind, and the lame.'
22 And the servant said: 'Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.'
23 And the lord said to the servant: 'Go out into the roads and hedges: and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled.
24 For I tell you, that none of those men who were called shall taste my dinner.'"
25 Now great crowds went with him: and turning he said to them:
<margin>† Matthew 10:37.</margin>
26 † "If anyone comes to me, and does not hate his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, and even his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.
<margin>† Matthew 10:38 & 16:24. Mark 8:34.</margin>
27 † And whoever does not carry his cross and come after me, cannot be my disciple.
28 For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the costs <term>original: 'sumptus' — the expenses or resources needed</term> that are necessary, whether he has enough to complete it?
29 Lest, after he has laid the foundation and is not able to finish it, all who see it begin to mock him,
30 Saying: 'This man began to build, and was not able to finish'?
31 Or what king, going to engage in war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
32 Otherwise, while the other is still far off, sending a delegation, he asks for terms of peace.
33 So therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all that he possesses, cannot be my disciple.
<margin>† Matthew 5:13. Mark 9:49.</margin>
34 † Salt is good. But if the salt has lost its flavor, with what shall it be seasoned?
35 It is useful neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, but it shall be thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear."

### C H A P T E R XV.

*While the Scribes and Pharisees murmur that he receives sinners, he proposes parables about the lost sheep and the lost coin that were found, and about the prodigal son returning to his father and being kindly received by him, while the elder son takes this indignantly: how great the joy is in heaven over a sinner performing penance.*

1 Now the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.
2 And the Pharisees and Scribes murmured, saying: "This man receives sinners and eats with them."
3 And he spoke this parable to them, saying:
<margin>† Matthew 18:12.</margin>
4 † "What man among you, who has a hundred sheep: and if he loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the desert and go after the one that was lost, until he finds it?
5 And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing:
6 And coming home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them: 'Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep which was lost'?
7 I tell you, that in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner performing penance <term>original: 'paenitentiam' — a conversion of heart or repentance</term>, more than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need penance.
8 Or what woman having ten silver coins <term>original: 'drachmas' — an ancient Greek silver coin roughly equivalent to a day's wage</term>, if she [loses one]...

8 Or what woman, if she loses one silver coin <note>original: 'drachmam'; a Greek silver coin roughly equal to a day's wage</note>, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search diligently until she finds it?
9 And when she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying: "Rejoice with me, for I have found the coin which I had lost."
10 In the same way, I tell you, there will be joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents.
11 And he said: A certain man had two sons.
12 And the younger of them said to his father: "Father, give me the share of the estate that falls to me." And he divided his wealth between them.
13 And not many days later, having gathered everything together, the younger son set off on a journey into a far country, and there he squandered his estate by living riotously.
14 And when he had spent everything, a severe famine occurred in that country, and he began to be in need.
15 And he went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, who sent him to his farm to feed pigs.
16 And he desired to fill his belly with the pods <note>original: 'siliquis'; the fruit of the carob tree, used for animal fodder</note> that the pigs were eating, and no one gave him anything.
17 But coming to himself, he said: "How many hired servants in my father’s house have more than enough bread, but I am perishing here from hunger!"
18 "I will get up and go to my father, and I will say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you."
19 "I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me like one of your hired servants."
20 And rising up, he came to his father. But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and running, he fell on his neck and kissed him.
21 And the son said to him: "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son."
22 But the father said to his servants: "Bring out quickly the best robe and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet."
23 "And bring the fatted calf and kill it, and let us eat and celebrate."
24 "Because this son of mine was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and is found." And they began to celebrate.
25 Now his older son was in the field; and as he came and approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
26 And he called one of the servants and asked what these things meant.
27 And he said to him: "Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fatted calf, because he has received him back safe and sound."
28 But he was angry and did not want to go in. Therefore his father, coming out, began to plead with him.
29 But answering, he said to his father: "Behold, for so many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed your command, and yet you never gave me a young goat so that I might celebrate with my friends."
30 "But after this son of yours came, who has devoured his wealth with harlots, you killed the fatted calf for him."
31 And he said to him: "Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours."

32 "But it was necessary to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life; he was lost and is found."

### CHAPTER XVI.

->*Through the parable of the dishonest steward, he exhorts them to give alms, teaching what the faithful or unfaithful manager of wealth deserves, and that no one can serve God and mammon <note>a term for wealth or property, often personified as a false god</note>. He says that the Law and the prophets were until John, and that nothing from the Law will perish; nor should a wife be dismissed in any way so that another may be married. Concerning the rich man who feasted, and Lazarus the beggar.*<-

1 And he also said to his disciples: There was a certain rich man who had a steward <term>original: 'villicum' — a farm manager or estate agent</term>, and this man was accused to him of squandering his goods.
2 And he called him and said to him: "What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward."
3 And the steward said within himself: "What shall I do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg."
4 "I know what I will do so that, when I am removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses."
5 Therefore, having called together each of his master's debtors, he said to the first: "How much do you owe my master?"
6 And he said: "A hundred measures <note>original: 'cados'; a liquid measure</note> of oil." And he said to him: "Take your bond, and sit down quickly and write fifty."
7 Then he said to another: "And how much do you owe?" Who said: "A hundred measures <note>original: 'coros'; a dry measure for grain</note> of wheat." He said to him: "Take your papers and write eighty."
8 And the Lord praised the dishonest steward because he had acted prudently; for the children of this world are more prudent in their generation than the children of light.
9 And I say to you: make friends for yourselves by means of dishonest wealth <note>original: 'mammona iniquitatis'</note>, so that when you fail, they may receive you into eternal dwellings.
10 He who is faithful in a very little thing is also faithful in much; and he who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
11 If therefore you have not been faithful with dishonest wealth, who will entrust to you what is true?
12 And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?
<margin>† Matthew 6:24</margin>
13 No servant can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
14 Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all these things, and they ridiculed him.
15 And he said to them: "You are those who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted among men is an abomination before God."
<margin>† Matthew 11:12; † Matthew 5:18</margin>
16 The Law and the prophets were until John; from that time the kingdom of God is preached, and everyone forces his way into it.
17 But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tiny stroke <note>original: 'apicem'; the smallest mark or serif in Hebrew script</note> of the Law to fail.
<margin>† Matthew 5:32; † Matthew 19:9; † 1 Corinthians 7:11</margin>
18 Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and he who marries a woman divorced from her husband commits adultery.
19 There was a certain rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen and feasted sumptuously every day.

20 And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, who lay at his gate, full of sores,
21 Desiring to be filled with the crumbs that fell from the rich man's table, and no one gave to him; moreover, even the dogs came and licked his sores.

23 And lifting up his eyes when he was in torments, he saw Abraham far away, and Lazarus in his bosom.
24 And he cried out and said: "Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water to cool my tongue, for I am tortured in this flame."
25 And Abraham said to him: "Son, remember that you received good things in your life, and likewise Lazarus received evil things; but now he is comforted here, and you are tortured."
26 "And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm <note>original: "chaos magnum"; a vast, fixed void</note> has been established, so that those who want to pass from here to you cannot, nor can they cross from there to us."

28 "For I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, lest they also come into this place of torments."
29 And Abraham said to him: "They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them."
30 But he said: "No, father Abraham; but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent."
31 And he said to him: "If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not believe even if someone rises from the dead."

### C H A P T E R XVII.

*Woe to the one who causes the little ones to stumble; a brother sinning against us must be rebuked, and if he repents, he must be forgiven: He teaches the Apostles the power of faith; and that when they have done all the things commanded of them, they should call themselves useless servants: ten lepers are cleansed, with only one, who was a Samaritan, returning to give thanks: He says the coming of the Son of God will not be hidden, but glorious, and will come unexpectedly, just as the flood came upon the world and the destruction upon Sodom.*

<margin>Matthew 18:7. Mark 9:41.</margin>
And he said to his disciples: "It is impossible that scandals <note>original: "scandala"; causes for stumbling or falling into sin</note> will not come: but woe to him through whom they come."
2 "It would be more profitable for him if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble."
<margin>Leviticus 19:17. Ecclesiasticus 19:13. Matthew 18:15.</margin>
3 "Watch yourselves: if your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him."
4 "And if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turns back to you, saying, 'I repent,' forgive him."
5 And the Apostles said to the Lord: "Increase our faith."
<margin>Matthew 17:19.</margin>
6 And the Lord said: "If you had faith like a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, <note>original: "moro"; specifically the sycamine or black mulberry tree</note> 'Be uprooted and transplanted into the sea,' and it would obey you."
7 "But which of you, having a servant plowing or tending sheep, would say to him when he has returned from the field: 'Come at once and sit down to eat'?"

8 "And would he not rather say to him: 'Prepare what I am to eat for dinner, and gird yourself, and serve me until I have eaten and drunk, and afterward you shall eat and drink'?"

10 "I think not. So you also, when you have done all the things that were commanded you, say: 'We are useless servants; <note>original: "servi inutiles"; meaning they have done only what was required, not earned extra merit</note> we have only done what we were duty-bound to do.'"

18 "Was no one found who returned and gave glory to God except this foreigner?"

20 And being asked by the Pharisees, "When is the kingdom of God coming?" he answered them and said: "The kingdom of God does not come with observation;"
21 "Neither shall they say: 'Look, here it is!' or 'Look, there!' For behold, the kingdom of God is within you." <note>original: "intra vos"; can also be translated as "among you" or "in your midst"</note>

<margin>Matthew 24:23. Mark 13:21.</margin>
23 "And they will say to you: 'Look, here!' and 'Look, there!' Do not go, nor follow them."
24 "For as the lightning flashing from under heaven shines upon the things that are under heaven, so shall the Son of Man be in his day."
25 "But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation."
<margin>Genesis 7:7. Matthew 24:37.</margin>
26 "And as it was in the days of Noah, <note>original: "Noe"</note> so shall it be also in the days of the Son of Man."
27 "They ate and they drank; they married wives and were given in marriage, until the day that Noah entered the ark; and the flood came and destroyed them all."

28 "Likewise, as it was in the days of Lot: they ate and they drank; they bought and they sold; they planted and they built;"
29 "But on the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed them all."
30 "Even so shall it be in the day when the Son of Man is revealed."
31 "In that hour, he who is on the housetop and his goods are in the house, let him not come down to take them; and he who is in the field, likewise, let him not return back."
32 "Remember Lot’s wife."

33 "Whoever seeks to save his life shall lose it; and whoever loses it shall preserve it."

### CHAPTER XVIII.

*Through the parable of the judge of iniquity and the persistent widow, he teaches that one must always pray; through the parable of the Pharisee and the Tax Collector, he shows how one should pray; he forbids children from being turned away from him; a rich man who said he had kept all the commandments from his youth, having heard Christ's counsel about leaving all things, went away sad; what the reward will be for those leaving all things for Christ; he foretells his passion, and near Jericho he gives sight to a blind man.*

1 And he also told them a parable, that it is necessary to always pray and not to lose heart,
2 Saying: There was a certain judge in a certain city who did not fear God, and did not respect man.

### CHAPTER XIX.

*He stays with Zacchaeus while many grumble; he tells a parable about a nobleman who, departing to receive a kingdom, gave ten minas to ten servants, whom the citizens did not want to reign over them; entering Jerusalem with honor upon the foal of a donkey, he weeps over the city and predicts its destruction; and entering the temple, he casts out those buying and selling.*

AND having entered, he walked through Jericho.
2 And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus: and he was a chief of the tax collectors <term>publican: a collector of Roman taxes, often seen as a traitor or sinner by fellow Jews</term>, and he was wealthy.
3 And he sought to see who Jesus was: and he could not because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.
4 And running ahead, he climbed up into a sycamore tree so that he might see him: for he was about to pass that way.
5 And when Jesus had come to the place, looking up he saw him: and said to him: Zacchaeus, make haste and come down: for today I must stay in your house.
6 And making haste he came down, and received him rejoicing.

8 But Zacchaeus, standing there, said to the Lord: Behold, half of my goods, Lord, I give to the poor: and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold.
9 Jesus said to him: Today salvation has come to this house: because he also is a son of Abraham.
<margin>† Matthew 18:11.</margin>
10 † For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.
11 While they were listening to these things, he added and spoke a parable, because he was near Jerusalem: and because they thought that the kingdom of God was to be manifested immediately.
<margin>† Matthew 25:14.</margin>
12 He said therefore: † A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive a kingdom for himself, and to return.
13 And calling his ten servants, he gave them ten minas <term>mina: a unit of Greek currency, worth about 100 drachmas or three months' wages for a laborer</term>, and said to them: Trade with this until I come.
14 But his citizens hated him: and they sent a delegation after him, saying: We do not want this man to reign over us.
15 And it happened that he returned, having received the kingdom: and he ordered the servants to be called, to whom he had given the money, so that he might know how much each one had gained by trading.
16 And the first came, saying: Lord, your mina has gained ten minas.
17 And he said to him: Well done, good servant, because you have been faithful in a very little thing, you shall have authority over ten cities.
18 And the second came, saying: Lord, your mina has made five minas.
19 And to him he said: And you, be over five cities.
20 And another came, saying: Lord, behold your mina, which I have kept laid up in a handkerchief:
21 For I feared you, because you are a harsh man: you take up what you did not lay down, and you reap what you did not sow.
22 He says to him: Out of your own mouth I judge you, you wicked servant; you knew that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not lay down, and reaping what I did not sow:

<column-break/>

23 And why then did you not give my money to the bank, so that when I came I might have collected it with interest?
24 And he said to those standing by: Take the mina from him, and give it to him who has ten minas.
25 And they said to him: Lord, he has ten minas.
<margin>† Matthew 13:12 & 25:29. Mark 4:25. Above 8:18.</margin>
26 † For I say to you, that to everyone who has, it shall be given, and he shall abound: but from him who has not, even that which he has shall be taken away from him.

31 And if anyone asks you: Why are you untying it? you shall say this to them: Because the Lord has need of its service.
32 And those who were sent went their way: and found the colt standing, just as he had said to them.

34 And they said: Because the Lord has need of it.

40 To whom he said: I tell you, that if these should keep silent, the stones will cry out.
41 And as he drew near, seeing the city, he wept over it, saying:
42 If you also had known, and indeed in this your day, the things that belong to your peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
<margin>† Matthew 24:2. Mark 13:2. Below 21:6. † Matthew 23:12. Mark 11:15. † Isaiah 56:7. Jeremiah 7:11.</margin>

### CHAPTER XX.

*He does not tell the priests and Scribes by what authority he does these things, because they did not respond to the question proposed about John's baptism: he relates the parable of the vinedressers, who, having killed the lord's servants, also killed his son: Jesus is tested concerning giving tribute to Caesar, and by the Sadducees concerning the resurrection: how they say Christ is the son of David: Beware of ambitious Scribes.*

Matthew 21:23.
Mark 11:27.

AND it happened on one of those days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the gospel, the chief priests and Scribes gathered with the elders,
2 And they spoke, saying to him: Tell us, by what authority do you do these things? Or who is he who gave you this authority?
3 But answering, Jesus said to them: I will also ask you one question. Answer me:
4 The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men?
5 But they thought within themselves, saying: For if we say, From heaven, he will say, Why then did you not believe him?
6 But if we say, From men, the whole people will stone us: for they are certain that John was a prophet.
7 And they answered that they did not know where it was from.
8 And Jesus said to them: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
9 And he began to tell the people this parable: † A man planted a vineyard, and leased it to tenants: and he himself was away in a foreign land for a long time.
<margin>
† Isaiah 5:1. Jeremiah 2:21.
Matthew 21:33. Mark 12:1.
</margin>
10 And at the proper time he sent a servant to the farmers, so that they might give him of the fruit of the vineyard. But they beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
11 And he went on to send another servant. But they, beating this one also and treating him with insults, sent him away empty-handed.
12 And he went on to send a third: and they, wounding him as well, threw him out.
13 Then the lord of the vineyard said: What shall I do? I will send my beloved son: perhaps, when they see him, they will respect him.
14 When the tenants saw him, they thought within themselves, saying: This is the heir, let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.
15 And having thrown him out of the vineyard, they killed him. What therefore will the lord of the vineyard do to them?
16 He will come, and destroy those tenants, and give the vineyard to others. Having heard this, they said to him: God forbid.
17 But he, looking at them, said: What then is this that is written: † The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner <note>original: "caput anguli", referring to the cornerstone of a building</note>?

† Psalm 117:22. Isaiah 28:16. Matthew 21:42. Acts 4:11. Romans 9:33. 1 Peter 2:7.

18 Everyone who falls upon that stone will be broken to pieces: but on whomever it falls, it will crush him.

<margin>
† Matthew 22:15. Mark 12:13.
</margin>

## CHAPTER XXI.

> *He prefers the widow offering two small coins over the rich offering many things: he predicts the destruction of the temple, and various wars, afflictions, and persecutions; against which he strengthens the Apostles: he also predicts the destruction of Jerusalem, and the captivity and dispersion of the Jews, and the signs preceding the judgment: warning against gluttony, drunkenness, and the cares of life, and the need to watch and pray.*

---

<margin>Mark 12:41.</margin> 1 Looking up, he saw the rich people who were putting their gifts into the treasury.
2 He also saw a certain poor widow putting in two small copper coins. <note>original: "æra minuta duo," referring to the smallest denomination of Greek copper currency, commonly called "mites."</note>
3 And he said: Truly I say to you, that this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
4 For all these contributed to the offerings of God out of their abundance; but she, out of her poverty, has put in all the living that she had.
5 And while some were speaking of the temple, how it was adorned with noble stones and offerings, he said:
<margin>† Matthew 24:2. Mark 13:2. Above 19:44.</margin> 6 These things which you see—† the days will come in which there shall not be left one stone upon another that shall not be thrown down.
7 And they asked him, saying: Teacher, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when they begin to happen?
8 He said: See that you are not led astray; for many will come in my name, saying, "I am he," and "The time has drawn near." Do not go after them.
9 But when you hear of wars and seditions, do not be terrified: these things must first happen, but the end is not immediately.
10 Then he said to them: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
11 And there will be great earthquakes in various places, and pestilences, and famines; and there will be terrors from heaven and great signs.
12 But before all these things, they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, delivering you to synagogues and prisons, dragging you before kings and governors for the sake of my name:
13 And it will lead to an opportunity for your testimony.
14 Therefore, settle it in your hearts not to meditate beforehand how you will answer.
15 For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries will not be able to resist or contradict.
16 And you will be betrayed even by parents, and brothers, and relatives, and friends; and they will put some of you to death:
17 And you will be hated by all because of my name:
18 But not a hair of your head shall perish.
19 In your patience you shall possess your souls.
<margin>Daniel 9:27.</margin> 20 † But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by an army, then know that its desolation has drawn near:
<margin>Matthew 24:15. Mark 13:14.</margin> 21 Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains; and let those who are in the midst of it depart; and let those who are in the country not enter into it:
22 Because these are the days of vengeance, so that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
23 But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who nurse infants in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land and wrath upon this people.

<column-break/>

24 And they will fall by the edge of the sword; and they will be led away captive into all nations; and Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles, until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
<margin>† Isaiah 13:10. Ezekiel 32:7. Joel 3:15.</margin> 25 † And there will be signs in the sun, and the moon, and the stars; and on the earth distress of nations, confused by the roaring of the sea and the waves:
26 Men withering away for fear and expectation of what shall come upon the whole world: for the powers of the heavens shall be moved:
<margin>Matthew 24:29. Mark 13:24.</margin> 27 And then they will see the Son of Man <note>A title Jesus used for himself, referencing a messianic figure in the book of Daniel.</note> coming in a cloud with great power and majesty.
<margin>† Romans 8:23.</margin> 28 But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, † because your redemption is drawing near.
29 And he told them a parable: Look at the fig tree and all the trees:
30 When they already sprout their fruit, you know that summer is near.
31 So also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
32 Amen I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
33 Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
34 But take heed to yourselves, lest perhaps your hearts be weighed down with gluttony, and drunkenness, and the cares of this life, and that day come upon you suddenly.
35 For it will come like a snare upon all who sit upon the face of the whole earth.
36 Watch, therefore, praying at all times, so that you may be held worthy to escape all these things that are to come, and to stand before the Son of Man.
37 And during the days he was teaching in the temple; but at night, going out, he stayed on the mountain called Olivet.
38 And all the people came early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.

### CHAPTER XXII.

> *The chief priests plot the killing of Jesus, whom Judas sells: he orders the Passover to be prepared: he delivers the bread and wine consecrated as his body and blood to the disciples, commanding them to do the same: a dispute among the disciples about which of them is greater: he predicts the triple denial of Peter, ordering a tunic to be sold and a sword bought: after a long prayer in agony, and sweat like blood running down to the ground, he is captured by the Jews, from one of whom Peter cuts off an ear: he complains that they came out to capture him as if he were a thief: in the house of the high priest he is denied three times by Peter, and is beaten and mocked by the Jews, and in the morning, questioned in the council, he confesses that he is the son of God.*

->THE HOLY GOSPEL OF JESUS CHRIST ACCORDING TO JOHN<-

### CHAPTER ONE.

*The Word is God, life, and the light that enlightens every person, through whom all things were made, and who was made man. John bears witness to him, saying that he himself is only a voice, and that he is not worthy to untie the strap of his sandal; and that Jesus is the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. Andrew, one of the two disciples of John who followed Jesus, also brings his brother Simon to him. Philip too, called by Jesus, brings Nathanael to him.*

**1** <image-desc>Decorative initial 'I' with floral scrollwork.</image-desc> In the beginning was the Word, <note>original: "Verbum" — in Greek, *Logos*, meaning both Word and divine Reason, a profound theological term identifying Christ with the eternal creative intelligence of God</note> and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

**2** This one was in the beginning with God.

**3** All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that was made.

**4** In him was life, and the life was the light of men.

<margin>† Matt. 3:1. Mark 1:2.</margin>
**5** And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.

**6** † There was a man sent from God, whose name was John.

<column-break/>

**7** He came as a witness, to bear witness about the light, so that all might believe through him.

**8** He was not the light, but came to bear witness about the light.

<margin>† Below, 3:19. Heb. 11:3.</margin>
**9** † The true light, which enlightens every person, was coming into the world.

**10** He was in the world, † and the world was made through him, yet the world did not know him.

**11** He came to his own, and his own people did not receive him.

**12** But to all who did receive him, he gave the right to become children of God — to those who believe in his name:

**13** Who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.

<margin>† Matt. 1:16. Luke 2:7.</margin>
**14** † And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory — glory as of the only Son from the Father — full of grace and truth. <note>This verse is the theological heart of the Christian doctrine of the Incarnation: the eternal divine Word taking on human nature</note>

**15** John bears witness about him, and cries out, saying: "This was he of whom I said: He who comes after me ranks before me, because he was before me."

<margin>† 1 Tim. 6:17.</margin>
**16** † And from his fullness we have all received, and grace upon grace. <note>original: "gratiam pro gratia" — literally "grace in place of grace," suggesting an inexhaustible, ever-renewed gift</note>

22 Therefore, when he had risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they † believed the scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
23 Now when he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, on the feast day, many believed in his name, seeing the signs that he performed.
24 But Jesus did not entrust <note>original: "non credebat semetipsum"; a play on words, as many "believed" (crederunt) in him, but he did not "believe/trust" (credebat) himself to them</note> himself to them, because he knew all people,
25 And because he had no need for anyone to bear witness about man; for he himself knew what was in man.

## C H A P T E R III.

*He teaches Nicodemus by night about being born again of water and the Spirit, and about his own being lifted up like the bronze serpent, and that God sent his Son to save the world: a question having arisen about purification, John—to his own disciples who were murmuring about Christ—praises him, saying that he must increase, but himself must decrease; and that the Father has given all things into his hand: so that whoever believes in him may have eternal life; but whoever does not believe, the wrath of God remains upon him.*

Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.
2 He came to Jesus by night and said to him: "Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher; for no one can do these signs that you do, unless God is with him."
3 Jesus answered and said to him: "Amen, amen, I say to you, unless someone is born again <note>original: "denuo"; this can mean 'again,' 'anew,' or 'from above'</note>, he cannot see the kingdom of God."
4 Nicodemus said to him: "How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother's womb and be born again?"
5 Jesus answered: "Amen, amen, I say to you, unless someone is born of water and the Holy Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
6 That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
7 Do not wonder because I said to you: you must be born again.
<margin>† Psalm 134:7 <note>Modern Psalm 135:7</note></margin>
8 The Spirit <note>original: "Spiritus"; in both Latin and Greek, this word means both 'Spirit' and 'wind'</note> blows where it wills, and you hear its voice, † but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes; so is everyone who is born of the Spirit."
9 Nicodemus answered and said to him: "How can these things be?"

<column-break/>

10 Jesus answered and said to him: "Are you a teacher in Israel, and you do not know these things?
11 Amen, amen, I say to you, that we speak what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and you do not receive our testimony.
12 If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
13 And no one has ascended into heaven except him who descended from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven.
<margin>† Numbers 21:9.</margin>
14 † And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of Man be lifted up;
15 So that everyone who believes in him may not perish, but may have eternal life.
<margin>† 1 John 4:9.</margin>
16 † For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish, but may have eternal life.
17 For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through him.
18 He who believes in him is not judged; but he who does not believe is already judged, because he does not believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.
<margin>† Above 1:9.</margin>
19 And this is the judgment: † that the light has come into the world, and men loved darkness more than the light; for their works were evil.
20 For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his works may not be exposed.
21 But he who does the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be made manifest, because they have been done in God."
22 After these things, Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea; and there he remained with them, <margin>† Below 4:1.</margin> and † baptized.
23 And John was also baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there; and they came and were baptized.
24 For John had not yet been cast into prison.
25 Then a question arose from John’s disciples with the Jews about purification.
26 And they came to John and said to him: "Rabbi, he who was with you across the Jordan, <margin>† Above 1:19.</margin> † to whom you bore witness—behold, he is baptizing, and everyone is coming to him."
27 John answered and said: "A man cannot receive anything unless it has been given to him from heaven.
28 You yourselves bear witness to me <margin>† Above 1:20.</margin> † that I said: 'I am not the Christ,' but that I have been sent before him.
29 He who has the bride is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices with joy because of the bridegroom's voice. This joy of mine, therefore, is fulfilled.
30 He must increase, but I must decrease.
31 He who comes from above is above all. He who is of the earth belongs to the earth and speaks of the earth. He who comes from heaven is above all.
32 And what he has seen and heard, this he testifies; and no one receives his testimony.
<margin>† Romans 3:4.</margin>
33 He who has received his testimony has certified that † God is true.
34 For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God; for God does not give the Spirit by measure.
35 The Father loves the Son, and has given all things into his hand.
<margin>† John 3:20 <note>Cross-reference to earlier in the chapter</note></margin>
36 † He who believes in the Son has eternal life; but he who is unbelieving toward the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him."

### C H A P T E R IV.

*Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman about living water, and worshiping God in spirit, revealing himself to her as the promised Messiah: he tells his disciples he has food they do not know, namely obedience to the Father: regarding the harvest and the reaper and the sower: many Samaritans believe in him: he restores the son of a royal official to health.*

<margin>† Above 3:22.</margin>
1 Therefore, when Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John,
2 (Though Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples did)
3 He left Judea and went away again into Galilee.
4 But it was necessary for him to pass through Samaria.
<margin>† Genesis 33:19 and 48:22. Joshua 24:32.</margin>
5 So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of land † that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
6 Now Jacob’s well was there. Jesus, therefore, being tired from the journey, sat down just as he was by the well. It was about the sixth hour <note>roughly noon, the hottest part of the day</note>.
7 A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her: "Give me a drink."
8 (For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.)
9 That Samaritan woman therefore said to him: "How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, who am a Samaritan woman?" For the Jews do not associate with the Samaritans <note>original: "non enim coutuntur Judaei Samaritanis"; highlighting the deep ethnic and religious rift between the two groups</note>.
10 Jesus answered and said to her: "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, 'Give me a drink,' you perhaps would have asked him, and he would have given you living water."
11 The woman said to him: "Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep; where then do you get that living water?
12 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well, and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?"
13 Jesus answered and said to her: "Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again; but whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst forever;
14 But the water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into eternal life."
15 The woman said to him: "Sir, give me this water, so that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw."
16 Jesus said to her: "Go, call your husband, and come back here."
17 The woman answered and said: "I have no husband." Jesus said to her: "You have spoken well, 'I have no husband';
18 For you have had five husbands, and the one you have now is not your husband; in this you have spoken truly."
19 The woman said to him: "Sir, I see that you are a prophet.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 12:5.</margin>
20 Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you say † that Jerusalem is the place where it is necessary to worship."

<column-break/>

truth. For the Father also seeks such people to worship him.

26 Jesus said to her: "I am he, the one who is speaking with you."
27 And immediately his disciples came; and they marveled that he was talking with a woman. Yet no one said, "What do you seek?" or "Why are you talking with her?"
28 The woman then left her water jar and went away into the city, and said to the people:

30 They went out of the city and were coming to him.

38 I sent you to reap that for which you have not labored; others have labored, and you have entered into their labors."
39 Now many of the Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the word of the woman bearing witness: "That he told me everything I ever did."

41 And many more believed in him because of his own word.
42 And they said to the woman: "Now we believe, not because of what you said; for we ourselves have heard him, and we know that this is truly the Savior of the world."
43 After two days he departed from there and went into Galilee.

### CHAPTER V.

->*Jesus, having healed a sick man at the pool who had suffered for 38 years, commands him to take up his mat on the Sabbath; and to the accusing Jews he responds that he performs all his works together with the Father, that he brings the dead to life, and that he has been appointed by the Father as the judge of all, to whom John, his own works, the Father, and even Moses himself bear witness.*<-

<margin>Leviticus 23:4-5. Deuteronomy 16:1.</margin>
1 After these things there was a feast day of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
2 Now there is in Jerusalem a Sheep Pool <note>original: "Probatica piscina"; a pool located near the Sheep Gate of the city</note>, which is called in Hebrew Bethsaida <note>frequently identified in other manuscripts as Bethesda</note>, having five porches.
3 In these lay a great multitude of sick people—blind, lame, and withered—waiting for the moving of the water.
4 For an angel of the Lord descended at certain times into the pool, and the water was stirred. And whoever stepped in first after the stirring of the water was made well from whatever infirmity held him.
5 Now a certain man was there who had been thirty-eight years in his infirmity.
6 When Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had already been in that state a long time, he said to him: "Do you want to be made well?"
7 The sick man answered him: "Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred; for while I am coming, another steps down before me."
8 Jesus said to him: "Rise, take up your mat <term>grabatum: a simple, portable bed or pallet used by the poor</term>, and walk."
9 And immediately the man was made well; and he took up his mat and walked. Now it was the Sabbath on that day.
10 Therefore the Jews said to him who had been healed: <margin>† Exodus 20:11. Jeremiah 17:24.</margin> † "It is the Sabbath; it is not lawful for you to carry your mat."
11 He answered them: "The one who made me well, he said to me: 'Take up your mat and walk.'"
12 They then asked him: "Who is that man who said to you, 'Take up your mat and walk'?"
13 But he who had been healed did not know who it was. For Jesus had withdrawn from the crowd gathered in that place.
14 Afterward Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: "See, you have been made well; sin no more, lest something worse happen to you."
15 That man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
16 For this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he did these things on the Sabbath.
17 But Jesus answered them: "My Father is working until now, and I am working."
18 Therefore the Jews sought all the more to kill him, because he not only broke the Sabbath but also called God his own Father, making himself equal to God. Jesus therefore answered and said to them:

<column-break/>

19 "Amen, amen, I say to you: the Son can do nothing of himself, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, these things the Son also does in like manner.
20 For the Father loves the Son and shows him all things that he himself does; and he will show him greater works than these, so that you may marvel.
21 For as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he will.
22 For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son,
23 So that all may honor the Son, just as they honor the Father. He who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
24 Amen, amen, I say to you, that he who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life and does not come into judgment but has passed from death into life.
25 Amen, amen, I say to you, that the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
26 For as the Father has life in himself, so he has also given to the Son to have life in himself;
27 And he has given him power to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man.
28 Do not marvel at this, for the hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear the voice of the Son of God.
29 <margin>† Matthew 25:46.</margin> † And those who have done good will come forth to the resurrection of life; but those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.
30 I can do nothing of myself. As I hear, I judge; and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will, but the will of him who sent me.
31 If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true.
32 <margin>† Matthew Above 1:15.</margin> † There is another who bears witness of me, and I know that the witness which he bears of me is true.
33 You sent to John, and he bore witness to the truth.
34 But I do not receive witness from man; but I say these things that you may be saved.
35 He was a burning and shining lamp. And you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.
36 But I have a greater witness than John. For the works which the Father has given me to finish—the very works that I do—bear witness of me, that the Father has sent me.
37 <margin>† Matthew 3:17 and 17:5. Deuteronomy 4:12.</margin> And the Father himself, who sent me, † has borne witness of me. You have neither heard his voice at any time, † nor seen his form.
38 And you do not have his word abiding in you, because you do not believe him whom he sent.
39 Search the Scriptures, for you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness of me.
40 And you will not come to me that you may have life.
41 I do not receive glory from men.
42 But I know you, that you do not have the love of God in you.
43 I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me; if another comes in his own name, him you will receive.
44 How can you believe, you who receive glory from one another, and do not seek the glory that comes from God alone?"

### C H A P T E R VII.

> *Going up to the Feast of Tabernacles <note>original: "Scenopegia"; a major Jewish autumn festival also known as the Feast of Booths</note> as if in secret, he convicts the Jews regarding his doctrine, because they were unjustly slandering him for healing a man on the Sabbath; he calls the thirsty to himself, and the crowd speaks of him in various ways; the officers who had been sent to arrest him, having heard his preaching, praise him; but also Nicodemus, defending him, is spoken of poorly by the chief priests and Pharisees.*

After these things, Jesus walked in Galilee, for he did not want to walk in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.

### CHAPTER VIII.

->*Regarding the woman caught in adultery: writing on the ground, he releases her from her accusers. He declares himself the light of the world, and that the Pharisees will die in their sin. He speaks of who are truly his disciples, and who are slaves or free. He tells them they are neither from God nor from Abraham, but from their father the devil, because they do not believe the one speaking the truth. To those blaspheming, he says he does not have a demon but honors the Father, and that he existed before Abraham was made. When they want to stone him, he hides himself from their sight and leaves the temple.*<-

1 But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
2 And at dawn he came again into the temple, and all the people came to him, and sitting down he taught them.
3 And the Scribes and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery, and they stood her in the middle,
4 And they said to him: "Teacher, this woman was just now caught in the act of adultery."
<margin>† Lev. 20:10</margin> 5 "Now in the law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What, therefore, do you say?"

<margin>† Deut. 17:7</margin> 7 When they continued questioning him, he stood up and said to them: "Let the one of you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her."
8 And leaning down again, he wrote on the ground.

10 Then Jesus, standing up, said to her: "Woman, where are those who accused you? Has no one condemned you?"
11 She said: "No one, Lord." And Jesus said: "Neither will I condemn you. Go, and from now on, sin no more."

### C H A P T E R IX.

->*He gives sight to a man blind from birth on the Sabbath, and the Pharisees labor with many tricks to take away the glory of this miracle from Christ; and because the man who had been blind defends Christ, he is cast out of the synagogue: but having been instructed by Christ, he believes and worships him, who says that he came into the world for judgment.*<-

4 "I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day: the night comes when no one can work."
5 "As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world."
6 When he had said these things, he spat on the ground and made clay from the saliva, and smeared the clay over his eyes,
7 And said to him: "Go, wash in the pool of Siloe"

### -> C H A P T E R X. <-

*Christ, describing the true shepherd and the hireling, says that he is the door of the sheep and the good shepherd; who also has other sheep to be brought to the same fold: he lays down his life, that he may take it up again: the Jews want to stone him, because, referring to his own works, he said he was one with the Father and the Son of God; which he nevertheless shows is not blasphemy.*

1 "Amen, amen, I say to you: he who does not enter by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up another way, he is a thief and a robber."
2 "But he who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep."
3 "To him the gatekeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out."
4 "And when he has let out his own sheep, he goes before them; and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice."
5 "But a stranger they will not follow, but will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers."
6 This <term>proverb <note>original: "proverbium," used here for a parable or figurative illustration.</note></term> Jesus spoke to them. But they did not understand what he was speaking to them.
7 Jesus therefore said to them again: "Amen, amen, I say to you, that I am the door of the sheep."
8 "All who have come before are thieves and robbers, and the sheep did not hear them."
9 "I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved: and he will go in and go out, and find pasture."
10 "The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I came that they may have life, and have it more abundantly."
<margin>† Isaiah 40:11, Ezekiel 34:23, & 37:24</margin>
11 "I am the good shepherd. † The good shepherd gives his life for his sheep."
12 "But the <term>hireling <note>original: "mercenarius," a worker who is paid only for his time and has no personal stake in the welfare of the flock.</note></term>, and he who is not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming, and leaves the sheep, and flees: and the wolf snatches and scatters the sheep:"
13 "The hireling flees because he is a hireling, and it does not concern him about the sheep."
14 "I am the good shepherd: and I know my own, and my own know me."

33 The Jews answered him: "We do not stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy; and because you, being a man, make yourself God."

34 Jesus answered them: "Is it not written in your law: † I have said, you are gods?"

<margin>† Psalm 81:6.</margin>
35 If he called them gods to whom the word of God was spoken—and the Scripture cannot be broken—

36 Do you say of him whom the Father has sanctified and sent into the world: "You blaspheme," because I said: "I am the Son of God"?

37 If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me.

38 But if I do them, even if you do not want to believe me, believe the works, so that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I am in the Father.

39 They sought therefore to seize him, but he escaped from their hands.

40 And he went again across the Jordan to the place where John was first baptizing, and he stayed there.

41 And many came to him, and they said: "John indeed performed no sign."

42 "But everything John said about this man was true." And many believed in him.

### C H A P T E R XI.

->*Jesus raises Lazarus, who had been dead for four days, after speaking much with his disciples and with Martha; because many believed in Christ due to this miracle, the Chief Priests and Pharisees took counsel and determined to kill him, with Caiaphas the high priest prophesying that it was necessary for Jesus to die so that the whole nation would not perish; Jesus then withdraws to the city of Ephrem.*<-

1 Now there was a certain man who was ill, Lazarus of Bethany, from the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

<margin>† Matthew 26:7, 37. Below 12:3.</margin>
2 (It was Mary † who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was ill.)

3 Therefore his sisters sent to him, saying: "Lord, behold, he whom you love is ill."

4 But hearing this, Jesus said to them: "This illness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it."

5 Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister Mary, and Lazarus.

6 When he heard therefore that he was ill, he remained in that same place for two days.

7 Then after this, he said to his disciples: "Let us go into Judea again."

8 The disciples said to him: "Rabbi, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?"

9 Jesus answered: "Are there not twelve hours of the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.

10 But if he walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him."

11 He said these things, and after this he said to them: "Lazarus our friend is sleeping; but I go so that I may awaken him from sleep."

12 Therefore his disciples said: "Lord, if he sleeps, he will be well."

13 But Jesus had spoken of his death; they, however, thought he was speaking of the rest of sleep.

14 Then Jesus said to them plainly: "Lazarus is dead.

15 And I am glad for your sake that I was not there, so that you may believe; but let us go to him."

16 Thomas, who is called <term>Didymus <note>A Greek name meaning "The Twin," corresponding to the Aramaic name Thomas.</note></term>, said to his fellow disciples: "Let us go also, that we may die with him."

17 And so Jesus came, and found that he had already been in the tomb for four days.

18 (Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about <term>fifteen stadia <note>A distance of approximately 1.8 miles or 3 kilometers.</note></term> away.)

19 Many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them concerning their brother.

20 Martha, therefore, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went to meet him; but Mary sat at home.

21 Martha said therefore to Jesus: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.

22 But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give to you."

23 Jesus said to her: "Your brother will rise again."

<margin>Above 5:29. † Above 6:40.</margin>

26 And everyone who lives and believes in me shall not die forever. Do you believe this?"

### C H A P T E R XII.

*Received at the home of Martha and Lazarus, Jesus is anointed with ointment by Mary, while the thief Judas murmurs; the chief priests also plot to kill Lazarus; Jesus enters Jerusalem with honor riding on a young donkey; when the Gentiles desire to see him, he says the hour of his glorification is near, but that the grain of wheat must first die; the voice of the Father is heard glorifying his name; the prince of this world is to be cast out; concerning the blindness of the Jews as prophesied by Isaiah; in Christ, the Father is either honored or rejected.*

### C H A P T E R XIII.

> Jesus, having girded himself with a linen cloth during supper, washes the feet of the disciples, with Peter at first refusing; he exhorts them to do the same for one another. He identifies his betrayer to John; after the betrayer leaves with the morsel, Jesus says he is glorified. Concerning the new commandment of love; he predicts Peter’s threefold denial.

<margin>Matthew 26:2. Mark 14:1. Luke 22:1.</margin> 1 Before the feast day of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that his hour had come to pass from this world to the Father—having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.
2 And when supper was finished, the devil having already put it into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him,
3 Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God,
4 rose from supper and laid aside his garments; and taking a linen cloth, he girded himself.
5 Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet, and to wipe them with the linen cloth with which he was girded.
6 Then he came to Simon Peter. And Peter said to him: "Lord, do you wash my feet?"
7 Jesus answered and said to him: "What I am doing you do not understand now, but you will know later."
8 Peter said to him: "You shall never wash my feet." Jesus answered him: "If I do not wash you, you will have no part with me."
9 Simon Peter said to him: "Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head."
10 Jesus said to him: "He who has bathed <note>original: "lotus est." This refers to a full ritual bath or washing of the whole body.</note> needs only to wash his feet, but is entirely clean. And you are clean, but not all of you."
11 For he knew who it was who would betray him; for this reason he said: "You are not all clean."
12 So after he had washed their feet and taken his garments, when he had sat down again, he said to them: "Do you know what I have done for you?
13 You call me Teacher and Lord; and you say well, for so I am.
14 If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
15 For I have given you an example, so that just as I have done for you, you also should do.
<margin>† Matthew 10:24. Luke 6:40.</margin> 16 † Truly, truly, I say to you: a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is an apostle greater than he who sent him."

### C H A P T E R XIV.

*Consoling the disciples, he says there are many dwelling places in his Father’s house, and that he will take them up again; he tells Thomas that he is the way, the truth, and the life; and to Philip, that the Father is seen in him; and that they will receive whatever they ask in his name, and that he will send them another Advocate from the Father: he teaches who should be said to love him, and what kind of peace he leaves to the disciples, who ought rightly to rejoice at his departure.*

"Let not your heart be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me.
2 In my Father’s house there are many dwelling places <note>original: "mansiones." Often translated as 'mansions,' it refers to staying or abiding places.</note>: if it were not so, I would have told you: Because I go to prepare a place for you.
3 And if I go and prepare a place for you, I come again and will take you to myself, that where I am, you also may be.
4 And where I go you know, and the way you know."
5 Thomas said to him: "Lord, we do not know where you are going; and how can we know the way?"
6 Jesus said to him: "I am the way, and the truth, and the life: no one comes to the Father, except through me.
7 If you had known me, you would surely have known my Father also; and from now on you shall know him, and you have seen him."
8 Philip said to him: "Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us."
9 Jesus said to him: "Have I been with you for so long a time, and you have not known me? Philip, he who sees me, sees the Father also. How can you say: 'Show us the Father'?
10 Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me? The words that I speak to you, I do not speak from myself. But the Father abiding in me, he does the works.
11 Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me?
12 Otherwise, believe because of the works themselves. Amen, amen, I say to you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he will do also; and greater than these will he do, because I go to the Father.
<margin>† Matthew 7:7 & 21:22. Mark 11:24.</margin>
13 † And whatever you shall ask the Father in my name, this I will do: so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
14 If you shall ask me anything in my name, this I will do.
<margin>See below 16:23.</margin>
15 If you love me, keep my commandments.
16 And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate <note>original: "Paraclitum." From the Greek 'Parakletos,' meaning one called to the side of another—a helper, comforter, or legal advocate.</note>, that he may stay with you forever,
17 The Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see him, nor know him; but you shall know him; because he will stay with you, and will be in you.
18 I will not leave you as orphans: I will come to you.
19 A little while longer, and the world sees me no more. But you see me: because I live, and you shall live.
20 In that day you shall know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
21 He who has my commandments, and keeps them: he it is who loves me. And he who loves me, shall be loved by my Father; and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him."
22 Judas said to him (not the Iscariot): "Lord, how has it happened, that you are going to manifest yourself to us, and not to the world?"
23 Jesus answered and said to him: "If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our dwelling place with him.
24 He who does not love me, does not keep my words. And the word which you have heard is not mine, but the Father's who sent me.
25 These things I have spoken to you, while staying with you.
26 But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and will bring to your mind all things, whatever I have said to you.
27 Peace I leave with you, my peace I give to you: not as the world gives, do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid."

### CHAPTER XV.

*Christ is the vine, the Father the gardener, and the disciples the*
*branches: the commandment of Christ concerning mutual love*
*is frequently repeated: the Apostles are the friends of*
*Christ, to whom he communicated his secrets,*
*and he chose them so that they might bring forth everlasting fruit:*
*he strengthens them against the hatred and persecutions*
*of the world: saying that the Jews have no excuse*
*for their sin.*

<margin>† Above 13:10.</margin>
1 **I** am the true vine: and my Father is the gardener.
2 Every branch in me that does not bear fruit, he will take away: and every one that bears fruit, he will prune, so that it may bring forth more fruit.
3 Now you are clean because of the word which I have spoken to you.

6 If anyone does not remain in me, he shall be cast out like a branch, and shall wither, and they shall gather him, and cast him into the fire, and he burns.
7 If you remain in me, and my words remain in you: you shall ask whatever you will, and it shall be done for you.
8 In this is my Father glorified, that you bring forth very much fruit, and become my disciples.
9 As the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love.
10 If you keep my commandments, you shall remain in my love, just as I also have kept my Father’s commandments, and remain in his love.
11 These things I have spoken to you, that my joy may be in you, and your joy may be filled.

### C A P T E R XIX.

*Jesus is scourged by Pilate, afflicted in various ways, and crowned with thorns; he is demanded for death. Examined again by Pilate, he shows that the governor's power over him comes only from above. The fearful Pilate sentences Jesus, whom he calls King of the Jews, to death. Jesus, carrying his own cross, is crucified between robbers; Pilate places a title above the cross, and the soldiers divide his garments, casting lots for his tunic. Jesus commends John to his mother, and his mother to John. Thirsting, he is given vinegar to drink; when all is finished, he gives up his spirit. The legs of the robbers are broken, but from Christ's opened side flow blood and water; his body, prepared with myrrh and aloes, is buried.*

---

1 Then Pilate therefore took Jesus and scourged <note>A brutal Roman punishment using a whip (flagrum) often embedded with metal or bone.</note> him.
2 And the soldiers, weaving a crown of thorns, placed it on his head: and they clothed him in a purple robe.
3 And they came to him, and said: Hail, King of the Jews: and they struck him with their hands.
4 Pilate therefore went out again, and said to them: Behold, I bring him out to you, so that you may know that I find no guilt <note>original: "causam," meaning a legal cause for charges</note> in him.
5 (Jesus then came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment.) And he said to them: Behold the man <note>original: "Ecce homo"</note>.

->### C H A P T E R  XX.<-

*Mary Magdalene comes first to the tomb, followed by Peter and John: she, weeping at the tomb, sees Angels, and finally recognizes Jesus: who, appearing to the Apostles, wishes them peace: and having shown his hands and side, gives them the Holy Spirit, that they may forgive and retain sins; appearing again to the unbelieving Thomas with the rest of the disciples, he offers his body to be touched, calling those blessed who have believed without seeing: many signs of Christ are not written in this book.*

1 **N**ow on the first day of the week <note>original: "Una sabbati" — the Sunday following the Jewish Sabbath</note>, Mary Magdalene came early, while it was still dark, to the tomb: and she saw the stone taken away from the tomb.
2 She ran, therefore, and came to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them: They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him.

4 And the two ran together, and that other disciple outran Peter, and came first to the tomb.

8 Then that other disciple, who had come first to the tomb, also entered: and he saw, and believed:
9 For as yet they did not understand the Scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.
10 Then the disciples went away again to their own homes.

->### C H A P T E R  XXI.<-

1 **A**fterward Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. And he manifested himself in this way:

### CHAPTER IV.

*After being held in custody, the Apostles are examined concerning the healing of the lame man; they show that salvation exists only in Christ, the cornerstone. They do not obey the leaders’ command to stop teaching in the name of Christ; once released, they pray and receive signs from the Holy Spirit. None of them held any personal property, but shared their value in common, just as Barnabas did by selling his field.*

1 While they were speaking to the people, the priests, the officer of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them,

2 Being annoyed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming the resurrection from the dead in Jesus:

3 And they laid hands on them and put them into custody until the next day, for it was already evening.

4 But many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of men grew to five thousand.

5 And it happened the next day that their leaders, elders, and scribes gathered in Jerusalem;

6 Including Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the high-priestly family.

7 And standing them in the middle, they questioned them: "By what power, or in what name, have you done this?"

8 Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: "Leaders of the people and elders, listen:

9 If we are being judged today for a good deed done to an infirm man, by which he has been made well,

10 Let it be known to all of you, and to all the people of Israel: that in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, by him this man stands before you whole.

### CHAPTER V.

*Ananias and his wife Sapphira sell a field and keep back part of the price: they deny this falsehood before Peter: because of this, at Peter's word, the wife is struck by sudden death after her husband: many signs are performed by the Apostles, and especially by Peter: they are led out of custody by an Angel, and when seized again, they refuse to stop preaching the name of Christ: by the advice of Gamaliel they are dismissed after being beaten, rejoicing that they were worthy to be scourged for the name of Christ, whom they continually proclaim.*

**A** certain man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold a field, 
2 and with his wife's knowledge, he kept back part of the price of the field: and bringing a certain portion, he laid it at the feet of the Apostles. 
3 But Peter said: "Ananias, why has Satan tempted your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit, and to keep back part of the price of the field? 
4 While it remained, did it not remain yours? And after it was sold, was it not in your power? Why have you conceived this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God." 
5 Hearing these words, Ananias fell down and breathed his last. And great fear came upon all who heard it. 
6 Then the young men rose up, removed him, and carrying him out, they buried him. 
7 It happened after an interval of about three hours that his wife, not knowing what had occurred, entered. 
8 Peter said to her: "Tell me, woman, did you sell the field for this much?" And she said: "Yes, for that much." 
9 Then Peter said to her: "Why have you agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they shall carry you out." 
10 Immediately she fell before his feet and breathed her last. When the young men entered, they found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her beside her husband. 
11 And great fear came upon the whole church, and upon all who heard these things. 
12 Moreover, by the hands of the Apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people. And they were all of one accord in Solomon's Portico. <note>A covered walkway on the east side of the Temple mount, a traditional place for teaching.</note>
13 But of the rest, no one dared to join them: yet the people magnified them. 
14 And the multitude of men and women believing in the Lord increased all the more, 
15 so much so that they brought the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and mats, so that as Peter came by, at least his shadow might fall upon any of them, and they might be delivered from their infirmities. 
16 A multitude from the neighboring cities around Jerusalem also gathered, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits: and they were all healed. 
17 Then the high priest rose up, and all who were with him (which is the sect of the Sadducees), and they were filled with jealousy: <note>original: 'haeresis Sadducæorum'. The Sadducees were a Jewish sect that denied the resurrection of the dead.</note>

39 But if it is of God, you cannot destroy it, lest perhaps you be found even to fight against God." And they agreed with him.

### CHAPTER VI.

> *The election of seven deacons as the number of believers increases daily: the intensity of Stephen, who performs signs and wonders, and against whom many Jews rise up: when they are unable to refute him, they attempt to overwhelm him with false witnesses.*

1 In those days, as the number of disciples was increasing, there arose a murmuring of the Greeks <note>The "Greeks" or Hellenists were Greek-speaking Jews.</note> against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.
2 So the Twelve, calling together the multitude of the disciples, said: "It is not right for us to neglect the word of God to serve tables."
3 "Therefore, brothers, look among yourselves for seven men of good reputation, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this task."
4 "But we will devote ourselves to prayer and the ministry of the word."
5 And the saying pleased the whole multitude. And they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicholas, a proselyte <note>A "proselyte" was a Gentile who had converted to Judaism.</note> from Antioch.
6 They presented these men before the Apostles; and after praying, they laid their hands upon them.
7 And the word of the Lord continued to spread, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem multiplied greatly; even a large crowd of priests became obedient to the faith.
8 Now Stephen, full of grace and fortitude, performed great wonders and signs among the people.
9 But some arose from the synagogue known as the Synagogue of the Libertines <note>The "Libertines" were likely "Freedmen"—Jews who had been enslaved by Romans and later liberated.</note>, and of the Cyrenians, and of the Alexandrians, and of those from Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen.
10 And they were not able to resist the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
11 Then they suborned <note>To "suborn" is to secretly bribe or induce someone to commit a crime, such as perjury.</note> men to say they had heard him speaking words of blasphemy against Moses and against God.
12 And so they stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes; and rushing upon him, they seized him and brought him into the council.
13 They set up false witnesses who said: "This man never ceases speaking words against this holy place and the law."
14 "For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the traditions which Moses handed down to us."
15 And all who sat in the council, looking intently at him, saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

### CHAPTER VIII.

> *In the persecution everyone is dispersed except the Apostles, as Saul devastates the Church: Philip converts many in Samaria, and among these he baptizes Simon the magician: Peter and John, sent by the apostles, obtain the Holy Spirit for the believing Samaritans through prayer and the laying on of hands: but Simon, wishing to buy the gift of the Holy Spirit with money, is harshly rebuked by Peter: Philip is sent by an Angel to the Eunuch; whom, when he had baptized him upon his believing, is carried away by the Spirit to Azotus.*
