<margin>† Exodus 20:17; Deuteronomy 5:21.</margin>
Far from it! But I did not know sin, except through the law: for I would not have known what it is to covet, unless the law had said: † Thou shalt not covet. <note>Paul uses the Tenth Commandment to illustrate how the Law defines moral boundaries.</note>
8 But sin, taking the opportunity through the commandment, worked in me every kind of covetousness. For without the law, sin was dead.
9 Once I was alive without the law. But when the commandment came, sin revived.
10 And I died: and the commandment, which was intended for life, I found to lead to death.
11 For sin, taking the opportunity through the commandment, seduced me, and through it, killed me.
<margin>† 1 Timothy 1:8.</margin>
12 † Therefore the law indeed is holy; and the commandment is holy, and just, and good.
13 Was that which is good, then, made death to me? Far from it! But sin, so that it might appear as sin, worked death in me through that which is good: so that through the commandment, sin might become sinful beyond measure.
14 For we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin. <note>The term "carnal" comes from the Latin *carnalis*, meaning "fleshly" or "of the senses."</note>
15 For I do not understand what I do: for I do not do the good that I want to do; but I do the evil that I hate.
16 But if I do that which I do not want, I agree with the law, that it is good.
17 So now it is no longer I who do it, but the sin that dwells within me.
18 For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, no good thing dwells. For the will to do good is present with me: but how to perform that which is good, I do not find.
19 For I do not do the good that I want: but the evil that I do not want, that is what I do.
20 But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but the sin that dwells in me.
21 I find then a law: that when I want to do good, evil is present within me.
22 For I delight in the law of God according to the inner man:
23 But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and making me a captive to the law of sin which is in my members.
24 Unhappy man that I am, who shall deliver me from the body of this death?
25 The grace of God, through Jesus Christ our Lord. Therefore, I myself with the mind serve the law of God; but with the flesh, the law of sin.

### C H A P T E R  V I I I .

->*He concludes that those grafted into Christ through baptism are free from all condemnation, those who do not follow the flesh, but the spirit which they have received: the spirit, I say, of adoption: which makes them sons of God and co-heirs of future glory with Christ. Toward the revelation of this glory, not only does the whole of creation aspire (being meanwhile subject to vanity), but also those who have received the first fruits of the spirit expect it with certain hope, the spirit strengthening them and instructing them in what ought to be prayed for. He also declares the incomparable love of God exhibited toward his own in Christ, asserting that nothing can separate them from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus.*<-

1 There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh.
2 For the law of the spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death.

<column-break/>

3 For what was impossible for the law, in that it was weakened through the flesh: God, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh,
4 So that the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.
5 For those who live according to the flesh, set their minds on the things of the flesh; but those who live according to the spirit, feel the things of the spirit.
6 For the wisdom of the flesh is death: but the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace.
7 Because the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God: for it is not subject to the law of God: nor indeed can it be.
8 For those who are in the flesh cannot please God.
9 But you are not in the flesh, but in the spirit: if indeed the spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to him.
10 But if Christ is in you: the body indeed is dead because of sin, but the spirit lives because of justification.
11 And if the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you: he who raised Jesus Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies, because of his Spirit dwelling within you.
12 Therefore, brothers, we are debtors not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh.
13 For if you live according to the flesh, you shall die: but if by the spirit you mortify the deeds of the flesh, you shall live. <note>To "mortify" means to put to death or subdue.</note>
14 For whoever are led by the spirit of God, they are the sons of God.
<margin>† 2 Timothy 1:7; † Galatians 4:5.</margin>
15 † For you have not received the spirit of servitude again in fear, but you have received the spirit of adoption of sons, in which we cry: Abba (Father). <note>original: "Abba (Pater)" - Paul uses the Aramaic word for Father followed by the Greek/Latin translation to show intimacy with God.</note>
16 For the Spirit himself bears witness to our spirit, that we are the children of God.
17 And if children, then heirs: heirs indeed of God, and co-heirs with Christ: if indeed we suffer with him, so that we may also be glorified with him.
18 For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come, which shall be revealed in us.
19 For the expectation of the creature waits for the revelation of the sons of God. <note>In this context, "creature" or "creation" refers to the entire natural world.</note>
20 For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected it in hope:
21 Because the creature itself shall also be delivered from the servitude of corruption, into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.
22 For we know that every creature groans and travails in pain even until now.
23 And not only it, but we ourselves also, having the first fruits of the spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption of the sons of God, the redemption of our body.
24 For we are saved by hope. But hope that is seen is not hope: for what a man sees, why does he hope for it?
25 But if we hope for that which we do not see: we wait for it with patience.
26 And in like manner, the spirit also helps our infirmity: for we do not know what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit himself asks for us with unutterable groans.
27 And he who searches the hearts knows what the Spirit desires: because he asks for the saints according to the will of God.

### CHAPTER IX.

->*Because of the ruin of the Jews, over which he greatly grieves, he asserts that the promises made by God to the sons of Abraham among the Israelites are not frustrated: namely, because those promises do not belong to all the physical descendants of Abraham, but only to those from among the Jews and Gentiles who are established as sons of Abraham through faith by God’s free election. God has mercy on whom he wills and hardens whom he wills. The Jews, however, because they sought righteousness not from faith in Christ (whom they rejected) but from the works of the law, were left in their iniquity, while the Gentiles were justified through faith in Christ.*<-

1 I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness to me in the Holy Spirit:
2 That I have great sadness and continual sorrow in my heart.

4 Who are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption as sons, and the glory, and the covenant, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises;
5 Whose are the fathers, and from whom is Christ according to the flesh, who is over all things, God blessed forever. Amen.

<margin>† Genesis 21:12.</margin>

<margin>† Galatians 4:28.</margin>

### CHAPTER X.

> The Apostle prays for the Jews, whom he asserts have a zeal for God and the law, but not according to knowledge: for, being ignorant that Christ is the end of the law, they sought righteousness from the works of the law. He speaks concerning the difference between the righteousness that comes from the works of the law and that which comes from faith, which is common to both Jew and Greek who believe in Christ: the faith of Christ has been preached everywhere on earth; while the Jews rejected it, the Gentiles received it.

**B**rothers, the desire of my heart indeed, and my prayer to God, is for them, for their salvation.
**2** For I bear witness to them that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
**3** For being ignorant of the righteousness of God, and seeking to establish their own, they have not submitted themselves to the righteousness of God.
**4** For Christ is the end of the law, for righteousness to everyone who believes. <note>The "end" (original: *finis*) here implies both the termination of the old legal system and the fulfillment or goal toward which the law was aiming.</note>
**5** <margin>† Lev. 18:5. Ezek. 20:11.</margin> For Moses wrote that the man who does the righteousness which is from the law shall live by it.
**6** <margin>† Deut. 30:12.</margin> But the righteousness which is from faith says this: Do not say in your heart: who shall ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down):
**7** <margin>† Deut. 30:14. <note>Modern Bibles typically cite Deuteronomy 30:13 for the "abyss" or "sea" reference.</note></margin> Or who shall descend into the abyss? (that is, to call Christ back from the dead).
**8** But what does the Scripture say? † The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart: this is the word of faith, which we preach.
**9** Because if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in your heart that God has raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
**10** For with the heart one believes unto righteousness; but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
**11** <margin>† Isaiah 28:16.</margin> For the Scripture says: † Everyone who believes in him shall not be put to shame.
**12** For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek: for the same Lord is over all, rich toward all who call upon him.
**13** <margin>† Joel 2:31. Acts 2:21. <note>The source refers to Joel 2:31 following the Vulgate numbering; in modern Bibles, this is Joel 2:32.</note></margin> † For everyone, whoever calls upon the name of the Lord, shall be saved.
**14** How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? Or how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher?
**15** <margin>† Isaiah 52:7. Nah. 1:15.</margin> And how shall they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: † How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the gospel of peace, of those who preach good things!
**16** <margin>† Isaiah 53:1. John 12:38.</margin> But not all obey the Gospel. For Isaiah says: † Lord, who has believed our report?
**17** Therefore faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.
**18** <margin>† Psalm 18:5. <note>Psalm 19:4 in modern Bibles.</note></margin> But I say: Have they not heard? † Indeed, their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
**19** <margin>† Deut. 32:21.</margin> But I say: Has Israel not known? First Moses says: † I will provoke you to jealousy by those who are not a nation; by a foolish nation I will send you into anger.
**20** <margin>† Isaiah 65:1.</margin> But Isaiah is bold and says: † I was found by those who did not seek me; I appeared openly to those who did not ask for me.
**21** <margin>† Isaiah 65:2.</margin> But to Israel he says: † All day long I have stretched out my hands to an unbelieving and contrary people.

### CHAPTER XI.

> God has preserved some of the Jewish people for himself through his free election, to be saved through faith in Christ, while the rest were left in their blindness because of unbelief according to the prophecies of the Prophets. The Gentiles were taken into their place by the free goodness of God, whom the Apostle warns not to boast against the Jews; and that the Jews, though deserted for a time, will at last be converted to Christ. He concludes by exclaiming at the incomprehensibility of divine wisdom.

**I** say then: Has God rejected his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
**2** God has not rejected his people, whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says concerning Elijah: how he pleads with God against Israel?
**3** <margin>† 3 Kings 19:10. <note>In the Vulgate, the books of Samuel and Kings are titled 1–4 Kings. This is 1 Kings 19 in modern translations.</note></margin> † Lord, they have killed your Prophets, they have torn down your altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.
**4** <margin>† 3 Kings 19:18.</margin> But what does the divine response say to him? † I have left for myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed their knees before Baal.
**5** So then at this time also, a remnant has been saved according to the election of grace.
**6** But if it is by grace, it is no longer by works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.
**7** What then? That which Israel sought, he has not obtained: but the election <note>Meaning the "elect" or the chosen group.</note> has obtained it; and the rest were blinded:
**8** <margin>† Isaiah 6:9. Matt. 13:14. John 12:40. Acts 28:26.</margin> As it is written: † God has given them a spirit of stupor: eyes so they might not see, and ears so they might not hear, until this very day.
**9** <margin>† Psalm 68:23. <note>Psalm 69:22 in modern Bibles.</note></margin> And David says: † Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumbling block, and a retribution to them.
**10** Let their eyes be darkened so they may not see; and bow down their back always.
**11** I say then: Have they stumbled so as to fall? God forbid. But by their offense, salvation has come to the Gentiles so as to provoke them to jealousy.
**12** Now if their offense is the riches of the world, and their diminishing the riches of the Gentiles: how much more their fullness?
**13** For I say to you Gentiles: As long as I am indeed the Apostle to the Gentiles, I will honor my ministry.
**14** If in any way I may provoke my own flesh <note>Meaning his own people, the Jews.</note> to jealousy, and save some of them.
**15** For if the loss of them is the reconciliation of the world: what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead?
**16** For if the first offering is holy, so is the whole mass; and if the root is holy, so are the branches. <note>Paul uses the metaphor of "firstfruits" (original: *delibatio*) and the "dough" (original: *massa*) to show how a consecrated part affects the whole.</note>
**17** And if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive tree, were grafted in among them, and became a partner of the root and the fatness of the olive tree,
**18** Do not boast against the branches. But if you do boast: you do not support the root, but the root supports you.
**19** You will say then: The branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.
**20** Well said; because of unbelief they were broken off: but you stand by faith: do not be high-minded, but fear.
**21** For if God did not spare the natural branches: perhaps he may not spare you either.
**22** Behold then the goodness and the severity of God:

**23** But those others also, if they do not persist in unbelief, will be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again.

## CHAPTER XII.

*He instructs the Romans that, drawn away from the vanity of the world, they should give themselves wholly to God; not puffing themselves up on account of the gifts they have received, nor transgressing their limits, but — after the manner of members of the same body — ordering all things toward the benefit of their neighbor, and doing good even to their enemies.*

<margin>† Philippians 1:28.</margin>
**1** I beseech you therefore, brothers, through the mercy of God, that you present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God — your reasonable service. <note>The phrase "reasonable service" (original: *rationabile obsequium*) suggests worship that is fitting to rational beings — an offering of mind and will, not merely of animal sacrifice.</note>
<margin>† Ephesians 1:17. 1 Thessalonians 4:3.</margin>
**2** And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind: that you may discern what the will of God is — good, and well-pleasing, and perfect.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 12:11.</margin>
**3** For I say, through the grace that has been given to me, to all who are among you: Do not think more highly of yourselves than you ought to think, but think with soberness; according to the measure of faith that God has dealt to each one.
<margin>Ephesians 4:7.</margin>
**4** For just as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same function:
**5** So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.
**6** Having gifts, then, that differ according to the grace that has been given to us: whether prophecy, in proportion to faith;

<column-break/>

**7** Or ministry, in ministering; or one who teaches, in teaching;
**8** One who exhorts, in exhortation; one who gives, in simplicity; one who leads, in diligence; one who shows mercy, in cheerfulness.

**9** Let love be without pretense. Hate what is evil; hold fast to what is good.
<margin>† Ephesians 4:3. 1 Peter 2:17.</margin>
**10** Love one another with brotherly affection; in honor, showing the way for one another;
**11** Not slack in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
**12** Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; persevering in prayer;
<margin>† Hebrews 13:2. 1 Peter 4:9.</margin>
**13** Sharing in the needs of the saints; pursuing hospitality.
**14** Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse.
**15** Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
**16** Being of the same mind toward one another; not setting your mind on high things, but going along with the humble. Do not be wise in your own estimation.
<margin>† 2 Corinthians 8:21. Hebrews 12:14.</margin>
**17** Repaying no one evil for evil; providing good things not only before God, but also before all people.
**18** If it is possible, as much as lies within you, be at peace with all people.
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 28:1–3. Matthew 5:39. Deuteronomy 32:35. Hebrews 10:30.</margin>
**19** Do not avenge yourselves, dearly beloved, but give place to wrath; for it is written: *Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord.* <note>original: "Mihi vindicta; ego retribuam, dicit Dominus"</note>
<margin>† Proverbs 25:21.</margin>
**20** But if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for in doing this, you will heap coals of fire upon his head. <note>The image of "heaping coals of fire" upon an enemy's head (original: *carbones ignis congeres super caput ejus*) is generally understood as inducing in them a burning shame and remorse — an act of kindness that overcomes hostility more powerfully than retaliation.</note>
**21** Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

## CHAPTER XIII.

*He urges those of lower rank to obey their superiors, even for conscience's sake — even when those superiors hold only civil authority — and to render to all what is owed to them. On love of neighbor, to which the whole law is reduced. And on the time of grace: that with the darkness of the law now past, they should lay aside vices and embrace the virtues of Christ.*

<margin>Wisdom 6:4. 1 Peter 2:13.</margin>
**1** Let every soul be subject to the higher powers. For there is no power except from God; and those that exist are ordained by God.
**2** Therefore whoever resists the power resists the ordinance of God. And those who resist bring condemnation upon themselves.
**3** For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to evil. Do you wish not to fear the power? Do good, and you shall have praise from it.
**4** For it is the minister of God to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for it does not bear the sword without reason. For it is the minister of God: an avenger to execute wrath upon the one who does evil.
**5** Therefore it is necessary to be subject — not only on account of wrath, but also on account of conscience.
**6** For this reason you also pay tribute: for they are the ministers of God, serving in this very thing.
<margin>† Matthew 22:21.</margin>
**7** Render therefore to all what is owed to them: to whom tribute is due, tribute; to whom tax, tax; to whom fear, fear; to whom honor, honor.
**8** Owe no one anything, except to love one another: for whoever loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.
<margin>† Exodus 20:14. Deuteronomy 5:18. Leviticus 19:18.</margin>
**9** For: *You shall not commit adultery. You shall not kill. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness. You shall not covet.* And if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: *You shall love your neighbor as yourself.*

### CHAPTER XIV.

*Those who are stronger in faith ought to cherish those who are still weak and not look down on them; neither the former nor the latter should judge anyone because of a distinction in foods or days, knowing that we all have the same Lord, for whom we live and die, and to whom each will render an account for himself. Although no food is now unclean, no one should eat anything if it causes a brother to stumble or goes against his own conscience.*

**1** Now, welcome the one who is weak in faith, but not for the purpose of disputing over his thoughts.
**2** For one believes he may eat all things; but he who is weak, let him eat vegetables.
**3** Let not him who eats despise him who does not eat; and let not him who does not eat judge him who eats; for God has accepted him.
<margin>† James 4:13.</margin>
**4** † Who are you to judge another man’s servant? To his own lord he stands or falls; but he shall stand, for God is powerful enough to make him stand.
**5** For one man judges one day above another; another man judges every day alike: let everyone be fully convinced in his own mind.
**6** He who regards the day, regards it for the Lord. And he who eats, eats for the Lord; for he gives thanks to God. And he who does not eat, for the Lord he does not eat, and gives thanks to God.
**7** For none of us lives to himself, and no one dies to himself.
**8** For whether we live, we live for the Lord; or whether we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or die, we are the Lord's.
**9** For to this end Christ died and rose again: that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.

**14** I know, and am confident in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean <note>original: "commune," meaning "common" or ritually impure in a Jewish context</note> of itself; except to him who thinks anything to be unclean, to him it is unclean.

### CHAPTER XV.

*The stronger ought to bear with and alleviate the imperfections of the weak, striving not for their own benefit but for the utility and mutual peace of their neighbors. # THE FIRST EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL
### TO THE CORINTHIANS.

### CHAPTER ONE.

> *Paul gives thanks to God for the gifts given to the Corinthians: furthermore he grieves that there were schisms among them regarding those who baptized them, rejoicing that he was sent to preach the Gospel and baptized few: showing also that the wisdom of the world is rejected, and the simple are chosen: just as life and salvation are in the death of Christ, whose preaching is judged as foolishness to the world, but to those who believe, it is power and wisdom: for this reason God chose the contemptible things of the world, lest anyone should glory in themselves.*

**1** Paul, called to be an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
**2** To the church of God which is at Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, in every place of theirs and ours.
**3** Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
**4** I give thanks to my God always for you for the grace of God, which is given to you in Christ Jesus:
**5** Because in all things you are made rich in him, in every word, and in all knowledge:
**6** Just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you:
**7** So that nothing is lacking to you in any grace, as you wait for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
**8** Who will also confirm you until the end without crime <note>original: "sine crimine," usually translated in a legal or moral sense as blameless or beyond reproach</note>, in the day of the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
<margin>† 1 Thessalonians 5:24.</margin>
**9** † God is faithful: by whom you were called into the fellowship of his son Jesus Christ our Lord.
**10** Now I beseech you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: that you all say the same thing, and that there be no schisms among you: but that you be perfect in the same mind, and in the same judgment.
**11** For it has been signified to me concerning you, my brothers, by those who are of Chloe, that there are contentions among you.
**12** Now I say this, that every one of you says: I indeed am of Paul: but I am of Apollo: but I am of Cephas <note>The Aramaic name for the Apostle Peter</note>: but I am of Christ.
<margin>† Acts 18:24.</margin>
**13** Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
**14** I give thanks to God that I baptized none of you, except Crispus and Gaius:
<margin>† Acts 18:8.</margin>
**15** Lest any should say that you were baptized in my name.
**16** And I also baptized the household of Stephanas: otherwise I do not know if I baptized any other:
**17** For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach the gospel: <margin>† 2 Peter 1:16. Below 1:4, 13.</margin> † not in the wisdom of words, lest the cross of Christ should be made void.
**18** For the word of the cross, to those who are perishing, in-

<column-break/>

deed is foolishness: but to those who are being saved, that is to us, † it is the power of God.
<margin>† Romans 1:16. † Isaiah 29:14. † Isaiah 33:18.</margin>
**19** For it is written: † I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will reject the prudence of the prudent.
**20** † Where is the wise man? where is the scribe? where is the searcher <note>original: "conquisitor," a researcher or debater</note> of this world? Has God not made the wisdom of this world foolish?
**21** For because in the wisdom of God the world did not know God through wisdom: it pleased God through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe.
**22** For both the Jews ask for signs, and the Greeks seek for wisdom:
**23** But we preach Christ crucified: to the Jews indeed a scandal, but to the Gentiles foolishness:
**24** But to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God, and the wisdom of God:
**25** Because that which is foolish of God is wiser than men: and that which is weak of God is stronger than men.
**26** For see your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many are powerful, not many are noble:
**27** But God has chosen the foolish things of the world, to confound the wise: and God has chosen the weak things of the world, to confound the strong:
**28** And the base things of the world, and the contemptible things God has chosen, and those things which are not, that he might destroy those things which are:
**29** So that no flesh should glory in his sight.
**30** But of him you are in Christ Jesus, who is made unto us wisdom from God, and justice, and sanctification, and redemption:
<margin>† Jeremiah 23:5. † Jeremiah 9:23, 24. 2 Corinthians 10:17.</margin>
**31** So that as it is written: † He that glories, let him glory in the Lord.

### CHAPTER II.

> *Paul shows that he preached Christ, and him crucified, to the Corinthians with great modesty and simple words: although he spoke wisdom also to the perfect, a wisdom hidden from the world: which can only be known by the spirit of God: for the <term>natural man</term> <note>original: "animalis," referring to one governed by the soul/senses rather than the Spirit</note> does not perceive those things which are [of the Spirit].*

**1** And I, when I came to you, brothers, came † not in loftiness of speech, or of wisdom, announcing to you the testimony of Christ.
<margin>† Above 1:17.</margin>
**2** For I did not judge myself to know anything among you, except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
**3** † And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling.
<margin>† Acts 18:1.</margin>
**4** And my speech, and my preaching, was not in the persuasive words of human wisdom, but in the showing of the spirit and of power: <margin>† 2 Peter 1:16.</margin>
**5** That your faith might not be in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
**6** But we speak wisdom among the perfect: yet a wisdom not of this world, nor of the princes of this world, who are being destroyed:

**7** But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, which is hidden, which God predestined before the ages for our glory,
**8** Which none of the princes of this age knew: for if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory.

->### C A P T E R III.<-

->*Paul could not preach the hidden mysteries of the faith to the Corinthians while they were still worldly: for they were arguing over those who were only ministers, since only God can give the increase of grace and virtues, and Christ is the foundation of the faith: upon which, how one builds—well or poorly—will be revealed on the day of judgment. The temple of God, which we are, must not be violated, nor should one glory in the ministers of God.*<-

**1** And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to worldly ones <note>original: "carnalibus," literally "fleshly" or "of the flesh"</note>. As to little children in Christ.
**2** I gave you milk to drink, not solid food: for you were not yet able to bear it: nor indeed are you able now: for you are still worldly.
**3** For while there is jealousy and contention among you, are you not worldly, and walking according to the way of man?
**4** For when one says: I am of Paul; and another: I am of Apollos: are you not merely men? What then is Apollos? and what is Paul?
**5** Ministers of him whom you have believed, and to each as the Lord has given.
**6** I planted, Apollos watered: but God gave the increase.
**7** And so neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters: but God, who gives the increase.
<margin>† Psalm 61:13; Matthew 16:27; Romans 2:6; Galatians 6:5</margin>
**8** † Now he who plants and he who waters are one. † And each shall receive his own reward according to his own labor.
**9** For we are God's helpers: you are God's husbandry <note>or "cultivated field"</note>, you are God's building.
**10** According to the grace of God which was given to me, as a wise architect <note>original: "architectus," here meaning a master builder</note> I have laid the foundation: but another builds upon it. But let each one see how he builds upon it.

<column-break/>

**11** For no one can lay any other foundation than that which has been laid, which is Christ Jesus.

**15** If anyone's work is burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved, yet so as through fire.

<margin>† Job 5:13</margin>

<margin>† Psalm 93:11</margin>
**20** And again: † The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain.
**21** Therefore let no one glory in men.
**22** For all things are yours, whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas <note>the Apostle Peter</note>, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come: for all things are yours:
**23** And you are Christ's: and Christ is God's.

->### C A P T E R IV.<-

->*One must not judge the ministers of God rashly: the Corinthians are reproved for glorying in their ministers and the gifts they received as if they had them of themselves; and by exalting themselves they even despised the Apostles, even though Paul had fathered them in Christ: he says he will soon come to Corinth to refute the false apostles.*<-

<margin>2 Corinthians 6:4</margin>
**1** Let a man so account of us as ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God.
**2** Here it is required among stewards that a man be found faithful.
**3** But to me it is a very small thing to be judged by you, or by a human day <note>original: "humano die," an idiom for a human court or judgment</note>: but neither do I judge myself.
**4** For I am conscious of nothing against myself: yet I am not justified by this: but he who judges me is the Lord.
**5** Therefore do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes: who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts: and then shall each have praise from God.
**6** Now these things, brothers, I have figuratively applied to myself and Apollos for your sakes: that in us you might learn not to be puffed up for one against another, beyond what is written.
**7** For who distinguishes you? And what do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you glory as if you had not received it?
**8** Now you are saturated, now you have become rich: you reign without us, and I wish that you did reign, so that we also might reign with you.
**9** For I think that God has shown us Apostles last, as those destined for death: because we are made a spectacle to the world, and to Angels, and to men.

### CHAPTER V.

*He reproves the Corinthians because they tolerated a man living publicly in incest; though absent, he delivers the man to Satan, advising them that once the leaven of vice is purged, they should celebrate a pure Passover; he does not want them to associate with Christians who are openly criminal.*

<margin>Leviticus 18:7-8 & 20:11</margin>
**1** It is heard everywhere that there is sexual immorality among you, and such immorality as is not even among the Gentiles, that someone should have his father’s wife.
**2** And you are puffed up with pride, and have not rather mourned, so that he who has done this deed might be taken away from your midst.
<margin>† Colossians 2:5</margin>
**3** † For I indeed, absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged as though present him who has so acted,
**4** In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you are gathered together with my spirit, by the power of our Lord Jesus,
**5** To deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
<margin>† Galatians 3:9</margin>
**6** Your glorying is not good. † Do you not know that a little leaven corrupts the whole mass?
**7** Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new dough, just as you are unleavened. For Christ our Passover <note>original: "Pascha," referring to the sacrificial lamb of the Passover</note> has been sacrificed.
**8** Therefore let us feast, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
**9** I wrote to you in a letter: Do not associate with the sexually immoral.
**10** Not at all meaning the immoral people of this world, or the greedy, or robbers, or idolaters; otherwise you would have to leave this world altogether.

<column-break/>

**11** But now I have written to you not to associate with anyone who is called a "brother" if he is sexually immoral, or greedy, or an idolater, or a slanderer, or a drunkard, or a robber; with such a person, do not even eat.
**12** For what have I to do with judging those who are outside? Do you not judge those who are within?
**13** For those who are outside, God will judge. Put away the evil person from among yourselves.

### CHAPTER VI.

*He corrects them for contending in judgment before a pagan judge; listing certain sins in which those involved will not possess the kingdom of God; he says some things are permitted that are not expedient; and for various reasons he shows that sexual immorality must be avoided.*

**1** Does any of you, having a matter against another, dare to be judged before the unjust, and not before the saints?
**2** Or do you not know that the saints shall judge this world? And if the world shall be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?
**3** Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more the things of this life?
**4** If therefore you have judgments regarding the things of this life, appoint those who are least esteemed in the Church to judge them.
**5** I speak this to your shame. Is it so that there is not one wise man among you who is able to judge between his brothers?
**6** But brother goes to law with brother, and that before unbelievers?
<margin>† Matt. 5:39; Luke 6:29; † Rom. 12:17</margin>
**7** † Now indeed there is altogether a fault among you, because you have lawsuits between yourselves. Why do you not rather take the injury? Why do you not rather suffer the fraud?
**8** But you do the injury and you defraud, and that to your brothers.
<margin>† 1 Thess. 4:6</margin>
**9** Do you not know that the unjust shall not possess the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers,
**10** Nor the effeminate, nor those who lie with men, nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor robbers shall possess the kingdom of God.
**11** And such were some of you; but you are washed, but you are sanctified, but you are justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in the Spirit of our God.
**12** All things are lawful for me, but not all things are expedient. All things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.
**13** Food is for the belly, and the belly for food; but God shall destroy both it and them. Now the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
**14** And God has both raised up the Lord, and will raise us up by his power.
**15** Do you not know that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them the members of a harlot? God forbid.
<margin>† Gen. 2:24; Matt. 19:5; Mark 10:8; Eph. 5:31</margin>
**16** Or do you not know that he who is joined to a harlot is made one body? † For they shall be, he says, two in one flesh.
**17** But he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.
**18** Shun sexual immorality. Every sin that a man does is outside the body; but he who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.

### CHAPTER VII.

*Paul instructs the Corinthians concerning marriage, its use and indissoluble bond, recommending celibacy to the unmarried; and how a believer should conduct themselves with an unbelieving spouse; and that everyone should remain in the state of life in which they were called to the faith: he prefers virginity to marriage: saying a wife is free when her husband is dead to marry whom she wishes, provided it is in the Lord.*

**1** Now concerning the things about which you wrote to me: It is good for a man not to touch a woman.
**2** But because of the risk of fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband.
<margin>† 1 Peter 3:7.</margin>
**3** † Let the husband render the debt <note>original: "debitum," referring to the "marital debt" or the obligation of sexual intimacy within marriage</note> to his wife, and likewise the wife to the husband.
**4** The wife does not have power over her own body, but the husband. And likewise the husband does not have power over his own body, but the wife.
**5** Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by consent for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer; and return together again, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
**6** But I say this by way of concession, not as a command.
**7** For I wish that you all were even as I myself am; but every man has his own gift from God, one in this way, and another in that.
**8** But I say to the unmarried and to the widows: It is good for them if they remain as I am.
**9** But if they cannot exercise self-control, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn <note>referring to burning with passion or desire</note>.
<margin>
† Matt. 5:32 & 19:9.
Mark 10:7.
Luke 16:18.
</margin>
**10** But to those who are joined in marriage, I command, not I, but the Lord: † that the wife should not depart from her husband.
**11** But if she does depart, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband. And let the husband not put away his wife.
**12** For to the rest I speak, not the Lord. If any brother has an unbelieving wife, and she consents to live with him, let him not put her away.
**13** And if any woman has an unbelieving husband, and he consents to live with her, let her not put away her husband.
**14** For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through the believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through the believing husband; otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
**15** But if the unbeliever departs, let them depart; for a brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases; but God has called us in peace.
**16** For how do you know, O wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, O husband, whether you will save your wife?
**17** But as the Lord has distributed to every man, as God has called every man, so let him walk; and so I teach in all the churches.
**18** Was anyone called being circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Was anyone called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.

**20** † Let every man remain in the same calling in which he was called.

**24** Brethren, let every man remain with God in the state in which he was called.
**25** Now concerning virgins I have no commandment of the Lord; but I give my advice, as one who has obtained mercy from the Lord to be faithful.
**26** I think therefore that this is good because of the present necessity, that it is good for a man so to be.
**27** Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be loosed. Are you loosed from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
**28** But if you take a wife, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned; nevertheless, such shall have tribulation in the flesh. But I spare you.

**31** And they that use this world, as though they used it not; for the fashion <note>original: "figura," the outward form or appearance</note> of this world is passing away.
**32** But I would have you without anxiety. He that is without a wife is anxious for the things of the Lord, how he may please God.
**33** But he that is with a wife is anxious for the things of the world, how he may please his wife, and he is divided.
**34** And the unmarried woman and the virgin think on the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But she that is married thinks on the things of the world, how she may please her husband.

**37** For he who has stood firm in his heart, having no necessity, but having power over his own will, and has judged this in his heart, to keep his virgin, does well.
**38** Therefore, both he that gives his virgin in marriage does well; and he that does not give her does better.

**39** † A woman is bound by the law as long as her husband lives; but if her husband falls asleep <note>a common biblical euphemism for death</note>, she is at liberty; let her marry whom she will, only in the Lord.
**40** But she will be more blessed if she remains as she is, according to my advice; and I think that I also have the Spirit of God.

->TO THE CORINTHIANS<-

## CHAPTER VIII.

*Although eating food sacrificed to idols is not in itself unlawful, since an idol has no real power or authority, such things should not be eaten if it goes against one's conscience or causes the weak to stumble; for eating or not eating does not make a person better.*

---

**1** Now concerning those things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
**2** If anyone thinks he knows something, he does not yet know it as he ought to know.
**3** But if anyone loves God, he is known by Him.
**4** Regarding the eating of foods sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God but one.
**5** For even if there are those called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (as indeed there are many "gods" and many "lords"),
**6** yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we in Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we through Him.
**7** But not everyone has this knowledge. For some, even until now, with a conscience accustomed to the idol, eat it as something sacrificed to an idol (<term>idolothytum</term> <note>original: "idolothytum," meaning food that has been ritually offered to a pagan deity</note>); and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
**8** Food does not commend us to God. For neither if we eat are we better off, nor if we do not eat are we worse off.
**9** But take care lest perhaps this liberty of yours becomes a stumbling block to the weak.
**10** For if someone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, since it is weak, be "built up" <note>Paul uses "built up" ironically here; the person is being encouraged to do something they believe is wrong</note> to eat food sacrificed to idols?
<margin>† Romans 14:15</margin>
**11** † And shall the weak brother perish through your knowledge, the one for whom Christ died?
**12** Thus, by sinning against the brothers and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
<margin>† Romans 14:21</margin>
**13** † Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat again, lest I cause my brother to stumble.

## CHAPTER IX.

*Paul did not accept a living from the Corinthians to whom he preached, so that he might remove every occasion for offense, even though he proves through many arguments that this was lawful for him. Instead, he adapts himself to every situation to lead more people to the worship of God. He exhorts the Corinthians to imitate those who run in a race or compete in a contest, saying that he also disciplines his own body.*

---

**1** Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
**2** Even if I am not an apostle to others, yet I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
**3** My defense to those who examine me is this:
**4** Do we not have the power to eat and to drink?
**5** Do we not have the power to take along a sister-woman <note>original: "mulierem sororem," likely referring to a Christian wife or a woman assisting in the ministry</note>, as do the rest of the apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas <note>Cephas is the Aramaic name for the Apostle Peter</note>?

<column-break/>

**6** Or is it only I and Barnabas who do not have the power to refrain from manual labor?
**7** Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not drink of the milk of the flock?
**8** Do I say these things according to human authority? Or does the Law not also say these things?
<margin>† Deuteronomy 25:4; 1 Timothy 5:18</margin>
**9** For it is written in the Law of Moses: † You shall not muzzle the ox while it treads out the grain. Is God concerned about oxen?
**10** Or does He say this entirely for our sake? Indeed, these things were written for us: because he who plows ought to plow in hope, and he who threshes, in hope of receiving the fruit.
<margin>† Romans 15:27</margin>
**11** † If we have sown spiritual things for you, is it a great thing if we reap your material things?
**12** If others share in this power over you, why not we even more? But we have not used this power; instead, we endure all things, lest we should give any hindrance to the Gospel of Christ.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 18:1</margin>
**13** † Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat what comes from the temple, and those who serve the altar share in the offerings of the altar?
**14** So also the Lord ordained for those who announce the Gospel to live by the Gospel.
**15** But I have used none of these things. Nor have I written these things so that they might be done for me; for it would be better for me to die than for anyone to make my glorying void.
**16** For if I preach the Gospel, it is no glory to me; for necessity is laid upon me. For woe is unto me if I do not preach the Gospel!
**17** For if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, a stewardship has been entrusted to me.
**18** What then is my reward? That in preaching the Gospel, I may offer the Gospel free of charge, so as not to abuse my power in the Gospel.
**19** For though I was free from all, I made myself the servant of all, that I might win more people.
**20** And to the Jews I became as a Jew, that I might win the Jews.
**21** To those who are under the Law, as though I were under the Law (though I myself was not under the Law), that I might win those who were under the Law. To those who were without the Law, as though I were without the Law (though I was not without the law of God, but was in the law of Christ), that I might win those who were without the Law.
**22** To the weak I became weak, that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all men, that I might save all.
**23** And I do all things for the sake of the Gospel, that I may become a partaker of it.
**24** Do you not know that those who run in a race (<term>stadium</term>) all run, but only one receives the prize (<term>bravium</term>)? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.
**25** Everyone who competes in a contest abstains from all things; they indeed to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible one.
**26** Therefore I run in this way, not as if aimlessly; I fight in this way, not as one beating the air.
**27** But I punish my body and bring it into subjection, lest perhaps after I have preached to others, I myself should become disqualified (<term>reprobus</term> <note>original: "reprobus," meaning cast away or failing the test</note>).

## CHAPTER X.

*By calling to mind the ungrateful Jews who were frequently punished by God for various sins, he deters these [the Corinthians] from similar ones: concerning human temptation, and God’s help in temptations: not only must idolatry be avoided, but also the table of those who eat foods sacrificed to idols; both because by this they seem to yield something to idols, and because they are a scandal to the weaker ones.*

<margin>Exodus 13, 23; Numbers 21</margin>
**1** For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea:
**2** And all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea:
<margin>Exodus 14:22</margin>
**3** And all ate the same spiritual food <note>This refers to the "Manna" provided to the Israelites in the desert.</note>.
<margin>Exodus 16:15</margin>
**4** And all drank the same spiritual drink: (for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them: and the rock was Christ)
<margin>Exodus 17:6</margin>
**5** But God was not well pleased with most of them: for they were struck down in the desert.
<margin>Numbers 10, 11</margin>
**6** Now these things were done as figures <note>original: "in figura," meaning these historical events serve as symbols or warnings</note> for us, so that we should not be desirers of evil things, just as they also lusted.
<margin>Numbers 26:64, 65</margin>
**7** Nor should you become idolaters, as some of them were; just as it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
<margin>Psalm 105:14; Exodus 32:6</margin>
**8** Nor let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
<margin>Numbers 25:1</margin>
**9** Nor let us tempt Christ: as some of them tempted Him, and perished by serpents.
<margin>Numbers 21:5, 6</margin>
**10** Nor should you murmur, as some of them murmured, and perished by the destroyer <note>original: "exterminatore," referring to the angel of death or destruction</note>.
<margin>Numbers 11:1, 14:1</margin>
**11** Now all these things happened to them in figure: and they are written for our correction, upon whom the ends of the ages have come.
**12** Therefore, let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall.
**13** Let no temptation seize you except what is human: for God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted beyond what you are able; but with the temptation He will also provide a way out <note>original: "proventum," literally an outcome or issue</note> so that you may be able to endure it.
**14** For this reason, my most dear ones, flee from the worship of idols:
**15** I speak as to wise men; judge for yourselves what I say.
**16** The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the participation <note>original: "communicatio," a sharing or communion</note> in the blood of Christ? And the bread which we break, is it not the participation in the body of the Lord?
**17** Since there is one bread, we who are many are one body, all of us who partake of that one bread.
**18** Look at Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants of the altar?
**19** What then? Do I say that what is sacrificed to idols is anything? Or that an idol is anything?
**20** But the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons, and not to God. And I do not want you to become associates of demons: you cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons:
**21** You cannot be partakers of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons.

## CHAPTER XI.

*A man should pray with his head uncovered, but a woman with it covered: he rebukes the Corinthians because they did not wait for one another to celebrate the Lord's Supper, but were divided among themselves: meanwhile reporting the institution of the Sacrament of the Eucharist by Christ, and the crime and punishment of those approaching it unworthily.*

**3** But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ: the head of the woman, the man; and the head of Christ, God.
**4** Every man praying or prophesying with his head covered dishonors his head.
**5** But every woman praying or prophesying with her head not covered dishonors her head: for it is the same as if she were shaved.
**6** For if a woman is not covered, let her hair be cut off. But if it is disgraceful for a woman to have her hair cut or to be shaved, let her cover her head.
<margin>Genesis 1:26</margin>
**7** A man indeed ought not to cover his head: since he is the image and glory of God, but the woman is the glory of the man.
**8** For the man is not from the woman, but the woman from the man.
<margin>Genesis 2:23</margin>
**9** For indeed the man was not created for the woman, but the woman for the man.
**10** Therefore the woman ought to have power <note>This "power" refers to a sign of authority or a veil.</note> over her head because of the angels.
**11** Nevertheless, neither is the man without the woman, nor the woman without the man, in the Lord.
**12** For as the woman is from the man, so also is the man through the woman: but all things are from God.
**13** Judge for yourselves: is it proper for a woman not covered to pray to God?

### CHAPTER XII.

*Various spiritual gifts of the same Holy Spirit are given, so that in the manner of a human body each person may perform his own office, and knowing that everyone needs each other’s help, they may cherish one another: and so Christ provided for his Church regarding the various states of men.*

1 Now concerning spiritual things, I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers.
2 You know that when you were Gentiles, you went to dumb idols, led as you were.

5 And there are divisions of ministries, but the same Lord.

9 To another faith in the same Spirit: to another the grace of healings in the one Spirit:
10 To another the working of miracles <note>original: "virtutum," literally "powers"</note>, to another prophecy, to another the discerning of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of speeches.

# CHAPTER XIII.

*He shows the necessity of charity, its duties, its permanence, and its excellence above faith and hope, and the other gifts of God.*

1 If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not charity <note>original: "charitatem," often translated as "love" in modern contexts, but historically "charity" implies a divinely inspired love for God and neighbor</note>, I have become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.
2 And if I should have prophecy, and should know all mysteries, and all knowledge: and if I should have all faith so that I could move mountains, but have not charity, I am nothing.
3 And if I should distribute all my goods to feed the poor, and if I should deliver my body to be burned, but have not charity, it profits me nothing.
4 Charity is patient, it is kind: Charity does not envy, it does not act wrongly, it is not puffed up with pride,
5 It is not ambitious, it does not seek its own, it is not provoked to anger, it thinks no evil,
6 It does not rejoice over iniquity, but rejoices with the truth:
7 It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
8 Charity never fails: whether prophecies shall be made void, or tongues shall cease, or knowledge shall be destroyed.
9 For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.
10 But when that which is perfect has come, that which is in part shall be done away.
11 When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child. But when I became a man, I did away with the things of a child.
12 We see now through a mirror in a riddle <note>original: "in ænigmate," referring to an obscure or dim reflection</note>: but then face to face. Now I know in part: but then I shall know even as I am known.
13 And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity.

---

# CHAPTER XIV.

*He says the gift of tongues is inferior to the gift of prophecy; it is useless if there is no one to interpret: he therefore gives them a rule to use these gifts in an orderly way: and he commands women to be silent in the churches.*

1 Follow after charity, be zealous for spiritual gifts: but especially that you may prophesy.
2 For he who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men, but to God: for no one understands <note>literally "hears"</note>. But in spirit he speaks mysteries.
3 But he who prophesies speaks to men for edification, and exhortation, and consolation.
4 He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself: but he who prophesies edifies the Church of God.
5 I wish that you all spoke in tongues: but rather that you prophesied. For greater is he who prophesies than he who speaks in tongues:

<column-break/>

unless perhaps he interprets, so that the Church may receive edification.
6 But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues; what shall I profit you, unless I speak to you either in revelation, or in knowledge, or in prophecy, or in doctrine?
7 Even things without life that give a sound, whether a pipe or a harp, unless they give a distinction in the sounds; how shall it be known what is piped or harped?
8 For if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself for battle?
9 So also you, unless you utter by the tongue a plain speech; how shall it be known what is said? For you will be speaking into the air.
10 There are, for example, so many kinds of languages in this world: and none is without its own sound.
11 If then I do not know the power of the voice, I shall be a barbarian <note>original: "barbarus," meaning a foreigner or someone who speaks an unintelligible language</note> to him to whom I speak: and he who speaks shall be a barbarian to me.
12 So you also, since you are zealots for spirits, seek that you may abound to the edification of the Church.
13 And therefore let him who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
14 For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is without fruit.
15 What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, I will pray also with the mind: I will sing with the spirit, I will sing also with the mind.
16 Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit: how shall he who occupies the place of the unlearned <note>original: "idiotæ," referring to a layperson or someone not trained in these spiritual gifts</note> say "Amen" to your blessing? Since he does not know what you are saying.
17 For you indeed give thanks well: but the other is not edified.
18 I thank my God that I speak in the tongue of all of you.
19 But in the Church I would rather speak five words with my understanding, so that I may instruct others also, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
20 Brothers, do not become children in your senses, but be like infants in malice: but in your senses be perfect.
<margin> † Isaiah 28:11.</margin>
21 In the law it is written: † That in other tongues and other lips I will speak to this people: and even so they will not hear me, says the Lord.
22 Therefore tongues are for a sign, not to believers, but to unbelievers: but prophecy is not for unbelievers, but for believers.
23 If therefore the whole Church comes together into one place, and all speak in tongues, and there come in unlearned persons or unbelievers, will they not say that you are mad?
24 But if all prophesy, and there comes in an unbeliever or an unlearned person, he is convinced by all, he is judged by all:
25 The secrets of his heart are made manifest, and so falling on his face he will adore God, declaring that God is truly among you.
26 What is it then, brothers? When you come together, every one of you has a psalm, has a doctrine, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation: let all things be done for edification.
27 If any speak in a tongue, let it be by two, or at most by three, and in turn, and let one interpret.
28 But if there be no interpreter, let him be silent in the Church; but let two or three speak to themselves,
29 And let the prophets speak, two or three, and let the others judge.
30 But if anything be revealed to another sitting by, let the first be silent.

### C H A P T E R XVI.

*Where he has exhorted them to collect alms for the Christians who were living in Jerusalem, he commends Timothy and the family of Stephanas to them: then he adds greetings.*

1 **Now** concerning the collections that are made for the saints, as I have ordered the Churches of Galatia, so do you also.
2 On the first day of the week, let every one of you put aside by himself, laying up what shall please him: so that when I come, the collections are not then being made.

<column-break/>

3 And when I am present: whomsoever you shall approve by letters, them will I send to carry your gift <note>original: "gratiam," literally "grace" or "favor," used here for a charitable donation.</note> to Jerusalem.
4 But if it be worthy that I go also, they shall go with me.
5 Now I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia; for I shall pass through Macedonia.
6 And perhaps I will stay with you, or even winter with you: that you may lead me on my way wherever I shall go.
7 For I do not wish to see you now in passing, for I hope to stay with you for some time, if the Lord permits.
8 But I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost.
9 For a door is opened to me, great and evident: and many are the adversaries.
10 Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear: for he works the work of the Lord, even as I do.
11 Therefore let no one despise him: but lead him on his way in peace, that he may come to me: for I look for him with the brothers.
12 As for the brother Apollos, I make it known to you that I much entreated him to come to you with the brothers: and it was certainly not his will to come now, but he will come when he has the time.
13 Watch, stand fast in the faith, act like men, and be strengthened.
14 Let all your things be done in charity.
15 And I beseech you, brothers, you know the house of Stephanas, and of Fortunatus, and of Achaicus: because they are the first-fruits of Achaia <note>Achaia was the Roman province covering southern Greece; "first-fruits" refers to the first converts in that area.</note>, and they have dedicated themselves to the ministry of the saints:
16 That you also be subject to such, and to everyone who co-operates and labors.
17 I rejoice in the presence of Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus: because that which was wanting on your part, they have supplied:
18 For they have refreshed both my spirit and yours. Know them, therefore, who are such.
19 The Churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, with their domestic church: with whom also I lodge.
20 All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
21 The greeting by my own hand, Paul's.
22 If anyone does not love our Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed, Our Lord comes. <note>original: "anathema, Maran Atha." Paul uses a Greek term for a curse followed by an Aramaic phrase meaning "The Lord is coming" or "Come, Lord."</note>
23 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
24 My charity be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.

Paul ends with personal news of his travels and greetings to his friends in the Corinthian church.</summary>

# THE EPISTLE
## OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL
### TO THE CORINTHIANS II.
---
#### CHAPTER ONE.

*The Apostle shows from what great adversities arising in Asia the Lord rescued him, so that he himself might comfort others: then, demonstrating the sincerity of his heart and doctrine, he shows that although he did not come to them according to what he had proposed, this was done by no fickleness of his own; asserting that the truth of his preaching is firm.*
---

1 Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints who are in all of Achaia <note>A Roman province covering the southern part of modern-day Greece.</note>.
2 Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
3 <margin>Ephesians 1. 1 Peter 1.</margin> † Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all consolation,
4 Who consoles us in all our tribulation: so that we ourselves may be able to console those who are in any pressure, through the encouragement with which we ourselves are encouraged by God.
5 For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us: so also through Christ does our consolation abound.
6 But whether we are troubled, it is for your encouragement and salvation; or whether we are comforted, it is for your consolation; or whether we are encouraged, it is for your encouragement and salvation, which works the endurance of the same sufferings which we also suffer.
7 That our hope for you may be firm: knowing that as you are sharers of the sufferings, so shall you be also of the consolation.
8 For we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of our tribulation which happened in Asia <note>Referring to the Roman province of Asia, located in modern-day western Turkey.</note>, because we were burdened beyond measure, beyond our strength, so that we were weary even of living.
9 But we had the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we should not be trusting in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead:
10 Who has rescued us and does rescue us from such great dangers: in whom we hope that he will yet rescue us,
11 You also helping in prayer for us: so that for the gift bestowed upon us by means of many persons, thanks may be given by many on our behalf.
12 For this is our glory, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity of heart and sincerity of God, and not in fleshly wisdom, but in the grace of God, we have conducted ourselves in this world: and more abundantly toward you.
13 For we do not write other things to you than what you have read and understood. And I hope that you will understand even to the end,
14 As also you have understood us in part, that we are your glory, even as you are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

<column-break/>

15 And in this confidence I wanted to come to you before, so that you might have a second grace:
16 And to pass through you into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and by you to be brought on my way into Judea.
17 When, therefore, I had intended this, did I use fickleness? Or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, so that with me there should be YES and NO? <note>original: "EST & NON." Paul is defending himself against the charge that he is indecisive or untrustworthy in his promises.</note>
18 But as God is faithful, our word which was with you is not YES and NO.
19 For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us—by me, and Silvanus, and Timothy—was not YES and NO, but in him was "YES." <note>original: "EST." Here "YES" signifies fulfillment and certainty in Christ.</note>
20 For however many are the promises of God, in him they are "YES": and therefore through him is the Amen to God for our glory.
21 Now he who confirms us with you in Christ, and who has anointed us, is God:
22 Who also has sealed us, and given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.
23 But I call God as a witness upon my soul, that to spare you, I did not come again to Corinth: not because we lord it over your faith, but we are helpers of your joy: for by faith you stand.

#### CHAPTER II.

*He shows that he did not come to them lest he be a cause of greater sadness, urging them to receive that fornicator <note>Referring to the man disciplined in the previous letter (1 Corinthians 5).</note> back into grace: at the same time indicating that he preached with great labor, yet also with great fruit, although his preaching, by its fragrance, was an occasion of death to some.*

1 But I determined this within myself, that I would not come to you again in sadness.
2 For if I make you sad, who is there then to make me glad, but he who is made sad by me?
3 And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I come, I might not have sadness upon sadness from those in whom I ought to rejoice: having confidence in all of you, that my joy is the joy of you all.
4 For out of much tribulation and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears: not that you should be made sad: but that you might know what more abundant charity I have toward you.
5 But if anyone has caused sadness, he has not saddened me: but in part, so that I may not overcharge you all.
6 To such a one, this rebuke which is given by many is sufficient:
7 So that on the contrary, you should rather forgive and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up by overmuch sadness.
8 Therefore I beseech you, that you would confirm your charity toward him.
9 For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.

<summary>Paul opens his second letter to the Corinthians by reflecting on his severe afflictions in Asia and explaining that his delayed visit to Corinth was intended to spare them from a painful confrontation. He emphasizes God's comfort in suffering and urges the congregation to forgive and restore a repentant member who had previously been disciplined.</summary>
<keywords>Paul the Apostle, 2 Corinthians, consolation, suffering, Asia, Macedonia, sincerity, forgiveness, Holy Spirit, Amen</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the Second Epistle to the Corinthians. This page begins with the conclusion of Chapter 2, regarding forgiveness and the "aroma of Christ," then moves into Chapters 3 and 4, which discuss the New Covenant and the perseverance of the Apostles.</meta>

10 To whom you have forgiven anything, I also forgive: for if I have forgiven anything, I did it for your sake in the person of Christ.
11 So that we might not be outwitted by Satan: for we are not ignorant of his designs <note>original: "cogitationes ejus." Referring to the deceptive thoughts or schemes of the devil.</note>.
12 When I had come to Troas for the sake of the Gospel of Christ, and a door was opened for me in the Lord,
13 I had no rest for my spirit, because I did not find Titus my brother; but saying goodbye to them, I set out for Macedonia.
14 But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ Jesus, and through us spreads the fragrance of his knowledge in every place:
15 For we are the good aroma of Christ to God, among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing:
16 To the one, an aroma of death leading to death; to the other, an aroma of life leading to life. And who is sufficient for these things?
17 For we are not like the many who adulterate <note>original: "adulterantes." This implies diluting or corrupting the word of God for personal gain, like a merchant watering down wine.</note> the word of God; but with sincerity, and as if from God, in the presence of God, we speak in Christ.

### CHAPTER III.

*The Apostle does not need the recommendation of men, since the fruit of his preaching recommends him: for the ministers of the New Testament and of the Spirit ought to be in much greater honor than those of the Old Testament and of the letter: and that the Jews still had a veil over their hearts in the reading of the Scriptures, which is taken away by faith in Christ.*

1 Are we beginning to recommend ourselves again? Or do we need (as some do) letters of recommendation to you, or from you?
2 You are our letter, written in our hearts, which is known and read by all men:
3 You are shown to be a letter of Christ, delivered by us, and written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not on tablets of stone, but on the fleshy tablets of the heart.
4 Such is the confidence we have through Christ toward God.
5 Not that we are sufficient to think anything of ourselves, as if it were from us: but our sufficiency is from God:
6 Who also made us fit ministers of a New Testament <note>The "New Covenant" established through Jesus.</note>, not of the letter, but of the Spirit: for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
7 Now if the ministry of death, carved in letters upon stones, was in such glory that the children of Israel could not look intently at the face of Moses because of the glory of his countenance—which was to fade away:
8 How much more shall the ministry of the Spirit be in glory?
9 For if the ministry of condemnation is glory, much more does the ministry of justice <note>or "righteousness"</note> abound in glory.
10 For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, because of the surpassing glory.
11 For if that which fades away was through glory, much more that which remains is in glory.
12 Having therefore such hope, we use great boldness:
<margin>Exodus 33.</margin>
13 † And we are not like Moses, who put a veil over his face, so that the children of Israel would not look intently at his face, which was fading away,

<column-break/>

14 But their minds were dulled. For until this very day, the same veil remains in the reading of the Old Testament, not taken away (because it is vanished in Christ).
15 But even to this day, when Moses is read, a veil is placed over their hearts.
16 But when one shall turn to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away.
<margin>† John 4:24.</margin>
17 † Now the Lord is the Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
18 But we all, beholding the glory of the Lord with unveiled face, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as by the Spirit of the Lord.

### CHAPTER IV.

*By the sincere preaching of the Apostles, the word of God is made manifest to all, except to those whose minds are blinded: that although the Apostles suffer many adversities, they never succumb: for momentary tribulation produces a great and eternal glory.*

1 Therefore, having this ministry, according to the mercy we have obtained, we do not lose heart.
2 But we renounce the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor adulterating the word of God, but by the manifestation of the truth, commending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.
3 And if our Gospel be hidden, it is hidden to those who are perishing:
4 In whom the God of this world has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so that the light of the Gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not shine for them.
5 For we do not preach ourselves, but Jesus Christ our Lord; and ourselves as your servants through Jesus.
6 For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, has shone in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God, in the face of Christ Jesus.
7 But we have this treasure in earthen vessels <note>original: "vasis fictilibus." A metaphor for the fragile, mortal bodies of the apostles carrying the precious message of God.</note>: so that the excellence of the power may be of God, and not from us.
8 In all things we suffer tribulation, but we are not distressed; we are perplexed, but not forsaken;
9 We suffer persecution, but we are not abandoned; we are cast down, but we do not perish;
10 Always carrying about in our body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our bodies.
11 For we who live are always being delivered unto death for Jesus' sake: so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our mortal flesh.
12 So then death works in us, but life in you.
<margin>† Psalm 115:10</margin>
13 But having the same spirit of faith, as it is written: † I believed, therefore I have spoken; we also believe, and therefore we speak:
14 Knowing that he who raised up Jesus, will raise us up also with Jesus, and will place us with you.
15 For all things are for your sake: so that grace, abounding through many in thanksgiving, may abound to the glory of God.
16 For which cause we do not lose heart: but although our outward man is corrupted, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.

<summary>Paul contrasts the fading glory of the Mosaic Law with the eternal glory of the New Covenant in the Spirit, explaining that while the Apostles suffer physically, they are sustained by inner renewal and the hope of the resurrection.</summary>
<keywords>New Testament, Spirit vs Letter, Veil of Moses, Earthen Vessels, Ministry of Justice, Fragrance of Christ, Corinthians, Transformation, Perseverance</keywords>
