TO THE SECOND CORINTHIANS.

17 For that which is momentary and light of our tribulation <note>original: "tribulationis." Referring to the trials and persecutions the Apostles faced.</note> at present, works in us an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure in the heights.
18 While we do not look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

### CHAPTER V.

->*From the certain hope of future glory, the Apostles desire to be released from the body, since they cannot otherwise enjoy it: but always desiring to please Christ, the just judge of all, they give their disciples an occasion to boast of them before their adversaries: performing a mission on behalf of Christ, they no longer know even Christ himself, whom they preach and by whose death the world is reconciled to God, according to the flesh.*<-

1 For we know that if our earthly house of this habitation is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
2 For in this also we groan, desiring to be clothed over with our habitation which is from heaven.
<margin>† Revelation 16:15.</margin>
3 † If indeed, being clothed, we be not found naked.
4 For we who are in this tabernacle <note>original: "tabernaculo." A metaphor for the human body as a temporary, portable dwelling like a tent.</note> groan, being burdened; because we do not wish to be stripped, but to be clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
5 Now he who fashions us for this very thing is God, who has given us the pledge of the Spirit <note>original: "pignus spiritus." A "pignus" is a legal or commercial term for a down payment or security deposit that guarantees a future transaction.</note>.
6 Therefore, being always confident, knowing that while we are in the body, we are on a journey away from the Lord:
7 (For we walk by faith, and not by sight)
8 We are confident, I say, and have a good will rather to be absent from the body and to be present with the Lord.
9 And therefore we strive, whether absent or present, to be pleasing to him.
<margin>Romans 14:10 <note>The source text cites Rom. 4:10, likely a printing error for 14:10.</note></margin>
10 † For we must all be manifested before the judgment seat <term>tribunal: the raised platform where a Roman magistrate sat to deliver official judgments.</term> of Christ, so that each one may receive the proper things of the body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil.
11 Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are manifest to God. And I hope also that we are manifest in your consciences.
12 We do not commend ourselves to you again, but we give you an occasion to boast on our behalf: that you may have something to say to those who boast in appearance, and not in heart.
13 For whether we are beside ourselves, it is for God; or whether we are sober, it is for you.
14 For the charity of Christ urges us: judging this, that if one died for all, then all have died:
15 And Christ died for all: so that they also who live may no longer live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose again.
16 Therefore, from now on, we know no one according to the flesh. And if we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him so no longer.
<margin>† Isaiah 43:19. Revelation 21:5.</margin>
17 If then any person is a new creature in Christ, the old things have passed away: † behold, all things have been made new.

<column-break/>

18 But all things are from God, who has reconciled us to himself through Christ, and has given to us the ministry of reconciliation.
19 For indeed, God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not counting their sins against them, and he has placed in us the word of reconciliation.
20 Therefore, we perform a mission <note>original: "legatione fungimur." This refers to the role of an ambassador or envoy representing a sovereign power.</note> on behalf of Christ, as though God were exhorting through us. We beseech you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
21 Him who knew no sin, he made to be sin for us, so that we might be made the justice of God in him.

### CHAPTER VI.

->*He exhorts them not to neglect the grace they have received, showing how much he has labored to show himself a proven minister of God, and warning that they should be separated from the fellowship and company of unbelievers.*<-

1 And helping them, we exhort you that you do not receive the grace of God in vain.
<margin>† Isaiah 49:8.</margin>
2 For he says: † In an accepted time I have heard you, and in the day of salvation I have helped you. Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 10:32.</margin>
3 † Giving no offense to anyone, so that our ministry may not be blamed:
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 4:1.</margin>
4 But in all things let us present ourselves † as the ministers of God, in much patience, in tribulations, in necessities, in distresses.
5 In stripes, in prisons, in seditions, in labors, in watchings, in fastings.
6 In chastity, in knowledge, in long-suffering, in sweetness, in the Holy Spirit, in charity unfeigned,
7 In the word of truth, in the power of God, through the armor of justice on the right hand and on the left.
8 Through glory and dishonor; through ill repute and good repute: as deceivers, and yet true; as those who are unknown, and yet known;
9 As dying, and behold, we live: as chastised, and not killed;
10 As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing: as needy, yet enriching many: as having nothing, and possessing all things.
11 Our mouth is open to you, O Corinthians, our heart is enlarged.
12 You are not restricted in us: but you are restricted in your own affections <note>original: "visceribus." Literally "bowels" or "innards," used in antiquity to represent the seat of deep emotions and mercy.</note>.
13 But having the same recompense (I speak as to my children), be you also enlarged.
14 Do not bear the yoke with unbelievers. For what participation has justice with injustice? Or what fellowship has light with darkness?
15 And what agreement has Christ with Belial? <term>Belial: a Hebrew term meaning "worthless," used here as a name for the devil.</term> Or what part has the faithful with the unbeliever?
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 3:16 & 6:19.</margin>
16 And what agreement has the temple of God with idols? † For you are the temple of the living God, as God says: † For I will dwell in them, and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
<margin>† Leviticus 26:12. † Isaiah 52:11.</margin>
17 † Wherefore, go out from the midst of them, and be separate, says the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing:
<margin>† Jeremiah 31:9.</margin>
18 And I will receive you: † and I will be a father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.

## CHAPTER VII.

*The Apostle shows with how much love he follows the Corinthians, and how much joy he received in his great tribulations from their corrected life, and how much good the sorrow produced which they had received from his letter.*

1 Having therefore these promises, most dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting holiness <note>original: "sanctificationem." This refers to the process of becoming more holy or set apart for God's purposes.</note> in the fear of God.
2 Receive us. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have defrauded no one.
3 I do not say this to your condemnation: for we have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
4 Great is my confidence with you, great is my boasting for you; I am filled with comfort, I exceedingly abound with joy in all our tribulation.
5 For even when we had come into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but we suffered every tribulation: fights without, fears within.
6 But God, who comforts the humble, comforted us by the arrival of Titus.
7 And not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted in you, reporting to us your desire, your weeping, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced the more.
8 For although I made you sad in the letter, I do not repent: and if I did repent, seeing that that letter (even if only for an hour) made you sad;
9 Now I rejoice: not because you were made sad, but because you were made sad unto repentance. For you were made sad according to God <note>original: "secundum Deum." Often translated as "godly sorrow," meaning a sadness that leads to positive change rather than despair.</note>, so that you might suffer harm from us in nothing.
<margin>
1 Peter
19.
</margin>
10 † For the sorrow that is according to God works a stable repentance unto salvation: but the sorrow of the world works death.
11 For behold this very thing, that you were made sad according to God, what great earnestness it works in you: but also defense, but also indignation, but also fear, but also desire, but also zeal, but also punishment: in all things you have shown yourselves to be untainted in the matter.
12 Therefore, although I wrote to you, it was not on account of him who did the wrong, nor on account of him who suffered the injury: but to make manifest our earnestness which we have for you
13 Before God: therefore we were comforted. But in our comfort, we rejoiced even more abundantly over the joy of Titus, because his spirit was refreshed by all of you.
14 And if I boasted anything to him about you, I have not been put to shame: but just as we spoke all things to you in truth, so also our boasting, which was made to Titus, was found to be the truth,
15 And his heart <note>original: "viscera." Literally "innards" or "bowels," a common biblical idiom for deep affection or the seat of emotions.</note> is more abundantly toward you: remembering the obedience of you all, how you received him with fear and trembling.
16 I rejoice that in all things I have confidence in you.

## CHAPTER VIII.

*He exhorts them to give alms with a ready mind to the poor who lived in Jerusalem, both by the recommendation of the Macedonians and by the example of Christ; advising that what they had already proposed to do a long time ago, they should now perform according to each one's ability: and he commends the ministers whom he sends to collect it.*

1 Now we make known to you, brothers, the grace of God, which was given in the Churches of Macedonia <note>A Roman province in northern Greece.</note>.
2 That in a great experience of tribulation, the abundance of their joy was found; and their deepest poverty abounded unto the riches of their simplicity.
3 For I bear witness to them that according to their power, and even beyond their power, they were willing of their own accord,
4 Begging us with much entreaty for the grace and the sharing of the ministry that is performed for the Saints.
5 And not just as we had hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord, then to us by the will of God;
6 So that we asked Titus, that just as he had begun, so he might also finish this same grace in you.
7 But as you abound in all things—in faith, and in word, and in knowledge, and in all earnestness, and moreover in your love toward us—so may you also abound in this grace.
8 I do not speak as one commanding: but through the earnestness of others, I am also testing the good nature of your love.
9 For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that for your sakes he became poor, though he was rich, so that by his poverty you might be made rich.
10 And I give advice in this: for this is useful to you, who began not only to do, but also to be willing, since the previous year:
11 Now therefore perform it in deed: so that just as there is a prompt mind of will, so there may be also a performance from that which you have.
12 For if the will is prompt; it is accepted according to what a person has, not according to what he does not have.
13 For it is not so that there should be relief for others, and tribulation for you, but by an equality.
14 In the present time let your abundance supply their want: so that their abundance also may be a supplement to your want, that there may be equality, as it is written:
<margin>
† Exodus
16. 18.
</margin>
15 † He who had much, did not have too much: and he who had little, did not have too little.
16 But thanks be to God, who gave the same earnestness for you in the heart of Titus,
17 Because he indeed accepted the exhortation: but being more earnest, he went to you of his own will.
18 We have also sent with him the brother whose praise is in the Gospel throughout all the Churches:
19 And not only that, but he was also ordained by the Churches as a companion of our travels for this grace, which is administered by us to the glory of the Lord, and our destined will:
20 Avoiding this, that no one should blame us in this abundance, which is administered by us.
<margin>
† Romans
12. 17.
</margin>
21 † For we provide good things not only before God, but also before men.

->TO THE SECOND CORINTHIANS<-

22 And we have sent with them also our brother, whom we have often proven to be diligent in many things, but who is now much more diligent due to his great confidence in you,
23 whether as regarding Titus, who is my companion and fellow-helper among you, or our brothers, the Apostles <note>original: "Apostoli." While usually referring to the Twelve, here it likely refers to "messengers" or "delegates" sent by the churches.</note> of the Churches, the glory of Christ.

### CHAPTER IX.

> *He continues by exhorting them to give alms promptly and abundantly; warning them not to fear poverty because of this, but to trust in divine providence: and he recounts the various fruits of such almsgiving.*

1 For concerning the ministry <note>original: "ministerio." Here referring specifically to the relief fund for the poor Christians in Jerusalem.</note> that is performed for the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you.
2 For I know your ready mind, for which I boast of you to the Macedonians: that Achaia <note>A Roman province in Greece, where Corinth was located.</note> has been ready since last year, and your zeal has provoked very many.
3 But I have sent the brothers, so that our boasting of you may not be made void in this regard, so that (as I said) you may be ready:
4 Lest when the Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we (not to say you) should be ashamed in this matter of substance.
5 Therefore I thought it necessary to ask the brothers to go before us to you, and prepare this promised blessing <note>original: "benedictionem." Paul uses the word for 'blessing' to describe the gift, suggesting it should be given freely rather than as a forced tax.</note> to be ready, as a blessing and not as an act of greed.
6 But this I say: He who sows sparingly shall also reap sparingly: and he who sows in blessings shall also reap of blessings.
<margin>Sirach 35:11</margin>
7 Everyone as he has determined in his heart, not out of sadness or out of necessity: for God loves a cheerful giver.
8 And God is able to make all grace abound in you: so that in all things, always having all sufficiency, you may abound in every good work,
<margin>Psalm 112:9</margin>
9 As it is written: He has dispersed, he has given to the poor: his justice remains forever and ever.
10 Now he that supplies seed to the sower will both provide bread to eat, and multiply your seed, and increase the growth of the fruits of your justice:
11 That being enriched in all things, you may abound in all simplicity <note>original: "simplicitatem." This carries the sense of sincere, open-handed generosity.</note>, which works through us thanksgiving to God.
12 For the ministry of this office not only supplies those things that the saints lack, but also abounds through many thanksgivings in the Lord,
13 through the proof of this ministry, as they glorify God for the obedience of your confession to the Gospel of Christ, and for the simplicity of your communication <note>original: "communicationis." This refers to their fellowship and the sharing of their resources.</note> toward them and toward all,
14 and in their prayer for you, as they long for you because of the excellent grace of God in you.
15 Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift.

<column-break/>

### CHAPTER X.

> *He begins to reveal his authority and the labors endured for Christ against the false apostles, who, by disparaging him and preaching that he was lowly, were hindering the fruit of his preaching.*

1 Now I, Paul himself, beseech you by the mildness and modesty of Christ, I who in person am indeed humble among you, but being absent am bold toward you.
2 But I ask you that when I am present, I may not have to be bold with that confidence by which I am thought to be bold against some, who reckon us as if we walked according to the flesh.
3 For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh.
4 For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal <note>original: "carnalia." Meaning worldly or purely human weapons.</note>, but mighty through God to the destruction of fortifications, destroying counsels,
5 and every height that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing every intellect into captivity to the obedience of Christ,
6 and having in readiness to avenge all disobedience, when your obedience shall be fulfilled.
7 Look at the things that are before your face. If anyone trusts in himself that he is Christ's, let him think this again within himself: that as he is Christ's, so are we also.
8 For even if I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord has given us for building up and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed.
9 That I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters:
10 For his letters, they say, are weighty and strong; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.
11 Let such a person think this, that such as we are in word by letters when absent, such also shall we be in deed when present.
12 For we dare not match or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves: but they, measuring themselves by themselves and comparing themselves with themselves, are not wise.
<margin>Ephesians 4:7</margin>
13 But we will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God has measured out to us, a measure to reach even unto you.
14 For we do not overextend ourselves, as if we did not reach unto you: for we have come as far as you in the Gospel of Christ.
15 Not boasting beyond measure in other men's labors: but having hope of your increasing faith, to be magnified in you according to our rule abundantly,
16 even to preach the gospel in those places that are beyond you, and not to boast in another man's rule in those things that are already prepared.
<margin>Jeremiah 9:23; 1 Corinthians 1:31</margin>
17 But he that glories, let him glory in the Lord.
18 For not he who commends himself is approved: but he whom God commends.

### CHAPTER XI.

> *Fearing for the Corinthians because of false apostles who are perverting Paul’s preaching, he explains why he accepted no financial support from them: then, to show that more faith should be placed in him than in those others, he recounts his own commendations; and first, the adversities he endured while preaching the faith of Christ, as well as his labors and anxieties.*

1 I wish you would bear with a little of my foolishness <note>original: "insipientiæ meæ." Paul uses irony here, adopting the "boasting" style of his rivals which he considers foolish, to prove his point.</note>, but please, do support me:
2 For I am jealous of you with the jealousy of God. For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
<margin>Genesis 4</margin> <note>Though the margin cites Genesis 4, the text refers to the serpent in Genesis 3.</note>
3 But I fear lest, as the serpent seduced Eve by his cunning, so your minds might be corrupted and fall away from the simplicity that is in Christ.
4 For if someone comes and preaches another Christ, whom we did not preach; or if you receive another spirit, which you did not receive; or another Gospel, which you did not accept, you might rightly endure it <note>Paul is being sarcastic: he is amazed they are so patient with false teachers but so critical of him.</note>.
5 For I consider that I have done nothing less than the "great Apostles."
6 For although I may be unskilled in speech, I am not so in knowledge: and in all things we have been made manifest to you.
7 Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted? Because I preached the Gospel of God to you for free?
8 I "robbed" other Churches, receiving wages from them for my ministry to you.
9 And when I was with you and in need, I was a burden to no one; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied what was lacking to me: and in all things I have kept myself from being a burden to you, and I will continue to do so.
10 As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting shall not be silenced in me in the regions of Achaia <note>The Roman province in Greece where Corinth was located.</note>.
11 Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do.
12 But what I do, I will continue to do: so that I may cut off the opportunity from those who desire an opportunity to be found equal to us in the things they boast about.
13 For such "false apostles" are deceitful workers, transforming themselves into Apostles of Christ.
14 And no wonder: for Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light.
15 Therefore, it is no great thing if his ministers are transformed as ministers of justice; their end shall be according to their works.
16 I say again (let no one think me a fool; otherwise, receive me as a fool, so that I also may boast a little).
17 What I speak, I speak not according to God, but as if in foolishness, in this matter of boasting.
18 Since many boast according to the flesh, I also will boast.
19 For you gladly suffer fools, since you yourselves are so "wise."
20 For you endure it if someone brings you into slavery, if someone devours your goods, if someone takes from you, if someone exalts himself, if someone strikes you in the face.
21 I speak according to my own "dishonor," as if we had been weak in this regard. In whatever anyone else dares to boast (I speak in foolishness), I dare to boast as well:

<column-break/>

22 Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? So am I.
23 Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as one less wise) I am more: in many more labors, in prisons more frequently, in beatings beyond measure, and often near death.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 25:3</margin>
24 Five times I received from the Jews the forty stripes, less one <note>Jewish law capped lashes at forty to prevent death; the "less one" was a precaution to ensure the law wasn't accidentally broken.</note>.
<margin>† Acts 14:18; Acts 16:22; Acts 17:37, 41</margin>
25 Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I suffered shipwreck, and for a night and a day I was adrift in the deep sea.
26 In journeys often, in perils of rivers, in perils of robbers, in perils from my own nation, in perils from the Gentiles, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brothers;
27 In labor and hardship, in many sleepless nights, in hunger and thirst, in many fastings, in cold and nakedness;
28 Besides those external things, there is my daily pressure: the concern for all the Churches.
29 Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?
30 If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
31 The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I do not lie.
<margin>† Acts 9:24</margin>
32 In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas guarded the city of the Damascenes to capture me;
33 But through a window in a basket <note>original: "sporta." A large wicker basket used for carrying goods.</note> I was let down over the wall, and so I escaped his hands.

---

### CHAPTER XII.

> *He recounts the divine visions granted to him fourteen years ago, and describes the "thorn in his flesh" given to him. He shows that the Corinthians compelled him to praise himself, when they ought rather to have commended him for the benefits they received from him—for whose salvation he is still ready to be sacrificed. However, he fears that upon arriving, he may find some still involved in dissensions and other vices.*

1 If I must boast (though it is not truly expedient), I will come to the visions and revelations of the Lord.
<margin>† Acts 9:3</margin>
2 I know a man in Christ <note>Paul refers to himself in the third person out of humility.</note> who, fourteen years ago (whether in the body I do not know, or out of the body I do not know, God knows), was caught up to the third heaven <note>In ancient cosmology, the "third heaven" represented the highest realm, the immediate presence of God.</note>.
3 And I know such a man (whether in the body or out of the body, I do not know, God knows),
4 How he was caught up into Paradise and heard secret words, which it is not permitted for a man to speak.
5 Of such a person I will boast; but for myself I will boast of nothing except my weaknesses.
6 For even if I should wish to boast, I will not be a fool, for I will speak the truth. But I refrain, lest anyone should think of me more highly than what he sees in me or hears from me.
7 And lest the greatness of the revelations should puff me up, there was given to me a thorn in my flesh <note>original: "stimulus carnis." Historically interpreted as either a chronic physical ailment, a recurring temptation, or the constant harassment of his enemies.</note>, a messenger of Satan, to buffet me.
8 For this thing I besought the Lord three times, that it might depart from me.
9 And he said to me: "My grace is sufficient for you; for power is made perfect in weakness." Gladly, therefore, will I boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.

<summary>Paul defends his apostolic authority by listing his extensive physical sufferings for the Gospel and recounting a mystical vision of heaven, concluding that God's strength is best revealed through human weakness.</summary>
<keywords>Paul, Corinthians, false apostles, suffering, shipwreck, Damascus, third heaven, thorn in the flesh, grace, weakness</keywords>

10 Therefore I take pleasure in my weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, and in distresses for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then I am powerful.
11 I have become a fool; you forced me to it. For I ought to have been commended by you: for I am in no way inferior to those who are "super-Apostles," even though I am nothing.
12 Yet the signs of my Apostleship were performed among you in all patience, with signs, wonders, and mighty deeds.
13 For what is there in which you were treated as less than the other Churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this injustice. <note>Paul is using heavy irony here; he refers to his refusal to take money from the Corinthians—a point of pride for him—as an "injustice" to mock the complaints of his critics.</note>
14 Behold, this third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be a burden to you. For I seek not what is yours, but you. For children ought not to save up treasures for their parents, but parents for their children.
15 And I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls; even if, the more I love you, the less I am loved.
16 But let it be so: I did not burden you: but being "crafty," I caught you with "guile." <note>Paul is likely quoting the accusations of his enemies, who claimed that even if he didn't take money personally, he was using his representatives to steal from the collection.</note>
17 Did I take advantage of you through any of those whom I sent to you?
18 I urged Titus to go, and I sent a brother with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not follow in the same footsteps?
19 Do you think all this time that we are defending ourselves to you? We speak in the sight of God in Christ; but all things, dearly beloved, are for your building up.
20 For I fear that perhaps, when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and that I may be found by you as you do not wish: lest perhaps there be contentions, jealousies, outbursts of anger, dissensions, slanders, secret gossip, conceit, and disorders among you.
21 Lest when I come again, God should humble me among you; and I should mourn for many of those who sinned before and have not done penance <note>original: "pœnitentiam." In this context, it refers to the act of repentance and a change of heart regarding their past behavior.</note> for the impurity, fornication, and lustfulness which they have committed.

### CHAPTER XIII.

> *He threatens those who have sinned, in order to provoke them to repentance, so that when he comes to them he is not forced to punish them severely with the power given to him by Christ, whose strength they should rightly recognize in themselves; he adds a general exhortation and greetings.*

<margin>Deuteronomy 19:15; Matthew 18:15</margin>
1 **B**ehold, this is the third time I am coming to you: by the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.
<margin>John 8:17; Hebrews 10:28.</margin>
2 I have told you before, and I foretell now—as if I were present, though I am now absent—to those who sinned before and to all the others: that if I come again, I will not spare you.
3 Do you seek a proof of Christ who speaks in me? He is not weak toward you, but is powerful in you.
4 For although he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you.
5 Test yourselves to see if you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Do you not know yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless perhaps you are rejected. <note>original: "reprobi," meaning those who fail the test or are found to be counterfeit.</note>
6 But I hope you will know that we are not rejected.
7 Now we pray to God that you do no evil; not that we might appear approved, but that you should do what is good, even if we should seem like those who are rejected.
8 For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth.
9 For we rejoice when we are weak and you are strong: this also we pray for—your perfection. <note>original: "consummationem," meaning a state of being fully joined together or completed.</note>
10 Therefore I write these things while absent, so that when present I may not act more harshly according to the power which the Lord has given me for building up, and not for tearing down.
11 For the rest, brothers, rejoice, be perfect, take comfort, be of the same mind, have peace; and the God of peace and love shall be with you.
12 Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.
13 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.

<meta>This page marks the beginning of the Epistle to the Galatians. The previous page concluded the Second Epistle to the Corinthians, where Paul defended his ministry against critics in Corinth. Here, he begins a stern letter to the churches in Galatia (modern-day Turkey), who have been influenced by teachers insisting that Christian converts must follow Jewish Law.</meta>

# THE EPISTLE 
# OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL
## TO THE GALATIANS.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*The Apostle rebukes the Galatians because they have allowed themselves to be led away from the truth which they had received from him, since only this truth must be held; he explains that he did not learn it from man, but through the revelation of Christ, and that he later taught it with as much skill as he had previously used to attack it: adding how God <unclear>prepared</unclear> <note>original: "formavit" — shaped or appointed</note> him for the work of the Gospel.*

1 Paul, an Apostle—not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead—
2 And all the brothers who are with me, to the Churches of Galatia.
3 Grace to you and peace from God the Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ,
4 Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present wicked world, according to the will of God and our Father,
5 To whom is glory for ever and ever. Amen.
6 I marvel that you are so quickly deserting him who called you into the grace of Christ, for another Gospel:
7 Which is not another, except that there are some who trouble you, and want to subvert the Gospel of Christ.
8 But even if we, or an Angel from heaven, should preach to you a gospel other than what we have preached to you, let him be <term>anathema</term> <note>original: "anathema" — a formal curse or being cut off from the community.</note>.
9 As we said before, so now I say again: If anyone preaches a gospel to you other than what you have received, let him be anathema.
10 For am I now seeking the favor of men, or of God? Or do I seek to please men? If I were still pleasing men, I would not be a servant of Christ.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 15.</margin>
11 For I make known to you, brothers, that the Gospel which was preached by me is not according to man:
<margin>† Ephesians 3.</margin>
12 For I neither received it from man, nor was I taught it, but I received it through the revelation of Jesus Christ.
13 For you have heard of my former way of life in Judaism: how I persecuted the Church of God beyond measure, and tried to destroy it,
14 And I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my contemporaries in my own nation, being more abundantly zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
15 But when it pleased Him, who set me apart from my mother’s womb and called me by his grace,
16 To reveal his Son in me, so that I might preach him among the Gentiles: immediately I did not consult with <term>flesh and blood</term> <note>A common idiom meaning "humanity" or "human counsel."</note>,
17 Nor did I go to Jerusalem to those who were Apostles before me; but I went away into Arabia, and returned again to Damascus.
18 Then after three years I went to Jerusa-

<column-break/>

-lem to see Peter, and I stayed with him for fifteen days:
19 But I saw no other of the Apostles, except James, the brother of the Lord.
20 Now regarding the things I am writing to you: behold, before God, I do not lie.
21 Afterward I came into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
22 But I was unknown by face to the Churches of Judea which were in Christ:
23 They only heard it said: "He who once persecuted us now preaches the faith which he once tried to destroy."
24 And they glorified God in me.

### CHAPTER II.

*Paul always taught the truth of the Gospel freely among the Gentiles, with the leading Apostles approving and adding nothing to it, but receiving Paul as a partner: he also openly rebuked Cephas, showing that no one is justified by the works of the law, but through faith in Christ.*

1 Then after fourteen years, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also.
2 And I went up according to a revelation: and I communicated to them that Gospel which I preach among the Gentiles—but privately to those who seemed to be of reputation—lest perhaps I should run, or had run, in vain.
3 But not even Titus, who was with me, though he was a Gentile, was compelled to be circumcised:
4 This was because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who slipped in to spy on our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into slavery.
5 To them we did not yield in subjection, even for an hour, so that the truth of the Gospel might remain with you.
<margin>
† Deuteronomy 10:17.
Job 34:19.
Ecclesiasticus 35:15.
Wisdom 6:8.
Acts 10:34.
Romans 2:11.
Ephesians 6:9.
Colossians 3:25.
1 Peter 1:17.
</margin>
6 But from those who seemed to be something (what they once were makes no difference to me. God shows no partiality to any man's person)—for those who seemed to be of reputation contributed nothing to me.
7 But on the contrary, when they saw that the Gospel to the <term>uncircumcised</term> <note>Refers to the mission to the Gentiles.</note> was committed to me, just as the Gospel to the <term>circumcised</term> <note>Refers to the mission to the Jews.</note> was to Peter:
8 (For he who worked in Peter for the Apostleship of the circumcised, worked also in me among the Gentiles)
9 And when they recognized the grace that was given to me, James, and <term>Cephas</term> <note>Cephas is the Aramaic name for Peter.</note>, and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship: that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised:
10 They only asked that we should be mindful of the poor: which very thing I was also eager to do.
11 But when Cephas came to Antioch, I withstood him to his face, because he was to be blamed.
12 For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles: but when they—

had come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who belonged to the circumcision party.
13 And the rest of the Jews agreed with his hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was led away by them into that same hypocrisy.
14 But when I saw that they were not walking uprightly according to the truth of the Gospel, I said to Cephas <note>original: "Cephæ" — the Aramaic name for the Apostle Peter</note> in front of everyone: If you, though you are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?
15 We are Jews by nature, and not "Gentile sinners."
<margin>† Romans 3:20.</margin>
16 Yet knowing that a person is not justified by the works of the law, but only through the faith of Jesus Christ, even we believe in Christ Jesus, so that we may be justified by the faith of Christ and not by the works of the law; † for this reason, by the works of the law, no flesh shall be justified.
17 But if, while seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are also found to be sinners, is Christ then a minister of sin? God forbid.
18 For if I build up again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a lawbreaker.
19 For I, through the law, am dead to the law, that I might live for God; I am crucified with Christ.
20 I live, yet now it is not I; but Christ lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself up for me.
21 I do not cast away the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died for nothing.

### CHAPTER III.

->*Just as it was for Abraham, so also for his descendants: the Holy Spirit is given not from the works of the law, but from faith in Christ. Those subject to the law are under a curse, since no one can perfectly fulfill the law; but Christ, by taking this curse upon himself, has freed us from it. The promises made to Abraham are fulfilled through faith, though in the meantime the law was given as a guardian, which was unable to justify.*<-

1 O foolish Galatians, who has bewitched you <note>original: "fascinavit" — to cast a spell or enchant</note> not to obey the truth, before whose very eyes Jesus Christ has been portrayed as crucified among you?
2 This only I want to learn from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
3 Are you so foolish that, having begun in the Spirit, you would now be perfected by the flesh?
4 Have you suffered so many things in vain? If indeed it is in vain.
5 Does he, therefore, who gives you the Spirit and works miracles among you, do so by the works of the law or by the hearing of faith?
<margin>† Genesis 15:6. Romans 4:3. James 2:23.</margin>
6 Just as it is written: † Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
7 Know then, that those who are of faith are the children of Abraham.
<margin>† Genesis 12:3. Sirach 44:20.</margin>
8 And the Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the Gentiles through faith, preached the news beforehand to Abraham: † In you shall all nations be blessed.
9 Therefore, those who are of faith shall be blessed with faithful Abraham.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 27:26.</margin>
10 For as many as are of the works of the law are under a curse; for it is written: † Cursed is everyone who does not remain in all things written in the Book of the Law, to do them.
<margin>† Habakkuk 2:4. Romans 1:17.</margin>
11 But that no one is justified by the law in the sight of God is evident, † because the just man lives by faith.
12 But the law is not of faith; rather, † He who does these things shall live by them.

<column-break/>

<margin>† Leviticus 18:5.</margin>
13 Christ has redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us; for it is written: <margin>† Deuteronomy 21:23.</margin> † Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree.
14 This was so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
<margin>† Hebrews 9:17.</margin>
15 Brothers (I speak in human terms), † even a man’s last will and testament, once confirmed, no one sets aside or adds to it.
16 The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. It does not say, "And to seeds," as if referring to many, but as referring to one: "And to your seed," who is Christ.
17 Now this I say: the testament confirmed by God was not made void by the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, so as to make the promise of no effect.
18 For if the inheritance is from the law, it is no longer from the promise. But God gave it to Abraham by promise.
19 Why then the law? It was put in place because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom he had promised, and it was ordained through angels by the hand of a mediator.
20 Now a mediator is not for one alone; but God is one.
21 Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid. For if a law had been given which could bring life, then truly righteousness would have been by the law.
<margin>† Romans 3:9.</margin>
22 † But the Scripture has confined all things under sin, so that the promise by faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe.
23 But before faith came, we were kept under the guard of the law, confined for that faith which was later to be revealed.
24 And so the law was our <term>pedagogue</term> <note>original: "pædagogus" — in the ancient world, this was a household guardian or tutor who supervised a child until they reached adulthood.</note> leading us to Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
25 But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a pedagogue.
26 For you are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
<margin>† Romans 6:3.</margin>
27 † For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
28 There is neither Jew nor Greek; there is neither slave nor free; there is neither male nor female. For you are all one in Christ Jesus.
29 And if you are Christ’s, then you are the seed of Abraham, and heirs according to the promise.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*Before Christ was born, the Jews, like an heir who is still a small child, were held under the law as if under a guardian. Paul attempts to recall them from the slavery of the law, since they have received the adoption of sons through faith; he reminds them with what great fervor they had previously received his preaching; and at the same time he brings forward the example of Abraham's two sons, representing the two testaments, by which he teaches that those who are jealous for the law are to be cast out from Christ's inheritance.*<-

1 Now I say: As long as the heir is a child, he differs nothing from a slave, though he is the master of all;
2 But he is under guardians and stewards until the time appointed by his father.
3 Even so we, when we were children, were serving under the elements of the world.
4 But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law,
5 To redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive the adoption of sons.

<summary>In this passage, Paul argues that justification comes through faith in Christ rather than the works of the Jewish Law, explaining that the Law served only as a temporary guardian until the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham. He emphasizes that through Christ, believers are no longer slaves to the Law but have been adopted as full heirs and children of God.</summary>

6 And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying: Abba, Father. <note>original: "Abba, Pater" — Abba is Aramaic for "Father," paired here with the Latin "Pater." This signifies the intimate relationship with God as a parent.</note>
7 Therefore he is no longer a slave, but a son. And if a son, then also an heir through God.
8 But then indeed, not knowing God, you served those who by nature are not gods.
9 Now, however, since you have known God, or rather have been known by God: how is it that you turn back again to the weak and beggarly elements, which you wish to serve once more?
10 You observe days, and months, and seasons, and years.
11 I fear for you, lest perhaps I have labored among you in vain.
12 Be as I am, for I also am as you are: brothers, I beg of you: You have not wronged me at all.
13 You know that because of an infirmity of the flesh I preached the gospel to you long ago: and your temptation in my flesh.
14 You did not despise or reject me: but you received me as an Angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
15 Where then is your happiness? For I bear you witness that, if it could be done, you would have plucked out your own eyes and given them to me.
16 Have I then become your enemy by telling you the truth?
17 They <note>The "Judaizers," or those trying to convince the Galatians to follow the Mosaic Law.</note> are zealously interested in you, but not for good: rather, they want to exclude you, so that you might be zealous for them.
18 But it is always good to be zealous in a good thing: and not only when I am present with you.
19 My little children, for whom I am again in labor, until Christ be formed in you.
20 I wish I were with you now, and could change my tone: because I am perplexed about you.
21 Tell me, you who want to be under the law, have you not read the law?

25 For Sinai is a mountain in Arabia, which corresponds to the present Jerusalem, and is in slavery with her children.

<margin>† Isaiah 54:1.</margin>

<margin>† Genesis 21:10.</margin>

## CHAPTER V.

> *He who desires to be justified by the works of the law is deprived of the fruit of Christ, in whom neither circumcision nor uncircumcision is of any use, but living faith: he therefore exhorts them to beware of deceivers, and to strive for mutual love: for the flesh, always resisting the spirit, drags one toward the works of the flesh, which separate one from the kingdom of heaven; but the spirit brings forth fruits by which we attain it, even if we do not perform the works of the law.*

1 Stand fast, and do not be held again by the yoke of slavery.
<margin>† Acts 15:1.</margin>
2 † Behold, I, Paul, say to you: that if you are circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing.
3 And I testify again to every man circumcising himself, that he is a debtor to perform the whole law.
4 You are separated from Christ, you who are justified in the law: you have fallen from grace.
5 For we in spirit, by faith, wait for the hope of justice.
6 For in Christ Jesus, neither circumcision is of any value, nor uncircumcision: but faith, which works through charity.
7 You were running well: who hindered you from obeying the truth?
8 This persuasion is not from him who calls you.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 5:6.</margin>
9 † A little leaven corrupts the whole lump.
10 I have confidence in you in the Lord, that you will think nothing else: but he who troubles you shall bear his judgment, whoever he may be.
11 And I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision: why do I still suffer persecution? Then the stumbling block of the cross has been removed.
12 I wish that those who trouble you would even cut themselves off.
13 For you, brothers, have been called unto liberty: only do not use liberty as an opportunity for the flesh, but through the charity of the Spirit serve one another.
<margin>† Leviticus 19:18. Matthew 22:39. Romans 13:8.</margin>
14 For the whole law is fulfilled in one word: † You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
15 But if you bite and devour one another: take care that you are not consumed by one another.
<margin>† 1 Peter 2:11.</margin>
16 I say then: † Walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfill the desires of the flesh.
17 For the flesh lusts against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh: for these are opposed to each other: so that you do not do whatever things you wish.
18 But if you are led by the spirit, you are not under the law.
19 Now the works of the flesh are manifest: which are fornication, uncleanness, immodesty, luxury:
20 Idolatry, witchcraft, enmities, contentions, rivalries, wraths, quarrels, dissensions, sects,
21 Envies, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these: of which I foretell you, as I have foretold, that those who do such things shall not possess the kingdom of God.
22 But the fruit of the Spirit is charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, long-suffering,
23 Mildness, faith, modesty, continence, chastity. Against such things there is no law.
24 And those who are Christ’s have crucified their flesh with its vices and lusts.

### CHAPTER VI.

*A neighbor should be helped with humility, and the praise of others should not be sought: we must always do good, so that in its own time we may reap eternal life: he warns them again to beware of deceivers, who while they urge the law, do not observe it themselves: Paul, however, glories in Christ alone, for whom neither circumcision nor uncircumcision mean anything.*

1 Brothers, even if a man is overtaken in some fault, you who are spiritual should instruct such a person in a spirit of gentleness, considering yourself, lest you also be tempted.
2 Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
3 For if anyone thinks he is something, when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
4 But let each one test his own work, and then he will have glory in himself alone, and not in another.
<margin>† 1 Cor. 3:8</margin>
5 † For each person shall carry his own load.
6 Let him who is instructed in the word share all good things with the one who instructs him.
7 Do not be deceived: God is not mocked.
8 For whatever a man sows, that he will also reap. For he who sows in his flesh will reap corruption from the flesh; but he who sows in the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.

<column-break/>

<margin>† 2 Thess. 3:13</margin>
9 † And in doing good, let us not grow weary: for in due time we shall reap, if we do not give up.
10 Therefore, while we have time, let us work good toward all, but especially toward those of the household of faith.
11 See with what large letters I have written to you with my own hand.
12 For whoever wishes to please in the flesh, they compel you to be circumcised, only so that they might not suffer persecution for the cross of Christ.
13 For even those who are circumcised do not keep the law; but they want you to be circumcised so that they may glory in your flesh.
14 But far be it from me to glory, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ: through whom the world is crucified to me, and I to the world.
15 For in Christ Jesus, neither circumcision nor uncircumcision <note>original: "præputium" — literally "foreskin," used here to represent those who are not Jewish or do not follow the Mosaic Law.</note> avails anything, but a new creation.
16 And whoever follows this rule, peace be upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
17 From now on, let no one be troublesome to me: for I carry the marks <note>original: "stigmata" — Paul refers to the scars and physical evidence of the trials he suffered for his faith, contrasting them with the ritual mark of circumcision.</note> of the Lord Jesus in my body.
18 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

## OF BLESSED PAUL THE APOSTLE
### TO THE EPHESIANS.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*The Apostle blesses God, who through Christ his Son bestows many and great benefits on those predestined: he gives thanks to God for the faith and love of the Ephesians toward their neighbors: praying that they may obtain perfect wisdom: showing also the exaltation of Christ raised from the dead, who is appointed head over the whole Church.*

<margin>1</margin>
Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to all the saints who are at Ephesus, and the faithful in Christ Jesus.
<margin>2</margin>
Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
<margin>3</margin>
<margin>† 1 Cor. 1:3, 1 Peter 1:3</margin>
† Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ.
4 Just as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and immaculate in his sight in charity.
5 Who predestined us to be adopted as sons through Jesus Christ into himself, according to the purpose of his will,

<column-break/>

6 To the praise of the glory of his grace, in which he has made us accepted in his beloved Son.
7 In whom we have redemption through his blood, the remission of sins, according to the riches of his grace.
8 Which has abounded in us, in all wisdom and prudence:
9 That he might make known to us the mystery <note>original: "sacramentum" — here used to mean a hidden plan or divine secret now revealed, rather than a ritual sacrament.</note> of his will, according to his good pleasure, which he purposed in him.
10 In the dispensation of the fullness of times, to restore all things in Christ, both those which are in heaven and those which are on earth, in him:
11 In whom also we are called by lot, predestined according to the purpose of him who works all things according to the counsel of his will:
12 That we might be for the praise of his glory, we who first hoped in Christ:
13 In whom you also, when you had heard the word of truth (the Gospel of your salvation) and believing in it, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
14 Who is the pledge of our inheritance, for the redemption of his possession, to the praise of his glory.
15 Therefore I also, hearing of your faith which is in the Lord Jesus, and your love toward all the saints.

<margin>† Colossians 3:19</margin>
25 † Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the Church, and delivered himself up for it:
26 That he might sanctify it, cleansing it by the washing of water in the word of life,
27 That he might present it to himself as a glorious Church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing, but that it should be holy and without blemish.
28 So also ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife, loves himself.
29 For no man ever hated his own flesh: but nourishes and cherishes it, as also Christ does the Church:
30 Because we are members of his body, of his flesh, and of his bones.
<margin>† Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:5; Mark 10:7</margin>
31 † For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they shall be two in one flesh.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 6:16</margin>
32 This is a great sacrament <note>original: 'Sacramentum hoc magnum est'; in this context, Paul refers to the 'mystery' of the union between Christ and the Church as mirrored in marriage</note>, but I speak in Christ and in the Church.
33 Nevertheless, let every one of you in particular love his wife as himself: and let the wife fear her husband.

## C H A P T E R VI.

*Children should obey parents, and servants their masters: and again, parents toward children, and masters toward servants should be mindful of their duty: he advises that the armor of God, the parts of which he explains, should be put on to resist spiritual enemies, asking also that they pray for him.*

1 **C**hildren, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is just.

<column-break/>

<margin>† Exodus 20:12; Deuteronomy 5:16; Ecclesiasticus 3:9; Matthew 15:4; Mark 7:10; Colossians 3:20</margin>
2 † Honor your father and your mother, which is the first commandment with a promise:
3 That it may be well with you: and that you may be long-lived upon the earth.
4 And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to anger: but bring them up in the discipline and correction of the Lord.
<margin>† Colossians 3:22; Titus 2:9; 1 Peter 2:18</margin>
5 † Servants, be obedient to your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in the simplicity of your heart, as to Christ:
6 Not serving to the eye, as it were pleasing men, but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart,
7 With a good will serving, as to the Lord, and not to men:
8 Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man shall do, the same shall he receive from the Lord, whether he be a servant, or free.
9 And you, masters, do the same things to them, forbearing threatenings: knowing that both their Lord and yours is in heaven: and there is no respect of persons with him.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 10:17; 2 Paralipomenon [Chronicles] 19:7; Job 34:19; Acts 10:34; Romans 2:11; Galatians 2:6; Wisdom 6:8; Ecclesiasticus 35:15; Colossians 3:25; 1 Peter 1:17</margin>
10 As for the rest, brethren, be strengthened in the Lord, and in the power of his might.
11 Put on the armor of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the devil.
12 For our wrestling is not against flesh and blood; but against principalities and powers, against the rulers of the world of this darkness, against the spirits of wickedness in high places.
13 Therefore, take unto you the armor of God, that you may be able to resist in the evil day, and to stand perfect in all things.
14 Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of justice <note>Often translated as 'righteousness' in modern English</note>,
15 And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace:
16 In all things taking the shield of faith, wherewith you may be able to extinguish all the fiery darts of the most wicked one:
<margin>† Isaiah 59:17; 1 Thessalonians 5:8; Colossians 4:2; 2 Thessalonians 3:1</margin>
17 † And take unto you the helmet of salvation: and the sword of the spirit (which is the word of God),
18 By all prayer and supplication praying at all times in the spirit: and in the same † watching with all instance and supplication for all the saints;
19 † And for me, that speech may be given me, that I may open my mouth with confidence, to make known the mystery of the gospel:
20 For which I am an ambassador in a chain, so that therein I may be bold to speak as I ought.
21 But that you also may know the things that concern me, and what I am doing: Tychicus, my dearest brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will make all things known to you:
22 Whom I have sent to you for this same purpose, that you may know the things that concern us, and that he may comfort your hearts.
23 Peace be to the brethren, and charity with faith, from God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
24 Grace be with all them that love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruption. Amen.

# THE EPISTLE OF BLESSED PAUL THE APOSTLE TO THE PHILIPPIANS.

## CHAPTER ONE.

*Out of the great affection he has toward the Philippians, he shows them that his hardships have resulted in the greater fruit of the Gospel: a benefit which, if he did not consider it, he would altogether desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ; and he exhorts them to live worthily according to the Gospel of Christ, saying that they have already endured afflictions for his sake.*

1 Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, with the Bishops <note>original: "Episcopis," referring to overseers or leaders of the local church</note> and Deacons.
2 Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
3 I give thanks to my God in every remembrance of you,
4 Always in all my prayers for all of you, making my supplication with joy,
5 For your fellowship in the Gospel of Christ from the first day until now.
6 Being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will perfect it until the day of Christ Jesus.
7 As it is right for me to feel this for all of you, because I have you in my heart, and in my chains, and in the defense and confirmation of the Gospel, you all are sharers of my joy.
8 For God is my witness, how I long for all of you in the heart <note>original: "visceribus," literally 'bowels' or 'entrails,' signifying deep-seated affection or the seat of emotions</note> of Jesus Christ.
9 And this I pray, that your charity may abound more and more in knowledge and in all understanding:
10 That you may approve the better things, that you may be sincere and without offense until the day of Christ,
11 Filled with the fruit of justice through Jesus Christ, unto the glory and praise of God.
12 Now I want you to know, brethren, that the things concerning me have turned out rather for the advancement of the Gospel:
13 So that my chains became manifest in Christ in all the praetorium <note>The headquarters of the Roman governor or the imperial guard barracks</note>, and in all other places;
14 And many of the brethren in the Lord, taking confidence from my chains, were much more bold to speak the word of God without fear.
15 Some indeed preach Christ even out of envy and contention, but some also out of good will.
16 Some out of charity, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the Gospel.
17 But some proclaim Christ out of contention, not sincerely, thinking that they raise up affliction for my chains.
18 What then? So long as in every way, whether by pretext or by truth, Christ is proclaimed; and in this I rejoice, and will continue to rejoice.
19 For I know that this shall turn out to my salvation, through your prayer and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.

<column-break/>

20 According to my expectation and hope, that in nothing shall I be confounded: but with all confidence, as always, so now also shall Christ be magnified in my body, whether by life or by death.
21 For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
22 But if living in the flesh is the fruit of my labor, then what I should choose I do not know.
23 For I am pulled between the two: having a desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ, which is far better:
24 But to remain in the flesh is necessary for your sake.
25 And being confident of this, I know that I shall remain, and continue with all of you, for your advancement and joy of faith:
26 That your rejoicing may abound in Christ Jesus in me, through my coming to you again.
<margin>† Ephesians 4:1; Colossians 1:10; 1 Thessalonians 2:12.</margin>
27 † Only let your conversation <note>original: "conversamini," meaning one's way of life or conduct as a citizen</note> be worthy of the Gospel of Christ: so that whether I come and see you, or being absent hear of you, that you stand fast in one spirit with one mind, laboring together for the faith of the Gospel:
28 And in nothing be terrified by the adversaries: which to them is a cause of perdition, but to you of salvation, and this from God:
29 For to you it is given for Christ, not only that you should believe in him, but also that you should suffer for him:
30 Having the same struggle which you have seen in me, and now have heard of me.

## CHAPTER TWO.

*He exhorts them with wonderful affection to mutual love, concord, and modesty of mind, following the example of Christ, in whose name every knee bows, and that they should work out their salvation in fear: he congratulates them that they live holily among the wicked, and himself that he has such disciples: he praises Timothy for his sincere preaching of the Gospel and obedience; and likewise Epaphroditus, whom he sends to them after he recovered from sickness.*

1 IF there be therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of charity, if any fellowship of the spirit, if any bowels <note>feelings</note> of mercy:
2 Fulfill my joy, that you be of the same mind, having the same charity, being of one accord, agreeing in one thing,
3 Doing nothing through contention, nor through vainglory: but in humility, each counting others better than themselves,
4 Each one considering not what is his own, but the things of others.
5 For let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus:
6 Who, being in the form of God, did not think it robbery to be equal to God:
7 But emptied himself <note>A reference to the 'kenosis' or self-emptying of Christ in the Incarnation</note>, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men, and in habit found as a man.

### CHAPTER III.

*No one can boast in legal matters; otherwise, it would suit Paul best. Yet he considers all these things as loss so that he might attain the justice of God through faith in Christ, always progressing so that at last he might reach perfection. Therefore, he exhorts the Philippians to imitate him, and not the troublesome ones, the enemies of the cross of Christ.*

1 Furthermore, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is not tedious for me, but it is necessary for you.
2 Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision <note>original: "concisionem," a derogatory play on the word for circumcision, implying a mere "mutilation" of the flesh</note>.
3 For we are the circumcision, who serve God in spirit, and glory in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh:
4 Although I might also have confidence in the flesh. If anyone else seems to trust in the flesh, I more so:
<margin>† Acts 23:6</margin>
5 Circumcised on the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; according to the law, a Pharisee;
6 According to zeal, persecuting the Church of God; according to the justice which is in the law, living without reproach.
7 But what things were gain to me, these I have considered loss for the sake of Christ.
8 Furthermore, I consider all things to be loss because of the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and I consider them as dung <note>original: "stercora," meaning refuse or waste</note>, that I may gain Christ,
9 And be found in him, not having my own justice, which is from the law, but that which is from the faith of Christ Jesus: the justice which is from God in faith,
10 To know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings: being conformed to his death:
11 If by any means I may attain to the resurrection which is from the dead.
12 Not that I have already attained it, or am already perfect: but I follow after, if by any means I may lay hold of that for which I have also been laid hold of by Christ Jesus.
13 Brothers, I do not consider myself to have laid hold of it. But one thing I do: forgetting those things which are behind, and stretching myself forward to those things which are ahead,
14 I press toward the mark, for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
15 Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, feel this way: and if in anything you think otherwise, God will reveal this also to you.
16 Nevertheless, to what we have already attained, let us be of the same mind; and let us remain in the same rule.
17 Be imitators of me, brothers, and observe those who walk so, as you have our pattern.
18 For many walk, of whom I have often told you (and now tell you even weeping) that they are enemies of the cross of Christ:
19 Whose end is destruction: whose god is their belly: and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.
20 But our citizenship <note>original: "conversatio," referring to one's manner of life or state of belonging</note> is in heaven: from whence also we look for the Savior, our Lord Jesus Christ,

### CHAPTER IV.
*He prepares them for perseverance and spiritual joy, modesty, prayers, and thanksgiving, wishing the peace of God upon them: and that they should hold fast to whatever belongs to God and is praiseworthy; and concerning what was necessary for Epaphroditus and what they had sent to him.*

1 Therefore, my brothers, most dear and most longed for, my joy and my crown: stand fast in the Lord in this way, most dear ones.
2 I beg Euodia, and I entreat Syntyche <note>These were two prominent women in the Philippian church who were apparently in disagreement</note>, to be of the same mind in the Lord.
3 And I ask you also, loyal companion <note>original: "germane compar," possibly referring to a specific unnamed person or a "true yokefellow"</note>, help those women who have labored with me in the Gospel along with Clement, and the rest of my fellow-workers, whose names are in the book of life.
4 Rejoice in the Lord always: again I say, rejoice.
5 Let your modesty be known to all men: the Lord is near.
6 Be anxious for nothing: but in every prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God.
7 And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, keep your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
8 For the rest, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever modest, whatever just, whatever holy, whatever lovely, whatever of good fame, if there be any virtue, if any praise of discipline, think on these things.

9 The things which you have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, these do: and the God of peace shall be with you.
10 But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at last your care for me has flourished again, as you were also mindful, but you were occupied.
11 I do not say this as if because of want: for I have learned, in whatever state I am, to be self-sufficient.
12 I know how to be humbled, and I know how to abound: (everywhere and in all things I am instructed) both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.
13 I can do all things in him who strengthens me.
14 Nevertheless, you have done well, communicating with my tribulation.
15 And you also know, Philippians, that in the beginning of the Gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me in the matter of giving and receiving, but you only;
16 For even to Thessalonica you sent once and twice for my use.
17 Not because I seek the gift, but I require fruit abounding in your account.
18 But I have all things, and I abound: I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things which you sent, an odor of sweetness <note>A phrase used in the Old Testament to describe sacrifices that are pleasing to God</note>, 
<margin>† Romans 12:1</margin>† an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
19 And may my God fulfill all your desire, according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
20 Now to God and our Father be glory forever and ever: Amen.
21 Salute every saint in Christ Jesus.
22 The brothers who are with me salute you. All the saints salute you, especially those who are of Caesar’s household <note>This suggests Paul had converts even among the Emperor's imperial staff or slaves in Rome</note>.
23 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

### TO THE COLOSSIANS.
#### CHAPTER ONE.
*Having heard of the faith, charity, and hope of the Colossians, the Apostle prays for them, that they may be perfected in the knowledge of God and in good works: he calls Christ the image of God, through whom all things were created, and who is the head of the Church, by whom all things are reconciled: he exhorts them therefore to remain immovable in faith: and says he is made a minister of Christ to preach the mystery hidden from ages, and now made manifest.*

2 To those who are at Colossae, the holy and faithful brothers in Christ Jesus.

5 For the sake of the hope which is laid up for you in heaven: which you have heard in the word of the truth of the Gospel:

7 Just as you learned from Epaphras, our most dear fellow-servant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ Jesus,
8 Who also has manifested to us your love in the spirit.
9 Therefore we also, from the day we heard it, do not cease praying for you, and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding:
10 That you may walk worthily of God, pleasing him in all things: being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God.

### CHAPTER II.

->He exhorts them to take care lest they be seduced from the faith of Christ by any persuasions or deceptions of philosophers, or of those wishing to introduce the Law; through Christ they have been freed from sins, from the power of the devil, and from the handwritten record that was against them, so that now legal decrees are to be held in no value.<-

1 For I want you to know what kind of concern I have for you, and for those who are at Laodicea, and for whoever has not seen my face in the flesh:
2 That their hearts may be comforted, instructed in charity, and unto all the riches of the fullness of understanding, unto the knowledge of the mystery of God the Father and of Christ Jesus:

<column-break/>

3 In whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
4 Now I say this so that no one may deceive you with the loftiness of words.
<margin>†</margin>
5 † For although I am absent in body, yet I am with you in spirit: rejoicing and seeing your order, and the firmness of your faith which is in Christ.
6 Therefore, just as you have received Jesus Christ the Lord, walk in him,
7 Rooted and built up in him, and confirmed in the faith, just as you have also learned, abounding in it with thanksgiving.
8 See that no one deceives you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ:
9 Because in him dwells all the fullness of the divinity bodily:
10 And you are filled in him, who is the head of all principality and power:
11 In whom also you are circumcised with a circumcision not made by hand in the stripping off of the body of the flesh, but in the circumcision of Christ:
12 Buried together with him in baptism, in which also you have risen again through faith in the working of God, who raised him from the dead.
<margin>† Ephesians 2:1</margin>
13 † And you, when you were dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he brought to life together with him, forgiving you all sins:
14 Blotting out the handwritten record <term>chirographum; a legal bond or certificate of debt</term> of the decree that was against us, which was contrary to us, and he took it out of the way, fastening it to the cross:
15 And despoiling the principalities and powers, he exposed them confidently, openly triumphing over them in himself.
16 Therefore let no one judge you in food, or in drink, or in respect of a festival day, or of the new moon <note>original: "neomenia"</note>, or of the Sabbaths:
17 Which are a shadow of things to come: but the body is of Christ.
<margin>† Matthew 25:4</margin>
18 † Let no one seduce you, willing in humility and the religion of angels, walking in things he has not seen, in vain puffed up by the sense of his flesh,
19 And not holding the head, from which the whole body, supplied and built up through joints and connections, grows into the increase of God.
20 If therefore you are dead with Christ to the elements of this world: why do you still decree as if living in the world?
21 "Do not touch, nor taste, nor handle":
22 Which things all perish in their very use, according to the precepts and doctrines of men:
23 Which indeed have an appearance of wisdom in superstition and humility, and in not sparing the body, but are not in any honor for the satisfying of the flesh.

### CHAPTER III.
