# THE EPISTLE
## OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL
### TO THE THESSALONIANS, THE FIRST.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*He commends the Thessalonians, giving thanks to God that they have preserved the faith once received, having become imitators of Paul, and indeed of the Lord himself, and a model for the rest of the believers, openly showing what fruit Paul's preaching had among them.*

Paul, and Silvanus <note>Also known as Silas, a leading member of the early Christian community who accompanied Paul on his second missionary journey.</note>, and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians, in God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Grace to you, and peace. We give thanks to God always for all of you, making memory of you in our prayers without ceasing,
3 Mindful of the work of your faith, and labor, and charity, and the endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father:
4 Knowing, brothers, beloved by God, your election <note>original: "electionem"; Paul refers to the belief that God has specifically chosen this community to receive the Gospel</note>:
5 Because our Gospel was not unto you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, and in great fullness, just as you know what kind of men we were among you for your sake.
6 And you became imitators of us, and of the Lord, receiving the word in much tribulation, with the joy of the Holy Spirit:
7 So that you have become a model to all believers in Macedonia, and in Achaia <note>Macedonia (northern Greece) and Achaia (southern Greece) were the two main Roman provinces of the region</note>.
8 For from you the word of the Lord has been spread abroad, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith, which is toward God, has gone forth, so that it is not necessary for us to say anything.
9 For they themselves report about us what kind of entrance we had to you: and how you were converted to God from idols, to serve the living and true God,
10 And to wait for his Son from heaven (whom he raised from the dead), Jesus, who rescued us from the coming wrath.

### CHAPTER II.

*He shows how sincere he showed himself to be in preaching the Gospel to them, giving thanks to God that they diligently kept the word of God they received, having suffered many things from their own countrymen, just as the Churches of Judea suffered from the Jews, who together with Christ also persecute all the godly: he also declares how ardent an affection he bears toward them.*

<margin>Acts 16:19.</margin>
For you yourselves know, brothers, our entrance to you, that it was not in vain:
2 But having suffered before, and † having been treated with indignity (as you know) in Philippi, we had confidence in our God to speak to you the Gospel of God in much concern.
3 For our exhortation was not from error, nor from impurity, nor in deceit,
4 But as we were approved by God to be entrusted with the Gospel: so we speak, not

<column-break/>

as pleasing men, but God, who proves our hearts.
5 For neither were we ever in the speech of flattery, as you know: nor in the opportunity for greed: God is witness:
6 Nor seeking glory from men, neither from you, nor from others.
7 When we could have been a burden to you as Apostles of Christ: but we became little ones <note>original: "parvuli"; some manuscripts read "gentle" (lenes), but the Vulgate uses the term for "little children" to show Paul's humility</note> in your midst, as if a nurse were to cherish her own children.
8 So desiring you, we were eagerly willing to hand over to you not only the Gospel of God, but also our own souls: because you have become most dear to us.
9 For you are mindful, brothers, of our labor and exhaustion: † working night and day <note>Paul famously worked as a tentmaker to support himself so as not to be a financial burden to the new churches</note>, so as not to burden any of you, we preached the Gospel of God among you.
10 You are witnesses, and God, how holily and justly, and without complaint, we were toward you who believed:
11 As you know, how [we treated] each one of you (like a father his own children)
12 Pleading with you and comforting you, we testified that you should walk worthily of God, who called you into his kingdom and glory.
13 Therefore we also give thanks to God without ceasing: because when you had received from us the word of the hearing of God <note>original: "verbum auditus Dei"; refers to the message heard from God's messengers</note>, you received it not as the word of men, but (as it truly is) the word of God, who works in you who have believed.
14 For you, brothers, became imitators of the Churches of God which are in Judea in Christ Jesus: because you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen, just as they did from the Jews:
15 Who both killed the Lord Jesus and the Prophets, and persecuted us, and they do not please God, and are adversaries to all men;
16 Hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles so that they might be saved, so that they might always fill up [the measure of] their sins: for the wrath of God has come upon them even to the end.
17 But we, brothers, being desolated from you for a short time, in presence, not in heart, hastened more abundantly to see your face with great desire:
18 Because we wanted to come to you: I, Paul, indeed, once and again, but Satan hindered us.
19 For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of glory? Are you not [so] before our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?
20 For you are our glory and joy.

### CHAPTER III.

*Fearing lest on account of his afflictions they might be moved from the faith, he sent Timothy to them, who might strengthen them: but when he returned, he gives thanks to God that they remained firm in faith and love: showing how much he desires to visit them, so that he might supply what is lacking in their faith.*

Because of which, bearing it no longer, it pleased us to remain at Athens, alone:

## C H A P T E R IV.

*He exhorts them to observe the precepts delivered to them, abstaining from fornication, and loving one another, and working with their hands, so that they might not be forced to desire anything from anyone: he teaches the manner of our resurrection, so that they are not tortured by inordinate sadness for those who die.*

1 Furthermore, therefore, brothers, we ask you and beseech you in the Lord Jesus, that as you have received from us how you ought to walk and to please God, so also you would walk, that you may abound all the more.
2 For you know what precepts I gave to you through the Lord Jesus.
<margin>† Rom. 12:2, Eph. 5:17</margin> 3 † For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you should abstain from fornication.
4 That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel <note>original: "vas suum"; likely referring to one's own body or one's wife, emphasizing self-control and honor</note> in sanctification and honor;
5 Not in the passion of desire, like the Gentiles <note>A term used by Paul to refer to non-Jewish people who did not yet know the God of Israel</note> who do not know God:
6 And that no man should overstep or deceive his brother in business: because the Lord is the avenger of all these things, as we have foretold to you, and have testified.
7 For God has not called us to uncleanness, but to sanctification.
8 Therefore, he who despises these things, despises not man, but God: who has also given his Holy Spirit in us.
9 But concerning the charity of brotherhood, we have no 

<column-break/>

need to write to you: † for you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another. <margin>† John 13:34 & 15:12, 17; 1 John 2:10 & 4:12</margin>

11 And that you strive to be quiet, and to attend to your own business, and to work with your hands, just as we commanded you: and that you may walk honestly toward those who are outside: and that you may desire nothing of anyone.
12 And we would not have you ignorant, brothers, concerning those who are sleeping <note>original: "de dormientibus"; a common early Christian metaphor for those who have died</note>, so that you may not be saddened, even as others who have no hope.

15 For the Lord himself, with a command, and with the voice of the Archangel, and with the trumpet of God, shall descend from heaven: and the dead who are in Christ shall rise first.
16 Then we who are alive, who are left, shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord.
17 Therefore, comfort one another with these words.

## C H A P T E R V.

7 For those who sleep, sleep at night: and those who are drunk, are drunk at night.

12 And we ask you, brothers, to recognize those who labor among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you,
13 That you might hold them more abundantly in charity because of their work: have peace with them.

->CHAPTER ONE.<-

*He gives thanks to God for the faith and endurance of the Thessalonians during persecutions, because of which he says they shall receive glory, while their adversaries shall receive vengeance on the day of judgment: praying that they may be found worthy of God's calling.*

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap P, square border with floral leaf designs.</image-desc>
**P**aul, and Silvanus, <note>Silvanus is the Latin form of Silas, a companion of Paul mentioned frequently in the Acts of the Apostles.</note> and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians, in God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
3 We ought to give thanks to God always for you, brothers, as is fitting, because your faith grows exceedingly, and the charity of every one of you toward each other abounds:
4 So that we ourselves glory in you in the Churches of God, for your patience and faith, and in all your persecutions and tribulations which you endure
5 As an example of the just judgment of God, that you may be found worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer.
6 For it is indeed just in the sight of God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you:
7 And to you, who are troubled, rest with us at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of his power,
8 In a flame of fire giving vengeance to those who did not know God, and who do not obey the Gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.
9 Who shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction from the face of the Lord, and from the glory of his power:
10 When he shall come to be glorified in his saints, and to be made wonderful in all those who have believed: because our testimony among you was believed on that day.
11 To which end also we pray always for you: that our God would count you worthy of his calling, and fulfill every desire for goodness and the work of faith in power,
12 That the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

<column-break/>

->CHAPTER II.<-

*Concerning the day of the Lord, he warns them not to believe deceivers, showing that the son of perdition must come first, who will perform various deceptive wonders by which the reprobate will be led astray: he gives thanks for the election and faith of the Thessalonians, warning them to keep the traditions received from him, and prays for their consolation and confirmation.*

**W**e beseech you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and of our gathering together unto him:
2 That you be not easily moved from your senses nor terrified; neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as if sent by us, as if the day of the Lord were at hand.
3 Let no one deceive you in any way: for unless the rebellion <note>original: "discessio"; often translated as apostasy or a falling away.</note> comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition, <margin>† Ephesians 5:6.</margin>
4 Who opposes and is exalted above all that is called God, or that is worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as if he were God.
5 Do you not remember that when I was still with you, I told you these things?
6 And now you know what withholds him, so that he may be revealed in his own time.
7 For the mystery of iniquity <note>original: "mysterium iniquitatis"; referring to a hidden lawlessness or evil already at work in the world.</note> is already at work: only that he who now holds back, let him hold back until he is taken out of the way.
8 And then that wicked one shall be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus shall kill with the breath of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming: <margin>† Isaiah 11:4.</margin>
9 Whose coming is according to the working of Satan, in all power, and signs, and lying wonders,
10 And in all seduction of iniquity for those who perish: because they did not receive the love of the truth that they might be saved. Therefore God shall send them the working of error, that they may believe a lie,
11 That all may be judged who have not believed the truth, but have consented to iniquity.
12 But we ought to give thanks to God always for you, brothers beloved by God, because God has chosen you as firstfruits unto salvation.

<margin>Acts 20:34. 1 Corinthians 4:12. 1 Thessalonians 2:9.</margin>
8 † Neither did we eat any man's bread for free, but worked with labor and weariness, night and day, so that we might not be a burden to any of you.
9 Not because we did not have the authority, but so that we might give ourselves as a model for you to imitate.
10 For even when we were with you, we gave you this charge: that if any man will not work, neither let him eat. <note>original: "si quis non vult operari, nec manducet"; a famous apostolic rule emphasizing communal responsibility and self-sufficiency.</note>
11 For we have heard that there are some among you who walk restlessly, doing no work at all, but acting as busybodies.
12 Now to those who are such, we charge and beseech them in the Lord Jesus Christ, that working in silence, they eat their own bread.
<margin>Galatians 6:9.</margin>
13 † But you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good.
14 And if anyone does not obey our word by this epistle, take note of him, and do not keep company with him, so that he may be ashamed:
15 Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but correct him as a brother.
16 Now may the Lord of peace himself give you everlasting peace in every place. The Lord be with you all.
17 The greeting is by my own hand, Paul's: which is the sign in every epistle; so I write. <note>Paul often used a scribe but would sign the end of his letters personally to verify their authenticity.</note>
18 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*He recalls the command he gave to Timothy concerning the restraining of certain people from perverse doctrine and the teaching of sound doctrine: the law is established because of the unjust: he gives thanks to God for calling him from the persecution of the Church to the Apostleship: and who obtained mercy, so that God's long-suffering might be shown as an example for sinners: he warns Timothy to act as a vigorous soldier.*

Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the command of God our Savior, and of Christ Jesus our hope:
<margin>Acts 16:1.</margin>
2 To Timothy, his beloved son in faith. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father, and Christ Jesus our Lord.
3 As I asked you to remain at Ephesus when

<column-break/>

I went into Macedonia, so that you might charge certain people not to teach otherwise,
<margin>Below 4:7. 2 Timothy 2:23. Titus 3:9.</margin>
4 Nor † to give heed to fables and endless genealogies: which provide questions rather than the edification of God, which is in faith. <note>original: "fabulis, & genealogiis interminatis"; likely referring to complex speculative theories about divine lineages common in early Gnostic or Jewish mystical circles.</note>
5 Now the end of the commandment is charity from a pure heart, and a good conscience, and faith unfeigned.
6 From which things some, having wandered away, have turned aside into vain talk,
7 Desiring to be teachers of the law, yet understanding neither what they say, nor whereof they affirm.

11 Which is according to the Gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which has been committed to my trust.

20 Of whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander: whom I have delivered to Satan <note>A term for excommunication or expulsion from the church community</note>, that they may learn not to blaspheme.

### CHAPTER II.

*He desires that prayers and thanksgivings be made for kings and magistrates, and says that there is one God and one mediator: how man and woman ought to pray, and how she should be adorned; it is not her part to teach, but to learn in silence.*

1 **I desire** therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men:
2 For kings, and all who are in high station, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life, in all piety and chastity.
3 For this is good and acceptable before God our Savior,
4 Who wishes all men to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
5 For there is one God, and one mediator of God and men, the man Christ Jesus:
6 Who gave himself as a redemption for all, a testimony in its own time:
7 Wherein I am appointed a preacher and an Apostle (I speak the truth, I do not lie), a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
8 I will therefore that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands, without anger and contention.
<margin>1 Peter 3</margin>
9 † In like manner also women in decent apparel, adorning themselves with modesty and sobriety, and not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly attire:
10 But as becomes women professing piety through good works.
11 Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection.
<margin>1 Corinthians 14:34, Genesis 2:27</margin>
12 † But I do not permit a woman to teach, nor to use authority over the man; but to be in silence.
13 † For Adam was first formed, then Eve:

<column-break/>

14 † And Adam was not seduced, but the woman being seduced, was in the transgression.
15 Yet she shall be saved through child-bearing, if she continues in faith, and love, and sanctification, with sobriety.

### CHAPTER III.

*He teaches Timothy what kind of men bishops, deacons, and women ought to be: so that he may know how he ought to behave in the Church, which is the pillar of truth; at the same time he commends the mystery of the Lord's incarnation.*

1 **A faithful** saying: If a man desires the office of a bishop <note>original: "episcopatum" - meaning an overseer or supervisor</note>, he desires a good work.
2 † It behoves a bishop, therefore, to be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober, prudent, of good behavior, chaste, given to hospitality, a teacher.
3 Not given to wine, no striker <note>not violent or prone to hitting</note>, but modest, not litigious, not covetous, but
4 One who rules well his own house, having his children in subjection with all chastity.
5 But if a man knows not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the Church of God?
6 Not a neophyte <note>original: "neophytum" - a new convert</note>: lest being puffed up with pride, he fall into the judgment of the devil.
7 Moreover, he must have a good testimony from those who are outside, that he may not fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
8 Deacons in like manner chaste, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre <note>dishonest profit</note>;
9 Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.
10 And let these also first be proved: and so let them minister, having no crime.
11 The women in like manner chaste, not detractors, sober, faithful in all things.
12 Let deacons be the husbands of one wife: who rule their children well, and their own houses.
13 For they who have ministered well shall purchase for themselves a good degree, and much confidence in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
14 These things I write to you, hoping that I shall come to you shortly.
15 But if I tarry long, that you may know how you ought to behave yourself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.
16 And evidently great is the sacrament of piety, which was manifested in the flesh, was justified in the spirit, appeared to angels, has been preached to the Gentiles, is believed in the world, is taken up in glory.

### CHAPTER IV.

*He foretells that some shall deliver false doctrine, especially concerning marriage and foods: but he advises his disciple that, having despised vain doctrine, he should exercise himself unto piety, which is preferred to bodily exercise: and though he be young, he should show himself an example to the rest.*

1 **Now the Spirit** manifestly says, that † in the last times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to spirits of error, and doctrines of devils.
2 Speaking lies in hypocrisy, and having their conscience seared,
3 Forbidding to marry, to abstain from foods...

### CHAPTER V.

*He teaches how he should govern the elders, the old women, and the young women; likewise the elder and younger widows: and concerning the conditions required in choosing a widow: that priests performing their office well should be honored doubly: that he should not easily accept an accusation against a priest, but should rebuke those who sin publicly; that he should keep these mandates, not imposing hands hastily on anyone: that he should use a little wine: and concerning the various sins of men.*

1 Do not rebuke an elder, but entreat him as a father; the young men, as brothers; 
2 The old women, as mothers; the young women, as sisters, in all purity: 
3 Honor widows who are truly widows. 
4 But if any widow has children or grandchildren: let her learn first to govern her own house, and to make a return of service to her parents: for this is acceptable before God. 
5 But she who is truly a widow and desolate, let her hope in God, and continue in supplications and prayers night and day. 
6 For she who lives in delicacies <note>or "pleasure-seeking"</note> is dead while she is living. 
7 And command this, that they may be blameless. 
8 But if any man does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his house, he has denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. 
9 Let a widow be chosen who is not less than sixty years of age, who has been the wife of one husband, 
10 Having a testimony for good works: if she has educated children, if she has received guests, if she has washed the feet of the saints, if she has assisted those suffering tribulation, if she has followed every good work.

<column-break/>

11 But avoid the younger widows. For when they have grown wanton against Christ, they want to marry: 
12 Having damnation, because they have made void their first faith. 
13 And at the same time, being idle, they learn to go about from house to house: and not only idle, but also talkative and curious, saying things they ought not. 
14 I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, be mistresses of families, and give no occasion to the adversary to speak evil. 
15 For some are already turned aside after Satan. 
16 If any of the faithful has widows, let him provide for them, and let the Church not be burdened: so that there may be enough for those who are truly widows. 
17 Let the priests <note>original: "presbyteri," elders or leaders of the community</note> who rule well be held worthy of double honor: especially those who labor in the word and doctrine. 
<margin>† Deuteronomy 25:4; 1 Corinthians 9:9.</margin> 
18 For the Scripture says: † You shall not muzzle the ox that treads out the grain. And: † The laborer is worthy of his reward. 
<margin>† Matthew 10:10; Luke 10:7.</margin> 
19 Against a priest, do not receive an accusation except under two or three witnesses. 
20 Rebuke those who sin in the presence of all: so that the rest also may have fear. 
21 I charge you before God and Christ Jesus, and the elect angels, that you observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing by leaning to one side. 
22 Do not impose hands lightly upon anyone, nor participate in the sins of others. Keep yourself chaste. 
23 Do not drink only water anymore, but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent infirmities. 
24 The sins of some men are manifest, going before them to judgment: but in others, they follow after. 
25 Likewise also, good deeds are manifest: and those that are otherwise cannot be hidden.

### CHAPTER VI.

<note>Chapter VI is mislabeled as Chapter IX in the original text.</note>

*Servants should be obedient to their masters, whether faithful or unfaithful: those who leave these things to teach vanities are to be avoided: how much evil avarice brings: having avoided it, he exhorts Timothy to embrace virtues, keeping the faith which he confessed in Baptism; let him keep these mandates until the end: let him restrain the rich from pride, leading them to give alms.*

1 Whoever are servants under the yoke, let them count their masters worthy of all honor, lest the name of the Lord and his doctrine be blasphemed. 
2 But they who have faithful masters, let them not despise them because they are brothers: but rather serve them the more, because they are faithful and beloved, who are partakers of the benefit. Teach and exhort these things. 
3 If any man teaches otherwise, and does not consent to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to that doctrine which is according to godliness: 
4 He is proud, knowing nothing, but sick with questions and debates about words: from which arise envy, contentions, blasphemies, evil suspicions, 
5 Conflicts of men corrupted in mind, and who are deprived of the truth, thinking that godliness is a source of gain. 
6 But godliness with contentment is great gain.

# THE EPISTLE
## OF BLESSED PAUL THE APOSTLE
### TO TIMOTHY II.

-> CHAPTER ONE. <-

*He gives thanks to God for Timothy's faith, which he commands to be exercised through fearless preaching: Christ destroyed death, and chose Paul as a teacher of the Gentiles, keeping for him the reward due to his labors: he says that all those in Asia <note>Referring to the Roman province in modern-day Turkey</note> have left him, praising the household of Onesiphorus because he received many services from there.*

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial P featuring floral patterns and a bird.</image-desc>
1 Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in Christ Jesus:
2 To Timothy, my most dearly beloved son: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
3 I give thanks to God, whom I serve from my forefathers with a pure conscience, that without ceasing I have a remembrance of you in my prayers, night and day.
4 Greatly desiring to see you, being mindful of your tears, that I may be filled with joy,
5 Recalling that faith which is in you, unfeigned, which also dwelt first in your grandmother Lois, and in your mother Eunice, and I am certain that it is in you also.
6 For which cause I admonish you that you stir up the grace <note>original: "gratiam," meaning the spiritual gift or charism</note> of God which is in you by the imposition of my hands.
7 <margin>† Romans 8:15</margin> † For God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of sobriety.
8 Be not therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but labor with the Gospel according to the power of God:

<column-break/>

9 Who has delivered us and called us with his holy calling, † not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before the worlds began.
10 But it is now made manifest by the illumination of our Savior Jesus Christ, who has indeed destroyed death, and has brought life and incorruption to light through the Gospel:
11 In which † I am appointed a preacher, and an Apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
12 For which cause I also suffer these things, but I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and I am certain that he is able to keep that which I have committed to him <note>original: "depositum meum," my trust or deposit</note> against that day.
13 Hold the form of sound words which you have heard from me in faith and in the love in Christ Jesus.
14 Guard the good trust <note>original: "depositum," the precious teaching</note> by the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
15 You know this, that all who are in Asia have turned away from me, of whom are Phigellus and Hermogenes.
16 May the Lord give mercy † to the house of Onesiphorus: because he has often refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain:
17 But when he had come to Rome, he carefully sought me out and found me.
18 May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord in that day. And in how many things he ministered to me at Ephesus, you know very well.

### C H A P T E R II.

->*He encourages Timothy to teach others sincerely and to suffer for Christ, mentioning the future reward and the resurrection of Christ: and that he should avoid contentions and profane idle talk, as well as foolish questions of the law; concerning the large house having various vessels, and which virtues the servant of God ought to pursue.*<-

**1** You therefore, my son, be strengthened in the grace which is in Christ Jesus:
**2** And the things which you have heard from me through many witnesses, commend these to faithful men, who shall be fit to teach others also.
**3** Labor as a good soldier of Christ Jesus:
**4** No one serving as a soldier for God entangles himself in secular business: that he may please him to whom he has proven himself.
**5** For if anyone also competes in a contest <note>original: "in agone," referring to the Greek athletic games</note>, he is not crowned unless he has competed according to the rules.
**6** The laboring farmer ought to be the first to partake of the fruits.
**7** Understand what I say: for the Lord will give you understanding in all things.
**8** Be mindful that the Lord JESUS CHRIST has risen from the dead from the seed of David, according to my Gospel,
**9** In which I labor even unto chains, as an evildoer: but the word of God is not bound.
**10** Therefore I endure all things for the sake of the elect, that they also may obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus, with heavenly glory.
**11** A faithful saying: For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him:
**12** If we endure, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us:
<margin>† Matthew 10:33. Mark 8:38. † Romans 3:3.</margin>
**13** † If we do not believe, he remains faithful; he cannot deny himself.
**14** Remind them of these things, testifying before the Lord. Do not strive with words: for it is useful for nothing, except for the subversion of the listeners.
**15** Carefully study to present yourself approved unto God, a workman who need not be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth:
**16** But avoid profane and vain babblings: for they lead much toward ungodliness:
**17** And their speech spreads like a cancer <note>original: "ut cancer serpit," a metaphor for how false teaching can consume a community</note>: of whom are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
**18** Who have fallen away from the truth, saying the resurrection has already happened, and they have subverted the faith of some.
**19** But the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal: the Lord knows those who are his: and let everyone who names the name of the Lord depart from iniquity.
**20** But in a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and of earth: and some indeed unto honor, but others unto dishonor.
**21** If any man therefore shall cleanse himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honor, sanctified and useful to the Lord, prepared for every good work.
**22** But flee youthful desires, and pursue justice, faith, charity, and peace with those who call upon the Lord from a pure heart.
<margin>† 1 Timothy 1:4, 7. Titus 3:9</margin>
**23** † But avoid foolish and unlearned questions: knowing that they beget strifes.
**24** But the servant of the Lord must not strive: but be mild toward all men, apt to teach, patient,
**25** With modesty correcting those who resist the

<column-break/>

truth: lest at any time God give them repentance to know the truth,
**26** And they recover themselves from the snares of the devil, by whom they are held captive at his will.

### C H A P T E R III.

->*He predicts that men in the future will be involved in various sins, and who, by seducing weak women, resist the truth: but he encourages Timothy that he should embrace virtues by his example, and endurance in persecutions: and concerning the utility of the holy scriptures.*<-

<margin>† 1 Timothy 1:1, 2 Peter 3:3, Jude 18.</margin>
**1** But know this, that in the † last days dangerous times shall come:
**2** Men shall be lovers of themselves, covetous, puffed up, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, wicked,
**3** Without affection, without peace, false accusers, incontinent, unmerciful, without kindness,
**4** Traitors, stubborn, bloated, and lovers of pleasures more than of God:
**5** Having an appearance indeed of godliness, but denying the power thereof. Flee from these also:
**6** For of these are they who creep into houses, and lead captive weak women <note>original: "mulierculas," literally "little women," used here to suggest those easily led astray</note> burdened with sins, who are led away by various desires:
**7** Always learning, and never attaining to the knowledge of the truth.
<margin>† Exodus 7:11.</margin>
**8** Now as † Jannes and Mambres <note>Traditional names for the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses</note> resisted Moses: so these also resist the truth, men corrupt in mind, reprobate concerning the faith.
**9** But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest to all, as theirs also was.
**10** But you have fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, love, patience,
**11** Persecutions, afflictions: such as came to me at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra: what persecutions I endured, and out of them all the Lord delivered me.
**12** And all who will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution.
**13** But evil men and seducers shall grow worse and worse: erring, and driving others into error.
**14** But continue in those things which you have learned, and which have been entrusted to you: knowing from whom you have learned them:
**15** And because from infancy you have known the holy scriptures, which can instruct you unto salvation, through the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
<margin>† 2 Peter 1:20</margin>
**16** † All scripture, inspired by God, is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in justice:
**17** That the man of God may be perfect, furnished unto every good work.

### C H A P T E R V.
<note>This chapter is labeled V in the source text, though it is historically cataloged as Chapter 4 in the Vulgate and modern Bibles.</note>

# THE EPISTLE OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL
## TO TITUS.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*Having mentioned in the greeting the hope of eternal life which has now been manifested, he shows what kind of priests and bishops he ought to ordain: concerning certain ones who, because of various vices, must be sharply rebuked: to the pure all things are pure: some falsely deny God.*

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'P' featuring scrolling foliage designs within a square border.</image-desc>
**1** Paul, a servant of God, and an Apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of the elect of God and the knowledge of the truth which is according to godliness.
**2** In the hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before the ages of time.
**3** But he has manifested his word in his own time through preaching, which was entrusted to me according to the command of God our Savior.
**4** To Titus, my beloved son according to our common faith, grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
**5** For this reason I left you in Crete, that you might set in order the things that are lacking, and appoint priests <term>priests: "presbyteros," elders or community leaders</term> throughout the cities, as I also directed you.
<margin>† 1 Timothy 3:2.</margin>
**6** † If any man is without reproach, the husband of one wife, having faithful children, not accused of luxury or disobedience.
**7** For it is necessary for a bishop <term>bishop: "episcopum," an overseer or supervisor of the church</term> to be without reproach, as God’s steward: not proud, not

<column-break/>

quick-tempered, not given to wine, not a striker, not greedy for filthy lucre <note>original: "turpis lucri," shameful or dishonest profit</note>:
**8** But hospitable, kind, sober, just, holy, continent,
**9** Embracing that faithful word which is according to doctrine; so that he may be able to exhort in sound doctrine and to convince those who contradict it.
**10** For there are also many disobedient, vain talkers, and seducers; especially those who are of the circumcision:
**11** Who must be rebuked: who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for the sake of filthy lucre.
**12** One of them, a prophet of their own, said: The Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, slow bellies <note>Paul is quoting the Cretan philosopher Epimenides here to illustrate the local reputation of the islanders</note>.
**13** This testimony is true. For which cause rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
**14** Not giving heed to Jewish fables and the commandments of men who turn themselves away from the truth.
<margin>† Romans 14:20.</margin>
**15** † To the pure, all things are pure: but to the defiled and the unfaithful, nothing is pure, but both their mind and conscience are defiled.
**16** They profess that they know God, but in their works they deny him: being abominable, and incredulous, and reprobate unto every good work.

### CHAPTER II.

->*How it ought to befit old men, old women, young*<-

1 But you, speak the things that befit sound doctrine:
2 That old men be sober, chaste, prudent, sound in faith, in love, in patience:
3 Old women likewise in holy attire <note>original: "habitu sancto," referring to a demeanor and dress appropriate for sacred duties</note>, not slanderers, not enslaved to much wine, teaching well.
4 That they may teach the young women prudence, to love their husbands, to cherish their children,
5 To be prudent, chaste, sober, having care for the home, kind, subject to their husbands, so that the word of God is not blasphemed:
6 Likewise exhort the young men to be sober.
7 In all things show yourself an example of good works, in doctrine, in integrity, in gravity,
8 A sound word, beyond reproach: so that he who is on the opposite side may be afraid, having nothing evil to say of us.

Colossians 3:22.
1 Peter 2:18.

<margin>† Below 3:4.</margin>
11 † For the grace of God our Savior has appeared to all men.
12 Instructing us, that denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we should live soberly, and justly, and piously in this age,
13 Looking for the blessed hope and the coming of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ.
14 Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and cleanse for himself an acceptable people, a follower of good works.
15 Speak these things, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. Let no one despise you.

### CHAPTER III.

->*To which virtues he should exhort his own, and from*<-
->*which vices he should discourage them: and that from*<-
->*former sins we are saved by the kindness of God alone*<-
->*through the washing of regeneration, having been made heirs*<-

1 Remind them to be subject to princes and powers, to obey the word, to be ready for every good work:
2 To blaspheme no one, not to be litigious, but modest, showing all mildness toward all men.
3 For we also were once foolish, unbelieving, wandering, serving various desires and pleasures, acting in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.
<margin>† Above 2:11.</margin>
4 † But when the kindness and humanity of God our Savior appeared;
<margin>† 1 Timothy 1:9.</margin>

6 Whom he poured out upon us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior.
7 That having been justified by his grace, we might be heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
8 It is a faithful saying: and concerning these things I want you to be firm: so that those who believe in God may take care to excel in good works. These things are good and useful to men.
<margin>† 1 Timothy 1:4 and 4:7.</margin>

<margin>2 Timothy 2:23.</margin>

12 When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, hasten to come to me at Nicopolis: for I have decided to winter there.
13 Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos carefully ahead, so that nothing is lacking to them.
14 And let our people also learn to excel in good works for necessary uses, so that they are not unfruitful.
15 All who are with me greet you: greet those who love us in faith. The grace of God be with you all. Amen.

# THE EPISTLE
# OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE PAUL
# TO PHILEMON.

## THE ONLY CHAPTER.

*He commends the charity and faith of Philemon, and sends back his servant Onesimus: whom he recommends to him, taking the servant's fault upon himself; indicating that he desires to keep him, so that he might serve him in the preaching of the Gospel.*

1 Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother; to Philemon, our beloved and fellow laborer,
2 And to our dearest sister Apphia, and to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church which is in your house.
3 Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
4 I give thanks to my God, always making mention of you in my prayers,
5 Hearing of your charity and the faith which you have in the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints:
6 That the sharing <note>original: "communicatio," referring to the participation or fellowship of faith</note> of your faith may become evident in the acknowledgment of every good work which is in you in Christ Jesus.
7 For I have had great joy and consolation in your charity, because the hearts <note>original: "viscera," literally the "bowels" or internal organs, used as a Hebrew idiom for the seat of deep emotion and compassion</note> of the saints have been refreshed by you, brother.
8 Therefore, though I have much confidence in Christ Jesus to command you what is proper:
9 For charity’s sake I rather beseech you, being such a one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ:

<column-break/>

10 I beseech you for my son, whom I have begotten in my bonds, Onesimus,
11 Who once was useless to you, but now is useful both to me and to you,
12 Whom I have sent back to you. And do you receive him as my own heart:
13 Whom I would have retained with me, that in your stead he might have served me in the bonds of the Gospel:
14 But without your counsel I would do nothing, so that your good deed might not be as if by necessity, but voluntary.
15 For perhaps he therefore departed from you for a season, that you might receive him again forever:
16 Not now as a servant, but instead of a servant, a most dear brother, especially to me; but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord?
17 If therefore you count me a partner, receive him as myself:
18 And if he has wronged you in any way, or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
19 I, Paul, have written it with my own hand; I will repay it—not to mention to you that you owe me even your own self.
20 Yes, brother. May I enjoy you in the Lord: refresh my heart in the Lord.
21 Trusting in your obedience, I have written to you: knowing that you will also do even more than what I say.
22 But at the same time, prepare me also a lodging: for I hope that through your prayers I shall be given to you.
23 Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, salutes you,
24 Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow laborers.
25 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

## CHAPTER II.

->*Since the transgression of angelic commands received a just punishment, much more will it follow those who transgress the commands of Christ: who, through his assumed humanity and the cross, was made lower than the angels, and by this was made the author of salvation for those who believe in him.*<-

1 Therefore we ought more diligently to observe the things which we have heard, lest perhaps we drift away. <note>original: "pereffluamus," literally to flow away or leak out, suggesting a slow loss of truth</note>
2 For if the word spoken through angels was made firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just reward of retribution:
3 How shall we escape if we neglect such great salvation? Which, having begun to be announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard him.
<margin>† Mark 16:20</margin>
4 † While God bore witness with signs and wonders, and various miracles, and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his own will.
5 For God has not subjected the world to come, of which we speak, to angels.
<margin>† Psalm 8:5</margin>
6 But someone in a certain place testified, saying: † What is man that you are mindful of him, or the son of man that you visit him?
7 You made him a little lower than the angels: you have crowned him with glory and honor: and have set him over the works of your hands.
<margin>† Matthew 28:18; 1 Corinthians 15:26; † Philippians 2:8</margin>
8 † You have subjected all things under his feet. For in that he subjected all things to him, he left nothing not subject to him. But now we do not yet see all things subject to him.
9 † But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honor: that by the grace of God, he might taste death for everyone.
10 For it became him, for whom are all things, and through whom are all things, who had brought many sons into glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.
11 For he who sanctifies, and those who are sanctified, are all from one. For which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers, saying:
<margin>† Psalm 21:23</margin>
12 † I will announce your name to my brothers: in the midst of the Church I will praise you.
<margin>† Psalm 17:3; † Isaiah 8:18</margin>
13 And again: † I will put my trust in him. And again: † Behold I, and my children, whom God has given me.
14 Since therefore the children partook of flesh and blood, he also shared in the same:

<column-break/>

† that through death he might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil:
<margin>† Hosea 13:14; 1 Corinthians 15:54</margin>
15 And might deliver those who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to servitude.
16 For nowhere did he take hold of angels <note>original: "apprehendit," meaning to take up or assume the nature of</note>, but he took hold of the seed of Abraham.
17 Wherefore it behooved him in all things to be made like his brothers, that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest <term>pontifex</term> <note>literally "bridge-builder," the standard Latin term for a high priest in the temple</note> before God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
18 For in that which he himself suffered and was tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.

## CHAPTER III.

->*Christ is far more excellent, as a son, than Moses, who was a faithful servant in the house of God: care must therefore be taken that we obey him in all things, lest like the unbelieving Jews we be driven away from his rest.*<-

1 Wherefore, holy brothers, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, Jesus:
<margin>† Numbers 12:7</margin>
2 Who is faithful to him who made him, just as † Moses was in all his house.
3 For this man was deemed worthy of more glory than Moses, just as he who built the house has more honor than the house itself.
4 For every house is built by someone: but he who created all things is God.
5 And Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken:
6 But Christ as a son in his own house: which house we are, if we hold fast the confidence and the glory of hope firm until the end.
<margin>† Psalm 94:8; Below 4:7</margin>
7 Wherefore, as the Holy Spirit says: † Today if you shall hear his voice,
8 Do not harden your hearts, as in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the desert,
9 Where your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works
10 For forty years: Therefore I was angry with this generation, and said: They always err in their heart. But they have not known my ways,
11 As I swore in my wrath: If they shall enter into my rest.
12 Take heed, brothers, lest perhaps there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God:
13 But exhort yourselves every day, as long as it is called "Today," so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
14 For we have been made partakers of Christ: if only we hold the beginning of his substance <note>original: "substantiæ," referring to the foundation of faith or the reality of Christ's nature</note> firm until the end.
15 While it is said: Today if you shall hear his voice, do not harden your hearts, as in that provocation.
16 For some, hearing, did provoke, but not all who went out of Egypt through Moses.
17 But with whom was he angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies were laid low in the desert?
18 And to whom did he swear that they should not enter into his rest, but to those who were unbelieving?
19 And we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.

### C H A P T E R IV.

*Since the Jews, because of their unbelief, did not enter into the promised rest, and it remains for others to enter, we must take care lest we be deprived of it; but as believers, we may be admitted into it: concerning the living and effective word of God which sees all things, and concerning his weakness, so that he might sympathize with our own infirmities.*

1 Let us fear, therefore, lest perhaps while the promise of entering into his rest remains, any of you should seem to fall short.
2 For the gospel has been announced to us, just as it was to them: but the word they heard did not profit them, not being mixed with faith by those who heard it.
<margin>Psalm 4:11</margin>
3 For we who have believed shall enter into that rest: as he said: † As I have sworn in my wrath: If they shall enter into my rest: <note>This "If they shall enter" is a Hebrew idiom meaning "They shall certainly not enter."</note> although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
<margin>Genesis 2:2</margin>
4 For he spoke in a certain place concerning the seventh day thus: † And God rested on the seventh day from all his works.
5 And in this place again: If they shall enter into my rest.
6 Since therefore it remains for some to enter into it, and those to whom it was first announced did not enter because of их unbelief.
<margin>Above 3:7</margin>
7 Again, he defines a certain day, "Today," saying through David after so much time, as was said above: † Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.
8 For if Joshua <note>original: "Jesus." In Latin and Greek, the names Jesus and Joshua are identical. The context here refers to the Old Testament leader Joshua who led the Israelites into the Promised Land.</note> had given them rest, he would never have spoken of another day after that.
9 Therefore, there remains a Sabbath rest <note>original: "sabbatismus," a special term for a divine rest patterned after the Sabbath.</note> for the people of God.
10 For he who has entered into his rest has also himself rested from his works, just as God did from his own.
11 Let us hasten, therefore, to enter into that rest: so that no one may fall into that same example of unbelief.
12 For the word of God is living, and effective, and more piercing than any two-edged sword: and reaching even to the division of the soul and the spirit, of the joints also and the marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
<margin>Psalm 3:16. Sirach 5:20.</margin>
13 And there is no creature invisible in his sight: but all things are naked and open to his eyes; to whom our speech is directed.
14 Having therefore a great High Priest <note>original: "pontificem magnum."</note> who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God: let us hold fast to our confession.
15 For we do not have a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our infirmities: but one tempted in all things just as we are, yet without sin.
16 Let us go, therefore, with confidence to the throne of grace: that we may obtain mercy, and find grace in timely help.

### C H A P T E R V.

*Christ, having been made our High Priest in the proper order, and offering prayers to the Father, is heard: and learning obedience from those things which he suffered, he became the cause of eternal salvation to those who obey him; but those to whom the Apostle was writing here were not capable of the hidden mysteries concerning him.*

1 For every High Priest taken from among men is appointed for men

<column-break/>

in those things which pertain to God, that he may offer gifts and sacrifices for sins:
2 Who can have compassion on those who are ignorant and who wander: because he himself is also surrounded by weakness.
3 And for this reason he must, just as for the people, so also for himself, offer for sins.
<margin>† Exodus 28:1; 2 Chronicles 26:18.</margin>
4 † And no one takes this honor for himself, but he who is called by God, just as Aaron was.
<margin>† Psalm 2:7.</margin>
5 So also Christ did not glorify himself to be made High Priest: but he who spoke to him: † You are my Son, today I have begotten you.
<margin>† Psalm 109:4.</margin>
6 As he also says in another place: † You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek. <note>Melchizedek was a mysterious king and priest in Genesis 14 who prefigures Christ's eternal priesthood.</note>
7 Who, in the days of his flesh, offering up prayers and supplications with a loud cry and tears to him who was able to save him from death, was heard because of his reverence.
8 And indeed, though he was the Son of God, he learned obedience from the things which he suffered:
9 And being made perfect, he became the cause of eternal salvation to all who obey him.
10 Called by God a High Priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
11 Of whom we have much to say, and it is difficult to explain: because you have become dull of hearing.
12 For whereas for the time you ought to be teachers, you need to be taught again what are the first elements of the words of God: and you have become such as have need of milk, and not of solid food.
13 For everyone who partakes of milk is unskilled in the word of justice: for he is a little child.
14 But solid food is for the perfect: for those who by custom have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.

### C H A P T E R VI.

*He does not intend to treat the first beginnings of faith, since those who fall back into sin after receiving baptism cannot be rebaptized, rather they must fear eternal malediction: by consoling the Hebrews, however, he exhorts them to imitate the patience of Abraham, and to make themselves partakers of those things which God promised to him by an oath.*

1 Therefore, leaving behind the word of the beginning of Christ, let us be carried toward perfection, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God.
2 Of the doctrine of baptisms, and also of the imposition of hands, and of the resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
3 And this we will do, if indeed God permits.
<margin>† Matthew 12:45. Below 10:26. 2 Peter 2:20.</margin>
4 † For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, have tasted also the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit,
5 Have tasted nonetheless the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,
6 And have fallen away: to be renewed again to repentance, crucifying again for themselves the Son of God, and making him a mockery.
7 For the earth, drinking in the rain that often comes upon it, and bringing forth herbs useful for those by whom it is cultivated, receives a blessing from God.

<header>TO THE HEBREWS.</header>

8 But that which brings forth thorns and thistles is rejected, and is near to a curse; its end is to be burned.
9 But, dearly beloved, we trust for better things from you, things closer to salvation, even though we speak in this way.
10 For God is not unjust, that he should forget your work and the love which you have shown in his name, you who have ministered to the saints, and continue to minister.
11 And we desire that every one of you should show the same concern toward the fulfillment of hope even until the end:
12 So that you do not become sluggish, but instead become imitators of those who, through faith and patience, shall inherit the promises.
13 For when God made his promise to Abraham, because he had no one greater to swear by, he swore by himself,
<margin>Genesis 22:16.</margin>
14 Saying: † Unless blessing I bless you, and multiplying I multiply you. <note>This "Unless" is a Hebrew idiom of a solemn oath, essentially meaning "I will surely bless you."</note>
15 And so, by waiting patiently, he obtained the promise.
16 For men swear by one greater than themselves: and an oath for confirmation is the end of all their disputes.
17 In this, God, wanting to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of his counsel, interposed an oath:
18 So that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a very strong comfort, we who have fled for refuge to hold fast the hope set before us:
19 Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, sure and firm, and which enters even into the inner part of the veil; <note>The "veil" refers to the curtain in the Temple that separated the holy place from the Most Holy Place, where God's presence dwelt.</note>
20 Where the forerunner, Jesus, has entered for us, having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.

->Since the priesthood of Melchizedek excelled the Levitical priesthood by the receiving of tithes and the giving of a blessing, the priesthood of Christ—established by necessity forever according to the order of Melchizedek and confirmed by an oath—surpasses the Levitical order and voids it along with the Law.<-

### CHAPTER VII.

<margin>Deuteronomy 18:3.</margin>
1 For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him:
2 To whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of everything: who is first, by interpretation, King of Justice; and then also King of Salem, which is, King of Peace:
3 Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but likened to the Son of God, he remains a priest forever. <note>This does not mean he was immortal, but that his family lineage and death were not recorded in the scriptures, making him a symbol of an eternal priest.</note>
4 Now consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave tithes from the best of the spoils.
5 And indeed, those of the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a mandate to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, from their brothers; although they also came from the loins of Abraham.
<margin>Genesis 14:18. Joshua 14:4.</margin>
6 But he whose lineage is not counted among them received tithes from Abraham, and blessed him who had the promises.
7 And without any contradiction, that which is less is blessed by the better.

<column-break/>

8 And here indeed, men who die receive tithes; but there it is witnessed that he lives.
9 And (as it may be said) through Abraham, even Levi, who receives tithes, paid tithes:
10 For he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him. <note>The author uses a genealogical argument: since Levi was a future descendant of Abraham, Levi "participated" in Abraham's act of submission to Melchizedek.</note>
11 If therefore perfection was through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the law), what further need was there for another priest to rise according to the order of Melchizedek, and not be called according to the order of Aaron?
12 For the priesthood being changed, it is necessary that a change of the law also be made.
13 For he of whom these things are spoken belongs to another tribe, from which no one served at the altar.
14 For it is evident that our Lord sprang from Judah; in which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priests.
15 And it is yet far more evident; if according to the likeness of Melchizedek there arises another priest,
16 Who is made, not according to the law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
<margin>Psalm 109:4.</margin>
17 For he testifies: † Because you are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.
18 For there is indeed a setting aside of the former commandment, because of its weakness and uselessness:
19 For the law brought nothing to perfection, but was the introduction of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
20 And inasmuch as it was not without an oath (for others indeed were made priests without an oath;
<margin>Psalm 109:4.</margin>
21 But this one with an oath, by him who said to him: † The Lord has sworn, and he will not repent: You are a priest forever:)
22 By so much has Jesus become the guarantor of a better testament. <note>original: "testamenti." This can mean either a 'will' or a 'covenant' between God and man.</note>
23 And others indeed were made many priests, because they were prevented by death from continuing:
24 But this man, because he remains forever, has an everlasting priesthood.
25 Therefore he is also able to save forever those who come to God through him; always living to make intercession for us.
26 For it was fitting that we should have such a high priest: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens:
<margin>Leviticus 16:6.</margin>
27 Who does not have a daily necessity, as the priests do, † to offer sacrifices first for his own sins, then for the people's: for this he did once, by offering himself.
28 For the law appoints men as priests who have infirmity: but the word of the oath, which is after the law, appoints the Son, who is perfected forever.

### CHAPTER VIII.

*Christ's priesthood is more excellent than the Levitical one, since He sits at the right hand of the Father in heaven and is the minister of greater sacraments than the priests of the old law. He also shows the necessity of a new covenant due to the imperfection of the old, and based on the promise of God through Jeremiah.*

1 Now the main point of the things being said is this: We have such a High Priest <note>The Latin *Pontifex* literally means "bridge-builder," but in this context refers to the High Priest, the supreme religious mediator.</note>, who has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of Majesty in the heavens,
2 A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle <note>The "tabernacle" refers to the portable tent-temple used by the Israelites before the permanent Temple was built.</note> which the Lord has set up, and not man.
3 For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; therefore it is necessary that this one also have something to offer.
4 If, then, he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, since there were already those who offered gifts according to the law,
<margin>† Exodus 27:40; Acts 7:44.</margin>
5 Who serve a copy and a shadow of heavenly things. As it was answered to Moses when he was about to finish the tabernacle: † "See," he said, "that you make all things according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain."
6 But now he has obtained a better ministry, in proportion as he is the mediator of a better covenant <note>original: *testamenti*. While "testament" is used in older translations, "covenant" better captures the sense of a solemn agreement between God and His people.</note>, which has been established on better promises.
7 For if that first covenant had been faultless, then no place would have been sought for a second.
<margin>† Jeremiah 31:31.</margin>
8 For finding fault with them, he says: † "Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will complete a new covenant for the house of Israel and for the house of Judah;
9 Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they did not continue in my covenant, and I neglected them, says the Lord.
10 For this is the covenant that I will arrange for the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: Giving my laws into their minds, and I will write them upon their hearts; and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people.
11 And no one shall teach his neighbor, and no one his brother, saying: 'Know the Lord'; for all shall know me, from the least of them to the greatest of them.
12 For I will be merciful to their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more."
13 In saying "a new one," he has made the first one old. Now that which is becoming obsolete and growing old is near to vanishing away.

### CHAPTER IX.

*From those things which were in the old covenant and the imperfection of those sacrifices, he shows the perfection of the new law, in which Christ the High Priest and victim, offered once, cleanses the conscience from sins; for it was necessary for him to die for the confirmation of his testament.*

1 Indeed, the first covenant also had regulations for worship and a worldly sanctuary.
<margin>† Exodus 26:1, 36:8.</margin>
2 † For the first tabernacle was constructed, in which were the lampstands, and the table, and the bread of presence <note>Also known as "showbread," these were twelve loaves set out before God as an offering.</note>, which is called the Holy Place.
3 But behind the second veil was the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies;

<column-break/>

<margin>† Leviticus 16; Numbers 16. † 1 Kings 8:9; 2 Chronicles 5:10.</margin>
4 Having a golden † censer <note>original: *thuribulum*. This may refer to the Altar of Incense or a specific vessel used for incense.</note>, and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold, in which was the golden jar containing the manna, and Aaron’s rod that had budded, and the tablets of the covenant;
5 And above it were the Cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat <note>The gold lid of the Ark where God's presence was said to dwell.</note>; about which things we cannot now speak in detail.
6 Now when these things were thus arranged, the priests always entered into the first tabernacle, performing the duties of the sacrifices.
<margin>† Exodus 30:10; Leviticus 16:2.</margin>
7 But into the second † the high priest entered alone once a year, not without blood, which he offers for his own and the people's ignorances.
8 By this the Holy Spirit signifies that the way into the sanctuary was not yet opened while the first tabernacle was still standing.
9 Which is a parable for the present time, according to which gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot make the worshiper perfect according to the conscience, being only matters of food and drink,
10 And various washings and fleshly regulations imposed until the time of correction.
11 But Christ, appearing as a high priest of the good things to come, through a greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hands, that is, not of this creation;
12 Neither by the blood of goats or calves, but by his own blood, he entered once into the sanctuary, having found eternal redemption.
<margin>† Leviticus 16:15.</margin>
13 † For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer being sprinkled sanctifies those who are defiled for the cleansing of the flesh,
<margin>† 1 Peter 1:19; 1 John 1:7; Revelation 1:5.</margin>
14 † How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the Holy Spirit offered himself unblemished to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
<margin>† Galatians 3:15.</margin>
15 And for this reason he is the mediator of a new testament: † so that by means of death intervening for the redemption of those transgressions which were under the first testament, those who are called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
16 For where there is a testament <note>The author uses a play on words here: the Greek and Latin word for "covenant" is the same as for a "last will and testament."</note>, the death of the testator must necessarily occur.
17 For a testament is confirmed after death; otherwise it has no force while the one who made the testament lives.
18 Hence not even the first one was dedicated without blood.
19 For when every commandment of the law had been read by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
<margin>† Exodus 24:8.</margin>
20 Saying: † "This is the blood of the testament which God has commanded to you."
21 Likewise, he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry with blood.
22 And almost all things are cleansed with blood according to the law; and without the shedding of blood there is no remission.
23 It was necessary, therefore, that the copies of heavenly things be cleansed with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
24 For Jesus did not enter into a sanctuary made with hands, a copy of the true one, but into heaven itself, so that he may now appear before the face of God for us.
25 Nor did he enter so that he might offer himself often, as the High Priest enters the sanctuary every year with the blood of another;
26 Otherwise he would have had to suffer frequently since the beginning of the world; but now once at the...

### C A P T E R X.

*Because of the imperfection of the sacrifices of the Old Testament, it was necessary for a new one to be introduced, whose single sacrifice takes away all sins: unless we cling to this through faith, hope, charity, and good works, we shall be punished more severely than the transgressors of the Old Testament: meanwhile, he praises the Hebrews because they have both suffered much and stood by those who were suffering.*

1 **F**or the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never make those who approach perfect by the same sacrifices which they offer continually every year.
2 Otherwise, they would have ceased to be offered: because the worshipers, once cleansed, would have no further consciousness of sin:
3 But in those sacrifices, a remembrance of sins is made every year.
4 For it is impossible for sins to be taken away by the blood of bulls and goats.
<margin>† Psalm 39:7.</margin>
5 † Therefore, coming into the world, he says: † Sacrifice and offering you did not desire: but a body you have prepared for me:
6 Holocausts <note>original: *holocautomata* — a religious sacrifice where the entire offering is burned by fire.</note> for sin did not please you:
<margin>† Psalm 39:8.</margin>
7 † Then I said: Behold, I come: † in the scroll of the book <note>original: *in capite libri* — literally "in the head of the book," referring to the opening section of the legal or prophetic scrolls.</note> it is written of me: That I should do your will, O God.
8 Above, saying: Because sacrifices, and offerings, and holocausts for sin you did not desire, nor were they pleasing to you, which are offered according to the law,
9 Then I said: Behold, I come to do your will, O God: he takes away the first, that he may establish the second.
10 By which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
11 And every priest indeed stands daily ministering, and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:
12 But this man, offering one sacrifice for sins, sits forever at the right hand of God,
<margin>† Psalm 109:2, 1 Corinthians 15:25.</margin>
13 † From then on waiting † until his enemies are made his footstool.
14 For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are sanctified.
15 And the Holy Spirit also bears witness to us. For after he had said:
<margin>† Jeremiah 31:33, Above 8:8.</margin>
16 † This is the covenant <note>original: *testamentum* — in this context, it refers to the formal agreement or "covenant" between God and His people.</note> that I will make with them after those days, says the Lord, giving my laws in their hearts, and in their minds I will write them:
17 And their sins and iniquities I will remember no more.
18 Now where there is remission of these: there is no longer an offering for sin.
19 Having therefore, brothers, confidence in the entrance into the sanctuary by the blood of Christ,
20 Which he initiated for us as a new and living way through the veil, that is, his flesh.

<column-break/>

21 And having a great priest over the house of God:
22 Let us approach with a true heart in fullness of faith, our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with clean water,
23 Let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering (for he who promised is faithful)
24 And let us consider one another to provoke charity and good works:
25 Not deserting our assembly <note>original: *collectionem nostram* — the gathering together of the early Christian community for worship.</note>, as is the custom of some, but consoling one another, and so much the more as you see the day approaching.
<margin>† Above 6:4.</margin>
26 † For if we sin willfully after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there is no longer left a sacrifice for sins,
27 But a certain terrible expectation of judgment, and the fury of fire, which shall consume the adversaries.
<margin>† Deuteronomy 17:6, Matthew 18:16, John 8:37, 2 Corinthians 13:1.</margin>
28 A person making void the law of Moses dies without any mercy † on the evidence of two or three witnesses:
29 How much more, do you think, does he deserve worse punishments, who has trodden underfoot the Son of God, and has considered the blood of the covenant — by which he was sanctified — to be unholy, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
<margin>† Deuteronomy 32:35, Romans 12:19.</margin>
30 For we know him who said: † Vengeance is mine, and I will repay. And again: Because the Lord will judge his people.
31 It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
32 But call to mind the former days, in which, being enlightened, you endured a great contest of sufferings.
33 On one hand, indeed, being made a spectacle by reproaches and tribulations: and on the other hand, being made companions of those living in such a way.
34 For you both had compassion on those in chains, and you accepted the seizure of your goods with joy, knowing that you have a better and lasting substance.
35 Therefore, do not lose your confidence, which has a great reward.
36 For patience is necessary for you: so that doing the will of God, you may receive the promise.
37 For yet a little while, and he who is to come will come, and will not delay.
<margin>† Habakkuk 2:4, Romans 1. 17. Galatians 3. 11.</margin>
38 † But my just man lives by faith: but if he withdraws himself, he shall not please my soul.
39 But we are not children of withdrawal unto perdition, but of faith unto the salvation of the soul.

2 For by this the elders obtained a testimony.
<margin>† Genesis 1:3.</margin>
3 † By faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that from invisible things visible things were made.

### CHAPTER XII.

->*By the example of the ancients, and even more by the example of Christ, he leads them to manfully endure afflictions, calling them back from sins: and because of the excellence of the New Testament over the Old, he deters them from disobedience, lest we be forced to suffer greater punishments than the Jews.*<-

<margin>† Romans 6:4. Ephesians 4:22. Colossians 3:8. 1 Peter 2:1 & 4:2.</margin>
1 And therefore, we also, having such a great cloud of witnesses placed around us, † laying aside every weight and the sin that surrounds us, let us run with patience the race proposed to us.

2 Looking to Jesus, the Author and finisher of faith, who, for the joy set before him, endured the cross, despising the shame, and now sits at the right hand of the throne of God.

3 For think diligently upon him who endured such opposition against himself from sinners: so that you may not grow weary, losing heart in your souls.

4 For you have not yet resisted unto blood, while fighting against sin:

<margin>† Proverbs 3:11. Revelation 3:19.</margin>
5 And you have forgotten the consolation which speaks to you as to sons, saying: † My son, do not neglect the discipline of the Lord: nor grow weary while you are rebuked by him.

6 For whom the Lord loves, he chastises: and he scourges every son whom he receives.

7 Persevere in discipline. God offers himself to you as to sons: for what son is there whom the father does not correct?

8 But if you are without discipline, of which all have been made participants: then you are illegitimate <note>original: *adulteri* — literally "adulterers," here used to mean children born out of wedlock/unauthorized heirs</note>, and not sons.

9 Furthermore, we have had the fathers of our flesh as instructors, and we revered them: shall we not much more obey the Father of spirits, and live?
