# THE CATHOLIC EPISTLE
## OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE JAMES.

### CHAPTER ONE.

*He teaches the usefulness of temptations, and that wisdom should be requested from God with confidence: God is not a tempter or the author of sin, but from him proceeds every good gift: he exhorts that they be swift to hear, but slow to speak and slow to anger: nor is it enough to hear the truth unless it is fulfilled in work: he adds also what true and undefiled religion is.*

1 James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are in the dispersion <note>original: "dispersione," referring to the Jewish Christian communities scattered outside of Israel</note>, greetings.
2 My brothers, count it all joy when you fall into various temptations <note>In this context, "temptations" refers to trials or testings of faith rather than just the impulse to sin</note>:
<margin>† Romans 5:3.</margin>
3 † Knowing that the testing of your faith produces patience.
4 And let patience have a perfect work: that you may be perfect and entire, lacking in nothing.
5 But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all abundantly and does not reproach: and it shall be given to him.
<margin>† Matthew 7:7 & 21:22. Mark 11:24. Luke 11:9. John 14:13 & 23:16, 24.</margin>
6 † But let him ask in faith, hesitating in nothing: for he who hesitates is like a wave of the sea, which is moved and carried about by the wind.
7 Therefore, let not that man think that he shall receive anything from the Lord.
8 A man double-minded <note>original: "duplex animo," literally "two-souled"</note> is inconstant in all his ways.
9 But let the humble brother glory in his exaltation;
<margin>† Ecclesiasticus 14:18. Isaiah 40:6. 1 Peter 1:24.</margin>
10 And the rich man in his humiliation, † because like the flower of the grass he shall pass away:
11 For the sun has risen with heat and dried the grass, and its flower fell off, and the beauty of its appearance perished: so also shall the rich man wither in his paths.
<margin>† Job 5:17.</margin>
12 † Blessed is the man who suffers temptation: because when he has been proven, he shall receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him.
13 Let no one, when he is tempted, say that he is tempted by God; for God is not a tempter of evils: he himself tempts no one.
14 But every person is tempted, being drawn away and enticed by their own desire <note>original: "concupiscentia," often translated as lust or strong worldly desire</note>.
15 Then, when desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin: but sin, when it is completed, generates death.
16 Do not err, therefore, my most beloved brothers.
17 Every best gift and every perfect gift is from above, descending from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change, nor shadow of alteration.
18 For of his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth, that we might be some beginning <note>or "first-fruits"</note> of his creature.
<margin>† Proverbs 17:27.</margin>
19 You know this, my most beloved brothers. † And let every man be swift to hear; but slow to speak, and slow to anger.
20 For the anger of man does not work the justice of God.
21 Because of this, casting away all uncleanness and abundance of malice, receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.

<column-break/>

<margin>† Matthew 7:21, 24. Romans 2:13.</margin>
22 † But be doers of the word: and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
23 Because if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he shall be compared to a man considering his natural face in a mirror.
24 For he considered himself and went away, and immediately forgot what kind of man he was.
25 But he who has looked into the perfect law of liberty and has remained in it, not having become a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work: this man shall be blessed in his deed.
26 But if anyone thinks himself to be religious, not restraining his tongue but seducing his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.
27 Pure and undefiled religion before God and the Father is this: To visit orphans <note>original: "pupillos"</note> and widows in their tribulation, and to keep oneself unspotted from this world.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Leviticus 19:15. Deuteronomy 1:17 & 16:19. Proverbs 24:23. Ecclesiasticus 42:1.</margin>
*He warns lest they be moved by respect of persons: for he who transgresses a single precept of the law is a transgressor of the law: he exhorts them to apply themselves to works of mercy, showing that a man is justified through works: for faith without works is dead.*

1 My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ of glory with respect of persons <note>meaning showing partiality or favoritism based on social status</note>.
2 For if there shall enter into your assembly a man having a gold ring and in white clothing, and there shall also enter a poor man in filthy attire,
3 And you look upon him who is clothed in excellent clothing and say to him: "You sit here in a good place"; but say to the poor man: "You stand there," or "Sit under my footstool":
4 Do you not judge within yourselves, and have you not become judges of unjust thoughts?
5 Hear, my most beloved brothers, has not God chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which God has promised to those who love him?
6 But you have dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you by power, and do they not draw you to judgments?
7 Do they not blaspheme the good name which has been invoked over you?
<margin>† Leviticus 19:18. Matthew 22:39. Mark 12:31. Romans 13:9. Galatians 5:14.</margin>
8 If, however, you fulfill the royal law according to the scriptures: † "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well:
9 † But if you show respect to persons, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
<margin>† Leviticus 19:15. Above verse 1. † Matthew 5:19.</margin>
10 † For whoever shall keep the whole law, but offends in one point, has become guilty of all.
11 For he who said, "You shall not commit adultery," also said, "You shall not kill." Now if you do not commit adultery, but you do kill, you have become a transgressor of the law.

## CHAPTER III.

->*He recounts the evils of the tongue, which is most difficult to govern rightly; and he adds the difference between earthly and heavenly wisdom.*<-

<margin>Matthew 23:8</margin>
1 My brothers, do not many of you become teachers, knowing that you shall receive a greater judgment.
2 For we all stumble in many things. If anyone does not stumble in word, he is a perfect man; he is also able to lead the whole body with a bridle.
3 If we put bridles into the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we also turn their whole body.
4 Look also at ships: though they are large and are driven by strong winds, they are turned by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the pilot wills.
5 So also the tongue is indeed a small member, and it boasts of great things. Behold how small a fire sets ablaze how great a forest!
6 And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity. The tongue is placed among our members, which stains the whole body and sets on fire the wheel of our birth <note>original: "rotam nativitatis," a phrase often interpreted as the whole course of a person's life or the cycle of human existence</note>, being set on fire by Gehenna <note>Gehenna: a valley near Jerusalem used as a metaphor for hell or a place of fiery judgment</note>.
7 For every nature of beasts, and birds, and serpents, and other creatures is tamed, and has been tamed by human nature;
8 but no man can tame the tongue: an unquiet evil, full of deadly poison.
9 With it we bless God and the Father; and with it we curse men, who are made in the likeness of God.
10 Out of the same mouth proceed blessing and curs-

<column-break/>

-ing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.
11 Does a spring pour out from the same opening both sweet and bitter water?
12 Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce grapes, or a vine produce figs? So neither can salt water produce sweet water.
13 Who is wise and disciplined among you? Let him show his work by his good conduct in the meekness of wisdom.
14 But if you have bitter jealousy and there are contentions in your hearts, do not boast and be liars against the truth.
15 For this is not the wisdom descending from above, but is earthly, sensual <note>original: "animalis," referring to the lower, unspiritual nature</note>, and devilish.
16 For where there is jealousy and contention, there is inconstancy and every wicked work.
17 But the wisdom that is from above is first indeed pure, then peaceful, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good, full of mercy and good fruits, not judging, without hypocrisy.
18 And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

## CHAPTER IV.

->*Lusts are not to be obeyed, but the devil is to be resisted, and one must draw near to God; mutual love must be pursued, and uncertain matters committed to divine providence.*<-

1 From where do wars and quarrels among you come? Is it not from here: from your lusts which war in your members?
2 You desire and do not have; you kill and are jealous, and cannot obtain; you quarrel and wage war, and you do not have because you do not ask.
3 You ask and do not receive because you ask wrongly, so that you may consume it on your lusts.
4 Adulterers, do you not know that friendship with this world is enmity with God? Whoever therefore wishes to be a friend of this world is made an enemy of God.
5 Or do you think the Scripture says in vain: "The spirit that dwells in you longs unto envy"?
<margin>† Proverbs 3:34</margin>
6 But he gives greater grace. Therefore he says: † God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
<margin>† 1 Peter 5:5</margin>
7 † Be subject therefore to God; but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
8 Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
9 Be miserable, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned into mourning, and your joy into sorrow.
<margin>† 1 Peter 5:6</margin>
10 † Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
11 Do not disparage one another, brothers. He who disparages a brother, or who judges his brother, disparages the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law, but a judge.
12 There is one lawgiver and judge, who is able to destroy and to set free.
<margin>† Romans 14:4</margin>
13 † But who are you to judge your neighbor? Behold now, you who say: "Today or tomorrow we will go into that city, and we will spend a year there, and we will trade and make a profit,"
14 you who do not know what will happen tomorrow.
15 For what is your life? It is a vapor appearing for a little while, then it shall vanish away. Instead, you ought to say: "If the Lord wills," and "If we live, we will do this or that."

16 But now you rejoice in your boastings. All such rejoicing is evil.

### CHAPTER V.

*He threatens the rich oppressors of the poor with heavy vengeance, but exhorts the poor to long-suffering: swearing is to be avoided, the sick are to be anointed with oil by the priests, and sins are to be confessed to one another: how effective the prayer of the righteous is: those who wander from the truth are to be brought back.*

1 Come now, you rich, weep and howl in your miseries that shall come upon you.
2 Your riches are rotted, and your garments are eaten by moths.
3 Your gold and silver are rusted: and their rust shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up wrath for yourselves in the last days. <note>The author uses the image of "rust" as a spiritual indictment of hoarded wealth that should have been put to use.</note>
4 Behold, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, which were kept back by fraud by you, cry out: and their cry has entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth. <note>original: "Sabaoth" — a Hebrew title for God meaning "of Hosts" or "of Armies."</note>
5 You have feasted upon the earth, and in luxuries you have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.
6 You have condemned and killed the just man, and he did not resist you.
7 Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, patiently enduring until he receives the early and the late rains.
8 Be you also patient, and strengthen your hearts: for the coming of the Lord has drawn near.

<column-break/>

9 Do not grumble against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Behold, the judge stands before the door.
10 Take as an example, brothers, of a bad outcome, of labor, and of patience, the Prophets: who spoke in the name of the Lord.
11 Behold, we call those blessed who have endured. You have heard of the suffering of Job, and you have seen the end intended by the Lord, for the Lord is merciful and compassionate.
<margin>† Matthew 5:34.</margin>
12 But above all things, my brothers, do not swear, neither by heaven, nor by the earth, nor any other oath. But let your speech be: Yes, yes; No, no: so that you do not fall under judgment.
13 Is any of you sad? Let him pray. Is he cheerful? Let him sing psalms.
14 Is any among you sick? Let him bring in the priests of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: <term>priests: the Latin 'presbyteros' refers to the elders or ordained leaders of the community.</term>
15 And the prayer of faith shall save the sick man, and the Lord shall raise him up: and if he be in sins, they shall be forgiven him.
16 Confess therefore your sins to one another, and pray for one another that you may be saved: for the persistent prayer of a righteous person is very powerful.
<margin>† 1 Kings 17:1; Luke 4:25.</margin>
17 Elijah was a man liable to suffering just like us: and he prayed with prayer that it might not rain upon the earth, and it did not rain for three years and six months.
18 And he prayed again: and the heaven gave rain, and the earth gave its fruit.
19 My brothers, if any of you wanders from the truth, and someone converts him:
20 He ought to know that he who causes a sinner to be converted from the error of his way, shall save his soul from death, and shall cover a multitude of sins.

<margin>† Lev. 11:44 and 19:2 and 20:7. † Deut. 10:17. Rom. 2:11. Galat. 2:6. † 1 Cor. 6:20 and 7:23. Hebr. 9:14. 1 John 1:7. Apoc. 1:5.</margin>

21 Who through him are faithful in God, who raised him up from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God:

23 Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of the living God, which remains forever.
<margin>† Ecclus. 14:8. Isaiah 40:6. James 1:10.</margin>

### CAPUT IV.

*He exhorts those redeemed by Christ's death to proceed in avoiding past sins: applying themselves to prayer and mutual love, always referring all things to the glory of God, and rejoicing if it is necessary to suffer for Christ.*

<margin>† Ephesians 4:23.</margin> 1 **C**hrist, therefore, having suffered in the flesh, be you also armed with the same thought: for he who has suffered in the flesh has ceased from sins:
2 That he may live the rest of his time in the flesh, no longer according to the desires of men, but according to the will of God.

<column-break/>

3 For the time past is sufficient to have fulfilled the will of the Gentiles, for those who have walked in luxuries, lusts, excess of wine, revelries, carousings, and unlawful worship of idols.
4 In which they marvel that you run not with them into the same confusion of luxury, speaking evil of you.
5 Who shall render an account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
6 For this cause was the Gospel preached also to the dead: that they might be judged indeed according to men in the flesh, but live according to God in the Spirit.
7 But the end of all things has approached. Be you therefore prudent, and watch in prayers.
<margin>† Proverbs 10:12. Romans 12:13. Hebrews 13:2.</margin> 8 But before all things, have a constant mutual charity among yourselves: for charity covers a multitude of sins.
9 † Using hospitality one towards another without murmuring.

<margin>† Philippians 2:14. 12 Dearly beloved, do not be surprised at the heat <note>original: "fervore" — referring to the "fiery trial" or intense persecution facing the believers.</note> which comes upon you for a trial, as if some new thing happened to you:
13 But communicating in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that you may also rejoice exulting in the revelation of his glory.
14 If you be reproached for the name of Christ, you shall be blessed: because that which is of honor, glory, and power of God, and that which is his Spirit, rests upon you.
15 But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or a slanderer, or a seeker of other men's goods.
16 But if as a Christian, let him not be ashamed: but let him glorify God in that name.
17 For the time is come that judgment should begin at the house of God. And if it first begins with us, what shall be the end of those who do not believe the Gospel of God?
<margin>† Proverbs 11:31.</margin> 18 † And if the just man shall scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?
19 Therefore, let those also who suffer according to the will of God, commend their souls in good deeds to the faithful Creator.

4 And when the prince of pastors shall appear, you shall receive a never-fading crown of glory.

### CHAPTER ONE.

->*He exhorts them that, mindful of the greatest gifts they have received from God, they should climb through various virtues, so that an entrance into the kingdom of the Lord may be provided for them: he says that he will soon die, and shows the certainty of his doctrine from Christ the teacher, whom both the voice of the Father and the Prophets commended.*<-

<columns>2</columns>
1 Simon Peter, servant and Apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a faith equal to ours in the justice of our God and Savior Jesus Christ.
2 Grace and peace be fulfilled in you in the knowledge of God, and of Christ Jesus our Lord:
3 According as all things of his divine power, which appertain to life and godliness, are given to us through the knowledge of him who has called us by his own glory and virtue.
4 By whom he has given us very great and precious promises: that by these you may be made partakers of the divine nature: escaping the corruption of that concupiscence <note>original: "concupiscentiae" — refers to strong worldly desires or lusts.</note> which is in the world.
5 And you, employing all care, minister virtue in your faith, and in virtue, knowledge.
6 And in knowledge, abstinence <note>original: "abstinentiam" — often translated as self-control.</note>; and in abstinence, patience; and in patience, piety.
7 And in piety, love of the brotherhood; and in the love of the brotherhood, charity.
8 For if these things be with you and abound, they shall make you to be neither empty nor without fruit in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
9 For he that lacks these things is blind, and groping with his hand, having forgotten the purging of his old sins.
10 Wherefore, brothers, labor the more that by good works you may make your calling and election sure: for doing these things, you shall not sin at any time.
11 For so there shall be ministered to you abundantly

an entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
12 For which cause I will begin to always remind you of these things: even though you know them and are confirmed in the present truth.
13 But I think it right, as long as I am in this tabernacle <note>original: "tabernaculo" — a metaphor for the human body as a temporary dwelling.</note>, to stir you up by reminder:
<margin>† John 21:19.</margin>
14 Being sure that the laying away of my tabernacle is at hand, according as our Lord Jesus Christ † signified to me.
15 And I will endeavor that you may frequently have a memory of these things after my death.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 1:17.</margin>
16 † For we have not followed learned fables when we made known to you the power and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ: but we were eyewitnesses <note>original: "speculatores" — literally watchers or onlookers; here referring to the Transfiguration.</note> of his greatness.
17 For he received from God the Father honor and glory, when there came such a voice to him from the magnificent glory: † This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear him.
<margin>† Matthew 17:5.</margin>
18 And this voice we heard brought from heaven, when we were with him on the holy mount.
19 And we have a firmer prophetic word: to which you do well to attend, as to a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns, and the day star <note>original: "lucifer" — literally "light-bringer," referring here to the morning star or Christ.</note> arises in your hearts:
<margin>† 2 Timothy 3:16.</margin>
20 Understanding this first, † that no prophecy of Scripture is made by private interpretation.
21 For prophecy was not brought at any time by human will: but the holy men of God spoke, inspired by the Holy Spirit.

### CHAPTER III.

->*Because of certain mockers who deny the second coming of the Lord, he affirms the future renewal of the world, when the Lord shall come shortly and unexpectedly; he warns them to prepare for this coming, praising the writings of Paul which the unlearned distort.*<-

**B**ehold, dearly beloved, this is the second epistle I am writing to you, in which I stir up your sincere mind by way of a reminder:
**2** That you may be mindful of the words I told you before from the holy Prophets, and of the precepts of the Lord and Savior given by your Apostles.
<margin>† 1 Timothy 4:1. 2 Timothy 3:1. Jude 18.</margin>
**3** Knowing this first: that † in the last days mockers shall come with deceits, walking according to their own lusts,
<margin>† Ezekiel 12:27.</margin>
**4** Saying: † "Where is the promise of his coming? For since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of creation."
**5** For they willfully ignore this: that the heavens existed long ago, and the earth was formed out of water and through water by the word of God;
**6** Through which that world then, being overflowed with water, perished.
**7** But the heavens and the earth which now exist are kept by the same word, reserved for fire until the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly men.
**8** But do not let this one thing be hidden from you, dearly beloved: that one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
**9** The Lord does not delay his promise, as some imagine, but deals patiently for your sake, not willing that any should perish, but that all should return to repentance.
<margin>† 1 Thessalonians 5:2. Revelation 3:3 & 16:15.</margin>
**10** † But the day of the Lord shall come like a thief: in which the heavens shall pass away with great violence, and the elements <note>original: "elementa" — the basic physical building blocks of the universe.</note> shall be dissolved with heat, and the earth and the works within it shall be burned up.
**11** Since therefore all these things are to be dissolved, what kind of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness,
**12** Waiting for and hastening toward the coming of the day of the Lord, by which the burning heavens shall be dissolved and the elements shall melt with the heat of fire?
<margin>† Isaiah 65:17 & 66:22. Revelation 21:1.</margin>
**13** † But we look for new heavens and a new earth according to his promises, in which justice dwells.
**14** Therefore, dearly beloved, while you wait for these things, be diligent that you may be found by him unspotted and blameless in peace.
<margin>† Romans 2:4.</margin>
**15** And † account the long-suffering of our Lord to be salvation; just as our most dear brother Paul, according to the wisdom given to him, has written to you,
**16** As he does in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things. In those letters are certain things hard to understand, which the unlearned and unstable distort—as they do the other Scriptures—to their own destruction.
**17** You therefore, brethren, knowing these things beforehand, take heed: lest being led away by the error of the unwise, you fall from your own steadfastness.
**18** But grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and unto the day of eternity. Amen.

# CHAPTER ONE.

*John announces what he has seen and heard concerning Christ, so that others may be joined in fellowship with him, with God, and with his son Christ, by whose blood the sins of men are cleansed: furthermore, whoever denies that they have sinned makes God a liar.*

1 <image-desc>Large decorative initial Q containing a landscape illustration with a figure, possibly St. John, seated and writing.</image-desc>That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, concerning the Word of life:
2 And the life was made manifest, and we have seen it, and we bear witness, and we announce to you the eternal life, which was with the Father, and has appeared to us:
3 That which we have seen and heard, we announce to you, so that you also may have fellowship with us, and our fellowship may be with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ.
4 And these things we write to you so that you may rejoice, and that your joy may be full.
<margin>† John 8:12.</margin>
5 And this is the announcement which we have heard from him, and announce to you: † That God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all.
6 If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not act in truth.
<margin>† Hebrews 9:14. 1 Peter 1:19. Revelation 1:5.</margin>
7 But if we walk in the light, as he himself is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and † the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin.
<margin>† 1 Kings 8:46. 2 Chronicles 6:36. Proverbs 20:9. Ecclesiastes 7:21.</margin>
8 † If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
9 If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just, to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all iniquity.
10 If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.

# CHAPTER II.

*Jesus Christ is our advocate and the propitiation <note>original: "propitiatio" — a theological term for an offering that restores a relationship or turns away divine anger; an atonement.</note> for the sins of the whole world: the true knowledge and love of God is proved by the observation of God's commandments: what the old and new commandment is: who is in light and who is in darkness: he writes to various ages, calling them away from the love of the world and from heretics, and advising that they adhere to the faith once received, following the guidance of the Holy Spirit.*

1 <image-desc>Decorative initial F with floral scrollwork.</image-desc>My little children, these things I write to you, so that you may not sin. But even if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous:
2 And he is the propitiation for our sins; and not for ours only, but also for those of the whole world.

<column-break/>

3 And by this we know that we have known him: if we keep his commandments.
4 He who says he knows him, and does not keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
5 But whoever keeps his word, in him truly the love of God is perfected: and by this we know that we are in him.
6 He who says he abides in him, ought himself also to walk just as he walked.
7 Dearly beloved, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment, which you had from the beginning: The old commandment is the word which you have heard.
<margin>† John 13:34 and 15:12.</margin>

9 He who says he is in the light, and hates his brother, is in darkness even until now.
<margin>† See below 3:14.</margin>
10 † He who loves his brother abides in the light, and there is no cause of stumbling in him.
11 But he who hates his brother is in darkness, and walks in darkness, and does not know where he is going: because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
12 I write to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for his name's sake.
13 I write to you, fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the wicked one.
14 I write to you, infants, because you have known the father. I write to you, youths, because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the wicked one.
15 Do not love the world, nor the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him:
16 Because everything that is in the world is the concupiscence <note>original: "concupiscentia" — strong, often disordered desire or lust.</note> of the flesh, and the concupiscence of the eyes, and the pride of life: which is not from the Father, but is from the world.
17 And the world passes away, and its concupiscence. But he who does the will of God abides forever.
18 Little children, it is the last hour: and as you have heard that Antichrist is coming, even now many Antichrists have arisen: by which we know that it is the last hour.
19 They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us: but it was so that they might be made manifest that not all are of us.
20 But you have an unction <note>original: "unctionem" — an anointing, referring here to the gift of the Holy Spirit.</note> from the Holy One, and you know all things.
21 I have not written to you as to those ignorant of the truth, but as to those who know it: and because no lie is of the truth.
22 Who is a liar, but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son.
23 Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father: he who confesses the Son has the Father also.
24 Let that which you have heard from the beginning abide in you: If that which you have heard...

### CHAPTER III.

->*Concerning the charity of God toward us, and how those who are of God are distinguished from those who are of the devil: concerning the love and hatred of brothers: that whoever seeks anything from God with purity of mind and faith in Christ, obtains it.*<-

See what kind of charity the Father has given to us, that we should be named and be the children of God. Because of this, the world does not know us: because it did not know him.

10 In this the children of God are made manifest, and the children of the devil. Everyone who is not just is not of God, nor is he who does not love his brother:

### CHAPTER IV.

->*Which spirits are from God, and which are not: since God has preceded us with his love, having given his Son for us, we also ought to love God and our neighbor: for perfect charity casts out fear.*<-

Most beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see if they are from God: because many false prophets have gone out into the world.

3 And every spirit which dissolves <note>original: *solvit*. This refers to "dividing" or denying the unity of Christ's person.</note> Jesus is not from God; and this is the Antichrist, of whom you have heard that he is coming, and now he is already in the world.

8 He who does not love does not know God: because God is charity.
<margin>† John 3:16.</margin>

### CHAPTER V.

*Concerning those born of God, and true charity toward him: faith conquers the world: three witnesses on earth testify to Christ as true man, and three in heaven testify to him as the true Son of God, in whom the believer has eternal life: concerning sin unto death, and sin not unto death.*

Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God. And everyone who loves him who begat also loves him who was born of him.
2 In this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and keep his commandments.
3 For this is the charity of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not burdensome.
4 For whatever is born of God conquers the world: and this is the victory which conquers the world — our faith.
<margin>† 1 Corinthians 15:57.</margin>
5 Who is it that conquers the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?

<column-break/>

6 This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ: not by water only, but by water and blood. And it is the Spirit who testifies, because Christ is the truth.
7 For there are three who bear testimony <gloss>in heaven</gloss>: the Father, the *Word*, and the Holy Spirit: and these three are one. <note>This is the famous *Comma Johanneum* — a brief passage asserting the heavenly Trinity. Its authenticity was debated by Renaissance-era scholars, as it is absent from many early Greek manuscripts.</note>
8 And there are three who bear testimony on earth: the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three are one.
9 If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater: for this is the testimony of God, which is greater, that he has testified concerning his Son.
<margin>† John 3:36.</margin>
10 He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony of God within himself. He who does not believe the Son makes him a liar: because he does not believe in the testimony which God has given concerning his Son.
11 And this is the testimony: that God has given us eternal life. And this life is in his Son.
12 He who has the Son has life: he who does not have the Son does not have life.
13 These things I write to you: so that you may know that you have eternal life, you who believe in the name of the Son of God.
14 And this is the confidence which we have toward him: that whatever we ask according to his will, he hears us.
15 And we know that he hears us in whatever we ask: we know that we have the petitions which we request of him.
16 He who knows that his brother is sinning a sin not unto death — let him ask, and life shall be given to him who sins not unto death. There is a sin unto death: I do not say that anyone should pray for that.
17 All wrongdoing is sin: and there is sin which is not unto death.
18 We know that everyone who is born of God does not sin: but the offspring <note>Latin: *generatio*, literally "generation" or "begetting" — here referring to the divine birth that protects the believer.</note> of God preserves him, and the evil one does not touch him.
19 We know that we are of God: and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.
20 And we know that the Son of God has come, and has given us understanding so that we may know the
<margin>† Luke 24:45.</margin>
true God, and that we may be in his true Son. He is the true God, and eternal life.
21 Little children, guard yourselves from idols. Amen.

# THE EPISTLE
## OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE JOHN
### THE SECOND.

*He confirms this chosen lady and her children in charity and faith, so that they are not led astray by heretics; and he does this in few words, saving the rest until he comes to them.*

<column-break/>

1 The Elder to the Chosen lady, and to her children, whom I love in truth—and not I alone, but also all who have known the truth—
2 For the sake of the truth which remains in us, and will be with us forever.
3 May grace, mercy, and peace be with you from God the Father, and from Christ Jesus the Son of the Father, in truth and charity <note>The Latin word *charitas* implies a selfless, brotherly love</note>.
4 I rejoiced greatly because I found some of your children walking in truth, just as we received the commandment from the Father.
<margin>
John 13:34 and 15:12.
</margin>
5 And now I ask you, lady, not as if writing a new commandment to you, but that which we have had from the beginning: † that we should love one another.

<column-break/>

6 And this is charity: that we walk according to his commandments. For this is the commandment, that just as you have heard from the beginning, you should walk in it.
7 Since many deceivers have gone out into the world, who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh; this is a deceiver and an antichrist.
8 Look to yourselves, so that you do not lose what you have worked for, but may receive a full reward.
9 Everyone who withdraws and does not remain in the doctrine of Christ does not have God; he who remains in the doctrine, he has both the Father and the Son.
10 If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into your home, nor say to him, "Greetings" <note>original: "AVE"</note>.
11 For he who says to him "Greetings" shares in his wicked works.
12 Having more things to write to you, I did not wish to do so through paper and ink; for I hope to be with you and to speak face to face <note>literally: "mouth to mouth"</note>, so that your joy may be full.
13 The children of your sister Electa <note>the "Chosen" one</note> greet you.

# THE EPISTLE
## OF THE BLESSED APOSTLE JOHN
### THE THIRD.

*He praises Gaius because he walks in truth and receives travelers kindly; adding a note about Diotrephes' slanders and unkindness, while offering an excellent testimony for Demetrius; he concludes by saying he will visit him soon.*

<column-break/>

1 The Elder to the most dear Gaius, whom I love in truth.
2 Most dear one, I pray concerning all things that you may progress prosperously and be in good health, just as your soul acts prosperously.
3 I rejoiced greatly when the brothers came and bore witness to your truth, just as you walk in truth.
4 I have no greater grace than this: to hear that my children walk in the truth.
5 Most dear one, you act faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, and especially for strangers,
6 Who have given testimony to your charity in the sight of the Church; whom, in doing well, you will send on their way in a manner worthy of God.

<column-break/>

7 For they set out for the sake of his name, receiving nothing from the Gentiles <note>The non-Christian nations</note>.
8 We therefore ought to receive such people, so that we may be fellow-workers for the truth.
9 I might have written to the Church; but he who loves to hold the first place among them, Diotrephes, does not receive us.
10 Therefore, if I come, I will call to mind his works which he does: prating against us with wicked words. And as if those things were not enough for him, he does not receive the brothers himself; and those who do receive them, he forbids, and casts them out of the Church.
11 Most dear one, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. He who does good is of God; he who does evil has not seen God.
12 Testimony is given to Demetrius by all, and by the truth itself, and we also bear witness; and you know that our testimony is true.
13 I had many things to write to you, but I did not wish to write to you through ink and pen <note>original: "calamum," a reed pen</note>.
14 But I hope to see you shortly, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to you. Our friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.

# THE EPISTLE OF THE
## BLESSED APOSTLE JUDE.

*He warns that they should be firm in the faith once delivered against the rising of the impious and lascivious, adding the punishment of these in the manner of the Jews and of Sodom: for these also, fearing nothing, are carried away unbridled into all concupiscence of the flesh; he compares them to various things and recalls to them the prophecies of Enoch and the Apostles regarding them.*

1 **J**ude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to those who are beloved in God the Father, and preserved for Jesus Christ, and called.
2 May mercy, peace, and charity be fulfilled in you.
3 Dearly beloved, taking all care to write to you concerning your common salvation, I found it necessary to write to you: beseeching you to contend earnestly for the faith once delivered to the saints.
4 For certain men have secretly entered in (who were long ago designated for this judgment) impious men, turning the grace of our God into luxury, and denying the only Sovereign and our Lord Jesus Christ.
5 But I desire to remind you, though you once knew all things, that Jesus <note>The Latin Vulgate uses "Jesus" here to refer to the divine act of deliverance from Egypt, whereas many other versions use "the Lord."</note>, saving the people out of the land of Egypt, † afterward destroyed those who did not believe:

<margin>† Genesis 19:24.</margin>

### CHAPTER ONE.

*John, exiled on the island of Patmos, is commanded to write what he saw to the seven churches of Asia, represented by seven lampstands, which he saw surrounding the Son of Man; describing the manner in which He was revealed to him.*

1 The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave to him to make known to his servants the things which must shortly come to pass: and he signified it, sending by his Angel to his servant John,

2 Who has given testimony to the word of God, and the testimony of Jesus Christ, in all things whatsoever he has seen.

3 Blessed is he who reads and hears the words of this prophecy: and keeps those things which are written in it: for the time is near.

9 I, John, your brother and sharer in tribulation, and in the kingdom, and patience in Christ Jesus, was on the island which is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus:

12 And I turned to see the voice that spoke with me: And being turned, I saw seven golden lampstands:

20 The mystery of the seven stars, which you saw in my right hand, and the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are the Angels of the seven Churches: and the seven lampstands are the seven Churches.

### CHAPTER II.

*John is commanded to write various things to the Churches of Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, and Thyatira: praising those who had not admitted the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, while calling others to repentance with threats: also detesting the lukewarm, and promising a reward to the one who conquers.*

1 To the Angel of the Church of Ephesus write: These things says he, who holds the seven stars in his right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands:

2 I know your works, and your labor, and your patience, and how you cannot bear evil men: and you have tried those who say they are Apostles, and are not: and have found them liars:

3 And you have patience, and have endured for my name, and have not fainted.

4 But I have somewhat against you, because you have left your first charity.

5 Be mindful therefore from whence you are fallen, and do penance, and do the first works: or else, I come to you, and will move your lampstand out of its place, except you do penance.

6 But this you have, that you hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans <note>An early heretical sect whose specific beliefs are debated, but were often associated by the Church Fathers with moral compromise</note>, which I also hate.

7 He that has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches: To him that overcomes, I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the Paradise of my God.

8 And to the Angel of the Church of Smyrna write: These things says the First and the Last; who was dead, and is alive:

9 I know your tribulation and your poverty, but you are rich: and you are blasphemed by those who say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.

10 Fear none of those things which you shall suffer. Behold, the devil will cast some of you into prison, that you may be tried: and you shall have tribulation ten days. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.

11 He that has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches: He that shall overcome shall not be hurt by the second death.

12 And to the Angel of the Church of Pergamum write: These things says he that has the sharp two-edged sword <term>rhomphæam: a large, heavy sword, symbolizing swift divine judgment</term>:

13 I know where you dwell, where the seat of Satan is: and you hold fast my name, and have not denied my faith. Even in those days when Antipas was my faithful witness, who was slain among you, where Satan dwells.

14 But I have against you a few things: because you have there them that hold the doctrine of † Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat, and to commit fornication:

<margin>† Numbers 24:3. & 25:2.</margin>

17 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches: To the one who conquers I will give the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone: and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.
18 And to the Angel of the Church of Thyatira write: These things says the Son of God, who has eyes like a flame of fire, and whose feet are like fine brass <term>aurichalco: a bright, gold-like alloy of copper and zinc, often translated as "fine brass" or "bronze"</term>:
19 I know your works, and your faith, and your charity, and your ministry, and your patience, and that your latest works are more than the first.
20 But I have a few things against you: because you permit the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication and to eat food sacrificed to idols.
21 And I gave her time to repent: and she will not repent of her fornication.
22 Behold, I will cast her into a bed: and those who commit adultery with her shall be in very great tribulation, unless they repent of their deeds.

But to you I say,

25 Yet that which you have, hold fast until I come.

### CHAPTER III.

*He is commanded to write to the Churches of Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea; calling back those who err to repentance with threats, but praising others, and promising a reward to the victor: saying that God knocks at the door, so that he may enter to the one who opens.*

1 And to the Angel of the Church of Sardis write: These things says he who has the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, but you are dead.
2 Be watchful, and strengthen the things that remain, which were about to die. For I do not find your works full before my God.
<margin>† 1 Thessalonians 5:2; 2 Peter 3:10; below 16:15.</margin>
3 Have in mind, therefore, how you have received and heard, and observe it, and repent. If therefore you do not watch, I will come to you like a thief, and you shall not know at what hour I will come to you.
4 But you have a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments: and they shall walk with me in white, because they are worthy.
5 He who conquers shall thus be clothed in white garments, and I will not blot out his name from the Book of Life, and I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.

<column-break/>

6 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.
<margin>† Isaiah 22:22. † Job 12:14.</margin>
7 And to the Angel of the Church of Philadelphia write: These things says the Holy One and the True One, † who has the key of David: † who opens, and no one shuts: who shuts, and no one opens:
8 I know your works. Behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut: because you have a little strength, and have kept my word, and have not denied my name.
9 Behold, I will bring some from the synagogue of Satan, who say they are Jews and are not, but do lie: Behold, I will make them come and adore before your feet: and they shall know that I have loved you.
10 Because you have kept the word of my patience, I also will keep you from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon the whole world to try those who dwell upon the earth.
11 Behold, I come quickly: hold fast that which you have, so that no one may take your crown.
12 He who conquers, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go out no more: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which descends out of heaven from my God, and my new name.
13 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.
<margin>† John 14:6.</margin>
14 And to the Angel of the Church of Laodicea write: These things says: The Amen, the faithful and true witness, † who is the beginning of the creation of God:
15 I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot: I would that you were cold or hot:
16 But because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will begin to vomit you out of my mouth.
17 Because you say: "I am rich, and made wealthy, and have need of nothing": and you do not know that you are wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked.
18 I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire, that you may be made rich, and be clothed in white garments, so that the shame of your nakedness may not appear, and anoint your eyes with eye-salve <term>collyrio: a medicinal salve or wash used for the eyes</term>, so that you may see.
<margin>† Proverbs 3:22; Hebrews 12:6.</margin>
19 † Those whom I love, I rebuke and chastise. Be zealous therefore, and repent.
20 Behold, I stand at the door and knock: if anyone hears my voice and opens the door to me, I will enter to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
21 To him who conquers, I will give to sit with me on my throne: as I also have conquered, and have sat with my Father on his throne.
22 He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the Churches.

### CHAPTER IV.

*After a door was opened in heaven, he sees the one sitting on the throne, and in his circle twenty-four elders sitting, and as he describes here, four living creatures, who together with the twenty-four elders were continually glorifying the one sitting on the throne.*

1 After these things I saw: and behold, a door opened in heaven, and the first voice which I heard was as it were of a trumpet speaking with me, saying: Come up hither, and I will show you the things which must happen after these.
2 And immediately I was in the spirit: and behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sitting upon the throne.

### C H A P T E R V.

*While John wept because no one could open the book sealed with seven seals, the Lamb who had been slain first opened it; once this was done, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders, with an innumerable multitude of Angels and every creature, greatly glorified him.*

**And** I saw in the right hand of him who sits upon the throne a book <note>original: "librum." In the ancient world, this would have been a scroll.</note> written within and without, sealed with seven seals.
**2** And I saw a strong Angel, proclaiming with a loud voice: Who is worthy to open the book, and to loose its seals?
**3** And no one was able, neither in heaven, nor on earth, nor under the earth, to open the book, nor to look upon it.
**4** And I wept much, because no one was found worthy to open the book, nor to see it.
**5** And one of the elders said to me: Do not weep: behold, the lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed to open the book, and to loose its seven seals.
**6** And I saw: and behold, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing as if it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes: which are the seven spirits of God, sent forth into all the earth.
**7** And he came, and took the book from the right hand of him who sat on the throne.
**8** And when he had opened the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each having harps, and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints:

<column-break/>

**9** And they sang a new song, saying: You are worthy, O Lord, to take the book, and to open its seals: for you were slain, and have redeemed us to God by your blood out of every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation:
**10** And you have made us a kingdom and priests to our God: and we shall reign upon the earth.
**11** And I saw, and I heard the voice of many Angels around the throne, and the living creatures, and the elders: and the number of them was † thousands of thousands,
<margin>† Daniel 7:10.</margin>
**12** Saying with a loud voice: Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, to receive power, and divinity, and wisdom, and strength, and honor, and glory, and blessing.
**13** And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them: I heard all saying: To him who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb, be blessing, and honor, and glory, and power, forever and ever.
**14** And the four living creatures said: Amen. And the twenty-four elders fell down on their faces: and adored him who lives forever and ever.

### C H A P T E R VI.

*With the opening of the four seals, various effects follow upon the earth: when the fifth is opened, the souls of the martyrs ask for judgment to be hastened: and at the opening of the sixth, signs of the coming judgment are shown.*

**And** I saw that the Lamb had opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as it were a voice of thunder: Come, and see.
**2** And I saw: and behold, a white horse, and he who sat upon it had a bow, and a crown was given to him, and he went forth conquering that he might conquer.
**3** And when he had opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying: Come, and see.
**4** And there went out another horse that was red: and to him who sat upon it, it was given to take peace from the earth, and that they should kill one another, and a great sword was given to him.
**5** And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying: Come, and see. And behold, a black horse: and he who sat upon it had a balance <note>original: "stateram," a pair of scales used for weighing goods.</note> in his hand.
**6** And I heard as it were a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying: A quart of wheat for a denarius <note>A denarius was a standard day's wage for a laborer; this indicates extreme inflation or famine.</note>, and three quarts of barley for a denarius, and do not harm the wine and the oil.
**7** And when he had opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying: Come, and see.
**8** And behold, a pale horse: and his name who sat upon him was Death, and hell <note>original: "infernus," referring to Hades or the realm of the dead.</note> followed him, and power was given to him over the four parts of the earth, to kill with the sword, with famine, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.
**9** And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held,
**10** And they cried with a loud voice, saying: How long, O Lord, (holy and true) do you not judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?
**11** And white robes were given to each of them: and...

### CHAPTER VII.

->*While the earth is to be punished, those bearing the sign upon their foreheads are ordered to be preserved without harm: those who are described are from both the Jews and the Gentiles, blessing God: and concerning those who were clothed in white robes.*<-

**1** After these things, I saw four Angels standing upon the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, so that they should not blow upon the land, nor upon the sea, nor upon any tree.
**2** And I saw another Angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God: and he cried out with a loud voice to the four Angels, to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea,
**3** Saying: Do not harm the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have signed the servants of our God upon their foreheads.
**4** And I heard the number of those who were signed: one hundred and forty-four thousand signed, from every tribe of the children of Israel.
**5** From the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand signed: From the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand signed: From the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand signed:
**6** From the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand signed: From the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand signed: From the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand signed:
**7** From the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand signed: From the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand signed: From the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand signed:
**8** From the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand signed: From the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand signed: From the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand signed.
**9** After these things I saw a great multitude, which no one could number, from all nations, and tribes, and peoples, and languages: standing before the throne, and in the sight of the Lamb, clothed in white robes, and palms in their hands:
**10** And they cried out with a loud voice, saying: Salvation to our God, who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.
**11** And all the angels stood around the throne, and the elders, and the four living creatures: and they fell upon their faces in the sight of the throne, and adored God,
**12** Saying, Amen. Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, honor, and power, and strength to our God, forever and ever, Amen.
**13** And one of the elders responded, and said

to me: These, who are clothed in white robes, who are they? and where did they come from?
**14** And I said to him: My lord, thou knowest. And he said to me: These are they who have come out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
**15** Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve him day and night in his temple: and he who sits on the throne shall dwell over them.

### CHAPTER VIII.

->*With the seventh seal opened, seven Angels with trumpets are shown, and after fire from the altar is cast upon the earth by another Angel, various storms occur: likewise, as the four Angels sound their trumpets, various plagues are brought forth against men.*<-

**1** And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
**2** And I saw seven Angels standing in the sight of God: and seven trumpets were given to them.
**3** And another Angel came, and stood before the altar, having a golden censer: and much incense was given to him, that he should offer it with the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar, which is before the throne of God.
**4** And the smoke of the incense from the prayers of the saints ascended from the hand of the Angel before God.
**5** And the Angel took the censer, and filled it with the fire of the altar, and cast it onto the earth, and there were thunders, and voices, and lightnings, and a great earthquake.
**6** And the seven Angels, who had the seven trumpets, prepared themselves to sound the trumpets.
**7** And the first Angel sounded his trumpet, and there was hail, and fire, mixed in blood, and it was cast upon the earth, and a third part of the earth was burned up, and a third part of the trees was consumed, and all green grass was burned up.
**8** And the second Angel sounded his trumpet: and as it were a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea, and a third part of the sea became blood.
**9** And a third part of those creatures which had life in the sea died, and a third part of the ships perished.
**10** And the third Angel sounded his trumpet: and a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell upon a third part of the rivers, and upon the fountains of waters:
**11** And the name of the star is called Wormwood <note>original: "Absinthium." A plant known for its extreme bitterness, symbolizing divine judgment or sorrow.</note>: and a third part of the waters became wormwood: and many men died from the waters, because they were made bitter.
**12** And the fourth Angel sounded his trumpet: and a third part of the sun was struck, and a third part of the moon, and a third part of the stars, so that a third part of them was darkened, and for a third part of the day there was no light, and likewise for the night.
**13** And I saw, and heard the voice of a single eagle flying through the midst of heaven, saying with a loud voice: Woe, woe, woe to the inhabitants of the earth, because of the remaining voices of the three Angels, who are about to sound their trumpets.

### CHAPTER IX.

*When the fifth Angel sounds his trumpet, a star falls, and locusts are described emerging from the smoke of the pit to torment men; then, when the sixth Angel sounds, four Angels are released who kill a third part of mankind with a massive cavalry army.*

1. AND the fifth Angel sounded his trumpet: and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth, and the key to the pit of the abyss was given to him.
2. And he opened the pit of the abyss: and smoke rose from the pit, like the smoke of a great furnace: and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the pit.
3. And from the smoke of the pit, locusts went out onto the earth, and power was given to them, just as the scorpions of the earth have power:
4. And they were commanded not to harm the grass of the earth, nor any green thing, nor any tree: but only those men who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.
5. And it was granted to them not to kill them, but that they should be tormented for five months: and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a man.
<margin>† Isaiah 2:19. Hosea 10:8. Luke 23:30.</margin>
6. † And in those days, men will seek death and will not find it: and they will long to die, and death will flee from them.
<margin>† Wisdom 16:9.</margin>
7. † And the appearance of the locusts was like horses prepared for battle: and upon their heads were something like crowns resembling gold: and their faces were like the faces of men.
8. And they had hair like the hair of women: and their teeth were like the teeth of lions.
9. And they had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of many horse-drawn chariots rushing into war:
10. And they had tails like scorpions, and there were stingers in their tails: and their power was to hurt men for five months: and they had over them
11. A King, the angel of the abyss, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon <note>original: "Abaddon." Means "Destruction."</note>, in Greek Apollyon <note>original: "Apollyon." Means "The Destroyer."</note>, and in Latin he has the name The Destroyer <note>original: "Exterminans."</note>.
12. One woe has passed, and behold, two more woes are coming after these things.
13. And the sixth Angel sounded his trumpet: and I heard a single voice from the four horns of the golden altar, which is before the eyes of God,
14. Saying to the sixth Angel, who had the trumpet: Release the four Angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.
15. And the four Angels were released, who had been prepared for that hour, and day, and month, and year, so that they might kill a third part of mankind.
16. And the number of the cavalry army was twenty thousand times ten thousand <note>This represents two hundred million.</note>. And I heard their number.
17. And thus I saw the horses in the vision: and those who sat upon them had breastplates of fire, and hyacinth <note>A deep blue or violet color.</note>, and sulfur: and the heads of the horses were like the heads of lions: and from their mouths proceeded fire, and smoke, and sulfur.
18. And by these three plagues, a third part of mankind was killed, by the fire, and by the smoke, and the sulfur, which proceeded from their mouths.
19. For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails: for their tails are like serpents, having heads: and with these they cause harm.
20. And the rest of the men, who were not killed by these plagues, still did not repent of

<column-break/>

the works of their hands, so that they would not worship demons, and idols of gold, and silver, and bronze, and stone, and wood, which can neither see, nor hear, nor walk:
21. And they did not repent of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.

### CHAPTER X.

*As another strong Angel cries out, seven thunders speak; furthermore, the Angel swears that time shall be no more, but that the mystery is to be fulfilled at the voice of the seventh Angel: and he gives a book to John to be eaten.*

1. AND I saw another strong Angel descending from heaven clothed in a cloud, and a rainbow was upon his head, and his face was like the sun, and his feet like columns of fire.
2. And he had in his hand a little book, opened: and he set his right foot upon the sea, and his left upon the land:
3. And he cried out with a loud voice, just as when a lion roars. And when he had cried out, seven thunders spoke their voices.
4. And when the seven thunders had spoken their voices, I was about to write: and I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: Seal up the things which the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write them.
<margin>† Daniel 12:7.</margin>
5. † And the Angel, whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the land, lifted up his hand toward heaven:
6. And he swore by him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things that are in it; and the earth and the things that are in it; and the sea and the things that are in it: That there shall be no more delay <note>original: "tempus non erit amplius." Literally "time will be no more," but often interpreted as "there shall be no more delay" before the final judgment.</note>:
7. But in the days of the voice of the seventh Angel, when he begins to sound the trumpet, the mystery of God shall be fulfilled, just as he announced it through his servants the Prophets.
8. And I heard the voice from heaven speaking with me again, and saying: Go, and take the open book from the hand of the Angel standing upon the sea and upon the land.
<margin>† Ezekiel 3:1.</margin>
9. And I went to the Angel, telling him to give me the book. And he said to me: † Take the book and devour it: and it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey.
10. And I took the book from the hand of the Angel and devoured it: and it was in my mouth sweet as honey: and when I had devoured it, my stomach was made bitter:
11. And he said to me: It is necessary for you to prophesy again to the Gentiles, and to peoples, and languages, and many kings.

### CHAPTER XI.

*John, measuring the temple, hears about the two witnesses who will preach, whom the beast ascending from the sea will kill: and they, rising again, ascend into heaven, and 7,000 men are killed in an earthquake; and at the sounding of the seventh Angel, the twenty-four elders give thanks to God.*

1. AND there was given to me a reed like a rod, and it was said to me: Arise, and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and those who worship in it.
2. But the court which is outside the temple, cast it out, and do not measure it: since it has been given—

...given to the Nations, and they shall trample the holy city for forty-two months. <note>A period of three and a half years, frequently appearing in apocalyptic literature to signify a limited time of suffering.</note>
3. And I will give power to my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy for one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.

11. And after three and a half days, the spirit of life from God entered into them. And they stood upon their feet, and great fear fell upon those who saw them.

13. And in that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth part of the city fell; and seven thousand names of men were killed in the earthquake; and the rest were struck with fear and gave glory to the God of heaven.
14. The second woe is past; and behold, the third woe will come quickly.
15. And the seventh Angel sounded his trumpet; and there were great voices in heaven, saying: "The kingdom of this world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Christ, and he shall reign forever and ever: Amen."

18. And the Nations were angry, and your wrath has come, and the time for the dead to be judged, and to give the reward to your servants the Prophets, and to the saints, and to those who fear your name, small and great, and to destroy those who have corrupted the earth."
19. And the temple of God was opened in heaven; and the ark of his testament was seen in his temple, and there were lightnings, and voices, and an earthquake, and great hail.

### C H A P T E R XII.

> *When the woman, while the dragon watched, had given birth to a son, her son was caught up to God; then, after a battle occurred in heaven, the fallen dragon began to persecute the woman's offspring.*

1. AND a great sign appeared in heaven: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars. <note>Traditionally interpreted as the Virgin Mary or as the Church.</note>
2. And being with child, she cried out while in labor, and was in pain to give birth.
3. And another sign was seen in heaven: and behold, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns; and on his heads were seven diadems.
4. And his tail drew a third part of the stars of heaven and cast them to the earth; and the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she had given birth, he might devour her son.
5. And she brought forth a male child, who was to rule all the Nations with a rod of iron; <note>original: "virga ferrea" — a symbol of absolute and unwavering authority.</note> and her son was caught up to God and to his throne.
6. And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she had a place prepared by God, that they might feed her there for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
7. And there was a great battle in heaven: Michael and his Angels fought with the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
8. And they did not prevail, nor was their place found any longer in heaven.
9. And that great dragon was cast out, that ancient serpent who is called the devil and Satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast down to the earth, and his angels were cast down with him.
10. And I heard a great voice in heaven saying: "Now salvation is come, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ; because the accuser of our brothers has been cast down, who accused them before the sight of our God day and night.
11. And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives even unto death.
12. Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them. Woe to the earth and to the sea, because the devil has come down to you, having great wrath, knowing that he has but a short time."
13. And after the dragon saw that he was cast down to the earth, he persecuted the woman who brought forth the male child.
14. And there were given to the woman two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the desert to her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, <note>Another reference to the three and a half year period of trial.</note> away from the face of the serpent.
15. And the serpent cast out of his mouth after the woman water like a river, that he might cause her to be carried away by the flood.
16. And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river which the dragon cast out of his mouth.
17. And the dragon was angry with the woman; and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.
18. And he stood upon the sand of the sea.

## C H A P T E R  XIII.

->*A beast rising from the sea with seven heads and ten horns and ten crowns, whose wound is healed, blasphemes God and wars against the saints: and another beast with two horns rising from the earth greatly favors it, forcing the image of the first to be made and worshipped, and its mark and name to be received.*<-

1 And I saw a beast rising from the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon its horns ten crowns, and upon its heads names of blasphemy.
2 And the beast which I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like the feet of a bear, and its mouth like the mouth of a lion. And the dragon gave it his own strength and great power.
3 And I saw one of its heads as if it were slain to death; and its death-wound was healed. And the whole earth followed the beast in wonder.
4 And they worshipped the dragon, who gave power to the beast; and they worshipped the beast, saying: "Who is like the beast? And who shall be able to fight with it?"
5 And there was given to it a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given to it to act for forty-two months. <note>A period of three and a half years, signifying a limited duration of trial or persecution.</note>
6 And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme His name, and His tabernacle, and those who dwell in heaven.
7 And it was given to it to make war with the saints, and to overcome them. And power was given to it over every tribe, and people, and tongue, and nation.
8 And all who dwell on the earth worshipped it: those whose names are not written in the Book of Life of the Lamb, who was slain from the beginning of the world.
9 If anyone has an ear, let him hear.
<margin>† Genesis 9:6. Matthew 26:52.</margin>
10 He who leads into captivity shall go into captivity; † he who kills with the sword must be killed by the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the Saints.
11 And I saw another beast rising from the earth, and it had two horns like a Lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.
12 And it exercised all the power of the first beast in its sight; and it caused the earth and those dwelling in it to worship the first beast, whose death-wound was healed.
13 And it performed great signs, so that it even made fire come down from heaven to earth in the sight of men.
14 And it seduced those dwelling on the earth by the signs which were given to it to perform in the sight of the beast, telling those dwelling on the earth to make an image of the beast which had the wound of the sword and yet lived.
15 And it was allowed to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast might speak; and it caused as many as would not worship the image of the beast to be killed.
16 And it shall cause all, small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to have a mark <term>characterem: a brand or stamped mark, often used to denote ownership or allegiance</term> on their right hand or on their foreheads.
17 And that no one might be able to buy or sell, except he who has the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of its name.
18 Here is wisdom. He who has understanding, let him calculate the number of the beast. For it is the number of a man: and its number is six hundred and sixty-six. <note>A famous enigma (gematria) where letters represent numbers; historically, many scholars have associated this with specific Roman emperors or symbolic systems of imperfection.</note>

## C H A P T E R  XIV.

->*The virgins walk singing with the Lamb, while one Angel announces the Gospel, another the fall of Babylon, and a third the torment of those who worshipped the beast: furthermore, two having sickles are commanded, the one to reap the harvest, the other the vineyard of the earth.*<-

1 And I looked, and behold, a Lamb stood upon Mount Zion, and with Him one hundred and forty-four thousand, having His name and the name of His Father written on their foreheads.
2 And I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of many waters, and like the voice of great thunder; and the voice which I heard was like that of harpers playing on their harps.
3 And they sang as it were a new song before the throne, and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one could learn the song except those one hundred and forty-four thousand, who were purchased from the earth.
4 These are they who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These were purchased from among men as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb.
5 And in their mouth no lie was found; for they are without spot before the throne of God.
6 And I saw another Angel flying through the midst of heaven, having the eternal Gospel, to preach to those sitting upon the earth, and over every nation, and tribe, and tongue, and people,
<margin>† Psalm 145:6.</margin>
7 Saying with a loud voice: "Fear the Lord, and give Him honor, for the hour of His judgment has come; and worship Him † who made heaven, and earth, the sea, and the fountains of water."
<margin>† Acts 14:14. † Isaiah 21:9. Jeremiah 51:8.</margin>
8 And another Angel followed, saying: "† Fallen, fallen is that great Babylon, who made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication." <note>Babylon is used here as a symbolic name for a city or empire characterized by decadence and opposition to God.</note>
9 And a third Angel followed them, saying with a loud voice: "If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives its mark on his forehead or on his hand,
10 He also shall drink of the wine of God's wrath, which is mixed pure in the cup of His wrath; and he shall be tormented with fire and sulfur in the sight of the holy Angels and in the sight of the Lamb.
11 And the smoke of their torments shall ascend forever and ever; and they have no rest day or night, who have worshipped the beast and its image, and if anyone receives the mark of its name."
12 Here is the patience of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
13 And I heard a voice from heaven, saying to me: "Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord. From now on, says the Spirit, that they may rest from their labors; for their works follow them."
14 And I looked, and behold, a white cloud; and upon the cloud sat one like the Son of Man, having on His head a golden crown, and in His hand a sharp sickle.
<margin>† Joel 3:13.</margin>
15 And another Angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to Him sitting upon the cloud: "† Put forth your sickle and reap, for the hour has come to reap, because the harvest of the earth is ripe."
<margin>† Matthew 13:39.</margin>
16 And He who sat on the cloud thrust His sickle into the earth, and the earth was reaped.
17 And another Angel came out of the temple which is in heaven, he also having a sharp sickle.

->*Those who had conquered the beast and his image and the number of his name glorify God; to the seven Angels having the seven last plagues are given seven bowls full of the wrath of God.*<-

2 And I saw something like a sea of glass mingled with fire, and those who had gained the victory over the beast, and over his image, and over the number of his name, standing upon the sea of glass, having the harps of God:
3 And singing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying: "Great and wonderful are your works, Lord God Almighty: just and true are your ways, King of the ages."
