### C H A P T E R XVI.

->*Upon the pouring out of the seven bowls onto the earth, the sea, the springs, the sun, the seat of the beast, the Euphrates, and the air, many plagues arise upon the earth.*<-

AND I heard a great voice out of the temple, saying to the seven Angels: "Go, and pour out the seven bowls of the wrath of God upon the earth."
2 And the first went, and poured out his bowl upon the earth: and there fell a sore and grievous wound upon the men who had the mark of the beast, and upon those who worshipped his image.
3 And the second Angel poured out his bowl upon the sea, and it became like the blood of a dead man: and every living soul died in the sea.
4 And the third poured out his bowl upon the rivers, and upon the fountains of waters, and they became blood.
5 And I heard the Angel of the waters saying:

<column-break/>

"You are just, O Lord, who are, and who were, the Holy One, because you have judged these things:
6 For they have shed the blood of saints and prophets, and you have given them blood to drink: for they are worthy."
7 And I heard another from the altar saying: "Even so, Lord God Almighty, true and just are your judgments."
8 And the fourth Angel poured out his bowl upon the sun, and power was given to him to afflict men with heat and with fire:
9 And men were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has power over these plagues, and they did not repent so as to give Him glory.
10 And the fifth Angel poured out his bowl upon the seat of the beast: and his kingdom became dark, and they gnawed their tongues for pain:
11 And they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their wounds, and did not repent of their works.
12 And the sixth Angel poured out his bowl upon that great river Euphrates: and its water was dried up, so that the way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun.
13 And I saw coming out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs.
14 For they are the spirits of demons, working signs, and they go forth to the kings of the whole earth to gather them to battle for the great day of Almighty God.
<margin>† Matthew 24:43; Luke 12:39; Above [Revelation] 3:3.</margin>
15 † "Behold, I come like a thief. Blessed is he who watches, and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame."
16 And he gathered them together into a place, which is called in Hebrew, <term>Armageddon</term>. <note>A name likely derived from "Har Megiddo," meaning the Mountain of Megiddo, a historical site of many battles.</note>
17 And the seventh Angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a great voice came out of the temple from the throne, saying: "It is done."
18 And there were lightnings, and voices, and thunders, and there was a great earthquake, such as never was since men were upon the earth: so great an earthquake, and so mighty.
19 And the great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the Gentiles fell, and great Babylon came into memory before God, to give to her the cup of the wine of the indignation of His wrath.
20 And every island fled away, and the mountains were not found.
21 And great hail, like a <term>talent</term> <note>original: "talentum." A talent was a massive weight, roughly 75 to 100 pounds (34-45 kg).</note>, fell down from heaven upon men: and men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail: because it was exceedingly great.

4 And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet, and gilded with gold, and precious stones, and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand, full of the abomination and the filthiness of her fornication.

<meta>This page marks the transition from the New Testament (concluding the Apocalypse on the previous page) to the non-canonical appendix of the Vulgate Bible. The catchword "LIBER" (Book) on the previous page pointed toward the beginning of this secondary section. The introductory text explains why these specific writings—the Prayer of Manasseh and 3–4 Esdras—were included despite not being considered part of the official Roman Catholic canon defined at Trent.</meta>

*The Prayer of Manasseh, as well as the two books that circulate under the name of the Third and Fourth Books of Esdras, are set apart in this place—namely, outside the sequence of the Canonical Books which the holy Council of Trent <note>The Council of Trent (1545–1563) formally defined the books to be included in the Catholic Bible. These three texts were moved to an appendix in 1592 to ensure they were preserved but not confused with the inspired Canon.</note> accepted and decreed to be held as Canonical—so that they might not utterly perish; for they are occasionally cited by some of the holy Fathers and are found in some Latin Bibles, both manuscript and printed.*

# THE PRAYER OF MANASSEH
## KING OF JUDAH,
->WHEN HE WAS HELD CAPTIVE IN BABYLON.<-

O Lord Almighty, God of our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of their righteous offspring; who made heaven and earth with all their adornment; who bound the sea by the word of your command; who shut up the abyss <note>original: "abyssus," referring to the primordial deeps or the underworld</note> and sealed it by your terrible and glorious name; before whom all things shudder and tremble at the presence of your power, because the magnificence of your glory is unbearable, and the anger of your threat against sinners cannot be endured: yet the mercy of your promise is immeasurable and unsearchable. For you are the Lord Most High, kind, patient, and very merciful, and grieving over the malice of men. You, O Lord, according to the abundance of your goodness, have promised repentance and forgiveness to those who have sinned against you, and in the multitude of your mercies, you have decreed repentance for sinners unto salvation. You, therefore, O Lord, God of the righteous, did not appoint repentance for the righteous—for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, those who did not sin against you—but you have appointed repentance for me, a sinner. For I have sinned more than the number of the sands of the sea; my iniquities are multiplied, O Lord, my iniquities are multiplied, and I am not worthy to look up and behold the height of heaven because of the multitude of my iniquities. I am bowed down by a heavy iron chain <note>Manasseh was taken to Babylon in hooks and chains, according to 2 Chronicles 33:11.</note>, so that I cannot lift up my head, and there is no relief for me: because I have provoked your wrath and done what is evil before you. I did not do your will, and I did not keep your commandments; I set up abominations and multiplied offenses. And now I bend the knee of my heart, begging goodness from you. I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned, and I acknowledge my iniquities. Therefore I ask, entreating you: forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and do not destroy me together with my iniquities, nor, being angry forever, reserve evils for me, nor condemn me to the lowest parts of the earth. For you are God, the God—I say—of those who repent; and in me you will show all your goodness, because you will save me, unworthy as I am, according to your great mercy. And I will praise you always, all the days of my life: for all the host of the heavens praises you, and to you is the glory forever and ever. Amen.

victims upon the sacrifice of the Lord, according to the command of King Josiah.

19 And the children of Israel, who were found at that time, kept the Passover: and the feast day of unleavened bread for seven days:

20 And such a Passover was not celebrated in Israel since the times of Samuel the prophet:

21 And all the kings of Israel did not celebrate such a Passover as Josiah did, and the Priests, and the Levites, and the Jews, and all Israel, who were found staying in Jerusalem.

22 In the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign, the Passover was celebrated.

23 And the works of Josiah were directed in the sight of his Lord with a heart full of fear:

24 And the things that were written concerning him in former times, concerning those who sinned, and who were irreligious against the Lord beyond every nation, and who did not seek the words of the Lord over Israel.

25 And after all this action of Josiah, Pharaoh the king of Egypt went up, coming into Carchemish from the route over the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.

26 And the king of Egypt sent to Josiah, saying: "What is there to me and to you, king of Judah?

27 I am not sent by the Lord to fight against you: for my war is upon the Euphrates; hurry and go down."

28 And Josiah did not return upon his chariot: but he attempted to fight him, not attending to the word of the prophet from the mouth of the Lord:

29 But he staged a battle against him in the field of Megiddo <note>original: "Mageddo"</note>. And the princes went down to king Josiah.

30 And the king said to his servants, "Move me away from the battle, for I am weakened greatly." And immediately his servants moved him from the battle line.

31 And he went up upon his second chariot: and arriving at Jerusalem, he died, and was buried in his father's tomb.

32 And in all Judea they mourned Josiah: and those who presided, with their wives, lamented him, even to this day. And this was given to be done always for all the kin of Israel.

33 Now these things are written in the book of the histories of the kings of Judah: both the individual deeds of Josiah's acts, and his glory and his understanding in the law of the Lord: and whatever was done by him, and what is not written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

34 And those who were of the nation, taking Jechonias <note>This name refers here to Jehoahaz, the son of Josiah who was deposed by Pharaoh</note> the son of Josiah, appointed him king instead of Josiah his father, when he was thirty-three years old.

35 And he reigned over Israel for three months. And the king of Egypt removed him, so that he should not reign in Jerusalem:

36 And he fined the nation a hundred talents of silver, and one talent of gold.

37 And the king of Egypt appointed Joachim <note>Also known as Jehoiakim</note> his brother, as king of Judah and Jerusalem:

38 And he bound the magistrates of Joachim, and Zaraceles his brother, and apprehending him, brought him back into Egypt.

49 Also the leaders of the people of the Lord committed many iniquities and acted impiously beyond all the uncleanness of the Gentiles, and they polluted the temple of the Lord, which was holy in Jerusalem.

58 "Until the land has enjoyed its Sabbaths, all the time of its desolation it shall keep Sabbath, until the completion of seventy years."

### C H A P T E R  II.

->*Cyrus, king of the Persians, releases the captive Jews in his kingdom to return to their land: as they were restoring Jerusalem, they were prohibited by Artaxerxes because of the accusations of certain men.*<-

1 In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, so that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished:

<column-break/>

2 The Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, also in writing,

3 Saying: "Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord of Israel, the Most High Lord, has appointed me king of the world.

4 And he has signaled to me that I should build a house for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judea.

5 If there is anyone of your nation, let his Lord be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem.

6 Therefore, let as many as dwell in the surrounding places help them with gold and silver,

7 With gifts, with horses and cattle, and with other things which are added according to vows for the temple of the Lord, which is in Jerusalem."

8 Then the leaders of the tribes of the districts of Judah, from the tribe of Benjamin, stood up, along with the priests and Levites, whom the Lord had stirred to go up and build the House of the Lord which is in Jerusalem; and those who were in their neighborhood

9 Assisted them with all their gold and silver, and cattle, and many with numerous vows, whose hearts had been stirred.

10 And King Cyrus brought out the sacred vessels of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had moved from Jerusalem and had consecrated to his own idol.

11 And Cyrus king of the Persians, bringing them forth, delivered them to Mithridates, who was over his treasures.

12 Through him, they were delivered to Sanabassar <note>original: "Salmanasaro," likely a variant of Sheshbazzar</note>, the governor of Judea.

13 This was the number of them: Two thousand four hundred silver libation bowls; thirty silver cups <note>original: "athifcæ," a rare term for a vessel</note>; thirty gold vials, and likewise two thousand four hundred silver ones; and a thousand other vessels.

14 All the vessels of gold and silver were five thousand eight hundred and sixty.

15 And they were counted out to Sanabassar, together with those who had come from the Babylonian captivity to Jerusalem.

16 But in the times of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, Balsamus, Mithridates, Sabellius, Rathimus, Balthemus, Samelius the scribe, and the rest of those dwelling in Samaria and other places, wrote to him concerning those who lived in Judea and Jerusalem, sending the following letter to King Artaxerxes:

17 "LORD, your servants Rathimus the recorder, Sabellius the scribe, and the rest of the judges of your court in Coelesyria and Phoenicia.

18 And now let it be known to our lord the king, that the Jews who came up from you to us, arriving in Jerusalem—that rebellious and wicked city <note>original: "civitatem refugam et pessimam"</note>—are rebuilding its furnaces, setting up the walls, and raising the temple.

19 Because if this city and its walls are finished, not only will they not endure to pay taxes, but they will even resist kings.

20 And because this work is being done around the temple, we thought it right not to overlook this matter;

21 But to make it known to our lord the king, so that, if it please you, O king, a search may be made in the books of your fathers.

22 And you will find written in the records concerning these things, and you will know that this city was rebellious, shaking both kings and cities,

23 And that the Jews are rebels, inciting battles there from of old; for which cause this city was laid waste.

24 Now therefore we make it known, lord king,"

25 Then the King wrote back to Rathimus, the recorder of events, to Balthemus, to Sabellius the scribe, and to the others stationed with them, and to those living in Syria and Phoenicia, regarding the matters submitted:
26 I have read the letter which you sent to me. Therefore, I ordered an investigation to be made, and it was found that this city has been resisting kings from ancient times,

### C H A P T E R III.

*While Darius was sleeping after a splendid feast given for all his officials, three of his bodyguards proposed a riddle: whether wine, the king, or women are strongest; however, truth is proved the strongest of all. First, the case for wine is argued.*

King Darius gave a great feast for all those born in his household, and for all the officials of Media and Persia,
2 and for all the nobles <note>original: "purpuratis," literally "those clothed in purple."</note>, the governors, the consuls, and the prefects under him, from India even unto Ethiopia, across one hundred and twenty-seven provinces.
3 and when they had eaten and drunk and were satisfied, they returned home; then Darius the king went up into his bedchamber and slept, and later woke up.
4 Then those three young men, the bodyguards who guarded the king’s person, said to one another:
5 "Let each of us speak a word that excels; and whoever’s word appears wiser than the others, King Darius shall give him great gifts:
6 to be clothed in purple, to drink from gold, to sleep upon gold, a chariot with a golden bridle, a turban of fine linen, and a chain around his neck.
7 And he shall sit second after Darius because of his wisdom, and he shall be called the kinsman of Darius."
8 Then each of them wrote his own word, sealed it, and placed it under the pillow of King Darius,
9 and they said: "When the king has risen, we will give him our writings; and whichever of the three the king and the nobles of Persia judge to have the wisest word, to him shall the victory be given, as it is written."
10 One wrote: "Wine is strong."
11 Another wrote: "The king is stronger."

<column-break/>

12 The third wrote: "Women are stronger; but above all things, Truth is the victor."
13 And when the king had risen, they took their writings and gave them to him, and he read them.
14 And sending out, he called all the nobles of the Persians and the Medes, the nobles, the governors, and the prefects.
15 And they sat in the council chamber, and the writings were read before them.
16 And he said: "Call the young men, and they shall explain their words." And they were called, and they entered.
17 And he said to them: "Explain to us these things that were written." And the first, who had spoken of the strength of wine, began,
18 and said: "O men, how wine prevails over all men who drink it! It leads the mind astray.
19 Likewise, it makes the mind of the king and the orphan alike empty; similarly the mind of the slave and the free man, the poor and the rich.
20 and it turns every thought to security and cheerfulness, and it remembers no sorrow or debt.
21 and it makes every heart feel rich, remembering neither king nor official, and it makes one speak of everything in terms of talents <note>A talent was a massive unit of weight/currency, implying the drunkard feels infinitely wealthy.</note>.
22 and they do not remember, when they have drunk, friendship or brotherhood; but not much later they draw their swords.
23 and when they have been overcome by wine and rise again, they do not remember what they have done.
24 O men, does not wine excel? Who would think to act thus?" And having said this, he fell silent.

### C H A P T E R IV.

*The excellent strength of the king, of women, and of truth is argued; but the prize is given to truth. At the petition of Zerubbabel, Darius returns the sacred vessels, writing so that liberty is given to the Jews and funds for the construction of Jerusalem.*

And the next man, who had spoken of the strength of the king, began to speak.
2 "O men, do not men excel, who rule the land and the sea and all things that are in them?
3 But the king excels above all, and is their lord; and whatever he tells them to do, they do.
4 and if he sends them against warriors, they go, and they level mountains, and walls, and towers.
5 They are killed and they kill, and they do not bypass the king's words; for if they conquer, they bring everything they have plundered to him.
6 Likewise, all others, as many as do not serve as soldiers or fight, but cultivate the land: when they have finished harvesting, they bring tribute to the king.
7 and he, being but one man—if he says 'kill,' they kill; if he says 'spare,' they spare.
8 if he says 'strike,' they strike; if he says 'destroy,' they destroy; if he says 'build,' they build.
9 if he says 'cut down,' they cut down; if he says 'plant,' they plant.
10 and all the people and the armies obey him; and besides this, he himself reclines, eats, drinks, and sleeps.
11 But these men guard him in a circle, and no one can go and do his own work, but they are obedient to him at his word.
12 Men, how does the king not excel, who is spoken of in such a way?" And he fell silent.

13 The third, who had spoken about women and the truth—this was Zorobabel <note>Zerubbabel, the leader of the Jewish people returning to Jerusalem</note>—began to speak:
14 "Men, is the king not great, and are men not many, and does wine not excel? Who is it, then, that rules over them?
15 Was it not women who gave birth to the king and all the people who rule over the sea and the land?
16 And from them they were born; and they themselves brought up those who planted the vineyards, from which wine is made.
17 And they make the robes of all men, and they bring glory to men, and men cannot be separated from women.
18 If they have gathered gold and silver and every beautiful thing, and they see one woman of good character and beautiful appearance,
19 leaving all these things, they gaze at her, and with open mouths they stare at her, and they are drawn to her more than to gold and silver or any precious thing.
20 A man leaves his own father who raised him, and his own country, and joins himself to a woman.
21 And with the woman he surrenders his soul; and he remembers neither father, nor mother, nor country.
22 And from this you ought to know that women rule over you. Do you not suffer?
23 And a man takes up his sword and goes out on the road to commit thefts and murders, and to sail the sea and the rivers;
24 and he sees a lion, and walks in the darkness; and when he has committed theft, and frauds, and robberies, he brings it back to his beloved.
25 And again, a man loves his own wife more than father or mother.
26 And many have become out of their minds because of their wives, and have become slaves because of them.
27 And many have perished, and been slaughtered, and have sinned because of women.
28 And now believe me, because the king is great in his power, and all regions fear to touch him.
29 Yet I saw Apame, the daughter of Bartacus <note>original: "Bezacis"</note>, the marvelous concubine of the king, sitting next to the king on the right,
30 and taking the diadem from his head and putting it on herself, and she struck the king with her left hand.
31 And besides this, he gazed at her with open mouth; and if she smiled at him, he laughed; but if she was angry with him, he flattered her until she was reconciled to his favor.
32 O men, why are women not stronger? The earth is great, and the heaven is high; who does these things?"
33 And then the king and the nobles <note>original: "purpurati" — literally "those dressed in purple," the highest rank of Persian courtiers</note> looked at one another. And he began to speak about the truth:
34 "O men, are women not strong? The earth is great, and the heaven is high, and the swift course of the sun turns the heaven in a circle to its own place in one day.
35 Is he not magnificent who does these things? And truth is great, and stronger than all things.
36 All the earth calls upon the truth, even heaven blesses it, and all works are moved and tremble at it, and there is nothing unjust with it.
37 Wine is unjust, the king is unjust, women are unjust, all the sons of men are unjust, and all their works are unjust, and there is no truth in them, and they shall perish in their own injustice.
38 But the truth remains and grows strong forever, and it lives and prevails for ages of ages."

<column-break/>

39 "Nor is there with truth any respect of persons <note>meaning partiality or favoritism</note>, nor differences; but it does what is just to all—to the unjust and the wicked—and all are pleased with its works.
40 And there is nothing unjust in its judgment, but there is strength, and the kingdom, and the power, and the majesty of all ages. Blessed be the God of truth!"
41 And he ceased speaking. And all the people shouted and said: "Great is the truth, and it prevails!" <note>original: "Magna est veritas, & prævalet" — a famous Latin proverb</note>
42 Then the king said to him: "Ask whatever you wish, more than what is written, and I will give it to you, according to how you have been found wiser than your neighbors; and you shall sit next to me, and be called my kinsman."
43 Then he said to the king: "Be mindful of your vow, which you vowed to build Jerusalem on the day you received your kingdom;
44 and to send back all the vessels that were taken from Jerusalem, which Cyrus set aside when he conquered <note>original: "mactavit" — literally 'slaughtered' or 'sacrificed,' used here for the defeat of the city</note> Babylon, and intended to send back there.
45 And you vowed to build the temple which the Edomites burned when Judea was laid waste by the Chaldeans.
46 And now this is what I ask, Lord, and what I seek; this is the majesty I ask from you: that you perform the vow which you vowed to the King of Heaven from your own mouth."
47 Then King Darius, rising, kissed him, and wrote letters to all the treasurers, and governors, and nobles, that they should escort him and all those with him who were going up to build Jerusalem.
48 And to all the governors who were in Syria, and Phoenicia, and Lebanon, he wrote letters to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to Jerusalem, to build the city with them.
49 And he wrote for all the Jews who were going up from his kingdom to Judea for their freedom, that no official, or magistrate, or governor should come upon their doors,
50 and that all the region which they held should be free of taxes for them, and that the Edomites should leave the villages which they held belonging to the Jews.
51 And he gave twenty talents every year for the structure of the temple until it was finished;
52 and to provide burnt offerings upon the altar every day, as they have a commandment to offer ten other talents every year.
53 And to all those who go from Babylon to build the city, there should be freedom for both them and their children, and for all the priests who go before.
54 He also wrote the amount, and ordered the sacred robe in which they should serve to be given;
55 and he wrote to give the Levites their support until the day when the house is finished and Jerusalem is built.
56 And to all who guarded the city, he wrote that land <note>original: "fortes" — likely referring to land allotments or strongholds</note> and wages should be given to them.
57 And he sent away all the vessels which Cyrus had set aside from Babylon, and everything Cyrus had said should be done, he himself commanded to be done and sent to Jerusalem.
58 And when that young man had gone out, lifting his face toward Jerusalem, he blessed the King of Heaven,
59 and said: "From You is the victory, and from You is wisdom and glory. And I am Your servant.
60 Blessed are You who have given me wisdom, and I will acknowledge You, Lord God of our fathers."

40 And Nehemiah and Atharates <note>original: "Attharas"; likely a title for the governor, equivalent to the 'Tirshatha' in the Hebrew Bible</note> said to them that they should not share in the holy things until a High Priest should arise learned in manifestation and truth <note>original: "ostensionem et veritatem," a Latin rendering of the Hebrew 'Urim and Thummim,' the sacred lots used by priests to determine God's will</note>.
41 Now all of Israel, excluding the male and female servants, was forty-two thousand three hundred and forty.
42 Their male and female servants were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven. The male and female singers were two hundred and sixty-five.
43 The camels were four hundred and thirty-five. The horses were seven thousand thirty-six. The mules were two hundred forty-five. The beasts of burden were five thousand twenty-five.
44 And some of the leaders of the villages, when they came to the temple of God which was in Jerusalem, vowed to rebuild the temple on its site according to their ability:
45 And to give into the sacred treasury for the works twelve thousand minas <note>a unit of weight or currency</note> of gold, and five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priestly robes.
46 And the Priests and the Levites, and those who had come out of the common people, lived in Jerusalem and in the surrounding region, as did the sacred singers, the gatekeepers, and all Israel in their own regions.
47 But when the seventh month arrived, and while the sons of Israel were each attending to their own affairs, they gathered with one mind in the courtyard which was before the East gate.
48 And Joshua <note>original: "Jesus"</note> the son of Josedek, and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers stood up and prepared the altar,
49 So that they might offer burnt offerings upon it, according to the things written in the book of Moses, the man of God.
50 And there gathered there people from other nations of the land, and all the peoples of the land raised the sanctuary in its place, and they offered sacrifices and morning burnt offerings to the Lord.
51 And they celebrated the <term>scenopegia</term> <note>the Feast of Tabernacles or Sukkot, a harvest festival where participants live in temporary booths</note> and the solemn day, as is commanded in the law; and the daily sacrifices, as was fitting.
52 And after these, they performed the established offerings, and the sacrifices of the Sabbaths, of the new moons, and of all the sanctified solemn days.
53 And as many as made a vow to the Lord from the new moon of the seventh month began to offer sacrifices to God, even though the temple of the Lord was not yet built.
54 And they gave money to the stone-cutters and craftsmen, and drink and food, with joy.
55 And they gave carts to the Sidonians and Tyrians, that they might transport cedar logs for them from Lebanon, making rafts to the port of Joppa, according to the decree that had been written for them by Cyrus, king of the Persians.
56 And in the second year after coming to the temple of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedek, and their brothers, and the priests and Levites, and everyone who had come from the captivity to Jerusalem, began the work.
57 And they laid the foundation of the temple of God on the new moon of the second month of the second year since they had come into Judea and Jerusalem.
58 And they appointed the Levites from twenty years of age over the works of the Lord; and Joshua and his son, and all his Levite brothers, stood together as one, along with the executors of the law, performing the work in the house of the Lord.
59 And the priests stood dressed in their robes with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals,

<column-break/>

60 praising the Lord and blessing Him according to the decree of David, king of Israel.
61 And they sang a song to the Lord, for His sweetness and honor are forever over all Israel.
62 And all the people sounded the trumpets and shouted with a loud voice, praising the Lord for the raising up of the house of the Lord.
63 And many from the priests and Levites, and the elders presiding over the villages, who had seen the former house, came;
64 and at the building of this one, they broke out with shouting and great weeping, while many others sounded trumpets with great joy:
65 So much so that the people could not hear the trumpets because of the weeping of the people. For the crowd was sounding the trumpets so magnificently that it was heard from far away.
66 And the enemies of the tribe of Judah and Benjamin heard it, and they came to find out what the sound of the trumpets was.
67 And they recognized that those who were of the captivity were building a temple to the Lord God of Israel.
68 And approaching Zerubbabel and Joshua, the leaders of the villages, they said to them: "We will build together with you;
69 For we also have heard your Lord, and we have walked in like manner since the days of Asbazareth <note>likely referring to Esarhaddon</note>, king of the Assyrians, who brought us here."
70 And Zerubbabel and Joshua, and the leaders of the villages of Israel, said to them:
71 "It is not for us and you to build the house of our God; for we alone will build for the Lord of Israel, according to the things that Cyrus the king of the Persians commanded us."
72 But the nations of the land, pressing hard upon those who were in Judea, and disrupting the work of building and laying traps, and bringing in other peoples, hindered them from building;
73 And by carrying out attacks, they prevented the building from being completed during the entire lifetime of King Cyrus, and they delayed the construction for two years, until the reign of Darius.

5 And the elders of the Jews found favor because a visitation was made upon those who were of the captivity by the Lord.
6 And they were not hindered from building until word was sent to Darius about all these things and a response was received.

23 Then King Darius commanded a search to be made in the libraries: and there was found in the town of Ecbatana <note>the ancient capital of Media</note>, which is in the region of Media, a certain scroll in which these things were written:

24 In the first year of the reign of Cyrus, King Cyrus commanded the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem to be built, where they used to burn with continual fire,

25 Of which the height shall be sixty cubits <note>a cubit is roughly 18 inches</note>, and the breadth sixty cubits, square, with three layers of polished stones, and one layer of local wood, and one new layer, and the expenses are to be given from the house of King Cyrus:

26 And the sacred vessels of the house of the Lord, both of gold and silver, which Nebuchadnezzar carried away into the house of the Lord, which is in Jerusalem, where they were placed, let them be put back there.

32 And let it be proclaimed, that whoever shall transgress any of these things which are written, or shall despise them, a beam shall be taken from his own property, and they shall be hanged, and their goods shall be forfeited to the king.

33 Therefore also may the Lord, whose name is invoked there, exterminate every king and nation that shall stretch out their hand to hinder or to ill-treat that house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.

34 I, King Darius, have decreed that it be done most diligently according to these things.

### CHAPTER VII.

->*The house of God, having been built, is dedicated and consecrated, and in it the Feast of Unleavened Bread is celebrated.*<-

Then Sifennes, the sub-governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia, and Satrabuzanes, and their associates, obeyed those things which had been decreed by King Darius,

2 They applied themselves to the most holy works very diligently, cooperating with the elders of the Jews, the princes of Syria.

3 And the holy works prospered while Haggai <note>original: "Aggæo"</note> and Zechariah <note>original: "Zacharia"</note> the prophets were prophesying.

4 And they finished all things by the commandment of the Lord God of Israel, and by the counsel of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes, the king of the Persians:

5 And our house was finished by the twenty-third day of the month of Adar <note>the twelfth month of the Hebrew calendar</note>, in the sixth year of King Darius.

6 And the children of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites, and the rest who were of the captivity, did according to those things which are written in the book of Moses.

7 And they offered for the dedication of the temple of the Lord, a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs,

8 And twelve goats for the sins of all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.

9 And the priests and the Levites stood clothed in their robes by their tribes, over all the works of the Lord God of Israel, according to the book of Moses, and the gatekeepers at every gate.

10 And the children of Israel, with those who were of the captivity, kept the Passover <note>original: "Phase"</note> on the fourteenth day of the first month, when the priests and the Levites were sanctified.

11 All the children of the captivity were not sanctified together, because all the Levites were sanctified together.

### CHAPTER VIII.

*As Ezra goes up from Babylon to Jerusalem, he is given a letter from Artaxerxes containing benefits granted to the Jews; those who went up with him are listed; and having committed the gold and silver to the priests, Ezra, after making a prayer, warns the people to repent because they had not separated themselves from foreigners.*

1 And after these things, during the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, there came Ezra, the son of Azarias, the son of Helcias, the son of Salomas,
2 The son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub, the son of Ameri, the son of Azahel, the son of Bocci, the son of Abisue, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the first priest:
3 This Ezra went up from Babylon, being a scribe and skilled in the law of Moses, which was given by the Lord God of Israel to teach and to do.
4 And the king gave him glory, because he had found favor in all dignity and desire in his sight.
5 And there went up with him some of the children of Israel, and of the priests, and the Levites, and the sacred singers of the temple, and the gatekeepers, and the temple servants to Jerusalem.
6 In the seventh year of the reign of Artaxerxes, in the fifth month—this is the seventh year of the reign—leaving Babylon on the new moon of the fifth month,
7 They came to Jerusalem according to his command, following the prosperity of the journey given to them by their Lord.
8 For in these matters Ezra possessed great discipline, so that he would not omit any of those things which were from the law of the Lord and the commandments, and in teaching all Israel all justice and judgment.
9 And those who wrote the decrees of King Artaxerxes approached and delivered the document which had come from King Artaxerxes to Ezra the Priest, and reader of the law of the Lord, a copy of which is set out below.
10 KING Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest, and reader of the law of the Lord, greeting.
11 Judging more humanely in matters of benefits, I have commanded those of the Jewish nation in my kingdom who desire it of their own accord—both of the priests and the Levites—to accompany you to Jerusalem.
12 If any therefore wish to go with you, let them gather and set out, as it has pleased me and my seven friends who are my counselors,
13 To oversee those things which are being done in Judea and Jerusalem, observing according to what you have in the law of the Lord,
14 And to carry gifts to the Lord God of Israel, which I and my friends have vowed to Jerusalem, and all the gold and silver that shall be found

<column-break/>

15 Which is donated for the Nation itself for the temple of the Lord, for those who are in Jerusalem, so that this gold and silver may be gathered for bulls, and rams, and lambs, and kids, and those things which are appropriate for them,
16 To offer sacrifices to the Lord upon the altar of their Lord which is in Jerusalem.
17 And whatever you and your brothers wish to do with the gold and silver, perform it according to your will, according to the command of the Lord your God:
18 And the sacred vessels, which are given to you for the works of the house of the Lord your God, which is in Jerusalem:
19 And other things, whatever may be needed by you for the works of the temple of your God, you shall give from the royal treasury:
20 When you wish to do anything with your brothers with gold and silver, perform it according to the will of the Lord.
21 And I, King Artaxerxes, have commanded the keepers of the treasures of Syria and Phoenicia, that whatever Ezra the priest and reader of the law of the Lord shall write, it shall be diligently given to him, up to a hundred talents of silver, and likewise of gold:
22 And up to a hundred bushels <note>original: "modios"; a Roman dry measure approximately equivalent to two gallons</note> of wheat, and a hundred jugs of wine, and other things in abundance without tax.
23 Let all things be done according to the law of God for the most high God, lest perhaps wrath should arise against the kingdom of the king, and his son, and his sons.
24 And it is told to you, that upon all the priests, and Levites, and sacred singers, and temple servants, and scribes of this temple,
25 No tribute, nor any other tax shall be imposed, nor shall anyone have the power to object to them in anything.
26 And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of God, appoint judges and arbiters in all Syria and Phoenicia: and teach all those who do not know the law of your God:
27 So that whoever shall transgress the law may be diligently punished, whether by death, or by torment, or even by a fine of money or by banishment.
28 And Ezra the scribe said: Blessed be the God of our fathers, who put this will into the heart of the king, to glorify his house which is in Jerusalem.
29 And he has honored me in the sight of the king, and his counselors, and his friends, and his nobles.
30 And I was made constant in spirit according to the help of the Lord my God, and I gathered men from Israel to go up with me.

62 And we departed from the river *Thia* on the twelfth day of the first month, until we entered into *Jerusalem*.

65 And the weight of them was recorded in that same hour.
66 Moreover, those who had come out of captivity offered a sacrifice to the Lord God of *Israel*: twelve bulls for all *Israel*, eighty-six rams,
67 Seventy-two lambs, twelve he-goats for sin; and twelve cows for safety—all as a sacrifice to the Lord.
68 And they delivered the king's decrees to the royal stewards and the governors of *Coele-Syria* and *Phoenicia*: and they honored the People and the temple of the Lord.
69 And when these things were finished, the leaders came to me, saying: The people of *Israel*, and the princes, and the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves,
70 Nor have the foreign nations and peoples of the land from their uncleanness: from the *Canaanites*, and *Hittites*, and *Perizzites*, and *Jebusites*, and *Moabites*, and *Egyptians*, and *Edomites*.
71 For they and their sons have joined themselves with their daughters, and the holy seed has been mixed with the foreign nations of the land: and the leaders and magistrates have been participants in this iniquity since the beginning of this reign.
72 And as soon as I heard these things, I tore my garments and my sacred tunic: and tearing the hair from my head and my beard, I sat down grieving and mournful.
73 And as many as were then moved by the word of the Lord God of *Israel* gathered to me as I mourned over this iniquity, and I sat in sadness until the evening sacrifice.
74 And rising from my fast, with my garments and sacred tunic torn, I knelt down and stretched out my hands to the Lord,

1 And Esdras, rising up from before the court of the temple, went into the chamber <term>pastophorium: a vestry or living quarters for priests within the temple complex</term> of Jonathan son of Nasabi.

->In all the descendants of Adam, and especially among the unfaithful Gentiles, malice abounds.<-

16 And you set Jacob apart for yourself, but Esau you separated. And Jacob became a great multitude.

<meta>This page continues the prayer of the prophet Esdras (also known as Ezra). On the previous page, Esdras was recounting the history of creation and God’s choice of Israel. Here, he moves into a deep lament over the "evil heart" that leads humanity to sin and questions why Israel suffers under Babylon when Babylon is just as sinful.</meta>

# THE FOURTH BOOK OF ESDRAS

...and you shook the world, and made the depths tremble, and disturbed the age,
19 And your glory passed through four gates: fire, earthquake, wind, and frost, so that you might give the law to the seed of Jacob, and the devotion <note>original: "diligentiam," implying careful observance or religious duty</note> to the generation of Israel.
20 And yet you did not take away from them their evil heart, so that your law might bear fruit in them.
21 For the first Adam, bearing an evil heart, transgressed and was overcome, and so were all who are born from him.
22 And the infirmity became permanent; the law was in the heart of the people along with the wickedness of the root: and what was good departed, and the evil remained.
23 And the times passed, and the years were finished: and you raised up for yourself a servant named David,
24 And you told him to build a city for your name, and to offer incense and oblations to you within it.
25 And this was done for many years, but those who inhabited the city went astray,
26 In everything doing just as Adam and all his generations had done; for they too used an evil heart.
27 And so you gave your city into the hands of your enemies.
28 Do those who inhabit Babylon do any better? And is it for this reason that Zion is ruled over?
29 It happened when I came here, and I saw impieties without number: and my soul saw many sinners in this thirtieth year, and my heart failed me:
30 For I have seen how you endure those who sin, and have spared those who act impiously, and have destroyed your people, and preserved your enemies, and you have not explained why.
31 I remember nothing of how this way should be abandoned. Does Babylon act better than Zion?
32 Or has any other nation known you besides Israel? Or what tribes have believed your covenants as Jacob has?
33 Whose reward has not appeared, nor has their labor borne fruit. For traveling about, I have passed through the nations, and I have seen them abounding in wealth, and not remembering your commandments.
34 Now therefore, weigh our iniquities in a balance, and the iniquities of those who inhabit the world; and your name will not be found except in Israel.
35 Or when have those who inhabit the earth not sinned in your sight? Or what nation has so observed your commandments?
36 You will find some individuals by name who have kept your commandments, but you will not find nations.

### CHAPTER IV.

-> The presumption of the curious seeker is rebuked, <-
-> by the use of various parables. <-

1 And the Angel who was sent to me, whose name was Uriel, answered
2 And said to me: Your heart has gone too far in this world, and you think to understand the way of the Most High?
3 And I said: Yes, my Lord. And he answered me, and said: I have been sent to show you three ways, and to set three parables before you.
4 If you can explain one of these to me, I also will show you the way you desire to see, and I will teach you where the evil heart comes from.

<column-break/>

5 And I said: Speak, my Lord. And he said to me: Go, weigh for me the weight of fire, or measure for me the blast of wind, or call back for me the day that has passed.
6 And I answered and said: Who among the living could do this, that you should ask me about such things?
7 And he said to me: If I were asking you, saying: How many dwellings are in the heart of the sea, or how many springs are at the source of the deep, or how many veins are above the firmament, or what are the exits of paradise:
8 You would perhaps say to me, "I have not descended into the deep, nor yet into hell, nor have I ever climbed up into heaven."
9 But now I have only asked you about fire, and wind, and the day through which you have passed, and things from which you cannot be separated: and yet you have not answered me about them.
10 And he said to me: You cannot know the things that are yours and grow up with you;
11 How then can your vessel <note>The human mind or body, often described in ancient texts as a "vessel" for the soul or for knowledge.</note> comprehend the way of the Most High, and—in a world already corrupted from the outside—understand the corruption that is evident before me?
12 And I said to him: It would be better if we did not exist at all than to live in impieties while still living, and to suffer, and not understand why.
13 And he answered me and said: I went out to a forest of trees of the field, and they made a plan,
14 And said: "Come, let us go and make war against the sea, so that it may recede before us, and we may make other forests for ourselves."
15 And likewise the waves of the sea also made a plan, and said: "Come, let us go up and conquer the forests of the field, so that there also we may gain another region for ourselves."
16 But the plan of the forest was in vain, for fire came and consumed it.
17 Likewise also the plan of the waves of the sea failed, for the sand stood firm and blocked them.
18 If you were the judge of these, which would you begin to justify, or which would you condemn?
19 And I answered and said: Certainly they both made a vain plan; for the land is given to the forest, and the sea has a place to carry its waves.
20 And he answered me and said: You have judged well, so why have you not judged for yourself?
21 For just as the land is given to the forest, and the sea to its waves, so those who inhabit the earth can understand only what is upon the earth: and those who are above the heavens can understand what is above the height of the heavens.
22 And I answered and said: I pray you, Lord, let the sense of understanding be given to me.
23 For I did not wish to ask about your higher ways, but about those things which pass by us daily: why is Israel given over as a reproach to the nations? Why has the people you loved been given to impious tribes, and the law of our fathers been brought to destruction, and the written ordinances are nowhere to be found?
24 And we pass from this world like locusts, and our life is terror and dread, and we are not even worthy to obtain mercy.
25 But what will He do for His name, which is invoked upon us? It is about these things that I have asked.
26 And he answered me and said: If you search more, you will often wonder; for the age <term>sæculum: the current world-order or era of time</term> hastens to pass away,
27 And it cannot bear the things that are promised to the righteous in future times: because this age is full of injustice and infirmities.

<meta>This page continues the dialogue between the prophet Esdras and the angel. In the preceding verses, Esdras lamented the suffering of Israel and the persistent "evil heart" inherited from Adam. Here, the angel explains the cosmic timing of God’s plan using metaphors of farming, pregnancy, and nature.</meta>

28 Regarding the things you ask, I will tell you. For evil has been sown, but its destruction has not yet come.
29 Therefore, unless that which is sown is harvested and turned over, and the place where the evil was sown passes away, the place where the good is sown will not come.
30 For a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning; how much godlessness has it produced until now, and how much will it yet produce until the threshing floor <note>original: "area," referring to the place where grain is separated, a common biblical metaphor for the final judgment</note> comes?
31 Consider for yourself: if a grain of evil seed has produced so much fruit of godlessness,
32 when the ears of grain—which are without number—are cut down, how great a threshing floor will they fill?
33 Then I answered and said, "How and when shall these things be? Why are our years so few and evil?"
34 And he answered me and said: "Do not be in a greater hurry than the Most High. For you hurry in vain to be above him; for your own emotion <note>original: "excelsus," here likely referring to Ezra's agitation or his attempt to reach beyond human understanding</note> is great."
35 Did not the souls of the righteous in their chambers <note>original: "promptuariis," meaning storehouses or secret rooms where souls await the resurrection</note> ask about these same things, saying, "How long must I hope in this way? And when will the harvest of our reward come?"
36 And Jeremiel the Archangel answered them and said: "When the number of seeds within you is fulfilled; for God has weighed the age in a balance,
37 and measured the seasons by measure, and numbered the times by number; and he will not move or disturb them until the predicted measure is fulfilled."
38 Then I answered and said, "O Lord, my master, but we all are full of godlessness.
39 Is it perhaps because of us, and because of the sins of those who inhabit the earth, that the threshing floors of the righteous are not filled?"
40 He answered me and said: "Go and ask a woman who is pregnant; when she has completed her nine months, can her womb still retain the child within her?"
41 And I said, "It cannot, Lord." Then he said to me: "In the underworld, the chambers of souls are like a womb.
42 For just as a woman in labor makes haste to escape the necessity of her pangs, so do these places hasten to give back those things that were committed to them from the beginning.
43 Then it shall be shown to you regarding the things you long to see."
44 I answered and said, "If I have found favor in your eyes, and if it is possible, and if I am worthy,
45 show me this: is there more to come than has already passed, or has more passed by than is yet to come?
46 What has passed, I know; but what is to come, I do not know."
47 And he said to me, "Stand on the right side, and I will show you the meaning of a vision."
48 So I stood and looked, and behold, a glowing furnace passed before me; and it happened that when the flame had passed, behold, the smoke remained.
49 After this, a cloud full of water passed before me and sent down a great, violent rain; and when the violence of the rain had passed, drops remained in the cloud.
50 Then he said to me: "Think on this: just as the rain is more than the drops, and the fire is more than the smoke, so the measure of what has passed exceeds. But the drops and the smoke remain."

<column-break/>

51 Then I prayed and said, "Do you think I will live until those days? Or what will happen in those days?"
52 He answered me and said, "As for the signs you ask me about, I can tell you in part; but concerning your own life, I am not sent to tell you, for I do not know."

### CHAPTER V.

-> Various signs of future things are shown to Esdras by the Angel for the hope and consolation of the captives. <-

**R**egarding the signs: behold, the days will come when those who inhabit the earth shall be seized with great dread, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith.
2 And injustice shall be increased beyond that which you yourself see now, and beyond what you heard of long ago.
3 And the region that you now see ruling shall be trodden down, and men shall see it desolate.
4 But if the Most High grants you life, you shall see after the third trumpet that the sun shall suddenly shine forth at night, and the moon three times in a day.
5 And blood shall drip from wood, and the stone shall give forth its voice, and the peoples shall be troubled.
6 and one shall reign whom those who inhabit the earth do not expect, and the birds shall migrate together.
7 And the Sodomite Sea <note>the Dead Sea</note> shall cast up fish, and give forth a voice at night which many have not known; yet all shall hear its voice.
8 And chaos shall occur in many places, and fire shall frequently break out, and wild beasts shall roam beyond their haunts, and menstruating women shall bring forth monsters.
9 And salt waters shall be found in sweet, and all friends shall fight against one another; then shall reason hide itself, and understanding shall withdraw into its own chamber.
10 It shall be sought by many and not found, and injustice and lack of self-control shall be multiplied upon the earth.
11 One region shall ask its neighbor, 'Has righteousness, or anyone who does right, passed through you?' And it will say, 'No.'
12 And it shall be at that time that men shall hope, but not obtain; they shall labor, but their ways shall not prosper.
13 I am permitted to tell you these signs; and if you pray again and weep as you do now, and fast for seven days, you shall hear even greater things than these."
14 Then I awoke, and my body trembled violently, and my soul was so troubled that it fainted.
15 But the Angel who had come to me and talked with me held me, and comforted me, and set me on my feet.
16 And it happened on the second night that Salathiel <note>traditionally identified with Ezra</note>, the leader of the people, came to me and said, "Where have you been? And why is your face so sad?
17 Do you not know that Israel has been entrusted to you in the land of their exile?
18 Rise up, therefore, and eat some bread, and do not abandon us, like a shepherd who leaves his flock in the hands of wicked wolves."
19 Then I said to him, "Go away from me, and do not come near me." And he heard me and left me.
20 So I fasted for seven days, wailing and weeping, just as Uriel the Angel had commanded me.
21 And it happened after seven days that the thoughts of my heart were again very painful to me.

22 And my soul regained the spirit of understanding, and I began again to speak words before the Most High,
23 and I said: "O Lord, my Master, from every forest of the earth and all its trees, you have chosen for yourself a single vine;
24 and from all the lands of the world, you have chosen for yourself a single dwelling place; and from all the flowers of the world, you have chosen for yourself a single lily;
25 and from all the depths of the sea, you have filled for yourself a single stream; and from all the cities that have been built, you have sanctified Zion for yourself;
26 and from all the birds that were created, you have named for yourself a single dove; and from all the livestock that were formed, you have provided for yourself a single sheep;
27 and from all the many peoples, you have acquired for yourself a single people; and to this people, whom you desired, you gave a law that has been approved by all.
28 And now, O Lord, why have you handed over this 'one' to the 'many'? And why have you dishonored <note>original: "praeparasti... super," meaning to set others over or prioritize others above the root</note> this one root above others, and scattered your only one among the many?
29 And those who spoke against your promises and did not believe your covenants have trampled them.
30 And if you truly hate your people, they ought to be punished by your own hands."
31 And it happened that when I had spoken these words, the Angel was sent to me—the one who had come to me the previous night—
32 and he said to me: "Listen to me, and I will instruct you; pay attention to me, and I will tell you more."
33 And I said: "Speak, my Lord." And he said to me: "You are deeply troubled in mind for Israel's sake. Do you love them more than he who made them?"
34 And I said to him: "No, Lord, but I spoke out of grief. For my heart <note>original: "renes mei," literally 'my kidneys,' which the ancients believed were the seat of deep emotion and conscience</note> torments me every hour as I seek to grasp the path of the Most High and to investigate a portion of his judgment."
35 And he said to me: "You cannot." And I said: "Why, Lord? For what purpose was I born? Or why did my mother’s womb <note>original: "matrix matris meae," referring to the origin of life</note> not become my grave, so that I would not see the struggle of Jacob and the exhaustion of the people of Israel?"
36 And he said to me: "Count for me the things that have not yet happened, and gather for me the scattered drops of rain, and make the withered flowers green again for me;
37 and open for me the locked storehouses <note>original: "promptuaria," used here to mean the secret places where the elements or souls are kept</note> and bring out for me the winds shut up within them; show me the image of a voice—and then I will show you the struggle you ask to see."
38 And I said: "O Lord, my Master, who is there who can know these things except one whose dwelling is not with men?
39 But I am a fool; how then can I speak of these things about which you have asked me?"
40 And he said to me: "Just as you cannot do even one of these things I have mentioned, so you will not be able to find my judgment, or the end of the love that I have promised to my people."
41 And I said: "But look, Lord, you are concerned for those who are alive at the end; but what will those do who were before me, or we ourselves, or those who come after us?"
42 And he said to me: "I will liken my judgment to a circle <note>original: "coronae," literally 'a crown' or 'wreath,' symbolizing that there is no beginning or end in God's timing</note>. Just as there is no slowness for the last, so there is no swiftness for the first."
43 And I answered and said: "Could you not have made those who have been, those who are, and those who will be, all at once, so that you might show your judgment more quickly?"
44 And he answered me and said: "A created

<column-break/>

thing cannot hurry faster than its Creator, nor could the world sustain all those created within it at one time."
45 And I said: "How then did you say to your servant that you will surely give life to your entire creation all at once? If the creation could sustain that, then it could also carry those present all at once now."
46 And he said to me: "Ask the womb of a woman, and say to her: 'If you give birth to children, why do you do so over time?' Ask her, therefore, to produce ten at once."
47 And I said: "She certainly cannot; it must be according to the proper time."
48 And he said to me: "So also have I given the 'womb' of the earth to those who are sown upon it over time.
49 For just as an infant does not bring forth the things that belong to the elderly, so have I disposed the world I created."
50 And I questioned him and said: "Since you have now given me the way, I will speak before you: is our mother, of whom you spoke to me, still young? Or is she now approaching old age?"
51 And he answered me and said: "Ask a woman who gives birth, and she will tell you.
52 For you shall say to her: 'Why are those you have brought forth now not like those who were before you, but smaller in stature?'
53 And she herself will tell you: 'Some are born in the strength of youth, and others are born in the time of old age when the womb is failing.'
54 Consider therefore that you also are smaller in stature than those who were before you;
55 and those who come after you will be smaller than you, as if the creation were already growing old and passing the strength of its youth." And I said: "I beg you, Lord, if I have found favor in your sight, show your servant through whom you will visit your creation."

### CHAPTER VI.

->*God knew all things before they happened; He created everything for the sake of man, and He considers the ends of all things.*<-

1 And he said to me: "At the beginning of the earthly world, and before the exits of the age were established, and before the gatherings of the winds blew,
2 and before the voices of thunder sounded, and before the brilliance of the lightning shone, and before the foundations of Paradise were made firm,
3 and before the beautiful flowers were seen, and before the powers of movement <note>likely referring to the orbits of stars or natural forces</note> were established, and before the innumerable armies of Angels were gathered,
4 and before the heights of the air were lifted up, and before the measures of the firmaments were named, and before the chimneys <note>original: "camini," referring to the sacrificial altars or fiery places</note> in Zion grew hot,
5 and before the present years were searched out, and before the inventions of those who now sin were cast aside, and before those who have stored up faith were sealed—
6 then I planned these things, and they were made through me alone, and not through another; and the end shall be through me, and not through another."
7 And I answered and said: "What will be the dividing of the times? Or when will the end of the first age be, and the beginning of the one that follows?"
8 And he said to me: "From Abraham to Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him...

53 And on the sixth day, you commanded the earth to create before you cattle, beasts, and creeping things;
54 and over these, you appointed Adam as leader over all the works you had made; and from him we all are brought forth, as are the people whom you have chosen.

### CHAPTER VII

*Without trials, one does not reach immortal life: and while the prayers of the righteous are effective now, after the final judgment nothing will be changed. Humanity subjects itself to various vices, but the Lord is merciful.*

1 And it happened that when I had finished speaking these words, the Angel who had been sent to me during the first nights was sent to me again,
2 and he said to me: "Rise, Esdras, and hear the words that I have come to speak to you."
3 And I said: "Speak, my God." And he said to me: "A sea is set in a wide space, so that it might be deep and immense;
4 but the entrance to it is set in a narrow place, so as to be like a river.
5 For if anyone identifies a desire to enter the sea, to look upon it or to master it, if they do not pass through the narrow part, how could they reach the wide expanse?
6 Or consider another thing: A city is built and set in a level plain, and it is full of all good things.
7 Its entrance, however, is narrow and set on a steep incline, so that there is fire on the right hand and deep water on the left.
8 And there is only one single path set between them—that is, between the fire and the water—so that the path can only hold the footprint of one man.
9 Now, if this city is given to a man as an inheritance, if he never passes through the danger set before him, how shall he receive his inheritance?"
10 And I said: "It is so, Lord." And he said to me: "So also is the portion of Israel.
11 For I made the world for their sake; and when Adam transgressed my <term>statutes</term><note>Latin: "constitutiones," referring to the divine laws or decrees given to humanity.</note>, that which was made was judged.
12 And the entrances of this world were made narrow, sorrowful, and laborious; they are few and evil, full of perils, and supported by great labor.
13 For the entrances of the greater world to come are spacious and secure, producing the fruit of immortality.
14 If, therefore, those who live do not enter these narrow and empty places, they cannot receive the things that are stored up for them.
15 Now, therefore, why are you troubled, since you are corruptible? And why are you moved, since you are mortal?
16 And why have you not considered in your heart what is to come, rather than what is present?"
17 I answered and said: "O Lord, my Master, behold, you have ordained in your law that the righteous shall inherit these things, but the ungodly shall perish.
18 The righteous, therefore, endure the narrow places while hoping for the spacious; but those who have acted impiously have suffered the narrow places and shall not see the spacious."
19 And he said to me: "There is no judge above God, nor any who has understanding above the Most High.
20 For many who are now present perish because the law of God which was set before them is neglected.
21 For God strictly commanded those who came into the world, when they came, what they should do to live, and what they should observe so as not to be punished.

<column-break/>

22 "But they were not persuaded, and spoke against him; they devised for themselves vain thoughts,
23 and proposed for themselves the deceit of sins. They even said of the Most High that he does not exist, and they did not acknowledge his ways.
24 They despised his law, denied his promises, had no faith in his statutes, and did not finish his works.
25 Because of this, Esdras: empty things for the empty, and full things for the full.
26 Behold, the time shall come, and it shall be that when the signs I have foretold to you come to pass, the bride shall appear, and she who is now withdrawn from the earth shall be shown and made visible.
27 And everyone who is delivered from the aforementioned evils shall see my wonders.
28 For my Son **JESUS** shall be revealed with those who are with him, and those who remain shall rejoice for four hundred years.
29 And it shall be after these years that my Son **CHRIST** shall die, along with all human beings who have the breath of life.
30 And the world shall be turned back into the silence of old for seven days, just as it was in the first beginnings, so that no one shall be left.
31 And it shall be after seven days that the world which is not yet awake shall be raised up, and the corruptible world shall die.
32 And the earth shall give up those who sleep in her, and the dust shall give up those who dwell in it in silence, and the <term>storehouses</term><note>Latin: "promptuaria," often interpreted as the intermediate chambers where souls await the resurrection.</note> shall give up the souls that were committed to them.
33 And the Most High shall be revealed upon the seat of judgment, and miseries shall pass away, and long-suffering shall be gathered up.
34 Only judgment shall remain, truth shall stand, and faith shall grow strong.
35 And work shall follow, and the reward shall be shown; righteous deeds shall be awake, and unrighteousness shall not have dominion.
36 And I said: 'First Abraham prayed for the people of Sodom, and Moses for the fathers who sinned in the desert,
37 and those who came after him for Israel in the days of Achaz and Samuel,
38 and David for the destruction, and Solomon for those who came to the dedication of the sanctuary,
39 and Elijah for those who received rain, and for the dead man that he might live,
40 and Hezekiah for the people in the days of Sennacherib, and many prayed for many.
41 If, therefore, now when corruption has increased and unrighteousness has multiplied, the righteous have prayed for the ungodly, why shall it not be so then?'
42 And he answered me and said: 'This present world is not the end; glory does not abide in it constantly; therefore they prayed for the weak.
43 But the day of judgment shall be the end of this time and the beginning of the future immortal time, in which corruption has passed away.
44 Intemperance is ended, unbelief is cut off, but righteousness has grown and truth has arisen.
45 For then no one will be able to save him who has perished, nor to overwhelm him who has conquered.'"
46 I answered and said: "This is my first and last word: that it would have been better not to give the earth to Adam, or when it was already given, to restrain him so that he would not sin."

### CHAPTER VIII.

<margin>God is recognized as merciful in this age for the sake of sinners, yet many are condemned; however, rewards are stored up for the righteous.</margin>

AND he answered me and said: "The Most High made this world for the sake of many, but the world to come for the sake of a few.
2 But I will tell you a parable, Esdras. Just as if you ask the earth, it will tell you that it gives much more soil from which earthenware is made, but only a little dust from which gold comes; so is the course of the present world.
3 Many indeed are created, but few shall be saved."
4 And I answered and said: "Then, O my soul, swallow up understanding and devour that which is wise.
5 For you have agreed to listen, and you wish to prophesy; but no more space is given to you than merely to live.
6 O Lord, if you will not permit your servant to pray before you, and give us seed for the heart and cultivation for the understanding so that fruit may come of it, how can any corruptible person live who carries the form of a human?
7 For you alone exist, and we are all one creation <note>original: "plasmatio", referring to the act of molding or shaping clay</note> of your hands, just as you have spoken.
8 And even as the body is now fashioned in the womb and you provide the limbs, your creation is preserved in fire and water; and for nine months your handiwork endures your creation which was created within it.
9 But both the womb that preserves and the thing that is preserved shall be preserved; and when the time comes, the womb restores again those things that grew in it.
10 For you have commanded the members themselves, that is the breasts, to provide milk for the fruit of the breasts,
11 so that what has been fashioned may be nourished for a time; and afterward you guide it by your mercy.
12 You have nourished it with your justice, and instructed it in your law, and corrected it with your understanding.
13 You shall put it to death as your own creature, and you shall make it live as your own work.
14 If therefore you should destroy him who was fashioned with such great labor, it would be easy by your command to ordain that the thing which was made should be preserved.
15 And now, Lord, I will speak: regarding every human, you know best; but regarding your people, for whom I grieve—
16 and regarding your inheritance, for whom I mourn; and for Israel, for whom I am sad; and for Jacob, for whom I am pained—
17 therefore I will begin to pray before you for myself and for them; for I see the failings of us who inhabit the earth.
18 But I have heard of the swiftness of the Judge who is to come.
19 Therefore hear my voice, and understand my words, and I will speak before you."

40 Therefore, as I have spoken, so it is.
41 For just as a farmer sows many seeds upon the ground, and plants a multitude of seedlings, but not all that are sown are saved in their time, nor do all that are planted take root: so also, of those who are sown in the world <note>original: "sæculo" — meaning the current age or world</note>, not all shall be saved.

### CHAPTER IX.

->*The judgments of God, as well as his other remarkable works, shall be preceded by certain signs.*<-

1 And he answered me, and said: Measure the time carefully within itself; and it shall be that when you see that a certain part of the predicted signs has passed,
2 Then you will understand that it is the very time in which the Most High will begin to visit the world which was made by him.
3 And when there shall appear in the world movements of places <note>earthquakes</note>, and the turmoil of peoples,
4 Then you will understand that it was of these things the Most High spoke from the days that were before you, from the beginning.
5 For just as everything that is made in the world has a beginning and likewise an end, and the end is manifest;
6 So also the times of the Most High have beginnings manifest in wonders and miracles, and endings in effects and in signs.
7 And it shall be that everyone who is saved, and who is able to escape because of his works and the faith by which you have believed, shall survive.

8 He shall be left behind from the predicted perils and shall see my salvation in my land and within my borders, for I have sanctified them for myself from the beginning of time.

10 For those who did not recognize me, though they received benefits while they lived;

18 And now, when I was preparing for those who now exist, before the world was made in which they would dwell, no one contradicted me.
19 For then everyone—and now the Creator in this prepared world, with an unfailing harvest and an unsearchable law—their ways have become corrupt.
20 And I considered the world, and behold, there was danger because of the thoughts that had come into it.
21 And I saw and spared it greatly; and I have kept for myself a grape from a cluster <note>original: "acinum de botro" — a metaphor for a small, precious remnant saved from a large group</note>, and a plant from a great tribe.

23 But if you will wait seven more days—though you shall not fast in them—

26 And I went forth, as he told me, into the field called Ardath, and I sat there among the flowers. And I ate of the herbs of the field, and that food satisfied me.
27 And it happened after seven days, as I lay upon the grass, my heart was troubled again as it was before.
28 And my mouth was opened, and I began to speak before the Most High, and I said:
29 O Lord, you showed yourself to us, you were shown to our fathers in the desert, in a place that is not trodden and is unfruitful, when they were coming out of Egypt.
30 And you spoke, saying: "Hear me, O Israel, and seed of Jacob, pay attention to my words."
31 For behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring forth fruit in you, and you shall be glorified in it forever.
32 But our fathers, receiving the law, did not keep it, and they did not observe my statutes; and yet the fruit of the law did not perish—nor could it, for it was yours.

33 But those who received it perished, because they did not keep what had been sown in them.
34 And behold, it is the custom that when the earth has received seed, or the sea a ship, or a vessel some food or drink, and that in which it was sown or placed is destroyed,
35 Then that which was sown or placed, or the things that were received, are destroyed along with it, and the things received no longer remain with us; but with us, it has not happened this way.

39 Then I dismissed the thoughts I was thinking and turned to her and said to her:

45 And it happened, after thirty years, God heard me, your handmaid, and saw my lowliness, and considered my trouble, and gave me a son. And I rejoiced over him greatly, I and my husband and all my fellow citizens, and we gave great honor to the Mighty One.
46 And I nourished him with much labor.
47 And it happened, when he had grown up and came to take a wife, I made a wedding feast."

-> Through the weeping woman, who then shines forth again, Jerusalem is shown to be represented. <-

1 AND it happened, when my son had entered into his wedding chamber, he fell down and died.
2 And we all put out the lights, and all my fellow citizens rose up to comfort me; and I rested until the next day, until night.
3 And it happened, when they had all stopped comforting me so that I might rest, I rose up by night and fled; and I came, as you see, into this field.
4 And I intend never to return to the city, but to stay here; and neither to eat nor drink, but without ceasing to mourn and to fast until I die.
5 Then I left off the words I was saying and answered her with anger, and said:
6 "You fool above all women! Do you not see our mourning, and what has happened to us?
7 For Zion, our mother, is saddened with all sadness, and is greatly humbled, and mourns most bitterly.
8 And now, since we all mourn and are sad—because we are all grieved—are you grieved for only one son?"
