### C H A P T E R XI.

->An eagle appears to Esdras in a vision, usurping the rule over the whole world.<-

1 AND I saw a dream, and behold, there rose up from the sea an eagle, which had twelve feathered wings and three heads.
2 And I looked, and behold, she spread her wings over all the earth, and all the winds of heaven blew upon her, and they were gathered together.
3 And I looked, and out of her wings grew opposing wings <note>original: "contrariae pennae" — often interpreted as smaller, rival, or secondary powers</note>, and these became small and tiny winglets.
4 For her heads were at rest, and the middle head was greater than the other heads, but it also rested with them.
5 And I looked, and behold, the eagle flew with her wings, and reigned over the earth, and over those who dwell in it.
6 And I saw that all things under heaven were subject to her, and no one spoke against her, not even one of the creatures upon the earth.
7 And I looked, and behold, the eagle rose up upon her talons, and sent out a voice to her wings, saying:
8 Do not all watch at the same time; let each sleep in his own place, and watch in turn.
9 But the heads shall be preserved for the last.
10 And I looked, and behold, the voice did not come out of her heads, but from the middle of her body.
11 And I numbered her opposing wings, and behold, there were eight of them.
12 And I looked, and behold, on the right side there rose up one wing, and it reigned over all the earth.
13 And it happened that while it reigned, its end came, and its place disappeared; and the next one rose up and reigned, and it held power for a long time.
14 And it happened that while it reigned, its end also came, so that it disappeared like the first one.
15 And behold, a voice was sent to it, saying:
16 Hear, you who have held the earth for so long a time: I announce this to you before you begin to disappear.
17 No one after you shall hold your time, nor even half of it.
18 And the third raised itself up, and held the rule just as the former ones did, and it also disappeared.
19 And so it happened to all the others, one by one, to hold the rule and then to appear no more.
20 And I looked, and behold, in time the following wings were raised up on the right side, so that they too might hold the rule; and there were some of them that

<column-break/>

held it, but yet they immediately disappeared.
21 For some of them were raised up, but did not hold the rule.
22 And after this I looked, and behold, the twelve wings disappeared, and two winglets;
23 and nothing remained in the eagle’s body except the three heads that were at rest, and six winglets.
24 And I looked, and behold, out of the six winglets, two were divided, and remained under the head that is on the right side; for four remained in their place.
25 And I looked, and behold, these under-wings <note>original: "subalares" — the smaller winglets</note> thought to raise themselves up and to hold the rule.
26 And I looked, and behold, one was raised up, but it immediately disappeared.
27 And the second disappeared even more quickly than the first.
28 And I looked, and behold, the two that remained thought within themselves that they also should reign.
29 And while they were thinking on it, behold, one of the resting heads, which was the middle one, awoke; for this was the largest of the three heads.
30 And I saw that the two heads were joined with it.
31 And behold, the head turned with those that were with it, and it ate the two under-wings that thought to reign.
32 Moreover, this head terrified all the earth, and dominated those who inhabit the earth with much labor, and it held the power of the whole world over all the wings that had been.
33 And after this I looked, and behold, the middle head suddenly disappeared, and this happened just as it did with the wings.
34 But two heads remained, which themselves likewise reigned over the earth and over those who dwell in it.
35 And I looked, and behold, the head on the right side devoured the one that was on the left.
36 Then I heard a voice saying to me: Look before you, and consider what you see.
37 And I looked, and behold, something like a lion was roused out of the forest, roaring; and I saw that it sent out a human voice to the eagle. And it spoke, saying:
38 Listen, you, and I will speak to you, and the Most High shall say to you:
39 Are you not the one who remains of the four animals <note>A reference to the vision in the Book of Daniel, chapter 7, regarding four great beasts representing world empires</note> which I made to reign in my world, so that through them the end of their times might come?
40 And you, the fourth, coming, have overcome all the animals that passed before, and have held the world in your power with much trembling, and the whole world with wicked labor, and for so long a time you have inhabited the world with deceit.
41 And you have judged the earth, but not with truth.
42 For you have afflicted the meek, and injured the quiet; you have loved liars, and destroyed the dwellings of those who were fruitful, and brought down the walls of those who did you no harm.
43 And your insolence has ascended to the Most High, and your pride to the Mighty One.
44 And the Most High has looked upon the proud times, and behold, they are ended, and its crimes are completed.
45 Therefore, you eagle, appear no more—you and your horrible wings, and your wicked winglets, and your malicious heads, and your cruel talons, and all your worthless body.

And it happened after seven days, I dreamed a dream in the night.

2 And behold, a wind arose from the sea, so that it stirred up all its waves.

3 And I looked, and behold, that man grew strong with the thousands of heaven; and wherever he turned his face to look, all things trembled that were seen under him.

4 And wherever the voice went out from his mouth, all who heard his voice burned, just as the earth rests when it feels fire.

5 And after this I looked, and behold, a multitude of men was gathered, without number, from the four winds of heaven, to fight against the man who had come up from the sea.

6 And I looked, and behold, he had carved out for himself a great mountain, and flew upon it.

7 But I sought to see the region or place from which the mountain had been carved, and I could not.

8 And after this I looked, and behold, all who were gathered to him to conquer him were very afraid, yet they dared to fight.

### CHAPTER XIV.

->*The Lord appears to Esdras in a bush and reveals certain future secrets.*<-

And it happened on the third day, I was sitting under an oak tree.
2 And behold, a voice came out of a bush opposite me, and said, "Esdras, Esdras!" And I said, "Here I am, Lord." And I stood up on my feet. Then he said to me:
3 "I did indeed reveal myself upon the bush, and spoke to Moses when my people were serving in Egypt;
4 and I sent him, and led my people out of Egypt, and brought them to Mount Sinai, and I kept him with me for many days.
5 I told him many wondrous things, and showed him the secrets of the times and the end; and I commanded him, saying:
6 'These words you shall make public, and these you shall hide.'
7 And now I say to you:
8 The signs which I have shown, and the dreams which you have seen, and the interpretations which you have heard—lay them up in your heart.

<column-break/>

9 For you shall be taken up from among all people; you shall dwell with my Son <note>A reference to the Messiah or the divine council</note> and with those like you, until the times are ended.
10 For the age has lost its youth, and the times begin to grow old.
11 For the age is divided into twelve parts, and ten parts of it and half of a tenth part have already passed.
12 And what remains is after the half of the tenth part.
13 Now, therefore, set your house in order, and reprove your people; comfort the lowly among them, and renounce now this corruption.
14 Let go of mortal thoughts, cast away from yourself human burdens, and put off now your weak nature. Set aside the thoughts that are most troublesome to you, and hasten to depart from these times.
15 For worse evils than those you have now seen happen will yet take place.
16 For the more the world becomes weak through old age, the more shall evils increase upon those who dwell in it.
17 For truth has withdrawn further away, and falsehood has drawn near. For even now the vision which you saw hastens to come."
18 Then I answered and said before you, O Lord:
19 "Behold, I will go as you have commanded me, and I will reprove the people who are now present. But as for those who shall be born afterward, who shall warn them?
20 For the world is set in darkness, and those who dwell in it are without light.
21 For your Law has been burned <note>Referring to the destruction of the Temple and the sacred scrolls during the Babylonian conquest of Jerusalem</note>, and therefore no one knows the things that have been done by you, or the works that are about to begin.
22 But if I have found favor before you, send the <term>Holy Spirit</term> into me, and I shall write everything that has happened in the world from the beginning, which were written in your Law, so that people may be able to find the path, and that those who wish to live in the last days may live."
23 And he answered me and said, "Go, gather the people, and tell them not to seek you for forty days.
24 But prepare for yourself many <term>boxwood tablets</term> <note>original: "buxos" — tablets used for writing</note>, and take with you Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Echanus, and Asiel—these five, who are ready to write swiftly.
25 And come here, and I shall light a lamp of understanding in your heart, which shall not be extinguished until the things you are about to write are finished.
26 And when you have finished, some things you shall make public, and some you shall deliver in secret to the wise. Tomorrow at this hour you shall begin to write."
27 Then I went out as he commanded me, and gathered all the people, and said:
28 "Hear these words, O Israel:
29 Our fathers dwelt as strangers in Egypt from the beginning, and were delivered from there.
30 They received the <term>law of life</term>, which they did not keep, and which you also have transgressed after them.
31 Then the land was given to you as a possession, even the land of Zion; but you and your fathers committed iniquity, and did not keep the ways which the Most High commanded you.
32 And because he is a righteous judge, he took from you in due time what he had given.
33 And now you are here, and your brothers are further inland."

43 But at night they ate bread; as for me, I spoke by day and was not silent at night.
44 In forty days, two hundred and four books were written.
45 And it came to pass, when the forty days were fulfilled, the Most High spoke, saying: The first books that you have written, publish openly, and let the worthy and the unworthy read them;
46 but keep the seventy last books, that you may deliver them to the wise among your people.
47 For in them is the vein of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the river of knowledge. And I did so.

### CHAPTER XV.

->Many calamities are predicted to come upon the world.<-

1 Behold, speak in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, which I will put into your mouth, says the Lord;
2 and cause them to be written on paper, for they are faithful and true.
3 Do not fear the plots against you, and do not let the unbelief of those who speak against you trouble you.
4 For every unbeliever shall die in his unbelief.
5 Behold, I am bringing, says the Lord, evils upon the whole world: the sword, and famine, and death, and destruction.
6 Because iniquity has completely polluted the whole earth, and their harmful works are fulfilled.
7 Therefore says the Lord:
8 I will no longer be silent concerning their impieties which they irreligiously commit, nor will I endure them in those things which they wickedly practice; behold, innocent and righteous blood cries out to me, and the souls of the righteous cry out perseveringly.
9 I will surely avenge them, says the Lord, and I will receive all innocent blood from among them to myself.
10 Behold, my people is led as a flock to the slaughter; I will no longer suffer them to dwell in the land of Egypt;
11 but I will bring them out with a mighty hand and an up-

<column-break/>

lifted arm, and I will strike Egypt with a plague as before, and I will destroy all its land.
12 Egypt shall mourn, and its foundations shall be struck with the plague and the punishment that God shall bring upon it.
13 The farmers who till the ground shall mourn, because their seeds shall fail due to blight and hail, and by a terrible star <note>original: "sidere terribili," likely referring to a comet or an omen of celestial disaster</note>.
14 Woe to the world and those who dwell in it!
15 For the sword and their destruction have drawn near, and nation shall rise against nation to fight, with large swords <note>original: "rhomphæa," a heavy, curved Thracian blade</note> in their hands.
16 For there shall be instability among men; and prevailing over one another, they shall not regard their king, nor the chief of their ways, in their power.
17 For a man shall desire to go into a city, and shall not be able.
18 For because of their pride, the cities shall be troubled, the houses shall be destroyed, and men shall be afraid.
19 A man shall have no pity upon his neighbor, but shall bring their houses to nothing by the sword and plunder their goods, because of the hunger for bread and great tribulation.
20 Behold, I call together, says God, all the kings of the earth to fear me, those who are from the East, and from the South, and from the East wind, and from Lebanon; to turn themselves against one another, and to repay what they have given them.
21 Just as they do even today to my chosen, so will I do and repay into their bosom. Thus says the Lord God.
22 My right hand shall not spare the sinners, nor shall the sword cease over those who shed innocent blood upon the earth.
23 Fire went forth from his wrath and has consumed the foundations of the earth, and the sinners like burnt straw.
24 Woe to those who sin and do not observe my commandments, says the Lord.
25 I will not spare them. Depart, you children, from the power; do not defile my sanctuary.
26 For the Lord knows all who sin against him; therefore he has delivered them unto death and unto slaughter.
27 For now calamities have come upon the whole world, and you shall remain in them; for God shall not deliver you, because you have sinned against him.
28 Behold, a horrible vision, and its face is from the East.
29 And the nations of the Arabian dragons <note>metaphorical for fierce desert warriors or armies</note> shall come out with many chariots, and as a wind their number shall be carried over the earth, so that all who hear them shall fear and tremble.
30 The Carmanians <note>referring to the people of Carmania, an ancient province of the Persian Empire</note>, raging in wrath, shall go forth like wild boars from the forest, and they shall come with great power and join battle with them, and shall lay waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.
31 And after this, the dragons, mindful of their origin, shall prevail, and turning themselves, they shall conspire in great power to pursue them.
32 These shall be troubled and silenced by their power, and shall turn their feet in flight.
33 And from the territory of the Assyrians an embattled one shall besiege them, and consume one of them, and there shall be fear and trembling in their army, and contention among their kings.
34 Behold, clouds from the East and from the North as far as the South, and their face is very horrible, full of wrath and storm.
35 And they shall collide with one another, and they shall clash a great star upon the earth, and their star; and there shall be blood from the sword as high as a horse's belly.

36 And the dung of man shall reach as high as a camel's belly, and there shall be great fear and trembling upon the earth.
37 And those who see that wrath shall be horrified, and trembling shall seize them. And after this, heavy rain-clouds shall be moved
38 From the south and the north, and another portion from the west.
39 And the winds from the east shall prevail over them and shall shut them up: even the cloud which I raised in my wrath; and the star <note>original: "sidus," likely referring to a comet or a destructive celestial omen common in apocalyptic literature</note> appointed to bring destruction by the east wind and the west wind shall be violated.
40 And great and mighty clouds, full of wrath, shall be lifted up, along with the star, to terrify all the earth and those who dwell in it; and they shall pour out upon every high and eminent place a terrible star,
41 Fire and hail, and flying swords <note>original: "rhompheas volantes," a rhomphaea was a large, ancient thracian sword; here it signifies a divine weapon of war</note>, and much water, so that even all the fields and all the rivers shall be filled with the fullness of those many waters.
42 And they shall destroy cities, and walls, and mountains, and hills, and the trees of the forests, and the grass of the meadows, and their grain.
43 And they shall go steadily on even unto Babylon and shall crush it.
44 They shall come to her and surround her, and they shall pour out the star and all its wrath upon her; and dust and smoke shall go up even to heaven, and all those who are around her shall mourn for her.
45 And those who remain under her shall serve those who have brought the terror.
46 And you, Asia, who share in the hope of Babylon and are the glory of her person,
47 Woe to you, wretch, because you have made yourself like her; you have adorned your daughters for fornication, to please and glory in your lovers, who have always desired to commit fornication with you.
48 You have imitated that hateful one in all her works and her inventions. Therefore, says God,
49 I will send evils upon you: widowhood, poverty, famine, the sword, and pestilence, to lay waste your houses with violation and death; and the glory of your power
50 Shall be dried up like a flower when the heat rises that is sent upon you.
51 You shall be weakened like a poor woman who is beaten and chastised by other women, so that the powerful and your lovers shall not be able to receive you.
52 Would I be so jealous against you, says the Lord,
53 If you had not killed my chosen ones at all times, exulting with the clapping of your hands and speaking over their death when you were drunk,
54 "Adorn the beauty of your face"?
55 The reward for your fornication is in your bosom; therefore you shall receive your repayment.
56 As you will do to my chosen ones, says the Lord, so God will do to you, and will hand you over to misfortune.
57 And your children shall perish from hunger; and you shall fall by the sword, and your cities shall be crushed, and all your people in the field shall fall by the sword.
58 And those who are in the mountains shall perish from hunger, and they shall eat their own flesh and drink their own blood, out of hunger for bread and thirst for water.
59 Unhappy, you shall come across the seas, and you shall receive evils again.
60 And in passing, they shall dash against the slain city, and they shall crush some portion of your land and destroy part of your glory, as they return again to the subverted Babylon.
61 And you shall be destroyed by them like stubble, and they shall be fire to you;

<column-break/>

62 And they shall devour you, and your cities, your land, and your mountains; they shall burn all your forests and your fruitful trees with fire.
63 They shall lead your children into captivity, and they shall have your wealth for a prey, and they shall destroy the glory of your face.

### CHAPTER XVI.

->*A horrible desolation for the whole world in the coming end.*<-

Woe to you, Babylon and Asia! Woe to you, Egypt and Syria!
2 Gird yourselves with sackcloth and haircloth, and wail for your children, and lament; for your destruction is at hand.
3 A sword is sent among you, and who is there to turn it back?
4 A fire is sent among you, and who is there to quench it?
5 Evils are sent upon you, and who is there to drive them away?
6 Will anyone drive away a hungry lion in the forest, or quench a fire in the stubble as soon as it has begun to burn?
7 Will anyone turn back an arrow shot by a strong archer?
8 The mighty Lord sends the evils, and who is he that can quench them?
9 Fire has gone forth from his wrath, and who is there to extinguish it?
10 He shall flash lightning, and who will not fear? He shall thunder, and who will not tremble?
11 The Lord shall threaten, and who will not be utterly crushed before his face?
12 The earth has trembled and its foundations; the sea tosses from the deep, and its waves shall be troubled, and its fish also, before the face of the Lord and the glory of his power.
13 For strong is his right hand that bends the bow; his arrows which he shoots are sharp and will not fail when they begin to be sent to the ends of the earth.
14 Behold, the evils are sent forth and shall not return until they come upon the earth.
15 The fire is kindled and shall not be extinguished until it consumes the foundations of the earth.
16 Just as an arrow shot by a mighty archer does not return, so the evils that shall be sent upon the earth shall not return.
17 Woe is me! Woe is me! Who will deliver me in those days?
18 The beginning of sorrows and many groans; the beginning of famine and much death; the beginning of wars, and powers shall stand in fear; the beginning of evils, and all shall tremble.
19 What shall I do in these things when the evils come?
20 Behold, famine and plague, tribulation and anguish, are sent as lashes for correction <note>original: "emendatione," implying these disasters are intended to discipline or reform humanity</note>.
21 And for all these things they will not turn from their iniquities, nor be always mindful of the lashes.
22 Behold, grain shall be so cheap <note>original: "annonae vilitas," a term for a low price of provisions, which here suggests a period of false prosperity before a sudden collapse</note> upon the earth that they will think peace is established for them; and then shall evils sprout upon the earth: the sword, famine, and great confusion.
23 For many of those who dwell on the earth shall perish by famine, and the sword shall destroy the rest who survive the famine.
24 And the dead shall be cast out like dung, and there shall be no one to comfort them; for the earth shall be left a desert, and the cities shall be cast down.

<summary>This page contains a series of intense apocalyptic warnings against the nations of the ancient world, predicting total destruction through fire, famine, and war as divine punishment. It emphasizes that these global disasters are unavoidable "lashes" meant for human correction, though the people remain unrepentant.</summary>
<keywords>Babylon, Asia, Egypt, Syria, divine wrath, famine, sword, apocalypse, day of judgment, Ezra prophecies, desolation</keywords>

25 None shall be left to till the earth, or to sow it.
26 The trees shall give fruit, but who shall gather it?
27 The grapes shall ripen, but who shall tread them? For in all places there shall be great desolation.
28 For one man shall desire to see another, or even to hear his voice.
29 Out of a city, only ten shall be left; and from the field, only two, who have hidden themselves in thick woods and in the clefts of the rocks.
30 Just as three or four olives are left upon each tree in an olive yard;
31 Or as a few clusters are left in a vineyard by those who search through the vines diligently:
32 So in those days, three or four shall be left by those who search through their houses with the sword <note>original: "rhomphæa," a large, ancient sword; here it represents the violent purging of the population</note>.
33 And the earth shall be left desolate, and its fields shall grow old; its roads and all its paths shall grow thorns, because no man shall travel through them.
34 The virgins shall mourn, having no bridegrooms; the women shall mourn, having no husbands; their daughters shall mourn, having no help.
35 Their bridegrooms shall be consumed in war, and their husbands shall be wiped out by famine.
36 But hear these things, and understand them, O you servants of the Lord.
37 Behold the word of the Lord; receive it. Do not believe in the gods of whom the Lord speaks.
38 Behold, the evils draw near, and they do not linger.
39 Just as a pregnant woman, when she brings forth her son in the ninth month, as the hour of her delivery approaches, two or three hours before, pains encompass her womb, and when the infant comes forth from the womb, they do not delay for a single moment:
40 Even so the evils shall not delay in coming upon the earth; the world shall groan, and pains shall encompass it.
41 Hear the word, my people: prepare yourselves for battle, and in the midst of these evils, be like strangers upon the earth <note>This encourages the faithful to remain unattached to worldly possessions, as they are only passing through a collapsing society</note>.
42 Let him who sells be as one who will flee; and he who buys, as one who is about to lose what he has.
43 He who trades, as if he will gain no profit; and he who builds, as if he will never dwell there.
44 He who sows, as if he will not reap; and he who prunes the vineyard, as if he will not gather the grapes.
45 Those who marry, as if they will produce no children; and those who do not marry, as if they were widowed.
46 Therefore, those who labor, labor in vain:
47 For strangers shall reap their fruits, and seize their goods, and overthrow their houses, and take their children captive; for in captivity and famine they beget their offspring.
48 And those who deal in robbery, the longer they adorn their cities and houses, their possessions and their persons:
49 The more I will be angry with them for their sins, says the Lord.
50 Just as a virtuous and very good woman is jealous of a harlot:
51 So shall Justice be jealous of Iniquity <note>original: "zelabitur iustitia iniquitatem," meaning Justice will zealously confront or contend with wrongdoing</note> when she adorns herself, and shall accuse her to her face, when He comes who will defend him that searches out every sin upon the earth.
52 Therefore, do not be like her, nor like her works.

<column-break/>

53 For in yet a little while, iniquity shall be taken away from the earth, and Justice shall reign over you.
54 Let not the sinner say that he has not sinned: for coals of fire shall burn upon his head who says: "I have not sinned before the Lord God and His glory."
55 Behold, the Lord knows all the works of men, and their inventions, and their thoughts, and their hearts.
56 For He said: "Let the earth be made," and it was made; "Let the heaven be made," and it was made.
57 And by His word the stars were established, and He knows the number of the stars.
58 He searches the abyss and its treasures; He has measured the sea and its contents.
59 He shut up the sea in the midst of the waters, and by His word He suspended the earth above the waters.
60 He spread out the heaven like a vaulted ceiling; He founded it upon the waters.
61 He placed springs of water in the desert, and lakes upon the tops of the mountains to send forth rivers from the high rocks to water the earth.
62 He formed man, and placed his heart in the middle of his body, and breathed into him spirit, life, and understanding,
63 And the breath of God Almighty, who made all things and searches out all hidden things in the secrets of the earth.
64 He surely knows your schemes, and what you think in your hearts, you who sin and wish to hide your sins.
65 For the Lord has searched out all your works with scrutiny, and He will bring you all to shame.
66 And you shall be confounded when your sins are brought forth before men, and your iniquities shall stand as your accusers in that day.
67 What will you do? Or how will you hide your sins before God and His angels?
68 Behold, God is the judge; fear Him. Cease from your sins, and forget your iniquities—never commit them again—and God will lead you forth and deliver you from all tribulation.
69 For behold, a burning heat <note>original: "ardor," likely referring to the fire of persecution</note> of a great multitude is kindled over you; they shall seize some of you and feed you with things sacrificed to idols.
70 And those who consent to them shall be held in derision, and in reproach, and shall be trodden underfoot.
71 For in every place, and in the neighboring cities, there shall be a great uprising against those who fear the Lord.
72 They shall be like madmen, sparing no one, but plundering and destroying those who still fear the Lord.
73 For they shall lay waste and plunder their goods, and cast them out of their houses.
74 Then the trial of my chosen ones shall appear, like gold that is tested by fire.
75 Hear, my beloved, says the Lord: Behold, the days of tribulation are at hand, but I will deliver you from them.
76 Do not fear, and do not hesitate, for God is your guide.
77 And you who keep my commandments and precepts, says the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift themselves up.
78 Woe to those who are bound by their sins and overwhelmed by their iniquities, even as a field is choked by a forest and its path overgrown with thorns, so that no man can pass through; it is shut out and left to be devoured by fire.

# INTERPRETATION OF HEBREW,
## CHALDEAN,
### AND GREEK NAMES.

## A
**Aaron**, Mountain, or mountaineer.
**Abba**, Father; it is a Syrian word.
**Abarim**, Passages (a plural noun), or those crossing over.
**Abdemelech**, Servant of the king.
**Abdenago**, Servant of brightness.
**Abdias**, Servant of the Lord.
**Abdon**, Servant.
**Abel**, (spelled with the letter *aleph*), Mourning, or a City.
**Abel**, (spelled with the letter *he* at the beginning), Vanity; the son of Adam.
**Abessalom**, Father of peace.
**Abia**, Father of the Lord.
**Abiathar**, Excellent father.
**Abigail**, Father of exultation.
**Abimelech**, Father-king.
**Abinadab**, Willing father.
**Abishag**, <note>original: Abifag</note> The father’s ignorance.
**Abner**, The father’s lamp.
**Abra**, Maidservant; a Greek word.
**Abram**, Exalted father.
**Abraham**, Father of a multitude.
**Absalom**, Father of peace.
**Achan**, <note>original: Acan</note> Tribulation.
**Ekron**, <note>original: Accaron</note> Barrenness.
**Ahab**, <note>original: Achab</note> Brother of the father.
**Achaia**, <note>original: Achaja</note> Pain, or sadness.
**Ahaz**, <note>original: Achaz</note> Seizing, or possessing.
**Ahimelech**, <note>original: Achimelech</note> My brother is king.
**Ahitub**, <note>original: Achitob</note> Brother of goodness.
**Adam**, Man, or earthly, or Red.
**Adon**, Lord, or a base/foundation.
**Adonai**, My lords (in the plural number): this is one of the names of God, which the translator sometimes used in place of the four-letter name of God. <note>original: "tetragrammaton" (YHWH)</note>
**Adonijah**, <note>original: Adonias</note> The Lord is the ruler.
**Egypt**, <note>original: Ægyptus</note> Narrowness, or tribulations; in Hebrew, it is called *Misraim*.
**Aeneas**, Praised.
**Ethiopia**, In Greek, it signifies burning heat. In Hebrew it is called *Cush*, which means blackness, or black.
**Agabus**, Locust.
**Agag**, Roof.
**Hagar**, <note>original: Agar</note> A stranger or sojourner.
**Haggai**, <note>original: Aggæus</note> Festive.
**Ehud**, <note>original: Ahod</note> Praising.
**Alexander**, Manly helper.
**Alexandria**, In Hebrew it is called *No*: which is interpreted as raw, or irritation.
**Alleluia**, Praise the Lord.
**Amalek**, <note>original: Amalech</note> A licking people.
**Amam**, Mother, or their fear.
**Haman**, <note>original: Aman</note> Disturbing.
**Amana**, Faith or truth.
**Amasai**, (spelled with the letter *aleph*), Strong or robust.

<column-break/>

**Amasai**, (spelled with the letter *ayin*), Gift of the people.
**Amalek**, <note>original: Amalech</note> King.
**Amen**, So be it, let it be done, or it is firm.
**Aminadab**, A willing people.
**Ammon**, His people.
**Amnon**, Faithful, or true.
**Amorites**, <note>original: Amorrhæi</note> Bitter ones, or Rebels.
**Amos**, (spelled with the letter *aleph*), Strong; the father of Isaiah.
**Amos**, (spelled with the letter *ayin*), Burdened; one of the twelve Prophets.
**Omri**, <note>original: Amri</note> (spelled with the letter *aleph*), Bitter, or speaking.
**Omri**, <note>original: Amri</note> (spelled with the letter *ayin*), A handful or dominion; a leader of the Israelite army.
**Ananias**, <note>original: Anania</note> Cloud of the Lord.
**Anathoth**, Answers, or songs.
**Andrew**, <note>original: Andreas</note> Very strong.
**Anna**, Gracious, or merciful.
**Antioch**, <note>original: Antiochia</note> For a vehicle.
**Africa**, In Hebrew it is called *Pul*, which means a fall or ruin, as in Isaiah 66:19.
**Africa**, In Nahum 3:9, called *Put*: meaning thick, or fat.
**Apostle**, <note>original: Apostolus</note> One who is sent, an envoy.
**Arabs**, <note>original: Arabes</note> Those of the evening, as in 2 Chronicles 26:7.
**Arabs**, In Psalm 72:15, in Hebrew it is *Saba*, which means conversion.
**Aram**, Height, or Sublimity.
**Ararat**, Curse of trembling.
**Arba**, <note>original: Arbee</note> Four.
**Master of the Feast**, <note>term: Architriclinus (The head of a banquet or the person in charge of the dining couches)</note> Leader of the dining room.
**Areopagite**, Of Mars' Hill.
**Areopagus**, Mars' Hill.
**Araunah**, <note>original: Areuna</note> Ark, or a song.
**Argob**, A clod of earth, or gravel.
**Armenia**, In Hebrew it is called *Ararat*, the Curse of trembling.
**Arnon**, Exulting.
**Arphaxad**, Healing.
**Artaxerxes**, Light, or a curse.
**Asaph**, Gathering.
**Asir**, <note>original: Afer</note> (spelled with the letter *samech*), Bound, the son of Kohath.
**Asher**, <note>original: Afer</note> (spelled with the letter *sin*), Blessedness, or happiness; the son of Jacob.
**Ahasuerus**, <note>original: Assuerus</note> Prince and head.
**Asshur**, <note>original: Assur</note> One lying in wait, or blessed.
**Ashtaroth**, <note>original: Astaroth</note> Flocks, or riches.
**Athaliah**, <note>original: Athalia</note> Time for the Lord.
**Athens**, <note>original: Athenæ</note> Without a heap.
**Attalia**, Increasing, or nourishing.
**Avva**, <note>original: Ava</note> Iniquity.
**Achsah**, <note>original: Axa</note> Adorned.
**Azariah**, <note>original: Azarias</note> Help of the Lord.
**Azor**, Helper.
**Ashdod**, <note>original: Azotus</note> In Hebrew *Ashdod*, meaning Plundering.

<meta>This page transitions from the index of names (Etymological Index) to the Biblical Index (Index Biblicus), which functions as a thematic concordance. While the previous page focused on the meanings of Hebrew and Greek names, this section begins an alphabetical subject index, providing chapter and verse references for key figures and concepts. Note that the book titles follow the Vulgate numbering (e.g., 3 Kings is 1 Kings in modern bibles).</meta>

# BIBLICAL INDEX,

## WHICH COMPRISES THOSE MATTERS DEALT WITH IN THE HOLY BIBLE,

->reduced to certain headings, arranged in alphabetical order, and completed with the greatest brevity.<-

In this Biblical Index, DEAR READER, the first number denotes the chapter of the book; the numbers immediately following up to this symbol †, or (if this symbol is not present) up to the next citation of a following book, are again marks for the verses in that same chapter. For example, under the entry AARON, for Exodus 4:14, 16, 30 † 5:1 † 6:13 † 7:1, 2, it should be read as: Exodus chapter 4, verses 14, 16, and 30; likewise chapter 5, verse 1; chapter 6, verse 13; chapter 7, verses 1 and 2. However, when an asterisk or star is placed next to a number in this manner (Lev. 8*), it is an indication that the matter being discussed is treated throughout several verses in that chapter; or it signifies that the place is to be noted more diligently than the others. Furthermore, if what you are looking for does not happen to be found so clearly in the verse noted here, then you should examine some of the neighboring verses, either preceding or following. Regarding the names of the books, for easier and more certain distinction, it has been observed that *Eccle.* denotes Ecclesiastes, while *Eccli.* denotes Ecclesiasticus <note>Also known as the Wisdom of Sirach, a book found in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles</note>.

---

**AARON** is joined to his brother Moses as a companion. Exodus 4:14, 16, 30* † 5:1* † 6:13 † 7:1, 2. Micah 6:4. He was the great-grandson of Levi. Exodus 6:16, 18, 20. He is consecrated by a special rite with his sons to the ministry of the priesthood. Leviticus 8* Numbers 3:10. Deuteronomy 18:5. Hebrews 5:4. Just as the Lord had prescribed. Exodus 29* † 40:12. The priestly ornaments of Aaron and his sons. Exodus 28*. Those who refused to acknowledge the authority of Aaron the priest perish by an unusual kind of death. Numbers 16:3, 11, 30, 31. Aaron is shown by a remarkable miracle to have been chosen by God as High Priest above all others. Numbers 17:5, 8. After making the offering, he blesses the people with an extended hand. Leviticus 9:22. By perpetual right, he receives offerings and first-fruits from the people for his priestly office. Numbers 18:8, 9, 11, 12* and from the Levites, a tenth of the tithes. Numbers 18:26, 28. He dies. Numbers 20:20 <note>original: "20. 20" - likely a typo for 20:28</note> † 33:38. Deuteronomy 10:6 † 32:50. Eleazar succeeds him in the High Priesthood. Numbers 20:28. Deuteronomy 10:6. Praise of Aaron. Ecclesiasticus 45:7, 8, 9*.

### H

**HERETICS and infidels** are left by God for the testing of the righteous. Judges 3:1. 1 Corinthians 11:19.
Heretics have existed even from the times of the Apostles. 1 Timothy 1:20. 2 Timothy 2:18. 1 John 2:18. 2 John 7. Revelation 2:15.
It was predicted that there would be heretics even in our own times. Matthew 24:5, 24. John 5:43. 1 Timothy 4:1. 2 Timothy 3:1. 2 Peter 2:1, 3:3. Jude 18.
The deaths and doctrine of heretics are found in the same place.
Heretics are to be avoided. Deuteronomy 13:1. Matthew 7:15. Romans 16:17. 2 Timothy 2:17, 3:5. Titus 3:10. 2 Thessalonians 3:14. 2 John 10.
Heretics are poorly tolerated by rulers <note>original: "præfectis", referring to civil or church leaders</note>. Revelation 2:14.
Heretics are to be removed from the midst <note>original: "tollendi e medio"</note>. Deuteronomy 13:5, 18:20. 1 Kings <note>original: "3 Reg."</note> 18:40. 2 Kings <note>original: "4 Reg."</note> 10:25.
**Heresy**, spiritual fornication. See **Fornication**.
**HAZAEL**, servant of Ben-hadad, king of Syria. 2 Kings 8:11, 15. According to the command of the Lord (1 Kings 19:15), he struck Israel in all their borders. 2 Kings 20:32 <note>likely 10:32</note>, 12:17, 13:3. Just as it was prophesied (2 Kings 8:11, 13), he dies. 13:24.
**ELIJAH** <note>original: "HELIAS"</note>, a hairy man, wearing a leather belt around his waist. 2 Kings 1:8.
